Article.Title: Longitudinal pre-diagnostic blood samples predict osteoporosis risk
Article.Authors: Lassen J.; Nielsen K.; Hindhede L.; Mikkelsen S.; Kjerulff B.; Ostrowski S.; Sørensen E.; Mikkelsen C.; Pedersen O.; Bruun M.; Aagaard B.; Johannsen M.; Erikstrup C.; Villesen P.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Cross-sectional biomarker discovery studies for degenerative diseases are limited by selection bias, post-diagnostic confounding, and high biological variability. Repeated pre-diagnostic sampling can address these limitations. We analyzed 538 plasma metabolomic profiles (1–6 samples per participant, yearly intervals) from 99 pre-diagnostic osteoporosis cases and 99 matched controls in the Danish Blood Donor Study. We compared performance of cross-sectional and longitudinal modeling using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression and random forest. Longitudinal LASSO modeling of metabolite trajectories achieved area under the curve (AUC) values between 0.67 and 0.76, outperforming cross-sectional models with AUC values of 0.57–0.63. Batch- and participant-independent validation of the best model demonstrated stable methodology (AUC: 0.70). The longitudinal data revealed that hippuric acid decreased over time in cases while increasing in controls. We conclude that longitudinal sampling costs more per participant, but the substantial information gain makes it a viable strategy when patient recruitment, not sampling capacity, is the bottleneck.

Article.Title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain
Article.Authors: Hammer V.; Ossowski S.
Article.Abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study generated the first resource of gene expression across tissue boundaries, covering five brain-meninges boundaries in the developing mouse brain. Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Overall, REBOSEP provides a systematic framework for studying gene expression regulation at tissue boundaries.

Article.Title: PTTG1 drives intestinal-type gastric cancer progression via G2/M checkpoint-mediated cell-cycle reprogramming
Article.Authors: Hu C.; Bian L.; Luo L.; Zheng Z.; Chen Y.; Gao X.; Li F.; Yang D.; Liu Y.; Li G.; Xu H.; Yan C.; Jin G.
Article.Abstract: Intestinal-type gastric cancer (IGC) progresses through the Correa cascade, yet the molecular determinants of this transition remain insufficiently defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on matched normal, intestinal metaplasia, and tumor tissues from five patients, we identified eight epithelial subtypes, including a transitional enterocyte population that expanded along the disease trajectory. Pseudotime and network analyses revealed a progressive upregulation of PTTG1 , which was further supported by public cohorts, bulk transcriptomics, and tissue microarrays. Functional assays demonstrated that PTTG1 knockdown impaired G2/M checkpoint regulation and reduced gastric cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas its overexpression enhanced organoid growth and altered mucin-related features. In xenograft models, PTTG1 depletion suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by secretory differentiation-associated histological changes. Collectively, these findings suggest that PTTG1 contributes to intestinal-type gastric cancer progression by regulating G2/M checkpoint-associated programs and modulating mucin-associated phenotypes, supporting its potential as a risk biomarker and candidate therapeutic target for IGC prevention.

Article.Title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics uncovers region-specific molecular features underlying selective aging vulnerability of cholinergic neurons
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Chen J.; Liu X.; Gong H.; Li X.; Ren M.
Article.Abstract: Cholinergic neurons exhibit functional and molecular heterogeneity across the basal forebrain (BF), midbrain (MB), and brainstem (BS), while the aging-associated transcriptional features remain poorly characterized. Here, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on 108,062 nuclei from the MS/VDB, HDB/SI, PPTG/LDTG, 7N, and 12N in adult and aged mice. BF cells showed greater age-associated transcriptomic alterations than MB and BS cells, with pronounced region-specific divergence among cholinergic neurons. Intercellular communication analysis revealed BF-specific age-related changes in APP and ApoE signaling. Within this altered milieu, intrinsic transcriptional responses varied across brain regions. In aged BF cholinergic neurons, transcriptional responses were characterized by increased oxidative stress and inflammatory signatures and reduced expression of genes involved in neuronal structural maintenance. In contrast, MB and BS cholinergic neurons maintained relatively stable transcriptional profiles. These findings reveal region-specific associations between extracellular signaling and intrinsic transcriptional stress, highlighting a selective imbalance that underlies the vulnerability of BF cholinergic neurons.

Article.Title: Global epidemiological and genetic burden of rare neurological diseases in children
Article.Authors: Xie Z.; Sun C.; Liang W.; Zhao X.; Miao L.; Liu X.; Lu Y.; Liu C.; Yin Z.; Li J.; Xie Z.
Article.Abstract: We assessed the global burden of rare childhood neurological diseases from 1990 to 2021 and projected trends to 2050 using Global Burden of Disease data, alongside an analysis of the genetic burden from ClinVar. Four neurological conditions were classified as rare childhood neurological diseases: motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis, neuroblastoma and other peripheral nervous cell tumors, and other neurological disorders. From 1990 to 2021, the global age-standardized prevalence and disability-adjusted life-year rates of rare childhood neurological diseases increased, with higher burdens among boys and in low-middle sociodemographic index countries. Our customized forecasting model projected that 110.2 thousand children would be affected by 2050, representing an 11.83% increase from 2021. Annual and cumulative increases in newly reported disease-causing genes and pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic neurological diseases were observed from 1990 to 2024. The increasing and disparate burden of rare childhood neurological diseases highlights the need for targeted prevention.

Article.Title: Enabling climate action: A nexus approach for delivering co-benefits across biodiversity, water, food, and health
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Gupta H.; Díaz-José J.; McElwee P.; Tirado M.; Cherubini F.; Duchková H.; Llope M.; Vale M.; Khan S.; Ito A.; Hori M.; Eriksen S.; Tiwari L.; Phang S.; Mason-D’Croz D.; Xu X.; van Huysen T.; Herrero M.; Ricketts T.; Harrison P.; Smith P.
Article.Abstract: Climate response options rarely affect biodiversity, water, food, and health in uniform ways. This comparative analysis examines why technically viable response options generate uneven cross-nexus outcomes, and how governance and justice conditions shape whether these outcomes become durable co-benefits. Anchored in the IPBES Nexus Assessment, the analysis synthesizes evidence from fifteen response options spanning land, ocean, energy, urban, industrial, and societal transitions. Ecosystem-centered and demand-side pathways more consistently produce synergies because they work through ecological functions that connect several nexus elements. Infrastructure- and technology-centered options deliver mitigation and health gains, but their wider effects are more context-dependent and often shaped by land use, water demand, biodiversity risk, tenure, access, and benefit-sharing. These patterns do not arise from technical design alone. By integrating nexus governance with Earth System Justice, the analysis indicates how cross-sectoral coordination, distributive equity, procedural inclusion, accountable finance, and knowledge pluralism can shape legitimacy and durability. Climate action is more likely to deliver sustained system-wide benefits when institutions align ecological interdependencies with social rights and responsibilities. Otherwise, promising interventions may remain partial, contested or short-lived.

Article.Title: Caloric restriction attenuates NLRP3 inflammasome activation and oxidative stress in leukocytes of patients with obesity
Article.Authors: López-Domènech S.; Perea-Galera L.; Pelechá-Salvador M.; Abad-Jiménez Z.; Hermenejildo J.; Fernández-Reyes M.; Luna-Marco C.; Cacace J.; Veses S.; Morillas C.; Víctor V.; Rocha M.
Article.Abstract: Obesity promotes chronic low-grade inflammation through metabolic stress and activation of the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome. The effects of caloric restriction on this pathway in humans are poorly understood; therefore, we evaluated the impact of a 6-month hypocaloric dietary intervention in 45 adults with obesity by assessing the metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, and inflammasome-related markers in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Weight loss improved metabolic parameters, reduced oxidative stress, and decreased the expression of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB), NLRP3, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), and pro-caspase-1, while there tended to be a reduction of active caspase-1. These changes were accompanied by lower circulating interleukin (IL)-1β (IL-1β) and IL-18 levels, suggesting systemic attenuation of inflammasome activity. Baseline adiposity and insulin resistance influenced the magnitude of the response to dietary intervention. These findings support caloric restriction as a strategy to mitigate obesity-associated immunometabolic dysfunction and identify the redox-inflammasome axis as a potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Chen R.; Ding S.
Article.Abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

Article.Title: A common germline 3′ UTR variant controls DDIT4 translation efficiency and stress responses in cancer cells
Article.Authors: Hamadou M.; Alunno L.; Venturelli T.; Valentini S.; Dalfovo D.; Lorenzini F.; Mattivi A.; Vigorito V.; Grupelli G.; Matte’ A.; Gatto P.; Pancher M.; Valentini C.; De Sanctis V.; Bertorelli R.; Marcel V.; Cusanelli E.; Freddi S.; Bertalot G.; Zaccara S.; Mione M.; Fava L.; Romanel A.; Inga A.
Article.Abstract: Systematic strategies for identifying and classifying variants that directly modulate ribosome engagement are lacking. Here, we develop and extensively validate a pipeline to identify translation-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (tranSNPs) by integrating analysis of total and polysome-associated mRNAs. Common variants showing allele-specific enrichment in polysomes, without corresponding changes in mRNA levels, were uncovered. We focused on rs1053639, a frequent germline SNP located in the 3′ UTR of DNA damage-inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4), a key negative regulator of mTORC1. Using edited cell models, we showed that this variant controls DDIT4 protein output. Mechanistically, the two rs1053639 alleles differ in their interaction with the RNA-binding protein RBMX, leading to altered mRNA subcellular localization and translation. Functionally, allele-specific regulation of DDIT4 translation impacts stress-dependent mTORC1 repression and autophagy, resulting in divergent competitive fitness in co-culture or xenograft assays and response to therapeutic perturbations. Analysis of cancer patient datasets revealed an association between rs1053639 genotype and clinical outcome in colorectal cancer.

Article.Title: Corrigendum to “Weak interface strong skeleton shrinkage resistant mix design for large cement stabilized base” [iScience 29 (2026) 117347]
Article.Authors: Zhang N.; Yan Z.; Wang H.; Tang D.; Zheng G.; Ma L.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Microbiota-constrained bacterial density limits phage infection in the gut and allows persistence of susceptible cells
Article.Authors: Bertola A.; Wenner N.; Rocha L.; Keys T.; Diard M.
Article.Abstract: With the rise of antibiotic resistance, bacteriophage-based treatments against bacterial infections have regained momentum. However, phage therapy has so far shown only moderate success in complex environments like the mammalian gut, where phages are particularly promising tools for microbiome engineering and specific elimination of opportunistic pathogens. Here, we use different murine models of intestinal colonization to quantitatively assess the minimal population size of susceptible Escherichia coli cells that is required for phage replication in the gut (replication threshold). We found that the composition of the intestinal microbiota is a key factor shaping phage–bacteria interactions by restricting the carrying capacity of susceptible host cells. We further demonstrate that the replication threshold enables coexistence of susceptible and resistant bacteria in phage-treated mice, with implications for phage-based applications in complex environments like the gut.

Article.Title: Where to improve the European protected areas network to represent threatened fungi?
Article.Authors: Copoț O.; Runnel K.; Lõhmus A.
Article.Abstract: To set a global example in biodiversity conservation, the European Union aims to protect 30% and strictly protect 10% of its land by 2030 and to invest in ecosystem restoration. Yet, the megadiverse fungal kingdom remains largely excluded from conservation planning and evaluation. We compiled occurrence data and developed species distribution models for 33 threatened macrofungi identified for potential inclusion under the Bern Convention across Europe. Comparing distributions of predicted habitats with existing protected-area networks provided robust evidence of large, uneven protection gaps among species and countries. We show that regionally coordinated improvements in protection and targeted habitat restoration would be more effective than addressing gaps independently within each country. By developing habitat models into tools for conservation management, spatial planning and monitoring, and by explicitly allocating those efforts across Member States, protection of neglected but threatened and functionally important taxa such as fungi can be systematically improved.

Article.Title: Similar aggregate but divergent disaggregate responses in human and AI under sequential reward-penalty incentives
Article.Authors: Tao S.; Wang L.; Zhu Z.; Lee D.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid advancement of general-purpose AI, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to simulate human decisions in structured environments. However, whether similarity in aggregate human and LLM responses extends to behavior under sequential reward-penalty incentives remains unclear. We address this question by introducing an established carbon mechanism to a repeated e-commerce delivery task and comparing decision responses between human, DeepSeek-v.3.2, and Qwen3-Max participants, wherein standard and slow delivery options are provided. In baseline settings, all participants predominantly select the theoretically dominant option. Under sequential reward-penalty incentives, all participant types shift toward slow delivery and exhibit comparably large aggregate changes. However, this aggregate-level similarity does not extend to "value of time" (VOT)-stratified response patterns and longitudinal trajectories. Humans exhibit gradual and incomplete adjustment, whereas LLMs display model-specific responses, including more stable or variable adjustment patterns depending on the model configuration. Thus, similar aggregate responses can coexist with divergent disaggregate behavioral patterns.

Article.Title: An integrated framework for agroclimatic, salinity, and groundwater assessment in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
Article.Authors: Amanov B.; Ghirardelli A.; Sherov A.; Gafarova A.; Gulomov D.; Tarolli P.
Article.Abstract: Climate change, salinization, and water scarcity increasingly threaten irrigated agricultural landscapes in arid regions. This study developed an integrated framework combining hydro-climatic, soil, and groundwater indicators to assess agricultural landscapes in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan. The framework integrated fourteen agroclimatic, soil-quality, and groundwater indicators into a unified scoring system. Results revealed persistent agroclimatic constraints during 2021–2024, with vegetation-period vapor pressure deficit (VPD) ranging from 1.91–1.37 kPa and hydrothermal coefficient (HTC) from 0.40–1.09, indicating high atmospheric water demand and semi-arid conditions. Groundwater mineralization remained predominantly within 1–3 g L −1 , while salinity risks persisted in the areas affected by shallow groundwater and elevated mineralization. Integrated assessment scores ranged from 11 to 16 points, classifying most districts as unsatisfactory in 2021 and satisfactory during 2022–2024. Zafarabad and, occasionally, Sh. Rashidov exhibited the lowest overall scores. The framework provides a practical tool for monitoring landscape vulnerability and supporting irrigation, reclamation, and salinity-management decisions.

Article.Title: Revolutionizing drought defense: The water-plant-microbe synergy in climate-smart agriculture
Article.Authors: Wang W.; He Z.; Chen J.; Ding R.; Wang L.; Chen M.; Kang J.; Tong L.; Du T.
Article.Abstract: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. While precision irrigation and microbial inoculants are recognized as effective individual strategies, their synergistic potential remains under-explored. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby defining the hydraulic niche for colonization. Conversely, functional microbes actively engineer the soil environment via exopolysaccharide production and hormonal modulation, thereby enhancing plant hydraulic status and water use efficiency (WUE). In contrast to previous reviews focusing on single factors, this review constructs an integrated framework linking soil hydrology with microbial ecology, supported by emerging comparative evidence. We conclude that future agricultural water management must shift from solely regulating water supply to managing the holobiont's hydrological interactions, offering a promising systems-level strategy to safeguard food security under climate stress.

Article.Title: Comparative efficacy of exercise modalities for mild cognitive impairment in older adults: A network meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents a critical window for dementia prevention, yet the comparative efficacy of diverse exercise modalities remains unclear. We conducted a frequentist network meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials to identify the optimal exercise intervention for improving global cognition in older adults with MCI. Combined physical-cognitive training ranked first with a 68.0% probability of being the most effective intervention, followed by Tai Chi (15.9%), while single-mode exercises and control groups showed substantially lower benefits. Interventions requiring simultaneous physical exertion and neural engagement confer superior cognitive benefits. This evidence supports tailored dual-component exercise regimens as a robust non-pharmacological strategy to mitigate cognitive decline in aging populations.

Article.Title: Harnessing hydrogel technology for advanced periodontitis therapy: A multifunctional approach to oral health restoration
Article.Authors: Zhuo X.; Wang S.; Liu L.; Zhu M.; Zhang Z.; Zhou Y.; Wang M.; Deng X.; Miao Y.; Li N.; Wang X.; Zhu H.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis is a bacterially driven inflammatory disease that can lead to tooth mobility and tooth loss. Conventional non-surgical therapy, antibiotics, and surgery may be limited by residual subgingival biofilms, antimicrobial resistance, and variable clinical outcomes. This review synthesizes recent studies of hydrogel-based systems for local periodontal therapy, focusing on stimuli-responsive release mechanisms, cargo-loading approaches, and regenerative outcomes in relevant animal models. Across these studies, hydrogels function as localized delivery matrices that can prolong retention at periodontal defects, regulate therapeutic exposure, and support tissue repair. We further evaluate translational considerations, including degradation behavior, long-term in vivo stability, and immunocompatibility. These findings position hydrogels as adaptable platforms for more precise periodontitis management and identify priorities for preclinical optimization before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Luo Y.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0–14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022–2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

Article.Title: PFKFB3 inhibition dictates the adaptive responses and cell fates in tumor cells
Article.Authors: Zheng D.; Mao Y.; Ai Z.; Song Y.; Liu X.; Xu R.; Ma C.; Meng W.; He F.; Liang H.; Ma J.
Article.Abstract: 6-Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3), a key regulator of glycolysis highly expressed in many tumor cells, has a critical role in promoting glycolysis and tumor progression. Consequently, anti-cancer strategies have sought to inhibit PFKFB3 to exploit this metabolic dependency of tumor cells. In this study, we employed a controlled protein degradation system to manipulate the kinetics of PFKFB3 depletion in investigating its impact on tumor cell growth. We show that, while slow depletion allows metabolic adaptation with a minimal effect on proliferation, rapid depletion or acute inhibition suppresses cell growth despite a similar glycolytic reduction. We show that rapid PFKFB3 loss activates AMPK, which perturbs cell cycle progression through the MAPK/ERK pathway. Importantly, AMPK inhibition was sufficient to rescue the adaptation failure caused by rapid PFKFB3 depletion. Together, our findings document that dynamic targeting of PFKFB3 can drive heterogeneous cancer cell fates, shedding light on cells' potential path toward developing resistance to anti-PFKFB3 treatments.

Article.Title: Earth-observation variables identify temperature-centered protein-family covariation across macroalgal genomes
Article.Authors: Mystikou A.; Nelson D.; El Assal D.; Jaiswal A.; Sultana M.; Rad-Menendez C.; Al-Mansoori N.; Elias S.; Abdul-Hamid M.; Nayfeh L.; Drou N.; Burt J.; Green D.; Salehi-Ashtiani K.
Article.Abstract: Macroalgal genome-environment associations are difficult to separate from lineage, geography, and uneven genome quality. We describe nine Arabian Gulf genomes and analyze them with 117 published genomes (126 total). We tested protein family (Pfam) profiles against 13 Google Earth Engine variables. Of 87,123 tests, 84 met global Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.05, and 49 pairs across 30 Pfams retained selected-family q < 0.05 with discovery-consistent direction in all seven post hoc specifications; all 13 pairs meeting global Bonferroni p < 0.05 were retained. The 49 pairs comprised 43 sea surface temperature, five depth, and one distance-to-coast association. PF16087 was positively associated with five temperature summaries, whereas PF12094 and PF01638 were negatively associated with four. A secondary same-site AlphaEarth Foundations crosswalk aligned latent axes A52 and A53 oppositely with five temperature summaries. Together, these analyses place temperature at the center of protein-family covariation in this cohort.

Article.Title: Speed-driven transitions between discrete and rhythmic dynamics in walking revealed by kinematic smoothness and muscle synergies
Article.Authors: Panconi G.; Minciacchi D.; Bravi R.; Dominici N.
Article.Abstract: Humans control movement through motor primitives that generate discrete and rhythmic actions. We investigated whether and how speed may drive a transition between discrete and rhythmic organization in walking, and whether muscle synergy changes are associated with kinematic shifts. Eighteen healthy adults walked on a treadmill during incremental and decremental trials (0.5–5 km/h in 0.5 km/h steps). Kinematics and bilateral lower-limb EMG were recorded. Smoothness was quantified using log dimensionless jerk (LDJ) and spectral arc length (SPARC). Both metrics indicated lower smoothness at low speeds and progressively stabilized as speed increased, with a transition region around 3–3.5 km/h showing inter-individual variability. In parallel, EMG synergies showed speed-dependent increases in dimensionality (2→3→4), consistent with module merging at slower speeds. Overall, these findings reveal coordinated kinematic and neuromuscular shifts with speed, indicating a transition from a discrete-dominated regime at low speeds toward a more stable rhythmic pattern at higher speeds.

Article.Title: Plasma proteomic analysis identified potential therapeutic targets for pulmonary arterial hypertension
Article.Authors: Hu S.; Xie Y.; Tan J.; Guo T.; Zhu S.; Lin Z.; Zhang J.; Hua L.
Article.Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive disease with high mortality. By integrating the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (49,272 participants, 337 incident cases) with drug-target Mendelian randomization, we identified 398 plasma proteins associated with incident PAH and 19 with potential causal relevance, 15 of which are druggable. Then we prioritized 5 candidates for expression validation in the Sugen5416 and hypoxia rat model and confirmed significant upregulation of TNFRSF10A and downregulation of UMOD in lung tissue, consistent with human plasma proteomic trends. Subsequent in vitro functional assays demonstrated that UMOD treatment attenuates PAH-related cellular phenotypes, whereas TNFRSF10A knockdown exacerbates pro-pathogenic progression. These results suggest UMOD as a promising protective therapeutic candidate and indicate the inherent complexity of the TNFRSF10A signaling. This integrative study provides a robust framework for translational research, future studies are warranted to elucidate downstream molecular mechanisms and further evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of these candidates.

Article.Title: Extensive monolayer formation after transplantation depends on an RPE subpopulation derived from human iPSCs
Article.Authors: Tessmer K.; Hammer J.; Gasparini S.; Schmidtke K.; Adhikari T.; Michalke L.; Schön A.; Sulaj F.; Loureiro L.; Last A.; Chelius N.; Kurtz A.; Johannsen H.; Carido M.; Ferguson S.; Petzold A.; Friedrich U.; Kurth T.; Dahl A.; Feldmann A.; Almedawar S.; Knöbel S.; Ader M.
Article.Abstract: Loss of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) in the eye leads to photoreceptor dysfunction, death, and eventually, vision loss. Cell replacement strategies using RPE cells derived in vitro from pluripotent stem cells are currently evaluated as a potential therapeutic strategy. Generation of polarized monolayers represents an essential prerequisite for proper RPE function; however, monolayer formation following transplantation of RPE suspensions has not been systematically assessed. Using the sodium iodate mouse model of acute RPE depletion, significant increase in monolayer formation capacity of passage 1 vs. 2 human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived RPE cells was observed three weeks post-transplantation. Transplant-derived monolayers showed characteristic apicobasal polarity, RPE marker expression, phagocytosis function, and preservation of the host outer nuclear layer. The cell surface marker panel CD54+/PSA-NCAM − was identified to enrich for an RPE subpopulation with a high potential for monolayer formation following transplantation. Results underline the importance of defining and isolating competent cell subpopulations for successful RPE transplantation.

Article.Title: Alternative splicing of a species- and skeletal muscle-specific microexon diversifies the menu of clathrin heavy chains in mice and rats
Article.Authors: Blue R.; Black A.; Cote J.; Addish S.; Kavalipati A.; Lyons S.; Ezzell J.; Bremmer S.; Dominguez D.; Giudice J.
Article.Abstract: Little is known about alternative splicing of microexons in most tissues other than the brain. Humans have two homologous clathrin heavy chains. Ubiquitously expressed, CLTC drives clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Highly expressed in skeletal muscles, CLTCL1 instead regulates glucose metabolism. Previously, we reported that a conserved microexon (exon 31) in the CLTC gene is alternatively spliced during striated muscle development. Here, we identified a novel Cltc microexon (exon 33, hereafter microexon 33), which is only included in mouse and rat adult skeletal muscles. Microexon 33 inclusion shortens the CLTC C-terminus and adds 10 distinct terminal residues. This divergence occurs at the same position at which the human CLTCL1 constitutively includes its penultimate exon (another microexon). CLTCL1 is a pseudogene in mice and rats. Humans diversified the menu of clathrin heavy chains by gene duplication and tissue-specific gene expression, whereas mice and rats might have achieved similar diversification by tissue-specific regulation of Cltc alternative splicing.

Article.Title: Volume electron microscopy reveals oligodendrocyte axon selection patterns and spatial assembly of myelin and nodes
Article.Authors: Monaco M.; Chiappini V.; Veloz Castillo M.; Kare K.; Clerico M.; Bartesaghi L.; Corrado Calì N/A.
Article.Abstract: Oligodendrocytes myelinate multiple axons, requiring single cells to coordinate target selection, sheath growth, and node formation across complex cortical geometry. We combined serial block-face electron microscopy, complete segmentation, and three-dimensional reconstruction to analyze early-myelinating oligodendrocytes in the somatosensory cortex of a postnatal day 14 rat at single-cell and nanoscale resolution. Individual oligodendrocytes initiated myelination across all contacted axons, while early ensheathment decreased with increasing process distance from the soma. Each oligodendrocyte also contacted axons within a restricted caliber range, independently of wrapping progression. At prospective nodes of Ranvier, transient cytoplasmic projections extended into axonal domains from adjacent oligodendrocytes and converged near presumptive paranodes. These observations support a structural model in which oligodendrocyte geometry, cell-specific axon selection, and intercellular interactions jointly organize early cortical myelination and nodal assembly, providing testable hypotheses for developmental myelination and repair after demyelination.

Article.Title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Zhang H.; Wang H.; Han S.; Chen X.; Nie X.; Liu J.; Tang Y.
Article.Abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing—such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms—their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

Article.Title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury
Article.Authors: Xue D.; Zhang M.; Chang X.; Wang T.; Ji B.; Xi C.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species
Article.Authors: Meng J.; Kang Y.; Lai A.; Feyerabend M.; Inoue W.; Martinez-Trujillo J.; Rudy B.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

Article.Title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation boosts evidence accumulation during perceptual decision making
Article.Authors: Su S.; Vanvoorden T.; Le Denmat P.; Zénon A.; Duque J.
Article.Abstract: Ascending arousal systems, including the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine (LC-NE) system, may shape perceptual decision-making by enhancing sensory processing ("gain") or accelerating response commitment ("urgency"). We examined how arousal-related neuromodulatory activity shapes decisions and whether its effects depend on arousal state. We tested 62 participants in three groups, receiving transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) at three timings during a random dot motion task. tVNS increased pupil-linked arousal, with early stimulation producing more sustained dilation into decision-making. Behaviorally, tVNS selectively improved accuracy under initially low performance without affecting response times. Drift diffusion modeling linked this improvement to increased drift rate, consistent with more efficient evidence accumulation. These effects occurred across groups but were most pronounced with early stimulation. Our findings support a gain-related enhancement of evidence accumulation under tVNS and suggest that pupil-linked arousal, potentially involving LC-NE among other ascending arousal pathways, may help stabilize attentional engagement when endogenous control is suboptimal.

Article.Title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke
Article.Authors: Ding J.; Chen Y.; Liu F.; Han J.; Zhu X.; Li Y.; Lu T.; Hu S.; Fu J.; Gai S.; Liu H.; Cheng S.; Tong D.; Cheng Y.
Article.Abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

Article.Title: Genetic polymorphisms and early responses predict refractory hyperthyroidism during antithyroid drug therapy
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Gong M.; Wang J.; Wang Q.; Xu K.; Fu Q.; Cai Y.; Wang Z.; Liu X.; Xu X.; Yang T.; Zheng X.
Article.Abstract: Antithyroid drugs (ATDs) are the first-line treatment for Graves' disease (GD), but variable outcomes require early risk stratification. We analyzed 578 adults, including 240 in a randomized trial of dose titration versus modified partial block-and-replace therapy and the remainder in a temporal observational cohort. Baseline characteristics, 3-month treatment indicators, and 13 GD-susceptibility single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were evaluated. An ATD-levothyroxine dose-correction method quantified thyroid function and autoantibody changes, informing clinical and SNP risk score-integrated models. The integrated model achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.841 in development and 0.805 in temporal validation, outperforming the clinical model ( p < 0.001) with good calibration and net benefit. Intermediate-risk patients derived the greatest incremental benefit. Baseline free thyroxine (FT4) was the strongest predictor, and the SNP risk score ranked fourth. No inter-regimen efficacy or safety differences were observed. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested that ATD therapy beyond 3 years may reduce recurrence risk, whereas modified partial block-and-replace showed no advantage over dose titration.

Article.Title: Central relaxin-3/RXFP3 signaling potently drives orexigenic behaviors and attenuates cisplatin-induced anorexia and body weight loss
Article.Authors: Subramanian K.; Belser D.; Orativskyi O.; Lee A.; Curtis G.; Kamicha S.; Yuki S.; Vu D.; Ko T.; De Jonghe B.; Doyle R.; Geisler C.; Hayes M.
Article.Abstract: Raw data values for each figure and supplemental figure for "Central relaxin-3/RXFP3 signaling potently drives orexigenic behaviors and attenuates cisplatin-induced anorexia and body weight loss" manuscript.

Article.Title: OGT regulates RNA-binding protein nucleocytoplasmic partitioning, but this fails in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Fournier L.; Wymann B.; Talbot K.; Luisier R.; Patani R.
Article.Abstract: O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (OGT) catalyzes the O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification to proteins and has been implicated in a range of diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a rapidly progressive and currently incurable neurodegenerative disorder. However, the precise mechanisms by which OGT influences ALS pathogenesis remain largely unresolved. In this study, we used human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived spinal motor neurons (hiPSC-MNs), the principal cell type that undergoes degeneration in ALS, to systematically reveal that OGT-related mechanisms regulate RNA-binding protein (RBP) nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalization. Using a combination of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) technology and small molecular pharmacology, we reveal two distinct regulatory mechanisms of RBP compartmentalization, including by intron-retaining transcript-mediated sequestration and O-linked N-acetylglucosaminylation (O-GlcNAcylation)-mediated nuclear transport. We finally examine the tractability of manipulating OGT activity in the ALS context but demonstrate that the OGT-related mechanisms governing RBP localization in healthy hiPSC-MNs are impaired in the context of ALS-causing VCP and TARDBP mutations.

Article.Title: CD8+ T cell transcriptional reprogramming toward TCF7-low cytotoxicity drives immune aging in viral ARDS
Article.Authors: Li K.; Ainiwaer K.; Song L.; Hu J.; Yang Y.; Liu Y.; Li H.; Xu S.; Wang Y.; Yin J.; Li L.; Wang X.; Hong X.; Xie L.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Viral acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) exhibits distinct clinical outcomes across age groups, but the immune mechanisms underlying this disparity remain unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic profiling, T cell receptor repertoire analysis, serum proteomics, and functional validation to characterize age-dependent T cell remodeling in influenza-associated ARDS. Adult ARDS was characterized by reduced T cell receptor diversity, expansion of CD8 + effector memory T cells, and enhanced cytotoxic programs marked by increased granzyme B (GZMB) expression compared with pediatric ARDS. At the transcriptional level, adult CD8 + effector memory T cells displayed a TCF7-low state associated with activation of a TGFB1-related RUNX3/PRDM1 program. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that TGFB1 promoted cytotoxic programming in CD8 + effector memory T cells and increased epithelial injury in a co-culture model. These findings identify age-associated CD8 + T cell remodeling as a potential mechanism contributing to immune dysregulation in viral ARDS.

Article.Title: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice
Article.Authors: Reyes-Ramírez L.; Ciaran-Alfano L.; Reixachs-Solé M.; Bergadà-Martínez A.; Galera-López L.; Martínez-Torres S.; Navarro-Romero A.; Maldonado R.; Eyras E.; Ozaita A.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Quantifying land transfer in China: Integrating its impacts on urban economy
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang T.; Hu S.; Feng Y.
Article.Abstract: In China's hierarchical land-governance system, the central government establishes the regulatory framework, while provincial and municipal authorities adapt the implementation according to local fiscal capacity, development priorities, and spatial constraints. Despite the importance of land transfer in shaping urban economic development processes, empirical research has long relied on fragmented samples or single-scale observations, and a unified long-term dataset spanning multiple administrative levels remains unavailable. To address this gap, this study constructs a multi-level spatiotemporal dataset of land transfer in China covering the period 2000–2024 at the national, provincial, and city levels. The dataset integrates seven standardized indicators, including land supply area, transaction price, gross floor area (GFA), payment amount, floor area ratio (FAR), building density, and greenery rate. Data are compiled from official land-market disclosure platforms and verified administrative transaction records and undergo systematic quality-control procedures, including cross-source reconciliation, unit harmonization, coverage diagnostics, and outlier screening to ensure temporal consistency and spatial comparability. The resulting database supports analyses of long-term land transfer dynamics, regional heterogeneity, and multi-level governance patterns. In addition, an illustrative empirical application demonstrates the analytical utility of the dataset for examining associations between land allocation and urban economic development indicators. This dataset provides a comprehensive empirical foundation for future research on land governance, land finance, urban spatial development, and regional transformation in China.

Article.Title: LncRNA Arsa-DT is required for spermatogenesis and male fertility by regulating G2/M progression
Article.Authors: Choi H.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Lee H.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Male infertility is a major reproductive health burden worldwide, yet its molecular etiology remains largely unknown. The testis expresses numerous long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), although their involvement in the pathophysiology of male infertility remains unexplored. Here, we identified Arsa-DT , a testis-predominant divergent lncRNA of Arsa , and demonstrated its essential role in maintaining male fertility. Loss of Arsa-DT leads to subfertility, characterized by reduced sperm production, increased sperm abnormalities, and decreased serum testosterone levels. Notably, Arsa-DT deficiency alters the testosterone-to-estradiol ratio through upregulation of aromatase expression. Specifically expressed in the nuclei of spermatogonia and spermatocytes, Arsa-DT regulates spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules. Mechanistically, Arsa-DT regulates G2/M phase progression and chromosome segregation in male germ cells. Collectively, our findings identify Arsa-DT , a testis-predominant lncRNA, as a regulator of spermatogenesis by controlling G2/M phase progression of male germ cells. This study provides mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of male infertility.

Article.Title: Diversity of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates of Staphylococcus aureus and its role in membrane potential
Article.Authors: Asada Y.; Nishihama S.; Kawada-Matsuo M.; Ohdan K.; Aikawa T.; Yanamoto S.; Komatsuzawa H.
Article.Abstract: Staphylococcus aureus colonizes human skin, nasal cavity, and oral mucosa and causes opportunistic infections. Host-derived fatty acids exhibit antibacterial activity against S. aureus , but the diversity and determinants of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates remain unclear. Here, we evaluated seven C14–C18 fatty acids selected from a physiologically relevant range of host-associated lipids. Linoleic acid (LA), palmitoleic acid (POA), and γ-linolenic acid (GLA) demonstrated significant antibacterial activity. We then analyzed LA and POA susceptibility in 253 clinical isolates. LA minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranged widely from 18.75 to 1,200 μM, whereas POA MICs clustered between 37.5 and 150 μM. Low-LA-susceptibility strains showed higher baseline membrane potential-associated signals and weaker LA-induced depolarization. Anaerobic culture and srrA inactivation reduced both of these signals and LA MICs. These findings indicate that membrane potential contributes to the heterogeneity of LA susceptibility and provide insight into host fatty acid-mediated control of S. aureus.

Article.Title: Minibeam radiation therapy supports CAR T therapy in a rat model of CNS lymphoma
Article.Authors: Iturri L.; Potiron S.; Sun L.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Espenon J.; Anegon I.; Ménoret S.; Soussain C.; Amigorena S.; Alcantara M.; Prezado Y.
Article.Abstract: Radiotherapy is increasingly combined with CAR T cell therapy in B cell lymphomas, but treatment outcome may depend on the irradiation modality. We evaluated minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) as a partner for CD19 CAR T cells in an orthotopic primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma model in immunodeficient rats. CAR T therapy prolonged survival compared with untreated controls. MBRT at 30 Gy followed by CAR T cells five days later produced the longest median survival among radiotherapy-containing regimens and improved outcome compared with conventional radiotherapy (CRT) based combinations. Histopathological findings were consistent with these survival differences. However, MBRT plus CAR T therapy did not significantly outperform CAR T monotherapy. These results indicate that MBRT provides a favorable, non-antagonistic radiotherapy context for CAR T therapy and suggest that radiation modality should be considered when designing combinations of radiotherapy with adoptive cellular therapies.

Article.Title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer’s disease using electronic records
Article.Authors: Katsuhara Y.; Khan U.; Miller Z.; Allen I.; Oskotsky T.; Sirota M.; Tang A.
Article.Abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Multi-omics profiling reveals molecular features of visceral adiposity in autonomous cortisol secretion
Article.Authors: Nakao H.; Yokomoto-Umakoshi M.; Fujita M.; Nakatani K.; Kitamura Y.; Ogasawara R.; Kaneko H.; Iwahashi N.; Nakano Y.; Fukumoto T.; Ogasawara T.; Takayanagi H.; Matsumoto T.; Izumi Y.; Eto M.; Bamba T.; Umakoshi H.; Ogawa Y.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous cortisol secretion (ACS) from adrenal adenomas increases cardiometabolic risk. Visceral adiposity is a hallmark of ACS. We characterized ACS-associated visceral adiposity using multi-omics profiling of periadrenal adipose tissue and plasma. ACS exhibited higher visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR), adipocyte hypertrophy, and inflammation-related pathway enrichment than non-functioning adrenal tumors. RNA-seq deconvolution and immunohistochemistry indicated increased macrophage infiltration. Plasma steroid metabolomics identified 11-deoxycorticosterone (11-DOC), a mineralocorticoid metabolite, as positively associated with VSR in premenopausal ACS women independent of cortisol. The 11-DOC-associated gene module correlated with inflammation-related pathways, notably macrophage activation. Lipidomics identified ceramides as ACS discriminators, with Cer(d18:1/16:0) most strongly associated with inflammation- and lipid metabolism-related pathways. Mendelian randomization showed genetically predicted plasma Cer(d18:1/16:0) was positively associated with trunk fat mass. These findings identify circulating 11-DOC and adipose ceramide accumulation as molecular features associated with adipose inflammation and visceral adiposity in ACS, providing hypothesis-generating insights that require functional validation.

Article.Title: Probing the role of left inferior frontal gyrus in vocal motor control: Evidence from TMS and causal inference analysis
Article.Authors: Chang Y.; Guo Q.; Zhao S.; Li T.; Wu X.; Liu D.; Dai G.; Zhu X.; Chen X.; Wang L.; Liu P.; Yan N.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Beyond an established role in speech initiation and planning, the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) may contribute to sensorimotor control of speech production. We applied continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) over the anterior (aIFG) and posterior (pIFG) regions to investigate their roles in vocal motor control. A causal inference analysis (CIA) framework was developed to characterize source-space network organization. cTBS over both left aIFG and pIFG reduced vocal responses and enhanced P2 responses to pitch feedback perturbations, with no significant differences between two active stimulations. However, global dissimilarity analysis revealed greater P2-related topographic deviation from sham stimulation following aIFG stimulation than following pIFG stimulation. CIA further identified different source-space network patterns associated with aIFG and pIFG stimulation. These findings demonstrate the causal involvement of the left IFG in auditory-vocal integration and highlight the potential of CIA for characterizing distributed network organization underlying vocal motor control.

Article.Title: Development of a predictive model and nomogram using CTPA parameters for the identification of group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension
Article.Authors: Yuan H.; Cheang I.; Liang G.; Zhu X.; Xing Y.; Li W.; Liao S.; He J.; Cao Y.; Li X.; Xu Y.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to identify computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-derived predictors of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and to develop a prediction model and nomogram for non-invasive diagnosis. We retrospectively analyzed CTPA datasets from 203 patients in the training cohort and 98 patients in the validation cohort, stratified into PAH (confirmed by right heart catheterization) and non-PAH groups. Pulmonary vascular and cardiac structural metrics were measured. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression identified interventricular septal angle (IVSA), interventricular septal thickness (IVST), and right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness (RVOTW) as independent predictors. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964 and 0.969 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively, with excellent calibration and clinical utility. The CTPA-based predictive model and nomogram may serve as a useful reference tool, potentially assisting in the identification of PAH and optimizing clinical workflows.

Article.Title: Repeated visual adaptation induces persistent behavioral and neural biases in body size perception
Article.Authors: Sang X.; Dong X.; Bao M.
Article.Abstract: Body size and shape misperception, notably body size overestimation, is prevalent among young people. It has been proposed that such a bias may stem from adaptation aftereffects caused by exposures to distorted bodies, yet whether adaptation can persistently alter daily body perception remains unclear. This study explored the long-term impacts of body size adaptation by having participants repeatedly view thin or large body images for 7 daily sessions, or comparing participants with varied experiences of exposure to the thin-ideal in life. Behavioral results revealed that repeated exposure to distorted body images persistently shifted participants' perception of body normality toward the adapting shape. ERP data showed that repeated adaptation to thin bodies or higher endorsement of the thin-ideal could enhance the early brain response bias to enlarged bodies. These findings collectively suggest that repeated exposure to distorted bodies contribute to the development of perceptual and neural response bias toward body shapes.

Article.Title: Reconstructing the genetic ancestry of the archaeological site in Amiternum: From Roman Imperial to early medieval times in Central Italy
Article.Authors: Moroni E.; Agostini V.; Ciabini D.; Colombo G.; Di Gerlando R.; Rambaldi Migliore N.; Zarivi O.; Semino O.; Achilli A.; Forgione A.; Poma A.; Olivieri A.
Article.Abstract: Central-southern Italy is pivotal for reconstructing the population history of the peninsula, yet the genetic impact of the complex demographic past in the Abruzzo region remains largely unexplored. This study integrates archaeological context with ancient DNA analysis of 16 individuals excavated at the Cathedral of Santa Maria in Civitate in Amiternum. The sample comprises one adult male from the Roman Imperial period and 15 subadults mainly from the early medieval period. Genome-wide data reveal a sharp genetic discontinuity between the two epochs. The Roman individual mirrors other Italians from the same period, characterized by significant Near Eastern ancestry. In contrast, the early medieval group—genetically homogeneous—clusters with late antique and medieval populations from Central and Southern Italy, showing significant genetic influence from Central and Northern Europe. Overall, the medieval genetic structure differs from the Roman one and closely resembles that of modern Central and Southern Italians.

Article.Title: Box C/D SNORD116-17 promotes prostate cancer progression by targeting the miR-206/E2F5 axis
Article.Authors: Pan X.; Kang Y.; Zhong J.; Yu T.; Zheng L.; Wei Y.; Tan J.; Nie L.; Zhang M.; Chen N.; Zhou Q.; Chen X.

Article.Title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
Article.Authors: La Manna G.; Merella M.; Crobu A.; Pansini A.; Ceccherelli G.
Article.Abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. Most studies examine short-term, individual-level responses, limiting inference on long-term effects. Impacts vary widely by stressor, taxon, and biological outcome. Invertebrates often show positive responses linked to reef effects, though key functional traits are vulnerable. Fish responses are largely neutral except under noise, while marine mammals exhibit the most consistent negative impacts. The impact score developed here highlights taxon-specific vulnerability and offers a scalable risk-assessment tool for data-poor regions. The review calls for standardized, long-term field monitoring to support OWF expansion while safeguarding biodiversity.

Article.Title: Targeting BCL11B-mediated JAK2/STAT3 activation: A novel therapeutic strategy for Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Chen W.; Zhang Y.; Zhou X.; Yan J.; Song Y.; Shen J.; Gu X.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is driven in part by neuroinflammation. We investigated whether the transcription factor BCL11B contributes to dopaminergic neurodegeneration in this context. Transcriptome sequencing of MPTP-induced PD mice revealed BCL11B upregulation, which was confirmed in MPP + -treated MN9D cells, MPTP-lesioned mice, and dopaminergic neurons exposed to inflammatory conditioned medium. BCL11B knockdown attenuated dopaminergic neuron loss, reduced apoptosis, improved motor deficits, and partially blocked JAK2/STAT3 pathway activation in both inflammatory and MPTP-induced PD models. Mechanistically, BCL11B mediated neurotoxicity through the JAK2/STAT3 pathway, with acetylation modifications potentially modulating its activity. These findings establish BCL11B as a key regulator of neuroinflammation and dopaminergic survival in PD, and suggest that targeting BCL11B may offer a therapeutic approach for this neurodegenerative disease.

Article.Title: Harnessing polymeric materials for applications in electric vehicle with sustainability contributions and prospects
Article.Authors: Rajeshkumar L.; Ramesh M.; Arulmozhivarman J.; Dinesh Kumar M.; Sathishkumar M.
Article.Abstract: The accelerated global shift to EVs is revolutionizing the field of materials science, thereby making polymeric materials indispensable to all subsystems in EVs. In this context, this review provides a critical analysis of the evolution, classification, and applications of polymeric materials within the different EV subsystems, including structural composites, battery housing, thermal systems, insulation, and interior parts. Building on this classification, this review further highlights the latest advances made in the fields of fiber-reinforced polymer composites, engineering thermoplastic polymers, elastomers, bio-based, and recyclable polymers with specific performance criteria and associated challenges. Beyond their technical role, this review also focuses on aligning the technological advancements of such materials with the United Nations sustainable development goals (UN SDGs). This review also highlights relevant knowledge gaps in scaling up bio-based polymer production, the longevity of polymer housings for batteries subjected to thermal cycling, and the lack of a universally agreed-upon EV polymer recycling protocol.

Article.Title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
Article.Authors: Halling A.; Goodson B.; Hirschmann A.; Wing B.; Simpson C.
Article.Abstract: During the 70-million-year Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity over 3-fold. Unicellular eukaryotes in this environment would have faced severe constraints on movement and nutrient uptake, while nascent multicellular organisms, with larger size and collective mobility, could have gained an adaptive advantage. We experimentally tested whether viscosity-induced metabolic constraints could have selected for multicellular phenotypes, potentially driving the origin or early diversification of multicellularity. Under Snowball Earth-like viscosities, populations of unicellular green algae evolved motile multicellular forms, along with other phenotypes that optimize size and speed. As oceans warmed and viscosities decreased, the diversity of multicellular phenotypes may have allowed early multicellular organisms to exert novel physical control over their local environments. This pivotal period in Earth's history could have shaped the emergence and eventual dominance of certain multicellular lineages, highlighting a potential ecological driver of one of life's major evolutionary transitions.

Article.Title: The circulating lipidome in severe obesity
Article.Authors: Anwar M.; Highland H.; Palmer A.; Duong T.; Lin Z.; Zhu W.; Sprinkles J.; Kim D.; Young K.; Chen H.; Krishnan M.; Gutierrez A.; Roshani R.; Frankel E.; Landman J.; Gordon-Larsen P.; Fried S.; Lee M.; Fisher-Hoch S.; McCormick J.; Curran J.; Blangero J.; Meikle P.; Giles C.; Below J.
Article.Abstract: Severe obesity (SevO; BMI ≥ 40 kg/m 2 ) is rising globally yet remains understudied mechanistically. To characterize lipidomic alterations at the species level, we analyzed Border Health Research Cohort participants with fasting plasma lipidomics and genetic data, comparing SevO ( n = 185) to non-obese controls (18.5 ≥ BMI < 25; n = 393). We quantified 830 lipid species across 49 classes and assessed associations using logistic regression, orthogonal projections to latent structures discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), and network deconvolution Mendelian randomization (NDMR). SevO participants showed more adverse cardiometabolic traits. Lipidomics revealed broad dysregulation: shorter, saturated, and monounsaturated triacylglycerols were elevated in individuals living with SevO compared to controls, while lysophospholipids, plasmalogens, cholesteryl esters, and long-chain species were reduced. OPLS-DA identified over 300 lipids strongly predictive of SevO, and NDMR implicated specific triacylglycerols as potentially contributing to SevO status. Influential lipids correlated with insulin resistance, liver fat, body composition, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Short-chain triacylglycerols emerged as a distinctive, consistently elevated SevO signature.

Article.Title: Limited global awareness of invasive alien species and little support for their management
Article.Authors: Novoa A.; Shackleton R.; Bacher S.; Pipek P.; Chaichana R.; El-Keblawy A.; Galil B.; Gioria M.; Golivets M.; D'Hertefeldt T.; Ikegami M.; Jarić I.; Kull C.; Mohanty N.; Pattison Z.; Pauchard A.; Pergl J.; Preda C.; Pyšková K.; Rodríguez J.; Štajerová K.; Hai van Nguyen T.; Yazlık A.; Zenni R.; Pyšek P.
Article.Abstract: Invasive alien species (IAS) are one of the main drivers of global change and can cause a wide range of negative ecological and social impacts. Addressing these impacts requires management actions, which can fail to be effective when not supported by the public. Here, we conducted the first global survey on people's awareness and perceptions of IAS and support for their management. Our results revealed low public awareness and understanding of biological invasions, and suggest that these are mainly influenced by people's sociodemographic status rather than the social-ecological contexts. Greater awareness of IAS was associated with more negative perceptions toward them and greater support for their management. A large majority of people did not support the use of most management measures. These results suggest that limited public awareness may represent a major obstacle to successfully managing IAS globally, highlighting the need for broader public communication, outreach, and engagement.

Article.Title: Dual impact of EZH1/2-targeted therapy in HTLV-1-associated inflammation: Direct and indirect mechanisms
Article.Authors: Zou Y.; Kamoi K.; Yang M.; Zong Y.; Zhang J.; Ohno-Matsui K.
Article.Abstract: Human T cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1)-associated inflammation, including uveitis, lacks effective targeted therapies. Here, we investigated whether epigenetic modulation through EZH1/2 inhibition could influence HTLV-1-related ocular inflammation using in vitro co-culture and infection models. HTLV-1 exposure increased EZH1 and EZH2 expression and the repressive histone mark H3K27me3 in retinal pigment epithelial cells. Treatment with the dual EZH1/2 inhibitor valemetostat reduced H3K27me3 levels. Valemetostat showed limited effects on cell viability and induced only modest, context-dependent apoptosis. Virological analyses showed model-dependent changes in proviral load, accompanied by reduced viral gene expression. Profiling of cytokines and chemokines revealed context-dependent modulation of inflammatory mediators. Functional assessment using p65 nuclear translocation assays indicated partial attenuation of NF-κB activation under inflammatory stimulation. Collectively, these findings suggest that EZH1/2-mediated epigenetic regulation is primarily involved in HTLV-1-related inflammatory responses, and that inhibiting EZH1/2 may be a potential approach to modulate inflammatory signaling.

Article.Title: Olfactory dysfunction among gas station employees exposed to fuel vapors using digital odor identification testing
Article.Authors: Viana dos Santos J.; Nakanishi M.
Article.Abstract: Gas station employees are chronically exposed to fuel vapors containing benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), raising occupational concerns about olfactory function. In this cross-sectional study, 116 Brazilian gas station employees (86 men and 30 women; median age, 37.5 years; range, 19–58) completed a questionnaire and underwent objective olfactory assessment with the MultiScent-20 digital odor identification test. Overall, 58.6% had olfactory dysfunction, including 46.6% with hyposmia and 12.1% with anosmia, whereas only 23.3% reported that their work affected their sense of smell. Longer employment duration was associated with lower olfactory scores (Spearman's ρ = −0.41; p < 0.001) and independently increased the odds of dysfunction (odds ratio [OR] = 1.15 per additional year; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06–1.26; p = 0.003). These findings support incorporating olfactory assessment into occupational health surveillance for workers chronically exposed to fuel vapors.

Article.Title: Repressed mTORC1 signaling and transient dendritic pruning support axonal regeneration in adult zebrafish
Article.Authors: Zhang A.; Masin L.; Bergmans S.; Putti E.; Albadri S.; Poulain F.; Del Bene F.; Moons L.
Article.Abstract: Dendrite degeneration is an early pathological feature following axonal damage, yet its role during successful axonal regeneration remains poorly understood. Using sparse labeling of retinal ganglion cells in adult zebrafish, we show that axonal regeneration is accompanied by a transient phase of dendritic pruning following optic nerve crush. Dendritic pruning occurs during axon elongation and is reversed after brain reinnervation. Although insulin–mTOR signaling is rapidly upregulated immediately after injury, it is subsequently suppressed, coinciding with dendritic pruning and sustained axonal growth. Prolonging mTOR activation through insulin treatment or direct pathway stimulation reduces dendritic pruning in an mTORC1-dependent manner but significantly delays axonal regrowth. Together, these findings identify dendritic remodeling as a temporally regulated component of axonal regeneration in zebrafish and reveal a functional trade-off between dendritic preservation and axon regrowth. This warrants further investigation on whether temporal modulation of dendritic remodeling could promote axonal regeneration in the mammalian CNS.

Article.Title: Context shapes action understanding in social interactions
Article.Authors: Keck J.; Sato K.; Cañal-Bruland R.
Article.Abstract: This repository contains processed data from dyadic interaction tasks (rock-paper-scissors), including classified hand poses and corresponding wrist movement trajectories for all valid games in each session. Each session folder contains: A) The MAT file wrist_trajectories.mat contains the extracted wrist movement data. Data are organized as a struct array (game_rep), where each element corresponds to one game. For each game, wrist trajectories are provided separately for both players and segmented into three movement phases: • phase_AB • phase_BC • phase_CD (final phase until the end of the movement) Each phase contains the preprocessed wrist trajectory time series for the respective player. B) The CSV file classified_poses_final.csv contains the behavioral labels for all retained games within each session. Each row corresponds to one game and includes: • game index • classified hand pose for player one • classified hand pose for player two • outcome variables for both players (e.g., win/loss/draw) • Only games that passed all preprocessing, cleaning, and alignment steps are included in these files. The analysis scripts and raw data (e.g., C3D files) are part of an ongoing project and will be made publicly available upon its completion; in the meantime, they can be obtained from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Found a bug? Please contact Johannes.keck@uni-jena.de
