Article.Keywords: Patch-seq; cross-species cellular homology; cross-species neuroscience; interneurons; single-cell transcriptomics; spatial transcriptomics

Article.Title: Oscillatory dynamics within fronto-insular-parietal networks integrate thermosensory signals into body ownership
Article.Authors: Mattavelli G.; Crottini F.; Gorrino I.; Arrigoni E.; Maiocchi C.; Pisoni A.; Bottini G.; Salvato G.
Article.Abstract: Cutaneous thermosensory signals are linked to survival and homeostatic regulation, yet their relationship with higher order cognitive functions remains poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests that skin temperature is associated with body ownership-the sense that a body and its parts belong to oneself-but the oscillatory basis of this relationship in healthy individuals is unknown. We combined a multisensory illusion paradigm with thermal imaging and electroencephalography to investigate the oscillatory correlates of skin-temperature changes during experimentally induced changes in body ownership. Selective perturbations in theta/low-alpha oscillatory activity, localized to right premotor regions, tracked a decrease in hand temperature during altered hand ownership. Moreover, the strength of a functional connectivity network spanning bilateral frontoparietal areas, including the insula, was associated with temperature changes coupled with ownership modulation. These findings identify a previously uncharacterized oscillatory signature associated with thermosensory changes during body ownership alteration, linking physiological fluctuations to neural dynamics of self-representation.
Article.Keywords: bodily self-awareness; body ownership; temperature; thermosensory signals

Article.Title: Network reorganization of anterograde thalamic connectivity during non-periodic patterned deep brain stimulation
Article.Authors: Johnson T.; Mohan B.; Huang H.; Cramer J.; Drees C.; Hoerth M.; Crepeau A.; Drazkowski J.; Noe K.; Baxter L.; Mbonde A.; Harris C.; Ince N.; Miller K.; Hermes D.; Worrell G.; Parker J.
Article.Abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) can reduce seizures in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. However, seizure freedom is rare, and there is no early response biomarker to predict long-term seizure suppression. To evaluate a candidate short-term biomarker of therapeutic response to DBS, we studied 18-min trials of ANT stimulation in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing intracranial electroencephalography. We compared a standard high-frequency periodic versus a non-periodic pulse pattern. We found that short-term ANT stimulation within the clinically used amplitude range preferentially altered the first 150 ms of anterograde ANT to anterior cingulate and superior frontal connectivity. Non-periodic ANT stimulation selectively modified early cortico-cortical evoked potentials more than periodic stimulation, and these changes were driven by the response phase. These pattern-specific changes in connectivity between the ANT and spatially restricted cortical areas suggest differing mechanisms and are a promising candidate biomarker for patients being treated with ANT-DBS.
Article.Keywords: cortico-cortical evoked potentials; deep brain stimulation; epilepsy; network modification; non-periodic stimulation

Article.Title: Tandem duplication upstream of HSF5 associates with transcript remodeling and triple-comb morphology in chickens
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Zhang Z.; Zhong Z.; Weng Z.; Xu Y.; Zhong G.; Li W.; Wang Q.; Du B.; Peng M.; Ma C.
Article.Abstract: The genetic basis of the triple comb in chickens remains unknown. Here, we integrated population genomics, genome-wide association studies, structural variant analysis, long-read sequencing, and embryonic transcriptomics in Wuhua Yellow chickens. We identified a 15.7-kb tandem duplication upstream of HSF5 on chromosome 19 as the primary candidate. At embryonic day 8, overall HSF5 expression was unchanged, yet we observed localized exon upregulation within the duplicated region, a dosage-dependent expression gradient, and extensive non-canonical splicing. Public epigenomic data further indicate baseline enhancer activity in this interval. Copy number correlated positively with comb prong number (R 2 = 0.45, adjusted p = 9.26 × 10-7). Exploratory fertility assessments revealed a lower fertilization rate in triple-comb crosses, suggesting a potential pleiotropic cost. These findings strongly implicate HSF5 as a key candidate and demonstrate that a tandem duplication associates with phenotypic innovation through transcript remodeling rather than simple gene misexpression.
Article.Keywords: HSF5; chicken; tandem duplication; transcript remodeling; triple comb

Article.Title: Quantitative photoacoustic endoscopy reveals early microvascular biomarkers of endometrial fibrosis in a rat model
Article.Authors: Liang X.; Guo Z.; Xiong K.; He Z.; Zhang D.; Kang S.; Chen H.; Du M.; Kui X.; Wen X.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Endometrial fibrosis, the core pathological feature of intrauterine adhesion, lacks effective early assessment methods. This study used a quantitative photoacoustic endoscopy (PAE) method to assess the relationship between early PAE-derived features and late-stage fibrosis by characterizing microvascular and inflammatory dynamics in the injured endometrium. PAE captured dynamic endometrial microvascular perfusion changes post-injury, with distinct late vascular remodeling patterns under mild and severe injury. PAE-derived vessel area and mean E lacunarity correlated strongly with histologically validated vascular density (r = 0.90 and −0.84, respectively), and at mid-to-later stages, PAE features correlated with inflammatory cell counts. Day 7 post-injury emerged as a key evaluation window, with vessel area showing AUCs of 0.938 for distinguishing mild fibrosis and 0.946 for severe fibrosis. These findings suggest that quantitative PAE provides high-resolution, biopsy-free monitoring of the endometrial microenvironment and may offer microvascular biomarkers that link early imaging changes to subsequent fibrosis progression.

Article.Title: Loss of SREBF1 disrupts lipid signaling and causes slow muscle fiber degeneration
Article.Authors: Donaka R.; Awad K.; Khrystoforova I.; Hezkial B.; Brotto M.; Karasik D.
Article.Abstract: SREBF1 , encoding the lipogenic transcription factor SREBP1, has been linked to lean mass by human genomics. We used a CRISPR-Cas9 srebf1 zebrafish knockout combined with LC-MS/MS lipidomics, RNA-seq, Lugol-enhanced micro-CT imaging, and functional assays. Srebp1 loss disrupted slow-fiber organization, increased locomotion in larvae, and reduced muscle mass in adults. This knockout muscle showed altered fatty acid composition, reduced arachidonoylethanolamide (AEA), elevated palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), broad remodeling of polyunsaturated fatty (PUFA) acid-derived mediators, and differential expression of cardiolipin-pathway genes. Integrated transcriptomic-lipidomic analysis revealed srebf1 -centered connections to myogenic regulators and calcium and lipid signaling, paralleling selective atrophy and loss of slow oxidative fibers under overfeeding and aging. Our data supports a model in which Srebp1 functions as a fiber-type-specific survival checkpoint that maintains lipid compositional and cardiolipin homeostasis, and whose disruption reprograms lipid mediators to drive slow-to-fast fiber switching and slow-fiber degeneration relevant to sarcopenia and sarcopenic obesity.

Article.Title: Tregs transduced with a Ro60-reactive TCR have increased immunosuppressive functions in Sjögren’s disease
Article.Authors: Sherman Lim Z.; Cheong R.; Vincent F.; Chang J.; Loh K.; Halim H.; Kwai-Wai Kong G.; Tay E.; Peh C.; Jia X.; Rischmueller M.; Ting Y.; Ooi J.
Article.Abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a T cell-driven autoimmune condition strongly associated with the HLA-DRB1∗03:01 allele and autoantibodies against the Ro60 protein. Previous studies have identified deficiencies in regulatory T cells (Treg) in patients, indicating a breakdown in immune tolerance. Current treatments remain limited to symptomatic relief or broad immunosuppression, without addressing the underlying immune dysregulation. In this study, we present the first preclinical evidence supporting a TCR-engineered Treg (TCR-Treg) therapy specifically targeting SjD. We designed a TCR-Treg that recognizes a dominant epitope of the Ro60 antigen (Ro60 369-383 ) presented by HLA-DRB1∗03:01 and demonstrate that these cells can selectively suppress autoreactive T cells more effectively than polyclonal Treg. These findings underscore the pathogenic significance of the Ro-HLA-DRB1∗03:01 axis and provide proof-of-concept for a targeted, antigen-specific Treg therapy. This approach offers a promising strategy to restore immune tolerance and represents a potential disease-modifying treatment for genetically defined subsets of patients with SjD.

Article.Title: Corrigendum to “Machine learning algorithms develop a tumor-educated platelets-related gene signature to predict colorectal cancer prognosis and therapy response” [iScience 29 (2026) 116229]
Article.Authors: Lao Y.; Yang J.; Hu M.; Li J.; Xu W.; Xu J.; Wang H.; Jiang H.; Pei Z.; Qiu X.; Wang K.; Li X.; Yang H.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Gapmers targeting conserved SARS-CoV-2 single-stranded regions reduce viral load and reshape inflammatory macrophage responses
Article.Authors: Gallo G.; Donnici L.; Colley L.; Loffreda A.; Fumagalli V.; Iannacone M.; Mazza D.; Incarnato D.; De Francesco R.; Monteleone E.; De Magis A.; Bianchi M.
Article.Abstract: The COVID-19 crisis is now over, but additional viral strains of SARS-CoV-2 that evade immunity are continuously emerging. We explored the design, evaluation, and optimization of anti-sense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting SARS-CoV-2 RNA, with the aim of providing a scalable strategy capable of responding to emergent outbreaks. Twenty-four ASOs were designed to target highly conserved, single-stranded regions of the SARS-CoV-2 genome. Extensive in vitro screening led to the identification of gapmers that exhibited high efficacy against four selected SARS-CoV-2 variants, significantly reducing intracellular viral RNA and virus production. Importantly, the antiviral efficacy correlates with viral RNA accessibility and is not due to activation of antiviral host responses. Finally, naked gapmers delivered intranasally can reach lung tissue, are preferentially internalized by alveolar macrophages, and modulate the inflammatory response to viral exposure. Taken together, our findings show that gapmers targeting the viral RNA are a promising approach to the development of antiviral therapies.

Article.Title: Corrigendum to “Aberrant CDK4/6-driven cell-cycle reentry drives neuronal loss and defines a therapeutic target in C9orf72 ALS/FTD” [iScience 29 (2026) 114596]
Article.Authors: Ali S.; Lian L.; Robinson H.; Daniels N.; Prieto G.; Poplawski G.; Lopez-Gonzalez R.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: FGFR kinase isoform and activation state modulate ATPase activity
Article.Authors: Besch A.; Lamon G.; Zhang Y.; Traaseth N.
Article.Abstract: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) binding to FGF receptor (FGFR) induces trans -autophosphorylation of activation loop tyrosine residues within the receptor's intracellular kinase domain, thereby activating the receptor and promoting downstream substrate phosphorylation. Here, using activity assays and 31 P NMR spectroscopy on the FGFR kinase domain, we show that phosphorylation of activation loop tyrosine residues not only enhances kinase activity but also increases the rate of ATP hydrolysis by 33-fold. This ATPase activity varies among FGFR kinase isoforms, with a 5.4-fold difference between FGFR2 and FGFR3 kinases. Conversion of ATP to ADP in phosphorylation assays also promotes the reverse phosphorylation reaction, which involves phosphoryl group transfer from phosphotyrosine to ADP to regenerate ATP. Based on these observations, we hypothesize that ATPase activity occurs in cells and may decrease the local ATP/ADP ratio surrounding FGFR. Such a mechanism would reduce the favorability of phosphorylation and may promote signal termination through reverse phosphorylation.

Article.Title: Hepatic TMEM30A deficiency disrupts lipid metabolism and liver regeneration through PPARα-ATGL pathway
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Gan X.; Cheng J.; Ren K.; Guo Y.; Zhang A.; Jin Y.; Ge Z.; Wang J.; Ju Z.; Shi L.; Zhang L.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: The lipid accumulation at early phase during liver regeneration is necessary process, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the role of TMEM30A, a β-subunit of P4-ATPases, in hepatic lipid homeostasis and regeneration. Tmem30a liver-specific knockout (LKO) mice and controls were fed a high-fat diet and subjected to two-thirds partial hepatectomy. TMEM30A deficiency led to hepatic steatosis, dyslipidemia, and impaired induction of key triglyceride degradation and PPARα pathway genes. Following hepatectomy, LKO mice exhibited increased mortality, severe liver injury, reduced hepatocyte proliferation, and downregulation of Cyclin B1, Cyclin D1, and Cyclin E1. The lipid accumulation was markedly exaggerated in LKO livers, primarily due to suppression of the PPARα-ATGL axis. Pharmacological activation of PPARα with Wy-14643 restored lipid metabolism, hepatocyte proliferation, and survival after surgery. These findings reveal that the PPARα-ATGL pathway functions as a crucial downstream axis of TMEM30A in coordinating lipid metabolism and regenerative capacity.

Article.Title: Neutrophil swarm formation on large targets
Article.Authors: Wine C.; Apostolopoulou A.; Lin C.; Sevenler D.; Mansour M.; Irimia D.
Article.Abstract: Neutrophils are smaller in size than most fungal hyphae. Yet, neutrophils can engage in collective actions known as swarming, during which they cover the hyphae and block their growth. To understand how neutrophil swarms cover large targets efficiently, we employed particle image velocimetry (PIV). We found that the process is initiated at a small number of sites on the surface of a large target. Radiating from these initial sites, waves of intracellular Ca 2+ increase in surrounding neutrophils, and neutrophils start converging toward these sites. Multiple swarms form which later merge and ultimately fully encapsulate the target. Neutrophils from immunocompromised patients after liver transplant or hematopoietic stem cell transplant produce swarms that grow slowly and end up smaller compared with those from healthy donors. In the future, the methods and metrics of neutrophil swarming toward large targets may help diagnose and monitor innate immune impairment in transplant patients.

Article.Title: Multiple drivers of genomic novelty across ruminants
Article.Authors: Kavanagh R.; Bertola L.; Nielsen S.; Hua Zhu H.; Heller R.; Bhatt S.; Duchêne D.
Article.Abstract: Ruminants are among the most ecologically and economically important groups of mammals and have accumulated some of the most remarkable traits and genomes across metazoans. Using genomic-scale data representing all ruminant families, we examined the traits that explain evolutionary rates across ruminant lineages and genes. Bayesian phylogenetic regression revealed that ruminant genome-wide rates are associated with chromosome number, longevity, sexual dimorphism, and domestication. Orthogonal dimensions of genomic rates showed that genes with the greatest rate change are associated with domestication, suggesting these events have a strong impact on ruminant genome evolution. Decomposition of d N / d S rates captured a signal of body size impacting a narrow and yet important portion of the genome in which larger ruminants show consistently weakened purifying selection. Protein-coding loci were associated with the greatest change in evolutionary rates across metabolic, gene signaling, and neurologically functional pathways, suggesting these are core to ruminant evolutionary diversity. This study reveals the primary forces driving biological novelty across the ruminants.

Article.Title: Bifidobacterium adolescentis SBT2786-induced early-night sleep requires CCHamide-1 signaling in Drosophila ellipsoid body ring neuron circuits
Article.Authors: Murakami H.; Kobayashi S.
Article.Abstract: We previously identified the sleep-promoting bacterium Bifidobacterium adolescentis SBT2786; however, its molecular mechanism remains unknown. In Drosophila melanogaster , tissue-/region-specific RNA interference (RNAi) targeted the gut-brain neuropeptide CCHamide-1 (CCHa1) and the CCHa1 receptor (CCHa1R). The increase in SBT2786-induced early-night sleep was abolished by systemic CCHa1 and pan-neuronal CCHa1R knockdown. This phenotype persisted after enteroendocrine cell-specific CCHa1 knockdown, suggesting that it is not fully explained by gut enteroendocrine cell-derived CCHa1 alone. Region-specific RNAi revealed that CCHa1R is required in the ellipsoid body (EB), not the fan-shaped body and tested dopaminergic populations. Ring-driver mapping implicated EB ring neuron circuits, including R3-enriched populations, in the SBT2786 effect: CCHa1R knockdown with the 189 years driver abolished the effect, whereas knockdown with drivers labeling R2/R4m populations did not. These findings show that SBT2786-induced early-night sleep requires CCHa1-CCHa1R signaling and EB ring neuron circuits, and is not fully explained by enteroendocrine cell-derived CCHa1.

Article.Title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors
Article.Authors: Li X.; Yu Y.; Liu L.; Du M.; Tang Q.; Kang J.
Article.Abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a held-out test dataset, DeepNPA achieved strong performance, with an accuracy of 0.953, an F1-score of 0.927, and an AUPRC of 0.965. On an independent benchmark dataset, DeepNPA outperformed NeuroCS and NeuroPred, achieving an ACC of 0.969 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.666. External validation further demonstrated its ability to identify neuropeptide regions and their associated cleavage sites. In addition, we provided an online prediction platform to facilitate neuropeptide precursor annotation and cleavage site analysis.

Article.Title: GPR82-mediated activation of TGF-β/SMAD signaling contributes to CD8+ T cell dysfunction in HBV-ACLF
Article.Authors: Yu D.; Wu Z.; Lin L.; Zou B.; Luo L.; Zhu G.; Yao X.
Article.Abstract: Patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) have severe CD8 + T cell dysfunction. This study examined G protein-coupled receptor 82 (GPR82) in CD8 + T cell exhaustion in hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). Using GEO analysis, clinical samples, GPR82 manipulation, transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β)/SMAD intervention, dual-luciferase assays, and a mouse hepatitis virus strain 3 (MHV-3) mouse model, we found GPR82 overexpression in ACLF liver and HBV-ACLF CD8 + T cells, correlating with T cell exhaustion. GPR82 knockdown enhanced CD8 + T cell function, while overexpression had opposite effects. Mechanistically, lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC) upregulated GPR82 transcription via TGF-β/SMAD1, and elevated GPR82 further activated TGF-β/SMAD, forming a positive feedback loop. In vivo , GPR82 knockdown partially restored CD8 + T cell function and alleviated liver injury in the MHV-3 mouse model. These findings indicate GPR82 promotes CD8 + T cell exhaustion via TGF-β/SMAD, and the LysoPC-GPR82 loop offers insight into ACLF immune dysfunction, suggesting GPR82 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Physical activity attenuates mortality risk associated with elevated resting heart rate in chronic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Zhan Y.; He B.; Pu L.; Bi W.; Wei G.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: The independent and combined associations of resting heart rate (RHR) and physical activity (PA) with mortality in diverse chronic kidney disease (CKD) populations remain unclear. We analyzed 12,042 patients from three cohorts using Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, joint-effect, mediation, and meta-analytic approaches. Elevated RHR was associated with increased risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, whereas higher PA levels showed consistent protective associations across cohorts. Combined analyses demonstrated that high RHR with low PA was associated with the greatest mortality risk, while high PA attenuated the adverse association of elevated RHR with mortality. Mediation analyses suggested that RHR partially contributed to the association between PA and mortality. RHR and PA are independent and modifiable risk markers for mortality in patients with CKD. Promoting PA and monitoring RHR should be integrated into CKD management to improve survival.

Article.Title: Physiological elasticity and topography modulate in vitro prostate cancer cell behavior
Article.Authors: Hoffmann M.; Paul R.; Herrmann A.; Gerlach S.; Bacmeister P.; Ermler T.; Book M.; Alexa R.; Honné A.; Müller J.; Brach J.; Fischer P.; Kranz J.; Wessling M.; Saar M.
Article.Abstract: Tissue elasticity and microenvironment are a hallmark of cancer, particularly in prostate cancer. Here, we investigate, how physiologically relevant mechanical properties affect prostate cancer cells using 2D-poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) and topographic 2.5D-poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate-glycidyl methacrylate hydrogel surfaces. Substrates reproducing the stiffness of tumor cell niches, altered cell morphology, metabolic activity, migration, cytokine expression, and therapeutic response. Elasticity-dependent effects included up to a 1.5-fold increase in LDH activity with concurrent cell proliferation, reduced migration rates with increased paxillin expression, and enhanced chemokine-mediated invasion. Adaptation to physiological elasticities was also associated with up to 90 % reduction in responsiveness to docetaxel and enzalutamide. Importantly, elasticity-adapted substrates supported primary prostate cancer cell growth while preserving characteristic expression profiles. These findings demonstrated that mechanical microenvironmental cues substantially shape prostate cancer cell phenotypes and highlight their importance for developing more physiologically relevant and translationally informative in vitro models.

Article.Title: Topical application of urolithin A activates mitophagy and enhances mitochondrial function to promote skin longevity
Article.Authors: D’Amico D.; Faitg J.; Amaral F.; Ballihaut C.; Fouassier A.; Tissot C.; Rana I.; Laboureau J.; Hennighausen N.; Brandt M.; Kron N.; Marat X.; Jouy C.; Black A.; Azadiguian G.; Guillon D.; Simonnet J.; Rinsch C.; Singh A.
Article.Abstract: Urolithin A (UA, Mitopure), a postbiotic that promotes mitophagy and mitochondrial function following oral administration, was evaluated for its effects on skin health in human skin models and when applied topically to healthy subjects in randomized clinical studies. UA tested in 2D and 3D reconstructed human skin and ex vivo human skin explants showed enhanced mitochondrial respiration, activated mitophagy markers, reduced inflammatory mediators and senescence-associated markers, and increased proteins involved in extracellular matrix structure and epidermal differentiation. Safety was confirmed in a human repeat-insult patch test. In randomized, placebo-controlled clinical studies, UA reduced periorbital wrinkle depth after 8 weeks and attenuated UVB-induced erythema. Skin transcriptomics supported increased extracellular matrix and epidermal development programs together with decreased inflammatory and senescence-associated signaling. These findings indicate that topical UA engages cellular pathways associated with skin resilience to promote skin health and longevity.

Article.Title: Thermoregulated photothermal therapy for bone defects using graphene oxide hydrogel with mesoporous silica-derived phase-change nanocapsules
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Zhao S.; Shang C.; Jiang Y.; Zhang W.; Pan S.
Article.Abstract: The clinical translation of photothermal therapy for bone repair is hindered by the risk of thermal damage to surrounding healthy tissues due to uncontrolled high temperatures. We addressed this by integrating phase change materials (PCMs) into a photothermal platform, developing a hydrogel scaffold with temperature regulation. Polyethylene glycol (PEG) was encapsulated in mesoporous nanosilica (MSNs) to form nanocapsules, achieving 82.5% efficiency. This encapsulation prevents PEG leakage and enhances thermal regulation and bioactivity. Graphene oxide (GO) was integrated into an alginate-chitosan matrix, yielding a GO/chitosan scaffold containing PEG@MSNs nanocapsules. The scaffold exhibits a phase transition at 41.2°C and latent heat of 95.5 J/g. Characterization confirms its physicochemical properties, biocompatibility, and cell affinity meet bone repair requirements. In vitro mineralization assays, osteogenesis studies, and in vivo bone defect models demonstrated its efficacy in temperature-controlled photothermal bone regeneration. This integration of photothermal control and biological activity represents an advance in scaffold design.

Article.Title: Non-volatile memristors as prospective radio frequency switches for 6G communications - A review
Article.Authors: Keat Seow E.; Toh R.; Ang D.
Article.Abstract: As communication technologies continue to improve to the 6G standard, highly performing radio frequency (RF) switches that have short switching times, high energy efficiency, high cutoff frequencies, capabilities of operating beyond 100 GHz while maintaining reasonable RF performance, and high data transmission rates of 100 Gbit s −1 are needed. Existing RF switches based on solid-state and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technologies fall short of meeting these requirements because of their volatility and parasitic inductive effects that lead to undesirably high insertion losses at high frequencies. Non-volatile memristors are emerging as likely candidates to replace traditional switches. They offer numerous benefits, including virtually zero static energy consumption, fast switching speeds, and excellent scalability. This review will provide an overview of the progress and challenges associated with implementing four types of non-volatile memristive technologies as RF switches: Resistive random access memory (ReRAM), conductive bridge random access memory (CBRAM), phase change memory (PCM), and memory based on two-dimensional (2D) materials, specifically molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The performance of these prospective switches is compared against one another and subsequently benchmarked against existing switch technologies. The review will provide an objective critique of the future readiness for 6G for the four main types of memristive switch technologies based on factors such as RF performance, CMOS compatibility, and fabrication maturity. Special attention is paid to 2D material-based memristors involving MoS 2 and hBN, which have attracted significant research interest for multiple benefits that are claimed to be distinctive. Finally, it will also propose research directions to further the progress of future memristive RF switches.

Article.Title: Global early-life cohorts for nutrition-neurodevelopment research including over 100 datasets representing over one million children
Article.Authors: Perrier S.; Foster A.; Sawant S.; Nassiwa F.; Kesri A.; Hsiao C.; Vyas R.; Grant P.; Durant K.; Morton S.; Ou Y.
Article.Abstract: Summary: The first 1,000 days of brain development are sensitive to nutrient availability, and large longitudinal early-life cohorts provide an opportunity to study early nutritional influences on neurodevelopment in generally healthy populations. We aimed to identify international pregnancy and birth cohorts with at least 1,000 children collecting early-life nutrition data, including maternal nutrition during pregnancy or lactation, breastfeeding, and solid-food feeding, along with later child neurodevelopmental outcomes. In total, 104 pregnancy and birth cohorts were identified, representing over 1.17 million children across 41 countries. Cohorts spanned six continents, with the largest participant representation from high- and upper middle-income settings. Maternal diet during pregnancy and breastfeeding status were the most frequently captured nutrition domains, while neurodevelopmental assessments varied across developmental periods, using over 200 assessment tools. These cohorts support future harmonized analyses of early nutrition and neurodevelopment, and further work will benefit from international collaboration, shared data standards, and pooled or federated infrastructures.

Article.Title: Targeting mutant NPM1-expressing AML with T cell receptor-like antibodies
Article.Authors: Hong Y.; Chen D.; Xu J.; Chen Y.; Shi Y.; Wang Z.; Gan C.; Wang Z.; Li Q.; Gao J.; Guo H.; Xia N.; Wu Y.; Zhang T.; Yuan Q.; Yang T.; Hu J.
Article.Abstract: This study developed T cell receptor (TCR)-like antibodies targeting the intracellular neoantigen derived from the common NPM1 type A mutation (NPM1 mutA ) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), presented by HLA-A∗02:01. Hybridoma technology was employed to generate a murine monoclonal antibody (m2E2) specifically recognizing the NPM1 mutA 283-291 -HLA-A∗02:01 complex. The lead antibody was humanized (hu2E2) and engineered into bispecific formats engaging CD3 or CD16, alongside an Fc-enhanced variant (hu2E2-GAALIE). In vitro , these antibodies mediated potent antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against NPM1 mutA -positive AML cell lines, inducing apoptosis and cytokine release. In vivo , a single dose of hu2E2 variants significantly suppressed tumor growth in NCG mice engrafted with OCI-AML3-LUC cells. Fc silencing abolished antitumor efficacy, confirming FcγR-dependent mechanisms. Critically, m2E2 specifically bound to primary CD33 + blasts from HLA-A∗02:01-positive, NPM1-mutated AML patients. These findings demonstrate a potent immunotherapeutic strategy for targeting intracellular oncogenic peptides in AML and support further clinical development of TCR-like antibodies.

Article.Title: Peroxisome-dependent and -independent functions of PEX19 in mouse embryonic stem cells
Article.Authors: Fan W.; Fang Y.; Hartsell J.; Wu X.; Xu X.; Li J.; Liu X.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Pluripotent embryonic stem cells (ESCs) possess a unique cell cycle pattern to support self-renewal and maintain pluripotency, and remodeling of this cycle by developmental cues is a key priming step for lineage commitment. Here we report an unexpected role of PEX19, a chaperone and receptor for peroxisomal membrane proteins, in regulating cell cycle and cell fates of mouse ESCs (mESCs) through a peroxisome-independent mechanism. We show that deletion of Pex19 in mESCs disrupts peroxisome assembly, elevating reactive oxygen species and impairing peroxisomal lipid metabolism. These peroxisomal defects increase cell death and diminish pluripotency. Intriguingly, PEX19 also interacts with α-tubulin to facilitate assembly of mitotic spindles in mitotic mESCs. Consequently, loss of Pex19 disrupts cell cycle progression and hinders the exit from pluripotency upon induction of neural differentiation, ultimately preventing differentiation of neural stem cells. Our study reveals a non-canonical function of PEX19 and underscores the importance of cell cycle regulation in cell fate decisions.

Article.Title: Midline thalamic neurons show early hypersynchrony during absence seizures in mouse models
Article.Authors: Dulko E.; Kilianski S.; Carns A.; Rajesh A.; Lesmana I.; Pikus M.; Beenhakker M.
Article.Abstract: Generalized seizures reflect a pathological state of sudden, global neuronal hypersynchrony. The mechanisms that support the initiation and maintenance of such synchrony remain unknown. Using simultaneous single-unit and electrocorticographic recordings in two mouse models of absence epilepsy, we evaluated the activity of approximately 2,000 individual neurons across 26 brain structures. By doing so, we resolved the temporal progression of single-neuron activity prior to and during generalized seizures. Surprisingly, we observed that rhythmic, synchronized activity emerges early and gradually in both the thalamus and cortex. Moreover, while we observe that individual neurons across most structures fire rhythmically and synchronously during seizures, a small subset of midline thalamic nuclei display activity that is strongly correlated across multiple regions. Finally, disturbing neuronal activity within the midline thalamus terminates seizures. Thus, our findings collectively highlight the possible role of the midline thalamus in emergence of neuronal hypersynchrony.

Article.Title: A Ca²⁺ level-independent component of recovery from sensory adaptation supports continuous vesicle supply at cochlear hair cell ribbon synapses
Article.Authors: Gribaudo W.; Catalano Di Meo C.; Agüero L.; Chequer Charan D.; Rutherford M.; Goutman J.
Article.Abstract: Maintenance of synaptic transmission can be accelerated by mechanisms dependent on intracellular Ca 2+ signaling. However, at the first auditory synapse between sensory inner hair cells (IHCs) and spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) in the cochlea, the process of synaptic vesicle recovery following strong, prolonged stimulation is unclear. To address this, we examined the Ca 2+ -dependence of presynaptic recovery in IHCs with measurements of postsynaptic activity in SGNs while depolarizing the IHC. Following vesicle-depleting stimulation of 1 second duration, SGN postsynaptic responses recovered completely within a few seconds. This process was unperturbed when reducing the intracellular Ca 2+ concentration by changing from 1 to 5 mM EGTA. Thus, synaptic recovery following depleting stimulation at IHC-SGN synapses may differ from the Ca 2+ -dependent process described during and after stimulation over shorter timescales. We propose a Ca 2+ level-insensitive mechanism of recovery at this continuously active sensory synapse to support vesicle release rates of hundreds per second indefatigably.

Article.Title: A method for expressing two proteins at a tunable ratio allows for studying the kinetics of creatine transport by MCT12
Article.Authors: Boytsov D.; Bicher J.; Kudlacek O.; Schicker K.; Tsurikov R.; Sucic S.; Freissmuth M.; Sitte H.; Sandtner W.; Roblek M.
Article.Abstract: Interactions between physically or functionally coupled proteins are often studied by co-expression from the same or separate plasmids, but protein ratios can vary widely between individual cells. To overcome this limitation, we developed a strategy to generate tunable and constant expression ratios using a single vector encoding two proteins separated by a P2A site followed by short AAA codon repeats that progressively reduce ribosomal readthrough. After validating this approach with the fluorescent proteins eGFP and mCherry, we applied it to characterize the transport cycle of the electroneutral monocarboxylate transporter MCT12, a task that is otherwise difficult to achieve experimentally. By co-expressing MCT12 with the concentrative creatine transporter CRT1 at defined ratios, we were able to determine the substrate turnover rate of MCT12 and its substrate K M . This approach enables precise control of protein stoichiometry, facilitating quantitative mechanistic studies of interacting proteins in cells.

Article.Title: Proteomic and functional profiling of suspended jejunal enteroids reveals pharmacokinetic fidelity to native intestine
Article.Authors: Tzioufa F.; Ceylan M.; Di Martino M.; Vo D.; Lopes A.; Hammar R.; Sundbom M.; Skogar M.; Hellström P.; Webb D.; Karlgren M.; Gardner I.; Lundquist P.; Eriksson J.; Hjelmqvist D.; Sellin M.; Hubert M.; Artursson P.
Article.Abstract: Intestinal enteroids are "mini-guts" that recapitulate essential features of the intestinal epithelium in vitro . We developed and characterized native basal-out (BO) and morphogenically everted apical-out (AO) jejunal enteroids cultured in suspension. Using quantitative proteomics and a range of advanced microscopy techniques, we show that these enteroids progressively adopt protein profiles closely resembling those of freshly isolated villus enterocytes and human jejunal tissue. Optimally differentiated enteroids exhibit mature epithelial morphology, intact barrier function, nutrient absorption, and clinically relevant transporter activity (P-glycoprotein; Pgp/ ABCB1 , breast cancer resistance protein; BCRP/ ABCG2 ), reflecting in vivo physiology. Metabolic assessment of orally administered cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) probe drugs, terfenadine and midazolam, accurately predicted first-pass metabolism and clinical pharmacokinetics via physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling. These findings establish suspension-grown 3D jejunal enteroids as a translationally relevant, human-derived platform that is advantageous over conventional cell line and animal models for studying drug disposition, nutrient transport, and intestinal barrier function.

Article.Title: HDAC inhibitor treatment restores transcriptome, chromatin accessibility, and memory deficits in a mouse model for Down syndrome
Article.Authors: Sierra C.; Crans R.; Dierssen M.
Article.Abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is associated with widespread molecular alterations, including aberrant gene expression, which not only affects chromosome 21 genes but perturbs the whole transcriptome. The genome-wide nature of this alteration suggests that it might be epigenetically mediated, which may also offer therapeutic opportunities given the reversibility of epigenetic modifications. Here, we show that decreased global acetylation level in the hippocampus of the trisomic mouse model Ts65Dn is associated with decreased chromatin accessibility at gene promoters in hippocampal neurons. Strikingly, pharmacological restoration of histone acetylation using the clinically approved histone deacetylase inhibitor suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA) normalized transcriptomic, epigenetic, and cortico-hippocampal memory deficits in trisomic mice. This rescue was mediated by an unexpected heterochromatization of the supernumerary chromosome. Altogether, our results identify an unanticipated epigenetic mechanism linking histone acetylation dynamics to chromosomal dosage homeostasis.

Article.Title: Divergent ectopic fat distribution and adipokine/hepatokine levels characterize the metabolically healthy overweight/obesity phenotype
Article.Authors: Clavero-Jimeno A.; Martin-Olmedo J.; Gatti A.; Cortés-Martín A.; Camacho-Cardenosa A.; Jurado-Fasoli L.; Dote-Montero M.; Molina-Fernandez M.; López-Vázquez A.; Lopez-Pascual A.; Ávila M.; Petrina E.; Zugasti A.; Urdiain I.; Concepción M.; Cabeza R.; Martín-Rodríguez J.; Labayen I.; R. Ruiz J.
Article.Abstract: The metabolically healthy overweight/obesity (MHOO) phenotype combines excess adiposity with preserved cardiometabolic health. We compared specific fat depots, circulating adipokine and hepatokine levels, and fecal microbiota composition between 384 adults classified as MHOO ( n = 99) or metabolically unhealthy overweight/obesity (MUOO; n = 285). Magnetic resonance imaging was used to quantify visceral adipose tissue (VAT) volume, hepatic and pancreatic fat fractions, abdominal and mid-thigh intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT), and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT). Despite similar whole-body fat mass, MHOO showed lower VAT volume, hepatic and pancreatic fat fractions, abdominal IMAT volume, abdominal VAT-to-SAT ratio, and mid-thigh IMAT area, together with higher mid-thigh SAT area. MHOO also had higher adiponectin and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) and lower retinol-binding protein 4 (RBP4) levels. Fecal microbiota composition was similar between groups. VAT volume and hepatic fat fraction were the strongest discriminative features, supporting fat distribution rather than total adiposity as a key feature of preserved metabolic health.

Article.Title: M2 type tumor-associated macrophage-derived CCL-18 promotes glioma cell proliferation but does not mediates glioma recurrence after radiotherapy
Article.Authors: Fan J.; Mao Y.; Liu L.; Ren Z.; Zhou Z.; Ma Y.; Lu X.; Cui G.; Zhang X.; Zhou X.
Article.Abstract: Most of glioma patients still experience relapse after radiotherapy owing to the formation of tumor immunosuppressive microenvironment. However, the comprehensive landscape of immune cell infiltration and the molecular mechanisms mediating glioma recurrence remains unclear. Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis revealed the significant changes in the immune system including increased total tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and elevated M2-TAMs in recurrent glioma accepting radiotherapy. Meanwhile, C-C motif chemokine 18 (CCL-18) was the highest elevated molecule after radiotherapy. Consistently, the aforementioned results were confirmed in tissue microarray containing 23 paired gliomas. In vitro , radiation promoted TAM polarization into M2-TAMs, accompanying CCL-18 secretion. However, CCL-18 promoted non-irradiated glioma proliferation but did not mediate glioma recurrence after radiotherapy. Mechanistically, the pro-tumor effect of CCL-18 was weakened by the down-regulation of CCL-18 receptors on glioma accepting radiotherapy. Our study indicates CCL-18 does not mediate glioma recurrence but has the potential to serve as a biomarker for recurrent gliomas.

Article.Title: Long-term ambient benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk through accelerated biological aging
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Peng Z.; Zhang J.; Cao H.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: The contribution of ambient air pollutants to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) remains undefined. This study included 401,472 adults from the UK Biobank (UKB), with residential benzene estimated at 1-km resolution from the DEFRA model (2006–2020). After multivariable adjustment in the Cox models, each interquartile-range (0.151 μg/m 3 ) increment in benzene was associated with a 26% higher risk of incident NAFLD (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21–1.30), following a nonlinear exposure-response relationship. Accelerated biological aging mediated 6.5% of this association, whereas homeostatic dysregulation and allostatic load contributed modestly. Benzene exposure and polygenic risk showed no multiplicative interaction, but their cumulative effect raised NAFLD risk among highly susceptible individuals. A machine-learning model integrating benzene and covariates predicted NAFLD with good discrimination (AUC = 0.753), and an external urinary-biomarker analysis in NHANES was directionally consistent. Thus, long-term low-level benzene exposure increases incident NAFLD risk, partly through accelerated biological aging.

Article.Title: Seeing the forest for the scenarios: Using decision trees to draw conclusions from large energy scenario sets
Article.Authors: Baader F.; Moret S.; Wiesemann W.; Staffell I.; Bardow A.
Article.Abstract: Energy transition studies often present hundreds of scenarios, yielding large datasets that are challenging to interpret. Alternative approaches define a few qualitative storylines, which are more accessible but disconnected from model-based evidence. Here, we show that decision trees, a popular machine learning technique, bridge this disconnect by distilling numerous scenarios into a small set of interpretable storylines centered around policy-relevant levers. We demonstrate this approach across three global and European case studies: First, we translate 1000 integrated assessment model scenarios into three storylines distinguished by their degrees of heating and industry electrification. Second, we show that 2°C warming pathways with continued fossil fuel usage only work under unusually mild climate responses. Third, we use 441 European pathways to show that high bioenergy or electrification are required for cost-effective climate neutrality. Our transferable approach helps decision-makers interpret large scenario sets by revealing how policy-relevant outputs are associated with different transition pathways.

Article.Title: Chaperone protein DnaK-mediated regulation of spore coat assembly in Bacillus subtilis
Article.Authors: Mu K.; Ling C.; Cui T.; Zhang Z.; Fang C.; Dong L.; Hu X.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial spores pose a significant challenge to the food industry due to their ability to germinate from dormancy and their extreme resistance. Spores are encased by a multilayered proteinaceous structure termed the spore coat. Previous studies on spore coat assembly have predominantly focused on the interactions among coat proteins, while the involvement of broader protein quality control systems remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the molecular chaperone DnaK is essential for the proper assembly of the inner spore coat in Bacillus subtilis . Deletion of dnaK leads to mislocalization of key morphogenetic protein SafA, reduced accumulation of full-length SafA, altered transcriptional dynamics of spoIIID and sigK , and ultimately impaired coat integrity and function. Our findings reveal that DnaK facilitates spore coat assembly through both transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, uncovering a previously unrecognized regulatory layer in spore coat morphogenesis.

Article.Title: Why cost reduction alone cannot deliver bankable carbon dioxide removal
Article.Authors: Smart J.; Mac Dowell N.
Article.Abstract: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) is indispensable for net-zero, yet CDR projects remain unbankable for institutional lenders. Using a stochastic project-finance model in which financing terms follow from simulated cash flows rather than being assumed, we examine when BECCS and DAC become bankable. Under unhedged conditions bankability is effectively zero, with lender coverage failing across most of the financing space and equity hurdles met in less than 0.1%. Contrary to the emphasis on cost reduction, credit-worthy offtake is the primary determinant. Learning alone lowers the levelized cost of removal by up to 38%, yet leaves projects unbankable, whereas offtake raises BECCS bankability to 43%, or 57% with learning. DAC requires offtake above US$2,500 per tCO 2 and remains marginally bankable, reflecting sole dependence on carbon revenues. An electricity-anchored BECCS pathway can reach investment grade without fully contracted carbon revenues. These results show where revenue support must be targeted to mobilize institutional capital.

Article.Title: Frequency-dependent cerebellar circuits independently gate social vocalizations and movement
Article.Authors: Brandenburg C.; Srivastava S.; Rey Hipolito A.; Lin T.; Arenkiel B.; Sillitoe R.
Article.Abstract: Communication depends on precise coordination between motor execution and cognition. Here we reveal that the cerebellum exerts real-time control over social vocalizations in adult mice. Optogenetic activation of excitatory cerebellar output in the superior cerebellar peduncle suppressed ultrasonic vocalizations with frequency-dependent potency while inducing distinct motor phenotypes. Systematic functional mapping across cerebellar regions and cell types revealed that vocal suppression can occur in the absence of overt motor impairment, suggesting selective control of vocal output beyond gross movement disruption. We identified the periaqueductal gray (PAG), a conserved midbrain vocal control center, as a key downstream mediator of this effect. Deep brain stimulation of the PAG rescued vocal deficits in a model of cerebellar dysfunction without rescuing motor incoordination. These findings define a cerebellar-midbrain pathway that gates vocal behavior and demonstrate that targeted therapeutic neuromodulation can selectively restore communication-related output even in the presence of persistent cerebellar-driven motor deficits.

Article.Title: Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific
Article.Authors: Berman Y.; Lee B.; Liu A.; Nishida Y.; Tan E.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is a complex multisystem disorder requiring coordinated multidisciplinary care. This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations for NF1 management in the Asia-Pacific region. A modified Delphi process involving two survey rounds and a virtual meeting was conducted with experts from nine countries. A total of 141 statements were evaluated using a 9-point Likert scale with a 75% consensus threshold. Consensus was achieved across key domains including diagnosis, genetic testing, surveillance, and management. Experts emphasized the importance of multidisciplinary care, risk-adapted surveillance, and integration of genetic counseling and imaging in clinical practice. These findings provide regionally relevant guidance to support consistent and practical NF1 management across diverse healthcare systems.

Article.Title: TXNRD1-driven enteric glial remodeling promotes neuronal dysfunction in Hirschsprung disease
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Jin Z.; Tang C.; Xia X.; Gong Y.; Du Q.; Huang L.; Li Z.; Liao Y.; He S.; Wang B.; Liu Y.; Zheng Z.
Article.Abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) is characterized by distal intestinal aganglionosis and persistent dysfunction of the enteric nervous system after surgical treatment. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomics, network-based virtual perturbation analysis, proteomics, human tissue validation, enteric glial cell assays, neuron-glia co-culture systems, and an Ednrb conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model to investigate TXNRD1-dependent enteric glial remodeling in HSCR. We found that thioredoxin reductase 1 (TXNRD1) enrichment was associated with expansion of an SPP1-high/CXCL9-low enteric glial state and selective ERK/MAPK activation. TXNRD1 overexpression increased oxidative stress, impaired enteric glial migration and neurotrophic support, and induced neuronal dysfunction through suppression of GDNF/GFRα1/RET signaling. TXNRD1 inhibition alleviated HSCR-like phenotypes in Ednrb cKO mice. These findings identify TXNRD1-driven redox-dependent enteric glial remodeling as a mechanism contributing to neuronal dysfunction and HSCR progression.

Article.Title: An ultrasound-switchable hydrogel enables sequential antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy for infected diabetic wounds
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Zhang C.; Zhang Q.; Xu F.; Wen B.; Xu Y.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Traditional dressings often fail to address the dynamic progression of infected diabetic wounds, which requires early bacterial elimination followed by timely control of oxidative stress and inflammation. Here, we developed an ultrasound-switchable Ce6/celastrol hydrogel for sequential antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy. Chlorin e6 (Ce6) and celastrol were co-encapsulated in a gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogel. Upon ultrasound irradiation, Ce6 generated singlet oxygen to reduce methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) in vitro . After ultrasound cessation, celastrol scavenged residual reactive oxygen species and suppressed inflammation. In an MRSA-infected diabetic wound model, the hydrogel with ultrasound reduced bacterial burden, alleviated inflammation, promoted collagen deposition, and accelerated wound closure. This strategy provides temporally regulated antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy for infected diabetic wounds.

Article.Title: Decoding how RNase E membrane targeting controls RNA degradosome activity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: Geslain S.; Allen G.; Geiser J.; Redder P.; Valentini M.
Article.Abstract: In many Proteobacterial species, transcription and RNA degradation are physically separated through segregation of the main ribonucleolytic machinery—the RNA degradosome—into RNase E-driven membrane-anchored assemblies that form discrete foci. Despite widespread conservation of the amphipathic membrane-targeting sequence (MTS) in RNase E, its function and biological importance remain poorly understood. Here, we have investigated how the MTS contributes to bacterial virulence or stress response in Pseudomonas aeruginosa . We show that membrane anchoring is dispensable for formation of RNA degradosome foci, but required for their proper morphology, dynamics, and localization, whereas the MTS sequence modulates foci behavior. Transcriptomic and mRNA spatial organization analyses further reveal specific stabilization of localized transcripts encoding membrane proteins in the MTS mutant, together with abnormal operon processing. Altogether, our study reveals the elegant MTS-mediated control of RNA degradosome spatial organization and target selection, shaping the transcriptome and bacterial stress responses.

Article.Title: Baseline techno-economic and life cycle assessment of black mass production
Article.Authors: Yingnakorn T.; Kansomket C.; Longbutsri C.; Scott S.; Patcharawit T.; Yang J.; Abbott A.; Khumkoa S.
Article.Abstract: Recycling lithium-ion batteries hinges on economically producing black mass—the electrode powder concentrate that feeds downstream metal recovery—yet public baselines pairing real process economics with environmental impacts remain scarce. Here we show that a purely mechanical flowsheet—shredding, zigzag air classification, and circular screen vibration—applied identically to two structurally distinct feedstocks recovers black mass at 93.28 wt % separation efficiency from electric-vehicle modules and 75.77 wt % from mobile phone cells. Built on measured pilot data, loaded processing costs of $0.31–0.73/kg yield net profits of $4.39–5.53/kg under realistic feedstock purchase prices, with a probability of unprofitability below 0.2% across simulated market scenarios. Life cycle assessment attributes most impacts to grid electricity, with a global warming potential of 0.210–0.241 kg CO 2 eq./kg input; a low-carbon grid cuts this by 62.8%. This paired baseline enables benchmarking of emerging recycling routes and supports circular battery supply chains.

Article.Title: Genomic structural variations distinguishing archaic and modern humans are associated with neurodevelopment
Article.Authors: Zha S.; Li C.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the divergence in neurodevelopment between extinct archaic hominins and modern humans is a central goal in evolutionary biology. Structural variants (SVs) are key genomic drivers of phenotypic change. Here, we identified a set of SVs present in archaic humans by screening fixed SV events from diverse non-human primate (NHP) lineages, termed archaic hominin structural variants (AHSVs). AHSVs are significantly enriched in genes governing brain development and function, many of which are implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. We found that several AHSVs overlap with brain cis -regulatory elements (CREs). Furthermore, in three neural-related genes ( PDE10A , RAPGEF4 , and DCTN4 ), modern human-specific chromatin loop anchors coincide with deletions shared by archaic hominins, suggesting that AHSVs may have influenced three-dimensional chromatin architecture. Overall, this study expands our understanding of the adaptive evolution of the modern human brain.

Article.Title: Domain-autonomous MKLP1 modules divergently regulate mitotic fidelity and polyploidy in a holocentric system
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Liu X.; Song M.; Qin M.; Tian S.; Lin Y.; Li D.; Yao L.; Ayra-Pardo C.; Kan Y.
Article.Abstract: While the kinesin MKLP1 is a well-established regulator of cytokinesis, whether its individual domains possess autonomous functions has remained unexplored. Here, using the holocentric Bombyx mori BmN4 system, we show that isolated head, stalk, and tail domains of MKLP1 exhibit distinct subcellular localization patterns and exert divergent control over mitosis. These domains differentially regulate cell-cycle progression, with the head and stalk inducing G2/M arrest, whereas the tail, and to a lesser extent the head, promotes polyploidization. Despite these divergent outcomes, all three domains converge on a shared pathological activity, aberrantly recruiting γ-tubulin, disrupting spindle organization, and compromising chromosome segregation. The domains also exert opposing effects on EdU incorporation, with the head suppressing EdU labeling and the stalk and tail enhancing it. Together, our findings redefine MKLP1 as a composite platform of regulatory modules, whose uncoupling reveals a principle of kinesin organization with broad implications for mitotic robustness and genomic stability.

Article.Title: Materials design strategies for green thermoelectric generators enabling sustainable and scalable energy harvesting
Article.Authors: Sabran N.; Fadzallah I.; Van Toan N.; Ono T.; Mohd Sabri M.; Jun H.
Article.Abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) harvest low-grade heat without moving parts and can be integrated into compact, flexible, or distributed systems. Progress in this field is typically measured through figure of merit, ZT , and the power factor, yet materials with high ZT often depend on scarce elements, toxic precursors, high-temperature processing, or difficult end-of-life recovery-considerations that matter for technologies intended to support sustainable energy systems. This perspective examines green thermoelectric design as a coupled materials, process, device, and life cycle problem, considering how aqueous processing, bio-assisted synthesis, hydrothermal methods, electrochemical deposition, and printable processing shape microstructure, defect chemistry, and charge-heat transport in conductive polymers, carbon nanotube hybrids, biomass-derived carbons, recycled inorganic compounds, and ionic thermoelectric systems. We propose a design framework that combines material abundance, process energy, solvent and waste burden, device lifetime, manufacturability, and circularity, and identify where environmentally responsible TEGs can deliver useful power with lower total burden.

Article.Title: Microenvironment shapes Staphylococcus aureus phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis over time
Article.Authors: Robaldi S.; Pereda R.; Pautasso M.; Blasko E.; Fretes A.; Jaureguialzo T.; Diaz Appella M.; Galeano M.; Rial M.; Smith S.; Ginestet E.; Gonzalez N.; González J.; Smania A.; Vila A.; Sola C.; Cassanelli P.; Tribelli P.
Article.Abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen in children with cystic fibrosis (CF), frequently preceding or coexisting with Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The impact of transient P. aeruginosa infection and therapeutic intervention on S. aureus phenotypic shaping remains poorly understood. We characterized 546 isolates from a longitudinal cohort of sixteen pediatric patients in CF follow-up, either monoinfected or coinfected, over eighteen months. Isolates were grouped into three phenotypic clusters. Monoinfected patients were enriched in a cluster with high pigment and biofilm, whereas transient P. aeruginosa detection was associated with a shift toward reduced pigment and biofilm, while coinfected patients maintained stable phenotypes. Phenotypes were determined by the airway microenvironment rather than by clonal background. In two monoinfected patients, this shift coincided with transient infection and ciprofloxacin treatment with increased MRSA; in vitro , MRSA predominated over MSSA when both P. aeruginosa and ciprofloxacin were present, underscoring the need to monitor S. aureus phenotypic transitions.

Article.Title: Choroid plexus remodeling associated with inflammatory CSF exposure in preterm acquired hydrocephalus
Article.Authors: Jison G.; Ramos N.; Cotrim-Gomes F.; Lee S.; Hanak B.; Muhonen M.; Castañeyra-Ruiz L.
Article.Abstract: Acquired hydrocephalus in preterm infants follows intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) or central nervous system infection and is associated with inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles. We integrated clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), CSF cytokine profiling, primary human choroid plexus (ChP) epithelial and endothelial cell assays, and independent transcriptomic and proteomic datasets to investigate ChP remodeling. Infants requiring CSF diversion exhibited greater ChP thickness independent of gestational age, ventricular size, and IVH severity, supporting its potential as a biomarker. Growth factor-enriched inflammatory CSF increased proliferation in primary human ChP epithelial and endothelial cells; EGFR and VEGFR inhibition attenuated these responses, and recombinant epidermal growth factor (EGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) reproduced proliferative effects. Independent IVH transcriptomic data confirmed Mki67 elevation in IVH ChP tissue. Integrated proteomic trajectories support a temporally dynamic remodeling framework linking acute inflammatory signaling to proliferative ChP activation and structural remodeling.

Article.Title: Comparing soil-health- and species-based sensitivity distributions for metal risk assessment in Tianjin soils
Article.Authors: Xu Q.; Shi Y.; Xiong X.; Qian L.; Fang L.; Zhou X.; Shao X.
Article.Abstract: Soil contamination threatens ecosystem functioning, while conventional ecological risk assessment (ERA) based on single-species toxicity may not capture system-level responses. We developed a probabilistic soil health sensitivity distribution (SHSD) framework integrating microcosm-derived soil health indicators with joint probability modeling and applied it to Pb, Cu, and Cd risks in Tianjin soils, northern China. SHSD-derived risks were lower than species sensitivity distribution (SSD)-based estimates by 61.90%, 59.55%, and 84.38% for Pb, Cu, and Cd, respectively. Normalizing SSD toxicity data to microcosm soil conditions reduced part of the SSD-SHSD discrepancy, highlighting the influence of soil physicochemical heterogeneity. Observed SHSDs were also shifted rightward relative to additive, non-interactive predictions, indicating lower apparent sensitivity of the integrated microcosm. These findings support SHSD as a higher tier, function-oriented complement to conventional SSDs, while emphasizing the need for independent field validation before regulatory application.

Article.Title: An unexploited almond biodiversity in central Italy: Genetic characterization and conservation strategies using molecular markers
Article.Authors: Savoia M.; Sgaramella N.; Micheletti A.; Staffolani P.; Gaeta L.; Venerito P.; Miazzi M.; Fanelli V.; Montemurro C.
Article.Abstract: Almond is one of the most important nut crops worldwide. In Italy, 96% of the national almond production is covered by the Southern regions. However, small resources of cultivated and wild trees are also found in central Italian regions like Abruzzo, Sardinia, and Marche. Exploratory missions throughout the Marche region revealed the presence of many local and uncharacterized almond genotypes. The aim of this study was to recover this germplasm and characterize it using molecular markers. The genetic analysis revealed a high genetic variation in Marche almond genotypes, which showed them to be genetically distinct from the Italian and international varieties. A great richness in private alleles was found in the Marche almond collection, supporting the uniqueness of this germplasm and the importance of this resource of genetic diversity for the development of conservation programs and the implementation of almond breeding activities.

Article.Title: Nonpharmacological interventions for frailty and sarcopenia in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers: A Bayesian network meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Hui X.; Fu Z.; Guo Y.; Duan L.; Shi W.; Dong Q.; Xu Q.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To compare the effects of nonpharmacological interventions on frailty, sarcopenia, and related physical-function outcomes in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers, we conducted a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 21 randomized controlled trials from 10 countries. Most interventions did not show clear benefits for frailty, sarcopenia, gait speed, Timed Up and Go performance, sit-to-stand performance, skeletal muscle index, or 6-min walk distance. Prehabilitation exercise showed a low-certainty benefit for handgrip strength, whereas enhanced nutritional support and intensive physiotherapy showed limited benefits for patient-reported physical function. However, these findings were based on small, sparsely connected networks, and the certainty of evidence was generally low or very low. No single intervention was consistently effective across outcomes. These results highlight the need for larger, cancer-specific trials using standardized outcome definitions and clearer reporting of intervention intensity, adherence, safety, and feasibility.

Article.Title: Host-response biomarker panels for distinguishing selected acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections from mono-infections
Article.Authors: Nahid-Samiei R.; Ebrahimi D.; Samiei M.; Nahand J.; Donyavi T.; Bokharaei-Salim F.
Article.Abstract: Acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections complicate antimicrobial decisions because pathogen detection may not establish whether both organisms are clinically contributing to disease. We synthesized evidence from adult and pediatric acute respiratory infection cohorts, including influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and selected mixed-detection febrile illness studies, to evaluate host-response biomarkers for distinguishing co-infection from mono-infection. Conventional C-reactive protein and procalcitonin were most useful as supportive or rule-out markers of bacterial involvement, but lacked sufficient specificity when used alone. Dual-axis strategies that combine antiviral and bacterial-response signals, including MxA/CRP, TRAIL/IP-10/CRP, CD169/CD64, IFI44L/FAM89A, and targeted transcriptomic or proteomic signatures, provided more biologically coherent discrimination of mixed infection states. These findings support prospective validation of integrated host-response panels as rapid decision-support tools for antimicrobial stewardship and clinically meaningful co-infection diagnosis.

Article.Title: Ectopic overproduction of cell wall glucan through membrane perturbation by an antifungal peptide theonellamide A in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Nakao K.; Carvalho V.; Suganaga A.; Osumi M.; Tokukura M.; Kakeya H.; Matsuyama A.; Yashiroda Y.; Matsunaga S.; Cortés J.; Yoshida M.; Ribas J.; Nishimura S.
Article.Abstract: Ergosterol has multiple functions in filamentous fungi and yeasts, although only a part of the functions seems to be understood. An antifungal peptide, theonellamide A (TNM-A) induces drastic morphological changes in fission yeast by targeting plasma membrane ergosterol. TNM-A induces overproduction and accumulation of cell wall glucan at growing tips and septum through a yet unknown mechanism. Here, we show that TNM-A causes accumulation of 1,3-β-glucan at cell-polarity sites, not by increased activity of 1,3-β-glucan synthase, but by an increased, persistent localization of the glucan synthases. Screening based on subcellular localization of proteins suggested the involvement of the Rho family GTPase Cdc42, a master regulator of cell polarity. In agreement, TNM-A increased active Cdc42 and enhanced the membrane trafficking of glucan synthases. In conclusion, our chemical genetics analyses using TNM-A suggest that membrane ergosterol regulates the Cdc42 activity, which further regulates the localization of glucan synthases and cell wall biosynthesis.

Article.Title: Genome-wide mapping of the Galleria mellonella transcription start sites during fungal infection and treatment
Article.Authors: Abugessaisa I.; Konings M.; Manabe R.; Tagami M.; Severin J.; Hasegawa A.; Kawashima T.; Kinoshita H.; Noma S.; Takahashi C.; Verbon A.; Okazaki Y.; van de Sande W.; Kasukawa T.
Article.Abstract: Galleria mellonella is an emerging experimental model, but its current genome annotation lacks transcription start site (TSS) information. Because TSS annotation is essential for understanding transcriptional regulation, we used low quantity single strand CAGE (LQ-ssCAGE) to map cap analysis of gene expression (CAGE)-defined TSSs from 72 G. mellonella larval samples. Among these, 36 larvae were infected with the fungal pathogen Madurella mycetomatis and 36 served as healthy controls, allowing identification of TSSs under both infected and healthy conditions. Infected and healthy larvae were treated with itraconazole or ravuconazole. To assess key characteristics of the CAGE data, TSS peaks and putative enhancers were intersected with the existing genome annotation for annotation and characterization. This analysis identified two sets of TSS peaks, permissive and robust, representing the first draft TSS atlas for G. mellonella . The atlas-derived annotations showed a markedly stronger core promoter sequence signature than the NCBI reference annotation, supporting improved resolution and accuracy of TSS annotation in the atlas.

Article.Title: Development of CNN and LSTM fusion model for early fault warning in hydro turbine units
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Chen Y.; Xiang X.; Wang J.; Wang S.; Jiang X.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Early fault detection is important for the safe and stable operation of large hydro turbine units under complex and variable operating conditions. This study develops an early fault warning framework for high dimensional multisource monitoring data by integrating Kendall rank correlation-based parameter grouping, systematic data governance, sparse principal component analysis, and a CNN LSTM prediction model. Fifty two operating parameters are organized into six groups and transformed into six sparse state features. The CNN LSTM model captures local correlations and temporal evolution, achieving R 2 values of 0.947, 0.955, 0.848, 0.701, 0.687, and 0.853 for SPCA1 to SPCA6. Prediction residuals combined with 2σ and 3σ thresholds identify early degradation before the recorded fault, with warning lead times of up to 33 time steps. The framework provides a practical approach for condition monitoring and hierarchical early warning of large hydro turbine units.

Article.Title: Trait anxiety selectively amplifies reward learning under uncertainty, while N3 sleep attenuates it
Article.Authors: Deshmukh R.; Ramakrishnan A.
Article.Abstract: Adaptive learning under uncertainty requires distinguishing random variability (stochasticity) from true environmental change (volatility), yet how trait anxiety and sleep together influence it remains unclear. Across two preregistered experiments, participants completed a probabilistic reversal-learning task that independently manipulated volatility and stochasticity. Hierarchical Bayesian modeling showed that in stable but noisy environments, individuals with higher trait anxiety appeared to treat stochastic fluctuations as indicators of genuine change, resulting in over updating and lower evidence accumulation, while preserving normative trends in volatile environments. In a second experiment combining task performance with overnight sleep electroencephalography, greater N3 sleep was associated with reduced updating and higher evidence accumulation in stable environments among individuals with higher trait anxiety. These findings suggest that trait anxiety selectively alters how uncertainty is computationally represented, while N3 sleep appears to attenuate it. Together, these findings provide a computational framework linking anxiety, sleep, and adaptive learning under uncertainty.

Article.Title: Bidirectional metabolic-vascular feedback loops in heart failure: From myocardial energetics to multisystem cardiometabolic crosstalk
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Li Y.; Qin C.; Chen X.; Wang K.; Zhang M.; Cheng W.
Article.Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a multisystem syndrome in which myocardial dysfunction is shaped by metabolic, vascular, and extracardiac abnormalities. Across HFrEF and HFpEF, impaired substrate utilization, mitochondrial function, endothelial signaling, coronary microvascular function, and mechano-energetic coupling disrupt the matching of ATP supply to cardiac demand, while obesity, insulin resistance, inflammation, and vascular stiffness further accentuate cardiometabolic HFpEF. In this Review, we integrate these processes into five self-reinforcing metabolic-vascular circuits: substrate-perfusion mismatch; mitochondrial reactive oxygen species-endothelial dysfunction; endothelial metabolism-nitric oxide-myocardial stiffness; immunometabolic-microvascular inflammation-fibrosis; and afterload-mechano-energetic uncoupling. We also examine how adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, liver, and kidney amplify these circuits. Together, this framework links myocardial energetic dysfunction with systemic vascular-metabolic stress and highlights circuit-directed opportunities for phenotype-informed HF therapy.

Article.Title: Urban habitats offer buffered environmental conditions for city-dwelling bats
Article.Authors: Ding J.; Boonman A.; Eitan O.; Werber Y.; Troupin D.; Sapir N.; Yovel Y.
Article.Abstract: Urbanization reshapes local climates, potentially altering how animals respond to environmental variation. We used continuous acoustic monitoring at 12 urban and 15 rural sites across a steep aridity gradient in Israel, recording bats for 2.5 months from midsummer to autumn. Across 1,151 site-nights, we detected 95,473 encounters from 11 species. Rural bat activity was strongly associated with temperature, humidity, wind speed, and illumination, whereas urban activity was less sensitive to these environmental factors and to building height and density. Rural specialists avoided cities and were active within relatively narrow environmental ranges, while generalists occurred in both habitats and used broader activity conditions in cities. Urban bat activity also remained comparatively stable as rural activity declined seasonally. These findings show that cities may buffer environmental variability, allowing bats to forage across broader weather and potentially remain active later in the year.

Article.Title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA
Article.Authors: Shi X.; Xu H.; Li W.; Wang J.; Song Y.; Yang M.; Wang B.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. Notably, microbial community structure evolved at a rate approximately one order of magnitude faster than community function. This decoupling was mediated by functional redundancy associated with bacterial keystone taxa, ultimately resulting in more negative sedimentary carbon and nitrogen isotopic compositions nearly a century later. Gene-level functional redundancy further buffered ecosystem function variability across biological scales. Collectively, our findings integrate omics and geochemical approaches to advance the understanding of lake ecological evolution under complex multi-forcing regimes.

Article.Title: An atlas of sarbecovirus infectivity across diverse ACE2 orthologs
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Cheng Z.; Wu X.; Liu K.; Wang L.; Yang D.; Huang W.; Nie J.
Article.Abstract: Sarbecoviruses pose a substantial zoonotic threat, yet the determinants governing their host range remain incompletely defined. To systematically investigate host entry mechanisms, we generated a panel of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudoviruses representing 46 sarbecoviruses and assessed their infectivity across 66 angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) orthologs. This analysis produced a high-resolution host-entry landscape with direct implications for cross-species transmission risk. We found that all severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) isolates, WIV1, and pangolin-derived sarbecoviruses demonstrated broad ACE2 usage, whereas no sarbecovirus utilized alternative entry factors including neuropilin-1, CD147, AXL, or TMEM106B. Notably, ACE2 orthologs from Rhinolophus affinis and Miniopterus schreibersii supported infection by nearly all clade 1 sarbecoviruses, identifying highly permissive host receptors. We also identified residues 27 and 42 of ACE2 as critical determinants of sarbecovirus host tropism. Together, these findings define host entry constraints relevant to receptor-based risk assessment and inform surveillance and pandemic preparedness.

Article.Title: Sulfate modification CeO2: A strategy for SF6 photocatalytic degradation
Article.Authors: Zhu S.; Zhao Y.; Wu Y.; Ma F.; Lin T.; Cao J.; Hang C.
Article.Abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) is extensively employed in high-voltage electrical equipment due to its exceptional dielectric properties, yet its potent greenhouse effect and extreme chemical inertness demand efficient abatement strategies. This study presents sulfate-modified ceria (CeO 2 ) photocatalysts designed to activate robust S–F bonds through surface Brønsted acid sites. Sulfate groups anchored on CeO 2 polarize SF 6 molecules and facilitate photogenerated electron injection into antibonding orbitals, enabling reductive bond cleavage under mild conditions. The optimized 0.5SCe catalyst achieves an SF 6 degradation amount of 7.41 mL g −1 within 24 h under 365 nm LED irradiation, representing a 10.4-fold enhancement over pristine CeO 2 . The catalyst maintains stable performance across consecutive cycles and 96 h of continuous operation. This surface acidity engineering strategy offers a sustainable pathway for controlling fluorinated greenhouse gas emissions.

Article.Title: Lipid-based mRNA chimeric antigen receptor T cells for enhanced in vitro antitumor activity
Article.Authors: Gao H.; Fang Y.; Tian Z.; Guo C.; Wang P.; Liu T.; Sun Y.; Zhang P.; Qian Q.
Article.Abstract: Summary: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy provides substantial clinical benefits in hematologic malignancies. However, cell engineering using conventional viral vectors is costly, labor intensive, and prone to safety risks, while electroporation-induced cellular damage limits manufacturing scalability. This study reports a safe, high-efficiency, nonviral platform for generating mRNA-engineered CAR T cells. Herein, eight ionizable lipids are synthesized and formulated into lipid nanoparticles.
