Article.Title: Prediction of dynamic retention during polymer flooding EOR in carbonate outcrops using empirical correlation
Article.Authors: Sebastian A.; Markovic S.; Al-Shalabi E.
Article.Abstract: Polymer retention is a critical parameter in polymer flooding and requires accurate measurement for successful field implementation. However, coreflood tests for measuring dynamic polymer retention are time-consuming, costly, and labor-intensive, motivating the application of correlations that map readily measurable static adsorption to dynamic retention. In this study, 36 coreflooding and 36 static adsorption tests were conducted on carbonate outcrops and crushed powder, respectively, under identical conditions to determine dynamic retention and static adsorption values. Existing mathematical correlations in the literature for predicting dynamic retention, primarily developed for sandstone outcrops under single-phase conditions, were fitted to the current dataset. In addition, empirical equations and regression models were developed to predict dynamic retention values from parameters influencing polymer retention, including static adsorption values, residual oil saturation, and the size ratio factor. An 80:20 train-test split and leave-one-out cross-validation were employed to evaluate the predictive performance of the regression models. The experimental dataset showed poor agreement with the existing correlations, primarily due to differences in rock type. Further, both a simple regression equation with static adsorption as the sole influencing parameter and a multiple linear regression equation incorporating additional parameters, including residual oil saturation and the size ratio factor, were developed to predict dynamic retention. The empirical equations demonstrated a strong fit to the experimental dataset, achieving R² values of 0.93 and 0.96, respectively. All regression models performed well in predicting dynamic retention from the influencing parameters, with R² testing values of at least 0.97.

Article.Title: Spatial differentiation and constraints of rural multifunctionality under urban and rural demands in the Hangzhou Metropolitan Area, China
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Xu K.; Chen Q.
Article.Abstract: Rural areas within metropolitan regions are increasingly shaped by expanding urban activity and internal rural transformation. This study develops a demand-oriented analytical framework that classifies rural functional indicators by whether they primarily reflect endogenous rural needs or exogenous urban demands, and applies it to assess rural multifunctionality. Drawing on township-level data from 2013 to 2023 in the Hangzhou Metropolitan Area, this study examines the spatial patterns, evolutionary dynamics, and constraints of rural multifunctionality. Rural multifunctionality generally increased over the period, and its spatial structure evolved from a scattered pattern in 2013 to a core–periphery gradient by 2023, with additional high-value areas around Jiaxing and Huzhou. Functional imbalances persist, with ecological dominance and relatively weak non-agricultural and cultural-recreational capacities characterising several peripheral areas. Based on the joint variation of the multifunctionality index and its coordination degree, four zones are delineated, namely priority promotion, potential promotion, collaborative optimisation, and moderate optimisation, and zone-specific constraints are diagnosed to inform differentiated planning. This study offers an analytical framework and township-scale evidence for advancing urban–rural integration.

Article.Title: Integrating artificial intelligence into higher education balances student learning benefits and cognitive overload
Article.Authors: Alam M.; Alharbi T.; Islam M.; Amin M.; Mustafa Z.; Ali Z.; Zygiaris S.; Azad M.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, reshaping how students access information, complete academic tasks, and engage with learning. Despite its growing educational role, the implications of AI-supported learning for students’ psychological well-being remain insufficiently understood, particularly in developing-country contexts. This study examines how Perceived Usefulness of AI Tools in Learning (PUAITL) and Frequency of AI Tool Usage in Academic Activities (FAITUAA) are associated with Student Mental Health (SMH), while investigating Cognitive Overload (CO) as a mediating mechanism and Digital Self-Efficacy (DSE) as a moderating factor. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 390 undergraduate and postgraduate students from public and private universities in Bangladesh and analyzed using PLS-SEM with Smart-PLS 4.0 and bootstrapping procedures. The findings indicate that both perceived usefulness and frequency of academic AI use are positively associated with SMH. Importantly, both PUAITL and FAITUAA are associated with lower cognitive overload, whereas greater cognitive overload is associated with poorer student mental health. CO partially mediates both relationships, indicating that AI-supported learning is associated with psychological well-being both directly and indirectly through reduced cognitive burden. DSE significantly strengthens the positive relationship between PUAITL and SMH, whereas its moderating effect on the relationship between FAITUAA and SMH is not statistically significant. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory, Conservation of Resources Theory, and Technostress Theory, the study provides an integrated explanation of the cognitive, resource-related, and psychological mechanisms underlying AI-supported learning. The findings emphasize the importance of responsible AI integration, cognitive-load management, digital capability development, and context-sensitive institutional support for promoting psychologically sustainable AI-enabled learning environments in higher education.

Article.Title: Accessible data visualization for university students screening positive on the adult ADHD self-report scale
Article.Authors: Khan R.; Shovon M.; Islam K.; Tamim R.; Noor J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital information is increasingly delivered through visual interfaces, yet these interfaces are rarely designed with neurodiverse cognitive profiles in mind. This study evaluated how different data visualization formats influence information processing, perceived cognitive demand, user preference, and supplementary physiological indicators among university students who screened positive or negative on the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS v1.1). A controlled experimental study was conducted with 70 participants (40 ASRS-negative and 30 ASRS-positive), who completed information-processing tasks using eight visualization formats: Plain Text, Highlighted Text, Bar Charts, Bar Charts with Images, Pictographs, Simplified Infographics, Detailed Infographics, and AI-modified Text. Performance was assessed using the Inverse Efficiency Score (IES), while heart rate and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO $$_2$$ ) were recorded as supplementary physiological measures. Data were analyzed using Two-Way Mixed ANOVA, Linear Mixed-Effects Models, MANOVA, Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, and Bayesian analyses. The results demonstrated a significant interaction between participant group and visualization format ( $$p<0.001$$ , partial $$\eta ^2=0.104$$ ), indicating that visualization effectiveness differed between students screening positive and negative on the ASRS. Plain Text, Highlighted Text, and Bar Charts with Images generally supported comparatively better behavioral performance across groups, whereas Detailed Infographics and AI-modified Text were associated with substantially poorer performance among ASRS-positive participants (Hedges’ $$g=-1.775$$ and $$-1.162$$ , respectively). Contrary to common assumptions, text highlighting did not consistently improve performance across groups, suggesting that attentional cues may not be universally beneficial. Evidence of divergence between subjective preference and objective performance was observed for selected visualization formats, indicating that user preference alone may not reliably predict behavioral effectiveness. Physiological measurements exhibited relatively limited variation across experimental conditions and are therefore interpreted as supplementary rather than primary indicators. These findings provide empirically derived recommendations for designing more accessible digital learning materials for university students who screen positive on the ASRS while highlighting the importance of evaluating visualization effectiveness using objective behavioral measures alongside subjective user feedback.

Article.Title: Early recurrent hemofilter thrombosis despite regional citrate anticoagulation during continuous renal replacement therapy: a prospective observational study
Article.Authors: Chardon N.; Florentin A.; Rimmelé T.; De-Wreede A.; Balança B.; Lukaszewicz A.; Fellahi J.; Juillard L.; Balice G.; Nougier C.; Rezigue H.; Bidar F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) is the recommended first-line anticoagulation strategy during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). However, early and recurrent hemofilter thrombosis may still occur despite apparently adequate RCA at the measured time points. This complication is poorly described and its mechanisms are unknown. We aimed to describe the clinical and laboratory profile of affected patients and to explore candidate mechanisms of thrombosis. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study in six medical and surgical ICUs in Lyon, France (September 2023–September 2025). Adult patients with early hemofilter thrombosis, defined as filter failure within 24 h of extracorporeal circuit initiation during RCA-CRRT, were included. Clinical, technical, and laboratory parameters were collected at the time of thrombosis. When available, laboratory variables were compared, using a paired within-patient design, with control samples obtained after thrombosis resolution and CRRT discontinuation. Retrieved thrombi were analyzed by fluorescence and electron microscopy with immunolabeling. Given the sample size and observational design, all analyses were exploratory and not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Twenty-five patients were included. All exhibited sepsis, and 17 (68%) had septic shock, defined by vasopressor requirement, with high severity at admission (sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) 10 [8–14]) and at CRRT initiation (SOFA 13 [9–15]). CRRT was delivered mainly as continuous veno-venous hemodialysis (64%). Post-filter calcium remained within target range in 90.3% of patients, and early thrombosis frequently recurred (median of 2 episodes per patient). At the time of thrombosis, patients showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, elevated C-reactive protein, and high fibrinogen, whereas conventional coagulation tests, natural anticoagulants, and thrombin generation assay parameters did not show overt systemic hypercoagulability. In exploratory paired analyses (n = 9), inflammatory markers were higher during thrombosis than at the control time point. Thrombus analyses showed abundant fibrin, platelets, neutrophil-rich cellular material, and extracellular citrullinated histone H3 labeling. In this exploratory study, early hemofilter thrombosis during RCA-CRRT occurred in critically ill septic patients with marked inflammatory activation despite apparently adequate regional anticoagulation, and was accompanied by neutrophil-rich, citrullinated histone H3–positive intrafilter thrombi. These findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest a predominantly local thrombo-inflammatory process. They need to be confirmed in larger, controlled studies including comparator groups before informing tailored anticoagulation strategies.

Article.Title: PoSFed: stake-aware validator selection and update filtering for blockchain-coordinated healthcare federated learning
Article.Authors: Lee C.; Lien J.
Article.Abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralizing sensitive patient data, but reliance on a single coordinating server may introduce service-disruption and update-integrity risks. We present PoSFed, a blockchain-coordinated federated learning framework that combines PoS-inspired validator selection, validator-side F1-score-based update filtering, and contribution-aware reward allocation. PoSFed was evaluated using the Pima Indian Diabetes, Wisconsin Breast Cancer, and COVIDx CXR-4 datasets in controlled single-server simulations with 5, 10, and 20 clients under IID, non-IID, and adversarial settings. When 50% of the simulated participants submitted malicious updates, PoSFed achieved an accuracy of 86.7 ± 1.4% and an F1-score of 88.6 ± 1.2%, showing improved robustness relative to the evaluated conventional federated optimization baselines. These results provide preliminary evidence of the feasibility of stake-aware update validation in the evaluated simulation. Validation on a concrete permissioned blockchain and geographically distributed healthcare networks remains necessary.

Article.Title: Deep learning-driven joint blind source separation and noise suppression for audio signals: a performance optimization study
Article.Authors: Xie R.; Tao Z.; Lei L.; Hu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Separating overlapping talkers and suppressing non-stationary noise are coupled problems, yet conventional pipelines solve them in isolation, so separation artifacts propagate untouched into the denoising stage. We therefore build a time–frequency joint separation–denoising network: a learnable encoder, a multi-scale dilated separator carrying channel and time–frequency attention, a per-stream noise-suppression module conditioned on the shared encoding, and an inverse-transform reconstructor, all reading one representation and trained end to end. A three-term objective binds scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio, spectral magnitude and perceptual weighting, and training spans input signal-to-noise ratios down to − 5 dB. Evaluation draws on LibriMix, WHAM! and WHAMR! for separation, VoiceBank-DEMAND and MUSAN for noise, and MUSDB18-HQ for a full-band check outside speech. Against seven baselines retrained under an identical recipe, with every difference tested on 3000 mixtures across three seeds, the model reached 15.60 ± 0.10 dB SI-SNR improvement, 3.02 PESQ and 0.917 STOI at 0 dB with 3.9 million parameters. It surpassed Conv-TasNet, DPRNN, SepFormer, a diffusion-based cascade and a serial separate-then-denoise pipeline; TF-GridNet and MossFormer2 scored 0.50 to 0.80 dB higher at seven to eleven times the arithmetic cost, so the contribution is accuracy per unit of computation rather than absolute accuracy. Cost measurements report 6.8 G multiply–accumulate operations per second of audio, a real-time factor of 0.51 on a single CPU core and 0.41 J per second of processed audio, and a causal variant suited to streaming gives up 1.70 dB. Ablation separates the two attention paths, at 4.50% and 7.10%, from the joint denoising route at 10.30%. Cross-corpus, unseen-language and reverberant tests bound generalization: transfer costs 0.70 to 2.20 dB, and improvement falls to 7.80 dB once reverberation time exceeds 0.90 s. Code, configurations and per-utterance records accompany the article.

Article.Title: Cross-attention fusion of biparametric MRI sequences with demographic and clinical variables for patient-level classification of clinically significant prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Dimitriadis A.; Kalliatakis G.; Osuala R.; Kessler D.; Diaz O.; Mazzetti S.; Regge D.; Lekadir K.; Fotiadis D.; Tsiknakis M.; Papanikolaou N.; N/A N/A.; Sfakianakis S.; Kalokyri V.; Trivizakis E.; Tachos N.; Mylona E.; Zaridis D.; Kalantzopoulos C.; de Almeida J.; Verde A.; Rodrigues A.; Rodrigues N.; Chambel M.; Huisman H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate patient-level risk stratification of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) on biparametric MRI remains challenging, as most existing approaches require costly lesion-level annotations or have not been evaluated in large temporally separated cohorts. We developed and validated a multimodal deep learning framework combining T2-weighted (T2w), diffusion-weighted (DWI), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) volumes with age, prostate-specific antigen (PSA), and PSA density (PSAD) for patient-level csPCa classification, trained without lesion-level annotations. The study included a retrospective development cohort of 3, 939 examinations and an independent temporal validation cohort comprising 1, 409 prospectively acquired examinations from 13 centers. The model employs three sequence-specific encoders with asymmetric cross-attention fusion and a two-stage transfer-learning strategy. Adding demographic and clinical variables consistently improved performance over MRI-only models, with PSAD emerging as the most informative complementary factor, primarily by improving specificity. The best-performing model—combining MRI, age, PSA, and PSAD with cross-attention—achieved a mean AUC of $$0.765\!\pm \!0.006$$ on the retrospective held-out test set and $$0.741\!\pm \!0.006$$ on the independent temporal validation cohort. Post hoc subgroup analyses suggested broadly stable rank-order discrimination (AUC) across most strata, though fixed-threshold sensitivity and specificity varied substantially, while Grad-CAM maps offered a qualitative indication of more frequent overlap with suspicious regions under cross-attention. These findings support PSAD-informed multimodal patient-level models as a viable tool for refined csPCa risk stratification on biparametric MRI, with potential to reduce false-positive classification of ISUP grade group 1 disease as clinically significant.

Article.Title: Development of gradient structured copper wire deformation and heat treatment technology for cable industry
Article.Authors: Volokitina I.; Volokitin A.; Denissova A.; Gelmanova Z.; Ulyeva G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study addresses the challenge of optimizing the trade-off between strength, ductility, and electrical conductivity in high-strength microcomposite Cu-14Fe alloy wires. A novel thermo-mechanical processing approach is proposed, combining successive cycles of twisting in an equal-channel step die with subsequent drawing along two temperature routes: cold (Route A, room temperature) and warm (Route B, 250 °C), followed by low-temperature annealing (300–500 °C). Results demonstrate that cold processing induces a sharp gradient microstructure (from submicron grains ~ 400 nm at the surface to 7 μm in the center), yielding maximum hardening. Conversely, warm deformation activates dynamic recovery, forming a uniform polygonized structure that preserves ductility. It was found that deformation processing along Route A ensures maximum workpiece hardening (ultimate strength σ в = 675 MPa), while warm deformation along Route B allows for the retention of an increased ductility resource δ = 19.0%, ψ = 25.0%. An anomalous change in mechanical properties was revealed during subsequent thermal treatment: annealing at 400 °C initiates a simultaneous increase in strength and ductility for both routes, achieving peak σ в values of 700 MPa (Route A) and 610 MPa (Route B). A key finding is an anomalous simultaneous increase in both strength and ductility during post-deformation annealing at 400 °C for both routes, driven by precipitation hardening from the decomposition of the supersaturated solid solution. Ultimately, preliminary warm deformation (Route B) proves technologically superior, establishing a thermally stable subgrain structure with enhanced resistance to softening and restrained recrystallization kinetics across the investigated temperature range.

Article.Title: A symmetric dual stream deep learning model with a shared encoder and topological attention gate for crack segmentation
Article.Authors: de Santana W.; de Lima V.; Madeiro F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Semantic crack segmentation is an important task in the automated inspection of civil structures, but preserving crack continuity, connectivity, and structural consistency remains challenging for conventional models. In this work, SkelTAG-Net (Skeleton Topological Attention Gate Network) is proposed as a symmetric dual-stream deep learning model with a shared encoder, composed of a segmentation stream and a supervised skeleton stream, in which structural information is injected into the segmentation decoder through a Topological Attention Gate (TAG) module. The model is evaluated on the CrackVision12K dataset and compared with CNN-based, Transformer-based, and hybrid architectures. The results show that SkelTAG-Net achieves the best overall performance, obtaining an IoU of 0.676, an F1-Score of 0.781, and a clDice of 0.848, outperforming models such as SegFormer-B2 and U-Net. These results indicate that SkelTAG-Net has potential for applications in the automated inspection of civil structures and for supporting Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems.

Article.Title: Fostering conceptual understanding of organic solar cells through immersive augmented reality: a quasi-experimental study in chemistry education
Article.Authors: Sarwar M.; Alharbi A.; Nazar M.
Article.Abstract: Organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly important in modern chemistry and sustainable energy education; however, undergraduate students often struggle to understand their molecular structure, charge generation, charge transport, and operating mechanisms because these processes are abstract, invisible, and difficult to convey using conventional instructional approaches. This study investigated whether an immersive augmented reality (AR) learning application could improve conceptual understanding of OSCs and reduce students’ misconceptions. The AR application was developed through a needs assessment with chemistry educators and incorporated interactive three-dimensional visualizations, molecular- and device-level explanations, and simulations of key OSC processes. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, combining a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study with semi-structured student interviews. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) revealed that the instructional method had a significant effect on post-test performance after controlling for pre-test scores (F(1,117) = 214.67, p < .001, partial η² = 0.823), indicating a large educational effect. Students who used the AR application demonstrated substantially greater improvements in conceptual understanding than those receiving conventional instruction, particularly regarding OSC structure, operating mechanisms, molecular interactions, and charge transport, while misconceptions were markedly reduced. Student interviews further confirmed that immersive visualization enhanced understanding by making abstract molecular and device-level processes more accessible and engaging. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of immersive AR for improving conceptual learning in chemistry education and highlight its potential for teaching emerging sustainable energy technologies.

Article.Title: Different dietary compositions shape reproductive physiology in Litopenaeus vannamei broodstock
Article.Authors: Abo-Al-Ela H.; Mosbah A.; Tahoun A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maintaining the reproductive performance of Litopenaeus vannamei broodstock toward the end of the breeding season remains a major challenge for commercial hatcheries, primarily due to physiological exhaustion. This study evaluated whether diversified dietary formulations could extend the breeding period and enhance larval quality. Broodstock (males: 50 ± 2 g; females: 69 ± 5 g) were allocated to four dietary treatments comprising worms ( Nereis spp., ragworm), squid ( Loligo forbesii ), and mussels ( Mytilus galloprovincialis ). Group 1: 80% worms and 20% squid; Group 2: 80% worms and 20% mussels; Group 3: 50% worms, 25% mussels, and 25% squid; and Group 4: equal proportions (25% each) of worms, mussels, squid, and chicken liver. Over a 30-day trial, reproductive indices (HSI, GSI, OMI), hemolymph biochemistry, hepatopancreatic antioxidant status, and the expression of key maturation-related genes ( vih , vtg , iag , igfbp1 ) were assessed, alongside histological examination of the hepatopancreas and gonads. Group 3 exhibited the highest reproductive efficiency, producing significantly greater egg output and larval yield compared with the worm-dominated control (Group 1). Molecular analyses showed a pronounced downregulation of vitellogenesis-inhibiting hormone ( vih ) in the eyestalks, accompanied by upregulation of vitellogenin ( vtg ) in the hepatopancreas of Groups 3 and 4. In males, expression of the insulin-like androgenic gland hormone ( iag ) peaked in Group 4, corresponding with enhanced histological structure of the vas deferens. Group 4 also exhibited enhanced hepatopancreatic antioxidant status, characterized by increased superoxide dismutase activity and reduced lipid peroxidation. Histological observations showed that diversified diets promoted healthy hepatopancreatic structure and sustained vitellogenic progression in the ovaries. Overall, reducing reliance on polychaetes and incorporating a balanced mix of mussels, squid, and chicken liver provides an effective nutritional strategy to rejuvenate aging broodstock. These findings offer a practical nutritional approach for hatcheries to enhance seed production and potentially prolong broodstock productivity, with the observed reproductive responses associated with changes in neuroendocrine-related marker gene expression.

Article.Title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
Article.Authors: Sapparojpattana P.; Likhitrakarn N.; Siriwut W.; Srisonchai R.; Wesener T.; Jeratthitikul E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. However, its historical biogeography has remained insufficiently understood. In this study, we used an integrative analysis combining morphology, comprehensive molecular phylogeny based on mitochondrial and nuclear genes, and biogeographic approaches to provide new insights into the evolutionary history of Rhopalomeris in Thailand. The multilocus phylogeny indicated the presence of 21 species-level subclades, with nine previously described species and 12 putative species. Divergence time estimation and historical biogeography analysis revealed that Rhopalomeris likely originated in the Tenasserim Range and the inner area of Indochina around the Late Eocene to Early Oligocene (41.39–28.89 Mya, mean age = 34.78 Mya), followed by southward expansion into the Thai-Malay Peninsula and a series of subsequent diversifications shaped by recurrent sea-level fluctuations and multidirectional dispersal. Our findings highlight the dynamic interplay between Earth’s history and biogeographic processes driving the diversity of these Southeast Asian pill millipedes.

Article.Title: Theory of planned behavior constructs and self-reported thyroid health-preventive behaviors among women of reproductive age in Khuzestan Iran
Article.Authors: Karimy M.; Hatamzadeh N.; Kasmaei P.; Haeri-Mehrizi A.; Zakerkish M.; Araban M.
Article.Abstract: Congenital hypothyroidism (CH) is the most common congenital endocrine disorder and one of the preventable causes of intellectual disability through timely diagnosis and treatment. Understanding thyroid health-preventive behaviors during the reproductive years may provide useful insights for health promotion. This study aimed to assess thyroid health–preventive behaviors and their associated beliefs among reproductive-aged women in Khuzestan Province, Iran, based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). This cross-sectional study included 411 women of reproductive age selected through multistage random sampling between May 2023 and February 2024. Data were collected using a self-designed questionnaire with established validity and reliability, covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, and TPB constructs. The outcome was self-reported thyroid health–preventive behavior, categorized as optimal or non-optimal adherence. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test, Mann–Whitney U test, correlation analysis, and univariate and multivariable logistic regression. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis of 411 participants, higher intention (adjusted OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.01–1.35), subjective norm (adjusted OR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.05–1.20), perceived behavioral control (adjusted OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.07–1.34), and attitude (adjusted OR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.06–1.23) were associated with higher odds of optimal adherence to thyroid health–preventive behaviors (all p < 0.05). Knowledge was significantly associated with preventive behaviors in the unadjusted analysis, but the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant after adjustment (adjusted OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.87–1.03, p = 0.203). This study found associations between TPB constructs and self-reported thyroid health–preventive behaviors among women of reproductive age. Attitudes, Subjective norm, perceived behavioral control, and intention may be relevant to preventive practices. These findings may inform the development of tailored educational and health promotion strategies that could be considered within existing preconception, antenatal, and postnatal healthcare services. Further longitudinal and intervention research is needed to determine whether such strategies are associated with sustained changes in preventive behaviors.

Article.Title: Trends in reported HIV diagnoses, exposure patterns, and AIDS-related mortality in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, 2014–2023
Article.Authors: Ebrahimi R.; Fekri M.; Nejadghaderi S.; Tahmasbi Arashlow F.; Bazrafshani M.; Alaama A.; Jamil M.; Karamouzian M.; Sharifi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) continues to face a substantial HIV burden, with increasing numbers of reported diagnoses, heterogeneous exposure patterns, and persistent AIDS-related mortality. Despite global progress, countries of EMR remain far from achieving the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. This analysis of regional HIV surveillance data presents trends in reported diagnoses, exposure patterns, and AIDS-related mortality across EMR countries from 2014 to 2023. We analyzed country-level aggregated HIV surveillance data submitted annually to the WHO Regional Office for the EMR from 2014 to 2023. Data included new HIV diagnoses, exposure modes, demographic characteristics, and AIDS-related deaths. Descriptive analyses were performed to assess temporal trends, country-level disparities, and reporting completeness. Newly reported HIV diagnoses in the EMR increased sevenfold, from 3,717 in 2014 to 26,314 in 2023, with men accounting for nearly three-quarters of diagnoses. Exposure data, available for 73.6% of cases in 2023, indicated heterosexual contact as the most frequently reported route, followed by injecting drug use, same-sex contact, and blood exposure, though substantial proportions remained unknown. Exposure patterns varied markedly across countries, reflecting both epidemiological context and surveillance limitations. Over the study period, 22,569 deaths were reported, with greatest numbers from Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Somalia. Mortality disproportionately affected men over the study period, though sex-disaggregated data were incomplete in several settings. HIV in the EMR is characterized by rising diagnoses, heterogenous reported exposure, and significant mortality, with major reporting gaps in coverage and completeness. Strengthening surveillance systems, expanding diversified testing strategies, and scaling up culturally sensitive prevention and treatment services are critical to improve epidemic control. Regional collaboration and integration of harm reduction, sexual health, and stigma reduction strategies remain essential for improving outcomes and achieving HIV control targets.

Article.Title: Vaginal and urinary microbiota in breast cancer survivors undergoing fractional CO2 laser therapy
Article.Authors: Jacobsen S.; Bundgaard-Nielsen C.; Glavind-Kristensen M.; Jensen A.; Forman A.; Sørensen S.; Bor P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is common in breast cancer survivors (BCSs) receiving endocrine therapy, and non-hormonal treatment options remain limited. Fractional CO₂ laser therapy has been investigated as a non-hormonal treatment option, but its influence on the genitourinary microbiota remains unclear. We conducted a prospective study of BCSs with GSM undergoing five sessions of laser therapy. Vaginal swabs and midstream urine samples were collected before the first treatment and after the final treatment. Microbiota profiles (only bacteria here) were generated using Nanopore long-read 16 S rRNA gene sequencing targeting the V1–V8 region and temporal changes in alpha and beta diversity were evaluated. Twenty-six participants completed both sampling time points. The vaginal microbiota was predominantly Lactobacillus -dominated and showed no detectable change in alpha diversity or overall community composition after treatment. In contrast, the urinary microbiota displayed greater interindividual variability and a reproducible shift in overall community composition from baseline to follow-up. These urinary shifts persisted after adjustment for relevant clinical covariates and were not explained by consistent changes in individual taxa on differential abundance testing. Functional pathway profiles were unchanged in both vaginal and urinary samples. Overall, the vaginal microbiota remained largely stable between baseline and follow-up, whereas a modest temporal difference in urinary microbial community structure was observed. Further randomized controlled trials are needed, to elucidate whether these changes in urine microbiota are the result of laser therapy or are the results of other temporal changes in the women.

Article.Title: The physiological and molecular responses of Ophiopogon japonicus to drought and waterlogging stresses at two growth stages
Article.Authors: Dai W.; Lai Q.; Wang J.; Fan H.; Zhang J.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growth and medicinal quality of Ophiopogon japonicus are susceptible to water stress, yet little is known about how drought and waterlogging differentially regulate physiological and molecular responses across developmental stages. This study conducted pot experiments during the vegetative growth stage (September–October) and tuberous root expansion stage (January–February), applying drought (soil water content maintained at 15%, w/w) and waterlogging (2–3 cm water layer above soil surface) for 3, 6, 12, and 24 days, with three biological replicates per treatment. Growth, yield, quality, antioxidant enzyme activities, membrane lipid peroxidation, osmolytes, and endogenous hormone levels were measured, and transcriptome profiling was performed at the 12-day time point. The results revealed significant stage- and organ-specific responses: during the vegetative stage, drought strongly inhibited root growth and activated antioxidant defense and osmotic adjustment, whereas short-term waterlogging slightly promoted growth and long-term waterlogging was mildly inhibitory; during the tuberous root expansion stage, short-term stress promoted dry matter accumulation whereas prolonged stress reduced yield, and ABA was prominently associated with drought response. Final harvest analysis showed that early drought inhibited shoot and fibrous root growth but promoted tuberous root yield, with opposite patterns for waterlogging; drought during the tuberous root expansion stage increased polysaccharide and methylophiopogonanone A/B contents, whereas waterlogging reduced quality. Transcriptome analysis suggested that drought-induced quality improvement was associated with enrichment of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, whereas waterlogging-induced yield and quality decline was associated with altered secondary metabolism and lipid metabolism pathways. This study demonstrates that O. japonicus dynamically adjusts physiological strategies according to growth stage, providing insights for precision water management.

Article.Title: 3D vascular quantitation with application to computational modeling: a pre-clinical light sheet microscopy, high resolution ultrasound, nano-computed tomography comparison study
Article.Authors: Zhang D.; Lindsey S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract It is increasingly necessary to both study biology in 3D and obtain quantitative measurements. Not all 3D-reconstructions are created equal, particularly when using the anatomical model as a basis for force calculations, i.e. computational modeling. Here, we compare 3D anatomical reconstructions from two emerging imaging modalities: 4D ultrasound (4DUS) and light sheet fluorescent microscopy (LSFM) against our previous nano-computed tomography (nanoCT) cohort data, using the tortuous highly intricate pharyngeal arch artery system of the chick embryo as a test bed. We highlight modality-specific morphological image acquisition discrepancies and their influence on subsequent computational fluid dynamics results. Overall, LSFM accurately captured quantitative volumetric measurements of small rapidly-changing vascular morphologies while 4DUS systematically inflated small tortuous vessels. Differences in image-based morphology changes led to significant changes in computationally-obtained force magnitudes and flow patterns linked to vessel angle and tortuosity. This validates LSFM as a comparative preclinical vascular quantitative imaging tool and suggests that 4DUS needs extensive 3D anatomical validation for small, non cardiac chamber, vessels.

Article.Title: Isolation and characterization of human skin-derived bacteriophages with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against coagulase-negative staphylococci
Article.Authors: Damar Celik D.; Karaynir A.; Ozkan R.; Aksu B.; Bozdogan B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus capitis , are significant opportunistic pathogens associated with biofilm-related infections and antimicrobial resistance. Although bacteriophage therapy is a promising alternative to antibiotics, human skin-derived phages targeting clinically important CoNS remain poorly characterized. Four bacteriophages were isolated from facial skin swabs of healthy volunteers, and two (phages Se_20 and Se_42) were selected for detailed characterization. Biological characteristics, antibacterial activity, genomic features, and preliminary in vivo activity were evaluated. Both phages exhibited lytic activity against clinically relevant CoNS and reduced planktonic bacterial counts by > 3 log₁₀ CFU/mL within 4–6 h. They showed strain-dependent antibiofilm activity, inhibiting biofilm formation by up to 88.6% and reducing preformed biofilm biomass by up to 86.3%. Both exhibited a latent period of 25 min, while the burst sizes were 142 PFU/cell for Se_20 and 70 PFU/cell for Se_42. Genome analyses confirmed that phages were lytic and lacked virulence factors, antimicrobial resistance genes, and tRNA/rRNA genes. In the Galleria mellonella infection model, phage treatment increased larval survival without detectable toxicity. This study demonstrates that the human skin microbiome is a valuable source of lytic bacteriophages against CoNS and supports their further preclinical evaluation as alternative antimicrobial candidates for biofilm-associated infections.

Article.Title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
Article.Authors: Panigada V.; Feliu-Tena B.; Belda E.; Degollada E.; Gallego V.; Nowacek D.; Santonja P.; Tort B.; Panigada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. Here, we present satellite telemetry tracks from seven fin whales (2022–2025) with five years of supporting evidence from systematic land-based observations (2021–2025) in the western Ibiza Channel to investigate movement patterns, behavior, and habitat use beyond the North-Western Mediterranean Sea. All tracked whales left the Mediterranean Sea passing through the Strait of Gibraltar and subsequently moved northward along the Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula, providing direct evidence of cross-basin movements from the Mediterranean to the North Atlantic. Behavioral analyses using two independent movement-modeling approaches identified a common pattern of directed transit followed by area-restricted search (ARS) behavior—commonly associated with foraging—in several Atlantic areas, including waters off the Iberian Peninsula and the Bay of Biscay. The occurrence of prolonged ARS behavior in these areas is consistent with the use of Atlantic feeding habitats. The similarity of movement trajectories across individuals, years, tagging locations, and data streams indicates that seasonal use of Atlantic waters may represent a regular component of the movement ecology of at least some fin whales in the Mediterranean Sea. Given that these movements span multiple jurisdictions and areas of intense maritime activity, conservation measures should consider both important feeding habitats and the migratory routes that connect them.

Article.Title: Deciphering the anticorrosion performance of Arnica montana extract for mild steel in 1.5 M HCl using experimental and computational insights
Article.Authors: Elebo A.; Adamu A.; Ogbonnaya H.; Ndaks B.; Bawa E.; Abatyough M.; Jibunor V.; Adegbe E.; Polycarp G.; Yaya S.; Endas L.; Drammeh A.
Article.Abstract: The increasing demand for environmentally benign alternatives to conventional corrosion inhibitors has stimulated interest in plant-derived materials. This study explores Arnica montana extract (AME) as a sustainable corrosion inhibitor for mild steel (MS) exposed to 1.5 M HCl, employing an integrated experimental and computational strategy. The novelty of the work lies in coupling a renewable botanical inhibitor with advanced soft-computing and molecular simulation approaches to simultaneously optimise, predict, and explain corrosion inhibition behaviour. The metal corrosion processes were evaluated using parameters such as AME concentration, immersion time and temperature, which were optimised by response surface methodology (RSM), artificial neural network (ANN) and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) models. Moreover, the results confirmed a remarkable decrease in both weight loss and corrosion rate as AME concentration increased, in parallel with improvement in inhibition efficiency; this suggests good surface coverage and better interaction of molecules of AME at high concentration. Mathematical assessment of all generated models demonstrated ANFIS being the best predictor with high predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.9803), with values of AARE, RMSE and SD being 0.0108, 0.0024 and 0.0019, respectively, compared to others. Electrochemical investigation via potentiodynamic polarisation and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy showed that AME acted as a mixed-type inhibitor. Calculations based on quantum chemical descriptors indicated interaction at the molecular level between MS and AME, and molecular dynamics simulations showed an optimum binding energy of the adsorption configuration, as well as formation of a denser protective film through O, N, and Br group interactions. These indicate that the good predictive capability of the ANFIS model and excellent adsorption ability of phytochemical constituents contribute to the usage of AME as a sustainable corrosion inhibitor for acidising industry applications.

Article.Title: Deployment-time action correction for steady-state reinforcement learning-based optimal power flow
Article.Authors: Cortés P.; Tabares A.; Mojica-Nava E.; Bolaños R.; Bonilla K.
Article.Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of constraint violations in reinforcement learning (RL) for power-system operation, with application to steady-state optimal-power-flow tasks. While RL-based controllers can achieve competitive reward performance, they may produce actions that violate operational constraints, limiting their practical applicability in steady-state optimal-power-flow (OPF) tasks. We investigate a deployment-time safety framework in which a continuous constraint-violation surrogate is learned directly from state–action–violation samples generated by the power-system simulator. Once the nominal Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy has been trained, it remains fixed, and candidate actions are corrected by minimizing their deviation from the original policy output while penalizing the violation predicted by the learned surrogate. The correction is performed directly over the nonlinear surrogate using projected gradient descent, and linear and quadratic penalty formulations are empirically compared. The framework is evaluated on two complementary OPF-Gym benchmarks, EcoDispatch and MaxRenewables, which differ in their optimization objectives, network topologies, actuator compositions, and control dimensionalities. Large-scale out-of-sample simulations show substantial reductions in the frequency and severity of constraint violations relative to nominal SAC, Lagrangian-penalty SAC, Recovery RL, and linearized correction baselines; across both benchmarks, the exact-gradient variants substantially reduce physical constraint violations relative to nominal SAC and the linearized correction strategies. In EcoDispatch, these feasibility improvements are additionally achieved while maintaining reward performance close to the underlying SAC controller. The results demonstrate the potential of simulator-driven deployment-time action correction for improving the empirical feasibility of RL-based OPF decisions without retraining the nominal policy or requiring the analytical OPF constraints to be exposed in differentiable form.

Article.Title: Clarifying the roles of hydrogen and peroxyl radicals in the degradation of aromatic hydrocarbon polymer-based proton exchange membranes
Article.Authors: Gubler L.; Han Z.; Yu Y.; Nauser T.; Nemeth T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chemical degradation by radicals limits the durability of aromatic hydrocarbon-based proton exchange membranes used in fuel cells and water electrolyzers. While hydroxyl radicals (HO • ) are recognized as important degradation initiators, the roles of hydrogen (H • ) and peroxyl radicals (HOO • /ROO • ) remain poorly understood. Here, γ-radiolysis of water was used to selectively generate H • and HOO • /ROO • along with HO • under acidic conditions relevant to device operation. Two aromatic sulfonate model compounds representing structural motifs of hydrocarbon ionomers were exposed to radicals in N 2 saturated and O 2 containing solutions at pH 0 and 2. In the presence of HO • , degradation increased with radical dose and was enhanced by oxygen and increasing pH, consistent with established HO • -induced degradation pathways. Selective suppression of HO • using tert -butanol showed that H • radicals cause negligible degradation of the aromatic substrates, while HOO • and organic peroxyl radicals (ROO • ) exhibit only minor reactivity. These results indicate that HO • is the principal radical responsible for degradation of the investigated aromatic hydrocarbon model compounds, whereas H • and HOO • /ROO • contribute little to substrate loss. The findings improve the mechanistic understanding of radical-induced degradation and provide guidance for the development of more durable hydrocarbon membranes.

Article.Title: Comparison between [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-RGDyK and [18F]FET for the assessment of gliomas: results of a pilot study
Article.Authors: Testart Dardel N.; Gnesin S.; Dunet V.; Schiappacasse L.; Ferraro D.; De Micheli R.; Hegi M.; Hottinger A.; Prior J.; Cicone F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Arg-Gly-Asp peptide (RGD) binds to α v β 3 integrins, which are involved in the development of new vessels, necessary for tumor growth. Several RGD-based PET radiopharmaceuticals have been developed to visualize integrin α v β 3 expression. Differences between O-(2-[ 18 F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine ([ 18 F]FET) and integrin-targeting radiopharmaceuticals in patients with brain tumors have not been evaluated so far. Our aim was to compare the diagnostic information provided by the α v β 3 integrin-targeting [ 68 Ga]Ga-NODAGA-RGDyK ([ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD) with that of [ 18 F]FET and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted sequences (CE-T1w) in 10 patients with newly diagnosed or recurrent diffuse glioma. After image registration, tumor segmentation of [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD and [ 18 F]FET PET images was performed using the average background signal multiplied by 1.6 as a threshold for positivity. The contrast-enhancing tumor portions were manually delineated on CE-T1w sequences. Tumor volumes (TV) identified by all three modalities (i.e. TV RGD , TV FET , TV CE−T1w ) were compared and their spatial congruence (SC) calculated. Thirteen brain lesions from 10 patients ( n = 4 with high-grade gliomas and n = 6 with low-grade gliomas) were analyzed, all showing increased [ 18 F]FET uptake. Nine lesions were [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD-positive, 4 were [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD-negative, all corresponding to non-contrast enhancing lesions. Tumor-to-background ratios (TBR) were higher for [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD-positive than for [ 18 F]FET -positive disease (median TBR = 3.92 vs. 2.12, respectively, p = 0.008). All [ 18 F]FET - and [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD-positive lesions extended beyond the contrast-enhancing tumor portions. In the whole cohort, TV FET exceeded TV RGD (median values = 11.2 vs. 7.7 mL, p = 0.014). In most high-grade glioma lesions (i.e. 5/7), however, TV RGD was larger than TV FET . Overall, median overlapping volume between [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD and [ 18 F]FET was 3.6 mL (range 0.1–8.13mL), and the median SC was 24.3% (range, 0.9–59.8%). [ 18 F]FET and [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD PET provide different information. In the overall cohort, TV FET was larger than TV RGD , however TV RGD tended to be larger than TV FET in the subgroup of patients with high-grade glioma. [ 68 Ga]Ga-RGD PET may delineate regions of active neoangiogenesis extending beyond gadolinium enhancement. Trial registration : https://www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02666547 , registered 2012-08-12.

Article.Title: Clinically benchmarked and interpretable machine learning for preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian tumors
Article.Authors: Barzegari-Ahranjani S.; Kalbkhani H.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer is a highly fatal gynecological malignancy, largely because it is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage. Although machine learning (ML) has shown promise for ovarian cancer classification using clinical laboratory data, many existing models operate as black boxes, limiting clinical interpretability. This study proposes an interpretability-centered ML framework for distinguishing malignant from benign ovarian tumors using a publicly available, retrospective, single-center Chinese cohort from the Third Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, comprising 349 patients with 171 malignant and 178 benign ovarian tumors. Variables with excessive missingness were excluded, while retained missing values were mean-imputed and features were min–max normalized. Imputation statistics and normalization parameters were estimated exclusively from the training data and applied unchanged to the evaluation data to prevent information leakage. Five classifiers, support vector machine (SVM), k-nearest neighbor, discriminant analysis, decision tree, and logistic regression, were evaluated using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization. SVM achieved the highest accuracy of 93.7% and sensitivity of 95.3% considering the leave-one-out cross-validation. The proposed framework optimizes both predictive and explanation stages: Bayesian optimization first tunes the classifiers, followed by joint optimization of LIME perturbation sample size and kernel width. The optimized LIME surrogate achieved 91.9% accuracy, only 1.8% points below the SVM, while identifying CA125 and CA19-9 as the dominant positive predictors of malignancy, consistent with established clinical knowledge. These findings indicate that systematic calibration can improve the fidelity and stability of patient-level explanations, although stronger predictive results have been reported on the same dataset and external validation remains necessary. However, prospective, multicenter, and clinician-in-the-loop validation is required before clinical decision-support use.

Article.Title: ROI-constrained query selection for small object detection with RT-DETRv2
Article.Authors: Fan Q.; Wu S.; Liao L.; Liu Q.; Fu J.
Article.Abstract: Object detection is a significant research direction within the field of computer vision. In recent years, Transformer-based object detection methods have achieved a commendable balance between detection accuracy and inference efficiency, with RT-DETRv2 demonstrating robust real-time detection capabilities. However, during the decoder query initialization stage, RT-DETRv2 primarily employs a global Top-K selection strategy based on encoder token classification scores. This approach tends to overlook local key regions, particularly in complex backgrounds and scenarios involving small objects, which complicates the effective retention of weak-response targets. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an enhanced method termed ROI-DETR, which is founded on ROI-constrained query selection. This method integrates the ROI Mask pass-through mechanism within the RT-DETRv2 framework and combines it with an adaptive token mask mechanism, a multi-scale budget allocation strategy, and an ROI-guided Mixed Top-K query selection strategy. These enhancements optimize the query generation process from the encoder to the decoder, thereby bolstering the model’s ability to concentrate on potential target regions. Experimental results indicate that on the COCO dataset, the Average Precision (AP) of ROI-DETR reaches 0.501, reflecting an improvement of 0.006 over RT-DETRv2, while the AP for small objects reaches 0.321, an enhancement of 0.015. Furthermore, three repeated experiments on DOTA and TinyPerson provide evidence of cross-dataset applicability. On DOTA, ROI-DETR achieves an AP of 0.259 ± 0.001 compared with 0.251 ± 0.001 for RT-DETRv2; on TinyPerson, the mean AP increases from 0.193 ± 0.002 to 0.197 ± 0.001, while the APs change remains marginal. In the ablation experiments, this paper substantiates the contribution of each sub-module to detection performance and analyzes the operational mechanisms of each module. The statistics and visualization results concerning Top-K token and ground truth (GT) matching further demonstrate that this method can enhance the coverage of target-related queries while mitigating background token interference. In summary, ROI-DETR significantly improves the selection quality of small target-related queries in complex backgrounds, offering a viable approach to optimizing the small target detection performance of real-time Transformer detectors.

Article.Title: The PairInteraction toolkit for modeling Rydberg physics in alkali and alkaline-earth-like atoms
Article.Authors: Mögerle J.; Hummel F.; Keil A.; Legrand T.; Braun E.; Menke H.; King J.; Olmos B.; Hofferberth S.; Büchler H.; Weber S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rydberg atoms provide a powerful platform for exploring strongly interacting quantum systems, both in free space and in structured electromagnetic environments, with growing applications in quantum technology. Accurately modeling their single-atom properties and mutual interactions is essential for interpreting experiments and designing new architectures. We present a unified theoretical framework for Rydberg atoms and their interactions based on multi-channel quantum defect theory (MQDT) and static electromagnetic Green’s tensors. MQDT provides a precise description of Rydberg states of divalent atoms such as strontium and ytterbium, while the Green’s tensor formalism provides a general and flexible approach for calculating interactions between two Rydberg atoms in arbitrary geometries, including modifications induced by nearby surfaces. We implement this framework in an updated version of the open-source toolkit PairInteraction [Weber et al., J. Phys. B 50 (2017)]. The implementation leverages high-performance libraries and achieves speedups of one order of magnitude for pair-potential calculations compared to prior software. We demonstrate the capabilities of the toolkit through example applications to divalent atoms and show excellent agreement with experimental data for an exemplary Stark map of $$^{174}$$ Yb. The modular software architecture enables the community to extend it further.

Article.Title: Buchdahl type anisotropic stellar configurations in Rastall gravity
Article.Authors: Kumar R.; Fatima S.; Dhankar P.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the impact of the Rastall coupling parameter on the internal structure, global properties, and stability of compact stellar configurations. Within the framework of Rastall gravity, an anisotropic relativistic stellar model is developed to explore how deviations from general relativity (GR) modify the fundamental physical properties of ultra-dense matter. A systematic comparison with the corresponding GR configuration is performed to elucidate the effects of the Rastall parameter on the density and pressure profiles, compactness, and other physical quantities. The resulting mass–radius (M–R) and moment of inertia–mass (I–M) relations demonstrate that Rastall corrections can significantly enhance the maximum mass and moment of inertia supported by compact stars, compared with the corresponding GR counterpart. Furthermore, the predicted M–R and M-I relations are confronted with astrophysical observational constraints associated with the neutron-star candidates, including PSR J0437-4715, PSR J222-0137, PSR J1614-2230, PSR J0348+0432. These comparisons provide bounds on the maximum permissible mass of the configurations and demonstrate their compatibility with the astrophysical observations. The physical viability and stability of the model are further examined through the standard energy conditions, causality constraints, adiabatic-index criterion, and hydrostatic equilibrium described by the generalized Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equation. Overall, our results reveal that the Rastall coupling parameter plays a significant role in determining the structural and stability properties of compact stars, highlighting modified Rastall gravity as a viable geometric extension of GR for modeling ultra-dense astrophysical systems.

Article.Title: Fractal and multifractal characteristics of particle-size distributions in debris-flow deposits
Article.Authors: Zongheng X.; Yilong L.; Jianjiao B.
Article.Abstract: Particle-size distribution is a fundamental characteristic of debris-flow deposits and provides important information on sediment transport, sorting, and depositional processes. This study investigates ten debris-flow deposit profiles along the sampled main-channel reach along Jiangjiagou, Yunnan Province, China. Mechanical sieving combined with laser diffraction was employed to obtain high-resolution particle-size data, and single-fractal and multifractal approaches were used to quantitatively characterize the spatial variability, structural complexity, and multiscale heterogeneity of particle-size distributions. The results reveal that the deposits were dominated by the coarse fraction (> 0.05 mm), which accounted for 95.75–99.82% of the total particle-size composition, whereas clay and silt contents varied among sampling sites, indicating clear spatial differentiation in particle-size organization. The global fractal dimension ranges from 2.09 to 2.40, reflecting substantial variability in particle mixing and granulometric complexity. The generalized dimension spectra exhibit a typical inverted S-shaped pattern, while D₀, D₁, and D₂ show marked spatial variations among sampling sites. The characteristic singularity strength (α₀) ranges from 0.768 to 1.714, and the spectrum width (Δα) varies from 1.19 to 2.49. D₁/D₀ values are consistently well below unity, further indicating pronounced heterogeneity and multiscale variability in particle-size distributions. Correlation analysis shows that the fractal and multifractal characteristics are closely related to particle-size composition, with fine-particle enrichment generally associated with higher granulometric complexity, whereas coarser deposits tend to exhibit relatively simplified fractal structures. These results demonstrate that fractal and multifractal parameters provide an effective quantitative framework for characterizing the complex particle-size architecture of debris-flow deposits and offer new insights into sediment sorting, transport, and depositional processes.

Article.Title: Explainable hybrid stacking ensemble for robust smart grid stability assessment under cyber–physical disturbances
Article.Authors: Shufian A.; Al Fatemi R.; Daiyan F.; Khan M.; Ashiquzzaman M.; Fattah S.
Article.Abstract: Modern smart grids increasingly rely on renewable generation, decentralized control, communication-dependent monitoring, and data-driven decision-making, making reliable stability assessment challenging under imperfect and potentially manipulated measurements. This paper proposes HARSE-SG (Hybrid Adversarially Robust Stacking Ensemble for Smart Grid Stability Assessment), a leakage-free, group-aware, and explainable hybrid stacking framework for binary smart-grid stability prediction. The framework excludes the target-derived stability index stab, applies group-aware partitioning to related augmented observations, and combines Random Forest, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and CatBoost through a Logistic Regression meta-learner using leakage-free out-of-fold predictions. Robustness is evaluated under Gaussian sensor noise, transferable untargeted FGSM, BIM, and PGD attacks, physically constrained false data injection, and missing delay-sensor conditions. SHAP and LIME are further used to examine global and local decision behavior, while explanation consistency is quantified across heterogeneous base learners. Under leakage-free testing, HARSE-SG achieves 97.10% accuracy, 97.73% F1-score, 99.69% ROC-AUC, and 93.74% MCC. Statistical analysis showed that HARSE-SG improved the F1-score over XGBoost by 0.0032, corresponding to a 0.3275% relative improvement, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.0013, 0.0052] and p = 0.001. McNemar’s test also indicated a significant difference in paired classification errors ( p = 0.0016). These results suggest a statistically significant but practically modest improvement over XGBoost. Additional analyses examine attack effectiveness, grouping sensitivity, error concentration near the stability boundary, repeated-seed variability, and adversarial-retraining performance. The results highlight the importance of leakage-controlled validation and multi-condition evaluation for stability prediction within the considered benchmark dataset.

Article.Title: Improved detection of email and SMS spam using a hybrid deep and shallow learning model
Article.Authors: Hadi A.; Mosleh M.; Mohebbi K.
Article.Abstract: This study addresses the critical challenge of detecting sophisticated spam in digital communications by developing an advanced hybrid machine learning framework. The primary objective is to enhance detection accuracy through the synergistic integration of traditional and deep learning approaches, thereby overcoming the limitations of existing single-method systems. Our methodology combines shallow linguistic features (BoW, TF-IDF, lexical statistics) with deep contextual embeddings from a fine-tuned BERT model, processed through a novel Deep-Shallow Hybrid Model (DSHM) architecture. The system employs a multilayer perceptron for feature fusion and a Gradient Boosting meta-learner to ensemble predictions from five baseline classifiers (GBAM, RL-SPAM, HMAM, SSHM, MSSL) with DSHM outputs. The research uses the SMS Spam Collection v.1 dataset, containing 5,574 messages, to evaluate the proposed framework under a realistic imbalanced spam distribution. Data collection followed standard preprocessing protocols, including tokenization, normalization, and stratified sampling to maintain dataset balance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid ensemble consistently outperforms the individual baseline models on the SMS Spam Collection v.1 dataset. The final ensemble achieves an accuracy of 98.8%, a ROC-AUC of 0.993, and an F1-score of 0.956 for the spam class while maintaining a low false positive rate (0.0058). The proposed Deep-Shallow Hybrid Model (DSHM) also demonstrates strong standalone performance, confirming that combining shallow linguistic features with contextual BERT embeddings substantially improves spam detection robustness. These findings indicate that the proposed hybrid feature-fusion and ensemble-learning strategy provides an effective and scalable solution for real-world spam detection.

Article.Title: Perceived sustainable construction waste management performance in the AIoT context: an integrated TAM–TOE framework in Malaysia
Article.Authors: Abkar M.; Al-Shaeer H.; Amran M.; Harouache A.; Alhudaibi M.; Yussef A.; Abdirahman A.
Article.Abstract: Improving construction waste management has become a strategic imperative as the construction industry faces mounting pressure to reduce environmental impacts, improve resource efficiency, and meet sustainability targets. While Building Information Modeling (BIM), the Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have individually attracted considerable research attention, empirical understanding of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) as an integrated intelligent ecosystem for sustainable construction waste management remains limited. More importantly, the organisational and behavioural processes through which contextual conditions shape perceptions of AIoT-related technologies and perceived sustainable construction waste management performance remain inadequately explained. To address this gap, the present study examines perceived sustainable construction waste management performance in the AIoT context by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework. Drawing on survey data collected from 315 construction professionals in selected regions of Peninsular Malaysia, the proposed framework, Perceived Usefulness, demonstrated the largest path coefficient. Perceived sustainable construction waste management performance was evaluated using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that technological, organisational, and environmental factors were significantly and positively associated with the perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use of AIoT-related technologies. Among the examined relationships, perceived usefulness emerged as the strongest predictor of perceived sustainable construction waste management performance. In contrast, organisational factors were the only contextual factor to exert a significant direct association with perceived performance. Notably, technological and environmental factors did not directly associate with perceived performance; instead, significant indirect associations were observed through perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. The mediation results further confirmed the pivotal roles of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use in linking contextual conditions to perceived sustainable construction waste management performance. The findings highlight the importance of organisational readiness and user perceptions of AIoT-related technologies in shaping perceived sustainable construction waste management performance, offering practical direction for construction firms, technology providers, and policymakers pursuing sustainability-oriented digital transformation.

Article.Title: AIMPOD: an explainable artificial intelligence engine for agentic digital manufacturing
Article.Authors: Farooq M.; Ashraf W.; Anwar S.
Article.Abstract: Manufacturing systems increasingly generate heterogeneous, high-dimensional data, yet many existing artificial intelligence (AI) frameworks remain problem-specific, weakly interpretable, and insufficiently adapted to temporal dependence or material-specific variability. This limits the reliable deployment of AI for process optimization, quality prediction, and future autonomous decision-making in digital manufacturing. To address this gap, this study develops AIMPOD (Artificial Intelligence for Manufacturing Process Optimization and Design), an explainable AI framework that unifies data conditioning, intelligent preprocessing, multi-model learning, ensemble optimization, and interpretability within a single manufacturing-aware workflow.The framework is demonstrated on two distinct case studies: time-aware energy prediction in steel manufacturing and material-aware relative density prediction in laser-beam powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M). For temporally ordered industrial data, AIMPOD applies leakage-aware chronological validation, while for heterogeneous additive manufacturing data, it adopts material-split modelling to preserve alloy-specific process–structure relationships. Across the steel case, nonlinear and ensemble models achieve test \(R^2\) values between approximately 0.98 and 0.99, while the optimized ensemble reduces RMSE to about 0.63 kWh, improving on the best individual model by roughly 20–25%. In the PBF-LB/M case, pooled materials’ dataset modelling reaches about \(R^2_{\text {test}} \approx 0.76\) , whereas material-specific learning improves performance to about 0.87 for 18Ni300 and 0.78 for CuCrZr. The results demonstrate that AIMPOD enhances predictive robustness while preserving interpretability and providing an adaptive pathway toward explainable and agent-ready manufacturing intelligence.

Article.Title: Laser micro drilled glass semipermeable membranes for microfluidic blood oxygenators
Article.Authors: Blauvelt D.; Vainoris M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapy for patients with severe respiratory failure, but current technology remains limited by hemocompatibility challenges. We previously developed microfluidic oxygenator prototypes utilizing rigid, flat-plate silicon membranes with etched micropores to improve blood flow dynamics and hemocompatibility. However, fabrication of the micropores with deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) is costly and limits scalability. In this study, we report the development of a low-cost alternative semipermeable membrane composed of laser micro drilled borosilicate glass bonded to a thin, gas-permeable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer. Uniform arrays of through-pores (10 μm diameter, 20 μm pitch) were successfully fabricated through the full 400 μm thickness of the glass substrate, achieving near-vertical sidewalls and robust mechanical integrity. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed precise pore geometry and uniform distribution. Oxygen transfer performance was evaluated using a benchtop flow circuit under varying sweep gas pressures and water flow rates. Compared to prior PDMS-on-silicon membranes, the glass-based membranes demonstrated improved oxygen transfer (volume percent: 0.59 ± 0.13% [laser micro drilling] versus 0.28 ± 0.09% [DRIE]) due to elimination of non-porous support regions. Importantly, laser micro drilling reduced projected membrane fabrication costs by more than an order of magnitude (estimated membrane costs for a 4000 cm 2 neonatal oxygenator: $100,000 [DRIE] versus $8500 [laser micro drilling]), supporting the feasibility of scaling toward clinically relevant ECMO devices.

Article.Title: Low rifampicin and early signs of next-line drug resistances: findings from Madagascar’s 2023–24 nationwide drug resistance survey
Article.Authors: Ratovoson R.; Knoblauch A.; Grandjean Lapierre S.; Andriamamonjisoa H.; Rasoloarisata R.; Randrianarivony R.; Raherison M.; Byabajungu H.; Andriambololona H.; Rakotoson A.; Ramananjanahary T.; Randremanana R.; Randriamanana D.; Ngimbi R.; Klinkenberg E.; Harison M.; Rakotosamimanana N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Madagascar’s first national drug-resistance survey (2005-06) reported multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) in 0.2% of new and 3.4% of retreatment patients. To generate updated resistance estimates, a national cross-sectional, cluster-randomised survey was conducted across 36 diagnostic and treatment centres between April 2023 and April 2024. Bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB patients were enrolled and sputum specimens collected for drug-resistance testing, including culture, line-probe assay, Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing. Of 2,250 enrolled patients, 1,987 were new (88.3%) and 263 were previously treated (11.7%). Weighted prevalence of rifampicin resistance was 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7%) among new patients and 3.7% (95% CI 1.7–7.8%) among previously treated patients, reflecting stability since the 2005-06 survey. No pre-XDR or XDR-TB was detected. However, resistance to bedaquiline or linezolid was found in 2 of 40 new patients and 2 of 11 retreatment patients among rifampicin- and/or isoniazid-resistant isolates. Overall, the findings indicate a stable and contained RR-TB burden in Madagascar. Sustaining this outcome will require continued investment in case detection, drug-susceptibility testing, effective treatment, and routine resistance surveillance.

Article.Title: Non-identifiability of autochthonous chikungunya risk from surveillance data, Japan, 2011–2025
Article.Authors: Kutsuna S.
Article.Abstract: Japan notifies imported chikungunya but has never detected autochthonous chikungunya, although Aedes albopictus transmits both chikungunya and dengue and Japan experienced an autochthonous dengue outbreak in 2014. This absence is often read as reassuring. We reconstructed weekly, prefecture-level dengue, chikungunya, and Zika notifications from 1,357 national surveillance bulletins (1999–2026) and combined a temperature-suitability index with notification-based introduction proxies in a branching-process model with an explicit cluster-detection process. A descriptive temperature-suitability–notification overlap index was highest in metropolitan prefectures and in late summer; this geographic ordering was stable across prespecified proxy variants, population and per-capita proxies, and prefecture-specific seasonality, but was driven predominantly by the notification proxy, not temperature. Zero detected chikungunya clusters over approximately 14.9 surveillance-years placed a one-sided 95% upper bound of about 0.20/year on the detected-cluster rate; the data constrained only the product of introduction pressure and per-introduction detection probability, identifying neither. Chikungunya risk relative to dengue was therefore not identifiable from surveillance counts alone. Absolute probabilities and importation multipliers were calibrated to two events and are scenarios, not forecasts. The absence of detected autochthonous chikungunya does not, by itself, establish low underlying transmission risk when ascertainment is unknown; resolving this non-identification requires disease-specific diagnostic and case-level data.

Article.Title: Global stability of leaning-type steel box arch bridges: mechanistic insights and quantitative evaluation of key design parameters
Article.Authors: She Z.; Lin Q.; Luo X.; Yang J.; She Z.; Zhou J.
Article.Abstract: Leaning-type arch bridges are attractive for wide-deck urban applications, but their elastic global buckling mechanisms and parameter sensitivities remain insufficiently quantified. This study investigates a leaning-type steel box arch bridge using a three-dimensional finite element model validated against field-measured arch deflections and hanger forces. Linear elastic eigenvalue buckling analyses examine the structural system, rise-to-span ratio, arch stiffness, leaning-arch inclining angle, and transverse-bracing characteristics, together with the coupled effect of rise-to-span ratio and main-arch stiffness. Within the investigated bridge configuration, the integrated leaning-arch–transverse-bracing system increases the stability coefficient by approximately 71% relative to the unbraced main-arch system. A relatively favorable main-arch rise-to-span ratio of approximately 1/7–1/4.5 is identified. Main-arch bending stiffness has a pronounced influence, and its quantitative effect depends on the rise-to-span ratio. Variations in leaning-arch inclining angle produce relatively limited net changes, while further increases in bracing stiffness yield diminishing improvements. For a fixed bracing quantity, balanced spatial distribution over the arch span is more effective than concentrating bracings within a limited region. These findings provide a quantitative basis for comparative stability assessment and preliminary design of similar bridge systems.

Article.Title: Machine learning enabled predictive framework for real time estimation of optimal PID controller parameters in renewable microgrids
Article.Authors: Gupta P.; Singh M.; Ralhan S.
Article.Abstract: The ability to predict optimal PID controller gains in real time is essential for maintaining frequency stability, voltage regulation, and power balance in renewable-energy-based microgrids. This paper presents a machine learning (ML)-driven predictive framework for a hybrid microgrid comprising photovoltaic (PV), wind, and battery energy storage systems developed in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. Initially, the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm is employed to determine the optimal PID controller gains under varying operating conditions. GWO achieves a minimum fitness value of 0.50 within 16 iterations, outperforming Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA), which converge to 3.00 and 1.90 after 23 and 22 iterations, respectively. The GWO-tuned controller also reduces voltage overshoot to 3.2–4.6% with settling times of 0.10–0.13 s, compared with 14.2–28.9% overshoot obtained using PSO and GOA. Using the optimized controller gains, a dataset of 3000 operating samples was generated by systematically varying solar irradiance, temperature, wind speed, and load conditions.
