Five ensemble machine learning models, namely AdaBoost, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Histogram Gradient Boosting, and Gradient Boosting, were trained to directly predict the optimal PID gains. Among them, the Gradient Boosting model achieved the highest prediction accuracy, with an average RMSE of 0.0805 and an average R 2 of 0.9981, outperforming Histogram Gradient Boosting (RMSE = 0.0851, R 2 = 0.9979), Random Forest (RMSE = 0.1152, R 2 = 0.9957), Extra Trees (RMSE = 0.1405, R 2 = 0.9935), and AdaBoost (RMSE = 0.3390, R 2 = 0.9669). Model performance was further validated using actual-versus-predicted analysis, residual distribution, scatter plots, cumulative distribution function (CDF), and Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) testing, confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed framework. The proposed approach effectively replaces computationally intensive real-time optimization with fast and accurate machine learning-based prediction of PID controller parameters, providing an intelligent and scalable solution for renewable microgrid control and future smart grid applications.

Article.Title: Structural analysis of porous humeral stems in reverse shoulder arthroplasty based on finite element analysis
Article.Authors: John P.; Nageswaran S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA) commonly employs solid humeral stems, which can alter the pattern of physiological load transfer, leading to stress shielding and potentially affecting implant durability and fixation. Additively manufactured humeral stems with porous lattice can lower the rigidity and weight while maintaining mechanical safety. In these implants, the porosity level directly influences weight reduction, implant stress, mechanical loading of bone and bone-implant stability. This study examines the structural integrity of porous RSA humeral stems with varying porosity levels using finite element analysis (FEA). Six standard humeral Ti-6Al-4 V stems, a solid stem and five stems with bone-mimicking architecture with varying porosity levels were designed. The lattice stems were analysed using a three-dimensional (3D) model of a humerus obtained from an adult Indian computed tomography (CT) dataset. The bone-implant assemblies of the models were subjected to loading conditions that represent various shoulder movements. Stress shielding signal (SSS), micromotion, and fatigue were evaluated. These findings indicate that porosity alone is insufficient to predict the mechanical behaviour of porous RSA humeral stems as differences in Voronoi architecture and load transfer also influence structural performance.

Article.Title: Positive emotional responses while walking along a forest route compared with a city route: evidence from wearable facial electromyography
Article.Authors: Sato W.; Tokuchi N.; Yoshikawa S.
Article.Abstract: The potential of forests to induce positive emotions is attracting increasing attention. Previous studies have reported that walking in forests, compared with cities, is associated with more positive subjective experiences and physiological changes in the autonomic nervous system. However, because autonomic activity primarily reflects emotional arousal rather than valence, physiological evidence for positive emotional elicitation has remained limited. We hypothesized that facial electromyography (EMG) could address this gap. We used a wearable device to obtain EMG measurements from the corrugator supercilii and zygomaticus major while participants walked along a forest route or a city route. First-person video was recorded, and cued-recall procedures were used to obtain dynamic valence ratings. Participants reported more positive valence and showed reduced corrugator supercilii activity while walking along the forest route than the city route. Dynamic valence ratings were also associated with corrugator supercilii activity. These findings provide initial evidence of positive emotional responses, reflected in both subjective states and facial muscle activity, while walking along the forest route compared with the city route.

Article.Title: Automatic disfluency correction for a linguistically complex language
Article.Authors: M. R.; Pravin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automatic disfluency correction is an important task in natural language processing, particularly for morphologically rich and low-resource languages such as Tamil. Disfluencies including repetitions, interjections, prolongations, and part-word repetitions can negatively affect the performance of speech transcription systems, conversational agents, and downstream language processing applications. This paper presents a hybrid BERT-BiLSTM-Attention framework for token-level Tamil disfluency correction using binary KEEP and DELETE sequence labeling. The proposed model integrates contextual multilingual BERT embeddings with bidirectional sequential modeling and an attention mechanism for token-level disfluency correction. To address the limited availability of Tamil disfluency correction resources, a Synthetic Tamil Disfluent Text Corpus (STDTC) was developed using rule-based augmentation strategies. Experiments were conducted on both the synthetic STDTC dataset and a merged evaluation setting incorporating a small curated subset of SPRING_INX_Tamil_R2 data. The proposed framework achieved a token-level accuracy of 96.57% and a macro F1-score of 96.46% on the STDTC dataset, and 96.77% accuracy and 96.67% macro F1-score on the merged evaluation setting (STDTC + SPRING_INX_Tamil_R2). This merged setting reflects a primarily synthetic evaluation supplemented by a small number of real conversational examples. Additional analyses, including deletion-specific precision and recall, confusion matrices, exact sentence match analysis, and bootstrap confidence intervals, were performed to assess model performance across multiple disfluency categories. The results indicate that the proposed framework can model common Tamil disfluency patterns while maintaining consistent token-level correction performance. The study further suggests that combining contextual embeddings, sequential learning, and attention mechanisms is beneficial for low-resource Tamil disfluency correction tasks.

Article.Title: Comparative accuracy of dynamic navigation versus static surgical guides for dental implant placement: an in vitro assessment of free-end and non-free-end configurations
Article.Authors: De Sui C.; Mohamad Suhaimi F.; Roffie J.; Mohamad A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare the accuracy of dynamic navigation and static surgical guides for dental implant placement, with emphasis on free-end versus non-free-end configurations. An in vitro study was conducted using stereolithographic models of partially edentulous maxillary and mandibular arches. Sixty implant sites were virtually planned in 3Shape software and allocated to static surgical guides ( n = 30) or dynamic navigation ( n = 30), each stratified by support configuration (free-end vs. non-free-end) and jaw location (maxilla vs. mandible). Dentium Superline implants (4.0 × 10.0 mm) were placed using 3D-printed static guides or a dynamic navigation system. CBCT scans were acquired before and after placement, and angular (°), entry-point (mm) and apical (mm) deviations were calculated. Dynamic navigation was significantly more accurate than static guides overall (angular 1.95°±0.24° vs. 2.68°±0.54°; entry-point 1.51 ± 0.18 vs. 2.24 ± 0.51 mm; apical 1.75 ± 0.21 vs. 2.51 ± 0.52 mm; all p < 0.001). Pooled across modalities, free-end sites showed higher deviations than non-free-end sites for all three metrics ( p < 0.01); this difference was confined to static guides (angular 3.16° vs. 2.19°) and was not seen with dynamic navigation (1.89° vs. 2.00°). In free-end sites, dynamic navigation reduced angular, entry-point and apical deviations by 40.2% (1.89°±0.23° vs. 3.16°±0.24°), 46.1% (1.46 ± 0.17 vs. 2.71 ± 0.20 mm) and 43.0% (1.70 ± 0.20 vs. 2.98 ± 0.22 mm), respectively (all p < 0.001). In non-free-end sites the advantage was smaller (8.7–12.4%) but significant ( p = 0.032, 0.002 and 0.005). A significant guidance modality × support configuration interaction was found for all outcomes ( p < 0.001; partial η² 0.59–0.68). Jaw location had no significant effect ( p > 0.05). Within the limits of this single-material in vitro model, dynamic navigation was more accurate than static surgical guides, with the largest advantage (40–46% improvement) in free-end sites where guide support is compromised. Dynamic navigation may therefore be preferable for distal extension cases, pending clinical validation.

Article.Title: Real-world effectiveness and tolerability of fixed dose netarsudil/latanoprost in the management of patients with uncontrolled glaucoma
Article.Authors: Siligato A.; Nardi C.; Bochicchio S.; Dipinto A.; Cozzi M.; Staurenghi G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This prospective cohort study evaluates the real-world effectiveness and tolerability of the fixed-dose combination of Netarsudil 0.02%/Latanoprost 0.005% in patients with uncontrolled glaucoma. Following sample size determination, patients with any type of uncontrolled glaucoma were consecutively enrolled. Seventy-one eyes from forty patients (mean age 74.7 ± 10.0 years) were included. The median baseline IOP was 18.00 mmHg [IQR: 10], with an average of 2.76 ± 1.10 glaucoma medications. A statistically significant reduction in IOP was observed at each follow-up: 14.00 mmHg [IQR: 6.50] at 1 month ( p < 0.001), 13.00 mmHg [IQR: 8] at 3 months ( p < 0.001), and 13.50 mmHg [IQR: 7.75] at 6 months ( p < 0.001). Subgroup analysis revealed significant IOP reductions in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and normal-tension glaucoma (NTG). Adverse events were reported in 52.1% of treated eyes, most commonly worsening of conjunctival hyperemia (36.6%). Treatment discontinuation due to adverse events and inadequate IOP control occurred in 15.5% of eyes, respectively. Overall, the Netarsudil 0.02%/Latanoprost 0.005% combination demonstrated meaningful IOP reduction and a manageable safety profile in a real-world clinical setting, even in patients receiving maximally tolerated medical therapy. These findings suggest it may offer an alternative for patients who are not candidates or unwilling for surgical intervention.

Article.Title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
Article.Authors: Werneburg I.; Kästle B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. Diversifications correspond with two areas of speciation: the Australasian and Caribbean archipelagos. Our results show a rather variable body size in the more rootward taxa, whereas an erratic increase of body size by 30% is noticed in a more advanced section of the genus tree, a radiation likely corresponding to a colder climate after the Mio-Pliocene border. Body size is correlated to the change of several morphological characters, but—unexpectedly—no correlation could be found with the reported living depths of the species. This suggests that physiological adaptation to large size appeared only once, at the origin of the genus, and a great environmental plasticity is present within the group.

Article.Title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
Article.Authors: Frontalini F.; Greco M.; Casadei N.; Angeles I.; Montresor M.; Martins M.; Pawlowski J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. Using benthic foraminifera from a Mediterranean CO 2 vent system, we identify an empirically derived pH threshold beyond which community structure and function shift markedly. Applying this threshold to end-of-century projections under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway SSP5-8.5 reveals that most western Mediterranean coastal zones will exceed critical acidification levels by 2090–2100. These results highlight the susceptibility of the Mediterranean coastal ecosystems to OA under high-emission scenarios, underscoring the risk of widespread biodiversity loss and impaired ecosystem functioning. Our approach provides a trait-based framework for forecasting ecosystem responses to OA and informing adaptation strategies in climate-sensitive marine regions.

Article.Title: Blockchain-enabled IoT security: a multi-layered framework for smart contract vulnerability detection and optimization
Article.Authors: Arora A.; Aggarwal M.
Article.Abstract: The exponential expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) applications has raised critical issues about data security, integrity, and scalability, especially in IoT systems based on a centralized architecture. The decentralized and immutable nature of blockchain technology provides a compelling alternative; but smart contract (SC) security and efficiency is still a critical issue. This research presents a layered, pipeline-based approach for secure and efficient deployment of SCs, with IoT and decentralized storage. The framework integrates real-time IoT data collection, secure data pre-processing, SCs development, SCs vulnerability detection and gas optimization into a single system. To overcome storage constraints, the approach uses InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for off-chain data storage, with on-chain hashes ensuring data integrity. The framework uses a multi-tool analysis to identify SC vulnerabilities and deploy and test them on the Sepolia Testnet. In addition to this, the framework adopts statistical validation methods such as Paired t-test (P–t Test), Kruskal–Wallis test(K-W Test) and Wilcoxon signed-rank test (WS-R Test) to assess the performance improvement and validate the effectiveness of the optimization approaches. Simulation-based testing results reveal that the proposed framework leads to lower gas usage, faster execution, and better security compared to conventional methods. The findings show that the proposed framework offers a scalable, secure, and efficient approach to design real-time IoT-based SC systems, which can be applied to environmental monitoring and smart city systems.

Article.Title: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for resilient recovery of electric–gas coupled energy systems under extreme disasters
Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Yang C.; He J.
Article.Abstract: Under extreme disasters, there are still significant gaps in the cascading failure propagation and collaborative recovery decision-making of electric-gas coupled integrated energy systems, making it difficult to form effective dynamic recovery paths under high uncertainty conditions. This paper constructs a Markov decision process environment under disaster conditions, setting multi-dimensional state variables including node fault states, pressure and voltage distribution, and recovery resource constraints. It employs Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MA-DRL) combined with a centralized training and distributed execution architecture. Policy coordination between the power grid subsystem and the gas grid subsystem is achieved through joint action value evaluation and local policy execution. A cross-round reward structure is designed to cover factors such as energy availability, recovery speed, and recovery stability. A curriculum learning mechanism is introduced to address the exploration failure and reward signal sparsity that arise when policies are directly trained under high-disturbance conditions: by organizing training scenarios in order of ascending disaster intensity, the policy first acquires stable recovery behavior in low-disturbance environments and progressively transfers this structure to extreme disturbance conditions, yielding accelerated convergence and robust generalization across disaster scenarios. Delay effect modeling is incorporated to propagate the long-term consequences of repair decisions back to the learning signal. Experimental results show that, under disaster intensity level IV, the proposed MA-DRL collaborative recovery strategy achieves a system energy availability rate of 82.4% within 0–3 h post-disaster; during the post-disaster collaborative recovery process, the overall recovery completion time is 5.7 h, and the proportion of stable operation after recovery reaches 93.1%. This research demonstrates the effective path and technological potential of deep reinforcement learning in enhancing the resilience of coupled energy systems.

Article.Title: An integrated framework for explainable and uncertainty-aware software defect prediction with adaptive risk scoring and multi-task deep residual learning
Article.Authors: Varma M.; Giri M.
Article.Abstract: Software defect prediction (SDP) is a challenging problem in SQA, the majority of the approaches that have been proposed so far focus on this problem as a binary classification problem, without taking into account the risk associated with each defective module. This paper introduces an integrated framework of adaptive risk scoring, Multi-Task deep residual learning with gated feature attention, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and SHAP-based explainability that is applied simultaneously towards both defect detection and risk classification. This is due to a data-d Single-Task riven parameter λ optimized via a Spearman correlation used to calculate the risk score and SMOTETomek resampling and focal loss to address severe class imbalance. A defect detection ROC-AUC of 0.9581, F1-score of 0.5928, and recall of 0.7616 is achieved by the proposed model on the pc5 dataset; while a macro F1-score of 0.98 and accuracy of 0.99 are achieved by the proposed model on the risk classification task, in which the three risk classes are model-derived prioritisation tiers rather than independently validated defect-severity labels. Monte Carlo Dropout also identifies 25.2% of modules as high uncertainty candidates for manual review, while feature attribution shows that cyclomatic density, comment percentage and global data density are the most important features affecting defect risk.

Article.Title: HDTBO_DMN: a secure IoT-enabled healthcare intrusion detection system for enhanced communication
Article.Authors: Yempally S.; Singh S.; Sarveshwaran V.
Article.Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has gained significant prominence in recent years, with increasing research efforts directed toward its diverse applications, especially within the medical domain. Even though, such IoT components make people’s activities simpler, such networks are exposed to diverse security attacks. Generally, Machine Learning (ML) algorithms are largely utilized in Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) for identifying and classifying threats. Conventional IDSs have some constraints, like a poor detection rate and low scalability. Consequently, the design of a robust IDS is necessary to protect the network from security threats while maintaining its integrity, privacy, and overall reliability. In this work, an effective IDS model is designed by employing a devised Hybrid Driving Training Based Optimization (HDTBO)-based Deep Maxout Network (DMN) for IoT-enabled healthcare and secure communication. This model comprises two phases that include the authentication and communication phase. The authentication phase involves initialization, registration, key generation, login, authentication, data protection, authorization, data sharing, and access control procedures, followed by data protection, where Rider Horse Herd Optimization (RHHO) is employed to generate the secret key. The input log data in the communication phase is initially processed by handling missing values, applying Min–Max normalization, and performing SMOTE-based data augmentation to alleviate the class imbalance problem. The resulting processed data is then used for feature fusion using Levenshtein distance with a Deep Neural Network (DNN), which is performed from the recorded log data. Then, intrusion detection is done by a DMN, which is trained by the proposed HDTBO. The HDTBO integrates both Hybrid Leader Based Optimization and Driving Training Based Optimization (DTBO). The devised HDTBO_DMN outperformed other traditional methods by performance metrics, such as attack detection rate, F1-score and False Positive Rate (FPR), precision, accuracy, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), with the values of 0.91, 0.918, 0.071, 0.927, 0.918, and 0.839, respectively.

Article.Title: Enhanced macroscopic model for simulating dynamic behavior of elastomeric bearings including axial shortening effects
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Guo Z.; Bao Y.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Elastomeric bearings undergo axial shortening as horizontal displacement increases. Existing studies predominantly focus on the static mechanical characteristics of bearings induced by axial shortening, while investigations concerning axial-shortening-effects on dynamic bearing responses remain insufficient. Two key limitations exist in current research: conventional macroscopic models cannot capture axial shortening behaviors of bearings under dynamic loading, and few studies distinguish the individual-bearing axial shortening responses from the vertical coupling interactions among multiple bearings within an isolation system. To address these gaps, this study incorporates a displacement-dependent variable stiffness function into the vertical spring of a baseline macroscopic model, developing an enhanced macroscopic model that enables the simulation of dynamic axial-shortening-effects on elastomeric bearings. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed model are validated against dynamic test data under extreme horizontal excitations. Comprehensive parametric analyses are further conducted based on the validated model. The main conclusions are drawn as follows: (1) Differential axial shortening among bearings generates vertical coupling interactions within the isolation system, leading to distinct dynamic mechanical behaviors of bearings compared with their quasi-static performance; (2) Axial shortening triggers vertical excitation of bearings, resulting in evident fluctuations in axial load and hysteretic responses; (3) Such axial-shortening-induced vertical excitation can be effectively mitigated by increasing the vertical stiffness and damping of elastomeric bearings.

Article.Title: Large language models reveal a systematic preference in clinical immunotherapy guidelines: a multi-model comparative analysis
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Lin A.; Shen J.; Xu W.; Ying H.; Jiang A.; Qi C.; Gan W.; Zhu L.; Mou W.; Zeng D.; Tang B.; Xiao M.; Chu G.; Peng S.; Wong H.; Zhang L.; Zhang H.; Deng X.; Cao X.; Chen W.; Liu X.; Zeng Q.; Wang X.; Cheng Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clinical guidelines may sometimes contain divergent treatment recommendations, creating uncertainty in therapeutic decision-making. To evaluate the performance of four large language models (LLMs) (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Deepseek-V3) in analyzing discrepancies between the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) guidelines. ICI-related guidelines published by ASCO and NCCN were collected, divergent recommendations were extracted and input into four LLMs for statistical analysis, and each model’s responses were independently evaluated by three oncology experts using Likert scales (focusing on accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, and potential harm). All models demonstrated a significant preference for NCCN. Gemini 1.5 Pro exhibited extreme rigidity (100% selection of NCCN). The remaining models showed moderate degrees of a systematic preference: Claude 3.7 Sonnet(73.7%) , Deepseek-V3(72.0%), and GPT-4o(71.3%) . Further stratification revealed a relative preference for ASCO guidelines under more conservative treatment protocols. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) demonstrates persistent and systematic preference in conflicting guideline interpretation, with an overall inclination toward NCCN guidelines, potentially related to training corpus distribution and differences in guideline articulation. These findings suggest the need to establish transparent and regulatory-compliant AI decision-making frameworks.

Article.Title: Fault sealing capacity of mudstone caprocks under contrasting brittle–ductile regimes
Article.Authors: Yan S.; Yang H.; Guan Y.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Evaluating the vertical sealing capacity of faulted mudstone caprocks is critical for assessing fluid preservation and trap integrity. However, common quantitative indices, such as hydrocarbon fault-connection thickness (Hfc) and Shale Smear Factor (SSF), often fail to provide reliable sealing thresholds within the brittle–ductile transition zone. To address this, we propose an integrated quantitative framework combining rock mechanical behavior with fault-zone compositional variations. We take the Central Structural Belt of the Xihu Sag (East China Sea Basin) as a case study. Using an integrated stress characterization based on core and logging data, calibrated with core measurements, we optimize log-derived predictions of rock brittle–ductile behavior and quantitatively define critical brittle–ductile transition depths of 3150 m and 8250 m. Subsequently, we incorporate the Shale Gouge Ratio (SGR) into an enhanced Fault-Throw-Knipe-Diagram (FKTD) to continuously quantify vertical shale content along fault planes. FKTD analysis effectively eliminates the threshold ambiguity inherent in isolated Hfc and SSF evaluations. Furthermore, it reveals a depth-controlled fluid flow system: open faults in structural lows serve as vertical fluid conduits, while sealed caprocks in shallower structural highs prevent upward migration. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that the clay content threshold required for effective fault sealing increases systematically with regional tectonic intensity. These findings establish a robust, geomechanically constrained predictive model for fault seal evaluation, providing new insights for deep petroleum exploration and secure CO2 geological storage in tectonically active basins worldwide.

Article.Title: Bio-waste-derived chicken feather carbon-integrated ZnGa2O4 nanocomposites for asymmetric supercapacitor application
Article.Authors: Selvam G.; Ramakrishnan P.; Ramesh S.; Govindarajan D.; Rajendran R.; Mani N.; Dheivasigamani T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The pursuit of next-generation energy storage systems necessitates the development of advanced electrode materials that offer both high charge storage capacity and outstanding cycling stability to meet the increasing need for advanced energy storage devices. Engineering hybrid nanostructures that combine conductivity, porosity, and electrochemical activity offers a promising pathway to elevate supercapacitor performance. This study reports the hydrothermal synthesis of ZnGa 2 O 4 /chicken feather carbon (ZGO/CFC) composites using varying amounts of chicken feather-derived carbon (40, 65, and 100 mg) as a sustainable carbon source. Comprehensive characterization techniques including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman Spectroscopy, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analyses confirm the formation of a well-crystallized cubic ZnGa 2 O 4 structure, along with its morphological characteristics, elemental composition, and porosity. Electrochemical characterization reveal that the ZnGa 2 O 4 /100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode exhibits the highest specific capacitance of about 642.0 F g − 1 at 1 A g − 1 surpassing its counterparts. Asymmetric supercapacitor fabricated from ZnGa 2 O 4 /100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode shows specific capacitance of 67.33 F g − 1 with energy and power densities of about 21.04 Wh kg − 1 ,750 W kg − 1 respectively. In addition, it achieves a capacitive retention rate of about 94.0% and coulombic efficiency of about 95.0% which demands the integration of metal oxides with low-cost, renewable carbon materials as an effective strategy for advancing the performance of supercapacitors. The optimized ZGO/CFC composites demonstrate promising prospects for high-performance supercapacitor applications, facilitating the development for green energy storage solutions.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of linear and nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques for breast cancer diagnosis
Article.Authors: Labdaoui A.; Mekki S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dimensionality reduction plays a crucial role in improving the interpretability and structural visualization of machine learning configurations applied to high-dimensional biomedical data. This study presents an exploratory comparative evaluation of four widely used techniques: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Self-Organizing Maps (SOM), mapping cytological breast cancer features derived from fine-needle aspirate (FNA) measurements in the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset. Each method was assessed according to its ability to preserve underlying geometric data distribution and enhance class separability margins within the reduced two-dimensional feature spaces. Experimental results demonstrate that the supervised projection layout of LDA achieves the highest class-separability, yielding an out-of-fold logistic-regression proxy accuracy of 98.83% and a Silhouette Score of 0.6776. We note that this accuracy figure is computed after fitting each projection on the full dataset (see Section 5.1) and should therefore be interpreted as a measure of class-consistent latent geometry rather than a leakage-free estimate of clinical predictive performance. PCA provides a stable representation of global data variance but exhibits overlapping boundaries across categories. t-SNE effectively captures local manifold structure to produce informative cluster visualizations; however, its resulting classification proxy score remains lower (95.32%). In contrast, SOM shows weaker topological grouping performance, reflecting the challenges of accommodating complex cytological distributions within rigid low-dimensional grids. Statistical validation using paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirms that the observed structural differences among the evaluated low-dimensional layouts are statistically significant across validation partitions. Rather than asserting clinical predictive readiness, these findings provide critical architectural insights into selecting appropriate dimensionality reduction techniques for the exploratory characterization of cytological features, establishing an essential geometric baseline for biomedical feature space mapping.

Article.Title: Dynamic pixel-wise hybrid multi-chaotic image encryption with DCT steganography and CNN-assisted restoration
Article.Authors: Makram A.; Saber A.; Hamdi A.; Elsayed R.; Awad W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Image encryption has become an essential requirement for protecting sensitive visual information, particularly in medical imaging, military communications, cloud storage, and multimedia transmission systems, where unauthorized access and cyberattacks continue to increase rapidly. However, many existing chaos-based image cryptosystems still suffer from several limitations, including weak randomness, insufficient resistance against statistical and differential attacks, fixed chaotic initial conditions, high computational complexity, and limited robustness against image-processing attacks such as filtering and histogram equalization. In addition, several conventional approaches focus solely on encryption without integrating secure steganographic protection mechanisms. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel hybrid multi-chaotic image cryptosystem combined with DCT-based steganography for secure image encryption and concealment. The proposed framework employs cosine-square chaotic modulation integrated with logistic, cubic, tent, Bernoulli, and quadratic chaotic maps to generate highly dynamic pixel-wise encryption keys with extreme sensitivity to initial conditions. Unlike traditional static chaotic systems, the proposed method generates distinct chaotic key streams for every image pixel according to the image dimensions, significantly improving randomness, diffusion, and unpredictability. Furthermore, the encrypted image is hidden inside a cover image using the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), providing an additional security layer against visual and statistical attacks. To improve the quality of the reconstructed images after decryption, adaptive enhancement and denoising stages using Gaussian filtering, median filtering, histogram equalization, and CNN-assisted restoration are incorporated. Extensive experimental and security analyses demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed cryptosystem. The obtained results achieved high entropy values reaching 7.99, NPCR values up to 99.99%, UACI values exceeding 33%, and correlation coefficients approaching zero, confirming excellent statistical randomness and strong resistance against differential attacks. Moreover, the generated chaotic sequences successfully passed the NIST statistical randomness tests and Chi-square analysis, demonstrating superior cryptographic randomness characteristics. Additional security evaluations including chosen-plaintext attacks, known-plaintext attacks, filtering attacks, histogram equalization attacks, Gaussian noise attacks, and cropping attacks further verified the robustness and stability of the proposed framework. Comparative analyses with several recent state-of-the-art encryption techniques confirmed that the proposed method provides enhanced security performance, improved attack resistance, high key sensitivity, and efficient computational complexity, making it highly suitable for secure real-time image communication applications.

Article.Title: Design of a soft-switched interleaved high step-up non-isolated DC-DC converter for renewable energy sources integration
Article.Authors: Falahi F.; Babaei E.; Alizadeh D.; Sabahi M.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces an interleaved high step-up non-isolated DC-DC converter which incorporates a soft-switching mechanism. The proposed design ensures that all the switches and diodes operate under soft-switching conditions, specifically operating with both zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS) during transitions. These favorable switching conditions are achieved using a low number of additional components namely, a single auxiliary resonant circuit and one auxiliary inductor without requiring any extra switches. As a result, switching losses are significantly reduced or effectively eliminated. This leads to enhanced performance and higher efficiency, particularly when operating at high switching frequencies. Furthermore, the converter is adaptable for multi-phase interleaved configurations, retaining all the advantages of the single-phase design. The paper provides a thorough theoretical analysis of the proposed structure. To validate the theoretical findings, a prototype was developed demonstrating a conversion from 40 V input to 300 V output with an efficiency of 94.42%.

Article.Title: Mobility-aware service migration and two-timescale task offloading for distributed edge computing in open RAN
Article.Authors: Mohajer A.; Mirzaei A.; Nouri-Moghaddam B.; Ghaffari A.; Fernando X.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a mobility-aware two-timescale orchestration framework for distributed edge computing in Open Radio Access Networks, where user mobility, handover events, service migration, task offloading, and radio–compute allocation are jointly considered. The framework exploits the functional separation between the Non-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller (Non-RT RIC) and Near-Real-Time RIC to coordinate decisions over different temporal scales. At the slower timescale, the Non-RT RIC analyzes historical traffic, regional load, and predicted mobility flows to generate service-placement guidance, resource envelopes, and migration-aware control parameters. At the faster timescale, a Near-RT RIC xApp performs handover-coupled task offloading, service migration, bandwidth allocation, and edge-computing assignment using instantaneous channel, queue, mobility, and resource states. A graph-contextual representation is further employed to capture neighboring-region congestion, available capacity, and mobility transitions, enabling scalable inter-region coordination. The resulting stochastic optimization formulation incorporates communication, computation, and migration delays together with resource, queue-stability, and service-continuity constraints. A hybrid actor–critic learning mechanism with centralized training and decentralized execution is adopted to obtain feasible mobility-aware orchestration policies for dynamic multi-service Open RAN edge environments.

Article.Title: Maternal immune activation disrupts maternal and offspring lipid signalling in association with reduced PPARα-FGF21 expression
Article.Authors: Murru E.; Santoni M.; Manca C.; Carta G.; Cabboi M.; Mastio A.; Banni S.; Pistis M.
Article.Abstract: Maternal immune activation (MIA) during gestation increases neurodevelopmental disorder risk, but its metabolic mechanisms remain unclear. Given the role of lipid metabolism in fetal brain development and endocannabinoid signaling, we investigated whether MIA is associated with alteration in maternal and offspring lipid pathways and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα)-related signaling. Pregnant rats received a single i.v. injection of the viral mimetic polyinosinic: polycytidylic acid [poly (I: C)] at gestational day 15. Lipidomic and gene-expression analyses were conducted in maternal, fetal, and adolescent male and female offspring tissues to assess fatty acid composition, desaturase activity, de novo lipogenesis (DNL), and N -acylethanolamines (NAE) signaling. MIA induced maternal weight loss, and was associated with lower hepatic DNL and Δ5/Δ6-desaturase activities, and decreased Fasn , Pparα , and Fgf21 expression, suggesting alterated PPARα-FGF21 signaling. These alterations were accompanied by reduced hepatic total NAE, including N -oleoylethanolamine (OEA), N -palmitoleoylethanolamine (POEA) and N -docosahexaenoylethanolamine (DHAEA), and hippocampal DHAEA. Fetal tissues showed diminished DHAEA and DNL indices. In adolescence, males displayed cortical decreases in NAE and 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol (2-AG), whereas females exhibited hepatic lipid accumulation but preserved cortical lipid signaling. These findings suggest that altered PPARα-related lipid signaling may contribute to the association between prenatal inflammation and metabolic alterations. Future studies should determine whether targeted nutritional activation of PPARα could mitigate MIA-induced alterations.

Article.Title: Shear wave velocity prediction from minimal well logs using neighborhood component analysis—guided XGBoost in carbonate reservoirs
Article.Authors: Ghimatgar H.; Khosravi R.; Rahimizadeh R.; Dadvar S.; Chaghazardi A.; Ranjbar A.
Article.Abstract: Shear wave velocity (Vₛ) is a critical parameter for petroleum geomechanics and reservoir engineering. Direct measurement via logging tools is often restricted due to economic and technical constraints, necessitating reliable indirect prediction methods. Traditional empirical correlations are lithology-dependent and lack generalization, while many machine learning (ML) approaches suffer from overfitting and limited interpretability due to suboptimal feature selection. This study introduces an interpretable computational framework integrating Neighborhood Component Analysis (NCA) with ML algorithms for accurate Vₛ estimation. Six ML models: XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Linear Regression, were evaluated using well-log data from a carbonate reservoir. The NCA-XGBoost model achieved superior accuracy (R 2 = 0.946, RMSE = 0.068 km/s), significantly outperforming the best empirical correlation (Castagna and Backus, R 2 = 0.698, RMSE = 0.075 km/s), representing an approximately 35% improvement in R 2 and a 10% reduction in RMSE. NCA identified compressional wave transit time (DTCO) as the dominant predictor, with a single log achieving near-optimal accuracy. This approach reduces dimensionality, mitigates overfitting, and enhances model transparency by identifying the dominant physical controls on Vₛ and quantifying their relative importance. The proposed framework offers a cost-effective, reliable alternative for Vₛ prediction in wells lacking direct measurements, with practical implications for wellbore stability analysis, hydraulic fracturing design, and seismic interpretation.

Article.Title: QGLH-Net: quality-guided local-global hierarchical deep learning framework for oral disease classification using intraoral images
Article.Authors: ul Mava J.; Ashraf M.; Alourani A.; Shinan K.; Alhazmi H.; Ilyas I.
Article.Abstract: Dental diseases are a widespread yet under-recognized health problem worldwide, and oral health problems are associated with several systemic conditions including diabetes, cardiovascular disease and depression. Early diagnosis is crucial but depends on access to the trained dental professionals, which is difficult in underserved and resource-limited communities. This study proposes QGLH-Net (Quality-Guided Local-Global Hierarchical Network), a dual-stream deep learning framework that classifies oral diseases at six classes (gingivitis, caries, ulcer, calculus, tooth discoloration and hypodontia) from intraoral images while addressing the challenges of image quality, class imbalance and spatially localized lesion features. Experiments were conducted on publicly available Kaggle Oral Diseases dataset. Following quality filtering and deduplication, 3,076 images were retained and stratified into 2,153 training, 461 validation, and 462 test images. QGLH-Net framework introduces a dual-stream design combining ResNet-50 global branch selected because it achieved the highest macro-F1 among the tuned baselines, while for local branch a lightweight ResNet-18 is used operating on Grad-CAM-guided regions. Unlike post-hoc Grad-CAM visualization approaches, QGLH-Net uses Grad-CAM derived information to generate a complementary local input stream and integrate it with quality-aware curriculum and hierarchical supervision. Hierarchical supervision jointly optimizes six fine-grained disease classes and three coarse anatomical categories. Training further incorporates a two-stage quality-guided curriculum and a dynamic class-balanced focal loss in which inverse-frequency class weights are adapted using class-specific false-negative and false-positive rates, together with supervised contrastive learning. QGLH-Net achieved a best observed accuracy of 98.27% and macro F1-score of 0.9691, has a per-class F1-score ≥ 0.955. Paired statistical evaluation against the strongest ResNet-50 baseline yielded p = 0.152 for accuracy and p = 0.441 for macro-F1; therefore, the observed improvements are interpreted as performance gains rather than statistically confirmed superiority. Minority-class recall estimates showed wider 95% confidence intervals, particularly for caries (0.759–0.979) and tooth discoloration (0.750–0.978), reflecting their limited test support. End-to-end inference required approximately 117.1 ms per image (~ 8.5 images per second) on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. Beyond classification, we also explored how model outputs could be made more directly usable in a clinical workflow. As an additional proof-of-concept element, AI-assisted reporting module built with CrewAI and Google’s Gemini-1.5 Flash was implemented as a post-classification interface; it does not contribute to reported classification performance and has not undergone formal clinician-based evaluation. QGLH-Net is presented as an explainable screening and decision-support oral disease classification framework for intraoral-image assessment rather than an autonomous diagnostic system, with further clinical validation required before deployment.

Article.Title: CNN-integrated deep learning optimization of SAG-derived Smoothened agonists relevant to holoprosencephaly
Article.Authors: Sahin S.; Ali N.
Article.Abstract: Holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a severe developmental disorder associated with impaired Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling, and no targeted pharmacotherapy is currently available to correct pathway insufficiency. Smoothened (SMO), a central SHH pathway transducer, provides a rational target for optimizing SAG-derived agonists. This study applied an integrated deep learning-guided in silico workflow to generate and prioritize optimized SAG derivatives. A molecular design platform integrating three-dimensional convolutional neural networks, conditional variational autoencoders, and long short-term memory-based molecular generation was used to design SAG analogues, followed by docking, binding-site validation, ADMET/toxicity profiling, pharmacophore analysis, density functional theory calculations, 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations, PCA/DCCM analysis, and MMGBSA estimation. Among eleven derivatives, AI Derivative 7 was the highest ranked compound in the docking screen (-11.396 kcal/mol) compared with SAG (-10.855 kcal/mol), with the margin relative to SAG lying within the uncertainty of the scoring function, and it showed conserved key interactions with ARG400 and ASP577, and expanded hydrophobic and electrostatic contacts. It also showed improved predicted gastrointestinal absorption, reduced lipophilicity (log Po/w 4.32 vs 5.62), lower predicted acute toxicity (LD50 900 vs 200 mg/kg), and a marginally smaller HOMO–LUMO gap for the isolated ligand (approximately 4.06 vs 4.23 eV), which was not related to binding energetics. During simulation, AI Derivative 7 reached a stable conformational state after ~ 200–250 ns with reduced fluctuations and sustained hydrogen bonding. MMGBSA gave a total binding energy of -46.56 kcal/mol for AI Derivative 7 and -46.97 kcal/mol for SAG, a difference of 0.42 kcal/mol that was not statistically distinguishable across the ten sampled snapshots (95% CI -3.96 to + 4.80 kcal/mol, p = 0.84). AI Derivative 7 showed a substantially stronger electrostatic contribution (-44.65 vs -20.75 kcal/mol), but this was offset by a correspondingly larger desolation penalty (+ 66.83 vs + 44.76 kcal/mol), so no net energetic advantage over SAG was obtained. These computational findings identify AI Derivative 7 as a prioritized SMO-targeted candidate requiring experimental validation.

Article.Title: Correction: Interplay of electron–phonon coupling, dissipative phonon bath, and electron–electron interaction in a triangular quantum-dot trimer
Article.Authors: Sharma H.
Article.Abstract: The original version of this Article contained an error in Equation 11. The error occurred during the assembly of the paper.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of regional resilience in China: evidence from provincial panel data using Spearman-CRITIC and XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Regional resilience is closely related to sustainable development because it reflects the capacity of a region to maintain stable economic, social, ecological, and infrastructural functions under long-term transformation. Based on provincial panel data for China from 2007 to 2024, this study constructs a regional resilience evaluation system covering economic resilience, social development resilience, ecological and environmental resilience, and infrastructure resilience. A Spearman-CRITIC model is used to calculate the resilience index, while cold–hot spot analysis and kernel density estimation are applied to examine spatial patterns and distributional dynamics. An XGBoost-CatBoost hybrid model and SHAP approach are further used to identify the explanatory contribution of potential influencing factors. The results show that China’s provincial resilience generally improved during the study period, although regional differences remained evident. Hot spots were mainly concentrated in eastern coastal and some central-eastern provinces, while cold spots appeared intermittently in western and southwestern areas. The SHAP results indicate that income level, private economic vitality, and urbanization rate make relatively large contributions to model prediction, with clear regional heterogeneity. Robustness tests using alternative weighting methods support the stability of the main explanatory patterns. These findings provide empirical evidence for understanding regional resilience improvement under sustainable development-oriented governance.

Article.Title: Association of first-24-hour hypernatremia and hyperkalemia co-occurrence with 30-day mortality in critically ill adults: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Chang W.; Yu K.; Kuo L.; Lee C.; Yang T.
Article.Abstract: First-24-hour hypernatremia–hyperkalemia co-occurrence may mark severe illness, but its incremental prognostic value is uncertain. We analyzed 13,383 adult ICU admissions (11,942 patients) in Taiwan during 2018–2020. Peak sodium > 145 and potassium > 5.5 mmol/L defined four phenotypes; peaks need not be simultaneous. This prognostic association analysis used information accumulated during the first ICU day. Patient-clustered logistic regression compared total APACHE II adjustment with complementary adjustment excluding its sodium/potassium points. Twenty repeated patient-grouped five-fold cross-validations assessed discrimination. Thirty-day mortality was 12.2%, 33.7%, 32.7%, and 74.4% in the neither ( n = 12,097), hypernatremia-only ( n = 841), hyperkalemia-only ( n = 367), and co-occurrence ( n = 78) groups. With total APACHE II, the co-occurrence odds ratio was 1.90 (95% CI 1.07–3.39), global phenotype P = 0.094, and mean AUC change 0.00007. With component-excluded adjustment, the corresponding odds ratio was 2.70 (1.53–4.75), global P = 0.002, and mean AUC change 0.00037. Additional sensitivity analyses examined outcome availability, in-hospital mortality, sparse data, and alternative thresholds. Outcome missingness and unavailable measurement/death timing limit interpretation. Co-occurrence characterized a small high-risk subgroup, but incremental discrimination was negligible; causality and clinical predictive utility were not established.

Article.Title: Occupancy-driven attenuation in radiation-sensitive chromatin domains as a statistical-mechanical model of the overkill effect and RBE maximum
Article.Authors: Rezaee L.
Article.Abstract: The reduction in biological effectiveness at high linear energy transfer (LET), commonly referred to as the overkill effect, remains an active area of investigation in high-LET radiobiology. Here, we present a statistical-mechanical framework in which attenuation emerges from the progressive occupancy of a finite population of radiation-sensitive chromatin domains. An effective free-energy formalism is used to describe the equilibrium occupancy state, yielding an LET-dependent occupancy fraction and an attenuation function representing the fraction of chromatin domains remaining available for the formation of additional biologically independent lethal events. The model predicts a continuous occupancy transition accompanied by a fluctuation maximum, identifying a characteristic LET range in which occupancy effects become most pronounced. When combined with a previously published LET-dependent damage-production model for carbon-ion irradiation of V79 cells, the framework predicts a maximum in lethal-lesion yield followed by a decline despite continued increases in damage production. The qualitative comparison of the RBE data in published works reveals the typical pattern of growth, peak value, and decline of the biological effectiveness, although the predicted values of the RBE continue to be lower than the experimental ones. These results suggest that finite chromatin-domain occupancy may provide a possible physical interpretation of attenuation, the overkill effect, and the emergence of an RBE maximum.

Article.Title: Interplay among neural synchronization, excitability, variability, and sequentiality across time scales in rhythmic bursting
Article.Authors: Sanchez-Martin P.; Garrido-Peña A.; Elices I.; Garcia-Saura C.; Levi R.; Rodríguez F.; Varona P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rhythmic neural activity in the form of robust sequential activations is present in many neural systems at multiple description levels. Circuits generating such activity often involve intrinsic neuronal variability and interactions mediated by distinct synapse types. The control of sequential rhythms requires coordination across short and intermediate time scales to adapt to conditions within each cycle of the rhythm or to adjust excitability and speed to meet specific functional demands. In this work we analyze the interplay among neural synchronization, excitability, variability and sequentiality timing in rhythmic bursting. We analyze long intracellular and extracellular recordings of the pyloric CPG quantifying these aspects and reporting their relationships at multiple time scales including the modulation of cycle-by-cycle sequential dynamical invariants among key time intervals. The results of the relationship between specific sequence intervals at different time scales provide a novel view on the understanding of autonomous motor coordination in robust, yet time-flexible sequential rhythms, even during transient dynamics.

Article.Title: LC-ESI/MS/MS profile of purslane (Portulaca oleracea) nanoparticles for reduction foodborne pathogens and enhancing quality parameters of guava nectar model
Article.Authors: Morsy M.; Mekawi E.; Nagar M.; Nagar M.; Al-Dalain S.; Abdelaziz M.; Elgabaly A.; Alfaleh A.; Aljehani A.; Helal M.; Kadi R.; Alqahtani A.; Alomari H.; Bedaiwi R.; M. Alessa F.; Alzahrani S.; Sami R.; Alshehry G.; Almehmadi A.; Alqurashi A.; Fadhul T.
Article.Abstract: Purslane ( Portulaca oleracea ) is a naturally growing weed, containing a lot of polyphenols. This study aimed to evaluate purslane nanoparticles (PUR-NP) as antimicrobial and antioxidant in guava nectar storage at 4 ± 1 ℃ for 6 weeks. PUR-NP were incorporated into freshly made guava nectar at 100, 200, 300, and 400 µg mL − 1 , and compared with natamycin 40 µg mL − 1 and a control positive (pasteurized) as a reference, and without addition as the control sample. The LC-ESI/MS/MS profile, antimicrobial activity, and antioxidant ability of PUR-NP were performed, as well as the physicochemical properties, and quality parameters of guava nectar were done. Results showed that PUR-NP (55 nm) exhibited high antimicrobial activity at 400 µg mL − 1 opposite E. coli O157:H7 , S. aureus , penicillium expansum , and Candida glabrata . A noteworthy distinction was noted between PUR-NP treatments and natamycin. Fifteen major polyphenol compounds were identified in the PUR-NP extract and exhibited high antioxidant capacity compared to purslane fresh leaves (PFL) or purslane dried leaves (PDL). A noteworthy distinction in physicochemical attributes was noted between the guava nectar including PUR-NP 100–400 µg mL − 1 and control. However, no discernible variation were noted between guava nectar containing PUR-NP and natamycin. Results showed that PUR-NP at 400 µg mL − 1 were more effective as an antimicrobial and antioxidant that improves the quality attributes and shelf-life in guava nectar.

Article.Title: Assessment of the health and economic benefits of PM2.5-O3 composite pollution in Henan Province, China, 2020–2024
Article.Authors: Wei L.; Cheng Y.; Liu R.; Si Z.; Wang D.; Zhou K.; Wang P.; Hu B.; Wei P.; Zhu R.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates the spatiotemporal evolution and health-economic impacts of PM 2.5 and O 3 composite pollution across 17 cities in Henan Province from 2020 to 2024. PM 2.5 declined by 9.8%, with sustained emission controls as the most plausible primary driver. O 3 rose fluctuantly, with 77% of its increase attributable to meteorological variability. Multi-layer validation of CHAP grids against ground data showed strong agreement at the monthly scale for both PM 2.5 (R² = 0.943) and O 3 (R² = 0.980), with consistent city rankings and spatial clustering. PM 2.5 -attributable deaths remained stable (48,000–49,000/year) during 2021–2024, while O 3 -attributable deaths increased by 14.8% in 2024 versus the 2021–2023 average. Achieving China’s Grade I standards by 2030 could reduce PM 2.5 - and O 3 -related deaths by 83.3% and 13.5%, respectively, yielding RMB 65.8 billion in economic benefits. Backward trajectory clustering and PSCF/CWT analyses of 4,039 trajectories show that compound pollution episodes are associated with two prevailing transport pathways and potential source regions over southern Hebei, western Shandong, and the Guanzhong Plain.

Article.Title: Integrating multi-environment and path coefficient analysis for the identification of yellow rust-resistant bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) genotypes
Article.Authors: Mulugeta T.; Tiruneh A.; Bezabih A.; Temeche D.; Tefera N.; Abate A.
Article.Abstract: Rapid turnover of varieties and limited access to rust-resistant wheat varieties across agroecologies are due to the rapid mutation of yellow rust pathogens. This study aimed to identify high-yielding, yellow rust-resistant genotypes and assess the severity of yellow rust across wheat growth stages. 150 bread wheat genotypes were evaluated using an alpha lattice design with two replications at three locations across two major wheat-producing areas of Ethiopia (Arsi and North Shewa) during the 2022 and 2023 main cropping seasons. A mixed-model analysis was conducted in R. The ANOVA results revealed highly significant (< 0.001) effects of genotype, year, and location interactions, thereby highlighting strong seasonal and environmental influences on yellow rust incidence and other traits. Yellow rust severity varied markedly across growth stages, with the highest disease pressure observed at the dough and heading stages. Thirteen genotypes at Kulumsa and 64 genotypes at Enewari showed high yellow rust severity, indicating the occurrence of different virulence spectra in the environments under study and the need for multiple-environment screening for a valid assessment of resistance to yellow rust. Path coefficient analysis further revealed that thousand kernel weight has the strongest direct positive effect (0.43) on grain yield. The coefficient of infection (CI) exhibits both direct (-0.29) and indirect negative effects, highlighting the significance of resistance in sustaining productivity. In conclusion, 16 high-yielding and yellow rust-resistant genotypes were identified as promising candidates for future wheat improvement.

Article.Title: Epidemiological study of factors associated with lifetime stillbirth among women in Isfahan Province, Iran
Article.Authors: Hojati M.; Izadi S.; Mansourian M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the epidemiological factors of stillbirth, including demographic, socioeconomic, reproductive, clinical, and lifestyle factors, among women in Isfahan province, Iran. A descriptive-analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2023 to May 2024, enrolling 2750 women aged 15 to 55 years with a history of at least one pregnancy. Participants were selected using multistage random sampling. Data were collected through structured interviews covering demographics, socioeconomic status, reproductive history, clinical parameters, and lifestyle factors. Clinical measurements, including fasting blood sugar, body mass index, blood type, platelet count, and blood urea nitrogen, were obtained from the SIB electronic health system during the first-trimester antenatal visit. Associations among variables were analyzed using Chi-square tests, Fisher’s exact tests, t-tests, and Firth’s penalized-likelihood logistic regression. Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were reported to present the findings. The proportion of women who reported a lifetime history of stillbirth was 1.38% (95% Confidence Interval: 0.96–1.80). In a multivariable Firth regression analysis, parity emerged as the strongest correlate. Women with three pregnancies exhibited an adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of 3.47 (95% CI: 1.44–8.37; p = 0.006), compared to those with two or fewer pregnancies. Furthermore, women with four or more pregnancies presented an AOR of 7.52 (95% CI: 2.83–20.01; p < 0.001). Additionally, each 1 mg/dL increase in fasting blood sugar during the first trimester correlated with a 3.5% increase in odds (AOR = 1.035; 95% CI: 1.017–1.053; p < 0.001). Each 1-unit increase in body mass index during the first trimester was associated with a 16% increase in odds (AOR = 1.163; 95% CI: 1.085–1.247; p < 0.001). Elevated parity, increased fasting blood sugar during the first trimester, and a higher body mass index in the first trimester are factors associated with stillbirth. These findings indicate valuable avenues for future prospective research, including improved glycemic control, effective weight management strategies, and enhanced antenatal surveillance for multiparous women.

Article.Title: Drill-suction end-effector for removing substandard substrate blocks in greenhouse tray seedling production
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu S.; Lu J.; Tong J.; Wu F.; Ye Z.
Article.Abstract: During greenhouse tray seedling propagation, certain cells may exhibit sowing failures or poor seedling growth, necessitating the removal of defective seedlings and subsequent replacement with healthy seedlings. However, conventional mechanical removal may result in substrate fragmentation or residual substrate retention, hindering replanting. This study employed negative-pressure suction for substrate removal. Under single-end operation, substrate removal rates exceeded 80% for both root-free and root-containing substrate blocks at moisture contents of 60–80%. To address pipeline blockage caused by substrate aggregation and insufficient suction, a drill-suction anti-clogging structure was designed. A three-factor, three-level response surface experiment was conducted using the nozzle inlet diameter, the “n”-type draft angle, and the nozzle descent height as factors. The optimal combination was a nozzle inlet diameter of 13 mm, an “n”-type draft angle of 8.4°, and a nozzle descent height of 21 mm. A dual-end synchronous operation mode was further developed. Although simultaneous operation reduced the substrate removal rate, particularly at high moisture contents, single-end operation maintained removal rates above 80% for both left and right ends within the tested moisture range.

Article.Title: TPH2 knockout impairs skilled motor performance and alters striatal dopamine metabolism in female rats
Article.Authors: Zhukov I.; Sviridova V.; Sysoev Y.; Shitc D.; Musienko P.; Alenina N.; Karpenko M.; Gainetdinov R.
Article.Abstract: Tryptophan hydroxylase 2 knockout (TPH2-KO) rats lack serotonin (5-HT) specifically in the central nervous system (CNS). While previous research has focused on limbic system-related behaviors, the intrinsic effects of CNS 5-HT depletion on baseline motor control and their neurochemical basis remain incompletely understood. Here, we compared the sensorimotor performance of TPH2-KO and wild-type (WT) female rats using a battery of behavioral tests and assessed monoamine content in key CNS motor regions via HPLC. TPH2-KO rats exhibited increased slips on the beam walking test and increased locomotor speed in kinematic analysis. Monoamine tissue content analysis of TPH2 knockout rats revealed a double dysregulation in both 5-HT and dopamine (DA) regulation in the CNS. DA levels were markedly reduced in the striatum and, even more severely, in the medulla oblongata, accompanied by elevated metabolite‑to‑DA ratios. This dual monoamine disruption likely contributes to the observed alterations in locomotor speed and precision motor control, without evidence of gross motor coordination or balance deficits in the rotarod and horizontal ladder tests. Our findings reveal a novel motor phenotype in TPH2‑KO rats and demonstrate the power of the homozygous TPH2 knockout. This broadens the model not only for major depression research, but also highlights the potential relevance of TPH2‑KO rats for studying serotonin‑associated mechanisms of locomotor speed regulation and motor precision.

Article.Title: SA-ADFQ: structure-aware activation distribution friendly quantization for vision transformers in medical image analysis
Article.Authors: Karthika K.; Aneja V.
Article.Abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have exhibited impressive performance in medical image analysis tasks like classification, detection, and segmentation. However, due to their computational and memory costs, it is difficult to efficiently deploy ViTs in resource-constrained clinical environments. Quantization is an efficient approach for mitigating this problem. However, existing Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) approaches face performance degradation at low-bit precision due to the complicated activation distributions in ViTs. To address these issues, Structure-Aware Activation Distribution Friendly Quantization (SA-ADFQ), a new extension to the existing quantization method, specifically for medical image analysis tasks, is introduced. By inheriting the Activation Distribution Friendly Quantization (ADFQ) method, which includes the per-patch outlier quantizer and shift-log2 quantizer to address the irregular and non-uniform distributions. Moreover, to further enhance quantization performance, a new module-wise optimization approach that maintains spatial dependencies and key feature representations in medical image data is also introduced. Furthermore, the method is extended to include medical image classification, detection, and segmentation tasks, demonstrating its flexibility for various image and video tasks. Through extensive experiments on medical image datasets, it is shown that the proposed method significantly improves performance over existing quantization methods, especially at low-bit precision, and is computationally efficient.

Article.Title: Improving employee performance rating prediction using ANN probability-enhanced ensemble learning
Article.Authors: Chang X.
Article.Abstract: Employee performance rating prediction is an important task in human resource management. It helps organizations identify high-performing employees, improve training programs, and support decisions regarding promotions and workforce allocation. However, employee performance is influenced by multiple factors such as job position, work experience, job satisfaction, overtime, department, and managerial environment. These factors are typically nonlinear and interrelated, making accurate prediction challenging. To address this issue, this study proposes an ANN probability-enhanced ensemble learning framework, in which the soft class-probability outputs generated by multiple ANN base learners are used for both weighted prediction fusion and feature enhancement by combining them with the original employee features for second-stage classification. First, multiple ANN base learners with different hidden layer structures are trained to obtain diverse predictive information. Then, the output probabilities of these base learners are utilized in two ways: weighted ANN ensemble and probability-enhanced feature construction. The probability-enhanced features are further combined with various meta-classifiers, including Random Forest, ExtraTrees, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors, HistGBDT, AdaBoost, Logistic Regression, and Linear Support Vector Machine (LinearSVM). Experiments were conducted on the IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition and Performance dataset from Kaggle. Results show that the proposed ANNProb-AdaBoost model achieves the best macro F1 score of 0.4885 and an accuracy of 0.8265. Compared to individual ANN models and traditional machine learning models, this approach delivers more balanced classification performance. Additionally, sensitivity analysis and feature importance analysis based on feature deletion were performed to evaluate the model's robustness and interpretability.

Article.Title: Development of an edible vaccine candidate conferring protective efficacy against pneumococcal challenge using conserved PspA epitopes in a murine model
Article.Authors: Akter S.; Stoger E.; Akhtar Banu T.; Goswami B.; Nashir Uddin M.; Khan S.; Nessa J.; Rafiqul Ahsan C.
Article.Abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae , also known as pneumococcus, is one of the leading causes of respiratory tract infections, meningitis, and septicemia in Bangladesh. In recent years, the pneumococcal surface protein A (PspA) has been suggested as a promising candidate, alone or with other immunogens, to be included in a future vaccine. Edible plant-based vaccines use recombinant antigens produced in plant tissues, providing an affordable and oral delivery option compared to traditional vaccines. This study applied a computational reverse vaccinology strategy to identify four potential B-cell epitope peptides from the PspA. Four epitope peptide sequences were found as the most potential B cell epitopes. Conservancy analysis was done using in silico tools. The sequences of S. pneumoniae epitope sequences were analyzed and placed in fusion with alpha zein. Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain LBA4404 containing the Ti plasmid was used for selection in all cases for the integration of the gene of interest. Antigens of S. pneumoniae fused to zein in Lycopersicon esculentum were generated using Agrobacterium -mediated genetic transformation protocols. The transformation through A. tumefaciens was confirmed by kanamycin selection and PCR analysis with the specific primers. Mice immunized with transgenic plant tissue and the control mice were challenged intraperitoneally with 10 times the LD 50 dose of the S. pneumoniae type 7F. The results demonstrated significant protection, with 83% of immunized mice surviving the live S. pneumoniae challenge compared to only 50% survival in control groups. These findings highlight the selected PspA epitope region as a promising target conferring protective efficacy in this murine model, supporting further development of an oral pneumococcal vaccine candidate.

Article.Title: How perceived restorativeness in rural tourism destinations influences job crafting willingness among knowledge workers through psychological restoration and psychological richness
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Su Q.
Article.Abstract: This study examines how perceived restorativeness in rural tourism destinations relates to knowledge workers’ willingness to engage in job crafting, through the parallel mediating roles of psychological restoration and psychological richness. Drawing on Attention Restoration Theory, Conservation of Resources Theory, and Broaden-and-Build Theory, we tested a structural model on survey data from 764 knowledge workers in China using AMOS 28.0. Three findings stand out. Extent and fascination were directly and positively associated with job crafting willingness, whereas mental escape and physical distance related to it only through psychological restoration (full mediation); compatibility showed neither a direct association nor significant mediation through either mechanism in the rural tourism context. Psychological restoration partially mediated the associations of extent and fascination with job crafting willingness and fully mediated those of mental escape and physical distance. Psychological richness mediated the fascination path significantly and the mental escape path tentatively (the bootstrap confidence interval excluded zero, but the z-test did not reach the 5% level), and did not mediate the compatibility, extent, or physical distance paths. The study contributes a dual-mechanism (recovery-and-growth) account of how off-the-job restorative experiences cross domains to shape proactive work behavior, and it extends psychological richness theory, so far confined largely to well-being research, into the organizational behavior domain. The results offer practical guidance for designing corporate vacation benefits and rural-destination marketing strategies for knowledge workers.

Article.Title: Prediction of blasting fragmentation based on geological characterization of in-situ rock mass discontinuities
Article.Authors: Cao J.; Han B.; Liu H.; Zou K.; Xiang Z.; Fang Y.; Ding H.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In mining metal deposits, blasting fragmentation is a key indicator that directly affects production efficiency and economic costs. To address the limitations of current post-blast assessment, which overlooks the intrinsic relationship between in-situ fragmentation (geological characterization of in-situ rock mass discontinuities) and the resulting blasting fragmentation, this paper proposes a quantitative prediction model and methodology for blasting fragmentation. Through field investigation of discontinuities and three-dimensional discontinuity network modeling, the in-situ fragmentation of rock mass was characterized. Combined with rock breakage characteristics under blasting loads, a fractal-based model was established to predict blasting fragmentation from in-situ fragmentation, yielding a quantitative prediction framework. Across the full size distribution, validation through an engineering case study showed an RMSE of 6.611% and a MAPE of 4.393% between the predicted and measured cumulative fragmentation percentages. The results indicate engineering applicability and provide a quantitative prediction methodology for blasting fragmentation, particularly for boulder yield prediction.

Article.Title: Bio-VQVAE: multivariate and multi-scale time-series generation for bioprocess data augmentation
Article.Authors: Ren F.; Zeng W.; Wang Y.; Wu J.; Xu L.; Sun H.
Article.Abstract: Biomanufacturing digitalization relies heavily on data-driven modeling, yet the scarcity of high-quality labeled data remains a bottleneck. Multivariate fermentation data exhibit temporal patterns at multiple scales and complex statistical dependencies among process-state and operational variables. Current time-series generation methods often have difficulty preserving multi-scale temporal patterns and statistical dependencies among process variables. This paper proposes Bio-VQVAE, a generative framework designed to improve the representation of these characteristics in a vector-quantized latent space. We introduce a Large Selective Kernel mechanism to adaptively capture temporal patterns at different scales by dynamically adjusting the effective receptive field. Furthermore, an Efficient Multi-Scale Attention module is integrated to enhance cross-dimensional feature interaction and facilitate the empirical learning of dependencies among process variables. Evaluation on the IndPenSim benchmark shows that Bio-VQVAE achieves the lowest mean values across all four quantitative metrics among the evaluated baseline models. Notably, the method achieves superior fidelity in preserving multivariate correlation structures and temporal autocorrelation consistency, even under constrained data regimes. These results demonstrate the potential of Bio-VQVAE for in-distribution augmentation of multivariate bioprocess time series and for supporting downstream predictive modeling.

Article.Title: Removal and biodegradation of the pharmaceutical pollutant cortisone acetate by Scenedesmus obtusus under varying salinity conditions
Article.Authors: Derakhshan Z.; Tavakoli F.; Samaei M.; Koucak N.; Kazeruni F.; Salmani M.; Kochaki S.; Feilizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Pharmaceutical contaminants such as cortisone acetate pose a significant environmental challenge due to their persistence in aquatic systems and the limited effectiveness of conventional wastewater treatment processes. This study evaluated the potential of the microalga Scenedesmus obtusus for the removal and biodegradation of cortisone acetate under varying salinity, pH, and exposure time conditions. An artificial neural network model (ANN) was developed to predict system performance, and a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently applied to this model to identify optimal operational parameters, which confirming the influence of environmental factors on treatment efficiency. Under optimized conditions obtained by GA (zero salinity, pH 7, and a 10-day retention period), the model predicted a cortisone acetate removal efficiency of 96.18%, which closely matched the experimentally observed removal efficiency of 97.68%. Additionally, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) analysis identified several degradation byproducts, consistent with possible biotransformation of cortisone acetate rather than simple retention in algal biomass. Moreover, monitoring of chlorophyll a and b levels indicated increased photosynthetic activity and sustained biomass accumulation throughout the experiment, supporting effective pollutant removal. Scanning electron microscopy further revealed structural changes in the microalgal cells after treatment, including surface roughening and pore formation, consistent with cellular stress responses associated with pollutant exposure. These findings confirm the potential of Scenedesmus obtusus as a sustainable and efficient bioremediation agent for pharmaceutical pollutants in aquatic environments.

Article.Title: Combining natural language processing with patient-reported outcome measures scores to investigate the association of pandemic regulations with anxiety in children
Article.Authors: Luijten M.; Gibbons C.; Harrison C.; van Oers H.; Zijlmans J.; Tieskens J.; Alrouh H.; Broek E.; de Boer J.; Haverman L.; Polderman T.
Article.Abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and the governmental regulations taken during the pandemic have been associated with the experienced anxiety of children. However, there is a gap in research that explains how and which regulations were associated with higher anxiety. In this study we combine quantitative and qualitative data through structural topic modelling (STM) and sentiment analysis. Children and adolescents (N = 3,821, aged 8–18 years old) completed an open-ended question; “ How are the corona-regulations for you? ”, and the PROMIS Anxiety questionnaire, bi-annually from April 2020 until March 2023 (7 measurement occasions). This yielded 7,605 open-ended responses, of which 6,672 contained anxiety, which was classified as (sub)clinical for PROMIS T-scores > 50.8. We applied STM to the open-ended responses to identify relevant topics, using dichotomized Anxiety as covariate.
