We used sentiment analysis to assess the affective state of responses and obtain polarity scores for each response (ranging from − 1 (negative) to + 1 (positive)). We identified the topics of importance to children during the pandemic and assessed the affective state of these responses per topic in the whole sample and split by presence of (sub)clinical anxiety. Eight topics emerged: (1) Adaptation/Resilience, (2) Distress, (3) Adherence to social distancing, (4) Limited social and family contact (5) Restrictions in activities/boredom, (6) Future perspectives, (7) Homebound (school closures), and (8) Lack of celebratory events. Compared to their peers, children with (sub)clinical anxiety reported significantly more negative sentiment, particularly regarding adaptation/resilience (-0.19 vs. -0.10, Cohen’s D = 0.24) and distress due to lockdown (-0.06 vs. 0.02, Cohen’s D = 0.20). They also expressed stronger emotional language when discussing these topics. We successfully identified topics relating to the governmental regulations that are associated with (sub)clinical anxiety during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study shows that children with (sub)clinical anxiety scores described the pandemic period and regulations slightly more negatively, which may indicate that they have more problems with coping and adapting to lockdown measures.

Article.Title: Hybrid quantum learning based fault detection method for an active distribution system
Article.Authors: Mallinath N/A.; Dutta S.; S. J.; Jadoun V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Modern distribution systems with integrated renewable energy sources exhibit complex fault behaviour due to inverter-based generation and bidirectional power flow, making conventional protection methods less reliable. This paper presents a PMU-based fault detection framework for active distribution networks using hybrid quantum machine learning (QML) techniques. A modified IEEE 34-bus system with solar photovoltaic and wind distributed generation units is modelled, and faults are systematically created near the DG locations with wide variation in fault type, location, and fault resistance. PMU-measured voltage and current phasors are processed using symmetrical component analysis to extract compact numerical features representing peak magnitudes and phase angles of sequence components. Two hybrid QML models, namely Quantum Random Forest (QRF) and Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC), are developed within a unified modular framework. In the QRF model, quantum computation is employed for nonlinear feature transformation, followed by classical ensemble learning for classification. In the VQC model, parameterized quantum circuits learn nonlinear decision boundaries through variational optimization. The performance results show a clear difference between QRF and VQC. QRF gives stable and reliable fault detection with high precision, but VQC performs better overall. The VQC testing accuracy reached 99.8%, with precision of 99.7%, recall of 100%, and an F1-score of 99.9%. These results were achieved through the consideration of SMOTE for class balancing and feature selection for enhanced model performance. When compared with classical and deep learning approaches, the advantage of using numerical PMU data with hybrid quantum learning becomes more evident, especially since no image-based signal conversion is required. Overall, hybrid QML can be considered as a useful technique for advanced protection system.

Article.Title: Evaluation of the clinical efficacy of repeated intra-articular injections of stanozolol in canine patients with spontaneous osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Sassaroli S.; Riccio V.; Serino F.; Galosi M.; Luca P.; Ciabocco F.; Giacomo R.; Biagini L.; Mario F.; Salvaggio A.; Giada V.; Piccionello A.
Article.Abstract: The study aimed to assess the clinical efficacy of repeated intra-articular (IA) administration of stanozolol for the management of spontaneous osteoarthritis (OA) in dogs. Clinical, radiographic, and synovial fluid cytological parameters were compared among dogs treated with IA stanozolol, IA hyaluronic acid, or oral mavacoxib (Trocoxil). Seventy-five client-owned dogs affected by unilateral OA were randomly assigned to three study groups of 25 dogs each: the stanozolol group (S), the hyaluronic acid group (HA), and the mavacoxib group (T). Dogs received either three IA injections of stanozolol or hyaluronic acid administered at two-week intervals, or oral mavacoxib (2 mg/kg) administered on days 0 and 15, followed by monthly administrations for a maximum of four doses. Clinical, radiographic, and synovial fluid (SF) cytological evaluations were performed at baseline (T0) and on days 15, 30, 60, 90, and 180 after the initiation of therapy (T15, T30, T60, T90, and T180, respectively). The following parameters were assessed and statistically analyzed: Canine Brief Pain Inventory (CBPI), including the Pain Severity Index (PSI) and Pain Interference Index (PII), lameness score, visual analogue scale (VAS), GAIT4Dog lameness score (GLS), total pressure index percentage (TPI%), range of motion (ROM), limb circumference (CRF), radiographic OA grade, and SF cytology score (SS). The following parameters were assessed and statistically analyzed. Statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Data from 59 dogs (59 joints; 26 males and 33 females; mean age 7.7 years; mean body weight 28.6 kg) were included in the final analysis: group S (n = 22), group HA (n = 20), and group T (n = 17). Statistical comparisons revealed significant improvements in PSI, PII, and lameness score in the S group at 60 and 180 days compared to baseline; improvements in VAS and SS were also observed at T30, while GLS showed significant improvement from the first follow-up (T15). The results demonstrated greater improvements in several clinical outcome measures, including pain scores, lameness, GLS, and synovial fluid cytology, compared with the other treatment groups. In conclusion, repeated IA administration of stanozolol was associated with clinically relevant improvements in dogs with OA and may represent a promising therapeutic option for the management of canine OA.

Article.Title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals multicellular remodeling beyond the aganglionic segment in Hirschsprung disease
Article.Authors: Qiu Y.; Zhang X.; Zhi Z.; Xiang Y.; Tang J.; Du C.; Li H.; Tang W.
Article.Abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) is defined by the absence of enteric ganglion cells in the distal bowel, yet postoperative bowel dysfunction and Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis (HAEC) can persist after resection of the aganglionic segment. Here, we generated a segment-resolved single-nucleus RNA sequencing atlas (snRNA-seq) of ganglionic, transition and aganglionic colonic segments from three children with short-segment HSCR and transverse-colon tissues from three age-matched control infants. After quality control, 93,256 nuclei were retained and annotated as 14 major colonic cell types. Enteric neurons from HSCR ganglionic segments showed reduced representation of molecular programs associated with synaptic organization, neuronal projection development, neurotransmission, and cholinergic synapses. Enteric glial cells showed compositional remodeling, while canonical enteric glia exhibited inflammation-associated transcriptional changes. Stromal analyses indicated segment-specific remodeling, with relative enrichment of inflammation-associated S4 fibroblasts in ganglionic and transition segments and more prominent myofibroblasts and collagen deposition in the aganglionic segment. Epithelial cells in the ganglionic segment showed transcriptional alterations in programs related to barrier homeostasis. CellChat analysis further suggested remodeling of candidate stromal–epithelial and neuron–glia communication networks. These findings provide a human single-nucleus resource and generate testable hypotheses regarding segment-specific multicellular remodeling in HSCR-affected bowel.

Article.Title: Enhancing collagen biosynthesis in mammalian cells through hypoxia-mimetic prolyl hydroxylase inhibition
Article.Authors: Shahar B.; Kilimnik I.; Lifshits L.; Netti F.; Sova M.; Rosin-Grunewald D.; Di Segni A.; Gal M.; Adler-Abramovich L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Collagen, the most abundant protein in the extracellular matrix of mammalian cells, is a key biomaterial in various biotechnological and therapeutic applications, such as tissue engineering and regeneration, cosmetics, and cultivated meat. Despite the increasing demand for culture-based collagen, it is still mainly produced from animal connective tissues. A recent study has shown that under hypoxia, activation of the hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) leads to enhanced type I collagen biosynthesis. However, under normal oxygen conditions, HIF activity is downregulated by the HIF-prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) enzyme. Based on these previous findings, we hypothesized that inhibiting PHD activity by exogenous modulators could mimic hypoxia, leading to elevated HIF transcriptional activity and enhancing collagen biosynthesis under normoxia. Our study demonstrates that pharmacological PHD inhibition using a set of small molecules targeting their 2-oxoglutarate (2-OG)-dependent activity is associated with enhanced HIF activity, upregulation of key-collagen modifying enzymes, including collagen prolyl 4-hydroxylases and lysyl hydroxylases, accompanied by a 10- to 29-fold increase in collagen type I fluorescence intensity in NIH/3T3 embryonic mouse fibroblast cells. These findings show that targeting PHD can effectively enhance collagen production in mammalian cells, suggesting that the modulation of intracellular key protein signaling pathways presents a promising strategy for enhancing the production of culture-based collagen.

Article.Title: Comparison of the performance of large language models (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1, and Claude 4.6) in answering pharmacology questions
Article.Authors: Khosravi M.; Naseri K.; Kiani Z.; Khosravi F.; Naraki K.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have introduced a fundamental transformation in healthcare and medical education. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of LLMs in answering pharmacology questions. This quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted in Iran in 2026. A 50-item Persian multiple-choice questionnaire assessing pharmacology knowledge was administered to ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1, and Claude 4.6. Data were analyzed using confusion matrix methods, Cochran’s Q, McNemar, and point-biserial tests. Sensitivity values were 1.00 for ChatGPT-5.5, 0.94 for Gemini 3.1, and 0.90 for Claude 4.6. Specificity values were 0.43, 0.50, and 0.35, respectively. Accuracy was 0.82 for both ChatGPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1, and 0.72 for Claude 4.6. Overall, the mean sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy across all LLMs were 0.95, 0.43, and 0.78, respectively. The analysis further revealed a statistically significant decline in performance of ChatGPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 when addressing quantitative questions (φ = −0.286, p < .05). LLMs have potential to support professionals in educational/knowledge contexts of pharmacology, provided ethical considerations are addressed, though further research is needed to better understand their performance and limitations.

Article.Title: Nonaffirmation as minority stress among Swiss sexual minorities
Article.Authors: Krückl J.; Huber C.; Garcia Nuñez D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined associations between minority stress and depression among cisgender sexual minority individuals, focusing on nonaffirmation , a distal stress process originally developed for gender minority populations. Data were obtained from a cross-sectional survey of gender and sexual minority populations in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland (2015–2016). Minority stress was assessed using an adapted version of the Gender Minority Stress and Resilience Measure , and depressive symptoms were measured using the Allgemeine Depressionsskala (ADS-K). Spearman rank correlations assessed associations between minority stressors and depression. Hierarchical multiple regression estimated the incremental contribution of nonaffirmation beyond established minority stressors and resilience factors, and moderated mediation analyses examined associations among proximal, distal stressors and depression. The sample comprised 473 participants categorized into four sexual identity groups. All distal and proximal minority stress factors, including nonaffirmation, were positively associated with depressive symptoms. Nonaffirmation remained independently associated with depressive symptoms in regression analyses. Proximal stressors partially mediated the association between distal stressors and depressive symptoms, whereas resilience factors did not moderate this association. These findings suggest that nonaffirmation is a distinct distal minority stress process among cisgender sexual minority individuals and may complement the Minority Stress Hypothesis by capturing subtle identity invalidation beyond indicators of overt stigmatization.

Article.Title: Integrated allometric scaling, physicochemical profiling, and random forest modelling for predicting antioxidant compounds in sweeteners from overripe Malaysian bananas
Article.Authors: Ibidoja O.; Ishak W.; Ali M.; Ng Y.; Hamzah N.; Zaini M.; Azhar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bananas ( Musa spp. ) are rich in bioactive compounds that are essential for health, including support for digestion, immunity, and sustained energy. This research compared the nutritional profiles, physicochemical properties, determinants of antioxidant compounds, and antioxidant activities of sweeteners from eight overripe banana species ( Tanduk, Batu, Nangka, Emas, Cavendish, Awak, Lemak Manis, and Kapas ) in Malaysia, using validated methods. All the chosen sweeteners produced from the different banana species exhibited significant differences in physicochemical and antioxidant properties. Based on the results obtained, Tanduk exhibited the highest TDF at 8.89 g/100 g, Lemak Manis exhibited the highest ash content (4.05 g/100 g) and crude fiber (0.80 g/100 g), Kapas exhibited the highest carbohydrate content (71.99 g/100 g), and Emas revealed the highest protein content (0.62 g/100 g). Conversely, Nangka exhibited the lowest antioxidant capacity but the highest sugar content, especially glucose. Cavendish exhibited the highest antioxidant capacity, as evidenced by the DPPH and FRAP assays. The Random Forest model identified banana species, caloric content, carbohydrates, total dietary fiber, peel weight, protein, colour L*, pulp peel ratio, and crude fibre as the primary determinants of variation in antioxidant compounds among the sweeteners of Malaysian banana species. The power-law model demonstrated a strong allometric relationship between pulp weight and fruit weight. Future work could integrate feature selection techniques and explainable AI methods to further enhance biological interpretability by quantifying the contribution of each nutritional and physicochemical attribute to antioxidant activity.

Article.Title: Correction: GNG12 overexpression inhibits triple-negative breast cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion
Article.Authors: Shan B.; Zhao L.; Hu T.; Xu J.; Zeng T.; Yu B.; Tang J.
Article.Abstract: The original version of this Article contained an error in the order of the author names, which was incorrectly given as Biao-Feng Shan, Le Zhao, Tao Hu, Jing-Hao Xu, Tong-Xu Zeng, Jian-Ming Tang, and Bo Yu.

Article.Title: Correction: Establishing the first Afro-Caribbean breast cancer cell lines reveals ECM pathway enrichment and distinctive drug sensitivities
Article.Authors: Clarke S.; Allen I.; Ravix J.; Marção M.; Carcanholo F.; Doughan A.; Sanchez-Covarrubias A.; Cornwall D.; Harrison S.; Volmar C.; Saigh S.; Bilbao D.; Plummer J.; Smith E.; Thompson R.; Ragin C.; George S.; Badal S.
Article.Abstract: The original version of this Article contained errors in the order of the Figures. Figure 6 was published as Figure 8, and Figure 7 was published as Figure 6.

Article.Title: A benchmark dataset for powershell fileless malware detection: methodology, validation, and n-Gram feature extraction
Article.Authors: Meher M.; Rath A.; Sahoo P.; Samantaray A.; Panda G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract PowerShell is now an integral part of the Windows operating system and includes robust system management, automation, and configuration capabilities. Yet the PowerShell-based malware detection is a challenge as its malicious functionalities can be covered with obfuscation and get executed without any conventional executable artifacts. Many existing detection approaches are limits with proper justification on validation and labeling. Also many of them focus on the detection of PowerShell based malicious script without give emphasis on the preprocessing and feature extraction process. This study proposed a benchmark-oriented detection framework considering the advanced multi-phase deobfuscation, script normalization, VirusTotal based label validation, n-gram feature extraction and Functional Link Artificial Neural Network based classification. The proposed framework is measured using multiple n-gram configurations and standard classification metrics with a regulated train-test protocol. The Trigonometric Functional Link Artificial Neural Network (TFLANN) model achieve an accuracy of 98.61% and 0.9930 ROC-AUC using 5-gram feature sets under the reported 70:30 evaluation setting. Repeated seed trails and paired statistical tests validated the model’s rank among the four functional expansions and conventional linear and ensemble classifiers were used to put the reported accuracy into perspective. The result represent that the efficient preprocessing and lexical representation support accurate detection of malicious PowerShell script to a grate extent.

Article.Title: Differentiation of the acute changes in the inter-limb strength asymmetry profile of the lower limbs between winners and defeated athletes following a simulated karate bout
Article.Authors: Gaweł E.; Kostrzewa M.; Zając A.; Gaweł D.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to (1) assess the acute impact of a simulated karate bout (SKB) on inter-limb peak vertical force (PVF) and RFD asymmetry of the lower limbs in elite athletes (U16, U18, Seniors), accordingly to the outcome of the SKB (victory/defeat) and to (2) indicate, which lower limb: dominant (DLL)/non-dominant (NDLL) is characterized with greater post-bout changes of the kinetic performance. Sixty-one elite karatekas participated in this study, which included a randomized crossover design. Asymmetry levels were evaluated based on the isometric mid-thigh pull test. Regardless of the age category and condition, higher changes in the inter-limb PVF and RFD asymmetry profile of the analyzed lower extremities tended to occur in winners. Successful outcome in karate bout may be associated with higher changes in the inter-limb strength asymmetry profile. The level of muscular strength and athlete’s ability to generate its high levels in limited time span (RFD) in the non-dominant lower limb may be essential for performance outcomes in karate bout. Karate bout may potentially induce acute karate-specific biomechanical changes, which may possibly impact on the inter-limb strength asymmetry levels in the lower extremities.

Article.Title: Strength and stiffness development of one-part fly ash-bottom ash geopolymer stabilized soft clay
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Lyu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract One‑part geopolymers—pre‑blending solid precursors with solid activators—circumvent on‑site handling of corrosive alkaline solutions, offering a viable route for soft soil stabilization. This study evaluates this approach using fly ash (FA) and bottom ash (BA) to stabilize a soft clay (LL = 38.8%), with FA:BA ratios of 100:0, 70:30, and 50:50; binder contents of 20–50%; initial water contents of 0.7LL–1.3LL; and curing times of 7–90 days. BA incorporation accelerates early strength but retards long‑term gain: the logarithmic coefficient declines from 0.436 (pure FA) to 0.397 (50% BA), quantifying the trade‑off between transient Ca 2+ ‑driven gelation and sustained N–A–S–H polycondensation. The FA70BA30 blend at 50% binder and 1.0LL attains a 28‑day UCS of 0.59 MPa, meeting the 0.5–0.8 MPa excavation‑support standard. Two predictive correlations are established: a linear UCS–1/ R relation for mix design, and an exponential UCS– V s relation for field quality control; the exponent increases systematically from 1.166 to 5.594 with BA content, indicating that stiffness in BA‑rich matrices becomes governed by interparticle packing rather than gel continuity. XRD and SEM–EDS reveal that gehlenite dissolution in BA releases Ca 2+ to form hybrid (N,C)–A–S–H gels, whereas abundant inert residues deplete alkali and suppress sustained N–A–S–H polycondensation. At equal binder content, FA70BA30 exhibits superior post‑28‑day strength gain (+ 44.1% vs. + 11.1% for OPC), coupled with 73% lower CO 2 footprint and ~ 14% lower material cost. The FA:BA ratio thus serves as a key design parameter for balancing early strength and long‑term performance, positioning one‑part FA–BA geopolymers as a low‑carbon, cost‑competitive alternative for soft clay stabilization.

Article.Title: HistoMRIFuseNet: retrospective confidence-calibrated decision fusion of independent histopathology and DCE-MRI classifiers
Article.Authors: Yadav H.; Kumar M.
Article.Abstract: Histopathology and dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) provide different information for breast lesion assessment, but public datasets rarely contain both modalities from the same patients. This study evaluates HistoMRIFuseNet as a retrospective decision-level framework for combining independently trained histopathology and MRI predictors without assuming patient-level correspondence. HistoMorphoMamba performs pathology-based classification of BreakHis histopathology images, while DCE-KineMamba performs BI-RADS-derived lesion-risk classification using LA-Breast DCE-MRI data. Their outputs are combined through confidence- and quality-adjusted logit fusion based on evidential uncertainty, prediction entropy, and image-quality measures. On 1,023 held-out label-consistent unpaired analysis pairs, the framework achieved 0.9462 accuracy, 0.9535 F1-score, 0.8898 MCC, 0.9786 AUROC, and 0.9822 AUPRC. In contrast, the strongest test-label-free validation-tuned weighted fusion achieved 0.9404 accuracy, 0.8635 MCC, and 0.9764 AUROC, while random unpaired fusion decreased to 0.7048 accuracy, 0.4052 MCC, and 0.7614 AUROC. Repeated pairing controls showed substantial dependence on pair construction. With identical frozen modality outputs, logistic stacking achieved 0.9410 accuracy, 0.8612 MCC, and 0.9760 AUROC, compared with 0.9462, 0.8898, and 0.9786, respectively, for confidence-calibrated fusion. The corresponding total-model differences were 0.7 million parameters, 0.5 GFLOPs, and 1.2 ms per inference. These results show larger numerical differences in balanced classification and calibration than in overall accuracy or discrimination. The study therefore supports a bounded retrospective analysis of confidence-aware decision combination rather than a same-patient clinical multimodal diagnostic system. Prospective assessment requires paired histopathology–MRI cohorts with a common pathology-confirmed reference standard.

Article.Title: Stability and synchronization of higher-order memristive Cohen-Grossberg bidirectional associative memory neural networks
Article.Authors: Othmani S.; Tatar N.; Bakalah E.
Article.Abstract: This work investigates the stability and synchronization of higher-order memristive Cohen–Grossberg bidirectional associative memory neural networks. Due to the discontinuities generated by memristive effects, the analysis is carried out within the Filippov framework. By constructing appropriate Lyapunov functionals and applying refined analytical techniques, we derive general conditions that guarantee global stability with both exponential and polynomial convergence for a broad class of kernel functions extending existing models. Unlike many previous studies, the boundedness assumption on activation functions is removed, which prevents reduction to a linear system and introduces additional nonlinear complexities. These challenges are addressed using nonlinear analysis methods combined with a differential inequality approach. Moreover, synchronization between drive and response systems is achieved through adaptive feedback controllers with newly designed update laws. Numerical simulations are provided to validate the theoretical results. Let us start with new definition

Article.Title: Test-time neural style transfer for domain harmonization, with application to cone detection in adaptive optics retinal imaging
Article.Authors: Bardet J.; Aujesky A.; Jacot-Guillarmod A.; Amiot V.; Potic J.; Elwakil A.; Canton D.; Wolfensberger T.; Bergin C.; Meloni I.; Eandi C.; Balazs F.; Dubis A.; Tomasoni M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Domain shift is a well-recognized challenge in medical image analysis using Deep Learning (DL), where variability in acquisition devices, operators, and patient populations can limit model generalization. Adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO) imaging exemplifies this issue, as variations in image appearance across acquisitions can affect downstream quantitative analyses. In this work, we repurpose Neural Style Transfer as a test-time augmentation strategy (TT-NST) to harmonize image appearance between training and target domains without model retraining. Our NST approach is model-agnostic and can be applied to standard DL architectures. We evaluated performance, with and without TT-NST, using a well-established DL cone detector (MultiDimensional Recurrent Neural Network) across three datasets spanning far-domain, near-domain, and in-domain imaging conditions. TT-NST substantially improved mean Dice on the far-domain dataset from 0.43 to 0.72, primarily by increasing recall (0.34 to 0.75) with a limited reduction in precision (0.91 to 0.71). More modest gains were observed on the near-domain dataset, while performance slightly decreased on the in-domain dataset, as expected when test images match the training distribution. Compared with alternative test-time augmentation methods, TT-NST achieved the highest mean Dice on far-domain data. These results indicate that TT-NST is a label-free strategy for domain harmonization with potential to improve robustness across medical image analysis tasks under domain shift.

Article.Title: Supercontinuum generation and absorption spectroscopy from 3 to 20 μm using a highly nonlinear telluride glass rod
Article.Authors: Serrano E.; Béjot P.; Billard F.; Gadret G.; Smektala F.; Mahlovanyi B.; Boussard-Plédel C.; Le Coq D.; Kibler B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Broadband light sources extending deep into the long-wavelength mid-infrared are of strong interest for molecular spectroscopy, sensing, and nonlinear photonics, but their generation remains challenging because of the limited availability of suitable materials and efficient nonlinear conversion schemes. Here, we demonstrate broadband supercontinuum generation in a bulk GeTe₄–AgI chalcohalide glass using intense femtosecond pulses centered at approximately 8.5 μm. The generated supercontinuum extends from 3 to 20 μm, corresponding to a spectral coverage of approximately 2.7 octaves, and reaches an output average power of 2.1 mW at a 1-kHz repetition rate. The high peak power relative to the estimated self-focusing critical power leads to strong nonlinear spectral broadening in the bulk glass, consistent with the regime of filamentation-assisted supercontinuum generation. The generated broadband source is further evaluated for long-wavelength mid-IR spectroscopy through absorption measurements of a 100-µm-thick polytetrafluoroethylene film. The main absorption features measured using the supercontinuum source agree well with those obtained using a conventional Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer, including characteristic bands around 16 and 18 μm. These results demonstrate the potential of telluride glasses for broadband nonlinear light generation and spectroscopy extending into the long-wavelength mid-IR.

Article.Title: Sustainable biofiltrate-modified natural coal as a green and efficient adsorbent for lead removal from aqueous solution
Article.Authors: Chekol F.; Adem A.; Asfaw M.; Tesfaw B.; Getachew T.
Article.Abstract: The increasing contamination of water resources by toxic heavy metals has created an urgent need for efficient, low-cost, and sustainable adsorbents for wastewater treatment. This study focuses on developing a highly efficient biofiltrate-modified coal(BFMC) for removing toxic lead ions (Pb(II)) from aqueous solutions. BFMC was synthesized by modifying natural coal (NC) with an alkaline-activated biofiltrate extracted from Solanum marginatum leaves. BFMC was characterized by using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction, confirming successful preparation. Operational parameters significantly govern adsorption performance onto BFMC. Solution pH determines surface charge and speciation, and optimal removal occurs at pH 5. The maximum uptake capacity was reached at 120 min, with optimal initial concentration and adsorbent dosage of 50 mg/L and 0.05 g, respectively. Equilibrium adsorption was analyzed using the Langmuir and Freundlich isotherm models, Langmuir model showing the best fit (R 2 = 0.999) and an adsorption capacity of 85.179 mg/g. Adsorption kinetics analysis showed the pseudo-second-order model fits best (R 2 = 0.999) compared to the pseudo-first-order model, indicating that the adsorption process is primarily governed by chemisorption. Thermodynamic properties indicated that the adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic. Hence, the findings demonstrate that BFMC is a highly efficient and promising adsorbent for Pb(II) removal from aqueous solutions while also enabling the value-added utilization of surplus natural coal resources.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial and inflammatory markers as promising tools to enrich the diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
Article.Authors: Bernard J.; Choi J.; Boukouaci W.; Wu C.; Bouassida J.; Godin O.; Hasty L.; Richard J.; Barau C.; Corvoisier P.; Andreazza A.; Leboyer M.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and low-grade inflammation have both been implicated in major mood and psychotic disorders, yet their interplay and association with specific symptom profiles and potential as diagnostic biomarkers remain unclear. We quantified mitochondrial markers including mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-cn), lactate, and circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) alongside immune markers in 934 individuals from the French I-GIVE cohort, including patients with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and healthy controls (HC). Both SCZ and BD were associated with increased lactate levels and with decreased mtDNA-cn during acute episodes. Mitochondrial markers correlated with inflammatory markers and clinical outcomes. Several inflammatory markers, including IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13, IL-16, IL-17, TNF-α, and CRP, were also elevated in patients compared to controls. Models combining mitochondrial and inflammatory markers discriminated patients from controls with high accuracy and moderately distinguished SCZ from BD, while showing more limited performance for global functioning and disease onset. These findings support a contribution of mitochondrial and inflammatory alterations to the biological profile of severe psychiatric disorders. If replicated, such potential biomarkers may help refine diagnostic stratification and improve the characterization of clinical profiles.

Article.Title: Joint association of eGDR and long-term maintenance of healthy BMI range with light BioAge acceleration
Article.Authors: Zhou P.; Yang S.; Xiong Y.; Meng X.; Lv T.
Article.Abstract: Biological aging trajectories vary considerably among individuals of the same chronological age, partly attributable to differences in metabolic health. Nevertheless, the combined influence of long-term weight maintenance and insulin resistance on Light BioAge acceleration remains insufficiently characterized. Data were derived from two population-based cohorts: the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and the UK Biobank. Time in target range for body mass index (TTR-BMI) was used to characterize long-term BMI stability, while insulin sensitivity was assessed using the estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR). Biological age was estimated using the Light BioAge model, which incorporates chronological age, serum creatinine, fasting glucose, and C-reactive protein. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analyses, joint analyses of TTR-BMI and eGDR, and exploratory mediation analyses were performed. The analysis included 7,962 CHARLS participants and 11,142 UK Biobank participants. Higher TTR-BMI was consistently associated with lower odds of accelerated aging in both cohorts. Compared with individuals who remained within the healthy BMI range, those with never or partial time within the target range showed higher odds of accelerated aging. Similarly, higher eGDR levels, indicating better insulin sensitivity, were associated with lower odds of accelerated aging. Exploratory mediation analyses yielded estimated proportions mediated by eGDR of 83.9% in CHARLS and 81.4% in the UK Biobank; however, the concurrent assessment of eGDR and biological age precluded establishing a temporal mediation sequence. Long-term BMI trajectories within the healthy range and higher eGDR levels were associated with lower odds of accelerated aging in two independent cohorts. Residual confounding, reverse causation, and selection into repeated assessments limit causal interpretation, and the exploratory mediation findings do not establish a pathway through insulin sensitivity.

Article.Title: A functional investigation of the natriuretic peptide receptor 3 (NPR3) in glomerular stability and disease progression
Article.Authors: Khbouz B.; Dumoulin B.; Kocylowski M.; Wu H.; Lin H.; Hutzfeldt A.; Aypek H.; Kretz O.; Wenzel U.; Rinschen M.; Fakler B.; Grahammer F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Podocytes are essential for maintaining the structural and functional integrity of the glomerular filter. While the signaling properties of the natriuretic peptide receptor 3 (NPR3) have long been debated, emerging data suggest a signaling role in podocytes through interactions with slit diaphragm (SD) proteins. However, its functional contribution to glomerular homeostasis remains unclear. To investigate its role, Podocyte-specific Npr3 conditional knockout mice ( Npr3 ΔPOD ) on a C57BL/6 background were exposed to two different models of glomerular injury: DOCA-high salt hypertension and Adriamycin nephropathy. Complementary in vitro phosphoproteomic profiling in CRISPR/Cas9-edited podocyte cell lines were performed to elucidate downstream signaling mediators. DOCA-salt treatment induced significant increases in systolic blood pressure, glomerular injury, and albuminuria in both genotypes without intergenotype differences. Following Adriamycin induction, WT mice developed mild albuminuria, whereas Npr3 ΔPOD mice were significantly protected. Similarly, transmission electron microscopy analysis (TEM) showed that the foot-process effacement (FPE) was attenuated in Npr3 ΔPOD mice. Proteomics did not identify major alterations in core SD proteins, whereas phosphoproteomics revealed signaling changes promoting cytoskeletal stability and stress resilience. Collectively, these findings identify NPR3 as a potential context dependent regulator of SD function and a candidate target in glomerular disease modulation.

Article.Title: Engineering efficient RbGeCl3 perovskite solar cells: A simulation-driven computational approach to performance optimization
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Mahedi A.; Tarekuzzaman M.; Al-Saleem M.; Al-Humaidi J.; Khan M.; Rasheduzzaman M.; Arafat Y.; Rahman M.; Hasan M.
Article.Abstract: The development of lead-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is critical for advancing environmentally sustainable photovoltaic technologies. This study systematically evaluates the photovoltaic potential of RbGeCl 3 as a lead-free absorber using SCAPS-1D simulations. Unlike studies, this work goes beyond limited configurations or single-layer studies by delivering multi-parameter optimization and comparative ETL engineering of RbGeCl 3 PSCs for high-performance lead-free devices. An initial screening of 48 device configurations with varied electron transport layers (ETLs) and hole transport layers (HTLs) identified four promising architectures of the form FTO/ETL/RbGeCl 3 /MoS 2 /Pt employing SnS 2 , WS 2 , WO 3 , and CdS as ETLs. Among these, the SnS 2 -based device delivered the highest performance, achieving a PCE of 19.29%, V OC of 0.692 V, J SC of 34.28 mA cm − 2 , and FF of 81.19% at an optimized absorber thickness of 0.5 μm and defect density of 10 15 cm − 3 . Comprehensive optimization- including absorber and ETL thicknesses, bulk and interfacial defect densities, temperature effects, and series/shunt resistances revealed strong structure-dependent performance trends. All devices exhibited excellent photoresponse, with EQE values exceeding 90% across 400–800 nm, confirming efficient photon absorption and carrier extraction. and alignment (VBO/CBO), Mott-Schottky and recombination analyses revealed favorable energy-level alignment and a strong built-in electric field across the optimized architectures, leading to reduced recombination losses and enhanced charge transport. Impedance analyses further verified the operational robustness of the optimized structures. Collectively, the findings of this study identify RbGeCl 3 as a promising lead-free absorber with strong optical response, suitable band energetics, and ETL compatibility, providing design insights for efficient and stable environmentally benign PSCs.

Article.Title: A hybrid deep learning and ensemble approach for accurate prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma from sequence variants of hepatitis B virus (HBV) X gene
Article.Authors: Ejaz S.; Nawaz S.
Article.Abstract: The current study presents a hybrid framework combining deep learning and ensemble learning models to predict hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on sequence variants of the hepatitis B virus (HBV)-X gene. In contrast to traditional single-model approaches, the proposed framework integrates deep learning architectures with data balancing and ensemble learning strategies to enhance predictive robustness and generalization. The dataset comprises 3,360 distinct DNA sequences categorized into HCC and Non-HCC classes, with a significant class imbalance favoring the Non-HCC group. To address this issue, the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to reduce classification bias and improve minority class learning. Two sequence encoding strategies, One-Hot encoding and K-mer encoding (K = 3 and K = 6), were employed to capture nucleotide composition and sequence dependencies. A range of machine learning models, including Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Nu-Support Vector Classifier (NuSVC), Logistic Regression (LR), XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), and AdaBoost, as well as deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), were systematically evaluated. To further enhance predictive performance, a hybrid stacking ensemble framework was developed, integrating a CNN–BiLSTM architecture and Random Forest as base learners, with Logistic Regression serving as the meta-classifier to combine their predictions. All methodological steps, model configurations, and evaluation strategies were explicitly defined to ensure reproducibility and facilitate verification. The proposed hybrid stacking ensemble model demonstrated superior performance compared to individual machine learning and deep learning models. One-Hot encoding consistently outperformed K-mer encoding across most models. The best-performing hybrid stacking ensemble achieved an accuracy of 0.9139 and an F1-score of 0.9126, indicating a strong balance between classification performance and generalization. The application of SMOTE further improved model stability and reduced classification bias. These results highlight that the integration of hybrid deep learning models with ensemble learning and class imbalance correction provides a significant improvement over conventional single-model approaches for HBV-related HCC prediction. The proposed framework has potential applications in clinical diagnostic systems for early and accurate detection of HCC. Future work will focus on external validation using independent datasets and further optimization of encoding strategies and advanced deep learning architectures.

Article.Title: Exploratory analysis of Notch and Wnt pathway gene expression across biofluids and tumor tissue in gynecologic cancer
Article.Authors: Vaicekauskaitė I.; Kazlauskaitė P.; Žilovič D.; Čiurlienė R.; Sabaliauskaitė R.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian (OC) and endometrial (EC) cancers are among the most clinically challenging gynecologic malignancies. The lack of reliable non-invasive biomarkers limits early detection of these malignancies. Notch and Wnt pathway members are frequently deregulated in EC and OC tissues and may serve as biomarkers. Liquid biopsy samples, including uterine lavage (UL), plasma and urine may serve as less-invasive alternatives to tissue biopsies. In this study, CTNNB1 , NOTCH2 , DLL1 , HES1 expression was determined by RT-qPCR in 103 uterine lavage, 15 urine sediment, 15 plasma and 65 tissue samples from patients with gynecologic conditions. NOTCH2 , DLL1 and CTNNB1 expressions were decreased in UL from EC patients compared to non-cancer samples ( p ≤ 0.003), while HES1 expression was increased in high-grade serous OC (HGSOC) ( p = 0.014). UL HES1 expression distinguished HGSOC from non-cancer cases (AUC = 0.688), while UL NOTCH2 separated EC and non-cancer cases (AUC = 0.865). HES1 showed concordance between tumor and UL, whereas HES1 , CTNNB1 , and NOTCH2 differed between plasma, urine sediment and tumor samples. The study provides the first comparison of these biomarkers between multiple types of liquid biopsy sample types, supporting UL as a promising biosample type for gynecologic cancer biomarker development.

Article.Title: Soil organic carbon dynamics and microbial responses to intercropping sweet corn with legumes under different row arrangements in coastal Odisha
Article.Authors: Pattnaik S.; Mohanty A.; Shatpathy P.; Kar I.; Prusty M.; Panigrahi K.; Behera B.; Sinha B.; Sahoo A.; Pradhan M.; Behera L.; Jena H.; Nayak R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intercropping of cereals and legumes can improve resource-use efficiency and soil fertility compared with monocropping. A field experiment was conducted during rabi , 2023–24 at OUAT, Bhubaneswar, India to evaluate the effects of sweet corn ( Zea mays L.) intercropped with cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata ) and black gram ( Vigna mungo ) under different row arrangements on soil organic carbon (SOC), biological properties and soil fertility. The experiment was conducted in a randomized block design comparing sole sweet corn with intercropping systems in 1:1, 1:2 and paired 2:2 row arrangements. Soil samples collected at 30 and 60 days after sowing (DAS) and at harvest were analysed for soil organic carbon (SOC), microbial populations, microbial biomass carbon (MBC), soil basal respiration (SBR), dehydrogenase activity (DHA), urease activity (UA) and available primary soil nutrients. Intercropping generally improved SOC and soil biological properties compared with sole sweet corn, with the paired 2:2 row arrangement showing the most pronounced response. At harvest, this treatment increased SOC by 5.9% and MBC by 67% over sole sweet corn and recorded the highest DHA (1.46 µg TPF g -1 soil h -1 ) and UA (67.0 µg NH 4 + -N g -1 soil h -1 ). It also recorded higher SBR and enhanced bacterial and actinomycete populations whereas fungal population remained unaffected. The paired 2:2 arrangement also enhanced available primary soil nutrients with the strongest response observed at harvest. These findings indicate that appropriate spatial arrangement in sweet corn-legume intercropping can improve soil organic carbon and microbial functioning within a cropping season. Paired-row intercropping therefore shows potential as a soil fertility management strategy for sustainable sweet corn production under the East and South Eastern Coastal Plain of Odisha.

Article.Title: Impact of pharmaceutical care on medication-related problems among ambulatory cardiovascular disease patients in Southwest Ethiopia: a quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: Senbeta B.; Liche T.; Ararame G.; Sarbesa N.; Teka F.; Geda T.; Achalu T.
Article.Abstract: The impact of pharmaceutical care service among cardiovascular disease patients was more efficient in improving quality of life and lowering the incidence of drug-related problems. However, to the best of our knowledge, there has been almost no study done on the impact of pharmaceutical care services on medication-related problems among Cardiovascular disorders, particularly in Ethiopia. To determine the impact of pharmaceutical care services on medication-related problems among ambulatory cardiovascular disease patients at Ilu Ababor and Buno Bedele Zones Hospitals. A multicenter quasi-experimental study design was conducted at four hospitals in the Ilu Ababor and Buno Bedele zones. Statistical Software Package for Social Sciences-version 25.0 was used to analyze the data. The primary outcome was reduction in medication-related problems following pharmacist-led pharmaceutical care intervention. The differences in medication-related problems between pre- and post-interventional were determined by using the McNemar test. Statistical significance was considered at a p-value < 0.05. Among 1269 study participants included in this study, 792(62.4%) were male, and the mean age with standard deviation was 53.88 ± 13.17 years. Of the total 1269 cardiovascular disease patients, 720(56.7%) patients had experienced medication-related problems before intervention. Among participants, 429(33.8%) patients had experienced medication-related problems after intervention. The McNemar test found that the pharmaceutical care service intervention was found to be statistically significant. The finding of study showed, medication-related problems were significantly reduced after pharmaceutical care service provided by clinical pharmacists. Hence, optimizing the integration of pharmaceutical care services is strongly recommended to support optimal management of cardiovascular disease.

Article.Title: The association between future time perspective and health behavior among patients with colorectal cancer: a moderated mediation model
Article.Authors: Hu X.; Zhang D.; Yao C.; Xu R.; Luo J.; Tang C.; Jin Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between Future Time Perspective (FTP) and health behavior among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), as well as the mediating role of intention and the moderating roles of behavior prepotency and self-regulatory capacity. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted from April to June 2025, including 635 postoperative patients with CRC from three tertiary hospitals in China. Participants completed validated scales measuring FTP, intention, health behavior, behavior prepotency, and self-regulatory capacity. A moderated mediation model was tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 16) with bootstrapping. FTP was positively associated with both health behavior and intention. Intention was positively associated with health behavior. Behavior prepotency significantly moderated the intention-health behavior association, but the index of moderated mediation was not significant; self-regulatory capacity significantly moderated the indirect effect. Overall, these findings are consistent with a dual-pathway pattern in which FTP is directly associated with health behavior and indirectly associated with it through intention, with behavior prepotency and self-regulatory capacity playing distinct moderating roles. The cross-sectional design precludes causal or temporal inferences.

Article.Title: Association of infant weight gain patterns with early childhood obesity among infants born small or large for gestational age
Article.Authors: Chang Y.; Yu T.
Article.Abstract: To characterize weight gain patterns in small-for-gestational age (SGA) and large-for-gestational age (LGA) infants during the first year and examine their associations with childhood overweight and obesity risk. Infants in a Taiwan national cohort (April 2016–June 2017) were assessed at 3, 6, 12, and 36 months of age. Patterns of weight-for-age Z-scores (WAZ) were classified, and their association with obesity risk at age 36 months was analyzed. There were 499 SGA, 389 LGA, and 3890 appropriate-for-gestational age (AGA) infants with complete records up to 36 months of age. The prevalence of overweight or obesity at age 36 months was 5.2% in the SGA group (overweight: 3%; obesity: 2.2%), 8.1% in the AGA group (overweight: 5.9%; obesity: 2.2%), and 14.6% in the LGA group (overweight: 10%; obesity: 4.6%). The prevalence of being underweight was 6.4%, 1.9%, and 0.3% in the SGA, AGA, and LGA groups, respectively. We identified four weight gain patterns for each birth weight category. An accelerated growth pattern was associated with increased obesity risk in all three groups. Compared with the group with stable growth pattern, SGA infants with WAZ change (△WAZ) > 1.88 had a 2.41-fold increased risk (95% CI: 0.99, 5.88) of overweight/obesity, whereas LGA infants with △WAZ > 1.21 had a 10.79-fold increased risk (95% CI: 4.33, 26.90). Among children classified as being with overweight/obesity at 3 years old by BMI-for-age, mean weight-for-height Z-score (WFHZ) was 2.75 ± 0.95 (78.79% with WFHZ > 2); among those with obesity, mean WFHZ was 3.92 ± 0.93 (100% with WFHZ > 2), confirming concordance between BMI- and WFH-based adiposity classification. Avoiding accelerated weight gain patterns across all birth weight categories may help decrease the risk of later obesity. Additionally, the influence of constitutional genetic factors that result in naturally small or large body phenotypes should be considered to ensure growth assessments are individualized and appropriate.

Article.Title: A hybrid AHP–PID framework balancing structural stability and behavioral adaptivity for 5G-enabled innovation and entrepreneurship education
Article.Authors: Cheng C.; Mokhtar M.; Azlan Z.; Huang J.
Article.Abstract: Ultra-low latency and high-frequency interaction in 5G-enabled learning environments pose engineering challenges to quality evaluation, as existing static and dynamic models cannot effectively balance structural stability and real-time responsiveness. This challenge is particularly pronounced in innovation and entrepreneurship education (IEE), where intensive interaction, rapid feedback, and heterogeneous learning behaviors are integral to instructional effectiveness. This study develops and validates a hybrid AHP–PID dynamic evaluation framework grounded in an integrated Structure–Behavior–Regulation perspective that synthesizes Complex Systems Theory (CST), the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Digital Control Theory (DCT) to reconcile structural stability and behavioral adaptivity. Based on a rigorously constructed 4–12–36 hierarchical indicator system incorporating pedagogical, behavioral, and 5G-specific metrics (e.g., 5G-supported AR/VR immersion and network latency), the framework uses high-frequency behavioral observations collected in 5G-enabled environments to support periodic re-weighting of the evaluation indicator set in an open-loop scoring design that does not actuate pedagogical intervention, while preserving structural consistency through expert-derived static weights. Using data from 200 participants (100 teachers and 100 students) across comprehensive universities, applied undergraduate institutions, and vocational colleges, the hybrid model achieves higher predictive accuracy than the traditional static Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), standalone dynamic models, and machine-learning benchmarks on the present cohort. It achieves an AUC of 0.94 and a Pearson r of 0.76 against an expert-specified multi-source gold standard. The results further indicate that an empirically optimized fusion coefficient β of 0.65 underpins these performance gains by effectively balancing institutional comparability and behavioral adaptivity, while exploration subgroup analysis across institutional types and course categories revealed no significant performance degradation ( p = 0.18). The comprehensive‑university subsample ( n = 34, 17%) is underpowered, so these subgroup generalizability results should be regarded as preliminary. Theoretically, this study advances a coherent Structure–Behavior–Regulation logic that clarifies how systemic structure, learner behavior, and adaptive regulation interact in digital educational evaluation. Practically, the framework supports a shift from post hoc assessment toward timely quality governance and offers a replicable and adaptive evaluation template for 5G-enabled IEE and similar technology-intensive learning environments.

Article.Title: An embedded deep learning–fuzzy logic framework for intelligent and automated irrigation in smart farming
Article.Authors: Luo Z.; Yang Z.; Hu Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Water scarcity and the need to improve resource efficiency have made intelligent and automated irrigation management an important research challenge in smart farming. This study proposes IrrigaDL-FL, a low-cost automated smart irrigation framework based on the internet of things, integrating intelligent data routing with adaptive irrigation decision-making. The proposed framework consists of two complementary components. First, a Deep Learning–Fuzzy Logic (DL-FL) framework is integrated with the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) protocol to enhance data routing efficiency in the network. The DL-FL framework combines these heterogeneous characteristics to identify suitable next-hop nodes and establish energy-efficient routing paths. Second, irrigation decision-making is performed using a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network–Fuzzy Logic Controller (CNN-FLC). The CNN-FLC processes sensor-derived and crop-related information, including air temperature, relative humidity, soil moisture, evapotranspiration rate, crop growth coefficient, crop water requirement, planting date, cumulative rainfall, recent rainfall, irrigation history, crop growth stage, and the difference between actual and target soil moisture. These inputs are used to characterize crop hydration stress and dynamically determine the appropriate irrigation program and sprinkler activation duration. The proposed IrrigaDL-FL framework is evaluated through simulations with different numbers of sensor nodes over predefined routing rounds and is compared with several existing approaches. The results demonstrate that IrrigaDL-FL achieves superior performance in terms of network lifetime, residual energy, energy variance, number of transmitted packets, and average path length.

Article.Title: Developmental temperature induces consistent patterns of plasticity in lower, but not upper, critical thermal limits in threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
Article.Authors: Stanford B.; Smith S.; Rogers S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Developmental plasticity, where early-life environmental cues shape developmental trajectories with lasting impact into adulthood, may play an important role in determining how species respond to changing thermal environments. We used marine threespine stickleback ( Gasterosteus aculeatus ) to investigate whether temperature experienced during embryonic development has persistent effects on critical thermal limits as adults. Egg clutches from six families of pure marine F2s were split across three developmental temperatures (12 °C, 15.5 °C, and 22 °C), transitioned to 15.5 °C once hatched, and reared to adulthood under common-garden conditions, before being assayed for critical thermal minimum (CT min ) and maximum (CT max ). Developmental temperature was found to have significant, persistent effects on CT min , where the direction of change tracked rearing temperature (i.e., CT min decreased as early life temperature decreased). While the extent of change (i.e., slope of reaction norm) and inherent values (i.e., height of reaction norm) varied across families, all families shared the same trend. In contrast, the effect of developmental temperature on CT max was minimal, with inconsistent patterns across families. The ability of marine stickleback to lower their CT min through developmental plasticity may help maintain phenotype-environment match under changing conditions; however, this will depend on congruence between early life and adult environments.

Article.Title: HemaNest-UNet++ and explainable vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia classification
Article.Authors: Rahman S.; Abbas N.; Ali S.; Alduailij M.; Salman M.; Jan S.; Kamal S.
Article.Abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is a rapidly progressing hematological malignancy in which early and reliable identification of abnormal lymphoblasts is essential for treatment planning and prognosis. Although deep learning has improved automated leukemia analysis, most existing studies focus on binary classification, rely on public peripheral-blood datasets, classify entire microscopic images without isolating diagnostically relevant cells, or provide limited interpretation of model decisions. These limitations reduce their suitability for fine-grained and clinically transparent analysis of bone marrow images. To address this gap, this study proposes a segmentation-guided and explainable deep learning framework for automated ALL detection and morphological subtype classification. A custom dataset of 387 expert-labelled bone marrow microscopic images was collected from Amreek Clinical Laboratory, Swat, Pakistan, comprising 117 ALL L1, 103 ALL L2, 62 ALL L3, and 105 Normal samples. Written informed consent was obtained, and all data were anonymized before analysis. The proposed framework first improves image quality through normalization, denoising, and contrast enhancement. It then applies the proposed HemaNest-UNet++, which combines nested skip pathways, dual-attention refinement, multi-scale contextual aggregation, and deep supervision to segment white blood cell regions. The resulting regions of interest are classified using an Explainable Vision Transformer that integrates attention rollout and gradient-based visual explanations. HemaNest-UNet + + achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.934, an intersection-over-union of 0.876, and a pixel accuracy of 0.978, outperforming established segmentation baselines. The proposed classifier achieved 94.8% accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.944, and a macro AUC of 0.982, exceeding CNN- and transformer-based comparison models. Most residual errors occurred between ALL L2 and ALL L3 because of their overlapping morphology. Explainability maps showed that predictions were primarily influenced by clinically relevant nuclear and cytoplasmic structures. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework as an accurate and interpretable decision-support approach for bone marrow-based ALL assessment.

Article.Title: A FOCUS-PDCA quality improvement model involving unlicensed assistive personnel for improving clinical effectiveness and efficiency in inpatient physical examination: a quasi-experimental, historical-control study
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhao Y.; Zhou S.; Lv G.; Huang W.; Hu J.; Chong J.; Li F.
Article.Abstract: The accuracy and efficiency of inpatient examinations depend on a well-collaborated working team that involves doctors, nurses, and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness and efficiency of a FOCUS-PDCA quality improvement model involving UAP in improving inpatient physical examinations. A quasi-experimental, historical-control before-and-after study was conducted among 372 patients who received the FOCUS-PDCA quality improvement examination management (the observation group) and another 385 patients under normal management (the control group). Clinical effectiveness and efficiency were compared between the two groups. Compared to the control group, the FOCUS-PDCA group had significantly lower rates of defect examinations (19.6% vs. 44.7%, p < 0.01), nursing interruption events (14.5% vs. 26.4%, p < 0.01), and nurse referral events (6.1% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.01). Furthermore, the FOCUS-PDCA group had higher patient satisfaction (9.04 ± 0.82 vs. 8.45 ± 0.96, p <0.01) lower hospital cost [Median: 29,434.70 RMB (IQR: 9,705.00–52,451.40) vs. 34,537.60 RMB (IQR: 14,689.98–64,222.12), p < 0.001], and shorter length of hospital stay [Median: 4.00 days (IQR: 3.00, 5.00) vs. 5.00 days (IQR: 4.00, 6.00), p < 0.001]. The FOCUS-PDCA model involving UAP was associated with improved clinical effectiveness and efficiency of inpatient physical examination, which may be applied in hospital management to enhance the quality of care and patient outcomes. Further validation in other clinical settings is needed to test its broader application.

Article.Title: Ceruloplasmin deficiency promotes osteoclast cuproptosis-like cell death and is associated with higher bone mass in OVX mice with coordinated activation of AMPK/p53 signaling
Article.Authors: Chen G.; Yan F.; Xiong Q.; Zhou Q.; Jiang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Osteoclast bone resorption consumes a large amount of energy, and its energy metabolism disorder is an important pathogenesis of bone metabolism diseases such as osteoporosis. Excessive copper ions interfere with the energy metabolism of the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid cycle, leading to cuproptosis—a recently identified form of regulated cell death. Ceruloplasmin (CP), a major copper-binding protein, is associated with osteoporosis. However, the role and mechanism of CP in regulating osteoclast energy metabolism in association with osteoclast cuproptosis remain unclear. Our research found that CP inhibited elesclomol-copper (ES-Cu)-induced osteoclast cuproptosis-like cell death, thereby promoting osteoclast formation and overall bone resorption. CP downregulated the expression of cuproptosis-related genes ( Lipt1 , Gls , Pdhb , Fdx1 , Dlat , and Pdha1 ) in osteoclasts. In vivo, CP deficiency preserved higher bone mass in OVX mice at the macroscopic tissue level. Mechanistically, CP suppressed ES-Cu-induced AMPK/p53 pathway activation during osteoclastogenesis. Notably, the direct causal relationship between AMPK/p53 signaling and CP-modulated osteoclast cuproptosis has not been definitively established in this study, and the observed regulatory correlation requires further rigorous functional verification. Targeting CP may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for postmenopausal osteoporosis by inducing osteoclast cuproptosis.

Article.Title: Increasing exposure to potential flooding in high-mountain catchments
Article.Authors: Watson C.; Rawlins L.; Chand M.; Bhambri R.; Khadka N.; Shrestha M.; Deepak K.; Routledge D.; Middleditch G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. Validation against a manually derived reference dataset revealed considerable differences in accuracy and completeness across five building footprint products. Google Open Buildings Temporal 2.5D (OBT) displayed the highest median accuracy (F1 = 0.68), followed by Google Open Buildings V3 (F1 = 0.62). We assessed exposure relative to river channels using the height above nearest drainage (HAND) metric and modelled glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) inundation extents. Building area within 0–50 m vertical proximity to channels increased by 46% between 2016 and 2023, while those located within modelled GLOF extents increased by 77%. Population projections indicate continued growth in areas of potential flood exposure, with 18% ( n = 293,800) of the study-area catchment population estimated to reside within 0–50 m HAND in 2026. Our results demonstrate rapidly increasing exposure in Himalayan catchments and highlight the importance of validated, multi-temporal exposure datasets to inform disaster risk reduction.

Article.Title: An experimental study of source and engagement cues for susceptibility to dietary supplement misinformation
Article.Authors: Roovers H.; Adriaanse M.; Vos H.; van Gestel L.
Article.Abstract: Misinformation is increasingly recognized as a public health threat. Still, dietary supplements remain an underexplored domain despite widespread misinformation on social media and documented harms from misuse. This study examined susceptibility to dietary supplement misinformation and the influence of source type and social engagement cues. It was hypothesized that misinformation would be perceived as more reliable when attributed to a health professional (vs. influencers) and when accompanied by high (vs. low) engagement. It was also expected that these effects would be mediated by perceived source credibility and social consensus, respectively. To study this, a high-powered experimental study was conducted among 1,298 Dutch-speaking adults measuring perceived reliability across 10 mock social media posts about dietary supplements, including five misleading and five non-misleading claims, classified according to the Dutch Keuringsraad Claims Database. Posts varied by source (fictional health professional vs. fictional influencer) and engagement (low vs. high likes and comments; both between-participants manipulations). Results showed little differentiation in participants’ perceived reliability between misleading and non-misleading posts. Misleading claims attributed to health professionals were consistently evaluated as more reliable than those from influencers, an effect largely explained by perceived source credibility. However, social engagement cues did not influence reliability judgments of misleading posts and there was no mediation by social consensus. These findings suggest that individuals may struggle to distinguish misleading from non-misleading claims about dietary supplements on social media. This underscores the importance of credible sources and highlights the responsibility of health professionals when communicating about dietary supplements online.

Article.Title: Impedance based prediction of pulsed field ablation lesion depth without contact force
Article.Authors: Ren B.; Li W.; Li F.; Hu X.; Gong A.; Cao Y.; Li Z.; Zhou Y.; Xiao M.; Deng L.; Huang Y.; Zhu X.; Zeng R.
Article.Abstract: The lesion depth prediction index has been demonstrated to optimize ablation strategies. However, contact force-based prediction of lesion depth is difficult to integrate into multi-electrode catheters with complex shapes. This study developed and validated a contact force-independent pulsed-field ablation (PFA) index, the depth prediction index (DPI). Computer modeling identified parameters potentially affecting lesion formation. For in vivo experiments, six swine were assessed 2 h post-ablation to evaluate the difference between DPI and actual lesion depth, and two swine were assessed one month post-ablation to evaluate the difference. DPI predicted 131 of 156 lesions (84.0%) within 1.0 mm of measured depth, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.74, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.68 mm, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.56 mm. The DPI–depth association remained significant after adjustment for application number and within-animal clustering (adjusted coefficient, 0.628 mm; 95% CI, 0.505–0.751; P < 0.001). The DPI effectively predicts lesion depth without requiring contact force. This provides proof of feasibility for impedance-based prediction of PFA lesion depth and opens up a new direction for future lesion depth prediction in multi electrode PFA catheters.

Article.Title: Cannabidiol treatment of IL-6/eATP activated microglia and cortical neurons
Article.Authors: Yeisley D.; Ebbert K.; Culibrk R.; Hahn M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the present study, we investigate the effects of combined stimulation with IL-6 and extracellular adenosine triphosphate (eATP) – two inflammatory stimuli often increased in neuroinflammatory disorders – on human microglia inflammatory marker expression. We then evaluate the potential of cannabidiol (CBD) treatment to mitigate the resulting microglial activation state in monoculture as well as in coculture with induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cortical neuron-like cells. To characterize IL-6/eATP microglial activation relative to a canonical control, the human microglial cell line HMC3 was activated with either combined 5 ng/mL IL-6 and 1 mM eATP or with combined 100 ng/mL lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and 1 mM eATP. Proteomic measures of secreted cytokines/chemokines were performed and compared to unstimulated controls. To assess the impact of CBD on IL-6/eATP activated microglia, HMC3 cells were exposed to IL-6/eATP and then treated with varying concentrations of CBD (0.1 µM, 1 µM, and 5 µM) or with 10 µM dexamethasone (Dex) for 6 h and 24 h, after which inflammatory cytokines/chemokines as well as oxidative stress associated enzymes NOS2 and NOS3 were quantified. The CBD concentration identified as most effective in mitigating IL-6/eATP HMC3 activation was then applied to a coculture model of HMC3 microglia and iPSC-derived cortical neuron-like cells. IL-6/eATP and LPS/eATP differentially activated HMC3 microglia, with LPS/eATP exposure inducing increased IL-8, IL-6, CCL2, VEGF-A secretion and IL-6/eATP stimulation inducing increased IL-1β, IFNγ, CCL2, VEGF-A, and IL-10 secretion relative to unstimulated controls. Application of 1 µM CBD to HMC3 cultures following IL-6/eATP activation resulted in decreased IL-6, VEGF-A, and NOS2 production at 6 h as well as reduced IFNγ, IL-1β, and IL-6 production at 24 h. In HMC3 cocultures with cortical neuron-like cells, IL-6/eATP stimulation increased neuron levels of proinflammatory proteins TNFα, cellular C1q, and NOS2. It also decreased extracellular levels of inflammatory modulator soluble neuropilin-1 (sNRP-1) and increased neuron levels of the excitatory receptor scaffolding protein PSD-95 relative to the general synaptic marker synaptophysin (SYP). Application of 1 µM CBD for 24 h to IL-6/eATP stimulated cocultures resulted in neuronal TNFα levels, NOS2 levels, and PSD-95/SYP ratios which were statistically indistinguishable from unstimulated cocultures, although sNRP-1 and cell-associated C1q remained at activated levels. Cumulatively, these data indicate that 1 µM CBD partially mitigated IL-6/eATP-associated alterations to HMC3 microglia and cortical neuron-like cells in terms of the assessed inflammatory markers. These results provide insight into the effects of IL-6/eATP-mediated microglial activation and the potential therapeutic efficacy of CBD in attenuating these effects.

Article.Title: Intake of foods containing phytochemicals is correlated with benign prostatic hyperplasia development: a long-term follow-up study
Article.Authors: Nakamura T.; Shiotani A.; Yasui C.; Takeyama I.; Ishikawa H.
Article.Abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a progressive disease affecting middle-aged and older men. Some phytochemicals are believed to prevent the development of BPH. However, evidence to demonstrate this association in middle-aged men is scarce. This study determined how the intake of various plant foods containing phytochemicals is associated with BPH development. Prostatic volume (PV) data were available for 120 participants during a long-term, cohort follow-up study. Participants with maximum PV ≥ 30 mL were diagnosed with BPH. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified independent risk factors for BPH using dietary data at entry. Maximum PV was reached at age 79 in patients without BPH ( n = 62) and 76.5 in patients with BPH ( n = 58). Multivariate logistic regression revealed that the risk of developing BPH was significantly higher among individuals with the highest intake of onions, daikon radish, or fruits than among those with the lowest intake. The risk of developing BPH was significantly higher among groups with the highest intake of β-carotene, lutein, or quercetin than among those with the lowest intake. After adjusting for phytochemicals, the risk was significantly lower among participants with the highest intake of lycopene or soybean polyphenols than among those with the lowest intake. Consuming foods containing phytochemicals with estrogen-like effects or anti-estrogenic effects might be associated with BPH development. Further research, such as incorporating biomarkers, expanding the cohort, and conducting intervention trials, is required to clarify these findings. Clinical trial registration: No. UMIN000037735.

Article.Title: Comparison of carbon and nitrogen turnover in normally grown and deformed foraminifera
Article.Authors: Lintner M.; Goleń J.; Gawin-Grębla A.; Cavanaugh C.; Cyran N.; Holzmann M.; Wanek W.; Tyszka J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the feeding behavior of deformed and normal benthic foraminifera (Protista, Rhizaria) of the species Ammonia veneta . The degree of deformation was visualized by scanning electron and light microscopy. Food uptake and assimilation were quantified in undeformed, slight deformed (1–3 abnormal chambers), and heavy deformed (irregular coiling) individuals using isotopic labeling and confocal microscopy. Specimens were collected from the Belle Isle Marsh (Boston, USA) and maintained under controlled laboratory conditions. After a three-day incubation, slight deformed individuals showed food uptake and isotopic enrichment comparable to undeformed specimens. In contrast, heavy deformed foraminifera exhibited significantly reduced carbon and nitrogen assimilation, as well as a lower number of ingested food particles. Confocal observations further indicated reduced food processing in heavy deformed individuals. These results demonstrate that pronounced morphological deformities are associated with impaired feeding and assimilation performance. Our findings highlight that severe test deformation can substantially affect physiological functioning and should be carefully considered when selecting specimens for laboratory experiments or observing them in polluted areas.

Article.Title: MSAT-KOA-Net: a multi-scale attention transformer network with retrieval-augmented knowledge (RAG) for interpretable knee osteoarthritis grading
Article.Authors: Jiang S.; Xu B.; Venkatachalam K.; Siuly S.
Article.Abstract: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) has become the leading degenerative joint problem affecting humans across the world, causing disability among the elderly population. The radiographic evaluation of KOA is often performed using the Kellgren–Lawrence grading system; however, grading is subjective and depends on expertise. Recently, deep learning (DL) models have shown promising results for KOA diagnosis; however, these approaches have limitations in representing multi-scale anatomical features, focusing on joint regions of interest, modelling global relationships between features, and interpretability of results. In this paper, a novel Multi-Scale Attention Transformer Network (MSAT-KOA-Net) architecture has been proposed for accurate grading of knee osteoarthritis from radiographic images while maintaining interpretability of results. The proposed architecture combines an EfficientNet-B4 backbone network with a multi-scale feature fusion layer, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), and a joint space attention mechanism to achieve discriminative feature representation of knee joint structures. Furthermore, a transformer encoder is employed to encode global contextual relationships between the extracted features. Additionally, an ordinal focal loss function is used to effectively learn the ordered relationships of KL grades and address the class imbalance issue. In addition to classification, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) module is employed to improve the model’s interpretability by retrieving relevant medical knowledge from scientific literature via FAISS-based semantic search and generating contextual explanations with a large language model. The proposed MSAT-KOA-Net framework performance is evaluated with the knee X-ray dataset, and the results show that the proposed framework outperforms the baseline models with a validation accuracy of 80.09% and a Quadratic Weighted Kappa score of 0.8523, thus validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework for improving the classification of KOA severity and providing relevant explanations for the decision-making process, which is very helpful for the diagnosis of osteoarthritis.

Article.Title: An inter-row navigation system design for a safflower picking robot
Article.Authors: Gao G.; Guo H.; Zhou C.; Gui S.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate inter-row navigation for safflower harvesting robots remains challenging in curved crop rows due to nonlinear terrain effects, sensor uncertainties, and limited interaction awareness between robots and crops. To address these issues, this study proposes a multi-sensor fusion navigation framework integrating GNSS, IMU, wheel encoders, and a nearside divider pressure sensor. A pure pursuit-based kinematic model is combined with an adaptive fuzzy PID controller to achieve global trajectory tracking, while a pressure-based local correction mechanism is introduced to incorporate crop–robot interaction feedback for local path adjustment under curved-row conditions. Field experiments demonstrate that the proposed system achieves a steady-state tracking error below 40 mm at 1 km/h, with steady-state errors ranging from 33 to 42 mm across different initial conditions. In the tested curved-row scenario, the proposed method maintains an average tracking error below 70 mm, indicating that pressure-based local feedback can contribute to trajectory correction under curved-row conditions. Comparative evaluations against PID, pure pursuit, and fuzzy PID controllers confirm that the proposed framework significantly improves tracking accuracy and adaptability in nonlinear agricultural environments. Ablation results further verify that the pressure-based interaction module is a critical contributor to performance improvement in curved-row navigation. The results demonstrate that integrating global navigation with local physical interaction feedback provides a robust and practical solution for autonomous inter-row agricultural operation in complex field environments.
