Article.Title: Structural instability and emerging energy–GDP decoupling in Saudi Arabia: exploratory evidence and forecasting implications
Article.Authors: Alnagar D.; Mohamed E.; Al-Shammry H.; Aljawni S.
Article.Abstract: Energy-demand relationships in resource-dependent economies may change when macroeconomic shocks, policy reforms, and structural transformation alter consumption patterns. This study provides an exploratory assessment of structural instability, energy–GDP decoupling, and energy-demand forecasting in Saudi Arabia using annual data from 1990 to 2023. Bai–Perron tests are applied under alternative specifications to identify endogenous changes in per capita energy consumption, while a policy-motivated test at 2016 evaluates whether the year associated with the launch of Vision 2030 is linked to a change in the energy–GDP relationship. The results indicate substantial structural instability in Saudi Arabia’s per capita energy-consumption trajectory. Major breaks are identified in the mid-1990s or early 2000s and around 2009, depending on the structural-break specification, with the 2009 breakpoint remaining robust across alternative models. In contrast, 2016 is not selected endogenously as a dominant breakpoint. A policy-motivated test at 2016 suggests a possible change in the energy–GDP relationship under conventional inference, although the evidence weakens after accounting for serial correlation. Break-adjusted cointegration results are interpreted as exploratory because of the short annual sample and uncertain integration properties. The decoupling analysis shows a descriptive change after 2016. During 2017–2023, real GDP per capita increased while per capita energy consumption declined, indicating strong decoupling. By contrast, the earlier period was characterised by strong negative decoupling. Forecasting comparisons indicate that models incorporating more recent observations produced lower forecast errors than the model estimated exclusively from pre-2016 data. Predictions incorporating realised real GDP per capita and Brent oil prices are interpreted as conditional ex post forecasts rather than fully operational ex ante forecasts. Overall, the findings provide exploratory evidence of substantial structural instability and an emerging energy–GDP decoupling pattern in Saudi Arabia. They do not establish a causal effect of Vision 2030 or demonstrate a permanent new energy regime. The results emphasise the importance of cautious interpretation, transparent data and code, and regularly updated break-aware models for energy-demand forecasting in resource-dependent economies.

Article.Title: Association between early postoperative acetaminophen exposure and acute kidney injury across surgical cohorts: a retrospective analysis of the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; Liu A.; Chen X.; Dang L.; Gao J.; Gao H.; Ma X.
Article.Abstract: The association between early postoperative acetaminophen exposure and acute kidney injury (AKI) remains uncertain. We evaluated this association across major surgical cohorts using the MIMIC-IV database. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 19,938 adult ICU patients undergoing cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, or neurosurgical procedures. Acetaminophen exposure was defined as at least one oral or intravenous administration within 0–48 h after surgery, and the primary outcome was AKI within 7 postoperative days. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were adjusted for demographic characteristics, surgical type, illness severity, renal function, comorbidities, and concomitant nephrotoxic medication exposure. Interaction analyses and sensitivity analyses, including a 48-hour landmark analysis and multiple imputation, were additionally performed. Acetaminophen exposure was associated with lower odds of postoperative AKI overall (OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.71–0.82; P < 0.001) and in cardiovascular (OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.68–0.83), gastrointestinal (OR = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78–0.99), and hepatobiliary surgery (OR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.54–0.88), but not neurosurgery (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.55–1.18). The overall Cox model yielded a similar association (HR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.73–0.82; P < 0.001). Associations differed by surgical type (global interaction P < 0.001), while exploratory interaction analysis suggested heterogeneity by SOFA category ( P = 0.021). In the 48-hour landmark analysis, the association remained evident overall and in the gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary cohorts, but not in the cardiovascular or neurosurgical cohorts. Early postoperative acetaminophen exposure was associated with lower observed AKI occurrence, although the findings varied by surgical context and were sensitive to exposure timing. The gastrointestinal association persisted in the landmark analysis but was no longer statistically significant after multiple imputation, whereas the hepatobiliary association was more consistent across sensitivity analyses.

Article.Title: Assessing the genetic diversity in potato genotypes to enhance yield and quality in temperate region of Kashmir valley
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Singh N.; Hussain K.; Thakur S.; Ali G.; Sharma S.; Rehan N/A.
Article.Abstract: Potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) is a food crop of a global significance, and the production of high yielding cultivars that matches a specific agro-climate, is important to achieve food security. This study explored the genetic variability, association of traits and phylogenetic variation available in 53 genotypes of potato, which were grown in temperate environment of Kashmir valley in India. Statistically significant genotypic variation was observed for all the 19 quantitative and qualitative traits that were observed. Notably, traits like tuber yield (q/ha), total phenolic content and protein content showed high phenotypic and genotypic coefficients of variation and heritability with substantial genetic advance, indicating strong additive gene action, proving that direct selection for these characters can yield progress in both yield and quality traits. The correlation studies reflected a significant positive relationship between the yield of tuber and percent emergence, plant height. Further path coefficient analysis identified the number of tubers plant − 1 as the primary contributor to tuber yield, followed by average tuber weight and plant height, establishing these parameters as vital selection criteria for yield enhancement. Mahalanobis D 2 analysis grouped the genotypes into four different clusters. The maximum inter-cluster distance observed between Clusters II and IV highlights substantial genetic distinctness suitable for exploiting heterosis. Integrating high-yielding genotypes (SKAU-P-9, CR-7, and SKAU-P-6) with quality-rich genotypes (K. Neelkanth, Gulmarg Special, and P-81) provides a strategic foundation for targeted hybridization. Utilizing these distinct parental lines will facilitate the development of high-yielding, nutritionally superior, and climate-resilient cultivars tailored for temperate regions.

Article.Title: Development of an open-access interactive tool for multi-index agricultural and environmental analysis using Landsat and Sentinel-2 on Google Earth Engine
Article.Authors: Ayek A.; Alshahrani N.; Elassal M.; Loho M.; Qaid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate and timely monitoring of vegetation health, soil conditions, surface water dynamics, and agricultural drought is essential for sustainable land management and food security. However, access to satellite based analytical tools remains constrained by technical barriers, including programming requirements, platform account dependencies, and fragmented analytical capabilities across specialized applications. This study presents an open access interactive tool developed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud computing platform, enabling users to extract and analyze more than forty spectral indices from Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel 2 imagery without programming expertise or a personal GEE account. The tool integrates vegetation, water, soil, chlorophyll sensitive Red Edge, and thermal drought indices, including the Vegetation Health Index (VHI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), and Temperature Condition Index (TCI) derived from Landsat thermal infrared bands, within a unified browser based interface that provides interactive raster maps, time series profiles, statistical histograms, and GeoTIFF and CSV export options. Cloud and shadow contamination are addressed using QA PIXEL masking for Landsat and the Cloud Score + algorithm for Sentinel 2, while optional Path/Row and MGRS tile filtering ensures temporal consistency in time series analyses by restricting input imagery to a single scene footprint. The tool's performance was demonstrated through four case studies: multi temporal vegetation expansion monitoring in the Toshka Canal region, Egypt (2020 to 2025); crop growth and land cover discrimination in an agricultural area west of Wuhan, China; flood extent mapping following the February 2023 earthquake in northwestern Syria; and an eleven year (2015 to 2025) agricultural drought assessment in the Al Ghab Plain, Syria, using integrated VHI and Land Surface Temperature records. Results confirm the tool's reliability and flexibility across diverse environmental and geographic contexts. Compared with existing platforms, including GEE PICX, Sentinel Hub, and NASA AppEEARS, the tool is distinguished by its integration of thermal drought monitoring, Red Edge chlorophyll indices, interactive time series analytics, and unrestricted open access without subscription requirements.

Article.Title: Conservation agriculture optimizes soil nitrogen stabilization and availability to crops under rice-based cropping
Article.Authors: Mukherjee S.; Sarkar D.; Kanthal S.; Mandal B.
Article.Abstract: Conservation agriculture (CA) is increasingly promoted in the Indo-Gangetic Plains to address sustainability challenges in soil-plant-environment system. Efficient nitrogen (N) management plan under CA is one of those challenges, which restricts its wider adoption. We hypothesized that appropriate CA management option optimizes the balance between soil N stabilization and N availability to crops. To evaluate this, a field experiment was conducted with 15 treatments involving three tillage practices [i.e., zero tillage, reduced tillage, and conventional tillage] and five residue+nutrient combinations [0% residue + 100% NPK, 100% residue + 50% NPK, 100% residue + 75% NPK, 50% residue + 100% NPK, and 50% residue + 75% NPK] in a rice-wheat-green gram rotation. After three years, the changes in soil organic [hydrolyzable (amino acid, amino sugar, hydrolyzable ammonium, serine+threonine and hydrolyzable unknown) and non-hydrolyzable] and inorganic N fractions, N stabilization and N availability to crops were assessed. Observations showed that zero tillage or minimum tillage combined with 50–100% rice residue retention and 75–100% NPK enhanced N sequestration in soils, preferentially by increasing organic N content (16 to 24%). Besides, these CA practices stabilized N in soils by increasing the ratio of organic to inorganic N (61 to 106%) and non-hydrolyzable to hydrolyzable N (3 to 42%) and maintained N availability to crops by increasing hydrolyzable N fractions [i.e., potentially mineralizable fractions including amino acid, amino sugar and hydrolyzable ammonium (6 to 28%)]. Optimizing N stabilization and availability to crops under intensive cropping, this study provides choices for the selection of appropriate CA practice(s) by farmers and policymakers.

Article.Title: Pre-diagnostic low muscle mass and sarcopenia associated with subsequent cancer in Chinese adults: a longitudinal CHARLS study
Article.Authors: Zhao W.; Wu X.; Cheng X.; Zhao N.; Xu H.; Cao D.
Article.Abstract: Loss of skeletal muscle may reflect systemic physiological compromise before cancer is clinically recognized. We examined whether low muscle mass, sarcopenia, and deterioration in these phenotypes were associated with subsequent first self-reported cancer in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. We analyzed China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) data from 2011 to 2020. Adults aged 45 years or older who reported no cancer in 2011 were eligible. The primary pre-diagnostic risk set excluded first cancer reports in 2013 or 2015, ensuring that 2015 muscle status preceded cancer reporting in 2018 or 2020. Low muscle mass was defined as height-adjusted appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM/height²) < 6.8 kg/m² in men or < 5.69 kg/m² in women. Low muscle strength was defined as grip strength < 28 kg in men or < 18 kg in women. Sarcopenia was identified using the composite c2015_sarcopenia indicator according to the prespecified sarcopenia definition. The analysis variables were c2015_lowmusclemass and c2015_sarcopenia (0 = no, 1 = yes, null=unknown/unavailable). The primary analysis used wave-based Cox regression with censoring at the last observed cancer-status wave. Models adjusted for demographic factors, smoking, drinking, hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia; expanded sensitivity models additionally considered baseline body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and 2011–2015 weight change. Firth logistic models and a 2020-only longer-lag analysis assessed rare-event robustness. Among 10,407 cancer-free participants at baseline, 254 first reported cancer during follow-up; 212 first reported cancer in 2018 or 2020. Only 22 participants in the pre-diagnostic risk set had cancer status missing at both target waves and were not classified as cancer-free. In the primary Cox models, 2015 low muscle mass (hazard ratio [HR] 2.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10–3.71; P = 0.023) and sarcopenia (HR 2.33, 95% CI 1.17–4.66; P = 0.016) were associated with later first cancer reporting. Cumulative reporting was 3.39% versus 1.87% for participants with versus without low muscle mass and 4.00% versus 1.90% for those with versus without sarcopenia. In four-level transition models, new/worsened low muscle mass (HR 3.45, 95% CI 1.44–8.25) and new/worsened sarcopenia (HR 4.31, 95% CI 1.80-10.32) showed the strongest associations. The findings remained directionally consistent after expanded confounder adjustment and in longer-lag Firth analyses. Low muscle mass and worsening sarcopenia measured before a first cancer report were associated with subsequent self-reported cancer. Given the low absolute event rates, self-reported outcome, residual confounding, and possibility of occult cancer preceding recognition, these findings support a pre-diagnostic vulnerability phenotype rather than a causal or screening interpretation.

Article.Title: A federated learning framework for Non-IID data : data feature optimization and personalization strategy
Article.Authors: Nie L.; Wang J.; Hu N.
Article.Abstract: Federated learning is an emerging distributed machine learning paradigm that enables multiple edge devices to collaboratively train task-specific models while preserving data privacy. However, the non-independent and identically distributed nature of client data often leads to client drift, slow convergence, and degraded model performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-stage collaborative optimization framework for federated learning under Non-IID settings. Specifically, the proposed framework first employs feature distillation to construct noise-perturbed proxy data for cross-client knowledge interaction. Then, to reduce proxy data redundancy and accelerate model convergence, an entropy-based dynamic selection mechanism is designed to prioritize informative proxy samples for local training. At the communication level, a partial parameter selection strategy is proposed to dynamically distinguish shared parameters from personalized parameters according to parameter update magnitude. In this way, only shared parameters are uploaded to the server for aggregation, while personalized parameters are retained locally, thereby reducing unnecessary communication transmission. In addition, a late-stage personalized fine-tuning strategy is further introduced to enhance the model’s adaptability to local client data distributions. Experimental results on multiple benchmark Non-IID datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing baseline methods, achieving up to 6.87% higher classification accuracy while effectively reducing the number of communication rounds required to reach the target performance. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving model performance, accelerating convergence, and reducing communication overhead.

Article.Title: DIC-based strain evolution of HRB500E reinforcing-bar upset straight-threaded sleeve splices under monotonic and cyclic loading
Article.Authors: Ran X.; Lu Y.; Ma K.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the strength, deformation recovery, and local load-transfer behavior of upset straight-threaded sleeve couplers for HRB500E reinforcing bars under monotonic and cyclic loading, 54 specimens with nominal bar diameters of 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, and 25 mm were tested. The program included monotonic tension, high-stress cyclic tension–compression, and large-deformation cyclic tension–compression tests. Extensometers were used to measure residual deformation and total elongation at maximum force, while digital image correlation was employed to characterize sleeve surface strain fields. Under monotonic tension, all specimens failed by fracture of the parent bar outside the sleeve. The mean tensile strengths ranged from 720.46 to 771.72 MPa, residual deformations were below 0.075 mm, and total elongations at maximum force ranged from 11.57 to 17.56%. After high-stress cyclic loading, specimens with bar diameters of 16–25 mm exhibited mean tensile strengths of 735.80–754.27 MPa and residual deformations of 0.0030–0.0877 mm, whereas buckling occurred in the unsupported bar segment of some 14 mm specimens. Under large-deformation cyclic loading, the 16–25 mm specimens retained high tensile strength after the prescribed cycles, while the 14 mm specimens showed greater buckling susceptibility and some 25 mm specimens exhibited pinching near zero load. Digital image correlation revealed relatively continuous sleeve strain distributions in bar-fracture specimens, but pronounced compressive strain concentration on the buckling side. These results provide experimental evidence for evaluating the splice-level performance of high-strength reinforcing-bar mechanical couplers and may provide useful guidance for connection detailing and their potential application in seismic structural systems.

Article.Title: Injection-rate histories and well placement influence fault yielding during CO2 geological storage
Article.Authors: Cui Z.; Liu D.; Li S.; Li X.; Peng R.; Jiao X.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Safe CO 2 storage requires injection designs that manage both when faults yield and how yielding spreads, yet temporal schedules and well layouts are often evaluated separately. We developed a two-dimensional quasi-static hydromechanical model of immiscible CO 2 –brine flow around an offset normal fault and compared constant and variable-rate histories, well-placement configurations, and well–fault distances over 30 d. Coulomb failure function (CFF) threshold attainment with frictional weakening defined modeled onset; failure-area ratio and maximum shear plastic strain served as within-mesh comparative indicators of domain-scale localization. The simulations reveal a hierarchy of controls: injection rate primarily governs pressure buildup and onset timing; rate history reorganizes transient stress paths and localization; and well placement and distance redistribute pressure and yielding across the fault. Higher rates increased the within-mesh failure-area ratio, whereas variable histories produced distinct responses that cannot be attributed to cycling alone because peak rate and shut-in transitions were confounded. Local threshold indicators and domain-scale metrics were complementary rather than interchangeable: temporal onset, spatial extent and deformation intensity were distinct response dimensions. These findings motivate joint optimization of injection schedules and well layouts against both temporal onset and spatial localization, while providing model-scale guidance for early quasi-static risk screening rather than predictions of seismicity, dynamic rupture or long-term stability.

Article.Title: Task-oriented RT-DETR adaptation for minute cigarette detection in complex laboratory scenes
Article.Authors: Hao J.; Shi G.; Li X.; Cui X.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Detecting minute cigarettes in complex laboratory surveillance scenes is challenging because of their small scale, partial occlusion, weak visual cues, cluttered backgrounds, and sensitivity to bounding-box deviations. This study develops a task-oriented adaptation of the Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR). Receptive Field Attention Convolution (RFAConv) is integrated into the ResNet-18 backbone, High-Low Frequency Attention (HiLo) is applied to high-level intra-scale interaction, and the existing Inner-MPDIoU formulation replaces GIoU as the intersection-over-union-based regression objective. Across three training runs, the complete model achieves an mAP@50 of $$89.6 \pm 0.4$$ % and an mAP@50:95 of $$50.2 \pm 0.2$$ %, compared with $$82.9 \pm 0.4$$ % and $$45.1 \pm 0.5$$ % for RT-DETR-R18. On an independent 150-image hold-out set, it achieves $$85.8 \pm 0.2$$ % mAP@50 and $$46.2 \pm 0.1$$ % mAP@50:95, exceeding the baseline values of $$77.2 \pm 0.2$$ % and $$41.7 \pm 0.3$$ %. In batch-one end-to-end inference on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti, the model achieves 18 ms per frame and 56 FPS, with 3.4 GB peak GPU-memory occupancy. Although computation increases from 58.3 to 98.3 GFLOPs, the results demonstrate improved detection and hold-out performance while retaining practical workstation-level inference efficiency.

Article.Title: BBCH-based phenological modeling of camelina under contrasting irrigation, nitrogen, and camelina–chickpea cropping patterns
Article.Authors: Somarin S.; Mohammadvand E.; Mohsenabadi G.; Majidian M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phenological responses of camelina to management were evaluated using days after planting (DAP) and cumulative growing degree days (GDD) at nine main BBCH stages. A two-year split-plot factorial experiment included two irrigation regimes, two nitrogen rates, seven camelina-containing cropping patterns, and three replications. For each stage, DAP was modeled from GDD and design covariates using multiple linear regression, quadratic regression, random forest (RF), support vector regression, and an artificial neural network. Supplemental irrigation was associated with stage-dependent differences in DAP and GDD, with lower values at BBCH 0–3 and higher values at BBCH 5–9; however, early-stage differences before irrigation application should not be interpreted as direct causal responses to irrigation. The higher nitrogen treatment (46 kg N ha⁻¹) was associated with greater DAP and GDD than the 11.5 kg N ha⁻¹ treatment at the observed stages; however, because the additional 34.5 kg N ha⁻¹ was applied only at 50 and 100 days after sowing, differences observed before these applications (particularly BBCH 0–3) should be interpreted as statistical differences among assigned nitrogen treatments rather than causal responses to the additional nitrogen. At BBCH 5, the nitrogen response depended on year and irrigation. Mixed cropping had the highest GDD throughout, whereas the lowest GDD occurred in sole camelina at BBCH 0–3 and in the 3:3 replacement pattern at BBCH 5–9. RF provided the best stage-specific predictive performance, with a macro-averaged performance of R² = 0.972, MAE = 0.23 d, and RMSE = 0.40 d, demonstrating strong agreement between predicted and observed phenological timing under the evaluated experimental conditions The resulting BBCH–GDD framework supports local phenological monitoring but does not support inferences about yield, product quality, resource-use efficiency, or economic performance.

Article.Title: Enhancing the accuracy of qPCR normalization in Bactrocera zonata: A systematic study for the selection of condition-optimized reference genes for gene expression studies
Article.Authors: Suman T.; Selvamani S.; Reddy N.; Ashok K.; Ramasamy G.; Mohan M.; Peter A.; Venkatesan T.
Article.Abstract: Bactrocera zonata (Diptera: Tephritidae) is a highly destructive polyphagous pest that infests a wide range of economically important fruit crops. Understanding its growth, development, reproduction, and responses to environmental stresses is essential for developing effective management strategies. Gene expression analysis is an important approach for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying these biological processes. Quantitative PCR (qPCR) is widely used for gene expression analysis but requires validated reference genes for accurate normalization. This study evaluated the expression stability of eight candidate reference genes ( GAPDH , G6PDH , TUBA1A , TUBB , RPL19 , EEF1A2 , SOD , and ATP6V0A1 ) across six biological and experimental conditions: sex, tissues, developmental stages, gamma irradiation, temperature stress, and dsRNA treatment. Stability was assessed using the comparative delta-Ct and standard deviation method, geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, and RefFinder. GAPDH showed the highest stability under gamma irradiation and dsRNA treatment, TUBA1A across developmental stages and temperature stress, RPL19 between adult males and females, and TUBB across tissues. These findings demonstrate condition-dependent reference-gene stability and provide validated reference genes for reliable qPCR normalization in B. zonata .

Article.Title: Improving DDoS detection in cloud computing through deep learning and feature fusion with TWBO optimization
Article.Authors: Nagarajan S.; Murugaiyan S.; Devaraj P.; Elwin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack is considered a subclass of Denial of Service (DoS) that causes the severity of the attack in the cloud environment, and the actual service of the network is disturbed by several malicious attempts. One of the general forms of attack is a DDoS attack, which leads to substantial harm and negatively impacts the efficiency of cloud services. Hence, the hybrid Sequential Convolutional Neural Network with Taylor’s Wolf Bird Optimization (SCNN-TWBO) is introduced. The cloud is simulated initially, where the attacker stops the valid users from accessing a specific network resource through a DDoS attack. Here, recorded log files are sourced and normalized by the Max-Min Normalization algorithm. Then, the features are fused by Spearman’s Rank Correlation Coefficient (SRCC) and Deep Neural Network (DNN). Next, fused features are augmented, and the DDoS attack detection is done by SCNN-TWBO. SCNN is trained by the TWBO, which is the integration of Taylor Series and Wolf Bird Optimization (WBO). The superior analytical findings are recorded by the BoT-IoT dataset, while the newly developed SCNN-TWBO acquired 92.88% of accuracy, 94.88% of True Positive Rate (TPR), and 90.88% of True Negative Rate (TNR) for 90% of the learning data.

Article.Title: Five-year survival following endoscopic submucosal dissection and gastrectomy in older early gastric cancer patients in the U.S.
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Lee S.; Sun J.; Choi K.; Choi D.; Choi E.; Chae H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gastric cancer remains a major global cancer burden and continues to contribute to cancer-related morbidity and mortality in the U.S. It predominantly affects older adults, with a median age at diagnosis of approximately 68 years and nearly 60% of cases occurring in individuals aged 65 years or older. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) may offer a less invasive alternative to gastrectomy for older patients with early-stage gastric cancer, but U.S.-based evidence remains limited, particularly with respect to outcomes stratified by invasion depth (T1a vs. T1b) and among the oldest age groups (75–79, ≥80). Using the 2022 National Cancer Database, we identified patients aged ≥75 years with first primary T1N0 gastric cancer (2004–2022) treated with ESD or gastrectomy. Propensity score full matching was used to balance demographic, clinical, tumor, and facility characteristics. Weighted Cox models estimated 5-year overall mortality, stratified by invasion depth and age group. Among 2,405 patients, 671 (27.9%) underwent ESD and 1,734 (72.1%) underwent gastrectomy. Gastrectomy was not associated with different mortality compared with ESD among patients aged 75–79 with T1a disease (hazard ratio [HR], 1.80; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.71–4.57), T1b disease (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.20–1.21), or patients aged ≥80 with T1a disease (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.58–1.78). However, among patients aged ≥80 with T1b disease, gastrectomy was associated with higher mortality (HR, 2.40; 95% CI, 1.23–4.71). In this nationwide cohort of older U.S. patients with early-stage gastric cancer, gastrectomy was associated with higher mortality among patients aged ≥80 with T1b disease. These findings support consideration of less invasive approaches in selected oldest-old patients.

Article.Title: Associations between early antidepressant exposure, affective states, and subjective sleep quality among euthymic depressive-onset bipolar patients: a cross-sectional parallel mediation analysis
Article.Authors: Ma J.; Liang S.; Wang M.; Yang C.
Article.Abstract: Bipolar Disorder (BD) is often misdiagnosed as major depressive disorder, leading to prolonged antidepressant use during the early stages. Antidepressant treatment has shown significant effects on affective states and sleep. However, the relationship between early antidepressant use, affective states, and sleep quality has yet to be explored in the BD population. A cross-sectional, single-blind study was conducted in Tianjin Anding Hospital between 1st September 2020 and 30th May 2023. BD patients were categorized into antidepressant treatment (AT) and non-antidepressant treatment (NT) groups based on whether they received early-stage systematic antidepressant treatment. Affective states and subjective sleep quality were measured using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), respectively. Spearman’s correlation examined associations among antidepressant use, affective states, and sleep; mediation effects of affective states were analyzed using a bootstrap method. A total of 124 participants were included. Descriptive statistics showed that the AT group had higher PSQI scores than the NT group (Z = − 5.414, p < 0.001). Preliminary correlation analysis revealed positive correlations between systematic antidepressant use and both scores of PSQI (r = 0.488, p < 0.001) and negative affect (NA) (r = 0.216, p = 0.016). Mediation analysis showed positive correlations between early antidepressant use and scores of PSQI (β = 0.8035, p < 0.001) and NA (β = 0.3804, p = 0.0297), while positive affect scores were negatively correlated with PSQI scores (β = − 0.1968, p = 0.0229). The total effect of antidepressant use on sleep quality was significant (95% bootstrap CI = 1.2940, 3.0595). The indirect effect of early antidepressant use on sleep quality through affective states was not significant (95% bootstrap CI = − 0.2190, 0.3602), but the direct effect was significant (95% bootstrap CI = 1.2467, 3.0220). Early systematic antidepressant use in the cohort is associated with poor subjective sleep quality and higher levels of NA, even in the euthymic phase, emphasizing the need for cautious early use of antidepressants in treating BD and the importance of early diagnosis.

Article.Title: A real-time validated improved voltage stabilizer with model predictive control–based hybrid energy storage optimization
Article.Authors: Mohanty A.; Ramasamy A.; Mohanty S.; Rajamony R.; Allasi H.; Alzahrani S.; Bhutto J.; Vayalpurayil T.
Article.Abstract: This work introduces an improved voltage stabilizer (IVS) architecture that combines a model predictive control (MPC)-based power system stabilizer (PSS) with a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to increase voltage stability in microgrids. The proposed IVS–MPC architecture manages the active power support of batteries and super capacitors to efficiently reduce voltage fluctuations caused by renewable energy sources that aren’t always available and quickly changing loads. The stabilizer uses MPC’s ability to forecast future events to anticipate possible problems and change the HESS’s charging and discharging activities in real time, allowing for quick remedial control actions. This predictive and coordinated control system makes both steady-state voltage regulation and transient voltage recovery better.The battery unit mostly deals with long-term power imbalances, while the super capacitor makes up for short-term changes, thus the system can adapt quickly to changes over a range of time scales. The control method also has an optimization layer that figures out the best power contribution from each storage component. This makes better use of energy and cuts down on wasteful battery cycling.The OPAL-RT platform was used to test the proposed IVS–MPC method in real time, which showed that it worked. When compared to traditional PSS and voltage stabilizer designs, the suggested method shows better performance in terms of reducing voltage deviation, faster settling time, and better damping when the load changes. Both simulated and real-time experimental results show that the IVS-assisted HESS coordination greatly improves the microgrid’s ability to regulate voltage.

Article.Title: Early neuromuscular and cognitive signatures in high-performance young male Muay Thai athletes
Article.Authors: Chainok P.; Vongjaturapat N.; Suwannawat N.; Yongtawee A.; Lin J.; Zacca R.; Fernandes R.; Vilas-Boas J.
Article.Abstract: Understanding developmental changes in neuromuscular and cognitive function is essential for evidence-based talent identification in striking sports. This study investigated age-related anthropometric, maturational, neuromuscular and cognitive characteristics in 215 high-performance young male Muay Thai athletes aged 8–18 years using a multivariate approach. Athletes completed a five-day evaluation including biological maturation profiling, anthropometry, training and competition history, computerized cognitive assessment and upper- and lower-limb neuromuscular testing. One-way ANOVA and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) revealed distinct developmental patterns across the four age groups. Anthropometric characteristics, maturity status, maximal strength and several cognitive measures improved significantly with age (all p < 0.05), whereas limb asymmetry, fatigue indices, Nordic hamstring exercise performance, lower-limb dynamic strength index and upper-limb push-up force showed no age-related differences. Exploratory PCA demonstrated excellent factorability (KMO = 0.89–0.95; Bartlett's χ 2 = 2008.74–5231.22, all p < 0.001). Across the entire cohort, neuromuscular performance was represented by a single strength-related component explaining 48.31% of the variance, whereas cognitive performance comprised two components explaining 76.29% of the cumulative variance. Age-specific exploratory PCA indicated differences in multidimensional neuromuscular and cognitive performance profiles across age groups. Collectively, these findings indicate age-associated differences in neuromuscular and cognitive performance profiles among young male Muay Thai athletes.

Article.Title: Investigation of the effect of gamma radiation on the mechanical properties of nanoclay-reinforced composite plates
Article.Authors: Erbilgin E.; Örçen G.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the effect of gamma radiation on the mechanical properties of pure and nanoclay-reinforced glass fiber/epoxy composite plates with nanoclay added of 0.75 wt%, 1 wt%, and 1.25 wt% was experimentally investigated. The composite plates were fabricated using the hand lay-up method and irradiated at approximately 10 and 20 kGy doses using a Co-60 gamma radiation source. Tensile, compressive, and shear tests were conducted on both irradiated and non-irradiated specimens in accordance with ASTM D3039, ASTM D6641, and ASTM D7078 standards, respectively. The resulting mechanical properties were determined and compared. The experimental results showed that the addition of nanoclay improved all mechanical properties of the composites, and the highest mechanical performance was obtained in specimens with 1.25 wt% nanoclay added. As the gamma radiation dose increased, a decrease in mechanical properties occurred; however, the changes in tensile strength and elastic modulus were found to be limited. In contrast, the shear strength and shear modulus were determined to be more significantly affected by gamma radiation. Nevertheless, the Poisson’s ratio was observed to be unaffected by the applied radiation doses. The tensile strength, compressive strength, shear strength, elastic modulus, and shear modulus values obtained from specimens with 1.25 wt% nanoclay content exposed to a 20 kGy gamma radiation dose were 1.19%, 5.02%, 19.9%, 0.70%, and 7.06% lower, respectively, compared to those obtained from specimens with the same nanoclay added that were not exposed to gamma radiation. These findings may provide reference data for the evaluation of nanoclay-reinforced glass fiber/epoxy composites for structural applications in radiation environments within the investigated low-dose gamma irradiation range of 10 and 20 kGy.

Article.Title: SAR object detection via adaptive shift-wise downsampling and frequency-spatially modulated feature fusion
Article.Authors: Hu H.; Liu J.; Liu X.; Tao J.; Chen L.; Shi Z.; Li P.
Article.Abstract: Object detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is challenged by speckle noise, background clutter, and large variations in target scale. We present ASCE-SAR, a YOLO11-based detector that coordinates adaptive shift-wise downsampling with frequency-spatially modulated multi-scale fusion. In the backbone, the Adaptive Downsampling with Shift-Wise Convolution (ADSC) block combines structure-preserving downsampling and enlarged receptive-field modeling. In the neck, Dynamic Shift-wise Feature Fusion (DSFF) uses content-aware resampling and frequency-spatial modulation to improve cross-scale feature alignment and weak-target representation. On the OGSOD-1.0 and HRSID test sets, ASCE-SAR achieves AP values of 59.9% and 67.9%, respectively, corresponding to gains of 7.1 and 1.8 percentage points over the YOLO11 Baseline under the same evaluation protocol. Under synthetic Gamma speckle perturbations on HRSID, the full model retains a 0.8–2.0 percentage-point mAP \(_{50{:}95}\) advantage over the Baseline across the clean condition and the evaluated noise levels. The full model contains 3.17 M parameters and requires 14.94 GFLOPS; its profiling results are reported with forward latency and peak memory to make the accuracy-cost trade-off explicit. These results indicate improved detection accuracy and noise-perturbed performance, accompanied by a measurable computational cost.

Article.Title: Control of variable power low voltage ride-through and imbalance under abnormal voltage conditions in grid-tied photovoltaic inverters
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Zhu H.; Wang E.; Xu H.; Yao L.; Ji B.
Article.Abstract: Grid connection is a key aspect of the stable operation of PV systems, and traditional grid connection methods rely on PV inverters. Existing power electronic hardware still faces challenges in providing sufficient transient support while maintaining stable power output under grid fault conditions. To address this, this paper proposes an improved fault ride-through control strategy for PV inverters. First, by adjusting the PV cell power tracking trajectory, the voltage at the battery end is effectively reduced, minimizing the generation of excess energy, thereby avoiding Direct Current (DC) bus overvoltage and grid current overcurrent, and achieving power balance on both sides of the inverter. Secondly, a current reference generator is used, combined with the inverter control algorithm and positive–negative sequence current inner loop control, to calculate current commands, achieving current balance and power stability. Then, a quantitative relationship between the power reference setpoint and current peak threshold is established through the power reference generator, guiding the inverter’s power reference setting under unbalanced voltage conditions. Finally, simulation verification is conducted based on the Rtlab platform. This strategy effectively improves the stability and reliability of PV inverters under grid fault conditions.

Article.Title: Assessment of uncertainty estimation and distillation for reliable 3D dental mesh segmentation in orthodontics
Article.Authors: Krenmayr L.; von Schwerin R.; Schaudt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The integration of deep learning into computer-aided orthodontic treatment planning has enabled automated tasks such as tooth segmentation from 3D dental models. However, the reliability of these systems remains a concern due to their black-box nature and tendency toward overconfident predictions. In this work, we present a comprehensive evaluation of uncertainty estimation methods for tooth segmentation on 3D intraoral scans. We investigate several state-of-the-art neural network architectures combined with uncertainty estimation techniques including predictive entropy, Monte Carlo dropout, test-time augmentation, deep ensembles, and evidential deep learning. Evaluation on the Teeth3DS benchmark, supplemented with synthetically incomplete scans and a custom out-of-distribution dataset, shows that sampling-based approaches, particularly deep ensembles, provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates. In contrast, entropy-based methods and evidential deep learning often produce overconfident predictions and fail to identify major segmentation errors. We further demonstrate that uncertainty estimation can detect out-of-distribution samples such as scans with artifacts or missing regions. Although deep ensembles provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates, their computational cost limits practical deployment. We therefore investigate uncertainty distillation and show that a single student model can achieve ensemble-like uncertainty quality with only one forward pass.

Article.Title: Indirect associations of perceived teacher autonomy support with dimensions of learning burnout through academic stress and self-efficacy among engineering students
Article.Authors: Zhao H.; Li J.; Zhang J.; Guan Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Learning burnout poses a major challenge in higher education, particularly in project-based and high-demand disciplines. Perceived teacher autonomy support may be associated with lower learning burnout, but the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined the associations among perceived teacher autonomy support, academic stress, academic self-efficacy, and three dimensions of learning burnout in 841 university students majoring in civil engineering and engineering cost. Structural equation modeling showed that perceived teacher autonomy support had significant negative indirect associations with dejection, improper behavior, and reduced personal accomplishment through academic stress. The indirect association through academic self-efficacy was significant only for reduced personal accomplishment. Multi-group analyses further showed that the association between perceived teacher autonomy support and academic self-efficacy was stronger among male students. Network analysis revealed gender differences in network structure, but not in global strength, with largely similar central nodes across genders. Overall, these findings suggest that perceived teacher autonomy support is associated with learning burnout in engineering students through distinct stress- and efficacy-related pathways.

Article.Title: Enhanced lipid production from acetate by oleaginous yeast co-cultivation and transcriptomic characterization
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang K.; Liu J.; Sun S.; Campos L.; Cheng S.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Microbial lipids are promising alternative oil sources, particularly for biodiesel production, but their industrial application is limited by high fermentation costs and low lipid yields. Volatile fatty acids (VFAs) derived from organic waste represent potential low-cost substrates for microbial lipid production. This study investigated the co-cultivation of oleaginous yeasts using acetic acid as a carbon source to enhance lipid production. Four oleaginous yeast strains were evaluated under mono- and co-cultivation conditions, and the combination of Yarrowia lipolytica and Rhodotorula glutinis showed the highest lipid production performance among the tested combinations. Response surface methodology was applied to optimize cultivation parameters, including acetate concentration, C/N ratio, and inoculation ratio. Under the optimized conditions, co-cultivation achieved a lipid concentration of 1.04 ± 0.05 g/L, with increases of 18.07% and 26.83% in dry cell weight and lipid concentration, respectively, compared with Y. lipolytica mono-cultivation, and increases of 47.47% and 30.00%, respectively, compared with R. glutinis mono-cultivation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed co-cultivation-associated changes in lipid metabolism-related gene expression in Y. lipolytica . Genes associated with fatty acid and triglyceride biosynthesis, including HTD2, MECR, FAS1, FAS2, AGPAT1_2, and DGAT1, showed increased transcript abundance, whereas TGL3 and TGL4 showed decreased expression. These transcriptional changes were associated with enhanced lipid accumulation under co-cultivation and provide insights into the metabolic responses of oleaginous yeasts during co-cultivation.

Article.Title: In-view vital-sign alarm recognition using a smart glass during simulated bronchoscopy: a phantom feasibility study
Article.Authors: Okachi S.; Ina T.; Ikeda A.; Kamenosono S.; Joki E.; Ipponsugi K.; Ota M.; Imaizumi K.; Hashimoto N.
Article.Abstract: Continuous vital-sign monitoring is essential during bronchoscopy under sedation, yet a dedicated observer may be unavailable, dividing operator attention between the procedure and monitoring. This small, single-arm phantom study explored whether an off-the-shelf smart glass showing vital signs as two-state in-view text can convey actionable alarms during simulated bronchoscopy, and assessed operator-reported usability. Six physicians performed simulated bronchoscopy on an airway phantom wearing a smart glass (Even Realities G2) with a purpose-built display; synthetic vital signs were broadcast at 1 Hz from a laptop (the bridge) that applied all threshold classification centrally. Each completed three standardized scenarios of two alarm events; on noticing an alarm, participants named the affected vital sign, and a single unblinded observer recorded response times. Of 35 evaluable events, 33 (94.3%, 95% CI 80.8–99.3) were recognized at a median 5.0 s (IQR 3.0–6.0), with correct identification in every recognized event; two were missed. Perceived contribution to safety was rated highest (median 5.0), but ease of noticing alerts and maintaining awareness only moderate (median 3.0). In-view alarm display appears technically feasible as a sole information source in this exploratory setting; recognition was not uniform, and any role alongside a certified monitor requires clinical evaluation.

Article.Title: Dietary carbamoyl aspartate supplementation alleviates high-fat diet induced lipid metabolism disorder in broilers
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Sun C.; Bai P.; Zhou Y.; Liu S.; Wu C.; Liu K.; Xiao Y.; Wang Y.; Sun Y.; Guan R.; Liu S.; Hao Y.; Du Q.; Zhou L.; Li Y.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: Obesity threatens both human and poultry health, with intensive farming exacerbating metabolic disorders such as fatty liver disease. Safe and effective nutritional interventions remain limited. Carbamoyl aspartate (CA), a pyrimidine biosynthesis intermediate, reduced hepatic triglyceride (TG) accumulation in vitro (HepG2 cells) and in vivo (broilers). In broilers fed a high-fat diet (HFD), CA supplementation (800 mg/kg) significantly decreased liver weight, hepatic TG/total cholesterol (TC) levels, and abdominal fat deposition ( P < 0.05), while improving meat color and increasing muscle yield. Network pharmacology identified 22 candidate targets linking CA to lipid metabolism, with PDE4B showing the most favorable predicted docking interaction among the screened candidates. The compound-target-pathway-disease network suggested potential multi-target molecular associations. These findings support the potential of CA as a nutritional intervention for HFD-associated lipid metabolic disturbances in broilers, while the predicted molecular mechanisms require further validation.

Article.Title: UAV close-range photogrammetry combined with adaptive octree-based point cloud filtering for rock joint extraction of open-pit mine slopes
Article.Authors: Jia X.; Huang J.; Li W.; Fan K.; Hou C.; Cheng N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Manual joint surveys on open-pit mine slopes are high-risk and inefficient, whereas conventional remote sensing and laser scanning are costly and limited in fine-crack detection. To enable low-cost, high-precision, noncontact structural plane interpretation, this study targets the southern slope of the Shitoumei No. 1 open-pit coal mine and presents a joint recognition method that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) close-range photogrammetry with an octree-based adaptive statistical outlier removal (SOR) filter using two-layer locality-sensitive hashing (2 L-LSH). High-overlap close-range images from real-time kinematic (RTK)-equipped UAVs are reconstructed into centimeter-scale dense point clouds. An octree-based multiscale density-driven adaptive filter, combined with 2 L-LSH for accelerated nearest-neighbor search, resolves the noise‒crack preservation trade-off caused by uneven point–cloud density and enhances computational efficiency. Four clustering algorithms, namely, discontinuity set extractor (DSE), K-means, region growing, and fuzzy C-means (FCM), were compared; FCM was optimized to semiautomatically extract five dominant joint sets with orientations, trace lengths, and spacings. Compared with the conventional SOR filter, the proposed method achieves a 188-fold increase in computational speed and yields a 126% improvement in comprehensive filtering performance. The optimized FCM achieves a mean orientation deviation of 3.2° and a misclassification rate of 3.3%. This workflow enables safe and efficient acquisition of rock-mass joint geometric parameters, as demonstrated for the investigated Shitoumei No. 1 open-pit mine site.

Article.Title: Development and validation of an explainable machine learning-based risk prediction model for macrosomia in han Chinese women with singleton cephalic pregnancies
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang X.; Yu Y.; Xiang W.; Li Y.; Zhang X.; Sun Q.; He Y.; Li J.; Yuan H.
Article.Abstract: To develop and internally validate an explainable machine learning model to predict macrosomia risk among Han Chinese women with singleton cephalic pregnancies during late gestation or at admission. Data from 3,233 women who delivered at a tertiary hospital from April 2024 to March 2025 were included (158 macrosomia cases). All candidate variables were derived from objective clinical data, including electronic medical records, admission measurements, and prenatal ultrasound examinations. To avoid data leakage, the dataset was initially partitioned using an 8:2 stratified split into training and held-out test sets. Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied exclusively within the training set and cross-validation training folds to address class imbalance. A complete analytical pipeline incorporating median imputation, appropriate feature scaling, and SMOTE was implemented. Multiple models were constructed and compared, including logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), CatBoost, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and multi-layer perceptron (MLP). Mean stratified cross-validation ROC-AUC on the training set served as the primary criterion for model selection, supplemented by the Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) to evaluate model reliability and clinical net benefit. LR achieved the highest cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training set, yielding an AUC of 0.934 (95% CI: 0.906–0.957), sensitivity of 0.833 (95% CI: 0.727–0.923), specificity of 0.876 (95% CI: 0.856–0.907), precision of 0.248 (95% CI: 0.184–0.322), and F1 score of 0.382 (95% CI: 0.295–0.458) on the held-out test set. Among the machine learning models, CatBoost exhibited relatively balanced performance regarding AUC, calibration, and clinical interpretability. Although XGBoost demonstrated the highest accuracy, its sensitivity was low, and it was thus not selected as the best model based solely on mean accuracy, precision, and recall. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicated that fetal abdominal circumference (AC), fundal height, maternal height, gestational weeks at delivery, and maternal AC at admission contributed most significantly to prediction. This study established a reproducible and interpretable macrosomia risk prediction pipeline tailored for late-pregnancy/admission decision support. The model provides supplementary information for managing delivery and care in high-risk pregnancies; however, its widespread clinical application requires large-scale, multicenter, and prospective external validation.

Article.Title: Microstructure, thermal conductivity and mechanical anisotropy of DURACON 45M fabricated by laser-wire directed energy deposition
Article.Authors: Hodek J.; Motycka P.; Hradil D.; Uhlík M.; Jansa Z.; Salvetr P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-thermal-conductivity tool materials are critical for reducing cooling-limited cycle times in polymer processing. Microstructure, mechanical anisotropy and thermal conductivity of the Fe–Co–Ni alloy DURACON 45M fabricated by laser-wire directed energy deposition (LW-DED) are investigated. The as-built material exhibits near-full density and a direction-dependent microstructure. EBSD analysis showed a refined grain structure with grain sizes predominantly below 10 µm in the X direction, while the Z direction contained coarser grains elongated along the thermal gradient. In comparison, the wrought base material (BM) exhibited grain sizes mainly around 10 µm. Mechanical testing revealed significantly enhanced tensile strength in the build plane, whereas ductility was markedly reduced along the build direction due to the anisotropic microstructure consisting of elongated columnar grains and crystallographic texture. Despite these microstructural changes, the thermal conductivity remained high ( $$\sim$$ 68 $$\mathrm {W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$$ ). No measurable anisotropy was observed within the uncertainty of the present measurements, and the values remained comparable to those of the base material. These results demonstrate the potential of LW-DED DURACON 45M produced using the investigated processing conditions for advanced tooling applications while emphasizing build-direction anisotropy as a key design constraint.

Article.Title: In-race continuous glucose monitoring in highly trained male distance runners: a context-dependent reversal of the glucose–performance association between training and competition
Article.Authors: Kajisa T.; Sakai T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To characterize in-race interstitial glucose dynamics in highly trained male distance runners using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), and to test whether the direction of the glucose–performance association differs between actual competition and race-pace training. Fifty-nine highly trained (McKay Tier 3) male distance runners from three collegiate squads wore flash CGM during 203 race-pace training sessions and 116 officially sanctioned races. Glucose was modelled with linear mixed-effects models including the athlete as a random intercept. Performance was defined in both conditions as attainment of a pre-established coach–athlete goal time, and additionally on a continuous rating scale within each condition. Because the two conditions were contributed by largely different athletes, the analysis was repeated in the 14 athletes observed in both. Glucose ran far higher in competition than in training (during-exercise average 193.1 ± 39.1 vs. 127.8 ± 27.3 mg/dL), and the separation was already present 2 h before the event began. The association with performance ran in opposite directions in the two contexts: athletes who met their goal time had lower glucose than those who did not during training (− 20.3 mg/dL, 95% CI − 29.9 to − 10.8), but higher glucose during competition (+ 33.3 mg/dL, 95% CI 19.2 to 47.4), an interaction of + 52.4 mg/dL (95% CI 36.1 to 68.8). About half of that difference was established before the start, and the interaction remained after adjustment for pre-exercise glucose (+ 28.5 mg/dL, 95% CI 16.4 to 40.6). It also held in the 14 athletes observed in both conditions (+ 41.9 mg/dL, 95% CI 13.8 to 70.0), although their competition-side association alone was not significant. In-race carbohydrate intake was not measured; excluding the races in which it was permitted did not materially alter the association, and neither did adjustment for event duration. Competition is accompanied by a large interstitial glucose elevation, and glucose relates to goal attainment in opposite directions in competition and in training. These data are consistent with a stress-related increase in hepatic glucose mobilization but cannot separate it from differences in exercise intensity, pre-event nutrition or other competition-specific factors, and the two conditions were contributed by largely different athletes. CGM nonetheless makes in-competition metabolic physiology directly observable in the field.

Article.Title: In vivo evaluation of noninvasive temporal interference stimulation for tibial nerve-mediated bladder reflex modulation in rats
Article.Authors: Marufa S.; Lin B.; Chin H.; Gustafson K.; Hsieh T.; Lo W.; Wu C.; Chen H.; Liou J.; Peng C.
Article.Abstract: Transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS) is an established noninvasive neuromodulation approach for modulating bladder reflexes, although neural recruitment may vary with electrode configuration and tissue electrical properties. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) is an emerging neuromodulation approach in which interacting kilohertz-frequency currents produce low-frequency amplitude modulation and may provide an alternative strategy for peripheral nerve stimulation. We investigated bladder reflex changes following noninvasive TIS applied over the intended tibial nerve region and explored its intensity-response pattern relative to conventional TTNS. In the primary experiment, rats were randomized to TIS or TTNS, and each rat was tested at five motor threshold (MT)-normalized intensity levels in a repeated-measures protocol. Cystometry assessed first voiding time (VT), intercontraction interval (ICI), and bladder pressure before and after each stimulation block. TIS showed the largest mean changes at 100% MT, with prolonged VT and ICI and reduced bladder pressure relative to baseline. Exploratory between-modality comparisons suggested different MT-normalized intensity-response patterns, with the largest VT and ICI differences at 100% MT; differences at other matched intensities were not significant. No significant between-modality bladder-pressure differences were detected. These findings provide a preliminary characterization of peripheral TIS intensity-response patterns for bladder reflex modulation and support further evaluation in disease-relevant models.

Article.Title: Adaptive, nonlinear, cooperative inter-vehicle distance control
Article.Authors: Mosiołek P.; Kabziński J.
Article.Abstract: A novel, adaptive, nonlinear controller is proposed for an adaptive cruise control (ACC) system, to maintain a desired distance between a leading and a following vehicle. The proposed solution takes into account unknown parameters of a nonlinear vehicle dynamics model, variable road inclination, aerodynamic resistance, and variable desired distance, as well as variable constraints on the follower’s velocity and the driving force. The stability of the system is formally proven using Lyapunov techniques. The resulting controller is tested in several simulations based on real-road scenarios, including emergency braking. It is shown that the proposed approach offers a potentially practical solution to enhance the control performance of ACC systems and is able to outperform some recently published solutions.

Article.Title: Near-null magnetic fields modulate photosystem II function and electron transport in Arabidopsis thaliana
Article.Authors: Olmo A.; Kanchiswamy C.; Maffei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The geomagnetic field (GMF) has shaped terrestrial life for over 4.2 billion years, yet the mechanisms underlying plant magnetic sensitivity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the immediate photosynthetic responses of Arabidopsis thaliana to rapid transitions between geomagnetic (GMF; ~45 µT), near-null magnetic field (NNMF; ~30 nT) and hypermagnetic field (HMF; ~1 mT) conditions. Using chlorophyll fluorescence analyses (OJIP and PAM), photosynthetic mutants ( ch1 , npq1 , npq4 , and pgr5 ), Fe-S-cluster-associated lines (KO- isca3 , OE- isca3 , and atx1 ), pharmacological (DCMU and NH 2 OH) perturbation of Photosystem II (PSII), and a simplified quantum spin-Hamiltonian framework, we examined how magnetic-field transitions influence photosynthetic performance. A 10-s transition to NNMF induced rapid increases in fluorescence amplitudes, reduced photochemical operating efficiency, and enhanced photoprotective energy dissipation under actinic illumination. The magnitude and expression of these responses varied among genetic backgrounds and were strongly influenced by donor- and acceptor-side perturbation of PSII. In contrast, HMF produced comparatively modest effects. Together, the genetic and pharmacological analyses indicate that the expression of the magnetic-field-dependent phenotype depends on the physiological state of the photosynthetic apparatus and associated regulatory pathways. Although the molecular origin of the response remains unresolved, the results support further investigation of PSII-associated photochemical and regulatory processes as possible contributors to the observed phenotype. More broadly, this study provides evidence that photosynthetic performance can respond rapidly to magnetic-field transitions and establishes an experimental framework for investigating the processes underlying magnetic-field-associated physiological responses in plants.

Article.Title: Association between primary tumor resection and survival in metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma: a real-world population‑based cohort Study
Article.Authors: You P.; Yin L.; Chen X.; Pu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The clinical value of primary tumor resection (PTR) for patients with de novo metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) remains controversial due to insufficient subtype-specific real-world evidence. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the association between PTR and survival in patients with metastatic FTC using a population-based cohort. Patients with newly diagnosed FTC between 2010 and 2020 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Kaplan–Meier survival curves and log-rank tests were used to compare overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) between patients treated with and without PTR. Propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted to balance baseline clinicopathological confounders. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent prognostic factors. Among 7636 FTC patients, 363 (4.75%) presented with synchronous distant metastasis at initial diagnosis. Of these metastatic cases, 238 (65.5%) received PTR, while 125 did not. Patients who underwent PTR were younger than those who did not (mean age 65.18 ± 13.08 vs. 70.30 ± 12.61 years, P < 0.01). In the entire cohort, patients undergoing PTR exhibited significantly longer median OS (70.0 vs. 27.0 months, P < 0.01) and median CSS (98.0 vs. 47.0 months, P < 0.01) than non-surgical patients. A survival advantage associated with PTR was also observed in several subgroups; the direction of the association was similar after PSM, although the matched cohort was small. The multivariable Cox regression analysis after adjustment for age and other confounders showed PTR was independently associated with a reduced risk of all‑cause mortality (HR=0.52, 95%CI 0.35–0.79, P < 0.01) and cancer-specific mortality (HR=0.49, 95%CI 0.31–0.79, P < 0.01). PTR is significantly associated with improved OS and CSS for patients with de novo metastatic FTC in this real-world cohort.

Article.Title: Exploring factors influencing enhanced recovery after surgery implementation in tertiary hospitals using a DEMATEL–ISM mixed methods approach
Article.Authors: Cao L.; Wang D.; Wang X.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: Despite increasing evidence supporting enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS), its adoption and depth of implementation remain inconsistent across institutions and surgical specialties. ERAS implementation is influenced by multiple factors; therefore, understanding their structural roles is important for informing implementation strategies. A systems modeling approach informed by the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework was employed. Influencing factors were identified through a literature review and semi-structured expert interviews conducted in tertiary hospitals in China. An expert panel of 18 evaluated factor relationships. The Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method was used to analyze influence patterns, and Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) was applied to construct a hierarchical representation of factor dependencies. Nineteen factors were identified across four dimensions: technology, organization, environment, and human. DEMATEL analysis identified successful ERAS pilot programmes (E5), mature organizational structures and support systems (O1), and innovative care model exploration and implementation (O4) as factors with the highest prominent within the influence network. Construction of medical alliances and tiered healthcare systems (E1) showed the highest positive net influence, followed by innovations in medical technology (T1), hospital information system development (T2), and institutional clinical capacity and expertise (O3). ISM revealed a five-level hierarchical structure, with organizational structures and support systems (O1) occupying the deepest structural level, suggesting the foundational role within the ERAS implementation structure. This exploratory systems model provides a structured perspective on the interrelationships and hierarchical dependencies among ERAS implementation factors and may inform implementation priorities while considering local organizational contexts.

Article.Title: MacroRisk-agent: a retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework with deterministic validation gates for auditable stress testing
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Shangguan J.; Wang Q.; Xu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems face three open challenges in high-stakes decision support: hallucination control in structured output generation, coupling of semantic reasoning with deterministic numerical simulation, and end-to-end auditability of multi-step agentic workflows. We present MacroRisk-Agent , a multi-agent architecture that addresses these challenges in the domain of financial stress testing—a setting that demands strict output validity, reproducibility, and regulatory traceability. MacroRisk-Agent introduces three technical contributions: (1) a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline with deterministic validation gates that converts natural-language stress intent into executable, schema-constrained parameter objects, achieving 92.6% validity rate versus 78.4% for RAG-augmented baselines ( $$p<0.001$$ ); (2) a constraint-coupled multi-agent simulation that models endogenous amplification through fire-sale, margin, and liquidity feedback loops, producing a 52% higher systemic-loss estimate than the one-pass configuration under the calibrated experimental setting; and (3) a counterfactual re-simulation framework that validates proposed interventions under identical scenario constraints, achieving 68.6% simulation-defined top-1 decision success rate. We evaluate MacroRisk-Agent as a proof-of-concept on public financial datasets (FRED, Yahoo Finance), a library of 150 curated crisis events, and 10 synthetic institutional portfolios; reported improvements are statistically significant across scenario validity, propagation modeling, and intervention quality within this synthetic evaluation environment . We position the framework as a proposed architecture—rather than an empirically validated, deployment-ready system—for building hallucination-controlled, provenance-tracked LLM-agent pipelines that are designed to improve auditability in high-stakes settings; validation on real institutional data is left to future work.

Article.Title: Critical risk node identification in enterprise resource planning heterogeneous knowledge graphs
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems record high-volume, multi-typed transactions that are difficult to audit with manually specified rules alone. Existing graph-based anomaly detection methods often simplify ERP data into homogeneous graphs or use attention mechanisms that do not explicitly model the temporal ordering of audit events. We propose AuditGain, a framework for constructing ERP heterogeneous knowledge graphs and identifying critical risk nodes with an Adaptive Graph Attention Network. The model combines three main components: type-specific feature extraction for ERP entities, LSTM-enhanced multi-head attention for temporally ordered neighborhoods, and a Diffeomorphic Graph-Adaptive Activation Function (DiGRAF) for graph-conditioned nonlinear transformations. A community-level memory module based on training-period spectral clustering is used to retain cross-period context. Experiments on three proprietary ERP audit datasets and two public fraud detection benchmarks (YelpChi and Amazon) show consistent gains over heterogeneous, temporal, and fraud-oriented graph baselines. On ERP-Audit-A, AuditGain outperforms TGN by 4.2 percentage points and the strongest recent temporal baseline in our comparison by 3.5 percentage points in F1-score. Because the ERP datasets cannot be released under non-disclosure agreements, we provide public benchmark experiments, configuration files, and a synthetic ERP graph generator to support independent checks of the evaluation pipeline. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Drake-crz/AuditGain .

Article.Title: Development and external validation of machine learning models for early prediction of delirium risk in patients with severe pneumonia
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Deng X.; Luo Y.; Wang Y.; Mi J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to construct and validate a machine learning-based model for early prediction of delirium risk in patients with severe pneumonia. Data on patients with severe pneumonia were extracted from the Medical Intensive Care Information Database IV (MIMIC-IV) and divided into a training set and an internal validation set at a ratio of 7:3. External validation was conducted using prospective data from a single center in southwest China. Potential feature variables were screened using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Random Forest(RF), and Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), and eight machine learning algorithms were employed to construct early prediction models for delirium in critically ill pneumonia patients, with the optimal algorithm model selected. Model performance was evaluated using multiple metrics, including the area under the curve (AUC), brier score, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The importance of predictive factors was ranked using the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and the streamlit framework was used to build an interactive web-based calculator. Among 8,059 critically ill patients in the MIMIC database, the incidence of delirium was 71.36%, with 5,641 cases assigned to the training set and 2,418 cases included in the internal validation set. External validation was conducted on 133 critically ill pneumonia patients in southwestern China, with a delirium incidence rate of 55.6%. In the internal validation set, the AUC for the eight machine learning models ranged from 0.58 to 0.73. Among them, the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model performed the best, with an accuracy of 0.75, precision of 0.77, recall of 0.75, positive predictive value(PPV) of 0.77, negative predictive value(NPV) of 0.63, F1 score of 0.72, and Brier score of 0.175. The LightGBM model achieved an AUC of 0.70 and a Brier score of 0.223 in the external validation set. Further DCA demonstrated that when the threshold probability ranged from 0 to 0.68, the net clinical benefit of the LightGBM model was consistently higher than that of the Treat-All and Treat-None strategies. SHAP algorithm feature importance analysis indicated that the three clinical features most influential on the LightGBM model output were sedatives_used, apsiii, and ventilation_status. This study demonstrates that machine learning-based models have the potential to be used for the early identification of high-risk patients with delirium in severe pneumonia. The interactive web-based calculator may serve as a practical predictive management tool for delirium in patients with severe pneumonia.

Article.Title: Seismic deformation and post-earthquake stability assessment of a slope-building system
Article.Authors: Turan C.
Article.Abstract: Time-history-based seismic assessment of slope-building systems remains limited, with most previous studies relying mainly on factor-of-safety based or simplified evaluations. This study addresses that gap through three-dimensional nonlinear numerical analyses of a site-specific slope–building system. The free-vibration characteristics of the building were first identified, and the initial static deformation field under self-weight and structural loading was then established. Five spectrum-compatible ground motions, scaled to the Design Basis Earthquake target spectrum for Kırşehir, were used in the time-history analyses. The peak (transient) total displacement increased from 0.099 m in the static condition to 0.139-0.402 m under seismic loading, while the post-earthquake factor of safety decreased from 1.69 to 1.16-1.18. Principal strain (ε₁) contours, plastic point accumulation, tension cut-off zones, and u z /H cumulative distribution functions show that failure is governed by combined shear and tensile mechanisms. The findings demonstrate the need for mechanism-based seismic assessment beyond factor of safety alone.

Article.Title: Smart city cloud-IoT analysis with spatio-temporal attention and uncertainty-aware spectral signal denoising
Article.Authors: Sudha Rani V.; Ali Shaik M.; Sawaran Singh N.; Vijaya Santhi P.; Madhav B.
Article.Abstract: The deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies in smart cities has generated massive amounts of energy consumption data, creating strong potential for intelligent energy demand forecasting. Noisy sensor readings, missing data, and complex temporal dependencies have prevented conventional deep learning methods from achieving higher prediction accuracy. To address this challenge, this paper presents an innovative approach for accurate energy demand forecasting: the Smart City Cloud-IoT Spatio-Temporal Attention Network with Uncertainty-Aware Spectral Signal Denoising (SCC-IoT-STAN-USSD). Firstly, IoT energy consumption data are preprocessed through Bayesian Boundary Trend Filtering (BBTF) to remove noise measurement, fill in missing data, and retain significant temporal patterns. Then, an Amplitude-Preserving Adaptive Synchro squeezed S-Transform (APST) is used to acquire time–frequency representations from the filtered signals. The above features are then analyzed using the Spatio-Temporal Attention Network (STAN) to extract spatial correlation and long-term temporal dependencies for accurate forecasting. In addition, the Uncertainty-Aware Spectral Signal Denoising (USSD) method improves prediction accuracy by reducing uncertainty during the process of model optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a prediction accuracy of 98.20%, MAE of 0.31, RMSE of 0.24, MAPE of 2.14%, SMAPE of 1.98%, R 2 score of 0.992, and energy efficiency of 97.84%, thus surpassing the performance of ANN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, GNN, and recently proposed methods. Additionally, statistical significance testing, regression analysis, and ablation tests show the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Article.Title: Load power matching MPPT for PV systems
Article.Authors: Eldessouky A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite their common use, conventional MPPT algorithms, such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (INC), exhibit several limitations. These include oscillations around the MPP, delayed tracking response, and incorrect tracking direction when the system operates far from the true MPP. Such drawbacks arise primarily because these algorithms rely solely on instantaneous and previous measurements of PV voltage and power without using predictive information or reference values. This paper presents a novel MPPT control algorithm that utilizes a dynamic power-matching strategy based on the rated power of the electrical load perceived by the PV system. The proposed method enhances PV system performance by dynamically regulating the operation of the DC-DC converter such that the perceived load power matches the PV operating capability. When a mismatch is detected, the controller increases or decreases the perceived electrical load by controlling the DC-DC converter. The direction of the control action is determined by the deviation of the PV operating voltage from its nominal value. Hence, the proposed algorithm provides the controller with a reference-based framework at each sampling instant, avoiding dependence on the power-voltage slope, which becomes very small near the MPP. The simulation results show stable operation around MPP under varying irradiance and partial shading conditions.

Article.Title: Regional variations in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest outcomes after the Great East Japan Earthquake: a 16-year cohort study
Article.Authors: Ito Y.; Omatsu K.; Inaba H.
