Evaluation used a held-out 22-patient internal test cohort, controlled component and architecture ablations, a three-seed SDF comparison, and zero-shot testing on three external BraTS cohorts. Internally, mean tumour-positive slice DSC was 0.8320, whole-cohort DSC was 0.9086, and mean patient-level DSC was 0.8731; mean slice HD95 was 7.66 pixels. The SDF regulariser showed favourable average multi-seed effects. Under the primary replicated-FLAIR external protocol, mean patient-level DSC was 0.6194 for TCGA-LGG, 0.6007 for full BraTS 2021, and 0.3862 for BraTS-Africa. These findings support encouraging internal performance but limited cross-dataset robustness.

Article.Title: Performance of the water cycle algorithm in optimal economic design of passive power filter
Article.Authors: AbdElaziz E.; Mahmoud M.; Salama A.; Ibrahim K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Harmonic distortion in power systems, caused mostly by nonlinear loads, results in significant power quality (PQ) issues such as higher losses, lower power factor (PF), and equipment malfunctions. Passive power filters (PPFs), which use tuned combinations of inductors and capacitors to attenuate specific harmonic frequencies, are widely used because of their lower cost and simpler design compared to active filtering systems. This paper proposes an optimal design of a single-tuned passive filter (STPF) based on the Water Cycle Algorithm (WCA). The optimization procedure employs a single-objective optimization strategy in which voltage total harmonic distortion (VTHD) minimization, power loss (Ploss) minimization, and PF maximization are investigated separately. At the same time, the remaining performance indices are imposed as constraints to ensure compliance with IEEE 519–2022 standards. The suggested method is assessed using two industrial case studies with varying system parameters and harmonic behavior. Simulation findings show that the WCA-based optimization surpasses the MIDACO technique on all assessed criteria. In the two case studies, VTHD values were lowered to 1.29% and 0.86%, respectively, while PF increased to 99.22%. The overall active Ploss was reduced to 5.76 kW, compared to 6.12 kW using MIDACO. Comparative investigation verifies WCA-based optimization’s efficiency, robustness, and speedier convergence, indicating that it is a potential approach for optimal filter design in power systems. In addition to technical performance, a thorough economic study was done to analyze the financial viability of the proposed STPF design, showing its potential for significant cost-effectiveness and practical implementation benefits.

Article.Title: Exopolysaccharide from Marinobacter nauticus strain GH3 reduces oxidative stress and neurotoxicity caused by Nickel in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Article.Authors: Khalil W.; Sabry N.; Abdel –Tawab M.; El-Fiky S.; Bassem S.; Hamed A.; Abdelrazik M.; Abdel-Razik G.; Eltaher A.; El Awady M.; Abdel-Gawad F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nickel (Ni) is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant that poses significant risks to the nervous systems of diverse organisms. This study investigated the neurotoxic effects of nickel chloride (NiCl 2 ) on Nile tilapia and the potential protective role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) derived from Marinobacter nauticus strain GH3 (GH3-EPS). Nile tilapia were divided into eight groups and fed for 8 weeks either a standard diet, diets supplemented with graded doses of GH3-EPS (0.075–0.3 g), GH3-EPS combined with sublethal Nickel (II) chloride exposure (1/10 LC50 ≈ 113.4 mg/L), or NiCl2 alone. At the experiment end, fish were euthanized, and brain, liver, and gill tissues were rapidly collected for accurate biochemical, molecular, and histological analyses. The expression of neurodegeneration-related genes (ApoE, Clu, and CR1) in brain tissues, antioxidant enzyme activities (GPx and GR) in liver tissues, and histopathological changes in gills and liver tissue were evaluated. NiCl 2 exposure significantly increased the expression of ApoE, Clu, and CR1 genes and decreased GPx and GR enzyme activities compared to the control group. Treatment with medium- and high-dose GH3-EPS significantly reduced the expression of these genes and increased GPx and GR activities in NiCl 2 -exposed fish. Additionally, GH3-EPS treatment significantly reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation in the liver of NiCl 2 -exposed fish, with medium and high doses exhibiting inhibition rates of 32.9% and 36.6%, respectively. These findings suggest that GH3-EPS may have protective effects against NiCl 2 -induced neurotoxicity in Nile tilapia by normalizing gene expression, improving antioxidant levels, and reducing oxidative stress. This study highlights the potential of EPS as a mitigation strategy for metal-induced neurotoxicity in aquatic organisms.

Article.Title: BERT-based medical chatbot with application-level cryptographic protection
Article.Authors: Altunay H.; Sarıyalçınkaya A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence technology has been frequently used in the personalized healthcare services domain in recent years. The quality of medical services has been improved and a new era has started for healthcare services with the use of Artificial Intelligence. Simultaneously, deep learning models, which are qualified as a special use of Artificial Intelligence, are preferred depending on the number of users and the amount of data increasing with each passing day. This study proposes a BERT-based medical chatbot architecture that combines contextual natural language processing with an application-level cryptographic protection layer for client-server communication. The cryptographic mechanism is intended as an additional protection layer around the transmitted chatbot payload and is not presented as a replacement for standard TLS or as a mechanism for protecting plaintext data during server-side inference. The NLP component uses a BERT-based Transformer model to process medical queries from the HealthFC and TREC-Health datasets. The experimental implementation was developed using the Hugging Face Transformers library with TensorFlow and spaCy, and the model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Five-fold stratified cross-validation was also employed to examine the consistency of the classification performance across data partitions. For communication security, RSA is used for the distribution of the AES secret key, AES is used to encrypt the transmitted medical payload, and SHA-256-based HMAC is employed to provide message integrity and authentication. The proposed model achieved 99% accuracy, 99% precision, 97% recall, 98% F1-score, and 97% AUC-ROC. In the five-fold evaluation, the accuracy values were 1.00, 0.99, 0.99, 0.98, and 0.99, respectively. Compared with the evaluated LSTM, SVM, and Bi-LSTM baselines, which achieved accuracies of 0.88, 0.91, and 0.94, respectively, the proposed BERT-based model achieved the highest classification performance. These results indicate strong classification performance on the evaluated benchmark datasets, while the cryptographic layer provides an additional application-level mechanism for protecting medical information during client-server communication. The proposed security mechanism should be interpreted within this scope: it complements, rather than replaces, TLS and does not protect plaintext medical data after decryption on the server during inference. The study establishes a BERT-based and security-oriented architecture for medical chatbot applications; however, clinical safety, external validation, paraphrase-aware leakage analysis, end-to-end latency, and multilingual or voice-based capabilities require further experimental evaluation.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation and analysis of void evolution and CO2 seepage characteristics in broken rock
Article.Authors: Wang F.; Li X.; Cao S.; Wu C.; Liu Y.; Zheng C.; Che C.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: To elucidate void-structure evolution and CO 2 seepage characteristics of broken rock masses during goaf compaction, confined compaction tests were conducted on broken argillaceous sandstone with different particle-size gradations and filling weights, while CO 2 seepage tests were performed at a fixed filling weight of 4.8 kg under different axial stress levels using a fractured rock mechanics–gas permeation testing system (FRM-GPTS). The results show that single-sized samples have higher initial porosities (0.490–0.541) than continuously graded samples (0.448–0.458), with porosity generally increasing as particle size decreases. Compaction proceeds through void compression, void filling, and void compaction, accompanied by progressive energy accumulation, particle breakage, and pore restructuring. At 25 MPa, deformation and breakage generally increase with particle size; at 4.8 kg filling weight, the relative breakage ratio increases from 36.33 to 66.35%. Continuously graded samples exhibit lower deformation and breakage because of fine-particle filling and skeleton-supporting effects. CO 2 seepage shows pronounced non-Darcy behaviour, with permeability decreasing continuously with increasing axial stress and decreasing porosity. Single-sized samples exhibit higher permeability (564.2–658.6 mD) than continuously graded samples (415.8–461.5 mD). These results reveal a coupled evolution mechanism of compaction deformation, particle breakage, pore restructuring, and seepage attenuation, providing an experimental basis for evaluating CO 2 storage capacity and migration in coal mine goafs.

Article.Title: Efficient Alzheimer’s disease classification with robust rank pooling
Article.Authors: Kang S.; Kim S.; Roh H.; Hong C.; Son S.; Ryu J.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) classification utilizing 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on brain MRI poses significant challenges, including high computational overhead, the scarcity of large-scale training data, and the inherent difficulty in capturing subtle pathological features. Existing 3D-to-2D compression methods simplify the data but suffer from critical information loss. We propose Robust Rank Pooling (RRP), a novel compression technique that employs a sliding window strategy to transform a 3D MRI volume into multiple 2D dynamic images. This approach effectively mitigates information loss by preserving robust structural features across different brain sections. We utilize these generated images to train an efficient, pre-trained 2D CNN architecture, which incorporates a model ensemble method to further enhance performance. The proposed method is validated on two T2-FLAIR MRI benchmarks, ADNI and BICWALZS. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods. Compared to the previous method, our model achieves improvements of approximately 2.3% in accuracy and 4.4% in Area Under the Curve (AUC). Relative to a standard 3D network, our method improves accuracy by 13.2% while demonstrating a 4.1 \(\times \) and 2.1 \(\times \) speedups in model inference and total processing time, respectively. Furthermore, qualitative analysis confirms that our model focuses on clinically relevant biomarkers, consequently offering a computationally efficient and effective solution for Alzheimer’s disease classification.

Article.Title: PCOS-FedSev: Federated severity-aware PCOS diagnosis with site-invariant disentanglement and conformal guarantees
Article.Authors: Venuthurumilli P.; Manam V.; Sivasubramanian R.; BabuMandru D.; Kumari T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a condition that affects between 8 and 13% of women during their reproductive years. However, PCOS continues to be vastly underdiagnosed despite its prevalence. Currently available AI-based PCOS diagnosis methods are limited by their centralized nature, making them difficult to deploy across multiple sites. They are not able to provide information regarding the severity of the PCOS diagnosis. The PCOS-FedSev method is comprised of five interwoven modules such as (1) Gradient Reversal Layer-Based Site-Invariant Feature Disentanglement (SiFD) for removing the domain shift induced by the medical imaging device across multiple hospitals (2) Conditional Ordinal Regression for Neural Networks (CORN), a technique enabling joint four-level monotonic severity classification alongside binary PCOS identification (3) Federated Prototype Replay (FPR), which avoids catastrophic forgetting when incorporating a new hospital without exchanging data between clients (4) Adaptive Quality-Aware Site Weighting (AQSW) enabling robust aggregation of the contribution of clients with differing image quality and finally (5) Federated Conformal Prediction (FCP), allowing for approximately 95% marginal coverage guarantees. In experiments performed on six simulated heterogeneous hospital clients with Dirichlet α = 0.4—corresponding to realistically varying PCOS prevalence between 0 and 85% across hospitals—PCOS-FedSev demonstrated an AUC-ROC of 1.0000, an F1 score of 0.9975, a severity MAE of 0.7365, an ECE of 0.0025, and reduced communication cost by 85%. This work constitutes the first federated learning framework for PCOS identification.

Article.Title: Towards sustainable Safety 4.0 adoption in manufacturing organizations: enabler modeling and readiness assessment
Article.Authors: Sivakami B.; Suresh M.; Muthuswamy S.; Rehman A.
Article.Abstract: The adoption of safety measures in Industry 4.0 (I4.0) is emerging as a strategic approach to reduce workplace accidents and improve the safety environment, which has led to the concept of Safety 4.0 (S4.0). With the technological advancements, there exist some new and emerging risks such as cognitive overload, cyber-physical risks, and psychosocial problems. However, the practical implementation of S4.0 remains limited in manufacturing organizations (MOs) due to various resource-related constraints. Hence, it is essential to assess the current level of Safety 4.0 readiness for the successful implementation. The current body of literature in the context of S4.0 related to MOs remains limited compared to I4.0. This study addresses the aforementioned contextual and methodological gaps by developing and analyzing a framework to evaluate S4.0 readiness. At the macro level, the interrelationships and the driving and dependence power of the enablers were identified using Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) and Cross-Impact Matrix Multiplication Applied to Classification (MICMAC) analysis. The key driving enablers are ecosystem and regulatory support, management, and employee readiness. The resulting framework comprises 6 enablers, 28 criteria, and 97 attributes. At the micro level, the readiness of the case organization was evaluated, and the Fuzzy Safety 4.0 Readiness Index (FSRI) was found to be at an average level. Based on ranking scores, 20 of 97 attributes were weaker. The novelty of the study lies in linking micro-level weaker attributes to macro-level driving enablers. This helps MOs to avoid investing resources in highly dependent factors, a common limitation of existing fuzzy logic studies. The study focuses on improvement strategies within the driving enablers.

Article.Title: Examining Thai CFL learners’ continuance intention to use kahoot! in Chinese language classrooms with an extended expectation-confirmation model
Article.Authors: Pan L.; Chen Q.; Ye Y.; Gu Q.; Yao L.
Article.Abstract: Although Kahoot! has been widely used in language classrooms and has been associated with greater classroom participation and engagement, less is known about whether learners with prior experience intend to continue using it and how different post-adoption perceptions are associated with such intentions. Drawing on the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM), this study examined perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEOU), perceived enjoyment (PENJ), and perceived interactivity (PI) as four distinct post-adoption perceptions within Kahoot!-supported Chinese as a foreign language (CFL) learning. Data were collected from 519 Thai high-school CFL learners in Bangkok with prior Kahoot! experience and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Confirmation (CON) was positively associated with all four post-adoption perceptions and with satisfaction (SAT), and each of the four perceptions was positively associated with SAT. PU, PEOU, PENJ, and SAT were positively associated with continuance intention (CI), whereas PI showed no significant direct association with CI but a significant indirect association involving SAT. Significant indirect associations linking CON and CI were also observed, including those involving the post-adoption perceptions and SAT. Theoretically, the differentiated associations with CI suggest that extending the ECM with context-relevant post-adoption perceptions requires attention not only to which perceptions are incorporated, but also to how each is associated with SAT and CI. Practically, CFL teachers considering continued Kahoot! use may benefit from obtaining separate feedback on learners’ PU, PEOU, PENJ, PI, and SAT across repeated classroom use when reviewing whether Kahoot! should be retained in subsequent CFL classes.

Article.Title: Modular design and multi-objective performance optimization of an extended mechanical spindle for DH horizontal machining centers
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Li H.; Dong C.; Tao Y.
Article.Abstract: Conventional horizontal machining centers face critical limitations in machining large-scale complex workpieces due to insufficient spindle extension capability. Existing extended spindle designs often suffer from severe stiffness degradation, increased vibration, and thermal deformation, which significantly compromise machining accuracy and stability. While extensive research has been conducted on spindle dynamics, few studies have systematically addressed the coupled stiffness-dynamic-thermal performance trade-offs in extended mechanical spindles for heavy-duty applications. To fill this gap, this paper presents a modular extended mechanical spindle design for DH series horizontal machining centers. A stepped hollow spindle shaft structure is proposed to balance bending stiffness and rotational inertia, and a combined bearing arrangement with optimized preload is adopted to enhance support rigidity. A multi-objective optimization framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and response surface methodology is developed to optimize key geometric parameters, including spindle diameter distribution, bearing spacing, and extension interface dimensions. Comprehensive simulations and experimental tests demonstrate that the optimized spindle achieves a 57.1% reduction in tool tip displacement under rated cutting load, a 12.3% increase in fundamental natural frequency, and significantly improved thermal stability. The proposed design effectively expands the machining range while maintaining high precision, providing a practical engineering solution for advanced horizontal machining centers.

Article.Title: MSAL-YOLO: a YOLOv8-based detector for small and densely distributed object detection in UAV aerial imagery
Article.Authors: Ding F.; Du X.; Zhang H.; Liu H.; Han L.
Article.Abstract: Object detection in UAV aerial imagery is challenging because of small object scales, dense distributions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds. To address these issues, we propose MSAL-YOLO, an improved YOLOv8-based detector for aerial object detection. Specifically, a Spatial–Channel Mixed Convolution (SCMConv) module is introduced to enhance local feature extraction by combining standard and dilated convolutions. A Multi-Branch Enhanced Coordinate Attention (MBECA) mechanism is further designed to strengthen spatial dependency modeling and contextual interaction. In addition, a Region-Adaptive Wise-IoU (RA-WIoU) loss is developed to alleviate scale imbalance by increasing the contribution of small objects during training. Experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that MSAL-YOLO improves mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 30.0% and 17.0% to 35.7% and 20.5%, respectively, while maintaining competitive model complexity. Cross-dataset experiments on DOTAv1 further demonstrate the robustness and generalization capability of the proposed method. These results indicate that MSAL-YOLO provides an effective solution for UAV aerial object detection in complex scenes.

Article.Title: Machine learning assisted seismic assessment of rock crack propagation and ground instability around underground passageways
Article.Authors: Long L.; Liu Y.; Fazli Shahgoli A.; khairy Y.; Escorcia-Gutierrez J.
Article.Abstract: Seismic instability around underground passageways is governed by rock cracking, ground deformation, groundwater condition, support response, and earthquake demand. This study presents a finite element (FE) and machine learning (ML) framework for seismic screening of rock and soil transition zones. Abaqus 2023 was used with a 200 m by 120 m plane strain domain, CPE4R elements, B21 lining elements, T2D2 support elements, and COH2D4 crack interfaces. Mesh and time increment studies limited changes in convergence, bending moment, crack extension, and plastic zone radius to less than 1.0% between adopted and finer analyses. The internal database contains 1536 numerical cases from 16 geotechnical condition groups, 24 earthquake records, and four intensity levels. Motion separated fitting, validation, and locked test blocks contain 1152, 192, and 192 cases. A separate 128 case numerical holdout uses eight geotechnical configurations and four earthquake records with no shared condition or motion identifiers. Laboratory material records support parameter assignment, while centrifuge tunnel response observations are retained separately for qualitative physical response checking and are excluded from ML development. Nine continuous FE responses and one categorical stability target are evaluated. Linear regression was selected from the fitting and validation stage before locked test evaluation and subsequently gave a mean locked test coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.979 and a four fold geotechnical group mean R 2 of 0.951. Across the numerical holdout, R 2 values range from 0.921 to 0.960, with a mean of 0.946. The selected support vector classifier gives locked test accuracy of 0.969, geotechnical group F1 score (F1) of 0.909, and holdout accuracy of 0.805 with receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.896. Sigmoid calibration gives a multiclass Brier score of 0.319 and expected calibration error of 0.118. Target specific grouped permutation analysis identifies the seismic intensity block as producing the largest predictive performance loss within the investigated holdout, followed by groundwater depth and response dependent contributions from support stiffness, burial depth, and crack density. The framework provides a documented mechanics informed screening approach within the investigated numerical parameter domain.

Article.Title: Loneliness, restless sleep, and incident possible or confirmed sarcopenia among middle-aged and older Chinese adults
Article.Authors: Wang T.; Xu C.; Shi Q.; Hu C.; Fan J.; Zhang J.; Li P.; Shi R.; Song Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Loneliness and sleep problems may mark vulnerability to sarcopenia, but prospective evidence on their co-occurrence is limited. Using 2011 and 2015 CHARLS data, we examined loneliness, restless sleep, and their joint exposure in relation to incident possible or confirmed sarcopenia. The unweighted complete-case analysis included 6,614 participants free of either category at baseline. Loneliness and restless sleep were coded from two CES-D-10 items. During follow-up, 1,067 participants developed the composite outcome. In the most extensively adjusted logistic model, loneliness (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.18–1.62) and restless sleep (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.03–1.38) were associated with higher odds. Compared with neither symptom, the OR was 1.32 (95% CI 1.02–1.71) for loneliness only, 1.13 (95% CI 0.95–1.34) for restless sleep only, and 1.53 (95% CI 1.26–1.87) for both symptoms. Modified Poisson analysis was consistent for both symptoms (RR 1.34, 95% CI 1.16–1.54), whereas multiplicative interaction was not supported. Loneliness and restless sleep were associated with the composite outcome, and their co-occurrence identified the highest odds. These observational findings do not establish causality.

Article.Title: Uniqueness and structure-preserving numerical simulations for an Ultrahyperbolic Schrödinger equation
Article.Authors: Kaytmaz Ö.; Hasdemir M.
Article.Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a Cauchy problem for an ultrahyperbolic Schrödinger equation posed in an unbounded domain. Ultrahyperbolic Schrödinger models arise in multidimensional wave propagation and have applications in water wave theory, quantum kinetic theory, ferromagnetism, nonlinear optics, and plasma physics. A uniqueness result for the considered Cauchy problem is established using a pointwise Carleman estimate. In addition, a second-order, structure-preserving Crank–Nicolson finite-difference scheme is developed for the numerical solution of the problem. For the homogeneous constant-coefficient problem, its discrete evolution is unitary and conserves the discrete \(\ell _{h}^{2}\) -norm exactly. Numerical experiments illustrate the behaviour of solutions and verify the accuracy and conservation properties of the numerical scheme.

Article.Title: Exploratory synovial fluid metabolomics suggests formate as a potential player in post-traumatic osteoarthritis: an 8-year case series report
Article.Authors: Oliveira J.; Capitão A.; Sousa C.; Mendes L.; Neves B.; Duarte I.; Coelho P.; Fonseca F.; Mendes A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traumatic knee lesions are among the most common injuries in sports and have long been recognized as a major risk factor for the development of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA). This work aimed at performing a metabolomic analysis of synovial fluid (SF) to identify biomarkers predictive of PTOA progression after acute anterior cruciate ligament or meniscal injury. In this single-center case series report with a mean follow-up of 96 ± 8 months, trauma patients were compared with two control groups [osteoarthritis (OA) and Non-OA]. At the end of follow-up, 44.4% of trauma patients showed signs of radiographic evolution to PTOA, with an interrater reliability of 0.8. Trauma patients exhibited a distinct SF metabolic profile, with PLS-DA models showing good internal cross-validated performance [Q²(cum) ≥ 0.70], supporting consistent metabolic differences between trauma and control groups. Of 30 identified metabolites, 16 showed significant differences between trauma patients and at least one control group after correction for multiple testing. Notably, formate showed the strongest nominal association with subsequent PTOA development, with higher levels in patients who progressed to PTOA (unadjusted p = 0.046); however, this association did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing ( q = 0.995). These findings identify formate as an exploratory candidate biomarker associated with PTOA progression.

Article.Title: Image-derived conjunctival hyperemia and clinical ocular surface changes after initiation of topical glaucoma therapy: a prospective longitudinal pilot study
Article.Authors: Hansapinyo L.; Pianwichanpong N.; Pathanapitoon K.; Hansapinyo C.; Hansapinyo N.; Kulniwatcharoen P.; Patanukhom K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Topical glaucoma therapy can affect the ocular surface, but objective longitudinal data on conjunctival hyperemia are limited. We prospectively followed 31 patients naive to topical antiglaucoma therapy for 24 weeks after treatment initiation, analyzing one baseline severity-selected eye per participant. All 31 participants contributed complete analyzable conjunctival image series at baseline and 6, 12, and 24 weeks. Automated image processing quantified strong red area as the primary hyperemia metric and blood vessel area as a secondary metric. Tear breakup time (TBUT), Schirmer I testing, National Eye Institute (NEI) corneal staining, Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), and NEI Visual Function Questionnaire-25 were also assessed. Strong red area increased numerically by 2.56 percentage points at 24 weeks (95% CI − 1.06 to 6.18; P = 0.165), while blood vessel area remained stable. NEI staining decreased, TBUT and Schirmer I showed no significant overall change, OSDI scores decreased (overall P = 0.002), and NEI-VFQ-25 scores improved. Over 24 weeks, image-derived conjunctival hyperemia showed no statistically significant persistent increase, whereas clinical ocular-surface signs and patient-reported outcomes followed differing trajectories. These preliminary findings characterize ocular-surface changes after initiation of topical glaucoma therapy, although the small uncontrolled design precludes causal or equivalence conclusions.

Article.Title: An optimized pipeline for cell-based validation of gRNAs designs to inactivate coding and non-coding RNAs using CRISPR-Cas9
Article.Authors: Jaouen F.; Lepolard C.; Bescond T.; Borges A.; Popa N.; Tzavara E.; Gascon E.
Article.Abstract: Genome-editing technologies based on bacterial Cas9 proteins have become a gold standard for introducing precise genetic modifications across multiple species and experimental models. These tools require the design and validation of guide RNAs (gRNAs) that direct the Cas9 protein to the actual genome location to be edited. Although numerous algorithms have been developed to design gRNAs, whether a gRNA is going to be effective or not need to be experimentally assessed. Since most of the times several designs are tested in parallel, we have set up an efficient cell-based approach to optimize this validation process by directly quantifying gRNAs effect on the downstream target RNA or protein. Our strategy relies on: (1) creating stable cell lines expressing the gene of interest and a fluorescent reporter; (2) transient transfection of these lines with the different gRNAs; (3) analyzing the efficiency of the designs at the transcriptomic and/or protein level in the whole population or in FACS sorted cells. We demonstrate the relevance of our approach by inactivating a coding gene (Elk1) and two short non-coding RNA (miR-218 and miR-124).

Article.Title: A comparative study for the isolation of rabbit phenotypically defined candidate HSPCs based on CD45 or CD34 marker expression
Article.Authors: Vašíček J.; Bauer M.; Baláži A.; Svoradová A.; Vozaf J.; Olexiková L.; Supuka P.; Nicodemou A.; Zemánek T.; Chrenek P.
Article.Abstract: Rabbit hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (rHSPCs) residing in bone marrow are still poorly characterized. Usually, human and animal HSPCs can be obtained by depletion of mature lineage-committed hematopoietic cells or via positive selection of primitive cells expressing CD34 antigen. Previously, we reported possible enrichment of potential rHSPCs by depletion of rabbit CD45 + cells. This study describes an improved depletion protocol with more satisfying cell purity. Additionally, enrichment of phenotypically defined candidate rHSPCs using new anti-rabbit CD34 monoclonal antibodies and MACS or FACS sorting is presented here to thoroughly compare these three methods according to the quality of isolated rHSPCs. Moreover, human bone marrow CD34 + cells were used to compare their specific features and abilities with enriched rabbit cell populations. We achieved high sorting efficiency and purity after rabbit CD45 depletion ( p < 0.001), as well as for MACS and FACS enrichment of CD34 + cells ( p < 0.0001). Satisfying viability was observed for rabbit CD45 - and FACS CD34 + cells (> 90%, p < 0.05), but not for MACS CD34 + cells (< 50%; p < 0.0001). Rabbit CD45 - ( p < 0.05) and human MACS CD34 + cells ( p < 0.01) expanded well, while rabbit FACS and MACS CD34 + cells did not. All three differently enriched rabbit cell populations exhibited phenotype like human CD34 + cells with slight differences. Almost all enriched rabbit cell populations (except for MACS sorted) showed high clonogenic capacity comparable to human CD34 + cells and produced BFU-E, CFU-E, CFU-GM and CFU-GEMM colonies. In addition, TEM analysis revealed same morphology and ultrastructure for all enriched rabbit cell populations as for human CD34 + cells. Here we isolated phenotypically defined candidate rHSPCs subpopulations with slightly different purity, viability, phenotype, expansion rate and clonogenic capacity. On the other hand, enriched rabbit cell populations showed very similar morphology and ultrastructure to human HSPCs. This study allowed us to isolate, cryopreserve and store rabbit phenotypically defined candidate HSPCs from native Holic Blue and Slovak Grey-Blue Rex rabbits in animal gene bank for future generations. Regarding CD34 enrichment, mAb 58/47/34 seems to be more suitable for the sorting procedures than other tested antibodies. However, further studies are required to improve the expansion method specific for rabbit HSPCs or to analyse transcriptome or secretome of these cells. Moreover, the major limitation of this study is the lack of in vivo repopulation experiments, which might prove the real HSPCs origin of the enriched rabbit cell populations.

Article.Title: Hydrological connectivity regulates CO2 and CH4 emissions from a temperate, natural river-floodplain system
Article.Authors: Pilicita J.; Grygoruk M.; Michałowski R.; Osuch P.; Stachowicz M.; Demeter K.; Mirosław-Świątek D.; Kustina R.; Sieczko A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural river-floodplains are significant sources of greenhouse gases (GHG) including CO 2 and CH 4 , yet the role of hydrological connectivity in shaping aquatic fluxes of these gases ( F CO 2 and F CH 4 ) remains unclear. This study was conducted in a temperate river-floodplain system (Poland), using manual and automated flux chambers where we measured 1776 F CH 4 and 1783 F CO 2 during various water levels in 15 locations across dormant and growing seasons. The system showed a high spatio-temporal variability, with the highest F CH 4 in the disconnected sidearms and the highest F CO₂ in the river. Hydrology strongly regulated F CO 2 , while F CH 4 responses were jointly shaped by temperature, connectivity and local hydrological conditions. The system was the strongest source of GHGs (in CO 2 -equivalent; CO 2-eq ) in the summer and the weakest in the spring. Over the last ten years (2015–2025), significantly more of the CO 2-eq was emitted during the growing seasons, despite a larger aquatic floodplain area during the dormant seasons. This study highlights that accounting for hydrological diversity is crucial to avoid bias in estimates of aquatic GHG balances, even in nearby physicochemically similar systems. This research fills a key gap in hydrological controls of F CO 2 and F CH 4 in natural river-floodplains, improves emission inventories via system-specific emission factors and highlights climate impacts on river-floodplain GHG emissions.

Article.Title: Comparison of machine learning and spatial interpolation methods for hourly rainfall data imputation in the Oliwski Stream catchment
Article.Authors: Shah G.; Artichowicz W.; Kolerski T.
Article.Abstract: Rainfall is a key factor in hydrological analysis, yet precipitation time series are often incomplete due to malfunctioning of instruments. This study evaluates methods for imputing missing precipitation data at the Oliwa gauging station in Gdańsk, Poland. Two approaches were compared: spatial interpolation (SI) and machine learning (ML). Data from nearby stations, obtained by Gdańskie Wody, were used as predictors. A three-year period with complete records across all stations was selected. ML models, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest (RF), and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), while SI methods included Mean, Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW), and Correlation Coefficient Weighted Method (CCWM). Two missing-data scenarios were simulated: Missing Completely At Random (MCAR) and Missing Not At Random (MNAR). Model performance was evaluated using R 2 , RMSE, and MAE. Results showed that ML methods outperformed SI methods. For MCAR scenarios (5%, 10%, and 15% missing data), MLP achieved R 2 values between 0.789 and 0.959, while XGBoost performed lowest among ML models (0.737–0.899). Among SI methods, IDW performed best (R 2 : 0.735–0.968), while the Mean method performed worst (0.634–0.933). Model accuracy decreased as the proportion of missing data increased. For MNAR scenarios, the model performed better when imputing missing values during the driest month compared to the wettest. Later, using the Osowa station as a predictor applying ML models only, MLP again performed best with (R 2 = 0.923). These findings support the use of ML methods for improving rainfall datasets in hydrological studies.

Article.Title: Brain tumor segmentation using particle swarm optimized histogram equalization and a VGG19 based U-Net
Article.Authors: Saifullah S.; Dreżewski R.
Article.Abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation in MRI scans is critical for diagnosis and treatment planning. Conventional methods are often time-consuming, error-prone, and subject to operator bias. Although recent deep-learning approaches show promise for automating medical image segmentation, challenges such as interpretability hinder their clinical adoption. To address these issues, we propose SPOHE-VGGNet, a novel segmentation model that integrates a modified U-Net architecture with VGG-19 and Particle Swarm Optimized Histogram Equalization (PSO-HE). This approach enhances MRI contrast and improves segmentation performance relative to the evaluated preprocessing baselines. PSO-HE outperforms traditional and PSO-based image enhancement techniques, delivering superior image quality and facilitating precise feature extraction by VGG-19. We evaluated SPOHE-VGGNet on the Figshare T1-CE MRI dataset (3,064 images encompassing meningioma, glioma, and pituitary tumor classes) and the BraTS 2021 dataset comprising 1,251 cases, with four MRI modalities processed independently for two-dimensional Whole Tumor segmentation. On the Figshare dataset, the model achieved Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) of 0.9522 for meningioma, 0.9428 for glioma, and 0.9518 for pituitary tumors. For whole tumor segmentation on the BraTS dataset, it attained a DSC of 0.9463. Performance metrics for Figshare included accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.9989, 0.9680, 0.9647, and 0.9662, respectively. On the BraTS dataset, these metrics were 0.9977, 0.9544, 0.9738, and 0.9640, demonstrating its applicability to independently evaluated two-dimensional slices from different MRI modalities. By combining segmentation performance with interpretability analyses, SPOHE-VGGNet provides a research-oriented framework for two-dimensional brain tumor MRI segmentation. Further external, volumetric, and clinician-centered validation is required before its use in clinical decision-making can be considered.

Article.Title: Mechanism-guided Bayesian diagnosis of progressive toppling in an interbedded sandstone–mudstone dangerous rock mass using multisource monitoring
Article.Authors: Pan S.; Yu L.; Wang C.; Lin G.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Progressive toppling of dangerous rock masses in steep mountain cliffs is governed by coupled water-induced weakening, toe-support retreat, deformation of overhanging sandstone, and rear-edge fracture development. Because monitoring signals operate at different spatial and temporal scales, isolated peaks or fixed thresholds cannot reliably distinguish environmental disturbances from progressive stability deterioration. This study investigates a toppling-prone sandstone–mudstone rock mass in the Three Gorges Reservoir area, southwestern China, using field geological investigation, laboratory mechanical and acoustic-emission tests, and multisource monitoring. A mechanism-guided Bayesian diagnostic framework is developed to organize rainfall and humidity as hydraulic evidence, earth pressure and crack displacement as support-adjustment evidence, and tilt and in-situ acoustic-emission observations as deformation–damage evidence. Laboratory tests show that increasing mudstone water content reduces cohesion and friction angle, while repeated wetting–drying promotes slaking and loss of durability. Field observations indicate weak, asynchronous or lagged relationships among rainfall, humidity, pressure, deformation, and acoustic-emission responses. Within the investigated 0–7 d lag window, the relative association between rainfall and acoustic-emission energy is highest at a 2 d lag, but remains weak overall. The Bayesian system therefore provides conditional posterior states under laboratory-informed parameter scenarios rather than uniquely identified failure probabilities. Posterior predictive checks, terminal-period temporal holdout, leave-one-sensor-out analysis, and comparison with external proxy indicators are used to examine temporal stability and evidential consistency. The framework provides a practical reference for long-term inspection and tiered risk management of unstable rock masses in mountainous canyon regions. It is a site-specific diagnostic prototype, not a fully validated failure-prediction or early-warning model; absolute stability indices and warning thresholds require additional geometric, mechanical, and documented failure-event data.

Article.Title: Safe reinforcement learning for aggregated demand response control of emerging flexible resources in active distribution networks
Article.Authors: Liu X.; An L.; Lu Y.; Liu J.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Aggregated demand response is a constrained sequential-control problem because electric vehicles, distributed batteries, thermostatically controlled loads, flexible industrial demand, and behind-the-meter photovoltaic systems are heterogeneous, uncertain, and connected to voltage- and thermal-limited feeders. We formulate portfolio dispatch as a constrained Markov decision process in which a stochastic policy proposes node-mapped aggregate set-points and a weighted projection corrects each proposal against linearized network constraints and aggregate resource constraints. Feasibility of that projection applies only to the linear surrogate at the current operating point; it is not a hard guarantee for the nonlinear feeder. A conditional-value-at-risk term and the measured projection correction discourage operation near critical margins. In the archived synthetic case study on a modified 33-bus feeder, the reported point estimates reduce daily operating cost from 152.3 to 121.4 USD/day, lower the displayed evening net-load peak from 5.8 to 4.7 MW, and increase reported renewable utilization to 90.1%. The archived constraint table contains two voltage samples outside limits, one branch-overload event, one EV departure shortfall, one comfort event, and no storage-state event for the projected controller. The corresponding opportunity counts, controller-time denominator, seed-level records, and paired linear-versus-nonlinear residuals were not retained; consequently, no violation percentage, confidence interval, or seed-independent performance claim is made. The results are descriptive evidence from the supplied aggregate outputs.

Article.Title: Effect of transitional nutrition in intake level of heavy metal from Iranian sauces consumption and its carcinogenic and health risks
Article.Authors: Torkashvand J.; Torkashvand S.; Tamjidi F.
Article.Abstract: Heavy metal content in food is a serious concern due to health consequences for consumers, which is more important in highly consumed foods such as sauces. The aim of this study was to evaluate the concentration of lead, chromium, manganese, zinc, aluminum, copper, and iron in Iranian mayonnaise and ketchup and assess its risk for junk food and health food pattern in three scenarios by Monte Carlo simulation. Sauce samples from four brands were selected based on packaging type into three groups for mayonnaise and two groups for ketchup. The samples were digested and then the metals concentrations were detected using Microwave Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (MP-AES). The results showed that the average concentrations of lead, chromium, manganese, aluminum, copper, zinc, and iron in the studied samples (mayonnaise, ketchup) were (0.67, 0.51), (0.40, 0.39), (0.23, 1.13), (0.89, 1.38), (0.38, 0.90), (4.45, 10.87), and (2.86, 4.12) µg/g, respectively. Although the level of heavy metal intake in the junk food increased significantly compared to the health food, The HI resulting from the detected concentrations in mayonnaise and ketchup was 8.20E-02 in junk food pattern, which indicated an acceptable non-carcinogenic hazard. Also, the ELCR associated with lead and chromium in the studied sauces was 7.56E-05 in junk food pattern, which indicated an acceptable carcinogenic risk. Although no significant risk was observed for consumers at the current consumption rate and the detected concentrations, but considering the increase in sauce consumption in recent decades, which could provide a higher risk, it is necessary to identify the source of heavy metals in sauces and ways to reduce it.

Article.Title: A study of the greenhouse gas emissions inventory and driving factors decomposition in Tongzhou, China
Article.Authors: Hu X.; Wen W.; Yang T.; Liu X.; Shen L.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract District-and county-level greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories remain insufficiently developed, limiting the formulation of targeted mitigation policies at the grassroots governance scale. Taking Tongzhou District, Beijing, as a representative rapidly urbanizing megacity sub-center, this study developed an integrated district-level GHG emissions inventory covering energy activities, agricultural production, LUCF, and waste treatment from 2018 to 2020, and applied the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method to identify sector-specific driving mechanisms. The results show that total GHG emissions excluding LUCF followed a “rise-then-decline” trajectory. Energy activities remained the dominant source, accounting for more than 94% of total emissions. The LMDI results revealed heterogeneous sectoral drivers: energy-sector changes were mainly influenced by energy intensity and emission intensity effects; agricultural emission reductions were primarily associated with African Swine Fever-induced contraction of livestock breeding; and waste-sector fluctuations were mainly driven by changes in municipal solid waste incineration, medical waste treatment, and wastewater-related emissions. These findings suggest that district-level mitigation should adopt differentiated strategies across energy, agriculture, and waste sectors.

Article.Title: High-density SNP mapping reveals genomic hotspots for photosynthetic traits under Huanglongbing disease in citrus
Article.Authors: Gaikwad P.; Sidhu G.; Chintale Y.; Kaur G.; Chhuneja P.; Rattanpal H.; Dhkal M.; Uppal G.
Article.Abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a major constraint to citrus production, but the genetic basis of physiological responses to Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus ( C Las) infection remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized photosynthetic and gas-exchange responses and investigated their genetic architecture in 120 F₁ hybrids derived from ‘Daisy’ tangerine × Carrizo citrange. Hybrids were evaluated before HLB infection and across four subsequent assessment periods following artificial C Las exposure. Fifteen physiological and environmental traits were measured and C Las infection was confirmed in all F₁ hybrids by quantitative real-time PCR. HLB-associated physiological responses were characterized by declines in net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, transpiration and intercellular CO 2 flux, accompanied by increased intercellular CO 2 concentration and vapour pressure deficit. Multivariate analysis indicated that gas exchange and water relations constituted the major sources of phenotypic variation, with the first three principal components explaining 81.81% of the total variation. High broad-sense heritability and genetic advance were observed for several key traits, particularly stomatal conductance, intercellular CO 2 flux, net photosynthetic rate, transpiration and vapour pressure deficit, indicating substantial genetic variation for these responses. High-density parental SNP linkage maps were subsequently used for QTL analysis. Twenty-six QTLs were detected on the ‘Daisy’ tangerine map and 28 on the Carrizo citrange map, with individual loci explaining 10.6–17.8% of phenotypic variance. Several QTLs were repeatedly detected across seasons and overlapping loci were identified for physiologically related traits. These stable genomic regions provide useful targets for validation and further dissection of the genetic basis of physiological responses under HLB infection.

Article.Title: An XGBoost-SHAP classifier to distinguish asymptomatic hyperuricemia from acute primary gouty arthritis
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Peng T.; Lin F.; Liang P.; Ding X.; Ou X.; Deng Q.; Su J.
Article.Abstract: Asymptomatic hyperuricemia (AH) is an important precursor of acute primary gouty arthritis (AGA), but not all patients with AH will progress to acute primary gouty arthritis. Given the limitations of relying solely on uric acid levels to accurately identify AH and AGA, there is an urgent clinical need for an auxiliary identification tool that integrates routine laboratory indicators, possesses discriminative ability, and is easy to interpret. Therefore, this study aims to use machine learning techniques, combined with routine clinical data and laboratory test indicators, to construct and validate an auxiliary decision-making model for identifying patients with AH and AGA and providing clinical support. We will compare the overall performance of different algorithms and elucidate the key features influencing model decisions through SHAP interpretability analysis. This is a single-center retrospective observational study involving a total of 11,763 AH and AGA patients treated at the Third Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine from 2015 to 2025. Cases were divided into a development cohort (2015–2023, n = 9,584) and a temporal validation cohort (2024–2025, n = 2,179), with the development cohort further split into a training set (80%) and a test set (20%). Baseline analysis, collinearity analysis, univariate analysis, multivariate analysis, and univariate ROC analysis were conducted in the training set. Feature selection was performed using LASSO regression and XGBoost-RFECV, followed by multivariate analysis to streamline variables, ultimately incorporating 16 core variables into the model. A total of nine machine learning models were constructed, and their performance was evaluated based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1 score, Kappa value, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHAP methodology was utilized for interpretability analysis of the models. After screening 34 indicators, 16 variables were incorporated into the model, including monocyte count (MONO), uric acid (UA), age (Age), coefficient of variation of red cell distribution width (RDWCV), lymphocyte/monocyte ratio (LYMPH/MONO), neutrophil count (NEUT), basophil count (BASO), creatinine (Crea), hematocrit (HCT), neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), red blood cell count (RBC), sex, percentage of eosinophils (EOrate), standard deviation of red cell distribution width (RDWSD), lymphocyte count (LYMPH), and percentage of monocytes (MONOrate). Comparative results indicated that the XGBoost model exhibited the best performance. The AUC of the validation set was 0.867, with an accuracy of 0.787, sensitivity of 0.775, specificity of 0.807, and average precision (AP) of 0.918. The AUC of the internal test set was 0.876, with an accuracy of 0.797, sensitivity of 0.763, and specificity of 0.851. In the temporal validation series, the XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.823, an accuracy of 0.720, a sensitivity of 0.634, and a specificity of 0.847, demonstrating a degree of generalizability. The XGBoost machine learning model constructed based on routine laboratory indicators (such as MONO, UA, age, RDW-CV, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, NEUT, BASO, creatinine, HCT, NLR, red blood cell count, sex, EO rate, RDW-SD, lymphocyte count, and MONO rate) demonstrated moderate discriminative ability and stability in identifying patients with acute primary gouty arthritis versus asymptomatic hyperuricemia, providing an important basis for clinical differential diagnosis and decision-making, and holding significant clinical value.

Article.Title: PGX-ChurnNet a leakage-controlled cross-schema network for telecom churn early warning
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Wang L.; Gan B.; Xu T.; Niu X.
Article.Abstract: Telecom churn prediction is useful for retention planning only when the observation window precedes the outcome and the evaluation reflects the intended deployment setting. We propose the Planning-Gap-aware Cross-Schema Churn Network (PGX-ChurnNet), integrating semantic-group tokenization, set interactions, training-only memory retrieval, reliability-controlled fusion, and a shared-backbone multi-member output layer. The development data comprised 3150 Iranian mobile customers, with predictors documented for months 1–9 and churn recorded at month 12. Five fixed stratified outer folds were evaluated with five model seeds, yielding 25 descriptive fold–seed evaluations. PGX-ChurnNet achieved F1 0.838 ± 0.010, PR-AUC 0.939 ± 0.007, ROC-AUC 0.986 ± 0.004, and Brier 0.057 ± 0.005. Its seed-averaged F1 difference from TabICLv2 was 0.013, but statistical superiority was not established (raw \(p=0.063\) ; Holm-adjusted \(p=0.625\) ). Frozen evaluation on 8454 Bulgarian business accounts yielded F1 0.306 with source-domain preprocessing and 0.333 with label-blind quantile alignment. Because the Bulgarian snapshot lacks an equivalent planning interval, these values assess cross-domain risk transport rather than replication of three-month early warning. Mapping, feature-eligibility, learning-curve, and scaling analyses defined additional sensitivity and implementation boundaries. Prospective operator-specific validation remains necessary before deployment.

Article.Title: Spatio-temporal assessment of mining-induced environmental changes using remote sensing: a case study of the Talcher Coalfield, Angul District, India
Article.Authors: Islam S.; Pakhira S.; Gogineni A.; Sembeta R.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates the spatio-temporal impacts of coal mining on environmental conditions in the Talcher coalfield region, India, using multi-temporal Landsat data (2000, 2014, and 2023) at 30 m resolution. Land use land cover (LULC) was derived using supervised classification (Maximum Likelihood Algorithm), while vegetation dynamics and thermal characteristics were assessed using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST). In addition, atmospheric column densities were incorporated to analyze key atmospheric pollutants SO₂, NO₂, and CO and to assess air quality variations associated with mining activities. The integrated assessment highlights substantial environmental changes associated with mining and land-use transformation. The LULC analysis (2000–2023) reveals a decline in forest cover (41.33% to 37.37%) and agricultural land (45.62% to 45.04%), accompanied by an increase in built-up areas (6.84% to 8.54%) and mining areas (2.12% to 4.94%), indicating intensified anthropogenic pressure. LST and NDVI analyses (2014–2023) show changes in surface thermal conditions and vegetation characteristics. LST results indicate higher maximum and mean temperatures in mining and built-up areas, with changes between 2014 and 2023 varying among land-use classes, with mining areas showing the highest thermal values, where mean summer LST increased from 42.97 °C (2014) to 46.28 °C (2023), and mean winter LST increased from 38.67 °C to 41.81 °C. NDVI analysis indicates a decline in maximum NDVI values over the study period. The results show a spatial association between LULC changes, NDVI, and LST, with areas of mining and built-up expansion generally corresponding to lower NDVI and higher surface temperatures. Analysis of satellite-derived atmospheric column densities indicates higher SO₂, NO₂, and CO values in mining and industrial regions, with higher values observed during winter.

Article.Title: Development of the impression material-saving (IMS) mixing tip by modifying the twist position and number of elements
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Heo Y.
Article.Abstract: The dental mixing tip is a device used to mix an impression material with a hardener to create a mold of a patient’s teeth, but a substantial amount of material remains inside the tip after use and is subsequently discarded. Because impression materials are expensive, the primary design objective is to minimize unnecessary remnants without compromising mixing efficiency. To meet these requirements, we investigated how the twist position (R L ) of each blade (element) and number of elements (n e ) affect mixing performance. The twist-position ratio was varied among 1.0, 1.5, 2.3, 4.0, and 9.0, and the number of elements was varied from 8 to 11, resulting in 20 different configurations. Mixing performance was experimentally evaluated based on the cross-sectional uniformity of the cured impression material, and the optimized design was further assessed by tensile strength and Shore hardness. Among the 20 configurations, the model with n e = 11 and R L = 4.0 exhibited the highest overall mixing uniformity. The most efficient model, with an internal volume of 1.22 mL compared with 2.22 mL for the commercial mixing tip, achieved a 45.0% reduction in internal volume and was designated as the IMS (Impression Material-Saving) mixing tip. The cured impression material prepared using the IMS tip exhibited a tensile strength of 3.36 MPa compared with 2.90 MPa for the commercial tip, corresponding to a 15.9% increase, while Shore hardness increased from 58 to 62, corresponding to a 6.9% increase. Computational simulations using the VBBC (Variance among Bimodal Bin Counts) index, a histogram-based metric for evaluating mixing uniformity, further confirmed the superior mixing performance of the IMS design. These results indicate that the newly developed IMS mixing tip can substantially reduce internal volume while maintaining effective mixing and the mechanical quality of the cured impression material.

Article.Title: Intra-articular injection of liraglutide attenuates capsular fibrosis and improves shoulder range of motion in a rat model of adhesive capsulitis
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Yeong J.; Kim B.; Suh D.; Jeong S.; Park Y.; Park H.; Yoo J.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adhesive capsulitis is a disabling shoulder disorder characterized by progressive pain and capsular fibrosis, for which intra-articular corticosteroid injection provides only short-term anti-inflammatory relief without directly targeting fibrosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have shown anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects in other organ systems, but their potential in musculoskeletal fibrosis is unexplored. We evaluated intra-articular liraglutide in a rat model of adhesive capsulitis. Thirty rats were allocated at the outset into a non-immobilized sham group and four immobilized groups (saline, triamcinolone, low-dose liraglutide, high-dose liraglutide); two rats died during immobilization, leaving 28 for analysis. After 6 weeks of shoulder immobilization, each immobilized rat received a single intra-articular injection of its assigned agent. Passive shoulder abduction angle, capsular thickness, and immunohistochemical markers of fibrosis were assessed. A linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction for abduction angle ( p = 0.002); at 3 weeks, all three treatment groups improved significantly more than saline. Capsular thickness and fibronectin expression were significantly lower than saline in all three treatment groups, while alpha-smooth muscle actin was significantly reduced only with high-dose liraglutide. These findings identify liraglutide as a candidate antifibrotic approach for adhesive capsulitis warranting further preclinical and clinical investigation.

Article.Title: Construct validity, responsiveness, and minimal important change of the 5 times sit-to-stand test when used with healthy community-living older adults
Article.Authors: Low D.; Shaheen A.; O’Reilly L.; Denny D.; Harkness Armstrong C.; Mitchelmore A.; Bibbey A.; Walsh G.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the responsiveness of five times sit-to-stand test (5STS) to changes in measures of mobility, strength, balance, participants’ quality of life (QOL) and global rating of change. Similarly, the construct validity of the 5STS is explored via comparison to measures of mobility, strength, balance, QOL at baseline. Ninety-six community-living older adults completed the following tests at baseline: the 5STS, single leg stand, timed up and go (TUG), 2-min walk distance (2MWD), and QOL. Correlation analyses compared the 5STS time to measurements of the other tests at baseline, as well as changes in the measurements after 12 weeks following a functional fitness assessment and advice for fitness improvement, given at the start of the summer. Furthermore, Receiver Operating Characteristics measured the 5STS’s discriminatory ability. Baseline 5STS correlated with measures of balance, mobility and QOL. The 5STS was also responsive to changes in QOL, TUG, and 2MWD and discriminated between those with a positive and no change in QOL; a 1.48 s reduction in 5STS is the threshold for this discrimination. The 5STS is a valid and responsive measure of dynamic balance and mobility. The time of 1.48 s offers a novel metric that demonstrates an important change in 5STS in a community-living older adult population.

Article.Title: Investigating the effect of theory-based educational intervention on enhancing physical activity and reducing weight among overweight and obese students
Article.Authors: Alizadeh N.; Keshavarz M.; Keshtkaran Z.; Salami J.; Golab F.; Kamyab A.; Jeihooni A.
Article.Abstract: Overweight and obesity among adolescents pose significant public health challenges worldwide, increasing the risk of chronic diseases and psychological problems. Promoting physical activity is a key preventive strategy, yet many adolescents do not meet recommended activity levels. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) provides a useful framework for designing educational interventions to modify health behaviors. This study aimed to investigate the effect of a TPB-based educational intervention on enhancing physical activity and reducing weight among overweight and obese high school students in Fasa city, Iran. A quasi-experimental study was conducted on 240 high school students randomly assigned to intervention ( n = 120) and control ( n = 120) groups. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire that included demographic information, constructs of the Theory of Planned Behavior (knowledge, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and behavioral intention), and the short-form International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) to assess physical activity levels. Anthropometric measurements (weight, height, and BMI) were recorded before and four months after the intervention. The intervention consisted of eight interactive educational sessions designed according to TPB constructs, employing lectures, group discussions, visual materials, and physical activities. Data analysis was performed using chi-square, independent t -tests, and paired t -tests, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 240 overweight and obese students (mean age 14.8 ± 0.7 years; 54.2% female) participated in the study. At baseline, both groups were comparable in demographic characteristics, TPB constructs, physical activity, and BMI (p > 0.05). Mean pre-intervention BMI was 26.3 ± 8.7 kg/m², and average physical activity was about 380 MET-min/week. Four months after the intervention, the intervention group showed significant increases in knowledge, attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, behavioral intention, and physical activity levels (p < 0.001), along with significant reductions in weight and BMI (p < 0.05). No significant changes occurred in the control group. The TPB-based educational program effectively enhanced physical activity-related cognitive and behavioral factors and contributed to weight reduction among overweight and obese adolescents. These findings support the integration of theory-driven interventions in school health promotion programs to address adolescent obesity.

Article.Title: Functional characterization and pharmacochaperone rescue of a novel SLC6A1 variant associated with developmental epileptic encephalopathies
Article.Authors: Song Z.; DeLeeuw M.; Mandelenaki D.; Shen W.; Eda R.; Wang J.; Kang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mutations in SLC6A1 , encoding the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter 1 (GAT-1), are associated with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy syndromes, intellectual disability (ID), and autism. An important question is whether the impact of these mutations can be predicted at scale using artificial intelligence (AI), and how such predictions correlate with experimental findings. In this study, AI was explored as a predictive tool, not as a replacement for data collected experimentally. We reported clinical presentations including seizures and EEG features, autism related phenotypes and motor skills in a novel variant c.1069G > A (p.Ala357Thr, A357T) in two siblings. We used both AI tools and experimental approaches to characterize this novel mutation in the SLC6A1 gene and compared it with another variant in the same amino acid, c.1070 C > T (p.Ala357Val, A357V). Both AI and experimental approaches indicate that the GAT-1(A357T) and (A357V) mutations destabilize the global protein conformation and have increased localization inside the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Additionally, the presence of the mutant GAT-1 made the wildtype GAT-1 less mature. Radioactive 3 H-labeled GABA uptake assay indicated the mutation drastically reduced the function of the GAT-1(A357T) compared with the wildtype across cell types and pharmacochaperones such as 4-phenylbutyrate rescued the trafficking and function of the mutant GAT-1. Common and differential clinical phenotypes were identified in the siblings carrying the same variant. Mutant GAT-1 caused increased ER retention and impaired the trafficking of wild type GAT-1. PBA treatment rescued the mutant GAT-1 protein expression and GABA uptake function. AI-assisted in silico protein structural modeling and experimental approaches consistently suggest that the A357T and A357V variants destabilize global GAT-1 protein conformation. AI-assisted protein stability predictions provide supportive structural insight but cannot replace experimental assessment of GAT-1 expression and function.

Article.Title: Rock mass quality characterization through integrated outcrop, petrographic, geomechanical, and geophysical methods of gabbronorites of Nawagai Mélange
Article.Authors: Idrees M.; Khan M.; Shah M.; Hasan M.; Doyoro Y.; Ali L.; Sajid M.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Reliable rock-mass characterization in structurally complex terrain requires spatial information beyond conventional drilling and surface mapping. This study presents an integrated framework combining outcrop mapping, petrography, synthetic and field electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), and laboratory testing to characterize gabbronorites in the Nawagai Mélange. Outcrop mapping reveals a two-layer gabbronorite structure: an intensely weathered, locally deformed upper layer (L1) overlying a relatively fresh, competent layer (L2). Synthetic and field ERT models corroborate this stratification, with L1 defined by low resistivity and L2 by high resistivity. L1 is characterized by resistivity < 1000 Ω m, Kv of 0.15–0.55, RQD of 25–75%, UCS of 40.4–55.0 MPa, porosity of 0.19–0.28%, and water absorption of 0.07–0.10%, while L2 shows resistivity > 1000 Ω m (locally exceeding 10,000 Ω m), Kv of 0.55–1.00, RQD of 75–100%, UCS of 70.5–97.9 MPa, porosity of 0.05–0.27%, and water absorption of 0.02–0.09%. Petrographic analysis supports these results, revealing extensive mineral alteration, clay formation, and microfracturing in L1 as against the intact mineral fabrics preserved in L2. Overall, the fresh gabbronorite (L2) with its higher UCS, RQD, Kv, and resistivity alongside lower porosity reflects good rock-mass quality, whereas the weathered L1 remains mechanically weak. This multi-scale approach enhances subsurface characterization in data-scarce, drilling-limited regions and highlights the value of integrating multiple methods for robust rock-mass assessment in complex tectonic settings.

Article.Title: Combined reinforcement mechanism of TEOS-barium oxalate-phosphate composite on weathered sandstone
Article.Authors: Huang D.; Ge M.; Qi Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sandstone is one of the main rock types constituting stone-based heritage objects. Due to long-term outdoor exposure, sandstone typically exhibits deterioration such as weathering, surface powdering, and structural weakening. To address these issues, this study developed a reinforcement material composed of tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), barium hydroxide, and oxalic-phosphoric acid. The reinforcement mechanism and microstructure of the material were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). The reinforcement applicability was systematically evaluated in terms of appearance, color difference, mechanical strength, and aging resistance. The results demonstrate that TEOS form silica–matrix materials, while barium hydroxide reacts with oxalic/phosphoric acid to form in-situ inorganic salt precipitates of barium oxalate and barium phosphate. The silica gel and inorganic precipitates mutually fill the pore spaces, enhancing the mechanical strength, structural stability, and weathering resistance of the sandstone, while largely preserving the original appearance of the cultural relics.

Article.Title: Synergistic emission-aware energy management of a multi-energy microgrid with electric mobility integration incorporating a new composite operational flexibility index
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Mahdiraji E.; Niaz Azari M.; Pahnehkolaei S.
Article.Abstract: Due to increasing integration of renewable energy sources along with electric vehicles, new uncertainties related to solar radiation, wind velocity, load consumption, and EV charging demand have emerged. Together with contradictory economic, environmental, and operational targets such as the requirement of flexibility, these uncertainties make it hard for traditional deterministic optimization methods to solve the problem. In this paper, a new paradigm is suggested for carbon-aware transactive energy management in multi-source microgrids, including photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WT), microturbines (MT), fuel cells (FC), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicle/e-bike charging stations with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and battery-to-grid (B2G) capabilities. The developed synergistic paradigm minimizes operating costs, reduces pollutant emissions, and increases a new composite operational flexibility index (COFI) over 24 h through a transactive energy coordination mechanism that enables efficient interaction between peers and the grid. In order to find a solution to this multi-objective optimization problem, the multi-objective Sinh Cosh Optimizer (MOSCHO) algorithm is proposed, using properties of hyperbolic functions in order to provide an effective combination of exploration and exploitation. Stochastic modeling is carried out by means of a cloud theory-based approach, where initially 1000 scenarios are generated with an incremental cloud generator and then reduced to 50 scenarios with the K-means algorithm. A fuzzy decision-making procedure is used to pick the best compromise solution from the found Pareto front. Simulations on a test microgrid showed that using the BESS allows decreasing the cost of operation by 10.7% and increasing COFI based-flexibility by 161%. Further, the introduction of V2G/B2G charging stations decreases the cost of operation and increases flexibility by 43.7%. The stochastic model ensures higher reliability of the results under uncertainties. Validation of the results obtained with the stochastic model with the Monte Carlo method proved high accuracy and a 17% reduction in computation time. Comparing with MOPSO, it is found that MOSCHO is better in quality of the Pareto front, convergence, and diversity of solutions. The proposed scheme can be regarded as an effective approach for energy management in microgrids under uncertain conditions.

Article.Title: Machine-learning prediction of optical band gaps and photocatalytic performance in rare-earth-doped spinel ferrites
Article.Authors: Katoch G.; Sharma G.; Santhosh A.
Article.Abstract: Rare-earth substitution is widely used to regulate the lattice structure, defect chemistry, optical absorption, charge-carrier dynamics, and magnetic recoverability of spinel ferrites. Published photocatalytic results, however, are distributed across different hosts, dopants, pollutants, irradiation sources, catalyst dosages, and reaction times, which prevents direct comparison by degradation percentage alone. A leakage-controlled and reproducible small-data machine-learning workflow was therefore developed from 37 records compiled from published literature and arranged into 20 analytical groups, with closely related catalyst-condition records retained within the same validation group. Ridge regression, random forest, extremely randomized trees, and gradient boosting were evaluated using leave-one-group-out cross-validation. Random forest gave the lowest error among the four candidate regressors, with a mean absolute error of 21.43 percentage points (95% analytical-group bootstrap confidence interval: 12.88–28.10), a root mean square error of 27.11 percentage points (95% confidence interval: 14.67–34.19), and R 2 = − 0.56. A training-fold mean baseline gave a lower MAE of 19.96 percentage points, confirming limited generalization performance for unseen groups. Random row-wise five-fold validation was substantially more optimistic (R 2 = 0.36), illustrating the risk of protocol leakage in literature-derived datasets. Optical band gap remained an informative descriptor but was not sufficient to explain activity. The study provides a reproducible benchmark, uncertainty-aware interpretation, and a practical reporting checklist for future machine-learning-assisted studies of rare-earth-doped spinel ferrites.

Article.Title: Knowledge, skills, and performance of maternal health literacy among Iranian midwives: a cross-sectional study in Kermanshah
Article.Authors: Qaderi K.; Hamidi N.; Bagherinia M.; Jamali B.; Heydarpour F.; Moradinazar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maternal health literacy is linked to improved pregnancy outcomes. This study quantifies knowledge, skills, and performance in maternal health literacy among practicing Iranian midwives. In this cross-sectional, descriptive-analytical study, 300 midwives from Kermanshah, Iran, were recruited by convenience sampling between December 2023 and May 2024. Data were collected using the standardized Instrument for Assessment of Knowledge, Skills, and Performance of Maternal Health Literacy among Midwives 15 , consisting of knowledge (5 items), skills (3 items), and performance (5 items) rated on 5-point Likert scales. Analyses were conducted using SPSS version 23. Descriptive statistics and inferential analyses, including independent t-tests, ANOVA, Spearman correlation, and multivariable linear regression analyses, were performed. Statistical significance was considered at p < 0.05. The mean age of participants was 39 ± 9 years (range: 23–65), and the mean work experience was 12.9 ± 8.7 years. The mean scores for knowledge, skills, and performance were 17.10 ± 3.35, 11.52 ± 2.10, and 20.80 ± 3.42, respectively. Work experience showed a significant inverse correlation with knowledge scores ( p = 0.026), whereas no significant correlations were observed between work experience and skills ( p = 0.913) or performance ( p = 0.461). Higher educational attainment was associated with higher knowledge scores ( p = 0.030). Skill level was the strongest predictor of performance in the multivariable linear regression model ( p < 0.001). Age was positively associated with performance ( p = 0.010), while midwives working in clinical care ( p = 0.048) and private sectors ( p = 0.010) had lower performance scores compared with those working in public health settings. Higher educational attainment was associated with knowledge scores, while age, skill level, and department of service were associated with performance scores among Iranian midwives; work experience showed only a weak inverse association with knowledge. These findings support targeted educational programs and improvements in workplace conditions that could be associated with improved maternal health literacy and quality of care.

Article.Title: Bayesian mediation multi-state model elucidates the impact of cancer immunity on multiple oncology endpoints after chemoradiotherapy for esophageal cancer
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhou J.; Wei P.; Liu Q.; Jiang X.; Xia H.; Zhou J.; Lin S.; Mohan R.; Hobbs B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Unraveling the complex relationships among interventions, intermediate health states, and survival outcomes is crucial to translating advances in clinical research into optimal cancer therapies. We propose a novel Bayesian multi-state mediation model to evaluate the direct and indirect effects of radiation modalities on overall survival (OS). Our model extends traditional mediation analysis by incorporating a multistate framework that accounts for intermediate outcomes, such as tumor response and progression or recurrence, providing a more detailed representation of treatment impact over time. Bayesian estimation and variable selection enhance model reliability and address uncertainty in parameters and structure, providing robust estimates of direct and mediated effects. The method characterizes dynamic relationships between endpoints and intermediate health states which may be time-varying mediators. Furthermore, our study highlights the clinical importance of considering intermediate outcomes in the evaluation of treatment efficacy and patient survival. The model is applied to a propensity-matched retrospective cohort of 510 esophageal cancer patients treated with proton beam therapy (PBT) or intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT).
