We used fMRI to ask: (A) to what extent does brain activity overlap between cognitive offloading and deliberate forgetting, and (B) what is the neural fate of offloaded information? Participants viewed face or scene pictures, then received a cue either to (A) remember them for a memory test, (B) offload them, meaning that the test would come with an automatic reminder, or (C) forget them because there would be no test. Offload cues generated brain activity that closely resembled forget cues. Moreover, multivariate pattern analysis showed that the neural trace of to-be-remembered information persisted in the remember condition but faded until it was statistically absent in both the offload and forget conditions, which did not differ from each other. Therefore, when people offload memories into external technology, this has similar neural correlates to deliberate forgetting, leading to a weakened neural representation of to-be-remembered information. We argue that this may be an adaptive process that prioritises the most valuable information for limited-capacity neural systems.

Article.Title: Label-free multimodal nonlinear optical imaging reveals key biomarkers of cellular radiation response
Article.Authors: Gagnon J.; Vuong N.; Flores D.; Buragina T.; Azzam E.; Chauhan V.; Murugkar S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ionizing radiation elicits complex and dynamic cellular responses that are not fully captured by conventional analytic approaches. Many existing assays typically rely on population-averaged measurements, require extensive and/or destructive sample preparation, or depend on exogenous contrast agents for single-cell analysis. Additionally, they often focus on isolated biomarkers rather than concurrent changes in key macromolecular constituents such as lipids and proteins. To address these limitations, we developed a label-free, multimodal nonlinear optical (NLO) imaging platform that integrates stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy at Raman shifts of 2850 cm⁻¹ and 2926 cm⁻¹ with two-photon excitation fluorescence (TPEF) microscopy targeting reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (phosphate) [NAD(P)H] and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD). In foundational studies, we characterized the radiobiological effects of clinical X-ray doses (2–10 Gy) in human lung cancer A549 cells. Irradiated cells exhibited multiple quantifiable biomarkers that varied with radiation dose and post-irradiation time. These included changes in lipid and protein signals, differences in NAD(P)H and FAD intensities, higher lipid-to-protein ratios, enhanced optical redox ratio, enlarged cell and lipid droplet areas, and increased colocalization of lipid droplets with mitochondria. Collectively, these results establish NLO imaging as a sensitive and powerful modality for quantitatively assessing cellular responses to clinical doses of ionizing radiation.

Article.Title: Investigating the high seismic velocities and buoyancy of cratonic roots – the possibility of diamond
Article.Authors: Debayle E.; Ricard Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. These keels have probably been formed early in Earth’s history, and the preservation of these deep, cold, and highly viscous roots in a convective mantle remains enigmatic. A classical view is that the excess density due to colder temperatures is compensated for by a light composition. Here, we map the magnesium number (Mg#, a proxi for mantle depletion) within cratonic keels, based on the thermochemical interpretation of a global shear velocity model. Our interpretation suggests that depletion is strong above 150 km (Mg#>92), and decreases with depth down to the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB). However, changing only the major element composition and the Mg# does not fully meet the requirements implied by seismology or gravity observations. We explore various hypotheses, varying the temperature of the lithosphere, considering the presence of eclogite, accounting for chromium or for a minute quantity of diamonds. We also discuss the uncertainties in seismological observations of velocity and radial anisotropy as well as in mineralogical models. Changes in temperature, the presence of eclogite, of Cr incorporated in garnet, or radial anisotropy are inconsistent with shear velocity and gravity constraints when considered individually. Below the graphite/diamond transition, the combination of depletion with a low volume fraction of diamond (< 1% at 150 km) appears to be the simplest way to explain the very high shear velocities, while maintaining the cratonic lithosphere close to neutral buoyancy. This small amount of diamond accounts for only 0.5% of the mantle’s carbon and can be formed within a reasonable geological timescale (> 180 Ma) through the subduction of organic carbon.

Article.Title: Virus-specific effects of disease-modifying therapies on herpesvirus antibody titers in multiple sclerosis
Article.Authors: Ruberto S.; Domínguez-Mozo M.; Villar L.; Costa-Frossard L.; Villarrubia N.; Aladro Y.; Casanova-Peño I.; Martínez-Ginés M.; García-Domínguez J.; Ortega-Madueño I.; Pérez de Villar G.; Alonso-Garrido A.; Pérez-Gutiérrez I.; García-Martínez M.; Arroyo R.; Álvarez-Lafuente R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) have both been implicated in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet it remains unclear whether disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) shape antiviral humoral responses. We analyzed antiviral IgG titers in MS patients stratified by current DMT (N = 498 for HHV-6A/B, 410 for EBNA-1, 361 for cytomegalovirus (CMV)). Multivariable regression models were built separately for each virus, adjusting for age, sex, HLA-DRB1*15:01 carriage, EDSS, treatment duration, and prior treatment efficacy, using interferon-beta (IFN-beta) as the reference category. The HHV-6A/B model showed a significant global fit (p = 1.16 × 10^-6), with fingolimod independently associated with reduced titers relative to IFN-beta (p = 0.006), alongside negative effects of age (p = 0.001) and higher titers among HLA-DRB1*15:01 carriers (p = 0.028). Neither the EBNA-1 nor the CMV model reached global significance, although age remained a strong predictor of CMV IgG (p = 0.002). These findings indicate that DMTs do not exert a uniform effect on herpesvirus serology in MS: fingolimod is specifically associated with attenuated HHV-6A/B seroreactivity, whereas EBNA-1 and CMV titers appear to be governed mainly by host factors. Interpreting antiviral serology in MS from a treatment-stratified perspective may therefore be necessary to identify biologically significant signals specific to each drug.

Article.Title: Engineering properties of green chickpea plants and pods for machine design of a green pod stripper
Article.Authors: Singh D.; Goyal R.; Singh M.; Singh I.; Bindra S.; Dixit A.; Singh B.
Article.Abstract: Sustainable product development in agricultural mechanization increasingly relies on data-driven knowledge to design efficient technologies and improve the utilization of energy inputs. Physical and engineering properties of the green chickpea crop plants and pods are necessary for designing efficient stripping, handling, and storage equipment. Two varieties (PBG7 and PBG10) and two planting methods (Bed and Flat) were taken as independent parameters. Study investigated plant parameters (3 replications of each treatment) such as plant height, width, primary and secondary branch angles along with pod properties (3 replications of each treatment) including pod placement, length, breadth, thickness, geometric mean diameter, sphericity, weight, bulk density, and angle of repose. Plant architecture and pod engineering properties were measured and analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) at p ≤ 0.05. Bed planting significantly increased plant height and width compared to flat sowing. Among the varieties, PBG10 was taller (79.4 cm) and more upright, producing pods having large geometric mean diameter of 14.7 mm by length (22.8 mm), breadth (11.8 mm), thickness (11.9 mm) and higher thousand pod weight of 833.5 g and sphericity of 64.5%, while PBG7 exhibited a wider branch angle (51.3°), higher bulk density (475.4 kg/m 3 ) and angle of repose (45.09°). PBG7 exhibited a bushier growth habit with a significantly greater plant width (50.6 cm) and produced a maximum of 53.5 pods per plant compared to 49.7 for PBG10. PBG7 pods were smaller, with mean dimensions of 20.77 mm (length), 9.59 mm (breadth), and 9.19 mm (thickness), and lighter, with a thousand pod weight of 590.71 g. Pod dimensions, geometric mean diameter, sphericity, thousand pod weight, and bulk density differed significantly between varieties, while the angle of repose did not differ significantly. This study provides important engineering information on green chickpea plants and pods for designing a mechanical green pod stripper. The findings can help in developing an efficient pod stripping machine by providing initial design parameters such as finger spacing, operating height, reel diameter and working width for different chickpea varieties.

Article.Title: Experimental evaluation of smart water flooding in heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs under high pressure and high temperature for enhanced oil recovery
Article.Authors: Al Alwan A.; Khamehchi E.
Article.Abstract: Smart-water flooding has emerged as a promising enhanced oil recovery (EOR) technique for improving oil production from heterogeneous carbonate reservoirs. This study experimentally evaluates engineered smart-brine injection using five carbonate core plugs from the WQ1-57 oilfield under high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) conditions. Three flooding scenarios were investigated sequentially: formation-water flooding, treated-water flooding, and engineered smart-water flooding. Core-flooding experiments were performed to evaluate cumulative oil recovery, differential pressure (ΔP), relative permeability, and effluent-ion behavior. Formation-water flooding produced oil recovery factors ranging from 31.7% to 50.4% OOIP, which increased to 41.2%-57.1% OOIP after treated-water injection and further improved to 47.2%-65.0% OOIP following smart-water flooding, corresponding to an incremental recovery of 16.8–28.9% OOIP over the formation-water case. Relative permeability analysis demonstrated a shift toward more water-wet conditions, accompanied by lower residual oil saturation and improved water-flow characteristics. Effluent-ion analysis confirmed the participation of Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, and SO₄²⁻ in fluid-rock interactions responsible for wettability alteration. The results also indicated that the tested cores exhibited pronounced permeability heterogeneity (17–1020 mD) compared with the relatively narrow porosity range (19.4–29.3%), resulting in differences in flow behavior and recovery response. The observed recovery improvement demonstrates the potential of engineered smart-water flooding under the investigated HPHT laboratory conditions. Further reservoir-specific investigation, numerical simulation, economic assessment, and pilot-scale validation are required before field implementation.

Article.Title: Binary phosphonium ionic liquids induced synergistic modulation of electrochemical performance in polymer electrolytes for dual energy devices
Article.Authors: Rawat S.; Singh P.; Aldosari S.; Diantoro M.; Alheety M.; Buraidah M.; Savilov S.; Johari R.; Singh R.; Osman Z.; Subramaniam R.
Article.Abstract: The advancement of cost-effective, efficient and sustainable electrochemical devices has garnered significate interest, leading to an aggressive expansion of research aimed at enhancing their performance across various dimensions, including electrode, electrolytes and even computational perspectives. Ionic liquids infused with polymer electrolytes have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for advanced devices, owing to their high conductivity and electrochemical stability. In this study, we present a binary system comprising a polymer electrolyte and phosphonium ionic liquids (PIL), employing polyethylene oxide (PEO) as host matrix and two phosphonium ionic liquids—specifically, tributylmethylphosphonium iodide (TMPI) and tributylmethylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TBMP-TFSI) at various compositions, with the aim of significantly enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals that the incorporation of a binary ionic liquid (IL) leads to a maximum ionic conductivity of 2.04 × 10⁻³ S/cm. Structural analyses confirmed the optimization of the amorphous phase and segmental motion within the polymer matrix. The optimized polymer electrolyte was subsequently evaluated in an electric double-layer capacitor (EDLC), achieving a specific capacitance of 138 F/g at a scan rate of 10 mV/s. The EDLC achieved a maximum specific discharge capacitance of 109 F/g, with a coulombic efficiency of 90%, an energy density of 17.7 Wh/kg and a power density of 5.4 kW/kg. Furthermore, its application in a dye-sensitized solar cell resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 1.48%. These results demonstrate that the optimized polymer electrolyte exhibits enhanced photovoltaic efficiency in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) and high capacitive performance in electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), thereby illustrating its dual functionality.

Article.Title: A novel machine-learning model using nuclear features to predict upper tract urothelial carcinoma recurrence
Article.Authors: Muraoka R.; Saito A.; Tokuyama N.; Matsubara S.; Shen B.; Tsujino T.; Komura K.; Hashimoto T.; Azuma H.; Nagao T.; Kuroda M.; Ohno Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Upper-tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is rare, constitutes < 5% of urothelial cancers, and, given its insidious clinical presentation, is typically diagnosed at advanced stages; post-radical nephroureterectomy recurrence remains challenging. Postoperative management is primarily guided by pathological factors, including T-stage and lymph-node status, which cannot accurately identify patients who would benefit from treatment intensification, particularly considering concerns regarding cisplatin-associated nephrotoxicity. Using an artificial intelligence (AI)-informed pathology model, we predicted postoperative recurrence using UTUC’s quantitative nuclear features. Among 222 patients with UTUC, support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) models were trained using pT3 cases ( n = 68) comprising sufficient recurrence events. Patient-level model performance was evaluated and validated using an independent test cohort ( n = 50; pT1 = 12, pT2 = 11, pT3 = 22, and pT4 = 5). RF and SVM models achieved patient-level accuracies of 77.3% and 63.6%, respectively, in pT3 cases and overall accuracies of 80% and 68%, respectively, in the independent pT1–pT4 cohort. Model-derived risk stratification (1 point per model with predicted recurrence probability ≥ 0.5 and classifying patients into low, intermediate, and high-risk groups [0, 1, and 2 points, respectively]) significantly discriminated recurrence-free survival in the independent test cohort (pT1–pT4), distinguishing risk groups (low-risk: n = 7, intermediate-risk: n = 8, high-risk: n = 35; log-rank p = 0.01); the low-risk group had no recurrence.

Article.Title: Incidence and predictors of acute decompensation in adult patients with cirrhosis: a retrospective cohort study at the University of Gondar comprehensive Specialized Hospitals, Northwest Ethiopia, 2025
Article.Authors: Altaye K.; Asmare L.; Mekonnen F.
Article.Abstract: Cirrhosis with its acute decompensation and its complications causes significant morbidity and mortality. It also markedly reduces the quality of life and is by far the main reason for repeated hospitalization in patients with cirrhosis. There is also global disparity in mortality rate, which is higher in developing countries than developed countries. The factors affecting the incidence and predictors of acute decompensations among cirrhosis patients are not well studied and known. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of acute decompensation among adult cirrhotic patients at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospitals in northwest Ethiopia in 2025. An institution-based retrospective cohort study was conducted from January 1, 2020 to December 30,2024 at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital among 403 participants. All adult patients aged ≥ 18 years who had cirrhosis during the study period were included. Data were collected using a structured, pre-tested checklist by reviewing patients’ charts. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the characteristics of the study population. Bivariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify the predictors of acute decompensation. 95% confidence intervals of hazard ratios and p-values < 0.05 in the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model were used to identify the significant predictor variables. The Schoenfeld residuals test was used to assess the fitness of the Cox proportional hazards model. A total of 403 adult patients with cirrhosis were followed for 965.71 person-years. At the end of the follow-up, 195/403 (48.3%) patients developed acute decompensations with an incidence rate of 20 acute decompensations per 100 person-years of observation (95% CI: 17–23). The overall median survival time was 3.73 years (95% CI for median survival: 3.50 − 4.24), and the median time to acute decompensation among acute decompensation patients was 1.53 years (IQR: 0.62–3.59). Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (59.9%) was the leading acute decompensation event, followed by Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (37.9%), jaundice (7.7%), and Hepatic encephalopathy (6.2%). The Cox proportional hazard regression model was fitted to identify predictors of acute decompensations. From the multivariable analysis Hemoglobin < 7 g/dl (AHR = 2.44, 95% CI:1.64–3.63), hemoglobin of 7–11.5 g/dl (AHR = 1.72, 95% CI:1.14–2.62), Serum Glutamic-Oxaloacetic Transaminase > 100 IU/L (AHR = 1.77, 95% CI:1.10–2.85,) and International Normalized Ratio > 2 (AHR = 1.55, 97% CI:1.01–2.37). and log-transformed creatinine (AHR = 1.50, 95% CI:1.12–2.01) were significant predictors of the incidence of acute decompensation. In this study, the incidence of acute decompensations in patients with cirrhosis is high and occurred early. Decreased Hemoglobin, high Serum Glutamic-Oxaloacetic Transaminase, International Normalized Ratio, and creatinine were significantly associated with increased risk of acute decompensation. Therefore, following these parameters and correcting these abnormal finding in patients with cirrhosis will decrease the incidence rate.

Article.Title: Machine learning-driven identification of a ubiquitination-related prognostic signature and potential target NRDP1 in bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Zhong Z.; Zheng F.; Li S.; He J.; Yuan Y.; Deng X.; Fu B.; Xiong S.
Article.Abstract: Ubiquitination-regulated molecular events exert crucial regulatory effects on the initiation and progression of bladder cancer (BCa), yet clinically actionable ubiquitination-related prognostic models are still in short supply. This study is designed to construct a ubiquitination-associated prognostic signature for BCa via machine learning strategies. Ten machine learning algorithms with 101 parameter combinations analyzed BCa transcriptomes. The prognostic model was validated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, nomogram construction, and multivariate Cox regression. To elucidate underlying biological functions, we conducted immune microenvironment profiling (via CIBERSORT algorithm) and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). Molecular docking experiments were performed using PubChem compound libraries, Protein Data Bank structures, and the CB-DOCK2 platform to screen potential drug targets. Subsequent experimental validation included Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), cell migration assays (Transwell and wound healing assays), and cell proliferation evaluations (colony formation and CCK-8 assays). Transcriptomic analysis identified 106 ubiquitination-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) specific to BCa, among which 9 prognosis-related genes were filtered out via univariate Cox regression analysis. Our machine learning-based ubiquitination-related prognosis-associated signature showed superior performance over conventional clinical predictors, enabling accurate stratification of BCa patients into high- and low-risk subgroups. Computational docking results revealed strong binding affinities between the E3 ubiquitin ligase NRDP1 and classic agents. Notably, targeted knockdown of NRDP1 substantially impaired the migration capabilities of BCa cells. This study introduces a BCa machine learning derived prognostic model, identifies NRDP1 as a key BCa prognostic and therapeutic target, and highlights the value of integrating machine learning and ubiquitination biology.

Article.Title: Functional independence and sociodemographic determinants of activities of daily living among patients with thalassemia in Southern Iraq: a cross-sectional analytical study
Article.Authors: Tuama A.; Hussein A.; hashim L.; Elbilgahy A.; Mohammed B.; Mersal F.; Hashad R.
Article.Abstract: Thalassemia is a chronic hereditary hemoglobinopathy that may impair functional independence and performance of activities of daily living (ADL) among affected children. This study aimed to assess the level of functional independence in activities of daily living (ADL) and examine its association with selected sociodemographic characteristics among pediatric patients with thalassemia in Southern Iraq. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted on a purposive non-probability sample of 150 children and adolescents (aged 6–18 years) with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia who attended the Thalassemia Center in Thi-Qar Province between March and May 2026. Data were collected through structured face-to-face interviews using a socio-demographic questionnaire and the Arabic-adapted Katz Index of Independence in ADL, comprising 18 items grouped into eight domains. Descriptive statistics, the chi-square test with Cramér’s V effect size, and Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test as sensitivity analyses, and multiple linear regression were used. Multicategory predictors were entered as dummy-coded categorical variables. Most participants (73.3%) demonstrated a moderate level of functional independence in ADLs, 22.0% demonstrated a high level, and 4.7% demonstrated a low level. No statistically significant associations were observed between ADL levels and residence, gender, age group, educational level, or family socioeconomic status (all p > 0.05; Cramér’s V = 0.073–0.192). Likewise, none of these sociodemographic variables independently predicted the total ADL score in the multiple linear regression model (all p > 0.05). Most pediatric patients with thalassemia in Southern Iraq exhibited a moderate level of functional independence in ADLs, with feeding and transfer as the domains with the highest performance. The examined sociodemographic characteristics were not significantly associated with and did not independently predict ADL performance, suggesting that factors other than the sociodemographic characteristics examined in the present study may contribute to functional outcomes; however, these factors were not directly measured.

Article.Title: Sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices, skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among Malaysian national-level outdoor athletes
Article.Authors: Shamsuri N.; Tham C.; Foo K.; Md Kamarulzaman E.; Sait N.; Mohad Kamil A.; Abdul Halim N.; Jamil N.
Article.Abstract: Outdoor athletes in equatorial regions are exposed to high levels of ultraviolet (UV) radiation year-round, increasing the risk of cumulative photodamage. However, evidence on sun protection behaviours and personal UVB exposure among athletes in tropical settings remains limited. This study assessed sun protection knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP), skin pigmentation and personal UVB exposure among national-level outdoor athletes in Malaysia. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 79 athletes (53.2% female) from five sporting disciplines. Sun protection KAP was assessed using a culturally adapted questionnaire. Skin pigmentation was objectively measured using spectrophotometry, while personal UVB exposure was quantified using polysulphone film badges. Male athletes were predominantly classified within the darker ITA-based skin colour categories and had greater exposed body surface area than female athletes during training and non-training periods. UVB exposure differed significantly across sporting disciplines, with sailing athletes recording the highest daily exposure (3.5 ± 1.2 SED/day). Female athletes had higher attitude scores than male athletes (79.8 ± 8.2% vs. 74.1 ± 8.8%; P = 0.003). Knowledge was positively correlated with attitudes ( ρ = 0.567; P < 0.001) and practices ( ρ = 0.305; P = 0.006). Overall, sun-protective practices remained inconsistent, highlighting the need for sport-specific sun safety strategies.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of behavioral interventions on knowledge, attitude, and adherence to prenatal Multiple Micro-nutrients Suplement among pregnant women in Ethiopia: a post-test only cluster randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Yadate T.; Lejore E.; Dagnaw T.; Kelemu H.; Sharma R.; Chiteckwe S.; Maru D.; Koki E.; Gelana N.; Assefa E.; Handebo S.
Article.Abstract: Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation (MMS) has been identified as a vital strategy to enhance maternal health; however, achieving sustained adherence remains challenging. There is insufficient evidence on the potential of contextually appropriate behavioral interventions to improve MMS-related knowledge, attitudes, and adherence beyond routine antenatal care. Thus, this trial was designed to provide empirical evidence on whether these specific strategies could improve MMS knowledge, attitudes, and adherence among pregnant women in Ethiopia. A post-test-only cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted from June 20, to October 20, 2024 in 29 health centers across 6 woredas in 5 Regions in Ethiopia to evaluate the effects of three behavioral interventions on MMS (knowledge, attitude, and adherence). A total of 588 pregnant women were assessed at the end-line, with 151 mothers in Treatment 1, 164 in Treatment 2, 106 in Treatment 3, and 167 in the control group. For both primary and secondary outcome variables, we employed mixed-effects logistic regression with a random intercept for the cluster to account for within-cluster correlation. The models adjusted for socio-demographic characteristics and pregnancy related profiles of participants. The mean age of participants was 25.3 years (SD ± 5), with significant differences across the four study arms ( p < 0.001). Overall, participants demonstrated high knowledge and attitude toward MMS, whereas adherence remained suboptimal. Compared to the intervention group the control group had highest knowledge score AOR = 0.20 (95% CI 0.07–0.54, p = 0.002). None of the intervention groups demonstrated a statistically significant impact on attitude toward MMS uptake. The Gameboard intervention had three times effect on adherence to MMS uptake in the last three months compared with the control group (AOR = 3.32 (95% CI 1.73–6.42), p < 0.001). Overall knowledge and attitudes toward MMS were high across all four study groups, while the adherence remained lower. The behavioral interventions exhibited mixed effects on MMS related to knowledge, attitude and adherence. Overall, the findings suggest that behaviorally informed approaches may have potential to support MMS adherence when integrated with routine maternal health services. Trial registration: PACTR202605655695088. Trial protocol: The trial protocol and statistical analysis plan was developed according to WHO’s recommended format for a 'research protocol' and uploaded as supplementary files with Protocol Identifying Code of MMS-BI-ETH-2024/01.

Article.Title: Phosphoprotein-enriched proteomics identifies heat shock cognate 71 protein as a host factor supporting chikungunya virus replication in macrophages
Article.Authors: Kamchompoo N.; Thongon S.; Athipanyasilp A.; Thiangtrongjit T.; Chantima K.; Reamtong O.; Boonnak K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection induces an acute illness and ongoing inflammatory symptoms, with macrophages believed to play significant yet not fully understood roles. To characterize host cellular responses associated with CHIKV infection, we performed mass spectrometry–based phosphoprotein enrichment-based proteomic analysis of CHIKV-infected RAW264.7 macrophages. Analysis of enriched phosphoproteins identified 2,096 altered proteins compared with mock-infected cells, of which 212 were differentially regulated, including 140 upregulated and 72 downregulated proteins (fold change ≥ 2, p < 0.05). Gene ontology enrichment analysis revealed that differentially regulated proteins were predominantly associated with cellular processes, biological regulation, and metabolic pathways, with molecular functions largely related to binding and catalytic activity, and localization primarily within intracellular compartments, including the cytoplasm and organelles. Notably, stress-response and protein homeostasis pathways were consistently enriched, including the upregulation of heat shock cognate 71 kDa protein (HSC71). Network analysis linked HSC71 to key cytosolic and metabolic regulatory pathways. Pharmacological inhibition of HSC71 resulted in reduced CHIKV replication without significant cytotoxicity. The findings indicate that host protein homeostasis and phosphorylation-dependent pathways may be implicated in CHIKV infection within macrophages. The direct mechanistic role of HSC71 requires further investigation, which could facilitate the future development of antiviral agents.

Article.Title: Active throttling and dual-thrust capability of 3D-printed swirl-star fuel grains for hybrid rocket engines
Article.Authors: Elnaggar M.; Hassan A.; Ahmed M.; Hashish A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The ability to rapidly and repeatably transition between boost and sustain thrust levels is fundamental for planetary landers and orbital manoeuvring vehicles, yet it remains challenging for hybrid rocket motors because of their inherently non-linear, diffusion-limited combustion. This study evaluates additively manufactured swirl-star and swirl-star-reverse (SSR) ABS fuel grains, with $$N = 5,7,9$$ star points, combined with a tangential swirl injector, in a 1-inch GOX/ABS hybrid motor. Sixty static-fire tests (three burn durations, seven grain configurations) and six dedicated boost-sustain throttling tests were performed. Empirical power-law regression-rate correlations were obtained for each configuration, with the regression exponent $$n$$ ranging from 0.567 (9SSR) to 1.080 (5SSR). Measurement uncertainty, propagated using the Kline-McClintock method, was estimated at $$\pm 5.3\%$$ for regression rate and $$\pm 5.1\%$$ for oxidizer mass flux, consistent with the observed repeatability (mean coefficient of variation $$2.8\%$$ ). Among the tested geometries, the 7SSR grain gave the most balanced combination of a high regression exponent $$(n = 0.911)$$ and a smooth, low-oscillation chamber-pressure transition between boost and sustain phases (pressure undershoot below $$5\%$$ ), while the 5SSR grain showed the highest exponent but an oscillatory pressure response, and the 9SSR grain showed a sluggish, low-exponent response. It should be noted that thrust was not measured directly; all throttling conclusions are based on chamber-pressure response, which serves as a proxy for thrust in a choked-nozzle configuration. These results are limited to a single 1-inch motor scale and a 2:1 throttling ratio (5 to $$2.5$$ g/s); they indicate that swirl-augmented port geometry is a promising, but not yet fully validated, route toward more linear, throttleable hybrid rocket combustion.

Article.Title: Comparison of mediastinoscopic and thoracoscopic esophagectomy for esophageal cancer using matched cohorts of 152 cases
Article.Authors: Hu Z.; Yang P.; Xu T.; Wang W.; Wei W.; Wei W.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) is currently the most widely used approach for esophageal cancer resection. It performs thoracic esophagectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection via a small incision, right thoracic approach. However, thoracoscopic access to the thoracic esophagus is often technically challenging in patients who have previously undergone lung surgery or pleurodesis. Inflatable video-assisted mediastinoscopic esophagectomy (VAMS) offers an option for these patients. The posterior mediastinum is inflated with carbon dioxide via the cervical incision to create an artificial space for radical esophagectomy. The operation avoids access to the pleural cavity, unlike VATS. Nevertheless, concerns have been raised about inadequate lymph node retrieval and a high risk of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy. Our study aimed to address these concerns by reviewing our recent operations, which incorporated significant technical improvements over our initial practice. We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of patients who underwent VAMS for esophageal cancer resection at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital from January 2023 to December 2024. The comparison cohort was selected from those who received VATS at Cancer Hospital Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences during the same period. Exclusion criteria included non-squamous cell carcinoma, reconstruction not using the stomach, multiple primary malignant neoplasms, and loss to follow-up. After propensity score matching to balance demographics and clinical features, the two cohorts were compared on operative time, blood loss, lymph node retrieval, postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, and 2-year survival. As a result, we reviewed 398 eligible patients, of whom 183 underwent VAMS. Propensity score matching generated two study cohorts, each with 76 patients, for comparative analysis. The two cohorts had similar blood loss, the number of dissected lymph nodes, and postoperative hospital stay. R0 resection without conversion to thoracotomy was achieved in all patients. There was no death in 30 days postoperatively. Postoperative complications were infrequent and did not differ significantly between the cohorts. The rate of vocal hoarseness appeared higher in the VAMS cohort than in the VATS cohort, although the difference was not statistically significant. Nevertheless, the VAMS cohort had a shorter operative time than the VATS cohort, with a median reduction of approximately 16 min. The 2-year disease-free and overall survival did not differ significantly between the cohorts. Tumor recurrence occurred in 13 patients in each cohort, with distant metastasis the most frequent cause. Only three patients had locoregional recurrence, including one case of anastomotic recurrence and two cases of regional lymph node metastasis. In conclusion, our study has revealed that VAMS has a shorter operative time and is not significantly different from VATS in lymph node retrieval, postoperative complications, and 2-year survival. These encouraging findings warrant prospective studies that include more high-volume hospitals with consensus on surgical procedures.

Article.Title: Synthesis of some indolone derivatives using modification of magnetic mordenite by KCC-1 and HKUST-1 as a new and effective nanocatalyst
Article.Authors: Abdollahi M.; Moradi L.
Article.Abstract: In this study, an effective nanocatalyst was prepared for the green synthesis of some dihydroxyacenaphtho[1,2-b]indolone derivatives. The nanocatalyst was synthesized by modifying magnetic mordenite nanoparticles with KCC-1/HKUST-1 MOF (M-MOR/KCC-1/HKUST-1). The Prepared catalyst was characterized by FT-IR, FE-SEM, VSM, XRD, BET, EDX and elemental mapping techniques and was used as a catalyst for the green synthesis of dihydroxyacenaphtho[1,2-b]indolone derivatives at 80 °C in EtOH/H 2 O (v/v: 1:1) solvent. Products were obtained in good to excellent yields (72-92%) within short reaction times (2–4 h) and their structures were identified by FT-IR, 1 HNMR, 13 CNMR and mass spectroscopy (MS) analysis. Furthermore, the antibacterial properties of some derivatives were investigated against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The results obtained using the agar diffusion method demonstrated that the synthesized compounds exhibited significant antibacterial activity.

Article.Title: Universal droop controller for the parallel operation of inverters with different output impedances
Article.Authors: Rajendran M.; Kumar L.; Manoharan P.; Kumari D.
Article.Abstract: Droop control techniques are commonly used in microgrids for the decentralized control of parallel-connected inverters in order to avoid the requirement for vital high-bandwidth communication links. However, when inverters with different output impedances—such as resistive (R), inductive (L), or capacitive (C) types—operate in parallel, typical droop techniques encounter serious difficulties that frequently result in poor power sharing accuracy and system instability This limitation motivates the development of a universal control strategy capable of varied inverter impedance characteristics without requiring prior knowledge of the impedance angle. This paper proposes a universal droop controller based on an orthogonal transformation matrix that unifies the active and reactive power control characteristics of inverters with different output impedances. The proposed controller is designed within a reliable droop control framework to minimise the impacts of parameter uncertainty and numerical inaccuracies and hence to achieve a single control law for active and reactive power where the active power is controlled to regulate the voltage and the reactive power is controlled to regulate the frequency. Three different inverters (0.9 kVA C-inverter, 0.6 kVA L-inverter, and 0.3 kVA R-inverter) working in parallel are used in MATLAB/Simulink simulations to verify the effectiveness of the suggested controller. In addition, a hardware prototype of the 0.6 kVA L-inverter is also designed to test the feasibility of the proposed control algorithm and its voltage and frequency regulation capabilities in practice. Parallel operation and power-sharing performance are validated through simulation. The findings verify that the universal droop controller maintains the voltage and frequency regulation within 5% and 2% of rated values, respectively, achieves accurate active and reactive power sharing, and guarantees system stability under changing load conditions and topology changes.

Article.Title: Low levels of Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda J.E. Smith) damage in Bangladesh are linked to farmers’ integrated pest management practices and weather conditions
Article.Authors: Amjath-Babu T.; Alam S.; Choudhury D.; Billah M.; Aravindakshan S.; Kamal M.; Harun-Or-Rashid M.; Dutta N.; Shah M.; Mitu A.; Krupnik T.
Article.Abstract: Fall Armyworm (FAW), Spodoptera frugiperda , is recognized as a major threat to maize production in Africa, the Americas (its native range in North, Central, and South America), and increasingly in Asia following its recent spread across the continent. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of FAW pest dynamics and yield impacts in Bangladesh, focusing on the efficacy of agroecological, cultural and chemical pest management practices. Multi-year data (2019–2022) on FAW population dynamics were collected through nationwide monitoring, farmer surveys, and satellite-based landscape diversity assessments across 31 out of 64 districts. Using structural equation modeling (SEM), we analyzed relationships among FAW damage at different maize growth stages to yield, given agronomic practices, and environmental variables. Our results suggest that FAW damage in Bangladesh ranged from 7.8 to 9.8% yield loss, which was significantly lower than 11.6% reported in Zimbabwe, 17–24% in India, 32% in Ethiopia and 47% in Kenya. Yield losses associated with indicators of vegetative and cob damage ranged from 0.78 t ha -1 in 2020 to 0.98 t ha -1 in 2022, but overall productivity remained above 9 t ha -1 . Integrated pest management practices embedding agroecological principles, that harness ecological processes and reduce reliance on external inputs—such as minimum tillage, intercropping, diversified cropping systems, mechanical and manual weed control, and larval handpicking, consistently reduced crop damage. Monitoring data were strongly correlated with field-level symptoms, reinforcing the value of pheromone traps in guiding integrated pest management (IPM) decisions. Results highlight the effectiveness of non-chemical strategies and suggest that blanket pesticide applications without field scouting may be unnecessary under current FAW pressure. These findings support evidence-based IPM policies and encourage resource-efficient pest management in Bangladesh.

Article.Title: Electronic structure, NBO, and radical stability analyses of thymol and carvacrol along metabolic transformation pathways: a DFT study
Article.Authors: Faal M.; Mehrafarin A.; Naghdi Badi H.; Asadi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the proposed reaction mechanisms and radical stabilization processes leading to the formation of the two bioactive monoterpenes, thymol and carvacrol, remains challenging because of complex reaction networks, tautomeric interconversions, and electron delocalization effects. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed at the B3LYP/6-311 + G(d) level using Gaussian 09 software. Ten proposed reaction pathways and twenty transition states were identified and analyzed, including key tautomeric transformations and intermediate rearrangements. Activation energies and Gibbs free energies were evaluated to assess the feasibility of the proposed reaction routes. To gain deeper mechanistic insight, molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), Natural Bond Orbital (NBO), and spin density analyses were performed for selected intermediates, transition states, and radical species. MEP analysis revealed notable changes in charge distribution during tautomeric interconversions, while NBO analysis indicated strong donor–acceptor interactions and extensive π-electron delocalization within the aromatic framework. Spin density analysis confirmed resonance-assisted delocalization of the unpaired electron following hydrogen abstraction, supporting the stabilization of the corresponding phenoxy radicals. Comparative analysis revealed slightly greater electronic delocalization in thymol than in carvacrol. Overall, the present computational results provide molecular-level insight into the proposed reaction mechanisms, electronic structure evolution, and radical stabilization behavior associated with the formation of thymol and carvacrol.

Article.Title: TrustAdaptRL: an online reinforcement learning framework for attack-resilient trust management in Fog-IoT networks
Article.Authors: .B P.; Venkatesh K.
Article.Abstract: Fog-empowered IoT networks (Fog-IoT) can support latency-sensitive, large-scale applications; however, they remain susceptible to adaptive trust attacks such as collusion, on–off, and grayhole attacks, while still requiring reliable QoS. Available trust-management schemes often use static weighting or rely on short-lived uncertain information from probabilistic or anomaly-detector-based analysis, and thus suffer from limited adaptivity to changing adversarial behaviours, ineffective security–performance management, and low scalability or poor understanding. This study aims to overcome these limitations by introducing an online reinforcement-learning framework, TrustAdaptRL, to enable attack-resilient trust management in Fog-IoT (F-IoT) networks. Behavioural, contextual, temporal, security, and cross-neighbour observations are used as inputs to formulate the long-term trust-updating decision process. An attack-aware reward function explicitly rewards grayhole, on–off, and collusive behaviours while maintaining packet-delivery and delay performance.The inference is finished at the IoT devices, while the replay-buffer management, model optimisation, and policy update are executed at the fog nodes. Evaluation is based on a public-traffic-driven simulation using realistic traffic and security attributes created in cooperation with TON_IoT, BoT-IoT, and IoT-23, as well as syntactic topology, trust labels, and attacks based on specific routes. TrustAdaptRL achieves 93.7% trust accuracy, surpassing the highest baseline by 4.3% points. The benefit of grayhole, on–off, and collusion detection increases by 6.4%, 13.8%, and 15.3%, respectively, and the packet delivery ratio is 95.1%. Cross-cluster transfer, statistical testing, and explainability analysis results further demonstrate stable, interpretable, and scalable transfer of trust within dynamic Fog-IoT environments. The complete TrustAdaptRL implementation and reproducibility materials are publicly available at: https://github.com/Pallavi-1981/TrustAdaptRL .

Article.Title: Efficacy of sound therapy in chronic tinnitus patients with mild hearing loss: a multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Fournier P.; Thai-Van H.; Reynard P.; Gallego S.; Liegeon F.; Weckel A.; Viudez P.; Loche V.; Lépingle O.; Holler-Houdoux C.; Villatte V.; Bonnard D.; Rio M.; Kossowski M.; Londero A.; Bischoff H.; Essebag C.; Noreña A.; Estève-Fraysse M.
Article.Abstract: Chronic tinnitus affects 10–15% of the population and can substantially impair quality of life. Sound therapies, including amplification and sound generators, are commonly used, but evidence from placebo-controlled trials remains limited. This multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial evaluated the efficacy of sound therapy in adults with chronic bilateral tinnitus and mild hearing loss. Participants with tinnitus (THI ≥ 38) and mild bilateral hearing loss (PTA < 35 dB HL at 0.5–4 kHz) were randomized (1:1:1) to receive placebo amplification, sound generators, or sound generators combined with amplification. The intervention lasted 12 weeks and included a 6-week monotherapy phase followed by a 6-week polytherapy phase, during which participants in the active arms could switch between amplification, sound generators, or a combined approach. The primary outcome, change in Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI) score, improved significantly in the active treatment arms compared with placebo (mean change: -21 and − 18 vs. -6; p < .001). Clinically meaningful improvement on the Global Rating of Change Scale was reported by 88% of participants in the sound generator group, 77% in the combined therapy group, and 33% in the placebo group ( p < .001). These findings support sound therapy as an effective intervention for chronic tinnitus in individuals with mild hearing loss.

Article.Title: A reliability-guided RGB-IR object detection network with complementary information decoupling for autonomous driving
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Guo F.; Cheng L.; Fang P.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous driving systems require robust object detection under complex open-road conditions, where RGB images are sensitive to illumination changes and background interference, while infrared images may suffer from weak textures and unreliable thermal responses. To improve RGB-IR detection performance, this paper proposes a Feature-level Scale-aware Multispectral Fusion Network, termed FSMF, for autonomous driving scenarios. The network consists of three key components. First, a Reliability-Guided Modulation module estimates RGB and IR feature reliability from channel, spatial, and cross-modal perspectives, and adaptively adjusts their contributions before fusion. Second, a Complementary Information Decoupling module separates shared semantics, complementary differences, and redundant interference, thereby enhancing target-related cross-modal cues while suppressing ineffective responses. Third, a Scale-Aware Fusion Pyramid Network performs differentiated enhancement for shallow, middle, and deep features to improve multi-scale feature representation. Experiments on M3FD and FLIR demonstrate the effectiveness of FSMF. The proposed FSMF-s achieves 87.3% mAP@50 and 58.1% mAP@50:95 on M3FD, and 73.2% mAP@50 and 39.0% mAP@50:95 on FLIR, outperforming mainstream detectors and existing RGB-IR methods. In terms of efficiency, FSMF-s requires 35.998 GFLOPs and achieves 156.1 FPS, while the lightweight FSMF-n requires 9.137 GFLOPs and achieves 268.3 FPS. Ablation results further verify the effectiveness of the proposed modules.

Article.Title: Highly active and stable functionalized MOF-based heterogeneous catalyst (Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd) for the Suzuki and Sonogashira reactions
Article.Authors: Mazini F.; Alinezhad H.; Tajbakhsh M.; Baharfar R.
Article.Abstract: A novel metal–organic framework-based nanocatalyst named Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd was synthesized by modifying Zn-MOF (TMU-17-NH 2 ) with glyoxal (Gly) and cephalexin (Cef) and palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs), and its catalytic characteristics for Suzuki and the Sonogashira coupling reactions were examined. Prior to incorporating the Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd catalyst in the Suzuki and Sonogashira reactions, its structural features were comprehensively characterized using a series of analytical techniques and approved accordingly. The results confirmed that the Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd demonstrated good catalytic efficiency in the synthesis of biphenyl derivatives from the reaction between phenylboronic acid and iodobenzene in EtOH under reflux conditions and the synthesis of diphenylacetylene derivatives from the reaction between phenylacetylene and iodobenzene in EtOH under reflux conditions. It is noteworthy that the functionalization of the Zn-MOF structure with the electron-rich ligand of cephalexin notably increased the loading capacity and stability of Pd nanoparticles, which could be due to the strong interaction between the metal species and the substrate of the catalyst. Short reaction time, highly efficient activity, stability, and excellent reusability up to 6 consecutive cycles are some of the extraordinary advantages of the present protocol.

Article.Title: Alkaloidal constituents of Crinum asiaticum L., toxicology and in silico studies against some piercing-sucking pests
Article.Authors: El‑Rokh A.; Suliman A.; Elaraby A.; Ibrahim T.; Darwish A.; El-Salam S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many important crops around the world have been severely damaged by piercing-sucking pests. These pests can be managed with botanical pesticides. A major alkaloid, hippeastrine- N -oxide 3 , was isolated from the Crinum asiaticum alkaloid fraction. In addition, four known compounds, 11-hydroxyvittatine- N -oxide 1 , lycoramine- N -oxide 2 , lycorine 4 , and vittatine 5 , were identified by LC-MS/MS. 1 H NMR and ESI-MS spectroscopy were used to identify the structure of the isolated compound. Pesticidal activity of the alkaloid fraction and hippeastrine N -oxide was tested against four piercing-sucking pests along with azadirachtin as a positive control under laboratory conditions. Hippeastrine- N -oxide showed high toxicity against four pests, especially Aphis craccivora , compared to the control, with LC 50 values of 16.00 and 26.90 mg/L, respectively. The LC 50 value of hippeastrine- N -oxide was used to evaluate the biochemical characteristics of six Aphis craccivora enzymes. Molecular docking and fingerprint analysis of the lead compound revealed strong binding interactions with key amino acid residues in the target enzymes, further validating the experimental findings. These computational results make it possible to understand the mechanism of action observed in the laboratory assays. These findings indicate that the C. asiaticum alkaloid fraction, and hippeastrine N ‑oxide in particular, exhibit insecticidal activity against the piercing‑sucking pests tested under laboratory conditions, supporting further evaluation of their potential as botanical pest-control agents.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning maps the efficiency-NOx trade-off of a hydrogen dual-fuel engine fuelled with a diesel–Mahua methyl ester-pine oil blend
Article.Authors: Elumalai P.; Subramonian S.; Yee S.; Kadirgama K.; Poungthong P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-enriched dual-fuel combustion offers a route to decarbonising compression-ignition (CI) engines, but its interaction with oxygenated ternary fuels remains poorly quantified. This study evaluates a Span 80-stabilised diesel-Mahua methyl ester (MME)-pine oil (PO) blend on a Kirloskar TV1 CI engine (5.2 kW, 1500 rpm, compression ratio 17.5:1). Twenty operating points for D70 + MME15 + PO15 were measured across five loads (20–100%) and four hydrogen rates (0, 5, 10 and 15 L min −1 , equivalent to a 0–15.4% hydrogen energy share at full load); the remaining sixty points of the design (D100, D80 + MME10 + PO10, D60 + MME20 + PO20) were generated with a calibrated zero-dimensional thermodynamic model and are identified as model-predicted throughout. Raising hydrogen from 0 to 15 L min −1 at full load increased brake thermal efficiency (BTE) by 5.6–8.0% and reduced CO by 59.1–63.0%, HC by 59.3–61.5% and smoke by 20.7–26.3%, while NOx rose by 15.0–21.4%; the highest BTE observed was 31.74%. A Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) outperformed XGBoost and an artificial neural network under five-fold cross-validation (mean R 2 = 0.9913). SHAP attribution identified engine load as the dominant driver of BTE (65.7%) and NOx (69.6%), and hydrogen induction as the dominant driver of CO (75.4%) and HC (54.7%), while conformal prediction supplied calibrated 95% intervals. NSGA-II optimisation of the KAN surrogate returned a 118-point Pareto front: an efficiency-priority solution retained 99.4% of the maximum BTE while lowering NOx by 7.4% and smoke by 10.4%, and a balanced solution traded 11.2% of BTE for a 40.9% NOx reduction. All optimisation results are surrogate predictions reported with calibrated 95% intervals and await experimental confirmation.

Article.Title: Exploring biomarkers related to branched-chain amino acid metabolism in childhood obesity based on transcriptomics and experimental verification
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Lei Y.; Guan L.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Childhood obesity (CO) is a complex chronic disease driven by environmental, behavioral, and genetic factors. Dysregulation of branched-chain amino acid metabolism (BCAAM) contributes to CO development, highlighting the need to identify reliable biomarkers for diagnosis and treatment. Biomarkers associated with BCAAM remain largely unexplored in pediatric populations. In this study, we used BCAAM-focused co‑expression network analysis with machine learning to identify biomarkers and construct a diagnostic nomogram for CO using transcriptomic data from blood and adipose tissue. Multidimensional analyses, including functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and drug prediction, were subsequently performed. Three putative biomarkers, PLEK, NIN, and COX1, were identified, and the resulting nomogram exhibited good predictive performance. These biomarkers showed strong transcriptional association with mitochondrial respiration pathways and immune cell infiltration signatures, suggesting mitochondria–immune crosstalk. We also predicted multiple candidate drugs that target these biomarkers, with quercetin among the top candidates. Validation of their expression by RT‑qPCR in clinical blood samples confirmed significant dysregulation of PLEK and COX1, which supports their potential as biomarker candidates. These results indicate that PLEK, NIN, and COX1 are candidate BCAAM-associated transcriptomic markers for CO. The nomogram shows promising diagnostic potential in retrospective datasets; however, its clinical utility and the underlying mechanistic framework require further study.

Article.Title: A randomized double-blind non-inferiority trial comparing LUCENTRA with DYSPORT for moderate-to-severe glabellar line improvement
Article.Authors: Kafi H.; Samadi A.; Zartab H.; Nassiri Kashani M.; Ayatollahi A.; Yazdanparast T.; Ahmad Nasrollahi S.; Sabzvari A.; Firooz A.
Article.Abstract: Botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) formulations are widely used for the treatment of glabellar lines, with DYSPORT being a well-established option; however, its high cost limits accessibility. LUCENTRA, a newly developed BoNT-A, may offer a more affordable alternative. This phase III, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of LUCENTRA compared with DYSPORT in participants with moderate to severe glabellar lines. Participants received 40–60 units of intramuscular injections of either formulation, and the primary endpoint was the proportion of responders at day 30, defined as a ≥ 2-grade improvement on the glabellar line severity score at maximum frown. Secondary endpoints included onset of action at maximum frown, response rates based on the glabellar line severity scale, and subject self-assessment at maximum frown and rest, and safety was assessed on days 14, 30, 90, and 120. A total of 146 participants were enrolled (73 per arm). LUCENTRA was non-inferior to DYSPORT, with responder rates of 69% and 60.8%, respectively (95% CI: − 7.0 to 24.7%). Median onset was four days for LUCENTRA and five days for DYSPORT. Adverse events, mainly mild headaches and injection site discomfort, were comparable, and no serious events occurred. LUCENTRA is non-inferior to DYSPORT in terms of improving glabellar lines at day 30 post-injection, supporting its efficacy as an alternative option of DYSPORT. Adverse events were also comparable between the two groups suggesting safety and tolerability of DYSPORT and LUCENTRA.

Article.Title: Dye-affinity functionalized magnetic nanoparticles enable direct immobilization of cellulase from cell-free microbial culture medium
Article.Authors: Hadadi M.; Habibi A.
Article.Abstract: Enzyme recovery and purification remain major challenges for the economical application of enzymes. In this study, one-step separation and immobilization of cellulase from fermentation medium of Trichoderma reesei was investigated using dye-affinity-functionalized Fe₃O₄ magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), with multi-covalent coupling proposed as a possible immobilization mechanism. This approach achieved a selective enzyme immobilization with a loading capacity of 70.29 ± 0.99 mg Protein g Support −1 and immobilization yield of 33.16 ± 0.83%. Evaluations of the catalytic activities of the immobilized biocatalyst showed the endoglucanase, exoglucanase, and β -glucosidase activities of about 143.3, 62.9, and 63.1% in comparison with the original free cellulase, respectively. The immobilized cellulase was stable in repeated saccharification cycles of carboxymethylcellulose and sustained 70.12% of the original activity after six cycles. Also, the immobilized biocatalysts retained 100% activity after being stored at 4 °C for 180 days. Further evaluation of the immobilized biocatalyst was performed on the hydrolysis of paper waste at different initial concentrations. The Michaelis-Menten model with observable constants of K m = 4.142 ± 0.700 mg mL − 1 and V max = 0.043 ± 0.003 µmol Glucose mg Protein −1 h − 1 well-described this hydrolysis reaction. Therefore, the developed biocatalyst shows promising potential for the enzymatic conversion of paper waste into value-added products.

Article.Title: Fecal microbiome dynamics across reproductive stages in primiparous Świniarka sheep: a longitudinal study
Article.Authors: Cholewinska P.; Wojnarowski K.; Nazar P.; Greguła-Kania M.; Junkuszew A.; Rant W.; Radzik-Rant A.; Szeligowska N.; Bodkowski R.
Article.Abstract: Reproductive transitions in ruminants are accompanied by substantial endocrine and metabolic changes that may be associated with alterations in gut microbial communities. However, temporal variation in the fecal microbiome across reproductive stages in primitive sheep breeds remains poorly characterized. This longitudinal study aimed to characterize temporal patterns in the fecal microbiome in primiparous Świniarka sheep across three reproductive stages: mating (T1), lambing (T2), and the end of lactation (T3), using 16 S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Alpha diversity did not differ significantly between stages, although several indices showed numerically higher values at T2 and T3; these differences did not reach statistical significance in repeated-measures analyses. Beta diversity analyses based on Bray–Curtis, weighted UniFrac, and unweighted UniFrac distances showed overlapping community profiles, with no significant stage-associated differences after accounting for repeated measurements within animals (PERMANOVA, P > 0.05). The fecal microbiome was dominated by Firmicutes and Bacteroidota across all reproductive stages. Core microbiome analysis identified 28 genera present at a relative abundance of at least 0.1% in at least 80% of samples, together accounting for an average of 83.45% of the microbial community. PICRUSt2 identified 329 predicted MetaCyc pathways, none of which differed significantly among reproductive stages after false-discovery-rate correction. DESeq2 identified stage-associated differences in selected genus-level taxonomic features, with 14 significant features between T2 and T1, 13 between T3 and T1, and four between T3 and T2. Within this exploratory longitudinal cohort, reproductive stage was not associated with statistically detectable differences in alpha diversity, overall microbial community structure, or predicted functional pathway profiles genus-level abundance after correction for multiple testing. However, differential-abundance analysis identified stage-associated changes in selected genus-level. Dominant taxonomic features, particularly in comparisons of T2 profiles and T3 with T1. A high-abundance shared microbial core was observed across all stages, indicating limited global restructuring of the fecal microbiome detectable temporal variation under the studied conditions. These findings do not establish ecological resilience or equivalence among reproductive stages.

Article.Title: Preparation of a magnetic Escherichia coli biosorbent for efficient dye removal from aqueous solutions
Article.Authors: Kazemi M.; Maleki B.; Ashrafi S.; Kargar P.
Article.Abstract: Synthetic dyes in industrial wastes are highly toxic, non-biodegradable and resistant to treatment processes and may pose serious threats to the environment and human health. Due to their high adsorption capacity, biocompatibility and easy magnetic separation, magnetic biosorbents, especially E. coli -based bio-nanocomposites, are considered promising adsorbents. However, studies on the simultaneous removal of both anionic and cationic dyes using such materials remain limited. The γ-Fe 2 O 3 @ E. coli magnetic biosorbent was successfully synthesized and characterized using various analytical techniques, including FT-IR, XRD, VSM, EDX, DLS, and FE-SEM. The effects of solution pH, initial dye concentration, biosorbent dosage, temperature and contact time were systematically investigated, with optimum conditions of pH 4, 30 °C, 20 mg/L, 0.025 g and 30 min for MO, and pH 10, 35 °C, 8 mg/L, 0.02 g and 30 min for MB, respectively. Under these conditions, the removal efficiencies were 94.90 and 95.14%, with equilibrium adsorption capacities of 9.49 and 3.81 mg/g for MO and MB, respectively. Equilibrium studies indicated that the Freundlich and Temkin isotherm models best described the experimental data, indicating heterogeneous adsorption with multilayer characteristics and non-uniform adsorption sites. The biosorbent maintained high removal efficiencies over six consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles, decreasing from 95.14 to 91.36% for MB and from 94.90 to 87.62% for MO. These results demonstrate that the γ-Fe 2 O 3 @ E. coli biosorbent combines effective dye removal with magnetic recoverability and good reusability, supporting its potential application in sustainable wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Integrated technology acceptance model and theory of planned behavior explain anti-osteoporosis medication prescribing among Thai orthopedic surgeons after hip fracture
Article.Authors: Piyaprapaphan P.; Wannamakok W.; Chotiyarnwong P.; Sithiwichankit N.; Gerdsri N.; Vanitcharoenkul E.
Article.Abstract: A persistent care gap leaves many patients without anti-osteoporosis medications (AOMs) after hip fracture, despite their proven benefit in preventing secondary fractures. We investigated the factors associated with orthopedic surgeons’ intention to prescribe AOMs. A cross-sectional online survey of 264 Thai orthopedic surgeons involved in hip fracture care integrated the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behavior. Partial least squares structural equation modeling assessed the measurement model’s reliability and validity and tested the hypothesized structural relationships. The integrated model accounted for 63.4% of the variance in prescribing intention. Perceived usefulness of AOMs ( β = 0.427; P < 0.001) and subjective norms ( β = 0.228; P < 0.001) predicted the surgeons’ attitude toward use. Attitude toward use was the strongest predictor of the intention to prescribe AOMs ( β = 0.622; P < 0.001). Self-efficacy did not moderate the attitude–intention relationship but was directly associated with intention ( β = 0.201; P = 0.004). These results indicate that prescribing intention is primarily predicted by perceived clinical value and professional norms rather than by procedural simplicity. Interventions to reduce the care gap should therefore emphasize clinical effectiveness, reinforce professional norms, and build surgeons’ self-efficacy through targeted education and training.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of sexual satisfaction in Polish patients with benign thyroid disease
Article.Authors: Sawicka-Gutaj N.; Nijakowski K.; Ziółkowska P.; Trocha M.; Miśkiewicz P.; Derwich-Rudowicz A.; Ruchała M.
Article.Abstract: The study aimed to assess sex life satisfaction among Polish patients with thyroid disease. A total of 378 participants (300 women, 78 men) treated between January 2018 and December 2019 completed validated questionnaires, including ThyPRO, WHO Quality of Life, the Sexual Satisfaction Questionnaire (women), the International Index of Erectile Function-15 (men), and the Self-Esteem and Relationship (SEAR) questionnaire (men). Overall, 58.7% of women and 40.3% of men reported a negative impact of thyroid disease on their sex life, and 71.4% of women and 47.2% of menreported decreased sexual desire. Among women with autoimmune thyroid disease, 67% with hypothyroidism and 65% with hyperthyroidism reported a negative impact despite pharmacological treatment. Among women, ThyPRO Impaired Sex Life scores correlated strongly with ThyPRO overall quality-of-life scores across all diagnoses ( p < 0.001). WHO-QoL scores correlated significantly only in patients with autoimmune thyroid disease. In men with autoimmune hyperthyroidism, sexual quality of life scores correlated with ThyPRO Overall Quality of Life ( p < 0.031), all IIEF-15 domains ( p = 0.011 for erectile function; p = 0.004 for intercourse satisfaction; p = 0.004 for orgasmic function; p = 0.003 for sexual desire; p < 0.001 for overall satisfaction), and most SEAR domains ( p < 0.001 for sexual relationship; p = 0.036 for confidence; p = 0.029 for self-esteem; p = 0.001 for overall score). These findings suggest that nearly 60% of women and 40% of men with benign thyroid disorders experience deterioration in sexual well-being, even when thyroid hormone levels are within normal ranges. Women with autoimmune hypothyroidism appear to be at the highest risk for impaired sexual quality of life.

Article.Title: A biomimetic bilayered vascular graft integrating electrospun polyurethane and gelatin/elastin hydrogel achieves arterial-like compliance and enhanced endothelialization
Article.Authors: Ebrahimi F.; Solouk A.; Yousefzadeh M.; Bahrami S.; Seifalian A.
Article.Abstract: Small-diameter (< 6 mm) vascular grafts continue to face high failure rates, primarily due to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and mechanical mismatch with native arteries. In this study, a biomimetic bilayered vascular graft was developed by integrating an electrospun polyurethane (EPU) nanofibrous inner layer with a gelatin/elastin (Gelastin) hydrogel outer layer to address these limitations. The bilayer architecture integrated the complementary functions of the two layers, combining the structural support of the EPU inner layer with the porous, hydrophilic, and swelling characteristics of the Gelastin hydrogel outer layer. Following cyclic tensile preconditioning, the bilayered grafts exhibited anisotropic mechanical behavior, reduced hysteresis, and improved elastic recovery compared with electrospun polyurethane alone. Among the fabricated samples, EPU/G 1 E 0.2 showed the highest elastic recovery (82.77 ± 2.54%) and compliance (10.93 ± 2.50%/100 mmHg) while maintaining high burst pressure (> 12,000 mmHg). Hemocompatibility assessment demonstrated low hemolysis ratios (< 2%), prolonged clotting times compared with commercial ePTFE ® , and limited platelet adhesion and activation on EPU. In vitro studies using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) confirmed favorable cell attachment, spreading, and proliferation over 7 days of culture.

Article.Title: Conditional survival and dynamic prognostic nomogram for histologically defined anaplastic ganglioglioma: a SEER-based analysis
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Ni J.; Tu C.; Qian H.
Article.Abstract: Anaplastic ganglioglioma (AGG) is an extremely rare glioneuronal tumor with low incidence and heterogeneous survival patterns driven by a limited set of prognostic factors, and conditional survival has not been systematically evaluated in this entity. Patients histologically diagnosed with AGG between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the SEER 17 registries. Age-adjusted incidence and annual percentage change (APC) were estimated by Joinpoint regression. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed with Kaplan–Meier curves and log-rank tests; 5-year conditional survival (CS) was computed at successive landmark times. Independent prognostic factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression. A CS-nomogram was constructed and evaluated by calibration plots, time-dependent ROC and C-index. Nomogram-derived risk scores were dichotomized using a cut-point selected on the basis of restricted cubic splines (RCS), and survival between strata was compared. A total of 143 AGG patients were identified, with 62 deaths during follow-up. Patients included pediatric (29.4%), AYA (38.5%), and adults ≥ 40 years (32.2%), and 64.3% were male; most tumors arose in cerebral lobes (73.4%). Age-adjusted incidence of AGG remained low throughout the study window, with crude annual rates of approximately 0.082 per 1,000,000 person-years. Five-year OS was 64.7%, while CS5 increased from 64.7% at diagnosis to 73.7% at 1 year, 82.5% at 2 years, and > 90% after 3 years. Multivariate analysis identified age ≥ 40, regional/distant stage, and multiple primary tumors as independent adverse factors. The CS nomogram showed good performance, with time-dependent AUCs > 0.75 and well-calibrated predictions, and risk stratification yielded significantly separated survival outcomes ( P < 0.001). Long-term prognosis in AGG is highly dynamic: patients who survive the first three years acquire a substantially improved residual life expectancy. A CS-based nomogram, combined with RCS-guided risk stratification, translates this dynamic information into an individualized tool for counselling and risk-adapted surveillance.

Article.Title: Quantum random access codes for image transmission
Article.Authors: ur Rehman J.; Iqbal N.; Rizvi S.; Shin H.
Article.Abstract: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) enable multiple classical bits to be encoded into fewer qubits, while allowing only a selected bit to be retrieved with probability greater than the corresponding classical limit. Here, we use $$2 \rightarrow 1$$ and $$3 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs for simultaneous transmission of multiple binary images through a single quantum data stream. At the receiver, the measurement choice determines which encoded image is reconstructed, while the remaining image information is disturbed by the measurement process. The inherent correct-bit probabilities of these QRACs are approximately 85.4% and 78.9%, respectively. By applying median and morphological filtering to the decoded binary images, we improve the reconstruction accuracy in an image-dependent manner, reaching 99.17% for $$2 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs and 98.36% for $$3 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs. We also analyze the effect of depolarizing noise on reconstruction quality using accuracy, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and structural similarity index measure. These results demonstrate a selective-access framework for QRAC-based image transmission with potential applications in controlled image/video transmission.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal coordination between a sports-tourism proxy subsystem and ecological conditions in Zhejiang Province, China, 2010–2024
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Samsudin N.; Wei X.
Article.Abstract: Sports tourism is closely related to ecological conditions, spatial resources and regional tourism-service capacity. Using 11 prefecture-level cities in Zhejiang Province as the study area, this study develops an evaluation framework comprising a sports-tourism proxy subsystem and an ecological subsystem for 2010–2024. The entropy-weight method, coupling coordination degree model, Global Moran’s I and exploratory spatial-association models are used to examine temporal variation, inter-city differences and conditional spatial associations in the coupling coordination degree.The ecological subsystem generally has a higher composite score than the sports-tourism proxy subsystem. This comparison reflects the selected indicators, standardization procedure and weighting scheme and does not independently demonstrate ecological stability or insufficient resource transformation. The coupling coordination degree follows a staged pattern of “early improvement–shock-related decline–gradual recovery”: it increased overall during 2010–2019, declined during 2020–2022 and increased again during 2023–2024. The cities exhibit distinct combinations of sports-tourism-related and ecological conditions, with Hangzhou and Wenzhou generally showing relatively high coordination levels. Global Moran’s I is negative in most years, but two-sided permutation tests based on 9,999 random permutations provide no evidence of statistically significant global spatial autocorrelation during 2010–2024. To reduce mechanical overlap with the construction of the coupling coordination degree, the spatial-association analysis uses external contextual variables, including GDP per capita, total employment, public-service expenditure, total water resources and ecological-space share. The exploratory spatial-association models identify conditional relationships between these local and neighbouring-city contextual variables and the coupling coordination degree. The findings provide a basis for comparing tourism-related and ecological conditions and for informing coordinated regional planning, but the aggregate index and observational spatial models should not be interpreted as direct evidence of causal interaction, ecological-service enhancement or ecological-resource transformation.

Article.Title: Cognitive phenotypes and neuropsychological trajectories in post-COVID-19 syndrome: a 12-month follow-up study
Article.Authors: Herrera E.; Señoráns A.; Barrenechea A.; Pérez-Sánchez M.; González-Nosti M.
Article.Abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) has been associated with cognitive difficulties, particularly in attention, processing speed, memory, and executive functions, but longitudinal evidence based on comprehensive neuropsychological assessment remains limited. This study examined the one-year evolution of neuropsychological performance and cognitive phenotypes in 92 patients with PCS who had participated in a previous assessment. Pre-post changes were analysed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with false discovery rate correction. Cognitive phenotypes were characterized in the complete phenotype sample ( N = 83) using a domain-based approach derived from the IC-CoDi-COVID criteria, with two representative tests for each cognitive domain and two impairment cutoffs: ≤ -1 SD and ≤ -1.5 SD. Significant improvements were observed mainly in verbal and visual memory, matrix reasoning, inhibitory control, and action processing (fluency and naming), whereas attention and processing speed measures remained largely stable. Phenotype analyses showed a shift toward less impaired cognitive profiles at follow-up. Normal cognition increased from 65.1% to 77.1% under the ≤ -1 SD criterion and from 83.1% to 86.7% under the ≤ -1.5 SD criterion. Impaired phenotypes were primarily driven by attention/processing speed. These findings suggest partial cognitive recovery in PCS, alongside persistent domain-specific cognitive vulnerability, particularly in attention and processing speed.

Article.Title: Terrain-corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method and its application to elevation determination in mountainous areas
Article.Authors: Lyu B.; Duan H.; Li S.; Yin Y.; Duan Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the difficulties in conventional elevation surveying caused by the strong topographic relief in mountainous areas and the dual constraints imposed on GNSS gravity potential leveling by the selection of the absolute gravity potential reference and local short wavelength terrain effects, a terrain corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method is proposed. The proposed method takes the normal height difference between two points as the quantity to be determined and directly determines the height difference of a survey segment through a differential strategy, thereby reducing the influence of common systematic errors at the two endpoints and weakening the dependence on the absolute gravity potential reference. Considering the significant local short wavelength terrain effects in mountainous areas, a residual terrain model is constructed using a high resolution digital elevation model. The Helmert second condensation method is employed to process the terrain mass, and the residual terrain potential is calculated based on the prism–plate model.
