Before cross-modal fusion, we jointly align the three modality-level features using both InfoNCE loss and batch-hard triplet loss, thereby explicitly modeling their consistency and relative distance. A modality-wise attention module is also incorporated to adaptively reweight and aggregate features. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that our approach outperforms existing methods, achieving overall accuracy improvements of 2.2% on Weibo and 1.5% on Gossipcop. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Ylh-s/MLCL .

Article.Title: Heat transfer enhancement via nanoparticle radius in non-Newtonian fluid flow around a rotating sphere
Article.Authors: Awan A.; Hussain M.; Ali B.; Ahammad N.; Gamaoun F.; Kafle J.; Nadeem S.
Article.Abstract: Efficient thermal regulation in magnetically actuated rotating systems motivates the examination of non-Newtonian nanofluids with adjustable nanoparticle radii. This study analyzes the time-dependent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flow of a non-Newtonian nanofluid over a rotating sphere, focusing on the impact of nanoparticle radius variation on fluid flow and thermal transmission. This specific aspect has not previously been addressed for Casson fluid flow over the rotating geometries. The flow governing equations are non-dimensionalized using appropriate similarity transformations and solved numerically via the finite element method (FEM). This work targets three main performance goals: minimizing skin friction (drag), enhancing Nusselt number (heat transmission), and maintaining both thermal and flow stability. The results reveal that the Nusselt number can be enhanced by 40% and skin friction decreased by 25% by reducing the nanoparticle radius from 2.5 nm to 0.5 nm. Furthermore, raise in the Casson parameter from 1.0 to 2.0 leads to an approximate 30% reduction in axial velocity as compared with the Newtonian fluid case. These outcomes offer valuable insights for improving the efficiency of non-Newtonian nanofluid systems in magnetized rotating configurations, with possible uses in advanced material processing and thermal management.

Article.Title: Metamaterial assisted hybrid response from frequency selective surface roll off and leaky wave resonator integrated antenna for underground applications
Article.Authors: Yadav V.; Chakraborty S.; Annavarapu S.; Ghosh A.; Singh L.; Chattopadhyay S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In emerging era of wireless technologies such as cognitive radio, wireless sensor networks etc., designing effective low frequency antennas < 1000 MHz and specifically < 700 remains a significant challenge due to its poor (often negative) gain and severely limited bandwidth (≈ 1%), despite exhibiting fair radiation profile. Therefore, challenges to design antennas suitable for above said applications have been taken up in the present investigation. Unlike, other metamaterial antenna, here, a unique approach is adopted by exploring frequency selective surface (FSS) filtering characteristics by employing simultaneous transmissive and reflective feature to achieve hybrid resonance. Additionally, an integrated leaky wave Fabry Perot type resonator is employed to produce additional distinct resonance. The proposed antenna yields resonances (˂700 MHz) with appreciable bandwidths and positive gains at 462.4 MHz (2.5%), 579 MHz (5.9%) and 663.5 MHz (1.9%) with 1.22, 3.5 and 4 dBi, as is confirmed by both the simulations and measurements.

Article.Title: Peak ground acceleration underestimates narrow-band seismic amplification on mountain slopes
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Iida T.; Kawabe H.; Sato M.; Senna S.; Yamada R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Topographic amplification is widely invoked to explain strong shaking and slope failure in mountainous terrain, yet direct field observations remain limited. Here we analyze 24 regional earthquakes recorded by a four-station strong-motion array spanning a ridge crest, a valley bottom, and two contrasting slope facets on a single ridge in central Japan. Peak ground acceleration (PGA) and frequency-dependent measures reveal markedly different representations of local seismic response. PGA ratios vary among events and are positively associated with epicentral distance; however, earthquake magnitude also increases with distance, so source-size and propagation-distance effects cannot be separated in this catalog. In contrast, the NS slope exhibits a persistent narrow-band station-to-valley Fourier spectral-ratio peak at 3.5–4.0 Hz that remains stable across events and processing choices. Absolute spectra confirm enhanced energy at the slope in this band, while also showing that a relative spectral depression at the valley reference contributes to the large ratio magnitude. Most importantly, the geometric-mean 5%-damped response-spectral ratio reaches 6.67 at 0.277 s (3.61 Hz), compared with a corresponding full-record geometric-mean horizontal PGA ratio of 1.13. These observations show that PGA can substantially under-represent frequency-specific elastic response on mountain slopes, while the responsible mechanism cannot be uniquely attributed to topography or near-surface structure alone.

Article.Title: Elemental profiling of zebrafish (Danio rerio) across developmental stages using ion beam analytical techniques
Article.Authors: Caloni M.; Zaluski A.; Valente C.; Bonan C.; Papaléo R.; Dias J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of zebrafish as a biological model, comprehensive baseline elemental data across its developmental stages remain limited. In this work, ion beam analytical techniques were employed to establish the elemental composition of zebrafish larvae and adults under controlled vivarium conditions. The combined use of these techniques enables quantitative elemental analysis and spatially resolved elemental mapping of small biological samples within the same analytical framework, providing an integrated elemental baseline across zebrafish development. We show that most elements detected in zebrafish larvae were retained throughout development into adulthood, whereas Al, Si, Mn, Cu, and Sr were detected only in adults, suggesting progressive accumulation during the life cycle. No significant differences were observed in elemental composition or concentration between sexes. Elemental maps of larvae show a homogeneous spatial distribution for most elements, except for elevated S in the eye’s lenses and increased Ca in the otoliths and the head region, highlighting the early compartmentalisation of certain elements during organ development. The resulting dataset provides a developmental elemental baseline for future environmental, pharmacological, and toxicological studies using zebrafish.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles analysis during human acclimatization to simulated high-altitude hypoxia
Article.Authors: Giannella A.; Mrakic-Sposta S.; Vezzoli A.; Magrini A.; Favero L.; Rigon L.; Khatoon N.; Strapazzon G.; Gatterer H.; Siebenmann C.; Schlittler M.; Ceolotto G.; Malacrida S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypobaric hypoxia (HH) induces coordinated physiological and molecular responses supporting acclimatization to reduced oxygen availability. However, the temporal integration of blood mRNA and miRNA expression during early HH exposure remains incompletely understood. Eight healthy males were exposed for 72 h to simulated moderate HH (~ 3500 m) in the terraXcube facility. Blood transcriptomic and miRNA profiles were analyzed at baseline and after 12, 24, and 72 h, together with physiological variables, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers. Differential expression analysis revealed a progression from early stress and innate immune responses at 12 h, involving FOSB , CITED4 , and IDO1 , to remodeling of lymphocyte-specific programs at 24 h, including PAX5 , TCF7 , and TNFRSF13C . At 72 h, broader changes involved AP-1 components ( JUN , JUNB , and FOSB ), lymphocyte regulators ( PAX5 and FOXP3 ), and the antioxidant gene SOD2 . Integrated analysis identified predicted miRNA–mRNA pairs displaying inverse expression patterns within these pathways. Notably, miR-486-3p was consistently upregulated and miR-29c-5p downregulated across all time points. Plasma biomarkers remained largely stable, except for a transient increase in ICAM-1 and a marked decrease in TNF-α at 12 h, while ROS increased early and subsequently stabilized. Together, these findings identify distinct but overlapping phases of early HH acclimatization, progressing from stress and innate immune activation to lymphocyte-specific and redox remodeling. The temporal dissociation between coordinated mRNA and miRNA expression changes and limited circulating inflammatory responses indicates that molecular adaptation extends beyond detectable systemic inflammatory activation.

Article.Title: A wastewater balance reveals unexpectedly high TFA input from human water use
Article.Authors: Frenzel I.; Hilgert P.; Herbstritt B.; Nöltge D.; Müller M.; Lange J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trifluoroacetate (TFA) is a member of the PFAS group and shares their persistence. Its very small molecular size and anionic character makes it, in contrast to many other PFAS, highly water-soluble and mobile in the aquatic environment. Wastewater shows elevated TFA concentrations. This TFA may stem from background sources such as drinking water, infiltrating groundwater, or rainwater. It may also come from human water use itself. To quantify a potential TFA surplus, we built a mass balance at three rural sewer sites in Freiburg, Germany. End-member mixing analysis yielded TFA loads from groundwater and drinking water. Flow comparisons between dry and rain-event conditions yielded the TFA load from rainwater. Groundwater and drinking water contributed the largest background TFA load at two sanitary sewers. During a storm event rainwater dominated the TFA load in the combined sewer despite diluting its concentration. At every site, human water use exceeded the sum of the three background sources and made up the largest share of the TFA load. TFA concentrations also peaked during the morning wastewater surge at every site. We attribute this surplus mainly to human excretion of ingested TFA from food and drink. However, a comparison with an approximate dietary TFA intake estimate shows that this source alone cannot explain the observed surplus. Other sources, such as cosmetic products, may contribute to the overall TFA load in the sewer. Our study highlights the need for more data on human TFA uptake and excretion, as well as on other potential sources of TFA in human water use.

Article.Title: Prediction of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities from well logs using artificial neural networks and statistical regression
Article.Authors: Teymouri H.; Nikrouz R.; Ciabeghodsi A.; Kadkhodaie A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities (Vs Fast , Vs Slow , and Vs Average ) is important for evaluating reservoir anisotropy, fracture networks, and stress regimes. In this study, multivariate statistical regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models were developed and compared to predict these velocity components in a well from the Sarvak Formation, Zagros Basin, Iran. The initial dataset comprised 3,234 depth points, of which 2,264 valid points were retained after data preprocessing and normalization. Compressional-wave velocity (Vp), neutron porosity (NPHI), and bulk density (RHOB) were used as input variables. For the statistical models, 70% of the data were used for calibration and 30% for testing, whereas the ANN employed a feedforward backpropagation architecture trained using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, with 70, 15, and 15% of the data allocated to training, validation, and testing, respectively. The statistical models achieved test-set R² values of 0.769129, 0.616225, and 0.725904 for Vs fast , Vs slow and Vs Average , respectively, while the corresponding ANN models achieved R² values of 0.786769, 0.641601, and 0.727609. The ANN therefore provided modest improvements over statistical regression, with the largest improvement observed for Vs Fast and Vs slow . Minor discrepancies at lower velocity ranges may reflect local geological complexities, including intense fracturing. Overall, the proposed approach, particularly the ANN models, provides a practical indirect method for estimating shear-wave velocity components from conventional well logs and may support reservoir characterization where direct dipole-shear measurements are unavailable.

Article.Title: Discovery and promotion of unknown sounds into operational detection targets for underwater passive acoustic monitoring under false alarm constraints
Article.Authors: Noda T.; Koizumi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Earth’s oceans cover 70% of the planet yet remain among the least observed regions. Underwater acoustics is a primary sensing modality, but recordings span biological, anthropogenic and natural sounds while labels remain sparse. We present an unknownness-aware monitoring framework for underwater acoustic sensing platforms: it adapts a pre-trained audio representation model to underwater soundscapes, defines an embedding-space unknownness score, and couples it with detector outputs in a Detect–Group–Promote–Union (DGPU) loop tuned under false positives per hour (FP/h) constraints: Detect surfaces candidate events from continuous audio; Group clusters unknown candidates in embedding space; Promote trains lightweight classifiers from sparse expert labels on selected clusters; and Union combines baseline and promoted detectors. Across a 56-class underwater Sound Event Detection (SED) benchmark and two cetacean field datasets, the framework attains a dataset-level bandwidth-matched out-of-distribution AUROC of 1.000 on Hawaiian survey data (HICEAS), raises right-whale upcall detection recall on continuous recordings (FRDR) from 0.027 to 0.390 at FP/h ≈ 10 with a supervised Promoter, with 300 labelled events (~ 32% of training-fold labels) reaching 0.37 (95% of the full-label recall), and classifies seven HICEAS cetacean species with the Promoter classifier alone (AUC 0.924–0.992 within-day and 0.51–0.97 cross-day with a fixed classifier), supporting stethoscope-like ocean monitoring.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of post-capture escape tactics in juvenile Japanese eels against various predatory fishes
Article.Authors: Hasegawa Y.; Yang W.; Kawabata Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although rare, it is possible for some prey species to actively escape from the digestive tract of predators after being captured. Because these tactics involve escaping after being swallowed by the predator, they are likely constrained by predator-specific factors. However, the limits of the effectiveness and the predator-specific factors that influence its success remain poorly understood. This study examined the effectiveness of a post-capture defensive tactic of juvenile Japanese eels, Anguilla japonica , in which they escape through the predator’s gills by navigating backward from the stomach. We evaluated the escape success of eels through predation experiments using six predator species that differ in habitat, swimming styles, and feeding styles (biting or suction feeding). The results indicated that eels escaped via the gills of all five suction-feeding predators examined (32%, 114/359), including Odontobutidae, Sebastidae, Lateolabracidae, Cyprinidae, and larger conspecific Japanese eels. In contrast, eels never escaped from the grass puffer Takifugu alboplumbeus (Tetraodontidae), the only biting-type predator, as the eels were torn into small pieces and consumed. Our results suggest that post-capture escape in eels is effective against diverse predator species encountered in nature. Meanwhile, predators that bite and kill prey before swallowing, such as tetraodontid fishes, may pose a greater threat to juvenile eels.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of measurement uncertainty for ICP-MS determination of platinum and palladium in ore using tolerance intervals and ISO 11352
Article.Authors: Lambarki L.; El Hajji R.; El-Ghaly W.; El Kamli T.; Bourass M.; Ihssane B.; Bakkali F.; Saffaj T.; Jhilal F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate determination of platinum (Pt) and palladium (Pd) in ore matrices remains analytically challenging due to matrix complexity, spectral interferences, and the ultra-trace concentrations at which these elements naturally occur. This work presents the development and full validation of an inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of Pt and Pd in ore samples, using lead fire assay with cupellation as the preconcentration step. Validation was performed using a β-content, γ-confidence tolerance interval strategy, which integrates method validation and measurement uncertainty estimation into a single coherent framework, without requiring additional experimental data beyond routine validation work. A simple linear regression calibration model was selected based on systematic evaluation of uncertainty profiles across the working concentration range. Trueness, expressed as relative bias, did not exceed − 2.03% for either element at any concentration level, and recovery was within the predefined acceptance criteria of ± 15%. Measurement uncertainty was subsequently assessed using two complementary top-down approaches: the uncertainty profile method and the ISO 11352 framework. Statistical comparison by Fisher’s F-test demonstrated that the two approaches yield statistically equivalent uncertainty estimates when the proportion β is set to 90% or 95%, establishing this threshold as the minimum requirement for reliable prediction of routine analytical performance from validation data. These findings confirm that the uncertainty profile approach constitutes a practical and resource-efficient alternative to ISO 11352 for laboratories involved in platinum-group element analysis, enabling simultaneous method validation and uncertainty characterization from a single experimental dataset.

Article.Title: Enhanced mechanical properties and reduced polymerization shrinkage in a light-cured flowable dental nanocomposite via incorporation of silane-functionalized ScYSZ nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Zendehdel E.; Loghman-Estarki M.; Li Z.; Davar F.; Jamali H.
Article.Abstract: The present investigation centers on the formulation and characterization of a light-cured nanohybrid dental composite, which incorporates a newly-proposed hybrid filler system composed of barium glass microparticles alongside surface-engineered zirconia nanoparticles. Notably, scandia- and yttria-stabilized zirconia nanoparticles (ScYSZ NPs) are introduced here for the first time within a methacrylate-based resin matrix. To improve interfacial compatibility, these nanoparticles were treated with γ-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (MPS), and three distinct dispersion techniques were systematically evaluated to secure a uniform particle distribution. Following identification of the optimal processing route, surface-modified ScYSZ (F-ScYSZ) was loaded at 1, 2.5, and 5 wt.% into a base resin already containing 48 wt.% barium glass. The resulting composites underwent thorough characterization through FT-IR, XRD, MTT and FE-SEM analysis. Mechanical response was quantified through three-point bending tests and Vickers indentation, whereas polymerization shrinkage was determined in line with ISO 17304 guidelines. The analyses verified the successful attachment of MPS moieties onto the nanoparticle surfaces and confirmed the retention of the non-transformable tetragonal (t′) polymorph within the ScYSZ structure. Incorporation of F-ScYSZ at 1 and 2.5 wt.% brought about substantial gains in mechanical performance; the best-performing formulation at 2.5 wt.% delivered a flexural strength of 134.33 MPa, an elastic modulus of 4.58 GPa, and a microhardness of 39.4 HV. At the 5 wt.% level, however, observable particle agglomeration occurred, which was accompanied by a pronounced deterioration in overall properties. Meanwhile, a consistent drop in polymerization shrinkage was noted with increasing filler loading. A side-by-side comparison against commercially available resin‑based composites reveals that the newly developed ScYSZ-reinforced nanohybrid achieves an attractive trade-off between enhanced mechanical strength and lower volumetric shrinkage, underscoring its viability as a high-performance flowable material for restorative dentistry applications.

Article.Title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
Article.Authors: De la Quintana P.; Solé M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. Dietary composition was quantified using the Index of Relative Importance (%IRI), trophic overlap was estimated using Pianka’s niche overlap index, and ontogenetic and morphological variation in prey use were evaluated using multivariate and linear models. Species differed in dietary composition and generally showed low trophic overlap, indicating differences in prey use among species. Juveniles consumed predominantly lizards, whereas adults incorporated proportionally more mammals and birds. Prey size increased with snake body size, whereas ontogenetic stage itself was not consistently associated with prey size. Head width was positively associated with prey width, indicating a relationship between predator cranial dimensions and prey dimensions. Because specimens were collected across different localities and were not necessarily syntopic, the observed differences should not be interpreted as direct evidence of local resource partitioning or competition. Overall, our results highlight interspecific and ontogenetic variation in prey use and provide a comparative assessment of dietary patterns and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus from Bahia.

Article.Title: A support vector machine classifier of PM₂.₅-based air quality index categories from co-pollutants and meteorological variables in Ahvaz, Iran
Article.Authors: Soltani F.; Soltani A.; Jaafarzadeh N.; Soltani N.; Talepour N.
Article.Abstract: Ahvaz, in southwestern Iran, experiences some of the most severe particulate air pollution in the world, driven by Middle Eastern Dust events, industrial emissions, and traffic. Continuous monitoring of fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is essential for public-health protection, yet PM₂.₅ monitors in the region frequently suffer outages and data gaps. This study evaluates whether the PM₂.₅-based Air Quality Index (AQI) category can be estimated from routinely measured co-pollutants (O₃, NO, NO₂, SO₂, CO, and PM₁₀) and meteorological variables (air temperature, dew point, relative humidity, wind speed, and wind direction), providing a surrogate risk label when direct PM₂.₅ measurements are unavailable. Hourly observations from the Naderi monitoring station in Ahvaz (October 2014 – July 2017) were aggregated into 3-hour intervals; each interval with at least two of three observed hourly PM₂.₅ values was labelled with one of six AQI categories using the U.S. EPA PM₂.₅ breakpoints in force during the study period, yielding 7,509 samples. A class-weighted radial-basis-function Support Vector Machine (SVM) was tuned by rolling-origin cross-validation within the training period (October 2014 – January 2017) and evaluated on a strictly held-out chronological test period (January – July 2017), alongside multinomial logistic regression, linear SVM, random forest, and gradient boosting baselines trained under identical protocols. On the unseen test period, the SVM achieved an exact-category accuracy of 0.633, macro-averaged F1 of 0.38, Cohen’s κ of 0.47, and quadratic-weighted κ of 0.61; 94.5% of predictions fell within one category of the truth, and misclassifications concentrated between adjacent categories. The random forest baseline performed best overall (accuracy 0.674; quadratic-weighted κ of 0.70; 97.7% within one category). Permutation importance and ablation experiments identified PM₁₀ as the dominant predictor: excluding it reduced SVM accuracy from 0.633 to 0.431, while PM₁₀ alone reached 0.523. Performance for the rare extreme categories (Very Unhealthy and Hazardous) remained limited and is reported transparently. At this station and over this period, co-pollutant and meteorological measurements—chiefly PM₁₀—can provide an operationally useful, near-real-time surrogate for the PM₂.₅ AQI category when the PM₂.₅ channel fails, while underscoring that such a surrogate cannot replace properly maintained PM₂.₅ instrumentation, particularly for extreme pollution episodes.

Article.Title: An explainable vision transformer approach for automated neurological disorder classification from brain MRI scans
Article.Authors: Alahmadi A.; Asim N.; Khan M.; Sirshar M.; Aljubayri I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diagnosing Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), and brain tumors early enough to matter still depends heavily on brain MRI, and brain MRI still depends on radiologists who are in short supply almost everywhere. Convolutional neural networks have made real progress on this problem, but a single convolution only sees a small patch of the image, which limits how well a purely convolutional model can tie together pathology that is spread across the brain. This study addresses that limitation from two directions at once: a controlled, same-protocol comparison of established CNN backbones, and a lightweight attention mechanism grafted onto one of them. We classify the full eight-class Multi-Class Neurological Disorder (MCND) dataset (AD MildDemented, AD ModerateDemented, AD VeryMildDemented, Multiple Sclerosis, Normal, and three brain-tumor subtypes: glioma, meningioma, and pituitary), comprising 9,564 MRI images split 80:20 into 7,651 training and 1,913 test images. Four established CNNs, VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNet-B0, were fine-tuned under one shared protocol to serve as controlled baselines. We then built VGG-16 + CBAM: a VGG16 backbone fitted with a Convolutional Block Attention Module and a much smaller classification head in place of VGG-16’s original fully connected layers, trained for 15 epochs under the same optimizer and augmentation settings used for the baselines. It reached 98.90% accuracy, a weighted F1-score of 0.9890, a macro F1 of 0.9893, a macro AUC-ROC of 0.9997, and an MCC of 0.9874 on the held-out test set, beating all four baselines (98.12%–98.85% accuracy) while using just 14.88 million parameters, roughly 9% of VGG-16’s 134.29 million, for a 56.8 MB model. We also report parameter counts, model size, FLOPs, GPU inference latency, and training time for every baseline, so the accuracy gain can be weighed against actual computational cost rather than accuracy alone. Grad-CAM maps for all eight classes show the model focusing on plausible anatomical regions: periventricular and hippocampal areas for the AD stages, white matter for MS, and the tumor core for each tumor subtype. A t-SNE projection of the learned features shows the eight classes forming distinct, mostly non-overlapping clusters. Taken together, the results suggest a small, attention-augmented CNN can match or beat larger backbones on this task at a fraction of the cost, without losing the interpretability a clinician would need to trust it.

Article.Title: Climate change and the weather-energy Nexus in US energy demand
Article.Authors: Akadiri S.; Awosusi A.; Sendi A.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the long-run and short-run elasticities of U.S. residential and commercial final energy consumption with respect to historical variations in heating and cooling degree days and compares these weather sensitivities across sectors. It also investigates whether joint exposure to heating and cooling conditions has an additive or attenuating effect on annual energy consumption. Using annual U.S. data from 1960 to 2025, we employ a Fourier-augmented bootstrap autoregressive distributed lag (Fourier ARDL) framework to estimate weather–energy relationships while accommodating smooth structural change. We also use a Fourier-augmented Toda–Yamamoto procedure to examine directional predictive relationships. The results confirm long-run equilibrium relationships in both sectors. Heating degree days have positive, significant long-run effects on residential and commercial energy consumption. Cooling degree days become significant when we include the heating–cooling interaction term. The interaction coefficient is negative and significant, indicating that joint heating and cooling exposure has an attenuating, non-additive association with annual energy consumption. Because we include the interaction term, we interpret the estimated HDD and CDD coefficients as conditional effects rather than unconditional elasticities. Residential energy demand adjusts to disequilibrium approximately three times faster than commercial demand. The causality results indicate directional predictive relationships from HDD to commercial consumption and from CHDD to residential consumption. Overall, the findings provide evidence on historical weather–energy relationships and offer implications for demand forecasting, grid planning, and energy-efficiency policy, but do not constitute a formal counterfactual attribution of energy changes to climate change.

Article.Title: Broadband asymmetric transmission and cross-polarization conversion in an interlayer-coupled bilayer chiral metasurface
Article.Authors: Sadeghi Chemeh P.; Jam S.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a bilayer 3D-chiral metasurface for broadband asymmetric transmission (AT) and cross-polarization conversion in the microwave regime. The structure achieves a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) above 93% over 10.0–15.3 GHz, peaking at 98%. Simulations further indicate that high PCR is largely retained under moderate oblique incidence around 45°. The structure employs a 90°-rotated and y-mirrored bilayer arrangement, whose interlayer coupling induces effective magnetoelectric interactions and enables efficient cross-polarization conversion. For backward incidence, the polarizer provides y-to-x polarization conversion across the operating band, and the conversion direction reverses under forward incidence. The resulting asymmetric transmission reaches a peak value of 0.93. To provide a physics-oriented interpretation, the effective electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric surface susceptibilities are retrieved using a complete reciprocity-constrained tangential GSTC model. The retrieved tensors provide a macroscopic description of the coupled anisotropic and bianisotropic response. Surface-current distributions complement this macroscopic description by indicating electric- and magnetic-type current excitations associated with polarization conversion. A fitted Foster equivalent-circuit model provides a compact circuit-level representation of the dispersive CST response. A fabricated prototype is experimentally characterized. The normal-incidence measurements show reasonable overall agreement with the simulated polarization-conversion and AT responses. Taken together, the combined performance characteristics and the physics-oriented interpretation of the conversion mechanism demonstrate its potential for broadband microwave polarization-control applications.

Article.Title: Sustainable production of critical components for the oil and gas industry
Article.Authors: Kusyi Y.; Ivanov V.; Horbal N.; Kostiuk O.; Klymash I.; Onysko O.; Zajac J.
Article.Abstract: This research addresses the need for sustainable manufacturing and quality assurance of high-load components in the oil and gas sector within the frameworks of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0. The primary objective was to optimize the finishing treatment of the functional internal surfaces of NB 32.02.102-04 cylinder liners for NB-32 drilling pumps by replacing conventional energy-intensive finishing processes with more resource-efficient alternatives. A progressive technological route was proposed in which traditional grinding and honing operations were replaced by pressure-based finishing using Vibratory-Centrifugal Hardening (VCH) and hard-alloy surface modification. A methodology was developed to analyze technological inheritability by evaluating the transfer and transformation of surface roughness parameters throughout the manufacturing route, from rough boring to final plastic deformation finishing (PDF). Volumetric vibratory equipment was adapted specifically to treat the hard-to-access internal surfaces of these critical components. The experimental results demonstrated a substantial improvement in surface roughness characteristics. The arithmetic mean deviation of the profile (Ra) decreased nearly tenfold, from 6.12 to 0.63 μm, while the ten-point height of irregularities (Rz) decreased by approximately 17-fold, reaching 1.38 μm. In addition, the load-bearing capacity of the surface was improved, as indicated by a 1.7-fold increase in the relative bearing length (tm). At the same time, the spacing parameters RS and RSm decreased by more than fourfold. The analysis of technological inheritability identified VCH as a critical technological barrier that effectively transforms the inherited surface characteristics and promotes the formation of a surface state with improved functional properties. The developed technology aligns with the principles of sustainable manufacturing. It supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, 12, and 13 by eliminating the use of potentially hazardous cutting fluids and abrasive materials, reducing energy demand, and minimizing material waste. The findings demonstrate the potential of integrating vibratory-centrifugal hardening into the manufacturing route of NB 32.02.102-04 cylinder liners as an environmentally responsible finishing strategy. At the same time, further research is required to establish its effects on wear resistance, fatigue strength, and the long-term reliability of critical industrial components.

Article.Title: Predicting the volumetric behavior of crumb rubber asphalt mixtures via machine learning
Article.Authors: Citakoglu H.; Aslan S.; Herdem S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined advanced machine learning models to predict key volumetric parameters of stone mastic asphalt (SMA) mixtures incorporating waste tire rubber. The input parameters were rubber aggregate and rubber modifier. The target outputs were air void, voids filled with asphalt, voids in mineral aggregate, and density. A total of 216 asphalt samples were prepared, representing 72 distinct mixture combinations, as three replicate samples were produced for each condition. Five machine learning techniques—Gaussian Process Regression, Support Vector Machine Regression (SVR), Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System, Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines, and Least Squares Support Vector Machines (LS-SVR) were implemented, and models were evaluated using the 5-fold cross-validation method. Model performance was assessed using mean absolute error, root mean square error, determination coefficient, Wilmott’s refined index, NSE (Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency coefficient), overall index, CA (Combined Accuracy), and RRMSE (relative root mean square error) indices. The LS-SVR model was found to achieve the best predictive performance across all four outputs, with an RRMSE value below 10%, an NSE value greater than 0.9, and a CA value closest to zero. Furthermore, the results show that LS-SVR provides the closest fit to the experimental data and the lowest error levels. In contrast, the standard SVR model produced the weakest predictions, with the widest error distributions and highest deviations. Transforming SVR into LS-SVR significantly improved accuracy. However, the use of only two input variables in this study represents a deliberate simplification that limits the generalizability of the model to broad applications. Consequently, this research is primarily positioned as a proof-of-concept investigation to demonstrate the applicability of ML to a controlled laboratory dataset. Furthermore, the lack of external (independent) validation prevents the developed models from being interpreted as universal predictive tools in practical asphalt mix design. Therefore, the results show that the models successfully capture the relationships between rubber content and volumetric properties within the narrow range of laboratory parameters examined in this study. For broader applications, the inclusion of additional inputs and testing with independent datasets are necessary; these steps will allow for stronger inferences about the actual generalization performance of the models.

Article.Title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening reveals a chromatin-to-mitochondrial dependency architecture underlying Galunisertib-induced OXPHOS vulnerability
Article.Authors: Akla N.; Boudah A.; Faye M.; Danalache B.; Annabi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Galunisertib (LY2157299), a selective TGF‑βRI/ALK5 inhibitor with limited single‑agent Phase II efficacy, was used as a pharmacological probe to ask whether sustained Galunisertib exposure reorganizes cellular dependencies toward an OXPHOS-associated state. A genome‑wide CRISPR‑Cas9 loss‑of‑function chemogenomic screen was performed in Galunisertib‑treated NALM‑6 pre‑B leukemia cells and analyzed with CRANKS scoring, Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis, STRING network mapping, subcellular compartment annotation, and MitoCarta3.0/MitoPathways3.0 cross‑referencing. Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) was the only Hallmark gene set significantly enriched after correction for multiple testing, and mitochondrial compartments, mitochondrial gene expression and mitochondrial translation were enriched among genes whose loss improved fitness under treatment. Prioritized hits resolved into a layered architecture in which a chromatin-associated transcriptional module, anchored by the high-confidence sensitizer TCF4, is coupled to post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA metabolism and to genes maintaining membrane and ionic homeostasis, converging on mitochondrial gene expression and translation as the terminal layer. Resistance-associated genes defined two routes out of this state: altered chromatin remodeling, and loss of mitochondrial translation or iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis. These dependencies derive from a single high-dose chemogenomic screen and await confirmation by individual gene perturbation or by direct metabolic measurement. Within that limit, the screen defines a reorganization of cellular dependencies under sustained Galunisertib exposure and nominates chromatin, post-transcriptional and OXPHOS-directed combinations as priority candidates for validation.

Article.Title: Retrospective modelling of space-time clusters of acute gastrointestinal syndromes in Lombardy, Italy
Article.Authors: Corrao G.; Crippa D.; Sguazzini E.; Conflitti C.; Bagarella G.; Maistrello M.; Covizzi A.; Colombo F.; Cereda D.; Gori A.; Franchi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal (GI) syndrome encompasses complex symptoms characterised by preventability, high morbidity, and relatively low mortality. We conducted this study to investigate the ability of syndromic surveillance for detecting space–time clusters of acute GI syndromes in Lombardy, Italy. The target population included the 10 million beneficiaries of the Regional Health Service during 2023. Individuals who experienced at least one Emergency Department (ED) admission for GI syndrome in 2023 were considered the main syndromic cases of interest, with retrospective data obtained from healthcare utilization databases. Two secondary case definitions, based on reports of GI infective disorders and drug dispensations for treating GI disorders, were also used. Daily data at the level of all 86 health districts composing Lombardy Region were monitored. By comparing observed and expected cases, space–time scan statistics were used to detect clusters within specific time frames and areas. Analyses were performed using SaTScan software. In 2023, 33.3 cases per 100,000 person-weeks were admitted to the ED for GI disorders. Based on the secondary definitions of cases, detection rates of 0.42 and 19.2 cases every 100,000 person-week were observed, respectively. Overall, 11 clusters were detected across 17 health districts, with durations ranging from 1 to 3 days. Clear positive linear trends were observed across the 86 health districts between ED-based rates and the corresponding reporting-based and drug-based rates. A syndromic surveillance system for acute GI syndromes is a promising tool for supporting policymakers in anticipating the emergence of new epidemics and evaluating the impact of actions aimed at reducing the risk of acute GI disturbances in endemic areas.

Article.Title: A hybrid machine learning framework integrating persian NLP for occupational risk classification in steel manufacturing
Article.Authors: Alamshah E.; Soleimani-Alyar M.; Hanifi S.; Jafari B.; Behravesh M.
Article.Abstract: Human error remains a leading cause of occupational accidents in high-risk industries, yet traditional risk assessment methods often overlook valuable information embedded in unstructured textual data. This study develops and validates a hybrid machine learning framework combining structured risk data with Natural Language Processing (NLP) to improve hazard classification accuracy in industrial settings. Data were collected from 258 work activities across 16 operational units in a steel manufacturing facility over five months, yielding 3,110 validated risk scenarios. Hazard identification employed Job Safety Analysis (JSA), while quantitative risk evaluation used the William Fine method. The dataset comprised structured variables (severity, exposure, probability) and unstructured Persian-language text (hazard descriptions, locations, activities). Text preprocessing included tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, and lemmatization. Features were extracted using TF-IDF vectorization for all models. Random Over-Sampling (ROS) addressed class imbalance. Four traditional machine learning algorithms were evaluated: Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). On unbalanced data, SVM achieved the highest accuracy (93%), with F1-scores of 0.96, 0.83, and 0.92 for low, medium, and high-risk categories, respectively. After ROS balancing, performance showed practical improvements across most models, particularly for minority risk classes; however, the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (p = 0.189), likely due to the small comparison sample (n = 3 models). SVM reached near-perfect classification, whereas KNN remained the weakest performer. The hybrid framework significantly outperforms traditional risk assessment methods by leveraging both structured data and unstructured textual information. The prevalence of low-risk scenarios (66.1%) suggests effective existing safety controls, while improved classification of medium and high-risk cases enables targeted interventions. This approach provides a foundation for real-time AI-driven safety monitoring systems in high-risk industrial sectors.

Article.Title: Nanoformulated silymarin enhances antifungal activity against resistant Candida albicans by reducing ergosterol and binding to cell envelope targets
Article.Authors: Ghodrati M.; Sharifzadeh A.; Fasaei B.; Malakootikhah J.; Koli A.; Khosravi A.
Article.Abstract: The increasing prevalence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans poses significant challenges in managing candidiasis. Silymarin, a flavonolignan mixture derived from milk thistle ( Silybum marianum ), has shown promising antimicrobial properties in prior research. Here, we evaluated the in vitro antifungal activity of free silymarin and its nanoencapsulated form against ten C. albicans isolates, including nine fluconazole-resistant clinical isolates and one reference strain. Nanocapsules were prepared and characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential measurements, yielding particles with mean diameters of 119.75 nm (SEM) and 157.5 nm (DLS), a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.407 and a highly negative zeta potential of − 77.9 mV. Susceptibility testing followed CLSI guidelines, revealing that nanoencapsulation improved efficacy: geometric mean minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) decreased from 7578.6 µg/mL (free silymarin) to 4061.3 µg/mL (nanosilymarin), while minimum fungicidal concentrations (MFCs) dropped from 15,157.2 to 7578.6 µg/mL. At sub-MIC levels, nanosilymarin reduced cellular ergosterol content to an extent similar to that observed with itraconazole, as measured by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Molecular docking simulations further indicated robust interactions of silymarin with key targets involved in cell wall integrity and ergosterol biosynthesis (namely Chs2, Erg11, and the transcription factor Upc2) with favorable binding energies of − 10.81, − 10.62, and − 12.84 kcal/mol, respectively. These results suggest that nanoformulation can enhance the antifungal action of silymarin against resistant C. albicans strains, likely through interference with ergosterol production and selective protein targeting.

Article.Title: Surface-modified magnetic polymeric–silver nanocomposites for broad-spectrum antibacterial applications
Article.Authors: Doan L.; Hoang L.; Nguyen K.; Dang Q.; Vo H.; Nguyen T.; Huynh K.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic antimicrobial nanocomposites have potential for applications in healthcare, food safety, and environmental settings. This study describes the synthesis of a multifunctional nanocomposite combining SPIONs with polylactic acid, an M8 polymer blend including PVA, PEG, PVP and chitosan, along with AgNPs to enhance antimicrobial activity while retaining potential for magnetic recovery. Strategies of surface modification, including carbon coating, SeNPs and chloramphenicol loading, were also systematically compared. Overall, SPION/PLA/M8Ag achieved > 92% OD-derived growth inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Salmonella enterica , and Escherichia coli without antibiotic loading. This was supported by physicochemical characterization (FE-SEM, XRD, FTIR, EDS and VSM), which revealed particle sizes of 12–24 nm, retention of the magnetite-like crystalline phase after surface functionalization, and superparamagnetism indicating potential for magnetic separation and recovery. The observed antibacterial activity may involve multiple factors, including Ag-associated effects, possible oxidative stress, electrostatic interactions, and interactions between the composite surface and bacterial cells; however, these mechanisms were not directly verified in the present study. These findings suggest that SPION/PLA/M8Ag may serve as a promising research platform for antibiotic-free antimicrobial materials.

Article.Title: Impact of Leishmania RNA virus 2 on immune response and pathogenesis in Leishmania major-infected BALB/c mice
Article.Authors: Riazi-rad F.; Katebi A.; Pakzad S.; Ajdary S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Leishmania RNA virus (LRV)1 has been associated with altered disease outcomes in cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), but the role of LRV2 in Leishmania major ( L. major ) infection remains poorly understood. This study investigated the impact of LRV2-positive L. major (Lm-LRV2 + ) on disease progression and host immune responses. J774A.1 macrophages were infected with Lm-LRV2 + or LRV2 - (Lm-LRV2 - ) parasites, and cytokine gene expression was measured by qPCR. BALB/c mice were inoculated subcutaneously with either strain; lesion development was monitored weekly, and parasite burden, cytokine responses (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17 A), and humoral responses (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a) were assessed. Macrophages infected with Lm-LRV2 + showed significantly elevated IL-6 and IL-1β mRNA levels compared to Lm-LRV2 - ( p < 0.01). In vivo, Lm-LRV2 + infection resulted in larger lesions and higher parasite loads ( p < 0.01). Lymphocytes from Lm-LRV2 + mice produced significantly more IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17 A at eight weeks ( p < 0.05), and antigen-specific IgG responses and IgG2a/IgG1 ratios were also increased. These findings demonstrate that LRV2 presence in L. major enhances pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and drives a more severe disease phenotype, with notable shifts in both cellular and humoral immunity. Our results underscore the critical role of LRV2 in CL pathogenesis and suggest that viral endosymbionts may serve as important modulators of disease outcomes in Leishmania infections.

Article.Title: Explainable deep learning for SEM-based classification of six Sclerodermataceae taxa
Article.Authors: Kumru E.; Aydoğan A.; Akarkamçi H.; Ekinci F.; Sevindik M.; Akata I.; Güzel M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate identification of closely related fungal species remains challenging because of substantial morphological similarities and overlapping diagnostic characters. This study evaluated explainable deep learning approaches for the image-level classification of six predefined Sclerodermataceae taxa using scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of fungal spores An original dataset consisting of 961 SEM micrographs representing Scleroderma areolatum , S. cepa , S. bovista , S. polyrhizum , S. verrucosum , and Pisolithus arhizus was constructed under specimen-preparation protocol. Image preprocessing included grayscale conversion, brightness normalization, histogram equalization, and annotation removal. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test subsets, and data augmentation was applied to improve model generalization. Nine pretrained convolutional neural network architectures, including ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, RegNet-Y8GF, ConvNeXt-Small, SENet-154, VGG-16, Inception-V3, Xception, and EfficientNet-B3, were comparatively evaluated using identical training conditions. Performance assessment was conducted using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews correlation coefficient, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, balanced accuracy, Cohen’s kappa, expected calibration error, and brier score. ResNet-50 achieved the highest classification performance with 99.48% accuracy, 99.49% precision, 99.48% recall, 99.48% F1-score, and 99.38% MCC, misclassifying only one test sample. Grad-CAM++ and occlusion sensitivity analyses suggested that model attention was predominantly associated with biologically relevant spore ornamentation regions. These findings support the applicability of SEM-based deep learning and qualitative XAI approaches for image-level classification among the six predefined Sclerodermataceae taxa examined under the present experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Correction: Immunogenicity of ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccine after a two-dose inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccination of dialysis patients and kidney transplant recipients
Article.Authors: Bruminhent J.; Setthaudom C.; Kitpermkiat R.; Kiertiburanakul S.; Malathum K.; Assanatham M.; Nongnuch A.; Phuphuakrat A.; Chaumdee P.; Janphram C.; Thotsiri S.; Chuengsaman P.; Boongird S.
Article.Abstract: This Article contains errors in the clinical trial registration numbers in the Abstract and the Materials and methods section, under the subheading ‘Study design’. Consequently,

Article.Title: Effect of 1-min versus 3-min epinephrine dosing regimens on 48-h survival in a porcine cardiac arrest model
Article.Authors: Ahn G.; Lee J.; Roh Y.; Jung W.; Lee Y.; Im H.; Hwang S.; Cha K.
Article.Abstract: The optimal epinephrine redosing interval during advanced life support remains uncertain. We randomized 48 Yorkshire pigs with ventricular fibrillation (VF) cardiac arrest to intravenous epinephrine 0.02 mg/kg every 1 or 3 min, with first defibrillation at 20 or 24 min. The primary outcome was 48-h survival; neurological assessment was blinded. Survival (70.8% vs 33.3%; P = 0.020) and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) (75.0% vs 33.3%; P = 0.008) were higher with the 1-min regimen than with the 3-min regimen. After adjustment for first-defibrillation timing, the 1-min regimen was associated with a lower hazard of death within 48 h (hazard ratio, 0.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.13–0.78), higher odds of sustained ROSC (odds ratio [OR], 5.40; 95% CI, 1.68–19.29), and a more favorable composite 48-h neurological deficit score, with deaths assigned 400 (common OR, 4.66; 95% CI, 1.49–15.90). Pressure–time integrals for systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure differed in rank-based but not permutation analyses. In this porcine model, the 1-min epinephrine dosing regimen was associated with higher 48-h survival and a more favorable composite 48-h neurological deficit score. However, clinical translation requires further study because dosing interval was inseparable from cumulative exposure and defibrillation timing was protocol-defined.

Article.Title: A decentralized multi-agent-based optimization framework for intelligent traffic systems
Article.Authors: Basingab M.
Article.Abstract: The increasing complexity of urban transportation has increased the importance of intelligent traffic systems (ITS). Conventional approaches, such as fixed-time control (STS), rule-based adaptive control (RBAC), and centralized optimization (CTO), struggle with traffic demand, and network complexity. These limitations highlight the need for decentralized control strategies. To address this challenge, this study proposes a Decentralized Agent-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Traffic Optimization (DAB-MARLTO) framework for smart traffic networks. The framework modeled urban road as a directed graph where vehicles, traffic signals, and road segments operate as autonomous agents. Traffic demand is modeled using a Poisson arrival process, while vehicle behavior is simulated via car-following, lane-changing, and queue models. Each signalized intersection is modeled as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and optimized using decentralized tabular Q-learning (QL). The framework is implemented in Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) via Traffic Control Interface (TraCI) policy execution. Performance metrics include Average Travel Time (ATT), throughput, average queue length, Congestion Index (CI), fuel consumption, and emission intensity. Results show DAB-MARLTO outperforms STS, RBAC, and CTO by reducing network delay, queue length, and congestion while improving efficiency. The framework achieves a 26.9% reduction in travel time, 46.4% reduction in queue length, 33.3% improvement in congestion index, and 27.4% increase in network throughput.

Article.Title: Reactive power sharing between parallel VSI into islanded microgrid based on PSO algorithm
Article.Authors: Shamkhi A.; Jasim B.; Alhasnawi B.; Jasim A.; Homod R.; Dočekalová A.; Bureš V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For islanded microgrids, the power sharing and frequency restoration significantly influence MG stability and reliability. This paper proposes a control strategy based on the PSO algorithm to modify a conventional droop control method. The active power sharing between parallel connected VSI can be ensured accurately by selecting a proper value of gain of p-f droop equation at each DG controller, but this produces a small steady-state frequency deviation. On the other hand, a proper selection of the gain of the Q-V droop equation cannot ensure accurate reactive power sharing. This paper proposed a centralized control strategy to compensate steady-state voltage and frequency error and ensure reactive power sharing between DGs into islanded MG. In this paper, a PSO algorithm is adopted to calculate the parameters of the PI controller of each DG unit, thus making system operation more stable and efficient for both transient response and a steady-state period. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in terms of active and reactive power sharing and frequency restoration accuracy compared to a conventional droop method.

Article.Title: Clinical and histopathological patterns of American cutaneous leishmaniasis: diagnostic and therapeutic implications for targeted therapy
Article.Authors: Rosette V.; Drak Alsibai K.; Pierre-Demar M.; Lebret J.; Blaizot R.; Grotta G.
Article.Abstract: American cutaneous leishmaniasis (ACL) is a neglected tropical disease that is endemic in French Guiana. While the proportion of treatment failures is high, the risk factors are poorly understood. Although histological analysis of ACL has been described, few studies have investigated its correlation with severity or response to treatment in America. Our objectives were to provide a precise dermatological description of the clinical forms, investigate the association between histological and clinical characteristics, and determine their links with treatment failure to guide new therapeutics. Among the 1,577 patients with positive analysis for cutaneous leishmaniasis in French Guiana between 2016 and 2024, 268 patients with available histological examination were included, of whom 245 had a confirmed ACL diagnosis with 80 pictures available. A negative parasite load was associated with large lesions (> 3 cm), gold mining and immunosuppression. The presence of papular lesions, more than five lesions and lower limb involvement were significantly associated with a poorer response to treatment. When classified according to the picture-based classification, the papulo-nodular form tended to exhibit an anergic histological pattern and a poorer response to treatment. The bacterial-infection-like form tended to have a neutrophilic folliculitis pattern. For 21 patients with negative parasitological tests, histopathology allowed to correct the diagnosis. The sensitivity of histopathology was 82%. Therefore, this study shows that histopathology remains useful in atypical ACL, to confirm the diagnosis and determine the histological pattern. Targeted therapies (increased doses of antiparasitic drugs for papulo-nodular forms or neutrophils inhibitors for bacterial-like forms) could be guided by histopathology.

Article.Title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
Article.Authors: Gomaa S.; Eissa M.; Abo Khashaba S.; Mostafa W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. In the context of escalating global energy demands, geothermal energy, defined as terrestrial heat extracted from the Earth’s crust through deep drilling and surface fluid transport, represents a viable pathway toward energy transition. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, environmental, and infrastructural parameters, each assigned relative weights commensurate with its significance. A robust correlation ( R = 0.975) was established between subsurface temperature and depth, yielding a mean geothermal gradient of 48.5 °C/km (R² = 0.9509) and affirming the reliability of the thermal model. The resulting suitability analysis demonstrates that the Gulf of Suez region possesses favorable conditions for the deployment of both Flash Steam and Binary Cycle power plant technologies. Along the eastern coastal corridor, localities including Hammam Faraun, Ras Sudr, and Abu Zenima were identified as suitable for Flash Steam systems at drilling depths of 3,000–4,000 m, corresponding to reservoir temperatures of 140–210 °C, while Binary Cycle systems are applicable at depths of 2,000–3,000 m with temperatures ranging from 100 to 160 °C. On the western coast, sites encompassing Ras Gharib, Ras Shukeir, Jabal al-Zeit, and Jabal Ataqa are technically viable for Flash Steam technology at depths of 3,000–4,000 m and temperatures of 140–210 °C, with supplementary Binary Cycle suitability observed at depths of 2,000–3,000 m and temperatures of 100–180 °C. Zones exclusively suited for Binary Cycle applications include Ayoun Moussa, Wadi Baaba, Wadi Feiran, and Wadi El-Tor to the east, and Zaafarana, Wadi Dara, and Wadi Araba to the west, at depths of 3,000–4,000 m with temperatures ranging between 100 and 160 °C and 100–155 °C, respectively. Northern portions of the study area, characterized by comparatively subdued geothermal gradients, are deemed appropriate for direct-use applications, including space heating, light industrial operations, and residential thermal supply.

Article.Title: Exploratory QSPR analysis of physicochemical properties of selected antifungal agents using topological indices
Article.Authors: Asim M.; Mufti Z.; Almehizia A.; Assiri A.; Ganati G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The structural-property relationships are key in the study of the physicochemical behavior of pharmaceuticals. The degree-based topological indices available through molecular graph theory are used to investigate the structure-property analysis of selected antimycotic agents in a quantitative way in this work. The molecular graphs of ten antimycotic agents were constructed, and several degree-based indices including $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$F^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$Y^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$S^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$G^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$P^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ were computed to describe their structural characteristics. To enhance descriptive reliability, this study introduces a novel integration of degree-based topological descriptors with comprehensive multivariate statistical techniques—combining linear regression, correlation profiling, and dimensionality reduction to evaluate structural-property dependencies. Statistical methods were applied to examine the connection between molecular structure and various physicochemical properties, including density, boiling point, enthalpy of vaporization, refractive index, molar refractivity, polarizability, molecular volume, surface tension, and atomic mass. The strength of the associations between topological descriptors and physicochemical parameters were analyzed using regression analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson analysis, and Spearman analysis of correlation. The accuracy of the fitted regression models was quantitatively evaluated for all parameters and showed to be property-dependent. The range of the standard model error metrics were: $$\textrm{MAE} = 0.0234$$ –161.7920 and $$\textrm{RMSE} = 0.0298$$ –262.6852 which scale directly with the magnitude of the target physicochemical properties. Furthermore, Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation yielded cross-validated performance metrics spanning $$Q^2_{\textrm{LOO}} = -2.1417$$ to 0.3514, with associated errors bounded by $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}MAE} = 0.0320$$ to 191.2633 and $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}RMSE} = 0.0371$$ to 304.5087. Moreover, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce data dimensionality and identify the most informative descriptors. These findings indicate that a number of topological indices have strong positive correlations with significant physicochemical characteristics, especially those of boiling point, molar refractivity, molecular volume, and atomic mass. Among descriptors that were examined, the most consistent correlations with physicochemical properties of antimycotic agents are observed in $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , where $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ achieved strong descriptive performance for polarizability ( $$R^2 = 0.989$$ , $$\textrm{RMSE} = 22.8565$$ , $$\textrm{MAE} = 17.7267$$ ).. The analysis of the results of PCA indicates that the first two principal components cover about 82 percent of the total variance and, therefore, the cumulative structural and physicochemical descriptors are effective in distinguishing the targeted compounds. Overall, the results indicate that degree-based topological indices are reliable descriptor of the physicochemical behavior of antimycotic agents and serve as effective tools in computational drug development and structure-property prediction.

Article.Title: Establishing a reflective-formative higher-order measurement model for the Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF)
Article.Authors: Wong B.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Given that model misspecification threatens the validity of constructs and distorts statistical findings, in the context of Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF), this study investigates whether smartphone addiction construct should be modelled using reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) or reflective-formative approach (Type II model). Drawing on theoretical criteria such as (1) direction of causality, (2) interchangeability of the indicators, (3) correlation/covariation among the indicators, and (4) the relationship of indicators with other constructs, this study has specified smartphone addiction as a second-order reflective-formative construct. To verify this model specification, data was collected from undergraduate students at a Chinese university and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), confirmatory tetrad analysis (CTA-PLS), and several recently developed model fit indices (SRMR, d_ULS, d_G). The results have not only determined that reflective-formative approach (Type II model) is more appropriate than reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) for modelling smartphone addiction construct but also provided strong evidence for construct validity. This study makes a significant theoretical and methodological contribution to the smartphone addiction literature by emphasizing the importance of considering the formative nature of the smartphone addiction construct when designing research frameworks.

Article.Title: Analysis of building seismic damage characteristics and topographic amplification effects of the 2026 Diebu Ms5.5 earthquake
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang J.; Wang P.; Wang Q.; Su W.; Zhang X.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract On January 26, 2026, an Ms5.5 shallow-focus earthquake occurred in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province. The affected area lies within the alpine gorge of the Bailong River on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, a region characterized by rugged topography and complex geological conditions that are typically prone to topographic amplification of ground motion. To address how topographic and site conditions control ground-motion amplification and the resulting spatial distribution of seismic damage, this study selected Dianga Town in Diebu County—the area covered by the earthquake damage survey—as the study area. Field damage surveys, seismic station monitoring data, and FLAC3D three-dimensional numerical simulations were integrated to systematically reveal the relationships among ground-motion amplification, building damage, and slope deformation. Results indicate that the seismic intensity in the study area reached VI–VII on the Chinese seismic intensity scale. Ground-motion amplification was closely associated with the spatially non-uniform distribution of seismic damage: at steep cliffs, slope shoulders, and high-elevation sites, peak ground acceleration (PGA) amplification factors approached 2.0, and buildings at these locations experienced significantly more severe damage than those at other sites. Seismic loading also altered the shear strain distribution pattern of the slope, causing the zone of concentrated shear strain to redistribute and extend toward the residential area. Topographic relief, excavation-induced free faces, and elevation differences were identified as the primary factors contributing to topographic amplification in the studied alpine gorge; in particular, an elevation difference of only about 100 m produced pronounced differences in seismic damage. These findings qualitatively reveal the mechanism of ground-motion amplification and provide a scientific basis for seismic fortification and geological hazard mitigation in villages and towns within alpine gorge areas on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau.

Article.Title: HSP90AA1 induces M2 macrophage polarization via stabilizing ITGB1 and promoting CCL2 secretion in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ding M.; Wang C.; Cao X.; Zong D.; Mao Y.; Wang W.; Ni X.; He X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) presents a major treatment challenge, largely due to immunotherapy resistance. The molecular mechanisms that drive the remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in NPC are still not well understood. This study explored how heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1) regulated the NPC immune microenvironment. A total of 54 NPC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy were analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). High HSP90AA1 expression predicted shorter progression-free survival (PFS). According to the TIMER database, HSP90AA1 expression positively correlated with M2 macrophage infiltration. Additionally, we established an indirect co-culture model containing NPC cells and THP-1-derived macrophages and found that HSP90AA1 facilitated macrophage M2 polarization. According to the results of co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays, HSP90AA1 associated with integrin β1 (ITGB1) and stabilized its protein expression, subsequently increasing C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) secretion. HSP90AA1 knockdown suppressed CCL2 secretion and M2 polarization, and ITGB1 overexpression partially reversed this effect. Taken together, our in vitro models and retrospective clinical correlation suggest that the HSP90AA1-ITGB1-CCL2 axis may drive immunosuppressive TME remodeling in NPC, highlighting HSP90AA1 as a promising predictive biomarker and therapeutic target against immunotherapy resistance.

Article.Title: Feasibility and expert evaluation of a medical large language model in an interdisciplinary clinical board
Article.Authors: Ronicke M.; Sollfrank L.; Sagonas I.; Atreya R.; Grieshaber-Bouyer R.; Hoerning A.; Jefremow A.; Kowalski I.; Krickau T.; Lermer J.; Meidenbauer N.; Rech J.; Rothhammer V.; Schley G.; Sondermann W.; Sticherling M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interdisciplinary clinical boards (ICB) on chronic inflammatory diseases discuss complicated and multidisciplinary cases with inflammatory conditions among experts in their discipline. Medically specialized large language models (LLMs) are finding increasingly widespread use among physicians to answer clinical questions. LLMs offer the potential to close the gap between rapidly expanding medical knowledge and limited time of physicians by providing evidence-based summaries to clinical questions and enable “real-time” literature search. However, it is unclear if LLMs can be implemented in clinical routine of ICB. In this prospective study, 100 consecutive real-world cases were discussed in our ICB. Each case was first discussed independently of the LLM and a preliminary recommendation was documented. The clinical question was then entered in the LLM “OpenEvidence”, the answer was reviewed by the board with the opportunity to add aspects not previously raised, and the recommendation was subsequently confirmed as final. Each participating expert evaluated the answer of the LLM using a questionnaire comprising eight Likert scale (1–5) items and one free-text item. Two physicians, blinded to each other, additionally evaluated outputs for their agreement with the board’s decision. The same cases were evaluated after prompt optimization at two different time points. The 100 discussed cases resulted in 759 rater-case evaluations. A mean of 2.3 specialties were directly involved in each case. The highest score was achieved by the item “OpenEvidence provided clinically relevant information for this case.” (4.06). Recommendation for future use achieved a mean score of 3.95. Complete agreement of the LLM answer with the final recommendation of the ICB was rated in 40.2% and 50.5% of all evaluable cases ( n = 97) by the two raters. When restricted to consensus cases, i.e. cases rated identically by both raters ( n = 62 of 97), complete agreement was 51.6%. Outputs after prompt optimization tended to be associated with higher agreement, but did not reach statistical significance. Outputs were not stable over time. The integration of OpenEvidence into an ICB was feasible and was perceived as useful by the participating specialists, with partial or complete concordance with the final board recommendation in the majority of evaluable cases. As the study did not assess patient outcomes, clinical harm or hallucinations, no conclusions on patient safety can be drawn. The LLM was naturally limited by the information provided in the prompt. Inadequate questions or missing information led to suboptimal answers, highlighting the importance of identifying and including relevant information beforehand. Expert oversight remains essential. Model drift of LLMs may outweigh prompt optimization.

Article.Title: Enhanced anti-ESKAPE pathogen and antibiofilm activities of Korean red ginseng-derived silver nanoparticles via membrane deformation: LC/HRMS profiling and dynamic correlations
Article.Authors: Aati S.; Bahr H.; Aati H.; Rajan S.; Shari F.; Sayed A.; Hassan H.; Basyony A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Red Ginseng is widely recognized for its diverse pharmacological activities, which are largely attributed to its ginsenoside content. A commercial processed Korean Red Ginseng extract product (HO3), hereafter referred to as “HO3 extract”, was used throughout this study. HO3 extract was analyzed using LC-HR-MS to evaluate and profile its ginsenoside content. LC-HR-MS analysis tentatively identified six major ginsenosides, namely Rh1, Rh2, Rg1, Rg2, Rg3, and Rb1. Subsequently, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) incorporating HO3 extract were synthesized and analyzed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), spectroscopy ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential measurements, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited a characteristic absorption band at 420 nm, indicating nanoparticle formation, while FTIR analysis revealed the presence of functional groups involved in nanoparticle stabilization. The antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of HO3 extract and HO3-mediated AgNPs were subsequently evaluated. Antibacterial assessment demonstrated that AgNPs significantly outperformed HO3 extract, exhibiting higher inhibition percentages and lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens. Furthermore, biofilm inhibition assays revealed markedly greater suppression by AgNPs (55–75%) than by HO3 extract (7–16%), with the highest activity observed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Time-kill assays further demonstrated that the antibacterial efficacy of AgNPs was both dose- and time-dependent. Moreover, the identified major ginsenosides were subjected to molecular dynamics (MD) simulations against microbial membrane models to predict their potential antimicrobial mechanisms. Notably, ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 exhibited the strongest membrane-disruptive effects, inducing substantial bilayer thinning and reducing local membrane thickness, thereby supporting their potential antimicrobial role.

Article.Title: Associations of cardiometabolic disease and depression with changes in instrumental activities of daily living disability among middle-aged and older adults
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Shin Y.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the independent and joint associations of cardiometabolic disease (CMD) and depression with changes in instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) disability among middle-aged and older adults. Longitudinal data were obtained from 16,780 individuals aged ≥ 45 years in the China Family Panel Studies from 2012 to 2020. Changes in IADL disability were assessed using transitions and trajectories. Mixed-effects models, Cox proportional hazards models, and multinomial logistic regression were applied, and joint associations were evaluated using multiplicative and additive interactions. CMD and depression were associated with higher IADL disability scores. Single CMD, cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), and depression were associated with increased risks of new-onset and persistent disability, a higher likelihood of severe disability trajectories, and a lower likelihood of recovery. The combination of CMM and depression showed evidence of multiplicative and additive interaction for IADL disability scores, with a broadly consistent adverse additive interaction pattern across new-onset disability, persistent disability, and severe disability trajectories. These findings suggest that CMD and depression are independently associated with adverse changes in IADL disability, with CMM and depression showing an additional adverse joint association. Integrated management of physical and mental health may help reduce disability in ageing populations.

Article.Title: Segmentation of brain tumors using a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model on MRI
Article.Authors: Kazemi M.; Farsi H.; Ghaffari A.; Mohamadzadeh S.; Barati A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for effective treatment planning and post-treatment monitoring. However, challenges such as intensity inhomogeneity, low-contrast boundaries, and highly irregular tumor morphology significantly complicate this task. In this work, we introduce a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates a convolutional U-Net for coarse tumor localization with a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model for precise boundary refinement.
