While the U-Net is trained using bimodal input (FLAIR + T1ce) to generate reliable initial masks, all refinement steps and final performance evaluations are conducted exclusively on single-modality FLAIR images—ensuring clinical simplicity and robustness. The proposed active contour incorporates a novel local fitting term based on morphological Laplacian operators, which capture structural transitions and enhance edge sensitivity. An adaptive weighting function dynamically balances the influence of local and global intensity information during contour evolution, improving resilience to noise and intensity variations without compromising computational efficiency. When evaluated on the BraTS 2020 dataset, the proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 96.48% ± 1.57%, a Jaccard index of 93.43% ± 2.92%, and a sensitivity of 97.01% ± 1.69%. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both classical active contour models and contemporary deep learning architectures in whole-tumor segmentation from FLAIR-only MRI. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

Article.Title: Characterization of plasma TNFRSF/TNFSF molecule profiles in HIV-associated disseminated Kaposi’s sarcoma over short- and long-term follow-up
Article.Authors: Ramón-Luing L.; Flores-Gonzalez J.; Espinosa E.; Islas-Muñoz B.; Briceño O.; Carpio-Guadarrama D.; García-Escutia D.; Volkow-Fernández P.; Chavez-Galan L.
Article.Abstract: The tumor necrosis factor superfamily (TNFSF) members regulate diverse cellular processes, yet their systemic profiles remain insufficiently characterized in persons living with HIV (PLHIV) with disseminated Kaposi sarcoma (DKS) caused by Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Plasma levels of fifteen TNFSF/TNFRSF molecules were quantified in twenty participants with DKS/HIV enrolled in a randomized clinical trial. Samples were obtained at diagnosis (week 0) and follow-up at weeks of treatment W 4 , W 12 , W 24 , W 48 , and W 365 . Three control groups were included: ten HIV-negative (HIV-), ten PLHIV without an AIDS defining event diagnosis (HIV+/AIDS-), and twenty-four HIV+ with an AIDS-defining event without KSHV- (HIV+/AIDS+). At baseline, DKS/HIV showed higher TNFR1 and TNFR2 levels than the control groups ( p < 0.0001). The APRIL level was lower compared to HIV+AIDS+ ( p < 0.0001) and HIV+AIDS- ( p = 0.0190). An exploratory multivariate ROC analysis identified TNFR1, TNFR2, and APRIL as the combination with the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.979) for distinguishing DKS/HIV patients from other groups, including HIV+/AIDS+ (significant predictive accuracy = 94.5%). Longitudinal analyses showed decreases in TNFR1 and BAFF at week 24 (W 24 ), ( p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0018, respectively) and decreases in TNFR2 beginning at week 12 ( p < 0.0001), with sustained reductions through week 48 ( p < 0.0001), and week 365 ( p < 0.0001). Mixed effects modeling indicated significant associations between follow-up time and changes in TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF. Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated significant associations between follow-up time and changes in TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF. This study describes baseline differences and longitudinal patterns of TNFRSF/TNFSF molecules in DKS/HIV. TNFR1, TNFR2, and APRIL showed the strongest baseline differences, whereas TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF displayed consistent temporal variations throughout the follow-up period. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of TNFRSF/TNFSF members as candidate biomarkers indicative of disease dynamics in DKS over both short-term (48 weeks) and long-term (7 years) follow-up.

Article.Title: Distinct host responses to whole-cell and CFS effects of Clostridium perfringens in Caenorhabditis elegans
Article.Authors: Sundararajan B.; Baskarapandian T.; Eswaran G.; Marudhamuthu M.
Article.Abstract: Clostridium perfringens is an important toxin-producing pathogen associated with a range of infections in humans and animals. Although its toxins are recognized as major virulence determinants, the extent to which toxin-mediated effects account for host responses during infection remains unclear. In this study, we used Caenorhabditis elegans as an in vivo model to compare the physiological and molecular responses elicited by whole-cell C. perfringens and its cell-free supernatant (CFS). The C. perfringens isolate obtained from the gastrointestinal tract of patients diagnosed with IBD was characterized and evaluated for pathogenicity in C. elegans . The CFS was prepared and validated functionally through hemolytic activity, heat-inactivation and dose-dependent toxicity assays. Host responses were assessed using lifespan, pharyngeal pumping, egg laying and microscopic analyses. Transcriptional changes were analysed by quantitative RT-PCR, keeping pmp-3 as the reference gene. Exposure to both whole bacterial cells and the CFS significantly impaired the survival, feeding behaviour, and reproductive capacity of C. elegans . However, the magnitude of these effects was greater during whole-cell exposure. The molecular study assessed the expression of genes associated with host defence and stress responses, including sek-1 and pmk-1 associated with p38 MAPK signalling, and the antimicrobial response marker lys-7 . skn-1 and gst-4 are associated with stress and detoxification responses, together with the oxidative-stress marker sod-3. Whole-cell exposure showed greater relative expression of sek-1 , pmk-1 , and lys-7 , compared with CFS treatment. Similarly, skn-1 and gst-4 were more highly expressed following whole-cell exposure than CFS treatment, while the oxidative-stress marker sod-3 was strongly induced by whole-cell exposure but showed minimal change following CFS treatment. These results suggest that while the toxin-associated components present in the CFS may contribute to the observed host responses, they cannot recreate responses observed during whole-cell exposure. This study also showed that C. elegans proved to be a useful model to evaluate the potential contribution of bacterial toxins to the development of infection and disease.

Article.Title: Hour-scale response of low-Earth-orbit satellite altitude to extreme geomagnetic storms revealed by the NinjaSat CubeSat during the 2024 solar maximum
Article.Authors: Tanaka H.; Nakagawa T.; Nozawa S.; Tamagawa T.; Enoto T.; Kitaguchi T.; Iwakiri W.; Mihara T.; Takeda T.; Ota N.; Aoyama A.; Iwata S.; Takahashi T.; Yamasaki K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extreme geomagnetic storms accelerate low-Earth-orbit satellite decay by inflating the thermosphere, yet the hour-scale pathway from solar-wind energy to atmospheric heating is poorly understood. Using the GNSS receiver of the NinjaSat CubeSat ( $$\sim 500$$ km, $$97^\circ $$ sun-synchronous), we tracked orbital altitude through solar-maximum 2024 and cross-correlated the storm-time altitude-change rate with geomagnetic indices during the two largest storms of the year. The EUV-corrected residual correlates with the polar-cap (PC) index at $$r\gtrsim 0.8$$ , PC leading or coincident with the response by up to $$\sim 3$$ h, as do the auroral electrojet indices AE and AL. It also correlates with the Dst index ( $$r\approx 0.82 - 0.84$$ ), but the altitude drop precedes the Dst minimum by $$\sim 3$$ h, attributing this to a common solar-wind driver rather than ring-current heating. XRISM ( $$31^\circ $$ , $$\sim 560$$ km) shows the storm-induced density enhancement reached low latitudes in May 2024 but not in October 2024, consistent with a shorter electrojet duration despite comparable peak intensity. Polar Joule heating, indexed by PC, is thus the dominant storm-time drag driver, providing a natural forecasting window of up to $$\sim 3$$ h.

Article.Title: Adsorption of hazardous Acid Violet 17 on Vachellia nilotica biochar: experimental and statistical physics modelling
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Al Shayeb A.; Naidu R.; Fegade U.; Jethave G.; Alluqmani A.; Martuza M.; Shatnawi Z.; Haque M.; Arifuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inadequate management of chemical industrial effluents necessitates the development of high-capacity, sustainable wastewater treatment technologies. This study investigates the adsorptive removal of hazardous Acid Violet 17 (AV17) dye using a novel biochar derived from Vachellia nilotica stems (VNBB). Characterization via HRTEM and BET analysis revealed a mesoporous, sponge-like architecture with a surface area of 50.92 m 2 g − 1 and an average pore diameter of 8.02 nm. Batch experiments demonstrated that VNBB is highly effective, achieving a maximum removal efficiency of 97.94% at pH 6. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm, yielding a superior maximum adsorption capacity ( Q max ) of 333.33 mgg − 1 . Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second order model, (R² = 0.995), implying strong correlation with the experimental results. From thermodynamic and statistical physics study, it was found that the adsorption mechanism followed mainly physical interaction. To provide deeper mechanistic insights, advanced statistical physics modeling was applied. A double-layer model with five parameters successfully described the adsorption isotherms. The steric parameter n ranged from 0.39 to 0.42, indicating a multi-docking mechanism where AV17 molecules maintain a horizontal orientation on the VNBB surface. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the process is endothermic and spontaneous, with adsorption energies ( E 1 ) between 22.16 and 24.48 kJmol − 1 , signifying a physical component to the binding. Furthermore, the biochar exhibited excellent stability, maintaining high performance across five regeneration cycles with less than a 2% loss in capacity. These findings position VNBB as a high-performance, cost-effective, and reusable adsorbent for the remediation of dye-contaminated industrial wastewater.

Article.Title: Prediction of Claudin18.2 expression in gastric adenocarcinoma by habitat radiomics based on spectral CT
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Pan X.; Ma H.; Tang C.; Lu L.; Yan X.; Huang J.; Tang X.; Qian T.; Liu K.
Article.Abstract: To explore the predictive value of habitat radiomics derived from Dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLSCT) for the preoperative evaluation of Claudin18.2 (CLDN18.2) expression in gastric adenocarcinoma. A retrospective cohort of 111 eligible patients with gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent preoperative dual-phase DLSCT examinations was randomly divided into training and test sets at a 7:3 ratio. On the basis of the DLSCT images, the habitat subregions were delineated by applying K-means clustering to the voxel intensity values. Habitat features were extracted and filtered from these subregions to construct a habitat radiomics model. A clinical model, a conventional radiomics model, and a combined habitat radiomics and clinical data nomogram model were subsequently constructed. Model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curves. The AUC values for the nomogram model in the training and test sets were 0.802 and 0.757, respectively, which were superior to those of the clinical model (AUC: 0.643 and 0.604, respectively), conventional radiomics model (AUC: 0.713 and 0.716, respectively) and habitat radiomics model (AUC: 0.768 and 0.726, respectively). The calibration curves demonstrated good consistency between the predicted results and actual outcomes. The results of the decision curve analysis(DCA) indicated that the model has high clinical applicability. The habitat radiomics model based on DLSCT outperforms the traditional radiomics model. Furthermore, integrating habitat radiomics with clinical indicators yields promising non-invasive predictive performance for preoperative CLDN18.2 stratification in gastric adenocarcinoma; large-scale prospective multicenter validation is required prior to clinical application.

Article.Title: Molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus in chigger mites
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Lim H.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with high case-fatality rates in East Asia. While hard ticks are recognized as the primary vectors of SFTS virus (SFTSV), the detection of SFTSV RNA in chigger mites suggests their involvement in viral maintenance in natural conditions. In this study, wild rodents were captured at 17 sites across the Republic of Korea in 2019, and spleen tissues and mites were collected and tested for SFTSV RNA using RT-PCR. To evaluate transovarial transmission, Leptotrombidium sp. collected from an endemic area were reared under laboratory conditions. Among 56 rodents and 3,402 mites, SFTSV RNA was detected in 3.6% of rodents and 2.3% of mite pools (minimum infection rate of 0.09%). Phylogenetic analysis revealed that all viral sequences clustered within genotype B. SFTSV RNA was detected in both parental mites and their F1 larvae, providing molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission. This study provides the first molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of SFTSV in chigger mites under laboratory conditions and indicates that chigger mites may contribute to the natural maintenance of the virus. Further animal model-based studies are needed to clarify their vector competence.

Article.Title: Development of a prediction model for occupational satisfaction among cancer patients following counseling in German psychosocial cancer counseling centers
Article.Authors: Lange H.; Kurth T.; Roth R.; Sibert N.; Breidenbach C.; Schellack S.; Ernstmann N.; Heidkamp P.; Hiltrop K.; Rother J.; Heier L.; Kowalski C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A prognostic model was developed and internally validated to predict satisfaction with the occupational situation among cancer patients receiving psychosocial counseling regarding return to work (RTW). Data were collected from outpatient cancer counseling centers in Germany and included individuals who had sought counseling on work-related issues at different stages of their illness. Satisfaction with the occupational situation was measured using a single-item scale. LASSO regression with cross-validation and bootstrapping was applied for predictor selection. The final model ( n = 259) identified satisfaction with life, baseline satisfaction with the occupational situation, and higher household and personal income as positive predictors, while workplace conflicts and psychological distress were negative predictors. The model showed moderate predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.29, RMSE = 2.55) and good calibration-in-the-large (predicted: 5.45; observed: 5.45). The model may support the identification of cancer survivors likely to report low satisfaction with the occupational situation following psychosocial counseling. External validation is required to assess generalizability. A web-based tool was developed to support application in counseling settings.

Article.Title: A single-user feasibility study demonstrating real-time raycast-based stair and elevation-change detection on consumer smartphone LiDAR hardware
Article.Authors: Herdt N.; Braun T.; Bell T.; Russell S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For individuals who are blind or visually impaired (BVI), undetected stairways, curbs, and sudden elevation changes represent a leading cause of fall-related injury. Herein we present a preliminary, single-operator feasibility evaluation of a computationally efficient geometric algorithm for detecting stair and elevation changes in real time, implemented entirely on an LiDAR-equipped consumer smartphone (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.2). The algorithm uses a set of eight downward- and forward-facing raycasts projected into an ARKit (Artificial Reality developer Kit)-reconstructed mesh and performs line-segment angular analysis at 60 Hz within a 16.7 ms per-frame budget, without requiring cloud processing, GPU inference, or custom hardware. A single trained operator conducted 120 trials spanning eight real-world hazard locations, five step heights (4.5 to 7.5 in; 11.4 to 19.1 cm), four stair grades (22 to 33 degrees), varied lighting conditions (indoor artificial, outdoor daytime, and outdoor nighttime), and both ascending and descending approaches, yielding an overall detection rate of 92.5% (95% CI 86.4–96.0%) and a mean alert distance of 2.31 ft (0.70 m; SD = 0.91 ft). No false-positive alerts were observed during the hazard-approach or traversal segments of these trials, although dedicated hazard-free control trials were not conducted, so this should not be read as a validated false-positive rate across general non-hazard environments. Detection rate and alert distance both tended to increase with step height, with the smallest steps and one specific indoor location accounting for most missed detections; however, pairwise differences across step-height, lighting, and approach-direction categories did not reach statistical significance at the sample sizes tested (Fisher’s exact p > 0.05 in all cases), and step geometry covaried with test location in this design, so these patterns should be treated as preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than as an established reliability threshold. Descending approaches produced numerically lower detection rates and shorter warning distances than ascending approaches, consistent with a geometric limitation intrinsic to depth-based sensing of hazards that only become visible at close range. These results indicate that low-latency elevation-hazard detection is technically feasible on commodity mobile hardware under controlled, single-operator conditions; confirming this feasibility finding for real-world use by BVI individuals will require larger, multi-participant studies incorporating natural scanning behavior and dedicated negative-condition testing.

Article.Title: Translation, cultural adaptation, and psychometric validation of the Persian ObsQoR-10 in inpatient women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery
Article.Authors: Maghalian M.; Rouhzendeh S.; Mirghafourvand M.
Article.Abstract: The quality of postpartum recovery is a complex process. In this study, we aimed to translate and culturally adapt the Persian version of the ObsQoR-10 instrument and evaluate its psychometric properties in inpatient women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery. This cross-sectional study translated and validated the Persian version of the Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 (ObsQoR-10) in accordance with COSMIN guidelines. A total of 408 postpartum women were recruited from Taleghani Hospital in Tabriz, Iran, between 2024 and 2025. The ObsQoR-10 underwent a rigorous translation process (forward and backward translation, followed by cognitive interviews) and comprehensive psychometric evaluation. Content validity was examined using expert panels through CVI and CVR indices, while face validity was assessed via patient feedback. Structural validity was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis (EFA, n = 150) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA, n = 258), and construct validity was assessed through hypotheses testing (convergent and known-groups validity). Reliability was assessed through Cronbach’s α, McDonald’s ω, and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) to determine test-retest stability. The ObsQoR-10 demonstrated excellent content validity (scale-CVI = 0.95, CVR = 0.89) and strong face validity (mean impact score = 4.37/5). EFA identified a single factor accounting for 73.4% of the variance. CFA supported acceptable model fit (scaled χ²/df = 1.53, CFI = 0.990, TLI = 0.986, robust RMSEA = 0.052, SRMR = 0.021). Internal consistency was high (α = 0.964, ω = 0.956), and test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.86). The total score was calculated as the sum of all 10 item scores (range: 0-100), with higher scores indicating better recovery. ObsQoR-10 scores correlated significantly with the Questionnaire About the Childbirth Experience (QACE) ( r = − .63, p < .001). No floor or ceiling effects were observed (0%). The Persian version of the Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 is a valid, reliable, and clinically practical patient-reported outcome measure for evaluating inpatient postpartum recovery among Persian-speaking women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning and hybrid transformer-based proteochemometric modelling for breast cancer molecular subtyping and multi-target natural product discovery
Article.Authors: Jakkula B.; Perugu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer comprises five intrinsic molecular subtypes with distinct transcriptomic programs, prognoses, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Yet, accurate subtype discrimination remains limited by boundary-overlap and poor cross-cohort generalisability, while single-target agents often fail against pathway redundancy and acquired resistance. We developed an integrated computational framework linking transcriptomic-classification, explainable target prioritisation, and multi-target natural-product discovery. Three transcriptomic cohorts (METABRIC-BRCA-2016, TCGA-BRCA-2012, and TCGA-BRCA-2018; n = 2512 after quality-control and ComBat-correction) were integrated. Differential-expression analysis and PCA-based feature selection yielded a 50-gene signature that retained more than 90% of the subtype-associated variance. Among the six evaluated classifiers, XGBoost achieved the best performance and generalised to an independent cohort of 3,409 samples (accuracy: 85.70%; ROC-AUC: 0.95–0.99). SHAP-analysis identified 30-candidate genes associated with Basal-like and HER2-enriched subtypes, which were cross-referenced against ChEMBL to retain 11 targets for proteochemometric (PCM) modelling. A hybrid PCM multilayer-perceptron integrating ProtBERT and ChemBERTa embeddings with molecular fingerprints and chemical descriptors achieved a balanced-accuracy of 0.9140 and mean ROC-AUC of 0.9696. Screening of 30,898 NPASS natural products identified 292 pan-active compounds. Independent binding- and safety-prioritisation strategies converged on three leads: NPC139056, NPC196231, and NPC471997. This reproducible pipeline provides computationally prioritised leads for experimental validation in clinically challenging breast cancer subtypes.

Article.Title: Proteomics characterization of muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma identifies molecular subtypes and subtype-specific biological processes
Article.Authors: Pedregosa-Barbas J.; Trilla-Fuertes L.; García-Fernández E.; Becerril-Gómez F.; Lalanda-Delgado P.; Zambrana F.; Martínez-Salas I.; Gajate P.; Dittmann A.; López-Vacas R.; Kunz L.; Rubio G.; Nieto-Torrero S.; Pertejo A.; Vara J.; González-Peramato P.; Gámez-Pozo A.; Pinto-Marín Á.
Article.Abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma (MIBC) has been classified into transcriptomic subtypes, but comprehensive proteomic characterization remains limited. In this study, we used data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) to characterize the proteomic landscape of MIBC and explore subtype-associated therapeutic opportunities. Proteins were extracted from 58 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) MIBC transurethral resection (TURBT) samples and analyzed by data-independent acquisition mass-spectrometry (DIA-MS). Proteomics data were processed using Perseus and analyzed by hierarchical clustering and network analysis with TMEV, gRapHD, and DAVID. Findings were validated using the TCGA MIBC cohort. By the analysis of TURBT samples, three proteomic clusters that recapitulate MIBC transcriptomic subtypes were identified: Luminal-papillary (high KRT20 expression, mitochondrial and metabolic activity), Basal-squamous (basal biomarkers, DNA replication, and glycosylation activity), and Luminal-infiltrated + Luminal (immune and extracellular matrix activity). Network analysis revealed subtype-specific biological processes that were supported by analyses of the Dressler’s and TCGA MIBC cohorts. Subtype-specific proteomic profiles suggested candidate therapeutic approaches. DIA-MS profiling of routine, pre-treatment FFPE TURBT specimens (the diagnostic material on which treatment decisions are made) reproduces the established transcriptomic classification at the protein level. These findings provide a proteomic framework for molecular subtype characterization in MIBC and support the investigation of subtype-informed therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: User-focused faceted aggregated exploratory multimedia search results framework
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Saadia A.; Rashid U.; Khan T.; Jan T.; Khalil R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Search engines have become a ubiquitous platform for finding information, yet web users still struggle to browse and filter retrieved results in exploratory search environments with ill-defined information needs. While search engines retrieve relevant results for keyword queries, users struggle to browse, filter, and comprehend disorganized, media-diverse, disjointed verticals. Existing research on vertical aggregation has mainly focused on aggregating heterogeneous verticals, thereby undermining crucial aspects such as organization, annotation, and personalization to support exploratory search. This research proposes an aggregated, personalized exploratory search framework that organizes search results into Named Entity Recognition (NER)-derived, domain-independent facet categories and ranks them using a modified Best Matching 25 Fielded (BM25F) ranking algorithm. The facets are linked to the user query as implicit pseudo-relevance feedback to personalize search results based on the user’s category-specific intent. We empirically validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on standardized benchmarks (SciFact, TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, FiQA, SCIDOCS, ArguAna). The results show that the proposed ranking algorithm provides, on average, 12.59% superior data exploration performance while preserving lexical relevance. The algorithm’s efficacy in real-world exploratory search was further validated through a user study (N=23) that evaluated users’ exploratory search outcomes using system usability and behavioral metrics. An independent user study with 23 participants further indicates higher perceived usability and task satisfaction compared with a Google baseline, with a 17.72-point improvement in system usability and a 25.3% relative improvement in satisfaction with exploratory task completion. Behavioral analysis additionally shows shorter queries and substantially fewer query reformulations, indicating reduced query-formulation effort during exploratory search. These findings show that aggregating, annotating, organizing, and personalizing search results can substantially improve exploratory search effectiveness, reduce cognitive load, and enhance user satisfaction.

Article.Title: Spatial variability of TEC perturbations and ROTI during the 3 october 2024 X9.0 solar flare: a multi-station GNSS analysis
Article.Authors: Data E.; Setegn G.; Okoh D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the spatially heterogeneous low-latitude ionospheric response to the 3 October 2024 X9.0 solar flare using GNSS observations from seven equatorial and low-latitude stations. TEC, quiet-time differential TEC ( $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ ), and ROTI were analyzed under relatively quiet geomagnetic conditions ( $$K_p=1$$ –3). The flare peaked at 12:18 UT, and comparison with quiet-time conditions revealed $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ perturbations of approximately 6–14% at several stations, with pronounced spatial differences. YKRO showed the largest positive perturbation at the flare peak, reaching 12.75 TECU (14.21%), whereas MBAR and CUSV exhibited negative perturbations of $$-10.98$$ TECU ( $$-10.77\%$$ ) and $$-6.14$$ TECU ( $$-9.29\%$$ ), respectively. However, substantial and sometimes larger $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ variations occurred outside the flare interval, indicating that their magnitude alone cannot establish a flare-driven response. ROTI remained generally below 0.04 TECU min $$^{-1}$$ during the flare, with stronger irregularity activity occurring predominantly after sunset. The results indicate a measurable and spatially heterogeneous ionospheric response temporally associated with the X9.0 flare, while highlighting the substantial contribution of intrinsic low-latitude variability. These findings emphasize the importance of multi-station observations and quiet-time normalization for robustly assessing solar-flare-associated ionospheric disturbances.

Article.Title: Unravelling the roles of redox homeostasis and antioxidant system in facilitating adaptive responses during Pb induced hormesis in Brassica juncea
Article.Authors: Dhiman S.; Naresh R.; Bhardwaj R.; Singh R.; Kapoor N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This research explores the role of the antioxidant-prooxidant balance in eliciting the hormesis effect in Brassica juncea seedlings exposed to mild Lead (Pb). Excessive Pb doses in plants causes oxidative stress, which damages plant cells, stunts growth, and reduces agricultural yield. Conversely, mild Pb doses induce a hormetic effect inside plants system, leading to beneficial adaptive changes at cellular, molecular, and physio-biochemical levels. The plant's antioxidant defence network often relieves Pb metal stress. Antioxidants, both enzyme-based and non-enzyme-based, neutralize reactive oxygen species (ROS) created by Pb stress, protecting cellular structures and promoting plant resilience. Also, the idea of hormesis, which describes how modest doses of toxins like Pb metals cause plants to adapt, helps us understand how plants protect themselves and enhance stress tolerance to handle stress by raising antioxidant activity. In the present study, mild Pb exposed 10 days old B. juncea seedlings were tested for antioxidant activity and gene expression. Moderate Pb exposure increased B. juncea seedling protein content, antioxidant enzyme activity, and gene expression. The results suggest the possible role of antioxidants in inducing hormetic responses in B. juncea seedlings exposed to Pb, laying the foundation for understanding how these mechanisms cooperate to minimize Pb impact and improve seedling resilience.

Article.Title: Quantifying metal transferability in soil and its relationship to metal-related health risks in the strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)-human food chain
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Yang H.; Liu H.; Wang Y.; Liu B.
Article.Abstract: Understanding metal transfer in soil-strawberry systems is indispensable for sustainable strawberry production. To date, much attention has been paid to metals in strawberries, while metal transferability in strawberry-growing soil has been ignored. In this study, the availability, mobility, and bioavailability indices established based on BCR-extracted metal fractions and previously used for metal bioavailability evaluation in sediments were utilized to estimate metal transferability in soil sampled from strawberry orchards in the Yangtze River Delta, China, and predict metal-related health risks in strawberries. Overall, soil Pb, Cr, Ni, and Cu had their average bioavailability index (BI) values lower than 0.1, indicating low bioavailability of these metals. In contrast, soil Cd and Zn generally exhibited very high and moderate bioavailability, as their mean BI values reached 1.46 and 0.241, respectively. Furthermore, the mean values of total mobility and availability indices were 0.427 and 0.566, respectively, suggesting high mobility and availability for soil metals. Notably, the significant increase of soil Cr bioavailability induced by the acidification of strawberry-growing soil exacerbated the cancer risk caused by gastrointestinal bioaccessible Cr in strawberries. Overall, these indices, particularly the bioavailability index, can effectively reflect soil metal bioavailability and predict metal-related health risks in strawberries.

Article.Title: A physics guided hybrid modeling framework for rainfall runoff forecasting in data scarce regions
Article.Authors: Molajou A.; Tajbakhsh A.; Shokatian-Beiragh M.; Variani H.; Aram S.; Brysiewicz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rainfall-runoff (R-R) forecasting in data-scarce regions remains challenging due to limited hydrometeorological observations, uncertainties in satellite-based precipitation products (SPPs), and the inability of individual modeling approaches to fully represent complex watershed dynamics. To address these challenges, this study develops a physics guided hybrid modeling framework that integrates bias-corrected satellite precipitation products, signal decomposition techniques, process-based hydrological modeling, and deep learning (DL) for improved runoff simulation and forecasting. In the proposed framework, physical knowledge is incorporated through the soil and water assessment tool (SWAT), which provides physically meaningful representations of watershed processes, while a long short-term memory (LSTM) network learns residual nonlinear relationships between physically simulated and observed runoff responses. Three widely used SPPs, including CHIRPS, IMERG, and PERSIANN-CDR, were evaluated against available rainfall observations, and a PDF-based additive bias correction approach was applied to improve precipitation estimates. Wavelet transform (WT) and variational mode decomposition (VMD) were further investigated within a time consistent feature construction framework to extract hydrologically relevant temporal patterns from corrected precipitation inputs and SWAT-simulated runoff outputs. The framework was evaluated in two hydroclimatically contrasting watersheds in Iran, namely the semi-arid Tabriz Basin and the humid Ghaem Shahr Basin. Results indicated that CHIRPS provided the most reliable precipitation estimates among the tested SPPs, while VMD outperformed WT in extracting temporal characteristics relevant to runoff generation. The proposed VMD-SWAT-LSTM framework generally achieved superior or comparable performance compared with standalone SWAT, LSTM, and conventional SWAT-LSTM models during training, validation, and testing periods under a temporally consistent evaluation framework. During the training phase, the proposed framework achieved CC = 0.99, NSE = 0.96, and RMSE = 2.61 m 3 . s − 1 in Tabriz Basin, and CC = 0.98, NSE = 0.97, and RMSE = 0.58 m 3 . s − 1 in the Ghaem Shahr Basin. The proposed approach also demonstrated improved robustness in multi-step-ahead forecasting (up to 7 days), although predictive performance decreased with increasing lead time, and maintained robust performance under uncertainty according to Monte Carlo (MC) analysis. The findings demonstrate that combining physically based watershed representation with decomposition assisted data-driven (DD) error learning within a physics-guided framework can improve R-R forecasting accuracy and robustness in data-scarce regions. The proposed methodology showed robust performance in the two investigated hydroclimatically contrasting basins, suggesting its potential for hydrological prediction in data-scarce regions. However, its transferability to other basins and broader hydrological and climatic conditions requires further evaluation.

Article.Title: An international multilocation trial reveals genotype-by-environment interactions in Arabica coffee across climate gradients
Article.Authors: Gautron R.; Berny Mier y Teran J.; Delgado Muñoz L.; Lemus S.; Rahn E.; Castro Llanos F.; Bunn C.; Gezan S.; Pruvot-Woehl S.; Maina C.; Cheserek J.; Alonso Castillo J.; López Morgado R.; Alpízar E.; Alvarado J.; Arevalo J.; Banda B.; Baudry D.; Bordeaux M.; Castro E.; Devasia J.; Gichuru E.; Gimase J.; Alunga C.; Kachiguma N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate change makes the future of Arabica coffee ( Coffea arabica L.) uncertain, a crop supporting Coffee is produced on approximately 12.5 million farms worldwide, predominantly family-run smallholdings. Identifying varieties that combine high productivity with disease resistance across diverse environments is critical for climate adaptation, yet global empirical evidence remains limited. We leveraged a dataset from an international multi-environment trial evaluating 32 varieties for yield and coffee leaf rust severity across a total of 30 sites in 17 countries. Genotype-by-environment interactions were analyzed using factor analytic mixed-effects models, and latent environmental factors were linked to climatic gradients through partial least squares regression. Yield stability was associated with thermal gradients, distinguishing varietal adaptation between cooler environments with high diurnal temperature variation and warmer, thermally stable conditions. In contrast, rust severity and its interactions were associated with joint gradients of temperature, precipitation, humidity, and thermal variability. Among the evaluated genotypes, the F1 hybrids H1 Centroamericano and EC16, followed by the introgressed line Parainema, showed the strongest combined performance for yield and rust resistance, although with distinct climatic preferences and trade-offs in yield stability. Overall, introgressed varieties consistently outperformed pure Arabica varieties, which exhibited lower yields and greater rust susceptibility. These findings provide a robust empirical basis for climate-informed variety deployment and breeding strategies in Arabica coffee.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of mental health literacy and associated factors among older adults with cataracts
Article.Authors: Tang X.; Li X.; Li J.; Long L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health literacy may shape how older adults with cataracts recognize psychological distress and seek support, but variation within this population remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study surveyed 209 hospitalized adults aged 60 years or older with cataracts using validated measures of mental health literacy, anxiety, perceived social support and sleep quality. Latent profile analysis identified three mental health literacy profiles: low-MHL/negative-attitude (16.7%), limited-recognition/moderate-attitude (33.5%) and high-MHL (49.8%). Multinomial logistic regression showed that diagnosis duration, anxiety level, living arrangement and primary caregiver were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight different patterns of recognition and attitudes within this hospitalized sample. They support examining these dimensions separately in nursing assessment research. Independent validation is required before using the profiles to guide nursing assessment or select educational support.

Article.Title: Tracing of 13C-labeled fatty acids indicate the lack of linoleic acid synthesis in mammalian cells
Article.Authors: Mika A.; Hliwa-Slazyk A.; Koszalka P.; Andrieu A.; Kokotkiewicz A.; Krol A.; Luczkiewicz M.; Sledzinski T.
Article.Abstract: The belief that n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) cannot be synthetized de novo in mammalian cells is based on evidence from very early experiments. In recent literature misinterpretations can be found suggesting de novo synthesis of n-3 and n-6 PUFA from monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA), which in turn originate from saturated fatty acids (SFA), in human and other mammalian cells. Thus, to draw attention to this problem, we performed experiments with 13 C-labeled stearic acid using a modern analytical technique to verify the possibility of de novo PUFA synthesis in mammalian cells. We have supplemented the cultures of human hepatoma-derived cells (HepG2), mouse primary fibroblasts, and Salvia apiana cells (as a positive control) with 13 C stearic acid. 13 C-labeled fatty acids originating from 13 C stearic acid were detected in cultured cells with gas chromatography – mass spectrometry with selective ion monitoring. In human and murine cells, we did not detect any n-3 or n-6 PUFA containing 13 C, whereas in Salvia apiana cells we have found linoleic acid (a representative of n-6 PUFA), which contained 13 C in its structure. Interestingly, both in human and murine cells, we have found 13 C18:2n-9. Our results agree with the early evidence that n-3 and n-6 PUFA are not synthetized de novo in mammalian cells using a modern mass spectrometry-based technique. This study should prevent the continued repetition of the erroneous notion that human or other mammalian cells can de novo synthesize n-6 or n-3 PUFAs in the lipid-related literature. Furthermore, our results show the possibility of synthesis of other, much less studied group of PUFA – n-9 PUFA from MUFA in mammalian cells.

Article.Title: Coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and leached plastic-derived additives during magnetite-assisted water treatment
Article.Authors: Kida M.; Dytłow S.; Pochwat K.; Strojny W.; Ziembowicz S.; Gruca-Rokosz R.; Koszelnik P.; Radoń M.; Bester K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and dissolved plastic-derived additives were investigated using magnetite (Fe₃O₄). The investigated materials included tire wear particles (TWP), poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) pipe particles, and reference polymers. Magnetite rapidly induced heteroaggregation and enabled efficient magnetic separation of the investigated MPs. Simultaneously, dissolved plastic-associated organic compounds were scavenged from model solutions, with removal depending on their physicochemical properties. SEM, FTIR, and magnetic analyses confirmed attachment of Fe₃O₄ particles to microplastic surfaces, the formation of Fe₃O₄–MP aggregates, and the absence of detectable chemical modification of the investigated polymers. Magnetic measurements further demonstrated that the magnetic response of the heteroaggregates depended on polymer type, pH, and aggregate organization. Statistical analysis and exploratory Random Forest modelling were used to examine relationships among the investigated variables and to identify their relative contributions within the experimental dataset. Phthalate release from TWP continued after rapid magnetite-induced aggregation and separation of the microplastic particles, indicating that removal of the particulate fraction did not immediately terminate additive release from the polymer matrix. The simultaneous presence of MPs and magnetite therefore involved coupled processes associated with particulate aggregation, additive release, and scavenging of dissolved compounds. These findings demonstrate that physical removal of microplastic particles alone does not necessarily eliminate the dissolved fraction of plastic-derived contamination. The study provides an experimental assessment of these coupled processes under controlled conditions and highlights the importance of considering both particulate and dissolved plastic-related contaminants when evaluating magnetite-assisted treatment strategies.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning-based adaptive FOPID tuning for power system stability enhancement: A twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient approach
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Singh M.; Singh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)-based adaptive fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative (FOPID) controller for joint load-frequency and voltage regulation in a renewable-rich power system. The proposed controller adaptively tunes five FOPID parameters, namely $${K_p}$$ , $${K_i}$$ , $${K_d}$$ ,λ, and µ, through a multi-objective reward formulation that simultaneously minimizes frequency integral time-weighted absolute error (ITAE), terminal-voltage ITAE, maximum frequency deviation, and tie-line power error. A curriculum-based training strategy is employed to progressively expose the TD3 agent to increasing disturbance severity. The proposed framework is evaluated on a modified IEEE 14-bus system incorporating 46% renewable penetration, comprising DFIG-based wind generation and photovoltaic generation under low-inertia operating conditions. Under the standard 0.10 p.u. step-load disturbance, the proposed TD3-FOPID controller achieves an ITAE of 0.0612, a settling time of 1.48 s, and an overshoot of 1.82%. Across four nominal disturbance scenarios, the obtained damping ratios range from 0.74 to 0.78, while the broader tested operating-envelope analysis gives a minimum damping ratio of 0.72. The maximum system-level ROCOF observed at disturbance inception across the evaluated scenarios is 0.82 Hz/s, below the 2 Hz/s reference threshold adopted in this study. Statistical evaluation over ten independent training/evaluation runs with different random seeds further demonstrates consistent performance of the proposed approach. Numerical Lyapunov verification using the linearized closed-loop model provides numerical evidence of stable closed-loop behaviour within the tested operating envelope. The results demonstrate the potential of TD3-based five-parameter FOPID adaptation for robust frequency and voltage regulation in renewable-rich power systems.

Article.Title: Gut microbiome composition and oxalate-related metabolic functions in staghorn calcium oxalate stone formers: a shotgun metagenomic analysis
Article.Authors: Lu Y.; Toh T.; Lim L.; Toh K.; Tan C.; Chong T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Introduction: To characterize gut microbiome composition and oxalate-related metabolic functions in patients with staghorn calcium oxalate (CaOx) stones using shotgun metagenomic sequencing, and to determine whether specific bacterial taxa and pathways differ from stone-free controls. Methods: We conducted a prospective study of adults aged 21–75 years with partial or complete staghorn stones composed of >80% CaOx who underwent percutaneous nephrolithotomy between January 2023 and April 2024. Age-matched stone-free individuals served as controls. Stool samples were collected before intervention, preserved in stabilizing buffer, and analyzed using metagenomic shotgun sequencing. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and metabolic pathway abundances were assessed using standard bioinformatic pipelines. Dietary intake and clinical covariates were incorporated into multivariable models. Oxalobacter formigenes prevalence was determined from metagenomic reads. Results: Fifty-six participants were included (28 stone formers, 28 controls). Stone formers demonstrated significantly reduced alpha diversity (Shannon and Chao1 indices, p<0.05) and distinct beta diversity profiles (PERMANOVA R²=0.030, p=0.009), independent of diabetes, hypertension, urolithiasis history, and respiratory conditions. Differential abundance analysis showed increased Erysipelatoclostridium ramosum SGB6744 and reduced levels of several commensals, including Bifidobacterium adolescentis , Faecalibacterium spp ., and Eubacterium rectale . Functional profiling revealed reduced abundance of bacterial pathways related to glycine, serine, and tryptophan metabolism. Oxalobacter formigenes was detected less frequently in stone formers than controls (3.6% vs 21.4%). Conclusions: Staghorn CaOx stone formers exhibit gut microbiome dysbiosis and reduced representation of metabolic pathways linked to endogenous oxalate handling. These findings support a potential mechanistic role of the gut microbiome in CaOx stone biology and justify future interventional studies targeting microbial metabolic functions.

Article.Title: The relationships among achievement motivation health related physical fitness and academic procrastination in adolescents from a multitheoretical perspective
Article.Authors: Ying J.; Feng L.; Qiu W.; Xiao H.; Yang X.; Wang Y.; Luo L.; Liu C.; Feng L.
Article.Abstract: Academic procrastination among adolescents is a complex phenomenon associated with multiple factors. This study aimed to examine the associations among achievement motivation, health-related physical fitness, and academic procrastination in adolescents. A cross-sectional study design was employed. Using a stratified cluster random sampling method, 700 adolescents aged 12–14 years were recruited from two secondary schools in Yunnan Province, China. Data were collected through an online self-report questionnaire assessing academic procrastination and achievement motivation, along with. objective field-based physical fitness tests administered by certified physical education teachers to evaluate health-related physical fitness. After excluding invalid responses, 625 valid questionnaires were retained, yielding a valid response rate of 89.28%. Statistical analyses, including correlation, regression, and mediation analyses, were conducted using SPSS version 29.0. Correlation analyses indicated significant pairwise statistical associations among achievement motivation, academic procrastination, and health-related physical fitness in adolescents. Further analysis showed that health-related physical fitness exhibited a significant indirect statistical association between achievement motivation and academic procrastination, with an indirect association estimate of − 0.014 (95% confidence interval [CI]: −0.0350 to − 0.0012). However, this indirect association was small in magnitude, accounting for only 8.33% of the total statistical association between achievement motivation and academic procrastination. Achievement motivation was significantly associated with academic procrastination among adolescents, while health-related physical fitness exhibited a significant indirect statistical association with the relationship between achievement motivation and academic procrastination. Future research should further examine the interconnected relationships among achievement motivation, health-related physical fitness, and academic procrastination to provide a more comprehensive understanding of adolescents’ academic behaviors and healthy development.

Article.Title: Initiation mechanism of irrigation-induced retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Tableland, China
Article.Authors: Ma P.; Chen L.; Xue Y.; Wang J.; Mu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repeated sliding disturbs the slope structure and degrades soil mechanical properties, promoting the progressive development of retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Plateau, China. These landslides progressively encroach upon the plateau surface and have caused substantial casualties and property losses. Field investigations revealed that two subsequent retrogressive failures caused the landslide crown to retreat by approximately 8 and 7 m, respectively, suggesting that the near-crown zone formed after the initial failure underwent sustained disturbance and structural readjustment. Accordingly, undisturbed loess samples were collected from a sliding-disturbed zone approximately 5 m from the current crown (No.1) and a relatively undisturbed zone approximately 50 m from the crown (No.2). Consolidated undrained triaxial tests, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) infiltration tests, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses were conducted to systematically compare the strength, water-migration characteristics, and microstructural damage of the soils from the two zones, thereby elucidating the triggering mechanism of retrogressive landslides. The results indicate that: (1) The soil in the sliding-disturbed zone exhibited pronounced mechanical weakening. Under natural conditions, the average shear strength of No. 1 was approximately 20% lower than that of No. 2; under saturated conditions, its shear strength was only 71.9–90.0% of that in the relatively undisturbed zone. The disturbed soil was characterized by a higher proportion of large pores, weaker interparticle bonding, and more irregular pore geometries, making its mechanical behavior more sensitive to variations in water content. (2) The sliding-disturbed zone exhibited more pronounced water migration. The average signal intensity of the second peak in the NMR T₂ spectrum was approximately 1.97 times that of the relatively undisturbed zone, indicating a stronger water-filling response within the larger-pore domain. During water infiltration, pore-structure readjustment and changes in pore morphology occurred in the disturbed zone, further promoting structural weakening of the soil. (3) The subsequent evolution of retrogressive landslides can be summarized as follows: the initial failure disturbs the slope and alters its stress state and pore structure; sustained water infiltration subsequently promotes further structural readjustment and degradation of the soil’s mechanical properties, thereby reducing slope stability and increasing the likelihood of renewed failure. This process ultimately produces a cascading “sliding–disturbance–re-sliding” evolution pattern.

Article.Title: Optical mediation of chlorophyll-a trends and radiative heating in coastal waters
Article.Authors: Adhikari A.; Cahill B.; Menon H.
Article.Abstract: Long-term trends in satellite-derived chlorophyll- a (Chl- a ) in optically complex coastal waters may reflect changes in multiple constituents rather than phytoplankton biomass alone. Using satellite Chl- a observations from 1998-2023 and 10 years of in situ hyperspectral remote-sensing reflectance data, \(R_{rs}(\lambda )\) (sr \(^{-1}\) ), together with derived constituent-specific absorption coefficients from the eastern Arabian Sea, we identified coherent positive and negative trends and classified eight optical water types. Positive-trend types generally exhibited greater particulate absorption, whereas negative-trend types showed greater fractional coloured dissolved organic matter (CDOM) absorption at shorter wavelengths. Three-stream radiative-transfer modelling revealed corresponding differences in dimensionless subsurface spectral irradiance reflectance, \(R(z,\lambda )=E_u(z,\lambda )/[E_d(z,\lambda )+E_s(z,\lambda )]\) , euphotic depth, and radiative heating rate. Positive-trend types exhibited mean euphotic depths of 4.0-5.3 m, whereas negative-trend types portrayed shallower values of 3.1-3.6 m and more surface-intensified heating. CDOM-enhanced types exhibited approximately 1.18-fold greater depth-integrated radiative heating within their respective euphotic zones, despite reduced water-leaving reflectance at strongly absorbed wavelengths. These results demonstrated that constituent composition and spectral absorption mediated both the expression of long-term variability in satellite ocean colour and the vertical distribution and transmission of solar irradiance.

Article.Title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
Article.Authors: Rizk N.; Marouf M.; Ahmed N.; El-Gayar M.; Kamel M.; El-Khateeb M.; Sedhom R.; Elfeky E.; El-Liethy M.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics to characterize DNA viral communities across the full treatment train of a full-scale WSP system in Giza, Egypt, with particular emphasis on maturation-stage restructuring. Viral community composition was strongly structured by treatment stage (PERMANOVA R² = 0.53, p < 0.05), with the most pronounced compositional turnover occurring between upstream ponds and the maturation pond. Relative abundance changes were highly taxon dependent. Human-associated viral families, including Adenoviridae and Poxviridae , were detected in the inlet but fell below detection in the maturation pond, whereas other groups such as Microviridae showed partial persistence. In contrast, several bacteriophage-associated signals increased in relative abundance in the maturation pond, suggesting stage-associated restructuring of viral DNA profiles that may be linked to host community shifts, environmental filtering, or particle-associated DNA dynamics. Notably, the maturation pond virome displayed differentiation from upstream stages, including the emergence of eukaryote-associated viral signals, consistent with potential co-variation with locally established microeukaryotic communities. Cross-domain network analysis further revealed that the maturation pond was characterized by tightly connected virus–bacteria–microeukaryote modules dominated by positive associations, indicative of coordinated responses to shared environmental filtering. Together, these findings position the maturation pond as a distinct ecological compartment associated with downstream virome restructuring under combined environmental filtering, treatment-stage conditions, and host-community-associated processes.

Article.Title: Prioritizing usability attributes in bottled food packaging for older consumers using the Kano model
Article.Authors: Jian X.; Mustafa M.
Article.Abstract: Bottled food packaging may pose operational challenges for older adults due to age-related declines in physical strength, joint mobility, and sensory perception. However, limited research has systematically examined how different packaging usability attributes influence user satisfaction and dissatisfaction. This study investigates operability-related design attributes of bottled food packaging for older consumers using a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured interviews were first conducted to identify common operational difficulties and generate candidate attributes. A two-round Delphi consultation with experts was then used to refine and validate the attribute system. Finally, a Kano-model questionnaire survey involving 385 older adults was conducted to evaluate how the presence or absence of specific attributes affects user satisfaction. The results identified 27 usability-related attributes across five dimensions: functionality, reliability, usability, proficiency, and creativity. Basic operational and safety-related attributes were mainly classified as Must-be or One-dimensional attributes, indicating that their absence strongly increases dissatisfaction. In contrast, innovation-related attributes were primarily categorized as Attractive attributes, contributing to satisfaction when present but not causing dissatisfaction when absent. These findings reveal an asymmetric satisfaction–dissatisfaction mechanism in older adults’ evaluation of packaging usability and provide design implications for developing ageing-friendly bottled food packaging.

Article.Title: Effect of Bacillus sp. N188 application on turf quality and functional value
Article.Authors: Radkowski A.; Szpytma M.; Radkowska I.; Bujak H.; Dobrzyński J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maintaining high-quality functional and recreational turfgrass requires effective management practices that support turf performance under field conditions. One promising strategy involves the use of plant growth-promoting microorganisms. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of Bacillus sp. N188 on turf quality and functional performance. A field experiment was conducted in 2024–2025 under the conditions of southern Poland on Haplic Phaeozem soil. The study included two lawn mixtures differing in species composition and intended use: “Uniwersalna U-1” and “Super Trawnik”. The experimental design comprised control treatments and variants with annual application of a preparation containing Bacillus sp. N188. Turf quality was assessed according to the COBORU methodology, including visual traits (overall appearance, turf density, leaf colour and structure, and disease susceptibility), as well as physiological indices (NDVI, LAI, SPAD) and selected indicators of functional value. The application of Bacillus sp. N188 significantly improved turf quality compared to the control treatments. An increase in sward density and uniformity, more intense leaf coloration, improved structural characteristics, and reduced incidence of fungal diseases were observed. The physiological indices confirmed improved plant condition in plots treated with the bacterial preparation. The positive effects of Bacillus sp. N188 were observed in both lawn mixtures, although the magnitude of the response varied depending on species composition. The results indicate that Bacillus sp. N188 has potential as a plant biostimulant for improving the aesthetic and functional properties of turfgrass under temperate climatic conditions.

Article.Title: A new evolutive clustering algorithm (eSIMBA) for active module identification in p-value attributed temporal biological networks
Article.Authors: Singlan N.; Abou Choucha F.; Pasquier C.
Article.Abstract: Biological processes are inherently dynamic: gene expression and molecular interactions fluctuate as cellular mechanisms evolve over time. Active Module Identification Methods (AMIMs) capture these functional behaviours by identifying sets of molecular entities exhibiting coordinated activity. Yet, understanding biological systems requires more than a static picture and calls for the temporal contextualization of such modular dynamics. To address this need, the proposed algorithm combines static and sliding-time-window community detection using a greedy matching procedure that maintains continuity across time. This method detects active modules at each time point and consistently tracks their evolution. Extensive experiments performed on both synthetic and real-world biological networks confirm its effectiveness. By explicitly embracing temporal variability, the proposed approach reveals how active modules emerge, split, merge, or disappear, providing new insights into the dynamic organization of node-attributed biological networks.

Article.Title: Design, implementation, and evaluation of a comprehensive educational program for microbiology laboratory personnel and graduate students in teaching hospitals
Article.Authors: Baseri Z.; Irajian G.; Dehghan A.
Article.Abstract: Patient care and clinical diagnosis are significantly dependent on laboratory results. Repeated shortages of skills and evolving technologies, however, highlight the need for continuous professional development in graduate students and laboratory personnel. The purpose of this study was to design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program for the microbiology personnel in the teaching hospitals of Tehran University of Medical Sciences as well as for postgraduate students. This single-group, uncontrolled pre-test/post-test evaluation included a nine-month pre-and-post audit of laboratory quality. Baseline assessments in 14 teaching hospitals identified training needs. Ten focused workshops on a set of priority topics, including quality control, antimicrobial resistance, and specimen processing were formulated. Personnel were required to attend, whereas students were invited to attend. Pre- and post-tests, follow-up laboratory audits, and participant satisfaction surveys were used to assess the program’s effectiveness. In total, 282 personnel and 200 student workshop attendances were analyzed; all participants who began a session completed both the pre- and post-tests. Post-test knowledge scores increased significantly for personnel (4.32 ± 1.66 to 7.52 ± 1.70; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d z = 1.68) and students (3.64 ± 1.08 to 7.35 ± 1.47; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d z = 2.33). At nine months, the mean audit score across 14 centers improved from 15.86 ± 2.99 to 17.93 ± 2.75 out of 20 (mean improvement 2.07, 95% CI 1.16–2.98; paired t (13) = 4.93, p < 0.001; Wilcoxon p = 0.001). Satisfaction was high: 85% rated the program as “very good,” and 15% rated it as “good.” The implementation of an organized program led to substantial improvements in knowledge and laboratory audit scores. Due to the lack of a control group and improvements in other areas apart from the training, one cannot conclude that these improvements can be directly attributed to the effect of the training alone. Control groups, individual attendance data, and validated assessment instruments need to be included in future evaluations.

Article.Title: Antioxidant treatments combined with refrigerated storage, modified atmosphere packaging, and precooling improve postharvest quality of red cabbage
Article.Authors: Abo Elmakarem A.; Mostafa N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postharvest deterioration of red cabbage involves water loss, oxidative imbalance, membrane damage, and loss of structural and sensory quality. This study evaluated the effects of four food-grade antioxidants—ascorbic acid, citric acid, glutathione, and α-tocopherol—together with an untreated control under three refrigerated storage strategies: conventional refrigeration, modified atmosphere packaging (MAP), and pre-cooling followed by MAP. A 5 × 3 factorial experiment was conducted to assess treatment effects and interactions on physiological, biochemical, oxidative, structural, and quality-related attributes after 12 weeks of storage. Antioxidant treatment, storage condition, and their interaction significantly affected several measured attributes, indicating that treatment responses varied with the storage environment. The combination of citric acid and pre-cooling followed by MAP resulted in the lowest weight loss (8.96%), representing a 69.6% reduction compared with the untreated control under the same storage condition (29.46%). Under this combination, SOD activity reached 49.08 units mg⁻¹ protein compared with 25.69 units mg⁻¹ protein in the corresponding control. Antioxidant treatments also influenced phytochemical retention, membrane stability, firmness, texture, and oxidative-stress-related responses, although the magnitude and direction of effects varied among antioxidant–storage combinations. Multivariate analyses supported associations among oxidative status, antioxidant defense, structural attributes, and postharvest quality. The results indicate that antioxidant application can complement refrigerated MAP-based storage, with citric acid combined with pre-cooling and MAP providing the lowest weight loss among the tested combinations. These findings support the potential of integrating food-grade antioxidant treatments with established refrigerated handling practices, while further studies are needed to evaluate their performance under commercial-scale conditions.

Article.Title: SGA-based volleyball teaching with explicit life skills instruction is associated with technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational improvements in school students
Article.Authors: Gonçalves C.; de Sá Filho A.; Arantes D.; Clemente F.; Silva R.; Gonçalves C.; Trybulski R.; Rodrigues M.; Noll M.; de Lira C.; Laporta L.; De Conti Teixeira Costa G.
Article.Abstract: This quasi-experimental study examined whether a school volleyball unit based on the Step-Game-Approach model combined with explicit life skills teaching (SGA + LS) was associated with changes in technical-tactical performance, life skills, motivation, and perception of success. Eighty-eight students aged 10–12 years participated in a quasi-experimental repeated-measures design with three groups: SGA + LS, direct instruction, and control. The intervention comprised 18 Physical Education classes. Outcomes were assessed before and/or after the intervention using IAD-VB, Life Skills Scale for Sport, Behavioral Regulation in Sport Questionnaire, and Perception of Success Questionnaire. Generalized Estimating Equations tested group, time, and group×time effects. Significant group × time interactions that remained significant after false discovery rate correction were observed for goal setting, Wald χ²(2) = 11.875, pFDR=0.009, time management, Wald χ²(2) = 10.203, pFDR=0.014, and communication, Wald χ²(2) = 7.538, pFDR=0.044. All technical-tactical outcomes showed significant adjusted interactions, Wald χ²(2) = 10.764–60.676, pFDR≤0.012, with both volleyball-specific conditions showing improvements across several outcomes. At post-test, SGA + LS showed higher decision-making than control, whereas SGA + LS and direct instruction did not differ significantly after Holm adjustment. For motivational regulation, significant adjusted interactions remained for identified regulation, global intrinsic motivation, goal achievement, stimulating experiences, and knowledge mastery, pFDR≤0.021. No adjusted group × time effect was observed for perceptions of success. Overall, the findings indicate selective rather than uniform associations between SGA + LS and technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational outcomes in school Physical Education.

Article.Title: Prevalence of ocular allergy among children in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Ismail M.; Khalafalla I.; Dirie A.; Alemayehu C.; Zalwango C.; Isse S.; Farah F.; Sheck Z.; Mire A.; Herow A.; Ahmed A.; Abdi F.; Mohamed I.; Jayte M.; Mumin B.; Hakizimana T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ocular allergy ranges from seasonal and perennial allergic conjunctivitis to chronic, potentially sight-threatening vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC). African prevalence studies use heterogeneous terminology and case-ascertainment methods, and their estimates have not previously been synthesized. To synthesise published prevalence estimates of ocular allergy among African children, quantify uncertainty around summary estimates, and describe between-study variation. PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, African Journals Online and African Index Medicus were searched for observational studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Disease-specific terms were supplemented with broader ocular-morbidity terminology, reference-list screening and citation verification to identify studies reporting ocular allergy as a secondary outcome. Eligible studies enrolled African children and provided an extractable numerator and denominator. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using a random-effects restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) model in Stata 17. Heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, diagnostic and setting subgroups, and sensitivity analyses were reported. Fourteen studies from five countries included 18,681 children, of whom 1,911 had ocular allergy, allergic conjunctivitis or VKC/vernal disease. The pooled prevalence was 9.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] 5.4%–15.6%), with extreme heterogeneity (τ2 = 1.23; I2 = 99.19%; Q(13) = 1844.38, p < 0.001) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8%–55.9%. The pooled estimate was 14.5% (95% CI 5.5%–33.0%; k = 6) for allergic conjunctivitis and 6.6% (95% CI 3.8%–11.2%; k = 8) for VKC/vernal disease; the subgroup difference was not statistically significant (Q β (1) = 1.99, p = 0.158). School/community studies yielded 8.9% (95% CI 5.0%–15.4%; k = 13), whereas the single clinic study reported 17.6% (95% CI 15.8%–19.6%). Substituting a narrower VKC case definition gave 8.4% (95% CI 4.9%–14.2%), and leave-one-out estimates ranged from 8.0% to 10.2%. Published studies consistently report ocular allergy among African children, although the available evidence is too heterogeneous to support a reliable continental prevalence estimate. Variation in case definition and ascertainment is a plausible and likely substantial contributor, but could not be quantified formally. The findings support consideration of ocular allergy within school eye-health and primary eye-care programmes while underscoring the need for standardised diagnostic and reporting methods.

Article.Title: Effect of extraction temperature on the fatty acid composition, metabolic profile, and bioactivity-related properties of Lepidium sativum seed oil
Article.Authors: Abdo M.; Elnaggar M.; Elissawy A.; Gad H.; El-Ahmady S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lepidium sativum L. (garden cress) seeds are a valuable source of oil rich in unsaturated fatty acids. This study examined the effect of extraction temperature on the yield, fatty acid composition, metabolic profile, and functional properties of L. sativum seed oil. Fixed oils were obtained by maceration in n-hexane at room temperature (cold-extracted seed oil, CSO) and by Soxhlet extraction in n-hexane at 70 °C (hot-extracted seed oil, HSO). Chemical characterization by GC–MS revealed marked differences between the two oils. α-Linolenic acid was the major fatty acid in CSO (36.04%), whereas oleic acid predominated in HSO (24.73%). The influence of these compositional changes on functional properties was assessed using DPPH radical-scavenging and α-amylase inhibition assays. CSO showed higher antioxidant activity (IC 50 = 138.47 ± 2.87 µg mL −1 ) and stronger α-amylase inhibitory activity (IC 50 = 123.46 ± 2.48 µg mL −1 ) than HSO. The results demonstrate that extraction temperature significantly affects the lipid composition of L. sativum seed oil and is associated with changes in its functional properties.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning based optimal control for wave energy converters: practical implementation and experimental validation
Article.Authors: Subramanian A.; Zou S.; Bosma B.; Lou J.; Beringer C.; Robertson B.; Lomonaco P.
Article.Abstract: Ocean wave energy resources are immense and, if harnessed, can serve as a reliable source to support a significant portion of electricity needs. However, the technology to convert wave power into useful electrical power is still cost-intensive. One significant challenge is inefficient Power Take-Off (PTO) control technologies. To address this challenge, the research team has previously developed a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based optimal control for Wave Energy Converters (WECs) and has shown promising performance in terms of power production and quality (in contrast to state-of-the-art advanced PTO controls). However, the study remains on paper, and the practical performance of the control is unknown. Therefore, in this study, we present the practical implementation and experimental validation of the DRL-based optimal control through wave tank testing, aiming to provide meaningful insights into (1) the challenges and limitations associated with implementing the DRL control in practice; and (2) the real-world power production performance (in contrast to numerical predictions), which is vital knowledge for the practical viability of DRL control (and, more broadly, other advanced controls). More specifically, the control is demonstrated using the Laboratory Upgrade Point Absorber (LUPA) WEC at Oregon State University and tested under a variety of regular and irregular wave conditions. Important takeaways from the testing results are: (1) The real-time implementation of the DRL control is straightforward with a low computational cost; (2) the robustness of the control under uncertainties and nonlinearities in real-world applications can be improved by introducing significant randomness during training; (3) The power produced in the real world is significantly less than that predicted by the numerical simulations due to various types of losses in the system (e.g., mechanical friction, electromagnetic damping, etc.), and (4) The DRL control is able to achieve good power production compared to practical control.

Article.Title: Knowledge attitudes and practices regarding toothbrush hygiene and disinfection among dental students in a multicenter cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Demircan B.; Çamgöz A.; Çalışkan A.; Selen M.; Aydogdu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate dental students’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding toothbrush contamination and disinfection, and to assess differences according to clinical training level and gender. A total of 1206 dental students (years 1–5) from three dental faculties in Turkey were included. Data were collected through an online questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Chi-square test, independent samples t-test, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) were used for statistical analysis. Of the participants, 767 were preclinical and 439 were clinical students. Mean knowledge, practice, attitude, and total scores were 3.87 ± 0.76, 3.45 ± 1.32, 2.83 ± 0.61, and 10.14 ± 1.86, respectively. Disinfection knowledge was higher in the clinical group ( p = 0.010), whereas disinfection practice was lower ( p = 0.001). The practice rate was significantly higher among students with disinfection knowledge (70.8% vs. 46.2%; p < 0.001) and among those who considered disinfection necessary (57.1% vs. 14.7%; p < 0.001). The most common source of information was social media, and the most frequently reported disinfection method was tap water. Knowledge and positive attitudes do not consistently translate into evidence-based practice among dental students. Although clinical training improves knowledge, it does not independently enhance disinfection behavior. Toothbrush hygiene should therefore be addressed through practice-oriented learning outcomes from the preclinical years.

Article.Title: A comprehensive study on multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis of machine learning models in diabetes detection
Article.Authors: Mumenin N.; Pranto M.; Yousuf M.; Monowar M.; Hamid M.; Alotaibi F.; Alassafi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High discrimination performance is often interpreted as evidence of model reliability in clinical machine learning (ML). However, strong predictive accuracy does not guarantee safe decision behavior. In safety-critical domains such as healthcare, miscalibrated probabilities, ineffective uncertainty estimation, and overconfident errors can lead to harmful decisions despite high area-under-curve metrics. This study presents a comprehensive multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis demonstrating that models with comparable discrimination performance can exhibit substantially different reliability and risk characteristics. We conduct a rigorous benchmarking evaluation across two heterogeneous diabetes risk datasets, a large population-scale BRFSS cohort and a small-sample early-stage clinical dataset. A diverse set of classical, ensemble, and deep tabular models are evaluated under a strict leakage-free cross-validation protocol with dedicated calibration splits. Beyond conventional discrimination metrics (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC), we assess probabilistic calibration (ECE, Brier score, NLL), epistemic uncertainty using a unified bootstrap-based framework, uncertainty–error correlation, selective prediction safety, high-confidence error rates, subgroup fairness across age and sex, and conformal prediction with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees under the standard exchangeability assumption. Our results reveal a consistent accuracy–safety gap that models achieving near-identical PR-AUC display markedly different calibration quality, uncertainty effectiveness, subgroup reliability, and overconfidence behavior. On the early-stage clinical dataset, near-ceiling discrimination performance is observed across models, but due to the limited sample size, these results should be interpreted cautiously, as variability across folds may affect the stability of comparative performance across models. The findings demonstrate that discrimination metrics alone are insufficient to characterize reliable clinical decision-making.
