A comprehensive evaluation incorporating calibration, uncertainty quality, subgroup fairness, and formal coverage guarantees is essential for the trustworthy pre-deployment assessment of machine learning in healthcare. Rather than introducing a new predictive algorithm, this work contributes a unified empirical audit of safety-relevant model behavior, addressing reliability dimensions that are commonly evaluated separately or omitted in conventional diabetes prediction benchmarks.

Article.Title: Using sensor and self-reported data to understand fatigue within the massage therapy profession
Article.Authors: Resnick P.
Article.Abstract: This exploratory study examined the relationship between the massage modalities used, the length of the massage treatment, and the areas of the body massaged on the perceived self-reported effort level and muscular fatigue as well as the ergonomic sensor data for average composite risk score and average fatigue risk score. Participants completed their normal routine of massages while wearing sensors: watch placed on the upper arm to collect physiological data; GoX ® sensor placed on the dominant upper arm and back of the shirt to collect ergonomic data. Participants performed massages in their regular clinic, following their normal treatment plan. Following each session, a survey was completed about the massage treatment, including areas massaged, techniques used and self-reported effort and muscle fatigue. Mean self-reported effort level was 10.71± 2.40, light level on the Borg Scale. Mean self-reported muscular fatigue level was 2.69 ± 0.75, light activity on the RPE scale. Length of time of the massage session was not a strong indicator of subjective or objective measures. No one technique provided an increased risk of fatigue. This exploratory study gave a snapshot into fatigue and risks for work-related musculoskeletal disorders in massage therapists while practicing in their normal clinical setting.

Article.Title: HIFN-Mamba: hybrid information flow networks with selective state-space sequence modeling for intrusion detection in the Internet of Medical Things
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Almekhlafi M.; Shakah G.; Al-walidi N.; Fathi I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The exponential growth of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) — a multi-billion-device infrastructure of clinically critical sensors, monitors, and connected medical equipment — has dramatically expanded the attack surface for ransomware, lateral-movement, and protocol-specific exploits against healthcare networks. Existing deep-learning intrusion detection systems (IDSs) for this domain suffer from three coupled limitations: fixed information-bottleneck hyperparameters that cannot adapt to heterogeneous protocol distributions, dependence on costly post-hoc explainability methods (SHAP, LIME) that violate sub-millisecond clinical latency budgets, and quadratic-cost attention mechanisms that are infeasible for edge deployment. This paper proposes HIFN-Mamba, a hybrid architecture that couples a two-layer Hybrid Information Flow Network (HIFN) trunk with a stack of selective state-space (Mamba/S6) sequence blocks. Each HIFN layer learns four information-theoretic regulators end-to-end: a static gate vector providing intrinsic sample-invariant feature interpretability, a magnitude scaling factor preventing latent collapse, an information retention coefficient replacing the fixed beta of the Variational Information Bottleneck, and an entropy budget enforcing a hinge constraint on latent differential entropy. We prove that HIFN strictly generalises VIB and that all four regulators remain bounded for any finite training dynamics. Empirical evaluation across the IoMT-focused CICIoMT2024 dataset and two cross-domain benchmarks (UNSW-NB15, CICIDS-2017) in six experimental settings yields 99.999% accuracy with zero false alarms on CICIoMT2024 binary, 99.995% accuracy and 0.9999 macro-F1 on CICIoMT2024 19-class, and sub-millisecond inference latency (0.0129–0.0170 ms/sample) on all six experiments. The static gates provide global feature rankings at zero inference cost, eliminating the exponential complexity of post-hoc SHAP. To our knowledge, HIFN-Mamba is the first IoMT IDS to combine learned information-theoretic regularisation with linear-time selective state-space modelling and to report verifiable sub-millisecond throughput on a nineteen-class IoMT benchmark.

Article.Title: Trajectories of body roundness index and risk of incident hyperuricemia in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: evidence from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study
Article.Authors: Zou C.; Huang L.; He L.
Article.Abstract: The body roundness index (BRI) is an emerging anthropometric indicator of abdominal obesity. However, the longitudinal association between BRI trajectories and the risk of hyperuricemia remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between long-term BRI trajectories and incident hyperuricemia among middle-aged and older Chinese adults. This prospective cohort study included 4565 participants aged ≥ 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) who were free of hyperuricemia at baseline. Group-based trajectory modeling was used to identify distinct BRI trajectories across the 2011, 2013, and 2015 waves. Multivariable logistic regression models were applied to estimate odds ratios for hyperuricemia assessed at the 2015 follow-up, with Model 2 (adjusting for demographic and lifestyle factors) designated as the primary model. Four distinct BRI trajectories were identified: low (19.2%), moderate-low (35.9%), moderate-high (28.8%), and high (16.1%). At the 2015 assessment, 458 participants (10.03%) were identified with hyperuricemia. In the primary model, participants in the moderate-low, moderate-high, and high trajectory groups had significantly higher odds of hyperuricemia compared with the low group, with odds ratios (ORs) of 1.92 (95% CI 1.35–2.73), 3.04 (95% CI 2.13–4.35), and 4.80 (95% CI 3.26–7.05), respectively (P for trend < 0.001). These associations persisted for the moderate-high and high groups after additional adjustment for baseline BRI and serum uric acid (ORs 1.79 and 2.35, respectively). Extended adjustment models incorporating additional clinical and laboratory covariates yielded consistent results. Higher long-term BRI trajectories were associated with greater odds of hyperuricemia among middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and this association persisted after additional adjustment for baseline BRI and serum uric acid. These findings support the relevance of longitudinal adiposity patterns to hyperuricemia risk, while the exposure–outcome overlap limits causal and prospective interpretation.

Article.Title: m6A-modified mRNA–LNP system enables in vivo CAR expression and is associated with antitumor immune responses
Article.Authors: Meng S.; Hara T.; Sato T.; Tatekawa S.; Yanagida K.; Nikaido K.; Saito Y.; Arao Y.; Motooka D.; Ofusa K.; Ogawa K.; Nishiyama N.; Mori M.; Eguchi H.; Satoh T.; Miura Y.; Ishii H.
Article.Abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have emerged as a versatile modality for transient gene delivery, but strategies to incorporate epitranscriptomic regulation into synthetic mRNA design remain limited. Among RNA modifications, N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) is a major regulator of mRNA stability, translation, and cellular signaling through coordinated actions of methyltransferases, binding proteins, and demethylases. However, the use of engineered m 6 A-modified mRNAs to modulate immune responses in vivo has been relatively unexplored. Here, we developed a tunable lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system using m 6 A-modified mRNAs encoding chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP). Administration of these mRNA–LNPs was associated with altered RNA methylation states in immune cells and elicited antitumor immune responses. Transcriptomic analyses indicated activation of immune-related pathways and signatures consistent with immune memory. The formulation design was modular, allowing modification of LNP composition. Substitution with pH-responsive polybetaines maintained therapeutic activity without substantial loss of efficacy. In addition, replacing the FAP-targeting sequence with cancer stem cell (CSC) markers, including EpCAM, LGR5, and CD133, preserved antitumor responses. Targeting CSC-associated antigens was also accompanied by suppression of tumor-intrinsic SPP1 signaling pathways. Together, these results suggest that mRNA–LNPs provide a flexible and programmable system for CAR targeting and immunotherapy, influencing epitranscriptomic states while enabling modulation of nanoparticle composition and antigen specificity. This work establishes a framework for the development of programmable mRNA-based cancer immunotherapies through synthetic RNA engineering and controlled m 6 A modification of exogenous mRNA.

Article.Title: A sliding mode control approach to suppress power quality challenges in single-phase variable frequency drives within the constant power region
Article.Authors: Maleki M.; Tafti M.; Motamedi M.; Vahidi B.; Montazeri S.; Hosseinian S.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a variable frequency drive (VFD) for single-phase induction motors that features power factor correction (PFC) and addresses power quality issues, including current and voltage harmonic distortion on the grid and load sides. The proposed VFD topology employs a two-stage architecture: a front-end totem-pole PFC stage for controlling the DC-link voltage and a subsequent neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter to supply the induction motor with the commanded output voltage waveform. To ensure robust performance, the front-end converter employs an adaptive gain super-twisting sliding mode control (SSMC). This approach concurrently achieves the unity power factor and minimizes the total harmonic distortion (THD) in the grid current and voltage. The NPC stage switches are governed/driven by a controller based on the unipolar selective harmonic elimination (SHE) technique to satisfy the load-side voltage quality specifications. Simulation results confirm that the designed VFD complies with relevant power quality standards across the entire constant power operating region of a typical single-phase induction motor. Furthermore, a comprehensive report covers the designed VFD performance across various frequencies of the output voltage. Results verify the superiority of the SSMC hysteresis current control over the PI peak current control within the power quality characteristics.

Article.Title: Performance assessment and parametric analysis of CFST columns with various concrete infills
Article.Authors: Zuhairudeen M.; James J.; Pandulu G.; Jayaseelan R.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the structural behaviour of Concrete Filled Steel Tubular (CFST) columns under axial compression using two infill materials: Lightweight Concrete (LWC) and Hybrid Fibre-Reinforced Concrete (HFRC). In Phase I, the LWC mix was developed by partially replacing the fine aggregate with perlite and the coarse aggregate with pumice stone, and incorporating PVA fibres. In Phase II, the HFRC mix was developed by partial replacement of cement by flyash with the addition of Polypropylene (PP) and Coconut Fibre (CF). In Phase III, CFST column specimens filled with both LWC(CFSTLWC) and HFRC(CFSTHFRC) were experimentally tested to examine load deformation response, ductility, energy absorption, and failure characteristics. CFST columns filled with LWC demonstrated reduced self-weight while maintaining satisfactory load-carrying capacity and deformation behaviour, and CFSTHFRC columns exhibited a significant improvement in structural performance, achieving approximately 39% higher axial load capacity compared to a CFST column filled with Control Concrete (CFSTCC). A parametric study was conducted by varying diameter-to-thickness (D/t) and length-to-diameter (L/D) ratios to assess their influence on axial performance using finite element analysis. The findings highlight that an increase in (D/t) reduces the confinement and thereby reduces the load-carrying capacity, and increasing (L/D) results in an increase in buckling behaviour, which reduces the load-carrying capacity. Axial load carrying capacity of CFST columns compared with existing codal provisions. A mathematical model was also developed with L/D and (D/t), which predicted the ultimate strength ratio of CFST columns filled with LWC and HFRC, having a coefficient of correlation of 0.934 and 0.948 and validated with the experimental results existing in the literature.

Article.Title: Linking environmental variability to diatom assemblages in seasonal wetlands
Article.Authors: Madonsela N.; Mangadze T.; Mpopetsi P.; Munyai L.; Dondofema F.; Dalu T.
Article.Abstract: Seasonal wetlands undergo recurrent inundation and contraction, creating strong hydrochemical variability and non–independent observations within pans. We tested whether this variability translated into diatom differentiation in five pans within each of two South African Ramsar wetland systems, Makuleke and Nylsvley, during cool–dry and hot–wet seasons. Two field replicates per pan–season yielded 40 diatom samples and 40 environmental records. Environmental replicates were averaged within pan–season; diatom relative abundances were calculated within each replicate and averaged with equal weight. Fifty–three taxa were detected. Makuleke had higher temperature, pH, total dissolved solids, conductivity and several major ions than Nylsvley, whereas temperature, total dissolved solids, conductivity, nitrate and sodium differed between seasons. Hierarchical permutation tests detected no community difference between systems or system by season interaction, and the seasonal pattern approached but did not reach the 0.05 threshold. Rarefied diversity and the six variable canonical correspondence model were also non–significant. Thus, hydrochemical separation did not yield supported assemblage separation at the sampled scale. These results caution against inferring ecological status from nested samples and identify repeated, substrate consistent monitoring as necessary for diatom–based assessment of seasonal wetlands.

Article.Title: TMEM174 deficiency reduces longevity by promoting phosphate-driven vascular calcification
Article.Authors: Miranda J.; Blaine J.; Miyazaki M.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulation of phosphate homeostasis contributes to reduced longevity and vascular complications in chronic kidney disease and aging. This study investigates the role of TMEM174, a proximal tubule-specific protein, in regulating the phosphate co-transporter NPT2A and its subsequent impact on lifespan and vascular health. TMEM174 knockout (KO) mice (C57BL6/J and DBA/2 J) were fed diets with varying phosphate concentrations (0.6% vs. 1.2%). In OKP cells, TIRF and FRET microscopy, alongside immunoprecipitation, were used to identify the TMEM174 protein regions essential for NPT2A binding and endocytosis. TMEM174 KO mice exhibited significantly shorter lifespans than wild-type controls. High phosphate diets exacerbated vascular calcification, stiffness, and mortality, while low phosphate diets rescued these phenotypes. In vitro, TMEM174 siRNA blocked PTH-induced NPT2A endocytosis, increasing its apical membrane retention. FRET and biochemical assays revealed that the C-terminal region of TMEM174 is essential for its association with NPT2A. While intact TMEM174 and N-terminal mutants (TMEM174ΔN) facilitated NPT2A degradation, C-terminal deletions (TMEM174ΔC) failed to associate with or degrade NPT2A. TMEM174 is a critical regulator of phosphate homeostasis and longevity. The C-terminal region of TMEM174 is specifically required for NPT2A endocytosis and degradation, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for managing phosphate-related vascular complications.

Article.Title: Correction: A miniature, subterranean, blind cobitid loach, Gitchak nakana, new genus and species, is the first groundwater-dwelling fish from Northeast India
Article.Authors: Britz R.; Marak W.; Velentina K.; Lokeshwor Y.; Raghavan R.; Pinion A.; Rüber L.
Article.Abstract: “Since scientific description of the Olm, Proteus anguinus , in the 18th century 3 , subterranean animals with their often-otherworldly appearance have peaked the interest of researchers and the public alike.”

Article.Title: Correction: Genomic insights into the persistence of Nubian giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis camelopardalis) in conflict-affected South Sudan
Article.Authors: van Giessen S.; Prochotta D.; de Jong M.; Harvey R.; Claase M.; Fennessy J.; Janke A.
Article.Abstract: In the original version of this Article, Fig. 3 B did not display correctly. The original Fig. 3 and accompanying legend appear below. Fig. 3 Full size image Admixture and geneflow indicate past connectivity between Nubian and Kordofan populations and between Nubian and West African populations. ( A ) Admixture plot for K = 2–6. Each vertical bar represents one individual from the five (Sub)species; Kordofan, Masai, Nubian, reticulated, and West African giraffe. The colours represent the division of the individuals into a specified number of genetic clusters (K). Individuals with mixed coloured bars indicate admixture, or artifacts of admixture when too few genetic clusters are imposed on the data. At the optimal K = 5 the Kordofan, Masai, reticulated, and West African giraffe show little admixture. Within the Nubian giraffe the individuals from Ethiopia, South Sudan and Uganda show admixed ancestry with the Kordofan giraffe. ( B ) Heatmap of estimated gene flow from Dsuite tests between major clades found in the dataset (Fig. 1B,C), using the Masai giraffe as an outgroup. The clades seen in the heatmap are Reticulated (ISC, SAR) (N = 4), West African (WA) (N = 9), Kordofan (ZNP, GNP, SNR) (N = 10), Nubian in South Sudan and Ethiopia (BAD, BOM, ETH) (N = 20), Nubian in Uganda (MF, KDV) (N = 4), and Nubian in Kenya (RUM, MNR, SOY, KWR, LNN) (N = 30). The darker coloured cells indicate higher levels of gene flow (f b ) between populations, the colours are assigned according to subspecies as in Fig. 1A.

Article.Title: Coordinated integration of renewables, STATCOMs, and V2G for hosting capacity improvement under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Ali Z.; Aleem S.; Aldawsari F.; Zenhom Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although incorporating renewable energy sources (RESs) into electric distribution networks (EDNs) offers significant sustainability and environmental benefits, improper management of RESs may threaten the technical performance of the network. To assess the safe integration of distributed generation (DG), the hosting capacity (HC) concept is employed. Plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), through coordinated charging and discharging, can further support RES integration. Moreover, reactive power compensation using devices such as static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) remains a key strategy for mitigating voltage violations under high RES penetration. This article proposes a novel stochastic multi-objective optimization framework, from the distribution system operator’s (DSO) perspective, to optimally coordinate the dispatch of PEV aggregators, wind-based DGs, PV-based DGs, and STATCOMs. The model accounts for uncertainties in load demand, solar radiation, wind speed, and PEV demand using stochastic programming. The objectives are to maximize HC while minimizing voltage deviation and power losses. The feasibility of employing a recent optimization technique, Tianji’s Horse Racing Optimization (THRO), to solve the proposed multi-objective problem is demonstrated and benchmarked against three other optimization algorithms on both the IEEE 33-bus system and a real 59-bus network in Cairo, Egypt. Results of IEEE 33-bus EDN show that optimal coordination of V2G-enabled PEVs and reactive power support via STATCOMs can enhance HC by 37%, reduce voltage deviation by 74%, and decrease power losses by 15%. In addition, the Cairo 59-bus EDN system exhibited similar trends, achieving an approximately 83% increase in hosting capacity, accompanied by nearly a 39% reduction in voltage deviation.

Article.Title: A train-once, evaluate-twice protocol for cross-lingual depression detection with large language models
Article.Authors: Abdalla A.; Parvez M.; Alam T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depression affects more than 280 million people worldwide, and social media text provides a large-scale resource for automated mental health assessment. Large language model (LLM)-based approaches have shown promising performance for social media-based depression detection; however, their cross-lingual robustness for underrepresented languages such as Arabic remains insufficiently explored. We proposed the “train once, evaluate twice” protocol to evaluate the cross-lingual robustness of eight LLMs for detecting depression in both English and Arabic. For six open-source LLMs, we used QLoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to adapt them; for two closed-source GPT models, we fine-tuned them with the OpenAI supervised fine-tuning (SFT) API. To provide context for understanding transfer performance, we also evaluated a translation-based pipeline (MarianMT + XLM-R) and a bilingual fine-tuning ablation using data-mixing techniques. The models performed nearly at ceiling in their monolingual evaluation (English), with the best Macro-F1 score of 0.990 in GPT-4.1 Mini, and moderately well in Arabic (best Macro-F1 of 0.800 in Qwen2). Cross-lingual evaluation revealed significant directional asymmetry. The strongest transfer performance was observed in AR → EN (Macro-F1 = 0.793 for GPT-4.1 mini), whereas EN → AR remained considerably more challenging (best Macro-F1 = 0.638 for GPT-3.5 Turbo). The MarianMT + XLM-R translate-then-classify baseline achieved consistently lower cross-lingual performance than the fine-tuned generative LLMs evaluated in this study. The results of a bilingual fine-tuning ablation experiment conducted using Qwen2-7B-Instruct suggested that bilingual data mixing is sufficient to preserve English performance at near-ceiling levels. However, bilingual data mixing did not improve Arabic performance relative to monolingual Arabic fine-tuning. Thus, for this family of models, simple bilingual exposure appears insufficient to address the cross-lingual performance gap. Error analysis showed that EN→AR transfer predominantly increased false negatives, whereas AR → EN transfer exhibited more balanced precision–recall degradation profiles. Notably, the two Arabic-specialized models evaluated did not consistently outperform the strongest general-purpose multilingual models under cross-lingual transfer settings. PEFT produced compact adapters with low local inference latency, whereas API-based GPT inference exhibited substantially higher end-to-end latency. These findings support the notion that standard single-language fine-tuning does not afford much robustness when models are deployed across languages, especially in the EN → AR direction; thus, providing impetus for further research into new methods for adapting LLMs across multiple languages. Trial registration: Not applicable.

Article.Title: Assessment of the appropriateness of the selection for radiotherapy intensity from a quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30) perspective in older patients with cancer
Article.Authors: Murofushi K.; Kuribayashi S.; Ohnishi K.; Hayakawa S.; Tsuchida K.; Inoue Y.; Ohkawa A.; Ishida T.; Machitori Y.; Murakami M.; Takizawa D.; Saito M.
Article.Abstract: We previously evaluated the predictive factors for reduced radiotherapy intensity based on radiation oncologist experience. In this study, we evaluated the appropriateness of the treatment intensity selection based on radiation and medical oncologists’ experience from a patient-reported outcome (PRO) perspective. We prospectively enrolled patients with non-metastatic cancer (≥ 70 years) between November 2020 and February 2022. Reduced treatment intensity implied changes to the irradiation field, radiotherapy schedule, and/or concurrent chemotherapy from the standard based on primary tumor guidelines. PRO was assessed using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality of Life Questionnaire scores before radiotherapy and at 3–5 and 8–16 weeks post-radiotherapy. A clinically relevant change was defined as a difference of ≥ 10 points. Overall, 294 of 317 enrolled patients were eligible for analysis. Treatment policies were modified in 72 patients (24%), and 43 patients (15%) experienced grade ≥ 3 acute adverse events. None of the observed differences between before and after radiotherapy were ≥ 10 points in the standard and reduced-intensity treatment groups. Significant differences were observed in physical and role functioning, and dyspnea (p = 0.015, 0.003, and 0.010, respectively) in patients with grade ≥ 3 adverse events, which deteriorated by ≥ 10 points. Our results indicate that the treatment intensity was appropriately selected from a PRO perspective. Nevertheless, it is necessary to pay attention to the deterioration of quality of life after radiotherapy for older patients with grade ≥ 3 adverse events. This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) under the number UMIN 000042473. We assessed the appropriateness of treatment intensity selection in cancer patients aged ≥ 70 years using PRO. Of 294 patients, 24% received reduced-intensity treatment and 15% experienced grade ≥ 3 adverse events. Quality of life changes were minimal, indicating appropriate treatment selection; however, a significant decline occurred in severe adverse events.

Article.Title: Testosterone exposure shifts female baseline phenotypes toward a male-associated tear-nerve-epithelial state in mice
Article.Authors: Feret N.; Megido A.; Pernot S.; Girard M.; Decoudu M.; Kindermans J.; Fichter L.; Llorens S.; Attina A.; Vialaret J.; David A.; Daien V.; Loulier K.; Hirtz C.; Michon F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sex and hormonal status are clinically relevant determinants of ocular-surface physiology, but whether adult androgen exposure shifts multiple components of the ocular surface in parallel remains poorly defined. We compared vehicle-treated female mice with testosterone-treated females and used intact males as a physiological reference rather than as a procedure-matched control. Modified-nucleoside profiling, tear proteomics, corneal and trigeminal ganglion RNA sequencing, corneal flat-mount nerve volumetry, von Frey aesthesiometry, phospho-histone H3 labelling and single-endpoint Krt14-CreERT; CAG-Cytbow lineage tracing were combined to examine the tear-nerve-epithelial system at baseline. Tear collection rate was unchanged, whereas total tear protein concentration and proteomic composition differed between vehicle-treated and testosterone-treated females and shifted toward the intact male reference; 1,052 of 3,125 identified tear proteins were modulated in at least one pairwise comparison. Testosterone-treated females also showed lower central βIII-tubulin-positive nerve-fibre volume and mechanical sensitivity and fewer mitotic epithelial cells than vehicle-treated females, while lineage-labelled epithelial foci showed a qualitatively concordant distribution. Corneal transcriptional responses were substantially broader than those in the trigeminal ganglion. These findings show that adult testosterone exposure is associated with coordinated plasticity across several baseline ocular-surface phenotypes. They establish endocrine status as an important biological variable for experimental design while leaving its consequences for injury and disease to future functional studies.

Article.Title: Assessment of antibacterial and antioxidant potentials of Aspergillus fumigatus crude extract, the isolated endophyte from Centella asiatica (L.) urban supported by molecular docking
Article.Authors: Rahman A.; Bhuiyan A.; Hossain M.; Uddin M.; Islam M.; Aziz I.; Alkubaisi N.; Giesy J.; Aboul-Soud M.; Haque S.
Article.Abstract: The growing burden of infectious and chronic diseases associated with bacterial infections and oxidative stress highlights the need for novel antibacterial and antioxidant agents. Fungal endophytes are promising sources of bioactive metabolites with pharmaceutical potential. This study focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of endophytic fungus extract obtained from the leaves of Centella asiatica (L.) Urban. The isolated fungus was identified as Aspergillus fumigatus through ITS-rDNA sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. GC–MS profiling of its ethyl acetate extract (CAL 3) revealed 37 volatile compounds, including Pyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrazine-1,4-dione, hexahydro-3-(2-methylpropyl)-, 9-Octadecenamide, and 1-Nonadecene. The extract showed moderate antibacterial activity at 500 µg/disc, with inhibition zones of 15.75 ± 0.14 and 16.61 ± 0.19 mm against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli , respectively. MIC values were 5 mg/mL against E. coli and P. aeruginosa and 10 mg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis . The extract exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities, with IC₅₀ values of 44.56 ± 0.50 and 48.77 ± 0.22 µg/mL, respectively. Molecular docking indicated favorable binding of selected metabolites to DHFR and MPO. These findings support further investigation of C. asiatica -associated endophytic fungi as potential sources of bioactive metabolites for future drug discovery.

Article.Title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention introduction is associated with sustained reductions in childhood malaria burden in northern Ghana
Article.Authors: Anafo A.; Gmayinaam V.; Aheto J.; Afrane Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five in northern Ghana. Transmission in this setting is intense and highly seasonal, with most cases occurring during the rainy season from June to September. Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), the monthly administration of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine to children aged 3–59 months during peak transmission, was introduced across the Northern Region in June 2019. However, its population-level association with childhood malaria outcomes, after accounting for background trends and climatic variability, had not been comprehensively assessed. Here we combined 10 years of monthly health facility data from 2015 to 2024 with four rounds of nationally representative household survey data from 2014 to 2022. We assessed the association between SMC implementation and childhood malaria outcomes using seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average models with exogenous covariates, incorporating monthly rainfall and temperature, alongside a Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual framework. Compared with the projected counterfactual trajectory, malaria death rates, admission rates, and incidence rates in the post-SMC period were estimated to be 80.3%, 23.0%, and 16.1% lower, respectively. However, because of uncertainty around the counterfactual estimates, these results should be interpreted as suggestive of a possible programme-level contribution rather than definitive evidence of statistically confirmed effects. At the individual level, children surveyed in the post-SMC period had significantly lower odds of malaria infection after adjustment for survey month (adjusted odds ratio = 0.595; 95% confidence interval: 0.470–0.751), with consistently lower predicted malaria probabilities observed across all child age groups. Although insecticide-treated net coverage declined during the post-SMC period, malaria burden continued to decrease across both routine facility and household survey data sources. These findings are consistent with an association between SMC implementation and reduced malaria burden among children under five in a high-transmission Sahelian setting and highlight the importance of maintaining high SMC coverage as part of an integrated malaria control strategy.

Article.Title: Seasonal and annual variation in Borrelia garinii infectiousness in a wild bird
Article.Authors: Zarka J.; Heylen D.; Fonville M.; Matthysen E.; Sprong H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Successful reproduction of zoonotic diseases depends, among others, on the reservoir host’s ability to maintain and transmit the infection. Temporal variation in host infectiousness, i.e. the capacity of the host to infect susceptible individuals, and contact rates with naïve hosts strongly influence transmission dynamics. The vector-borne Borrelia garinii , causative agent of Lyme neuroborreliosis, is maintained in the environment through transmission between birds and Ixodes ricinus ticks. Although temporal variation in avian infectiousness affects B. garinii spread, it remains poorly understood in wild populations. Here, we assessed year-round variation in infectiousness of wild great tits ( Parus major ) using xenodiagnosis. Over seven consecutive seasons (from the 2022 until the 2024 breeding season), we conducted 420 xenodiagnoses. Our results showed a higher prevalence of infectious individuals during breeding seasons, particularly in 2023 (49% of birds were infectious). This peak was followed by a sharp decline in autumn and winter, which could suggest transient infectiousness. Few birds were repeatedly infectious, and most birds transmitted a single B. garinii haplotype, further indicating that most infections were transient. Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for species-specific temporal variation in host infectiousness, in addition to spatiotemporal host-vector overlap, when estimating avian contributions to Lyme neuroborreliosis transmission.

Article.Title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles attenuate inflammation-associated cognitive impairment and hippocampal microglial-synaptic remodeling
Article.Authors: Ayyubova G.; Gasimov E.; Rzayev F.; Mehraliyeva G.; Sadigi I.; Guliyeva N.; Ismayilova S.; Ayyubova N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microglia are central regulators of synaptic structure and cognitive function, yet under chronic inflammatory conditions, they can adopt stress-associated states associated with neuronal and synaptic vulnerability. Although inflammation-driven cognitive decline is often attributed to synapse loss, increasing evidence suggests that synaptic remodeling may precede or occur independently of overt synapse elimination. In this study, we combined behavioral testing, immunofluorescence, microglial morphometric analysis, and quantitative transmission electron microscopy to define structural correlates of inflammation-induced cognitive dysfunction and to evaluate the therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs). Chronic systemic inflammation was induced in mice by repeated lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration, followed by intravenous MSC-EV treatment during the inflammatory phase. LPS exposure impaired working memory, object recognition, and spatial recognition memory without affecting locomotor activity. Immunofluorescence revealed increased CD68 immunoreactivity detected with the ED1 antibody clone within IBA1-positive cells, together with increased microglial soma area, reduced arborization area, and an elevated morphological index, consistent with microglial inflammatory remodeling and enhanced endolysosomal/phagolysosomal engagement. Ultrastructural analysis further demonstrated increased phagolysosomal inclusion burden, increased blood vessel-associated microglial profiles, elevated dark microglia-like profiles, reduced neuronal soma profile area, decreased SYN- and PSD95-positive structures, and coordinated pre- and postsynaptic alterations. Total excitatory synapse density showed only a non-significant numerical reduction, indicating synaptic vulnerability characterized primarily by structural remodeling rather than definitive synapse loss. MSC-EV treatment was associated with attenuated microglial inflammatory and morphometric alterations, reduced phagolysosomal and dark microglia-like ultrastructural features, partially restored synaptic marker-positive structures and synaptic ultrastructure, and improved hippocampus-dependent cognition, particularly spatial recognition memory. Together, these findings suggest that MSC-EVs are associated with partial normalization of inflammation-induced microglial, neuronal, and synaptic alterations.

Article.Title: Quantum-compatible error correction using a Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse transformer in discrete-variable quantum key distribution
Article.Authors: Raoof S.; Tejasree G.; Satheesha T.; Chhetri Y.; Eduru S.; M. P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation with information-theoretic security guaranteed by the principles of quantum mechanics. However, achieving high reconciliation efficiency, high throughput, and low frame error rates under noisy channel conditions remains a significant challenge for practical and cost-effective Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (DV-QKD) systems. To address this issue, this research proposes a Quantum-based Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse Transformer (Q-BDPT) framework for quantum-compatible error correction during the reconciliation stage of DV-QKD. Initially, a system model for DV-QKD is presented. Subsequently, an adaptive error-correction framework comprising Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder modules is developed. Unlike physical quantum error-correction codes that operate directly on qubits, the proposed framework processes measurement-derived error features, syndrome information, and channel-dependent error characteristics obtained after quantum-state transmission and measurement. The Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder are constructed using Q-BDPT with Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) loss. The proposed Q-BDPT integrates Bayesian Adversarial ProbSparse Transformer (BAPT) and Dual-Gated Spatiotemporal Attention Network (DSANet), while harmonic analysis is employed to enhance feature integration and adaptive error modelling. The framework learns probabilistic, spatial, and temporal error dependencies associated with quantum-channel behavior and generates adaptive reconciliation decisions to improve key recovery performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Q-BDPT achieves a minimum Bit Error Rate (BER) of 0.01760, a minimum Logical Error Rate (LER) of 0.00776, and a maximum Secure Key Rate (SKR) of 0.65805, thereby improving reconciliation effectiveness and secure key generation performance in DV-QKD environments.

Article.Title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection is associated with a shift in the human secondary sex ratio at birth
Article.Authors: Ammar O.; Rimmer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human sex ratios at birth are remarkably stable, yet may be sensitive to events during fertilisation and early embryo development. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) bypasses sperm-zona interaction by injecting a selected sperm directly into the oocyte and is increasingly used beyond severe male-factor infertility. We analysed anonymised UK Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority registry data for 2005–2018 to test whether fertilisation method is associated with the secondary sex ratio among singleton live births. The cohort included 164,684 singleton live births after conventional IVF or ICSI with recorded infant sex. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, treatment year, number of embryos transferred, and fresh or frozen embryo transfer. The adjusted proportion of male live births was 52.6% after IVF and 49.2% after ICSI, an absolute difference of 3.4 percentage points (95% CI 2.8–3.9); the adjusted odds ratio for male live birth after ICSI versus IVF was 0.88 (95% CI 0.86–0.89). The association was consistent across single-embryo transfers, fresh and frozen cycles, cycles without recorded male-factor infertility, and analyses excluding preimplantation genetic testing and donor-gamete cycles. These data identify a small association between fertilisation method and the proportion of male singleton live births within this ART cohort. They do not establish that ICSI causes a shift in the secondary sex ratio in the wider population and should not alter individual counselling, but support deeper study of sex-specific selection across fertilisation, embryo culture, transfer, and early survival.

Article.Title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in relation to metabolic profile and dietary antioxidant quality in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
Article.Authors: El-Sehrawy A.; Salah A.; Kandil I.; Yusuf S.; Abohassan M.; Alanazi M.; Kurbaniyazova F.; Almansouri T.; Basunduwah T.; labib S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a common metabolic condition characterized by hepatic steatosis and chronic low-grade inflammation, with oxidative stress playing a pivotal role in its progression. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has been proposed as an accessible marker reflecting systemic inflammatory status. This study aimed to examine the relationship between NLR, metabolic risk factors, body composition indices, and dietary antioxidant quality in adults with NAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 257 adults with ultrasound-confirmed NAFLD were enrolled. Anthropometric parameters and body composition were measured using standardized procedures and bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fasting biochemical markers were assessed via enzymatic colorimetric methods. NLR was calculated from complete blood count data. Dietary intake was evaluated using a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire, and the Dietary Antioxidant Quality Score (DAQS) was derived based on the adequacy of vitamins A, C, and E, selenium, and zinc intake. Comparisons across NLR tertiles were performed using one-way analysis of variance, followed by Tukey’s post hoc test, and multivariable multinomial logistic regression was used to assess associations. Participants in the highest NLR tertile had significantly higher FBS (93.33 ± 11.03 vs. 88.40 ± 9.65 mg/dL), TC (191.81 ± 38.78 vs. 169.58 ± 32.62 mg/dL), and LDL-cholesterol levels (115.26 ± 33.63 vs. 99.11 ± 28.57 mg/dL) compared with those in the lowest tertile (all P < 0.05). Higher NLR levels were significantly associated with lower DAQS values and reduced intake of antioxidant vitamins A and C (p < 0.05). In stratified multinomial logistic regression analyses by physical activity, higher NLR was associated with increased FBS in the low activity group (Third tertile: OR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.03–1.13, P = 0.003) and with higher TC in the high activity group (second tertile: OR: 1.02, 95% CI: 1.00–1.04, P = 0.05; third tertile: OR:1.02, 95% CI: 1.005–1.04, P = 0.016). Elevated NLR is associated with an unfavorable metabolic profile and poorer dietary antioxidant quality among individuals with NAFLD. These findings support the potential role of NLR as a practical inflammatory marker linked to metabolic risk and highlight the relevance of antioxidant-rich dietary patterns in mitigating inflammation in NAFLD.

Article.Title: A cautionary tale on the cost-effectiveness of collaborative AI in real-world medical applications
Article.Authors: Cremonesi F.; Innocenti L.; Goh V.; Ourselin S.; Antonelli M.; Lorenzi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) has gained wide popularity as a collaborative learning paradigm allowing collaborative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in sensitive healthcare applications. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of FL presents technical and organizational challenges, as it generally requires complex communication infrastructures. In this context, consensus-based learning (CBL) may represent a promising alternative for collaborative learning, allowing the combination of local knowledge into a federated decision system, while potentially reducing deployment overhead. Nevertheless, a comprehensive assessment of the viability of consensus-based learning as a cost-effective and sustainable alternative to federated learning has not yet been conducted. In this work we propose an extensive benchmark of the accuracy, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability of a panel of FL and CBL methods in a wide range of collaborative medical data analysis scenarios. The benchmark includes 7 different medical datasets, encompassing 3 machine learning tasks, 8 different data modalities, and multi-centric settings involving 3 to 23 clients. Our results reveal that CBL is a cost-effective and more sustainable alternative to FL. When compared across the panel of medical datasets in the considered benchmark, CBL methods provide equivalent accuracy to the one achieved by FL. Nonetheless, CBL significantly reduces training time and communication cost (resp. 15 fold and 131 fold decrease) ( p -value< 0.05). This study opens a novel perspective on the deployment of collaborative AI in real-world applications, whereas the adoption of cost-effective methods is instrumental to achieve sustainability and democratization of AI by alleviating the need for extensive computational resources.

Article.Title: Text–relation joint modeling improves the robustness of Chinese social bot detection against paraphrasing attacks
Article.Authors: Guo S.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Generative language models have made paraphrasing a low-cost and practical evasion strategy against social bot detectors, especially on Chinese platforms where textual content is a major detection signal. We introduce TRJD-AT, a text-relation joint framework that combines a Chinese MacBERT encoder, a two-layer heterogeneous graph attention network over user-post publication and user-user follow relations, a lightweight gated fusion module, and Fast Gradient Method (FGM) training on input embeddings. We further define a three-tier paraphrasing protocol - lexical substitution, sentence-level rewriting, and benign-token insertion - with explicit attack budgets and automatic semantic-preservation constraints, while separating post-level attack construction from account-level evaluation. On the Chinese Weibo Social Bot dataset, TRJD-AT obtains a clean macro-F1 of 0.891. Under the default Tier 2 condition (semantic-similarity threshold 0.80), it obtains a macro-F1 of 0.835, corresponding to a 5.6-percentage-point reduction, whereas the MacBERT + MLP text-only baseline obtains 0.733, corresponding to a 13.4-point reduction. Clean performance and adversarial degradation are reported as distinct quantities. Ablation results indicate that the observed robustness is mainly associated with relational modeling; FGM improves clean performance in this setting but does not provide an independent gain in attacked macro-F1. A density-based analysis further identifies reduced relational benefit for accounts with sparse interaction histories.

Article.Title: Ga-induced defect engineering and charge transport mechanisms in ZnO ceramic materials
Article.Authors: Chouiref L.; Benamara M.; Hammami I.; Moussa S.; Alzahrani A.; Valente M.; El Mir L.; Graça M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ga-doped ZnO (G3ZO) ceramics were successfully synthesized and their structural, electrical, dielectric, impedance, and relaxation properties were investigated to understand the effect of Ga incorporation on charge transport. X-ray diffraction confirmed the hexagonal wurtzite structure without detectable secondary phases. Williamson–Hall analysis showed a decrease in crystallite size from 51.7 nm for pure ZnO to 29.4 nm for G3ZO, while FE-SEM revealed agglomerated nanoparticles with an average particle size of about 38 nm. Electrical conductivity increased with frequency and temperature and followed Jonscher’s universal power law. The activation energy was 0.132 ± 0.007 eV, indicating thermally activated, defect-assisted charge transport. Impedance analysis showed a decrease in resistance with increasing temperature, while dielectric measurements revealed strong low-frequency dispersion associated with interfacial polarization. Electric modulus analysis indicated non-Debye relaxation behavior. Compared with pure ZnO, G3ZO exhibited improved electrical conductivity, dielectric response, and polarization, which can be related to Ga-related donor defects and increased charge-carrier concentration. These results demonstrate that Ga incorporation can effectively modify the structural and electrical properties of ZnO ceramics and may be useful for electronic and dielectric applications.

Article.Title: In silico design and immunogenic assessment of a strain-specific peptide in Brucella melitensis 16 M for DIVA diagnosis
Article.Authors: Procopio A.; Soggiu A.; Hussein H.; Bonizzi L.; Zecconi A.; Guzzi P.; Urbani A.; Roncada P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brucella melitensis is a facultative intracellular pathogen that causes brucellosis in small ruminants and humans. Strain-specific molecular targets are needed to improve vaccination monitoring and epidemiological surveillance, particularly for DIVA strategies aimed at distinguishing naturally infected animals from Rev.1-vaccinated animals. Here, we performed a computational, hypothesis-generating characterization of the RD3-associated genomic interval 824,171 − 824,131 on chromosome II of the virulent reference strain Brucella melitensis 16 M. Comparative sequence analyses were conducted across a selected DIVA-oriented panel of 56 publicly available bacterial chromosomal/genomic sequence records, including Brucella melitensis biovar 3 strain Ether chromosome II (NZ_CP007761.1), and the 16 M/Rev.1 locus was further inspected using the NC_003318.1 and CP024716.1 chromosome II FASTA sequences. The 16 M interval contains a 39-nt ATG-initiated coding segment on the negative strand that translates into the 13-amino-acid peptide MDHRSSGRGYDEK, whereas the homologous Rev.1 locus lacks the corresponding 40-bp ATG-containing segment. IEDB Next-Generation tools prioritized three MHC class I candidates, HRSSGRGY, MDHRSSGRGY, and DHRSSGRGY, while cross-species mapping using bovine MHC alleles as exploratory proxies identified Ovar-N*14:01 as the closest ovine sequence comparator. VaxiJen and BepiPred analyses provided complementary antigenicity and linear-epitope support, and host-proteome similarity screening against Ovis aries and Capra hircus did not identify full-length host matches or exact 8-13-mer host-protein matches. These findings support MDHRSSGRGYDEK as a panel-level, 16 M/RD3-positive-context computational candidate for DIVA-oriented assay development, but not as a validated diagnostic marker. No experimental evidence is currently available for peptide expression, antigen processing, MHC presentation, antibody reactivity, ELISA performance, PCR/qPCR/ddPCR diagnostic accuracy, or biological absence of cross-reactivity; therefore, no diagnostic performance or broad field applicability is claimed here.

Article.Title: Effects of speed and lane on lateral offset of vehicles in desert expressway
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Zheng C.; Xu J.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Desert expressways feature straight alignments, monotonous roadside environments and limited external disturbances, which lead to distinctive speed selection and lateral control behaviors of drivers. This study aims to explore the coupling mechanism between vehicle speed and lateral trajectory on desert expressways. Taking passenger cars on straight segments of desert expressways as the research objects, this study obtained high-precision vehicle trajectory data through unmanned aerial vehicle field measurement. The speed distribution and lateral offset rules under different speed intervals and lane positions were analyzed. Correlation analysis and regression analysis were adopted to quantify the independent influence of vehicle speed on lateral trajectory characteristics. A multi-dimensional evaluation system was further constructed to determine the optimal safe driving speed ranges for inner and outer lanes.Lane position presents a significant stratified constraint effect on vehicle speed, and obvious heterogeneity exists in trajectory offset features and driving risk levels, between inner and outer lanes. Vehicle speed shows an extremely weak positive correlation with lateral offset, indicating that speed is not the core factor affecting vehicle trajectory behavior on desert expressways.The comprehensive evaluation results demonstrate that the optimal safe speed range for the inner lane is 125–130 km/h, while that for the outer lane is 95–100 km/h. Significant lane-based differences in vehicle lateral trajectory and speed adaptation behavior exist on desert straight expressways. Speed variation has limited influence on trajectory stability, whereas lane location dominate driving safety performance. The defined sectional safe speed intervals can effectively support speed limit calibration, dynamic traffic safety control, and safety facility layout optimization for desert expressways in arid regions.

Article.Title: Novel avian hepadnaviruses in passerine birds
Article.Authors: Pellegrini F.; Casalino G.; Lombardi R.; Lanave G.; Diakoudi G.; Bugarim T.; Banyai K.; Camero M.; Di Martino B.; Camarda A.; Circella E.; Martella V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We identified hepadnaviruses in passerine birds. The virus was detected in four eggs from Gouldian finches ( Chloebia gouldiae ), in three feather quills, and in a liver sample from other ornamental birds. The full-length circular genome (~3 kb in length) of hepadnavirus strains detected in a Gouldian finch, a Society finch ( Lonchura striata domestica ) and a Long-tailed finch ( Poephila acuticauda ) was reconstructed. Hepadnavirus replicative circular DNA was detected in the egg and quill samples, suggesting the presence of cccDNA in these sites. The viruses were genetically distantly related to other avian hepadnaviruses and endogenous hepadnavirus elements, suggesting geographical or host-species restriction in passerine birds.

Article.Title: Time to death and predictors of in-hospital mortality among adults underwent emergency abdominal surgery at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia: a retrospective follow-up study
Article.Authors: Bayleyegn N.; Kune G.; Birhanu A.; Sisay A.; Merga H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency abdominal surgery is burdened by significant mortality and morbidity rates. There is a short window between the time of presentation and the time of surgical intervention which causes an inherent risk of increased perioperative and postoperative morbidity and mortality. This study is aimed at determining the time to in-hospital mortality as well as its predictors in patient who underwent emergency abdominal surgery. Retrospective cohort study was conducted among adult patients who underwent surgery for emergency abdominal conditions from January 1, 2019 to December 30, 2023 at JUMC (Jimma University Medical Center). Three hundred records were selected by systematic random sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured data extraction checklist with Kobo Toolbox by trained data collectors at JUMC. The collected data were exported into STATA Version 17 for analysis. Bivariate Cox regression analysis was conducted to identify candidate variables at p-value < 0.25 for multivariable Cox regression model. Finally, in multivariable Cox-Regression analysis, the p-value < 0.05 and Adjusted Hazard Ratio (AHR) with 95% CI were used to judge statistical significance. 300 medical records of surgical patients with emergency abdominal surgical conditions who underwent surgery during the five-year study period at JUMC were reviewed. Out of the 300 patients, 37 had died in the hospital and the median time of death was 40 days. The overall incidence rate of death was 1.35 (95% CI: 0.98–1.86) per 100 person-days. Being male (AHR = 4.1, 95% CI 1.25–15.42), and older adults (AHR = 7.77, 95% CI 2.57–33.5) had an increased hazard of death. Patients’ American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (AHR = 2.81, 95% CI: 1.2–6.6), shock (AHR = 9.7, 95% CI: 1.8–39.9), surgical site infection (AHR = 0.43, 95% CI 0.23–0.79) and re-laparotomy (AHR = 2.18, 95% CI 1.35–13.6) were significant predictors of time to death. In-hospital mortality among adults undergoing emergency abdominal surgery remained high in our study. The condition of the patient at presentation and postoperative complications were significant predictors of in-hospital mortality. Devising special integrated efforts and guidelines for perioperative management of patients can improve survival outcome and decrease postoperative complications.

Article.Title: Seasonal variation in water quality and evaluation of optimal iron removal conditions in acid mine drainage at A mine, Japan
Article.Authors: Fuchida S.; Nakamura A.; Kato S.; Ito H.; Ohara Y.; Kawahara R.; Otake T.; Makita H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acid mine drainage (AMD) often contains high concentration of iron (Fe), which can exceed 100 mg/L, while speciation and precipitation are key factors controlling the removal efficiency of Fe and other elements. This study monitored seasonal variations in AMD quality at A mine, Japan (pH: 2.6–3.2, Total-Fe: 128–162 mg/L), and found the dominant dissolved Fe species shifted from ferrous ion (Fe(II) aq ) in summer to ferric ion (Fe(III) aq ) in winter. Neutralization experiments using simulated AMD containing either Fe(II) aq or Fe(III) aq revealed that initial Fe speciation had little effect on arsenic and copper removal efficiency at this site. Furthermore, the reaction experiments using natural AMD in the presence or absence of Fe precipitates (5 v/v%) revealed the Fe(II) aq oxidation rate was 3 × 10 5 and 8 × 10 5 times higher in the presence of Fe precipitates at pH 3.0 and 3.5, respectively. Fe(II) aq oxidation was reduced substantially when using autoclaved Fe precipitates, suggesting that Fe(II) aq oxidation might be enhanced by processes associated with Fe precipitates, including microbial activity, rather than by homogeneous chemical oxidation alone. Therefore, promoting interaction between AMD and Fe precipitates, together with slight pH adjustment, could be effective for Fe removal from AMD at A mine.

Article.Title: Potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in marine fish caught from the mediterranean sea at Damietta city, Egypt: perspective on cooking effects and health hazard assessment
Article.Authors: Yusuf S.; Mahros M.; Zaher H.; Sallam K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the concentrations of mercury (Hg), arsenic (As), lead (Pb), and cadmium (Cd) in 270 fish muscle samples comprising 90 each of flathead grey mullet ( Mugil cephalus ), gilthead bream ( Sparus aurata ), and brushtooth lizardfish ( Saurida undosquamis ) collected from the Mediterranean Sea at Damietta, Egypt. The impact of common household cooking methods (grilling and frying) on toxic metal levels and the associated human health risks was assessed in 90 fish samples comprising 30 from each fish species. Fish samples were subjected to wet digestion using a nitric-perchloric acid mixture and analyzed with the atomic absorption spectrophotometer for heavy metal determination. Mean ± SE concentrations (mg/kg wet weight) of Hg, As, Pb, and Cd were 0.05 ± 0.004, 11.69 ± 0.72, 0.895 ± 0.14, and 0.046 ± 0.005 in raw flathead grey mullet; 0.069 ± 0.005, 12.38 ± 0.45, 0.865 ± 0.13, and 0.062 ± 0.004 in raw gilthead bream; and 0.145 ± 0.011, 8.215 ± 0.50, 1.012 ± 0.13, and 0.087 ± 0.006 in raw brushtooth lizardfish, respectively. Arsenic concentrations exceeded permissible limits in all examined samples, while Pb and Cd surpassed regulatory limits in substantial proportions of the tested fish. In contrast, Hg levels remained below the recommended limit in all samples. Grilling and frying generally reduced toxic metal concentrations in the three fish species tested; however, grilling increased As levels in brushtooth lizardfish by 8.2%. Dietary exposure was evaluated by comparing estimated daily intake (EDI) with available health-based guidance values, whereas potential non-carcinogenic risk for Hg, Pb, and Cd was evaluated separately using USEPA reference-dose-based target hazard quotients (THQs). Health risk assessment revealed that estimated daily intakes of all analyzed metals were below their provisional tolerable daily intake values. Total arsenic concentrations exceeded the applicable maximum permissible level in all examined fish samples. However, arsenic-specific non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risk estimates were not derived because total arsenic was measured without determination of its inorganic fraction. The present findings demonstrate considerable contamination of fish from the study area, particularly with As, Pb, and Cd, and highlight the need for continuous monitoring, stricter environmental controls, and effective regulatory strategies to protect public health and ensure seafood safety.

Article.Title: Sustainable production of pure nanocrystalline cellulose (NCCs) as a binder for enhanced aspirin tablets: Valorization of palm kernel waste
Article.Authors: Alminderej F.; El-Sayed W.; Ragab T.
Article.Abstract: The search for new efficient drug-excipient from natural resources will be of interest in drug delivery research. The current study demonstrates the optimal valorization of palm kernel (PK) residue to create value-added materials for biomedical applications. Valorization of palm kernel (PK) residue by producing nanocrystalline cellulose (NCCs) as a binder in aspirin tablets was studied. Applying the factorial design (2 2 ) and investigating the effect of two independent variables with two levels involving binder type (Avicel and NCCs), and binder concentration (40% and 50% w/w). Powder blends containing NCCs (F1 and F2) exhibited superior flow properties compared to Avicel blends (F3 and F4). The physiochemical analysis of PK residues was studied and Characterization was investigated by FT-IR spectroscopic analysis, phase analysis by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscope (SEM) and TEM analysis. The Formulated tablets were evaluated via studying weight variation, hardness, friability, wetting test, dispersion times and water solubility. The powder blend was evaluated and the In-vitro dissolution was studied. Post-compression evaluation showed all tablets met USP standards for weight variation (< 2%) and demonstrated acceptable hardness and friability (< 0.75%), with NCCs tablets showing faster wetting, shorter dispersion times (21–48 s), and improved aspirin solubility due to the high surface area of nanocellulose. NCCs were non-cytotoxic to normal human epithelial cells (1-BJ1) and exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Bacillus cereus , Bacillus subtilis , and Clostridium perfringens . Additionally, NCCs tablets showed prebiotic activity, particularly with L. casei . These findings highlight NCCs as a biocompatible, effective excipient for enhanced tablet performance and potential biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Temperature susceptibility and structural performance of CORMBB: A bio-based asphalt binder for the paving application
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Suman S.; Dwivedi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable pavement materials has increased interest in bio-based alternatives to petroleum bitumen. This study develops castor oil- and rice husk ash-modified bio-bitumen (CORMBB) by partially replacing VG-30 and evaluates its physical, chemical, temperature-dependent, and rheological properties. Temperature susceptibility was assessed using penetration index (PI), penetration viscosity-number (PVN), viscosity-temperature susceptibility (VTS), and Arrhenius activation energy, while rutting performance was evaluated using the 2.2 kPa failure-temperature criterion. The colloidal index decreased from 0.33 for the base binder to 0.26 for CORMBB-2, suggesting a more stable colloidal composition. FTIR indices showed increased aliphatic and methylene contents and reduced carbonyl and sulfoxide indices after modification. PI decreased from − 1.26 for the base binder to − 1.64 and − 2.37 for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, respectively, while PVN decreased from − 10.77 to − 12.30. Activation energy decreased markedly from 57.81 kJ/mol for the base binder to 43.77 and 42.67 kJ/mol for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, indicating lower viscosity sensitivity to temperature. However, the RTFOT-aged rutting failure temperature declined from 94.7 °C for the base binder to 76.7 °C and 74.1 °C for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, respectively. Overall, CORMBB showed improved thermo-viscous response but reduced high-temperature rutting resistance, highlighting a trade-off between temperature sensitivity and stiffness.

Article.Title: Intelligent hierarchical control for SI-SIDO buck converters
Article.Authors: Averneni V.; Gangula S.; Nizami T.; Chakravarty A.; Teli N.; Momin M.; Ahmad F.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This article describes a nonlinear control strategy for a single-inductor single-input dual-output (SI-SIDO) DC–DC buck converter. To competently regulate the multiple outputs while sharing a common inductor, a hierarchical control architecture is proposed, enabling coordinated control of the dual-output system. The proposed adaptive control framework ensures accurate voltage regulation at both output terminals while explicitly addressing the challenges of cross-regulation and cross-coupling effects inherent in SI-SIDO converters. By decoupling the control objectives across different hierarchical levels, the proposed approach enhances dynamic performance and improves steady-state voltage tracking under load and reference variations. Comprehensive simulation studies are carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed nonlinear hierarchical controller under various operating points. Furthermore, the simulation results are validated through extensive experimental implementation using the dSPACE DS1104 platform, demonstrating fast output tracking, superior regulation, robustness and practical feasibility of the proposed control scheme.

Article.Title: A conditional generative adversarial network with dual-context aggregation and color enhancement for digital mural creation
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an improved model based on generative adversarial networks to address the problems of unreasonable structural layout, color gradient distortion, and limited style controllability in digital mural generation. This model integrates the Dual Aggregation Context Module, Fast Fourier Convolutional Global Encode, Color Enhancement Polarized Self Attention Mechanism, and Pre trained Style Encoder, aiming to enhance the structural integrity, color authenticity, and style diversity of mural generation through multi-scale feature fusion, frequency-domain spatial domain joint modeling, and color space optimization. Experiments on Dunhuang murals and MetCollection datasets have shown that this method significantly outperforms mainstream generative models in objective evaluation metrics. The introduced evaluation of interaction efficiency and style consistency shows that this method can achieve higher consistency with the target style (CLIP similarity 0.891) with fewer interaction rounds (average 2.3 rounds) and faster response time (153 ms). In subjective evaluation, the average scores of generated images in terms of aesthetics, style consistency, and other dimensions are all higher than 4.3 points. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively enhance the quality control of the structure, color, and style of digital murals, providing a reliable technical path for the digital restoration and creative generation of cultural heritage.

Article.Title: Breaking the $$\:{\varvec{T}}_{\varvec{g}}$$ barrier in 4D printing: ultra-high temperature GF/TPI shape memory composite
Article.Authors: Kumar K.; Kumar S.; Doddamani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrating 4D printing with high-performance thermoplastic polyimide (TPI) offers significant potential for developing adaptive/self-deployable structures for extreme environments. However, processing TPI through fused filament fabrication (FFF) remains challenging due to its elevated melt viscosity and high melting temperature. In this work, glass fiber (GF) reinforced TPI (GF/TPI) composites are developed for ultra-high-temperature 4D printing applications. Firstly, the GF/TPI composite is developed through melt-mixing, followed by filament preparation and 3D printing. Printed specimens are subsequently post-processed and systematically characterized for microstructural and shape-memory properties to evaluate their suitability for high-temperature 4D printing. Microstructural analysis confirmed uniform material deposition, strong fiber-matrix interfacial bonding, and good printing integrity, validating selected processing parameters. The 4D printed GF/TPI composite showed excellent shape-memory behavior, exhibiting a shape fixity ( $$\:{R}_{f}$$ ) of 93.33% and shape recovery ( $$\:{R}_{r}$$ ) of 98.70% in the first cycle, which further decreased to 91.62% and 90.19% in the tenth cycle. A reduction of 8% in the $$\:{R}_{r}$$ across the successive ten cycles is observed, indicating good cyclic stability of the shape memory effect (SME). The comparative study demonstrated superior shape-memory performance of the developed GF/TPI composite compared with existing high-temperature polymer systems under repeated cycles. The 4D-printed GF/TPI soft robotic gripper demonstrated excellent dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and stable actuation, confirming its suitability for deployable structures in space.

Article.Title: Design, modeling, and characterization of a low-pressure dual-mode pneumatic soft actuator-gripper
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Xiong Y.; Qu X.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soft pneumatic grippers show immense promise in grasping fragile, irregular, and unknown objects; however, simultaneously achieving high payload capacity and grasping flexibility under low actuation pressure remains a critical challenge. In this paper, we propose a low-pressure dual-mode pneumatic soft gripper, which is constructed by rigidly coupling a cylindrical enveloping module and a three-finger soft pneumatic network (PneuNet) bending module. The cylindrical module achieves an active enveloping grasp for heavy loads through inward radial expansion, whereas the three-finger module flexibly accommodates objects of various shapes and sizes via bending deformation. To characterize the actuation behavior of the cylindrical module, its deforming architecture is modeled as a thin-walled curved chamber, and the deformation process is conceptualized into two sequential stages: inversion and bulging. By combining analytical formulations and finite element analysis (FEA), a two-stage inflation mechanics model is established, augmented by a semi-empirical correction to account for non-ideal boundary constraints and material softening effects. Furthermore, FEA is utilized to predict the bending deformation of the PneuNet fingers, exhibiting excellent agreement with experimental measurements. Experimental results demonstrate that under a low actuation pressure of merely 20 kPa, the dual-mode gripper can achieve an exceptional vertical payload of up to 6.5 kg when grasping a 36-mm-diameter sphere. Moreover, the two grasping modules can synergistically interact to manipulate and reorient a single complex target, or independently grasp two distinct objects simultaneously. Ultimately, the proposed low-pressure, dual-mode soft gripper demonstrates substantial potential for versatile, safe, and highly efficient robotic manipulation.

Article.Title: Magnetically supported Cobalt (II) Schiff base complex as a recoverable catalyst for the synthesis of Betti base compounds
Article.Authors: Moosavi-Zare A.; Darvishi Z.; Balali M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cobalt (II) Schiff base complex supported on cobalt ferrite magnetite nanoparticles was used as a heterogeneous and reusable catalyst for the preparation of 1 Betti base compounds by the reaction of 2-naphthol with different aldehydes and morpholine. Cobalt (II) complex by the rearrangement from tetrahedral to square planar structure, and then increasing the coordination number of cobalt can be accelerated and catalyze the synthesis of Betti base compounds.

Article.Title: Fault identification and localization in transmission lines using an IVY-optimized generalized additive model
Article.Authors: Qiao R.; Zhou W.; Dai W.; Wu T.; Liu F.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate fault-type identification and fault-distance estimation are essential for the reliable operation of transmission lines, yet their simultaneous realization remains challenging under nonlinear transient responses and limited labeled data. This study proposes an IVY-optimized generalized additive model (IVY-GAM) framework that combines physically guided feature construction, interpretable nonlinear modeling, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization. A 200 km two-terminal transmission-line model is established in MATLAB/Simulink to generate 385 fault samples covering 11 fault categories. Twelve features are constructed from phase-mode transformation, db4 wavelet decomposition, transient modulus maxima, three-phase voltage statistics, and double-ended wavefront-arrival indices. IVY is then used to optimize the key GAM parameters for fault identification and localization. Under a fixed train–validation–test partition, IVY-GAM achieves an identification accuracy of 99.987% and a localization $$R^2$$ of 0.99674, with an MAE of 3.16 km, an RMSE of 3.91 km, and a maximum error of 11.84 km. Stratified five-fold out-of-fold evaluation further yields an identification accuracy of 99.22% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.992, while the localization task obtains a mean MAE of 7.08 km and a mean $$R^2$$ of 0.9520. Feature-group ablation, permutation importance, and GAM main-effect analyses show that three-phase voltage means primarily support fault-type discrimination, whereas double-ended arrival indices dominate distance estimation and modal maxima provide complementary information. The proposed framework therefore offers a balanced solution for accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient transmission-line fault diagnosis.

Article.Title: SentiGraphRec: sentiment perception entity graph for personalized news recommendation
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Wang J.; Zhang Y.; Hang H.; Cao S.; Yang X.; Ibrahim N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the digital era, accurate news recommendation is essential for improving user engagement and supporting effective information delivery. Most existing methods mainly focus on semantic or structural signals, while largely overlooking users’ sentiment preferences toward entities in their reading histories. As a result, these approaches struggle to model dynamic sentiment patterns and fail to provide sufficiently personalized recommendations. To address this issue, we propose SentiGraphRec, a sentiment-aware entity graph model for personalized news recommendation. SentiGraphRec constructs a global entity graph that jointly encodes semantic relations, structural connections, and entity-level sentiment information. By explicitly modeling the interactions among users, news articles, and entities with sentiment orientations, the proposed framework captures both semantic relevance and affective preferences in a unified manner. Extensive experiments on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that SentiGraphRec consistently outperforms strong state-of-the-art baselines across multiple evaluation metrics. In particular, the model achieves notable improvements in recommendation accuracy and diversity. These results validate the effectiveness of sentiment-aware entity modeling and highlight the general applicability of SentiGraphRec for personalized news recommendation.

Article.Title: Research on multi-objective scheduling optimization of emergency resources based on simulated annealing algorithm
Article.Authors: Song Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency departments face persistent challenges including prolonged patient wait times, unbalanced resource utilization, and high staff overtime. To address these issues, this study proposes a multi‑objective resource scheduling model based on real hospital data and optimizes it using a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. The model discretizes time slots and integrates multiple resources (doctors, consultation rooms, beds), with objectives of minimizing weighted waiting time and labor cost under triage‑priority and maximum‑wait constraints. A neighborhood operation set (patient exchange, cross‑doctor reallocation, shift fine‑tuning) was designed to fit clinical workflows. Simulation on annual 2023 data from a tertiary hospital showed that, compared to the current system, the SA‑optimized schedules reduced average waiting time by 20–35%, lowered the overall threshold-violation rate by 46.8% (26.7 to 14.2%), and balanced resource utilization across weekday, peak‑day, and night‑shift scenarios. These gains were not cost-neutral: total daily labour cost rose by 11.4% (CNY 31,680 to 35,280) and cost per patient visit by 10.6% (CNY 102.3 to 113.1), while overtime hours fell by 29.7% and overtime cost by 30.2%. The SA-based framework converged reliably and retained its ordering across scenarios, and is best described as a candidate decision-support component that buys substantial improvements in timeliness, resource equity and staff workload at a quantified increase in labour expenditure. Although the framework was validated only in a simulation environment calibrated with one year of real ED data and has not yet undergone prospective real-world deployment, the results suggest that it constitutes a potentially deployable decision-support component for intelligent ED scheduling. All results derive from a single-centre in-silico evaluation calibrated on one tertiary emergency department; prospective and multi-centre validation is required before any claim of generalisability or operational readiness can be supported.

Article.Title: Multimodal customer intent recognition and profile dynamic update network based on temporal attention and gated fusion
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Lei G.; Guan J.; Pan Y.; Zheng W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate recognition of customer intent, together with the timely maintenance of user profiles, underpins a range of downstream applications including personalized recommendation, customer segmentation, targeted promotion, customer relationship management (CRM) and customer service quality assurance. Three practical limitations continue to constrain existing systems: multimodal fusion strategies remain insufficiently adaptive to per-sample modality reliability, temporal behavior models tend to collapse short-term intent shifts and long-term preference drift into a single flat sequence, and intent recognition pipelines are typically decoupled from downstream profile update mechanisms, so newly detected signals only propagate to profiles after a batch cycle. To address these gaps in a unified way, this paper proposes the Multimodal Customer Intent Recognition and Profile Dynamic Update Network (MCIP-DUN).
