The framework combines a pre-trained language backbone with a cross-modal gated fusion unit that reweights textual, behavioral and interaction-attribute streams per sample, a time-decay-aware temporal attention module that separates short-term tactical shifts from long-term preference evolution, and a gated recurrent profile update module in which the forget gate and update gate are decoupled so that stable dimensions and volatile dimensions can be governed independently. A joint training objective with homoscedastic uncertainty weighting balances the intent classification loss against a bounded-target profile reconstruction loss. On the Alibaba User Behavior Dataset (AUBD) and the Customer Service Dialog Intent Dataset (CSDID), MCIP-DUN reaches 89.46% accuracy and 87.77% macro-F1, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.59 and 3.25% points; the profile update pipeline achieves 88.39% tag accuracy with an end-to-end persistence lag of roughly 18 min — measured from event ingestion to database refresh, and clearly distinguished from the 14.1 ms model forward latency reported separately. Ablation studies isolate the individual contribution of each component. It should be noted that the evaluation is restricted to e-commerce and customer-service data; generalization to other verticals such as power-utility customer service is discussed as future work.

Article.Title: Gestational age and antenatal growth discordance are principal predictors of composite neonatal outcomes in very preterm twins
Article.Authors: Hašlík L.; Korček P.; Hanulíková P.; Krofta L.; Širc J.; Straňák Z.; Hanáček J.; Halaj M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Very preterm twin pregnancies show heterogeneous neonatal trajectories that are incompletely captured by infant-level survival alone. Pregnancy-level neonatal outcomes and their antenatal and perinatal determinants were evaluated in 434 dichorionic and monochorionic twin pregnancies managed at a national tertiary referral center between 2013 and 2024. The primary outcome was composite survival without major neonatal morbidity (C-SNM). Secondary outcomes were composite morbidity burden (CoMB; neither twin, one twin, or both twins affected), cumulative morbidity burden (CMB; the unweighted number of affected clinical domains across both infants), and dominant organ-system morbidity (DSM; organ system contributing most to morbidity). C-SNM was achieved in 222/434 pregnancies (51.2%). In multivariable analyses, gestational age at delivery and antenatal estimated fetal weight discordance ≥ 25% were the principal predictors of C-SNM. A significant interaction was observed ( P = .003): the odds of C-SNM increased by approximately 80% per additional week among pregnancies with discordance < 25% and by approximately 30% among pregnancies with discordance ≥ 25%. Lower gestational age and greater discordance were also associated with worse CoMB and higher CMB, whereas dichorionicity was associated with lower morbidity burden. For DSM, discordance was most strongly associated with respiratory morbidity. Pregnancy-level composite assessment may refine risk stratification and strengthen prenatal counseling.

Article.Title: Canagliflozin reduces the recovery of intracellular uropathogenic Escherichia coli from uroepithelial cells and affects α-hemolysin function
Article.Authors: Hilger A.; Adick A.; Putze J.; von Vietinghoff S.; Dobrindt U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SGLT2 inhibitors, used for diabetes treatment, have been discussed with an increased urinary tract infection (UTI) risk due to increased glucose excretion in urine. Beyond their primary function, these drugs exhibit diverse off-target effects. We investigated whether canagliflozin and other SGLT2 inhibitors impact the interaction between the host and uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), as well as UPEC pathogenicity. In vitro cultures of uroepithelial cell lines were infected with UPEC strains CI5 and CFT073. Effects of different SGLT2 inhibitors were assessed by measuring the intracellular bacterial burden, glucose uptake and ATP levels of host cells, and the hemolytic activity of the toxin α-hemolysin. Canagliflozin showed the most pronounced and consistent reduction in intracellular UPEC recovery, while ipragliflozin showed a weaker effect. We observed the same effect of canagliflozin for the intracellular recovery of Salmonella Typhimurium strain LT2 from uroepithelial cells, an invasive pathogen that employs different invasion mechanisms than UPEC. The effect of canagliflozin on the recovery of intracellular UPEC and Salmonella was cell type-dependent and was observed in uroepithelial cell lines and macrophage-like THP-1 cells, but not in human colorectal adenocarcinoma-derived Caco-2 cells. Additionally, several SGLT2 inhibitors interfered with hemolysis. Taken together, canagliflozin demonstrated activity against UPEC regarding intracellular bacterial numbers and hemolytic activity in vitro, suggesting novel avenues for UTI treatment. Targeting the pore-forming toxin α-hemolysin and reducing the number of intracellular UPEC may offer a potential complementary strategy to antibiosis in combating recurrent UTI.

Article.Title: Somatic symptoms in cisgender men, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals assigned male at birth: a Swiss Nationwide Study
Article.Authors: Lieb M.; Jedamzik J.; Laskowski N.; Müller R.; Paslakis G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Somatic symptoms are highly prevalent and constitute a major public health concern. Sociodemographic factors associated with these symptoms, particularly among cisgender men, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals, remain insufficiently explored in Switzerland. We analyzed data from the Swiss Health Survey 2022, a nationally representative cross-sectional study. The sample included cisgender men, transgender men (i.e., assigned female at birth and identifying as men), and gender-diverse assigned male at birth (AMAB) individuals (i.e., assigned male at birth and currently identifying as nonbinary or another gender). Somatic symptom load was assessed by combining common somatic complaints including gastrointestinal issues, pain, palpitations, and weakness and subsequently dichotomized into lower vs. severe symptom burden. Sleep problems were measured by difficulties falling asleep, restless sleep, repeated awakenings, and early-morning awakening and categorized into no/few vs. moderate/severe sleep problems for subsequent analyses. Energy and vitality were assessed using the Short Form 36 Health Survey (SF-36) Vitality (VT) subscale, capturing fatigue, tiredness, and overall vitality over the past four weeks and were analyzed as a continuous outcome. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics©. Two binary logistic regression analyses were conducted for symptom load and sleep problems, respectively, and one linear regression analysis was performed for vitality as a continuous outcome. To account for the complex survey design, all analyses incorporated survey weights and canton as the stratification variable using design-based (complex samples) procedures. The analytical sample comprised 8,699 individuals (unweighted), representing an estimated population of 3,505,801 after applying survey weights. Compared with cisgender men, gender-diverse AMAB individuals showed higher odds of severe somatic symptom load (OR = 7.82, 95% CI [2.50; 24.45]), whereas transgender men did not differ significantly on this outcome (OR = 1.22, 95% CI [0.39; 3.76]). Both groups showed higher odds of sleep problems (transgender men: OR = 4.66, 95% CI [1.64; 13.25]; gender-diverse AMAB individuals: OR = 3.87, 95% CI [1.21; 12.30]) and lower vitality scores (B=-13.70, 95% CI [-20.04; -7.35]; B=-14.70, 95% CI [-25.93; -3.47], respectively). These estimates rest on small unweighted subgroups (35 transgender men, 16 gender-diverse AMAB individuals), are correspondingly imprecise, and should be read as exploratory. Additional factors associated with poorer outcomes included non-heterosexual orientation, nonemployable status, migration background, and residence in French- or Italian-speaking regions. Older age (65 + years) was associated with lower odds of severe somatic symptom load (OR = 0.71, 95% CI [0.53; 0.96]) but higher odds of sleep problems (OR = 1.35, 95% CI [1.08; 1.70]) and higher vitality scores (B = 8.89, 95% CI [6.83; 10.95]). Factors associated with somatic symptom load, sleep problems, and vitality showed both shared and outcome-specific patterns. Gender identity was associated with poorer sleep and lower vitality in transgender men and gender-diverse AMAB individuals compared with cisgender men, whereas higher somatic symptom load was found only in gender-diverse AMAB individuals. Given the small unweighted subgroup sizes and the resulting imprecision of the estimates, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. These preliminary findings highlight the importance of differentiating gender identities and adopting a gender-sensitive perspective in research and healthcare to better identify vulnerable groups and inform targeted interventions.

Article.Title: Multi-trait selection using the MGIDI for simultaneously improving rapeseed performance and energy-eco efficiency in dryland farming
Article.Authors: Khoshhal-Zolpirani F.; Majidian M.; Banaeian N.; Sabouri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attaining sustainability in agroecosystems requires balancing trade-offs between maximizing yield, optimizing energy efficiency, and minimizing environmental footprints. Yet, determining the optimal configuration of tillage and fertilisation regimes to satisfy these multifaceted goals under dryland farming conditions remains a complex agronomic challenge. This two-year field experiment aimed to identify the most efficient integrated management strategy for winter rapeseed ( Brassica napus L.) using a split-plot design comprising three tillage intensities and ten integrated fertilisation protocols. For the first time in rapeseed agronomic assessment, the Multi-trait Genotype-Ideotype Distance Index (MGIDI) was deployed to rank treatments based on 23 morphological, yield-related, quality, and environmental traits. Factor analysis reduced data dimensionality into two principal factors (agronomic and yield components: 63.19% and sustainability and energy indices: 28.25%) which collectively accounted for over 91% of the total variance. The MGIDI analysis identified conventional tillage combined with farmyard manure as the treatment closest to the ideotype. Analysis of Selection Differentials (SD) revealed that this strategy yielded substantial gains over the grand mean, including increases in oil performance (+ 26.09%), net energy (+ 31.13%), seed yield (+ 16.76%), and energy use efficiency (+ 71.62%). Concurrently, marked reductions were observed in specific energy (-51.73%) and, most notably, total CO 2 equivalent emissions (-98.94%). These findings demonstrate the robustness of the MGIDI as a multi-criteria decision-making tool in cropping systems, highlighting conventional tillage supplemented with farmyard manure as the superior strategy for maximizing productivity and eco-efficiency in dryland farming rapeseed.

Article.Title: Fabrication of three-dimensional MXene-MWCNT composite for the swift removal of cationic BB3 Dye from aqueous solution
Article.Authors: Goswami M.; Srivastava A.; Kumar B.; Sar P.; Jangde D.; Tiwari K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The contamination of aquatic ecosystems with synthetic dyes is a considerable environmental concern due to their detrimental properties and persistence. Basic blue 3 (BB3), an aromatic dye, poses significant hazards owing to its cancer-causing properties, hence requiring efficient removal techniques. Investigating versatile materials that effectively remove contaminants from wastewater is of paramount significance for ecological restoration. This study developed an MXene-Multi-walled carbon nanotube (MXene-MWCNT) composite adsorbent for the removal of BB3 dye from aqueous solutions. Multi-layered MXene was produced via the etching of the Ti 3 SiC 2 MAX phase employing HF–H 2 O 2 , followed by the preparation of the MXene-MWCNT composite via a solvothermal approach. The synthesized composite was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), Raman, and infrared (IR) spectroscopic techniques, suggesting the effective incorporation of MWCNT with MXene nanosheets. BET studies revealed that MXene-MWCNT maintained a mesoporous structure (39.46 Å) with a specific surface area (SSA) of 15.37 m 2 g − 1 . The adsorbent exhibited swift and effective BB3 elimination, attaining 99% removal within 27 min and showcasing an adsorption capacity of 217 mg g − 1 . Adsorption kinetics adhered to a pseudo-second-order model. Adsorption isotherm analysis demonstrated a strong correlation with the Langmuir model (R 2 = 0.9996), implying the occurrence of monolayer adsorption. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that the adsorption process is spontaneous and endothermic in nature. Electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking govern the mechanisms of adsorption between BB3 molecules and the functional groups of MXene-MWCNT. The composite demonstrated a removal efficacy over 90% after five rejuvenation cycles, affirming its notable reusability. These findings indicate that the MXene-MWCNT nanocomposite shows potential for BB3 removal from aqueous solutions.

Article.Title: An uncertainty and interaction-aware framework for sustainable additive manufacturing decisions in electric vehicle applications
Article.Authors: Momena A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Expert-based sustainability assessment of additive manufacturing (AM) for electric-vehicle (EV) components frequently relies on crisp ratings due to elicitation simplicity and auditability. However, crisp evaluations conceal three critical uncertainty sources: inter-expert disagreement, heterogeneous assessor reliability, and criterion-dependent ambiguity. This paper proposes an aggregation-centered decision framework that (i) adaptively transfers crisp evaluations into trapezoidal fuzzy numbers using a Takagi–Sugeno (TS) uncertainty inference mechanism driven by dispersion, reliability, and criterion volatility; (ii) performs interaction-aware robust aggregation through a consensus-based capacity, Shapley-effective weights, and power-support adjustment to mitigate unsupported or weakly aligned opinions; and (iii) completes the decision using value–ambiguity ranking with an explicit ambiguity-aversion parameter. A full EV bracket manufacturing-route case study demonstrates deterministic matrix construction, uncertainty propagation, interaction-aware aggregation, comparative prioritized (TrIFPWA) and Einstein-induced baselines, module-ablation analysis, controlled expert-conflict stress testing, and extensive sensitivity and uncertainty analyses. Results show that the ranking favors the polymer-composite route, and the preferred alternative remains stable across the tested ranges of ambiguity aversion, interaction strength, robustness parameters, uncertainty scaling, reliability perturbation, module-ablation variants, and progressively stronger expert conflict. Under maximum controlled conflict, the full model attenuates the conflicting expert more strongly and preserves a larger top-second score gap than additive aggregation. The proposed workflow enhances interpretability, robustness, and traceability in sustainability-driven manufacturing decision making.

Article.Title: Droplet-scale combustion memory analysis of hydrogen-enriched date palm pollen biodiesel using a novel ant colony optimization algorithm with Lévy flight
Article.Authors: Khan O.; Alnamasi K.; Yahya Z.; Yadav A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The implementation of biodiesel in diesel engines is limited by high viscosity, lower heating value, poor atomization, incomplete combustion, and increased fuel consumption. Hydrogen enrichment ca. overcome these limitations by improving flame propagation, premixed combustion intensity, and burning stability; however, the simultaneous variation of hydrogen supply and injection timing creates nonlinear ignition-delay, heat-release, pressure-rise, and emission interactions that are difficult to optimize using conventional methods. This study novelly investigates date palm pollen biodiesel under hydrogen-enriched diesel engine operation, integrating droplet-scale combustion memory with engine-level performance, combustion, emission, and acoustic analysis. A 64-run full-factorial design was developed using engine load, injection timing, and hydrogen flow rate as input factors. Pearson correlation was used to establish combustion-memory relationships among outcomes, while entropy priority weighting assigned the highest importance to BTE (22%), BSFC (18%), and NOx (18%), followed by peak pressure (12%), CO (10%), HRR (10%), vibration (6%), and sound pressure level (4%). Conventional ACO converged within 20 iterations, stabilizing near a fitness value of 0.80 in 12.8 s. Incorporating Lévy flight improved global exploration and avoided local pheromone stagnation, achieving a higher fitness value of 0.94 within 9 iterations in 6.3 s with only two inflection points. The optimum condition is dataset 59/Path-1, corresponding to 100% load, 4 LPM hydrogen flow, and 23° bTDC injection timing, producing BTE 38.7%, BSFC 0.21 kg/kWh, peak pressure 98 bar, HRR 82 J/deg, vibration 3.6 mm/s, and sound 93 dB. The results establish date palm pollen biodiesel as a feasible hydrogen-assisted biodiesel candidate and demonstrate that ACO–Lévy optimization effectively resolves coupled hydrogen–injection timing combustion complexity.

Article.Title: Noise scheduling and out-of-distribution generalisation in deep reinforcement learning for 6-DOF robotic grasping
Article.Authors: Mizhimakoski I.; Zlatinov S.; Gjoreski H.; Nadzinski G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exploration strategy is a fundamental but underexplored design choice in deep reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation. This paper presents a controlled empirical comparison of three off-policy configurations on a 6-DOF robotic grasping task using a Universal Robots UR5e in the RoboSuite simulation environment: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with automatic entropy tuning, Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with piecewise linear noise decay, and TD3 with constant Gaussian noise. All configurations share identical network architectures, reward functions, and training budgets. The two TD3 variants differ only in the action-noise schedule and form the controlled comparison of the study, while SAC serves as a widely used entropy-regularised reference. Each configuration is trained over 10,000 episodes across five independent runs and evaluated over 1,000 deterministic episodes both within and beyond the training distribution. SAC achieves the highest in-distribution success rate (89.6%) and training efficiency, with a large effect size over both TD3 variants ( $$d = 1.32$$ and $$d = 1.47$$ ) and complete rank separation in area under the learning curve. Within the training distribution, the two TD3 variants are statistically indistinguishable ( $$d = 0.04$$ ). Under out-of-distribution evaluation, however, this contrast changes sharply: the noise-decay variant reaches a mean success rate of 43.1% against 32.3% for constant noise — an effect size of $$d = 1.08$$ , where the same comparison within the training distribution is negligible — together with the lowest cross-run variance of the three configurations and a more uniform distribution of success across the workspace. No pairwise difference reaches significance at five runs per configuration, and the comparisons are interpreted through effect sizes and confidence intervals. These results indicate that noise schedule design has a measurably different effect on in-distribution performance and spatial out-of-distribution generalisation, and that standard single-metric evaluation protocols may fail to capture meaningful differences between exploration strategies.

Article.Title: Association of a structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program with treatment tolerance and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing precision radiotherapy for head and neck cancer: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Su N.; Huo Z.; Zhang Z.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malnutrition, systemic inflammation, and treatment-related toxicity may compromise radiotherapy tolerance in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated a structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program during precision radiotherapy. This prospective cohort included 258 patients with HNSCC receiving intensity-modulated or volumetric-modulated arc radiotherapy. Patients entered the comprehensive nutritional management (CNM) group ( n = 129) or usual care (UC) group ( n = 129) according to program availability. Outcomes included radiotherapy interruption, Grade ≥ 3 oral mucositis, treatment delay, longitudinal nutritional and inflammatory markers, quality of life, and exploratory survival outcomes. Linear mixed-effects, parsimonious logistic, and Cox regression models were used. Radiotherapy completion without major interruption was 95.3% in the CNM group and 89.1% in the UC group ( P = 0.063). Grade ≥ 3 oral mucositis was less frequent with CNM (14.0% vs. 26.4%; P = 0.013), as was Grade ≥ 2 dysphagia (17.1% vs. 28.7%; P = 0.026). Treatment delay was shorter with CNM [2 (IQR 1–3) vs. 5 (IQR 3–7) days; P = 0.018]. CNM was associated with more favorable longitudinal trajectories of PNI, SII, global health status, and swallowing symptoms (all interaction P ≤ 0.020). Adjusted analyses showed lower odds of severe mucositis (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.27–0.92), while the association with major interruption was not statistically significant (OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.17–1.05). A structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program was associated with lower treatment-related toxicity, shorter delays, and more favorable nutritional, inflammatory, and quality-of-life trajectories during radiotherapy.

Article.Title: Heavy metal bioaccumulation potential of indigenous rhizospheric soil fungi with comparative assessment of lead and cadmium resistance
Article.Authors: Amin I.; Nazir R.; Rather M.; Hamid B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungi are highly suitable for use in bioremediation processes because of their high degree of metal tolerance. The present investigation focused on comparing the tolerance levels of the two most toxic metals, such as lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd), and the bioaccumulation capacities of certain unexplored fungi isolated from rhizospheric agricultural soils. Twenty-one (21) fungal strains were isolated, observed for their morphological features and then identified via molecular approach using ITS rDNA regions for Sanger sequencing (ITS1 and ITS4). The tolerance of the fungal isolates to Cd and Pb was assessed by examining their growth response to increasing concentrations of Cd and Pb in the form of cadmium chloride (CdCl₂·H₂O) and lead nitrate [Pb (NO₃)₂], respectively. The majority of the isolates showed tolerance to both Pb and Cd, as indicated by visual observation of growth on solid media. Species-specific differences in metallic tolerance were determined by minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and tolerance index (TI) assays, with Penicillium atramentosum (IA47) having the highest resistance to Cd, with MIC of 500 ppm. Against Pb, both Aspergillus calidoustus (IA40) and Penicillium atramentosum (IA47) , showed highest MIC of 400 ppm. The isolates demonstrating the best resistance and growth rates were further investigated for their ability to uptake metals. For that purpose, the fungal biomass was asceptically spiked with 50 and 100 ppm cadmium chloride (CdCl₂·H₂O) and lead nitrate [Pb (NO₃)₂]. The concentration of accumulated metals in the digested biomass was quantified through atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS). It was found that Phoma herbarum (IA52) had the greatest ability to bioaccumulate Cd (3.693 mg/g) at a 100 ppm concentration. The isolates showed a greater ability to uptake Cd than Pb because Pb tends to be less soluble than Cd and is therefore less readily available for fungal cells. These findings provide valuable insights into the selection of native fungal strains for eco-friendly and sustainable bioremediation of heavy metal contaminated environments and support their potential application in future environmental remediation strategies.

Article.Title: Moored observations of the deep western boundary current east of the Gagua Ridge in the Northwestern Pacific
Article.Authors: Xun H.; Zhou C.; Xiao X.; Zou T.; Qu T.; Zhang Z.; Guan S.; Huang X.; Zhao W.; Tian J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The deep western boundary current (DWBC) of the Pacific serves as a lower limb of the meridional overturning circulation that has been identified as a key component of the global climate system. Here, we report the results of observations from a set of full-depth subsurface moorings deployed in the Northwestern Pacific from August 2017 to May 2020. The observations reveal a southward, bottom-intensified DWBC east of the Gagua Ridge, featuring a core velocity of 4.5 cm/s and a mean southward volume transport of 1.79 ± 0.75 Sv (1 Sv = 10 6 m 3 /s). Seasonally, this DWBC shows a tendency to move southward with relatively cold water in summer and northward with warm water in winter. On intraseasonal time scales, its variability is closely related to surface-detectable mesoscale eddies, suggesting that some of these eddies are deep ocean reaching and can directly modulate the bottom current as deep as ~ 5500 m east of the Gagua Ridge. These results enhance our understanding of the deep circulation and pathway of deep water in the Pacific.

Article.Title: Emotionally intelligent preference optimization for conversational behavior change support
Article.Authors: Chen B.; Dethlefs N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Procrastination negatively affects productivity and well-being, yet current large language models (LLMs) often lack the nuanced emotional understanding necessary for effective behavior-change support. This study proposes emotionally intelligent preference optimization (EIPO), a unified framework integrating emotional chain-of-thought reasoning, teacher-guided self-correction, and direct preference optimization to enhance emotional intelligence in conversational user interfaces. Through ablation experiments evaluated using the emotional generation score (EGS), we demonstrate that EIPO significantly improves empathetic and constructive responses in procrastination-related interactions. Crucially, cross-model validation on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-2-2B confirms EIPO’s model-agnostic design, with consistent EGS gains ( $$\Delta = +0.13$$ to $$+0.27$$ ) and robust independent evaluation using Claude-3.5-Sonnet. These findings establish EIPO as a principled, transferable framework for embedding emotionally intelligent behavior-change support into diverse LLM-driven CUIs.

Article.Title: Bone-adapted oral squamous cell carcinoma cells show adaptive responses to the osseous microenvironment in a murine tumor transplantation model
Article.Authors: Vohl N.; Herrmann A.; Ooms M.; Müller-Diesing F.; Heitzer M.; Schaffrath K.; Apel C.; Hölzle F.; Modabber A.; Winnand P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bone invasion is a decisive step in the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and is associated with increased tumor aggressiveness, worsening the prognosis. Under the selection pressure of the bone microenvironment, a fundamental biological divergence arises. Bone-adapted cells represent not only a variant but also a distinct subpopulation with stable pro-invasive properties. To model tumor biological selection through the bone microenvironment, the murine OSCC cell line SCC-7 was injected under the periosteum of immunocompetent C3H mice and cultured in situ for a period of 25 days. A cell population was then isolated from the induced bone-invasive tumor and established in vitro. The selected cells were systematically characterized. Migration and invasion behavior, cellular morphology, size, and metabolism were examined using standardized functional and metabolic analysis methods. Compared with the parental tumor cell line, bone-selected SCC-7 cells showed significantly increased migration and invasion activity as well as clear morphological differences. A constant change in the metabolic profile was detected. Phenotypic alterations indicated adaptive reprogramming as a result of exposure to the bone microenvironment, which selects for a distinct, stably altered tumor cell population. Thus, bone-infiltrating OSCC cells fundamentally differ phenotypically and metabolically from non-bone-invasive tumor cells.

Article.Title: Staphylococcus aureus in bovine mastitis in northwestern Iran: patterns of antimicrobial and multidrug resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence/resistance gene carriage
Article.Authors: Hosseini R.; Aram M.; Nofouzi K.; Asadpour R.; Ghorani M.; Ateba C.; Enferadi A.; Sadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ), a major cause of bovine mastitis, represents a significant challenge for the dairy industry due to its economic and zoonotic importance. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of major virulence-associated genes (lukE, seA, sei), the methicillin-resistance gene (mecA), antimicrobial susceptibility, and biofilm formation in S. aureus isolates obtained from cases of bovine clinical mastitis in dairy farms of East and West Azerbaijan provinces, Iran. A total of 138 milk samples were collected from East Azerbaijan (67; 48.6%) and West Azerbaijan (71; 51.4%) provinces. S. aureus isolates were identified by culture, biochemical tests, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the nuc gene for confirmation. Target genes were detected using conventional PCR. Antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated by the disk diffusion method, and biofilm formation was assessed using the crystal violet microtiter plate assay. Of the 138 samples, 42.0% were positive for S. aureus . The prevalence of lukE, seA, sei, and mecA genes was 39.7%, 36.2%, 17.2%, and 6.9%, respectively. Resistance was highest to penicillin (94.8%) and lowest to gentamicin (22.4%). Overall, 39 isolates (67.2%) were classified as multidrug-resistant (MDR), of which 25.8% were resistant to four or five of the six antimicrobial classes tested and 10.3% were resistant to all six tested antimicrobial classes, with a mean multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) index of 0.53 ± 0.23. Resistance profiles did not differ significantly between provinces, whereas biofilm formation showed a significant interprovincial difference ( P = 0.002), with a moderate degree of herd-level clustering (ICC = 0.158). These results indicate a high isolation proportion of S. aureus with substantial multidrug resistance and regional variation in biofilm-forming capacity, emphasizing the necessity of targeted antimicrobial stewardship and improved surveillance.

Article.Title: Thymol as a potential botanical insecticide against Tuta absoluta: life history parameters, toxicity and enzymatic responses
Article.Authors: Rostami E.; Afrazeh Z.; Nemati A.; Jalali Sendi J.; Zhao Q.; Zhang Y.; Li L.; Lin K.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the insecticidal potential of thymol against the pest Tuta absoluta (Meyrick) (Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae), its effects on key physiological enzyme activities, and investigated the duration of the insect's developmental stages. Initially, the study's complete objectives and conducted experiments were detailed, including toxicity assessment via topical bioassays and the estimation of lethal doses (LD 50 ) using probit analysis. Thymol exhibited high toxicity, with a 24-h LD 50 calculated at 6.866 µg/larva. The larval development period and adult longevity were significantly reduced at LD 30 and LD 50 compared to the control, and the oviposition rate also decreased. Biochemical assays revealed substantial alterations in the activities of detoxification and antioxidant enzymes. Antioxidant enzyme activities were elevated. In contrast, detoxification enzymes, including glutathione S-transferase, α- and β-esterases, and cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, were significantly and dose-dependently decreased, as was acetylcholinesterase. Thymol was also observed to reduce sodium–potassium adenosine triphosphatase (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase) activity. The results indicate that thymol induces toxicity through multiple physiological pathways, including disruption of detoxification systems and ionic homeostasis. These findings introduce thymol as a promising candidate for a botanical insecticide in managing the T. absoluta .

Article.Title: Differences in competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH4 and CO2 in mylonitic and primary structure coal
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Chen X.; Li J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tectonically deformed coal exhibits significantly different gas adsorption-desorption characteristics from primary structure coal due to intense coal mass deformation, making it a research hotspot in coalbed methane development and gas disaster prevention and control. To explore the differences in the competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH 4 and CO 2 between mylonitic coal and primary structure coal, this study took No. 8 coal from the Zhuxianzhuang Mining Area as the research object. Based on experimental results, molecular models of mylonitic coal (C 214 H 159 N 3 O 20 ) and primary structure coal (C 208 H 152 N 2 O 18) were constructed respectively. Isothermal adsorption simulations of single-component and mixed gases of CH 4 andCO 2 at different ratios were carried out using molecular dynamics methods. The results show that the adsorption of CH 4 and CO 2 in both types of coal belongs to physical adsorption, with stronger adsorption capacity under low temperature and high pressure. Under the same conditions, the adsorption capacity and adsorption heat of CO 2 are higher than those of CH 4 , and the adsorption advantage of CO 2 in mylonitic coal is more prominent. This is closely related to the more complete aromatic ring conjugated π-electron system, abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and a higher proportion of ultramicropores in mylonitic coal. With strong polarity and small kinetic diameter, CO 2 molecules are more prone to interact with π-electrons and produce the “pore-filling effect”. In mixed gas adsorption, the total adsorption capacity and interaction energy of both coal types increase with the rise of CO 2 molar fraction. Although the adsorption selectivity coefficient of CO 2 to CH 4 decreases, it is always greater than 1, and the selectivity coefficient of mylonitic coal is higher. The energy distribution curve of CO 2 shifts to adsorption sites with low interaction energy, while that of CH 4 shows the opposite trend, and the shift amplitude of gas molecular curves in mylonitic coal is larger. In addition, the interaction energy of mylonitic coal is dominated by van der Waals force, accounting for a higher proportion than that of primary structure coal. Its CH 4 adsorption heat also has a larger fluctuation range, reflecting a stronger competitive adsorption capacity for CO 2 . The research findings provide a theoretical basis for mine gas prevention and control and efficient coalbed methane development.

Article.Title: Differentiating acute from chronic pulmonary thromboembolism: a preliminary study using dual-layer CT
Article.Authors: Bae K.; Cho M.; Jeon K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate the actual values and ranges of conventional and spectral parameters in pulmonary thromboembolism (PE) and assess their potential for distinguishing acute PE (APE) from chronic PE (CPE) using dual-layer CT (DLCT). This retrospective study included 52 patients with central PE diagnosed with CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) using DLCT. Patients were categorized into APE and CPE groups. Conventional and spectral parameters including Hounsfield unit (HU) and electron density (ED) values were measured at the thrombus and pulmonary trunk on both pre- and post-contrast images. Additionally, in vitro experiments were conducted to generate clots of varying compositions. Apart from D-dimer levels, no significant clinical differences were found between APE and CPE groups. APE showed significantly higher mean HU and ED values than CPE on both unenhanced and enhanced images (both p < 0.001). Thrombus enhancement, using true non-contrast (TNC) values as a reference, was similar between groups. APE showed greater variability in HU and ED values, whereas CPE consistently demonstrated lower values across all imaging phases. Unenhanced HU and ED values provided better discrimination than post-contrast values, with high AUCs ( p < 0.05). The in vitro findings were consistent with these observations and may provide a plausible explanation for the compositional differences between APE and CPE. APE showed higher HU and ED values than CPE. Conventional and spectral CT parameters could help differentiate APE from CPE, reflecting distinct thrombus compositions.

Article.Title: Cognitive and affective drivers of VR adoption in heritage tourism: Integrating UTAUT and Anticipated emotions
Article.Authors: Lorandi M.; Mandolfo M.; Di Dalmazi M.; Noci G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While the potential of Virtual Reality (VR) in destination marketing is recognized, tourists’ motivations to adopt it remain underexplored. This paper investigates cognitive and affective factors influencing intentions to use VR in heritage tourism contexts. Integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with Anticipated Emotion, an online survey was conducted on 626 respondents. Structural Equation Modelling-Partial Least Squares was employed to test the effects of cognitive and emotional predictors. Results reveal that Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Attitude, Positive and Negative Anticipated Emotions significantly predict VR adoption intentions. Findings further show that combining cognitive and affective antecedents enhances explanatory power. For practitioners, the study offers strategies to promote VR in heritage sites by addressing both rational and emotional motivations, fostering pre-visit engagement and enriching on-site experiences. This represents the first integration of UTAUT and Anticipated Emotion in heritage destination marketing, offering a perspective on VR adoption among visitors.

Article.Title: DuSR-Net: a statistical- and optimization-prior-guided deep-unrolled network with cross-scale manifold alignment for hyperspectral image classification
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Chang Y.; Li Q.; Wang X.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the issues of missing interpretability in existing deep learning models, weak spatial-spectral structure preservation,and poor generalization in small-sample-size scenarios, this paper proposes a Deep Unfolding Tensor Low-Rank Network(DuTLR-Net) that deeply integrates physical priors. First, a Cross-Scale Manifold Alignment (CSMA) module is designed,which uses a global PCA manifold as guidance to dynamically select high-variance spectral bands, achieving alignment ofmulti-scale features. Subsequently, the constructed ADMM-based deep unfolding backbone network explicitly models thespectral low-rankness and noise sparsity constraints as a differentiable iterative optimization process, enabling end-to-endlearning through parameterized dictionaries and adaptive soft-thresholding. Experiments demonstrate that DuTLR-Net, withfewer parameters and faster convergence speed, exhibits superior classification accuracy and spatial consistency underextremely low labeling rates.code:https://github.com/yongqichang202-beep/DuTLR-Net

Article.Title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of immunosuppressive regimens and immune-related outcomes in adeno-associated virus-based gene therapy
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Wu N.; Fu D.; Zhao Q.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Significant progress has been made in adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapy. However, host immune responses remain a major challenge to its widespread clinical application, making immunosuppressive regimens an important component of clinical management. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to characterize immunosuppressive regimens and immune-related outcomes in clinical AAV gene therapy. The primary outcomes were the proportions of humoral immune responses, gene therapy-associated uveitis (GTAU), elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and elevated creatine kinase (CK). A total of 73 studies involving 1773 participants were included and categorized as ocular (n = 31), liver (n = 22), muscle (n = 12), or central nervous system (n = 8) according to the primary target organ. Primary subgroup analyses were restricted to studies in which immunosuppression was used prophylactically. The pooled proportions of humoral immune responses were 27.7%, 75.8%, 35.2%, and 42.6% for ocular-, liver-, muscle-, and central nervous system-directed AAV gene therapy, respectively. The pooled proportions of GTAU in ocular-directed studies, elevated ALT in liver-directed studies, elevated CK in muscle-directed studies, and elevated ALT in central nervous system-directed studies were 24.2%, 49.5%, 5.1%, and 16.5%, respectively. Statistically significant regimen-based subgroup differences were observed for GTAU in ocular-directed studies and for humoral immune responses in muscle-directed studies. However, the current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific immunosuppressive regimen. These findings highlight variation in immune-related outcomes across target organs and the need for more clinical studies with standardized outcome reporting to better inform immunosuppressive strategies in AAV gene therapy.

Article.Title: EIDrive: an efficient and interpretable visual-language framework for low-level control signal prediction in autonomous driving
Article.Authors: Dong W.; Cai Y.; Sun X.; Liu Z.; Wang H.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, end-to-end autonomous driving models have shown promising potential by directly generating waypoints or control signals from sensor data. In particular, low-level control signals, such as steering angle and vehicle speed, directly determine vehicle motion, making their prediction accuracy and interpretability important to the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. However, existing methods mainly regress control signals from visual inputs and lack explicit semantic characterization of the basis underlying control generation, making it difficult to establish a traceable link between scene understanding and control outputs. To address this issue, we propose E fficient and I nterpretable Driving (EIDrive), an efficient visual-language framework for low-level control signal prediction in autonomous driving. Given monocular driving videos, EIDrive jointly performs control signal prediction and natural-language explanation generation. Specifically, a sparse orthogonal subspace projection mechanism is introduced to improve feature compactness and structural expressiveness. A lightweight fine-tuned BERT model is employed as a shared semantic backbone, together with a structured control prediction head to model structured correlations among control-related features. On the BDD-X dataset, EIDrive achieves a turning-angle RMSE of 6.1 and a speed prediction accuracy of 88.2% under the $$1.0\,\mathrm {m/s}$$ threshold. It also demonstrates competitive language-generation performance while maintaining a compact computational profile.

Article.Title: Automated SSIM regression for detection and quantification of motion artefacts in brain MR images
Article.Authors: Sciarra A.; Chatterjee S.; Dünnwald M.; Placidi G.; Nürnberger A.; Speck O.; Oeltze-Jafra S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motion artefacts in magnetic resonance brain images can have a strong impact on diagnostic confidence. The assessment of MR image quality is fundamental before proceeding with the clinical diagnosis. Motion artefacts can alter the delineation of structures such as the brain, lesions or tumours and may require a repeat scan. Otherwise, an inaccurate (e.g. correct pathology but wrong severity) or incorrect diagnosis (e.g. wrong pathology) may occur. “ Image quality assessment ” as a fast, automated step right after scanning can assist in deciding if the acquired images are diagnostically sufficient. An automated image quality assessment based on the structural similarity index (SSIM) regression through a residual neural network is proposed in this work. Additionally, a classification into different groups - by subdividing with SSIM ranges - is evaluated. Importantly, this method predicts SSIM values of an input image in the absence of a reference ground truth image. The networks were able to detect motion artefacts, and the best performance for the regression and classification task has always been achieved with ResNet-18 with contrast augmentation. The mean and standard deviation of residuals’ distribution were $$\mu =-0.0009$$ and $$\sigma =0.0139$$ , respectively. Whilst for the classification task in 3, 5 and 10 classes, the best accuracies were 97, 95 and 89%, respectively. The results show that the proposed method could be a tool for supporting neuro-radiologists and radiographers in evaluating image quality quickly.

Article.Title: Prevalence and risk of colorectal adenomas and colorectal cancer among Thai population aged under 50 years
Article.Authors: Kotchanan N.; Kositamongkol C.; Auesomwang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rising global incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) has prompted re-evaluation of screening strategies. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of colorectal adenoma and CRC and associated clinico-metabolic risk factors among 500 patients younger than 50 years who underwent colonoscopy at Siriraj Hospital between January 2022 and December 2023. The cohort was stratified into three age groups (20–29, 30–39, and 40–49 years), with a secondary analysis comparing the 20–39, 40–44, and 45–49 age subgroups. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent associated factors for colorectal adenoma and CRC. The prevalence of colorectal adenoma and CRC increased significantly with age: 0% (0/35) in the 20–29 age group, 13.1% (14/107) in the 30–39 age group, and 20.7% (74/358) in the 40–49 age group ( p < 0.001). Secondary analysis revealed a sharp increase in prevalence starting in the early 40s, with 22.7% (30/132) in the 40–44 age group, which was higher than the 9.9% (14/142) observed in the 20–39 age group ( p = 0.004) and similar to the 19.5% (44/226) in the 45–49 age group ( p = 0.463). Multivariable logistic regression model revealed that each 1-year increase in age (aOR 1.06; 95% CI 1.01–1.10; p = 0.018) and male sex (aOR 1.95; 95% CI 1.17–3.25; p = 0.010) were independently associated with a higher prevalence of early-onset colorectal adenoma and CRC. These findings underscore the critical need for prompt diagnostic evaluation and early colonoscopy in adults under 50-particularly males and those in their early 40s-rather than informing average-risk screening guidelines.

Article.Title: Deep-learning-enabled distributed acoustic monitoring of bird activity on overhead transmission lines
Article.Authors: Fan X.; Wu B.; Gui J.; Xue B.; Xu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the mismatch between the urgent need for bird-hazard prevention on transmission lines and the spatiotemporal limitations of existing monitoring approaches, and to support operation and maintenance (O&M) units in implementing targeted mitigation strategies, we propose a distributed acoustic sensing-based method for bird-call event detection and bird-call classification on overhead transmission lines. To resolve the difficulty of detecting bird calls under complex noisy conditions, we develop a bird-call event detection model that integrates time-frequency feature extraction with time-frequency joint attention. Using log-Mel spectrograms as input, the model achieves a detection accuracy of 97.48 ± 0.12%, with a detection latency of 7.3 ms for a single 0.5 s window. The detected signals are then further transformed into MFCC heatmaps, from which time-cepstral features are extracted using a multi-scale convolutional backbone. Combined with denoising autoencoder (DAE)-based feature enhancement, this framework enables bird-call classification under severe environmental noise. Ablation experiments show that each module contributes substantially to the overall classification performance. Across five independent runs on the fixed independent test set, the full classification model achieved a mean accuracy of 95.67 ± 0.16%, outperforming the adapted TSAM-Net by 5.61% points. These results demonstrate the feasibility, accuracy and robustness of the proposed method under simulated transmission-line conditions with complex noise, and provide a promising technical basis for future monitoring of bird activity along long-distance transmission lines.

Article.Title: Development of a PLS-SEM-ANN hybrid model for predicting college students’ academic achievement from physical exercise through social support and psychological resilience
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; Lyu C.; Zhu Y.; Guo H.; Zhang Q.; Fan Y.
Article.Abstract: As national strategies for education reform deepen, exploring the association between physical exercise and college students’ academic achievement has become a critical priority in higher education. Although existing literature has confirmed a positive association between physical exercise and academic achievement, scant attention has been paid to systematically elucidating the underlying mechanism by integrating social support and psychological resilience within a serial mediation framework (chain mediation model). Drawing upon Social Support Theory (SST), Conservation of Resources Theory (COR), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study constructs a theoretical model to unravel how physical exercise is associated with academic achievement via the serial indirect pathways of social support and psychological resilience, while also examining the moderating effect of time management ability. A total of 950 valid responses were collected, and a two-stage hybrid approach combining Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was employed for empirical validation. The PLS-SEM results indicate that physical exercise shows a significant direct positive association with academic achievement (β = 0.156, $$\:p<0.001$$ ) and an indirect effect was identified via the serial mediation path of “Physical Exercise → Social Support → Psychological Resilience → Academic Achievement” ( $$\:\beta\:=0.008$$ , $$\:p=0.006$$ ). The ANN sensitivity analysis aligns highly with the PLS-SEM findings, further corroborating that psychological resilience is the strongest associate of academic achievement in terms of normalized importance (normalized importance = 64.580%), followed by physical exercise (44.950%) and social support (25.550%), thereby verifying the robustness of the conclusions. This study elucidates the underlying mechanisms by which physical exercise is positively associated with academic achievement via the indirect pathways of social support and psychological resilience, as well as the boundary condition of time management ability. These findings provide a theoretical basis and practical guidance for higher education administrators to formulate differentiated and precise student development strategies.

Article.Title: Subsurface basin structure, seismic site conditions and earthquake damage: case study of the Gölbaşi basin, Türkiye
Article.Authors: Büyüksaraç A.; Bektaş Ö.; Pamuk E.; Fırat S.; Işık E.; Işık N.; Çetin K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gölbaşı (Adıyaman) Town, located within a basin along a left-stepping segment of the East Anatolian Fault Zone in Türkiye, experienced severe damage during the 6 February 2023 Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.6 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. Widespread liquefaction, ground subsidence, lateral spreading, bearing capacity failures and building collapses occurred, with their spatial distribution suggesting a strong association between basin geometry and ground motion amplification. This study investigates the subsurface geometry and sediment thickness of the Gölbaşı Basin using an integrated approach combining microgravity measurements and Spatial Autocorrelation (SPAC) analyses. A total of 120 microgravity measurements were conducted to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of low-density alluvial deposits, and two-dimensional gravity models were constructed along four profiles. Additionally, SPAC measurements at 20 locations yielded deep shear-wave velocity (Vs) profiles, from which Vs30 values were derived. Basin-depth proxies (Z 1.0 and Z 2.5 ) were subsequently estimated from Vs30 using empirical relationships. The basin contains up to approximately 700 m of unconsolidated sediments. Variations in sediment thickness and basin geometry produce significant lateral heterogeneity in seismic velocity and impedance contrasts across the basin. Areas underlain by the thickest sediments experienced the most severe structural damage. The results demonstrate a strong spatial association between sediment thickness, basin geometry, seismic site conditions, and the observed distribution of structural damage. A neighborhood-based Pearson correlation analysis revealed a very strong positive relationship between the severe-damage ratio and sediment thickness ( r = 0.905, p < 0.001), a strong positive correlation with Z 2.5 ( r = 0.763, p = 0.017) and a strong negative correlation with Vs30 ( r = − 0.698, p = 0.037). Although the correlations with Z 1.0 and the gravity anomaly did not reach the 5% significance level, they exhibited similarly strong spatial trends. Given the limited number of neighborhoods analyzed ( n = 9), these results are interpreted as exploratory spatial associations rather than evidence of causal relationships. Nevertheless, the agreement among the gravity-derived basin geometry, SPAC-derived site parameters, and the damage analysis indicates that sediment thickness and subsurface basin structure were significant contributors to the spatial distribution of earthquake damage.

Article.Title: Machine learning predicts diuretic resistance via cardio hepato renal axis in heart failure comorbid with MASLD
Article.Authors: Huang A.; Zhao J.; Leng T.; Li S.; Wan Y.; Hao S.; Nie Q.
Article.Abstract: To explore machine learning models for predicting diuretic resistance (DR) in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) comorbid with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this retrospective study of 586 patients, four predictive algorithms were evaluated. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was further interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify non-linear feature interactions. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC: 0.850). SHAP analysis indicated that hepatic parameters, particularly the FIB-4 index and serum albumin, were strongly associated with DR, potentially rivaling traditional cardio-renal indices. Interaction analyses suggested that concurrent hepatic and renal impairment synergistically correlated with elevated DR risk. Patients stratified into the AI-derived high-risk phenotype experienced lower freedom from HF re-hospitalization (Log-rank P < 0.001). The XGBoost model, coupled with SHAP analysis, may serve as a valuable tool for DR risk stratification. Assessing multi-organ crosstalk across the cardio-hepato-renal axes could inform personalized volume management in this complex cohort.

Article.Title: Accelerometer-derived ‘weekend warrior’ physical activity, genetic susceptibility, and the associated risk of osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Wei S.; Yu S.; Chen G.; Zhang Z.; Lei Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical activity is important for health, but the association between the temporal distribution of weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and incident osteoarthritis (OA) remains uncertain. This observational cohort analysis included 70,608 UK Biobank participants. Physical activity exposure was based on UK Biobank processed accelerometer variables derived from wrist-worn Axivity AX3 devices. Participants were classified as inactive (< 150 min/week MVPA), regularly active ( > = 150 min/week with < 50% accumulated during the two most active days), or weekend warriors (WW; >=150 min/week with > = 50% accumulated during the two most active days). The two most active days were not required to be Saturday and Sunday. Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations with incident overall, knee, hip, and hand OA after covariate adjustment; associations were also examined across OA polygenic risk strata. Compared with inactivity, both the WW and regularly active patterns were associated with lower overall OA risk. A direct comparison of the WW and regularly active groups showed no statistically significant difference in overall OA hazard. Site-specific associations differed: the two patterns showed similar associations with knee OA, while the WW group had a 21% higher risk of hand OA than the regularly active group. For hip OA, an inverse association was observed for the WW group, whereas the estimate for the regularly active group was not statistically significant. Associations between activity patterns and OA were observed across polygenic risk strata. The WW pattern defined by the two most active days was associated with lower overall OA risk compared with inactivity, and the direct comparison with regularly distributed activity was not statistically significant. Site-specific findings should be interpreted cautiously. Because this was an observational analysis of processed wrist-accelerometer variables, the results do not establish causality or identify joint-level mechanisms.

Article.Title: Genetic diversity of Plasmodium vivax apical membrane antigen 1 (PvAMA1) and erythrocyte binding protein (PvEBP) from malaria endemic areas of Pakistan
Article.Authors: Khan I.; Suphakhonchuwong N.; Ali O.; Kuesap J.
Article.Abstract: Malaria remains a major global health challenge, with Plasmodium vivax as a key contributor to disease burden across endemic regions. Apical membrane antigen-1 ( PvAMA1 ) and erythrocyte binding protein ( PvEBP ) of P. vivax are the genes encoding erythrocyte invasion protein which promising as a target of erythrocytic vaccine candidate. However, limited genetic study of PvAMA1 and PvEBP in Pakistan was revealed. The objective was to investigates the genetic diversity of PvAMA-1 and PvEBP gene in isolates obtained from diagnostic facilities in malaria-endemic regions of Pakistan. A total of 50 leftover blood samples collecting from diagnostic facilities located in Khyber Pakhthukhwa (KP) and Sindh, Pakistan between May and October 2025 were analyzed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and sequencing. Genetic polymorphisms, genetic diversity, neutral selection, population differentiation and haplotype network were performed. Twenty-six and 25 non-synonymous mutations were revealed in PvAMA1 and PvEBP , respectively. Considering haplotypes, 28 haplotypes of PvAMA1 and 25 haplotypes of PvEBP were identified. Notably, one previously unreported non-synonymous mutation of PvAMA1, while 11 non-synonymous mutations of PvEBP were observed. The full-length sequence of PvAMA1 revealed a slightly higher nucleotide diversity (π = 0.00784 ± 0.00056) with the highest diversity located in domain I (π = 0.01973 ± 0.00066). Lower nucleotide diversity was identified in PvEBP (π = 0.00180 ± 0.00013). The neutrality test, Fu and Li’s D* and F* was statistically significant positive in domain I of PvAMA1 ( p < 0.02) with positive values suggesting a significant departure from neutral expectations occur in this region. Global population differentiation analysis by F ST revealed low to high differentiation of both PvAMA1 and PvEBP. PvAMA1 exhibited higher genetic diversity than PvEBP among the Pakistani isolates, with the observed patterns broadly consistent with those reported in global P. vivax populations. The observed genetic diversity of PvAMA1 and PvEBP provides baseline information on sequence variation in these antigen genes among the analyzed Pakistani isolates.

Article.Title: Infrared intensity-aware feature learning for robust target detection in infrared images
Article.Authors: Yu J.; Liu S.; Li Q.; Zhang C.; Qiu J.; Li Z.; Wan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infrared target detection is challenging because of strong background noise, weak foreground–background intensity contrast, blurred boundaries, and limited target pixels. Motivated by the challenges observed in infrared inspection scenarios, this paper proposes YOLOv11-IR-TSD, an infrared-adaptive detector for improving feature representation and localization accuracy. In the backbone, a lightweight DnCNN-Lite module is introduced to suppress infrared imaging noise, while the original spatial pyramid pooling structure is replaced with an infrared-intensity-aware spatial pyramid pooling–fast (IIA-SPPF) module to enhance multi-scale feature representation. In the neck, a DINOv2-assisted self-supervised contrastive guidance mechanism and an infrared-intensity-gradient-weighted fusion strategy are employed to improve feature discrimination under complex backgrounds. In addition, a feature alignment constraint, an infrared-intensity-adaptive activation function, and a lightweight bounding-box refinement module are incorporated into the detection head to improve cross-stage feature consistency and localization accuracy. Experiments on the public FLIR and LLVIP infrared detection benchmarks show that YOLOv11-IR-TSD achieves mAP@0.5 values of 91.0% and 89.5%, respectively, while maintaining inference speeds of 64 and 62 FPS. Compared with existing infrared detection approaches, the proposed detector achieves improved detection accuracy while maintaining efficient inference, and exhibits enhanced robustness under noise interference, weak intensity contrast, and complex background conditions. Additional analyses under different target scales and contrast conditions further indicate the effectiveness of the proposed feature-learning strategy for challenging infrared scenes. Further evaluation on dedicated real-world infrared insulator datasets is required to investigate its applicability to abnormal-heating inspection.

Article.Title: Development and reliability test of the work stress questionnaire for cancer survivors after returning to work (WSQ-CS)
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Zhong Y.; Dai J.; Shen P.; Ma L.; Peng P.; Guo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To develop and conduct an initial psychometric evaluation of a context-specific questionnaire measuring perceived work-related stress among cancer survivors after returning to work. A descriptive phenomenological study was conducted with 20 cancer survivors, and the interview data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step method to generate the initial item pool. The Transactional Model of Stress served as a sensitizing framework for developing the interview guide. Two rounds of Delphi expert consultation were conducted between May and July 2022, followed by pilot testing in July 2022. Independent samples of 252 and 200 cancer survivors were recruited from two tertiary hospitals in Nanjing and Taizhou, China, for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, respectively. The final WSQ-CS comprised 24 items across five dimensions: physiological load, psychological load, economic load, obstruction of self-development, and social support deficit. The I-CVI values ranged from 0.83 to 1.00, and the S-CVI was 0.966. The overall Cronbach’s α was 0.914. EFA identified a five-factor structure accounting for 63.44% of the total variance. CFA showed that most fit indices met recommended thresholds, providing preliminary support for the five-factor structure. The questionnaire has undergone rigorous development and psychometric testing, and the findings support its reliability and validity. It can serve as an important assessment tool for the psychosocial rehabilitation of cancer survivors and provides a reliable measurable instrument for related research.

Article.Title: Application optimization of visual-verbal cue learning in image search system
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Hong J.; Luo X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In modern image retrieval systems, effective alignment between visual and language modalities and efficient retrieval are critical for enhancing system performance. However, traditional prompt learning methods struggle to achieve good generalization. This paper proposes a visual–language prompt learning method, MaPLeMeta, designed to improve the overall performance of image retrieval systems. MaPLeMeta combines dual-modal prompt learning techniques by introducing learnable prompts in both the visual and text encoders, enabling deep alignment between visual features and textual descriptions. Additionally, MaPLeMeta optimizes visual and textual prompts through an asymmetric contrastive learning objective, improving the semantic consistency and retrieval accuracy of cross-modal features. After representation learning, a standard HNSW index is employed only as an engineering component to accelerate approximate nearest-neighbor search; it does not participate in prompt optimization or visual–language alignment. Experiments on DeepFashion show consistent improvements over the evaluated baselines: compared with the strongest baseline, MaPLeMeta increases Recall@1 by 1.3 percentage points (81.5% versus 80.2%) and NDCG@10 by 0.01 (0.89 versus 0.88). These results indicate competitive performance in cross-domain, cross-category, and few-shot retrieval, while the HNSW backend separately improves query efficiency.

Article.Title: Conflict-guided feature filtering for efficient exact decision trees
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Zheng S.; Pan S.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exact decision-tree search is sensitive to the number of candidate predicates, motivating efficient front-end mechanisms for controlling the optimization space. We study conflict-guided feature selection (CGFS), in which discretized conflict relevance (DCR) ranks features by the fraction of sampled opposite-label pairs that they distinguish, and introduce joint conflict coverage (JCC) to reduce redundant selections. On five datasets spanning 569–45,222 instances and 14–500 original features, depth-3 PyDL8.5 experiments with a 60-s solver limit show that DCR at $$K=10$$ reduces end-to-end time by $$2.74$$ – $$348.60\times $$ on completed full-feature runs, while the all-timeout Madelon configuration yields a $$>397.78\times $$ lower bound. Direct MurTree validation independently reproduces substantial reductions on the harder Hill–Valley and Madelon representations. JCC further recovers complementary signal groups under controlled redundancy. Together, these results establish conflict coverage as an auditable front-end criterion for reducing candidate-predicate burden before exact decision-tree optimization, with predictive effects characterized explicitly across datasets.

Article.Title: Temporal soil nitrogen dynamics with stand age of Betula platyphylla forests in the permafrost region of Northeast China
Article.Authors: Wei H.; Chen X.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) is a key nutrient regulating plant growth, forest productivity and ecosystem functioning in permafrost regions. Despite the critical role of succession in modifying soil N processes, how soil N dynamics respond to mid-successional Betula platyphylla forest development remains poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize soil N transformations across a 25- to 61-year stand-age gradient in permafrost forests of Northeast China. We determined soil inorganic nitrogen concentrations and net nitrogen mineralization (ammonization + nitrification) using in‑situ incubation experiments in 25-, 40- and 61-year-old mid-successional Betula platyphylla forests. Ammonium N increased significantly with stand age, whereas nitrate N concentration exhibited a decreasing trend. Generalized least‑squares (GLS‑AR1) modelling detected no significant main effect of stand age on soil inorganic N or net N mineralization rate (Rm). Mean Min-N remained stable across stands (8.39, 8.15 and 8.49 mg·kg⁻¹ for the 25-, 40-, and 61-year-old stands, respectively). Rm showed a numerical increase along the age gradient (0.11, 0.46, 0.67 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹). Soil N dynamics were driven by significant stand‑age × soil‑depth and stand‑age × sample‑month interactions rather than stand age main effects. Inorganic‑N and mineralization rates were higher in topsoil (0–10 cm) than subsoil (10–20 cm). Ammonification dominated net N mineralization across all stands, contributing on average 3.88% (0–10 cm) and 4.18% (10–20 cm). Hierarchical partitioning analysis identified stand age as the primary driver of soil‑N variation, followed by sampling month, soil chemical properties and microbial biomass. Mid‑successional Betula platyphylla forest succession accelerates soil N turnover and modifies inorganic‑N composition without expanding total mineral‑N pools. These findings inform vegetation restoration and sustainable management of permafrost forest ecosystems.

Article.Title: Psychological pathways associated with gamified physical education and perceived learning in adolescents and young adults
Article.Authors: Wang D.; Duanmu S.; Yao L.; Liu Y.; Xiao T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gamified technology is increasingly used in physical education (PE), but evidence remains fragmented across motivation, engagement, and learning-related outcomes. This study proposed and empirically tested an integrated model linking students’ perceptions of gamified PE with psychological need satisfaction, motivation, multidimensional engagement, and perceived learning outcomes. A cross-sectional survey was completed by 500 secondary and tertiary students (mean age = 18.90 years, SD = 3.77; 51.4% female) from five institutions across three countries. Participants had experienced institution-approved gamified PE platforms sharing points, badges, feedback, challenges, progress indicators, meaningful choice, and cooperative activities, with limited teacher-level variation. A 43-item questionnaire measured 11 reflective constructs; 42 indicators were retained. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Gamified Technology Use and Perceived Enjoyment were positively associated with autonomy, competence, and relatedness satisfaction. Need satisfaction was positively associated with intrinsic and extrinsic motivation; motivation was positively associated with behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement; and all engagement dimensions were positively associated with perceived learning outcomes. The model explained 58.9% of PLO variance. Direct GTU–PLO and PE–PLO associations were nonsignificant, whereas the specified sequential indirect associations were significant. The findings support a cross-sectional pattern consistent with the proposed framework but do not establish causal or temporal mediation. Mastery-oriented feedback, meaningful task choice, progress tracking, and cooperative missions warrant further experimental evaluation, while public ranking should be used cautiously.

Article.Title: A national propensity score-matched analysis of simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplantation from donation after circulatory death and brain death donors
Article.Authors: Lim T.; Crichton E.; Baselious E.; Ketsan T.; Jurkovich A.; Cui Y.; Nissen N.; Kosari K.; Voidonikolas G.; Todo T.; Steggerda J.; Wisel S.; Kim I.; Brennan T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Increased use of donation after circulatory death (DCD) organs can lessen the ongoing organ shortage in transplantation. While DCD donor utilization has increased in other types of organ transplantation, with outcomes comparable to donation after brain death (DBD) donors, DCD use in pancreas transplantation is declining. To rigorously define the risk of DCD pancreas donors and control for confounding variables, we performed a propensity score-matched analysis of adult simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) transplantations. Using data from the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) registry, we examined 1036 propensity-matched pancreas transplant recipients of 777 DBD and 259 DCD donor organs between 2010 and 2022. In univariable Cox proportional hazards models fitted in the propensity score-matched cohort, with robust variance estimates clustered by matched set, SPK recipients of DCD donors had post-transplant patient and graft survival outcomes comparable to those of DBD donors at 1 and 3 years. DCD recipients experienced similar rates of treatment for graft rejection at 6 months and 1 year, comparable rates of postoperative complications, and similar renal function at 1 year compared with DBD recipients. SPK recipients of DCD donors benefited from significantly shorter wait times for organs than recipients of DBD donors. The use of DCD donors in pancreas transplantation can safely increase organ availability.

Article.Title: Lake Urmia desiccation drives building heating and cooling energy demand in northwestern Iran
Article.Authors: Maboudi Reveshti A.; Maroofiazar R.; Ebrahimpour A.; Fatourehchi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The progressive desiccation of terminal lakes under global climate change represents an emerging environmental challenge with significant implications for regional climate and building energy demand. This study investigates the impact of Lake Urmia desiccation on building energy consumption across 13 cities in the Lake Urmia Basin in northwestern Iran during 2001–2023. Using MODIS land surface temperature, Landsat water-extent monitoring, MERRA-2 reanalysis, and GPM precipitation data, we generated 299 year-specific weather files for 13 cities across the Lake Urmia Basin. Year-by-year EnergyPlus simulations of representative residential and commercial building archetypes were conducted to quantify the progressive impacts of drought-induced climatic changes on heating and cooling demand. Results show that the 90% reduction in lake surface area coincided with a 1.8–2.4 °C rise in summer temperatures and a 0.8–1.2 °C increase in annual mean temperatures. A control-city analysis indicates that the majority of these temperature changes can be attributed to lake-desiccation-driven mesoscale forcing rather than generic urban or regional warming. Annual cooling energy increased by 18–35% for residential and 22–42% for commercial buildings, while heating demand declined by 8–15%, resulting in a net HVAC energy increase of 12–23%. Cities within 30 km of the former lakeshore experienced impacts 40–60% greater than those in more distant areas, confirming the spatial attenuation of lake-related climatic effects. Strong negative correlations between lake surface area and cooling energy (r = − 0.82 to − 0.91, p < 0.001) further demonstrate a robust association between lake desiccation and increasing cooling demand. The cumulative additional annual energy cost across the basin was estimated at $127–218 million, while peak cooling demand increased by 15–25%, potentially placing additional pressure on electricity-grid stability. These findings have important implications for regional energy-infrastructure planning, climate-adaptive building design, urban cooling strategies, and lake-restoration policies in semi-arid regions undergoing large-scale environmental degradation.

Article.Title: Comparative characterization of the mucosal eukaryotic virome across independent whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing cohorts
Article.Authors: Na H.; Park J.; Kim T.; Choi N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The human mucosal eukaryotic virome remains incompletely characterized because methodological heterogeneity limits direct comparisons across independent whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing (WMS) datasets. To address this limitation, we reanalyzed publicly available DNA-based WMS datasets representing healthy body-site samples together with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated disease, and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) using the same ViromeScan-based analytical approach. Viral count profiles were converted to within-sample relative abundances for Bray–Curtis analyses, host-unmapped read depth was included as a covariate in PERMANOVA, and alpha-diversity findings were evaluated using repeated rarefaction. Anatomical site remained associated with eukaryotic virome diversity and community structure in the HMP cohort after accounting for sequencing depth, and site-associated differences were also observed in the independent NPC cohort analyzed using the same approach. HPV infection status was also associated with viral community structure after depth adjustment, whereas DOI-defined OSCC groups showed no significant global differences in alpha diversity, normalized viral recovery, or community structure and yielded only exploratory taxon-level signals. Across datasets, viral recovery varied with host-unmapped sequencing depth, with substantial between-sample heterogeneity. Together, these findings show that consistent application of publicly available analytical tools can support comparative characterization of eukaryotic virome profiles from existing WMS datasets, while also highlighting the importance of sequencing depth and cautious interpretation of taxon-level associations.

Article.Title: Isolation and phenotypic characterization of bacteriophages targeting multidrug-resistant biofilm-forming uropathogenic Escherichia coli from hospital sewage
Article.Authors: Tamrat E.; Derbie A.; Mekonnen F.; Asmare Z.; Geteneh A.; Kassa T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) is a major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), with multidrug resistance (MDR) and biofilm formation complicating treatment. This study isolated and phenotypically characterized bacteriophages targeting MDR and biofilm-forming UPEC from hospital sewage in Ethiopia. Twenty-three archived MDR UPEC isolates were screened for biofilm formation, and phages were characterized by host range, efficiency of plating, multiplicity of infection (MOI), adsorption kinetics, one-step growth, environmental stability, and biofilm biomass reduction. Eight isolates (34.8%) formed biofilms, including 3 strong, 1 moderate, and 4 weak biofilm formers. Two phages, ΦET-3175 and ΦFETA-207, were isolated with titers of 1.35 × 10⁹ and 1.12 × 10⁹ PFU/mL, respectively. ΦET-3175 showed broader activity, with detectable activity against 6/23 (26.1%) isolates, an optimal MOI of 0.1, > 95% adsorption within 20 min, a latent period of approximately 30 min, and a burst size of 147 ± 4.6 PFU per infected cell. Both phages retained detectable activity across pH 4–10 and at temperatures up to 50 °C.
