ΦET-3175 reduced biofilm biomass by 3.2–39.5% among four susceptible biofilm-forming isolates, but the paired difference was not statistically significant (Z = − 1.826, p = 0.068). These findings provide preliminary in-vitro phenotypic evidence and support further genomic, structural, and biological characterization.

Article.Title: Dynamically tunable anisotropic Rabi model in circuit QED
Article.Authors: Tabatabaei S.; Zare Rameshti B.; Akbari M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We propose a circuit QED architecture that realizes the full anisotropic Rabi model (ARM) with in-situ tunability of its interaction symmetry. The circuit comprises a superconducting qubit coupled to a resonator through two simultaneous channels: a direct inductive path and a flux-tunable capacitive path mediated by a transmon coupler. By controlling the external magnetic flux, the destructive and constructive interferences between these paths continuously tune the ratio of the Jaynes–Cummings (JC) and anti-Jaynes–Cummings (AJC) couplings, sweeping the system across the entire ARM parameter space from pure JC, through the standard Rabi regime, to pure AJC without requiring rotating-wave approximations or external parametric drives. Furthermore, we identify a coherence sweet spot where the dispersive shift and photon shot-noise dephasing are suppressed. In the pure AJC regime, we demonstrate that the vacuum Rabi splitting vanishes and the Purcell decay rate is strongly mitigated while preserving high qubit readout contrast.

Article.Title: Environmental and personal BTEX exposure and inhalation health risks in healthcare-waste treatment units
Article.Authors: Shojaei A.; Khazaei M.; Rostami R.; Bahrami A.; Samarghandi M.; Samadi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated spatial and operational variations in airborne benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX), personal exposure, and inhalation health risks in eight healthcare-waste treatment units in Hamadan, Iran. A total of 64 area air samples were collected, with 16 samples for each location–condition combination (indoor inactive, indoor post-treatment, perimeter inactive, and perimeter post-treatment), and personal breathing-zone samples were obtained from 16 workers. BTEX was analyzed by gas chromatography, and health risks were estimated using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency framework. Risk estimates were based on 4 h/day of exposure, 300 exposure days/year, and the selected toxicity values. Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations characterized risk variability and sensitivity. Mean total BTEX increased significantly from 178.50 ± 15.56 to 307.57 ± 19.45 µg/m 3 indoors and from 34.54 ± 3.18 to 64.22 ± 6.69 µg/m 3 at perimeter locations. Post-treatment concentrations were positively associated with temperature and the number of autoclave cycles and inversely associated with time since the last cycle and relative humidity (RH). Post meridiem (PM)-shift workers had higher total BTEX exposure, hazard index (HI), and daily inhalation dose than ante meridiem (AM)-shift workers. Aggregate HI remained < 1 in observed and simulated estimates under the specified exposure assumptions. In contrast, benzene and cumulative carcinogenic risks exceeded 1 × 10 –6 but remained below 1 × 10 –4 . Exposure time was the dominant contributor to non-carcinogenic risk variability. These findings support continued occupational monitoring and control of autoclave-related BTEX exposure, particularly during post-treatment activities and prolonged exposure.

Article.Title: Cloud-deployable deep learning for smartphone-based body fluid cytology: a multi-architecture evaluation of YOLO and RT-DETR models
Article.Authors: Chomean S.; Khemtonglang N.; Mukda E.; Sittiphokkhasap N.; Changtrakul Y.; Wongphat K.; Mungmai A.; Tanantong T.; Kaset C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate cytological evaluation of body fluid specimens is essential for diagnosing inflammatory and malignant conditions, yet manual interpretation remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. This study developed and deployed a smartphone-based deep learning framework for multi-class body fluid cell classification integrating object detection, ROI-based classification, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Three hundred Wright–Giemsa–stained cytospin slides, one per patient, were used to generate 7149 smartphone-acquired images, which were annotated and curated into seven predominant cell classes. To reduce data leakage, images were partitioned at the source-photograph (slide-field) level. Five detection architectures (YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLOv11n, YOLOv11n-seg, and RT-DETR) were trained and evaluated on a held-out test set. YOLOv11n-seg achieved the highest mAP@50 (0.840), mAP@50–95 (0.757), and precision (0.772), while YOLOv11n achieved the highest recall (0.823). For YOLOv11n-seg, confusion-matrix macro-F1 and weighted-F1 were 0.720 and 0.730, respectively. Eosinophils, lymphocytes, and neutrophils were among the better-recognized classes, whereas errors were more frequent among monocytes, macrophages, and mesothelial cells. Grad-CAM++ analysis showed that model activation was predominantly centered within cell regions but was interpreted only as supportive model-inspection evidence. A Streamlit web application demonstrated browser-based inference with detection overlays, cell counts, differential composition, and data export. The system should currently be regarded as research, educational, and decision-support prototype rather than a standalone diagnostic device. External validation with patient-level separation, multiple imaging configurations, and broader cell populations is required before clinical application can be considered.

Article.Title: Assessment of information quality and reliability on lumbar disc herniation in short videos from Douyin
Article.Authors: Shen T.; Gong Q.; Hu Y.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lumbar disc herniation is a common cause of neurological symptoms and is associated with substantial decreases in health-related quality of life. Douyin has emerged as a leading social media platform, and an increasing number of users seek information on lumbar disc herniation there. However, the quality of such content remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the informational quality of Douyin short videos related to lumbar disc herniation. Using a cross-sectional design, we retrieved the top 100 videos related to lumbar disc herniation from the Douyin platform on October 17, 2025, using the default ranking. Video quality and reliability were evaluated with the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) tools. Videos were compared across uploader categories, and correlation analyses were conducted to examine factors potentially associated with video quality. Among the 96 videos related to lumbar disc herniation ultimately included in the analysis, the median duration was 71 s. The median counts were 17,240 likes, 9,749 collections, 1,041 comments, and 6,830 shares. Overall information quality was modest, and reliability was low. Differences in GQS and mDISCERN scores across uploader groups were not statistically significant. Correlation analyses indicated that the numbers of likes, comments, collections, and shares were not associated with video quality. The quality of Douyin videos related to lumbar disc herniation warrants improvement. Establishing minimum quality standards for health education videos is essential to ensure that the public receives trustworthy information.

Article.Title: Numerical analysis of hydrodynamic responses to bed roughness in vegetated open channels under subcritical flow conditions
Article.Authors: Mumtaz M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vegetation is widely recognized as an effective nature-based solution for flood mitigation because it increases hydraulic resistance and promotes flow energy dissipation. Although numerous studies have investigated vegetation-induced flow resistance and the influence of bed roughness independently, the coupled effects of vegetation and varying bed roughness under subcritical flow conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a validated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model based on the standard k-epsilon (k-ε) turbulence closure to investigate roughness-vegetation interactions in a vegetated open channel. The numerical model was validated against experimental streamwise velocity profiles under three subcritical flow conditions (Froude number (Fr) = 0.40, 0.44, and 0.48), yielding good agreement with laboratory measurements (correlation coefficient (R) = 0.91–0.96 and root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.0152–0.0259). Following validation, the model was applied to seven subcritical flow conditions (Fr = 0.40–0.65) and four equivalent sand-grain roughness heights (Ks = 0, 7.22, 14.32, and 24.47 mm) to evaluate their influence on velocity distribution, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), turbulent eddy dissipation (TED), and bed shear stress (BSS). The results showed that increasing bed roughness enhanced flow resistance and significantly modified turbulence characteristics within the vegetated channel. Relative to the smooth-bed condition, the maximum velocity decreased by 6%, based on the validated velocity field and the associated k–ε turbulence closure, TKE was found to decreased by 31.4%, and the maximum BSS increased by 70% at the highest roughness height (Ks = 24.47 mm). These findings demonstrate that bed roughness substantially alters vegetation-controlled flow behavior and provide new insight into roughness–vegetation interactions for the design and optimization of sustainable nature-based flood mitigation systems.

Article.Title: Mammalian recombinant production of mature peptide hormone insulin-like 3 (INSL3)
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Metivier R.; Fischer E.; Kruse A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Insulin-like 3 (INSL3) is a peptide hormone important for regulating male reproductive physiology. INSL3 belongs to the insulin/relaxin family of peptide hormones, which are synthesized in cells as prohormones containing B-C-A chains. These hormones mature following proteolytic processing by prohormone convertases to remove C chain and yield mature hormones containing B-A chains that are stabilized by two inter-chain and one intra-chain disulfide bonds. It has been a challenge in the field to produce recombinant active mature INSL3 in large quantities because the enzymes that process INSL3 are unclear. Here we report prohormone convertases PCSK1 and PCSK3, and carboxypeptidase E together process INSL3 prohormone into mature INSL3 and established a simple method to produce recombinant active mature INSL3 in a mammalian expression system using an engineered Fc-fusion approach with co-expression of processing enzymes. Furthermore, we confirmed the molecular weight of the recombinant INSL3 matches the native hormone by intact mass spectrometry, and the recombinant mature INSL3 display full activity (EC 50 = 360 pM) in signaling assays of its cognate receptor RXFP2. Notably, the Fc-fusion INSL3 is also fully active (EC 50 = 609 pM) and has a much higher yield and a simpler production method. Lastly, peptide hormones of this family are conserved prohormone convertase substrates, therefore this method can potentially be applied to the expression and purification of other peptide hormones within this family with some optimization.

Article.Title: Structural equation model of gratitude, two-way social support, and smartphone addiction among nursing students
Article.Authors: Luo J.; Ye T.; Xue C.; Gong F.; Liu X.; Wang H.; Yang Z.; Zhong M.; Yang Z.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Gratitude and social support are considered important intervention factors within the framework of positive psychology. However, their roles in influencing smartphone addiction among nursing students remain insufficiently understood. From a positive psychology perspective, this study aims to further elucidate the underlying mechanisms through which gratitude and two-way social support influence smartphone addiction. A stratified sampling method was employed to conduct an online survey among 1,200 undergraduate nursing students from four medical universities in western China. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, the Mobile Phone Addiction Index, the Gratitude Questionnaire, and the Two-way Social Support Scale. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was performed using AMOS 28.0, and the bias-corrected percentile Bootstrap method was applied to examine mediating effects. Gratitude, two-way social support, receiving social support, and giving social support were all negatively correlated with smartphone addiction. SEM results indicated that two-way social support, receiving social support, and giving social support each independently mediated the relationship between gratitude and smartphone addiction. Further analysis of the sequential mediation effects revealed that the pathway from receiving social support to giving social support was significant, whereas the reverse pathway (giving → receiving) was not. Moreover, when both dimensions were simultaneously included in the model, giving social support remained a significant independent mediator, whereas receiving social support did not show a significant independent mediating effect. Gratitude not only directly predicts smartphone addiction but also indirectly influences it through the mediating role of two-way social support. In the sequential mediation process, both the order and the relative strength of receiving and giving social support should be taken into account. These findings suggest that nursing educators should pay close attention to the directional dynamics and relative contributions of social support when developing interventions targeting smartphone addiction among nursing students.

Article.Title: Unveiling crash risks at left-side diverging areas considering drivers’ physiological and behavioral dynamics: a driving simulation study
Article.Authors: Zeng K.; Ding N.; Sun W.; Zhang H.; Guan H.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Diverging areas are widely-recognized as one of the most accident-prone areas on urban expressways. In particular, left-side diverging areas contradict conventional right-side ones in terms of driving habits, driving expectancy, and microscopic maneuvers, leading to sever traffic uncertainty and crash risks. However, to the best of our knowledge, we are still quite ignorant of the characteristics and variations of the driving behaviors at the left-side diverging areas, and the critical factors contributing to crash risks there. To this end, this study aims to investigate crash risks at urban expressway diverging areas and identify contributing factors. To achieve this, a series of driving simulation experiments was conducted, and 3444 traffic conflict cases were identified via the indicator of time to collision (TTC) and recorded along with driving behavioral, physiological characteristics, and personal traits, and the deceleration lane length was also included. A multinomial logit model was employed to explore relationships between identified crash risks and the above factors. The results show that fewer lane changes and longer deceleration lane lengths can effectively mitigate crash risks in the left-side diverging areas. Driving experience, pupil dilation, fixation duration, and saccade duration show significant positive effects on crash risk probabilities in left-side diverging areas. The findings provide insights into the in-depth understanding of the driving behaviors and crash risks at left-side diverging areas, which is supposed to benefit to develop and implement more effective approaches to improve traffic safety of urban expressway.

Article.Title: Determinants of multidimensional child health outcomes among infants in an urban poor setting in Makassar, Indonesia
Article.Authors: BaharuddinNur R.; Wijaya E.; Irmayanti I.; Wahyuni A.; Ansariadi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Child malnutrition remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. However, the factors associated with multidimensional child health outcomes (MCHO), defined as the coexistence of anthropometric failure and infectious morbidity, remain poorly understood. Examining these conditions jointly is important because undernutrition and infection are biologically interconnected, frequently coexist, and together impose a greater burden on child health than either condition alone. This study examined maternal and child determinants of MCHO in a cross-sectional analysis nested within an ongoing birth cohort of 142 mother–child pairs (children aged 6–13 months) participating in an ongoing birth cohort in an urban poor setting in Makassar, Indonesia. Nutritional status was assessed using World Health Organization anthropometric indicators, and associations were estimated using Firth penalised-likelihood logistic regression with sensitivity analyses based on modified Poisson regression and E-values. MCHO affected 14.79% of children, while stunting, wasting, underweight, and recent infectious morbidity affected 23.94%, 19.72%, 11.97%, and 30.99%, respectively. Caesarean delivery was independently associated with MCHO, though estimated from a model with a modest events-per-variable ratio (AOR 3.09, 95% CI 1.18–8.10, p = 0.022; adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 2.60, 95% CI 1.17–5.77; E-value 5.63). Recent infectious morbidity was independently associated with wasting (AOR 2.57, 95% CI 1.07–6.16, p = 0.034; aPR 2.01, 95% CI 1.03–3.93; E-value 4.58). Unimproved drinking water showed consistent positive associations with MCHO, stunting, and wasting (all p < 0.10). These findings highlight the associations of maternal, infectious, and environmental factors with child health and underscore the need for integrated interventions that address nutrition, infection prevention, maternal and child health, and household environmental conditions simultaneously.

Article.Title: Pulse duration and pulse repetition frequency shape cavitation dynamics and volumetric liquefaction by histotripsy in a fibrous tissue-mimicking phantom
Article.Authors: Nanda Kumar Y.; Wang Y.; Kreider W.; Han Q.; Liu J.; Vlaisavljevich E.; Schade G.; Maxwell A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Histotripsy is a focused ultrasound technique that mechanically liquefies tissue through cavitation bubble activity and has shown promise for noninvasive tumor ablation. However, treating fibrous, mechanically robust tissues remains challenging, and the influence of pulse parameters on cavitation dynamics and liquefaction efficiency in these tissues is not well understood. Here, we systematically investigated the combined effects of pulse duration and pulse repetition frequency (PRF) on cavitation behavior and lesion formation in a fibrous tissue-mimicking double-network hydrogel. Pulse duration and PRF were varied over four orders of magnitude while maintaining a constant 1% duty cycle. High-speed photographic imaging, shear wave elastography (SWE), B-mode ultrasound, and open-top light-sheet (OTLS) microscopy were used to relate cavitation behavior to phantom damage and liquefaction. The 1-cycle condition produced the largest bubble cloud area at longer exposure times, while the 1 and 10-cycle conditions exhibited higher frame-to-frame correlation and greater spatial persistence. In contrast, longer-pulse, low-PRF exposures (≥ 100 cycles) produced more localized cavitation and contiguous lesion formation. Among the tested parameters, 1,000 -cycle pulses at 10 Hz yielded the highest volumetric liquefaction rates. In contrast, short-pulse, high-PRF conditions generated substantial total damage but little to no fully liquefied volume. These findings show that pulse duration and PRF shape cavitation behavior and liquefaction in this fibrous tissue-mimicking model.

Article.Title: PPO-based QoS-aware resource management for multi-class URLLC and eMBB slices in NR/NR-U HetNets
Article.Authors: Elmosilhy N.; Elmesalawy M.; El-Haleem A.; Ibrahim I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exploiting new radio (NR) and NR-unlicensed (NR-U) technologies within a multi-RAT heterogeneous network can leverage traffic congestion and enhance overall capacity. thus, an optimization problem is introduced and formulated to maximize users’ quality of service (QoS) satisfaction by maximizing data rates while satisfying critical latency requirements. To accommodate heterogeneous URLLC services, multiple traffic classes with different delay requirements are considered, and a scalable numerology mini-slot technique is employed to satisfy the QoS requirements of each traffic class. An iterative framework is presented that combines regret matching learning for user association considering coexisting Wi-Fi users and a proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm which determines the optimal resource distribution based on a predefined numerology value for each slice. A logarithmic utility function is presented to enforce proportional fairness while satisfying each user’s service requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an overall QoS satisfaction rate of 74% significantly outperforming benchmark architectures including NR-only, NR-Wi-Fi, NR-NR-U, and LWA. Furthermore, comparative evaluations against other reinforcement learning algorithms—such as Q-network, deep Q-network (DQN), double DQN, dueling DQN, and actor-critic confirm stability and performance of the proposed PPO-based approach.

Article.Title: Decomposing deep neural network-brain representational similarity reveals distinct sources across the human visual hierarchy
Article.Authors: Li X.; Zhang F.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep neural networks predict neural responses across the visual hierarchy, yet published alignment scores do not reveal whether this correspondence reflects learned representations, architectural inductive biases, low-level image statistics, or categorical structure. We decompose DNN-brain alignment into four sources using variance partitioning on representational similarity analysis, applied to 7T fMRI from eight participants viewing approximately 10,000 natural images. The composition of alignment shifts systematically along the cortical hierarchy: in primary visual cortex, architecture and low-level statistics account for 46% of total explained variance, whereas in high-level visual cortex model-specific learned representations dominate, reaching 68% in the parahippocampal place area. The same framework applied to language models processing image captions reveals that alignment is strongly model-dependent: a sentence embedding model contributes 51% unique variance in higher visual cortex, whereas an autoregressive model contributes only 4%, with the remainder attributable to surface text statistics and category structure. Across nine models, alignment scores varied substantially in composition. Decomposing alignment into its sources is necessary before a score can be interpreted as evidence for convergent processing.

Article.Title: Assessing urban water consumption dynamics using machine learning and spatial variables under normal and pandemic conditions: A case study
Article.Authors: Sabzchi-Dehkharghani H.; Majnooni-Heris A.; Fakherifard A.; Safari M.; Shakouri B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study developed a spatially explicit framework to estimate household water consumption (HWC) and the number of household water subscribers in each consumption class (NHWSCC) using land surface temperature (LST), land value, and elevation. Three machine-learning (ML) models were applied: symbolic regression (SR), an extreme learning machine (ELM), and an ELM hybridized with the artificial bee colony algorithm (ELM-ABC). The spatial predictors supported the generation of HWC maps for normal and pandemic-period conditions in Tabriz, Iran. Model performance was generally more stable at grid resolutions of 600–700 m, although the achievable resolution varied among consumption classes. The models captured spatial patterns for many low- and intermediate-consumption classes but performed less well for the highest-consumption categories. SR sensitivity analysis identified LST as the most influential predictor of NHWSCC. Differences in predictor sensitivity between the study periods suggest changes in the relationships between spatial characteristics and household water use. Observed annual consumption increased in lower-land-value areas and decreased in higher-land-value areas during the pandemic period. These findings support the use of readily available spatial proxies for within-city water-consumption mapping, while recognizing the limitations of the predictors and validation design.

Article.Title: On the use of machine learning in damage identification of offshore jacket wind turbine: a virtual case study
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Pugliese F.; Christie J.; Titurus B.; De Risi R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a high-fidelity, simulation-based Finite Element – Operational Modal Analysis – Machine Learning (FE–OMA–ML) framework for damage diagnosis of a jacket-type offshore wind turbine support structure. Finite-element-simulated acceleration responses are processed using Enhanced Frequency-Domain Decomposition (EFDD) to identify modal frequencies and damping ratios, which are then used as machine-learning input features. A progressive stiffness-degradation dataset covering 13 structural conditions and multiple sensor configurations is constructed to represent the gradual nature of in-service deterioration. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of exact component-level classification, binary damage detection, layer-level localisation, ensemble-vote-based ranking, response-noise robustness, and sensor-layout optimisation. The reliability of the extracted modal features is further examined through FE–EFDD consistency checks of natural frequencies and mode shapes. The results show that the workflow retains useful hierarchical and ranked diagnostic information across different degradation levels, sensor layouts, and noisy-response conditions. However, exact component localisation becomes more sensitive as data complexity and measurement noise increase. The analysis also supports identifying efficient sensor configurations that preserve useful diagnostic performance. The proposed framework therefore provides a structured numerical strategy for evaluating modal-feature-based damage diagnosis of offshore jacket support structures.

Article.Title: Machine learning prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement after TAVI
Article.Authors: Shan Y.; Liu P.; Zhao Z.; Wang H.; Lai J.; Qiu X.; Li X.; Wang S.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The fate of mitral regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation is highly heterogeneous, and accurate preoperative prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based predictive model for regurgitation improvement following transcatheter aortic valve implantation. This single-centre retrospective study included 324 patients with moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation who underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation between 2019 and 2024 (development cohort) and 120 patients in 2025 (temporal validation cohort). Eleven machine learning algorithms were compared. Feature selection was performed using a dual-screening strategy combining the Boruta algorithm and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis was used to interpret predictor contributions to model predictions. Six variables were identified as robust predictors: functional mitral regurgitation, interventricular septal thickness, atrial fibrillation, left ventricular ejection fraction, surgical approach, and left atrial diameter. In temporal validation, logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.788 (95% CI 0.694–0.883), followed by Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression (AUC, 0.787; 95% CI 0.693–0.882) and CatBoost (AUC, 0.778; 95% CI 0.683–0.872). Interventricular septal thickness showed a significant nonlinear association with mitral regurgitation improvement, with approximately 1.1 cm suggested as a provisional breakpoint in an exploratory analysis. This machine learning model enables individualized prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement after transcatheter aortic valve implantation using readily available preoperative parameters. The identification of interventricular septal thickness as a nonlinear predictor with a potentially clinically relevant threshold suggests promise for preoperative risk stratification. Nevertheless, because both the development and temporal validation cohorts were derived from a single centre, these findings are preliminary and require prospective multicentre validation before any clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Integrated classical/quantum–classical neural networks, DFT, and experiments for predicting bandgap and color of CrxSbxTi1−2xO2 yellow-orange pigments
Article.Authors: Vaselnia S.; Aminian M.; Banadaki R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The accurate prediction of the bandgap ( $$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$ ) and color of ceramic pigments is of considerable importance in materials science research. In this work, we investigate the $$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$ and color of Cr $$_x$$ Sb $$_x$$ Ti $$_{1-2x}$$ O $$_2$$ rutile pigments by combining experimental, density functional theory (DFT and DFT+ U ) calculations, and neural network approaches. The main novelty of this study is the application of classical/hybrid quantum–classical neural networks to the prediction of pigment color and $$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$ . Cr/Sb co-doped rutile pigment was synthesized and characterized, and the electronic structures of undoped and doped $${\textrm{TiO}}_{2}$$ were analyzed using first-principles calculations. In parallel, classical and hybrid quantum–classical neural network models were developed and trained on datasets compiled from the Materials Project database and literature-reported rutile-based pigments. The models successfully captured the trends in $$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$ and chromaticity, with the hybrid architectures providing slightly improved predictive performance and more consistent agreement with experiment. Overall, this work demonstrates an effective framework that links experiment, first-principles calculations, and classical/quantum–classical neural networks for predicting key properties of ceramic pigments, and it points toward the future use of fully quantum machine learning models for materials design.

Article.Title: Generation of a recombinant, antibiotic resistance gene-free Leishmania tarentolae strain as a live vaccine platform
Article.Authors: Taheri T.; Davarpanah E.; Santi A.; Gholami E.; Seyed N.; Späth G.; Rafati S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Live vaccines based on non-pathogenic microorganisms are among the most effective vaccine platforms. L. tarentolae , a non-pathogenic protozoan for humans, is a valuable expression system capable of producing eukaryotic proteins while preserving their native structure and post-translational modifications. Leishmaniasis, a sand fly–borne disease with diverse clinical forms, remains a significant health concern. Sand fly salivary proteins such as PpSP15 and PsSP9 have been identified as promising protective vaccine candidates. However, the common use of antibiotic resistance genes as selection markers in recombinant strains raises safety concerns for human applications. In this study, an antibiotic marker–free system was developed by removing the neomycin resistance gene (Neo r ) from the pLEXSY-Neo r vector to construct pLEXSY-noNeo r . The PpSP15-T2A-PsSP9 fragment was cloned into this modified vector, and CRISPR-Cas9 technology was used to integrate the genes into the SSU locus of L. tarentolae . Successful gene insertion and expression were confirmed at DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Importantly, mutant parasites showed infectivity comparable to wild-type strains. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generating antibiotic resistance–free transgenic L. tarentolae , supporting its potential as a safe live vaccine platform.

Article.Title: Stability-aware social welfare optimization for renewable power dispatch with virtual synchronous generators
Article.Authors: Maity S.; Shrivastav A.; Chanda S.; Kumar P.; Dutta S.; De A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the last few decades, there has been a considerable increase in the implementation of renewable generation technologies within power systems, owing to the fact that there is a need to provide sustainable and environment- friendly options for generating electricity, as opposed to the traditional modes. However, the unpredictable nature of the renewable generation makes it necessary to implement proper demand management techniques. Demand response-based rescheduling algorithms such as Social Welfare Maximisation are thus gaining attention for mitigating this problem in the dispatch planning stage of power system. However, for very short or real time equilibrium system has to rely on inherent inertia. Conventional thermal power plants generate considerable rotational inertia using synchronous machines; therefore, they can deal with real-time disturbances because of load fluctuations, generation variations, and faults in the electrical system. To address these challenges of rich Renewable power systems, the Virtual Synchronous Generator’s theories has proven to be a potential solution. The virtual inertia and damping parameters are software-defined, but constrained by converter power ratings and control loop bandwidth. Also, excessively high virtual inertia settings can cause slow dynamic response or instability under fast disturbances. This paper revisits the VSG approach and intended to extend the range of controllability of VSGs by additional closed loop control circuit, enhancing the inherent software inertia adaptively, and thereby improving transient stability of VSG augmented renewable systems. Further, the renewable model thus developed with VSG was used in a benchmark IEEE 30 bus system with demand response based Social Welfare allied optimisation algorithm which demonstrated improvement of the values of Critical Clearing Time during worst possible contingencies and electrical faults of the system. The DEQPSO algorithm, based on the combination of the Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm and the Quantum Particle Swarm Optimisation (QPSO) algorithm, is ideal for solving the nonlinear optimization problem investigated in this research, where not only static operating constraints but also transient stability constraints are involved. In this respect, the current research aims to incorporate renewable energy sources with the VSG controller in the power system in order to improve its transient stability and reliability.

Article.Title: Controlled water immersion as a post-harvest strategy for the valorization of underripe Coffea arabica L. fruits
Article.Authors: de Souza G.; Zagato N.; Júlio A.; dos Santos M.; dos W.; Gomes S.; Moreli A.; Menini L.; Pereira L.
Article.Abstract: Underripe coffee fruits are frequently associated with reduced beverage quality; however, they represent an underutilized fraction with potential for valorization through post-harvest processing. This study evaluated the physicochemical, structural, chemical, and sensory changes in underripe Coffea arabica L. fruits subjected to different water-immersion regimes, aiming to identify processing conditions capable of improving the technological use of this fraction. Underripe fruits were subjected to static immersion, immersion with daily water renewal, or a combined regime consisting of daily water renewal up to 96 h followed by static immersion, for periods ranging from 24 to 192 h. After immersion, two fractions were evaluated: underripe fruits successfully hulled during processing and fruits that remained unhulled because of their greater resistance to mechanical hulling. Physicochemical properties of the immersion water, bioactive compounds, visual characteristics, multivariate relationships, and beverage sensory quality were assessed. Static immersion resulted in a marked accumulation of soluble electrolytes in the medium, with electrical conductivity increasing from approximately 2,000 µS cm⁻¹ at 24 h to more than 7,000 µS cm⁻¹ at 192 h, whereas daily water renewal maintained substantially lower values. The pH of the static system increased from approximately 4.0 to 5.7 over the immersion period. Caffeine, trigonelline, and chlorogenic acid showed treatment- and time-dependent variations, indicating that water management and fruit structure affected the relative distribution of these compounds during processing. Hulled underripe coffees showed sensory scores ranging from 79.00 ± 3.60 to 81.21 ± 0.44, with treatment means of 80.44–80.69, whereas unhulled coffees ranged from 78.03 ± 0.89 to 79.47 ± 1.08, with treatment means of 78.53–78.79. No significant differences among immersion times were detected within each treatment ( p > 0.05). The ripe-coffee control scored 80.75 ± 0.65. Overall, controlled water immersion, particularly when associated with water renewal and hulling, maintained sensory quality while modulating physicochemical and compositional characteristics of underripe coffee fruits, supporting its potential as a post-harvest strategy for the technological valorization of this underutilized fraction.

Article.Title: Solar-driven MOF-derived Co–N–C@TiO₂ direct Z-scheme heterostructure for efficient antibiotic degradation via enhanced interfacial charge transfer
Article.Authors: El-Sawaf A.; Nassar A.; Mohamed M.; Ali A.; Mubarak M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of efficient and sustainable photocatalysts for solar-driven environmental remediation remains an important challenge in the elimination of emerging water contaminants. In this study, a MOF-derived Co–N–C@TiO₂ direct Z-scheme heterostructure was rationally engineered to enhance visible-light utilization and interfacial charge transfer for tetracycline degradation. The composite was synthesized through pyrolysis of a cobalt-based zeolitic imidazolate framework to produce a conductive Co–N–C scaffold, followed by sol–gel deposition of TiO₂ nanoparticles. Structural and physicochemical characterizations (XRD, FTIR, BET, SEM/TEM, XPS, UV–Vis DRS, PL, and Mott–Schottky analyses) confirmed the formation of a porous architecture with a high specific surface area (176.4 m² g⁻¹), uniformly dispersed TiO₂ nanodomains, enhanced visible-light absorption, and efficient suppression of electron–hole recombination. Under visible-light irradiation, the Co–N–C@TiO₂ photocatalyst achieved 93.7 ± 0.8% tetracycline degradation within 60 min, accompanied by a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.054 ± 0.001 min⁻¹ and 67.5 ± 2.3% total organic carbon removal, indicating substantial mineralization. The superior photocatalytic performance is attributed to the synergistic interaction between the conductive MOF-derived carbon framework, Co–Nₓ active sites, and the direct Z-scheme heterojunction, which facilitates rapid charge separation while preserving strong redox capability. By efficiently utilizing solar energy for advanced water treatment, this work provides a sustainable photocatalytic strategy that contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

Article.Title: Source apportionment and health risk assessment of PAHs in commercial fish from Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alluhayb A.; Algreiby A.; Younis A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in ten commercially important fish species from the Al-Jubail industrial coastline, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia. Muscle tissue concentrations were quantified by GC-MS. Source apportionment used diagnostic molecular ratios, positive matrix factorization (PMF), and hierarchical clustering, and health risk was assessed separately for adults and children. Total Σ16PAH concentrations ranged from 481.99 to 758.82 ng/g wet weight, with Scomberomorus commerson carrying the highest burden. Pelagic species accumulated consistently more PAHs than demersal fish, suggesting atmospheric deposition and surface microlayer enrichment are the dominant exposure routes here. Low-molecular-weight compounds made up 55.16% of the total profile. PMF modeling traced most of the contamination to pyrogenic combustion (53–67%), with petrogenic inputs making up the rest (28–42%). Cluster analysis grouped the species by trophic level, matching the bioaccumulation patterns already observed. Benzo[a]pyrene concentrations exceeded EU regulatory limits for thermally processed seafood. The non-carcinogenic hazard index came in above the acceptable threshold for adults (2.07–3.18) and, more sharply, for children (4.52–6.95). Incremental lifetime cancer risk for benzo[a]pyrene ranged from 7.73 × 10⁻⁵ to 1.52 × 10⁻⁴ with values exceeding the 10⁻⁴ acceptable threshold for several species, indicating a potential carcinogenic concern that warrants proactive management consideration. Taken together, this points to meaningful dietary exposure risk in this population, particularly for children, and supports calls for stricter industrial emission controls and routine seafood monitoring along heavily industrialized coasts.

Article.Title: Influence of seed sources and seeding rates on bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) productivity in Banja District, Northwestern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Aleminew A.; Achenef E.; Azmeraw Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bread wheat productivity in Northwestern Ethiopia is extremely low due to poor-quality seeds and inappropriate seed rates. To address these problems, field and laboratory experiments were conducted during the 2024 cropping season in Banja District to evaluate the effects of seed sources and rates. Seed quality was evaluated in the laboratory using a Completely Randomized Design with three replications. The field experiment employed a factorial randomized complete block design with three replications, including four seed rates (125, 150, 175, and 200 kg ha⁻¹) and three seed sources: Adet Research Center, Ediget Bandnet Cooperative, and farmer-saved seeds of the Danda’a variety. Laboratory results indicated that seed sources significantly influenced by initial seed quality of bread wheat. Seeds from Adet Research Center showed the highest physical purity (99.97%), standard germination (98.33%), thousand kernel weights (41.20 g), seedling vigor index I (27.18), and seedling vigor index II (0.02). In the field experiment, grain yield was highly significantly affected by both seed sources and rates. The highest grain yield of 5.39 t ha⁻¹ was achieved with Adet Research Center seeds, while 200 kg ha⁻¹ seed rate produced 5.37 t ha⁻¹. The combination of Adet Research Center seed with 200 kg ha⁻¹ contributed the maximum net benefit of 103,480.30 Ethiopian Birr ha⁻¹ and a marginal rate of return of 582.9%. These results suggest that using 200 kg ha⁻¹ of Danda’a variety seeds from Adet Research Center can substantially improve wheat productivity. Further verification across multiple varieties, locations, and years is recommended to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Occupational stress and associated factors among industrial workers across industries in Markazi Province Iran
Article.Authors: Zokaei M.; Falahati M.; Parvari A.; Karsidani S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Occupational stress is an important psychosocial hazard influencing the physical and mental health of employees. This study assessed the levels and determinants of occupational stress among industrial workers in Markazi Province, Iran one of the country’s major industrial regions. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 2023–2024 among 1,102 employees from four sectors: metal, construction, chemical, and food–pharmaceutical industries. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering demographic, occupational, socioeconomic, and lifestyle variables, along with the validated HSE Occupational Stress Indicator Tool (35 items, seven subscales). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS v26 and R version 4.5.0, including descriptive tests, ANOVA, and multiple regression analysis ( p < 0.05). The final analysis included 1,102 participants (mean age 39 ± 7.5 years; 73% male). The mean total HSE score was 120.19 ± 14.11, with significant differences observed across industrial sectors ( p = 0.022). Several HSE dimensions also differed significantly between industries, particularly role, communication, control, and demand. Significant differences were observed across sectors ( p < 0.001), with chemical and construction workers reporting higher demands and lower control compared to the metal and food sectors. The multiple regression model explained 11.6% of the variance in stress scores (R 2 = 0.116). Income satisfaction was negatively associated with HSE scores (B = − 0.186, p < 0.001), inadequate job control (B = 0.225, p < 0.001). Occupational stress was generally low but varied across industries. Findings indicate that stress is shaped mainly by organizational and economic factors such as workload, job control, and fairness of rewards rather than individual characteristics. Strengthening participation, welfare, and supportive supervision, alongside periodic stress monitoring and mental health programs, can effectively enhance resilience and productivity among industrial workers.

Article.Title: HQDeTransformer: hybrid quantum denoising Transformer for time series forecasting
Article.Authors: Jeong S.; Moon K.; Hwang W.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is critical for enhancing the reliability and safety of battery-powered systems, especially in electric vehicles. While recent machine learning approaches such as Transformers and recurrent neural networks have shown promising results, their deployment in resource-constrained environments is limited due to high computational costs and large model sizes. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid quantum-classical denoising Transformer (HQDeTransformer) architecture that integrates variational quantum circuits (VQCs) and quantum-enhanced attention mechanisms into a Transformer-based framework. The proposed HQDeTransformer employs a hybrid quantum denoising autoencoder to mitigate noise in capacity degradation sequences and utilizes hybrid quantum-classical neural networks to construct lightweight multi-head attention and feedforward blocks. Experimental evaluations on the NASA and CALCE benchmark datasets demonstrate that HQDeTransformer achieves superior performance compared to conventional machine learning models and quantum machine learning models, while reducing the number of trainable parameters. Furthermore, the use of angle-amplitude quantum embeddings and deeper quantum layers contributes to enhanced generalization and expressivity. These results highlight the potential of hybrid quantum-classical models for lightweight, accurate, and noise-resilient RUL prediction in practical battery management systems.

Article.Title: Advanced machine learning framework for hole quality prediction and optimization in polycarbonate AWJD
Article.Authors: Bharani Chandar J.; Rathinasuriyan C.; Lenin N.; Sivakumar M.; Singh R.; Salunkhe S.; GaneshKumar P.; Palanisamy R.; Nasr E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abrasive waterjet drilling of polymers is difficult to optimize owing to nonlinear interactions and conflicting performance requirements. This study suggests combining experimental, ML models, multi-objective optimization, and statistical validation to improve polycarbonate drilling performance. A full factorial design was used to vary water pressure (250–350 MPa), standoff distance (1.5–2.5 mm), and traversal rate (300–500 mm/min) in 125 tests. DE and drilling rate were performance responses. Analysis of variance showed water pressure and standoff distance were the principal variables affecting the hole diameter error (DE) and drilling rate (DR). Four machine learning models, namely XGBoost, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and AdaBoost Regressor were built in the Anaconda-based Python environment. The Random Forest model demonstrated high reliability in capturing complex process behavior, with R² = 0.92263 for DE and 0.90471 for DR. Random Forest was utilized as a stand-in paradigm for multi-objective optimization using the Grey Wolf optimizer, Whale optimization algorithm, and Arithmetic optimization algorithm. With Whale optimization method, Water pressure = 350 MPa, Standoff distance = 2.5 mm, and Traverse rate = 300 mm/min produced the highest performance with decreased DE (0.1238) and improved DR (2.0450). The Friedman test ( p < 0.001) and post-hoc analysis show that Whale optimization method outperforms Grey Wolf and Arithmetic optimization algorithms. The results of confirmation tests with the optimized parameters for the WOA showed good agreement with the predicted results, within a range of ± 3%.

Article.Title: Novel intercalation of MnPS3 with polypyrrole and effect on magnetic and optical properties
Article.Authors: El-Meligi A.; Abdel-karim A.; Farghaly T.; Nassar S.
Article.Abstract: This research focuses on the novel intercalation of the polypyrrole (ppy) to the layered nanomaterial manganese phosphorus trisulphide (MnPS 3 ) and its effect on the magnetic and optical properties. Synthesis of MnPS 3 was processed by applying novel steps to run the solid-state reaction of the pure elements under vacuum at 650 °C. The intercalation of ppy was run using different percentages of ppy under stirring for 20 h. at 60 °C. The green powder of MnPS 3 was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), infrared spectroscopy (IR), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM-EDX). The magnetic and optical properties of MnPS 3 were tested before intercalation and intercalation with ppy.XRD shows clear intercalation of ppy due to appearing of new hkl phases, and disappearance of the hkl (001) phases of MnPS 3 . IR measurements reveal the intercalation of ppy due to splitting of the main stretching peak of MnPS 3 to 602 and 555 cm − 1 , and the presence of the recognized peaks of the ppy. SEM-EDX measurements shows the layered structure morphology of MnPS 3 , and the presence of the ppy intercalated in the interlayer space by detecting the main elements, C, H. Magnetic behavior of the MnPS 3 isparamagnetic, and the intercalated compound MnPS 3 -ppy shows the paramagnetic behavior. The magnetic parameters of MnPS 3 , such as Hc, Ms and Mr, have changed after intercalation with ppy. The optical properties of MnPS 3 have been affected due to intercalation of ppy where the increase of optical band energy after intercalation indicates strong interaction between MnPS 3 and ppy.

Article.Title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
Article.Authors: Kasada M.; Shinohara N.; Tanaka K.; Fukasawa R.; Tanabe A.; Yamakawa H.; Abe H.; Abe M.; Araki H.; Enoki T.; Fukuoka M.; Fukuzawa K.; Goto R.; Hamaguchi M.; Hamaoka H.; Hasegawa N.; Henmi Y.; Hori M.; Igari T.; Ishii M.; Ito A.; Kadota T.; Kajita T.; Kasai A.; Kishida O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). Importantly, the strength of the gradient varied seasonally, with steeper slopes observed during warm seasons compared to winter. This seasonal restructuring of LDGs may reflect the increased occurrence of tropical vagrant fish, rather than the commonly assumed pattern of seasonal migration. These transient taxa may temporarily elevate observed richness at higher latitudes but do not persist through winter conditions. As a result, short-term increases in biodiversity under warming conditions may not necessarily indicate stable ecological change. Our findings highlight that eDNA-based richness metrics can capture both persistent community structure and transient ecological processes, underscoring the need for careful interpretation of biodiversity patterns in a changing climate.

Article.Title: Spatial estimation of standardized precipitation index based drought severity across Türkiye using machine learning models
Article.Authors: Atasever U.; Taşkanat T.; Erol A.; Köylü Ü.; Citakoglu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable spatial estimation of extreme drought intensity represented by the minimum SPI value is essential for water resources management under increasing climate variability. However, conventional assessments often rely on station-based temporal indices, providing limited representation of spatial heterogeneity and topographic controls. This study developed a machine learning framework to estimate the spatial distribution of extreme drought intensity represented by the minimum SPI value across Türkiye using long-term precipitation records from 102 meteorological stations. For each station and SPI accumulation period, extreme drought intensity was represented by the minimum (most negative) SPI value observed over the 1935–2024 record; this minimum SPI value was used as the machine-learning target, while latitude, longitude, and elevation were used as geographic predictors. Seven machine learning models were evaluated; among them, GBM yielded the highest accuracy (R 2 = 0.991, RMSE = 0.007), followed by XGBoost and CatBoost. These results indicate that ensemble tree-based methods reproduce the observed spatial pattern of extreme drought intensity across the station network with high accuracy; establishing predictive skill at unmonitored locations would require evaluation under a station-grouped partition. Furthermore, feature importance and SHAP analyses showed that spatial predictors (longitude, latitude, and elevation) were substantially more influential than the time-scale variable, although their relative importance varied among the evaluated models. This framework offers a robust tool for interpretable and spatially explicit drought monitoring in topographically complex regions.

Article.Title: Synthesis, characterization, biological evaluation, and computational studies of novel metal complexes derived from 1-isopropyl-1H-benzimidazole-2-carbaldehyde and tri-substituted imidazole
Article.Authors: Almohyawi A.; Abdou A.; Al-Rooqi M.; Samman S.; Alsimaree A.; Alkubaysi S.; Moussa Z.; Timoumi A.; Jassas R.; Ahmed S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Two novel Ni(II) and Cu(II) mixed-ligand complexes, NiMBIM and CuMBIM, were successfully synthesized using 1-isopropyl-1H-benzimidazole-2-carbaldehyde (MB) and 2-(4,5-diphenyl-1H-imidazol-2-yl)phenol (IM). Their structures were characterized via CHN elemental analysis, UV–Vis and FT-IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, molar conductivity, magnetic susceptibility, and thermal analysis. NiMBIM adopts a tetrahedral geometry, while CuMBIM forms a distorted octahedral structure with coordinated chloride and water. Conductivity measurements indicated that NiMBIM behaves as a 1:1 electrolyte in ethanol (43.15 μS cm 2 mol −1 ), whereas CuMBIM is non-electrolytic (9.06 μS cm 2 ol −1 ). Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed the presence of one coordinated water molecule in CuMBIM and none in NiMBIM. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations revealed that CuMBIM possesses the smallest HOMO–LUMO gap (1.61 eV), highest softness (σ = 0.62), and electrophilicity (ω = 9.58), indicating superior reactivity. TD-DFT simulations of the electronic spectra showed good agreement with experimental UV–Vis data, supporting the proposed structures and transition assignments. Biological evaluations demonstrated promising in vitro antimicrobial activity for both complexes, with CuMBIM exhibiting the highest inhibition against Klebsiella pneumoniae (26.00 ± 0.14 mm) and Candida albicans (24.30 ± 0.15 mm). Anti-inflammatory assays confirmed effective inhibition, with IC50 values of 30.25 µg/µL for CuMBIM and 32.88 µg/µL for NiMBIM. Molecular docking studies targeting FabH-CoA (PDB: 1HNJ) and COX-2 (PDB: 1CX2) corroborated these results, showing CuMBIM achieves the strongest binding affinities (− 8.80 and − 10.90 kcal/mol) through key hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions, consistent with its enhanced in vitro biological activity.

Article.Title: Experimental context determines repeated UVB responses and photoageing-associated phenotypes in human dermal fibroblasts
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Ye H.; Jia H.; Ren S.; Cui Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repeated ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure of dermal fibroblasts is widely used to investigate photoaging-associated cellular stress responses; however, substantial variation in experimental design limits reproducibility and complicates comparison across studies. Here, We systematically evaluated how experimental context—including seeding density, cumulative UVB dose, irradiation schedule and experimental time—collectively shapes repeated UVB responses in human dermal fibroblasts. Full-factorial analysis demonstrated that cumulative UVB dose and experimental time accounted for the largest proportion of biological variation, while Dose × Day, Dose × Schedule, and Dose × Density interactions were also substantial. Experimental observations confirmed that identical cumulative UVB doses produced distinct proliferative outcomes depending on irradiation schedule, culture density and recovery time. Experimental validation showed that initial cell density reshaped the apparent dose-response relationship, with low-density cultures exhibiting greater UVB sensitivity but reduced experimental stability, whereas intermediate-density cultures revealed distinct low- and high-response states. Furthermore, equivalent cumulative UVB doses delivered under different irradiation schedules produced distinct proliferative responses, demonstrating that recovery interval modifies cumulative UVB responses independently of total dose. A representative repeated-UVB condition reproduced canonical photoaging-associated phenotypes, including recurrent oxidative stress, impaired migration, extracellular matrix remodeling, and activation of stress- and senescence-associated transcriptional programs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that repeated UVB responses are determined not only by cumulative UVB dose but also by experimental context. Considering seeding density, experimental time, and recovery dynamics alongside UVB dose provides a practical framework for improving the reproducibility, interpretation, and comparison of fibroblast-based photoaging models.

Article.Title: Deep binarized photonic reservoir computing for ultrafast multimedia signal processing
Article.Authors: Iqbal M.; Alassir M.; Marsal N.; Rontani D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We present a deep photonic neural network architecture based on ultrafast binary optical modulation using a digital micromirror device (DMD), optical scattering in a random medium, high-speed photodetection with a CMOS sensor, and a time-multiplexed multilayer structure. Operating at Gigabit-per-second (Gb/s) optical information throughput, our system based on the reservoir computing (RC) framework achieves state-of-the-art performance across various multimedia tasks, including video, image and speech recognition. We show that the careful optimization of key physical intra- and inter-layer hyperparameters can significantly enhance the deep photonic RC system’s ability to extract relevant temporal and spatial features by balancing memory retention and dynamical response of individual layers. This approach paves the way for highly scalable hierarchical photonic reservoir computing systems for high-throughput real-time multimedia signal processing.

Article.Title: A memory-adaptive Karma–Dharma optimizer for global optimization and VLSI design
Article.Authors: Moodi H.; Razavi S.; Hajiaghaei-Keshteli M.; Hadavandi E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While many recent metaheuristics rely on elaborate biological or physical metaphors, their underlying mathematical mechanics often remain obscured. This paper introduces the Karma–Dharma Optimizer (KDO), a transparent, memory-adaptive metaheuristic designed for continuous and constrained engineering optimization. KDO couples two complementary phases: a memory-guided exploration phase that utilizes a historical success archive (the Dharma operator) and a structured exploitation phase (the Karma operator). An adaptive stagnation-recovery mechanism, termed Nirvana Reset, is further incorporated to help the search escape locally stagnant regions. The global search capability and dimensional scalability of KDO are extensively evaluated on the CEC-2017 and CEC-2022 benchmark suites across dimensions up to $$D=50$$ . Furthermore, KDO is applied to four constrained analog, RF, and VLSI circuit design problems: a two-stage Miller operational amplifier, an RF CMOS cascode LNA, a low phase-noise LC-VCO, and a 6T FinFET SRAM cell. These circuits are evaluated under both closed-form analytical surrogates and an automated, physics-driven MATLAB–ngspice-in-the-loop simulation framework accounting for process–voltage–temperature (PVT) variations and Monte Carlo yield constraints. Non-parametric statistical analyses alongside component-wise ablation studies, reveal a problem-dependent performance profile for KDO. It achieves the best overall rank on the constrained VLSI design problems under both analytical and physics-based evaluations, while remaining competitive against strong mathematical optimizers (DE, GBO) on the standardized CEC benchmarks.

Article.Title: P2Y receptor-mediated regulation of lipolysis, lipid droplet dynamics, and energy metabolism in podocytes
Article.Authors: Szrejder M.; Audzeyenka I.; Rachubik P.; Grochowalska K.; Rogacka D.; Narajczyk M.; Piwkowska A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abnormal lipid metabolism that results in excessive lipid accumulation in the kidney is closely associated with the pathogenesis of glomerulopathies. Podocytes cover the external surface of glomerular capillaries and are known to be particularly sensitive to lipid overload. Lipids accumulate in lipid droplets, specialized organelles that store neutral lipids. Lipid droplets regulate the mobilization of free fatty acids (FFAs) through lipolysis, coordinated by complex machinery, including adipose triglyceride lipase and perilipins. Moreover, activation of the lipolytic cascade leads to the release of stored energy in the form of FFAs, which serve as substrates for subsequent mitochondrial oxidation. Because cyclic adenosine monophosphate, a key second messenger downstream of purinergic P2Y receptors, governs lipolysis, we investigated whether P2Y signaling modulates podocyte lipid metabolism and bioenergetics. Primary rat podocytes were stimulated with uridine-5’-triphosphate and selective P2Y₁ and P2Y₄ receptor agonists. P2Y activation suppressed lipolysis, reflected by alterations of lipolytic protein levels, lower FFA levels, and changes in lipid droplet morphology and distribution. Lower FFA availability was accompanied by a decrease in oxidative phosphorylation and a compensatory increase in glycolysis. Altogether, these findings highlight a significant role for P2Y signaling in overall podocyte metabolism through the regulation of lipid metabolism. Targeting purinergic signaling to control lipolysis may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate lipid-driven podocyte injury and glomerular dysfunction.

Article.Title: National trends, incidence and regional variations in lower extremity amputations in Sweden, 2008–2024: a register-based study
Article.Authors: Swärd N.; Nilsson G.; Axenhus M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lower extremity amputation (LEA) trends are changing worldwide. This population-based study aimed to describe the incidence, temporal trends, demographic distribution, and regional variation of LEA in Sweden from 2008 to 2024. Data were obtained from the Swedish National Patient Register, and individuals undergoing LEA from toe to hip-level were identified using NOMESCO procedure codes. Incidence were calculated per 100,000 inhabitants/year and analyzed by sex, age, and geographic region. A total of 53,005 patients underwent LEA during the study period, corresponding to an overall incidence of 37.9 per 100,000 person-years. Men had significantly higher incidence than women ( p < 0.001). Incidence declined over time, with an estimated future decrease of 0.5% per year in men and 1.9% per year in women. The reduction was mainly driven by decreasing incidence of transtibial amputations and knee disarticulations. Incidence was highest among older individuals and varied geographically, with higher incidence observed in rural regions compared with urban areas. In conclusion, the incidence of LEA in Sweden decreased during the study period, although substantial differences by sex, age, and region persist. Understanding these patterns may help guide preventive strategies and improve equity in healthcare access.

Article.Title: Application of a PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents
Article.Authors: Feng S.; Zhong B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Teaching film-reading is the most basic clinical teaching activity in the standardized residency training of laboratory medicine department. How to integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical cases and imaging data in a resident-centered manner remains a challenge. Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centered teaching method that fosters critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Considering that artificial intelligence technology has a wide range of application prospects in the field of medical education, we introduced a combined pedagogical package of PBL and ChatGPT in teaching film-reading. The aim of the study was to measure the effectiveness of the PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents in comparison with traditional teaching. Residents were randomly assigned to receive either the PBL-ChatGPT combined package (hereafter referred to as the PBL-ChatGPT group) or traditional teaching (traditional group). After each course, the members of each group were required to complete in-class quizzes and a standardized film-reading assessment form for residency training. Residents’ acceptance and satisfaction with the combined package were evaluated through a survey. Both the theoretical and film-reading examination scores were significantly higher in the PBL-ChatGPT group than in the traditional group (both P < 0.001), with large effect sizes (rank-biserial correlation 0.72 and 0.65, respectively). On the standardized film-reading assessment form, the PBL-ChatGPT group scored significantly higher in the preparation, methodology and overall evaluation domains (all P < 0.001, below the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of 0.0125 applied across the four pre-specified domains) and in the total score ( P < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was detected in the process domain ( P = 0.121). Residents’ feedback on the combined package was highly positive. The study indicates that the PBL-ChatGPT combined package holds significant potential as an innovative model for teaching film-reading to laboratory medicine residents.

Article.Title: Attitudes toward patient safety culture among respiratory therapy students: an online cross-sectional study in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Aldhahir A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patient safety culture is a fundamental component of healthcare quality; however, limited evidence exists regarding safety attitudes among respiratory therapy (RT) students. This study aimed to assess the attitudes toward patient safety and identify factors associated with positive safety attitudes among RT students in Saudi Arabia. An online survey using the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire (SAQ) was conducted between August 28 and December 27, 2025. RT students from the second academic year through internship year were recruited using convenience sampling through social media channels. A mean SAQ score of ≥ 75 defined a positive safety attitude. Non-parametric tests were used to compare SAQ scores and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with positive safety attitudes. A total of 1,457 RT students from 18 programs across Saudi Arabia participated in the study, with a mean age of 23 ± 2 years; 68.4% were male. Overall, only 26.9% of RT students demonstrated a positive safety attitude. Male gender (aOR = 1.4, 95% CI: 1.03–1.81) and increasing age (aOR = 1.1, 95% CI: 1.06–1.21) were independently associated with higher odds of positive safety perception. Internship RT students were significantly more likely to report positive safety attitudes compared with second-year RT students (aOR = 3.0, 95% CI: 1.10–7.98). Significant regional disparities were observed, with RT students from the Southern, Northern, and Central regions demonstrating higher odds of positive safety perception compared with those from the Eastern region. Higher cumulative GPA was also strongly associated with positive safety attitudes, particularly among RT students with GPAs ≥ 4.00. Safety attitudes among RT students in Saudi Arabia remain suboptimal, highlighting the need to strengthen patient safety education during professional training.

Article.Title: Cumulative-incidence crossover and conditional mortality after definitive surgery for endometrial cancer: a population-based competing-risk analysis
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Guo C.; Tong F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-term survivors of endometrial cancer face competing risks from cancer and other conditions, but how these risks evolve remains uncertain. We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of 255,104 women who underwent hysterectomy-based definitive surgery for endometrial cancer in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program (2000–2021). Cause-specific cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen–Johansen methods. Crossover was the earliest month when composite non-endometrial mortality (cardiovascular, other malignant cancer, or other non-cancer death) exceeded endometrial cancer-specific mortality and remained higher for 12 months. During a median follow-up of 8.2 years, 62,347 deaths occurred. Endometrial cancer mortality was 6.2%, 7.1%, and 7.4% at 5, 10, and 15 years, compared with 5.3%, 16.6%, and 28.3% for composite non-endometrial mortality. Crossover occurred at 5.6 years (95% confidence interval, 5.4–5.8) overall but was not reached within 15 years for stage III/IV disease or chemotherapy recipients. Among 10-year survivors, subsequent 5-year mortality was 0.4% from endometrial cancer and 15.3% from non-endometrial causes; cardiovascular mortality remained elevated relative to U.S. female rates (standardized mortality ratio, 1.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.16–1.26). These findings support integrated cardiovascular and metabolic risk management from diagnosis alongside individualized, guideline-concordant oncologic surveillance.

Article.Title: Adiposity and insulin resistance indices and progression to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in Chinese adults
Article.Authors: Jiang Z.; Zhang J.; Zhang X.; Jin L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metabolic and adiposity-related indices may help identify individuals at increased risk of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) progression; however, comparative prospective evidence remains limited. We examined the associations of seven metabolic and adiposity-related indices with progression to advanced CKM stages and assessed their incremental discrimination and exploratory internal machine-learning performance. This prospective analysis included 2,871 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study with CKM stages 0–2 at baseline in 2011. CKM progression was defined as progression to stages 3–4 at the 2015 follow-up. Associations of the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), lipid accumulation product (LAP), visceral adiposity index (VAI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and body roundness index (BRI) with CKM progression were examined using multivariable Cox regression after multiple imputation. Dose–response, subgroup, sensitivity, and incremental discrimination analyses were performed. Separate LAP-, TyG-WC-, and TyG-WHtR-based machine-learning frameworks were evaluated using a stratified 70:30 training/test split. During follow-up, 595 participants (20.7%) progressed to CKM stages 3–4. In fully adjusted analyses, the highest versus lowest quartile of each index was associated with a higher risk of CKM progression, with HRs ranging from 1.52 for TyG (95% CI, 1.20–1.94) to 2.03 for TyG-WC (95% CI, 1.60–2.57; all P for trend < 0.001). Corresponding HRs were 2.01 (95% CI, 1.57–2.57) for TyG-WHtR and 1.98 (95% CI, 1.55–2.54) for LAP. Six indices showed nonlinear dose–response associations. Subgroup analyses showed significant interactions by sex for TyG-WHtR, LAP, WHtR, BRI, and VAI; by smoking status for TyG-WHtR, LAP, and VAI; and by age for WHtR (all P for interaction ≤ 0.049). Addition of individual indices to the covariate model yielded C-indices of 0.702–0.715, compared with 0.701 for the basic model; TyG-WC achieved the highest C-index. In the held-out internal test set, logistic regression achieved the highest ROC-AUC in the LAP (0.721), TyG-WC (0.729), and TyG-WHtR (0.726) frameworks. SHAP analyses of the corresponding logistic regression models identified age as the predictor with the largest mean absolute contribution across all three frameworks. Elevated levels of all seven indices were associated with CKM progression, particularly TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR, and LAP. Given the structural overlap between several index components and the CKM staging framework, the incremental discrimination and machine-learning findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

Article.Title: Material recognition from cross-category morphing
Article.Authors: Liao C.; Schmidt F.; Cheeseman J.; Sawayama M.; Fleming R.; Xiao B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Materials from distinct categories share common image features but also exhibit unique characteristics. How do humans recognize materials despite their enormous appearance variations? Using generative neural networks, we create both prototypical and ambiguous materials that morph between categories. To capture the richness of material representation, we characterize how people judge materials using cross-material morphs through three behavioral tasks: material categorization, material property rating, and visual similarity judgment. We find that morphing smoothly modulates perceptual scales of material appearance. Despite this smooth variation, participants can reliably identify the prototypical materials within given appearance ranges, indicating a strong association between material categories and their visual characteristics. Material properties structure the perceptual space, where the salient dimensions–particularly rigidity–strongly correlate with perceived material categories. In contrast, analyzing image embedding derived from a self-supervised deep learning model reveals that learning visual similarities alone is insufficient to reproduce human perceptual space of materials. Together, our results suggest that material representation is more than visual similarities and may require learning material properties that structure relationships among materials within and across categories. Visual features might be used flexibly and task-dependently to support multiple levels of material perception, ranging from discrimination to material property inference to categorization.

Article.Title: Population driven emissions call for earlier climate mitigation
Article.Authors: Liuzzi D.; Lupi V.; Marsiglio S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Econometric studies based on the STIRPAT framework suggest that carbon emissions respond more strongly to population size than to per capita income, yet this relationship has not been explicitly incorporated into the integrated assessment models used for climate policy analysis. We extend one of the most widely known framework, namely the DICE model, to allow population to directly determine emissions beyond its indirect effect through economic activity, calibrating the relevant elasticities on existing empirical estimates. We find that unabated emissions may exceed twice the standard DICE baseline by 2100, requiring substantially earlier and more intensive abatement effort. Full decarbonization appears necessary around mid-century to meet the 2 $$^{circ}$$ C temperature target, and socially optimal by 2070 when mitigation costs and benefits are weighed against each other. These results are primarily driven by a population elasticity above unity which amplifies emissions, combined with a sub-unitary response to per capita income which partly offsets this effect. Our analysis suggests that explicitly accounting for non-proportional effects of population and income on emissions can significantly affect conclusions about the urgency and cost of climate action.

Article.Title: HandPD37: advanced handwriting dataset for Parkinson’s disease diagnosis using stack ensemble ML
Article.Authors: Shin J.; Miah A.; Hashimoto A.; Hirooka K.; Hasan M.; Hassan N.; Aihara M.; Takahashi R.; Kobayashi S.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects older individuals, especially in aging countries like Japan. A key symptom of PD is hand tremor, which impairs fine motor skills, including handwriting. Early detection is crucial for treatment and management. However, existing datasets often lack sufficient task variety for effective, computer-aided PD recognition. To address this, we propose the HandPD37 dataset, which includes handwriting samples from 78 PD patients and 54 healthy individuals across 37 tasks. These tasks assess both fine motor skills and linguistic complexity, capturing diverse handwriting characteristics indicative of PD. Data was recorded using tablet devices, providing detailed information like X–Y coordinates, pen pressure, and time stamps. Additional kinematic features, such as speed and acceleration, were extracted, totaling 171 features per sample. We applied a stack ensemble of 10 machine learning (ML) algorithms, with Logistic Regression (LR) for classification, and evaluated the tasks using a meta-ensemble approach. Tasks 18, 28, 33, and 34 were most effective for distinguishing PD patients from healthy controls. The results demonstrate that combining kinematic and pressure-based features with ML models improves PD recognition accuracy. The HandPD37 dataset and ensemble approach provide a promising solution for clinical decision-support for PD diagnosis.
