The 37 tasks, tailored for Japanese participants, enhance the dataset’s applicability for more accurate and generalized PD detection.

Article.Title: Effects of compound microbial fertilizer combined with potassium fulvic acid on soil physicochemical properties, microbial community structure, and cotton productivity in saline-alkali soil
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Ma Y.; Ma X.; Liu H.; Pu S.
Article.Abstract: To explore the effects of compound microbial fertilizer (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus and Corynebacterium glutamicum ) combined with potassium fulvic acid on cotton growth and soil ecology in Xinjiang saline-alkali soil, a two-year field experiment with seven treatments was conducted in a randomized block design. We analyzed cotton emergence rate, yield components, rhizosphere soil physicochemical properties (pH, water-soluble salts, major ions), and soil microbial community structure using high-throughput sequencing. Results showed that HT5 (150 L·hm⁻² microbial fertilizer + 15 L·hm⁻² potassium fulvic acid) significantly increased cotton emergence rate to 85.00%. HT4 (120 L·hm⁻² microbial fertilizer + 15 L·hm⁻² potassium fulvic acid) achieved the highest yield increase of 13.31% compared with the fulvic acid-only control. Application of microbial fertilizer effectively reduced soil pH, water-soluble salt, Cl⁻, and Na⁺ contents, and the improvement effects were enhanced with increasing application rate. Bacterial diversity was relatively stable among treatments, while fungal diversity and the relative abundance of beneficial fungi such as Pseudeurotium and Mortierella increased significantly. Overall, compound microbial fertilizer combined with potassium fulvic acid improved soil physicochemical conditions, optimized rhizosphere microbial community structure, and enhanced cotton growth and yield under saline-alkali conditions. The HT4 treatment was identified as the optimal application scheme under the experimental conditions, providing a feasible strategy for high-quality and high-yield cotton production in Xinjiang saline-alkali soils.

Article.Title: Physicochemical properties, selective cytotoxicity, and hemocompatibility of silver nanoparticles biosynthesized using Schizophyllum commune extract
Article.Authors: Sukdee S.; Prajuabjinda O.; Thepsilvisut O.; Chutimanukul P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The integration of biologically derived surface functionalities into metallic nanomaterials offers a promising approach for tailoring nanoparticle performance. In this study, structure–property-bioactivity relationships of biofunctionalized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized using Schizophyllum commune extract were investigated. The fungal extract contained abundant phenolics, triterpenoids, proteins, and carbohydrates that mediated nanoparticle formation and surface functionalization. The resulting AgNPs exhibited a face-centered cubic crystalline structure, an average hydrodynamic size of approximately 50 nm, a zeta potential of − 20.2 mV, and stable colloidal behavior. FTIR analysis revealed the persistence of hydroxyl, amide, and carbohydrate-associated functional groups on the nanoparticle surface, supporting the presence of a fungal-derived biomolecular surface layer rather than confirming the formation of a complete biomolecular corona. These surface characteristics were closely associated with enhanced biological performance, including strong antioxidant activity and selective cytotoxicity against cancer cells. The AgNPs demonstrated potent anticancer activity with IC 50 values of 5.07, 27.93, and 29.07 µg/mL against HepG2, SW480, and NCI-N87 cells, respectively, corresponding to selectivity index (SI) values of 44.18, 8.02, and 7.71. Furthermore, hemolytic activity remained below 5%, indicating acceptable hemocompatibility. Overall, the findings establish a direct relationship between fungal-derived surface chemistry, nanoparticle physicochemical properties, and biological performance, highlighting the potential of S. commune -mediated biofunctionalized AgNPs as advanced nanotherapeutic materials with promising anticancer and biocompatible characteristics.

Article.Title: Dynamic response and damage mechanism of deep overburden layer slope based on shaking table tests
Article.Authors: Yan J.; He Y.; Wen H.; Lian J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: The mountain areas of southwest China are widely covered with loose fractured rock bodies, which are prone to large-scale landslides under seismic action. It is known that the response of the acceleration amplification factor field is closely related to the seismic damage state of the overburden. In order to study the dynamic response and damage mechanism of overburden layer slopes under seismic action, a deep base-covered slope model containing two layers of stacks is used as a prototype in this study, and a series of shaking-table modeling experiments of progressive damage of earthquake-induced slopes are carried out. The cumulative seismic damage deformation process of the slope overburden was identified based on embedded sensors and Particle Image Velocimetry technology, and the energy transfer mechanism of the process was revealed by Hilbert Huang transform. The results show that the non-coherent motion (vibration frequency difference) between the shallow overburden layer-thick overburden layer-bedrock layer is the main controlling factor inducing the slope landslide, and the damage form of the deep overburden slope manifests itself in the form of the trailing edge sliding and extruding the central shear out. The damage starts from the back edge of the slope with increasing seismic intensity and gradually moves toward the middle to lower part of the slope, while extending from the surface to the deeper part of the slope.

Article.Title: A protective oxide strategy for stable graphene gas sensors
Article.Authors: Baloglu A.; Kodu M.; Rubin P.; Pärna R.; Kahro T.; Kasikov A.; Kozlova J.; Avarmaa T.; Jaaniso R.
Article.Abstract: Graphene is an exceptional transducer for chemical sensing owing to its two-dimensional structure and distinctive electronic properties. However, coupling graphene to noble-metal catalysts remains intrinsically challenging: catalytic oxygen dissociation, essential for sensing many gases and volatile analytes, produces reactive oxygen species that irreversibly oxidize graphene and degrade device performance. Here we overcome this limitation with a heterostructure architecture that spatially decouples catalytic activation from the graphene conduction channel, demonstrated for CO sensing. An ultrathin Sb₂O₃ interlayer inserted between CVD graphene and a platinum catalyst serves as a chemically inert barrier that suppresses oxidative attack while maintaining charge-transfer-based transduction. The resulting Pt/Sb₂O₃/graphene devices deliver reproducible CO sensing during prolonged heating, in ozone-rich atmospheres and after 20 months of ambient storage. This architecture provides a general route to stable catalyst-integrated graphene gas sensors.

Article.Title: Cross-configuration data-driven modeling of separation efficiency and diluate production flux in Persian Gulf seawater electrodialysis
Article.Authors: Sharafi S.; Sharafi M.; Sharasfi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study compared four data-driven approaches, GMDH-GA, ANFIS-PSO, support vector machine (SVM), and pattern mining engine (PME), for predicting separation efficiency and diluate production flux in laboratory-scale electrodialysis treatment of Persian Gulf seawater. A complete 486-run factorial dataset covering volumetric flow rate, solute concentration, temperature, applied voltage, and pressure was evaluated using 31 predictor configurations and a common 340/146 development/test partition. Factorial decomposition identified volumetric flow rate as the dominant source of response variation, accounting for 73.90% of the corrected variation in separation efficiency and 59.65% in diluate production flux, while interaction terms contributed 10.44% and 23.67%, respectively. Under the primary held-out evaluation, PME achieved the lowest median test RMSE across the 31 predictor structures for both separation efficiency (0.5774 percentage points) and diluate production flux (0.0934 l m -2 h -1 ), producing the lowest RMSE in 17 and 23 configurations, respectively. Repeated-resampling analysis revealed a metric-dependent pattern for separation efficiency, with GMDH-GA achieving the lowest mean RMSE while PME showed the highest mean Pearson correlation. In contrast, PME retained the lowest mean RMSE, highest predictive R 2 , and highest correlation for diluate production flux across repeated evaluation resamples and remained comparatively stable across temperature and concentration regimes. These results demonstrate that model performance depends on predictor composition, response variable, evaluation metric, and operating regime, with the most persistent predictive advantage of PME observed for diluate production flux.

Article.Title: Application of eDNA metabarcoding for high-resolution reconstruction of the trophic web of an Arctic fjord
Article.Authors: Piroli C.; Marinchel N.; Galli S.; Russo T.; Azzaro M.; Filiciotto F.; Di Marco G.; D’Agostino A.; Gismondi A.; Profeta A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In a rapidly changing Arctic, the Kongsfjorden marine ecosystem was investigated to explore its community composition and structural dynamics using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Samples were collected with metaprobes , passive eDNA samplers deployed within fish traps in the coastal zone and towed along a transect in the mid-fjord zone. Mitochondrial COI and ribosomal 18 S SSU (V8-V9 region) genes were amplified to characterize metazoan and protist communities, respectively. Community analysis highlighted significant differences between coastal and mid-fjord sites (ANOSIM, R = 0.7, p < 0.05), identifying 23 taxa as indicators of one of the two zones. Taxa identified through metabarcoding were used as nodes in trophic networks, while feeding relationships (producer–consumer and predator–prey) were reconstructed through literature review. Qualitative food webs were obtained for each sampling site and for the coastal and mid-fjord zones. The networks were characterized using key trophic indicators and differences emerged in the apical part of the webs. Overall, eDNA proved to be a sensitive and effective tool for detecting spatial differences in community structure. This approach also shows strong potential for long-term monitoring, offering a rapid, cost-effective, and scalable alternative to traditional methods.

Article.Title: Sexual dimorphism and hemispheric asymmetry in the morphology of the sylvian fissure: a magnetic resonance imaging based study
Article.Authors: Phuyal N.; Pandey N.; B.C. B.; Pandeya A.; Mishra A.; Khanal B.; Shrestha A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Sylvian Fissure, the first sulcus to appear during the embryological period, is considered a conventional passageway by neurosurgeons for surgeries related to insular and temporal horn tumours and aneurysm clipping. This study aimed to report the morphological types of the sylvian fissure, explore their distribution patterns among sexes and age groups, and assess the symmetry of morphology between the right and left cerebral hemispheres. A prospective cross-sectional study was performed with 520 participants who visited the Department of Radiology for brain MRI. The participants were recruited after ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Review Committee and after written informed consent was obtained from participants. MRI scans were assessed during the reporting of the MRI, and the categorization was performed by a senior radiologist. Statistical methods such as Pearson’s chi-square test, Bowker’s test, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient were used to assess the association and symmetry of the Sylvian fissure morphology. The type II Sylvian fissure was found to be the most prevalent among both males and females and in both right and left hemispheres. It was also the most common in all age groups except for the > 50 years group, where type I was the most common. The assessment of symmetry reported κ = 0.879 (SE = 0.021, p < 0.001), indicating concordance between the right and left hemispheres. Multinomial regression analysis revealed that older participants and females were associated with lower odds of having SF of types I and III in both hemispheres. Younger participants were more likely to have a narrow Sylvian fissure, whereas wider types were more prevalent in older patients. Future studies should focus on exploring the associations between surgical outcomes and Sylvian fissure morphology.

Article.Title: Inclisiran ameliorates diabetes-associated skeletal muscle remodeling through modulation of FOXO1/PDK4 and ER stress-UPR signaling
Article.Authors: He Z.; Li H.; Ran L.; Zhong Y.; Luo Y.; Wu W.; Bao D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is accompanied by pathological alterations in skeletal muscle, yet effective therapeutic strategies targeting these alterations remain limited. Current interventions, including exercise and nutritional supplementation, often exhibit poor long-term adherence and limited efficacy under diabetic conditions. Therefore, convenient, durable, and metabolically effective therapies are urgently needed. Evidence suggests that excessive endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR) activation contribute to diabetic skeletal muscle remodeling, while pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4) may serve as a key mediator linking metabolic dysfunction to ER stress signaling. A T2DM mouse model was established using high-fat diet feeding combined with streptozotocin administration. Inclisiran was administered intraperitoneally after model establishment. RNA sequencing combined with SVM-RFE analysis identified key targets potentially associated with protective effects of inclisiran. Metabolic parameters, muscle atrophy markers, ER stress/UPR signaling, and muscle fiber type transition were evaluated by real-time qPCR, immunoblotting, and immunofluorescence. Inclisiran significantly reduced fasting blood glucose levels and improved metabolic abnormalities in diabetic mice. Transcriptomic analysis identified PDK4 as a key hub gene potentially associated with pathological alterations in diabetic skeletal muscle and the response to inclisiran treatment. Diabetic mice exhibited marked activation of ER stress/UPR signaling and increased expression of FOXO1, PDK4, and FBX32, whereas inclisiran treatment significantly suppressed these alterations. Additionally, inclisiran partially reversed diabetes-induced muscle fiber type transition from oxidative to glycolytic phenotypes. Inclisiran was associated with improved metabolic abnormalities and favorable alterations in skeletal muscle molecular and fiber-type remodeling in diabetic mice. Transcriptomic analysis identified PDK4 as a potential molecular factor associated with these skeletal muscle alterations. Inclisiran treatment was associated with reduced expression of FOXO1, PDK4, and ER stress-UPR-related markers, together with partial preservation of skeletal muscle fiber-type homeostasis. These findings provide preliminary molecular and histological evidence supporting a potential protective effect of inclisiran on diabetes-associated skeletal muscle remodeling.

Article.Title: Changes in essential oil yield and composition of purple basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) genotypes under ontogenetic and morphogenetic variability
Article.Authors: Koçer O.
Article.Abstract: Composition of three purple basil ( Ocimum basilicum L.) genotypes were investigated. Plants were harvested three times during the pre-flowering period, twice during the full flowering period, and once during the post-flowering period. In the pre-flowering period, plants reached this stage three times within a single growing season. The purple basil genotypes reached full flowering twice during the season. The vegetation period ended before the plants harvested after flowering could reach the post-flowering stage a second time. Analyses were conducted separately on the flowers and leaves of the plants. The highest essential oil content (1.63%) was obtained from the second harvest during the pre-flowering period in the Piros genotype. The lowest essential oil content (0.15%) was detected in the flowers of the Midnight genotype during the post-flowering period and the first harvest of the full flowering period. Essential oil components were identified using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The main components of the essential oil were linalool and methyl cinnamate. The highest linalool content (71.95%) was detected in the leaves of the Piros genotype during the first harvest of the full flowering period, while the lowest linalool content (23.64%) was found in the flowers of the same genotype during the post-flowering period. The highest methyl cinnamate content (60.43%) was identified in the leaves of the Arapgir genotype during the full flowering period.

Article.Title: Physics-informed sparse deep neural networks for ultra-fast solar power forecasting and frequency response support in ancillary service markets
Article.Authors: Mohanty A.; Ramasamy A.; Mohanty S.; Rajamony R.; Satpathy A.; Bhutto J.; Alzahrani S.; Ali Arabi A.; Mohanty P.; Allasi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rising penetration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into the current power grid leads to large variations and uncertainties, which are key challenges to frequency stability and reliable auxiliary services. In this research, a novel Physics-Informed Sparse Deep Neural Network (PI-SDNN) framework is proposed for quick and accurate solar power forecasting specially built to enable fast frequency response (FFR) in auxiliary service markets. The proposed approach incorporates domain-specific physical constraints such as irradiance-power correlations, inverter dynamics and ramp-rate limitations, in a sparsity-promoting deep learning framework, which facilitates superior generalization, lower computational complexity and improved interpretability. The PI-SDNN model exploits structured physics-informed regularization to capture rich spatiotemporal features from high-resolution meteorological and historical generation data. The approach ensures fast inference suitable for real-time grid operations while preserving the forecasting accuracy in highly dynamic environmental scenarios. Furthermore, the forecasting findings are strongly related to a frequency response support module for proactive deployment and reserve allocation of solar-integrated ancillary services. Extensive simulations on real solar datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms classical deep learning and statistical models, yielding 25–40% improvement in forecasting accuracy metrics and significant reduction in computational latency. The integration of PI-SDNN with grid frequency management enhances the reaction speed and reduces frequency nadir variations during disturbances. The results show the potential of physics-informed sparse learning as a disruptive tool for reliable, scalable and commercially viable participation of solar in fast frequency response services, thus increasing the resilience and sustainability of future low-carbon power systems.

Article.Title: Aberrant CPS1 expression is linked to metabolic alterations and metastatic phenotypes in colorectal cancer liver metastasis
Article.Authors: Xiang Q.; Yang M.; Li X.; Tang J.; Yang X.; Zhang F.; Wu S.; Song X.; Wu Z.; Xiang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colorectal carcinoma liver metastasis (CRLM) is the main cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its metabolic drivers remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated three GEO datasets to identify metabolic reprogramming signatures distinguishing CRLM compared to primary tumors. A four-gene metabolism-related risk model was constructed using LASSO-Cox regression in the TCGA M1 cohort and independently validated in GSE17536. Carbamoyl-phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1) emerged as an independent prognostic factor and was markedly upregulated in CRLM tissues compared with matched primary tumors and normal colon, as validated by immunohistochemistry and qRT-PCR in seven paired clinical specimens. Reciprocal loss- and gain-of function experiments in HCT116 and SW480 cells demonstrate that CPS1 promotes invasion and migration without affecting proliferation. Mechanistically, CPS1 exerted pro-metastatic effects independently of canonical urea cycle activity. Instead, CPS1 positively correlated with ether lipid metabolism, reciprocally regulating key enzymes including AGPS and modulating cadherin expression to enhance cellular plasticity. These finding reveal a previously unrecognized role of CPS1 in promoting CRLM via ether lipid metabolic remodeling, highlighting its potential as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Developing analysis algorithm for engineered skeletal muscle contractile function based on a microphysiological system
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Li Y.; Li Y.; Du X.; Zhang Z.; Song B.; Li X.; Zhang J.; Ouyang J.; Si N.; Li Q.; Gu Z.; Yin N.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autonomous contractility is a key functional characteristic of skeletal muscle and an important indicator of engineered muscle maturation. Conventional contact-based force measurements are limited by mechanical interference, restricted spatial resolution, and poor compatibility with high-throughput microphysiological systems. Here, we present a non-contact optical–mechanical framework for quantitative evaluation of contractile dynamics in three-dimensional engineered skeletal muscle. C2C12-derived muscle bundles were generated in fibrin–Matrigel hydrogels and cultured within a customized PDMS microdevice incorporating dual elastic cantilevers and integrated electrodes for controlled electrical stimulation. High-resolution video microscopy combined with optical flow tracking was used to quantify cantilever deformation, which was subsequently converted into contractile force using cantilever beam theory. This approach enabled the extraction of multiple functional parameters, including contraction amplitude, frequency, velocity, and force–time characteristics. The engineered tissues formed aligned, striated myofibers and exhibited rhythmic contractions synchronized with stimulation. Quantitative analysis demonstrated a strong correlation between separately recorded optical deformation and calcium transient signals (r = 0.88 ± 0.03, n = 5 independent constructs, p < 0.01). Reproducible force outputs and frequency-dependent changes in deformation amplitude and contraction velocity were observed across stimulation frequencies from 1 to 3 Hz. Estimated cantilever forces were consistently higher on the right than on the left, suggesting a possible contribution from systematic device- or measurement-related factors. Overall, this framework provides a non-invasive and quantitative approach for functional assessment of engineered skeletal muscle and may facilitate applications in disease modeling, drug evaluation, and microphysiological system-based research.

Article.Title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward pulmonary function testing among patients with cough
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Liu J.; Cheng Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This cross-sectional study aimed to examine the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to pulmonary function testing (PFT) among patients presenting with cough. Self-designed KAP questionnaire was conducted at Ruijin Hospital, involving 387 patients between 24 June 2024 and 7 March 2025. Participants were mostly female (53.0%) and aged 35–54 years (47.5%). The majority were married (82.9%) and lived in urban areas (88.6%). Regarding cough duration, 37.7% reported ≥ 8 weeks and 35.7% <3 weeks. Most had never smoked (84.2%). For prior pulmonary function testing (PFT), 39.3% reported undergoing testing within 1 year. The mean ± SD knowledge and attitudes scores were 21.53 ± 6.66 (possible range: 0–23), 30.48 ± 3.76 (possible range: 8–40), respectively. Adherence to routine pulmonary function testing was observed in 57.9% of patients. In multivariate analysis, higher knowledge scores (OR = 1.080, 95%CI: 1.037–1.124, P < 0.001) and attitude scores (OR = 1.133, 95%CI: 1.052–1.220, P = 0.001) were significantly associated with increased PFT adherence. Conversely, a lower Body Mass Index was associated with active practice (< 18.5: OR = 13.413, P = 0.013), though this warrants cautious interpretation due to the small subgroup size. Additionally, employees from enterprises showed significantly higher adherence (OR = 4.353, P = 0.009). Patients presenting with cough showed good awareness of general PFT concepts but poor understanding of specialized pulmonary function tests, also, patients showed passive attitudes and suboptimal practices toward pulmonary function testing.

Article.Title: Digital twin-guided service-aware graph attention ant colony optimization for reliable dynamic IPv6 routing in power data networks
Article.Authors: Hu F.; Huang Y.; Zhang S.; Lin X.; Wu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Power data networks operating over IPv6-enabled communication infrastructures carry heterogeneous grid services with different latency, bandwidth, operational-risk, and recovery-priority requirements. Static routing metrics and manually weighted Quality of Service (QoS) objectives are insufficient to represent the dynamic coupling among traffic load, service priority, link risk, queueing delay, and fault states in dynamic IPv6 routing environments. This paper proposes a digital twin-guided service-aware graph attention ant colony optimization framework, termed SAG-RTACO, for reliability-oriented dynamic IPv6 routing in power data networks. A routing-oriented network digital twin is first constructed to synchronize topology, traffic, QoS, risk, service, and fault states into a time-varying graph for IPv6 service flows. A service-aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) then learns link suitability under heterogeneous service requests, and the learned edge scores are incorporated into a risk-time Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) search process. A priority-aware primary-backup routing and fault-recovery mechanism is further designed to improve the recovery priority of critical grid services carried by the IPv6-enabled network. Experiments on a 14-node power data network with ten representative service types show that SAG-RTACO achieves a mean path satisfaction of 0.538, reduces average risk cost to 28.7, improves backup availability to 88.9%, and lowers the service failure rate to 9.4%. Additional out-of-distribution IPv6 routing tests under priority-skewed traffic, bursty arrivals, clustered faults, and combined distribution shifts yield GAT AUC values of 0.761–0.816 and SAG-RTACO path satisfaction values of 0.478–0.522 without retraining, indicating graceful performance degradation under unseen operating conditions. Additional fidelity, ablation, robustness, and statistical analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed framework under the tested routing scenarios.

Article.Title: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms and sleep disturbance in college freshmen: a cross-sectional conditional process analysis
Article.Authors: Luo K.; Li C.; Huang J.; Wang L.; Liu Y.; Sun C.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleep disturbance is common among college students, but the statistical relationships linking obsessive-compulsive symptoms (OCS), affective symptoms, and problematic Internet use remain unclear in nonclinical freshmen. In this cross-sectional study, 9,418 college freshmen aged 18–23 years (M = 19.60, SD = 0.65; 3,660 females) completed relevant subscales of the Chinese College Students’ Mental Health Screening Scale. Covariate-adjusted conditional process analyses (analytic N = 9,416) estimated separate and serial indirect associations through anxiety and depression and first-stage moderation by Internet addiction (IA). OCS was positively associated with sleep disturbance (B = 0.284, t = 20.58, p < .001, 95% CI [0.257, 0.311]). Indirect associations were observed through anxiety (estimate = 0.263, 95% bootstrap CI [0.232, 0.293]), depression (estimate = 0.098, 95% bootstrap CI [0.084, 0.114]), and anxiety followed by depression (estimate = 0.113, 95% bootstrap CI [0.098, 0.130]). The OCS × IA interaction in the anxiety equation was statistically significant but small (B = 0.0057, SE = 0.0015, t = 3.71, p < .001). Concurrent measurement prevents conclusions about temporal ordering or causality.

Article.Title: Analysis of unloading failure mechanical characteristics in columnar jointed rock mass
Article.Authors: Ma S.; Yuan Y.; Zhou Y.; Ma D.; Kang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study fabricated columnar jointed rock mass specimens with varying joint inclination angles using rock-like materials and conducted triaxial unloading tests under different initial confining pressures and unloading rates to investigate their mechanical characteristics under various conditions. The results indicate: (1) As the initial confining pressure increases, the peak strength of the specimens gradually rises, and the elastic modulus progressively increases. With increasing joint inclination angle, both the peak strength and elastic modulus of the specimens exhibit a "U"-shaped trend, initially decreasing and then increasing. (2) Under triaxial unloading conditions, the stress–strain curve of columnar jointed rock mass shows an inflection point at the unloading stage, where the elastic modulus suddenly increases, and the specimen volume transitions from compression to expansion. The strength of columnar jointed rock mass under triaxial unloading conditions is lower than that under conventional triaxial compression conditions. Moreover, as the unloading rate increases, the specimen strength gradually decreases, and the characteristics of brittle failure become more pronounced.

Article.Title: Social context information and acoustic convergence in elephant vocal choruses
Article.Authors: Mahon L.; Pardo M.; Miron M.; Chemla E.; Granli P.; Njiraini N.; Moss C.; Keen S.; Poole J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Elephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. Here, we address this gap by investigating multi-caller rumble choruses recorded in several behavioral contexts. We show that behavioral context can be predicted from single (i.e., non-overlapping) and from overlapping, chorused rumbles. We find that individual rumbles in a chorus share structural similarities with single rumbles used in the same behavioral context, suggesting that choruses are composed of context-matched individual elements that together form a distinct multi-caller signal. We also find that the rumbles within choruses converge acoustically in particular behavioral contexts. Lastly, we find that the rumbles associated with various contexts vary systematically among individuals and family groups and suggest that individual acoustic differences may account for the observed family-level variation. Our findings extend previous work showing that rumbles encode behavioral context and caller identity, providing novel evidence that elephant choruses function as group signals encoding context through both their composition and patterns of acoustic convergence.

Article.Title: Discrepancy between soil safety and herbal risk: high cadmium enrichment in roots and leaves of Plantago asiatica and associated health implications
Article.Authors: Qiu S.; Dong Y.; Ai Q.; Yu X.; Liang J.; Zhang L.; Ye M.; Shao H.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plantago asiatica ( P. asiatica ) plays an important role in traditional Chinese medicine treatments and ecological environment assessments. This study focused on the heavy metals discrepancy between soil safety and health risk from different parts of P. asiatica . The contents of 10 heavy metals in the roots, stems, leaves, seeds and corresponding soils were determined using ICP-MS. A health risk assessment method for heavy metal elements was established and simulated by Monte Carlo. The assessment integrated the Bioconcentration Factor (BCF), Hazard Index (HI) and Total Carcinogenic Risk (TCR) models. Results revealed significant variations in heavy metal concentrations and exceedance rates among different plant parts. Roots and leaves exhibited the highest exceedance rates (100% and 57.69%, respectively), while the growth soils remained below the risk screening values for agricultural land. This was primarily attributed to their strong Cd enrichment capacity (BCF: 10.18 in roots, 6.73 in leaves). However, low translocation factors (TF < 1) were found in stems, leaves and seeds, suggesting P. asiatica as a potential candidate for phytostabilization research. Furthermore, risk assessment from the proposed medicinal material safety threshold indicated that heavy metal levels in all four parts posed potential non-carcinogenic health risks for both adults and children under the conservative assumption that all measured As was inorganic As. This contrasted with the food safety framework, under which only roots exceeded the threshold. Moreover, a potential carcinogenic effect was identified in roots for adults under the conservative assumption that all measured As was inorganic As. Therefore, significant discrepancy existed in heavy metal contamination and associated health risks across different parts of P. asiatica . In particular, As in roots and leaves were identified as the primary drivers of potential non-carcinogenic health risks, warranting prioritized attention in quality control and risk management. It was recommended to avoid or reduce using high-risk parts (especially roots) in medicinal applications.

Article.Title: Cu(II) coordination complex doped PVA/NaAlg polymer blend as a redox active composite electrodes for energy storage devices
Article.Authors: Elamin N.; Rajeh A.; Gomaa E.; Zaky R.; El-Hady M.; Alqarni M.; Alzahrani S.; Mannaa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polymer-based composite electrodes with tunable electrochemical properties are of growing interest for energy storage applications. In this work, flexible PVA/NaAlg polymer blend films were modified via molecular coordination doping using a Cu(II) coordination complex as filler to elucidate the structure–property-performance relationship governing their electrochemical behavior. The induced increase in the amorphous structure of the PVA/NaAlg mix and the development of intermolecular contacts between the host polymer and the additional filler were shown by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra. The direct and indirect band gaps decreased from 4.75 to 3.50 eV and from 4.49 to 3.11 eV, respectively, as filler loading increased, according to UV–visible spectroscopy. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements in acidic electrolyte demonstrated a transition from weakly capacitive behavior in the pristine blend to a mixed electric double-layer/pseudocapacitive response in the doped films, driven by redox-active coordination centers. The specific capacitance, calculated from CV curves, increased markedly upon Cu(II) complex incorporation and decreased with increasing scan rate, consistent with diffusion and kinetics-limited pseudocapacitive systems. The 1.00 wt% Cu(II) doped film exhibited the highest capacitance, while intermediate loadings showed improved rate capability. Overall, the results highlight coordination-based molecular doping as an effective strategy for tailoring the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of polymer composites for energy storage applications.

Article.Title: Prevalent α-chain–centric TCR metaclones shape specificity and focus early SARS-CoV-2 T cell responses
Article.Authors: Bansal S.; Bottorff T.; Linsley P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chain-centric TCRs or metaclones, in which one chain pairs with diverse partners, are well documented, but their role in immunity remains unclear. Here, we characterize paired human αβ TCR datasets and show that alpha-centric TCRs are more prevalent than beta-centric TCRs across healthy and diseased individuals. Sequence modeling links alpha-centricity to shorter TRA CDR3 length, greater flexibility, and increased hydrophobicity. Alpha-centric TCRs are enriched for multi-epitope VDJdb annotation, especially for epitopes most dissimilar to each other in sequence. T cells with Spike-motif alpha-centric TCRs, including 1–2-mismatch variants, are activated in COVID-19 patients. These TCRs also share TRA junctions with CMV, EBV, and influenza-reactive TCRs, consistent with broadly cross-reactive, TRA -dominant CD4+ responses. Our findings suggest a role for TRA -dominant recognition in shaping cross-reactive CD4+ T cell immunity.

Article.Title: ACPSO: a novel PSO variant for 3D UAV path planning in multi-threat environments
Article.Authors: Ma S.; Ma C.; Wen L.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) has been widely applied in the fields of numerical optimization and UAV path planning, but it suffers from inherent limitations such as a tendency toward premature convergence, weak parameter adaptability, and insufficient population diversity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel PSO variant algorithm (ACPSO) that integrates the Actor-Critic framework with genetic strategies. First, a dynamic collaborative parameter optimization mechanism based on Actor-Critic is designed to break through the constraints of traditional fixed or single-parameter adjustment strategies. The Actor network outputs the optimal combination of core PSO parameters ( w , \(c_1\) , and \(c_2\) ) according to the real-time population state, while the Critic network evaluates the effectiveness of parameter strategies via a long-term cumulative reward mechanism, thereby achieving a dynamic balance between global exploration and local exploitation. Second, two-point crossover and adaptive mutation operations are incorporated into the iteration process to enhance population diversity, which effectively helps the algorithm escape local optima. Finally, for the UAV path planning task in multi-threat scenarios, a two-stage path smoothing strategy combining three-point neighborhood moving average filtering and cubic spline interpolation is proposed to ensure the smoothness and obstacle avoidance safety of the planned path. To verify the competitiveness of the proposed algorithm, comparative experiments were conducted on the CEC 2017 test suite, against the canonical PSO and seven other state-of-the-art PSO variants, as well as two championship algorithms. In addition, based on the innovatively designed two-stage path smoothing strategy, UAV path planning experiments were carried out under four scenarios with varying difficulty levels to verify the path planning capability of the ACPSO algorithm. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm demonstrates excellent performance in both numerical optimization and UAV path planning tasks. The source-code link for the ACPSO algorithm is: https://github.com/msz-deep/msz.git .

Article.Title: Reliability gated cross-modal attention with shear reparameterized directional reasoning for RGB-thermal salient object detection
Article.Authors: Othman K.; Noorwali A.; Alohali M.; Ullah I.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract RGB-Thermal (RGB-T) salient object detection localizes salient regions where appearance cues alone are insufficient, since thermal radiation stays informative under poor illumination. Two limitations persist. Cross-modal attention is applied at a strength fixed in advance, so a momentarily uninformative stream continues to contribute in full, and directional reasoning is confined to the two image axes, because diagonal coverage has required a dense affinity mask of quadratic cost. We present CDRNet, a Confidence and Directional Reasoning Network with dual ResNet-50 encoders. Cross-modal attention is reliability-gated: a coefficient estimated for each modality from spatial entropy and gradient energy scales the transferred context through a gated residual, and the attention scale is derived from the cosine discrepancy between the pooled modality embeddings, so sharpness follows the semantic gap instead of a fixed constant, and balanced inputs recover symmetric fusion. Directional reasoning is shear-reparameterized: a circular shear maps each diagonal onto an axis, so a single axial operator covers four orientations at axial rather than quadratic cost, a per-pixel gate exposes the learned anisotropy, and a weight-shared second stage refines the result without additional parameters. A boundary gated decoder returns edge evidence to the representation through multiplicative modulation under auxiliary supervision, and its cross scale aggregator mixes two dilation rates per branch under context-dependent weights. On VT821, VT1000, and VT5000, CDRNet attains S-measure values of 0.908, 0.949, and 0.918, surpasses 19 recent methods on all metrics, and ablations isolate each contribution.

Article.Title: Phytotoxicity of potassium antimony(III) oxide tartrate trihydrate in Allium cepa revealed through multilevel biological responses
Article.Authors: Sarsar O.; Çavuşoğlu K.; Yalçın E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimony is an increasingly widespread environmental metalloid capable of exerting significant toxic effects on biological systems. However, the mechanisms underlying its multi-faceted toxicity in plant cells remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to provide an integrated assessment of the physiological, cytogenetic, biochemical, and anatomical effects of potassium antimony (III) oxide tartrate trihydrate in Allium cepa L. root meristem cells. Root-based endpoints were evaluated following exposure to 20, 100, and 500 µg/L Sb for 72 h, whereas exposure was extended to 144 h to allow sufficient leaf development for chlorophyll analysis. Germination and growth parameters, mitotic index, micronucleus frequency, chromosomal abnormalities, DNA damage, malondialdehyde content, superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, chlorophyll contents, and anatomical alterations were evaluated. Antimony exposure significantly reduced germination, root length, weight gain, and mitotic index, while markedly increasing micronucleus and chromosomal abnormality frequencies. Comet assay revealed a reduction in head DNA from 96.9% to 66.5%, accompanied by an increase in tail DNA from 3.10% to 33.5%. Moreover, antimony exposure markedly enhanced lipid peroxidation and antioxidant enzyme activities, while substantially reducing chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b contents. Anatomical analyses demonstrated increases in epidermal cell damage, cortical cell wall thickening, and flattened nucleus. Collectively, these findings suggest that antimony suppresses cell division, disrupts genomic integrity, and induces structural tissue damage in A. cepa root meristem cells. This integrated assessment demonstrates the multilevel phytotoxic effects of potassium antimony(III) oxide tartrate trihydrate and provides a basis for future investigations of its toxicological mechanisms and ecotoxicological significance.

Article.Title: Skin carotenoid levels are associated with blood amyloid-beta 42/40 ratios in healthy individuals under 60 years of age
Article.Authors: Yamauchi T.; Waki N.; Suzuki S.; Murakami S.; Ishiki K.; Yamashita K.; Miura M.; Sato J.; Sato T.; Mikami T.; Murashita K.; Nakaji S.; Tamada Y.; Itoh K.
Article.Abstract: Dementia prevalence is increasing worldwide, with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) being the most common type. Amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregation is an early pathological event in AD. Although carotenoids have been shown in vitro to inhibit Aβ aggregation through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, human evidence remains limited. Recently, blood-based biomarkers such as Aβ42/40 ratios, phosphorylated tau (p-tau181, p-tau217), and neurofilament light chain (NfL) have enabled assessment of AD-related pathology. We analyzed 770 participants from the 2024 Iwaki Health Promotion Project in Japan. The associations between circulating carotenoid levels (skin and blood) and blood AD-related biomarkers were examined using adjusted linear and nonlinear regression models in a cross-sectional design. Among participants under 60 years, those in the highest quartile of skin carotenoid levels had significantly higher Aβ42/40 ratios than those in the lowest quartile (β = 0.0024, 95% CI: 0.0003–0.0046). The magnitude of the association was comparable to the cross-sectional difference in Aβ42/40 ratio observed across approximately 4–8 years of age. Among the blood carotenoids measured, lutein and α-carotene were positively associated with Aβ42/40 ratios. In summary, higher circulating carotenoid levels were associated with more favorable Aβ profiles in individuals under 60 years.

Article.Title: The impact of self-rated health on the Parkinson’s disease-disability association: evidence from CHARLS
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Wang Z.; Xia H.; Yang X.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a major cause of functional disability among older adults, yet the role of patients’ subjective health perceptions in this association remains poorly quantified. This study aimed to examine the independent association between PD and impairments in basic (BADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL), and to decompose the relative contributions of multi-domain factors—with a primary focus on self-rated health—in a nationally representative Chinese population. This cross-sectional analysis used data from the 2020 wave of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), enrolling 17,311 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 45 years, including 196 with physician-diagnosed PD. Multivariate logistic regression with sequential adjustment was applied to estimate the independent association of PD with BADL/IADL disability. A stepwise effect-size decomposition approach was employed to quantify the percentage contribution of each covariate block (sociodemographic, lifestyle, and clinical factors) to the total PD–disability effect, with particular emphasis on self-rated health. PD was independently associated with significantly elevated risks of BADL impairment (OR = 2.73, 95%CI: 1.99–3.75) and IADL impairment (OR = 1.88, 95%CI: 1.37–2.60) after full adjustment. Sequential effect decomposition revealed that self-rated health accounted for the largest attenuation of the association, explaining 26.5% of the PD–BADL effect and 29.8% of the PD–IADL effect—far exceeding the contributions of depression, multimorbidity, and cognitive dysfunction. Subgroup analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings across all strata (all P for interaction > 0.05). Self-rated health emerges as the dominant explanatory factor in the PD–functional disability pathway, outperforming conventional clinical indicators. These findings advocate a paradigm shift from symptom-focused management toward integrated care that prioritizes patients’ subjective health perceptions. We recommend incorporating routine self-rated health assessment and targeted psycho-behavioral interventions into standard PD care as a promising strategy to slow progressive functional decline.

Article.Title: Adaptive evolutionary PID controller using SHADE and L-SHADE for TRIGA mark-II reactor
Article.Authors: Lokman G.; İşcan S.; Çelik E.; Sharma S.; Sharma G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a trajectory-tracking PID (TTPID) controller optimized using Success-History Based Adaptive Differential Evolution (SHADE) and its improved variant Linear Population Size Reduction SHADE (L-SHADE) for power regulation of the ITU TRIGA Mark-II research reactor. The main novelty of the study is the integration of adaptive differential evolution mechanisms with a trajectory-tracking PID framework for nuclear reactor power control, which has not previously been reported in the literature. A constrained Integral of Time-Weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) objective function is employed to simultaneously minimize tracking error and limit excessive control-rod motion. The optimization performance of SHADE and L-SHADE is first compared, showing that L-SHADE achieves faster and more stable convergence with lower fitness fluctuations. The optimized controller is then evaluated under different initial and desired power levels ranging from 50 to 250 kW. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed L-SHADE-TTPIDC successfully tracks the reference trajectory with negligible steady-state error and overshoot below 1.1% at a target power level of 225 kW. The controller achieves settling times below 23 s and response times as low as 17 s, outperforming previously reported FLC-PSO and MFLNN-PSO controllers in most operating scenarios. In addition, all operational constraints were satisfied while maintaining smooth control-rod movement. The results confirm that adaptive differential evolution-based PID tuning provides an effective and robust solution for nonlinear reactor power control and represents a promising alternative to existing intelligent control approaches.

Article.Title: Preliminary safety and efficacy of liquid-type polycaprolactone for neck rejuvenation in Asian adults in a prospective pilot study
Article.Authors: Thongjaroensirikul P.; Techapichetvanich T.; Maneeprasopchoke P.; Nokdhes Y.; Buranaporn P.; Wannawittayapa T.; Bhorntarakcharoen W.; Sittiwanaruk S.; Abhinoraseth P.; Yamlexnoi P.; Meethong O.; Wanitphakdeedecha R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The neck is a challenging area for aesthetic rejuvenation due to its thin dermis and the risk of nodule formation associated with traditional particulate fillers. A novel, liquid-type polycaprolactone (PCL) offers a potential alternative by mitigating these risks. To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of liquid-type PCL for the treatment of horizontal neck lines in Asian patients. In this prospective, open-label, single-arm pilot study, 30 Asian subjects received three sessions of liquid-type PCL (GOURI; 210 mg/mL, 21% PCL) injections at one-month intervals using a subdermal cannula technique. All participants completed the treatment series; follow-up data were available for 29 participants at 1 month and 28 participants at both 3 and 6 months after completion of treatment. Objective biophysical parameters, including skin elasticity (Cutometer) and skin texture/wrinkle depth (Antera 3D), were assessed over a 6-month follow-up period. Subjective satisfaction and safety were also evaluated. Visual and quantitative assessments demonstrated measurable improvement in horizontal neck lines and skin quality over 6 months. In participant-level paired analyses, skin distensibility (R0) decreased from 0.214 ± 0.089 at baseline to 0.102 ± 0.091 at 6 months (mean change, −0.109; 95% CI, −0.152 to −0.066; standardized mean change [Cohen’s dz], −1.03; p < 0.001). Gross elasticity (R2) changed from 66.66 ± 15.72 to 38.16 ± 29.35 (mean change, −28.68; 95% CI, −40.70 to −16.67; dz, −0.93; p < 0.001). Skin roughness, volume of depression, and melanin index also decreased significantly. At 6 months, 85% of participants with available follow-up data reported ≥ 51% improvement. The treatment was generally well tolerated; one participant developed mild bruising that resolved spontaneously within 8 days. Liquid-type PCL may represent a safe and minimally invasive option for neck rejuvenation in appropriately selected patients. These pilot data suggest measurable improvement in neck skin texture, firmness-related parameters, and pigmentation; however, controlled studies with longer follow-up and blinded evaluation are required to confirm efficacy, durability, and optimal candidate selection.

Article.Title: A study on kindergarten teacher–child interaction quality based on a multimodal emotion recognition model integrating speech and text
Article.Authors: Han J.; Yuchi X.; Qi X.
Article.Abstract: Emotion recognition offers a route to quantifying interaction quality in early childhood education, yet existing methods suffer from unimodal input, poor real-time performance and weak generalization. This study proposes a speech-text multimodal model built on a Mamba encoder with a GatedxLSTM fusion mechanism, in which frame pooling and temporal masking resolve the temporal misalignment between modalities and a learnable gate adjusts modality contribution. Experiments on IEMOCAP and FAU-AIBO, together with an in-house KTC-Pilot corpus of authentic kindergarten interactions used for ecological validation, show that the approach outperforms mainstream baselines in F1, WA and UA. Three child-speech-aware adaptations, namely pitch and formant augmentation, silence-aware frame pooling and disfluency-tolerant text encoding, close the domain gap with authentic kindergarten dialogue, and modality-dropout training, cross-modal reconstruction of missing text and gating regularisation maintain robustness under incomplete inputs. A contamination audit against the CLAP pretraining corpora confirms that the gains do not arise from data leakage. A downstream evaluation using an Interaction Quality Index calibrated against expert observer ratings achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.692 with expert scores. An on-device deployment study on two embedded platforms further shows that the quantised framework sustains an end-to-end latency of 377 ms per utterance at a real-time factor of 0.075 and a board power of 9.6 W while retaining an F1 score of 0.706 on authentic kindergarten audio, and a stage-wise data-handling design keeps raw audio, spectral features and transcripts inside the classroom node so that only a scalar interaction quality value is written to persistent storage. Ablation and visualization analyses confirm the contribution of each structural component to recognition performance and interpretability.

Article.Title: PPTM-IoV: a privacy-preserving trust management framework for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV)
Article.Authors: Malik A.; Mian Qaisar S.; Shah S.; Uddin M.; Salhi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) enables seamless Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication among connected vehicles, infrastructure, and cloud services, supporting Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) through real-time information exchange. However, the dynamic and decentralized nature of IoV environments introduces significant challenges related to trust management, privacy preservation, and secure communication. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose PPTM-IoV, a privacy-preserving trust management framework that enables vehicles to establish trust without revealing their private data. The framework first introduces a privacy-preserving identity and credential management scheme that uses pseudonymous identities and verifiable credentials, combined with a non-interactive zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) mechanism based on established cryptographic techniques. Next, a dynamic trust evaluation mechanism is designed by combining direct observations and weighted indirect recommendations. The trust model is further strengthened with adaptive updating based on significant behavioral changes and supported by analytical properties. To protect sensitive trust information during outsourced computation, the framework employs Paillier-based homomorphic encryption, enabling secure trust aggregation in the encrypted domain. A privacy-preserving trust processing workflow is achieved by integrating homomorphic computation with trusted-authority-assisted proxy re-encryption. Furthermore, a proxy re-encryption mechanism supports authorized trust verification between vehicles without exposing trust scores to unauthorized entities. Finally, a secure and trust-aware communication protocol incorporates bidirectional trust verification, threshold-based decision-making, and encrypted as well as digitally signed message exchange to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and mutual trust enforcement. The proposed framework is implemented using SUMO and NS-3 simulators. Experimental results demonstrate that PPTM-IoV achieves superior performance compared to the best-performing benchmark schemes, reducing average latency by 4.80%, while improving PDR by 1.43%, throughput by 4.09%, and trust accuracy by 1.47%.

Article.Title: Discovery of FGFBP1 as a novel target of isorhamnetin against LUSC and preliminary study of sea buckthorn-derived carbon dots
Article.Authors: Ji H.; Li X.; Luo J.; Nie C.; Liu C.; Yao W.; Gan J.; Jin Y.; Chen W.; Fu A.; Wu H.; Cui Y.; Mo F.; Ge Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a challenging malignancy with limited targeted therapies. Isorhamnetin (ISO), a natural flavonoid derived from sea buckthorn, exhibits promising antitumor activity. However, its molecular targets and underlying mechanisms in LUSC remain unclear. Concurrently, carbon dots (CDs) synthesized from herbal sources have emerged as promising nanoplatforms for cancer theranostics. This study aimed to elucidate the antitumor mechanism of ISO in LUSC and explore the potential of sea buckthorn-derived CDs as a functional nanomedicine. LUSC cells were treated with different concentrations (0, 50, 100 μM) of ISO. The effects on cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed via CCK-8 assays, colony formation assays, scratch assays, and Transwell assays. Differentially expressed genes were screened through transcriptome sequencing, with key targets validated by Western blot analysis. Construct FGFBP1 overexpression cell lines for reversal experiments and detect downstream FGF2c/ERK signalling pathway-related protein expression. Additionally, sea buckthorn carbon dots (SB-CDs) were synthesised via hydrothermal synthesis using sea buckthorn as the carbon source. Characterisation was performed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Preliminary evaluation assessed their inhibitory effect on the malignant phenotype of LUSC cells. ISO significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of LUSC cells in a dose-dependent manner. Transcriptomics and protein analysis revealed that ISO downregulated fibroblast growth factor binding protein 1 (FGFBP1) and inhibited the downstream FGF2/ERK signaling pathway. Overexpression of FGFBP1 partially reversed the antitumor effects of ISO. Meanwhile, SB-CDs were successfully prepared with excellent fluorescence properties and effectively inhibited the malignant behaviors of LUSC cells in a concentration-dependent manner. ISO exerts its anti-tumour effects in LUSC by downregulating FGFBP1 and inhibiting the FGF2/ERK signalling pathway. Furthermore, sea buckthorn-derived carbon dots exhibit inherent antitumor properties, demonstrating a successful transformation from medicinal plant to functional nanomaterial. This study not only provides new insights into the mechanism of ISO but also offers a green and sustainable strategy for developing plant-based nano-theranostic agents against LUSC.

Article.Title: Ultrasonic-assisted green synthesis of schiff base-functionalized CdS nanoparticles with enhanced optical, anticancer, and antibacterial properties
Article.Authors: Kumar K.; Reena V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the present investigation, a novel Schiff base ligand was synthesized through the condensation of benzaldehyde, o-hydroxyacetophenone, and 1,2-ethylenediamine using an ultrasonically assisted green chemical approach. The resulting ligand was subsequently employed as a capping agent for the synthesis of cadmium sulfide nanoparticles (CdS NPs), yielding Schiff base-functionalized CdS nanoparticles (L–CdS NPs). The synthesized Schiff base ligand and functionalized nanoparticles were comprehensively characterized by elemental analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV–Vis, IR, 13 C and 1 H NMR, and HRMS techniques. XRD analysis confirmed the crystalline nature of CdS and revealed nanoscale crystallite dimensions, while the observed peak broadening was indicative of reduced particle size and the formation of a highly crystalline, phase-pure structure. Photoluminescence studies further demonstrated enhanced emission characteristics of the Schiff base-capped CdS nanoparticles compared with the uncapped CdS nanoparticles. These results indicate that Schiff base functionalization not only contributes to the stabilization of the CdS nanoparticle surface but also modulates its physicochemical and biological properties. Both the free Schiff base ligand and L–CdS NPs exhibited appreciable in vitro cytotoxicity against Dalton’s lymphoma ascites (DLA) cells, with the nanoparticle formulation displaying substantially enhanced cytotoxic efficacy. Consistent with these findings, in vivo studies demonstrated pronounced antitumor activity against both Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC)-induced ascites and DLA-induced solid tumour models in Swiss albino female mice, underscoring the therapeutic potential of the Schiff base-functionalized CdS nanostructure as a multifunctional bioactive platform. The L–CdS NPs were further investigated for their biological potential, particularly antibacterial activity. Overall, the findings demonstrate that Schiff base capping provides an effective strategy for stabilizing CdS nanoparticles while enhancing their biological activity, highlighting their potential for future biomedical and nanotechnological applications.

Article.Title: Terminal hydroxylation of eIF5A hypusination influences mitochondrial protein expression and cellular metabolism in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Kondo N.; Shirai A.; Magpantay H.; Arioka M.; Hamamoto M.; Yoshida M.; Matsuyama A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypusination of eIF5A is an essential, oxygen-dependent post-translational modification catalyzed sequentially by DHPS and deoxyhypusine hydroxylase (DOHH). Although previous SILAC-based studies in budding yeast established that DOHH acts as an oxygen sensor regulating mitochondrial translation, whether this mechanism represents a generalized eukaryotic paradigm or a species-specific adaptation remains unknown. Here, we investigated the proteome-wide impact of disrupting the terminal hydroxylation of eIF5A using a DOHH-deficient mutant ( mmd1 Δ) in the evolutionarily distant fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe . Utilizing an ORFeome-scale proteomic approach under a uniform expression framework, we demonstrate that DOHH loss does not uniformly reduce protein abundance but preferentially alters the abundance of mitochondrial proteins, specifically oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) components. Reflecting these proteomic shifts, mmd1 Δ cells exhibited impaired respiration and a compensatory metabolic shift toward fermentation. Crucially, oxygen limitation reduced hypusinated eIF5A levels and recapitulated the mmd1 Δ phenotype in fission yeast. By demonstrating that this post-translational circuit operates identically across highly divergent yeast models, our results establish the evolutionary conservation of the DOHH-eIF5A axis, firmly validating it as a universal mechanism coupling environmental oxygen availability to mitochondrial translation.

Article.Title: Characteristics of ESBL-positive Escherichia coli causing community-acquired UTIs in India
Article.Authors: Kocher D.; Pundir S.; Mohapatra S.; Kalaivani M.; Gautam H.; Sood S.; Dhawan B.; Nayak B.; Kumar A.; Kumari R.; Mahajan S.; Hari P.; Kapil A.; Das B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) is the predominant uropathogen in community-acquired urinary tract infections (CA-UTIs) globally. However, data from India on relationship between antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, and clonal markers in UPEC remain scarce. We studied 80 ESBL-positive UPEC isolates causing CA-UTI across four Indian regions. Antimicrobial susceptibility done using VITEK-2. PCR assays detected ESBL genes ( bla CTX-M-15 , bla TEM ), carbapenemase genes ( bla NDM , bla OXA-48-like ), virulence genes ( fimH, pap, sfa, hlyA, aer ) and serogroup O25b. Phenotypic virulence assays assessed hemolysin, haemagglutination, biofilm and gelatinase production. All isolates susceptible to fosfomycin, with high susceptibility to nitrofurantoin (87.5%) and ertapenem (85%). Predominant resistance gene was bla CTX-M-15 (97.5%), followed by bla TEM (55%), bla NDM (16.3%) and bla OXA-48-like (5%). Biofilm formation (41.3%) most prevalent virulence trait, followed by haemagglutination (35%). Frequently detected virulence genes were pap (61.3%), fimH (55%), and aer (48.8%). The O25b serogroup found in 41.3% of isolates had lower ertapenem resistance than non-O25b strains. This study shows ESBL-producing UPEC isolates from community settings in India frequently harbour multiple beta-lactamase resistance genes and virulence factors, underscoring their adaptability and clinical threat in CA-UTIs. These findings emphasize the critical need for continued molecular surveillance, strengthened infection control, and robust antibiotic stewardship programs to mitigate the spread of multidrug-resistant, virulent UPEC strains.

Article.Title: Empirically informed AHP-FR modeling for multi-hazard susceptibility mapping in a mountainous transport corridors
Article.Authors: Hussain M.; Xie X.; Su C.; Mehvish F.; Muneer M.; Akbar M.; Alanazi A.; Pinto M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. However, most susceptibility assessments for high-mountain corridors still focus on single hazards or rely heavily on expert-based weighting, which can introduce subjectivity into spatial decision-making. This study develops an empirically informed Analytical Hierarchy Process–Frequency Ratio (AHP-FR) framework for integrated landslide, debris-flow, and flood susceptibility mapping along the Barakhan–Gilgit–Juglot section of the northern China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). The main methodological contribution is the use of frequency-ratio-derived empirical evidence that was integrated with AHP-derived factor weights to calculate final subclass weights and thereby reducing reliance on purely subjective expert judgment. Field surveys, remote sensing datasets, historical hazard inventories, and 12 conditioning factors were integrated in a GIS environment to generate single-hazard susceptibility maps and an eight-class multi-hazard susceptibility map. Independent ROC-AUC validation showed acceptable to very good predictive performance, with AUC values of 0.803 for landslides, 0.762 for debris flows, and 0.872 for floods. The results indicate that 63% of the corridor is exposed to one or more hazards, including 59% exposed to two or more overlapping hazards; 41% are co-susceptible to landslides and debris flows, while 37% falls within the no/very low multi-hazard susceptibility class. The spatial outputs identify major hazard-prone sections, including Attabad, Chalt, and Passu, providing practical guidance for road-maintenance prioritization, slope-stabilization planning, drainage improvement, and emergency preparedness. The added value of this study lies in combining empirical FR-based weighting with AHP and translating separate hazard maps into explicit multi-hazard combination classes, offering a reproducible decision-support framework for resilient planning in mountainous transport corridors.

Article.Title: Factors associated with persistent post-COVID-19 condition and functional limitation four years after SARS-CoV-2 infection
Article.Authors: Faraj M.; Grosshennig A.; Goedecke N.; Dirks M.; Hennemann A.; Greten S.; Ehrenreich H.; Blasczyk R.; Weissenborn K.; Beutel G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) can persist for years after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, but factors associated with long-term persistence and functional outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this longitudinal cohort study, adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection who had volunteered for plasma donation completed surveys approximately 16 and 48 months after infection. Acute-phase demographic characteristics and symptoms were examined for associations with PCC and persistent PCC using multivariable logistic regression analyses. Persistent symptoms at follow-up and their associations with functional limitation, assessed with the Post-COVID Functional Status (PCFS) scale, were examined separately. Among 992 participants in 2021, 609 (61.4%) met criteria for PCC, while 333 of 568 participants (58.6%) fulfilled PCC criteria in 2024. Older age, fatigue, palpitations, depressive symptoms, and concentration and memory difficulties during acute infection were associated with PCC at both follow-up assessments, whereas female sex was associated with PCC only at the 4-year follow-up. Among participants with PCC in 2021, 77.4% continued to meet PCC criteria in 2024; concentration difficulties, depressive symptoms, and older age were associated with persistent PCC. Functional limitation was associated with persistent fatigue, concentration difficulties, dyspnea at rest, and depressive symptoms. These findings demonstrate the persistent nature of PCC and highlight the need for further research into the mechanisms behind PCC and the development of therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: Design and realization of robust disturbance rejection decoupling control strategy for time delayed multi-variable process
Article.Authors: Maniramakrishna A.; Mahapatro S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents design and development of a robust decentralized PI controller exploiting an analytical model based approach for multi-variable system. In this work, a two-degree-of-freedom control approach is employed to tackle load disturbance rejection, enhance robustness against parametric uncertainties, and ensure precise set-point tracking. Proposed 2-DoF based disturbance rejection decoupling control guarantees robust stability in the face of a $$\pm 40\%$$ variation in process gain and delay, while preserving equivalent performance.The robustness of the proposed controller has been verified by sensitivity analysis employing various perturbation levels range of $$\pm 40\%$$ . To exhibit the superiority of the proposed controller, three industry-scaled case studies are considered. The obtained response of the proposed controller has been compared with similar other model-based controllers. From the obtained results it is envisaged that, the proposed controller provides adequate servo and regulatory performance as compared to other earlier reported approaches.

Article.Title: Monocular depth estimation for endoscopic surgery using swin transformer and conditional random fields
Article.Authors: Deng Y.; Yan C.; Cheng N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Monocular depth estimation in endoscopic surgery is challenging due to weak tissue textures, uneven illumination, specular reflections, and frequent smoke or instrument interference. This paper proposes CRFDepth, a pseudo‑supervised framework for endoscopic monocular depth estimation. A Swin Transformer encoder extracts hierarchical global features under weak‑texture conditions. The proposed CRFDepth framework effectively addresses key challenges in endoscopic monocular depth estimation, achieving superior accuracy and robustness. A Pyramid Scene Parsing module aggregates multi‑scale contextual information to improve structural perception in distorted regions. A NeWCRF decoder performs cross‑scale structured inference for boundary refinement and detail recovery. A RangeAwareLoss is introduced to stabilize optimization within the narrow endoscopic depth range. The network is trained with stereo-derived pseudo-ground-truth supervision using binocular image pairs, while only monocular input is required during inference. Experiments were conducted on the da Vinci laparoscopic dataset. CRFDepth achieves 44.27 dB PSNR and 0.9942 SSIM, outperforming baseline methods, and demonstrates strong robustness to occlusion and smoke interference.

Article.Title: Species distribution models of ESA-listed corals highlight niche differences among taxa that may guide recovery planning
Article.Authors: Tanaka K.; Oliver T.; Couch C.; Shantz A.; Turnham K.; Sena E.; Perelman J.; Huntington B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the biogeography of living marine resources is essential for informed management, particularly in data-limited environments. Here, we use two corals listed under the U.S. Endangered Species Act (ESA) around Tutuila, American Samoa, to evaluate a transferable workflow that combines presence-only occurrence records, open biodiversity repositories, and open-access environmental data to extend existing survey records and support species monitoring. We developed ensemble maximum entropy (MaxEnt) models for two Indo-Pacific corals, Acropora globiceps and Isopora crateriformis , using multi-source occurrence records collected from 2007 to 2025. Dynamic environmental predictors, including thermal stress, water clarity, and wind variability, were derived from open-access satellite datasets and temporally summarized to match field sampling dates, while static predictors represented seafloor structure and land-based stressors. To evaluate one-year-ahead forecast performance, we trained models on records through 2024, generated 2025 relative habitat-suitability forecasts using lagged 2024 environmental summaries, and evaluated them against independent 2025 observations. The 2025 forecasts showed moderate discrimination under temporal validation, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.74 for A. globiceps and 0.71 for I. crateriformis . The models revealed contrasting realized niches: A. globiceps was associated with shallower, rugose habitats and specific thermal-history conditions, whereas I. crateriformis showed highest suitability at intermediate depths and appeared more constrained by thermal variability. These results suggest that occurrence-based SDMs can help distinguish species-specific habitat associations and guide monitoring or spatial prioritization, while remaining best interpreted as relative habitat suitability rather than definitive forecasts of occurrence. Because the workflow relies on presence-only records and open-access environmental data, it can be adapted to other taxa, regions, and applied questions where field data are limited.

Article.Title: Hybrid-integrated nonreciprocal polarization rotator based on dielectric metasurfaces and a magnet-free thin-film Faraday rotator
Article.Authors: Sunwoo Y.; Kwon Y.; Jeong J.; Zou X.; Lee W.; Choi D.; Kim J.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrated nonreciprocal polarization control is essential for optical isolators and circulators that suppress back-reflection in photonic integrated circuits. In this study, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a hybrid-integrated metasurface-based nonreciprocal polarization rotator (MNPR) consisting of a metalens (ML), a magnet-free Faraday rotator (MFFR), and a bifunctional metasurface (BFMS). The ML provides reciprocal beam collimation and focusing, while the BFMS combines the same wavefront-shaping function with half-wave-plate-like 45° polarization rotation. The MFFR provides nonreciprocal 45° Faraday rotation without an external magnetic field. By aligning the beam path and polarization axes of the three components, the MNPR preserves the input polarization in the forward direction and converts it into the orthogonal polarization in the backward direction. The fabricated MNPR operates over the C-band (1527–1565 nm). At 1550 nm, the MNPR exhibits polarization extinction ratios of 21.3 ± 1.6 dB and 21.2 ± 0.7 dB and insertion losses of 6.4 ± 0.5 dB and 6.4 ± 0.1 dB in the forward and backward directions, respectively. After integration with a silicon waveguide chip, the MNPR preserves its nonreciprocal behavior, with insertion losses of 12.6 dB and 12.5 dB in the forward and backward directions, respectively. Structural optimization strategies are presented to reduce the insertion loss, suggesting its potential as a polarization-control building block for future on-chip optical isolators and circulators.

Article.Title: Fear of progression as a mediator between symptom burden and social alienation in lung cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy
Article.Authors: Xu F.; Xie S.; Li Q.; Zhang P.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Chemotherapy is one of the main treatment methods for lung cancer patients, but it brings a serious symptom burden to patients. Previous studies have shown that symptom burden may lead to social alienation, but the underlying mechanism of this relationship is not yet fully understood. This study aims to explore the mediating effect of fear of progression (FoP) between symptom burden and social alienation in lung cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy. This study adopted a cross-sectional survey design. A total of 216 lung cancer patients receiving chemotherapy were recruited from the outpatient clinics or inpatient wards of the Oncology Department at a tertiary grade-A hospital in Deyang City from March to July 2025 using convenience sampling. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the M.D. Anderson Symptom Inventory-Lung Cancer Module (MDASI-L), the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF), and the Social Alienation Scale for Cancer Patients (SAS-CP). R version 4.5.2 was used to analyze the correlations among symptom burden, FoP, and social alienation, as well as to test the mediating effect of FoP between symptom burden and social alienation. The total social alienation score was 82.77 ± 10.48. Pearson correlation analysis showed that the total symptom burden score was positively correlated with the total social alienation score ( r = 0.356, P < 0.01) and with the FoP score ( r = 0.232, P < 0.01). The FoP score was also positively correlated with the total social alienation score ( r = 0.489, P < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed that FoP partially mediated the relationship between symptom burden and social alienation, with a mediating effect of 0.103, accounting for 30.3% of the total effect. Symptom burden in patients with lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy can directly affect social alienation, and it can also indirectly affect social alienation through FoP. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen the symptom assessment and management of lung cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, and carry out targeted psychological counseling in a timely manner, especially the intervention of FoP, in order to reduce the patients’ sense of social alienation.

Article.Title: Success rate and determinants of intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke from the Malaysia National Stroke Registry
Article.Authors: Sies N.; Mat Ruzlin A.; Sidek N.; Ibrahim K.; Law W.; King T.; Chen X.
