Article.Abstract: Abstract Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is an established intervention for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet comprehensive real-world evidence on its success rate and determinants in low and middle countries (LMCs) remains limited. This retrospective cohort study aimed to determine the success rate of IVT and identify key determinants using data from the Malaysian National Stroke Registry (2014–2023) from two tertiary hospitals. Successful IVT was defined as a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of ≤ 4 at 24 h post-IVT. Individual-related, clinical-related, and treatment-related determinants were included as the independent variables. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify the determinants of successful IVT. A total of 1,011 eligible patients were included in the study with a median (IQR) age of 62.0 (19.0) years and 61.3% were males. The success rate of IVT was 37.8% (95% CI 34.8–40.8), with median onset-to-needle time of 192.0 (95.0) minutes. Younger age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.99 (95% CI 0.98–0.99)), lower baseline NIHSS score (aOR 0.87 (95% CI 0.84–0.89)), and small vessel occlusion subtype (aOR 2.52 (95% CI 1.65–3.86)) were significant determinants of successful IVT. These findings highlight important determinants that may help optimize IVT delivery and improve stroke outcomes in Malaysia.

Article.Title: A novel hybrid and ensemble deep learning model for enhancing sentiment analysis in Persian context
Article.Authors: Rasooli A.; Servi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Advances in mobile technologies have established social media as a major platform for expressing emotions and opinions. Analyzing such publicly shared sentiments enables companies and political organizations to make informed and data-driven decisions. As a result, sentiment analysis has become an essential tool for researchers and policymakers seeking to accurately interpret public opinion. However, traditional text processing approaches often struggle to achieve high accuracy when dealing with complex and informal textual data, highlighting the need for more robust analytical frameworks. Although deep learning techniques have recently achieved notable success in Natural Language Processing (NLP), research on Persian sentiment analysis remains relatively limited. The primary objective of this study is to propose a novel hybrid and ensemble deep learning framework specifically designed for sentiment analysis in the Persian language. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach, multiple architectures were examined, including standalone models (BERT, RoBERTa, RNN, and BiLSTM), ensemble models based on averaging and majority voting strategies, and two hybrid configurations that integrate sequential and transformer-based models. Experimental results indicate that BiLSTM outperforms other standalone approaches, while the ensemble model using average voting and the hybrid configuration Hybrid-1 (BERT-RNN-BiLSTM) achieve the highest classification performance across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating diverse deep learning strategies and emphasize the practical applicability of hybrid and ensemble architectures for Persian sentiment classification. This study presents a comprehensive and systematic investigation of hybrid transformer–recurrent architectures and ensemble learning strategies for Persian sentiment analysis, supported by extensive experiments on benchmark datasets. The proposed models were evaluated on four benchmark Persian sentiment analysis datasets, namely the Persian Electronic Dataset, MirasOpinion Dataset, Instagram Persian Comment Dataset and SentiDariPers Dataset. Experimental results, supported by comparative analysis with existing studies, demonstrate the consistent superiority of the proposed framework across all datasets. In particular, the Hybrid-1 (BERT-RNN-BiLSTM) model achieved the highest accuracy of 97.00% on the Persian Electronic Dataset, while accuracies of 84.00%, 80.75% and 95.19% were obtained on the MirasOpinion, Instagram Persian Comment and SentiDariPers datasets, respectively. Furthermore, the Hybrid-2 (RoBERTa-BiLSTM-RNN) and the proposed ensemble models also demonstrated strong and consistent performance across all four datasets, confirming the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed architectures for Persian sentiment classification.

Article.Title: Exploratory analysis of peripheral blood monocytes in breast cancer using prospective high-dimensional immune profiling
Article.Authors: Alsuwaidi L.; Panicker N.; AlHalabi W.; Samreen B.; Abdulrahim M.; AlSharhan M.; Otaki F.; Ghazi E.; Al Awa A.; Senok A.; Hachim M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is a heterogeneous disease characterized by diverse molecular and immune features and blood-based immunophenotyping may provide insights into systemic immune variation relevant to treatment. Baseline immune profiling before surgery or systemic therapy reflects the natural tumor–host interaction and systemic immune status. In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating study, we integrated in silico analysis of publicly available high-dimensional immune profiling data with an independent prospective assessment of selected peripheral immune populations. Publicly available mass cytometry data from CD45 + viable singlet peripheral blood mononuclear cells of healthy donors, hereditary breast and ovarian cancer predisposition carriers, and breast cancer patients were analyzed using the CATALYST pipeline in R. Based on the immune patterns identified in the public dataset, selected immune populations were subsequently examined in an independent cohort of 11 treatment-naïve breast cancer patients using eight-color flow cytometry. The two approaches were used as complementary analyses rather than as direct technical validation of one another. Unsupervised clustering identified 20 immune metaclusters, with CD4 + T-cell and CD14 + monocyte subsets showing the greatest variation across groups. Patients subsequently allocated to neoadjuvant chemotherapy exhibited higher lymphocyte percentages (median, 53% vs. 42%, P = 0.004) and classical CD14 + + CD16 − monocytes (median, 73% vs. 58%, P < 0.0001), whereas patients undergoing surgery showed higher non-classical CD14 + CD16 + + monocytes (median, 16% vs. 10, P = 0.078). CD80/CD86 co-expression further classified patients into high, moderate, and low activation profiles. These baseline immune differences were associated with subsequent treatment allocation but remain descriptive, as patients had not yet received treatment at the time of peripheral blood sampling, providing preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence of peripheral immune variation in breast cancer and supporting further investigation of monocyte and lymphocyte populations in larger prospective cohorts.

Article.Title: Types and prevalence of digital harassment from external and unknown individuals and prospective associations with employee health outcomes
Article.Authors: Winding T.; Pedersen A.; Andersen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital harassment from individuals external to the workplace is an emerging occupational health concern, but evidence on its longer-term health consequences remains limited. This prospective cohort study investigated characteristics associated with exposure, its prevalence, types, employee reactions, and associations with health outcomes among employees in Danish workplaces. Data were collected through two survey rounds in 2024, completed by 991 employees. Digital harassment was defined as harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse, threats, or unwanted sexual attention delivered through digital media. Qualitative thematic analysis identified ten harassment types and thirteen employee reactions. Outcomes included burnout, psychological well-being, and self-rated health. Overall, 28% reported at least one incident within the past year. Prevalence was higher among public sector employees, permanent staff, and employees with longer seniority. The most common forms were condescending or offensive messages and false accusations, typically eliciting irritation, intimidation, shock, or emotional exhaustion. Adjusting for gender, age, and seniority, baseline harassment was associated with higher burnout symptoms (β = 3.28, 95% CI 0.54–6.02) and higher odds of low self-rated health at follow-up (OR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.05–2.72), but not psychological well-being. These associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the respective baseline health outcome.

Article.Title: A personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated knee registration using single-plane moving fluoroscopy
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Li X.; Ćuković S.; Vogl F.; R. Taylor W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate knee joint kinematics are essential for biomechanical research and clinical assessment. Single-plane fluoroscopy is one of the most accurate tools for measuring in vivo joint motion, but manual estimation of three-dimensional bone pose from individual fluoroscopic frames remains labor-intensive and time-consuming. In this study, we present a personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated registration of knee fluoroscopic images acquired using single-plane moving fluoroscopy. The proposed framework combines pose standardization across acquisition sessions, subject-specific learning-based pose estimation, and differentiable-rendering-based pose refinement. Tested using fluoroscopic datasets of both natural knees and knee implants together with a PyTorch3D-based differentiable renderer, we trained subject-specific pose estimation networks for both anatomy types. Evaluation against manually matched reference poses showed mean initial in-plane translation differences of approximately 1.1–2.1 mm and geodesic rotation differences of 1.3–3.6 $$^\circ$$ with mask-only input, while out-of-plane translation differences remained larger, as expected in single-plane imaging. Gradient-based refinement using gradient correlation coefficient (GCC) further reduced the disagreement with the manual reference poses, resulting in sub-millimetre in-plane translation differences and sub-degree rotational differences, with over 95% of test frames satisfying the predefined success criterion that both the femoral and tibial registrations had absolute in-plane translation differences below 1 mm in both $$T_x$$ and $$T_y$$ and a geodesic rotation difference below 1 $$^\circ$$ . These results quantify agreement with the existing manual registration workflow rather than independently validated anatomical pose accuracy.

Article.Title: Dual fear mechanisms shaping stochastic population dynamics under the Allee effect
Article.Authors: Gültekin Ö.; Muradli M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional population models that include predator–prey interactions attribute demographic changes directly to predation-related effects. However, predator-induced fear in prey has increasingly been recognised as an important factor shaping population dynamics. In this study, we propose a cubic population model in which fear acts through two distinct functional channels for a single-species population exhibiting the Allee effect. In this model, fear reduces the intrinsic growth rate through a multiplicative suppression mechanism while also playing an integrated role in modulating the growth and interaction dynamics by rescaling the saturation structure of the Holling type III interaction term. The stochastic extension of the model is described by a Langevin formalism containing correlated additive and multiplicative Gaussian noise, and the steady state probability distribution (SSPD) is analytically obtained using the corresponding Fokker–Planck equation. The analytical solution is validated by numerical simulations. The SSPD reveals both noise-induced transitions and fear-controlled regime changes between low- and high-density states, with the dual-channel structure producing structural competition and non-monotonic changes in the distribution. These are analysed through phenomenological bifurcation (P-bifurcation) diagrams and three-dimensional distribution surfaces. Additionally, statistical properties, parameter sensitivity, and escape dynamics are investigated through normalised moments, Fisher information, and mean first-passage time (MFPT) calculations. Notably, our model treats fear as an independent control parameter and provides a theoretical mechanism capable of generating qualitatively contrasting population responses across parameter regimes, while also offering a framework for examining critical transition dynamics of potential relevance to conservation and management.

Article.Title: Neuro-immune transformer with contextual self-attention for IoT intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Bajpayi P.; Mathur S.; Gaur M.
Article.Abstract: The exponential growth in IoT gadgets has made the attack surface in contemporary. The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has dramatically expanded cyber attack surfaces, while existing intrusion detection systems struggle to cope with evolving attack patterns, noise, and imbalanced network traffic. Deep learning models fail to generalize to novel attacks, and biological models lack the contextual understanding required to capture complex relationships within network data. To address these limitations, we propose the Neuro-Immune Transformer (NIT), a novel hybrid architecture that integrates a transformer-based contextualization engine with an adaptive Artificial Immune System (AIS) employing Clonal Selection Algorithm for detector evolution. The transformer module utilizes multi-head self-attention to capture long-range dependencies in network behavior, while the immune module maintains an evolving detector population to identify unknown attack patterns through co-evolutionary training in an end-to-end framework. We evaluate NIT on the imbalanced WUSTL EHMS 2020 IoMT dataset and compare against state-of-the-art bio-inspired, deep learning, and hybrid approaches. NIT achieves superior performance with 98.04% accuracy, 92.9% detection rate, 0.9168 F1-score, and only 1.4% false alarm rate, significantly outperforming all baselines. Ablation studies confirm the critical contribution of each architectural component, while robustness tests demonstrate resilience against Gaussian noise and FGSM adversarial attacks. With 856 K parameters and 3.2 ms inference latency, NIT offers a computationally efficient and practical solution suitable for resource-constrained edge-IoT deployment, providing scalable and robust intrusion detection for healthcare IoT networks.

Article.Title: Repeatability of upper limb volume measurements based on the Kuhnke measurement protocol and frustum volume calculation in women after unilateral mastectomy: a cross-sectional methodological study
Article.Authors: Smoter M.; Roczniok R.; Muracki J.; Maliszewski D.; Tarkowski R.; Trybulski R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to assess the repeatability of upper limb volume measurements performed with the Kuhnke method using the Frustum Volume Calculation (FVC) in women with lymphedema after unilateral mastectomy. This cross-sectional methodological study included 101 women (stage I: n = 52; stage II: n = 49). Three independent physiotherapists, each with at least five years of clinical experience, performed two repeated measurements (T1, T2) of both the affected and the healthy limb using the Kuhnke FVC method. Repeatability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEM), and minimal detectable change (MDC). The mean volume of the healthy limb was ~ 2209–2210 ml, while the affected limb averaged ~ 2438–2440 ml, yielding a mean interlimb difference of 229–230 ml. Intra-rater reliability was excellent, with ICC values of 0.986 for the healthy limb, 0.983 for the affected limb, and 0.945 for the interlimb difference. SEM values ranged from 6 to 8 ml, and MDC values were 16–22 ml, indicating very low measurement error. Inter-rater analysis confirmed high agreement, with no statistically significant differences between raters (p≈0.99). The interlimb volume difference was more than twice as large in stage II lymphedema (314.7 ± 67.1 ml) compared with stage I (148.6 ± 38.7 ml; p < 0.000001). The Kuhnke method with FVC formula demonstrates excellent intra- and inter-rater repeatability and can be recommended as a simple, cost-effective, and clinically reliable tool for diagnosing and monitoring upper limb lymphedema in women after mastectomy.

Article.Title: Sustainable construction and artificial intelligence: the role of agile project management in construction project resilience in Pakistan
Article.Authors: Miao M.; Naqvi M.; Naqvi M.; Jamal E.
Article.Abstract: This research analyzes sustainable construction practices and technology adoption, and their relationships with the adoption of Agile Project Management and the resilience of construction projects. Agile Project Management is incorporated in the model as a bridge. Employing DCT as the major research foundation, this study assesses the role of integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and sustainable construction practices with project resilience through Agile Project Management. The Technology-Organization-Environment framework provides context to the integration of AI and construction in Pakistan. The CAS theory provides a wider framework to think about the system. The T-O-E framework and the CAS theory are integrated and do not require empirical evidence. Agile Project Management combines sustainability and construction practices with Artificial Intelligence to facilitate achievement of project resilience. Findings demonstrate that both the integration of AI with construction practices and project resilience are positively influenced by sustainable construction practices. Of all the relationships evaluated, AI integration with construction practices showed the highest positive influence on project resilience. It is important to exercise caution when interpreting this relationship, as all the relationships were assessed in a single, cross-sectional survey, therefore, it could be attributed to common method biases. The T-O-E framework addresses the integration of AI with construction in Pakistan, while the CAS theory is integrated and does not require empirical evidence. A Construct validity approach was used to assess professionals and students of Construction and related disciplines in the Punjab province of Pakistan. Of the 300 questionnaires distributed, 244 completed responses were received. PLS-SEM analysis was performed on 188 questionnaires, from which 56 were rejected due to failure to meet quality standards. The analysis was conducted using an adapted form of multi-item scales of 5-point Likert scale, to assess sustainable construction, artificial intelligence, and agile project management. Data were analyzed through the framework of PLS-SEM. Results showed that integration of Artificial Intelligence in project management enhanced project resilience. The effect of agile project management on project resilience also was positive. Further, the effect of sustainable construction on project resilience also was positive. Additionally, the effects of integration of Artificial Intelligence and sustainable construction combined positively influenced project resilience. This research extends Dynamic Capabilities Theory, by incorporating AI and construction methods focused on sustainability in the field of agile project management and project resilience.

Article.Title: High-throughput screen identifies metabolite regulators of endothelial function
Article.Authors: Oliveira F.; Bondareva O.; Hoffmann A.; Geier F.; Kyselova A.; Karantanou C.; Bibli S.; Sheikh B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Endothelial cells (ECs) line blood vessels, regulate organ homeostasis, and their dysfunction is central to the development of cardiovascular diseases. Metabolites are critical regulators of EC health and function, yet only a limited number of metabolites that impact ECs have been identified. Here, we undertook a high-throughput screen of 884 metabolites and common drugs found in human biofluids to systematically identify compounds that impact barrier function in primary human umbilical vein ECs (HUVECs). Seven metabolites that deregulate vascular barrier function without causing cell death were shortlisted. These include (-)-epigallocatechin gallate, (±)-3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid, taurocholic acid, myricetin, meloxicam, hesperetin and trans-3-indoleacrylic acid. These metabolites elicited differential effects on HUVECs, coronary artery ECs and pulmonary ECs. Transcriptional profiling revealed that each of the seven metabolites triggered distinct transcriptional responses in ECs, suggesting distinct mechanisms triggering EC barrier disruption. Notably, trans-3-indoleacrylic acid deregulated VE-cadherin junctions and increased EC sprouting, suggesting a potential role in angiogenesis. Together, these results provide a screening resource for metabolite-endothelial interactions and identify candidate circulating metabolites that regulate endothelial function.

Article.Title: Real-time heuristic evacuation pathfinding algorithm for flood avoidance
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Tian L.; Feng Y.; Ma D.
Article.Abstract: Floods rank among the world’s most devastating annual disasters in terms of casualties and economic losses, making evacuation route planning crucial for mitigating flood risks. This study proposes a Real-time Heuristic Flood Evacuation Path Planning Algorithm (RHEPFA) based on dynamic flood simulations using the ANUGA 2D model. Its core innovation lies in a novel dual-range (dangerous and safe) heuristic weighting mechanism that efficiently anticipates flood progression. Uniquely coupled with hydrodynamic forecasts, RHEPFA conducts real-time pathfinding based on moving speeds, terrain constraints, and inundation dynamics. This innovative approach maintains over 90% accessibility, which outperforms static Dijkstra and ant colony optimization algorithms. Compared to the dynamic Dijkstra algorithm, RHEPFA still demonstrates outstanding performance with 12.5% higher accessibility, 22.8% shorter path length, 81.3% lower computational cost, and more importantly, 10.43% longer evacuation time window. Entrapment rate is further found to have a negative correlation with evacuation speed, as taking a faster transit means can significantly reduce entrapment rates.

Article.Title: Generative AI-powered multimodal physiological sensors for personalized edge health monitoring
Article.Authors: Aldehim G.; Nair R.; Aldhyani T.; Sharma V.; Ahmad S.; Alzahrani A.; Al-Adhaileh M.; Osman A.
Article.Abstract: This study focuses on personalized edge inference for multi-source physiological time-series signals instead of imaging data. The main contribution is a lightweight model for personalized, calibrated prediction that integrates a generative prior and flexible latent structures for denoising and imputation for short segments of ECG/PPG followed by prediction. Supporting components include federated learning, privacy-preservation mechanisms, and TinyML. Experiments were performed using the public MIMIC-III Waveform Database. The analyzed dataset comprised 10,282 patients and 22,317 patient-disjoint, record-level windows for binary (abnormal/risk) event classification. Positive labels were assigned to the physiological abnormality window intervals, and negative labels were assigned to the stable, non-event interval classes. Separating the data for training, validation, and testing was performed at the patient level using a disjoint 70%/15%/15% split of the patient datasets (7,197/1,542/1,543 patients), with approximately 30% positive-class examples, and ensured that no windows occurred across multiple partitions. Within this primary experimental setting, GenWear achieved an AUROC of 0.956 ± 0.006, AUPRC of 0.735 ± 0.026, F1 of 0.842 ± 0.016, and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.017; the best edge baseline achieved an AUROC of 0.951 ± 0.008. An INT8 implementation of GenWear on a GAP9 chip achieved 45 Hz and had a latency of 22/34 ms for p50/p95 with an inference energy of 1.45 mJ. Several studies assessed the robustness of the model against missing data, noise, and domain shift. Given MIMIC-III contains ICU data, the data should only be considered a proof of concept for physiological sensing with wearable devices. A validation study on a real-world ambulatory dataset is still required.

Article.Title: Regional climate variability and rice yields prediction in Bangladesh using machine learning and deep learning models
Article.Authors: Rahman N.; Haque N.; Akhtar P.; Fatema M.; Shrabony N.; Begum R.; Anik A.; Parvin M.
Article.Abstract: This study compared conventional regression, machine-learning, and deep-learning models for Aman and Boro rice across the Barind, Coastal, and Riverine regions of Bangladesh using data from 1970 to 2024. Climate records from the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) and rice-yield data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) were matched by location and date; 1287 records were retained for each season before region-specific modeling. Predictors included maximum and minimum temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, and sunshine duration. Nine models were evaluated using cross-validation-based hyperparameter selection and multiple metrics, including MAE, RMSE, MAPE, R 2 , and prediction bias; MAE and RMSE are reported in t ha⁻ 1 . Correlation analysis showed consistently negative associations of temperature with rice production ( r = − 0.13 to − 0.28), while rainfall ( r = 0.03–0.21) and relative humidity ( r = 0.07–0.32) showed positive but region-dependent associations; sunshine relationships were weak. TFT achieved the lowest RMSE in four of six region–season combinations: Coastal Aman (0.22), Barind Boro (0.30), Riverine Aman (0.16), and Riverine Boro (0.31 t ha⁻ 1 ). For Coastal Aman, TFT achieved MAE = 0.20 t ha⁻ 1 and R 2 = 0.958; for Riverine Aman, MAE = 0.14 t ha⁻ 1 and R 2 = 0.773. GBM performed best for Coastal Boro (RMSE = 0.64 t ha⁻ 1 ; R 2 = 0.308), while CatBoost and GBM showed the lowest RMSE for Barind Aman (0.54 t ha⁻ 1 ). The study provides a region- and season-specific comparison of statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning approaches, supporting targeted forecasting and adaptation priorities for drought-prone Barind, salinity-affected Coastal, and flood-prone Riverine areas.

Article.Title: Exploring the potential of distributed acoustic sensing for fish bioacoustics
Article.Authors: Eceiza A.; Sladen A.; Brunel O.; Bonnet N.; Gaglio V.; Simonet R.; Mittaine F.; Cottalorda J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underwater soundscapes are critical indicators of marine ecosystem health, but traditional passive acoustic monitoring with hydrophones is spatially limited and logistically challenging for long-term observations. This study investigates the potential of distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) to overcome these limitations. A field trial was conducted using a bespoke fiber-optic cable deployed off the coast of Monaco, focusing on three sound-producing Mediterranean species: Ophidion rochei , Sciaena umbra , and Epinephelus marginatus , all known for their distinct acoustic signatures. DAS recordings reveal species-specific patterns consistent with documented behaviors, and are validated by co-located hydrophone recordings. Due to its high sensor density, DAS allows the isolation and localization of individual sounds over tens of meters. The results demonstrate that DAS can detect and locate fish sounds under real-world conditions, while also assessing ambient noise levels. The DAS setup in this experiment may not match the performance of conventional hydrophones, but the approach’s potential for dense, continuous, and low-maintenance monitoring, particularly where suitable fiber-optic infrastructure already exists, points to a promising complementary role in marine conservation in the context of climate change and biodiversity loss.

Article.Title: Adipose-derived stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles promote critical-sized bone defect repair by enhancing the homing of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Jing J.; Tong X.; Ma S.; Qiu Y.; Liu Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: The repair of critical-sized bone defects remains a significant clinical challenge. As a cell-free alternative, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs-EVs) hold promise, yet their precise mechanism in promoting bone repair is remain to be fully elucidated. This study investigated whether ADSCs-EVs enhance bone repair by promoting the homing and osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). ADSCs-EVs were isolated and co-cultured with BMSCs to assess proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation in vitro. Key gene expression (e.g., Cxcr4, Runx2) was analyzed. A highly elastic hydrogel was used for sustained EVs delivery in a rat calvarial defect model. mouse bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (mBMSCs) homing was monitored via live imaging, and bone regeneration was evaluated by micro-CT and histology. Results showed that ADSCs-EVs promoted BMSCs migration and osteogenesis, rapidly upregulating homing-related genes (Ccr7, Cxcr4) and subsequently activating osteogenic genes (Runx2, OPN). In vivo, the ADSCs-EVs/hydrogel complex enhanced the recruitment of BMSCs to the defect site compared with the control group, which was associated with improved new bone formation. This study demonstrates that ADSCs-EVs enhance BMSCs migration and osteogenic differentiation in vitro. Mechanistically, ADSCs-EVs rapidly upregulated homing-related genes (Ccr7, Cxcr4, MMP9) in BMSCs at 12 h, followed by activation of osteogenic genes (Runx2, OPN, OCN) at later time points, revealing a two-stage ‘recruit-and-activate’ mechanism. When delivered via a highly elastic hydrogel, ADSCs-EVs promoted the recruitment of intravenously administered BMSCs to a critical-sized bone defect in vivo, as visualized by bioluminescence imaging. These findings support a strategy that combines EVs-mediated homing enhancement with cell transplantation, while also suggesting potential implications for endogenous cell recruitment.

Article.Title: Nano route with DFT, docking studies, ADMET, and SAR of a pyran-functionalized pyrimidine scaffold as a potent Rhizoctonia solani
Article.Authors: Farag B.; El-Bana G.; El-Lateef H.; Bouachrine M.; El-Sayed A.; Saeed A.; Fouad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Numerous plant infections known as phytopathogenic fungi are responsible for a broad range of agricultural illnesses. Recent research focuses on developing, synthesizing, and evaluating pyran-linked pyrimidine hybrids as potential antifungals. In this study, the target hybrids of the pyran-functionalized pyrimidine scaffold were optimized synthesized using nanoscience-based techniques. A multi-step process involving nucleophilic substitution reaction, cyclization, acetylation, hydrolysis, condensation, and Dimroth rearrangement afforded pyran-pyrimidine hybrids 1–7. In this study, the antifungal potency of optimized synthesized compounds (3, 5, and 6) against various therapeutic targets of the phytopathogenic fungus Rhizoctonia solani was assessed using a thorough computational approach. Investigated hybrids, especially 3, 5, and 6 at 20 ppm and 50 ppm, exhibited strong resistance to the fungus Rhizoctonia solani , representing a potential antifungal control against soil-borne plant pathogens. Molecular docking analyses revealed these compounds exhibit potent, multi-target binding affinities, frequently outperforming the reference drug fluconazole, particularly against sterol-14-alpha-demethylase, chitin synthase, cellulose synthase, and cytochrome bc 1 . Simulations involving molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA (Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area)/PBSA (Poisson-Boltzmann Surface Area) free energy computations over trajectories for compound 3 confirmed the formation of highly stable and dynamically viable complexes. Pharmacokinetically and according to ADMET assessments, tested hybrids comply with accepted drug-likeness rules (Lipinski, Pfizer, and Golden Triangle) and present minimal risk of cytochrome P450 inhibition. According to findings of computational analyses that confirmed fungal potency evaluation, optimized synthesized compounds are promising bioactive candidates for developing effective fungicides. This study is the first to compare the protective effects of pyran-functionalized pyrimidine against Rhizoctonia solani supported by computational analyses.

Article.Title: Improving inconsistency in pairwise comparison matrices using normalized euclidean distance and grey wolf optimization in multicriteria decision making
Article.Authors: Kaushik S.; Pant S.; Kumar A.; Joshi L.
Article.Abstract: Ensuring the Consistency of the Pairwise Comparison Matrix (PCM) is crucial in the Multicriteria Decision Making (MCDM) process. This study not only addresses inconsistency correction in PCM but also identifies a substitute matrix that closely approximates the original. To achieve this, we propose a novel distance metric, the Normalized Euclidean Distance (NED), which helps determine the substitute matrix within a maximum correction range. It ensures that the modified matrix remains as close as possible to the original while improving Consistency. Additionally, we introduce an advanced swarm intelligence technique, Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), which researchers have widely adopted for various optimization problems due to its efficiency. Unlike many other swarm-based methods, GWO requires relatively few parameters and does not rely on derivatives during the initial search. By integrating the NED formula, the maximum correction range, and GWO, our approach achieves better consistency repair than existing methods while minimizing deviations from the original matrix. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and improved performance of the proposed method.

Article.Title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and regression of the effect of CPAP on metabolic and inflammatory markers in obstructive sleep apnea
Article.Authors: Atanasescu A.; Ciorobea A.; Tora F.; Topoliceanu I.; Nedelcu R.; Ion D.; Bălășescu E.
Article.Abstract: The effect of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) on reducing inflammatory and metabolic markers plays an important role in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) management, however data remains inconsistent. This systematic review and pre-post meta-regression indicate the effect of CPAP on improving inflammation and metabolic markers in patients with OSA. A systematic search was performed on PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus, including English, full-access trials with CPAP-naïve adult patients with OSA. Markers of choice were CRP, IL-6, TNF-alpha, LDL, insulin, insulin resistance, leptin, adiponectin and homocysteine. Data about confounders were collected and used in a meta-regression to assess their relationship with the intervention. Studies underwent a sensitivity analysis and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE frameworks. CPAP therapy significantly reduces CRP (-0.48 SMD [-0.65, -0.31]) and LDL (-0.32 SMD [-0.43, -0.20]) levels. The effect on reducing insulin resistance remains fragile and lacked robustness in sensitivity analysis. Evidence certainty proved low across these outcomes due to heterogeneity, indirectness and publication bias. CPAP improved IL-6 levels (-0.31 SMD [-0.54, -0.08]). After the sensitivity analysis, post-therapeutic leptin levels showed to be slightly improved (-0.19 SMD [-0.32,-0.05]). Meta-regression results indicated that daily CPAP hours usage was associated with better CRP reduction (β = −0.117 per hour/night). No other confounder showed a significant association. CPAP improves inflammatory and metabolic status, lowering inflammatory markers, LDL and insulin resistance, although the certainty of evidence was low.

Article.Title: Development and validation of the eHealth literacy scale for college students aged 18-24 years, Faridabad, India
Article.Authors: Haldar P.; Jeer G.; Kant S.; Malhotra S.; Dwivedi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Internet is commonly used source of health information all over the world. Despite this availability, many people doesn’t have ability to use this health information for their benefit. This ability depends on eHealth literacy’s underlying concept, which is the ability to seek, find, understand, and appraise health information from electronic resources and apply that knowledge in making a health-related decision. There is no studies on eHealth literacy among college students in India who frequently use the internet to access health-related information. The present study was conducted to develop and validate an eHealth literacy scale for college students. The initial phase of the study focuses on developing items from literature review and focus group discussions (FGD) and also on assessing the face and content validity of items through content validity index(CVI). The next three phases focused on design validation, factor analysis, and reliability of newly developed scale among 163 college students. Exploratory factor analysis used to assess construct validity. The internal consistency reliability was measured using Cronbach’s alpha. The tool, which began as a 30-item draft, was gradually reshaped through a series of modifications. A total of 163 participants (81 boys; 82 girls) aged 18 to 24 (mean = 21.21; SD = 1.64) completed the survey. Parallel analysis and exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor solution (eigenvalues ranging from 2.428 to 1.269), which aligned with our conceptual domains of eHealth Literacy. Retained items demonstrated salient factor loadings (> 0.30). Cronbach’s alpha value of scale came to be 0.75. A 21-item, comprehensive eHealth Literacy scale structured across five distinct factors for college students was developed. The scale demonstrated acceptable overall internal consistency and preliminary evidence of construct validity. Further validation using larger, independent samples is required to confirm the factor structure.

Article.Title: A resource-efficient Q-learning algorithm using Boltzmann policy
Article.Authors: Bazmalah A.; Kamal N.; Chellappan K.; Moubark A.; Bazmalah A.
Article.Abstract: Q-learning (QL) faces a challenge in balancing exploration and exploitation. QL typically employs an ε-greedy policy. However, the ε-greedy policy leads to slow convergence and excessive resource consumption on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) due to unnecessary exploration. This paper proposes a hardware Q-learning architecture that integrates the Boltzmann policy using fixed-point representation. The design is implemented on the Genesys 2 Kintex7 (XC7K325T-2FFG900C) FPGA. Utilizing the Boltzmann policy's ability to prioritize optimal actions, the present design significantly reduces the number of iterations required to update states. This reduction results in faster convergence and a more efficient resource allocation strategy. Experimental results demonstrate improved FPGA resource efficiency. For 16-bit implementations, the proposed design limits the usage of Look-Up Tables (LUTs), LUTRAMs, Flip-Flops (FFs), and Block Random Access Memories (BRAMs) to just 0.86%, 0.06%, 0.27%, and 0.79% of the total available hardware resources, respectively. Similar for 32-bit implementations, the usage of LUTs, LUTRAMs, FFs, and BRAMs is restricted to 1.26%, 0.01%, 0.38%, and 2.02%, respectively. Moreover, the proposed design achieves power efficiency improvements of 46% for 16-bit configurations and 28% for 32-bit configurations. Based on these results, the proposed Boltzmann-based QL architecture effectively optimizes FPGA resource utilization while enhancing overall system performance.

Article.Title: Imbalance-robust predictive maintenance using deep learning with virtual measurement modeling and explainable AI
Article.Authors: Eldeeb O.; Aboutabl A.; Bahloul M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predictive maintenance (PdM) has become a key enabler of intelligent industrial systems; however, its effectiveness is often constrained by measurement uncertainty, the absence of raw sensor signals, and severe class imbalance between normal and failure events. This paper proposes a measurement-aware predictive maintenance framework that utilizes operational variables as virtual measurement proxies, enabling measurement-oriented analysis without requiring raw sensor signals. Using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset, the proposed framework integrates a hybrid imbalance-handling strategy that combines Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and cost-sensitive learning to improve failure detection under highly imbalanced conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework consistently outperforms the baseline, the SMOTE-only configuration, and the cost-sensitive configuration. Among the evaluated classifiers, LightGBM achieved the best overall performance with an F1-score of 0.9043, followed by DNN (0.8708) and XGBoost (0.8680). SHAP-based explainability analysis identified tool wear and torque as the most influential predictors of machine failure. At the same time, robustness experiments with simulated Gaussian measurement noise demonstrated stable performance across low and moderate noise levels. An ablation study further confirmed the complementary contributions of SMOTE and cost-sensitive learning. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable approach for predictive maintenance on the AI4I 2020 benchmark dataset, while further validation using real industrial datasets is required before practical deployment.

Article.Title: DOMS: Dynamic Occupancy Management System - a space management technique for smart buildings
Article.Authors: Roshan A.; SK K.; Ricky Issac T.; Pramodh A.
Article.Abstract: Space management in smart buildings requires expert knowledge and demands manual intervention. Analysing the space, choosing spots to deploy sensors are manually done by experts even in this modern era. Though planned by experts there are inefficiencies in sensor placement and deployment. To address this issue, we propose a framework for better space management in smart buildings called as DOMS (Dynamic Occupancy Management System). In this framework, we have integrated computer vision, language model and graph based intelligence for achieving the smart space management solution. We have utilized YOLOv5 for extracting the structural and geometric features from the floor plan. These extracted features are used to build the Spatial Knowledge Graph (SKG) where SKG helps in finding semantic relationship between the identified objects in the floor plan. This SKG is then processed by a fine-tuned LLaMA 3.2 model that performs semantic reasoning to recommend suitable sensor types, optimal placement strategies, and communication modules based on contextual constraints such as room purpose and occupancy flow. This hybrid reasoning enables DOMS to achieve adaptive, explainable, and automated configuration of IoT-based smart environments. Experimental results demonstrate improved coverage accuracy, reduced manual intervention, and enhanced scalability compared to conventional occupancy systems.

Article.Title: Enhancing production assurance in longwall coal mining through reliability assessment of the shearer
Article.Authors: Rahimdel M.; Sadeghzadeh S.
Article.Abstract: Mechanized longwall mining is one of the most productive methods for underground coal extraction, where continuous operation of the shearer machine is essential for maintaining stable production levels. Failures in the shearer or its subsystems can lead to unplanned downtime, reduced availability, and significant production losses. Therefore, evaluating the operational reliability of shearer machines and quantifying their impact on production performance are critical for effective mine management. In this study, the production capacity of a mechanized longwall coal mine is assessed through reliability analysis of the shearer machine, with particular attention to its critical subsystems. Reliability functions were developed for the water supply and electrical subsystems, which were identified as the main contributors to operational interruptions. The results show that the reliability of the electrical and water subsystems approaches zero after approximately 1500 h and 2500 h of operation, respectively. Using the derived reliability models, the associated production risk was quantified and estimated at 0.38 tons per hour. The proposed approach provides a practical and transferable framework for linking subsystem reliability to production risk in mechanized mining operations. The findings can support maintenance planning, downtime reduction strategies, and improved production reliability in underground coal mines.

Article.Title: Serum metabolomic signatures associated with growth hormone replacement therapy in children with postoperative craniopharyngioma
Article.Authors: Xu R.; Du H.; Zhang L.; Song S.; Chen S.; Duan L.; Zhu H.; Pan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Growth hormone replacement therapy (GHRT) is commonly used to treat growth hormone deficiency (GHD) after craniopharyngioma (CP) surgery, but its metabolic consequences in pediatric patients remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to investigate serum metabolomic alterations associated with GHRT in pediatric patients with postoperative childhood-onset CP. We conducted an untargeted serum metabolomics study in 60 pediatric patients with childhood-onset CP following surgery, including 32 patients receiving GHRT and 28 patients not receiving GHRT. Clinical data and biochemical parameters were collected. Serum metabolites were profiled using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Differential metabolite identification, pathway enrichment analysis, and correlation analyses were conducted to characterize GHRT-associated metabolic signatures and their relationships with clinical indicators. Patients receiving GHRT had higher insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels, whereas conventional lipid parameters did not differ significantly between groups. HOMA-IR was higher and QUICKI was lower in the GHRT group. Using stringent criteria of VIP > 1, BH-FDR q < 0.05, and |log₂FC| > 2, 10 key positive-ion metabolites were identified, including phosphatidylcholine, triglycerides, sphingomyelins (SMs), and 3,5-diiodo-L-thyronine (T2). Nine lipid-related metabolites were higher and T2 was lower in the GHRT group. These associations remained significant after adjustment for chronological age and postoperative interval and in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for sex-steroid replacement. GHRT exposure in children and adolescents with postoperative childhood-onset CP was associated with distinct serum metabolomic signatures, predominantly involving phosphatidylcholine, triglycerides, and SMs. These findings represent exploratory associations and require confirmation in longitudinal studies before treatment-related or clinical implications can be established.

Article.Title: Respiration–action coupling and intentional binding in a Libet clock paradigm
Article.Authors: Shibata H.; Patchitt J.; Nagai Y.; Mizuhara K.; Critchley H.; Ohira H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interoception, the physiological sensing of internal bodily states, has been proposed to contribute to the sense of self. However, empirical research that directly investigates interoceptive contributions to the sense of agency remains limited. Based on the observed synchronisation between respiratory phase and the initiation of voluntary action, we implemented the Libet clock task to test the hypothesis that the respiratory phase would modulate intentional binding (IB), a temporal binding phenomenon often used as an implicit measure related to agency. Additionally, we aimed to replicate respiration–action synchronisation and to examine exploratory cardiac-phase effects on binding. The overall key-binding effect was small and did not reach statistical significance, whereas tone binding was significant. Neither key nor tone binding showed reliable respiratory-phase modulation, although respiration–action synchronisation was replicated. Bayesian model comparisons strongly favoured models in which binding did not vary with respiratory phase. For cardiac phase, a frequentist mixed-effects model suggested phase-dependent modulation of key binding, but Bayesian model comparison did not support including cardiac-phase interactions. Together, these findings show that respiration–action coupling was present in the task but was not accompanied by detectable respiratory-phase modulation of intentional binding; the cardiac finding should be considered exploratory.

Article.Title: Characterization of the gut microbiota in older adults with vascular stiffness
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vascular stiffness is a hallmark of vascular aging and a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases in older adults. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may contribute to vascular dysfunction; however, the microbial characteristics associated with vascular stiffness remain insufficiently understood. This cross-sectional study included older adults with and without vascular stiffness. A total of 110 adults aged ≥ 60 years were recruited from nursing homes and categorized into the vascular stiffness group (baPWV ≥ 1800 cm/s, VG, n = 91) and a non–vascular stiffness group (baPWV < 1800 cm/s, CG, n = 19). Fecal samples were analyzed using shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the BGI DNBSEQ platform. Microbial composition, α-diversity, and functional profiles were characterized, and differential taxa and their associations with vascular stiffness-related parameters were evaluated. VG exhibited significantly higher abundances of Deltaproteobacteria , Desulfovibrionales , Rikenellaceae , Desulfovibrionaceae , and the genera Alistipes , Ruthenibacterium , and Eisenbergiella ( P < 0.05). In contrast, Holdemanella biformis and Veillonella tobetsuensis were enriched in CG (LDA score > 2). Functional pathway analysis revealed significant upregulation of lipid metabolism and betalain biosynthesis pathways in VG. Correlation analysis showed that Alistipes putredinis was positively associated with SBP, whereas Veillonella tobetsuensis was negatively associated with baPWV ( P < 0.05). Older adults with vascular stiffness exhibited distinct alterations in gut microbiota composition and functional profiles compared with non-affected controls. Although several microbial taxa were differentially abundant between groups, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for age, sex, and lipid profiles, suggesting that individual microbial taxa may be influenced by host aging and metabolic status. These findings indicate that vascular stiffness-associated gut microbiota alterations are more likely to reflect broader changes in microbial community structure and function rather than the independent effects of specific microbial taxa (Ethics committee: 2020082 H).

Article.Title: Synthesis of a 2D/2D g-C3N4/UiO-66 S-scheme heterojunction for enhanced photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants
Article.Authors: Rezaei P.; Tanzifi M.; Peyravi M.
Article.Abstract: A unique 2D/2D g-C 3 N 4 /UiO-66 S-scheme nano-heterojunction was successfully developed via a straightforward hydrothermal approach to enhance the photocatalytic decomposition of organic contaminants under visible light. Comprehensive characterization techniques were employed to systematically examine the properties of the individual semiconductors and the newly synthesized heterostructure. PL, EIS and PR analyses confirmed that the photo-generated charge carries in 2D/2D nano-heterojunction/visible-light system have been efficiently separated. The improved photocatalytic performance could be ascribed to the strong contact between nanosheets of two semiconductors, uniform dispersion of UiO-66 nanosheets on the surface of large g-C 3 N 4 nanosheets and synergistic effect of S-scheme electron-hole migration. The nano-heterojunction synthesized at the mass ratio of 0.2:1 of UiO-66 nanosheets to g-C 3 N 4 nanosheets, g-C 3 N 4 /UiO-66/20, exhibited the highest MB photo-degradation rate (70.19% and 98.25% at catalyst dosages of 0.1 and 0.3 g/L, respectively), where the kinetic constant is 2.53 and 4.10 times of pristine g-C 3 N 4 and UiO-66, respectively. Quenching experiments identified \(\:{.O}_{2}^{-}\) , \(\:.OH\) and \(\:{h}^{+}\) as the predominant active species, in descending order of importance. g-C 3 N 4 /UiO-66/20 nano-heterojunction indicated tremendous reusability and consistency, and it can be employed to successively uptake pollutant molecules from wastewater. This paper paves the way to construction of new visible-light driven 2D/2D nano-heterojunctions for the wastewater treatment process.

Article.Title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of INPP5K-related congenital muscular dystrophy in four Egyptian patients
Article.Authors: Zaki M.; Abdel-Ghafar S.; Rafat K.; Elbendary H.; ElKhayat S.; Saleh D.; Gleeson J.; Abdel-Salam G.; Abdel-Hamid M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract INPP5K -related congenital muscular dystrophy is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by variable combinations of early-onset cataracts, proximal muscle weakness, elevated serum creatine kinase, and intellectual disability. To date, about 31 affected individuals have been reported worldwide, and the clinical and molecular spectrum of the disorder remains incompletely defined. Herein, we describe four patients from three unrelated consanguineous Egyptian families. All patients presented with hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, microcephaly, waddling gait, elevated serum creatine kinase, and mild intellectual disability. Cataracts were identified in only two patients, highlighting the incomplete penetrance of this hallmark feature. Brain MRI was normal in two patients whereas mild asymmetry of the lateral ventricles and thin corpus callosum were identified in the remaining two patients. Axonal neuropathy and delayed puberty, features infrequently reported in INPP5K -related disease, were also observed in our cohort. Exome sequencing identified three homozygous INPP5K variants, including the recurrent p.(Ile50Thr) and two previously unreported missense variants: p.(Arg234Pro) within the catalytic 5-phosphatase domain and p.(Tyr349Ser) within the C-terminal SKICH domain. Both variants affected highly conserved residues, were absent from public population databases, and consistently predicted to be deleterious by multiple in-silico tools and protein structural modeling analyses. Our findings refine both the clinical and molecular spectrum of INPP5K -related muscular dystrophy and present the first report from Egypt and North Africa. In addition, the identification of variants affecting both major functional domains of the protein further supports the marked molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity associated with INPP5K deficiency.

Article.Title: Effect of herbal toothpaste versus conventional one on black stains in a group of Egyptian children: a randomized controlled study
Article.Authors: Rashed M.; Zaki Z.; Zeidan H.; Hashish A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To determine the recurrence rate of Black Stain (BS) in children using herbal versus fluoridated toothpaste formulations, in terms of stain recurrence, stain score, and parental satisfaction. Twenty- eight children with BS were randomly allocated into two groups: Control group I received a fluoridated toothpaste (Signal Cavity Fighter™), and experimental group II received an herbal toothpaste (Dabur Red™). Following dental polishing and salivary sample collection, the levels of four bacterial species— Streptococcus mutans (SM), Lactobacillus casei (LB), Actinomyces naeslundii (AC), and Prevotella melaninogenica (PM), were measured utilizing quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Both groups were evaluated for changes in stain score, percentage reduction in bacterial load, and degree of parental satisfaction. After 6 months, 85.7% of participants in the herbal group were significantly free from stain recurrence (p = 0.013, ω = 0.53; large effect size), achieved a stain score of 0 (p = 0.004, ω = 0.38; small effect size), and reported a satisfaction score of 5 (p = 0.008, δ = − 0.51; large effect size) compared with the control group. With regard to bacterial counts, the reduction in SM was significantly greater in the control group, whereas reductions in the other bacterial species were significantly greater in the herbal group, all with large effect sizes. Within the limitations of this study, herbal toothpaste may demonstrate promising efficacy in stain removal in terms of improving parental satisfaction, reducing stain recurrence and all included bacteria except SM in comparison to the control group. Trial registration: This study was registered retrospectively on Clinical Trials. gov on 03/06/2025 as first posted date before any outcome assessment; ID: NCT06872827; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06872827 .

Article.Title: Machine learning prediction and analysis of area-averaged external pressure coefficients for low-rise dual-slope building roofs in a uniform turbulent flow field
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Fu Y.; Yuan Y.; Duan H.; Wang J.; Yang I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of roof area-averaged external pressure coefficients ( $${\overline{C}}_{p,A}$$ ) is crucial for low-rise building design. To isolate geometric and turbulence effects from atmospheric wind shear, wind tunnel experiments were conducted under uniform turbulent flow conditions covering roof pitch angles (0°–30°), wind directions, and turbulence intensities. To overcome the smoothing limitations of conventional regression methods, an ensemble learning framework (Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM) was developed and evaluated using a rigorous Leave-One-Slope-Out (LOSO) cross-validation strategy. Results show that around the roof pitch angle of α = 18.4°, a pronounced variation in aerodynamic pressure response occurs under oblique wind conditions. XGBoost maintains robust predictive performance, outperforming conventional response surface modeling under nonlinear transition conditions. Furthermore, extrapolation failure at α = 30° delineates the practical limits of data-driven models in predicting unseen aerodynamic regimes. Finally, SHAP analysis demonstrates that the model-derived feature attribution patterns are generally consistent with previously reported aerodynamic observations, providing a physically interpretable framework for wind load prediction under complex flow transitions.

Article.Title: Limited impact of ivermectin on immune response and transcriptional profiles in mild COVID-19
Article.Authors: Ribes M.; Canyelles M.; Torres C.; Rubio R.; Vidal M.; Izquierdo L.; Blanco-Di Matteo A.; Pineda I.; Fernandez-Montero A.; Jordan-Iborra C.; Carmona-Torre F.; Yuste J.; Del Pozo J.; Reina G.; Sadaba B.; Fernández-Alonso M.; Santamaria P.; Carolis C.; Aguilar R.; Macià D.; Chaccour C.; Dobaño C.; Moncunill G.
Article.Abstract: Ivermectin (IVM) was tested as a treatment for COVID-19 due to its in vitro antiviral activity and possible immunomodulatory properties. Here, we studied the immunomodulatory effects in a clinical trial involving 24 mild COVID-19 patients who received IVM within 72 h of symptoms onset by comprehensively analyzing immune responses over 28 days. The IVM group had statistically significant increased levels of IgG against the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid compared to the control group at days 4 and 7 post-treatment. IVM did not affect the kinetics of leukocyte subsets or SARS-CoV-2-specific T cells, despite a decrease in naïve CD4 + T cells, which was non-significant after adjusting for multiple comparisons. Although differential gene expression was not observed between IVM-treated and placebo groups, blood transcriptional module analysis revealed statistically significant decreases in innate and antiviral signatures and increases in adaptive signatures over time, with 10 modules upregulated (related to innate responses) and 15 modules downregulated (related to T cells and cell cycle) in the IVM-treated group compared to placebo. In conclusion, despite some weak differences in IVM treated participants, our detailed analyses do not support significant immunomodulatory effects that could benefit disease progression.

Article.Title: Multi-parametric quantitative ultrasound imaging evaluation of rat sciatic nerve regeneration
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Pan K.; Cheng X.; Orozco E.; Han A.; Andre M.; Chang E.; Shah S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral nerve injury is a prevalent condition that significantly impairs patients' sensorimotor function. Noninvasive monitoring of peripheral nerve regeneration could serve as a valuable clinical tool for improving the timing and effectiveness of surgical interventions. We present a multiparametric high-frequency quantitative ultrasound evaluation to noninvasively track temporal and spatial peripheral nerve regeneration following early (n = 16) and delayed (n = 15) graft-based repair of rat sciatic nerve gaps, compared with a sham control group (n = 8). Multiple ultrasound parameters—including backscatter coefficient (BSC) spectra-based measurements (integrated BSC and midband fitted slope), homodyned K envelope statistics (μ and $$\kappa $$ ), gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features, and B-mode morphological measurements were acquired using a Vevo MD UHF 48 transducer at proximal, intra-graft, and distal nerve locations at 1, 2, and 3 months post-repair. Four sciatic nerve samples were extracted after each time point from each experimental group. A histological grading scheme was applied to classify nerve sections into mild, moderate, and severe pathological grades. Principal component analysis (PCA) combined with support vector machine (SVM) classification was employed to establish decision boundaries among pathological groups. Four parameters (μ, cross-sectional area, normalized integrated BSC, midband fitted slope) significantly differentiated groups with varying pathological severity. PCA-SVM analysis achieved excellent classification performance with an area under the ROC curve of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.85 for distinguishing minimal versus severe pathological injured nerves. These findings demonstrate that multiparametric quantitative ultrasound (qUS) effectively characterizes nerve pathologies by integrating complementary information about microstructural changes across different structural scales, potentially offering a comprehensive, noninvasive assessment of the regenerative microenvironment.

Article.Title: Paternal early-life stress and diet influence sperm DNA methylation, female offspring behavior and amygdala transcription
Article.Authors: Yadid T.; Kisliouk T.; Ramaty M.; Weller A.; Meiri N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Obesity is a global epidemic influenced by stress-related experiences during development, which can program behavioral traits, with the amygdala playing a central role in stress regulation. These programmed effects may be inherited through epigenetic mechanisms. Here, we examined the impact of paternal early-life stress (ELS), alone or combined with a high-fat diet (HFD), on offspring behavior and gene regulation. Male Wistar rats underwent maternal separation to induce ELS, followed by elevated plus maze (EPM) testing and exposure to either HFD or standard chow. These males were bred with naïve females, and F 1 offspring were raised under standard conditions. Amygdala tissue and sperm were collected; RNA from paternal and offspring amygdalae was deep-sequenced, and sperm DNA was analyzed using Reduced Representation Bisulfite Deep Sequencing (RRBS). Paternal exposure to ELS and HFD independently and jointly altered physiology and behavior in F 1 female offspring. Offspring of ELS fathers showed increased exploratory behavior and mobility in the EPM; paternal HFD increased time spent in open arms. In the paternal amygdala, ELS and HFD induced distinct gene expression changes. Sperm methylation analysis revealed many differentially methylated genes, some overlapping with transcriptional changes in the F 1 female amygdala, consistent with a potential role for epigenetic inheritance. Overlapping expression patterns in F 0 and F 1 included genes involved in dopamine signaling and epigenetic regulation. Notably, the imprinted gene GRB10 showed increased promoter methylation in sperm and reduced expression in both paternal and offspring amygdala, validated by immunostaining. These findings suggest that paternal ELS and HFD shape offspring phenotype through heritable epigenetic modifications.

Article.Title: A dual-stage self-attention hybrid convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit architecture for real-time power quality disturbance diagnosis
Article.Authors: Samanta I.; Sahoo B.; Rout P.; Mohanty S.; Jha S.; Swain K.; Cherukuri M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increased adoption of the smart grid (SG) infrastructure to overcome the limitations of traditional grid have faced growing challenges for real-time monitoring and classification of features due to the complexity and dynamic nature of power quality disturbances (PQDs). In particular, when PQDs overlap each other, traditional approaches relying on signal processing techniques tend to lose the dynamic, non-periodic characteristics which define certain PQDs. In this proposed work, a novel dual-stage hybrid architecture based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and gated recurrent units (GRUs) augmented by self-attention at both stages for real-time high performance PQD classification is presented. This novel hybrid architecture is allows for spatial and temporal feature extraction from electrical power signals, overcoming the weaknesses encountered in traditional approaches. In contrast to previous models that consider either local or sequential patterns independently, the proposed architecture combines both techniques enabling a more robust and computationally-efficient architecture demonstrates software-level real-time inference (21 ms) and provides a computationally efficient architecture suitable for future embedded deployment. The experimental outcomes on the benchmark databases compared to the state-of-the-art convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture offers improved execution time of 21 ms and a classification accuracy of 98.6%. It also outperforms both traditional CNN architecture with improved latency and high accuracy proposing it as a viable alternative for smart grid use cases like phasor measurement units (PMUs), microcontroller-based devices, etc.

Article.Title: A method for predicting tool remaining useful life based on a physics-informed neural network
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Shen L.; Ye Z.; Chen J.; Luo K.; Chen W.; Li S.; He R.; Han Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)-based method for tool remaining useful life (RUL) prediction by incorporating physical wear evolution laws into a data-driven prediction framework. The method improves prediction accuracy and enhances cross-scenario adaptability through consistency with tool wear mechanisms. First, a quantitative mapping model between tool RUL and flank wear is established based on tool wear theory, clarifying the mathematical relationship between the tool degradation state and its RUL. A PINN is then constructed by embedding the wear rate derived from the Archard wear equation as a physical constraint in the loss function. A hybrid loss function integrating data-driven and physics-informed terms is designed, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based time-series prediction model is developed. The method is validated using the PHM2010 dataset, including comparative tests on labeled sub-datasets D 1 , D 4 , and D 6 against multiple baseline methods, as well as generalization tests on unlabeled sub-datasets D 2 , D 3 , and D 5 . The results show that the proposed method achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 4.25 μm and a Root Mean Square Error of 4.83 μm on the test dataset, reducing MAE by 57.33% compared with Support Vector Machine and by 37.13% compared with Convolutional Neural Network. The end-of-life prediction deviation rate under the same working conditions is 2.46%, and the model shows reliable generalization ability on unlabeled data. It should be noted that, in the current implementation, the wear coefficient k in the Archard constraint is fixed to a handbook value and treated as a constant during training; online adaptive estimation of k is left to future work. These results provide a physically interpretable technical approach for intelligent tool health management and maintenance decision-making.

Article.Title: Multifunctional marine polymers composite supplemented with Artemisia absinthium emulsion for improving chronic wound healing: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Gaspar-Pintiliescu A.; Seciu-Grama A.; Plangu A.; Manoiu V.; Râpă M.; Serafim A.; Tomescu J.; Craciunescu O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to develop a 3D multifunctional porous composite based on marine polymers, fish collagen (COL) extracted from Dicentrarchus labrax skin and sulfated polysaccharides (SP) extracted from Cladophora vagabunda seaweed, supplemented with wormwood ( Artemisia absinthium ) emulsion (WE) for improving the healing of chronic wounds. Characterization of the submicron WE based on wormwood hydrolate showed spherical droplets by TEM, Z-average diameter of 21.31 nm and negative zeta potential determined by DLS and antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus. The 3D COL-SP-WE composite revealed porous morphology by SEM, and a gradual stress increase characteristic for a soft network capable of sustaining medium loads before deformation. The composite had good cytocompatibility in human HaCaT keratinocytes culture. In addition, supplementation of marine composite COL-SP with WE demonstrated higher decrease of the intracellular ROS production in oxidative stressed HaCaT cells, reduced level of pro-inflammatory cytokines in inflamed human THP-1-derived macrophage cells, and downregulation of matrix metalloproteinases mRNAs expression and secretion level in a HaCaT/THP-1 co-culture. However, WE supplementation did not significantly improve HaCaT migration rate in a scratch assay. All these results highlighted multifunctionality of marine composite COL-SP supplemented with WE and recommend further in vivo testing in relevant wound healing models.

Article.Title: Optimal hybrid PV-PTC integration with existing hydropower for reliable and cost-effective energy supply
Article.Authors: Ahmadullah A.; Faizi M.; Bourezgui A.; Ali E.; Elazim S.; Irshad A.; Muslih N.; Ghazouani N.; Senjyu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the integration of existing hydropower with photovoltaic (PV), parabolic trough collector (PTC), and hybrid PV-PTC systems to achieve zero loss of power supply probability (LPSP), minimum levelized cost of energy (LCOE), and near-complete hydropower utilization (remaining ≤ 0.05%). An 8760-hour simulation and coarse-to-fine parametric optimization framework are employed to evaluate system reliability, renewable-energy utilization, curtailment, and economic performance. The PV-based system requires 177.48 MW, utilizes 289.90 GWh of PV energy, exhibits 7.88% curtailment, and achieves an LCOE of 0.090576 $/kWh. The PTC-based system requires 143.36 MW, utilizes 289.96 GWh, reduces curtailment to 4.05%, and achieves an LCOE of 0.087199 $/kWh. The optimal hybrid configuration comprises 52,000 PV units (12.43 MW) and 724 PTC units (131.88 MW), achieving zero unmet load and utilizing 696.160178 GWh of hydropower with only 0.00026% remaining. It supplies 22.05 GWh from PV with zero curtailment and 267.85 GWh from PTC with 3.66% PTC curtailment, while achieving the lowest baseline LCOE of 0.087156 $/kWh. Sensitivity analysis shows that the economic advantage over the PTC-only system is marginal and dependent mainly on PV and PTC investment costs. Overall, the hybrid configuration provides the most balanced technical performance through high reliability, reduced renewable curtailment, and effective utilization of the existing hydropower resource.

Article.Title: Effects of deposition parameters and cobalt hexacyanocobaltate surface modification on magnetron-sputtered ZnIn₂S₄ thin film photoanodes
Article.Authors: Roda D.; Trzciński K.; Sawczak M.; Ilnicka A.; Szkoda M.; Nowak A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For the first time, ZnIn₂S₄ (ZIS) thin films were successfully prepared by magnetron sputtering and systematically investigated as photoanodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. The PEC performance of the layers strongly depended on the deposition parameters. The highest photocurrent density of 2.77 mA cm⁻² at 1.62 V vs. RHE was achieved for films deposited at 200 °C for 90 min, whereas films deposited at 300 °C for 90 min exhibited improved stability. The optimized ZIS photoanode was subsequently modified with a cobalt hexacyanocobaltate (Cohcc) surface layer formed via electrooxidation of a Co layer in an electrolyte containing Co(CN)₆³⁻. This surface modification improved photoanode performance, particularly in terms of stability, likely due to enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics at the electrode surface. Cohcc-modified photoanode generated almost 3 times higher photocurrent density after 100 s operation compared to unmodified photoanode. Electrochemical measurements performed under dark conditions further confirmed the role of Cohcc as cocatalyst toward OER. Overall, the results demonstrate that magnetron sputtering enables effective control over the properties of ZIS photoanodes through optimization of deposition parameters, while surface modification with cobalt hexacyanocobaltate represents a viable strategy for tuning interfacial kinetics and improving the functional performance of ZIS-based photoanodes.

Article.Title: Modelling the efficacy of CAR-CIK cell immunotherapy targeting MET-expressing mesothelioma cells
Article.Authors: Padovano F.; Lombardi A.; Novello S.; Lorenzi T.; Vigna E.; Leschiera E.; Villa C.
Article.Abstract: Malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM) is an aggressive tumour associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options, motivating the investigation of novel therapeutic approaches. Among these, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)–based adoptive cell therapy has attracted considerable interest given its potential to achieve durable clinical responses. In this paper, we combine experimental and mathematical approaches to investigate the efficacy of a CAR-based immunotherapy using cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells engineered with a MET-specific receptor targeting MET-expressing tumour cells. In vitro data from diverse MPM cell lines and CIK preparations are used to develop and calibrate a mathematical model describing the interaction dynamics between tumour cells, structured by their MET expression level, and CIK cells. The model successfully reproduces experimental observations and is used to predict treatment efficacy under previously untested conditions, which are validated with new data from MPM primary cell lines, supporting the robustness of the mathematical framework. Our results elucidate the interplay between three key factors positively impacting treatment efficacy: the initial immune-to-tumour cell ratio, the percentage of CAR-MET-expressing CIK cells generated upon engineering, and the MET expression level of tumour cells. Together, these findings provide a quantitative basis for assessing CAR-CIK therapy effectiveness, which supports clinical decision making.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
Article.Authors: Muhsen M.; Elhannani M.; Almanasra A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. Spatiotemporal analysis is used to quantify land use changes using the GIS tool and fieldwork methods to study vegetation cover. Findings have revealed significant changes in the land use over the study period. The total area of rangeland and grassland has decreased 12.2%, while the total area of urban fabric has increased 7% due to Israeli activities and 5.2% due to the expansion of Palestinian built-up areas, at the expense of rangeland and grassland. Additionally, the environmental impact on vegetation cover has been evidenced by an increase in the number and density of unpalatable and invasive plants, in contrast to the degradation in the number, density, and diversity of palatable plants. Consequently, the conversion of land use reduces the area of land available for livestock grazing. The natural landscape has become highly converted to an urban landscape pattern as a result of the rapid increase in urban areas. In response to these results, more efforts must be imposed to enforce strict land use control and management to slow down environmental degradation.

Article.Title: Hybrid GA-DQN for opportunistic cluster head selection and routing in resource constraint Internet of Things networks
Article.Authors: Thalaimalaichamy M.; Baskaradas J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Energy efficiency and reliable data transmission are two important challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) networks because of the limited energy resources of sensor nodes and their dynamic nature. Accordingly, this research develops a Genetic Algorithm Deep Q-Network (GA-DQN) based hybrid framework for intelligent cluster head selection and adaptive IoT Network routing to counter these threats. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) selects the best cluster heads based on residual energy, coverage ratio, inter-cluster distance, and node density. In turn, this ensures balanced cluster formation and efficient energy utilisation. Next, the Deep Q-Network (DQN) learns the forwarding decision from a network state, including the node’s energy level, node location, information of a neighbour node, link quality, and distance to the sink. The reward mechanism has been formulated to reduce energy consumption, enhance communication reliability, and optimise routing efficiency.
