One representative record was retained per configuration, and all reported quantities derive from measured load. Capacity was frequently governed by the steel anchor rod rather than by the resin bond: five of the eight configurations reached or exceeded the rod yield load, so their reported bond stresses are lower bounds. Where bond capacity could be measured at matched geometry, the epoxy system was stronger, yielding 6.47 MPa against at least 9.45 MPa at 160 mm embedment and 6.24 MPa against at least 7.15 MPa at 245 mm embedment; the epoxy bond was not brought to failure in any configuration. The vinyl ester system developed at least 11.14 MPa in weathered rock, compared with a measured 6.24 MPa in concrete at comparable embedment, and mobilised full steel capacity at 250 mm embedment, whereas the epoxy system required 350 mm. Interpreting pull-out results without reference to steel utilisation risks, attributing to the resin a capacity determined by the steel.

Article.Title: Balancing renewables and carbon capture in emerging economies: a decarbonization pathway for ASEAN
Article.Authors: Han S.; Addanki T.; Chidire A.; Devihosur S.; Massier T.; Hamacher T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emerging economies such as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) face rapid electricity demand growth alongside increasingly ambitious decarbonization targets. Yet, their power systems remain strongly dependent on coal and natural gas fleets. Here we show that carbon capture can play a critical system-level role in enabling high solar photovoltaic penetration in the ASEAN region by providing dispatchable low-carbon generation that reduces renewable curtailment and storage requirements. Using an established linear optimization framework with new enhancements that allow for explicitly modeling carbon capture retrofits alongside new carbon capture installations and cross-border transmission expansion, we find that carbon capture deployment cuts solar photovoltaic curtailment by more than half by 2050, while costs can be lowered by retrofitting existing power plants. Our results highlight carbon capture as a complementary flexibility resource rather than a competing mitigation option to renewables, with broader implications for decarbonizing power systems in emerging economies with large existing fossil fleets.

Article.Title: Association of serum sodium concentration and duration with 28-day mortality in critically ill patients
Article.Authors: Ding X.; Zhang X.; Zhang J.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients, but the prognostic relevance of its duration remains uncertain. This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV data from 2008 to 2022. Of 94,458 ICU records screened, 9,799 adults with a first ICU stay of at least 7 days were included. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality; no secondary outcome was prespecified. Associations were evaluated using concentration–duration heatmaps, restricted cubic splines, and Fine–Gray models treating discharge alive as a competing event. MIMIC-IV was approved by the review boards of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, with consent waived for deidentified data. Within 28 days, 2,002 patients (20.4%) died. In fully adjusted analyses, each 1-percentage-point increase in monitored time at < 125 mmol/L was associated with a higher subdistribution hazard of death (sHR 1.016, 95% CI 1.006–1.026), whereas time at 135–140 mmol/L was associated with a lower hazard (sHR 0.996, 95% CI 0.994–0.997). Positive associations were also observed at 150–155 mmol/L (sHR 1.013, 95% CI 1.009–1.018) and ≥ 155 mmol/L (sHR 1.021, 95% CI 1.017–1.026). Time-weighted analyses showed a U-shaped association, with the lowest estimated mortality probability near 140.6 mmol/L. These findings may inform risk assessment but do not establish causality or treatment targets.

Article.Title: Failure mechanisms and paths of freeze–thaw-treated single-flaw sandstone under triaxial compression in ultra-high-altitude cold-region open-pit mine slopes
Article.Authors: Xiong H.; Zhang Z.; Liu Z.; Liu Y.; Li M.; Zhao Z.; Wang C.; Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ultra-high-altitude cold-region open-pit mine slopes are affected by seasonal freeze-thaw (F-T) weathering, structural discontinuities, and excavation-induced stress changes. Sandstone sampled from a mining bench at 5074 m a.s.l. in the Dahongliutan area of Hotan County, Xinjiang, China, was used to examine failure-path evolution under prior F-T history. To distinguish F-T pretreatment from subsequent mechanical loading, single-flaw specimens were first subjected to 0, 20, 40, or 60 air-freezing/water-thawing cycles and were subsequently tested under conventional triaxial compression with acoustic emission (AE) monitoring at confining pressures of 5, 10, and 15 MPa; flaw inclinations were 45° and 80°. The study addresses two questions: whether a pre-existing flaw remains the final macroscopic failure band after closure, and how flaw inclination biases path selection through normal-shear stress partitioning on the closed flaw plane. The final macroscopic failure band did not necessarily coincide with the pre-existing flaw. The 45° conditions more commonly exhibited flaw-tip interaction, path deflection, and oblique coalescence, whereas the 80° conditions were dominated by near-axial matrix paths and local branching. Under the idealized mean-stress transformation, τ/q = 0.50 for the 45° flaw and approximately 0.17 for the 80° flaw; the corresponding peak-load η = τ/σₙ values for the FT20 conditions were approximately 0.83–0.87 and 0.15–0.17, respectively. AE results showed that increased hit activity could precede the concentration of signals with higher AE waveform energy near the peak, while similar near-peak AE concentration could accompany different final paths. The combined evidence supports a load-transfer/path-competition interpretation in which the flaw is interpreted as evolving from an initial discontinuity into a closed internal contact interface; flaw inclination biases the competing paths, whereas AE primarily constrains the timing of localization. The stress transformation is used as a first-order mean-field interpretation and does not resolve local three-dimensional flaw-tip or partial-contact stresses.

Article.Title: Robust UAV target detection under synthetic severe weather degradations with adaptive feature propagation
Article.Authors: Fan J.; Zheng Z.; Zhao J.; Du P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adverse weather attenuates fine-grained target cues, disrupts cross-scale feature propagation, and weakens long-range contextual dependencies in UAV imagery, making the detection of small and partially occluded objects particularly challenging. Existing state-of-the-art detectors for adverse weather are typically tailored to specific weather types, scene domains, or detector families. Meanwhile, restoration-assisted and feature-decoupling frameworks often introduce additional computational overhead and may not directly preserve detection-relevant semantics. Consequently, the development of a lightweight end-to-end UAV detector that jointly captures robust local, multi-scale, and contextual representations under adverse weather remains insufficiently explored. To address this gap, we propose SW-DEIM, a severe-weather-oriented extension of DEIM, and construct two synthetic adverse-weather benchmarks, Drone-SW and SW-UAVDT, using TPSeNCE-generated rain, fog, and snow. The proposed SW-DEIM is built around a Severe Weather Vision Mamba (SWVIM) module, which integrates lightweight local convolution, multi-scale spatial context modeling, and learnable channel-wise residual modulation to adaptively regulate local and long-range information under degraded visibility. An Adaptive Feature Propagation Pyramid Network (AFPPN) and a Diverse Branch Block (DBB) are further introduced to mitigate cross-scale information loss and enhance the robustness of local features, respectively. On Drone-SW, SW-DEIM achieves an AP50 of 68.1% and an AP50:95 of 50.0% at 188.2 FPS, outperforming the DEIM baseline by 7.9 and 6.5 percentage points, respectively. On the naturally captured foggy UAV subset of HazyDet, SW-DEIM achieves an AP50 of 55.8% and an AP50:95 of 38.2%, exceeding the DEIM baseline by 7.1 and 6.8 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off under TPSeNCE-generated rain, fog, and snow degradations and indicate that the learned degradation-oriented representations can transfer to an independent real-world foggy UAV domain. However, because equivalent independent evaluations on naturally captured rainy and snowy UAV imagery are not included, the present results should not be interpreted as establishing general real-world robustness across all severe-weather types. Relevant data can be accessed at https://github.com/Thehao1123/SW-DEIM .

Article.Title: Multiparametric senescence profiling by spectral flow cytometry uncovers endothelial heterogeneity following irradiation
Article.Authors: Beck T.; Benadjaoud M.; Buard V.; Tarlet G.; Guipaud O.; François A.; Milliat F.; Paget V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cellular senescence can be premature in response to high levels of ROS, oncogene activation or radiation. Although radiation is now well known to induce this state of senescence, there appears to be considerable heterogeneity in the response among surviving cells. This is particularly true for endothelial cells, whose dysfunction is the basis for many radiation related complications. The senescent cells can be identified by various methods more or less time consuming (in situ labelling, confocal imaging, flow cytometry, etc.) Here we have designed and developed a fourteen-colour panel (plus cell morphology parameters (size/granularity)) by using full-spectrum flow cytometry. To validate this approach, the cellular response of human normal endothelial cells was investigated after exposure of confluent monolayers to high-energy x-rays (10 or 18 MV) at the same dose rate (2.5 Gy min − 1 ) and for a dose range from 0 to 20 Gy. Data representation based on Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) was used to uncover heterogeneous cellular responses. Taken together, these experiments demonstrated a dose-dependent response for both energy levels, as well as a deleterious effect associated with higher energy exposure, which was strongly linked to senescence-related markers. Finally, this approach enables the simultaneous consideration of the full spectrum of heterogeneous responses observed across all tested markers, regardless of the irradiation dose.

Article.Title: Seed bio-priming with Streptomyces sp. UTMC 3136 and Streptomyces sp. UTMC 2482 enhances physiological traits of Triticum aestivum L. under drought stress
Article.Authors: Hasani T.; Rezayian M.; Niknam V.; Hamedi J.
Article.Abstract: The use of bacteria to enhance drought tolerance in plants holds considerable promise for agricultural production. However, the effects of Streptomyces on plant drought tolerance remain poorly understood. In the present study, we investigated how wheat cultivars bio-priming with two desert-derived Streptomyces strains influences drought tolerance by examining both their physiological effects and the underlying mechanisms. Following seed bio-priming with two desert-derived Streptomyces strains (designated strains B3136 and B2482), we evaluated plant growth, lipid peroxidation, antioxidant capacity, and the accumulation of selected metabolites in two wheat cultivars (Sirvan and Moghan3) subjected to drought stress. Drought stress significantly enhanced shoot growth in Moghan3. In contrast, Sirvan exhibited a greater reduction in biomass under drought conditions than Moghan3. Bio-priming with strain B2482 significantly improved growth in Sirvan under 15% PEG-induced drought stress. A notable finding was the marked difference in proline accumulation between shoots and roots in both cultivars. Strain B3136 significantly increased proline accumulation and improved osmotic adjustment in both the shoots and roots of Sirvan under severe drought stress. Drought stress also increased H₂O₂ accumulation in the shoots of both cultivars, although this increase was more pronounced in Moghan3. Malondialdehyde (MDA) content was significantly higher in the shoots than in the roots of both cultivars. However, under moderate drought stress, the increase in root MDA content was substantially greater in Sirvan than in Moghan3. Bio-priming with both Streptomyces strains significantly reduced MDA accumulation in the roots of Sirvan under both moderate and severe drought stress. Interestingly, drought stress resulted in a reduction of MDA content in the roots of Moghan3, suggesting a more effective mechanism for limiting lipid peroxidation in this cultivar. Correlation analysis among the measured parameters indicated that flavonoids may contribute to reducing lipid peroxidation and mitigating oxidative damage in the roots of Moghan3. Based on the physiological and biochemical responses observed in this study, Moghan3 was characterized as drought-tolerant, whereas Sirvan was classified as drought-sensitive. Overall, seed bio-priming with both Streptomyces strains significantly enhanced the activity of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD) in both the shoots and roots of the two wheat cultivars under drought stress.

Article.Title: Fresh-semen proAKAP4 concentration predicts sperm cryotolerance independently of conventional semen quality across three goat breeds
Article.Authors: Eser A.; Bağcı K.; Alakuş A.; Cihangiroğlu A.; Yağcıoğlu S.; Arıcı R.; Özöner Ö.; Özöner M.; Arkalı G.; Demir K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cryopreservation compromises sperm quality, yet conventional semen analysis poorly predicts which ejaculates will withstand freezing. proAKAP4, a sperm-specific structural protein, is a candidate freezability biomarker, but is usually measured after thawing. We tested whether proAKAP4 quantified in fresh semen predicts post-thaw sperm quality in bucks across breeds. Five ejaculates from each of 23 bucks (Boer, n = 10; Anglo-Nubian, n = 8; Murcia-Granada, n = 5) were cryopreserved and assessed for computer-assisted motility and flow-cytometric plasma membrane integrity, acrosome integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential, viability and DNA fragmentation; fresh-semen proAKAP4 was measured by ELISA. Fresh-semen proAKAP4 was repeatable (average-measure ICC = 0.84) and correlated strongly with post-thaw membrane integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential, viability, motility and velocity, and inversely with DNA fragmentation. Notably, it was unrelated to any fresh-semen parameter, indicating that it captures cryotolerance-specific rather than baseline quality. Using a composite cryotolerance score, proAKAP4 discriminated high- from low-cryotolerance bucks with high accuracy (AUC = 0.985; exploratory cut-off 36.81 ng/10 6 sperm). Although both proAKAP4 and cryotolerance differed among breeds, partial correlation ( r = 0.86) and a linear mixed model ( p < 0.001) indicated that, under the cryopreservation conditions applied, proAKAP4 predicted cryotolerance consistently across the three breeds examined. These findings identify fresh-semen proAKAP4 as a promising, non-invasive candidate biomarker for selecting bucks with superior freezability, warranting validation in larger, independent cohorts and under different cryopreservation protocols.

Article.Title: Integrating spatial econometrics and remote sensing for pixel-level wind energy corridor identification: evidence from West Bengal, India
Article.Authors: Pal S.
Article.Abstract: This study integrates remote sensing and spatial econometric techniques to identify pixel-level wind energy corridors in West Bengal, India. Weibull scale (A) and shape (K) parameter rasters at 100 m resolution were combined with Dynamic World land-cover data to evaluate how landscape characteristics influence wind resource potential. District-level zonal statistics were analysed using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Spatial Autoregressive (SAR), Spatial Error Model (SEM), and Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). Global Moran’s I (0.723, p < 0.01) revealed significant positive spatial autocorrelation, confirming the importance of explicitly accounting for spatial dependence. Model comparison showed that the Spatial Error Model (SEM) provided the most parsimonious specification based on the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria, whereas the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) achieved the highest overall model fit by capturing additional spatial spillover effects. Building on these results, a pixel-level wind suitability index was developed to delineate contiguous wind energy corridors across the state. The analysis identifies several districts in the southern and coastal regions of West Bengal as possessing relatively high wind energy development potential, demonstrating the value of integrating remote sensing with spatial econometric modelling for renewable energy planning. The proposed framework provides a statistically rigorous planning-support tool; however, engineering feasibility, environmental assessments, transmission infrastructure analysis, and field validation remain essential before implementation.

Article.Title: Multi-objective sustainable DER allocation in active distribution networks based on Slime Mould Algorithm
Article.Authors: Shrivastav A.; Indra S.; Pal S.; Kumar P.; Dutta S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid increase in deployment of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) is transforming traditional passive distribution networks into active and intelligent power systems capable of meeting the objectives of the sustainable energy transition. However, identifying appropriate locations and capacities for DER installation is a difficult multi-objective optimization problem since technical, operational and environmental aspects are to be satisfied simultaneously. This paper is focused on presenting a sustainability-oriented optimization framework for optimal DER placement and sizing in the IEEE 33-bus radial distribution system based on Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA). The developed framework takes into account several performance objectives including; minimizing the total active power loss, reducing the reactive power loss, improving the voltage stability, reducing the carbon emissions and increasing the penetration of renewable energy. A detailed mathematical model for multi-objective problem is developed under constraints on power balance, voltage regulation, feeder current and DER capacity. Back ward forward sweep load-flow calculation is performed to determine network performance during the optimization process. Besides, a sensitivity analysis is presented to demonstrate the effect of DER penetration, variations in the load and selection of weights of objective-function on network performance. The robustness and efficiency of the proposed approach is further verified using Friedman ranking and Wilcoxon signed rank statistical tests. The proposed SMA-based allocation reduces active power loss from 202.67 kW to 58.73 kW (71.0%) and reactive power loss from 135.14 kVAr to 42.85 kVAr (68.3%). The minimum bus voltage improves from 0.9131 p.u. to 0.988 p.u., while the voltage stability index increases from 0.6678 to 0.9548. Annual carbon emissions decrease from 1,455,819 kg CO₂/year to 842,600 kg CO₂/year (42.1%), accompanied by an increase in renewable energy penetration to 92.35%. The proposed SMA also demonstrates superior convergence, computational efficiency, and robustness compared with PSO, DE, GA, and WOA. These results establish SMA as an effective optimization tool for sustainable DER planning and the development of resilient active distribution networks.

Article.Title: Gender, parenthood, pay, working time, and organizational authority among social workers in China
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Wang Y.; Pang J.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Research on parenthood-related labor-market inequality increasingly distinguishes hourly pay from employment, working time, earnings, occupational allocation, and authority. We examine these dimensions within Chinese social work, a female-dominated occupation in which numerical representation may coexist with unequal organizational authority. Using the 2019 China Social Work Longitudinal Study ( N = 6,776), we estimate OLS models for log hourly wage, weekly hours, and log monthly salary, and logit models for management and supervisory roles. All labor-outcome models use a common sample ( N = 6,102) and six gender-marriage-parenthood groups, with unmarried childless men as the reference group. In adjusted models, mothers worked 1.31 fewer hours per week ( p < .001) and had lower monthly salary ( b = -0.066, p < .001) than reference men; their hourly-wage difference was smaller and nonsignificant ( b = -0.024, p = .240). Direct comparisons showed no hourly-wage difference between mothers and unmarried childless women, but a difference relative to married childless women; winsorized and single-year-age specifications also indicated modest sensitivity. Mothers had lower odds of management ( OR = 0.62) and supervision ( OR = 0.52) than reference men. Fathers did not differ significantly from married childless men. Among currently employed social workers, parenthood-related inequality is therefore more consistent across working time, monthly earnings, and organizational positions than across hourly wage rates. Cross-sectional employed-worker data do not capture employment or occupational exit and cannot establish causal effects.

Article.Title: Biochar–polymer synergy enhances soil health, root growth, and maize yield under rainfed conditions
Article.Authors: Abrol V.; Khenrab S.; Sharma P.; Brar A.; Kumari V.; Singh A.; Gupta R.; Chand G.; Singh S.; Chandra S.
Article.Abstract: Biochar and polymers have sparked widespread interest due to their ability to increase soil health and crop yield. However, research into the combined impacts of rice husk biochar (RHB) and anionic polymer (P) on soil characteristics, root growth, and crop performance under rainfed circumstances is limited. A two-year pot experiment was carried out to determine the effectiveness of RHB and polymer in improving soil properties, root growth, and maize performance in nutrient-deficient sandy loam. The study used ten treatments: biochar (5 and 10 t ha −1 ), polymer (10 and 20 kg ha −1 ), their combinations, a prescribed amount of fertilizers, and a control (unfertilized with no amendments). Over a two-year trial period, the RHB10 + P10 treatment reduced soil penetration resistance by 37% while increasing soil moisture content by 64% compared to the control. Similarly, RHB10P10 application increased nutritional availability and absorption compared to other treatments. Furthermore, the addition of biochar and polymer (RHB10P10) increased root length 2.0 times, root volume 1.8 times, and maize yield 2.23 times over the control. In comparison to the control , improved soil properties permitted greater root growth and maize grain output. Our results showed that adding biochar (10 t ha −1 ) and polymer (10 kg ha −1 ) considerably enhanced soil characteristics, encouraged root development, and enhanced crop yield . These data imply that combining biochar and polymer is a more viable soil management technique than applying either amendment alone to improve maize output and soil resilience in nutrient-poor rainfed soils.

Article.Title: Psychosocial adaptation experiences among patients with ischemic stroke: a qualitative study
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Zhang W.; Yu Y.; Zhang Y.; Zhang J.; Zou W.; Huang T.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Based on the Roy Adaptation Model, this study aims to explore the factors influencing of psychosocial adaptability in patients with ischemic stroke, so as to provide evidence for formulating intervention programs. A descriptive qualitative study with a phenomenological approach was conducted. Using purposive sampling with maximum variation strategy, 15 patients with ischemic stroke and poor psychosocial adaptation (PAIS-SR scores > 50) were recruited from the Department of Neurology at a tertiary hospital in Qiqihar City between July and November 2025. Data were collected through face-to-face, semi-structured interviews lasting 25–30 min each. The interview guide was developed based on the four adaptive modes of the Roy Adaptation Model. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim within 24 h. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step phenomenological method, with coding independently performed by two researchers and managed using NVivo 15 software. Thematic saturation was achieved after 15 interviews. Four themes and sixteen sub-themes were generalized, including the following: Theme1 Disease and physiological related stimuli (physical symptom distress, disease uncertainty, dependence in daily activities, somatic perception abnormalities); Theme2 Disease perception and emotional coping(inadequate and misaligned disease perception, reduced self-worth and negative emotional spillover, passive coping and passive adaptation); Theme3 Social support and role pressure (limited or absent sources of social support, family role conflicts and pressure, supporting perceived differences, social isolation and fear of discrimination, economic pressure and weak perception of relevant policies); Theme4 Self-identity and behavior management (identity crisis, perceived self-burden, challenges in health behavior change, barriers in rehabilitation knowledge acquisition and application). This study employed the Roy Adaptation Model to explore factors influencing psychosocial adaptation in stroke patients. Through comprehensive assessment across four domains, four themes and sixteen sub-themes were identified. The findings reveal that adaptation experiences are shaped by the interplay of physiological impairments, cognitive biases, emotional distress, inadequate social support, role conflicts, identity crises, and behavioral change difficulties. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive, individualized support strategies that address patients’ multifaceted needs. They also highlight the importance of recognizing dynamic interactions among the four domains, as interventions targeting a single domain may have ripple effects across others. Future longitudinal or mixed-methods studies with larger, multi-center samples are warranted to validate and extend these findings and to evaluate intervention strategies derived from this qualitative evidence.

Article.Title: Opuntia ficus-indica glochids as a sustainable source of antioxidant and antimicrobial specialized metabolites
Article.Authors: Pulvirenti L.; Botta L.; Mistretta M.; Faulisi M.; Restuccia C.; Liguori G.; Siracusa L.; Rizzarelli P.
Article.Abstract: Cactus pear ( Opuntia ficus-indica (L.) Mill.) glochids, a largely neglected agro-industrial waste, were investigated as a novel source of bioactive compounds within a circular economy framework. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) morphological characterization revealed specialized surface structures supporting the defensive role of glochids. Hydroalcoholic extracts obtained from mechanically recovered glochids were characterized by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with diode array detection and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (UHPLC/DAD/ESI-MS), allowing the tentative annotation of a series of phenolic compounds, including hydroxycinnamic acid derivatives and flavonoids, which together constitute the phenolic profile of the cactus pear glochid extract. Two hybrid flavonoids, tentatively identified as quercetin 3- O -hexosyl-hydroxyferuloyl and quercetin 3- O -hexosyl-sinapoyl, were detected for the first time in O. ficus-indica tissues. The antioxidant activity of the glochid extract was evaluated by complementary 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 2,2′-azinobis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS), and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) assays, showing strong DPPH radical scavenging activity (83.85 ± 1.07% at 20 µL of extract; 13.75 ± 0.18 µmol TE/g extract), ABTS radical scavenging activity (39.57 ± 3.44% inhibition; 3.45 ± 0.32 µmol TE/g extract), and ferric reducing capacity (48.66 ± 0.15 µmol Fe²⁺ equivalents/g extract). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations supported these findings, revealing favorable highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy gaps and quantum descriptors indicative of high reactivity toward radical species. In silico molecular docking demonstrated significant binding affinities (up to − 8.58 kcal/mol) of selected metabolites toward key Staphylococcus aureus targets, while in vitro assays confirmed antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, with inhibition zones up to 4.00 ± 1.50 mm, particularly against Staphylococcus haemolyticus and Staphylococcus aureus , whereas no activity was detected against Listeria innocua or the tested Gram-negative strains. Overall, the integration of phytochemical, computational, and biological analyses highlights cactus pear glochids as a promising source of antioxidant and antimicrobial metabolites, warranting further investigation for food preservation and bio-based material applications.

Article.Title: Indigenous harvesters detect climate-sensitive emerging disease in barren-ground caribou (Rangifer tarandus) threatening food security
Article.Authors: Vada R.; Akeeagok R.; Mavrot F.; MacDonald P.; Goldsmith D.; Hamou H.; Thomas A.; Leclerc L.; Milton T.; N/A N/A.; Melin A.; Soghigian J.; Kulpa M.; Verocai G.; Kutz S.
Article.Abstract: We report a filarioid nematode outbreak in barren-ground caribou ( Rangifer tarandus ) from the Canadian Arctic that was identified by Inuit harvesters through a community-based surveillance program. Harvesters reported discolouration of tissues and presence of yellowish fluid across peritoneal and pleural surfaces, within subcutaneous tissues, and along fascial planes between muscles. Histopathology identified eosinophilic inflammation and occasionally nematode parasites. We identified DNA of Setaria yehi and Onchocerca sp. lineage 2 in submitted lesions. These are two filarioid nematode species that have been circulating in caribou since before 2015, but have only recently caused these emerging syndromes. These outbreaks raise concerns regarding the health and conservation of already-declining populations of caribou, an ecological and cultural keystone species in the Arctic, and regarding food safety for Indigenous Peoples. The emergence of clinical disease associated with these parasites may be linked to climate change, which is altering vector ecology and host susceptibility in the Arctic. Continued surveillance, led by and meeting the needs of Indigenous communities, is recommended to support food security, public health and caribou conservation. The solidity and trust underlying the surveillance program enabled rapid detection and management of the outbreak.

Article.Title: Optimized renewable dual-biopolymer hydraulic fracturing fluid with zirconium crosslinker for enhanced thermal stability
Article.Authors: Zahiri M.; Mirabbasi S.; Akbari M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The declining productivity of conventional reservoirs has increasingly shifted attention toward the development of unconventional resources, where efficient and sustainable hydraulic fracturing (HF) fluids are critical to successful reservoir stimulation. In this study, a polymer-based fracturing fluid was formulated and optimized through the synergistic incorporation of two renewable biopolymers, guar gum and xanthan gum, together with a newly synthesized zirconium (Zr)-based crosslinker. A controlled breaker was also incorporated to facilitate the gradual reduction of fluid viscosity following fracturing operations. The proposed formulation was designed to enhance the mechanical stability of the fracturing fluid while simultaneously addressing practical technical and economic requirements. A series of fluid formulations with different concentrations of the biopolymers and crosslinking agent was prepared, and their rheological characteristics were systematically investigated. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to optimize the rheological performance and quantify the interactions among the formulation variables. The principal rheological parameters, including apparent viscosity (AV), plastic viscosity (PV), and yield point (YP), were determined, and the experimental data were subsequently characterized using the Bingham plastic, Herschel–Bulkley, and power-law models. In addition, proppant suspension experiments were performed to evaluate the capacity of the formulated fluid to maintain proppant particles in suspension under elevated-temperature conditions. The results indicated that the optimum formulation comprised 1 wt% guar gum, 1 wt% xanthan gum, and 0.05 wt% each of the Zr-based crosslinker and breaker. At 105 °C, the optimized fluid exhibited an apparent viscosity of 140 cP and a plastic viscosity of 121 cP, demonstrating its ability to maintain a stable rheological structure under high-temperature conditions. The proppant suspension test further showed that approximately 89% of the introduced proppant remained suspended after 30 min, confirming the high structural stability and particle-carrying capacity of the developed fluid. The principal novelty of this work lies in the synthesis and application of a Zr-based crosslinker in combination with two renewable natural biopolymers, along with the incorporation of a controlled breaker to regulate post-treatment viscosity. Furthermore, the formulation strategy was developed in conjunction with techno-economic considerations, providing a more comprehensive basis for fluid optimization. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed formulation as a cost-effective, high-performance, and bio-based hydraulic fracturing fluid for applications in unconventional reservoirs.

Article.Title: Energy and spectral indicators support screening for soil structure interaction sensitivity in steel moment frames
Article.Authors: Mortezaie H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil–structure interaction (SSI) can increase or decrease seismic demand depending on structural, foundation, and ground-motion characteristics. This study evaluates whether SSI-sensitive cases in steel special moment-resisting frames can be prioritized using energy-based flexibility indices and record-specific spectral information. Three 4-, 8-, and 16-story frames were analyzed under five far-field records, three intensity levels, and three soil-stiffness levels, yielding 180 nonlinear analyses and 135 fixed-base/SSI comparisons. Larger translational and rocking flexibility contributions were associated with larger absolute drift changes, while spectral information improved directional interpretation within the development data. A frozen model was then tested without recalibration on 17 additional FEMA P695 records, adding 204 analyses. For 81 spectral-eligible comparisons from 10 independent new events, the combined model yielded an RMSE of 0.0191, a sign balanced accuracy of 0.628, and a three-class balanced accuracy of 0.514, and did not outperform a zero-change baseline in continuous RMSE. Thus, the indices retain value for mechanistic interpretation and within-domain prioritization, but the fitted coefficients and screening performance are not uniformly transferable. The framework is therefore a screening heuristic, not a substitute for direct nonlinear SSI analysis.

Article.Title: Cross-sectional multi-omics analysis reveals stage-associated differences in gut microbiota–fecal metabolite–peripheral immune modules across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum
Article.Authors: Wei Z.; Wu J.; Wang X.; Yi J.; Liu Z.; Zhang H.; Gong J.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly viewed as a disorder involving systemic immune and metabolic changes, but how gut microbial composition, fecal metabolites, and peripheral immune proteins vary across the AD clinical continuum remains unclear. We conducted a cross-sectional multi-omics study of 78 participants, including cognitively healthy controls (CH), individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and patients with AD. Fecal 16 S rRNA gene sequencing, fecal untargeted metabolomics, selected serum immune proteins, and AD-related blood biomarkers were analyzed using group comparisons and exploratory integrative analyses. Cognitive scores were consistent with the predefined CH, MCI, and AD classifications. Blood biomarker and peripheral immune protein analyses showed group-dependent patterns, including higher Aβ1–42 and p-tau-181 in cognitively impaired groups than in CH, the highest NfL and MCP-1 levels in AD, higher sTREM2 and PGRN in cognitively impaired groups, and lower CX3CL1 in MCI and AD. Microbiome beta-diversity analyses did not support robust categorical separation among groups, whereas selected genus-level analyses highlighted lower relative abundance of Faecalibacterium and Agathobacter and higher relative abundance of Faecalitalea in cognitively impaired groups. Fecal metabolomics highlighted alterations involving lipid/fatty acyl-, bile acid-, and amino acid/peptide-related metabolism, including 3-methyladipic acid, linoleoyl ethanolamide, lauroyl- l -carnitine, cholic acid, 7-ketodeoxycholic acid, and α- l -Glu-Gly. Integrative analyses suggested fecal metabolites as possible statistical links between gut microbial features and peripheral immune or cognitive readouts. These findings provide hypothesis-generating evidence for gut microbiota–fecal metabolite–peripheral immune associations across the AD continuum and require validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

Article.Title: Nonlinear joint modeling of oxygenation indices for dynamic mortality prediction in neonates with persistent pulmonary hypertension receiving inhaled nitric oxide
Article.Authors: Li D.; Feng L.; Shi H.; Li B.; Pu W.; Ma L.; Tang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) remains a life-threatening disorder with considerable mortality despite the widespread use of inhaled nitric oxide (iNO). Current risk assessment relies on static indices and cannot capture the rapid physiological changes characteristic of this disease. We aimed to evaluate the association between dynamic oxygenation indices and mortality, and to develop a nonlinear joint modeling framework for individualized prediction in neonates receiving iNO therapy. In this retrospective cohort of 377 PPHN neonates, serial blood gas and ventilator data were used to compute oxygen saturation index (OSI) and oxygen index (OI). Linear and nonlinear joint models linking longitudinal OSI/OI trajectories with time-to-death were constructed via Bayesian estimation. Results Non-survivors showed persistently higher OSI and OI trajectories than survivors (p < 0.001). Among six candidate models, the nonlinear OSI-based joint model achieved the best performance (lowest DIC/WAIC, highest LPML) and excellent discrimination (24-h AUC = 0.93, cross-validation AUC = 0.90, validation AUC = 0.84), substantially outperforming linear (validation AUC: 0.78–0.82), OI-based (validation AUC: 0.75–0.83), time-varying Cox (validation AUC: 0.74–0.79), and nSOFA-based models (validation AUC: 0.68–0.70). Dynamic predictions demonstrated that early OSI trajectories strongly influenced survival probability. Dynamic OSI trajectories are independent predictors of mortality in PPHN neonates. Nonlinear OSI-based joint modeling enables individualized, time-updated mortality prediction within the first 24 h of iNO therapy and may inform early clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: Mineralogical and geochemical constraints on high-sulfidation epithermal alteration in the Zamharir kaolin deposit, northwestern Iran
Article.Authors: Abedini A.; Calagari A.; Sasmaz A.
Article.Abstract: The Zamharir kaolin deposit in northwestern Iran represents hydrothermal alteration of the Oligocene andesitic rocks within a high-sulfidation epithermal system. Mineralogical assemblages display conspicuous spatial zonation, with kaolinite, alunite, pyrite, and rutile concentrated in the central part of the deposit, whereas peripheral zones are characterized by smectite, illite, and goethite. Mass balance calculations indicate extensive depletion of major, trace, and rare earth elements, including Si, Fe, Ti, Ca, Mg, Na, K, P, Rb, Cs, Ni, U, Cr, Co, and heavy rare earth elements (HREE), throughout the hydrothermal system. These geochemical patterns reflect pervasive leaching under the influence of acidic sulfate-rich hydrothermal fluids. Geochemical proxies further suggest dominance of hypogene oxidizing acidic conditions, with only limited contribution from supergene processes. Elemental behavior during kaolinization is controlled by variations in alteration intensity, fluid pH, complexation of ions in solution, adsorption onto secondary minerals, and the development of mineralogical zonation. The integrated evaluation of mineralogical zonation, elemental mobility, mass-balance constraints, and REE behavior provides a comprehensive understanding of the hydrothermal kaolinization processes and highlights the role of acidic hydrothermal fluids in mobilization and redistribution of the elements. These findings may serve as a useful framework for assessing similar volcanic-hosted kaolin systems worldwide.

Article.Title: Online social interaction is associated with theory of mind in adolescence
Article.Authors: Yasiniyan S.; Kurtisi E.; Tong D.; Lecce S.; Talwar V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social media has become a central context for adolescent social interaction, yet little is known about the social-cognitive processes that support adolescents’ online engagement. This study examined whether Theory of Mind (ToM) was associated with multiple dimensions of adolescents’ online behavior. Participants were 127Canadian adolescents aged 11–18 recruited and assessed online. ToM was assessed using the Strange Stories and Silent Films tasks, and verbal reasoning was measured using the WISC-V Similarities subtest. Online behaviors were assessed through self-report measures of preference for online social interaction, online conversation frequency, and online self-disclosure. Multivariate analyses showed that Silent Films ToM, but not Strange Stories ToM, was significantly associated with online behavior after controlling for age and verbal reasoning. Follow-up regressions indicated that higher Silent Films ToM was associated with greater online conversation frequency, greater online self-disclosure, and lower propensity for online social interaction. These findings suggest that stronger ToM was associated with adolescents’ online communication behaviours. This study highlights the importance of examining specific social-cognitive processes in understanding adolescents’ engagement in online contexts.

Article.Title: Response surface optimization and ultrasonic modification of soy protein isolate–gellan gum composite films
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Lu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soy protein isolate (SPI)-based films are promising biodegradable packaging materials but often have limitations in mechanical strength and barrier performance. In this study, gellan gum (GG) was incorporated into SPI films, and response surface methodology (RSM) based on a Box–Behnken design was used to optimize the formulation. SPI concentration, GG content, glycerol content (w/w, based on SPI mass), and pH were selected as independent variables, with tensile strength (TS) as the response. The quadratic model was significant (R² = 0.93) with a nonsignificant lack of fit. The optimized formulation (5.00% SPI, 0.30% GG, 25.00% glycerol, pH 10.00) produced a TS of 25.45 ± 0.54 MPa, consistent with the predicted value. Ultrasonic modification significantly increased elongation at break while maintaining TS and reduced water vapor permeability (WVP) and oxygen permeability (OP) by 59.5% and 63.9%, respectively. It also improved dispersion stability, as indicated by decreased particle size and increased absolute zeta potential. FTIR analysis indicated subtle rearrangement of existing intermolecular interactions without the formation of new major chemical functional groups. These findings demonstrate that integrating RSM-based formulation optimization with ultrasonic modification effectively improves the functional performance of SPI–GG composite films and supports their development as biodegradable packaging materials.

Article.Title: Effects of zinc deficiency and arsenic exposure on bone in growing female mice
Article.Authors: Beaver L.; Wong C.; Hasler S.; Prati M.; Dashner-Titus E.; Ho E.; Branscum A.; Turner R.; Iwaniec U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Arsenic contamination in groundwater often co-exists in regions prone to zinc deficiency. The goal of this research was to evaluate the independent and combined effects of zinc status [adequate, marginally-deficient, severely-deficient (30, 6, and < 0.5 mg Zn/kg diet)] and arsenic exposure (0, 50, or 500 ppb sodium arsenite) on bone in growing female mice (n = 7–8/treatment). Two experiments were conducted; the first focused on 4 weeks of severe zinc deficiency, the second on 6 weeks of marginal zinc deficiency. Bone response was evaluated in femurs using dual energy X-ray absorptiometry and microcomputed tomography. Severe zinc deficiency resulted in lower total femur bone mass, lower midshaft cortical thickness, and lower cancellous bone volume fraction in distal femur. Arsenite exposure did not significantly alter bone response to consuming a zinc-deficient diet. Neither marginal zinc deficiency nor combined marginal zinc deficiency and arsenite exposure affected the endpoints evaluated. In summary, severe but not marginal zinc deficiency, in growing mice, lowered bone mass and altered bone microarchitecture. In contrast, exposure to arsenite had little effect on bone in severely zinc-deficient, marginally zinc-deficient, or zinc-adequate mice.

Article.Title: Inert gas atmospheric pressure plasma post-processing of fused silica micro-lenses produced by means of femtosecond laser-induced chemical etching
Article.Authors: Pecorari A.; Tümmel A.; Tasche D.; Kariman B.; Osellame R.; Candeo A.; Paiè P.; Bragheri F.; Gerhard C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this work, we report on the application of inert gas atmospheric pressure plasma polishing as a post processing approach for fused silica micro-optical components produced by femtosecond laser-induced chemical etching (FLICE). We demonstrate that this method effectively reduces the surface roughness of laser-etched fused silica micro-lenses from an average Ra value of 0.207 ± 0.044 µm to as low as 0.047 ± 0.018 µm, corresponding to a reduction of more than 75%, while preserving the lens geometry. The influence of the discharge gap thickness and plasma power on polishing efficiency is systematically analysed, where an optimum working distance and plasma power of 5 mm and 5.5 W, respectively, were identified for the used setup. At this configuration, the highest plasma polishing efficiency was observed due to the formation of a stable plasma discharge with high electric field strength whereas for higher power and working distance, plasma instability and inhomogeneity occurred, lowering the process efficiency. The improvement in surface roughness achieved via plasma‑post‑processing of laser‑written lenses is verified through microscopic and interferometric characterisation as well as the measurement of light scattered at unpolished and polished surfaces produced via FLICE.

Article.Title: Troll detection using generative adversarial network (GAN) based on social network features
Article.Authors: Ahmadi A.; Khansari M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A troll is an online user who deliberately disrupts discussions, spreads misleading or provocative messages, and incites conflict or disorder in digital interactions. Troll detection based on behavior change is one of the new methods of research in this field. The feedback-oriented nature of GANs, coupled with the relational insights from social network analysis, allows for effective simulation and identification of behavioral changes, resulting in improved detection performance across diverse trolling strategies. In this paper, we utilize Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) as a new semi-supervised method from the deep learning approach to detect troll behavior changes. The suggested approach comprises three elements: a Generator, a Discriminator, and a Classifier. These components collaborate not only to classify troll opinions but also to produce samples closely resembling the training dataset. This Method operates by leveraging two neural networks engaged in a min-max adversarial framework. In this process, the Discriminator is responsible for distinguishing between real and synthetic samples, while the Generator aims to create realistic fake samples to deceive the Discriminator. A key aspect of this method is the integration of the Generator and Classifier through an LSTM layer, which serves as a shared channel between them. The proposed approach is compared with LSTM and logistic regression on two Twitter troll datasets, including a small-scale labeled dataset of 14,940 instances and a large-scale corpus comprising approximately three million Russian troll-related tweets. Accuracy and F1-score are used for performance evaluation. The results indicate that the proposed TrollGAN model achieves higher accuracy and more robust generalization than baseline methods, while maintaining stable discriminative behavior under increased data scale and behavioral complexity. These findings highlight the suitability of adversarial learning for large-scale and dynamic troll detection tasks.

Article.Title: Digital literacy shapes AI chatbot adoption, barriers, and performance outcomes in football coaches: a multi-method analytical study
Article.Authors: Ghorbel A.; Yaakoubi M.; Trabelsi O.; Elkholi S.; Kammoun M.; Masmoudi L.; Gharbil A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The adoption of AI chatbots among football coaches is primarily determined by their digital literacy. An international cross-sectional online survey of 213 professional coaches measured adoption and digital literacy using a psychometrically evaluated 31-item index. Data were analyzed using mediation models, ROC curves, ANOVA, and cluster analysis. Four key findings emerged. First, digital literacy completely mediated the negative effect of age on adoption (indirect effect ab = − 0.31). Second, a critical competency threshold of 4.5/7 was identified, with adoption probability rising from 28% below to 78% above this threshold (χ 2 (1) = 48.7, p < 0.001). Third, the perception of a “cultural barrier” among highly experienced coaches (> 15 years) was fully explained by lower digital literacy (indirect effect ab = 0.38). Finally, cluster analysis revealed a distinct “AI Value Chain” user group (10%), which reported significantly higher satisfaction (M = 8.9, F(2,121) = 15.8, p < 0.001) and time savings exceeding three hours per week. These results underscore that foundational digital competency, more than age or experience, is crucial for successful technology integration. Coach education should therefore prioritise developing core digital literacy and integrate threshold-based learning approaches.

Article.Title: Effect of propofol versus midazolam on short-term outcomes in patients with sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome
Article.Authors: Guo T.; Sun Y.; Zhu X.; Yang Z.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: Propofol and midazolam are commonly used sedatives for mechanically ventilated patients in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU); however, there remains a lack of research on the impact of these two drugs on the prognosis of patients with sepsis-associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome(S-ARDS). A statistical analysis was conducted on 4692 patients with S-ARDS in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database(MIMIC-IV). The baseline characteristics of the patients were grouped according to the use of two sedative drugs, propofol and midazolam alone. Cox proportional hazards models, logistic regression models and PSM analysis were used to compare the effects of propofol and midazolam on the short-term outcomes of patients with S-ARDS, including 30-day mortality, 90-day mortality, and duration of mechanical ventilation. In this study, a total of 4692 patients were included in the statistical analysis, of whom 1081 were on midazolam and 3611 on propofol. Compared with the midazolam group, the propofol group had a lower 30-day mortality rate [HR = 0.592 (95% CI 0.518–0.676, P < 0.001)] and a lower 90-day mortality rate [HR = 0.581 (95% CI 0.513–0.657, P < 0.001)]. The propofol group had a shorter duration of invasive mechanical ventilation compared with the midazolam group [OR = 0.741 (95% CI 0.633–0.869, P < 0.001)], indicating more ventilator-free days in the propofol group. The Kaplan Meier curve showed a lower probability of 90-day survival in the midazolam group (P < 0.001). Further PSM analysis showed that propofol had a very broad and strong protective effect on the short-term prognosis of patients with S-ARDS. Compared with midazolam, propofol was associated with lower 30‑day and 90‑day mortality and a shorter duration of invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with S‑ARDS. These findings collectively suggest that propofol may confer more favorable short‑term outcomes for this patient population.

Article.Title: The effect of thickness, arch type, and storage duration on the dimensional stability and seating accuracy of 3d-printed implant surgical guides
Article.Authors: Jin G.; Kim K.; Lee S.; Ayukawa Y.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of guide thickness, arch span, and storage duration on the dimensional stability and seating accuracy of 3D-printed implant surgical guides. Forty-eight surgical guides were fabricated using stereolithography (SLA) in partial-arch (PA) and full-arch (FA) designs across three thickness levels (2, 3, and 4 mm). The guides were stored for up to 14 days and evaluated at five time points (0, 1, 3, 7, and 14 days). Dimensional changes were quantified using root mean square error (RMSE) and visualized through colormap analysis, and seating accuracy was assessed by model-based mounting analysis. Most dimensional deformation occurred within the first 24 hours, with stabilization thereafter. Among PA guides, the 2-mm-thick group exhibited a pronounced increase in deformation at day 7 (RMSE: 200.14 ± 37.52 µm), whereas 3-mm and 4-mm PA guides remained dimensionally stable throughout the observation period (4-mm at day 14: 45.90 ± 3.73 µm). FA guides showed more consistent RMSE values across thicknesses and time points than PA guides (4-mm at day 14: 65.16 ± 0.47 µm) and maintained consistent seating accuracy throughout the study. Three-way ANOVA revealed significant main effects and interactions among thickness, arch span, and storage duration with respect to both deformation and seating accuracy (p < 0.001). Based on these findings, a minimum guide thickness of 3 mm is recommended, with 4 mm preferred for PA designs, and at least 24 h of post-curing stabilization should be observed before clinical use.

Article.Title: Rheological, physicochemical, and structural properties of fish gelatin/carboxymethyl cellulose/Persian gum ternary edible films
Article.Authors: Hosseini S.; Allahyari M.; Gómez-Guillén M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study explored the modulation of fish gelatin (FG)/carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) edible films using Persian gum (PG), focusing on structure-rheology-function relationships and physicochemical performance. Ternary FG/CMC/PG films with mass ratios of 60/40/0, 54/36/10, 48/32/20, 42/28/30, and 36/24/40 were prepared by solution casting. Rheological analysis of film-forming solutions revealed shear-thinning behavior across all formulations, with 10% PG increasing viscosity, possibly because of favorable polymer associations and entanglements, whereas higher PG concentrations (20–40%) decreased viscosity, possibly reflecting concentration-dependent network rearrangement and increasing heterogeneity. Dynamic oscillatory measurements showed that incorporation of PG shifted the viscoelastic response toward a more elastic, solid-like network, suggesting enhanced interactions between PG and FG/CMC chains. Mechanical testing indicated that increasing PG content decreased tensile strength and elongation-at-break, while water vapor permeability increased from 0.74 to 0.95 g mm/kPa h m 2 , and solubility decreased by up to 41% relative to the control, reflecting changes in polymer interactions and film structure. Optical analyses demonstrated that PG improved film transparency. Structural characterization through Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analyses provided evidence of intermolecular interactions and compositional effects on molecular organization, while SEM and AFM observations revealed increasing morphological heterogeneity at higher PG concentrations, suggesting possible microphase separation. Overall, the FG/CMC/PG ternary films developed in this study exhibited tunable functional properties and demonstrated the potential of Persian gum as a natural modifier for developing biodegradable films with potential suitability for food-packaging applications.

Article.Title: Nano clay mitigation of wind induced soil loss across aggregate sizes through wind tunnel experiments and explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Wehliye A.; Kaplan S.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate, under wind-tunnel conditions, the effects of different nano-clay application rates (0, 0.94, 1.88, and 3.75 g m⁻²) on wind-induced soil loss across different aggregate sizes (0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm) and wind speeds (8, 10, and 12 m s⁻¹). In addition, the study aimed to model wind-induced soil loss processes using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence methods. The wind-tunnel experiments revealed that nano-clay applications significantly reduced soil loss across all aggregate sizes and wind-speed conditions. The highest protective effect was obtained at the 3.75 g m⁻² nano-clay rate; soil loss decreased by 80.8% in the 2 mm aggregates, by 93.2% in the 1 mm aggregates, and by 95.9% in the 0.5 mm aggregates. The protective effect of the nano-clay applications was found to be particularly pronounced at high wind speeds and in fine aggregates. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost showed the strongest development-stage performance under repeated nested group-aware cross-validation (R² = 0.835 ± 0.064, RMSE = 11.896 ± 2.229, MAE = 6.686 ± 0.854) and was selected before independent holdout evaluation. On the group-held-out test set, the selected XGBoost model achieved R² = 0.882, RMSE = 13.298, and MAE = 9.443. The lower performance of the linear baseline suggested that the tree-based models captured predictive structure not adequately represented by a simple linear formulation. SHAP analysis indicated that nano-clay dose made the largest mean absolute contribution to the fitted model predictions, followed by wind speed and aggregate size. Overall, nano-clay substantially reduced wind-induced soil loss within the controlled experimental conditions examined here; broader practical applicability requires validation under field conditions.

Article.Title: Factors associated with surgical outcomes following maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Nadershah M.; Baabdullah R.
Article.Abstract: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) is one of the most effective surgical treatments for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but treatment response varies considerably among patients. We performed a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis to evaluate factors associated with treatment response following MMA. The review protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251274643). PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library were searched for observational studies reporting postoperative outcomes together with factors associated with surgical response. Study quality was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when studies were sufficiently comparable; otherwise, findings were synthesized narratively. Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Definitions of surgical success varied substantially across studies, although most used the Sher criteria or postoperative apnea–hypopnea index thresholds. Across six independent cohorts, the random-effects pooled surgical success rate was 70.7% (95% CI, 62.5%–77.7%), although this estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of methodological heterogeneity. Younger age, lower central apnea burden, and favorable cephalometric and upper airway characteristics were more consistently associated with improved treatment response, whereas evidence for body mass index, sex, baseline disease severity, and the magnitude of skeletal advancement was inconsistent. These findings support comprehensive patient selection integrating clinical, polysomnographic, and anatomical characteristics and underscore the need for prospective studies using standardized outcome definitions and validated prediction models.

Article.Title: Local climate modifies associations between environmental exposures and paediatric asthma hospitalisation
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Cortes-Ramirez J.; Davies J.; Hu W.
Article.Abstract: Paediatric asthma hospitalisations have marked seasonal peaks, but it remains unclear whether associations with environmental exposures vary under different local climatic conditions. This study aimed to quantify regional- and season-specific associations between environmental factors and paediatric asthma hospitalisations. We conducted a retrospective ecological time-series study in Australia using statewide inpatient administrative records, including all asthma hospitalisations among children and adolescents from 2003 to 2019 in three previously identified high-risk local government areas with contrasting climatic characteristics. Environmental exposures included meteorological variables, air pollutants, and vegetation greenness. Associations were estimated using distributed lag non-linear models, and random forest was used to assess predictor importance. A total of 11,177 hospitalisations were analysed. Environmental associations showed substantial regional and seasonal heterogeneity. Higher vegetation greenness was associated with increased hospitalisation risk across all regions, with the strongest association observed in the tropical monsoon/rainforest region (IRR 1.65, 95% CI 1.29–2.11). Higher mean temperature was inversely associated with risk in all regions, with an estimated 5–8% lower risk per 1 °C increase. By contrast, air pollutant effects were region- and season-dependent, with the largest estimates observed in the tropical savannah wet season, particularly for SO₂ (IRR 2.11, 95% CI 1.56–2.85). Variable-importance analyses consistently identified vegetation greenness and temperature as leading predictors across climatic settings. These findings suggest that associations between environmental exposures and paediatric asthma hospitalisations vary by region and season. Local climatic context may partly explain this heterogeneity, supporting further investigation of region- and season-specific approaches to asthma risk surveillance and prevention.

Article.Title: Danshensu attenuates type 2 diabetes-related osteoporosis via the PI3K/AKT/Nrf2 signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Deng H.; Yu L.; Dai C.; Tao L.; Liang J.; Zhou X.; Chen Y.; Deng P.
Article.Abstract: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble phenolic acid derived from Salvia miltiorrhiza, exhibits antioxidant and osteoprotective properties; however, its effects on type 2 diabetes-related osteoporosis (T2DOP) have not been fully defined. We therefore evaluated the effects of DSS on T2DOP and examined whether PI3K/AKT/Nrf2 signaling participates in its actions. Potential molecular targets and signaling pathways associated with DSS were first screened through a network pharmacology approach. In vivo, T2DOP was induced in mice by high-fat feeding followed by low-dose streptozotocin administration; in parallel, high-glucose-exposed BMSCs served as the cellular model. DSS improved trabecular bone microarchitecture and alleviated bone loss in T2DOP mice. In high-glucose-treated BMSCs, DSS reduced ROS and MDA levels, enhanced SOD and CAT activities, and preserved osteogenic capacity, with higher ALP activity, greater mineralized nodule formation, and increased expression of osteogenesis-related markers. DSS treatment was also accompanied by enhanced PI3K and AKT phosphorylation together with higher Nrf2 expression. Blocking either PI3K or Nrf2 pharmacologically weakened the DSS-induced responses. Collectively, DSS appears to counter T2DOP partly by engaging PI3K/AKT/Nrf2-related antioxidant responses and maintaining osteogenic differentiation.

Article.Title: Non-resonant air-coupled ultrasound for quantifying leaf hydration dynamics and turgor loss in potato leaves
Article.Authors: Sattar M.; Alvarez-Arenas T.; Gil-Pelegrín E.; Sancho-Knapik D.; Ninkovic V.; Laila D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the use of non-resonant air-coupled ultrasound technique as a non-destructive tool for quantifying leaf water status dynamics in potato ( Solanum tuberosum ) leaves. Conventional methods for measuring leaf water status, such as relative water content or pressure–volume (P–V) curves, are destructive and labor-intensive, whereas ultrasound can probe internal tissue structure through mechanical wave propagation. In this work, freshly detached potato leaves were gradually dehydrated under controlled laboratory conditions while ultrasonic transmission signals were recorded using broadband air-coupled transducers operating between 250 kHz and 900 kHz. Time-domain and frequency-domain features, including peak-to-peak amplitude, time-of-flight (ToF), spectral amplitude, and transmission coefficient, were extracted and analyzed as a function of relative water content (RWC). The normalized peak-to-peak (pk–pk) amplitude curve exhibited a clear correlation to the P–V curve, with ultrasonic turgor loss point (TLP) candidate ( $$\mathrm {TLP_c}=0.973$$ ) that closely matched the physiological turgor loss point (TLP) obtained from P–V analysis ( $$\mathrm {RWC_{TLP}}=0.978$$ ). ToF showed a characteristic biphasic response with a slight initial decrease at high RWC followed by a sharp decrease around the dehydration threshold ( $$\mathrm {TLP_c} \approx 0.956$$ ), reflecting the progressive loss of cell-wall tension and increasing mesophyll deformability that are expected to reduce acoustic velocity during dehydration. Spectral amplitude and transmission coefficient exhibited frequency-dependent sensitivity that peaked near 650 kHz. All ultrasonic parameters produced TLP candidates within 2.5% of the physiological reference, confirming that acoustic propagation is governed by turgor-driven structural transitions in the mesophyll. These results establish that non-resonant ultrasound technique can characterize water status in leaves that lack thickness resonances, extending the scope of ultrasonic hydration sensing beyond resonant techniques. The high physiological TLP observed for potato confirms that turgor is lost very early during dehydration, reflecting the species limited osmotic adjustment and drought sensitivity. The limitation of this study is that measurements were performed on detached leaves under controlled conditions; future in situ validation on intact plants under varying microclimates is required. Future work will also focus on deriving attenuation coefficients to separate intrinsic viscoelastic attenuation from absorption mechanisms. Overall in this study, pk–pk amplitude emerged as the most sensitive, computationally efficient, and practical parameter for real-time ultrasonic monitoring of leaf water status and early stress detection.

Article.Title: Neuro-fault recognition-based cybersecurity framework for cardio-hydro-electromechanical stimulators
Article.Authors: Nguyen T.; Vu M.; Loc L.; Nguyen-Huy H.; Dong H.; Voznak M.; Tran T.
Article.Abstract: The modern bio-medical systems are equipped with communication networks for remote control and monitoring purposes. However, the networked systems are susceptible to cyber-attacks, which degrade system operation. This work addresses the cybersecurity problem of cardio-hydro-electromechanical stimulator (C-HEMS) under measurement tampering attacks. To do this, a safety-constrained cyber defense mechanism has been developed to ensure the security of C-HEMS system under such threats under two steps: (i) identification phase: a neuro-fault recognition scheme is proposed to identify tampering attacks by exploring the discrepancy between the observed outputs and estimated states, and (ii) alleviation phase, a non-integer model predictive control (Ni-MPC) is designed to counteract the destructive impacts of cyber anomalies in the C-HEMS. Due to the sensitive nature of the C-HEMS, a safety-enhanced deep reinforcement learning (safe-DRL) is utilized to adaptively adjust the Ni-MPC-based alleviation mechanism. By considering lower and upper bounds, the deep neural network of safe-DRL generates adaptive policies under constraint conditions. The simulation tests on the C-HEMS reveal the feasibility and accuracy of safety-resilience, based on Ni-MPC, to handle measurement tampering attacks. This bounded-policy strategy provides the possibility to dynamically avoid constraint violations, where the safeguarding of cardiac diseases will be realized by following the electrocardiogram (ECG) references under measurement tampering attacks. Quantitative results demonstrate that the proposed safety-resilient Ni-MPC improves the control performance by approximately 27.4% compared with RL-based MPC and 49.8% compared with the unprotected proportional-integral (PI) scheme, confirming its superior cardiac tracking and cyber-attack rejection capability.

Article.Title: Formation and preservation of high-quality reservoirs in the Sha 4 lower submember (Es4x), lacustrine rift bonan depression, Bohai Bay Basin, China
Article.Authors: e Room S.; Liqiang Z.; Wenzhao Z.; Yiming Y.; Hongmei L.; Bilal M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The formation of high-quality reservoirs remains a critical challenge in the exploration and development of deeply buried clastic systems, particularly in lacustrine rift basins where reservoir quality evolution is governed by complex depositional, diagenetic, and structural interactions. This study focuses on deep reservoirs within the lower submember of the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation (Es4x) in the Bonan Depression, Bohai Bay Basin, China. To elucidate the mechanisms controlling reservoir quality, an integrated analytical framework combining core observations, petrographic thin-section analysis, petrophysical measurements, well-log interpretation, and three-dimensional seismic characterization was established. Sedimentary facies analysis indicates that depositional architecture exerted a first-order control on reservoir heterogeneity, with high-energy fan delta front distributary channel and mouth-bar sand bodies providing favorable conditions for primary pore preservation and fluid storage capacity. Reservoir quality evolution is subsequently modified by diagenetic processes, including compaction, cementation, and dissolution, which collectively regulate porosity preservation and secondary pore development. Overpressure evolution and hydrocarbon charging are interpreted to contribute to reservoir preservation, potentially reducing effective compaction and modifying diagenetic pathways. Structural elements, particularly faults and unconformities, are interpreted as fluid migration conduits associated with more efficient hydrocarbon charging and pressure transmission. Evaporative mineral precipitation is interpreted to exert an additional but secondary influence on reservoir physical properties. The formation of high-quality reservoirs is interpreted to result from the coupled effects of sediment supply, transport pathways, diagenetic evolution, and fluid charging processes, which are integrated into a “source-flow-sink” reservoir development framework. Within this framework, favorable depositional conditions, efficient migration systems, short source-to-reservoir distances, and sustained hydrocarbon supply collectively control the distribution and preservation of high-quality reservoirs. This study establishes an integrated genetic model linking depositional processes, diagenetic modification, structural controls, and fluid evolution, providing a predictive framework for reservoir quality evaluation and exploration target identification in deeply buried clastic reservoir systems within lacustrine rift basins.

Article.Title: Inter-model variations in meniscal morphology assessed using fully automatic three-dimensional analysis across five magnetic resonance imaging systems
Article.Authors: Okada R.; Nagai K.; Katano H.; Sasaki E.; Hashiguchi N.; Kaneko H.; Ishibashi Y.; Adachi N.; Ishijima M.; Masumoto J.; Kuroda R.; Sekiya I.
Article.Abstract: The reliability of automated three-dimensional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis of meniscal morphology across different systems remains unclear. The present study investigated inter-model variations in meniscal measurements across five 3-Tesla MRI systems. Ten healthy volunteers (age: 22–60 years) underwent knee MRI scans using five different MRI models. Using fully automated three-dimensional analysis software, the width, thickness, and volume of the medial and lateral meniscus were measured in the anterior, middle, and posterior segments. Inter-model differences were evaluated using the Kruskal–Wallis test. Inter-measurement errors, defined as the absolute difference between each value and the median, were evaluated using histograms. Contributing factors to significant differences among models were also analyzed. Meniscal width and volume were consistent across models ( p > 0.05), with a significant difference in thickness ( p < 0.05) in the middle medial and anterior lateral segments. Among 300 measurements, the width error was ≤ 1.0 mm in 91%, the thickness error was ≤ 0.50 mm in 91%, and the volume error was ≤ 150 mm³ in 97%. Some variations in thickness were attributable to inherent limitations in the resolution of MR images and segmentation errors. These findings suggest that three-dimensional MRI analysis of meniscal morphology provides largely consistent results across different systems, although model-dependent variation was observed in selected thickness measurements. This robust reproducibility may facilitate future investigations of meniscal morphology in clinical and multicenter MRI studies.

Article.Title: Feasibility of micro-CT and Raman spectroscopic characterization of human jaw bone regenerated with particulate cancellous bone and marrow
Article.Authors: Yanagisawa Y.; Koyama S.; Morishima H.; Nogami S.; Yamauchi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Jaw reconstruction using autogenous particulate cancellous bone and marrow (PCBM) is widely performed; however, objectively evaluating regenerated bone quality remains challenging because conventional assessments rely on density-based imaging. In this retrospective study, we characterized PCBM-regenerated jaw bone using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) and Raman spectroscopy. Bone samples were obtained from nine patients during implant placement 6 months after PCBM transplantation. Micro-CT quantified trabecular microarchitecture, including bone volume fraction, trabecular bone thickness, trabecular number, and trabecular separation. Raman spectroscopy assessed the mineral- and matrix-related compositional parameters, including the mineral-to-matrix ratio, carbonate-to-phosphate ratio, and apatite crystallinity. No statistically significant differences in microstructural or Raman-derived parameters were observed between PCBM grafts covered with skin flaps and those covered with gingival mucosa. Similarly, no significant differences were observed between male and female patients. Histological analysis demonstrated newly formed lamellar bone in all specimens. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using micro-CT, Raman spectroscopy, and histological evaluation for multimodal characterization of PCBM-regenerated jaw bone. The specimens showed interindividual structural and compositional variability. Further studies in larger, controlled cohorts are needed to determine the clinical significance of this variability.

Article.Title: Design of a novel filtering antenna using waveguide with enhanced stopband attenuation
Article.Authors: Iram L.; Elmunim N.; Memon A.; Sethi W.; Sarfraz H.; Malik B.; Li X.; Khan S.; Dalarsson M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This work details a novel type of waveguide filtering antenna (filtenna) with a two-post design for use in wireless satellite communications and radar systems. The proposed design incorporates the filtering and radiating capabilities in one small, rectangular, rigid system to overcome the constraint of conventional design methods which demand distinct filtering and radiating elements. The design uses a rectangular waveguide (WR-90) with two metallic posts, in two configurations inline and rotated offset which allows accurate control of the transmission zeros (TZs), high quality factor and stopband attenuation. This novel approach eliminates the requirement for the usual coupling irises to control bandwidth. The inline filtenna has a filtering bandwidth of 1.02 GHz at the X-band and a radiation bandwidth of 0.20 GHz . In contrast, the rotated-offset filtenna has been demonstrated at 9 GHz to 9.5 GHz , with a radiation bandwidth of 0.5 GHz . The simulated and measured results are in good agreement, with maximum gains of 7.05 dBi in the inline and 6.15 dBi in the rotated-offset orientations, and overall efficiency greater than 90 %. The inline filter has a reflection coefficient of less than -19 dB over the 10.6 GHz to 11.25 GHz range, which guarantees a good impedance match. The rotated-offset filtenna has wideband characteristics whose impedance is closely matched in the 8.92 GHz to 9.5 GHz operating band. The final design combines filtering and radiation capabilities in a compact form, increasing frequency selectivity and efficiency. These results emphasize the suitability of the suggested design for radar and satellite systems requiring small size and high-performance RF components.

Article.Title: A prospective split-scar randomized controlled trial of post-operative silicone tape improves scar appearance
Article.Authors: Burke E.; Krauss E.; Atkinson H.; Harrison J.; Leblanc M.; Bezuhly M.; Williams J.; Wheelock M.
Article.Abstract: Topical silicone dressings show promise in improving scar appearance in procedural scars; however, limited high-quality evidence exists.
