This randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed to determine the efficacy of silicone tape (3 M Kind Removal Silicone Tape 2770) as a simple affordable post-operative dressing in improving abdominal scar quality. A prospective single-blind self-controlled trial consisted of a 10-week treatment using split scar methodology in adult patients undergoing breast reconstruction with an abdominal donor site scar. Fifty participants were screened and 41 randomized (1:1) to the treatment side of the abdominal scar to apply silicone tape beginning 2 weeks postoperatively. Significant attrition occurred including six participants lost to follow-up and 22 trial discontinuations primarily for wound-related complications. A per-protocol analysis for the primary outcome observer total score on the validated Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS) between the treated and untreated scar using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests was significantly improved on the silicone-treated side at 3-, 6-, and 12-months post-operatively ( p = 0.0005, p = 0.0025, p = 0.029). The POSAS scores reported by patients were significantly improved with silicone tape at 6 weeks, 3-, and 6-months ( p = 0.014, p = 0.0044, p = 0.001). This trial suggests efficacy of silicone tape to improve scar appearance with near-perfect application as a post-surgical dressing.

Article.Title: Predominantly anthroponotic spread and divergent Giardia assemblages drive co‑circulating lineages in pediatric infections from Egypt
Article.Authors: Naguib D.; Rosenthal B.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Giardia duodenalis is a zoonotic protozoan causing significant waterborne diarrheal disease, yet its genetic diversity and population structure remain under-characterized in many endemic regions. This study examined 451 diarrheic children using qPCR targeting the SSU rRNA gene and multi-locus genotyping of the tpi , gdh, and bg loci to assess prevalence, assemblage distribution, and population-genetic patterns. G. duodenalis was detected in 10.64% of children, with significantly greater prevalence in those aged 1–5 years. Assemblages A and B were detected at nearly equal frequencies. All assemblage A isolates belonged to the human-adapted AII sub- assemblage, whereas assemblage B consisted of diverse BIII/BIV variants or isolates that remained unassigned due to insufficient locus‑specific resolution, particularly at the bg and gdh loci. No mixed infections were detected, and animal contact did not elevate infection risk, definitively demonstrating anthroponotic transmission. Multi-locus analyses revealed striking contrasts between assemblages: assemblage A exhibited extremely low nucleotide and haplotype diversity, complete linkage disequilibrium, absence of recombination, and a highly clonal structure, whereas assemblage B displayed markedly greater polymorphism, increased sub-structuring, elevated haplotype richness, and reticulated phylogenetic networks. Analysis of Molecular Variance (AMOVA) demonstrated near-complete genetic differentiation between assemblages. These findings show that assemblages A and B follow distinct genetic patterns and that giardiasis transmission in this region is driven overwhelmingly by human‑to‑human spread. The strong anthroponotic signal, coupled with the high burden in children aged 1–5 and the absence of any association with animal contact, indicates that public health efforts should prioritize interrupting transmission among young children, particularly in household and childcare settings. Repositories: Representative sequences were deposited in GenBank under accession numbers PX778845-PX778891 for the tpi locus, PX778892-PX778937 for the bg locus, and PX782280-PX782323 for the gdh locus.

Article.Title: Allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells on a decellularized lung scaffold accelerate healing of experimental burn injury in rabbits
Article.Authors: Niazi M.; Maleki M.; Hayati F.; Mohri M.; Mirshokraei P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Full-thickness burn wounds present significant clinical challenges due to impaired healing. This study evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ASCs) combined with decellularized rabbit lung scaffolds (DRLS) in a rabbit burn wound model. A DRLS was fabricated and validated histologically and quantitatively by residual DNA analysis. Two full-thickness experimental burn injuries were created on the dorsal aspect of 18 adult male rabbits. The animals were randomly divided into three groups ( n = 6 per group): an untreated control group, a DRLS-treated group, and an ASCs-DRLS-treated group (4.6–5.0 × 10⁵ cells per wound). Wound healing was assessed on days 14 and 28 using the wound contraction rate, wound area measurement, and histopathological scoring performed by pathologists blinded to the treatment groups. Wound area did not differ significantly among the groups on day 14 ( P = 0.225). By day 17, wounds in the ASCs-DRLS group were smaller than those in the control group (0.20 ± 0.01 vs. 0.61 ± 0.04 cm², P = 0.0002). On day 14, the ASCs-DRLS group exhibited greater re-epithelialization (3.17 ± 0.33 vs. 1.33 ± 0.33, P = 0.007) and higher inflammation resolution scores (2.83 ± 0.33 vs. 1.50 ± 0.00, P = 0.023), with enhanced collagen deposition on day 28 (3.83 ± 0.16 vs. 2.17 ± 0.33, P = 0.006). The DRLS alone did not significantly differ from the control at any time point. These findings indicate that ASCs delivered on DRLS significantly accelerated burn wound healing, with the therapeutic effect attributable to the cells delivered on the scaffold rather than the scaffold alone. The lung-derived scaffold appeared to provide a supportive microenvironment that enhanced ASC paracrine activity and promoted tissue regeneration. This ASCs-DRLS combination represents a promising cell-scaffold strategy for burn wound therapy.

Article.Title: Aerobic exercise induces selective changes in skeletal muscle protein quality control markers in rats with heart failure
Article.Authors: Pigg Q.; Inoue D.; Harris D.; Zhang D.; Boland D.; Janini Gomes M.
Article.Abstract: The objective of this study was to determine whether aerobic exercise could aid in the preservation of the autophagy lysosomal system and mitigate oxidative stress in skeletal muscle during heart failure (HF) progression. Exercise tolerance was lower in HF groups compared to Control (C) groups ( p < 0.05). In skeletal muscle, HF induced type II fiber atrophy (type IIa: p = 0.0007; type IIx/b: p < 0.0001) and impaired all five oxidative phosphorylation complexes ( p < 0.05). Exercise reduced protein carbonyls ( p = 0.0043), while HF decreased antioxidant enzymes (manganese-superoxide dismutase: p = 0.0077; glutathione peroxidase: p = 0.0497) compared to C groups. HF elevated LC3B-II/I ratio compared to C ( p = 0.0246) and reduced cathepsin B ( p = 0.0484), consistent with altered autophagy, although autophagic flux was not assessed. Exercise lowered p62 expression ( p = 0.0449). WGCNA analysis identified an inverse correlation between MEbrown genes and autophagy-lysosomal markers. HF reduced aerobic capacity, likely due to mitochondrial impairments and reduced antioxidant defenses. Autophagy-related pathways remained partially responsive to exercise and may represent an adaptable component of muscle remodeling during HF progression.

Article.Title: Leukocyte glucose index as an early predictor of composite adverse outcomes in clinically diagnosed acute methanol poisoning: a two-centre retrospective observational study
Article.Authors: Tatlı M.; Sutaşır M.; Eyüpoğlu G.; Hökenek N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute methanol poisoning is a life-threatening emergency, and early risk stratification at admission is critical. The leukocyte glucose index (LGI), a marker of systemic inflammation and stress hyperglycaemia, has prognostic value in acute illness but has been studied in only one small methanol cohort. We evaluated admission LGI in clinically diagnosed acute methanol poisoning at two tertiary emergency departments in Türkiye. We conducted a two-centre retrospective study of adults (≥ 18 years) with clinically diagnosed acute methanol poisoning (compatible history, characteristic features, and high anion-gap metabolic acidosis; serum methanol was not measured) admitted between January 2021 and December 2025. LGI was calculated as (WBC [× 103/µL] × plasma glucose [mg/dL])/1000 from the first admission panel. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital mortality, invasive mechanical ventilation, or haemodialysis; mortality alone was a key secondary outcome. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis with paired (DeLong) comparisons, and adjusted associations by logistic regression, including a Firth model containing venous pH, Glasgow coma scale (GCS), and creatinine. Among 83 patients (mean age 40.7 ± 17.4 years; 71.1% male), the composite outcome occurred in 34 (41.0%): mortality 21, intubation 30, and haemodialysis 29. Admission LGI was approximately threefold higher in patients with an event (median 2.75 vs. 0.91; p < 0.001) and correlated with acid–base markers, lactate, GCS, and APACHE-II (all p < 0.001). For the composite outcome, LGI yielded an AUC of 0.879 (95% CI 0.790–0.950), not significantly different from venous pH, GCS, bicarbonate, or creatinine on paired comparison; an exploratory cut-off of 1.24 gave 82.4% sensitivity and 79.2% specificity. For mortality alone, AUC was 0.857 (95% CI 0.733–0.962). Adjusted for age and GCS, log-transformed LGI remained independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR 12.08, 95% CI 1.70–85.92; p = 0.013), although this estimate was imprecise. After adjustment for venous pH, GCS, and creatinine, LGI retained an independent association (Firth aOR 4.70, 95% CI 1.30–31.52; p = 0.017) but improved discrimination only marginally (ΔAUC + 0.020, 95% CI − 0.003 to + 0.044). In clinically diagnosed acute methanol poisoning, admission LGI was independently associated with adverse short-term outcomes, including mortality alone, with discrimination numerically similar to that of established acid–base and clinical severity markers. It added little discrimination once venous pH, GCS, and creatinine were available; its potential value lies in rapid risk stratification where blood-gas analysis is unavailable or delayed. The cut-off of 1.24 is exploratory. Because serum methanol was not measured and two composite components are treatment decisions, prospective external validation in analytically confirmed cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Hydrogen gas alleviates osteoarthritis by inhibiting oxidative stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and extracellular matrix catabolism via the Nrf2/HO-1/NOX4 signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Li M.; Yang J.; Zhou H.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative and debilitating disease. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidative stress play key roles in OA. NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) represents a major ROS source in chondrocytes. Nuclear factor erythroid 2 (NF-E2)-related factor 2 (Nrf2) activation results in the activation of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), which can suppress NOX4 activity. Hydrogen gas (H 2 ) exerts antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic effects. This research aimed to explore whether H 2 can suppress NOX4 via activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and thereby reduce oxidative stress to delay OA progression. An in-vivo OA model was established in male rats through anterior cruciate ligament transection coupled with medial meniscus resection, and an in-vitro OA model was constructed via IL-1β (10 ng/mL) stimulation of human primary chondrocytes. H 2 intervention was performed by intraperitoneal injection of hydrogen-rich saline (in vivo) and incubation with hydrogen-rich medium (in vitro). Nrf2 overexpression plasmids and siRNA knockdown techniques were used in vitro experiments. Detection methods included histological evaluation, apoptosis assays, CCK-8 assay, ROS fluorescence detection, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and western blotting to quantify oxidative stress, inflammatory, and apoptosis factors, as well as extracellular matrix (ECM) and pathway-related proteins. In vivo results showed that H 2 reduced OARSI scores, alleviated cartilage destruction, decreased TUNEL-positive cells, and downregulated MMP-1 and MMP-13 expression. In vitro results demonstrated that H 2 restored chondrocyte viability; reduced levels of ROS, 8-OHdG, and HNE; downregulated cleaved caspase-3 and Bax while upregulating Bcl-2; inhibited iNOS, COX-2, and IL-6 expression; promoted upregulation of collagen II and downregulation of MMP-1 and MMP-13. H 2 also promoted the expression of Nrf2 and HO-1 while suppressing NOX4 expression both in vivo and in vitro. Nrf2 knockdown eliminated the protective influence of H 2 . This research shows that Nrf2 is a crucial mediator of the effects of H 2 , which can activate the Nrf2/HO-1/NOX4 signaling pathway to decrease ROS production and reduce oxidative stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and ECM catabolism, thereby delaying OA progression. Mechanistically, H 2 promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation and inhibited NF-κB signaling via a Nrf2-dependent mechanism.

Article.Title: RCMS: a robust cybersecurity metamodel for cloud computing in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Al-Dhaqm A.; Alshammari A.; Ali A.; Nasser M.; Jhanjhi N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cloud computing underpins Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, making cybersecurity an escalating national concern. Existing security frameworks incorporate relevant measures but lack cloud-specific constructs in identified areas and are not localized to Saudi regulatory requirements. This study has two objectives: to review existing cybersecurity approaches for cloud computing using the PRISMA methodology, appraising their strengths and weaknesses against a stated rubric; and to develop a high-level cybersecurity metamodel for cloud computing in Saudi Arabia, designated RCMS, through a metamodeling approach with modeling rules that include four compliance constraints expressed against NCA and SAMA obligations. RCMS defines seventeen concepts spanning AI-enhanced security, threat detection and incident response, data confidentiality and integrity, encryption, identity and device authentication, multi-cloud and critical infrastructure security, and data classification and residency. Each concept is mapped to Vision 2030 themes, NCA ECC-1:2018 controls and SAMA Cyber Security Framework domains. RCMS was appraised against thirteen security frameworks and eight security metamodels, and was instantiated for banking, healthcare and energy. The instantiations, and the accompanying threat modeling walkthrough, are illustrative and author-constructed; no measured deployment is reported. Practitioners can use RCMS to derive solution models for specific security challenges; scalability and reusability remain design intentions awaiting independent evaluation.

Article.Title: Nonlinear wave dynamics and structural response of hybrid nanocomposite open shells under aerodynamic forces on a friction-coupled elastic foundation
Article.Authors: Safarpour H.; Foong L.; Yaylacı M.; Bayram M.
Article.Abstract: It is extremely important to have information about the stability and wave propagation characteristics of the aircraft structure due to high-speed aerodynamic loads in order to design the next generation of flight vehicles. In this research work, a new coupled methodology between aerodynamics and foundation for nonlinear dispersion of a doubly curved nanocomposite fuselage panel in a supersonic flow regime is proposed. The material is made of an epoxy-based matrix reinforced by nanocrystalline alumina and is resting on a viscoelastic foundation with consideration of all possible interaction forces. Unlike the traditional aeroelastic theory, the proposed methodology offers a physically sound modification to the classical first-order supersonic piston theory. As a result, the aerodynamic loading is state-dependent and inherently dependent on the supporting medium, and the model naturally reduces to classical piston theory in the absence of any foundation effects. The deformation kinematics of the structure are formulated based on higher-order shear deformation theory having a hyperbolic shear strain distribution, while the geometric nonlinearity in the model has been accounted for by means of von Kármán strain-displacement relations. Hamilton’s principle is utilized to develop the fully coupled nonlinear governing equations, and these governing equations have been validated by making extensive comparisons with published results as well as by a separate finite element formulation. The system of nonlinear algebraic equations obtained from the governing equations is solved using the harmonic balance method to determine dispersion characteristics along with nonlinear group and phase velocities. Extensive parametric studies show that the proposed fully coupled aeroelastic model is capable of predicting very complicated instability characteristics, flutter boundaries, wave propagation characteristics, and dispersion properties that cannot be captured by traditional uncoupled models.

Article.Title: Machine learning and GIS-based spatiotemporal prediction of urban sprawl in a rapidly growing African city: a case study of Dodoma, Tanzania
Article.Authors: Mlaga P.; Babere N.
Article.Abstract: Rapid urbanization poses significant challenges to sustainable land use management, particularly in developing countries where growth often occurs in an unplanned manner. In Tanzania, the designation of Dodoma as the national capital has accelerated urban expansion, increasing pressure on land resources and highlighting the need for effective spatial planning. This study analyzes historical urban sprawl and predicts future land use/land cover (LULC) dynamics in Dodoma City. These were derived using the Random Forest (RF) method and later used as transition potential inputs in the CA–Markov model. Multi-temporal satellite imagery for 1996, 2006, 2016, and 2026 was classified into four LULC classes (water, built-up, vegetation, and bare land), achieving overall accuracies ranging from 75 to 95% and Kappa coefficients between 0.66 and 0.93. Future scenarios for 2036 and 2046 were simulated using the CA–Markov model, yielding strong predictive performance (AUC = 0.906 and 0.844, respectively). Results show that built-up land increased from 0.63% in 1996 to 14.32% in 2026 and is projected to reach 25.53% by 2046. Population density, elevation, and road accessibility were identified as the dominant drivers of urban expansion. Urban sprawl risk mapping indicates that over 52% of the study area is classified as low risk, while approximately 12% falls within medium-to-high risk zones requiring planning intervention. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating machine learning and spatial simulation models in urban growth analysis and provides critical insights for evidence-based planning and sustainable urban development in a rapidly growing cities.

Article.Title: Tail weighted multi criteria probability distribution selection for drought frequency analysis
Article.Authors: Zolfaghari F.; Matinzadeh M.; Eslamian S.; Gohari A.; Azadi S.; Jamali M.
Article.Abstract: Drought is a complex hydroclimatic hazard whose probabilistic characterization is strongly influenced by the drought index and probability distribution adopted. This study develops a distribution-sensitive framework for assessing drought frequency and long-term trends in the Zayandehrud Basin, Iran. Five 12-month drought indices, including SPI, SPEI, EDDI, RDI, and PDSI, were evaluated at seven meteorological stations during 1993–2024. Eighteen candidate probability distributions representing classical, generalized, heavy-tailed, extreme-value, and bounded-support families were fitted independently to each station–index series. Distribution selection was performed using a tail-weighted composite goodness-of-fit criterion integrating AIC, BIC, KS, standard Anderson–Darling, lower- and upper-tail Anderson–Darling statistics, and cross-validated log-likelihood. Bootstrap resampling and Q–Q plots were additionally used to assess fitting stability and graphical adequacy. The results revealed substantial spatial and inter-index distributional variability, with Cauchy frequently selected for EDDI and Beta commonly identified for PDSI, while RDI, SPEI, and SPI exhibited greater distributional diversity. Return-period analysis demonstrated increasing spatial divergence toward rarer drought events, emphasizing the importance of distributional uncertainty in extreme drought estimation. Trend analysis further revealed localized and index-dependent changes rather than a uniform basin-wide trend. The proposed framework provides a robust basis for drought-frequency assessment and supports location-specific drought-risk management and water-resources planning.

Article.Title: Beyond conventional performance assessment of recycled aggregate concrete through integrated data analytics
Article.Authors: Mohamud M.; Yildizel S.; Özkılıç Y.
Article.Abstract: The mechanical performance of recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) varies with aggregate quality, mixture composition, and experimental conditions, complicating the interpretation of published replacement-ratio trends. This study integrates descriptive statistics, LOWESS smoothing, bootstrap uncertainty estimation, derivative-based analysis, and clustering to examine five normalized indicators: compressive strength, splitting tensile strength, flexural strength, bulk density, and elastic modulus. Property-specific complete-case analyses cover RCA replacement ratios from 0 to 100%. The fitted relationships indicate overall reductions relative to the reference mixtures, together with property-specific non-monotonic features. Elastic modulus exhibits the largest between-category effect-size estimate, whereas bulk density shows comparatively small absolute changes in normalized response. The maximum-absolute-slope locations differ among properties and do not consistently represent deterioration: the NCS location occurs on a local upward segment of the bootstrap-mean curve. These locations and the associated high-slope intervals are therefore interpreted as method-dependent descriptors rather than physical failure thresholds. Four fixed RCA intervals provide an exploratory description of the compiled evidence, without defining safe replacement limits or structural application classes. The framework supports transparent synthesis and hypothesis generation, while source heterogeneity, within-study dependence, uneven coverage, and sensitivity to the analytical specification limit broader inference.

Article.Title: Microsatellite instability detection in extracellular vesicles of short-chain fatty acids-treated colorectal cancer cells
Article.Authors: Macedo D.; Teixeira A.; Lage T.; Sampaio-Marques B.; Xavier M.; Abalde-Cela S.; Diéguez L.; Preto A.; Honrado C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Late-stage diagnosis renders colorectal cancer (CRC) a major health challenge, mostly due to the lack of reliable non-invasive biomarkers. Although microsatellite instability (MSI) is a promising genetic biomarker guiding immunotherapy selection, its detection still relies on invasive sampling. Here, we explored whether short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), gut microbiota-derived metabolites with established pro-apoptotic and anti-tumorigenic functions, could enhance extracellular vesicle (EV) production and improve the recovery of tumor-derived DNA. EVs represent a promising source of nucleic acids for liquid biopsy applications. Two CRC cell lines with distinct MSI status were exposed to SCFAs, followed by isolation and characterization of small and large EVs. SCFA treatment significantly increased EV production (1.38-fold in RKO and 2.15-fold in SW480), without affecting the expression of known EV markers (i.e., CD9, CD63, Alix). This response was accompanied by caspases detection and a DNA redistribution, with reduced total DNA (cell and cell-free) and increased EV-DNA (17.7-fold in L-EVs and 32.8-fold in s-EVs from SW480 cells). Importantly, we demonstrate, for the first time, the capability to identify MSI-specific alterations in EV-DNA using droplet digital PCR. These findings indicate that SCFA-associated EV release favors the recovery of DNA-rich EVs, highlighting EV-DNA as a promising substrate for non-invasive MSI diagnostics.

Article.Title: Data-driven and interpretable modeling frameworks for frost accumulation during natural convection on polymer composite fins
Article.Authors: Al Bustanji S.; Alrihaim T.; Kumar R.; Chauhan M.; Abbas W.; Bains P.; Gill H.; Sabirov S.; Ranjbar F.
Article.Abstract: Frost formation on heat-transfer surfaces remains a critical challenge in refrigeration, cryogenic systems, and energy-efficient thermal management. Accurate prediction of frost layer thickness (FLT) is particularly important for carbon fiber reinforced polymer composite fins (CFRPCFs), where distinct thermophysical properties alter frost growth dynamics relative to conventional metallic substrates. Because existing empirical correlations struggle to capture the highly nonlinear heat and mass transfer mechanisms unique to composite substrates, this study develops interpretable machine learning frameworks to model FLT during natural convection. Using an experimental database of $$\:356$$ observations, four models, i.e., support vector machine (SVM), artificial neural network (ANN), radial basis function neural network (RBFNN), and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), were constructed using physically informed dimensionless inputs and optimized via Bayesian optimization. The developed RBFNN model demonstrated superior predictive capability, yielding mean absolute percentage deviation (MAPD) values of $$\:1.07\text{\%}$$ and $$\:2.06\text{\%}$$ for learning and validation, respectively, representing a major improvement over literature correlations. A grouped nine-fold (condition-wise) cross-validation protocol, iteratively holding out entire operating conditions, confirmed robust model generalization to unseen operational states, while applicability domain analysis verified model reliability across the experimental parameter space. Crucially, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were integrated to resolve the black-box nature of these models. The resulting model-attributed feature-importance patterns were found to be qualitatively consistent with established frost-growth mechanisms. This work provides a highly accurate, stable, and physically interpretable framework for FLT prediction on composite fins, establishing a reliable modeling template for advanced thermal materials.

Article.Title: MRGAN: a multi-resolution residual generative adversarial network with wavelet decomposition and phase-aware loss for microseismic waveform denoising
Article.Authors: Gu L.
Article.Abstract: Microseismic monitoring plays a critical role in hydraulic-fracturing evaluation, enhanced geothermal system (EGS) development, and mining-induced hazard assessment, but the extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of field waveforms and the difficulty of preserving phase information continue to limit its practical value. Existing deep-learning denoisers primarily focus on amplitude fidelity while introducing measurable phase distortions that degrade downstream source-localization tasks. We present MRGAN, a multi-resolution residual generative adversarial network that integrates three-level Daubechies wavelet decomposition, multi-scale residual encoding with kernels of size 3, 5, and 7, a wavelet feature fusion module with channel attention, and a multi-scale PatchGAN discriminator. The network is optimized under a composite loss function combining Wasserstein adversarial loss with gradient penalty, L1 reconstruction loss, a novel Hilbert-transform-based phase-aware loss, and a wavelet-domain coefficient loss. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks (STEAD, EGS Collab Experiment 2, and PNW-ML) show that MRGAN reaches 14.28 dB output SNR and 3.21 \(^{\circ }\) mean phase error at −5 dB input SNR—a 61.5% phase-error reduction over the DeepDenoiser baseline. On field data, MRGAN achieves a 10.72 dB SNR improvement while retaining 96.8% of microseismic events, and it generalizes to unseen event categories in PNW-ML without retraining. Inference runs in 12.85 ms per sample, making MRGAN directly deployable in operational monitoring pipelines.

Article.Title: Optimized design of 3D human pose estimation algorithm based on improved adaptive attention mechanism for sports training
Article.Authors: Li P.; Huang R.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate three-dimensional (3D) human pose estimation is fundamental to sports training analysis, athlete performance monitoring, and rehabilitation guidance. Existing deep learning-based methods are primarily limited by two key deficiencies: (1) fixed receptive fields of convolutional networks hinder the effective learning of long-range joint dependencies, and (2) standard residual backbones fail to differentiate the discriminative importance of individual feature channels, which is particularly detrimental to depth coordinate regression accuracy in complex athletic scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel 3D human pose estimation network enhanced by an Improved Adaptive Attention Mechanism, specifically optimized for sports training scenarios. Building upon a weakly supervised transfer learning baseline, we introduce a Residual Attention Module (RAM) that integrates ECANet into the ResNet50 residual blocks to reinforce channel-wise feature discrimination critical for depth estimation. Additionally, we design an Adaptive Attention Mechanism based on Batch Normalization initialization to ensure seamless compatibility with pre-trained weights, preventing the disruption of learned semantic information during early training. Extensive experiments on the Human3.6M benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves significant performance gains, reducing the Mean Per Joint Position Error (MPJPE) from 64.9 mm to 58.6 mm–a 9.7% relative improvement. To explicitly validate the model’s utility in real-world sports training, we extend our evaluation to the AthleticsPose dataset, featuring authentic high-speed athletic motions. Furthermore, comprehensive evaluations on 2D sports datasets yield state-of-the-art results, including a 94.3% PCK@0.2 on the LSP dataset, with notable accuracy gains in challenging distal joints such as wrists and ankles. Ablation studies validate the distinct and cumulative contributions of the channel and spatial recalibration modules. Finally, qualitative assessments and inter-joint cosine similarity matrix analyses confirm that the proposed architecture markedly improves the modeling of structural biomechanical relationships and provides robust depth estimation under severe self-occlusions and complex asymmetric postures–capabilities directly beneficial for precise technique analysis in athletic environments.

Article.Title: Structural, thermal, mechanical and physical performance of cellulose fibers based low-density polyethylene/recycled polyethylene terephthalate blend composites
Article.Authors: Boussehel H.; Alloui L.; Ouaar A.; Reis P.; Karim Z.; Jawaid M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing interest in recycled polymer composites and natural fiber reinforcement, relatively few studies have systematically examined low-density polyethylene (LDPE)/recycled polyethylene terephthalate (r-PET) blend systems reinforced with cellulose fibers recovered from used disposable paper cups, particularly through a direct comparison of untreated and methacrylic acid-grafted fibers. In this context, the present study developed sustainable composites based on LDPE and r-PET reinforced with cellulose fibers extracted from post-consumer paper cups and chemically modified with methacrylic acid. FTIR analysis indicated successful surface modification, as evidenced by the disappearance or reduction of lignin- and hemicellulose-related bands after bleaching and the appearance of a carbonyl band at approximately 1712 cm − 1 after grafting. XRD results showed a marked increase in crystallinity after bleaching, from 21.13% for washed fibers to 54.70% for bleached fibers. Grafted fibers retained an intermediate crystallinity of 46.75%, reflecting the partial disruption of the cellulose structure by grafting. TGA showed that methacrylic acid grafting improved the thermal stability of the fibers, increasing the main decomposition temperature from 327 °C for washed fibers to 354.48 °C for grafted fibers. DSC analysis was consistent with the enhanced thermal response and crystallization behavior of the composites, whereas r-PET incorporation increased the rigidity and thermal resistance relative to neat LDPE. Mechanically, blending LDPE with 25 wt% r-PET increased the ultimate tensile strength from 1.69 MPa to 7.40 MPa and Young’s modulus from 101.55 MPa to 272.17 MPa. The addition of grafted fibers further improved the tensile strength to 6.78 MPa and modulus to 218.58 MPa compared with untreated fibers. Water absorption tests showed that untreated fibers significantly increased moisture uptake, whereas methacrylic acid-grafted fibers markedly reduced water absorption and improved dimensional stability. Overall, the results suggest that integrating recycled PET and chemically modified cellulose fibers into LDPE matrices can yield composites with improved mechanical performance, enhanced thermal stability, and reduced water uptake relative to neat LDPE, thereby contributing to waste valorization and circular-economy-oriented applications within the limitations of the present system.

Article.Title: No detectable association of APOE ε4 with spatial navigation and broader cognition in healthy young adults
Article.Authors: Graichen L.; Schenk L.; Gausterer C.; Wagner I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) causes progressive memory loss and disorientation. It is preceded by a prolonged preclinical phase marked by pathological changes in medial temporal lobe regions involved in spatial navigation. Spatial navigation tasks have been proposed for early AD detection, and altered navigation performance was reported in older carriers of the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele, the major genetic risk factor for sporadic AD. However, whether spatial navigation or other cognitive abilities are affected in younger ε4 carriers remains unclear. Here, we genotyped 1,000 healthy young adults (18–35 years) who completed the app-based navigation game “Sea Hero Quest” and several tasks assessing working memory, processing speed, executive functioning, and face recognition. APOE ε3ε4 carriers ( N = 88) showed no detectable differences from ε3ε3 carriers ( N = 327) on the assessed spatial navigation and cognitive measures, supported by equivalence testing and Bayesian analyses. Exploratory findings in smaller APOE ε2 subgroups (ε2ε2/ε2ε3/ε2ε4, N s = 7/51/7) suggested navigation closer to environmental borders and better memory updating, better face recognition, and faster processing speed than in ε3ε3 controls. Therefore, APOE-related behavioural differences in young adults appeared small at best, highlighting the need for paradigms sensitive to very subtle changes decades before potential dementia onset.

Article.Title: Administration of a phosphodiesterase 4B inhibitor reduces hippocampal neuronal cell death after global cerebral ischemia
Article.Authors: Park S.; Choi B.; Kho A.; Hong D.; Lee M.; Lee S.; Kang B.; Park M.; Lee C.; Yang H.; Woo S.; Kim D.; Yang W.; Jung H.; Suh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global cerebral ischemia (GCI) causes widespread neuronal injury, with hippocampal neurons being particularly vulnerable. This study examined whether post-GCI treatment with amlexanox (AMX), a phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B) inhibitor, reduces hippocampal neurodegeneration and modulates lysosome/autophagy-associated processes. In a mouse model of GCI, AMX (10 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) was administered daily, and hippocampal injury was evaluated using histological and molecular analyses. AMX treatment reduced neuronal degeneration and preserved neuronal integrity in the hippocampus. These effects were accompanied by reduced PDE4B expression, increased levels of proteins associated with lysosomal and autophagic processes, and changes in apoptosis-related protein expression. Overall, AMX treatment exerted neuroprotective effects and was associated with alterations in lysosome/autophagy-associated markers following GCI. Although the underlying signaling mechanisms and autophagic flux were not directly examined, these findings suggest that AMX may represent a potential therapeutic approach for reducing ischemia-induced neuronal injury.

Article.Title: Green-synthesized copper nanoparticles differentially modulate germination and selected stress-response genes in Phelipanche aegyptiaca
Article.Authors: Ibrahim M.; Zaitoun F.; Hafez E.; Komeil D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Egyptian broomrape ( Phelipanche aegyptiaca ) is a devastating parasitic weed requiring eco-friendly control strategies. This in vitro study investigated the effects of green-synthesised copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticles, produced using Anethum graveolens extract, on P. aegyptiaca germination and targeted stress-gene expression. Nanoparticles were physicochemically characterised via TEM, DLS, and FTIR. Germination bioassays (1–25 mg L⁻¹ CuO-NPs; 25 mg L⁻¹ bulk CuSO₄) were conducted under four distinct physiological conditions. Under non-inductive conditions, 1 mg L⁻¹ CuO-NPs stimulated germination from ~ 0.7% to ~ 8.1%, indicating a clear hormetic response. Conversely, 10–25 mg L⁻¹ CuO-NPs caused strong germination inhibition and radicle-growth suppression (> 97% reduction), even under optimal strigolactone stimulation. Unlike bulk CuSO₄, CuO-NPs triggered dose-dependent upregulation of antioxidant and phenylpropanoid genes ( SOD , APX , PAL ) and significantly elevated phenolic and flavonoid contents. Furthermore, EDS revealed that CuO-NPs produced more spatially dispersed copper deposition on seed coats compared to localised aggregates formed by bulk copper. These findings demonstrate that green-synthesised CuO-NPs effectively modulate parasitic weed germination and stress-related gene expression in vitro , highlighting their promising potential for targeted seed-bank management pending further comprehensive environmental and host-safety validation.

Article.Title: Musculoskeletal pain and atrial fibrillation: the Framingham Heart Study
Article.Authors: Zertuche J.; Felson D.; Neogi T.; Roseen E.; Benjamin E.; Preis S.
Article.Abstract: Given the morbidity and mortality of atrial fibrillation (AF), identifying factors associated with its onset is a priority. Chronic pain affects one-third of Americans and is linked to cardiovascular disease outcomes, including stroke and mortality. Since there are common pathophysiological mechanisms, including inflammation and oxidative stress, we sought to investigate whether musculoskeletal pain, including widespread pain (WSP), was associated with AF. Participants aged ≥ 45 years from the Framingham Heart Study (FHS) Original and Offspring cohorts who completed a pain assessment were included. Pain was categorized into three groups: widespread pain (WSP), non-widespread pain (non-WSP), and no pain. Incident AF was identified using ECGs and medical records. We assessed the relation of pain and risk of incident AF using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard modeling accounting for competing risk of death. Models were adjusted for potential confounders. The incident AF analysis included 3,740 participants ( N = 358 AF events). Mean age at pain assessment was 62 ± 11 years and 56% were women. Compared to those with no pain, the risk for incident AF was modestly elevated among those with non-WSP (sHR = 1.30 (95% CI: 1.03–1.64); p = 0.03) and WSP (sHR = 1.41 (95% CI: 1.01–1.98); p = 0.04) in age/sex-adjusted models. The association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (sHR non-WSP = 1.26 (95% CI: 1.00-1.59; p = 0.05) and sHR WSP = 1.35 (95% CI: 0.96–1.88; p = 0.08). We observed a modest association between musculoskeletal pain (WSP and non-WSP) and 10-year incident AF in age and sex-adjusted models that accounted for the competing risk mortality, however, this finding did not attain statistical significance after adjustment for the CHARGE-AF 1 risk factor score components in the multivariable model.

Article.Title: Correction of extreme wind speed forecasts using ensemble learning over typical gale areas in Xinjiang, China
Article.Authors: Kuerban Y.; Pan X.; Hai S.; Ge Y.; Liu B.; Hu C.; Aihaiti A.
Article.Abstract: The complex terrain of Xinjiang generates frequent extreme winds, posing risks to transportation safety. Numerical forecasts along transportation routes suffer from systematic biases stemming from limited observational data and terrain-amplification effects. Using observations from representative stations in key gale zones of Xinjiang, this study evaluates ECMWF gust forecasts from January 2023 to December 2025. While the model exhibits good correlation with observations, it generally underestimates wind speeds in the “Front Baili Wind Zone” and “Baili Wind Zone”. RMSE increases as wind speeds become more extreme, with the maximum RMSE reaching 10.24 m s⁻ 1 at the representative station. Accordingly, several ML techniques are employed to correct ECMWF gust forecasts. Results indicate that stacking (a machine-learning ensemble model) reduces RMSE by a maximum of 51.8% relative to the raw ECMWF forecast at Station A., while XGBoost achieves a maximum RMSE reduction of 47.9%. Notably, the stacking model demonstrates limited but useful generalization capabilities in areas with sparse observations and complex underlying surfaces. In terms of extreme wind speeds, ECMWF forecasts exhibit very low accuracy for wind speeds above level 14 in the verification samples. However, forecasts corrected by Stacking model effectively capture such extreme wind speeds, with gust forecast accuracy reaching up to 77.8% (Force 16) at representative stations.Therefore, integrating ensemble ML models into operational applications holds promising prospects for improving the forecasting performance of numerical models in areas with complex terrains.

Article.Title: Improved DASP-guided normal vector refinement for automatic discontinuity identification in 3D rock mass point clouds
Article.Authors: Leng B.; Ye F.; Jiang Y.; Zhu J.; Yuan N.; Che X.; Jiang Y.; Xiang L.; Yu Z.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The spatial orientation of rock discontinuities is a fundamental parameter for evaluating rock mass stability and designing engineering support systems. This study proposes an automatic discontinuity identification method for three-dimensional rock mass point clouds based on improved density analysis of stereographic projections (DASP)-guided normal vector refinement. An adaptive voxel partitioning strategy and an improved DASP algorithm are employed to automatically determine the number of clusters and the initial orientation centers for K-means clustering. Furthermore, a prior orientation-guided normal vector diagnosis and selective re-estimation strategy is developed to mitigate the influence of mixed normal vectors on discontinuity identification. Validation using both a publicly available dataset and an in situ tunnel-face point cloud demonstrates that the proposed method achieves mean absolute errors as low as 0.89° and 1.05° for dip direction and dip angle, respectively. The proposed approach enables efficient discontinuity identification and automatic extraction of orientation parameters from complex rock mass point clouds.

Article.Title: ANN modelling and GA optimisation of microalgal removal of cortisone acetate, organic matter and nutrients
Article.Authors: Derakhshan Z.; Tavakoli F.; Feilizadeh M.; Samaei M.; Kazeruni F.; Kouchak N.; Asadollahi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microalgal treatment can couple pharmaceutical attenuation with organic-matter and nutrient removal, but the operating windows for saline and freshwater species remain insufficiently defined. This laboratory study combined a central composite design, dual-detector confirmation of cortisone acetate (CA) removal, biomass mass balance, and artificial neural network (ANN) modelling and genetic algorithm (GA) optimisation to evaluate Tetraselmis chui ( T. chui ) and Scenedesmus obtusus ( S. obtusus ) under salinity, pH, and treatment-time variation. Cortisone acetate was evaluated with T. chui , whereas biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) were measured for both species. At 30.00 g/L salinity, pH 8.00, and 10.00 days, T. chui achieved 96.62% CA removal and 95.69–96.91% removal of the four water-quality parameters. At 0.00 g/L salinity, pH 7.00, and 10.00 days, S. obtusus achieved 96.25–98.41% removal of BOD, COD, TN, and TP. Species-specific ANN models accurately reproduced the experimental response surfaces (R² = 0.997 for T. chui and 0.978 for S. obtusus ), and the GA identified species-specific optima within the experimental ranges. The integrated experimental–analytical–modelling framework identifies salinity as the principal operational control while distinguishing the saline niche of T. chui from the freshwater niche of S. obtusus .

Article.Title: Family acceptance as a buffer against hate-speech induced depression and suicidal ideation among gay and lesbian individuals in Poland
Article.Authors: Soral W.; Bilewicz M.; Winiewski M.; Bulska D.
Article.Abstract: Experiences of minority stress likely contribute to elevated levels of depression and suicidal ideation among LGBT individuals. We examined whether the self-reported frequency of exposure to hate speech targeting gay men and lesbians was associated with these outcomes and whether family acceptance of one’s sexual orientation attenuated these associations. We used data from a national survey of the Polish LGBTQiA community ( N = 3827 gay men and lesbians). Participants reported the severity of eight symptoms of depression, as well as the frequency of suicidal ideation. They also indicated how often they had encountered homophobic hate speech, and which categories of close family members accepted their sexual orientation. A higher self-reported frequency of exposure to homophobic hate speech was associated with greater severity of depressive symptoms and more frequent suicidal ideation. These associations were moderated by family acceptance, such that they were weaker among participants with higher family acceptance scores. Our findings provide evidence that family acceptance may buffer negative mental health outcomes of hate speech exposure among gay men and lesbians.

Article.Title: In vitro evaluation of pH, calcium ion release and interfacial characterization of calcium silicate–based and epoxy resin–based sealers
Article.Authors: Radwanski M.; Piwonski I.; Wojtczak M.; Boneta A.; Sauro S.; Matinlinna J.; Lukomska-Szymanska M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This in vitro study evaluated the physicochemical properties and interfacial behavior of four calcium silicate–based sealers (CSBS) compared to an epoxy resin–based sealer. Specimens were prepared under standardized conditions, and pH and calcium (Ca 2+ ) ion release were measured over time. The interfacial characterization was performed on selected extracted teeth using scanning electron microscopy to evaluate gap formation and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy to determine elemental composition. Statistical analysis included linear mixed-effects models for repeated pH and interfacial gap measurements, one- and two-way ANOVA with Tukey’s HSD post hoc test, and Kruskal–Wallis test with Dunn’s post hoc test, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. All CSBS exhibited consistently high alkaline pH values and measurable calcium ion release, whereas the epoxy resin–based sealer showed neutral pH and no detectable Ca 2+ release. Interfacial analysis revealed higher Calcium-to-Phosphorus (Ca/P) ratios and lower relative calcium differences for CSBS, whereas the resin-based sealer showed greater differences in calcium and carbon content at the dentine–sealer interface. Additionally, interfacial gap width differed according to sealer type and canal region, with CSBS generally showing smaller SEM-measured gaps than AH Plus and gap widths tending to increase toward the apical region. CSBS demonstrated higher alkalinity, measurable calcium ion release, and generally favorable interfacial adaptation compared with the epoxy resin–based sealer. The observed alkaline pH, calcium ion release, and favorable interfacial adaptation highlight physicochemical and interfacial characteristics that are relevant when considering CSBS for root canal obturation.

Article.Title: S2DFusion: a statistical and scale difference attention network for infrared and visible image fusion
Article.Authors: Bian Z.
Article.Abstract: Infrared and visible image fusion aims to integrate cross-modal complementary information for comprehensive all-weather scene perception. However, existing methods often fail to effectively decouple background noise from modality-specific salient features, leading to contrast degradation, diminished thermal target prominence, and the loss of fine texture details in the fused images. To address these limitations, we propose S2DFusion, a novel statistical and scale-differential attention network that constructs a “difference-oriented” explicit decoupling and fusion paradigm. Specifically, the infrared branch introduces a Statistical Difference Attention (SDA) module to actively separate and refine high-energy thermal targets from the background. Concurrently, the visible branch employs a Scale Difference Large Kernel (SDLK) module to capture and enhance multi-scale high-frequency textures. To prevent spatial confusion during feature integration, we design a lateral branch with a Local Attention Module (LAM) to preserve unique features, and a Common-Unique Cross Aggregation Module (CUCAM) at the bottleneck to achieve deep semantic integration. Furthermore, the network is driven by a multi-task loss function combining feature decoupling, intensity fidelity, and salient gradient boosting to maximize structural detail and contrast preservation. Extensive experiments across multiple public datasets demonstrate that S2DFusion achieves state-of-the-art performance in both subjective visual quality and objective metrics. Moreover, evaluations on downstream YOLO object detection tasks validate that the proposed method significantly enhances detection accuracy and robustness in complex environments by preserving high-fidelity thermal targets and multi-scale details. Feature-level decomposition analysis further verifies that the learned common and unique representations exhibit the intended cross-modal similarity and intra-modal orthogonality. Sensitivity and perceptual-quality analyses show that the gradient amplification factor provides a controllable trade-off between edge enhancement and perceptual naturalness, while downstream evaluations with both YOLOv5s and YOLOv8s demonstrate that the benefit is not detector-specific.

Article.Title: Association between trajectory patterns of urea-to-creatinine ratio within 7 days after admission and prognosis in patients with sepsis
Article.Authors: Li X.; Pan H.; Li R.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by substantial clinical heterogeneity. The urea-to-creatinine ratio (UCR) is a readily available biomarker reflecting systemic metabolic stress and renal handling; however, the prognostic value of its dynamic trajectories in sepsis remains unclear. This study aimed to identify UCR trajectory phenotypes in patients with sepsis using longitudinal data analysis and to investigate their associations with 30-day all-cause mortality. This retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the MIMIC-IV database. A total of 7145 patients who met the Sepsis-3 diagnostic criteria were included. Longitudinal UCR measurements within the first 7 days after ICU admission were analyzed using latent class growth mixture modeling (LCGMM) to identify distinct trajectory patterns. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were performed to evaluate the associations between UCR trajectory phenotypes and 30-day all-cause mortality. Five distinct UCR trajectory classes were identified by LCGMM: Class 1 (low-to-high sharp increase, 2.9%), Class 2 (low-to-moderate gradual increase, 24.3%), Class 3 (persistently low stable, 55.6%), Class 4 (high-to-low rapid decline, 2.0%), and Class 5 (moderately high gradual decline, 15.1%). Using Class 1 as the reference, multivariable Cox regression analysis demonstrated significantly lower mortality risks in all other classes (hazard ratios [HRs]: Class 2: 0.469; Class 3: 0.346; Class 4: 0.251; Class 5: 0.350; all P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses further revealed that the prognostic value of UCR trajectories was more pronounced in patients without acute kidney injury (AKI) and in those not requiring mechanical ventilation (interaction P < 0.001). LCGMM-based modeling of dynamic UCR trajectories effectively identifies sepsis phenotypes with distinct prognoses. Trajectories characterized by a sharp increase or persistently elevated UCR are associated with the highest mortality risk. This approach demonstrates enhanced risk stratification capability, particularly among patients without documented AKI. Our findings provide novel evidence supporting the use of routinely available, dynamic laboratory indicators for prognostic assessment and individualized management in patients with sepsis.

Article.Title: Local versus central differential privacy under final-model privacy attacks in low-client-count cross-silo federated learning
Article.Authors: Kokin H.; Lytvyn O.; Nguyen G.
Article.Abstract: Federated learning reduces the need to centralize raw data, but does not prevent privacy leakage from client updates, aggregation messages, or the final released model. This work compares local differential privacy (LDP), central differential privacy (CDP), record-level differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), and secure aggregation (SecAgg) in a low-client-count cross-silo setting with full client participation, across four datasets spanning image classification, tabular binary classification, and two time-series forecasting tasks. The study separates training-time confidentiality from final-model leakage and evaluates the released models under two final-model privacy attacks, membership inference and targeted reconstruction. Under these attacks, SecAgg leaves final-model leakage essentially unchanged: it protects the confidentiality of per-client updates during training but provides no $$(\varepsilon ,\delta )$$ guarantee for the released model, and is therefore evaluated as a complementary training-time mechanism whose principal cost is a training-time overhead of approximately 49% to 106%, varying by dataset and client count. Differential privacy constrains final-model leakage more directly, but its practical value depends on the balance between privacy protection and retained utility. Across the evaluated configurations, record-level DP-SGD, implemented locally on each client by clipping and perturbing per-example gradients, preserved utility best, staying closest to the non-private baseline on every task and remaining usable on image classification, where both client-contribution-level mechanisms collapsed to chance-level accuracy. Among the client-level mechanisms, CDP matched or exceeded LDP at equal privacy budget, because under a single consistent accountant the two share the same noise calibration and LDP carries $$\sqrt{M}$$ more aggregate noise; the advantage of DP-SGD in turn follows from privacy amplification by subsampling, which lets it reach a given budget at roughly a tenth of the client-level noise. Under both final-model attacks the released models leaked little: membership inference stayed close to random guessing on the classification tasks, with a modest, temporally confounded elevation on the time-series tasks, and targeted reconstruction never improved on an uninformed baseline. These findings support selecting privacy-enhancing mechanisms according to the attacker model, trust assumptions, privacy unit, and acceptable utility loss, rather than by mechanism label alone.

Article.Title: Prevalence and associated factors of traditional eyelash epilation among patients with trachomatous trichiasis in South Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Ware E.; Wegayehu T.; Woldeyes D.; Zerdo Z.
Article.Abstract: Trachoma remains the leading infectious cause of blindness globally, with Ethiopia bearing the highest disease burden. Trachomatous trichiasis (TT), the advanced stage of trachoma, requires surgical correction to prevent irreversible blindness. However, many affected patients rely on traditional eyelash epilation as an alternative to surgery. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of traditional eyelash epilation and identify factors associated with its practice among TT patients in South Ethiopia. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted using baseline data from a cluster randomized controlled trial carried out in selected woredas, in South Ethiopia, in 2026. A total of 464 adult TT patients were included through multistage cluster sampling across 58 kebeles. Data were collected using interviewer-administered structured questionnaires and clinical eye examination. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with traditional eyelash epilation, accounting for clustering at the kebele level. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05. The prevalence of traditional epilation among TT patients was 46.8% (95% CI 42.2–51.3). Each additional month of symptom duration increased the odds of traditional epilation by 7% (AOR = 1.07, 95% CI 1.04–1.10). Similarly, participants who lived more than a 30 min walk from a health facility had significantly higher odds of traditional epilation than those living within 30 min (AOR = 1.87, 95% CI 1.00–3.48). Participants with adequate knowledge about TT surgery (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI 0.16–0.62) and favourable attitudes toward TT surgery (AOR = 0.56, 95% CI 0.32–0.98) were less likely to practice epilation. Traditional epilation remains prevalent among patients with TT in South Ethiopia. Longer duration of symptoms, limited access to health facilities, and inadequate knowledge and unfavourable attitudes toward TT surgery were associated factors. Strengthening social and behavioural change communication to improve awareness and attitudes toward surgical management, along with expanding access to TT surgical services, is essential to reduce reliance on traditional epilation.

Article.Title: Data-driven identification of economic drivers and regional disparities of ecological resilience in china’s urban agglomerations: an explainable deep learning framework
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Wang Y.; Ding X.; Li L.; Tang J.
Article.Abstract: As key spatial carriers for regional economic growth and ecological protection, urban agglomerations’ ecological resilience is critical to regional risk adaptation and sustainable development. This study examines 92 prefecture-level and above cities in China’s five major urban agglomerations from 2007 to 2021. An ecological resilience evaluation system is constructed under the resistance–adaptability–recovery framework and measured using the CRITIC method. The CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model combined with the SHAP explainable framework is then employed to explore the economic drivers and their heterogeneous impacts, and its predictive performance is benchmarked against seven established baseline models. Results show that ecological resilience presents a distinct “core-periphery” spatial pattern with strong path dependence, and central-city polarization dominates over diffusion effects. The proposed model achieves the lowest prediction errors and the smallest training-to-testing performance gap among all compared models, confirming both its accuracy and generalization. Per capita GDP, population density, and urbanization rate are core drivers: per capita GDP has the highest explanatory power but an overall negative effect, while population density and urbanization rate mostly show positive contributions. The SHAP interaction analysis further reveals a pronounced inhibitory coupling between per capita GDP and local fiscal expenditure, wherein their joint high levels compound rather than mitigate ecological pressure. Drivers feature nonlinearity, thresholds, and interactions, and the dominant predictors differ across agglomerations in ways that map onto their distinct structural characteristics. These findings connect urban ecological resilience to the global Sustainable Development Goals agenda and offer transferable lessons for developing countries facing development–conservation tensions, supporting differentiated governance and policy optimization for high-quality and resilient urban development.

Article.Title: Attenuation of self-produced touch in the posterior insula reflects body image disturbances in anorexia nervosa
Article.Authors: Frost-Karlsson M.; Zetterqvist M.; Olausson H.; Boehme R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Body image disturbance (BID) is a core feature of anorexia nervosa (AN), encompassing multimodal distortions in bodily self-perception. Affective touch, a gentle, emotionally salient tactile stimulus, is implicated in body ownership but has not been extensively studied in AN. Affective touch is processed in the insula, an area involved in interoception and bodily self-awareness which has been shown to be altered both structurally and functionally in AN. This study explored the neural mechanisms underlying BID by examining how individuals with AN process self-produced affective touch. Women with AN ( n = 44) and age-matched healthy controls (HC, n = 40), participated in a self-other-object touch task during functional brain imaging and filled out questionnaires related to body image and eating disorder symptomatology. During self-touch, individuals with AN exhibited increased activation in the right posterior insula compared to object-touch, whereas HC did not. This insular activation correlated positively with body attitude (BAT) and body size estimation (FRS) scores in AN, but negatively in healthy controls, suggesting divergent processing of self-related tactile input. These findings suggest that posterior insular responses to self-produced touch may reflect disturbed sensory self-processing in AN, and that touch-based mechanisms contributing to body ownership in healthy individuals may operate differently in the context of AN. Broadening BID research beyond the visual modality opens new avenues for translational research and treatment.

Article.Title: Improving frequency stability in islanded urban microgrids by improved cascaded controller (1+PD-3DOF-FOPID) mobile EV energy storage
Article.Authors: Amiri F.
Article.Abstract: Maintaining frequency stability in islanded urban microgrids (IUMs) in the presence of disturbances from renewable energy sources such as photovoltaics and wind turbine generators, along with parameter uncertainties, constitutes a fundamental challenge. Owing to their inherent intermittency and low inertia, these sources can significantly jeopardize frequency stability in islanded operation. Mobile EV energy storage can play a pivotal role in enhancing frequency stability within IUMs. However, to ensure that such storage effectively contributes to system stability, a robust load frequency control system (LFC) is essential, one that performs reliably under both disturbances and parametric uncertainties. In this paper, a 1 + PD‑3DOF‑FOPID cascaded controller is designed for the LFC system of the IUM. In this structure, the inner (1 + PD) loop is responsible for rapid disturbance rejection, while the outer 3DOF‑FOPID controller handles fine adjustment and steady‑state error elimination. This combination effectively reduces frequency overshoot and undershoot, improves damping of oscillations, and maintains stability even under severe variations in system parameters. The coefficients of the proposed cascade controller are optimally tuned using the Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) algorithm, which offers advantages such as avoiding local minima and achieving fast convergence. To evaluate its performance, the proposed method is compared with several existing approaches, including PD‑3DOF‑PID (COA), 3DOF‑PID (COA), and FOPID. The comparative results indicate that the proposed controller improves overshoot by 30%, undershoot by 54%, and frequency deviation settling time by 66% relative to the other methods. Moreover, the results confirm that the proposed approach exhibits strong robustness against both disturbances and parameter uncertainties, and it significantly enhances the overall frequency stability of the islanded urban microgrid.

Article.Title: Coronary tortuosity as a novel characteristic associated with adverse events in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Article.Authors: Li W.; Ma P.; Huang Y.; Ge Y.; Lin Q.; Wang S.; Gao C.; Yao E.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between coronary tortuosity (CoTo) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and to evaluate its potential prognostic value. A total of 195 patients with HCM and a matched non-HCM cohort were enrolled. The prevalence of CoTo was significantly higher in HCM group than in non-HCM controls (63.6% versus 37.9%, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression demonstrated that HCM was independently associated with a 3-fold increased odds of CoTo (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.97–4.61, P < 0.001). During a mean follow-up of 2.57 ± 1.2 years, HCM patients with CoTo experienced worse primary outcomes than those without CoTo (RR 2.39, 95% CI 1.03–5.54, P = 0.031), and each 1-point increase in the CoTo score was associated with a 51% higher hazard of the primary outcomes (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.27–1.80, P < 0.001). In a subgroup of 62 patients who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance strain analysis, basal global longitudinal displacement (GLD) was significantly lower in the CoTo group (5.11 ± 0.95 versus 5.90 ± 1.20, P = 0.007) and was independently and inversely associated with CoTo (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49–0.97, P = 0.032). In conclusion, patients with HCM are more susceptible to CoTo, which is associated with an elevated risk of adverse events, and CoTo correlates with reduced basal myocardial longitudinal motion.

Article.Title: TDPO: two-stage differentiated prompt optimization for image classification
Article.Authors: He Q.; Zeng Y.; Ye Z.; Xie Q.; Mei M.; Guo J.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Prompt engineering has emerged as an effective paradigm for adapting vision-language models (VLMs) to image classification. Although large language models (LLMs) could generate rich visual descriptions, their hallucination often produces inaccurate or weakly discriminative class-specific prompts. Moreover, existing prompt optimization methods uniformly optimize all classes, overlooking inter-class heterogeneity. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage differentiated prompt optimization (TDPO) that refines prompts from task-specific templates to class-specific descriptions. In the first stage, TDPO optimizes templates via roulette-wheel selection to balance efficiency and diversity. In the second stage, salient classes are sampled via a class group sampling strategy, and prompts are optimized using hybrid breeding optimization algorithm (HBO). This cooperative algorithm assigns class-specific prompts to three evolutionary lines based on inter-class heterogeneity, enabling the efficient discovery of discriminative class-specific prompts while preserving stable prompts for well-performing classes. In the setting of challenging one-shot image classification, extensive experiments on seven image classification datasets demonstrate that the proposed TDPO effectively improves classification accuracy, particularly on the Flowers102 and DTD datasets with gains of 2.9% and 1.7% over the previous state of the art. This work provides a promising direction for prompt optimization in vision-language applications.

Article.Title: Kinetic and thermodynamic study of faba bean hulls pyrolysis with machine learning-based bio-oil modeling
Article.Authors: Abdelmotalib H.; Samee A.; Handawy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for sustainable, low-carbon energy has intensified research into biomass pyrolysis as a promising route for biofuel production. This study provides a comprehensive investigation of the kinetic and thermodynamic behavior of faba bean hulls, an underutilized agricultural byproduct, to evaluate their potential for bio-oil generation. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was conducted at heating rates of 10, 15, and 20 °C/min to determine the kinetic triplet and thermodynamic parameters. A multi-model iso-conversional approach, including Friedman (FR), Flynn–Wall–Ozawa (FWO), Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose (KAS), Starink (STK), and Vyazovkin (VYZ) methods, was applied to enhance the reliability of kinetic evaluation. The activation energy ranged from 143.6 to 194.2 kJ/mol, reflecting the complex multi-step decomposition process, with the Šesták–Berggren model identified as the most suitable reaction mechanism. Thermodynamic analysis revealed average enthalpy (ΔH) values between 142.48 and 182.51 kJ/mol, Gibbs free energy (ΔG) from 127.18 to 128.70 kJ/mol, and entropy (ΔS) from 24.27 to 86.91 J/mol·K, providing detailed insight into the energy requirements, spontaneity, and disorder changes during pyrolysis. Additionally, a machine learning-based predictive framework using Random Forest was developed to model and optimize bio-oil yield. The Random Forest model achieved the highest predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.92), identifying pyrolysis temperature and volatile matter content as the most influential factors. Optimal bio-oil yield was achieved at 500–550 °C. This study establishes an integrated thermo-kinetic and data-driven modeling framework, providing a promising basis for future validation throughout additional feedstocks and larger-scale pyrolysis systems.

Article.Title: Incidence trends and five-year survival of multiple myeloma and other plasma cell neoplasms in Girona, Spain: a population-based study, 1994–2020
Article.Authors: Garrochamba K.; Villavicencio A.; Ameijide A.; Trallero J.; Romaguera A.; Sanvisens A.; Saez M.; Marcos-Gragera R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multiple myeloma is the most common malignant tumor originating in plasma cells. Its incidence varies across populations according to demographic and environmental factors, although its exact etiology remains unclear; reports on survival and advances in treatment are lacking in some geographic areas. The aim of the study was to evaluate the incidence, trends, and survival of multiple myeloma and other plasma cell neoplasms (MM and other PCNs) using data from the Girona Cancer Registry between 1994 and 2020. Incidence trends, observed survival (OS), and net survival (NS) were evaluated using Joinpoint regression, Kaplan–Meier, Cox regression, and the Pohar-Perme method. A total of 1137 cases were identified, with a median age of 72 years [IQR 63.0–79.0]. Incidence trends remained stable in both men and women, with annual percent changes (APCs) of 0.2% [95% CI −1.1; 1.4] and −0.7% [95% CI: −1.9; 0.5], respectively. Median net survival significantly increased from 2.58 to 4.17 years between 1994–2001 and 2010–2016, respectively. Five-year net survival increased from 31.9% [95% CI 24.6–41.3] to 46.5% [95% CI 40.6–53.3] between 1994–2001 and 2010–2016, respectively. Incidence trends remained stable during the study period, whereas myeloma survival improved significantly. The impact of new immunotherapies on future myeloma survival remains promising.

Article.Title: A compact dual – band meander line-based MIMO antenna for intra oral tongue drive system applications
Article.Authors: Mohan A.; Kumar N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a compact dual-band meander line-based multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) antenna developed for intraoral tongue-drive system (iTDS) applications aimed at individuals with significant physical limitations. The antenna facilitates operation in the 1.4 GHz WMTS band and the 2.4 GHz ISM band, ensuring extensive bandwidth and consistent performance in the extremely changeable and detuning-sensitive environment of the human mouth cavity. The suggested structure has compact footprint of $$\:8\:mm\:\times\:\:4.5\:mm\:\times\:\:0.254\:mm$$ , fabricated on a Rogers RO3010 substrate. Miniaturization is accomplished via the integration of a small meander-line radiator, while robust mutual coupling suppression (below − 30 dB) is enabled via an improved fence-strip isolation structure. The antenna has two probe-fed radiating elements that utilize a shared ground plane and are spaced 0.4 mm apart (edge-to-edge), facilitating authentic MIMO functionality for high-data-rate communication. This arrangement mitigates multipath effects and guarantees dependable signal delivery, as shown by link budget and MIMO channel performance studies. Ex vivo assessment with minced pork exhibits outstanding performance, attaining a bandwidth of 528 MHz at 1.4 GHz and 720 MHz at 2.45 GHz, while maintaining isolation below − 40 dB for both frequency bands. Omnidirectional radiation patterns were recorded, exhibiting peak realized gains of − 18.8 dBi at 1.4 GHz and − 17.2 dBi at 2.45 GHz. The examination of specific absorption rate (SAR) and input power further substantiates patient safety. The findings indicate that the suggested dual-band meander-line MIMO antenna offers extensive bandwidth, consistent in-mouth functionality, robust isolation, and dependable high-rate communication, positioning it as a formidable choice for next-generation intraoral tongue-drive system applications.

Article.Title: Photocatalytic degradation of methyl orange under ultraviolet–visible light irradiation using WO3-ZnO nanocomposites synthesized via Saffron petal extract
Article.Authors: Irankhah R.; Balooch A.; Koohestani H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The elimination of organic dyes through photocatalysis is an effective approach for achieving pollution-free environments. WO 3 -ZnO nanocomposites with ZnO:WO 3 weight ratios of 100:0, 80:20, 60:40, 40:60, 20:80, and 0:100, labeled as 100Z, 20WZ, 40WZ, 60WZ, 80WZ, and 100W, respectively, were synthesized through an environmentally green synthesis method. Subsequently, the WO 3 -ZnO nanocomposites were utilized for the photocatalytic degradation of methyl orange (MO) under the irradiation of ultraviolet -visible light. The resultant products were characterized using a comprehensive suite of characterization techniques, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), dynamic light scattering (DLS), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS). The XRD patterns indicated the formation of crystal structures of ZnO, WO 3 , and the WO 3 -ZnO nanocomposites. Based on optical investigations, the direct optical band gaps of 100Z, 20WZ, 40WZ, 60WZ, 80WZ, and 100W were measured to be 3.29, 3.27, 3.09, 3.26, 3.05, and 2.99 eV, respectively. The photocatalytic efficacy of the synthesized nanocomposites was evaluated through the degradation of MO. The obtained results demonstrated that the synergistic effect between WO 3 and ZnO contributes to the enhancement of the charge separation and reduction in the recombination rates of charge carriers, thereby significantly augmenting the photocatalytic efficiency. Notably, the 40WZ nanocomposite exhibited the highest photocatalytic degradation efficiency of MO under UV -vis light irradiation. It was observed that 100% degradation of the MO dye could be achieved by the 40WZ nanocomposite within 15 min of light irradiation.

Article.Title: Enhancing drought stress tolerance in faba bean using phosphate nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Mahdy A.; Abouellail G.; El-Din R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Drought stress is a major environmental constraint that limits the growth, productivity, and metabolic performance of faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) by disrupting nutrient uptake, impairing physiological processes, and inducing oxidative damage. This study investigated the effects of HA-NPs (phosphorus hydroxyapatite nanoparticles) applied through soil and foliar methods on mineral nutrition, biochemical attributes, and antioxidant defense mechanisms of faba bean plants under different drought stress levels. A comprehensive analysis of variance was conducted to evaluate the effects of drought, PHANPs concentrations, and their interactions on nutrient contents (N, P, Na, and K), photosynthetic pigments, protein levels, osmolyte accumulation, and antioxidant enzyme activities. Results showed that drought stress significantly ( P ≤ 0.001) reduced nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, chlorophyll content, and protein levels, while increasing sodium accumulation, proline, soluble sugars, and antioxidant enzyme activities (catalase and peroxidase), indicating severe physiological and oxidative disturbances. In contrast, HA-NPs application significantly improved all measured parameters under both soil and foliar treatments. HA-NPs enhanced nutrient uptake and improved ionic balance by increasing N, P, and K concentrations while reducing Na accumulation, thereby improving plant nutritional status under drought conditions. Additionally, HA-NPs promoted chlorophyll retention, protein synthesis, and osmolyte accumulation, contributing to improved osmotic adjustment and metabolic stability. Moreover, HA-NPs modulated the antioxidant defense system by regulating catalase and peroxidase activities, suggesting reduced oxidative stress and improved ROS homeostasis in treated plants. The interaction between drought stress and HA-NPs was significant for most traits, indicating that HA-NPs effects were more pronounced under higher drought intensity. Although both application methods were effective, soil application generally resulted in more stable and consistent improvements across most parameters. Overall, the study demonstrates that HA-NPs effectively mitigate drought-induced damage in faba bean plants by enhancing nutrient acquisition, strengthening antioxidant defense systems, and improving physiological and biochemical resilience. These findings highlight the potential of HA-NPs as a promising nanobiostimulant for improving drought tolerance and sustaining productivity of faba bean under water-limited conditions.

Article.Title: Comprehensive gait characteristics on electromagnetic stance-control knee ankle foot orthosis in healthy individuals
Article.Authors: Imura T.; Tanabe J.; Taki S.; Iwamoto Y.; Fukuma T.; Iwamoto Y.; Ikeda R.; Kusuda K.; Kurose T.; Kota M.; Tanaka R.; Takahashi M.; Urakawa S.
