Article.Title: A multi-level computational analysis identifies Ocimum basilicum phytochemicals as potent inhibitors of the Marburg virus VP40 matrix protein
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Khan M.; Ahmed M.; Dutta S.; Tapti F.; Tasnim U.; Talukder M.; Rahman M.; Imtiaz M.; Roman M.; Ankhi L.; Al-Forkan M.
Article.Abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is an extremely lethal hemorrhagic fever with no approved antiviral treatment available, which emphasizes the need to develop newer and safer drug candidates. In the current study, we used an in silico approach to identify candidate inhibitors of the Marburg virus matrix protein VP40, which plays a vital role in the viral assembly and budding process using bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum . A homology model of the Marburg virus VP40 protein was built and assessed by Ramachandran, QMEAN, ProSA, Verify3D and ERRAT analysis, and 156 bioactive compounds derived from Ocimum basilicum were then screened against it by molecular docking. Rutin ranked first, with a docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol and hydrogen-bonded and van der Waals contacts to residues of the predicted pocket. A 500 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation indicated a stable VP40-rutin complex, with a backbone RMSD of 1.98 ± 0.19 Å, a mean Cα RMSF of 1.10 ± 0.52 Å, and a compact, well-preserved fold (radius of gyration 19.77 ± 0.15 Å). End-state binding free energies calculated over 51 uniformly sampled trajectory frames were favourable under both solvation models, at -46.08 ± 5.96 kcal/mol (MM/GBSA) and -27.92 ± 7.63 kcal/mol (MM/PBSA), driven primarily by van der Waals and electrostatic contributions. ADMET profiling, however, revealed a substantial pharmacokinetic liability: rutin violates three of Lipinski’s criteria (molecular weight 610.52 g/mol, topological polar surface area 269.43 Å 2 , 10 hydrogen-bond donors and 16 acceptors) and its predicted human intestinal absorption is only 23.45%, so it is best regarded as a lead scaffold requiring structural or formulation optimisation rather than a ready-to-use agent. Validation of the docking protocol against independent molecular dynamics reference poses gave a mixed result. The predicted affinity was reproducible, and the predicted pocket was clearly preferred over decoy boxes placed elsewhere on the protein surface, but pose recovery failed. No top-ranked pose fell within the conventional 2 Å success threshold of the reference pose. Docking was therefore used only as an initial screening filter to rank compounds, and neither the binding geometry nor any mechanism of inhibition is inferred from it. All structural and energetic conclusions reported here rest on the molecular dynamics ensemble and the end-state free-energy analyses. Gas-phase DFT analysis gave a narrow HOMO-LUMO gap (4.13 eV), high softness and a moderate electrophilicity index, which offer supportive electronic evidence of charge-transfer capacity rather than independent confirmation of affinity. Taken together, these findings identify rutin as a natural lead compound against VP40, subject to the pharmacokinetic and docking limitations set out above, and provide a critically validated computational framework for anti-Marburg drug discovery.

Article.Title: Visual functions and neuroretinal status in relation to cognitive functions and fatigue in post-COVID-19: an exploratory study
Article.Authors: Venkataraman A.; Nilsson M.; Möller M.; Stenberg J.; Hedström S.; Borg K.; Gyllenberg A.; Granberg T.; Johansson J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract After a SARS-CoV-2 infection, neurological manifestations may persist as part of long COVID/post COVID-19 condition (PCC). The pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study therefore aimed to investigate visual symptoms, visual and neuroretinal status, and their associations with fatigue and cognitive performance in individuals with PCC. Twenty-three individuals with PCC and nineteen matched controls underwent standardized assessments of visual symptoms and function, neuroretinal structure using optical coherence tomography (OCT), and cognition using a neuropsychological test battery. The PCC group reported higher levels of visual symptoms, general fatigue, and mental fatigue. Visual function was largely preserved, although symptomatic individuals demonstrated reduced performance on vergence facility and developmental eye movement tests. No significant group differences were found in retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) or ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness; however, disrupted correlations between RNFL and GCL were observed in the PCC group. In PCC, lower RNFL was associated with worse executive function (Stroop color-word test) and vergence facility. The findings suggest a dissociation between subjective visual complaints and objective dysfunction, with convergence facility emerging as a potentially sensitive marker. Altered structure-function relationships in OCT metrics may reflect subtle neuroretinal involvement. Visual symptoms and fatigue were prominent in PCC. While overt neuroretinal thinning was not observed, altered correlations and associations with cognitive function underscore the need for further research into neuro-visual mechanisms in post-COVID sequelae.

Article.Title: FactorDGL: factor-driven dynamic graph learning for stock price forecasting
Article.Authors: Jiao X.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Predicting stock price movements is highly challenging due to the noisy, nonlinear, and multi-factor nature of financial markets. Most traditional and deep learning models mainly rely on the observed price sequence, making it difficult for them to capture complex latent temporal patterns associated with short-term fluctuations. These models also struggle to represent higher-order temporal dependencies and often fail to organize different sources of market variation in a structured manner. To address these limitations, we propose FactorDGL: factor-driven dynamic graph learning for stock price forecasting (FactorDGL), a framework designed to progressively learn and refine hierarchical latent representations underlying price movements. FactorDGL uses a temporal hypergraph to represent complex relationships among multiple historical time points and incorporates a cascading residual mechanism to progressively extract latent representations from residual signals that remain after accounting for known influences. In addition, we formulate stock forecasting as a joint price-risk representation learning problem by integrating auxiliary volatility and Sharpe-ratio prediction tasks, which helps the model better adapt to dynamic market regimes and structural shifts. Experiments on MasterCard, Visa, and DJIA datasets indicate that FactorDGL consistently outperforms existing baselines under the evaluated market settings.

Article.Title: Flavonoid-rich Albizia niopoides leaf extract shows anti-Trypanosoma cruzi activity against benznidazole-resistant parasites
Article.Authors: Lima L.; Milagre M.; Reis A.; Pedrosa T.; de Medeiros Teixeira L.; Kohlhoff M.; de Lana M.; Brandão G.
Article.Abstract: Chagas disease affects approximately 6–7 million people worldwide, with current treatments limited by toxicity and parasite resistance. This study evaluated ethanolic extracts from stems and leaves of three Brazilian Cerrado species ( Curatella americana , Nectandra nitidula , and Albizia niopoides ) against the benznidazole-resistant Trypanosoma cruzi Y strain (DTU II) in vitro. Cytotoxicity assessment in Vero cells revealed high toxicity for most extracts, with only A. niopoides leaves showing a favorable therapeutic window (CC 50 > 1600 µg/mL). Against epimastigotes, A. niopoides leaf extract exhibited the highest antiparasitic effect (IC 50 = 150.72 µg/mL) among plant extracts. This extract was selected for intracellular amastigote assays in H9c2 cardiomyocytes, achieving 85.9% inhibition at 400 µg/mL with an IC 50 of 150.72 µg/mL. The selectivity index was > 10.61 in Vero cells and 1.6 in H9c2 cells, remaining below the threshold of ≥ 50 recommended for drug development. UHPLC-MS analysis identified four flavonoids: rutin (50.2% relative abundance), isoquercitrin (7.5%), luteolin-7- O -rutinoside (1.9%), and 7- O -methyl- quercetin (25.3%) as potential chemical markers. These identifications were classified as Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) Level 2 (rutin, isoquercitrin, and luteolin-7- O -rutinoside, confirmed against authentic standards) and Level 3 (7- O -methyl-quercetin, tentative). These findings identify flavonoid glycosides as potential chemical markers in A. niopoides leaves with activity against benznidazole-resistant parasites, providing defined targets for future bioassay-guided fractionation. However, the modest selectivity and lack of isolated compound testing preclude conclusions about therapeutic potential at this stage.

Article.Title: Major microbiota transitions across liver disease progression are mediated by key taxa linking host environments and microbial communities
Article.Authors: Suzuki K.; Kamiya T.; Fujii H.; Takano S.; Yukawa-Muto Y.; Kawada N.; Fukuda S.; Masuya H.; Ohtani N.
Article.Abstract: The gut microbiome plays a critical role in chronic liver disease, yet quantitative methods that integrate microbial community structure with clinical indices remain limited. Here, we applied an energy landscape analysis (ELA)-based framework to characterize transitions in gut microbiota along a clinical gradient of liver disease severity, as measured by the FibroScan-AST (FAST) score. The analysis revealed characteristic community states corresponding to low, intermediate, and high FAST scores, indicating that liver disease progression is associated with structured transitions in microbial community organization rather than simple changes in overall diversity. To further dissect community-level organization, we developed the community shaping index (CSI), which quantifies how strongly individual taxa are associated with specific community structures. Integrating CSI with species–environment association parameters identified key taxa with distinct ecological roles, including unclassified Subdoligranulum taxon, an unclassified Ruminococcus gnavus group taxon, and Streptococcus salivarius , that link host environmental conditions with community composition. Exploratory causal discovery suggested that Streptococcus salivarius and the unclassified Subdoligranulum may play distinct, potentially active roles in linking liver health with gut microbial organization, but with contrasting associations: S. salivarius was linked to disease-related liver deterioration and dysbiotic states, whereas the unclassified Subdoligranulum was associated with healthier liver function and coherent community organization. Overall, this ecologically grounded framework provides a unified and mechanistic foundation for analyzing microbiome structure and disease-associated transitions.

Article.Title: A hierarchical deep learning framework for inter-patient cardiac arrhythmia classification with class imbalance handling
Article.Authors: Ahmadabadi M.; Sadr A.
Article.Abstract: Early detection of arrhythmia can prevent stroke and other cardiovascular complications. However, inter-patient variability in ECG signals makes developing a generalizable and accurate automated diagnostic method challenging. This paper presents an effective hierarchical deep learning framework for inter-patient heartbeat classification by combining convolutional neural network (CNN), autoencoder (AE), RR interval features, residual bidirectional long short-term memory (ResBiLSTM), and multi-head self-attention (MSA) to improve feature representation and classification performance. The proposed framework comprises two stages. In the first stage, VEBs are distinguished from non-VEB beats using a jointly trained morphology-oriented network that combines a simplified ResNet (sResNet) for discriminative feature extraction with an autoencoder for reconstruction-constrained latent representation learning. The second stage classifies supraventricular ectopic beats (SVEBs) and normal (N) beats using a two-step strategy. An RR-based MLP first performs preliminary SVEB screening, while heartbeats initially classified as normal are subsequently evaluated by a verification network that integrates CNN-ResBiLSTM-MSA-based ECG representations with an auxiliary RR feature branch. A bagging-based ensemble strategy has been implemented to address class imbalance by improving the reliability of the minority class. Our proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, namely the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database, SVDB, and INCART. Our model achieves competitive performance on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia database, achieving an overall accuracy of 97.23%. For VEB detection, it attains 97.07% sensitivity and 99.05% specificity, while for SVEB classification, it achieves 93.23% sensitivity and 98.35% specificity. Cross-database evaluation without retraining on the SVDB and INCART datasets demonstrated that the proposed framework retained a reasonable ability to detect SVEB and VEB beats across unseen databases. However, the lower positive predictive value for SVEB, particularly on INCART, indicates that additional efforts are required to reduce false-positive detections and further improve cross-database generalization.

Article.Title: Formula feeding practices and associated factors among neonates in public hospital neonatal intensive care units in Bahir Dar Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Derseh H.; Ambaw M.; Bayih M.; Demilew Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The practice of feeding formula milk to infants less than six months, can significantly increase infant mortality and lead to various diseases. Evidence on formula-feeding practices among neonates admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) in Ethiopia is limited, and community estimates may not describe this clinically vulnerable population. This study aimed to assess formula feeding practices and their associated factors among neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of public hospitals in Bahir Dar City, Northwest Ethiopia, in 2022. We conducted a convergent parallel mixed-methods study from 30 November to 30 December 2022. Quantitatively, 331 mothers of neonates aged 0–28 days were selected using systematic sampling from three public-hospital NICUs. Qualitatively, five mothers from urban areas and five NICU nurses were purposively selected for in-depth and key-informant interviews. Quantitative data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire and analyzed in SPSS version 25 using binary logistic regression. Variables with p < 0.20 in bi-variable analysis were entered into the multivariable model; p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Qualitative data were analyzed inductively using a reflexive thematic approach and integrated with the quantitative findings. Formula feeding practice was reported for 124 of 331 neonates (37.5%; 95% CI 32.0–43.2); 64 (19.4%) were exclusively formula-fed and 60 (18.1%) received both formula and breast milk. In the adjusted model, formula feeding was associated with cesarean delivery (AOR, 4.09; 95% CI 1.47–11.37), no breastfeeding counseling after delivery (AOR, 3.11; 95% CI 1.43–6.76), information about formula milk (AOR, 5.86; 95% CI 2.73–12.56), low versus high knowledge (AOR, 3.00; 95% CI 1.22–7.36), and neutral (AOR, 2.32; 95% CI 1.08–4.96) or positive (AOR, 4.25; 95% CI 1.70–10.60) attitude toward formula feeding. Qualitative findings indicated that insufficient perceived milk, maternal illness or postoperative discomfort, formula availability and promotion, and gaps in facility-based counseling shaped feeding decisions. Formula feeding practice was common in this NICU-admitted sample. The observed associations should be interpreted cautiously, as the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal or causal relationships. Strengthening context-appropriate breastfeeding counseling, particularly after cesarean delivery and when direct breastfeeding is difficult, may help facilities support mothers to provide breast milk when clinically feasible.

Article.Title: Association of lidocaine mucilage administration timing with gastric mucosal visibility and pharyngeal anesthesia during transoral gastrointestinal endoscopy
Article.Authors: Ye S.; Gu Q.; Liu W.; Zhou C.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Lidocaine mucilage is a compound preparation commonly used before gastroscopy to provide topical pharyngeal anesthesia and improve gastric mucosal visibility. However, the optimal interval between administration and endoscopic insertion remains unclear, particularly because excessive shortening of this interval may compromise mucosal visualization, whereas prolonged waiting may affect workflow and patient experience. In this single-center prospective observational study, 317 adult patients undergoing routine upper gastrointestinal endoscopy were evaluated according to the time interval between administration of 7 mL lidocaine mucilage and the start of examination. Gastric mucosal visibility and pharyngeal anesthesia were assessed using predefined scoring systems. The results showed that when the interval exceeded 5 min, gastric mucosal visibility was significantly improved compared with shorter intervals, while no clear additional gain in visibility was observed with further prolongation. Overall pharyngeal anesthesia was adequate, and the incidence of adverse events was low, with only mild events such as cough and retching and no cases of hypoxemia or allergic reaction.

Article.Title: Protocatechuic acid inhibits high shear stress-induced platelet adhesion and aggregation through the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway
Article.Authors: He C.; Ma H.; Zhang T.; Deng S.
Article.Abstract: High shear stress in stenotic arteries triggers platelet activation and aggregation, contributing to atherosclerosis and thrombus formation. Protocatechuic acid (PCA), a polyphenol metabolite, has been reported to inhibit shear-induced platelet aggregation (SIPA), but its precise mechanism remains unclear. We aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which PCA inhibits SIPA via the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. A stenotic microfluidic chip model was used to simulate pathological high shear conditions (10,000 s −1 ). Platelet aggregation and activation were assessed, and the impact of PCA (51.91 μmol/L) on SIPA was evaluated. Flow cytometry was used to quantify platelet surface markers (using P-selectin and PAC-1 as indicators). Platelet morphology was examined via scanning electron microscopy. Platelet aggregation status was observed through electron microscopy. Western blotting was performed to assess PI3K/Akt signaling pathway proteins. PCA inhibited SIPA across the studied concentration range. At 51.91 μmol/L, PCA significantly reduced platelet adhesion and aggregation. Flow cytometry results indicated that PCA significantly inhibited the expression of the platelet activation marker CD62P. Western blot analysis revealed that PCA markedly inhibited PI3K expression and Akt phosphorylation induced by high shear stress. Co-treatment with the PI3K inhibitor TGX221 further enhanced PCA’s inhibitory effect on Akt phosphorylation. PCA suppresses platelet activation and aggregation under high shear stress, likely by inhibiting the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, highlighting its potential as an antiplatelet agent.

Article.Title: Infection prevention and control knowledge, practices and associated factors among healthcare workers in the neonatal intensive care unit in public hospitals, Sidama Regional State, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Haji Y.; Gebretsadik A.; Geleta D.; Jisso M.; Dulla D.; Shiferaw Y.; Spigt M.; de Bont E.
Article.Abstract: Effective infection prevention and control (IPC) practices reduce healthcare associated infections (HAIs) and increase new-born survival rates in resource-constrained settings such as Ethiopia. However, there is a paucity of literature describing the knowledge and practices of healthcare workers (HCWs) regarding IPC, particularly in South Ethiopia. the aim of this study was to determine the levels of IPC knowledge, practices and assess its associated factors within neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and conduct observational assessments of services availability in South Ethiopia hospitals. we conducted a hospital-based, cross-sectional study in Sidama Regional State, South Ethiopia. A total of 126 HCWs employed in public hospitals with NICU services were included in the study. Data were collected using structured, self-administered questionnaires, complemented by standardized observations of the general hospital setup with the specific focus on the NICU environment. Data were recorded using KoboToolbox and subsequently exported to Stata for statistical processing. Bayesian logistic regression was employed to identify factors associated with IPC practices. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with their 95% credible interval (Cr.I) were calculated to assess these associations, with posterior distributions regarded statistically significant if their Cr.I exclude the null value. The mean knowledge score of HCWs regarding IPC was 63.8% (95% CI: 61.70–66.00). Approximately 61% (95% CI: 52.00–70.00) of HCWs demonstrated good IPC practices. Factors significantly associated with adequate IPC practices included receiving formal training (AOR = 9.45, 95% Cr. I: 1.91–37.31), belonging to the nursing profession (AOR = 7.21, 95% Cr. I: 1.88–20.70), and working in primary-level hospitals (AOR = 4.00, 95% Cr. I: 1.11–10.74). This study found moderate levels of IPC knowledge and practices among healthcare workers in the NICUs. Factors statistically associated with good IPC practices included receiving formal training, being a nurse, and the specific tier of the hospital. To improve these outcomes, tailored training should be provided, specifically targeting physicians and staff in tertiary-level hospitals.

Article.Title: A hybrid deep learning algorithm for ECG-based heart disease classification
Article.Authors: Ibrahim S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) classification for heart disease detection encounters significant challenges, such as patient variability, inter-patient differences in heart signals, and data leakage when information from the same patient is present in both training and test sets. To mitigate these challenges, a Hybrid 1D CNN-BiLSTM (one- dimensional convolutional and bidirectional long short-term memory) deep learning framework is introduced, employing rigorous patient-wise validation on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. Patient-wise data splitting (34 records for training, 14 records for testing) ensures that each patient’s data is confined to a single set, effectively preventing data leakage. Under these conditions, the proposed Hybrid with GAN model achieves 91.69% accuracy (95% confidence interval: 91.41−91.99%), with a macro F1-score of 0.547 ± 0.374. Conditional GAN augmentation significantly improves minority class performance: Supraventricular recall increases from 9.2% to 20.9% (+127.2%), and Ventricular recall improves from 77.7% to 80.9% (+4.1%). Statistical significance testing using McNemar’s test demonstrates the superiority of Hybrid with GAN over the non-augmented hybrid model ( $$\chi ^2 = 12.41$$ , p = 0.0004). The observed 7.31% performance gap between beat-wise (99.0%) and patient-wise (91.69%) evaluation highlights the critical importance of patient-wise validation for clinically realistic performance estimates. Overall, this framework provides a rigorous patient-wise evaluation protocol for automated ECG classification, with patient-wise results for a GAN-augmented hybrid model on the full 5-class MIT-BIH dataset.

Article.Title: Antiviral action of different molecules obtained from invertebrates against avian coronavirus
Article.Authors: Mendonça R.; Nascimento R.; Fernandes A.; de Almeida M.; Negri G.; Silva Júnior P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Incidences of emerging/re-emerging deadly viral infections have significantly affected human health. For this reason, the search for new products against these agents has become an urgent need. The bioprospecting for bioactive molecules obtained from invertebrates, or their products, sources of research for new antibiotics and antivirals. Honey and propolis obtained from bees and stingless bees demonstrated antimicrobials, anti-inflammatory, antitumor, healing proprieties and several other functions. However, bioactive have also been obtained from other invertebrates, such as caterpillars and spiders, as demonstrated by our group. In this study, we identified potent antiviral effect against avian coronavirus in propolis from Scaptotrigona aff postica, hemolymph of Lonomia obliqua and from mygalin, isolated from hemocytes of spider Acanthoscurria gomesiana. The antiviral focus reduction assay was carried to evaluate the efficacy of treatment by measuring its ability to inhibit viral replication in cultures of infected cells (TCID) treated with sources of three different invertebrates. The main objective was to evaluate if the compounds can contain the infection, reduce the viral load, preventing that new viral particle from leaving the infected cell to spread the infection. Propolis and crude hemolymph reduced avian coronavirus by an average of 256 x. Fraction purified of propolis and a synthetic peptide from hemolymph (transferrin), reduced the virus titer by an average 64-fold. Reduction of 8-fold was observed when 160 µM of crude mygalin was used. Virus reduction with 26 µM of synthetic mygalin was average of 16 times. The antiviral responses of the three substances were dose dependent. The virus titer reduction was 2 times more intense when the substances were added 1 h before cell infection with the virus.

Article.Title: The future of tanner’s sumac (Rhus coriaria) in a warming world
Article.Authors: Çivğa A.
Article.Abstract: This study applies a MaxEnt-based species distribution modelling framework to characterize the current climatically suitable habitat of Rhus coriaria across Türkiye and to project its potential redistribution under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5) by 2100. A final set of 146 spatially thinned occurrence records and seven environmental variables (annual mean temperature (bio1), roughness index, temperature seasonality (bio4), topographic position index, precipitation seasonality (bio15), annual precipitation (bio12), and maximum temperature of the warmest month (bio5)) were retained following multicollinearity screening. The model demonstrated good predictive performance (mean test AUC = 0.811). Under current conditions, 214,672 km² (32.7% of Türkiye) was identified as climatically suitable. All three future scenarios project an increase in total suitable area at the national scale — reaching 345,063 km² under SSP1-2.6, 316,448 km² under SSP3-7.0, and 276,186 km² under SSP5-8.5 — driven by substantial northward expansion into the Black Sea Region. However, this national-scale gain masks a pronounced contraction of suitable habitat in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions, where the species currently attains its highest abundance and economic importance. These findings provide a spatially explicit, climate-informed evidence base for conservation prioritization and sustainable management planning for this ecologically and economically valuable species.

Article.Title: Unsupervised and semi-supervised fuzzy modularity clustering via multi-view affinity fusion
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Long J.; Zhou E.; Wu M.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, fuzzy modularity clustering has gained widespread attention owing to its alignment with evaluation criteria and learning objective, as well as its robust adaptability to noisy data. However, existing fuzzy modularity clustering methods rely solely on a single distance-based metric to construct the initial affinity graphs, which imposes strong assumptions about the intrinsic data distribution and leads to inferior clustering performance in real-world applications. To address this limitation, this study introduces the concept of the multi-view affinity graph, which is free from the constraints of any single metric. We further employ an affinity fusion technique to integrate initial graphs from multiple views, allowing the combined graph to simultaneously reflect the characteristics of diverse metrics. Subsequently, the notion of fuzzy modularity is adopted to formulate the learning objective, and a novel clustering method called Fuzzy Modularity Clustering via Multi-view Affinity Fusion (FMC-MAF) is proposed. Moreover, the semi-supervised learning variant, sFMC-MAF, is also developed to effectively utilize labeled samples while introducing only one additional hyperparameter and maintaining the optimization framework. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of both the proposed FMC-MAF and sFMC-MAF.

Article.Title: Grouting reinforcement mechanisms and their significance in controlling surrounding rock deformation of tunnels passing through fault zones
Article.Authors: Yan B.; Lv X.; Qiao C.; Zhao J.; Pang T.; Bian W.
Article.Abstract: The stability of tunnel surrounding rock in deep-mine fault fracture zones is poor, significantly affecting safe and efficient mining operations. Thus, exploring the deformation and failure mechanisms of tunnel surrounding rock and researching reinforcement measures for tunnels passing through fault zones are important. This study analyzed rock specimens' deformation and failure mechanisms with varying joint angles and penetration rates. Subsequently, it investigated the strengthening effects of different joint-filling materials on the mechanical properties of jointed rock specimens and their impacts on failure modes. Through numerical simulation, a rock-mass model with a fault fracture zone was constructed to explore the diffusion law of grouting slurry in tunnel surrounding rock and evaluate the grouting reinforcement effect. Additionally, grouting reinforcement and water-blocking measures for the surrounding rock of tunnels in deep-mining fault-fracture-zone areas were studied. The main innovative contributions of this study are as follows: the coupled effects of joint dip angle, penetration rate, and filling material type on the strength and failure modes of jointed rock specimens were systematically revealed, clarifying the control mechanism of filling-body bond performance on crack propagation paths at joint tips; a grouting diffusion–stress coupling model for fault fracture zones was established by introducing the time-dependent viscosity of Bingham fluid into the modified Darcy's law, quantifying the spatiotemporal evolution of slurry density at different distances from grouting holes; a field-scale "water-release-then-grouting" sequential treatment technology was proposed for high-pressure and high-flow water-inrush channels in the Sanshandao Gold Mine, and the optimization suggestions for grouting parameters were verified by field applications. The research findings offer theoretical and technical guidance for preventing and controlling rock instability and water-seepage inflow in surrounding rock.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of free and encapsulated Ziziphus jujuba extract in functional beverages using alginate and alginate-soy protein isolate beads
Article.Authors: Khoshdouni Farahani Z.; Ebrahimzadeh Mousavi M.; Utra U.; Mohammadi Nafchi A.
Article.Abstract: The use of encapsulation and biopolymer-based carriers provides an efficient strategy to develop functional beverage systems by improving the physical stability of bioactive constituents. In this study, beads for beverage formulation were prepared by encapsulation with alginate-based carriers and subsequently coated with soy protein isolate (SPI). Three beverage formulations were produced and evaluated, including a free-extract beverage (free extract), an alginate-bead encapsulated beverage (ALG beads), and an alginate/SPI bead encapsulated beverage (ALG/SPI beads). The pH, acidity, Brix, viscosity, and physical stability parameters were assessed during 14 days. The pH and acidity variations were attributed to the gradual release of small amounts of encapsulated extract components, which influenced the beverage’s equilibrium. With respect to viscosity (ALG: 48.7 cp. ± 0.50 and ALG/SPI: 45.6 ± 0.30 cp.) and related stability, the encapsulated systems exhibited greater resistance to phase changes than the free-extract beverage (60.7 ± 0.50 cp.). Notably, neither sedimentation nor visible phase separation was observed in any formulation, and complete suspension behavior was maintained throughout the storage period, indicating satisfactory gravitational and colloidal stability. Moreover, the beverage containing ALG/SPI beads exhibited superior physical stability. This enhancement is attributed to the formation of a reinforced composite network within the beads, where the interaction between alginate and SPI increases the mechanical strength of the capsules. This structural reinforcement minimizes bead deformation and aggregation, allowing the encapsulated system to maintain better dispersion and resistance to sedimentation within the beverage matrix. Overall, the results demonstrate that the alginate/SPI coating strategy improves the stability of the functional beverage, offering a promising carrier system for maintaining quality attributes during storage.

Article.Title: A unified framework for the systematic detection of non-canonical proteins in standard proteomics workflows using a Ribo-seq informed transcriptomic language model
Article.Authors: Provencher N.; Leblanc S.; Jacques J.; Roucou X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) has revealed widespread translation of non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs), integrating this information into routine mass spectrometry (MS) workflows remains challenging due to biochemical constraints and large search databases. We retrained TIS Transformer, a transcriptomic language model, by incorporating 40,397 Ribo-seq-derived non-canonical translation initiation sites, thereby enabling the prediction of 48,265 ncORFs, including non-AUG starts, with only a minor impact on canonical protein detection. We combined these predictions with Swiss-Prot sequences to create Swiss-Prot/ncProt, a size-controlled database suitable for standard proteomic analysis. Reanalysis of three independent MS datasets using this database maintained over 98% concordance with Swiss-Prot searches, identifying 541 non-canonical proteins, 429 of which had orthogonal evidence of their existence. This unified framework facilitates systematic detection of non-canonical proteins in conventional proteomics workflows, bridging the gap between canonical and non-canonical proteome analyses without requiring specialized experimental protocols.

Article.Title: Multi-domain feature fusion and machine learning-based SFRA diagnosis of transformer winding faults using a novel fault deviation index
Article.Authors: Keleş C.; Mamiş M.; Arkan M.; Köseoğlu M.; Yalçınöz Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) is one of the commonly used techniques for evaluating transformer winding integrity. However, the interpretation of the SFRA results remains qualitative and depends on expert evaluation. In this study, a quantitative, measurement-oriented diagnostic framework based on the advanced normalized Multi-Domain Fault Deviation Index (MFDI) is proposed. Within this method, magnitude, phase, impedance, and resonance-based descriptors are integrated in a unified formulation. The proposed method combines frequency band decomposition with multi-domain feature fusion to capture both local and global spectral deviations. This framework is experimentally validated under both intra-phase (U–N) and inter-phase (V–W) fault scenarios using SFRA measurements. The results demonstrate that the proposed MFDI captures the obvious difference between healthy and faulty states. For intra-phase fault scenarios, the proposed method provides quantitative differentiation among the investigated fault conditions despite the high similarity of their corresponding spectral signatures. In contrast, inter-phase faults generate more pronounced global spectral deviations, leading to highly separable feature representations for Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) classifiers. These findings demonstrate that the proposed approach advances SFRA from a predominantly qualitative interpretation technique toward a quantitative, interpretable, and machine-learning-compatible diagnostic methodology suitable for intelligent transformer condition monitoring.

Article.Title: The impact of wildfire smoke on acute cardiovascular and respiratory illness in the US
Article.Authors: Hughes F.; Parsons L.; Alhanti B.; Simon J.; Kasibhatla P.; Shindell D.; Ohnuma T.; Ragunathan K.; Montgonery H.; Krishnamoorthy V.
Article.Abstract: Escalating wildfire frequency increases population exposure to wildfire smoke. To evaluate the association between wildfire-specific particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) and acute health impacts a retrospective cohort study was conducted utilizing National COVID Cohort Collaborative health records from 109,012 patients across 58 US health systems from 2020 to 2021. County-level wildfire-specific PM 2.5 concentrations were estimated using a fire emissions database and chemical transport modeling. Generalized linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the association between weekly county-level wildfire-specific PM 2.5 exposure (up to 50 µg/m³) and hospital encounters for a series of cardiac, pulmonary, obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Statistically significant increases in weekly encounters per county of residence were observed for every 10 µg/m³ rise in weekly maximum wildfire-specific PM 2.5 for acute myocardial infarction (0.084, 95% CI, 0.023–0.146), cardiac arrest (0.011, 95% CI, 0.001–0.021), heart failure (0.083, 95% CI, 0.024–0.142), atrial fibrillation (0.115, 95% CI, 0.014–0.216), COPD exacerbation (0.034, 95% CI, 0.001–0.066) and pulmonary embolism (0.048, 95% CI, 0.003–0.094). COVID infection status was not found to have a modifying effect on these relationships. There was no significant increase in COVID pneumonia admissions in response to increasing wildfire smoke. These findings demonstrate quantifiable increases in acute cardiorespiratory morbidity associated with wildfire smoke exposure.

Article.Title: Multifunctional investigation of a chalcone derivative: nonlinear optical properties, and potent antifungal activity
Article.Authors: Koppal V.; Hebasur R.; Patil N.; Gummagol N.; Yaraguppi D.; Kusanur R.; Nivedhitha K.; Banapurmath N.; Badruddin I.; Abdul Khader S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The nonlinear optical (NLO) and antifungal properties of 3-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-1-phenylprop-2-en-1-one (3DPPP) were investigated through a combined experimental and computational approach. UV–Vis spectroscopy revealed an optical band gap of 2.88 eV and a cut-off wavelength of 421 nm, consistent with TD-DFT predicted HOMO–LUMO gap of 4.03 eV. Z-scan measurements confirmed third-order NLO behavior with significant reverse saturable absorption and an optical-limiting threshold of 1.33 kJ/cm². Computational studies provided insight into molecular geometry, electronic transitions, global reactivity parameters, and molecular electrostatic potential. The molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations against the ‘Candida albicans’ target protein (PDB: 4M80) revealed stable binding (-8.4 kcal/mol) supported by hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. Corresponding in vitro assays confirmed notable antifungal activity, comparable to itraconazole. These results position 3DPPP as a promising multifunctional candidate for photonic device applications and as an antifungal therapeutic.

Article.Title: Microplastics ingestion and mouthpart morphology in common coastal marine peracarids (Arthropoda, Crustacea)
Article.Authors: Dobrzycka-Krahel A.; Pladzyk A.; D’Aleo S.; Martino C.; Iaciofano D.; Lo Brutto S.
Article.Abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is a significant threat due to its widespread presence, hidden diffusion through ingestion by organisms, and entry into edible species. In this study, MPs were assessed in the digestive canal of peracarid crustaceans. The amphipod Gammarus insensibilis , G. subtypicus , Parhyale plumicornis , Orchestia montagui , Speziorchestia stephenseni and the isopod Ligia italica were collected in the central Mediterranean Sea and analysed to search for the relationship between mouthparts’ morphology and MPs ingestion in marine coastal environments. The specimens showed a comparable average total length (12 mm) and a similar trophic behaviour, i.e., phyto-detritophagous. The highest MP prevalence was found in the hyalid P. plumicornis (51.5% of the individuals). The second highest, the talitrid Speziorchestia stephenseni , had MPs in 40% of the individuals. In contrast, gammarid G. insensibilis and G. subtypicus had respectively 8.3% and 3.5% of the total individuals containing MPs. The results may suggest that the hyalid and the talitrid amphipod species store increased levels of MPs in coastal marine environments, as these species show morphological functional traits susceptible to ingestion of MPs, i.e. the absence of a mandibular palp, and the reduction of the maxilla-1 palp in either size and articulation.

Article.Title: Binding and toxicological insights into Direct Yellow 8 and bovine serum albumin: fluorescence quenching and cytotoxicity studies
Article.Authors: Bisht B.; Sangeeta N/A.; Dey P.; Kujur P.; Singh A.; Mehata M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial dyes are ubiquitous in nature, making it essential to assess their toxicological effects on humans and animals. Azo dyes, due to their structural composition (azo linkages), are resistant to biodegradation. Direct Yellow 8 (DY8), a monoazo industrial dye, may exhibit carcinogenic properties; therefore, it is imperative to extensively explore its effects on biomolecules. In this study, for the first time to the best of our knowledge, we elucidate the binding interaction between DY8 and bovine serum albumin (BSA) using multi spectroscopic techniques. Changes in the secondary structure of BSA were assessed using circular dichroism (CD). Fluorescence (FL) intensity of BSA was quenched upon interacting with DY8. Moreover, the lifetime of BSA is nearly constant in the presence of DY8. The change in the absorption spectrum, along with the constant FL lifetime in the presence of DY8, ensures the dominant static quenching. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed a stable binding configuration with minimal fluctuation. Furthermore, the effect of DY8 in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells has also been discussed.

Article.Title: Design and implementation of a multilingual chatbot for global fashion E-commerce CX using the RASA machine learning framework
Article.Authors: Suryawanshi S.; Gohil J.
Article.Abstract: The increasing globalization of markets necessitates robust multilingual customer service solutions to meet diverse consumer linguistic preferences. Traditional customer service systems, often constrained by language barriers, limited availability, and scalability issues, are insufficient to meet the demands of a globalized customer base. This paper presents the design and implementation of a multilingual chatbot leveraging the open-source RASA machine learning framework to address these challenges. The proposed architecture integrates a language detection module, a multilingual Natural Language Understanding (NLU) pipeline, a sophisticated Core Dialogue Manager, and an Action Server capable of dynamic response translation. The chatbot supports three languages: English, Devanagari Hindi, and Hinglish, using a custom-built multilingual dataset comprising 1350 utterances manually annotated, 450 utterances for each of the three supported languages. The dataset comprises 11 customer-service intents , with the three language-specific intents represented by a larger number of training examples than the supporting conversational intents, reflecting the primary objective of multilingual language identification and routing. The dataset was divided into training and testing sets using an 80:20 split. Evaluation metrics, including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score for intent classification, demonstrate strong performance across all three languages. The proposed RASA-based system outperforms a non-multilingual RASA baseline and a Translate-to-English pipeline, while achieving competitive performance relative to the standalone fine-tuned XLM-R model, with additional advantages in end-to-end dialogue management, deployment flexibility, and data privacy. However, the Hinglish component requires further development. User testing results, encompassing Customer Satisfaction (CSAT), average resolution time, and overall satisfaction rates, further validate the system’s practical utility. Key outcomes highlight RASA’s flexibility in adapting to diverse linguistic requirements and its potential to significantly enhance global customer support by providing instant, culturally sensitive, and cost-effective AI assistance. The findings underscore the importance of robust NLU and a hybrid approach to translation for maintaining semantic consistency across languages, while also identifying critical research gaps in domain-specific multilingual corpora, particularly for code-switched varieties such as Hinglish.

Article.Title: First principles investigation of NO2 and NH3 adsorption on a two-dimensional CrTe monolayer with environmental interference from H2O, CO2 and N2
Article.Authors: Sengar S.; Gupta D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The adsorption behaviour of NO 2 , NH 3 , H 2 O, CO 2 , and N 2 molecules on a two-dimensional CrTe monolayer was systematically investigated using spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the adsorption mechanism and adsorption induced modifications in its electronic and magnetic properties. Dispersion interactions were explicitly considered using the PBE-D3(BJ) approach. The structural stability, adsorption characteristics, charge transfer, electronic structure, magnetic response, and thermal stability were analysed through optimized adsorption geometries, adsorption energy calculations, charge density difference (CDD) analysis, Mulliken population analysis, density of states (DOS), projected density of states (PDOS), spin-polarized band structures, phonon calculations, and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. The calculated adsorption energies reveal that all investigated gas molecules interact favourably with the CrTe surface. NO 2 exhibits the strongest adsorption at the hollow (4-fold) site with an adsorption energy of -2.91 eV, followed by H₂O with -2.08 eV, NH₃ with -1.92 eV, CO₂ with -1.27 eV, and N₂ with -1.23 eV. Charge density difference and Mulliken population analyses demonstrate pronounced interfacial charge redistribution for NO₂ adsorption, resulting in significant modifications of the electronic and magnetic properties, whereas the other gas molecules induce comparatively weaker perturbations. DOS, PDOS, and spin-polarized band structure analyses further confirm stronger electronic coupling and adsorption induced electronic perturbations for NO 2 . Phonon and AIMD simulations confirm the dynamical and thermal stability of the CrTe monolayer. These findings provide comprehensive insight into molecule surface interactions and indicate that the CrTe monolayer is a promising platform for selective NO 2 adsorption, providing a theoretical basis for future gas-sensing studies.

Article.Title: Antitumor potential of teriflunomide alone and in combination with vitamin D3 and tamoxifen in DMBA-induced breast cancer in BALB/c mice
Article.Authors: Dahi W.; Aljamali M.; Al laham S.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer represents a predominant malignancy which is a critical healthcare concern globally. To date, the antitumor potential of teriflunomide (Ter) in murine breast cancer models remains unexplored. Thus, the present research aimed to evaluate the potential antineoplastic efficacy of Ter in combating this fatal malignancy, alone or in combination with vitamin D 3 (Vit. D 3 ) and tamoxifen (Tam) against mammary carcinogenesis in a BALB/c mouse model induced by 7,12 dimethylbenz[a]anthracene (DMBA). BALB/c mice were divided into six groups including 7 mice each; (i) Control, (ii) DMBA, (iii) DMBA + Vit. D 3 , (iv) DMBA + Tam, (v) DMBA + Ter, and (vi) DMBA + Ter + Vit. D 3 + Tam. Results revealed that DMBA administration caused tumors with invasive ductal carcinoma of grade II and III, with a significant increase in the total microscopic score. Also, DMBA caused an increase in lipid peroxidation and a decrease in cellular antioxidants, catalase and superoxide dismutase. This was accompanied with substantial increase in expression of mutant P53. Administration of Ter individually or in combination with Vit. D 3 and Tam attenuated the development of DMBA-induced mammary tumors, and minimized the associated tissue damage, with the combination therapy demonstrating the most pronounced therapeutic impact. Our in vivo data suggest that Ter holds therapeutic potential as a promising anti-cancer candidate against breast cancer either alone or in combination with Vit. D 3 and Tam.

Article.Title: Strategies for enhancing alkaline stress tolerance in strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa cv. Sabrina) using zinc oxide nanoparticles and plant biostimulants
Article.Authors: Danaeifar A.; Khaleghi E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa ) is a globally cultivated fruit crop valued for its nutritional quality and short production cycle. However, alkaline stress caused by high soil pH and sodium carbonate/bicarbonate accumulation significantly impairs plant growth, photosynthesis, and nutrient uptake. This study aimed to enhance alkaline stress tolerance in Sabrina strawberry using zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) and plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). A factorial experiment based on a completely randomized design with three replicates was conducted, including two pH levels (6.5 and 8.0), three ZnO NPs concentrations (0, 100, and 200 mg L⁻¹), and Bacillus velezensis inoculation treatments. Results showed that alkaline stress (pH 8.0) significantly reduced shoot and root biomass, photosynthetic rate, water use efficiency, and pigment content. However, the combined application of ZnO NPs and B. velezensis alleviated the adverse effects of alkalinity. Under alkaline conditions (pH 8.0), 200 mg L⁻¹ ZnO NPs and B. velezensis inoculation significantly improved morphological traits, increased Relative Water Content (RWC), gas exchange parameters while reducing Electrolyte Leakage (EL). This treatment led to a 14.92% enhance in RWC, a 47.43% increase in photosynthetic rate, a 44.44% rise in carotenoid content and a 4.8% decrease in EL compared with the control treatment (pH 8.0, 0 mg L⁻¹ ZnO NP and without bacterial inoculation). The highest levels of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) (51.29 µmol L⁻¹) and malondialdehyde (MDA) (135.00 µmol g − 1 f.w) were observed at pH 8.0 in the absence of nanoparticles and bacteria. Conversely, the addition of ZnO NPs and B. velezensis significantly reduced both H₂O₂ and MDA levels under alkaline stress. At pH 8.0, the combined application of bacteria and ZnO resulted in a significant increase in osmotic protectant content (proline, starch) and antioxidant enzyme activity (peroxidase, superoxide dismutase). Under alkaline stress, the highest activities of peroxidase (POD) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) were recorded in plants treated with 100 and 200 mg L⁻¹ ZnO-NPs, respectively, in combination with B. velezensis inoculation. In addition, the maximum enzymatic activities for CAT and APX were achieved at 200 and 100 mg L⁻¹ ZnO NPs, respectively, in the absence of bacterial inoculation. These results suggest that ZnO nanoparticles and B. velezensis may enhance antioxidant defenses and improve tolerance to alkaline stress.

Article.Title: Enhanced hippopotamus optimization for attention-gated lightweight spatio-temporal boxing sports recognition
Article.Authors: Luo H.
Article.Abstract: Accurate boxing sports recognition is the core foundation of intelligent combat training, action standardization evaluation, and competitive match tactical analysis. Existing methods still face critical challenges: insufficient fine-grained feature extraction for high-speed non-rigid boxing motions, weak robustness to occlusion, motion blur and complex backgrounds, unstable performance caused by manual hyperparameter tuning, and the difficulty in balancing lightweight deployment and recognition accuracy. Meanwhile, the original Hippopotamus Optimization (HO) algorithm 1 suffers from insufficient population diversity, poor exploration-exploitation balance, and premature convergence in high-dimensional neural network hyperparameter optimization. To address these issues, this paper proposes an integrated boxing sports recognition framework named Enhanced Hippopotamus Optimization optimized Attention Gated Depthwise Separable Convolution Spatio-Temporal Network (EHO-AGDSC-STN). The contribution lies in a systematic engineering integration of established lightweight components with three targeted algorithmic enhancements to the HO optimizer. First, an AGDSC-STN backbone is designed, which integrates depthwise separable convolution units, spatio-temporal attention gating, anti-motion blur convolution, and occlusion-aware enhancement, to improve fine-grained feature extraction while ensuring model lightweight and inference efficiency. Second, a Key Frame-guided Bidirectional Spatio-Temporal Feature Fusion Pyramid (KF-BSTFP) and a multi-task collaborative decision head are constructed to realize end-to-end “detection–pose estimation–action classification” inference. Third, an Enhanced Hippopotamus Optimization (EHO) algorithm is proposed for end-to-end automatic hyperparameter optimization, which adopts Sobol–Tent chaotic initialization, adaptive nonlinear convergence factor, and hybrid mutation strategy to alleviate the inherent defects of the original HO. Experiments on two public professional boxing datasets show that the proposed method achieves 95.7% and 94.9% recognition accuracy on the BoxingVI Dataset and Olympic Boxing Punch Classification Dataset, respectively, outperforming all mainstream comparison methods. We further report standard deviations across 10 independent runs, robustness evaluations under controlled blur and occlusion, parameter/FLOP analysis, optimizer sensitivity analysis, and cross-backbone validation of EHO. The proposed framework provides an efficient, robust, and lightweight technical solution for intelligent boxing sports recognition.

Article.Title: Enhancing filler for elastomeric compositions based on sunflower husk carbonizates
Article.Authors: Kaiaidarova A.; Bobrova V.; Kasperovich A.; Lezhnev S.; Panin E.; Nechipurenko S.; Efremov S.; Burkitbayev M.
Article.Abstract: The growing interest in plant-based materials has contributed to the development of elastomer compositions containing biomass as a new component for rubbers. Materials obtained by carbonization of sunflower husks at various temperatures (from 400 to 800 °C) and processing media (argon and oxidative) were used in a model rubber mixture based on butadiene‑nitrile rubber of special purpose BNKS-18AMN at various dosages (5.0; 10.0 and 15.0 phr). The purpose of this study was to evaluate how the temperature and pyrolysis medium, as well as the dosage of biomass, affect the technological, physical-mechanical and structural properties of vulcanizates. Mechanical properties, including conditional tensile strength, relative elongation at break and Shore A hardness, were determined. The density of cross-linking of rubbers was determined by the equilibrium swelling method. The studied materials had a significant effect on the rheological and physical-mechanical properties: biomaterials obtained in both inert and oxidative media led to an increase in the Mooney viscosity and density of cross-linking of rubbers with an increase in the dosage, and also increased the rigidity of the system, thereby leading to an increase in strength and Shore A hardness compared to the model unfilled composition. The maximum values of physical-mechanical indicators were possessed by rubbers containing sunflower husk carbonizates obtained in an inert medium at 700 and 800 °C. At the same time, a decrease in the resistance of rubber mixtures to premature sub-vulcanization was determined, especially when using material obtained in an oxidative medium, due to the high amount of metal impurities acting as additional activators of vulcanization and an increase in the time to reach the vulcanization optimum due to the adsorption of vulcanizing system components on the surface of biomaterials. The study also examined the effect of elevated temperatures and air oxygen on vulcanizates, which allowed to obtain insights into the changes in the elastic-strength properties of elastomer compositions with biomaterials under conditions simulating aging.

Article.Title: Integration of lipid metabolism and clinical features for discriminating recurrent patellar dislocation using interpretable machine learning
Article.Authors: Dong C.; Hao K.; Wang F.; Wang J.; Wang J.; Zheng R.; Kang H.
Article.Abstract: Recurrent patellar dislocation is a common condition in active adolescents, yet current diagnostic approaches mainly rely on imaging assessments, limiting their accessibility for early screening. This study aimed to develop an explainable ensemble machine learning framework that integrated lipid metabolic factors and clinical variables to discriminate recurrent patellar dislocation patients from healthy individuals. We retrospectively analyzed data from 260 patients with recurrent patellar dislocation and 547 controls, incorporating demographic characteristics and routine blood lipid profiles (total cholesterol, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein, low-density lipoprotein, very low-density lipoprotein, apolipoprotein A1, apolipoprotein B, lipoprotein(a), and apolipoprotein A1/apolipoprotein B ratio). A two-layer ensemble learning structure was implemented, consisting of ten base classifiers (Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Adaptive Boosting, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, CatBoost, Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, and K-Nearest Neighbors) and a logistic regression meta-classifier. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were used to interpret the outputs of the model and identify the features that contributed most to the discrimination of recurrent patellar dislocation. The explainable two-layer ensemble machine learning model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.82 and average precision of 0.71 in discriminating recurrent patellar dislocation. SHAP analyses consistently identified age, gender, low-density lipoprotein, very low-density lipoprotein, and lipoprotein(a) as key discriminatory features. Age and low-density lipoprotein exhibited significant non-linear interactions, with elevated low-density lipoprotein amplifying the discriminatory signal in adolescents. A strong, non-linear relationship was observed between low-density lipoprotein and apolipoprotein B. The ensemble model showed good calibration and favorable clinical net benefit. In conclusion, blood lipid metabolic factors, particularly low-density lipoprotein, very low-density lipoprotein, and lipoprotein(a), combined with age and gender, enabled successful discrimination of recurrent patellar dislocation via an explainable ensemble machine learning framework.

Article.Title: Dihydroartemisinin overcomes cisplatin resistance in bladder cancer via suppression of the PI3K/AKT/ABCB1 signaling Axis
Article.Authors: Qiao X.; Li J.; Li S.; Xu R.; Ji C.; Jiang R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cisplatin resistance substantially limits the efficacy of bladder cancer chemotherapy, and effective strategies to overcome resistance remain insufficient. In this study, we demonstrate that dihydroartemisinin (DHA) restores cisplatin sensitivity in resistant bladder cancer cells by suppressing the PI3K/AKT/ABCB1 signaling axis. A cisplatin-resistant 5637&Cis cell line was established from parental 5637 cells and exhibited stable resistance, with an IC₅₀ of 15.41 µg/mL compared with 2.85 µg/mL in parental cells. DHA at 10 µg/mL showed limited intrinsic cytotoxicity but enhanced cisplatin sensitivity in a time-dependent manner, producing reversal folds of 1.19, 2.07, and 5.14 at 24, 48, and 72 h, respectively, and promoting apoptosis. Integrated bioinformatics analysis identified PI3K/AKT signaling as a key enriched pathway and ABCB1, AKT1, and STAT3 as resistance-related hub genes. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable binding between DHA and ABCB1. DHA downregulated ABCB1 expression, inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, increased intracellular Rhodamine 123 accumulation, and reduced P-glycoprotein-mediated efflux. These effects were attenuated by 740 Y-P and mimicked by PKI-402. In xenograft models, DHA inhibited tumor growth by 60.54% without apparent systemic toxicity and promoted the expression of apoptotic markers. These findings suggest that DHA may serve as a low-toxicity chemosensitizer for cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer and warrant further validation in additional models and combination-treatment studies.

Article.Title: Dual-scale undulation characterisation and modelling of sedimentary bauxite deposits
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Huang B.; Zhao X.; Wu Z.; Li B.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sedimentary bauxite deposits exhibit both regional-scale orebody undulations and irregular local ore–rock interfaces, which cannot be adequately represented using models constructed solely from borehole data. Taking the Aojiawan II bauxite mine in Lüliang, Shanxi Province, China, as a case study, this study proposes a dual-scale method for characterising and modelling orebody undulations using borehole data and roadway-exposure data. An ore-seam undulation coefficient is introduced to quantify the dispersion of the ore seam relative to its macro-scale trend surface, while a local interface undulation coefficient is used to describe the relative dispersion of the roof and floor interfaces. Scale-sensitivity analysis is conducted to determine an appropriate macro-scale evaluation grid. A dual-scale orebody model is then constructed by superimposing local stochastic residual fields derived from roadway-exposure data onto the macro-scale trend generated from borehole data. The results show that a 50 m × 50 m evaluation grid provides a suitable balance between data support and spatial resolution. The classification thresholds for macro-scale undulation are 24% and 26%, while the local interface undulation coefficient ranges from 23.66% to 46.78%, indicating marked spatial variations in interface geometry. Across the four independent validation profiles, the dual-scale mean model reduced the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and maximum absolute error (MaxAE) by 41.02%–76.26%, 33.47%–72.30%, and 28.11%–40.93%, respectively, relative to the macro-scale trend model. The model integrates regional ore-seam geometry with local ore–rock interface undulations and may provide a refined geometric basis for subsequent ore–rock boundary delineation and stope-layout assessment.

Article.Title: A task-adapted structurally reparameterized diverse-branch YOLO network for mulberry leaf disease detection
Article.Authors: Haider N.; Alam K.; Paik J.
Article.Abstract: Mulberry leaf diseases reduce leaf yield and quality, with direct consequences for sericulture. Detecting symptoms in field imagery is challenging because lesions are often small and visually similar across disease types. In this study, a task-adapted YOLOv10-based detector is proposed that integrates a modified diverse-branch feature extraction module (C2fDBN) and maintains efficient inference through structural reparameterization. The detection target is defined as the whole-leaf category rather than individual lesion spots to align with practical classification requirements. Experiments were conducted on an in-house field-collected mulberry leaf dataset and an independent public dataset, both annotated for healthy leaves and disease classes. On both datasets, the proposed detector achieves competitive performance and frequently surpasses or attains performance comparable to strong object detection baselines (YOLOv8, YOLOv9, YOLOv10, YOLOv11, YOLOv26, RT-DETR, Faster R-CNN) in terms of mAP, while maintaining a comparable inference-efficiency profile. These results indicate that the proposed model can support leaf-level field scouting and agricultural decision-making within the evaluated datasets.

Article.Title: Predicting ecosystem services values using land use land cover and climate change scenarios in Maze National Park and its surroundings, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Wana D.; Simeon M.; Woldu Z.
Article.Abstract: Land-use and land-cover and climate change are significant environmental factors affecting ecosystems and the services they provide. Their impacts are evident, and continued changes are expected to significantly affect future ecosystem services. Therefore, this study predicts the values of ecosystem services under land-use and land-cover and climate change scenarios in Maze National Park and its environs, Ethiopia. The 1985, 1995, and 2020 land-use and land-cover maps used for predictions were obtained from our previous studies, while projected temperature and precipitation data were obtained from the WorldClim database. A multilayer perceptron neural network was used to predict land-use and land-cover changes under business-as-usual and governance scenarios for 2050. Climate change predictions were based on General Circulation Models under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways 2-4.5 and 5-8.5. The Spearman correlation was employed to analyze the impacts of predicted climate change on ecosystem services. The results indicate that under the business-as-usual scenario, food production is projected to rise slightly (+ 2.3%), whereas water supply (-7.61%), raw materials (-6.72%), and climate regulation (-5.57%) services are expected to decline. In contrast, the governance scenario forecasts substantial gains in food production (+ 10.94%), water supply (+ 22.26%), raw materials (+ 19.93%), and climate regulation (+ 17.07%) services in 2050. Compared to historical data, both climate scenarios predict higher minimum and maximum temperatures and lower rainfall in the future. The predicted increases in temperature, along with declines in rainfall under both emission scenarios, are expected to negatively affect the provision of key ecosystem services. This highlights the critical need to integrate future climate and land-use and land-cover change predictions into regional planning and development policies.

Article.Title: Distinct immune inflammatory markers and proteomic signatures underlying psoriasis with pruritus
Article.Authors: Choi M.; Kim J.; Jung J.; Park S.; Yu J.; Kim K.; Song Y.; Chang S.
Article.Abstract: Pruritus is a common and burdensome symptom in patients with psoriasis, yet its underlying systemic mechanisms are not sufficiently defined. To characterize systemic immune-inflammatory profiles and serum proteomic differences associated with pruritus in patients with psoriasis and identify potential biomarkers linked to pruritus. Serum immune-inflammatory markers from 267 psoriasis patients were analyzed. Proteomic profiling was performed by mass spectrometry in pruritic psoriasis ( n = 8), non-pruritic psoriasis ( n = 5), and healthy controls ( n = 3). Pruritic psoriasis patients tended to be younger with shorter disease duration, while other clinical characteristics were comparable. Total IgE tended to be higher in pruritic psoriasis, particularly in moderate-to-severe cases. The eosinophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (ELR) was significantly elevated in pruritic psoriasis, whereas other inflammatory indices did not differ. Proteomic analysis revealed distinct clustering of pruritic psoriasis from non-pruritic psoriasis and healthy controls, with enrichment of complement activation, coagulation, and fibrinolysis. Compared with non-pruritic psoriasis, pruritic psoriasis additionally showed upregulation of actin cytoskeletal organization, wound healing proteins, and transient receptor potential melastatin 2 (TRPM2). Pruritic psoriasis is characterized by elevated ELR and distinct proteomic signatures involving complement activation, coagulation, tissue remodeling, and TRPM2 upregulation, implicating these pathways in the mechanisms underlying psoriatic pruritus.

Article.Title: Field-validated climate-resilient HVAC control for mixed-use buildings in a hot-arid region
Article.Authors: Alsulami M.; Gnaba H.; Elhassan Z.; Andiye Y.
Article.Abstract: Buildings in desert cities are difficult to operate efficiently because heat waves and airborne dust increase cooling demand, alter short-term thermal behavior, and reduce HVAC efficiency. This study develops and field-validates an adaptive control framework for mixed residential and commercial buildings in a hot-arid climate. The framework integrates a continuously calibrated digital twin, a heterogeneous spatiotemporal graph neural network for short-horizon thermal and load prediction, and decentralized multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. The control architecture uses Proximal Policy Optimization and a shared graph embedding to update HVAC setpoints. Its comfort constraints align with ASHRAE Standard 55 and the high-performance building objectives of ASHRAE Standard 189.1. The framework was evaluated for 18 months in eight occupied buildings in Hail, Saudi Arabia: six residential units and two small commercial facilities. The evaluation included periods with outdoor temperatures above 45 °C and 48 recorded dust-storm events. Compared with conventional thermostat operation, the controller reduced electricity use by 37.8% and maintained the ASHRAE PMV comfort band during 93.5% of occupied hours. Energy savings were 36.5% in residential buildings and 41.8% in commercial buildings. During dust events, anticipatory control increased these savings to 44.2% and 46.8%, respectively. The framework also outperformed model predictive control and a local DRL baseline without graph-based coordination. Transfer learning reduced commercial training time by 38% and computational demand by 56%. Separate community-scale simulations based on the calibrated digital twin projected 41.2% energy savings and a 43.8% peak-load reduction for 150 buildings; these values were not obtained from an additional field deployment. The field results show that climate-specific AI control can improve energy efficiency and operational resilience in cooling-dominated buildings under severe desert conditions. Validation in larger and more diverse building portfolios is still required.

Article.Title: Generative synthesis of high-fidelity pathological brain MRI via label-conditioned latent diffusion
Article.Authors: del Castillo M.; Alfano F.; Mazón M.; García R.; Fontecha D.; Fernández-Miranda P.
Article.Abstract: The synthesis of high-fidelity brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is essential for addressing data scarcity and privacy constraints in medical research. In this study, we present a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) for conditional MRI generation, operating in a compressed latent space to optimize computational efficiency while preserving anatomical integrity. The model is conditioned on both pathology (Healthy, Glioblastoma, Sclerosis, and Dementia) and acquisition modality (T1-weighted, T1ce, T2-weighted, FLAIR, and Proton Density). Trained on a diverse cohort of 1477 subjects from six public repositories, the framework learns disentangled representations of pathological features and imaging contrasts. To ensure methodological rigor, we comprehensively evaluated the framework across structural fidelity, latent disentanglement, and clinical utility. Quantitative analysis utilizing Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) with domain-specific MedicalNet features and Multi-Scale Structural Similarity (MS-SSIM) indicates that the synthetic images statistically align with real-world biological variance. This structural coherence is further validated by Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) for structural similarity, while deterministic label-swap experiments quantitatively support the meaningful disentanglement of the learned conditions. Furthermore, a blinded evaluation by expert radiologists confirmed that the synthetic volumes exhibit high perceptual realism, with quality scores comparable to real diagnostic scans. Crucially, the model demonstrates effective zero-shot extrapolation capabilities, successfully synthesizing anatomically plausible scans for combinations of pathology and modality that were completely absent from the training set. The functional utility of these extrapolated volumes is validated through a downstream 3D pathology classification task, where synthetic augmentation significantly stabilized decision boundaries and improved minority-class performance. By disentangling latent representations of anatomy, pathology, and modality, our approach facilitates scalable cross-condition data generation while reducing patient privacy risks, as no individual anatomy or source image is referenced during the inference phase.

Article.Title: Preoperative sleep quality as a predictor of postoperative pain, function, and recovery after total knee arthroplasty: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Durmaz M.; Koçak A.; Gündüz E.; Odabaşı E.; Eravşar E.; Aydın B.
Article.Abstract: Sleep quality is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of surgical recovery; however, evidence regarding its longitudinal relationship with postoperative recovery outcomes after total knee arthroplasty remains limited. Poor preoperative sleep may impair postoperative pain control, mobility, and functional independence. Therefore, this study examined the effect of preoperative sleep quality on postoperative sleep, pain, range of motion, and activities of daily living in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty. A prospective cohort study was conducted with 70 patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty at a university hospital between February 2023 and December 2024. Data were collected at three time points preoperatively, and at 30 and 90 days postoperatively using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Visual Analog Scale, goniometric range of motion measurement, and the Modified Barthel Index. Statistical analyses included Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, correlation analyses, and multiple regression models. Preoperative sleep quality significantly predicted postoperative sleep quality (β = 0.970, p < 0.001) and pain intensity (β = 0.091, p = 0.046). Poor sleep quality was negatively correlated with range of motion and activities of daily living at 90 days postoperatively. Preoperative sleep quality plays a meaningful prognostic role in postoperative recovery following total knee arthroplasty. Integrating routine sleep assessment and sleep-focused nursing interventions into perioperative care may optimize recovery trajectories, improve pain control, and enhance functional independence. Nurses should incorporate sleep quality screening into preoperative evaluations and implement integrated sleep–pain management strategies to support holistic recovery and potentially improve postoperative rehabilitation outcomes.

Article.Title: Shift in streamflow seasonality and regime due to precipitation variability in a snow-influenced mountainous watershed
Article.Authors: Nabavi S.; Mirzaei Hassanlu A.; Mostafazadeh R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In mountainous regions, water availability and flood hazards are tightly linked to the timing and seasonality of streamflow, making their analysis indispensable for sustainable resource planning. In this regard, this study examines changes in seasonality and precipitation in the Khiav Chai River watershed, a snow-influenced mountainous region in northwest Iran, over the 1970–2022 period, using Innovative Trend Analysis (ITA), Pettitt change-point detection, and circular statistical analysis. Contrasting results were observed in relation to the hydro-climatic variables studied in the research period. While annual precipitation followed an upward trend (ITA slope = 0.022), the streamflow data indicated a decreasing trend (ITA slope = -0.00093). The Pettitt test found that statistically significant changes occurred in 1984 and 1995 in streamflow and precipitation, respectively, implying that changes in the hydrological regime occurred prior to changes in precipitation. According to the circular statistics, the Center of Mass Timing showed only a minor difference between precipitation and streamflow (precipitation: 5.09 months; streamflow: 4.45 months) between these two hydro-climatic variables over time. On the contrary, seasonality index showed opposite directions. Decreasing seasonality was observed in precipitation (τ=-0.23, p = 0.01) implying an even distribution of rainfall throughout the year, while increasing seasonality was observed in streamflow (τ = 0.34, p < 0.001) indicating a higher amount of streamflow occurring at specific periods during the hydrological year. Based on polar vector analysis, clustering and seasonal concentration were significantly more pronounced in streamflow than precipitation, showing the effect of snow accumulation and melt processes in watersheds. The results indicate a growing trend of separation between the seasonality of precipitation and streamflow, implying the non-stationarity of the hydrological regime within the watershed. This study demonstrates that precipitation and streamflow seasonality can decouple in snow-influenced watersheds, where snow dynamics mediate hydrological responses to climate change. These results suggest that the effects on the hydrological system cannot be solely attributed to modifications in precipitation patterns and that seasonal flow adjustments should be taken into account for adaptation purposes.

Article.Title: Integrative analysis and external validation identify a novel seven-gene signature for preeclampsia risk stratification
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Miao L.
Article.Abstract: Placental transcriptomic alterations play a critical role in the pathophysiology of preeclampsia (PE), yet robust gene signatures for risk stratification remain underexplored. We first integrated four GEO datasets (GSE75010, GSE25906, GSE24129, and GSE10588). Using the GSE75010 dataset as the training cohort, we applied LASSO regression and SVM algorithms to screen and identify seven key genes. A risk stratification model for PE was then constructed based on these seven genes. The model’s performance was validated in the other three independent GEO datasets.
