By integrating full moment tensor solutions, Savage–Wood radiation efficiency, pore-pressure diffusion modelling, and global migration-scaling relationships, our results suggest a mechanically partitioned rupture behaviour, whereby events exhibiting positive isotropic components (up to ~ 40%) preferentially occur within the central portion of a high-attenuation fluid-rich domain, whereas high-radiation-efficiency earthquakes preferentially localize along its boundary. The swarm exhibits consistent empirical scaling trends: migration velocity scales as V ∝ T − 0.69 and cumulative moment as M₀ ∝ T⁰·⁷⁶, consistent with the fluid-induced domain of global compilations and implying a reciprocal balance between spatial expansion and energy release. Despite this anomalous kinematics, near self-similar moment-length scaling and stress drops of ~ 1 MPa confirm that fault strength remains typical of tectonic earthquakes. These results provide qualitative scaling indicators for distinguishing fluid-modulated swarms from purely tectonic sequences and highlight the role of aseismic slip and fluid overpressure in shaping seismic hazard in active fault systems.

Article.Title: Bioinformatic analysis, gene expression, and in silico characterization of the transcription factor MYB1 in sweet orange (Citrus sinensis)
Article.Authors: Salehi Sardoei A.; Mazarei A.; Fazeli-Nasab B.; Asgharipour M.
Article.Abstract: The diverse MYB transcription factor family regulates key plant processes, including pigment biosynthesis and critical abiotic stress responses such as cold tolerance. This study aims to characterize the MYB1 protein and analyze its expression in citrus species subjected to low-temperature stress. One-year-old grafted seedlings of four citrus cultivars on sour orange rootstock were subjected to controlled freeze stress in a factorial, completely randomized design. Temperatures were gradually decreased to + 4 °C (control), − 4 °C, and − 8 °C for 10 h, with root zones insulated. Following a 24-hour recovery at + 4 °C, leaf samples were collected. Anthocyanin content was quantified spectrophotometrically from acidified methanol extracts. Total RNA was extracted from frozen leaf powder, treated with DNase I, and reverse-transcribed into cDNA. Gene-specific primers for MYB1 and the EF1 reference gene were designed using Oligo7 software. Quantitative PCR was performed using SYBR Green master mix. Gene expression was calculated via the ΔΔCt method, and data were analyzed by ANOVA and Duncan’s test ( p < 0.05). ANOVA revealed a highly significant interaction between temperature and cultivar for all traits. Anthocyanin content increased with declining temperature in a genotype-dependent manner, peaking in Thomson Navel orange at − 8 °C. MYB1 gene expression was significantly upregulated by cold stress, with the highest induction in Thomson Navel orange (36.25-fold at − 8 °C). Bioinformatic analysis characterized the MYB1 gene, its promoter containing stress-responsive elements, and predicted the protein’s structure, which was validated as acceptable by Ramachandran plot analysis. Cold stress significantly induces MYB1 expression and anthocyanin accumulation in citrus, with strong genotype-specific variation.

Article.Title: Experimental and numerical failure analysis of SLJ and SSLJ CFRP joints using the LaRC05 criterion within a combined XFEM-CZM
Article.Authors: Boubenia A.; Houari A.; Chellil A.; Tablit B.; Amroune S.; Hakizimana E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, we present an experimental and numerical analysis of single-stepped-lap joint (SSLJ) and single-lap joint (SLJ) assemblies made from carbon/epoxy composites (CFRP). The study aims to evaluate the impact of joint geometry and substrate thickness (2.0 mm and 4.0 mm) on the mechanical behavior and structural integrity of the joints. CFRP composite plates were machined using CNC milling and then bonded using a structural epoxy adhesive before being subjected to tensile testing. A three-dimensional finite-element model in Abaqus, incorporating cohesive zone modeling (CZM) for the adhesive and the LaRC05 criterion coupled with the extended finite element method (XFEM) for the composite substrate, was developed. The numerical predictions show very good agreement with the experimental data. The results show that the stepped joint (SSLJ) consistently outperforms the conventional SLJ joint, increasing the ultimate load at failure by 11.15% for a thickness of 2.0 mm (reaching 7,584 N compared to 6,823 N for the SLJ). This improvement is due to better alignment of the load line and a reduction in the secondary bending moment (Goland and Reissner effect). Conversely, increasing the substrate thickness from 2.0 mm to 4.0 mm results in a gradual reduction in ultimate strength for both configurations (a decrease of 4.13% for the stepped joint and 6.36% for the SLJ). Although a thicker substrate increases the overall flexural stiffness of the plate outside the joint, the increased eccentricity of the load accentuates the local out-of-plane bending moment and intensifies the combined stresses at the ends of the adhesive joint. The LaRC05/XFEM model accurately captured the transition from cohesive failure of the adhesive to localized delamination of the substrate. This work demonstrates that the stepped configuration, combined with an optimal substrate thickness of 2.0 mm, offers the best mechanical performance.

Article.Title: High-speed directional eddy-current smart sensor with VDA 5.1–compliant uncertainty analysis
Article.Authors: Mussatayev M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-speed in-line (up to 1 m s −1 ) Non-Destructive Testing requires measurement systems whose uncertainty is traceable under realistic operating conditions. In this study, the uncertainty of a directional Eddy Current Testing (ECT) sensor is quantified in accordance with Verband der Automobilindustrie (VDA) 5.1 for two defect-severity metrics: voltage-based and phase-based signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). Ten inspection speeds (0.1–1.0 m s −1 ) were investigated with ten repeated scans per speed, enabling an ANOVA-based decomposition of Type A components and a systematic evaluation of Type B contributions. Both channels exhibited a statistically significant speed dependence of comparable magnitude (between-speed (speed-effect) variance component $$u_{\textrm{AV}}\approx 1.43$$ –1.44 SNR units), while voltage-based SNR retained the lower repeatability uncertainty ( $$u_{\textrm{EV}}=1.03$$ versus 1.41 SNR units for phase). Combining Type A and Type B components yields expanded uncertainties of $$U_{\textrm{MP}}={}$$ 3.5155 (voltage) and $$U_{\textrm{MP}}={}$$ 4.0364 (phase), corresponding to minimum permissible tolerances of 7.0311 and 8.0729 SNR units, respectively. These results demonstrate that voltage-based SNR provides the most metrologically robust characteristic for downstream machine-learning analysis and establish a traceable VDA 5.1 framework for uncertainty quantification in high-speed EC inspections.

Article.Title: Microscopy-based classification reduces overdiagnosis of acute vulvovaginal candidiasis relative to culture alone in pregnant women
Article.Authors: Jonani B.; Betty N.; Enock S.; Kwizera R.; Bongomin F.; Mboowa G.
Article.Abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is commonly diagnosed using fungal culture, which cannot distinguish colonisation from infection. This study evaluated discordance between culture and a microscopy-based definition of acute VVC, assessed microscopy performance against culture, and MALDI-ToF species identification. We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of microscopy and culture data from 154 vaginal swab specimens from symptomatic pregnant women in Uganda, recruited between March and June 2023. A five-category microscopy-based definition informed by BASHH 2019 guidelines was applied. We calculated sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) using culture as the reference method. Agreement between microscopy phenotype and MALDI-ToF species identification was assessed using Cohen’s kappa. Culture was positive in 103/154 (66.9%) women, whereas microscopy identified 44 (28.6%) as likely Candida albicans infection and 16 (10.4%) as possible non- albicans infection. Based on microscopy, 45.6% of culture-positive cases lacked evidence of active infection (95% CI 35.9–55.7%). Microscopy showed sensitivity of 54.4% (95% CI 44.2–64.2%), specificity of 92.2% (81.1–97.8%), PPV of 93.3% (83.8–98.2%), and NPV of 50.0% (39.5–60.5%). Culture-positive but microscopy-negative cases had significantly lower colony counts ( p = 0.006). All participants were symptomatic, with no difference in symptom burden across microscopy categories ( p = 0.284). Agreement between microscopy phenotype and MALDI-ToF species identification was moderate (κ = 0.454, p < 0.001). Microscopy-based classification reduces apparent overestimation of VVC associated with culture alone while demonstrating high specificity and PPV. Prioritizing microscopy with selective culture may improve diagnostic precision and support antifungal stewardship in low-resource antenatal settings, although this approach requires prospective validation.

Article.Title: Stratification of salivary sIgA variability identified by time-series feature clustering
Article.Authors: Akiyama Y.; Shiga T.; Minagawa H.; Fujita T.; Shiratori I.
Article.Abstract: Salivary secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) is a biomarker of mucosal immunity, but its day-to-day variability hampers interpretation of single-timepoint measurements. We sampled saliva daily from 46 healthy adults for 56 consecutive days, extracted 23 time-series features per trajectory and retained twelve for clustering. Clustering of component scores gave three groups: Stable-balanced ( n = 26; intermediate levels, low variability), High-variable ( n = 7; high concentrations, large fluctuations) and Low-unstable ( n = 13; lowest concentrations, greatest variance instability). Neither the gap statistic nor a parametric bootstrap null supported three natural clusters (silhouette 0.283, P = 0.246); we therefore present an exploratory stratification. Mean level and variability drifted little between the two halves in 18/25 (72.0%, 95% CI 52.4–85.7), 5/7 (71.4%, 35.9–91.8) and 4/13 participants (30.8%, 12.7–57.6) respectively, intervals that overlap widely. Individual-level prediction was poor; the residual component held 75–85% of the variance (an upper bound). Cough was most frequent in the Low-unstable group (5/13, 38.5%, 17.7–64.5, versus 3/26 and 0/7), but this exploratory association was not significant ( P = 0.072). A single measurement therefore cannot separate an individual’s level from day-to-day fluctuation: characterising salivary sIgA requires repeated sampling over weeks, for which this stratification is a starting point.

Article.Title: Clinically staged prediction of paediatric dental non-cooperation: temporal validation and model interpretation
Article.Authors: Yu J.; Xie L.; Sun S.; Zhang F.; Zheng X.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: This retrospective model-development and same-centre temporal-validation study evaluated staged prediction of paediatric dental non-cooperation in 1120 unique children. The development period comprised 577 training and 248 internal-selection children; 295 later children formed a non-overlapping temporal-validation dataset. Five information scenarios represented basic triage (S1), child behavioural vulnerability (S2), caregiver-family context (S3), full pre-treatment information (S4), and a focused peri-visit set (S5). Non-cooperation occurred in 35.4% (397/1120). Temporal ROC AUCs for S1–S5 were 0.700 (95% CI 0.637–0.764), 0.824 (0.774–0.869), 0.856 (0.807–0.897), 0.905 (0.867–0.937), and 0.857 (0.812–0.897), respectively. S4 achieved PR-AUC 0.864 and Brier score 0.119; S5 had lower paired temporal discrimination than S4 (ΔROC AUC − 0.049, 95% CI − 0.080 to − 0.018). S4 had approximately seven training events per encoded feature, indicating limited information relative to model complexity. The study quantified predictive performance and decision-analytic value. Multicentre external validation and prospective implementation studies are required to establish robustness and clinical effectiveness before routine use.

Article.Title: MRI-based radiomics model for predicting symptomatic hemorrhage in cerebral cavernous malformations: a two-center study
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Liu Y.; Hu J.; Zheng Y.; Li C.; Zhuo L.; Wang H.; Mou H.; Zhuang W.; Kang Y.; Huang W.; Wang L.; Lin X.; Ma K.; Wang D.; Lin Y.; Wang S.; Lin F.; Kang D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predicting hemorrhage in cerebral cavernous malformations (CCM) supports clinical decisions by preventing the risk of fatal or disabling outcomes. This study developed models to predict symptomatic hemorrhage using radiomics features. A total of 153 non-hemorrhagic lesions from the TOUCH cohort (NCT03467295) were analyzed for model development and 54 lesions from the CRESS cohort (NCT04076449) for external validation, with lesions classified as hemorrhagic or stable based on 3-year follow-up. Clinical variables were screened via univariate analysis, and radiomics features from T1- and T2-weighted MRI were selected through LASSO regression. Multivariate logistic regression was used to build three models: clinical, radiomics, and an integrated model combining both. The integrated model demonstrated superior predictive performance, achieving AUCs of 0.860 (training), 0.976 (internal validation), and 0.980 (external validation). Decision curve and calibration analyses confirmed its clinical utility and robustness. This integrated model effectively stratifies hemorrhage risk in this study and shows potential as a supporting tool to inform clinical decision-making in CCM, pending further prospective validation.

Article.Title: Attention-guided multi-view video fusion for real-time sports injury risk assessment
Article.Authors: Siyuan L.; Yunan Q.; Jiaze L.; Jiuzhi B.
Article.Abstract: Sports injuries impose significant burdens on athletes and healthcare systems, yet current assessment methods lack real-time intervention capabilities. This study presents an attention-guided multi-view video fusion framework that enables real-time injury risk evaluation during athletic training. The system employs cross-view attention mechanisms to adaptively integrate information from multiple camera perspectives, coupled with temporal attention modules to maintain assessment stability across movement sequences. We constructed a comprehensive dataset comprising 11,206 movement samples from 156 athletes across four sports disciplines. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 85.7% classification accuracy and a mean absolute error of 6.83 in continuous risk scoring, representing 28.4% improvement over single-view baselines. With an average processing latency of 87 milliseconds, the system meets real-time deployment requirements while maintaining strong agreement (Pearson correlation of 0.79) with expert clinical assessments. Field validation across three sports facilities confirmed practical feasibility for proactive injury prevention through immediate corrective feedback during training sessions.

Article.Title: Physics informed muon scattering tomography with momentum integration for nonintrusive monitoring of microreactor cores
Article.Authors: Ughade R.; Chatzidakis S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Next-generation microreactors enable remote deployment and semi-autonomous operation, but compact, sealed, heterogeneous cores limit conventional safeguard approaches that rely on access and bulk accountancy. Limited inspection access and complex internal geometry reduce sensitivity to localized anomalies such as missing fuel. Here we demonstrate missing-fuel detection in microreactor scale geometries using muon scattering tomography under realistic cosmic-ray conditions. We introduce $$\mu$$ TRec, a physics-informed framework that reconstructs event-level curved muon trajectories by combining a Gaussian multiple Coulomb scattering model with Bayesian updating, then maps scattering density through voxel wise M-values for core integrity verification. We evaluate a representative hexagonal core containing 61 fuel flakes with embedded control drums and shutdown rods, using both idealized 5 GeV muons and zenith-angle-dependent 0-60 GeV cosmic-ray spectra. A single missing fuel flake is detected with $$3\times 10^6$$ muons at 50 mm voxel resolution. Incorporating per-muon momentum further improves detectability, with gains of up to 2.4 times for laser-driven sources and 2.3 times for cosmic-ray sources relative to momentum-agnostic reconstruction. The method remains robust under practical detector limitations, showing only an 8.88% reduction in detectability for 10 mm spatial resolution combined with 10% energy resolution. Compared with PoCA, $$\mu$$ TRec achieves up to 4.8 times higher detectability at equal muon counts, supporting faster and more reliable defect identification.

Article.Title: Vision-based human pose estimation for intelligent sports training and teaching assistance
Article.Authors: Li P.; Lu L.; Zheng T.; Xue Z.; Lu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vision-based human pose estimation can support intelligent sports training and teaching, but fast motion, motion blur, occlusion, background interference, and computational constraints remain challenging in practical scenarios. This study proposes a sports-oriented framework integrating motion deblurring, target tracking, and a lightweight high-resolution pose estimator termed GSANet. GSANet redesigns HRNet using Ghost modules, Sandglass structures, Coordinate Attention, and unbiased data processing to reduce computational complexity while retaining high-resolution spatial representation. COCO and MPII are used as the principal benchmarks, while a small supplementary sports-oriented set, SGDN, is used to examine the influence of motion blur and preprocessing-based deblurring. GSANet substantially reduces model parameters and computational complexity relative to the reported HRNet-W32 configuration without ImageNet pre-training, although its absolute pose-estimation accuracy is lower. On SGDN, preprocessing-based deblurring produces a modest but statistically supported improvement in PCKh. Overall, the results support GSANet as an efficiency-oriented alternative under the evaluated settings rather than as a universally more accurate or deployment-ready pose estimator.

Article.Title: Efficiency of activated and nano activated carbon catalyzed ozonation for inactivation of antibiotic resistant bacteria and abatement of resistance genes in hospital wastewater
Article.Authors: Dehghanzadeh R.; Baghal Asghari F.; Shanehbandi D.; Mahvi A.; Yaghmaeian K.; Oskoei V.; Dehghani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a leading global health threat, and hospital wastewater is a critical hotspot for its emergence and dissemination. Hospital wastewater is a major reservoir for antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARBs) like Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and their resistance genes (ARGs). We assessed ARB/ARG removal via catalytic ozonation (CATO) enhanced with AC or NAC (20–60 mg L −1 ) in 24-h hospital wastewater composites. Sterilized samples were spiked to 10 6 or 10 8 CFU mL −1 . Ozone (22 mg L −1 at 0.2 L min −1 ) delivered TOD of 11–45 mg L −1 . ARB viability was assessed by selective plating; ARGs ( sul1 , bla CTX-M , bla TEM , bla VIM , qnrS ) and the 16S rRNA reference gene by PMA-qPCR. Statistics (R): one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons, Kruskal–Wallis with Dunn's post-hoc and Bonferroni correction, paired and independent two-sample t-tests; significance set at p < 0.05. Bacterial inactivation was significantly TOD dependent at 10 8 CFU mL −1 , with 40 mg L −1 NAC optimal at TOD = 45 mg L −1 , whereas no catalyst effect was detected at 10 6 CFU mL −1 . ARG abatement ( sul1 , bla CTX-M , bla TEM ) was greatest at higher TOD and 60 mg L −1 NAC, while bla VIM remained comparatively resistant. E. coli and A. baumannii showed generally greater ARG reduction than P. aeruginosa . SEM indicated preliminary NAC stability after single cycle ozonation. Under the tested high load batch conditions, the process reduced culturable ARB counts and viable cell associated ARG loads, while bla VIM in P. aeruginosa remained the most recalcitrant carbapenem resistance marker. These findings indicate that NAC assisted ozonation may improve treatment performance in hospital effluents; however, because the study was conducted in a sterilized, spiked batch matrix and did not include catalyst-only or non-ozonated blank controls, validation in continuous-flow systems treating native hospital wastewater and across multiple catalyst-reuse cycles is required before operational deployment.

Article.Title: Plasma level of soluble urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor as a prognostic marker of disease severity in Streptococcus dysgalactiae subspecies equisimilis bacteremia
Article.Authors: Saukkosaari M.; Aittoniemi J.; Huttunen R.; Seiskari T.; Junttila I.; Luukkaala T.; Rantala S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Streptococcus dysgalactiae subspecies equisimilis (SDSE) causes severe bacteremic infections. Elevated soluble urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR) has been studied as a biomarker in several infectious conditions. We evaluated the association between suPAR levels, clinical characteristics and disease severity in SDSE bacteremia. Adult patients with a positive blood culture for SDSE in two hospitals in Tampere, Finland, between 11/2015 and 11/2019 were prospectively studied. Severe disease ( N = 15) was defined as intensive care unit treatment ( n = 10) and/or death ( n = 7). Plasma suPAR levels were quantified in 293 samples from 153 patients. The median of the first suPAR concentrations was 4.81 ng/mL. SuPAR concentrations were significantly higher in severe disease compared with non-severe disease (medians 8.03 ng/mL vs. 4.54 ng/mL). Patients with underlying chronic liver (10.7 ng/mL), cardiovascular (5.80 ng/mL) or kidney disease (6.89 ng/mL), and those with alcohol abuse (7.54 ng/mL) had elevated suPAR levels compared to those without such condition. Elevated suPAR levels were associated with pneumonia (6.15 ng/mL) and abscesses (7.43 ng/mL). High suPAR levels correlate with severe disease in SDSE bacteremia patients. SuPAR measurement could support early risk assessment and management of SDSE bacteremia patients.

Article.Title: Nonlinear associations between the built environment and urban vitality in Anyang using multi-source data and explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Zhang K.; Xu Q.; Wei Q.; Bao J.
Article.Abstract: As China’s urban development shifts from spatial expansion toward quality-oriented renewal, scientific planning has become increasingly important for small and medium-sized cities. Taking the main urban area of Anyang, China, as a case study, this study developed an integrated framework to assess urban vitality and explore its associations with the built environment. A four-dimensional vitality index covering economic, social, cultural, and ecological dimensions was constructed. Four regression models were compared, and SHAP was employed to interpret feature importance, nonlinear relationships, thresholds, and interactions. Results showed that urban vitality was concentrated in the eastern core area, with local clusters in the west and a gradual decline toward the periphery. XGBoost achieved the best performance. SHAP analysis revealed that distance to the nearest commercial center was the most influential factor, followed by POI mix degree, health service accessibility, general POI density, and building height. Interaction analysis indicated that vitality was shaped by the combined effects of functional diversity, development intensity, facility accessibility, and transport connectivity. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated urban functions and provide insights for differentiated renewal strategies in small and medium-sized cities.

Article.Title: Development and cross national external validation of a model for incident depressive symptoms in adults aged 50 years or older
Article.Authors: Wang G.; Zhang H.; Ren S.; Chen L.; Wang L.; Ye L.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Depressive symptoms in older adults coexist with chronic disease and functional limitations, yet cross-national longitudinal prediction remains limited. We developed and externally validated a model to estimate the 4-year risk of screening-defined incident depressive symptoms in adults aged 50 years or older. The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) was used for development and internal validation, and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) for external validation. Nine approaches were compared using repeated nested cross-validation with multiple imputation. The cohorts included 5,816, 11,337, and 5,818 participants, respectively, with 4-year event proportions of 36.1%, 21.2%, and 19.8%. Among the nine candidate approaches, logistic regression was selected for the final model, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) of 0.675 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.661–0.689) in internal validation. External ROC AUCs were 0.728 (95% CI, 0.717–0.739) in HRS and 0.745 (95% CI, 0.730–0.761) in ELSA. Brier scores were 0.1505 and 0.1399, and observed-to-expected event ratios were 0.814 and 0.844, respectively. A web-based risk calculator was developed. The model showed moderate external discrimination but overestimated absolute risk. Local recalibration and prospective impact evaluation are needed before individual risk assessment in new populations.

Article.Title: Profiling essential oils from leaf extract of Azadirachta indica inducing apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells and evaluating systems biology for drug discovery
Article.Authors: Soofiyan J.; Rahimi M.; Mohkami Z.; Ranjbary A.; Bidarnamani F.; Yamchi A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to assess cellular toxicity and to determine apoptosis-associated expression changes in adjacent colorectal cancer (HT-29) cell cultures treated with Azadirachta indica essential oil (AIEO). It also aimed to elucidate molecular targets and mechanisms of action in colorectal cancer (CRC) using network pharmacology and in silico approaches. Essential oil was extracted from AIEO leaves, and GC–MS was used to identify its components. Cell viability of treated HT-29 cancer cells was assessed using the MTT assay. Based on the essential oil’s toxicity, 5 and 10 μg/mL were used to treat HT-29 cells, and apoptosis was monitored by flow cytometry. The effect of the AIEO on HT-29 cell proliferation was evaluated using the reactive oxygen species (ROS) and BrdU assays. Expression of apoptosis-related mRNA and proteins was analyzed by qPCR and Western blotting. From GC–MS analysis, the seven most abundant phytochemicals were evaluated for drug-likeness and ADMET properties. Their anticancer targets and mechanisms were then investigated using network pharmacology and molecular docking. Primary apoptosis was 24.3 and 41.8% when the HT-29 cells were incubated for 24 h with 5 and 10 μg/mL of the essential oil, respectively. BrdU and ROS assays showed a significant inhibitory effect of AIEO on HT-29 cell proliferation. The expression of Caspase 3 and 9, as well as Bax, increased in the treatment group compared with the control group, whereas BCL-2 expression decreased significantly. Network pharmacology identified 135 overlapping gene targets between AIEO and CRC. Cathepsin D, STAT3, HSP90AA1, and NFKB1 were consistently among the top 10 hub proteins interacting with AIEO in CRC networks and were therefore selected for molecular docking with the seven AIEO compounds. Docking results showed that, among the seven compounds and four reference inhibitors, phytol produced the highest docking score for binding to the four oncoproteins.

Article.Title: Microstructure and performance of hot-pressed aluminum matrix nanocomposites
Article.Authors: Yehia H.; Daoush W.; Allam S.; Hoziefa W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Al-10 wt% Cu-10 wt% Ni matrix composites reinforced with 0, 10, 15, 20, and 25 wt% silver-coated Al₂O₃ particles were fabricated using hot pressing. The study investigated the effect of Al₂O₃-Ag content on the microstructure, mechanical, tribological, and corrosion properties of the fabricated composites. The composites achieved relative densities exceeding 96%, while X-ray diffraction confirmed the formation of strengthening intermetallic phases, including Al₃Ni, Al₃Ni₂, CuAl₂, and Al₃.₈₉₂Cu₆.₁. The hardness increased from 95.31 HV for the unreinforced alloy to 451.59 HV at 25 wt% Al₂O₃-Ag, representing an approximately 374% increase. The compressive strength increased from 147.59 to 169.02 MPa, representing an improvement of approximately 14.5%, while the maximum compressive strain remained approximately 0.70 mm/mm. The wear rate decreased from 4.2 to 0.88 mg/min, corresponding to an approximately 79% reduction. In contrast, increasing the Al₂O₃-Ag content progressively deteriorated the corrosion resistance, with the corrosion rate increasing from 0.00093 to 0.09596 mm/y in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Overall, increasing Al₂O₃-Ag content improved hardness, compressive strength, and wear resistance, while reducing corrosion resistance.

Article.Title: Sensing of nitrogenous toxic gases on X-SnSe2/SnO2 heterostructures by doping with rare earth (X=La, Pr)
Article.Authors: Rhaif W.; Al-Badry L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The detection of toxic gases, particularly nitrogenous ones, has a direct impact on human health and safety. This study investigated the adsorption behavior of four nitrogenous gases (NO 2 , NO, NH 3 , and HCN) using density functional theory. These gases were detected using a heterostructure of SnSe 2 /SnO 2 doped with rare-earth elements (La and Pr). Analysis of the results revealed distinct reaction patterns on both heterostructures. For nitrogenous gases containing oxygen, high adsorption energies (E ads ), high charge transfer (Q t ), and a high work function were observed, particularly in Pr-SnSe 2 /SnO 2 , where the highest values reached − 2.75 eV, -0.34e, and 5.76 eV, respectively, upon adsorption of NO 2 . The results also indicate a significant convergence of these values for both heterostructures upon the adsorption of hydrogen-containing gases. This study demonstrates that Pr-SnSe 2 /SnO 2 is more effective at sensing oxygen-containing gases than hydrogen-containing gases, making it a promising sensor for this class of gases.

Article.Title: HiD-CLIP integrates hierarchical semantic scoring, dual-stream localization and training-time pixel refinement for cross-domain industrial anomaly detection
Article.Authors: Wu T.; Liu W.; Yang S.; Wang Y.; Jiang M.; Jing J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial inspection models may degrade when they are applied to product categories, materials, or imaging conditions that differ from the training data. We introduce HiD-CLIP, a CLIP-based anomaly detection framework that keeps the pretrained backbone frozen and adds adapters for product-level anomaly scoring and pixel-level defect localization. The method combines information from multiple visual depths, fuses an adapted similarity map with an attention-based map, and applies a training-only auxiliary pixel-refinement loss for multi-scale localization. In source-supervised experiments, no target labels or masks are used for adaptation, and HiD-CLIP is evaluated on seven public target domains. Using the public or corresponding training procedure for each method, HiD-CLIP achieves Image AUROC/AP of 89.76/89.24 and Pixel AUROC/PRO of 95.89/85.47. It gives the highest average Image AUROC and Pixel AUROC in this comparison, while the Image AP and Pixel PRO results indicate remaining room for better score calibration and region overlap. The reported accuracy is accompanied by higher inference cost and peak GPU memory than several lighter CLIP-based alternatives.

Article.Title: Probabilistic reliability cost of drift uniformity in optimized strongback steel frames
Article.Authors: Jahankhani E.; Rezaifar O.; Gholhaki M.; Homami P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Strongback system effectively mitigates soft-story mechanisms by enforcing uniform inter-story drift. While deterministic optimization utilizing the Drift Uniformity Factor (DUF) achieves this target, it inherently neglects structural uncertainties. This study quantifies the “probabilistic cost” of the DUF constraint through a system reliability assessment of optimized 4- and 6-story Strongback steel frames across three topologies ( $$\alpha$$ = L/4,L/3,5L/12). Utilizing a Stochastic Finite Element Method framework, 12,000 simulations (1000 per scenario) were executed, incorporating four lognormal random variables for material and load uncertainties with a 10% coefficient of variation. The probabilistic results reveal a scale-dependent paradox. In 6-story frames, enforcing DUF systematically degraded system reliability; for the optimal $$\alpha =L/3$$ configuration, the probability of failure ( $${P}_{f}$$ ) surged by 208%, escalating from 14.7% (without DUF) to 45.3% (with DUF). Conversely, in shear-dominant 4-story frames ( $$\alpha =L/3$$ ), the DUF constraint acted as a “redemptive penalty” its deterministically imposed structural overstrength inadvertently enhanced stochastic robustness, reducing $${P}_{f}$$ from $$49.1$$ to 37.7% (a 23.2% reduction). Ultimately, this study demonstrates that imposing rigid kinematic constraints like DUF tightens the feasible design space, often critically compromising probabilistic safety margins. Geometric nonlinearities are approximated through P–Δ effects using leaning columns in OpenSees. These findings are specific to the adopted linear-static equivalent-load framework and should not be interpreted as general nonlinear dynamic seismic performance.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of deep recurrent neural networks in classifying COVID-19-related respiratory conditions using clinical reports
Article.Authors: Murthy Y.; Sekar K.; Thanushri R.; Vinod V.; Kalnoor G.; Cenkeramaddi L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Countries all around the world have been severely affected by the novel coronavirus, popularly known as COVID-19, causing hundreds of thousands of unfortunate deaths without having found a widespread immunization method. It is extremely crucial for healthcare officials and the Governments of various countries to be able to differentiate the possible coronavirus strains to provide appropriate care and treatment. This paper proposes an effective way to set apart coronavirus strains into classes such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and COVID-19 using machine learning algorithms and recurrent neural networks (RNN). Natural language processing (NLP) techniques were performed on textual clinical reports to structure the data and improve its usability for the model. Bag of words model and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) vectorization were some of the few processes involved in extracting the prominent symptoms associated with each variant. The same has fed to various machine learning algorithms include multinomial naive Bayes (NB), logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), support vector machines (SVMs), and random forest (RF). Moreover, two more algorithms namely bagging, and gradient boost, are used for classification purposes. The reasons for choosing them are to observe their performance while classifying the proposed problem and compare the overall potency of the prediction system with RNNs. From this investigation, RNNs proved to be the optimal and expeditious technique to distinguish the covid strains. Adding more layers to the RNN has been noted to increase the efficacy of the system. The proposed approach with RNNs is giving an accuracy of around 99.14%.

Article.Title: Microstructural, thermal, and free-volume properties of silver nanoparticle/reduced graphene oxide-loaded poly(vinyl alcohol)–poly(vinyl pyrrolidone)–carboxymethyl cellulose nanocomposites
Article.Authors: El Sayed M.; El-Gamal S.; Ismail A.; Attallah A.; Hirschmann E.; Elsayed M.; Ashry A.; El-Maqsoud D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study reports the development of bio-based polymer nanocomposite films comprising a poly(vinyl alcohol)–poly(vinyl pyrrolidone)–carboxymethyl cellulose (PVA–PVP–CMC) ternary blend loaded with silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) and reduced graphene oxide nanosheets (rGO NSs). Nanocomposites containing single and hybrid nanofillers (1–3 wt%) were fabricated via a solution casting technique. Structural analysis using XRD confirmed an average Ag NP crystallite size of 24.82 nm and a specific surface area (SSA) of 22.92 m 2 /g. The XRD patterns further confirmed the crystalline nature and purity of Ag NPs with an FCC structure and the graphitic rGO (002) reflection, while the nanocomposites exhibited predominantly amorphous characteristics with enhanced crystallinity upon filler incorporation, ranging from 5.99% for the pure blend to 15.07% for the film containing 3 wt% rGO NSs. FTIR revealed strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding among the polymer constituents and progressive interfacial interactions with the nanofillers, reflected in systematic shifts and intensity changes of the O–H, C = O, and C–O–C bands. SEM and EDX analyses of representative sample regions indicated generally uniform apparent dispersion and effective integration of the nanofillers within the polymer matrix. Thermal properties investigated by DSC showed a rise in Tg from 72.1 °C for the pure blend to 88.8 °C for the film containing 3 wt% Ag NPs, suggesting reduced polymer chain mobility resulting from strong interfacial interactions between the matrix and nanofillers. Free-volume characteristics evaluated by positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) showed that the ortho-positronium lifetime (τ 3 ) and corresponding free-volume size (V F ) ranged from 1.452 to 1.530 ns and 52.04–59.51 Å³, respectively, across the filler series. The largest free volume was observed at 1 wt% Ag NP loading, indicating that low filler loading promotes free-volume formation, whereas higher loading reduces the free-volume size. Temperature-dependent PALS further confirmed the correlation between free-volume expansion and Tg. These findings establish a structure–property framework connecting nanofiller dispersion, free-volume architecture, and thermal transitions in this ternary matrix, positioning it as a candidate tunable platform for lightweight, sustainable nanocomposite films, pending complementary mechanical, electrical, and functional testing.

Article.Title: Inflationary dynamics in combined $$f(\phi )T$$ and Gauss-Bonnet gravity with three representative coupling schemes
Article.Authors: Younesizadeh F.
Article.Abstract: We analyze inflationary dynamics in combined \(f(\phi )T\) and Gauss-Bonnet gravity, considering three representative coupling schemes: (i) exponential \(V(\phi )=V_0 e^{-\lambda \phi }\) , \(f(\phi )=f_0 e^{-\lambda \phi }\) , and linear \(\xi (\phi )=\xi _0\phi \) ; (ii) power-law \(V(\phi )=V_0\phi ^2\) , inverse power-law \(\xi (\phi )=\xi _0/\phi ^2\) , and constant \(f(\phi )=f_0\) ; (iii) dilaton-like \(V(\phi )=V_0(1-\phi )^{-2}\) , \(f(\phi )=f_0(1-\phi )^{-1}\) , \(\xi (\phi )=\xi _0(1-\phi )^2\) . For each case we derive slow-roll parameters and compute the scalar spectral index \(n_s\) and tensor-to-scalar ratio r , comparing with Planck 2018+BK18 ( \(n_s=0.9665\pm 0.0038\) , \(r<0.065\) at \(95\%\) CL) and ACT DR6 ( \(n_s=0.969\pm 0.004\) , \(r<0.021\) at \(95\%\) CL). Case 1 yields \(r\sim 10^{-4}\) – \(10^{-3}\) with \(n_s\) within Planck \(68\%\) CL for \(Y=\beta f_0\sim 8.3\) –8.7. Case 2 gives \(r\sim 0.03\) –0.07, consistent with Planck+BK18 but disfavored by ACT DR6. Case 3 produces \(r\sim 10^{-4}\) with \(n_s\) matching Planck central values for \(X\equiv \xi _0 V_0\sim 0.20\) . This comparative analysis provides testable signatures for future CMB experiments including LiteBIRD and CMB-S4.

Article.Title: Workplace environment and burnout among hemodialysis healthcare professionals: a pilot study
Article.Authors: Sági B.; Fejes É.; Csiky B.; Ságiné É.; Fehér G.; Tibold A.; Szigeti N.; Csiky B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This pilot study investigated burnout among healthcare professionals (HCPs) working in center-based and satellite hemodialysis units and examined its association with patient clinical complexity. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 39 HCPs in Pécs, Hungary. Burnout was assessed primarily using the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), with the Mini Oldenburg Burnout Inventory (MOLBI) used as a complementary measure of exhaustion and disengagement. MBI dimensions were analyzed separately, with Emotional Exhaustion (MBI-EE) prespecified as the primary burnout-related outcome for multivariable analysis. Patient clinical complexity was assessed using the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) and Karnofsky Performance Scale (KPS). Exploratory multivariable linear regression was performed with a parsimonious set of prespecified predictors. Patients treated in the center-based dialysis unit had a significantly higher comorbidity burden (CCI: 6.62 vs. 5.55, p = 0.003) and poorer functional status (KPS: 67.9 vs. 85.7, p < 0.001) than those treated in the satellite unit. Healthcare professionals working in the center-based dialysis unit had significantly higher Emotional Exhaustion scores than those working in the satellite unit (29.2 ± 7.2 vs. 22.2 ± 7.1, p = 0.002). MOLBI-measured exhaustion was positively correlated with patient CCI (r = 0.426, p = 0.028). In exploratory multivariable analysis, center-based dialysis unit employment remained associated with higher Emotional Exhaustion after adjustment for age category and marital status (B = 5.587, SE = 2.196, standardized β = 0.351, p = 0.016). Greater patient clinical complexity and functional dependency in the center-based dialysis setting were accompanied by higher Emotional Exhaustion among healthcare professionals. Because dialysis setting and patient case mix were closely related, the observed association should not be interpreted as a causal organizational effect. Larger multicentre longitudinal studies incorporating objective workload measures are warranted.

Article.Title: Association of APOC3 promoter variants with hypertriglyceridemia and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in a Thai cohort
Article.Authors: Yaikwawong M.; Kamdee K.; Chuengsamarn S.
Article.Abstract: Apolipoprotein C-III (APOC3) regulates triglyceride metabolism by inhibiting lipoprotein lipase activity and reducing the clearance of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. We investigated the associations of APOC3 promoter polymorphisms (rs2854116 and rs2854117) with hypertriglyceridemia and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in a Thai cohort. This cross-sectional study included 276 Thai adults from a MASLD case-control cohort. MASLD was defined using controlled attenuation parameter (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m) measured by transient elastography. APOC3 rs2854116 and rs2854117 were genotyped, and associations with hypertriglyceridemia and MASLD were evaluated using logistic regression under a prespecified additive genetic model. Sensitivity analyses stratified by and adjusted for MASLD status were performed. Exploratory haplotype analyses were also conducted. Under the additive model, rs2854116 was associated with hypertriglyceridemia in crude (OR 1.58 per T allele, 95% CI 1.08–2.33; p = 0.019) and adjusted analyses (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.06–2.36; p = 0.025; FDR-adjusted p = 0.050), meeting the prespecified FDR threshold for the primary hypothesis family. The association remained significant after adjustment for MASLD status (OR 1.61, 95% CI 1.08–2.41; p = 0.020) and was consistent across MASLD strata ( p for interaction = 0.61). The minor T allele was more frequent among participants with hypertriglyceridemia than among normotriglyceridemic controls (54.5% vs. 43.7%; OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.06–2.24; p = 0.022). Neither rs2854116 nor rs2854117 was associated with MASLD. Exploratory haplotype analyses likewise showed no consistent association with MASLD. APOC3 rs2854116 was associated with hypertriglyceridemia in this Thai cohort, supporting its role in triglyceride metabolism. In contrast, no clear evidence was found for an association between APOC3 variants and MASLD. Because the cohort was selected according to MASLD status, potential selection or collider bias cannot be excluded, and these findings require confirmation in larger, population-based Thai cohorts.

Article.Title: Musculoskeletal simulation of load placement and speed effects on gait dynamics and energetics
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang X.; Shen Z.; Zhang L.; Zhao Y.; Zhan H.; Pires G.; Lin M.; Vrionis F.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the biomechanical and energetic effects of load placement (ankle vs. back) on human walking and running across a spectrum of speeds, addressing a gap in speed-dependent quantification of muscle and joint adaptations. We used a direct collocation optimal control framework integrated with a musculoskeletal model to simulate gait under varied conditions. Simulations covered walking (1.1, 1.3, 1.5 m/s) and running (2.5, 3.0, 3.5 m/s) with ankle-attached loads (1–5% body weight) and back-mounted loads (10–50% body weight). The simulations revealed distinct adaptation strategies. Ankle loading primarily increased swing-phase muscle activation. Conversely, back loading enhanced stance-phase extensor activity and altered joint kinetics. A key finding is that back loading was associated with a relative improvement in simulated transport economy compared with ankle loading. The metabolic demand associated with ankle loads was comparable to that of substantially heavier back loads across both walking and running. Load placement substantially influenced muscle coordination strategy and relative energetic outcomes during locomotion. These findings provide a mechanistic, simulation‑based framework for understanding trade‑offs in loaded gait by linking load placement and magnitude to phase‑specific changes in kinematics, kinetics, muscle recruitment, joint reaction forces, and energetic cost. The resulting simulation‑derived mappings can serve as virtual pre‑tests to screen load‑carriage designs and to generate testable hypotheses for targeted experimental validation and training prescriptions.

Article.Title: Dual-stream frequency-spatial fusion and feature calibration for robust thyroid nodule segmentation
Article.Authors: Qin C.; Sun S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate segmentation of thyroid nodules in ultrasound (US) imaging is a critical prerequisite for automated clinical diagnosis. However, this task remains highly challenging due to inherent speckle noise, low tissue contrast, and severely ambiguous lesion boundaries. Conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) primarily focus on local spatial domains, which inevitably leads to the progressive loss of high-frequency boundary cues and the introduction of semantic noise via standard skip connections. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a novel architecture named Dual-Stream Frequency-Spatial Fusion Network (DS-FSFNet). Specifically, we introduce a Frequency-Spatial Fusion (FSF) module at the network bottleneck. By leveraging the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), the FSF module explicitly extracts and integrates high-frequency structural representations, effectively compensating for the spatial blurring effect of deep convolutions. Furthermore, a Spatial-Channel Feature Calibration (SFC) module is embedded within the skip connections to adaptively filter out semantic noise using dual-attention mechanisms prior to feature decoding. Extensive experiments on three challenging thyroid US datasets (DDTI, TG3K, and TN3K) demonstrate that DS-FSFNet achieves competitive segmentation performance compared with representative medical image segmentation methods. In addition, evaluation on the CVC-ClinicDB dataset, which involves a substantially different medical imaging task, provides further evidence of the transferability of the proposed architecture across different segmentation scenarios.

Article.Title: Etiology and clinical severity of community-acquired acute gastroenteritis in adults at a coastal provincial hospital in Thailand
Article.Authors: Mon N.; Phuttasiriwat S.; Lawpoolsri S.; Poovorawan K.; Muangnoicharoen S.; Imad H.; Charunwatthana P.; Kittitrakul C.
Article.Abstract: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) remains a common cause of illness in tropical regions, but its etiology and predictors of severe disease in adults are incompletely characterized. We conducted a prospective study of adults with community-acquired AGE at Samut Sakhon Hospital, Thailand, from December 2019 to May 2020. Of 534 patients assessed, 266 were included; 161 (60.5%) had severe disease requiring hospitalization and 105 (39.5%) had mild disease managed as outpatients. Among 165 patients who underwent all four diagnostic tests, including stool examination, concentration testing, culture, and viral RT-PCR, an enteropathogen was detected in 49 (29.7%). Detection was similar between severe and mild cases (29.6% vs. 30.0%). Viral pathogens were detected in 10.2% of patients, while parasites were detected in 0.9%. Among patients undergoing stool culture, bacterial pathogens were identified in 15.8%, most commonly Salmonella spp. (6.7%) and Vibrio parahaemolyticus (4.8%). All bacterial isolates were susceptible to ciprofloxacin. Thai nationality, the presence of any comorbidity, history of fever, dehydration, higher diarrhea frequency, higher neutrophil percentage, and lower hematocrit independently predicted severe disease. These findings support early clinical risk stratification and improved diagnostic stewardship to guide targeted treatment and reduce unnecessary antibiotic use in adults with AGE.

Article.Title: Overexpression of FTO inhibits ferroptosis induced by OGD/R in mouse renal tubular epithelial cells
Article.Authors: Su X.; Li G.; Liu J.; Duan F.; Ou M.; Lou J.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) is recognized as one of the major causes of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanism by which FTO alleviates AKI through activating the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway to inhibit ferroptosis. AKI model induced by renal I/R in mice and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) cell model were established, and FTO was overexpressed in the cells and treated with NRF2 inhibitory ML-385 and ferroptosis activator. The levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), serum creatinine (Scr), and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) in serum and cell supernatant were detected by ELISA. Western blot was performed to detect the protein expression of m6A modification enzymes (METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, FTO, ALKBH5) and ferroptosis-related pathway proteins (NRF2, SLC7A11, GPX4) in both in vivo and in vitro models. RT-qPCR was used to measure the mRNA levels of KIM1 and NGAL in cells. Subsequently, FTO-overexpressing lentivirus was transfected into OGD/R-induced cells, and cell viability, apoptosis rate, Fe 2+ concentration, and levels of oxidative stress markers (ROS and MDA) were detected. Finally, Western blot was used to assess the protein expression of NRF2, SLC7A11, and GPX4 in each group. Compared with the control group, the protein expression of METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, and ALKBH5 was significantly upregulated, while FTO was markedly downregulated in both in vivo and in vitro models of renal injury, with FTO showing the most prominent expression difference ( P < 0.05). The levels of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, Scr, and BUN were significantly increased in the in vitro and in vivo models ( P < 0.05). In the OGD/R group, compared with the control group, KIM1 and NGAL mRNA levels were significantly increased, accompanied by decreased cell viability, increased apoptosis rate, elevated levels of Fe 2+ , ROS, and MDA, and reduced SOD activity ( P < 0.05). Meanwhile, the protein levels of NRF2, SLC7A11, and GPX4 were also significantly decreased ( P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed between the OGD/R group and the empty vector-overexpressing group. However, FTO overexpression significantly reversed all these aforementioned phenomena ( P < 0.05). Compared with the OE-FTO group, ML-385 and erastin could significantly weaken the protective effect of overexpressed FTO ( P < 0.05). FTO overexpression inhibits ferroptosis by activating the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway and reduces OGD/ R-induced cell injury. FTO may be a potential target for regulating ferroptosis in AKI.

Article.Title: Peatland diversity in Belizean wetlands and the challenges of greenhouse gas reporting
Article.Authors: Malpica-Piñeros C.; Morrissette H.; Iglesias A.; Correa E.; Guerra F.; Joosten H.; Correa I.; Peters J.; Loisel J.; Jensen K.; Santos L.; Balan L.; Carcamo M.; Latimer M.; Martinez N.; Baez S.; Sabal T.; McKoy T.; Elshehawi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the important climate change mitigation and adaptation benefits, including carbon storage and hydrological regulation that they provide, peatlands in the Caribbean are poorly characterized and increasingly under threat. Here we provide a first-time national assessment of peatlands in Belize. They cover approximately 6% of the land area and store around 165Mt of carbon. The marine-terrestrial system includes mangrove peatlands and the terrestrial-freshwater system is formed by open peatlands (sedges and grasses) and peat swamp forest. The oldest peatlands, in coastal sites (cayes), are characterized by over 800 cm of peat and started to grow around 7500 CalBP, concordant with regional sea-level stabilization. Coarse stratigraphic observations indicate most peatlands started as mangroves, some of which transitioned into open peatlands and peat swamp forests. The transitions are likely caused by rising peat accumulations over the tidal influence. Only ~ 29% of peatlands in Belize are within protected areas, which leaves many peatlands threatened by land conversion and drainage; particularly the case in coastal areas. Belize is one of the first Caribbean countries to include peatlands in its NDCs. However, due to the mosaic nature of its peatlands, reporting under the IPCC guidelines represents a challenge for the country and the region.

Article.Title: New Contracaecum species records in fish and the description of C. sistanense sp. nov. in birds from Iran
Article.Authors: Shamsi S.; Khedri J.; Borji H.; Francis N.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in aquatic ecosystems is important because these zoonotic nematodes circulate through complex food webs involving invertebrates, fish, birds, and occasionally humans. This study investigated the species richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in Iranian waters through a literature review combined with morphological and molecular characterisation of adult specimens collected from piscivorous birds. The literature review demonstrated that most previous reports involved larval stages recovered from 39 fish species across 16 families inhabiting freshwater, marine, and brackish environments in 9 Iranian provinces. However, the identity of most larval forms remains unresolved due to the absence of molecular data. Molecular and morphological analyses of adult nematodes collected from the great white pelican, Pelecanus onocrotalus , confirmed the presence of Contracaecum micropapillatum and C. gibsoni in Iran for the first time and led to the description of a new species, Contracaecum sistanense sp. nov. Together with the previously molecularly confirmed record of C. multipapillatum , these findings increase the number of confirmed Contracaecum species recorded in Iran to four. The present study improves current knowledge of Contracaecum spp. in Iran and highlights the need for broader surveys across diverse hosts and geographical regions to better understand the distribution, taxonomy, and zoonotic potential of these parasites.

Article.Title: Dynamic microbial succession during chicken-manure composting and its links to physicochemical environments
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Nian L.; Li J.; Tang Y.; Yuan H.; Haider F.
Article.Abstract: Microbial community diversity, abundance, and activity drive composting by governing organic matter decomposition and nutrient turnover. Despite extensive work, the links between microbial succession and physicochemical dynamics, and the role of microbial co-occurrence patterns, remain poorly understood. This study characterizes the temporal succession of bacterial and fungal communities during aerobic chicken manure composting and relates these changes to key physicochemical indicators. Fresh chicken manure and wheat straw (8:1, v/v) were composted for 35 days, with samples collected at four stages: initial (day 0), thermophilic (day 3), bio-oxidative (day 15), and maturation (day 35). High-throughput sequencing, bioinformatics analyses, and statistical approaches were used to characterize microbial community diversity, structure, and network interactions, and to assess their relationships with temperature, pH, moisture, and nutrient contents. During composting, physicochemical properties changed dynamically. Bacterial community diversity and richness decreased from 391 genera at T1 to 229 at T4, while fungal genera fluctuated, peaking at T1 (565) and reaching a minimum at T4 (379). Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota were the dominant phyla, while Pseudogracilibacillus, Penicillium, and Aspergillus were the predominant genera across stages. Network analysis revealed clear separation and reorganization of microbial communities during composting. The principal drivers for bacterial communities were total nitrogen (TN), ammonium-N (NH4+-N), the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (C/N), and temperature, whereas for fungal communities the primary influences were pH, nitrate-N (NO3−-N), and total organic carbon (TOC). Collectively, the findings demonstrate that fluctuations in physicochemical conditions steer microbial succession in chicken-manure composting and imply that adjusting key environmental factors and microbial assemblages could enhance compost maturation and final quality.

Article.Title: The association between social media addiction and psychological well-being in adolescents with sequential mediation by physical activity and loneliness
Article.Authors: Mallı A.; Düğenci A.; Ayhan C.; Seçer E.; Kaçay Z.; Şahinler Y.; Işık Ö.
Article.Abstract: Social media addiction is a phenomenon that may adversely affect adolescent mental health and is increasingly recognized as a public health concern by international authorities such as the World Health Organization. Understanding the potential mechanisms underlying the association between social media addiction and psychological well-being is important for informing effective intervention strategies. This study aimed to examine the sequential mediating role of physical activity and loneliness in the association between social media addiction and adolescents’ psychological well-being. This cross-sectional study included 290 high school students (mean age = 15.73; 59% female, 41% male) enrolled in high schools in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, the UCLA Loneliness Scale (Short Form), and the Psychological Well-Being Scale. Data were analyzed using SPSS. Normality assumptions were first examined, followed by descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses to assess the relationships among the study variables. Subsequently, Hayes’ PROCESS Macro Model 6, a bootstrap-based sequential mediation analysis, was employed to examine the hypothesized indirect associations. Social media addiction was significantly and negatively associated with psychological well-being. The sequential mediation analysis indicated that social media addiction is associated with lower levels of physical activity, which in turn is associated with higher levels of loneliness, and that the proposed sequential indirect association with psychological well-being was statistically significant (indirect effect = -0.0259, 95% CI [-0.0488, -0.0072]). Conclusion The results indicate that physical activity and loneliness may represent an important sequential pathway in the association between social media addiction and adolescents’ psychological well-being. Accordingly, public health interventions targeting adolescent mental health may benefit from addressing social media use while also promoting physical activity as a potential component of strategies to support psychological well-being.

Article.Title: LAFNet: a lightweight neural network with fuzzy attention mechanism for rail surface defect classification
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Osman G.; Mustapha M.; Dai L.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rapid and accurate detection of rail anomaly is crucial for railway transportation safety. Although existing deep learning methods have achieved certain progress, they generally suffer from large model parameter sizes and high computational costs, making it difficult to meet the requirements of real-time performance and resource constraints for on-site deployment. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight neural network model (LAFNet) for rail anomaly classification. The model first adopts a three-layer convolutional structure to extract deep features. Then, an enhanced fuzzy neural network branch generates fuzzy rule activation vectors with clear semantics, and a fuzzy attention gating module is introduced to adaptively perform channel-wise reweighting of convolutional features using the rule vectors, thereby enhancing anomaly-related features and suppressing irrelevant ones. Furthermore, a residual fully connected block is employed to improve nonlinear representation capability and ensure stable gradient propagation. Experimental results show that the proposed model has only 0.46 million parameters, an CPU inference time of 1.045 milliseconds, and achieves a classification accuracy of 99.5%.

Article.Title: Deep learning framework for automated cervical vertebral maturation staging using CBCT scans
Article.Authors: Milani O.; Nikho A.; Mills L.; Tliba M.; Allareddy V.; Ansari R.; Cetin A.; Atakan A.; Elnagar M.
Article.Abstract: Automated skeletal maturity assessment is essential in orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, guiding the optimal timing of interventions such as myofunctional appliances and orthognathic surgery. This study aims to develop and evaluate deep learning algorithms for the assessment and classification of cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) stages using sagittal views derived from cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans. The sample consisted of 364 CBCT scans of orthodontic patients from private practices in the midwestern United States. The CVM stages were classified by two orthodontists and an oral and maxillofacial radiologist. Distinct experimental settings evaluated image-based classification, prompt-guided anatomical localization using the Segment Anything Model (SAM), demographic conditioning with age and sex information, knowledge distillation from a teacher network pretrained on a skeletal maturity dataset, and tri-modal input fusion. Because data availability differed across settings, these components were evaluated on different eligible subsets rather than as a unified sequential ablation. In the full 364-sample six-class baseline setting, ResNet34 achieved 66.76% accuracy. In the separate 96-sample, stage-aligned five-class knowledge-distillation setting, ResNet50 achieved the highest observed accuracy of 88.54% (5-fold cross-validation average), compared with 87.10% for its non-distilled counterpart in the stage-aligned five-class knowledge-distillation setting using a paired subset of 96 scans. The distillation effect varied across architectures, and the 96-sample subset was small and class-imbalanced. The findings support the feasibility of deep learning-based CVM staging from CBCT-derived sagittal views across distinct experimental settings. The results do not establish that anatomical guidance, demographic conditioning, and knowledge distillation jointly improve classification because these components were not evaluated through a unified ablation on a common cohort. Within the separate five-class knowledge-distillation setting, performance changes were backbone-dependent, with only a modest numerical improvement observed for ResNet50. The findings should therefore be considered preliminary and internally validated. Larger, balanced, and externally validated cohorts are required before broader clinical applicability can be established.

Article.Title: Food allergen sensitization on a standardized specific-IgE core panel in the West Bank, Palestine: a retrospective analysis of 1,339 Patients, 2016–2026
Article.Authors: Salhi I.; Mazraawi A.; Badran Z.; Salhi I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Local data on food allergen sensitization in the West Bank of Palestine are scarce, and clinicians rely on allergen panels derived from dissimilar Western populations. We describe the sensitization profile of patients referred for specific-IgE (sIgE) testing, using a deduplicated cohort and a fixed core panel to enable valid patient-level and temporal inference. We analysed routinely collected food sIgE records from a multi-branch private laboratory network (archive 2004–2026). Specific IgE was measured with the EUROLINE semi-quantitative line immunoblot assay (EUROIMMUN, Lübeck, Germany). Records were deduplicated to unique individuals using a patient identifier. The primary cohort comprised patients tested on the standardized panel introduced in 2016. Because the panel’s composition changed once during the study, all primary analyses were based on a stable core of 19 food allergens assayed in ≥ 99% of patients, giving a common denominator across patients and calendar time. Sensitization was defined as sIgE ≥ 0.35 kU/L. Associations were assessed by multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, calendar period and governorate. Of 1,675 records, 1,633 represented unique patients; 1,339 tested on the standardized panel (2016–2026) formed the primary cohort (median age 23 years; 43.5% aged < 18). On the core panel, 26.7% (95% CI 24.4–29.1) were sensitized to ≥ 1 food and 18.7% were polysensitized. The leading sensitizers were cow milk (11.5%), sesame (10.0%), peanut (8.8%), egg white (8.7%) and rice (8.1%). Sensitization peaked in early childhood (40.9% at 1–5 years; adjusted OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.89–3.59) and was higher in males (34.3% vs. 19.9%; aOR 1.83, 1.42–2.37). The infant subgroup (< 1 year, n = 40) was underpowered (aOR 1.94, 0.95–3.93). Core-allergen sensitization was stable across calendar periods (27.4%, 25.1%, 27.5%; trend p = 0.48); an apparent decline seen when non-core allergens were included was an artefact of a mid-study panel change. Governorate was not independently associated with sensitization. Among West Bank patients tested on a standardized panel, food sensitization was common and polysensitization frequent, with a distinctly Levantine hierarchy led by cow milk and sesame. The early-childhood peak (1–5 years) and male excess were robust to adjustment, while apparent temporal and geographic differences reflected changes in testing rather than disease. Findings describe sensitization in referred patients, not clinical food allergy.

Article.Title: Multifunctional TiO₂-modified cement mortar: experimental investigation, machine learning prediction, and life cycle assessment
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Ashraf M.; Ashraf M.; Riaz N.; Bhatti A.; Ahmad F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract TiO₂-modified cement mortar is a multifunctional construction material that enhances both mechanical performance and environmental remediation. This study investigated the photocatalytic activity, compressive strength, machine learning prediction, and life cycle assessment of cement mortars containing 0–12 wt% TiO₂. Photocatalytic performance was evaluated through the degradation of Reactive Blue 19 (RB19) dye under visible-light irradiation, while SEM, XRD, and FTIR analyses were used for material characterization. Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were developed to predict dye removal efficiency and compressive strength. The photocatalytic efficiency increased with TiO₂ content, reaching 87.13% RB19 removal within 60 min at 10 wt% TiO₂. Acidic conditions enhanced dye degradation, whereas higher dye concentrations reduced removal efficiency. Compressive strength increased to 23.4 MPa at 28 days with 6 wt% TiO₂, representing a 12.3% improvement over the control. The microstructural analysis provide qualitative support for the strength improvement observed at 6 wt% TiO₂. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with testing R 2 values of 0.96 for dye removal and 0.92 for compressive strength. LCA identified cement production as the primary environmental hotspot, while TiO₂ mainly contributed to acidification and particulate matter formation. Findings demonstrate the potential of TiO₂-modified cement mortar as a sustainable multifunctional construction material.

Article.Title: Ethnobotanical and phytochemical insights into native and naturalized plants for cashew pest control in Guinea-Bissau
Article.Authors: Sierra-Baquero P.; Monteiro F.; Duarte M.; Romeiras M.; Indjai B.; Varón-Devia E.; Figueiredo A.; Catarino L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Essential oils are increasingly recognized as ecofriendly alternatives to synthetic pesticides, especially in tropical regions with high pest pressure and limited crop protection resources. This study evaluates native and naturalized plants in Guinea-Bissau— Ageratum conyzoides , Azadirachta indica , Chromolaena odorata , Cymbopogon giganteus , and Mesosphaerum suaveolens —for sustainable pest management, combining ethnobotanical documentation, essential oils characterization, and existing bioactivity data focused on cashew pests. An African-wide ethnobotanical assessment using Plant Resources of Tropical Africa (PROTA) and Scopus databases revealed that these species were predominantly used for medicinal and pest-related applications, most frequently reported in West Africa. Essential oils were extracted from leaves by hydrodistillation and chemically characterized using gas chromatography coupled with flame ionization detection and mass spectrometry. Essential oils yields varied among species; C. odorata and C. giganteus yielded the highest. Chemical profiling revealed species-specific compositions dominated by chromenes, monoterpene hydrocarbons, and sesquiterpene hydrocarbons. Major constituents included precocene I, limonene, sabinene, β-caryophyllene, and 1,8-cineole, compounds widely reported for their insecticidal, repellent, and antifeedant properties, indicating their potential for sustainable management of cashew pests in West Africa. By combining ethnobotanical knowledge with phytochemical characterization, this study highlights the untapped potential of locally available plant-derived essential oils, rooted in traditional practices, as potentially valuable resources for sustainable agriculture.

Article.Title: A novel deep learning-based approach for liver segmentation from 3D CT images using probabilistic shape guidance
Article.Authors: Semida A.; Sharafeldeen A.; Amer H.; Khalil A.; Mahmoud A.; Karam R.; Elged B.; Shiha U.; Mounir A.; Taher F.; Ghazal M.; Giridharan G.; Contractor S.; El-Baz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate liver segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems, yet it remains challenging due to anatomical variability, indistinct organ boundaries, and tissue intensity variations in both normal and pathological cases. To address these challenges, a deep learning-based framework is proposed for segmenting liver regions from 3D computed tomography (CT) volumes. Initially, this system creates a 3D probabilistic shape map to estimate the probability of each voxel being a liver voxel, utilizing a reference atlas dataset. To facilitate this, the atlas references are first aligned with the input CT volume via 3D affine registration, establishing a coarse but essential spatial correspondence. Following this alignment, the model adaptively matches each voxel in the input CT volume with cubic neighborhoods of varying sizes derived from the aligned liver atlas to compute the final shape map probabilities. Finally, a dual-path UX-Net (DPUX-Net) architecture is introduced which receives the original CT volume, combined with its corresponding probabilistic shape map, as input, and produces accurate and anatomically consistent liver segmentations. The efficacy of the proposed liver segmentation system is assessed on 120 CT volumes using multiple quantitative metrics, including the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Jaccard index, absolute volume difference (AVD), and Hausdorff distance (HD), achieving scores of $$93.19\%\pm 2.53\%$$ , $$87.12\%\pm 4.42\%$$ , $$4.53\pm 3.20$$ , and $$7.37\pm 5.19$$ , respectively. The evaluation includes both hold-out test samples from the training dataset and entirely unseen external datasets, demonstrating the robustness and generalizability of the proposed framework. In comparison to the current state-of-the-art deep learning-based segmentation models, the proposed system surpasses them, highlighting its potential and reliability in precisely segmenting liver regions in CT volumes.

Article.Title: Auditory-inspired cross-attention learning of spectral and modulation signatures for ship recognition
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhang D.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Underwater ship recognition is fundamentally challenged by acoustic complexity and limited labeled data. This paper proposes a physics-driven multidimensional feature fusion (MDFF) framework via auditory-inspired cross-attention learning. Rather than relying on isolated acoustic features or simple shallow concatenation, the method integrates bio-inspired Gammatone filtering with both LOFAR (structural line-spectra) and DEMON (propeller modulation) representations. A deep cross-attention architecture (MDFF-SL) is designed to effectively decouple machinery and propulsion signatures, mapping these physically heterogeneous components into a compact, highly discriminative representation space while suppressing overfitting under small-sample conditions. Extensive experiments on real-world sea-trial data demonstrate that MDFF-SL achieves 92.96% recognition accuracy with exceptionally low standard deviation, substantially outperforming conventional single-domain and shallow-fusion baselines. These results establish a high-precision, computationally efficient paradigm for reliable maritime surveillance in non-stationary underwater environments.

Article.Title: CHO cell production of a single, enveloped VLP vaccine co-displaying SARS-CoV-2, influenza and RSV antigens
Article.Authors: Sanchez-Martinez Z.; Stuible M.; Cass B.; Lord-Dufour S.; Tran A.; Akache B.; Renner T.; Mahimkar R.; Morasse A.; Baardsnes J.; De Crescenzo G.; Durocher Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Concurrent circulation of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (IAV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major public health concern, driving the need for multivalent, combined vaccines. Here, we report the generation of trivalent enveloped virus-like particles (eVLPs) co-displaying SARS-CoV-2 spike (S), influenza A H1, and RSV fusion (F) proteins produced in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. Using both transient and stable gene expression systems, we achieved intrinsic co-assembly of all three antigens within enveloped particles. Stable CHO eVLP expression yielded antigen volumetric titers of 48 ± 2 mg/L. A prefusogenic F variant showed superior expression and incorporation efficiency compared to wild-type F and prefusion-stabilized forms. The adjuvanted trivalent eVLPs elicited IgG responses against S, H1, and F, together with S- and F-specific T-cell responses and antibodies targeting the palivizumab-binding site II of RSV-F, a clinically relevant neutralizing epitope. Notably, the formulation provided complete protection against homologous A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8; H1N1) challenge in mice , supporting further evaluation of this CHO-derived platform for combined respiratory-virus vaccination.

Article.Title: Physicochemical and sensorial properties of chocolate spread substituted with oleogel based on palm oil and coconut oil
Article.Authors: Subroto E.; Ramadhan E.; Zulafa Y.; Rahimah S.; Sumanti D.; Andoyo R.; Indiarto R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fat plays an important role in the texture and structure of chocolate spread, but excessive fat use negatively affects health. In general, oleogel can be used as an alternative to conventional fats. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the effect of substituting beeswax-structured oleogel prepared from 1:1 palm: coconut oil on the characteristics of chocolate spread. The fat in chocolate spread was substituted with palm-coconut oleogel. The substitution levels included A-0%, B-25%, C-50%, D-75%, and E-100%. The results showed that substituting oleogel increased the color chromaticity for L*, a*, and b*. The texture increased for hardness, adhesiveness, and cohesiveness. Sensory characteristics also increased, as evidenced by taste, texture, spreadability, and overall acceptance. Chocolate spread, which was substituted with palm-coconut oleogel at 25%, showed suitable characteristics and was acceptable to the panelists. The hardness, adhesiveness, and cohesiveness of chocolate spread were 6.89 ± 0.46 g, -8.07 ± 1.00 g.s, and 0.65 ± 0.03, respectively, while the color chromaticity of L*, a*, and b* was 29.17 ± 0.13, 8.50 ± 0.11, and 9.09 ± 0.14, respectively. The crystal microstructure consisted of small spherulites without needle-like crystals, dominated by β΄-crystal polymorph. These results showed that substitution of palm-coconut oleogel for up to 25% improved physicochemical and sensorial properties of chocolate spread. However, the high levels of oleogel had limitations, including compromised spreadability and texture.

Article.Title: Parametric sensitivity and variability-aware evaluation of CNTFET Full adders for robust nanoelectronic design
Article.Authors: Talawar V.; Shah O.; Sreenivasulu V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFETs) offer a promising pathway beyond silicon complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS), yet comprehensive circuit-level evaluations addressing statistical process variability and system-level validation remain scarce. This study presents a rigorous, multi-dimensional benchmarking of eleven full adder topologies—five CNTFET-native and six CMOS-derived—implemented uniformly in a 32 nm CNTFET technology node using the Stanford Verilog-A compact model.
