We systematically evaluate nominal performance, supply voltage scaling (0.7–1.1 V), frequency operation (100–400 MHz), chiral vector tuning from (16,0) to (19,0), and static leakage across all eight input combinations. Monte Carlo simulations (200 iterations, ± 10% parameter variation) quantify statistical yield, revealing that simplified approximate architectures achieve near-perfect robustness (98–100% yield), while transmission-gate designs balance energy efficiency and process resilience. Notably, Chew’s 17-transistor adder emerges as the optimal ultra-low-power archetype, achieving a power-delay product of 0.081 aJ, 82% statistical yield, and 3.2× lower system power in a 4:2 compressor application. These findings establish actionable, variability-aware design guidelines for CNTFET-based arithmetic units, bridging the gap between device physics and practical nanoelectronic deployment.

Article.Title: Health-related quality of life in patients with spinal muscular atrophy receiving nusinersen and their caregivers: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Kim A.; Lee H.; Na J.; Lee S.; Lee H.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder characterized by progressive motor decline. Although nusinersen has improved survival and motor outcomes, patients and caregivers continue to face substantial medical and psychosocial challenges. As treatment goals have expanded beyond survival to include health-related quality of life (HRQoL), understanding relationship between patient and caregiver has become increasingly important. In this cross-sectional study, we evaluated 36 patients with SMA receiving nusinersen and their 32 caregivers at a tertiary hospital. Patient HRQoL was assessed using the EQ-5D-5 L and PedsQL-NMM, while caregiver HRQoL was measured using the EQ-5D-5 L, CarerQoL-7D, and CarerQoL-VAS. Spearman’s rank correlation coefficients were used to examine associations between patient and caregiver HRQoL. Patients showed substantial impairment (mean EQ-5D-5 L utility 0.30; PedsQL-NMM 57.7), while caregiver reported relatively high overall HRQoL (mean CarerQoL-7D 68.4). Moderate positive correlations were observed between patient and caregiver HRQoL across multiple measures (e.g., PedsQL-NMM vs. CarerQoL-7D: rₛ=0.46). Correlations were generally stronger in sitters than in non-sitters. The observed associations between patient and caregiver HRQoL highlight the importance of considering caregiver perspectives in SMA management and resource planning. Stronger correlations in sitters may be related to closer daily interactions between patients and caregivers; however, further investigation is needed to clarify underlying mechanisms.

Article.Title: BICLARE: bio-inspired collaborative lightweight algorithm for robust swarm exploration
Article.Authors: van Dijk H.; Sharma S.; Prasad R.; Ambroziak L.
Article.Abstract: Having access to a floor plan upon arrival enables first responders to act swiftly and efficiently. This study investigates the use of robotic swarms for autonomous environment mapping, with the aim of generating maps before emergency personnel arrive at the scene. We introduce BICLARE, a lightweight exploration algorithm inspired by ant-colony pheromone-based communication and navigation. BICLARE employs a confidence model to estimate cell occupancy within a map and optimizes target selection based on travel time and battery estimates to improve efficiency. The algorithm is designed to run efficiently on low-cost hardware. The performance of BICLARE is validated through simulated experiments in diverse and dynamic environments, demonstrating accurate mapping and robust coverage even in the presence of noise and uncertainty. Field trials further confirm the feasibility of the approach on low-cost COTS devices.

Article.Title: Rational design of nickel cobalt phosphate-sensitized tungsten-doped titania nanotubes (NiCoP@WTNT) for efficient light-assisted energy storage in flexible photo-supercapacitors
Article.Authors: Varnoosfaderani S.; Momeni M.
Article.Abstract: Developing efficient and low-cost systems for simultaneous solar energy harvesting and storage remains a critical challenge in next-generation energy technologies. Herein, we report a flexible photo-supercapacitor based on nickel–cobalt phosphate (NiCoP)-sensitized tungsten-doped titania nanotube arrays (NCP@WTNT) as a dual-function photoelectrode. The heterostructure combines enhanced light absorption, improved charge transport, and abundant redox-active sites, leading to enhanced photo-assisted energy storage. The optimized electrode exhibits a 4.1-fold increase in areal specific capacitance under illumination, from 9.20 to 37.54 mF cm −2 , demonstrating its effective photoresponse. Flexible devices fabricated from this material show rapid self-charging behavior, stable cycling performance, and good mechanical stability under different bending conditions. In addition, photocharging without an external bias and stable electrochemical performance under illumination demonstrate the feasibility of integrating solar energy harvesting and storage within a single device. By coupling bimetallic phosphate chemistry with tungsten-doped titania nanotube architectures, this work provides an effective strategy for improving the performance of flexible photo-supercapacitors. The results demonstrate the potential of the NCP@WTNT architecture as a cost-effective platform for integrated solar energy conversion and storage, offering opportunities for self-powered, light-responsive, and flexible energy storage devices for wearable and portable electronics.

Article.Title: Classification of real plastic waste using machine learning-assisted laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Kang J.; Lee J.; Bak M.; Im S.; Kwon S.
Article.Abstract: Plastic type classification using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) was evaluated using actual waste samples under non-optimized experimental conditions designed to approximate laser-sample variability encountered in industrial operation. The study addresses challenges in plastic sorting crucial for enhancing recycling efficiency and mitigating $$\:{co}_{2}$$ emissions and environmental harm from plastic waste overflow. Held-out testing using physically separate real-waste specimens was performed using data from standard materials for modeling and data from real waste for the test. The target plastic types were polypropylene, polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, and low-density polyethylene, which are major types of plastic waste. Plastic sorting was assisted by two machine-learning techniques: principal component analysis and k-nearest neighbors. Twenty-three pre-processes and seven variable selection methods were examined to enhance accuracy. The synergistic impact of preprocessing and variable selection was evident, elevating accuracy from 0.617 to 1.00. This study demonstrates the potential of machine learning-assisted LIBS for real plastic waste classification, emphasizing the importance of relevant wavelength selection.

Article.Title: Enhanced private set union from secret-shared private membership test
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Kim J.; Son Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Private Set Union (PSU) is a critical cryptographic tool, but designing protocols that are efficient and secure against recent threats, such as during-execution leakage, remains a challenge. The dominant approach to avoid such leakage is over Cuckoo hashing paradigm, which has led to increasingly complex designs that require multiple layers of costly cryptographic patches. Furthermore, there has been reported an additional vulnerability that broadly affects Cuckoo hashing based PSU protocols, rendering even these enhanced solutions vulnerable. In this work, we depart from this complex paradigm and introduce a new PSU protocol that is simple, efficient, and secure against known during-execution leakage and hashing-related leakage without relying on Cuckoo Hashing. At the core of our design, we propose a novel and highly efficient construction of secret-shared Private Membership Test (ss-PMT), which is enabled by the use of a modern, Multi-Party Computation (MPC)-friendly Alternating Moduli pseudorandom function (PRF). Our protocol achieves linear complexity, and our implementation outperforms prior state-of-the-art enhanced PSUs (ePSUs) by 6.58 to 6.74x across various set sizes and network settings. Our results show that it is possible to achieve robust security and superior performance in PSU through a fundamentally simpler and more direct design, offering a cleaner blueprint for future private set operations.

Article.Title: Factors associated with quality of life in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Kheradmand K.; Fathnezhad-Kazemi A.; Habashizadeh N.; Milanchian N.
Article.Abstract: Quality of life (QoL) is an important patient-centered outcome in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Psychosocial and self-management factors, including Perception of illness, illness acceptance, self-care behaviors, and perceived social support, have been associated with QoL, but their relative associations remain insufficiently understood. This study examined these associations among patients with T2DM. We conducted a cross-sectional study among 305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Data were collected using standardized questionnaires assessing general quality of life (SF12), illness acceptance, Perception of illness, self-care behaviors, and perceived social support. We used descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation coefficients, and linear regression analyses. The mean quality-of-life score was 32.91 (SD = 7.49), indicating a moderate level of QoL. Men reported significantly higher QoL than women (34.48 vs. 31.63, P = 0.001). Significant differences were also observed by educational level ( P < 0.001) and family income ( P = 0.002). Quality of life was positively correlated with illness acceptance ( r = 0.565, P < 0.001), Perception of illness ( r = 0.579, P < 0.001), self-care behaviors ( r = 0.284, P < 0.001), and perceived social support ( r = 0.357, P = 0.001). In the multiple variable models, Perception of illness (β = 0.380, P < 0.001), illness acceptance (β = 0.359, P < 0.001), and perceived social support (β = 0.147, P < 0.001) were significantly associated with QoL, whereas self-care behaviors were not (β = 0.024, P = 0.604). The model explained 47.5% of the variance in QoL. Exploratory regression-based analyses indicated indirect statistical associations of Perception of illness and perceived social support with quality of life through illness acceptance. Perception of illness, illness acceptance, and perceived social support were significantly associated with quality of life among patients with T2DM. The findings suggest that interventions aimed at improving patients’ understanding and acceptance of their illness, alongside strengthening social support networks, may contribute substantially to enhancing quality of life. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to confirm the causal pathways identified in this study.

Article.Title: Effects and dose-response relationship of core strength training on balance performance in adolescent athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Liu P.; Yan J.
Article.Abstract: Core strength training (CST) is widely prescribed to improve balance performance, yet its dose-response relationship in adolescent athletes has not been quantified. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of parallel-group randomized controlled trials evaluating CST versus control on balance outcomes in adolescent athletes aged 10–19 years. Six databases were searched from inception to 30 April 2026. Hedges’ g values were pooled under random-effects models; six training parameters were examined by univariate meta-regression, and restricted cubic splines were used to model dose-response relationships. Thirteen RCTs ( n = 337) were included. CST produced a moderate-to-large improvement in balance performance (g = 0.84, 95% CI 0.38–1.30, p < 0.001), with larger effects for dynamic (g = 1.01) than static (g = 0.39) balance. Session duration was the only parameter showing a significant non-linear dose-response relationship ( p < 0.001), with effects peaking at 31–45 min per session. Certainty of evidence was low (dynamic) to very low (static) by GRADE. A trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis attenuated the pooled estimate (g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.10–1.10) but it remained statistically significant. CST was associated with improved balance in adolescent athletes, with session durations of 31–45 min yielding the largest effects; this dose-response finding is exploratory and requires prospective confirmation.

Article.Title: A prognostic model to predict the risk of cesarean delivery after induction of labour: development, validation, and clinical utility
Article.Authors: Mekonnen E.; Coenen S.
Article.Abstract: Induction of labour (IoL) is an increasingly common obstetric procedure aimed at artificially stimulating labour. However, cesarean delivery could occur due to various complications associated with the procedure. Evaluating the risk of cesarean delivery after IoL is crucial for making informed decisions between IoL and pre-labour cesarean delivery. A prospective cohort study was conducted at the University of Gondar Specialized and Tertiary Hospital, Ethiopia, involving 628 pregnant women. Univariable and multivariable analyses were used to identify predictors, and model selection was based on the log-likelihood ratio test and Bayesian information criterion. Model accuracy was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and a calibration plot. Internal validation was performed through bootstrapping, and the clinical utility of the model was evaluated using decision curve analysis. A simplified risk score and web calculator were developed for practical use. The rate of cesarean delivery (CS) was 51%. The final model included three predictors: parity, history of stillbirth, and Bishop score. The model exhibited good discrimination (AUC = 0.82; 95% CI: 0.79 to 0.85) and calibration. The model demonstrated similar performance (AUC: 0.82) to the original model in the validation sample, indicating a low risk of overfitting. Decision curve analysis demonstrated a higher net benefit for treatment decisions guided by the model. The risk prediction model, based on parity, history of stillbirth, and Bishop score, demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility in stratifying women undergoing IoL based on their risk of CS. This model has the potential to guide clinicians in decision-making regarding IoL, thereby improving labour outcomes.

Article.Title: Simultaneous fermentation of beetroot juice and pulp with water kefir grain – a sustainable approach for zero waste
Article.Authors: Jaeger A.; Sahin A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reducing food waste represents a challenge in the transformation of our food system towards sustainable practices. Amongst these losses are nutritious by-products, like vegetable pulp during juicing. A simultaneous fermentation of beetroot juice and pulp was performed using water kefir grains, a consortium of lactic acid bacteria (LAB), acetic acid bacteria (AAB), and yeast (Y), to transform waste (pulp) into value (ingredient) with fermented juice as a valuable ready-to-drink by-product. During fermentation an increase in LAB-, AAB-, and Y-cell count occurred, indicating the suitability of beetroot as a substrate. The pH decreased from 5.78 to 3.89 in beetroot juice, and from 5.35 to 4.35 in beetroot pulp. The TTA increased by 9.87 ml 0.1 M NaOH in juice and by 6.47 ml in pulp. Fermented beetroot juice retained its high foaming capacity (108–114%) but showed reduced foam stability (-49%). Total polyphenol content (TPC) slightly decreased. Pulp showed stable foam stability up to 48 h of fermentation followed by a decline. Water- and oil-holding capacity of pulp increased, and TPC was elevated. The outcome of this study demonstrate that simultaneous fermentation of juice and pulp using water kefir grains is a suitable process to reduce waste by using minimal resources and time.

Article.Title: Distribution of movable fluid and its influencing factors in super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs: a case study of Chang 6 member, Wuqi area, Ordos Basin
Article.Authors: Zhong H.; Yang Z.; Zhang Y.; Jia X.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The influences of multiple factors on movable fluid saturation remain inadequately constrained for continental tight sandstones. Moreover, comparative studies on the occurrence characteristics of movable fluids between tight sandstone reservoirs and super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs are relatively scarce. This research takes Chang 6 member in the Wuqi area as an example, and through a series of experiments, analyzes the distribution patterns and influencing factors of movable fluids. The results show that the super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs in this research have porosity values ranging from 8.78% to 16.12%, permeability values ranging from 0.094 mD to 2.453 mD, and the values of movable fluid saturation ranging from 31.38% to 62.67%. All the samples can be broadly divided into two types, type I samples have higher content of feldspar, more developed dissolved pores, and generally locate in middle part or top part of thicker sand bodies. For all the samples, permeability, peak pore-throat radius, and average pore-throat radius exhibit strong mutual correlations, which may be associated with the development of large pore-throats, and all show a strong correlation with movable fluid saturation. Although the movable fluid occurs in pore-throat with a wide size range, the development of micron pore-throats is the key factor influencing the values of movable fluid saturation, differentiating super-low to ultra-low permeability reservoirs and tight sandstone reservoirs.

Article.Title: Large-scale chromatin topological remodeling accompanies hepatocellular carcinoma progression
Article.Authors: Jiang F.; Zhang Z.; Chen Z.; Xu S.; Cai S.; Liu J.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multistep hepatocarcinogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is associated with dynamic alterations in chromatin topology. Previous studies have primarily compared three-dimensional (3D) genomic structure between tumor and normal adjacent tissues, largely overlooking the role of cirrhosis, a major precancerous lesion and risk factor in HCC pathogenesis. Here, we systematically analyzed chromatin conformation changes across paired tumor, cirrhotic, and normal adjacent tissues to identify stage-specific structural alterations during hepatocarcinogenesis. We constructed high-resolution 3D genomic maps using pore chromatin conformation capture (Pore-C), complemented by chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), RNA-seq, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS), to investigate key chromatin topological remodeling events in HCC development. Significant alterations in A/B compartments, topologically associating domains (TADs), and chromatin loops were observed across different tissue types and patients. Comparisons between normal liver and cirrhotic tissues revealed predominant enhancement of inter‑chromosomal interactions; comparisons between cirrhotic and HCC tissues showed predominant elevation of intra‑chromosomal interactions. Across normal, cirrhotic and HCC disease states, we observed compaction of the highly active A compartments and concomitant decompaction of the silent B compartments. In general, both cirrhosis and tumor exhibited more transcriptionally active compartment states compared to normal adjacent tissues. TAD size and numbers were more conserved within tissues from the same individual than across different patients with the same tissue type. Few TAD boundaries were gained or lost consistently. Integrative analysis with H3K27ac identified genomic regions co-occurring with loop formation and enhancer activation. In normal adjacent tissue, the CXCL12 gene locus maintained a well-defined chromatin loop structure that was disrupted in tumor tissues. Corresponding RNA-seq analysis confirmed significant downregulation of CXCL12 expression in tumors. By integrating SVs identified from Pore-C datasets and the Chinese Liver Cancer Atlas (CLCA), we identified SV-induced neo-loops, which were more prone to transcriptional alterations and could promote cell proliferation by activating choline metabolism and phospholipase D signaling pathways. Comparing the three disease states, cirrhosis represents an intermediate state with reversed patterns of chromosomal interactions relative to normal liver and HCC. Although canonical A/B compartment shifts involved limited genomic regions, we consistently observed progressive compaction of compartment A and decompaction of compartment B. Compared with normal tissues, HCC exhibits the disruption of CXCL12 chromatin loop and a significant reduction in enhancer signals, accompanied by a marked downregulation of CXCL12 expression in tumor tissues. SV-induced neo-loops were key events influencing gene expression. The proteins encoded by these genes are highly involved in homologous recombination, and drove cell proliferation via specific signaling pathways. Our findings revealed that stage-specific chromatin structural changes and provided novel insights into the mechanisms of gene dysregulation in hepatocarcinogenesis.

Article.Title: A noise-aware hardware-software co-design framework for real-time EEG-based stress detection across heterogeneous embedded platforms
Article.Authors: Zia Z.; Amin F.; Qureshi M.; Fatima M.; Rahman J.; Mashal A.; Hamd Z.; Almudaimeegh L.; Ali B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deploying EEG-based stress detection on embedded hardware demands that the signal processing pipeline and classification algorithm to be jointly co-designed with the resource constraints of the target platform, rather than optimized in isolation. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design framework centered on a noise-aware feature selection strategy that jointly optimizes three competing objectives: maximization of mutual information with respect to stress labels, robustness of features under degraded signal-to-noise conditions, and minimization of inter-feature redundancy. Applying this strategy reduces an initial 312-dimensional EEG feature space to a compact set of 47 discriminative features, yielding a 3.8 MB Random Forest model that generalizes across deployment targets without platform-specific retraining. The framework is validated on six heterogeneous embedded systems spanning a wide capability spectrum from FPGA-accelerated SoCs to commodity microcontrollers costing as little as $4 demonstrating that a single trained model can be deployed across divergent hardware architectures while preserving classification fidelity. This paper aims to balance algorithmic accuracy with the hardware constraints by proposing a hardware-software co-design system that allows the real-time, energy-efficient monitoring of stress in small embedded systems. In this direction, we initially develop a strict software pipeline, which integrates robust preprocessing methods, such as Independent Component Analysis and adaptive filtering, along with a noise-sensitive feature-selection strategy comprising 47 dimensions.. Based on this unified methodology, there is an ensemble classification model which achieves a high accuracy of 99.57% to detect exam induced stress. We explored deployment of six non-homogenous platforms, including a desktop CPU (HP G10 450, Intel Core i7-1355U), a hybrid Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)FPGA ARM system on chip (SoC)SoC (PYNQ-Z2, Zynq-7020), an embedded ARM processor (Raspberry Pi 4), and two resource-constrained Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) (Tang Nano 9 K, ICESugar iCE40UP5K), and an IoT microcontroller (ESP32). An important observation is that the classical Random Forest models (3.8 MB) are edge compatible.. The PYNQ-Z2 has a 7.9 speedup and 48.1 energy efficiency improvement with 99.57% accuracy with hardware acceleration. The hybrid ICE Sugar FPGA + ESP32 system provides 92.7% energy efficiency with a 99.57% classification accuracy and 19-h battery backup on a 5000 mAh battery. The standalone S4 ESP32 microcontroller alone in 35-h of battery life achieves an accuracy of 99.21%, showing that stress monitoring at a clinical level is possible on a commodity microcontroller. These findings establish a comprehensive methodology for signal acquisition and silicon implementation of enabling technologies, facilitating the development of on-demand wearable neurotechnology capable of continuous mental health monitoring across educational, clinical, and occupational settings.

Article.Title: Development of a sustained-release PLGA–MFSC nanoparticle formulation and its long-term anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects in osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Park J.; Min K.; Lee I.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to develop a PLGA-based nanoparticle formulation for the sustained delivery of membrane-free stem cell (MFSC) derived from human adipose-derived stem cells and to evaluate its anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective efficacy in an osteoarthritis model. Although MFSC has emerged as a promising cell-free therapeutic approach for osteoarthritis treatment, its rapid clearance and limited retention following intra-articular administration may reduce its long-term therapeutic efficacy. To overcome these limitations, MFSC was encapsulated into poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles using a double-emulsion solvent evaporation method to establish a sustained-release delivery system. The morphological characteristics and in vitro release behavior of the formulation were analyzed. The results showed that PLGA–MFSC nanoparticles exhibited a spherical morphology in the nano–submicron size range. In a preliminary in vitro release assessment conducted at room temperature, PLGA–MFSC showed prolonged and non-linear release of the MMP-9 analytical marker over 31 days without a pronounced initial burst, with a cumulative release of 67.2%. An osteoarthritis model induced by monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) in rats was used, and the efficacy of PLGA–MFSC was evaluated via intra-articular administration. Histological analysis revealed that the PLGA–MFSC group exhibited reduced cartilage surface damage and improved chondrocyte organization compared with the control group. Furthermore, immunohistochemical analysis showed reduced expression of inflammatory mediators, including iNOS, COX-2, and IL-6. Immunofluorescence staining revealed restored ZO-1 expression in RAW264.7 macrophages alongside suppression of TLR4, IL-6, and NF-κB signaling activity. In addition, serum CRP and MMP-9 levels in the PLGA–MFSC (W2) group were reduced by 28.5% and 53.2%, respectively, compared with those in the MIA control group, indicating attenuation of osteoarthritis-associated inflammatory responses. These results suggest that PLGA–MFSC has potential as a delivery system for MFSC-associated components and exerts anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective effects in an experimental osteoarthritis model. Therefore, PLGA–MFSC may represent a promising local delivery strategy for MFSC-based osteoarthritis therapy by combining the biological activity of MFSC with the delivery properties of PLGA nanoparticles.

Article.Title: High-performance asymmetric coin cell supercapacitors utilizing N-doped graphene oxide/iron-polyporphyrin electrodes
Article.Authors: Norouzhaji S.; Baboli M.; Taherimehr M.; Lashkenari M.
Article.Abstract: With the increasing demand for efficient energy storage systems, the development of advanced electrode materials for supercapacitors has attracted considerable attention. In this study, a novel nitrogen-doped graphene oxide/iron-polyporphyrin (NGO/Fe-POP) nanocomposite was synthesized through an ultrasonic-assisted method for use as an advanced electrode material for supercapacitors. Among the investigated compositions (NGO75/Fe-POP25, NGO50/Fe-POP50, and NGO25/Fe-POP75), the NGO25/Fe-POP75 electrode exhibited the best electrochemical performance owing to the synergistic interaction between NGO and Fe-POP, which provided abundant redox-active sites, accelerated charge transfer, and improved electrolyte ion diffusion. Furthermore, the reduced Warburg impedance suggested improved electrolyte ion diffusion within the porous electrode structure. The NGO25/Fe-POP75 electrode exhibited a specific capacitance of 733 F g −1 at a current density of 1 A g −1 , with an energy density of 36.65 Wh kg −1 and a power density of 300 W kg −1 . Furthermore, an asymmetric coin-cell supercapacitor was assembled using NGO25/Fe-POP75 as the positive electrode and GO as the negative electrode. The device achieved a specific capacitance of 234.5 F g −1 , an energy density of 32.56 Wh kg −1 , and a power density of 174.94 W kg −1 at a current density of 0.35 A g −1 . Moreover, it retained 70.93% of its initial capacitance after 1000 consecutive charge/discharge cycles at 1.4 A g −1 and successfully powered a 2 V light-emitting diode (LED), demonstrating the promising potential of the NGO/Fe-POP nanocomposite for advanced supercapacitor applications.

Article.Title: Renal microcirculatory impairment on contrast enhanced ultrasound predicts persistent renal impairment in cardiogenic shock patients receiving venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
Article.Authors: Chen W.; Wang B.; Pan H.; Pei M.; Chen S.; Wei Y.; Zhou Y.; Wu R.; Qiu G.; Duan W.; Tang Y.; Chen X.; Li Z.; Qin Q.; Liu J.; Liao H.; Zhang L.; Zhong Z.; Meng L.; Li K.; Lyu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is one of the most frequent complications in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) receiving veno‑arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Microcirculation dysfunction is an important mechanism and it can be effectively evaluated by contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). This study aimed to investigate the association between CEUS-derived parameters and the progression of persistent renal impairment following AKI in this population. This prospective observational study involved 127 CS patients receiving VA-ECMO and developing AKI within 48 h. All patients underwent CEUS at 48 h after ECMO initiation. The study endpoint was the non-recovery of renal function at the 7, 30 and 90 days after ECMO initiation. CEUS-derived parameters included time to peak (TTP), rise time (RT) and time from peak to one half (TPH). Logistic regression was used to identify the correlation between these parameters and study endpoints. Additionally, seven machine learning (ML) algorithms were employed to validate the comprehensive predictive power of CEUS parameters. The proportions of AKI non-recovery at 7, 30 and 90 days were 67.72%, 37.79%, and 23.62% respectively. The univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis for the clinical outcomes demonstrated increased TTP, RT and TPH in both cortex and medulla were associated with increased risk of AKI non-recovery at 7, 30, and 90 days (all P < 0.05). All ML algorithms demonstrated acceptable discrimination in predicting endpoints. CEUS may be a valuable tool for assessing renal microcirculation alterations. CEUS-derived indices were effective in predicting the progression of renal impairment after AKI.

Article.Title: Predicting anemia risk in Iranian adults without diagnostic blood indices: an interpretable machine learning approach integrating dietary, clinical, and non-diagnostic laboratory patterns
Article.Authors: Pourmahmoudi A.; Malekzadeh J.; Noormohammadi A.; Salehnasab C.; Ghaderzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Anemia remains a major public-health burden, disproportionately affecting adults of reproductive age. In the original submission, an interpretable machine-learning framework trained to predict anemia status in Iranian adults achieved a near-perfect AUC (≈ 1.00) using XGBoost; closer methodological scrutiny of this result identified two critical flaws that undermine its validity as a measure of genuine predictive power: (i) hemoglobin-defining hematological indices (HGB, HCT, RBC, MCV, MCH) were included as predictors, creating circular prediction, and (ii) feature selection was performed on the full dataset before train/test splitting, causing data leakage. This revised analysis removes both flaws: diagnosis-defining indices were excluded from the predictor set, and the entire pipeline — feature selection, SMOTE oversampling, and hyperparameter tuning — was rebuilt inside a leakage-free pipeline confined strictly to each training fold. Twelve supervised algorithms were compared on an independent, held-out test set ( n = 641 of 3,203 records). Logistic Regression achieved the best discrimination (AUC = 0.8625, 95% bootstrap CI 0.8168–0.9053; Recall = 0.7738, 95% CI 0.6854–0.8589; F1 = 0.5350, 95% CI 0.4561–0.6081; Accuracy = 0.8237), clearly outperforming a simple demographic baseline (AUC = 0.5284). The drop in AUC from ≈ 1.00 to 0.86 after removing the diagnosis-defining indices empirically confirms that the original near-perfect performance was an artifact of circular prediction and data leakage. SHAP analysis of the corrected model shows that, alongside dietary and lifestyle variables (dairy-product intake, carbohydrate intake, household-cleaning activity), several non-diagnostic hematologic markers (RDW-CV, platelet count, WBC count, PDW) remain influential — an important nuance discussed below, since these still require venipuncture even though they are not part of the anemia diagnostic criterion. The corrected framework offers a more honest, generalizable, and clinically defensible foundation for anemia risk screening in Iranian adults.

Article.Title: Ecophysiological and anatomical variation in Setaria parviflora (Poaceae) between contrasting environments in the Brazilian Cerrado
Article.Authors: Sousa M.; Sanches M.; Welker C.; Boselli M.; Alonso A.; Marzinek J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Environmental heterogeneity can be associated with substantial phenotypic variation in plant populations, but the integration of ecophysiological and anatomical variation under natural field conditions remains poorly understood for many tropical grasses. Setaria parviflora is a perennial C 4 grass occurring in contrasting environments of the Brazilian Cerrado. We compared ecophysiological and anatomical traits of populations from a preserved palm swamp and an adjacent dry disturbed area. Net CO₂ assimilation, water-use efficiency, and instantaneous carboxylation efficiency were higher in plants from the dry disturbed area, whereas stomatal conductance, transpiration, relative water content, and specific leaf area did not differ between populations. Root aerenchyma area and vascular cylinder area were greater in individuals from the palm swamp, whereas the number of xylem poles was greater in the dry disturbed area. Culm vessel element area was greater in the dry disturbed area, whereas abaxial stomatal density was higher in the palm swamp. Principal component analyses showed clearer differentiation between populations for physiological than for anatomical traits, while the environmental PCA summarized the distinct field conditions recorded during the two sampling campaigns. Together, these results show that anatomical and ecophysiological traits vary differently between natural populations of S. parviflora under contrasting local conditions, highlighting the value of integrating structural and functional traits when assessing phenotypic variation in field populations.

Article.Title: Prioritizing environmental anxieties and mitigation strategies across eco-anxiety, climate, health, economic, and social domains
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Hanif M.; Li Y.; Afridi M.; Zahra Z.
Article.Abstract: This study assesses environmental anxieties and prioritizes strategies to address them using an integrated expert-based multi-criteria framework. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Fuzzy TOPSIS are combined to identify, weight, and rank sub-anxieties across five domains: eco-anxiety, climate change anxiety, health, economic, and social anxiety. AHP results indicate that climate-related anxiety received the highest expert-assigned weight, followed by eco-anxiety, with economic, health, and social anxieties receiving comparatively lower priority within the evaluation framework. At the sub-domain level, helplessness in mitigating climate risks, intergenerational uncertainty, and fear of worsening disasters emerge as the highest-ranked concerns within the expert evaluation. Fuzzy TOPSIS prioritizes the evaluated strategies accordingly: nature-based prescribing and targeted cognitive-behavioral and acceptance-based therapies receive the highest rankings, followed by structured media diets for information hygiene; psychoeducation, mindfulness, health-protection planning, and financial-resilience counseling form a second tier of support. Sensitivity analysis across alternative weighting scenarios indicates ranking stability, supporting the robustness of the prioritization framework. The findings offer a structured prioritization framework for environmental policy and management by highlighting expert-assessed priority areas, including clinically grounded treatments, trusted information systems, health-protective infrastructure, and economic coping supports. These priorities provide a basis for future empirical validation regarding their potential contribution to reducing distress and supporting adaptive environmental governance.

Article.Title: Small idiopathic full-thickness macular holes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Marolo P.; Fallico M.; Abbasi M.; Borrelli E.; Caselgrandi P.; Parisi G.; Trunfio T.; Elfalah M.; Toro M.; Reibaldi M.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the anatomical and visual outcomes of three vitrectomy techniques—internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling, inverted flap, and no peeling—for the treatment of idiopathic small full-thickness macular holes (FTMH; ≤250 μm). A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Medline were searched up to April 2025. Eligible studies reported outcomes of small FTMH treated with vitrectomy using one of the three specified techniques, with a minimum follow-up of 3 months. Primary endpoints were FTMH closure rate and change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR). Subgroup, meta-regression and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate technique-specific estimates and the influence of baseline BCVA. Eleven non-randomized studies comprising 957 eyes were included. The overall FTMH closure rate was 96.6% (95% CI: 93.2–98.3%; I² = 61.6%, τ² = 0.681, p = 0.0036). Closure rates were 98.4% for ILM peeling, 97.6% for inverted flap, and 86.5% for no peeling (test for differences between pooled technique subgroups: p < 0.0001; I² = 0% in all subgroups). The pooled BCVA improvement was 0.40 logMAR (95% CI: 0.36–0.44; I² = 64.4%, τ² = 0.0027, p = 0.002). Mean gains were 0.45 logMAR for no peeling, 0.41 for ILM peeling, and 0.39 for inverted flap (test for differences between pooled technique subgroups: p = 0.37). Exploratory meta-regression suggested that poorer baseline BCVA may be associated with a lower likelihood of closure. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the main findings. ILM peeling showed the highest pooled closure estimate, while visual improvement did not differ significantly across technique subgroups. Given the predominantly observational and indirect evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and do not establish comparative superiority.

Article.Title: A multi-level mental health intervention using Bronfenbrenner’s theory and PRECEDE-PROCEED to improve adolescent help-seeking and life satisfaction
Article.Authors: Zare E.; Karimi M.; Kaveh M.; Ghahremani L.
Article.Abstract: Schools require well-designed mental health education programs to address adolescent hesitation in help-seeking. This mixed-methods study evaluated a promotion program integrating Bronfenbrenner’s socio-ecological theory into the PRECEDE-PROCEED model to improve help-seeking behaviors and life satisfaction among Iranian female adolescents. Following qualitative focus groups to identify barriers, a randomized controlled trial was conducted with 174 high school girls aged 15–17 (intervention = 86; control = 88). The intervention group completed a six-session educational program. Data analysis using Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) revealed significant overall Group × Time interactions across all outcome variables ( p < 0.001). The most substantial intervention effect was observed for multidimensional students’ life satisfaction (MSLS), which showed a notable positive change (B = 0.888, 95% CI: 0.341 to 1.434, p < 0.001). Help-seeking intention (HSI) and recognition of personal need for professional psychological help (RPNPPH) also improved considerably (B = -0.542 and B = -0.370, respectively, p < 0.001). Perceived social support (MSPSS) and mental health literacy (MHL) demonstrated significant enhancements (B = -0.839 and B = -0.521, respectively, p < 0.001). Although the main effect of group was not statistically significant for actual help-seeking behavior (HSB) and ways of coping (WOC) (B = 0.433, p = 0.072), the group-by-time interaction for both outcomes was highly significant ( p < 0.001), indicating that the intervention group showed distinct longitudinal improvements compared to the control group. These findings indicate that structured multi-level educational interventions can effectively enhance female adolescents’ help-seeking behaviors and overall life satisfaction.

Article.Title: Effects of exercise interventions on mental health and social function reconstruction in individuals with substance use disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Chen X.; Tang Y.; Wang T.; Zou W.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of exercise interventions on mental health and social adaptation in individuals with substance use disorders (SUDs) to inform evidence-based physical/psychological rehabilitation and social reintegration. We retrieved randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Library, EBSCOhost, and Embase (inception to July 2026). Quality was assessed using Cochrane ROB 2.0; RevMan 5.4 analyzed heterogeneity and effect sizes and generated plots, with Stata 18 for sensitivity analyses. 13 RCTs (953 participants; sample size 20–70; intervention 2–6 months; mostly moderate-intensity exercise; controls: health education/standard care) were included. Exercise significantly improved depression ( SMD = − 1.15, 95% CI − 1.87 to − 0.43, P = 0.002), anxiety ( SMD = − 0.68 , 95% CI − 1.19 to − 0.18 , P = 0.008), sleep quality ( MD = − 2.93 , 95% CI − 5.13 to − 0.73 , P = 0.009), degree of craving (SMD = − 0.43, 95% CI − 0.68 to − 0.19, p < 0.001 ), and relapse tendency ( SMD = − 1.73, 95% CI − 2.83 to − 0.63, P = 0.002). Significant enhancements were also observed in social function domains: physical function ( SMD = 0.70, 95% CI 0.11 to 1.29, P = 0.02), psychological function ( SMD = 0.71, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.95, p < 0.001), social adaptation ( SMD = 0.69, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.96, p < 0.001), and overall scores ( SMD = 0.68, 95% CI 0.30 to 1.05, p < 0.001), although the improvement in withdrawal symptoms did not reach statistical significance ( SMD = 0.59, 95% CI − 0.07 to 1.25, P = 0.08), likely reflecting the complex neurobiological nature of withdrawal and its limited short-term responsiveness to exercise alone. The available evidence suggests potential benefits of moderate-intensity mind–body and aerobic exercise on mental health and social functioning in individuals with SUDs, pending confirmation in larger, pre-registered RCTs with objective endpoints.

Article.Title: Adaptive search-space reduction and partial shading detection for high-efficiency MPPT in photovoltaic systems
Article.Authors: Rouabah D.; Azri M.; Ramli M.; Lekbir A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an integrated maximum power point tracking (MPPT) framework for photovoltaic systems operating under uniform and partial shading conditions. The framework incorporates a partial shading detection technique (PSDT) that simultaneously identifies the operating condition and adaptively reduces the search space by eliminating regions that cannot contain the global maximum power point (GMPP) and avoiding redundant sampling, thereby accelerating the subsequent MPPT process. Based on the identified condition, an enhanced divide-and-conquer algorithm with ternary ratio (EDCA-TR), designed to avoid unnecessary inner-point evaluations, is deployed under uniform shading conditions, while a modified JAYA (M-JAYA) algorithm is employed under partial shading conditions. Unlike conventional iteration-based metaheuristic approaches, the proposed M-JAYA employs particle-based updates that immediately incorporate newly acquired search information, together with an adaptive search-space confinement mechanism based on iteration count and particle power information. Experimental validation under seven shading patterns demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an average tracking time of 1.86 s and an average tracking efficiency of 95.27%, outperforming the Hybrid, improved coot optimization algorithm (ICOA), and improved water cycle optimization algorithm (IWCO) benchmark methods. Moreover, the proposed framework achieves an average tracking energy loss of 3.45 W·s, representing a reduction of more than 50% compared with the benchmark methods. Repeated-run simulation analysis further demonstrates generally consistent performance despite the stochastic nature of the M-JAYA algorithm. Overall, the proposed framework improves convergence speed, tracking stability, and energy extraction by combining condition-dependent MPPT selection with adaptive search-space reduction and particle-based optimization.

Article.Title: Environmental noise exposure partially accounts for the association between socioeconomic status and neural encoding of speech
Article.Authors: Marcotti A.; Ianiszewski A.; Silva-Letelier C.; Fuentes-López E.; Savio G.; López V.
Article.Abstract: Socioeconomic status (SES) has been associated with variability in neural speech encoding as indexed by the frequency-following response (FFR), yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. Environmental noise exposure represents a plausible pathway, given its socioeconomic patterning and established effects on neurophysiology. This cross-sectional study examined whether environmental noise exposure mediates the association between SES and neural speech encoding. Forty-seven young adults with normal hearing underwent FFR recordings to a speech syllable presented in quiet and noise. SES was operationalized using a composite index derived from maternal education, household income, and school type. Environmental noise exposure was estimated using modeled noise maps and quantified across cumulative lifetime and age-specific developmental windows. Multilevel mediation analyses estimated total, direct, and indirect effects of SES on FFR timing, magnitude, and fidelity. Higher SES was associated with lower cumulative lifetime noise exposure. Cumulative lifetime noise exposure partially mediated SES-related differences in onset and transition timing and stimulus–response correlation, whereas no mediation was observed for age-specific windows or frequency-specific magnitude measures. These findings suggest that chronic environmental noise constitutes one pathway through which socioeconomic conditions shape auditory neural function, with effects reflecting long-term accumulation. Persistent direct SES effects indicate additional contributing pathways.

Article.Title: Correction: Documenting the occurrence of microbial carbonate deposits in Puerto Rico
Article.Authors: Rodríguez-Colón B.; Ramírez-Martínez W.; Chabrier-Alpi A.; Ríos-Velázquez C.; Martínez-Rivera N.; Baker G.; Hiripitiyage Y.; Sturm B.; Roberts J.
Article.Abstract: The original version of this Article contained errors in Figure 6. Specifically in Figure 6c, the x-axis title “Relative Abundance (%)” is present, but the numerical x-axis tick marks and labels are missing. They were erroneously omitted during the preparation of Figure 6. The stacked bar plots and underlying relative abundance data were and remain correct. The error is limited to the numerical percentage scale on the x-axis and does not affect the scientific results of the paper. The original Figure 6 appears below.

Article.Title: Metacognitive regulation of cognitive control to adjust choice accuracy in rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Lespart A.; Bénon J.; Daunizeau J.; Bouret S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Making the best choice in one situation is critical, but it relies on limited cognitive capacities. Numerous animal species adjust the amount of cognitive resources allocated to a decision using a trade-off between speed and accuracy, where decision time corresponds to an investment of cognitive control, which scales with the expected increase in reward. In humans, recent studies indicate that control allocation is regulated not only based upon its potential benefits, but also upon its potential cost, through a metacognitive monitoring process. Is it the case in other primates? We addressed this issue in rhesus monkeys with a detailed analysis of the relation among choice accuracy, choice difficulty and response time in a two-choice task. In contrast to typical demonstrations of speed-accuracy trade-off, we found higher choice accuracy in trials with faster response time, above and beyond choice difficulty. This relationship can be explained by a model of metacognitive decision monitoring where the cost of cognitive control is traded against confidence benefits. Thus, rhesus monkeys also seem to rely upon supervisory monitoring to modulate the amount of control exerted over their decision efficacy. This might drive future research on the evolution of cognitive and neurophysiological processes underlying decision making.

Article.Title: Decoding the ICU resistome: integron-mediated spread of blaIMP-85 and novel gene cassettes in XDR pathogens
Article.Authors: Abdelrazik M.; Gameel W.; Alsayed Y.; El-Demerdash A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) are critically compounded by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial pathogens. Mobile integrons act as pivotal site-specific recombination systems that facilitate the capture and horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of antimicrobial resistance determinants. This study aimed to characterize the molecular epidemiology, cassette array diversity, and clinical impact of plasmid-borne integrons ( intI1 , intI2 , and intI3 ) among bacterial isolates recovered from ICU patients in Egypt. A total of 153 non-duplicate clinical bacterial isolates were recovered from 117 ICU patients (50 monomicrobial and 67 polymicrobial specimens). Isolates were stratified into Gram-negative bacilli and Gram-positive cocci. Species identification and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) were performed using the VITEK® 2 system, Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion, and CLSI-compliant broth microdilution assays. Extrachromosomal plasmid DNA was extracted and screened for integrase genes and variable cassette regions via PCR, followed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing, restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) validation, and bioinformatic analysis. Statistical associations and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted $$p$$ -values were evaluated using R software (v4.3.3). Gram-negative isolates (n=116) comprised Klebsiella pneumoniae (49.1%, n= 57), Escherichia coli (37.1%, n= 43), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (11.2%, n= 13), Proteus mirabilis (1.7%, n= 2), and Serratia fonticola (0.9%, n=1). All Gram-positive isolates were identified as Staphylococcus aureus (n =37), with 100% exhibiting resistance to cefoxitin and oxacillin ( mecA -positive MRSA status). Isolates displayed elevated rates of MDR (49.2%) and extensive drug resistance (XDR; 27.0%), with high-level vancomycin resistance (VRSA) confirmed in 70.3% of S. aureus strains. Integron prevalence was significantly higher in Gram-negative isolates (91.3%) than in S. aureus (44.0%). Class 1 integrons ( intI1 ) predominated (52.1%), whereas intI2 (13.0%) and intI3 (17.4%) were restricted exclusively to Gram-negative species. Sanger sequencing confirmed the metallo- $$\beta $$ -lactamase allele bla IMP-85 (GenBank: PP663295) in P. aeruginosa , a novel tandem dfrA27 – aadA2 cassette structure (PP663294) in E. coli , and an extrachromosomal sat2 – aadA1 array (PP663297) harbored by S. aureus , confirming cross-gram-class interspecies HGT. Non-synonymous point mutations within aadA1 , sat2 , and intI3 indicated active genetic drift. Correlation analysis demonstrated that total Gram-negative integron carriage strongly predicted XDR phenotypes ( p = 0.69, p < 0.01) and resistance to levofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, gentamicin, and imipenem. Plasmid-borne integrons are strongly associated with MDR and XDR profiles in critical care pathogens. The identification of functional, plasmid-located intI1 arrays bridging Gram-negative species and S. aureus underscores the urgent necessity of integrating molecular integron surveillance alongside routine AST to combat plasmid-mediated resistance dissemination in ICUs.

Article.Title: Characterization of the complete chloroplast genomes of three grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi Macfad.) cultivars
Article.Authors: Singh N.; Sétamou M.; Kunta M.; Mendu V.
Article.Abstract: Chloroplast genomes (plastomes) are valuable resources for understanding evolutionary relationships and tracing maternal lineages. Citrus is a genus shaped by extensive hybridization, introgression, and complex domestication histories, which complicate phylogenetic signal in the nuclear genome. Here, we present complete, high-confidence chloroplast genome assemblies for three red-fleshed grapefruit cultivars, Rio Red (RR), Ruby Red (RU), and Texas Red (TX), assembled from PacBio HiFi whole-genome sequencing data without dedicated organellar enrichment. All three plastomes were recovered as single-contig circular molecules of 160,185 bp exhibiting the canonical angiosperm quadripartite structure with identical partition sizes: a large single-copy region (LSC) of 87,790 bp, a small single-copy region (SSC) of 18,395 bp, and two inverted repeats (IRs) of 27,000 bp each. Annotation identified 113 unique genes per plastome, comprising 79 protein-coding genes, 30 tRNAs, and 4 rRNAs, including the two-intron genes clpP1 and pafI and the trans-spliced rps12 . All three cultivars share fully identical plastome architectures, gene content, codon-usage profiles, and repeat landscapes dominated by short A/T-rich mononucleotide cpSSRs, confirming a common maternal plastid haplotype. IR boundary organization was conserved, with only minor 2–4 bp variation at the SSC/IRb junction in Texas Red. Pairwise whole-plastome comparisons using MUMmer4 confirmed zero sequence variation among cultivars and between each cultivar and pummelo, while comparisons against sweet orange revealed 131–137 variant sites. A maximum-likelihood phylogeny placed all three cultivars in a strongly supported clade sister to pummelo.

Article.Title: Retraction Note: Loss of PTEN-assisted G2/M checkpoint impedes homologous recombination repair and enhances radio-curability and PARP inhibitor treatment response in prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Mansour W.; Tennstedt P.; Volquardsen J.; Oing C.; Kluth M.; Hube-Magg C.; Borgmann K.; Simon R.; Petersen C.; Dikomey E.; Rothkamm K.
Article.Abstract: Following publication, concerns were raised that the PTEN blot in Figure 1B duplicates the CtIP expression blot in Figure 4B of a prior publication with overlapping authorship [ 1 ]. Further investigation found irregularities with other Figures including 1B, 4A, 4F, 6A–B, and S3, which the Authors could not satisfactorily explain. The Editors therefore no longer have confidence in the results and conclusions presented in this Article.

Article.Title: Closed-form solution and parametric study on lateral dynamic response of pile-type bridge piers resting on cement-soil composite pipe piles
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Zhu W.; Dai G.; Ji Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper develops a closed-form analytical framework for the lateral dynamic interaction between a pile-type bridge (PTB) pier and a cement-soil composite (CC) pipe pile in viscoelastic soil, based on Timoshenko beam theory. The derived analytical solutions are rigorously verified through two parallel approaches: comparison with published theoretical results and cross-validation against PLAXIS 3D numerical simulations. On this basis, systematic parametric analyses are conducted to quantify the influences of key parameters of the PTB pier, cement-soil pile and PHC pipe pile on the lateral dynamic response of the coupled system. The results reveal that piers with smaller heights deliver stronger low-frequency load-bearing performance but face a higher risk of resonance under high-frequency excitation, whereas taller piers can effectively postpone the occurrence of resonant peaks. Enlarging the reinforcement radius and elastic modulus of the cement-soil pile, as well as increasing the outer radius and elastic modulus of the inner PHC pipe pile, all improve the lateral vibration resistance of the entire coupled system. In particular, increasing the structural mass at the pier top amplifies the horizontal inertial force of the system, which adversely affects the lateral vibration resistance of the coupled pile-pier system.

Article.Title: A two-stage deep learning approach for multiclass DGA-based malware communication detection and classification in DoH network traffic
Article.Authors: Abdumalik H.; Hou W.; Zhuang Y.; Ali M.
Article.Abstract: The adoption of DNS over HTTPS (DoH) has substantially improved user privacy by encrypting DNS queries, but it has also introduced new opportunities for attackers to hide Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA)-based malware communications. In this study, we propose a novel two-stage deep learning framework that integrates an Autoencoder (AE) with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for detecting and classifying DGA-based malware in DoH traffic. The first stage employs an AE for dimensionality reduction and optimal feature extraction, followed by hybrid feature selection combining Random Forest (RF) importance scores and Mutual Information (MI). The second stage utilizes LSTM and GRU for binary and multiclass classification of malware families. To ensure robust evaluation, we employed stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 5) and applied temporal SMOTE (tSMOTE) to training data to address class imbalance while avoiding data leakage. The proposed framework was evaluated on the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 and DoH-DGA-Malware-Traffic-HKD datasets. AE-LSTM achieves 0.9958 accuracy for binary classification, while AE-GRU attains 0.9925 accuracy for multiclass classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively identifies DGA-based malware in encrypted DoH traffic and outperforms standalone models across most evaluation metrics.

Article.Title: Multi-directional control of a bio-inspired robot with a single undulating fin propulsion
Article.Authors: Garcia G.; Uddin M.; Odeh O.; Karim M.; Curet O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Control of agile and highly maneuverable underwater vessels is fundamental to explore complex maritime environments including survey closed to ocean structures and shallow waters. Currently, traditional autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and remote operated vehicles (ROVs) can encounter challenges navigating through these tight spaces. In this work, we explore the use of a flexible undulating membrane as a propulsive and force control mechanism for an underwater vehicle. We present a control scheme where modulations in the amplitude of two counter-propagating waves can provide a wide range of motion control including station keeping, heading, turning and speed control. We first present it through a user-operated control and then in closed-loop feedback to modulate the fin actuation to control the motion of the vessel. Free-swimming is executed with an elongated membrane positioned ventrally along the vehicle. The membrane fin was actuated through independently controlled flexible rays. The vehicle was tested in a flume at different flow speeds and pool where real-time tracking was used to obtain the position and orientation of the vessel. Using time-varying and spatial modulations of sinusoidal traveling waves, controlled trajectory of the vessel in addition to station-keeping in the presence of external perturbations can be achieved. Finally, we present the vessel swimming in the wake of an object where the fin has to overcome flow fluctuations from the shed vortices. We found that relatively simple controllers for flexible fin kinematics are sufficient to perform path following and station keeping and a variety of swimming maneuvers, providing a versatile alternative to conventional propulsion mechanisms in complex environments. Although control was implemented with sinusoidal traveling waves, it is envisioned that further exploration of a wider range of kinematics for optimal swimming will allow engineered vessels to the perform the graceful maneuvers that aquatic animals can.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of a multi-input converter for renewable energy integration in rural electrification
Article.Authors: G R.; R K.; V V.; J S.
Article.Abstract: The growing need for high-efficiency power management in hybrid renewable energy systems has highlighted the limitations of conventional multi-port converters, which often involve complex circuitry, many components, significant power losses, and thermal inefficiencies. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a novel bridgeless modified multi-input mono-output (MIMO) converter for Rural Electrification Applications, specifically designed for systems integrating solar photovoltaic (PV) and fuel cell energy sources. The proposed converter features a simplified architecture with a reduced number of components, resulting in lower switching and conduction losses, improved power density, and enhanced thermal performance. Its dual-input capability allows simultaneous energy harvesting from solar and fuel cell sources, leading to improved reliability and operational flexibility in hybrid systems. A key advantage of this topology lies in its ability to minimize voltage and current stresses across components, thereby increasing the overall system lifespan and efficiency. The Perturb and Observe algorithm is employed to implement maximum power point tracking for the solar PV input, ensuring optimal energy extraction and maintaining stable power delivery under fluctuating input conditions. A comprehensive mathematical model is developed, and operational modes are thoroughly analysed to support component selection and performance optimization. The effectiveness of the proposed design is validated through experimental testing using a 1 kW hardware prototype. Results confirm the converter’s high efficiency, reduced losses, and real-world applicability. On the whole, the proposed bridgeless modified MIMO converter presents a compact, efficient, and practical solution for hybrid renewable energy applications, offering significant performance improvements.

Article.Title: Effects of beetroot juice or dietary nitrate supplementation on swimming performance and physiological responses: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Vega-Monzó L.; Ranchal-Sanchez A.; Baena-González R.; Durán-López N.; Jurado-Castro J.
Article.Abstract: Beetroot juice (BRJ) and dietary nitrate supplementation have been widely investigated as ergogenic aids due to their potential to enhance exercise efficiency and performance through increased nitric oxide bioavailability. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness in swimming remains limited and inconsistent. This study evaluated whether acute or chronic BRJ or dietary nitrate supplementation improves swimming performance, post-exercise blood lactate concentration, and Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) in swimmers of different competitive levels. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251106680). A comprehensive search until June 11, 2026 identified eligible randomized controlled trials comparing BRJ or nitrate supplementation with placebo or no supplementation in swimmers, and random-effects models were applied to analyze effects on time-trial performance, lactate responses, and RPE. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria, of which nine contributed data to the quantitative meta-analysis ( n = 120 swimmers). BRJ or dietary nitrate supplementation did not significantly improve swimming time-trial performance in a multilevel meta-analysis including 12 comparisons from nine studies (SMD (standardized mean difference) = − 0.04, 95% CI − 0.21 to 0.13; p = 0.667) or post-exercise blood lactate concentration (k = 7; SMD = − 0.04, 95% CI − 0.27 to 0.19; p = 0.745). However, supplementation produced a small but statistically significant reduction in RPE (k = 7; SMD = − 0.33, 95% CI − 0.64 to − 0.001; p = 0.044). Subgroup analyses according to event duration did not identify significant differences between swimming effort categories. Overall, current evidence does not support a meaningful ergogenic effect of BRJ or dietary nitrate supplementation on swimming time-trial performance or post-exercise blood lactate responses, although supplementation may produce a small reduction in perceived exertion.

Article.Title: Paternal antenatal depression and its associated factors among expectant fathers in Debre Tabor Town, Ethiopia: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Dagne A.; Erlandson K.; Seyoum T.; Azale T.; Lindgren H.; Wells M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Paternal antenatal depression remains under-recognized and under-investigated, particularly in low-and middle-income countries such as Ethiopia, where evidence on its prevalence and associated factors is limited. This study aimed to determine paternal antenatal depression symptoms and identify its associated factors in expectant fathers during their partners’ third-trimester pregnancy. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 859 expectant fathers, selected through stratified multistage cluster sampling techniques from March 27 to July 31, 2025. The Edinburgh postnatal depression scale assessed depression symptoms. Descriptive statistics were computed, and bivariable logistic regression identified variables with p < .2 for multivariable analysis. Statistically significant associations were declared at p < .05 using adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). The prevalence of paternal antenatal depression symptoms was 22.6% (95% CI: 19.8–25.4%). Significant predictors included fathers’ age (AOR = 1.07, CI = 1.02–1.11), lower wealth index (AOR = 1.89, CI = 1.05–3.40), first-time fatherhood (AOR = 9.25, CI = 3.54–24.14), work-family conflict (AOR = 1.14, CI = 1.10–1.19), poor social support (AOR = 7.29, CI = 3.49–15.22), and maternal depression symptoms (AOR = 10.64, CI = 6.50–17.40). In conclusion, over one-fifth of expectant fathers experienced antenatal depression symptoms. Statistically significant associated factors included fathers’ age, lower wealth, first-time fatherhood, poor social support, work-family conflict, and maternal depression.

Article.Title: First experimental results on range monitoring in carbon therapy with the TIARA detector
Article.Authors: Pinson M.; André A.; Boursier Y.; Dupont M.; Gallin Martel M.; Garnier A.; Hoarau C.; Kavrigin P.; Maneval D.; Morel C.; Muraz J.; Pullia M.; Savazzi S.; Marcatili S.
Article.Abstract: In the context of range monitoring for particle therapy, this study presents the first experimental results obtained with the TIARA detector using carbon-ion beams at the CNAO clinical center in Pavia, Italy. TIARA is based on the Prompt Gamma Timing (PGT) technique, which measures the time of flight (TOF) between incident ions and prompt gamma rays (PGs) emitted during nuclear interactions in the target. While the TIARA prototype has previously been validated with protons, carbons present a more challenging scenario due to their higher linear energy transfer, nuclear fragmentation products, and the continuous beam time structure of synchrotron accelerators. Experiments were performed by irradiating PMMA targets of different thicknesses with 200 MeV/u carbon beams. A coincidence time resolution of 284 ± 32 ps FWHM was achieved, outperforming results previously obtained with protons at the same facility. A range accuracy of 4.74±0.36 mm at a 2 \(\sigma \) confidence level was measured at clinical intensity, when considering 5600 detected PGs, corresponding to the grouping of four irradiation spots of 2.4 \(\cdot \) 10 \(^6\) ions each. Overall, the results demonstrate that PGT-based range monitoring remains viable for carbon-ion beams, although increased background from secondary charged fragments indicates that detector configuration adaptations are required.

Article.Title: Pesticide safety behavior and associated factors among farmers in Northwest Iran
Article.Authors: Najafi E.; Parastar S.; Frarouei M.; Ansari F.; Sarooeyeh F.; Najafi B.; Vosoughi M.; Jafari Malekabad A.; Hajjari A.
Article.Abstract: Pesticide use in Iran is a long-lasting environmental and health concern. A cross-sectional study was carried out during the 2024 growing season among 352 cucumber farmers in Kosar and Khalkhal Counties, northwest Iran. Data were gathered using a validated structured questionnaire that assessed various aspects, namely: pesticide handling practices, personal protective equipment (PPE) use, knowledge, perceived barriers, training exposure, and acute health symptoms. Safe behavior was evaluated using a five-stage model, and multiple linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with safety behavior. An 10.2% (95% CI 6.5–14.8%) of farmers demonstrated safe pesticide-handling behavior, and only 6.0% consistently used PPE, a figure significantly lower than the rate reported across low- and middle-income countries. Acute pesticide-related symptoms affected 76.7% of farmers and 89.5% of household members or workers in Kosar and Khalkhal Counties, a figure more than twice the pooled global estimates. Knowledge of safety practices was the strongest independent predictor (standardized β = 0.350, p < 0.001), followed by training participation (β = 0.155, p = 0.016) and perceived barriers (β = 0.157, p = 0.012). Despite 58% having received training, only 22.7% demonstrated adequate knowledge. Cost and limited availability were the main barriers to PPE use. Northwest Iran emerges as a high-risk area for pesticide-related health issues. Urgent comprehensive actions are needed, including experiential Farmer Field School programs, PPE subsidies, behavioral nudges for low-literacy populations, and mobile units for treatment of poisoning.

Article.Title: Research on isomorphic fusion of multi-source geological data for open-pit coal mines
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Liu G.; Liu C.; Ni K.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Transparent geological conditions are essential for intelligent open-pit coal mining. To address insufficient exploration accuracy and weak integration of heterogeneous geological data, this study proposes a multi-source geological data isomorphism method for open-pit coal mines. The method analyzes the spatial variability of coal-rock strata and geological structures, evaluates the applicability and complementarity of different datasets, and applies a stepwise pairwise fusion strategy: Kriging fusion of geological maps and boreholes, Zoeppritz-equation-based fusion of boreholes and seismic data, and Faust-equation-based fusion of seismic and electromagnetic data. The fused outputs were then comprehensively integrated to construct a stratigraphically and structurally screened dataset. Taking Dananhu No. 2 Open-Pit Coal Mine as a case, data for coal seams, other strata, Quaternary deposits, faults, burnt rock, and groundwater were processed. Case-specific evaluation used a locked external holdout dataset and four benchmark methods. To avoid overgeneralizing single-case numerical outcomes, performance was expressed using four ordinal grades (Excellent, Good, Moderate, and Poor) across five accuracy dimensions and six engineering-efficiency/cost dimensions. The proposed method was graded Excellent across all five accuracy dimensions; for engineering performance, it was graded Moderate in preliminary data-collation and single-run computational efficiency and Excellent in repeated-correction efficiency, overall engineering efficiency, cost control, and accuracy-cost suitability. The resulting model maintained interpreted structural and stratigraphic discontinuities while improving continuity where supported by observations; surface smoothness was treated only as a continuity diagnostic. These grades are case-specific and require site-specific recalibration and multi-mine validation before broader generalization.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of two-year overall survival in metastatic endometrial cancer: a SEER population-based study
Article.Authors: Ozberk U.; Uguz A.; Sekmek S.; Ucar G.
Article.Abstract: Metastatic endometrial cancer carries a poor prognosis. Accurate prognostic tools are lacking. Machine learning (ML) may improve survival prediction using available clinicopathological and sociodemographic data. We analyzed 11,720 patients with metastatic endometrial cancer from the SEER database. The primary outcome was two-year overall survival (OS). Thirteen ML classifiers were trained (70/30 split) and evaluated using AUC, accuracy, and F1 score. SMOTE and calibration analysis were applied to the best-performing model. Kaplan–Meier, Cox regression, and SHAP-based interpretability analyses were performed. XGBoost achieved the highest AUC (0.726). Following SMOTE, F1 improved from 0.446 to 0.516 (AUC 0.715), with a calibration intercept and slope of -0.097 and 0.941, respectively. SHAP analysis identified histologic subtype and chemotherapy receipt as the most influential predictors, followed by tumor grade, age, and race/ethnicity. On multivariate Cox regression, Grade IV (HR 2.08), undifferentiated histology (HR 1.97), age ≥ 80 years (HR 1.71), and Non-Hispanic Black race (HR 1.35) were independently associated with worse OS; chemotherapy receipt was associated with improved observed survival (HR 0.43). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed significant differences in overall survival by histologic subtype and chemotherapy status (log-rank p < 0.001 for both). ML models using registry-based data predict two-year OS in metastatic endometrial cancer with modest but consistent performance. Histologic subtype, chemotherapy, tumor grade, and age are important predictors of survival. Racial disparities in survival persisted after adjustment, underscoring the need for targeted interventions to address healthcare inequities.

Article.Title: Machine-learning prediction of postoperative delirium and characterization of clinical heterogeneity after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: a prospective observational cohort study
Article.Authors: Peng Q.; Zhang J.; Cai J.; LaiTi P.; Xu W.
Article.Abstract: To develop and internally validate machine-learning models for predicting postoperative delirium (POD) after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), and to characterize clinical heterogeneity across data-driven patient subgroups within the same cohort. In this prospective single-center observational cohort study, 729 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB were included. Multidimensional perioperative variables were analyzed, with postoperative predictors restricted to measurements obtained before the first documented delirium episode. Seven supervised machine-learning models were developed and internally validated for POD prediction, and unsupervised hierarchical clustering was performed in the full cohort to characterize clinical heterogeneity across data-driven patient subgroups. During the predefined postoperative observation period, 262 of 729 patients (35.9%) developed POD. In the independent test set, discrimination ranged from 0.718 to 0.861 across the seven models. In cross-validated analyses, random forest showed the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.841) and the lowest overall prediction error by Brier score. In the clustering analysis, three data-driven subgroups with different observed POD burdens were identified, showing distinct perioperative profiles across inflammatory, functional, comorbidity, and procedural domains. POD was additionally associated with prolonged total hospital stay. Machine-learning models integrating preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative variables showed potential for predicting POD after cardiac surgery with CPB. In addition, unsupervised clustering provided a subgroup-level perspective on perioperative clinical heterogeneity within the cohort.

Article.Title: An adaptive multi-objective differential evolution algorithm to fine-tune the constructive cost model constants for software effort estimation
Article.Authors: Gouda S.; Ramasubbareddy S.; Chaudhury K.; Mishra S.; Mohapatra H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The primary goals of software effort and cost estimation are to determine project cost, shorten development time, and provide a reliable prediction. This issue is also classified as a multi-objective optimization problem. A new adaptation-based multi-objective differential evolution algorithm, enhanced with Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, solves these problems by tuning the parameters. This paper includes new mutation techniques with a Pareto-based differential evolution algorithm, leveraging Generative AI to increase candidate solution diversity. The new mutation operator provides more bandwidth, which helps the differential evolution algorithm to avoid local optimality problems. This study applies a non-dominated sorting technique to lower the computational complexity involved in Pareto dominance. The article further examines the software cost estimation problem by fine-tuning the parameters for a multi-objective constructive cost model using Generative AI to predict software costs accurately. The software cost estimation problem aims to minimize prediction errors while maximizing accuracy, ultimately reducing overall project costs.
