Compared to existing modern versions of multi-objective evolutionary optimization algorithms across all objective problems, the proposed approach, which integrates Generative AI, shows improved prediction and lower error rates on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)-93 and Constructive Cost Model (COCOMO)-81 datasets.

Article.Title: Exercise decreases stress induced bladder hyperalgesia, voiding frequency and oxidative load
Article.Authors: Chaudhary S.; Balkaya M.; Rodriguez L.
Article.Abstract: Chronic stress contributes to voiding dysfunction and bladder pain, especially in interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS). Oxidative stress has been suggested as a main pathophysiological mechanism underlying IC/BPS. Exercise, with its benefits in pain conditions and efficacy in reducing oxidative load, is a promising treatment. This study investigated the efficacy of exercise treatment on stress-induced hyperalgesia and urinary dysfunction in a water-avoidance stress (WAS) model that mimics the main behavioral and histopathological features of IC/BPS. Rats were exposed to WAS for 10 days, followed by three weeks of voluntary running exercise. Pain phenotypes were assessed via von Frey testing, and voiding parameters were evaluated in metabolic cages. Bladder mast cell infiltration was investigated histologically, and permeability was assessed electrophysiologically in Ussing chambers. Biomarkers of oxidative damage, including lipid peroxidation, protein carbonylation, and DNA oxidation, were measured. WAS increased urinary frequency, allodynia, hyperalgesia, and oxidative stress markers. It also increased mast cell infiltration in the bladder and impaired bladder permeability. Exercise treatment significantly reduced WAS-induced increases in voiding frequency, allodynia, and hyperalgesia. Exercise also increased total antioxidant capacity and reduced oxidative damage markers to control levels. WAS replicates key features of IC/BPS, and exercise ameliorates its effects through antioxidant mechanisms.

Article.Title: Fractal gene losses and concomitant genesis of novel clades sculpt the metazoan Gα gene repertoire
Article.Authors: Abu Obaid A.; Abdullahi A.; Korsching K.; Oka Y.; Korsching S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gα proteins are integral components of cellular signaling, with an ancient evolutionary origin. Within animals, Gα proteins have been categorized into five canonical classes: Gαs, Gαi, Gαq, Gα12, and Gαv, with few unclassified genes outside of these groups. Here we have performed comprehensive phylogenetic analyses of nearly one thousand metazoan species, focusing on two species-rich phyla, arthropods and nematodes. Our analysis reveals a fractal pattern of gene loss in all five canonical classes, with Gαs and Gαv most prone to gene loss. On the other hand, gene gains are common in all five classes, most pronounced in Gαq and Gα12. Unexpectedly, we observe the emergence of thirteen novel clades, the majority specific to single phyla (arthropods, nematodes, tardigrades) and some even specific to lower taxonomic classifications. Those new clades exhibit all G box and switch region motifs, characteristic for the five canonical classes. For all of the new clades we observe many representatives in transcriptome assemblies, validating their expression and suggesting a functional role for them. Our results show a highly dynamic evolutionary landscape for Gα proteins, including extensive gene losses and frequent gains in the five canonical classes and recurrent genesis of new clades—unexpected in such a highly conserved and ancient family of proteins with central importance in cellular signalling. Our findings advance the understanding of Gα protein evolution, and lay the foundation for deciphering the functional role of the novel Gα clades.

Article.Title: Deployment-oriented evaluation of large language models for Arabic emotion classification
Article.Authors: Al-Shamaileh O.; Alzubi S.; Almehrzi M.; Mubin O.; Alnajjar F.
Article.Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for emotion classification, yet Arabic evaluations remain limited and typically emphasise predictive performance alone. This study presents a deployment-oriented evaluation framework for Arabic emotion classification that complements conventional accuracy-based assessment with measures of output validity, operationalised through coverage and unknown rate, together with strict versus covered evaluation. The evaluation is conducted on 1002 manually annotated Arabic sentences spanning five emotion categories, with very high inter-annotator agreement ( \(\kappa = 0.9722\) ). We evaluate multiple proprietary and open-weight LLMs under a harmonised zero-shot setting and further examine the effects of few-shot prompting, three-vote stochastic aggregation, and run-to-run stability. Supervised Arabic encoder baselines, AraBERT and MARBERT, are additionally included as contextual task-specific reference models. The results show that the highest-performing LLMs combine strong predictive performance with high output validity, while differences in non-evaluable outputs are model- and protocol-specific. Few-shot prompting improves performance for most, but not all, evaluated models, whereas three-vote aggregation produces inconsistent effects across systems. Overall, the findings demonstrate that deployment-oriented indicators provide complementary information beyond predictive performance and support a more transparent evaluation of Arabic emotion classification systems under controlled inference conditions.

Article.Title: Neurotensin stimulates androgen production by theca cells in the monkey ovarian follicle
Article.Authors: Sage M.; Curry T.; Duffy D.
Article.Abstract: Androgen production by theca cells of the ovarian follicle is required for follicle growth and ovulation. Although theca steroidogenesis is known to be stimulated by luteinizing hormone (LH), the role of LH-stimulated paracrine mediators of ovulation such as neurotensin (NTS) has not been investigated. To explore the effect of NTS on ovarian theca steroidogenesis, monkey theca cells were treated with NTS or the LHCGR-ligand human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG). NTS increased theca production of the major theca androgen, androstenedione, as well as testosterone and dehydroepiandrosterone. Theca androgens were stimulated by hCG. Levels of progesterone, 17α-hydroxyprogesterone, and dehydroepiandrosterone were all stimulated by hCG. NTS decreased theca lipid droplet content but had no effect on theca LDL uptake or cholesterol quantity, while hCG did not affect theca cholesterol or lipids. NTS increased expression of CYP17A1 mRNA but not LDLR, STAR , CYP11A1 , or HSD3B , while hCG did not significantly impact any steroidogenic protein or enzyme mRNA examined. Altogether, NTS stimulates androgen production by monkey theca cells through increased utilization of stored lipids and upregulation of CYP17A1 expression. Increased dehydroepiandrosterone, in the absence of altered progesterone and 17α-hydroxyprogesterone, supports the concept that NTS stimulates androgen synthesis preferentially via the Δ 5 -steroidogenic pathway.

Article.Title: An intelligent virtual coaching system for traditional martial arts based on 3D pose estimation and generative adversarial networks
Article.Authors: Fu C.; Yin L.; Yang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional martial arts are hard to hand on. The masters who hold the repertoire are ageing, instruction rarely travels beyond the training hall, and verbal correction remains stubbornly subjective. This paper presents an intelligent virtual coaching system that couples enhanced three-dimensional pose estimation with generative adversarial network refinement. A modified High-Resolution Network, augmented with attention and temporal convolution, extracts skeletons that survive fast strikes and self-occlusion, while a discriminator-guided sequence optimization module pulls noisy trajectories back onto the manifold of biomechanically plausible movement. On top of these components, a hierarchical feedback mechanism turns quantitative learner-reference comparisons into real-time, multimodal corrections. Evaluated on public benchmarks and on a purpose-built martial arts corpus, the pipeline reaches 38.6 mm Mean Per Joint Position Error while sustaining 28.4 frames per second, and its automated quality scores track expert ratings closely, with a correlation coefficient of 0.847. Taken together, the results describe a workable technological pathway for preserving intangible cultural heritage and for widening access to high-quality martial arts instruction.

Article.Title: Spatial heterogeneity and nonlinear drivers regulate vegetation productivity in Hubei Province China
Article.Authors: Wang C.; He R.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Rising global carbon emissions have intensified the greenhouse effect and placed growing pressure on terrestrial ecosystems. Understanding the spatiotemporal variability of vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is therefore essential for assessing environmental quality, quantifying carbon source-sink dynamics, and guiding ecological restoration. This study examined the spatial heterogeneity and nonlinear controls of NPP in Hubei Province, China, from 2001 to 2024 using the MOD17A3HGF dataset, GeoDetector, and geographically weighted regression (GWR). NPP showed a clear spatial gradient, with high values in the western mountains, intermediate values in the eastern hilly areas, and low values in the central plains. Annual mean NPP increased significantly during the study period and exhibited quasi-periodic fluctuations at approximately 3-, 6-, and 12-year intervals. Driver analysis showed that altitude was the dominant factor, while climate, human activity, and their interactions had strong spatially heterogeneous and nonlinear effects. Greening and browning areas differed markedly in their controlling mechanisms, and factor interactions amplified NPP variation beyond the effects of individual drivers. GWR further revealed strong spatial non-stationarity in driver-NPP relationships. These findings clarify the coupled human-natural mechanisms regulating vegetation productivity and provide a basis for targeted ecological restoration, land-use planning, and climate-adaptive management in subtropical regions.

Article.Title: Optimization scheduling of cascade reservoirs under an ecological approach: a case study
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang S.; Xiao G.; Fu X.; Ming L.; Huang W.; Liang C.; zhan Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Yalong River Basin is a significant hydropower base and a crucial component of the global biodiversity hotspot, Mountains of Southwest China. There are five key cascade reservoirs in the lower reaches of Yalong River. The current optimal operation focuses on power generation and flood control, which alters the natural flow regime and adversely affects the river ecosystem. To address the lack of ecological flow considerations in this basin, a study on optimal dispatching of cascade hydropower stations with minimum ecological flow requirements incorporated was conducted. First, based on hydrological variations in the study area, the Improved Ten-day Frequency Method (ITFM) is used to calculate the minimum ecological flow requirements. Second, a medium- and long-term multi-objective optimization model balancing power generation and ecological objectives was established, which aimed to maximize power generation and minimize the sum of ecological alteration degrees for the cascade hydropower stations, and was solved using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Subsequently, ecological scheduling schemes for cascade reservoirs in various typical years are determined. The results show that the hydrological change point of the Yalong River Basin occurred in 1992, with the runoff differences before and after this point are significant. Compared to conventional scheduling schemes, under the ecological-prioritizing scheme, the proposed ecological scheme achieved reductions in ecological alteration degrees of 37.74%, 19.84%, and 58.6% in the three typical years of wet, normal, and dry, which shows a significant increase in ecological benefits. This approach demonstrates the significant role of ecological regulation in facilitating the restoration of river ecosystems and provides a valuable reference for reconciling the conflict between reservoir power generation and downstream ecological water use.

Article.Title: Knockdown of SPAG6 regulates triglyceride metabolism via the P38 MAPK/ERK/PPARα axis in acute myeloid leukemia
Article.Authors: Su R.; Zhao H.; Luo J.; Ding L.; Zang X.; Pan S.; Liu L.; Li P.
Article.Abstract: Numerous studies have already revealed that the development of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is closely related to the dysregulation of lipid metabolism. The aim of this study was to elucidate the biological role and molecular mechanisms of Sperm Associated Antigen 6(SPAG6) in AML. Our research found that the expression level of SPAG6 was significantly elevated in clinical samples of AML compared to normal samples. Meanwhile, the expression of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 A (CPT1A), a marker associated with lipid accumulation, also showed an upward trend. Lentivirus knock-downing SPAG6 was used to investigate the tumorigenic phenotypes of AML.The results indicated that knockdown of SPAG6 increased lipid accumulation both in vivo and in vitro by downregulating the expression of fatty acid oxidation (FAO)-related genes, thereby slowing the progression of the disease. Furthermore, PPARα was found to upregulate the expression of FAO-related genes through activation of the P38 MAPK/ERK pathway, thereby promoting tumor development. Our study uncovers a novel function of SPAG6 in lipid metabolism via the P38 MAPK/ERK/PPARα axis, providing new theoretical insights into the pathogenesis of AML. Targeting SPAG6 may emerge as a potential strategy for AML treatment.

Article.Title: Designing an mRNA vaccine encoding multi-epitopes to combat Pipistrellus bat coronavirus BtHKU5-CoV-2 based on consensus sequence using an immunoinformatics approach
Article.Authors: Ali M.; Islam J.; Majumder U.; Ahmed E.; Munsi M.
Article.Abstract: The bat-derived Pipistrellus bat coronavirus BtHKU5-CoV-2, a merbecovirus lineage, is an emerging zoonotic risk due to its ability to utilize human ACE2 receptors and ongoing spike protein recombination events that enhance cross-species transmission potential. At the moment no authorized vaccines are available against this emerging threat which emphasizes the urgent need for proactive vaccine development. This study employed reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics approaches to design a novel mRNA vaccine candidate encoding multiple epitopes, aiming at conserved regions across four structural proteins (E, M, N, and S) of the virus. Protein sequences from UniProt underwent BLAST analysis, multiple sequence alignment, and phylogenetic mapping to identify conserved regions. Twenty-four high-affinity epitopes were selected: eight CTL, eight HTL, and eight linear B lymphocyte epitopes, meeting strict criteria of antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. The selected epitopes achieved 100% combined coverage worldwide. The L7/L12 adjuvant was fused at the N-terminus via EAAAK linker, with epitopes linked by AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers, resulting in a 539-residue construct. The vaccine demonstrated excellent physicochemical stability, high solubility, and broad population coverage. Refined 3D structure (Z-score − 7.5, Ramachandran favored 92.6%) docked favorably with TLR-3/4 (− 1043/ − 1125 kJ/mol), preferring TLR-4 (RMSD 5.41 Å vs. 9.03 Å, RMSF 2.33 Å, Rg 34.15 Å, H-bonds 889-1006, MM-GBSA ΔGbind − 187.10 kcal/mol post-100 ns MD). Immune simulations predicted robust Th1-biased responses following three doses: persistent cytotoxic T-cells, NK/DC/macrophage activation, year-long IgM/IgG memory, and elevated IFN-γ/IL-12/TNF-α cytokines. Codon-optimized mRNA (CAI 0.982, GC 52.56%) cloned into pET-28a (+) showed stable folding. PbatCoV-mVax represents a promising, stable, and theoretically immunogenic prioritization candidate requiring extensive in-vitro and in-vivo validation to establish actual preventive protection against BtHKU5-CoV-2 spillover.

Article.Title: Clinical documentation quality in routine care with AI scribe support: a large‑scale Spanish analysis
Article.Authors: Álvaro de la Parra J.; Alcázar-Peral J.; Blanco D.; Martín C.; Rodríguez B.; Campos S.; Espelt E.; Cristóbal I.; Caramés C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clinical documentation is essential for care quality, safety, and coordination, yet the growing burden of electronic health record (EHR) tasks contributes to clinician burnout and may compromise documentation quality. Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribe systems have emerged as a potential solution, but their impact on documentation quality and readability remains underexplored. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the effect of an AI-assisted scribe system (Scribe) on the semantic agreement, readability, and structured quality of outpatient clinical documentation across multiple specialties in a large Spanish healthcare network, within the framework of value-based healthcare (VBHC). Thus, we conducted a retrospective, multi-method study of over 2.3 million outpatient consultations across 45 specialties (Oct 2024–Dec 2025). Documentation with and without Scribe was compared using automated metrics (semantic agreement, INFLESZ and Perspicuity) and an 18-item structured quality rubric. Semantic agreement was evaluated across all 45 specialties, whereas report quality was assessed in a stratified sample of 300 reports from 15 specialties. A manual audit evaluated completeness of key safety elements (past medical history, allergies), and statistical analyses included descriptive metrics, Welch and paired t-tests, and Hedges’ g. Notably, Scribe achieved a weighted mean semantic agreement of 89.3% (SD 2.1). Readability improved significantly: INFLESZ scores increased from 72.05 to 77.61 ( p < 0.001), and Perspicuity scores from 76.19 to 81.49 ( p < 0.001). Structured quality scores rose from 5.79 (95% CI 5.60–5.99) to 8.02 (95% CI 7.87–8.17), with a large effect size (Hedges’ g = 2.06; p < 0.001). A manual audit showed significant improvements in documentation of past medical history (7.75 vs 1.75; p < 0.001; dz = 1.10) and allergy status (9.75 vs 7.75; p = 0.010; g = 0.43). Altogether, AI-assisted scribe technology was associated with improvements in documentation quality, readability, and safety-related documentation elements. These improvements align with VBHC principles by supporting better patient outcomes, safer care, and more efficient use of clinical resources through high-quality documentation.

Article.Title: Modeling hierarchical response accuracy of large language models using a Bayesian generalized linear mixed model
Article.Authors: Emir B.; Ay Keselik G.
Article.Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong performance in Natural Language Processing. In neuroanatomy, their response accuracy across hierarchical data structures (responses nested within questions) has not yet been investigated. Evaluating how these models perform under varying cognitive demands is important for their effective integration into medical education. A total of 183 neuroanatomy questions from the Turkish Medical Specialization Examination (2013–2021) were reviewed, and 176 single correct answer questions were obtained by excluding seven figure-based questions. Each question was reformulated into prompts representing three role-based prompt levels: medical student, recently graduated physician, and doctoral-level specialist. Responses from the three LLMs were scored as correct or incorrect. Data were analyzed using a Bayesian Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) with a mixture prior for the random intercept, with model type, prompt level, and their interaction as fixed effects. The distribution of the question-level intercept was highly skewed, showing a ceiling for the items answered correctly by all LLMs under all prompt levels (141 of 176 questions, 80.1%). To deal with this excess of one, a spike and slab prior was specified for the random intercept, separating a ceiling component (spike) from a variable-difficulty component (slab). Posterior estimates were obtained using Monte Carlo sampling with CmdStan in Python. ChatGPT-4o and Microsoft Copilot showed higher overall accuracy than Google Gemini, with ChatGPT-4o performing best across all prompt levels. The spike and slab model showed better out-of-sample predictive performance than the standard model specifications (ΔELPD-WAIC = 22.64). The posterior global spike probability ( \(\:\varphi\:\) =0.706, 95 % HDI [0.516, 0.826]) indicated that 141 questions (80.1 % ) were assigned to the ceiling component, while the remaining 35 questions (19.9 % ) showed true variability in item difficulty. The question level random intercept standard deviation for the slab component ( \(\:{\sigma\:}_{question}\) =2.158, 95 % HDI [1.289, 3.312]) reflected substantial between item variability in baseline easiness among non-ceiling neuroanatomical questions. The Bayesian GLMM approach implemented with a spike and slab prior distribution modeled the hierarchical structure of the data where responses were nested within questions. The ceiling effect was addressed by decomposing question level random intercepts into separate components representing the ceiling and variable difficulty providing an estimate of performance variability. It was obtained between-item variability in LLM performance among non-ceiling questions. Role-based prompt differentiation alone was insufficient to generate systematic differences in model accuracy.

Article.Title: Accelerated development and deployment of computer vision models for invasive aquatic pests
Article.Authors: Pearson R.; Preston G.; Bulleid J.; David S.; Zareie-Vaux F.; Clements D.; Tait L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aquatic non-indigenous species (NIS) incur significant cultural, environmental and economic costs worldwide, and human surveillance is expensive and impractical at large scales. Computer vision models (CVMs) deployed on remote and autonomous vehicles can reduce the burden on trained human observers, but aquatic environments present unique challenges and lack frameworks for biosecurity-focused development and deployment. We present a practical framework for developing and deploying new species-specific CVMs for real-time use across surface vessel and remote vehicle platforms. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through its application to several taxonomically and ecologically diverse NIS in New Zealand: Mediterranean fanworm Sabella spallanzanii , South African oxygen weed Lagarosiphon major, and exotic Caulerpa ( Caulerpa brachypus and C. parvifolia ). For S. spallanzanii , we demonstrate efficient training from small datasets and deployment for real-time detection. Using exotic Caulerpa , we show how CVMs can be rapidly improved during an early incursion response. For L. major , standardised field validation methods enable the comparison of CVM and human detection rates across diverse locations and operating conditions. Collectively, these case studies demonstrate that our framework enables accurate detection and the robust assessment of model effectiveness under realistic field conditions and can be effectively applied to imagery from multiple platforms.

Article.Title: Biomechanical evaluation of porous tantalum and titanium dental implants under different bone quality conditions using three-dimensional finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Li R.; Zhang Y.; Zhang Z.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to compare the biomechanical responses of titanium and porous tantalum implants under different bone quality conditions using three-dimensional finite element analysis with sequential loading conditions simulating posterior mastication. Three-dimensional finite element models of titanium and porous tantalum implants placed in Type II (D2) and Type IV (D4) bone conditions were constructed based on cone-beam computed tomography data. Porous tantalum was modeled as a homogeneous equivalent material using an effective elastic modulus. Sequential loading conditions representing different phases of a posterior masticatory cycle were applied. Equivalent von Mises stress distributions within the implant components and surrounding cortical and cancellous bone tissues were evaluated. Stress distribution was influenced by both bone quality and implant material. Compared with D2 bone, D4 bone conditions resulted in higher stress concentrations within the implant system and surrounding tissues. Titanium implants exhibited higher peak von Mises stress values at the implant body and implant–abutment connection region, particularly under D4 bone conditions. Porous tantalum implants demonstrated lower peak stress concentrations within the implant components, while showing increased stress transfer to surrounding cancellous bone compared with titanium implants. The highest stress values were observed during oblique loading phases. Within the limitations of this finite element study, porous tantalum implants demonstrated potentially favorable stress-transfer characteristics compared with titanium implants under the simulated loading conditions, particularly under low-density bone conditions. The lower elastic modulus of porous tantalum may contribute to a more balanced redistribution of mechanical loads between the implant structure and surrounding bone tissues. However, these findings should not be interpreted as direct evidence of superior clinical performance, and further experimental and clinical studies are required to validate the potential biomechanical benefits of porous tantalum implants.

Article.Title: PID controller parameter optimization for ship fin stabilizers based on an improved secretary bird optimization algorithm
Article.Authors: Ye L.; Liu Y.; Guo J.; Zhang M.; Zhang D.; Tong Z.; Shen J.
Article.Abstract: Fin stabilizers governed by proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers dominate active ship roll reduction, yet their performance depends critically on gain tuning under nonlinear hydrodynamics and time-varying sea states. This paper proposes an Improved Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (ISBOA) combining a Logistic-Tent chaotic map with opposition-based learning, a DE/rand/1/bin operator in the predation phase, and a nonlinear adaptive control factor with energy-driven stagnation escape. Across 29 CEC2017 and 12 CEC2022 functions ISBOA ranks first overall; of 246 pairwise comparisons 199 are significant and 173 also reach medium or large favourable effect size, the exception being CCO. Ablation confirms that each strategy contributes. Applied to PID tuning in a Matlab/Simulink closed loop driven by a Pierson-Moskowitz spectrum, minimizing a roll-angle ITAE index, ISBOA reduces RMS and peak roll by 95.3% and 94.4% against 85.6% and 82.7% for a conventionally tuned fixed PID. With the gains fixed across nine off-design conditions the reduction stays within 94.2–95.9% in eight, but the loop diverges in the ninth; a coefficient sweep shows the tuning is stable only to 0.90 of nominal whereas lower-gain settings tolerate 0.75, an explicit performance/stability-margin trade-off. Test bench measurements show peak pipeline vibration falling 25.2 dB.

Article.Title: Correction: High-energy γ-photons and pair electrons generation in polarized ultraintense laser fields
Article.Authors: Agarwal S.; Gupta D.
Article.Abstract: “However, at the laser field is modeled as a plane wave with four-potent high intensities ( \(a_{0} \gg 1\) ), the relativistic mass increase of electrons leads to a reduced effective plasma frequency, and the slightly overdense plasma becomes relativistically transparent when \(\gamma = \sqrt {1 + a_{0}^{2} } { \gtrsim }\frac{{n_{0} }}{{n_{c} }}\) 46,47 .”

Article.Title: Financial literacy and gambling-related risk in adult ADHD: a decision-making perspective
Article.Authors: Hamurcu Ç.; Öztürk M.; Hamurcu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gambling-related risk represents a financially consequential form of risk-taking and may be particularly relevant in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This cross-sectional study examined associations among ADHD symptom severity, financial literacy, and gambling-related risk in 83 adults with clinically diagnosed ADHD who had not yet started methylphenidate treatment. Financial literacy was assessed using basic financial literacy questions, gambling-related risk with the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS), and ADHD symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS). Structural equation modeling showed that higher financial literacy was associated with lower gambling-related risk in the Maximum Likelihood estimation, although this association was not statistically significant in the bootstrap analysis. ADHD symptom severity was not directly associated with either gambling-related risk or financial literacy. Gender was associated with ASRS, financial literacy, and SOGS scores in both the Maximum Likelihood and bootstrap analyses. These findings suggest that financial literacy may be a relevant correlate of gambling-related risk among adults with ADHD, while ADHD symptom severity alone may not account for individual differences in gambling-related risk. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these associations and their underlying mechanisms.

Article.Title: Magnetic-field-assisted photocatalytic activity of CoFe₂O₄/graphene oxide nanocomposite for dye degradation
Article.Authors: Negedu S.; Assaro A.; Ayalew M.; Sewnet A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient removal of persistent organic dyes from wastewater remains a significant environmental challenge. This study presents the hydrothermal synthesis of a CoFe 2 O 4 /graphene oxide (CF/GO) nanocomposite and evaluates its photocatalytic performance under magnetic-field assistance for the degradation of methylene blue (MB) and Congo red (CR) under visible-light irradiation. Comprehensive characterization was conducted using SEM, EDX, TEM, XRD, FTIR, Raman, UV-Vis DRS, and VSM techniques. The incorporation of GO reduced the band gap from 2.4 eV to 1.9 eV, enhancing visible-light absorption, while the nanocomposite maintained strong ferromagnetic properties (Ms = 53.29 emu/g, Hc = 949 Oe), facilitating magnetic recovery. Under visible-light irradiation, the CF/GO nanocomposite achieved degradation efficiencies of 84% for MB and 74% for CR within 90 min. Applying an external magnetic field (0.5 T) further increased the efficiencies to 98% and 86%, respectively. This enhancement is attributed to Lorentz-force-induced charge-carrier separation, which suppresses recombination and increases the generation of reactive oxygen species, primarily • O₂⁻ and h⁺. The photocatalyst exhibited excellent reusability, retaining over 93% efficiency after five cycles. These findings demonstrate that the CF/GO nanocomposite is a highly efficient, magnetically separable photocatalyst for wastewater treatment and underscore the synergistic effect of magnetic-field assistance in ferrite-graphene systems.

Article.Title: COH fluids and melts drive mantle refertilization and organic synthesis in nascent subduction zones
Article.Authors: Herviou C.; Soret M.; Debret B.; Andreani M.; Montagnac G.; Olivieri O.; Vitale Brovarone A.; Rividi N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Slab-derived fluids and melts released during subduction refertilize the mantle wedge, shaping arc magmatism and volatile transfer. Yet the nature and efficiency of the earliest metasomatizing agents active under the warm thermal gradients of nascent subduction zones remain poorly constrained. Here, we report multiphase and polymineralic inclusions from the high-temperature metamorphic sole of the Semail ophiolite (Oman–United Arab Emirates), which record the trapping of COH fluids and hydrous silicate melts derived from both mafic and sedimentary slab components during subduction infancy. Multiphase inclusions act as micro-reactors where fluids react with host minerals during exhumation, driving the abiotic synthesis of solid organic compounds, including nanodiamond-like structures, demonstrating that subduction zones can generate molecules of prebiotic relevance. Combined with the ophiolite record, our results indicate that such COH fluids and melts refertilize the mantle wedge from the onset of subduction, generating proto-arc magmas and promoting deep carbonation and hydration.

Article.Title: Empagliflozin restores colonic fatty acid metabolism and ameliorates fibrotic signalling despite gut dysbiosis in Western diet-fed mice
Article.Authors: Radlinger B.; Ress C.; Folie S.; Landolfo M.; Salvà C.; Rungger K.; Monfort-Lanzas P.; Hackl H.; Salzmann K.; Staudacher G.; Kaser S.
Article.Abstract: Gut dysbiosis and an altered host colonic transcriptomic contribute to Western diet (WD) induced metabolic deterioration. In this pilot study we investigated the effect of empagliflozin on intestinal transcriptomics and microbiome. CL57BL/6J mice were fed a WD or control-diet with or without empagliflozin supplementation for 10 weeks. Colon and stool samples were used for transcriptomics and 16 S amplicon sequencing. An additive model with global drug and diet effects was compared to a full interaction model. Colon transcriptomics data suggested an interaction effect between drug and diet ( p = 0.001; PERMANOVA). From overall 1136 interacting genes, gene ontology analysis revealed two major biological processes being involved: In WD fed mice empagliflozin activated fatty acid metabolism and protected against fibrosis related genes. The drug-diet interaction was also found in representative regulators Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha and Nuclear factor kappa B subunit p65 ( p < 0.05). In microbiome analysis WD significantly reduced alpha diversity and distinct clustering with regards to beta-diversity. In conclusion, WD but not empagliflozin treatment altered gut microbiome suggesting microbiome-independent effects of empagliflozin on the colonic transcriptome. Upregulation of fatty acid metabolism, and protection against fibrosis related genes in gut dysbiosis represent novel mechanisms of actions with SGLT2 inhibition.

Article.Title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the beck depression inventory among university students
Article.Authors: Amos P.
Article.Abstract: Accurate assessment of depressive symptoms requires instruments that are both psychometrically sound and culturally appropriate. This study examined the cultural adaptation and psychometric properties of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) among 600 Ghanaian university students, focusing on reliability, factor structure, and cross-cultural construct validity. Following item refinement, psychometric analyses were conducted on a 15-item version of the BDI, reduced from the original 21-item instrument. Comparisons across gender, language, and regional subgroups indicated broadly consistent factor structures, high internal consistency (α = 0.89–0.91; ω = 0.90–0.92), acceptable composite reliability (CR = 0.91–0.93), and convergent validity (AVE = 0.51–0.54), with factor congruence coefficients ≥ 0.96. However, because formal measurement invariance testing was not conducted, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary evidence of cross-group and cross-cultural stability rather than definitive evidence of measurement invariance. Exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor structure cognitive, affective, somatic, interpersonal, and motivational/behavioral accounting for 68.3% of the total variance, with strong factor loadings and moderate inter-factor correlations (0.42–0.62), indicating multidimensionality without redundancy. Confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated good model fit (CFI = 0.95; TLI = 0.93; RMSEA = 0.054; SRMR = 0.045), confirming structural validity. Cross-cultural analyses across gender, language, and regional subgroups revealed stable factor structures, high reliability (α = 0.89–0.91; ω = 0.90–0.92), and strong construct validity (CR = 0.91–0.93; AVE = 0.51–0.54), with factor congruence coefficients ≥ 0.96. In all, the culturally adapted BDI is a reliable, valid, and multidimensional tool for assessing depressive symptoms among Ghanaian university students, supporting its use in culturally sensitive research and practice.

Article.Title: Impact of premixing on the propulsion performance of N2O/hydrocarbon thrusters: a combined numerical and experimental study
Article.Authors: Jung E.; Kim J.; Lee K.; Kim Y.; Lee E.; Jung E.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N $$_2$$ O)-based bipropellant systems utilizing self-pressurizing hydrocarbon fuels offer a promising non-toxic alternative for space propulsion applications. However, a systematic comparison between non-premixed and premixed combustion modes under controlled operational conditions remains unreported. This study quantitatively evaluates the propulsion performance of a 10 N-class N $$_2$$ O/C $$_2$$ H $$_6$$ thruster using a combined framework of three-dimensional numerical simulations and hot-fire experiments. A non-premixed unlike-impinging injector was compared against two premixed configurations under identical propellant mass flow rates, mixture ratios, and combustor geometries. Numerically, the premixed like-doublet impinging configuration showed a 16.4% increase in thrust over the non-premixed baseline, and these trends were successfully validated through hot-fire tests. While the single-hole configuration experienced flashback, the premixed like-doublet thruster sustained stable 5-s combustion, delivering a sea-level thrust of 5.34 N and a specific impulse ( $$I_{sp}$$ ) of 111 s. This represents an 11.1% increase in $$I_{sp}$$ over the non-premixed baseline, along with a characteristic velocity rise from 1336 to 1350 m/s. This improvement is attributed to enhanced propellant mixing and a more uniform axial flow field through the nozzle. This comprehensive numerical and experimental investigation demonstrates the definitive performance advantages of the premixed injection strategy, providing critical design benchmarks for next-generation high-performance propulsion systems.

Article.Title: Membrane lipid composition is associated with differential sensitivity to apigenin in U937 and HL-60 cells: insights from cell-based and Langmuir monolayer studies
Article.Authors: Kreczmer B.; Dyba B.; Barbasz A.; Binkowski Ł.; Nowak-Gawryał L.; Rudolphi-Szydło E.
Article.Abstract: Apigenin is a naturally occurring dietary flavonoid increasingly investigated for its biological activity, including effects on cell survival, oxidative stress, and membrane-associated processes. Interactions between polyphenols and membrane lipids may influence membrane organization and contribute to differences in cellular responses. This study examined the effects of apigenin on human myeloid U937 and HL-60 cells using an integrated approach combining biological assays with biomimetic membrane models. Cell viability and oxidative stress-related parameters were evaluated using MTT, LDH, and MDA assays. In parallel, Langmuir lipid monolayers reproducing the characteristic membrane lipid compositions of U937 and HL-60 cells were used to investigate the effects of apigenin on membrane mechanical properties. Apigenin reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner, with HL-60 cells exhibiting greater sensitivity than U937 cells. Biophysical analyses showed that apigenin altered lipid monolayer properties by decreasing the compression modulus and increasing membrane elasticity. The magnitude of these effects depended on membrane lipid composition and was more pronounced in HL-60 membrane models, paralleling the greater sensitivity observed in cellular assays. These findings demonstrate that membrane lipid composition may contribute to variations in cellular sensitivity to apigenin and highlight the importance of membrane organization in studies of lipid-polyphenol interactions and their biological consequences.

Article.Title: Predicting meteorological-disaster-induced damage to melon crops in Taiwan by using decision-tree-based algorithms
Article.Authors: Fang S.; Chang Y.; Chang S.; Tsai B.; Kuo B.
Article.Abstract: Agrometeorological disasters pose substantial risks to melon ( Cucumis melo L.) production. This study developed interpretable decision-tree-based models to predict both the occurrence and severity of crop damage caused by typhoon-induced rainfall (TIR), non-typhoon-induced rainfall (NTIR), and cold events—the primary hazards affecting melon cultivation in Taiwan. Classification and regression tree (CART) and M5′ regression tree models were used to predict damage occurrence and damage percentage, respectively, based on county-level disaster records (2003–2022) and meteorological data. The model-derived decision rules were consistent with Taiwan’s climatic characteristics and identified an average temperature of approximately 22.4 °C as an empirical threshold for melon cultivation based on the present dataset. The CART models achieved reliable classification performance, with recall, precision, accuracy, and kappa values exceeding 82.46%, 88.24%, 88.43%, and 76.65%, respectively. The M5′ model showed the highest accuracy for predicting damage percentage in cold events but performed less effectively for TIR and NTIR events. More complex models (random forest and Cubist) did not yield consistent improvements, suggesting that performance limitations are primarily due to missing key predictors rather than model complexity. Overall, this study highlights both the potential and limitations of machine learning for agricultural risk assessment under data constraints.

Article.Title: Evaluation of haematological inflammatory ratios in migraine: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Sochań P.; Grodzka O.; Sochań P.; Kępczyńska K.; Domitrz I.
Article.Abstract: Haematological inflammatory ratios, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), have emerged as potential biomarkers in various neurological disorders. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate these ratios in patients with migraine compared with healthy controls and other headache disorders, and to assess differences across migraine subtypes and clinical phases. The systematic review with meta-analysis was conducted according to the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed (MEDLINE), Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE Ultimate, and Embase were searched from their inception to 26 April 2025. Additionally, backward and forward citation searches were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models employing the DerSimonian–Laird method and Hartung–Knapp adjustment were used to estimate pooled mean values with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I² and Cochran’s Q tests. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Begg’s test. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria, and 21 were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled mean NLR was significantly higher in patients with migraine compared to healthy controls, particularly in those with migraine with aura and during the ictal phase. No significant differences were found between migraine and tension-type headache. Other ratios showed no significant intergroup differences. S ubstantial heterogeneity and the observational design of included studies were noted as limitations. Among the evaluated ratios, the NLR appeared to most consistently reflect inflammatory processes in migraine, especially in migraine with aura and during the ictal period. However, its clinical utility remains uncertain and further studies are needed to clarify their potential role as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251041190. No external funding was received.

Article.Title: Thermal management characteristics of lithium-ion batteries based on spring baffle design
Article.Authors: Tang Y.; Shao X.; Hu Y.; Guan T.; Wang P.; Wang L.; Deng G.; Wei W.
Article.Abstract: To address the issues of elevated temperature and poor temperature uniformity in battery modules during high-intensity operation when using traditional parallel flow channel liquid cooling plates, this study proposes a biomimetic fin liquid cooling plate integrated with spring baffles. Numerical simulations were conducted to compare the performance differences between the proposed cooling plate and conventional parallel channel designs. The effects of three inlet clearances ( H 1 , H 2 , and H 3 ) of the spring baffles on cooling performance were systematically investigated, and the optimal parameters were determined through orthogonal experiments. The results indicate that the influence of inlet clearance on cooling performance follows the order: H 3 > H 1 > H 2 . Under the optimal configuration (Case 5-2: H 1 \(= 2.5\,\textrm{mm}\) , H 1 \(= 5.0\,\textrm{mm}\) , H 3 \(= 7.5\,\textrm{mm}\) ), significant improvements were achieved compared to the conventional system. Specifically, the maximum temperature decreased by \(2.312\,^{\circ }\textrm{C}\) ( \(8.027\%\) ), and the maximum temperature difference was reduced by \(2.055\,^{\circ }\textrm{C}\) ( \(77.811\%\) ), while the pressure drop increased slightly by \(6.081\,\textrm{Pa}\) ( \(2.183\%\) ). These results demonstrate that the proposed design effectively enhances thermal performance while maintaining a relatively low hydraulic penalty, providing a promising solution for battery thermal management applications.

Article.Title: Federated privacy-preserving facial paralysis severity classification using hybrid deep learning and pufferfish optimization
Article.Authors: Kiruthiga S.; Anbuananth C.; Dhilipkumar V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Facial paralysis (FP) severity assessment requires accurate identification of subtle facial asymmetry while maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive patient information. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches require patient images to be transferred to a central repository, which can increase privacy risks and limit collaborative learning across healthcare institutions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Federated Learning-based Secure and Privacy-Preserving Hybrid Deep Learning with Pufferfish Optimization (FLSDPP-HDLPO) framework for automated FP severity classification. The proposed framework first performs image preprocessing and augmentation to improve facial-image quality and class representation. A hybrid feature extraction strategy integrating Capsule Network (CapsNet), ResNet50, and LeViT is then employed to learn complementary spatial, hierarchical, and attention-based facial representations. The extracted features are classified using a CNN-BiGRU architecture, while the Pufferfish Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to optimize the relevant model parameters. To preserve data confidentiality during distributed learning, homomorphic encryption is incorporated into the federated learning process so that sensitive model information can be securely exchanged without exposing the original patient data. The framework is evaluated using combined MEEI and YFP facial paralysis datasets containing six severity classes. Experimental evaluation under different training and testing configurations demonstrates that the proposed FLSDPP-HDLPO framework achieves a maximum classification accuracy of 97.56%, with precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score of 92.48%, 92.53%, 98.54%, and 92.50%, respectively. Repeated experiments further produced an accuracy of 97.56% ± 0.42%, demonstrating consistent performance. The proposed framework therefore provides an accurate and privacy-preserving approach for distributed FP severity assessment. Future work will focus on larger multi-center datasets, stronger robustness evaluation, computational optimization, and real-world clinical validation.

Article.Title: Innovative application of frankincense resin as a sustainable bio-adhesive for insect trapping in legume crops
Article.Authors: Ammar R.; Kandil R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Field experiments were conducted in Kafr El-Dawar, El-Beheira, Egypt during the 2025 summer season using a completely randomized design with four replications to evaluate bio-adhesive sticky traps formulated from frankincense resin as eco-friendly alternatives to imported commercial traps in cowpea fields. Two colors (yellow and blue) were tested for each trap. Luban-based adhesive was prepared using frankincense resin, starch, sugar, yeast, beeswax, molasses, and essential oils. Yellow traps captured significantly higher numbers of aphids and whiteflies compared with other pest groups, with no significant differences between Luban-based and commercial traps for most pests, except cotton bollworm where Luban traps recorded significantly higher captures. Blue Luban traps also outperformed commercial ones in capturing whiteflies, jassids, thrips, and cotton bollworm, while aphid and cowpea beetle catches were statistically similar. Economic analysis revealed that Luban-based traps cost less (360 L.E/fed) than commercial traps (780 L.E/fed). Although commercial traps resulted in a significantly higher yield, the net return and investment ratio remained comparable between treatments (0.26 and 0.27). Furthermore, a preliminary carbon-footprint assessment indicated that Luban-based traps reduced estimated environmental emissions by approximately 25–40% compared to imported synthetic traps, due to their biodegradable composition and reliance on locally sourced natural materials, supporting low-carbon agricultural systems. These findings indicate that Luban-based sticky traps are cost-effective, environmentally sustainable, and demonstrate considerable potential as patentable innovations that enable sustainable pest management in cowpea systems and reducing dependence on chemical insecticides.

Article.Title: Machine-learning classification of myocardial infarction and ST/T-change ECG phenotypes across complementary evaluation settings
Article.Authors: Jin M.; Tang X.; Lei Y.; Sun X.
Article.Abstract: The primary PTB-XL outcome was an operational ECG phenotype defined by myocardial infarction and/or ST/T-change diagnostic superclass labels, rather than adjudicated active ischemia. Public ECG datasets were harmonized to 10-s, 12-lead, 100-Hz inputs. Patient-disjoint PTB-XL partitions were used to compare an age/sex baseline, a downsampled-waveform logistic-regression model, a compact residual network, MiniRocket–ridge, and a fusion model. In the primary held-out test set, AUROC/AUPRC were 0.649/0.654 for the linear waveform model, 0.964/0.967 for the residual network, and 0.953/0.960 for MiniRocket. Exploratory subgroup AUROCs for the unchanged composite-trained MiniRocket model were 0.923 for MI-only, 0.969 for ST/T-change-only, and 0.998 for combined MI + ST/T-change ECGs. In the PTB Diagnostic ECG Database, MiniRocket achieved an AUROC of 0.936 (95% CI, 0.899–0.965) and AUPRC of 0.987 (0.977–0.993), versus 0.924 (0.888–0.954) and 0.983 (0.972–0.991) for the residual network; paired analyses showed no clear difference in external discrimination. The 0.5 threshold was descriptive, while validation-derived thresholds were applied unchanged externally. In STAFF III, model probability increased during coronary occlusion in 51/80 paired comparisons, with changes dependent on baseline definition. Overall, the models classified dataset-defined ECG phenotypes, while the STAFF III findings support only an exploratory, baseline-dependent association with controlled occlusion. Clinical evaluation requires representative cohorts with adjudicated outcomes.

Article.Title: Disturbance-aware hybrid signal–vehicle control for service maintenance in mixed-autonomy urban networks
Article.Authors: Fang H.; Yin Z.; Wang Y.; Tang Z.; Zhu G.; Lu Q.
Article.Abstract: Mixed-autonomy urban networks may experience rapid service degradation when local capacity losses interact with demand surges and queue spillback. This study formulates disturbance-period traffic management as a service-maintenance problem and proposes Res-STC (Resilience-oriented Signal-Traffic Cooperative Control), a hybrid multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework that coordinates network-level signal decisions with local speed guidance for eligible connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs). A cascaded graph-attention/Transformer encoder represents adjacent-intersection coupling and longer-range network dependencies, while an engineering-constrained execution layer enforces minimum and maximum green times, yellow/all-red transitions, and directional anti-starvation rules. Experiments were conducted in SUMO on a 4 × 4 Hangzhou benchmark network adapted from the network used in CoLight, comprising 16 signalized intersections, under 13 demand, disturbance, and CAV-penetration scenarios. Across 10 matched simulation seeds for a selected trained policy, Res-STC achieved the highest or near-highest mean operational performance in most scenarios, particularly in average speed, throughput, and completion rate. Relative to the signal-only ablation, the scenario-level mean change in average speed ranged from − 0.01% to 4.90%, and the corresponding mean change in throughput ranged from − 0.29% to 3.89%. These descriptive results indicate that network-level signal coordination is the primary source of improvement, whereas CAV speed guidance acts as a complementary, scenario-dependent local actuator rather than a substitute for signal control.

Article.Title: A VSV-based pseudotyping system for studying entry and neutralization of papiine alphaherpesvirus 2
Article.Authors: Elsasser L.; Gärtner S.; Stomberg P.; Schröter L.; Naßl A.; Decker K.; Arora P.; Damert A.; Pöhlmann S.; Winkler M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simplexviruses of non-human primates differ in their capacity to cause severe disease in humans. Papiine alphaherpesvirus 2 (PaHV-2) of baboons has not been reported to be pathogenic in humans while human infection with macacine alphaherpesvirus 1 (McHV-1, Herpes B Virus) can cause fatal disease. In order to study PaHV-2 entry into cells, we established a pseudotyping system based on vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). For this, the genes coding for core glycoproteins of PaHV-2, gD, gH, gL and gB as well as gC were cloned and the glycoproteins were equipped either with the native signal peptide or a heterologous signal peptide and an epitope tag. Glycoproteins with Igκ-signal peptide were most robustly expressed and incorporated into pseudotyped VSV particles. VSV bearing the core glycoproteins (DHLB pp ) or an extended set of glycoproteins (DHLBC pp ) efficiently entered several cell lines of human, rhesus macaque, African green monkey and mouse origin. In addition, DHLB pp were efficiently neutralized by baboon sera at levels comparable to those determined with a PaHV-2 reporter virus. In summary, VSV particles bearing glycoproteins of PaHV-2 are a novel tool to study PaHV-2 entry and neutralization.

Article.Title: From arithmetic-sequence gradient architectures to interfacial-modulus-corrected bending models in laser-sintered laminates
Article.Authors: Han Z.; Wang Y.; Liu S.; Hu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Laser-sintered 316 L/CuSn10 laminates with slow, medium, and fast gradient transitions are fabricated via arithmetic-sequence stacking. Classical laminate theory predicts nearly identical elastic bending stiffness for all configurations (differences < 1%). Three-point bending tests, however, reveal strong gradient-rate dependence: the medium-gradient configuration exhibits the highest maximum bending load (837.850 N), which is ~ 103% and ~ 55% higher than those of the slow- (412.247 N) and fast-gradient (540.714 N) configurations, respectively. The experimental bending stiffness per unit width also varies markedly (slow: 59,851 N·mm; medium: 136,249 N·mm; fast: 94,375 N·mm), contradicting classical predictions. This discrepancy exposes a fundamental limitation of classical laminate theory—its neglect of interfacial modulus degradation induced during laser sintering. To address this, a modified bending stiffness model is developed, incorporating elastic modulus attenuation within the interfacial transition zone and a gradient-distribution-controlled weakening factor. The modified model quantitatively reproduces the experimental bending stiffness values and their ranking (medium > fast > slow). These results establish a quantitative framework for regulating elastic behaviour through gradient sequence design in laser-sintered multi-material laminates.

Article.Title: Association of post-therapy serum 131I counts with treatment outcomes in differentiated thyroid cancer: a prospective observational study
Article.Authors: Hwang S.; Cha J.; Kim J.; Kang S.; Jeong J.; Nam K.; Chung W.; Kang W.; Chun J.; Cho A.
Article.Abstract: We investigated the association of post-therapy serum 131 I counts with treatment outcomes in differentiated thyroid cancer. We prospectively enrolled patients receiving high-activity 131 I as initial postoperative radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy (n = 84), repeat therapy (n = 24), or metastatic disease treatment (n = 23). Serum 131 I counts and day-7 whole-body scintigraphy (WBS) were evaluated against treatment success and recurrence in the non-metastatic cohort, and favorable response (≥ 25% TSH-suppressed thyroglobulin [on-Tg] reduction) and progressive disease in the metastatic cohort. In non-metastatic patients, serum 131 I counts strongly correlated with WBS neck counts (ρ = 0.778, p < 0.001), whereas stimulated thyroglobulin (off-Tg) correlated with WBS counts only in treatment-naïve patients (ρ = 0.334, p = 0.001). Treatment success was independently associated with high serum 131 I counts (OR 11.02) and low off-Tg (OR 88.32), and serum 131 I counts further stratified outcomes within off-Tg-defined groups. In metastatic patients, serum 131 I counts were more strongly associated with on-Tg reduction than off-Tg (OR 45.50 vs. 19.27), and low serum 131 I counts were associated with progressive disease. Findings in the metastatic cohort should be considered exploratory given the small sample size and limited number of progression events. Post-therapy serum 131 I counts correlated with WBS uptake and were associated with subsequent treatment outcomes.

Article.Title: Baseline characteristics of a randomized cohort of black women enrolled in a stress-management enhanced behavioral weight loss intervention
Article.Authors: Cooper A.; Sutton S.; Henderson J.; Pittman S.; Peña A.; Doerr V.; Baskin M.; Epel E.; Gwede C.; West D.; Carson T.
Article.Abstract: “Reducing Weight and Elevated Stress Levels Using Educational and Behavioral Tools”- The RESET Study, is a randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy of a culturally relevant stress management enhanced behavioral weight loss intervention (BWL-Stress) to improve weight loss outcomes in Black women with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m 2 ) compared with behavioral weight loss alone (BWL-Alone). This report describes the baseline characteristics of our randomized cohort, and the relationships among weight, perceived psychological stress, diet, and physical activity (PA) at baseline. Eligible participants were Black/African-American women, 21–75 years old, with obesity and elevated stress levels (PSS-10 ≥ 13) in the Tampa Bay area. Participants ( n = 343) were randomized to BWL-Stress or BWL-Alone, of which baseline data for 338 participants were used for these analyses. There were 172 BWL-Alone and 166 BWL-Stress participants. Ages ranged from 22 to 74 years (mean ± SD, 49.8 ± 11.8). Mean BMI was 40.5 (± 7.5) kg/m 2 . The mean PSS-10 score was 22.4 (± 5.3). Significant differences in main outcome variables (i.e., weight, BMI, perceived stress) were observed between treatment groups at baseline. Participants who engaged in PA at least once per week had lower weight (r(337)= -0.11, p = 0.04). There was a significant correlation between weekday energy intake and PSS-10 (r(254) = 0.13, p = 0.033). Significant correlations among demographic variables and weight and PSS-10 were also observed. The RESET study has successfully randomized a large cohort of Black/African-American women with obesity and self-reported elevated stress levels. Baseline analyses demonstrate significant associations among weight, stress, and demographic characteristics. The study will longitudinally examine the effects of the intervention on weight loss outcomes over a 1-year period. Trial registration: Clinical trials # NCT04335799, 06/04/2020.

Article.Title: Plasma membrane vesicles preserve cell type specific physicochemical signatures
Article.Authors: Pogoda K.; Chrabąszcz K.; Deptuła P.; Bucki R.; Piergies N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The plasma membrane encodes critical information about cellular identity and phenotype, yet detailed characterization of this complex interface remains technically challenging in whole cells. Giant plasma membrane vesicles (GPMVs), generated via chemically induced blebbing, offer a simplified yet biochemically rich model of the cell membrane. Here, we investigate whether GPMVs retain biophysical and biochemical properties reflective of their cell of origin. Using a panel of human cell lines - including microglial and four glioblastoma cell lines - we characterized both cells and their vesicles using fluorescence microscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, and principal component analysis (PCA). GPMVs preserved cell-line-specific stiffness ranking observed in AFM measurements, and notably, FT-IR spectra of GPMVs enabled discrimination between cell lines, unlike spectra from intact cells. Our results highlight GPMVs as faithful surrogates of native membranes and suggest their utility for biophysical phenotyping in health and disease.

Article.Title: Thermo-hydraulic limits of streamwise rib height grading in high-aspect-ratio cooling channels
Article.Authors: Yekani S.; DindarSafa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rib turbulators are the standard means of enhancing internal cooling in gas turbine blades, and a recent line of work proposes grading the rib height along the flow so that turbulence is generated where the coolant is coldest. The degree of grading over which this remains beneficial has not been established. The present study quantifies that range for a high-aspect-ratio (AR = 4) rectangular channel with five square ribs mounted on a uniformly heated wall. The grading is described by a single parameter, the rib height ratio RHR, defined as the ratio of the first to the last rib height at a fixed pitch and a fixed downstream rib height, and five configurations from RHR = 1 (uniform) to RHR = 5 are compared on an otherwise identical geometry. Three-dimensional steady RANS simulations with the SST k–ω model are performed for Reynolds numbers from 2 × 10⁴ to 8 × 10⁴. Increasing RHR raises the normalised Nusselt number monotonically, from 1.29 to 1.42 at Re = 8 × 10⁴, but the normalised friction factor rises from 2.05 to 4.30 over the same range, an increase an order of magnitude larger. Both performance criteria therefore fall monotonically with RHR: at Re = 8 × 10⁴ the thermal performance factor η₁ decreases from 1.016 to 0.870, so that under an equal-pumping-power constraint the uniform array outperforms every graded array examined. The flow field identifies the cause: beyond moderate grading the tall leading ribs cease to act as discrete turbulence promoters and collectively deflect the bulk flow away from the heated wall, lifting the shear layer off the surface and leaving a low-momentum, low-Nusselt-number region downstream that offsets much of the upstream gain. Applying η₁ ≥ 1 as a design criterion yields an admissible upper limit that contracts from RHR = 4.41 at Re = 2 × 10⁴ to RHR = 1.36 at Re = 8 × 10⁴. Height grading therefore remains attractive where heat transfer rather than pumping power is the binding constraint, since it delivers up to 10% more heat transfer, but the admissible degree of grading must be selected for the design Reynolds number.

Article.Title: Culture conditions influence biomass and alkali-insoluble cell-wall polysaccharide production in indigenous Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains
Article.Authors: Mosallaie F.; Falah F.; Rahimi A.; Khabiri Noghani M.; Kashaninejad M.; Alizadeh Behbahani B.; Vasiee A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Saccharomyces cerevisiae is an important source of yeast biomass and alkali–insoluble cell–wall polysaccharide fractions (AICWP), which may contain substantial β–glucan. In the present study, indigenous yeast isolates from diverse natural sources were screened for biomass formation and AICWP accumulation. Four S. cerevisiae strains, selected from 54 previously isolated yeasts, were evaluated for growth performance under the investigated culture conditions. Yeast isolates were obtained through selective cultivation and characterized morphologically and microscopically. High biomass–producing isolates were identified through growth–based screening, and the effects of glucose, ammonium sulfate, and inoculum size on biomass accumulation were assessed using a Plackett–Burman (PB) design and further examined by Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Under one set of selected cultivation conditions, biomass concentration reached 250.01 g/L wet weight (100.04 g/L dry weight), and the alkali–insoluble cell–wall fraction contained 7.01 g/L total carbohydrate expressed as glucose equivalents. Because the phenol–sulfuric acid assay is non–specific, this value represents total carbohydrate equivalents in the extracted alkali–insoluble fraction and does not constitute a direct measurement of purified β–glucan. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed dense aggregation of yeast cells with predominantly oval–to–round morphology and generally intact surfaces, consistent with the typical morphology of S. cerevisiae . Biomass concentration declined by approximately 18% under 5% sorbitol and by 36% under 0.005% SDS; viable counts were 8.83 and 8.20 Log CFU/mL, respectively, compared with 9.07 Log CFU/mL in the control. Evaluation in a 3–L stirred–tank bioreactor with a 1–L working volume revealed that spray drying yielded a higher recovered dry powder concentration (144.75 ± 2.90 g/L) than freeze drying (125.12 ± 2.50 g/L), whereas freeze drying yielded higher viable–cell recovery after rehydration and 24 h incubation (0.2 × 10 9 vs. 0.9 × 10 8 CFU/mL). These findings provide preliminary feasibility evidence under the tested bioreactor conditions; further studies are required to evaluate oxygen transfer, hydrodynamics, reproducibility, and scalability.

Article.Title: Social influence under uncertainty: decision-making in anonymous crowds
Article.Authors: Konya K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uncertainty and limited access to information may trigger unpredictable group dynamics and unsafe movements in urban crowds. Although such situations are common in everyday life, the socio-psychological mechanisms that guide decision making in crowds have scarcely been explored, apart from the controversially discussed concept of contagion. This experimental study aims to make an initial empirical approximation of this issue by examining how (non-)communication and group size affect the duration and homogeneity of group-level decisions in an anonymous setting. The results show that communication does not affect the duration of finding final solutions, but it can lead to both polarized or homogeneous outcomes. The absence of communication, on the other hand, may activate self-presentational concerns and lowers the possibility of highly homogeneous outcomes. These findings are discussed in light of mechanisms of social influence and conformity that could be identified through the videographic analysis of the experiments.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware yield prediction for data-limited polystyrene autoxidation using heteroscedastic ensemble learning
Article.Authors: Lee Y.; Kim T.; Moon H.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning-based yield prediction in chemical reaction systems is often limited by small experimental datasets and condition-dependent variability. Here, we develop an ensemble regression framework that combines Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost) with a heteroscedastic deep learning with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to predict reaction yields from limited data while estimating condition-specific uncertainty. The framework was evaluated using 137 experimental samples from polystyrene autoxidation reactions. The ensemble model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.4 ± 0.2, up to a 62% reduction relative to linear baseline methods (Linear Regression, Ridge, Lasso), and an approximately 24% reduction relative to the strongest single-model baseline evaluated (NGBoost alone, MAE = 7.1), outperforming the individual NGBoost and MLP models. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-based interpretation showed that the model captured non-linear response patterns associated with NaBr/Mn acetate loading, and reaction time, which were consistent with experimentally observed trends. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware ensemble learning can support reaction condition screening and prioritization in data-limited chemical systems.

Article.Title: Independent genome-wide association mapping confirms a major genomic region associated with curly wood formation in Betula pendula var. carelica
Article.Authors: Tis M.; Shumkova V.; Karzhaev D.; Safronycheva E.; Grigoreva E.; Volkov V.; Vetchinnikova L.; Zhigunov A.; Potokina E.
Article.Abstract: Curly birch ( Betula pendula Roth var. carelica (Mercklin) Hämet-Ahti) is a rare and highly valued tree characterized by a distinctive figured wood phenotype, but the genetic basis of this trait remains unresolved. Here, we independently tested and refined a chromosome 10 region previously associated with curly wood formation. A ddRADseq-based GWAS in 96 unrelated birches confirmed the major association previously detected in full-sib families. Whole-genome resequencing of four curly and two non-curly trees identified 1,872 SNVs within the previously defined ~ 1.2 Mb interval, which were subsequently subjected to annotation-guided prioritization and KASP/STS marker testing. Local linkage disequilibrium analysis further defined an ~ 275 kb LD-enriched interval (3,249,985–3,524,841 bp) containing 22 annotated protein-coding loci. Several annotation-prioritized variants within this interval showed strong and reproducible marker-phenotype associations in both unrelated and full-sib populations, although none have yet been established as causal. The reproducibility of the chromosome 10 association across independent sample designs supports a major-locus architecture of curly wood formation. The refined interval provides a focused target for identifying the causal variation and for further validation of molecular markers for early selection.

Article.Title: Reinitiation rates after discontinuation of glaucoma eye drop therapy: evidence from Japanese Health Insurance Claims
Article.Authors: Kabeya K.; Satoh H.; Yanagi N.; Sawada Y.
Article.Abstract: Glaucoma is the leading cause of blindness in Japan, yet persistence with topical intraocular pressure–lowering therapy is poor and many patients discontinue treatment. What happens after discontinuation—whether patients reinitiate therapy—has been little studied. Using a nationwide Japanese health insurance claims database, we analyzed outpatient records from January 2005 to June 2024 to quantify reinitiation after discontinuation of glaucoma eyedrop therapy. Discontinuation events were identified, and annual reinitiation rates were calculated for each of the five years thereafter; associations with patient and product characteristics were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Among 111,438 patients who discontinued therapy, 82,215 remained observable through the end of the first year following discontinuation; of these, 42.3% reinitiated treatment within that year, and the 5-year cumulative reinitiation probability was 52.5%. Younger age and discontinuation early after treatment initiation were associated with a lower likelihood of resuming therapy, and products requiring more frequent daily instillation were likewise linked to lower reinitiation. These findings indicate that prescription records are consistent with short cycles of treatment interruption and resumption being common in routine practice, and they may help clinicians prioritize follow-up and select regimens that support treatment continuity and return to care.

Article.Title: G protein-coupled estrogen receptor protects renal ischemia-reperfusion injury by reducing endoplasmic reticulum stress apoptosis in rat kidney
Article.Authors: Ma Y.; Liu N.; Yang J.; Zhang Q.; Chang Y.; Jiang R.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the relationship between G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) and renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. Twelve-week-old female rats were randomly divided into normal control group, ovariectomized (OVX) group, OVX + I/R group, OVX + I/R + vehicle group, OVX + I/R + E2 (estrogen intervention) group, OVX + I/R + G1 (GPER agonist intervention) group, OVX + I/R + G15 (GPER antagonist) + G1 group. The renal function of rats in each group after ischemia-reperfusion was detected. The transcriptomic profile of renal tissue in estrogen intervention group and ischemia-reperfusion group was analyzed by mRNA sequencing, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were enriched in negative apoptosis regulation and other pathways. The expression of renal tissue myeloperoxidase (MPO) and endoplasmic reticulum stress apoptosis-related proteins and the apoptosis of renal tubular epithelial cells were observed. Compared with the OVX group, the serum creatinine (SCr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) in the OVX + I/R group were significantly increased ( P < 0.01), the Paller score was significantly increased ( P < 0.01), and the MPO level was significantly increased ( P < 0.01). The expression of GRP78, CHOP and Caspase-12 proteins in renal tubular epithelial cells was significantly increased ( P < 0.01), and TUNEL staining showed a significant increase in apoptotic renal tubular epithelial cells. Compared with OVX + I/R group, the serum creatinine (SCr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) of renal function in OVX + I/R + E2 group and OVX + I/R + G1 group were significantly decreased ( P < 0.01), the Paller score was significantly decreased ( P < 0.01), the MPO level was significantly decreased ( P < 0.01), the expression of GRP78, CHOP and Caspase-12 proteins was significantly decreased ( P < 0.01), and the apoptosis of renal tubular epithelial cells was significantly decreased ( P < 0.01). Activation of G protein-coupled estrogen receptor may attenuate renal I/R injury, which is associated with down-regulation of the endoplasmic reticulum stress-mediated apoptotic pathway.

Article.Title: Reinforcement learning for multi-metric QoS optimization in 5G/6G networks with Shannon capacity integration
Article.Authors: Ibrahim H.; Elewah I.; Alanazi T.; EL-Afifi M.; Hamza A.; Sakr H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the use of reinforcement learning (RL) techniques to optimize Quality of Service (QoS) parameters in both 5G and 6G wireless networks. A multi-phase experimental framework was employed to evaluate key QoS metrics including latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and bit error rate (BER) across both generations. In the first phase, an RL agent was trained in a 5G environment, achieving notable improvements in latency reduction, jitter control, and throughput enhancement. Comparative analysis in the second phase demonstrated that 6G networks consistently outperformed 5G, yielding higher RL rewards, lower packet loss, and reduced jitter and latency. In the final phase, Shannon Capacity theory was integrated into the RL model, further enhancing transmission reliability and signal quality in the 6G context. Additional testing with video streaming scenarios confirmed 6G’s superior capability in supporting real-time, high-reliability applications. Overall, the findings indicate that 6G networks, when optimized with RL, provide a more intelligent, robust, and efficient solution for future wireless communication systems.

Article.Title: EU ETS carbon price forecasting via VMGE-Net: a variational decomposition and channel-aware GRU framework
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Zhang X.; Tao T.; Peng C.; Xi F.
Article.Abstract: Daily carbon prices in the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) exhibit non-stationarity, multi-scale fluctuations, and changes in market regimes, which complicate short-horizon forecasting. This study proposes VMGE-Net, a compact forecasting model that combines Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) encoder, and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA). VMD organizes the target-price sequence permitted under the specified evaluation protocol into frequency-specific components, the GRU encoder models temporal dependencies in the fused mode and covariate sequence, and ECA recalibrates the resulting hidden channels without dimensionality reduction. The empirical analysis uses 1994 daily EU ETS observations collected between January 20, 2017 and March 18, 2026, together with 25 market and engineered predictors. Under the diagnostic full-series VMD setting, VMGE-Net obtained an $$R^2$$ of 0.8834, an RMSE of 2.1009 EUR/ton, an MAE of 1.3639 EUR/ton, and a MAPE of 1.92%. Under stricter expanding-window and 252-trading-day rolling-window VMD protocols, the corresponding $$R^2$$ values were 0.8657 and 0.8587, respectively, and both settings remained more accurate than the raw-sequence GRU benchmark. Ablation, repeated-run, sensitivity, direct multi-step, rolling-backtesting, complexity, paired-significance, and block-permutation analyses indicate that the observed improvement is associated primarily with frequency-aware signal organization, with an additional contribution from lightweight hidden-channel recalibration. These findings support VMGE-Net as a computationally compact approach to short-horizon EU ETS carbon-price forecasting, while its generalizability to other markets and temporal resolutions remains to be examined.

Article.Title: Retraction Note: Climatic zoning of Xinjiang for heterogeneous production of high-quality wine
Article.Authors: Feng X.; Xiang-ling T.
Article.Abstract: After publication, concerns have been raised about reliability of the references. Specifically, multiple References (1-6, 8-12, 15- 25, 29, 31, 35) could not be verified, and References 3, 7, 22 and 23 appear to be duplicates of 14, 30, 33 and 34, respectively. The Authors did not respond to the concerns raised.

Article.Title: Author Correction: N-mixture models with camera trap imagery produce accurate abundance estimates of ungulates
Article.Authors: Harris G.; Stewart D.; Butler M.; Rominger E.; Ruhl C.; McDonald D.; Schmidt P.
