Article.Abstract: “Abundance estimates from filtered images captured by motion detection in 3-day intervals included the censused value across all seasons for adult DBS, rams and ewes, indicating “best practices”. This “best practices” method also captured censused values for population estimates of bison (detection-nondetection) and cattle with both priors. Our assessment validates the use of N-mixture with camera trap imagery, while presenting sampling approaches, data handling procedures and model calibration to estimate wildlife population sizes more appropriately and accurately.”

Article.Title: Caspase-11-mediated non-canonical pyroptosis is a key mechanism of alveolar epithelial cell injury in LPS-induced ARDS
Article.Authors: Yin Y.; Zeng Z.; Wei S.; Wei X.; Shen Z.; Zeng Y.; Yu Y.; Cong Z.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Alveolar epithelial cells (AECs) injury is a critical event in the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS); however, the underlying mechanisms remain complex, and it is still unclear which cell death or inflammatory pathway predominates. In this study, we analyzed transcriptomic data from primary AECs in ARDS and compared the enrichment levels of six cell death pathways, and found that pyroptosis was the most significantly altered pathway. Subsequently, we validated these findings using a mouse model of ARDS and an in vitro LPS transfection model, and demonstrated that AECs pyroptosis is primarily mediated by Caspase-11. Furthermore, we optimized the conditions for LPS transfection to establish a model of non-canonical pyroptosis in AECs. Collectively, these results indicate that Caspase-11‑mediated non‑canonical pyroptosis is an important mechanism of AECs destruction in ARDS, and provide a new strategy for targeted therapy.

Article.Title: Comparison of quality of life and burnout between professional family caregivers for older adults and nursing assistants in nursing homes: results from KASA studies
Article.Authors: Boucaud-Maitre D.; Dramé M.; Belmin J.; Simo N.; Pic O.; Dartigues J.; Amieva H.; Tabué-Teguo M.
Article.Abstract: In the French Caribbean Islands, professional foster families provide care for older adults with clinical and functional profiles comparable to those of residents in nursing homes. This study aimed to compare quality of life and burnout risk between foster caregivers and nursing assistants employed in nursing homes over a one-year period. Two parallel, prospective observational cohorts were conducted among foster caregivers and nursing assistants, with assessments at baseline (T0), 6 months (T6), and 12 months (T12) through on-site evaluations. Data collection included sociodemographic characteristics, quality of life measured using the 36-item short form health survey (SF-36), and burnout symptoms assessed with the professional quality of life scale (Pro-QOL). Analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models. A total of 56 foster caregivers (mean age 60.3 ± 6.8 years; 2% male) and 82 nursing assistants (mean age 45.8 ± 11.3 years; 17% male) were included. Foster caregivers reported significantly higher SF-36 scores across nearly all domains, with the largest differences observed for vitality (β = 23.6; 95% CI: 16.1–31.1), role-emotional (β = 17.9; 95% CI: 7.7–28.0), and mental health (β = 12.3; 95% CI: 6.2–18.5). Burnout scores were significantly lower among foster caregivers (β = 8.2; 95% CI: 5.9–10.4). At 12 months, mean burnout scores were 13.3 in foster caregivers versus 23.4 in nursing assistants, with 9.8% and 40.9%, respectively, classified as being at moderate risk ( p < 0.001). No significant time-by-group interaction was observed for either SF-36 or Pro-QOL scores. Overall, foster caregivers reported better quality of life and a substantially reduced risk of burnout compared with nursing assistants. As the foster family model for older adults continues to expand, nursing assistants interested in transitioning into this role may represent particularly suitable candidates for professional foster caregiving.

Article.Title: Integrated seismic and petrophysical characterization of the Kharita Formation in the SELKIT and SETHOS fields, Western Desert, Egypt
Article.Authors: Sarhan M.; Abdel-Fattah M.; Hamdan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Kharita Formation represents one of the principal Lower Cretaceous clastic reservoirs in the Shushan Basin, Western Desert, Egypt. This study integrates seismic interpretation and petrophysical analysis to evaluate the reservoir characteristics, structural controls, and hydrocarbon potential of the Kharita Formation in the SELKIT and SETHOS fields, South Umbaraka Area. The investigation was based on the interpretation of thirty 2D seismic profiles and conventional well-log data from the SELK-6, SELK-7, and SETHOS-16 wells. Seismic interpretation was conducted to delineate the structural framework, fault architecture, and trapping configurations, while petrophysical analysis was performed to determine lithology, shale volume, porosity, fluid saturation, and net-pay distribution. Neutron-density crossplots were also utilized to identify lithological variations and potential gas-bearing intervals. The seismic interpretation reveals that the study area is structurally controlled by a series of major normal faults and fault-bounded anticlinal closures that significantly influence reservoir distribution and hydrocarbon accumulation. Time- and depth-structure maps of the Kharita Formation indicate that both the SELKIT and SETHOS fields occupy structurally elevated four-way dip closures, providing favorable trapping conditions. Correlation of the Cretaceous succession further demonstrates the influence of fault-controlled compartmentalization and differential subsidence on reservoir geometry and thickness distribution. Petrophysical analysis indicates that the Kharita Formation consists predominantly of sandstone reservoirs with variable shale content and favorable reservoir properties. Seven hydrocarbon-bearing zones were identified, with net-pay thicknesses ranging from 11 to 63 ft. Shale volume values vary between 4 and 20%, total porosity ranges from 8 to 18%, and effective porosity ranges from 6 to 17%. Water saturation values range from 20 to 45%, corresponding to hydrocarbon saturation values of 55% to 80%. The most prospective reservoir intervals occur in Zone D of SELK-6 and Zone F of SETHOS-16, which exhibit favorable combinations of net-pay thickness, porosity, and hydrocarbon saturation. The integrated results demonstrate that hydrocarbon accumulation within the Kharita Formation is controlled by the combined influence of depositional architecture, reservoir quality, and fault-related structural trapping. This study highlights the value of integrating seismic and petrophysical datasets for reducing exploration uncertainty and improving reservoir characterization in the Shushan Basin and analogous Lower Cretaceous reservoirs of the Western Desert.

Article.Title: Engineered platelet extracellular vesicles delivering miR-320a promote proliferation, neuronal differentiation, and dopaminergic function in SH-SY5Y cells by targeting ITGβ1
Article.Authors: Yuan Q.; Hu S.; Cai Z.; Liu J.; Jiang L.; Luo C.; Huang Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (PEVs) hold promise as drug delivery vehicles, due to their abundance, clinical accessibility, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. Building on our previous identification of miR-320a as a candidate for schizophrenia, we engineered PEVs to deliver miR-320a via electroporation. The resulting PEVs-miR-320a were readily internalized by SH-SY5Y cells. PEVs-miR-320a—but not free miR-320a, native PEVs, or vehicle—markedly potentiated SH-SY5Y cell viability and enhanced retinoic acid (RA)-induced neuronal differentiation. In RA-differentiated SH-SY5Y cells, PEVs-miR-320a selectively elevated extracellular dopamine levels without affecting glutamate or serotonin. Mechanistically, PEV-mediated delivery elevated intracellular miR-320a, which in turn downregulated its target, integrin β1 (ITGβ1). Together with our previously published in vivo evidence showing that PEVs-miR-320a improved behavioral abnormalities in an MK-801-induced schizophrenia-like rat model, the present study provides cellular-level proof-of-concept evidence that PEVs can deliver miR-320a and modulate neuronal phenotype-related readouts, supporting further investigation of the miR-320a/ITGβ1 pathway as a candidate therapeutic/regulatory axis for schizophrenia.

Article.Title: Cross-cultural variation in eye contact comfort
Article.Authors: Sorokowska A.; Rokosz M.; Kowal M.; Misiak M.; Malecki W.; Sorokowski P.; Roberts S.
Article.Abstract: Eye contact is a fundamental component of nonverbal communication, yet affective evaluations of direct gaze are complex and highly context-dependent. Cultural background appears to play a crucial role in shaping the interpretation and social function of gaze behaviors, likely leading to significant cross-cultural variation in preferences for eye contact. However, cross-cultural empirical research on eye contact comfort remains limited. The present study addresses this gap using a large and diverse sample of 10,387 participants (aged 18–73) from 51 study sites, who reported their comfort with direct eye contact when interacting with strangers, acquaintances, and close others. In line with expectations, individuals report feeling most comfortable making eye contact with close others, followed by acquaintances, and finally strangers. Beyond geosocial factors such as socioeconomic status, Human Development Index, and climate, our analyses identify collectivism and gender equality as important predictors of eye contact comfort. These findings suggest that cultural variation in gaze behavior is more multifaceted than commonly assumed and cannot be reduced to simple regional dichotomies. Although the present study is exploratory and based on self-reported assessments of eye contact comfort, it provides one of the first large-scale cross-cultural examinations of this construct and generates novel, testable hypotheses regarding the cultural and socioecological foundations of gaze behavior. Overall, the findings highlight the need to consider both individual-level and contextual variables when examining nonverbal communication across societies and provides a unique, large-scale dataset documenting global variation in eye contact comfort.

Article.Title: Fetal cardiac function and doppler parameters in relation to preeclampsia severity and neonatal outcomes
Article.Authors: Yılmaz E.; Özler M.; Sağlam E.; Yalçınkaya Z.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the associations between preeclampsia severity and fetal cardiac function and Doppler parameters and to explore the discrimination of individual parameters for severe preeclampsia and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission within the study cohort. This prospective, single-center observational study included 224 women with preeclampsia, classified as non-severe ( n = 150) or severe preeclampsia ( n = 74). Fetal cardiovascular assessment included the Tei index, isovolumetric contraction time (IVCT), isovolumetric relaxation time (IVRT), ejection time (ET), umbilical artery pulsatility index (UA PI), pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PA PI), and pulmonary artery peak systolic velocity (PA PSV). Separate multivariable linear regression analyses were performed for each parameter, adjusting for gestational age at fetal assessment, maternal age, and body mass index. Sensitivity analyses additionally accounted for early-onset preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses assessed the cohort-specific discrimination of individual parameters. Compared with the non-severe group, women with severe preeclampsia had higher Tei index, IVCT, IVRT, UA PI, and PA PI and lower ET and PA PSV (all p < 0.001). All associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for gestational age at fetal assessment, maternal age, and body mass index and in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for early-onset preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction (all p < 0.001). The severe preeclampsia group also had earlier delivery, lower birth weight and 5-minute Apgar scores, and more frequent NICU admission (23.0% vs. 5.3%, p < 0.001). In exploratory ROC analyses, IVRT showed the highest cohort-specific discrimination for severe preeclampsia (AUC, 0.861; 95% CI, 0.81–0.91), followed by the Tei index (AUC, 0.849; 95% CI, 0.79–0.90). Discrimination for NICU admission was limited, with the highest AUC observed for the Tei index (0.650). In this cohort, severe preeclampsia was associated with altered fetal cardiac function and Doppler parameters after adjustment for gestational age at fetal assessment, maternal age, and body mass index. Similar findings were observed in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for early-onset preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, although residual confounding cannot be excluded. The ROC findings represent exploratory, cohort-specific measures of discrimination and should not be interpreted as validated evidence of clinical utility. Given the observational design, these findings do not establish causality. Further multicenter studies are required to confirm these associations, and internal and external validation is needed to assess the reproducibility and potential clinical relevance of the ROC findings.

Article.Title: Structure-based mechanical properties of human carotid arteries and their effect on stress-strain response
Article.Authors: Hrubanová A.; Bednařík Z.; Staffa R.; Johnston R.; Thomková B.; Lally C.; Burša J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mechanical properties and structure of components of an atherosclerotic arterial wall are important for computational prediction of atheroma vulnerability. In this study, a total of 36 specimens harvested during standard carotid endarterectomies were tested under uniaxial tension, followed by histological examination to distinguish their tissue types. The structural composition of the specimens was found to have a significant impact on their mechanical properties, more specifically the extensibility. Specimens with severe atherosclerotic changes exhibited lower extensibility compared with those less impacted by the disease ( p -value < 0.005), while no difference was observed in strength. These findings suggest that deformation-related parameters (strains) may be more sensitive to tissue-level disease changes than stress-based measures. A total of 64 computational simulations was performed using patient-specific geometry with isotropic and anisotropic models of individual arterial layers. These models demonstrate that local collagen fibre distribution in the fibrous cap where rupture can occur, is necessary for accurate assessment of strains and stresses. In contrast, population-specific data, such as those obtained in this study, may be sufficient for modelling the outer artery layers where the collagen fibre orientation did not have a significant impact on the strains and stresses in the fibrous cap.

Article.Title: Mitigating common-mode noise in high frequency LLC resonant converters: a parallel interleaved approach
Article.Authors: Zahraei M.; Tahami F.; Rezazadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing demands for efficiency and power density in modern applications such as electric vehicles, 5G infrastructure, and data centers have accelerated the adoption of high-frequency DC-DC converters. The use of wide-bandgap semiconductors enables switching frequencies in the megahertz range facilitating the miniaturization of passive components. However, these benefits come with challenges: high dv/dt transitions and parasitic capacitances in planar transformers often result in significant common-mode (CM) noise, leading to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Although conventional mitigation techniques such as structural symmetry, winding balance, and shielding offer partial relief, they frequently necessitate large CM filters. This paper presents an alternative approach by optimizing the magnetic structure and circuit layout of matrix planar transformers to intrinsically suppress CM noise. The proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive high-frequency transformer modeling, circuit-level optimization, and experimental evaluation of a 1 kW GaN-based LLC converter with an input voltage range of 375–405 V and a 48 V output. Results confirm that the proposed design achieves effective CM noise reduction, significantly minimizing the required filter size.

Article.Title: Acclimatization effects on partial pressure of arterial oxygen at high altitude: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Fischer H.; Gaisl T.; Forrer A.; Orler N.; Lichtblau M.; Ulrich S.; Furian M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract During acclimatization to high altitude with reduced barometric pressure, the rate of increase in PaO 2 after its initial drop has not been quantitatively described in healthy lowlanders. We therefore performed a systematic search on PubMed and Embase up to 4 October 2025, identifying 39 prospective studies that reported at least two PaO 2 measurements at > 1500 m in initially unacclimatized healthy adults. Additionally, changes in other blood gas parameters were investigated. The primary outcome was the mean effect and 95%CI for changes in PaO 2 during high altitude exposure in healthy, unacclimatized lowlanders. Data from 490 participants (mean[SD] age 30.5[5.4] years; 76.1% male), comprising 1109 measurements at a mean altitude of 4140 m (range 1600–5334 m), were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. PaO 2 showed an increase of 0.1 kPa/day (95%CI − 0.02;0.22; p = 0.10). Across all studies with the first measurement not restricted to day one, the increase was 0.06 kPa/day (95%CI − 0.02;0.15; p = 0.14). Neither altitude nor duration of exposure significantly influenced these estimates. Concurrently, SaO 2 increased, PaCO 2 decreased, and pH remained unchanged. Although not reaching statistical significance, the PaO 2 showed a clear trend of increasing by 0.06 to 0.1 kPa/day at high altitude over an observation period of several weeks. These values may serve as reference estimates for physiological acclimatization in healthy individuals at high altitude.

Article.Title: Effects of high-intensity bodyweight interval training and breathing exercises on quality of life, psychological distress, inflammatory biomarkers, and blood pressure in adults with hypertension: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Herawati I.; Rozali W.; Ishak I.; Mutalazimah M.; Farah N.; Mat Ludin A.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension is a major public health challenge associated with impaired quality of life, psychological distress, inflammation, and cardiovascular risk. This randomized controlled trial compared high-intensity bodyweight interval training (HIBIT), breathing exercises (BE), and their combination with a non-exercise control. Ninety-six adults with hypertension were randomized equally to control, BE, HIBIT, or combined exercise for 10 weeks. Quality of life (QoL), psychological distress, cortisol, C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and resting heart rate were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. The primary intention-to-treat analysis included all 96 randomized participants and used ANCOVA adjusted for the corresponding baseline outcome; a per-protocol analysis of 87 participants was conducted as a sensitivity analysis. Adjusted group effects were observed for CRP (F(3, 91) = 4.79, p = 0.004, partial eta squared = 0.136), SBP (F(3, 91) = 19.06, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.386), and DBP (F(3, 91) = 9.42, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.237). Adjusted CRP was lower in the BE and combined-exercise groups than in the control group, while adjusted SBP and DBP were lower in all three intervention groups than in the control group. No adjusted group effects were identified for QoL, psychological distress, cortisol, IL-6, or resting heart rate. The per-protocol analysis produced the same overall pattern. HIBIT, BE, and their combination were associated with lower post-intervention blood pressure than control, but the combined intervention was not superior to either single intervention. The CRP finding and model-sensitive secondary outcomes should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger, more diverse samples. Clinical trial registration number : Thai Clinical Trials Registry, TCTR20230707003 (https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org), registered 6 July 2023.

Article.Title: High-salt intake during the growth period elevates blood pressure and alters heart rate variability trajectories in rats
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Hong S.; Oh C.; Kim J.; Lee H.; Shon Y.; Park E.
Article.Abstract: Chronic high-salt intake may exert lasting effects on autonomic regulation across the life course. The growth period is a critical window during which the autonomic nervous system matures, yet how high-salt exposure shapes autonomic maturation remains insufficiently understood. In this study, male Sprague–Dawley rats (5 weeks of age at diet onset) were assigned to a control (0.5% NaCl) or a high-salt (> 4% NaCl) diet for 12 weeks (to 17 weeks of age). Systolic blood pressure (SBP) was measured twice weekly in conscious animals using a tail-cuff system, and heart rate variability (HRV) was derived from electrocardiographic recordings twice weekly under isoflurane anesthesia. Longitudinal changes were modeled using generalized linear mixed models. The high-salt group showed a significant increase in SBP relative to controls (Group × Time, p < 0.001). For frequency-domain HRV, LFnu increased and HFnu decreased significantly over the 12 weeks in the high-salt group, and the between-group differences reached statistical significance (LFnu, p = 0.031; HFnu, p = 0.021). These findings suggest that longitudinal, repeated-measures HRV may serve as a complementary, non-invasive approach for tracking autonomic development, warranting further investigation.

Article.Title: Machine learning-guided drug repurposing for targeting PDK1 in breast cancer treatment
Article.Authors: Ganjipete S.; Kumar B.; Dinesh B.; Ramesh S.; Ammunje D.; Kunjiappan S.; Pavadai P.
Article.Abstract: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase-1 (PDK1)/protein kinase B (AKT) signaling axis is dysregulated in breast cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. In this study, an integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize FDA-approved drugs as potential PDK1-targeting candidates using machine learning-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, applicability-domain (AD) assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) prediction. We used a curated set of 1,971 compounds with experimentally reported PDK1 inhibitory activity to develop five regression models. The Random Forest model performed best with 10-fold cross-validation R² = 0.83, RMSE = 0.60, MAE = 0.44, and an independent test set based on scaffolds R² = 0.84, RMSE = 0.58, MAE = 0.44. Among 1,615 structurally eligible FDA-approved compounds, 83 compounds had predicted IC₅₀ values below 500 nM. Allopurinol was the only FDA-screened compound accepted by all six complementary AD methods in the consensus applicability-domain analysis. The prioritized compounds were docked at the ATP-binding site of PDK1, and the predicted docking score ranged from − 10.6 to -6.5 kcal/mol, with Allopurinol having the best score. We used comparative 100 ns MD simulations to prioritize Allopurinol for further analysis. A subsequent 1,000 ns simulation confirmed the persistent association with the ATP-binding region, but with dynamic rearrangement; the overall compactness of the protein was maintained. We analyzed overall structural behavior and conformational changes using trajectory analysis based on radius of gyration (Rg), solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), principal component analysis (PCA), and free-energy landscape (FEL). The ADMET properties were generally good, with predictions of drug-likeness and permeability, and potential pharmacokinetic and toxicity liabilities that need experimental evaluation. Overall, Allopurinol was computationally prioritized for further biochemical, cellular, and in vivo validation.

Article.Title: Interpretable bulge-part descriptors identify region-specific pedestrian-level wind responses around T-form high-rise buildings
Article.Authors: Gan W.; Wu J.; Li S.; Li J.; Peng S.; Li B.; Qiu L.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: Protruding façade volumes (hereafter referred to as bulge parts) are frequently used in T‑form high‑rise building designs, yet their pedestrian‑level aerodynamic effects are challenging to evaluate across different configurations. This study develops physically interpretable derived descriptors, together with a framework combining computational fluid dynamics and statistical analysis. It quantifies statistical associations between the geometry of wind‑facing bulge parts and pedestrian‑level wind speeds at the 1.5‑m plane across windward, lateral and leeward regions. Steady RANS simulations pass grid convergence checks and wind‑tunnel validation. The Extra Trees Regressor (ETR) surrogate serves as a supplementary tool to predict pedestrian‑level wind speeds. From multivariate‑regression inference within the investigated parametric range, the following conclusions can be drawn: bulge-part geometric parameters show region-dependent statistical associations with pedestrian-level wind speeds; for derived descriptors, windward‑face surface area of the bulge part (S2) shows a significant positive association across all three regions; bulge-part windward-face diagonal length (L4) is positive only windward, bulge-part lateral-face diagonal length (L5) negative for lateral‑leeward regions; for raw parameters, bulge-part length (L1) is consistently positive across all regions; building height (H) is negative for lateral‑leeward regions, main-body width (W2) significant only windward; compared with raw parameters, the proposed derived descriptors offer supplementary statistical interpretive capacity.

Article.Title: Urban building change detection with satellite imagery: a temporospatial attention Siamese SNUNet-ECAM framework
Article.Authors: Tiwari V.; Singhal R.; Gangrade S.; R. M.; Gangrade J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban building change monitoring on bi-temporal Very High Resolution (VHR) satellite imagery is critical for land-use monitoring, post-disaster assessment, and urban planning. We use LEVIR-CD, a public benchmark of 637 bi-temporal 1024 $$\times$$ 1024-pixel image pairs at 0.5 m/pixel resolution, collected from Google Earth imagery of 20 regions in Texas, USA, with a 5–14-year interval between acquisitions and a $$\sim$$ 4.6% building-change pixel ratio. Rather than proposing a new architectural module, this paper presents a systematic integration of a Siamese ResNet50 encoder, the Temporospatial Interactive Attention Module (TIAM), and the SNUNet dense nested decoder with Ensemble Channel Attention (ECAM) — into a single end-to-end trainable pipeline, evaluated on the official LEVIR-CD split. The central empirical finding, based on a controlled ablation, is that full-resolution image tiling (versus resizing) is the dominant driver of performance on this benchmark, improving F1 by 17.11 percentage points (73.24% $$\rightarrow$$ 90.35%) — an effect several times larger than the combined, measured contribution of the three architectural modules (TIAM +6.83 SNUNet +5.31, ECAM +3.87 F1%). We additionally document three previously unreported training instabilities (NaN propagation from Lovász-Hinge loss, silent fp16 overflow in TIAM’s attention computation, and catastrophic forgetting without progressive unfreezing) along with the engineering fixes that resolve them. Using the decision threshold selected on the validation set (0.56, avoiding test-set threshold tuning and test-set augmentation), the system reaches F1 90.35%, IoU 82.40%, Precision 91.70%, Recall 89.04%, and Overall Accuracy 99.03% on the official LEVIR-CD test split—essentially matching, rather than exceeding, a simpler ResNet-50 U-Net baseline (90.38% F1) and remaining below ChangeFormer (90.40% F1). Notably, our model achieves this comparable performance with substantially fewer parameters than ChangeFormer, demonstrating a more parameter-efficient architecture without sacrificing predictive performance. We report this honestly as evidence that, on this benchmark, correct preprocessing can be as important as architectural sophistication.

Article.Title: Supply chain resilience prediction and industrial economic shock transmission path analysis integrating knowledge graphs and deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Mounting geopolitical frictions, trade disputes and public health emergencies have exposed structural fragilities in global supply chains, yet the tools built to anticipate those fragilities still keep relational reasoning and adaptive decision-making apart. This paper joins them. We assemble a multimodal supply chain knowledge graph spanning 1.86 million entities and 23 relation types drawn from input–output tables, customs records, corporate disclosures and a curated disruption case repository, then design an attention-augmented R-GCN encoder that compresses topology, attributes and temporal disruption signals into resilience-sensitive embeddings. On that representation the proposed KG-PPO algorithm couples a clipped policy objective with cascade-aware reward shaping, so that interpretable transmission paths emerge alongside the resilience forecast. Experiments on automotive, electronic information and pharmaceutical chains benchmark KG-PPO against eleven baselines, among them three recent supply chain graph models and information-matched variants that receive the same graph features as the proposed agent. Averaged over five seeds, KG-PPO lowers MAE by 18.3% and lifts AUC by 3.5 points relative to the strongest baseline; both gaps survive paired testing with Holm correction, while several mid-ranked baselines cannot be told apart from one another. A streaming experiment over a twelve-week crisis window shows that incremental graph updates hold the rolling error near its pre-crisis level at roughly a twelfth of the cost of full retraining, and a six-factor sweep places the reported configuration on a flat optimum rather than a knife-edge. Rare-earth refining and semiconductor foundries emerge as the deepest chokepoints under the shock protocol used here, and strategy simulations trace the cost-resilience frontier under inventory redundancy, multi-source procurement and capacity flexibility. The ontology schema, the per-seed records behind every table and the code that regenerates every figure are released with the paper.

Article.Title: Real-time flood forecasting in lowland rivers exposed to levee breaches using GPU hydrodynamics
Article.Authors: Ferrari A.; Passadore G.; Crestani E.; Pivato M.; Vacondio R.; Mignosa P.; Viero D.; Carniello L.
Article.Abstract: With the increasing frequency of extreme hydrometeorological events due to climate change and the raise of floods in lowland regions triggered by sudden levee failures, early warning systems capable of alerting at-risk populations have become a cornerstone of contemporary flood risk management. Despite recent advances in flood forecasting, achieving accurate predictions in low-lying areas remains a major operational challenge due to the need of coupling high-resolution hydrological and hydrodynamic models while ensuring a remarkable computational efficiency. Moreover, the presence of extensive and aging levee systems, whose failure is often driven by multiple and uncertain processes, calls for the enhancement of these tools to account for flooding scenarios induced by potential breaches. This study develops an integrated flood forecasting system to predict real-time floods, including those triggered by levee failures. The modelling chain combines within a unique operational platform the gathering of meteorological weather forecasts and observed data, a rainfall-runoff model, and a two-dimensional hydrodynamic model taking advantage of Graphic Processing Units (GPUs). The procedure is designed to identify potentially at-risk areas in advance, supporting timely decision-making for flood risk management. The application to a lowland area in Northern Italy highlights the capability of the proposed framework to simulate complex flood dynamics at high-resolution by reproducing a real event occurred in March 2025 and by providing hypothetical levee-breach flood scenarios with lead times of up to two days for civil protection actions, even in fast reactive basins.

Article.Title: BIA-estimated visceral fat level and selected regional body composition measures are associated with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein in Thai adults
Article.Authors: Buddhisa S.; Satthakarn S.; Prakobkaew N.; Padkao T.; Boonla O.; Prasertsri P.
Article.Abstract: Chronic low-grade systemic inflammation plays a central role in the development of cardiometabolic diseases. Although excess adiposity has been linked to systemic inflammation, the independent associations of overall and regional body composition characteristics with circulating inflammatory biomarkers remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the associations of overall and regional body composition characteristics with circulating inflammatory biomarkers among Thai adults. In this cross-sectional study, 206 Thai adults aged ≥ 18 years underwent body composition assessment using bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). Overall body composition parameters included body mass index, body fat percentage, fat mass, visceral fat level, waist-to-hip ratio, and skeletal muscle mass, whereas regional body composition included segmental fat and muscle mass. Circulating inflammatory biomarkers, including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), were measured using standard laboratory methods. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlation analysis and multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors after log transformation of inflammatory biomarkers. Relative importance analysis was performed to quantify the contribution of individual body composition parameters to each model. hs-CRP showed significant positive correlations with multiple adiposity-related body composition parameters, including body mass index, body fat percentage, fat mass, visceral fat level, waist-to-hip ratio, and regional fat mass (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted q < 0.05). Within the overall body composition model, visceral fat level was independently associated with higher hs-CRP concentrations (standardized β = 0.340, 95% CI: 0.043–0.637, p = 0.025) and accounted for 52.9% of the variance explained by that model. This percentage represents its relative contribution to the model R 2 and not to the total variability in hs-CRP. In the regional models, mean arm fat, mean leg fat, mean arm muscle, and abdominal muscle were also positively associated with hs-CRP after FDR correction (all q ≤ 0.001). No body composition measures were independently associated with TNF-α or IFN-γ. These findings suggest that hs-CRP is associated with multiple BIA-derived dimensions of body composition. BIA-estimated visceral fat level was the largest contributor to explained variance within the overall body composition model; however, confirmation using direct imaging-based assessment of visceral and regional tissues is required.

Article.Title: A prognostic nomogram based on log odds of positive lymph nodes for non-metastatic upper tract urothelial carcinoma after radical nephroureterectomy with lymph node dissection
Article.Authors: Jiang Z.; Hu H.; Wang J.; Zhang G.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate prognostic value of LODDS and develop nomograms for overall survival (OS) and cause-specific survival (CSS) in upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) patients after radical surgery. Methods A retrospective cohort of 1,970 patients from SEER (2004–2022) was split into training (70%) and validation (30%) cohorts. Multivariate Cox regression compared LODDS, N classification, positive lymph node count (PLN), and lymph node ratio (LNR). Optimized OS and CSS models based on lymph node metrics were built using Cox regression. Time-dependent AUC, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) assessed nomogram performance. Results Tumor stage, grade, age, and lymph node indicators (N stage, LODDS, PLN, LNR) were independent predictors for OS and CSS (all p < 0.05). Nomograms combining LODDS, age, grade, and T classification showed superior performance with lowest AIC, highest C-indices, and favorable time-dependent AUCs. Validation confirmed excellent calibration and clinical utility. In repeated 10-fold cross-validation, LODDS modestly but significantly outperformed N classification (mean C-index: 0.6946 vs. 0.6923; p = 0.0438). Conclusion LODDS outperformed traditional lymph node metrics, offering robust risk stratification. The nomograms provide individualized survival predictions to aid postoperative counseling and adjuvant therapy. Future external validation and biomarker integration are warranted.

Article.Title: Meandering fluvial architecture and geological modeling of Minghuazhen Formation in Q Oilfield Bohai Bay Basin China
Article.Authors: Qiao Y.; Kong Y.; Song F.; Qiu L.; Han Y.; Deng B.; Shao X.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: The research is focused on the meandering fluvial reservoir of NmⅠ3-2 Formation in Q Oilfield, Bohai Bay Basin. It utilizes core analysis, well logging data, and 3D seismic cube to effectively identify the architectural elements. The study area exhibits six lithofacies types, and the spatial distribution of architectural elements within the study area is determined based on the analysis of logging curves, seismic properties, and sandbody isopach maps. The truncated Gaussian simulation method with trend is employed for random lithofacies simulation of the point bar element. Additionally, the sequential indication simulation method is utilized for random lithofacies simulation of the floodplain, abandoned channel, and crevasse splay elements. Subsequently, a three-dimensional geological model is constructed to accurately depict the internal architecture of meandering fluvial sandbody. The architectural model demonstrates that the point bar element primarily exhibits lateral accretion by the development of high porosity and permeability at the base of the lateral accretion body. Additionally, vertical accretion occurs within the abandoned channel, crevasse splay, and floodplain. The abandoned channels and floodplain consist predominantly of silty mud and mudstone, characterized by low porosity and permeability values. In the floodplain elements, there are some crevasse splay sandbodies with high porosity and permeability. The poor physical properties of the abandoned channel, resulting from the influence of reservoir architecture, contribute to a decrease in tracer advancement speed. The velocity perpendicular to the lateral accretion direction of the tracer is significantly lower than that parallel to the lateral accumulation direction. The pronounced longitudinal heterogeneity of the fluvial channel architecture results in delayed response to water injection in production wells, an extended duration for injection effects to manifest, and relatively limited incremental oil production per well.

Article.Title: Prediction model for complex venous malformation complete remission after sirolimus using clinicopathological and CEUS parameters
Article.Authors: Sun B.; Lei H.; Li M.; Zhang B.; Dong C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To develop and validate a machine learning model incorporating clinicopathological features and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) parameters for predicting complete remission (CR) following sirolimus therapy in patients with complex venous malformations (CVM), thereby supporting individualized treatment decisions. A retrospective cohort of 260 CVM patients treated with sirolimus (January 2014-December 2024) was enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated to training (n = 182) and validation (n = 78) sets (7:3 ratio). Baseline clinicopathological (e.g., maximum lesion diameter, volume), CEUS (time-to-peak [TTP], peak intensity [PI]), and laboratory (D-dimer, hemoglobin) data were collected. Univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors. Subsequently, random forest, logistic regression, and K-nearest neighbors models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHAP values and a nomogram enhanced interpretability. The training set CR rate was 30.77% (56/182). Maximum lesion diameter, volume, TTP, PI, hemoglobin, and D-dimer were significantly associated with CR on univariate analysis (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified maximum lesion diameter (OR = 0.800), lesion volume (OR = 0.987), TTP (OR = 1.189), PI (OR = 0.815), and D-dimer (per 0.1 mg/L FEU increase: OR = 0.415) as independent predictors (P < 0.05). The RF model yielded an AUC of 0.869 (95%CI: 0.809–0.929) in the training set and 0.766 (95%CI: 0.629–0.902) in the validation set, with satisfactory calibration with satisfactory calibration (calibration intercept and slope close to 0 and 1; Hosmer-Lemeshow P > 0.05), supported by bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit. SHAP value ranking was D-dimer > TTP > PI > maximum lesion diameter > lesion volume. The nomogram enabled individualized CR risk visualization. A random forest model and nomogram based on clinicopathological and CEUS parameters accurately predict sirolimus‑induced CR in CVM patients. Maximum lesion diameter, volume, TTP, PI, and D-dimer are independent predictors. This model offers an effective tool for candidate selection and personalized treatment planning.

Article.Title: Application of depth migration velocity modeling technology based on multi-information constraint in deep seismic imaging
Article.Authors: Cao L.; Gu G.; Wu Y.; Sun S.; Wang S.; Wang Y.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate seismic imaging of deep, low signal-to-noise ratio zones in faulted basins remains a persistent challenge. To address this, we propose a pre-stack depth migration (PSDM) velocity modeling workflow that integrates multiple information constraints. Shallow velocities are derived from micro-logging constrained first-arrival inversion, while intermediate and deep interval velocities are converted from root-mean-square velocities using horizon-constrained constrained velocity inversion in the depth domain. Horizon-guided residual velocity analysis is iteratively applied from top to bottom, generating a low-frequency velocity model that captures the structural trends of the faulted basin. Multi-attribute constrained grid tomography—incorporating logging curves, azimuth, dip, continuity, and other seismic attributes—iteratively updates interval velocities through PSDM. The workflow combines model-based tomography for macroscopic along-horizon velocity trend control with multi-attribute constrained grid tomography for high-resolution interval characterization, enabling robust delineation of the faulted basin's velocity architecture and improved interval velocity accuracy. Application to 3-D data from Block H in an eastern China oilfield demonstrates clear sequence contacts, abundant interval details, a well-defined deep basement boundary, and improved imaging quality.

Article.Title: Reboxetine blocks NMDA receptors in a voltage-, use-, and activity-dependent manner
Article.Authors: Föhr K.; Jungwirth B.; Schrezenmeier H.; Messerer D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reboxetine is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor which has initially been approved as an antidepressant. In addition, it has been used off label for panic disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, particularly when methylphenidate is ineffective. As the action of other known monoamine reuptake inhibitors, including fluoxetine and atomoxetine, turned out to be effective blockers of NMDA receptors, we analyzed whether reboxetine similarly inhibits NMDA receptors. The whole-cell configuration of the patch-clamp technique was used to analyze the effect of reboxetine on recombinant NMDA receptors transiently expressed in tsA201 cells. Reboxetine reversibly blocked NMDA receptors in a concentration-dependent manner with a half-maximal inhibition of 20.4 ± 3.6 µM, when NMDA (50 µM) and glycine (10 µM) were used to activate GluN2A containing receptors. For GluN2B a corresponding value of 12.6 ± 3.1 µM was estimated. Inhibition increased at higher agonist concentrations, consistent with an uncompetitive, activity-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, the block occurred in a voltage- and use-dependent manner, indicating an open-channel blocking mechanism with an interaction site located deep within the channel pore (zδ = 0.94). In addition, a modest subunit dependence was observed, with greater inhibition of GluN2B- than GluN2A-containing receptors. Finally, Reboxetine belongs to a rare group of NMDA receptor antagonists whose efficacy increases with the concentration of the agonist. This activity-dependent profile is therapeutically attractive because it predicts preferential suppression of pathological NMDA-receptor over-activation while leaving low-frequency physiological signaling comparatively unaffected.

Article.Title: Age-dependent heterogeneity in brain networks and interhemispheric synchrony in overactive bladder syndrome
Article.Authors: Hua Y.; Fu S.; Yin L.; Zhang Y.; Gu K.; Lu F.; Xuª J.; Zhou Y.; Miao H.; Gu J.; Sun Y.; Chen Y.; Fan Y.; Feng N.
Article.Abstract: Overactive bladder (OAB) may involve age-dependent alterations in brain networks, but whether age modifies structural network organization and interhemispheric synchrony remains unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 111 participants with OAB and 114 healthy controls were classified as young (≤ 40 years), middle-aged (41–65 years), and older (> 65 years). The primary hypothesis was tested using diagnosis-by-age-stratum interaction models in global structural network topology and whole-brain voxelwise degree centrality (DC) and voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity (VMHC). Complementary continuous-age models were supportive, whereas seed-based connectivity and imaging–clinical correlations were exploratory. Significant interactions were observed for clustering coefficient (Cp), right supramarginal gyrus DC, and left inferior parietal lobule VMHC. Cp and right supramarginal gyrus DC were higher in middle-aged but lower in older participants with OAB than in age-matched controls; older participants also showed reduced left inferior parietal lobule VMHC and left IPL–right SMG functional connectivity. Parietal imaging measures were associated with greater clinical burden, particularly in older adults. Continuous-age analyses supported the DC and VMHC findings but not Cp. These results indicate age-dependent neuroimaging heterogeneity in OAB and suggest that age should be considered when characterizing brain–bladder network alterations.

Article.Title: Bridging the gap between damaged infrastructures and disaster mortality
Article.Authors: Bhattacharyya A.; Aydin N.; Comes T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Driven by the lack of global empirical data, there is limited research that analyzed the relationship between infrastructure damage and disaster impact. In this research, we addressed this gap by scraping 79 Post Disaster Needs Assessment reports to collect disaster specific infrastructure damage data for 79 disaster events of this century. Then, we used the data in the Generalized Propensity Score method allowing us to reveal the real effect of infrastructure damage on disaster mortality by accounting for all other confounding factors. We derived an aggregate hazard agnostic response function indicating that damaged infrastructures exponentially increase disaster mortality. We also found that the impact of damaged infrastructures on disaster mortality is more profound among the low- and lower-middle-income countries as compared to overall impact. Lastly, we found that among different infrastructure sectors, the damage to energy, WASH (water, sanitation and hygiene), and health sectors lead to higher disaster mortality as compared to transport, communication, and education sectors. Through these empirical relationships, this research bridges the evidential gap between damaged infrastructures and disaster mortality that can help decision-makers forwarding infrastructure resilience agendas and prioritizing infrastructure sectors for resilience related investments.

Article.Title: A multi-algorithm ordinal classification framework with SHAP interaction analysis for predicting construction accident injury severity
Article.Authors: Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Construction remains one of the most hazardous industries worldwide, yet existing machine learning studies on construction injury severity have largely focused on single-factor importance rankings and have rarely quantified how risk factors combine to amplify fatality probability. This study developed a unified ordinal-classification framework benchmarking seven machine learning algorithms on 22,217 construction accident records extracted from the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) database between 2015 and 2023. Inverse-frequency class weighting was applied across all models, and a custom focal-loss objective was additionally used in the three gradient-boosting learners to address class imbalance. All models were tuned through Bayesian optimization with five-fold cross-validation, and the best model was interpreted using TreeSHAP global importance, dependence, and pairwise interaction values. CatBoost achieved the best performance (Accuracy = 0.768, Macro-F1 = 0.721, AUC-ROC = 0.862, Fatal-Recall = 0.663), improving upon the Logistic Regression baseline by 6.1 percentage points (relative + 10.1%) in fatal recall. Height-related work, fall events, fall height, company size, and construction phase emerged as the top five predictors. Two pairwise interactions, company size × construction phase and height-related occupations × warm season (Spring/Summer), produced synergistic risk associations that are invisible to single-factor analyses. The strongest interaction (company size × construction phase) yielded a joint SHAP contribution 1.8 times the linear-additive expectation. These associations were translated into four threshold-based managerial rules with empirical fatality rates ranging from 12.8 to 21.3% (1.7 × to 2.8 × the sample baseline of 7.6%), supporting post-incident severity triage, targeted regulatory inspection prioritization, and risk-rated insurance underwriting. The analytical workflow is designed to be transferable to other national accident databases, though feature-specific thresholds require recalibration to account for differences in regulatory regimes, workforce composition, and climatic conditions.

Article.Title: Alterations in 5hmC and TET2 expression in bladder cancer and their associations with clinicopathological features and patient outcome
Article.Authors: Strasenburg W.; Jóźwicki J.; Rogalla-Ładniak U.; Piątkowska D.; Wojtasik J.; Grzanka D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bladder cancer (BLCA) remains a major clinical challenge due to its high recurrence rate and the limited availability of reliable prognostic biomarkers. Since epigenetic dysregulation is a hallmark of urothelial carcinogenesis, we investigated the expression patterns, clinicopathological associations, and prognostic significance of 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and TET2, a key regulator of active DNA demethylation. Immunohistochemical analysis of 5hmC and TET2 was performed in 133 BLCA specimens and 88 matched adjacent non-tumour tissues. TET2 mRNA expression was further evaluated using RT-qPCR and publicly available transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and genotype-tissue expression (GTEx) cohorts. Reduced 5hmC levels were significantly associated with muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Although high 5hmC expression was associated with a lower descriptive post-selection hazard, the survival association was not significant after accounting for the data-driven threshold search (Cutp p = 0.259). TET2 protein expression was significantly lower in BLCA than in adjacent non-tumour tissues. In contrast, both RT-qPCR and in silico analyses demonstrated increased TET2 mRNA expression in BLCA, revealing a previously unrecognised discordance between transcript and protein levels. This discrepancy may reflect post-transcriptional or post-translational regulation and/or tumour microenvironment-related effects. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate reduced TET2 protein expression in BLCA using immunohistochemistry while simultaneously showing increased TET2 mRNA expression using independent transcriptomic approaches. Our findings suggest that 5hmC may have potential prognostic relevance in BLCA, and provide new insight into the complex regulation of TET2 in bladder tumorigenesis. The integrated assessment of TET2 at both the protein and transcript levels highlights the importance of multi-level molecular analyses for understanding epigenetic dysregulation in bladder cancer.

Article.Title: Paradoxical prognosis of extracellular vesicle-derived miR-4435 expression in advanced colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Kang J.; Koo B.; Bae C.; Kim D.; Kwon H.; Kim Y.; Shin Y.; Lim S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived microRNAs are promising non-invasive biomarkers for colorectal cancer (CRC), but their stage-specific prognostic significance remains unclear. We evaluated circulating EV-derived miR-4435 and its target TIMP3 in a retrospective cohort of 100 plasma samples (20 healthy controls and 80 CRC patients evenly distributed across stages 0–1, 2, 3, and 4). EVs were isolated, and miR-4435 and TIMP3 expression were quantified by real-time PCR. Patients were stratified into high- and low-expression groups using predefined cohort mean cutoffs, confirmed by median-cutoff sensitivity analysis. TIMP3 was significantly lower in CRC than in healthy controls, remaining significant after age adjustment; miR-4435 was also elevated in CRC, though attenuated after age adjustment. Stage-stratified survival analysis revealed a paradoxical, stage-dependent pattern for miR-4435: elevated expression was associated with significantly poorer recurrence-free survival and a non-significant trend toward poorer overall survival in early-stage CRC, but with significantly improved overall and recurrence-free survival in advanced-stage CRC, a pattern preserved under median-based stratification. TIMP3 was not significantly associated with survival at any stage. These findings suggest circulating EV-derived miR-4435 may have stage-dependent prognostic relevance, potentially reflecting tumor biology and tumor–host interactions across disease stages rather than indicating uniformly adverse prognosis.

Article.Title: Protective effects of flunarizine and ATP against pembrolizumab-associated gastric injury in rats
Article.Authors: Tanas S.; Sezgin E.; Cerrah S.; Baykan A.; Baykan E.; Haciyeva S.; Gunay M.; Gungor A.; Ozkaraca M.; Suleyman H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pembrolizumab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor targeting pro-grammed cell death protein-1 (PD-1), is widely used in cancer therapy. However, its potential gastrotoxic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Flunarizine has antioxidant, calcium channel-blocking, and mitochondria-protective properties, whereas ATP plays a central role in maintaining cellular energy metabolism. Therefore, the present study investigated the possible protective effects of flunarizine, ATP, and their combination against pembrolizumab-associated gastric injury in rats. To our knowledge, the combined protective effects of flunarizine and ATP against pembrolizumab-associated gastric injury have not previously been investigated. Thirty male Wistar rats were randomly divided into five groups: healthy control (HG), pembrolizumab (PZB), flunarizine + pembrolizumab (FPZB), ATP + pembrolizumab (APZB), and flunarizine + ATP + pembrolizumab (FAPZB). Pembrolizumab (5 mg/kg, i.p.) was administered daily for one week. Flunarizine (5 mg/kg, oral gavage), ATP (5 mg/kg, i.p.), or their combination was administered 1 h before pembrolizumab. Gastric tissues were evaluated macroscopically, biochemically, histopathologically, and by double immunofluorescence analysis. Gastric tissue ATP, malondialdehyde (MDA), and total glutathione (tGSH) levels, together with cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression, were assessed. Pembrolizumab administration was associated with marked gastric mucosal injury characterized by ulcerative lesions, hyperemia, edema, decreased gastric tissue ATP and tGSH levels, increased MDA levels, increased COX-2 expression, and suppressed COX-1 expression compared with the healthy group. Flunarizine and ATP treatments significantly attenuated these alterations. Notably, ATP levels were significantly higher in the APZB group than in the FPZB group, whereas combined flunarizine and ATP treatment restored tissue ATP levels to values comparable to those of the healthy group. Among the treatment groups, FAPZB showed the most prominent gastroprotective effect by markedly improving biochemical, histopathological, and immunofluorescence findings. The findings indicate that pembrolizumab-associated gastric injury is accompanied by reduced gastric tissue ATP levels, oxidative stress, and inflammatory and structural alterations. Flunarizine and ATP attenuated these changes, while their combined administration produced the most pronounced overall protective effect and restored tissue ATP levels to values comparable to those of the healthy group. These findings support an association between preservation of tissue energy status and gastric mucosal protection; however, the underlying Ca²⁺- and mitochondrial-dependent mechanisms require further investigation.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning identifies candidate shared neuroanatomical features in Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s via importance inversion transfer
Article.Authors: Caligiore D.; Torsello S.
Article.Abstract: Despite significant neurobiological and pathological overlaps, Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases–the primary threats to healthy aging–are still managed as distinct clinical entities. Standard machine learning exacerbates this diagnostic fragmentation by prioritizing divergent markers over shared traits, thereby obscuring the invariant foundations of neurodegeneration. This study introduces Importance Inversion Transfer, an explainable machine learning framework designed to identify neuroanatomical invariants across the neurodegenerative spectrum. Prioritizing structural stability over discriminative utility isolates a shared pathological core consisting of ten regional volumetric anchors, validated through an inductive protocol with high diagnostic fidelity (AUC = 0.894). The identified morphological continuum between healthy aging and neurodegeneration delineates shared structural substrates consistent with–though not demonstrative of–a potential common early-phase vulnerability. Aligned with the Neurodegenerative Elderly Syndrome hypothesis, this evidence establishes a possible paradigm for early, system-level diagnosis.

Article.Title: Deep learning quantification of mouse nesting behavior for tracking cognitive decline in models of aging & Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Miot F.; Shih Z.; Salloum S.; Chum P.; Behringer E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aging brain and development of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are characterized by neurological degeneration. Nest-building performance captures deteriorating cognitive and motor functions in rodent models of AD; albeit qualitative while limited in physiological scope. To enhance sampling depth and frequency, we developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered image analysis pipeline (“CozyScores”) built on the ResNet18 architecture. In male & female C57BL6/J wild-type (WT) & 3xTg-AD mice (AD) mice [Young, 3–6 mo; WT, n = 28; AD, n = 32) & (Old, 21–26 mo; WT, n = 20; AD, n = 12)], we monitored progressive nest organization using photo acquisition across timepoints (0.5 to 24 h) relative to baseline on a 5-point scoring system. At the 4 h benchmark timepoint, a significant ( P < 0.05) difference in performance scores was detected as a function of age and genotype [Young WT (mean ± SEM, 3.80 ± 0.18) > Young AD (3.16 ± 0.24) > Old WT (3.08 ± 0.32) > Old AD (1.71 ± 0.14)]. At 24 h, maximum performance scores declined in Old (WT: 4.24 ± 0.13; AD: 3.59 ± 0.35) versus Young (WT: 4.60 ± 0.05; AD: 4.33 ± 0.13) groups. Males generally performed better than females throughout groups, particularly during nest construction (2 to 8 h). Overall, CozyScores is an automated, high-resolution analysis of behavioral kinetics in mouse models of aging and AD.

Article.Title: An integrated augmented reality (AR) and embedded electronics-based toolkit for improved visualization and understanding of network graphs
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Colson C.; Fatemi A.; Dudas P.; Manogharan G.; Menold J.; Veturi Y.
Article.Abstract: Network graphs are all-pervasive, and an in-depth understanding of networks is important for students and researchers across a variety of disciplines that involve analysis of multi-modal data. Networks can be challenging to conceptualize due to their complexity, and immersive technologies are needed to parse network graphs. This study introduces a novel immersive toolkit grounded in multimedia learning and embodied cognition theories to improve network graph comprehension in undergraduate STEM students. The toolkit integrates embedded electronics with Augmented Reality (AR) to create synchronized physical-virtual visualizations of complex networks featuring: (1) visual attributes to communicate network properties, (2) tactile interaction through physical network models, (3) local and global views of network graphs, and (4) contextual AR overlays. We present two implementations of this toolkit, one of which was implemented as a case study (intervention) in a senior-level undergraduate class ( N = 25) during finals week with statistically significant improvement (FDR adjusted p = 0.0018) in study outcomes post-intervention compared to pre-intervention. Notably, the improvement was pronounced among students that reported low confidence in subject matter pre-intervention. This study demonstrates how technology can be used to augment human cognition for complex mental tasks and demonstrates the utility of our toolkit to serve as a technology-enabled teaching aid.

Article.Title: Temporal trend analysis and multi-temporal satellite feature integration for mango orchard acreage estimation using machine learning algorithms approach
Article.Authors: Raju V.; Garde Y.; Thorat V.; Shinde V.; Varshney N.; Shrivastava A.; Chaudhary A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of horticultural crop acreage is essential for agricultural planning, market forecasting and evidence-based policy formulation. The present study investigated long-term trends in mango cultivation and developed a multi-temporal remote sensing framework for mango orchard acreage estimation in Navsari District using integrated optical, SAR and machine learning approaches. Time-series (temporal) data spanning 23 years (2001–02 to 2023–24) were analyzed using polynomial regression models to evaluate trends in mango area and production. Linear regression best represented area expansion trends (Adj. R² = 0.969), whereas cubic regression better captured production variability (Adj. R² = 0.634), indicating climatic and seasonal influences on productivity. For orchard classification and acreage estimation, multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery acquired from November 2023 to March 2024 was processed within a phenology-guided framework. Monthly composites were generated and integrated with Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter data, vegetation indices (NDVI, GNDVI, NDRE, SAVI, EVI and NDMI) and texture metrics derived from Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) analysis. A comprehensive 72-band feature stack was developed for classification. Four machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multinomial Logistic Regression (MNLR) were evaluated for orchard discrimination. Among the tested models, RF achieved the highest classification performance with an Overall Accuracy of 99.80% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.997, followed by SVM (99.30%), MNLR (98.21%) and XGB (9.20%). The RF model estimated mango orchard area at 36,099.94 ha, showing the closest agreement with official horticultural statistics (34,363 ha) with only 5.05% estimation error. In contrast, SVM and MNLR overestimated orchard extent by 16.03% and 43.37%, respectively. The proposed framework provides a reliable and scalable methodology for operational horticultural monitoring, crop inventory generation and precision agricultural planning in tropical orchard ecosystems.

Article.Title: An edge-adaptive vision-language framework for real-time open-set violence recognition in surveillance videos
Article.Authors: Bian B.; Zhang D.; Bai J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-latency violent event detection is essential for intelligent edge surveillance. Current violent recognition models suffer three critical deployment drawbacks: prohibitive computational overhead from full fine‑tuning, inadequate temporal modeling for continuous video streams, and severe performance degradation when handling unseen violent categories in open surveillance scenes. We propose a lightweight open-set vision-language framework based on pre-trained CLIP. Its dual‑branch structure achieves cross‑modal alignment to support cross‑scene generalization toward novel violent patterns, and we further conduct preliminary explorations for open‑set violent identification for long monitoring footage. Evaluations on five surveillance datasets confirm competitive accuracy. Our parameter-efficient fine-tuning(PEFT) alleviates the inherent conflict between generalization and edge computing overhead, with strong adaptability across low-power embedded terminals. The framework establishes an extensible paradigm for real-time public safety early warning on edge devices, providing generalizable technical references for deploying multi-modal foundation models in urban security governance and broader edge vision perception tasks.

Article.Title: Spatio-temporal dynamics, clustering, and hotspot evolution of reported foot-and-mouth disease outbreak burden in Nigeria, 2015–2025
Article.Authors: Awoseyi A.; Onuiri E.; Olarinmoye A.; Ademola M.; Adebowale O.
Article.Abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) is endemic in Nigeria, yet the national spatio-temporal structure of officially reported outbreaks remains poorly characterised. We analysed the temporal dynamics, clustering, and hotspot evolution of reported FMD outbreaks across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory from 2015 to 2025, using World Animal Health Information System records and exploratory spatial data analysis. Outbreak burden followed an episodic pattern, with major surges in 2017 and 2021. The 2021 peak was followed by sustained elevated reporting through 2024. Geographically, burden shifted from North Central dominance in 2017 to a persistent North West configuration by 2023, accounting for 71.3% of nationally reported outbreaks. Spatial autocorrelation analysis combining Global Moran’s I, LISA, and Gi* traced a transition from a low-burden fragmented baseline to a consolidated hotspot anchored on Zamfara, Kebbi, and Sokoto, alongside persistent cold-spot structures across southern states. Reported FMD burden in Nigeria was temporally uneven and spatially concentrated. The Zamfara-Kebbi-Sokoto belt warrants prioritisation for field investigation and veterinary deployment, while persistently low-burden states bordering confirmed high-burden zones require structured surveillance capacity assessment rather than passive monitoring.

Article.Title: Long-term surveillance reveals weak coupling between chigger burden on Apodemus agrarius and Orientia tsutsugamushi pool positivity
Article.Authors: Shin H.; Jeong J.; Hong C.; Lee H.; Um T.; Kang S.; Park J.; Song D.; Moon C.; Hwang H.; Sang M.; Lee W.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: Long-term vector surveillance often reports ectoparasite burden and pooled pathogen detection together, but their quantitative relationship is rarely tested. We analysed rodent-associated chigger surveillance conducted from 2018 to 2025 across five habitat strata in Yesan-si, Republic of Korea. During the eight-year surveillance period, 152 small mammals were captured and examined, comprising 123 Apodemus agrarius , 26 shrews ( Crocidura spp.), two Micromys minutus , and one Craseomys regulus . Chiggers were recovered from 135 of 152 hosts (88.8%): 120 of 123 A. agrarius , 12 of 26 Crocidura spp., both M. minutus , and the single C. regulus . A total of 20,239 chiggers were recovered, of which 12,763 were assigned to molecular testing. These chiggers were distributed into 502 host-specific pools containing no more than 30 chiggers, with no pool combining chiggers from different hosts; 58 pools were positive for Orientia tsutsugamushi . Inferential analyses were restricted to A. agrarius because it accounted for most examined hosts and recovered chiggers and was the only host taxon with sufficient host-level replication and pool observations for stable hierarchical modelling. Among the 120 chigger-infested A. agrarius that generated molecular pools, 50 of 468 pools were positive (10.7%). Chigger counts were strongly overdispersed. In a hierarchical binomial mixed model, standardized log host chigger burden showed little association with pool positivity (odds ratio 0.998; 95% credible interval 0.672–1.483), whereas between-year heterogeneity was substantial. Pool positivity was temporally heterogeneous, with the strongest signal in 2023. In the A. agrarius analytic cohort, this increase involved multiple hosts (29/45 positive pools; 13/17 hosts with ≥ 1 positive pool), rather than a single sparse host record. Because this operational surveillance prioritized O. tsutsugamushi screening of pooled chiggers rather than species-resolved mite identification, habitat terms were treated as sampling-stratum adjustments and were not interpreted as species-specific vector effects. These findings indicate that temporal pathogen-detection dynamics in local surveillance cannot be inferred from host chigger burden alone.

Article.Title: Hi-SCCG: Hierarchical Structure-aware Chunking and Context Generation for document-level information extraction
Article.Authors: Tian P.; Xie P.; Li Q.; Gu J.
Article.Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based generative Information Extraction (IE) over long documents is constrained by finite context windows, and the necessary text-chunking step disrupts semantic continuity, causing subject drift, unresolved coreference, and loss of the global constraints required for fine-grained knowledge graph construction. Existing context-augmentation methods either provide only limited local context or incur substantial computational cost while introducing irrelevant information, largely because they do not fully exploit document hierarchy. We propose Hi-SCCG (Hierarchical Structure-aware Chunking and Context Generation), a framework that models document structure by reconstructing the logical skeleton as a semantic tree through LLM-based heading correction and by generating cached multi-granularity summaries with a bottom-up recursive strategy. During inference, Hi-SCCG injects a lightweight path-aware context formed by concatenating ancestor summaries from the leaf chunk to the document root, thereby helping anchor local text to its document-level and section-level subjects. We further introduce LDE-500, a focused benchmark for document-level IE over Chinese hierarchical documents, and use Subject Restoration Rate (SRR) as a diagnostic subset-recall measure for triples that require subject restoration. On LDE-500, Hi-SCCG achieves an F1-score of 0.82 and a diagnostic SRR of 82.1%, with a 9.4 percentage-point absolute SRR improvement over the strongest evaluated baseline. In a representative token-accounting case involving a 45K-token document, after including one-time heading correction, recursive summary-generation calls, extraction input tokens, and extraction output tokens, Hi-SCCG reduces total KG-construction token consumption by 75.4–77.7% relative to SLIDE. These results suggest that structure-aware path injection is a promising strategy for fine-grained IE in structure-rich long documents when SRR is interpreted together with standard triple-level metrics and subset-level precision. A supplementary fully human-annotated Legal-OOD-60 evaluation shows a similar trend in this compact legal-domain sample, where Hi-SCCG achieves an F1-score of 0.77 and an SRR of 75.0%, although broader cross-domain validation remains necessary.

Article.Title: Fenofibrate, but not fenofibric acid, reduces fenestrations and impairs endocytic function in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells
Article.Authors: Luty M.; Borah D.; Szafrańska K.; Giergiel M.; Trzos K.; McCourt P.; Lekka M.; Kotlinowski J.; Zapotoczny B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fenofibrate is widely prescribed for hyperlipidaemia and has been associated with rare but severe cases of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), yet its effects on liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) remain to be investigated. LSECs maintain a highly permeable specialised sinusoidal barrier characterised by transcellular pores (fenestrations), regulating the bidirectional transfer of circulating compounds to and from the hepatocytes. As drug-induced alterations in fenestration architecture could influence xenobiotic access to hepatocytes, these changes may modulate pathways associated with DILI. Understanding the effects of fenofibrate on LSEC ultrastructure may therefore provide insights into previously underexplored endothelial contributions to hepatic drug responses. Both fenofibrate and its active metabolite, fenofibric acid, were evaluated for their effects on LSEC ultrastructure, mechanical properties, and functional markers. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electron microscopy were used to quantify fenestration architecture. AFM was additionally used to measure cellular mechanical properties, which were interpreted in the context of fluorescence-based quantification of cytoskeletal organisation. Gene expression, viability, and cytotoxicity were assessed using PCR-based and biochemical assays. Fenofibrate reduced fenestration number and porosity at both tested concentration (10, and 25 µM). It also decreased the apparent Young’s modulus of LSECs, accompanied by changes in tubulin and actin architecture, without detectable cytotoxicity. In contrast, treatment with fenofibric acid did not result in significant structural or mechanical effects on LSECs, even at higher concentrations. Together, these data identify LSECs as a drug-responsive hepatic cell type for fenofibrate, suggesting that LSECs could represent an underrecognised contributor to the complex, multifactorial processes underlying DILI. This work provides a framework for evaluating endothelial contributions to fenofibrate-associated liver effects in more complex models.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving intrusion detection in mobile edge networks via federated adaptive probabilistic stacking with clan–flock optimisation and explainable AI
Article.Authors: N. J.; P. D.; A. H.
Article.Abstract: Mobile edge networks require intrusion detection systems (IDS) that are private, accurate and interpretable. We present FedAPS–CFO, a federated IDS coupling four mechanisms: prediction-level federated averaging (FedAvg), so raw traffic never leaves the edge; an Adaptive Probabilistic Stacking (APS) ensemble fusing a stacking meta-learner, Bayesian model averaging and a feature-conditioned ensemble; Clan–Flock Optimisation (CFO), a hybrid metaheuristic that tunes the fusion weights and decision threshold on inner validation splits; and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), validated quantitatively for stability, fidelity and faithfulness. Under stratified 10-fold cross-validation, FedAPS–CFO attains F1-scores of 0.997 on NSL-KDD, 0.951 on UNSW-NB15, 0.979 on CICIDS2017 and 0.998 on CIC-IoT2023, matching the strongest constituent ensemble on every dataset and significantly surpassing the remaining components (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Holm-corrected). In federations of up to 100 clients with Dirichlet label skew, FedAPS–CFO sustains detection within 1.2 F1 points of its ideal operating point — up to 46 points above its federated base learners — showing that the trained fusion absorbs client heterogeneity. Under matched budgets, CFO is the most reliable optimiser for the tuning task. Adaptive posterior fusion thus offers a practical route to accurate, interpretable, privacy-preserving intrusion detection at the network edge.

Article.Title: Maximizing area coverage for multi-robots using cloud
Article.Authors: Bagathi N.; Samarakoon S.; Apuroop K.; Elara M.; Sheu B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents an integrated framework for multi-robot task allocation and area coverage using an MQTT-based cloud communication architecture for waypoint delivery. A cost-based allocation strategy is proposed, incorporating factors such as battery level, robot age, approximate path distance, and number of turns required for coverage to optimize robot-to-region assignments using the Hungarian algorithm. For coverage, an A*-assisted Boustrophedon path planning algorithm is utilized, improving coverage efficiency and enabling effective navigation. The system is implemented using ROS2 with MQTT-based cloud communication for waypoint delivery and validated through simulations and hardware experiments. Across the simulated cases, the exact assignment attains a lower total allocation cost than distance-only, uniform, and greedy battery-aware selection rules scored on the same objective, with a mean saving of 11.0% over the greedy baseline, and the hardware trials achieved 93.3–96.4% area coverage. The cloud component is demonstrated as a feasible and practical waypoint delivery mechanism with measured latency of 120 to 180 ms and zero message loss; a rigorous comparison against edge or onboard alternatives is identified as future work.
