Among the formulations with different ratios, 2:1:2 ratio of HNT:CS:XG,HNT–CS–600XG exhibited optimal particle size (442 nm), excellent dispersion stability (PDI = 0.071) and high drug encapsulation (EE = 33%), offering a favourable balance between colloidal stability and bio-interface compatibility. In-vitro release studies for the nanocomposites, compared to halloysites alone, demonstrated a sustained and pH-responsive behavior, with significantly higher release at alkaline pH (43%) relative to acidic conditions (19%) proven advantageous for chronic infection. Kinetic modeling for MC release followed first-order and Korsmeyer–Peppas models, suggesting a diffusion-controlled mechanism. This observation arises from the hierarchical transport barriers created by the polymer-nanotube interface. The results highlight the potential of HNT–CS–XG as a biopolymer-based framework for prolonged and targeted antibiotic delivery.

Article.Title: Adaptive entropy and robust aggregation for client selection in federated credit risk modeling
Article.Authors: Zhou M.; An Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Federated learning enables collaborative modeling for financial risk prediction including credit default and transaction fraud without exposing raw local data. However, client heterogeneity, Non-IID data distribution, and dynamic participant involvement inevitably degrade model performance and incur excessive communication overhead. Existing client selection methods, either heuristic strategies or deep reinforcement learning solutions, suffer from inadequate exploration–exploitation tradeoff and overlook the inherent instability of local model updates. This paper proposes ERPPO-VA, an entropy-regularized proximal policy optimization framework for federated client selection. We formulate the client‑selection procedure using a heuristic‑augmented Markov‑decision‑process‑style framework, introduce an adaptive entropy coefficient together with prioritized experience replay to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, and further design an exponential moving average based confidence-weighted aggregation mechanism to suppress the negative impact of unstable clients. Extensive experiments are conducted on three real-world financial datasets, namely CCFD, HCDR and IEEE-CIS, with over one million samples in total. The proposed approach is compared with Random selection, Greedy selection, DDQN, standard PPO, FedProx, MAPPO, and a faithful reimplementation of ERPPO. Under typical Non-IID settings, ERPPO-VA elevates the AUC metric by 4.5–8.7%, cuts total cumulative communication energy consumption by 52% over 200 federated rounds compared to ERPPO, accelerates the convergence speed by approximately 30%, and also achieves superior client fairness. Extensive empirical convergence analysis confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Article.Title: Predicting mortality risk among non-cardiac surgical patients in the surgical intensive care unit: a retrospective study based on the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Ma M.; Liu J.; Li C.; Chen Y.; Jia H.; Hou A.; Xu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Timely and accurate mortality risk stratification for patients admitted to surgical intensive care units (SICUs) following non-cardiac surgery facilitates rapid risk triage and rational allocation of medical resources. In this retrospective analysis, multiple machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models were constructed to quantify 30-day postoperative mortality risk in this patient population. Clinical laboratory indicators and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals were extracted from non-cardiac surgical patients recorded in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Five classical ML models were developed to predict 30-day mortality: logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM). Two additional DL architectures, backpropagation neural network (BPNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN), were established for comparative performance testing. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to the optimal predictive model to identify dominant mortality-associated risk factors from both global and local interpretability perspectives. A total of 4 843 eligible patients were included, among whom 526 (10.9%) died within 30 days after non-cardiac surgery. The LGBM model outperformed all alternative machine learning and deep learning architectures, achieving the highest F1 score (0.934, 95% CI 0.913–0.942), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC, 0.977, 95% CI 0.972–0.982). Compared with the traditional Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI), the LGBM framework delivered substantially improved classification performance. Global SHAP analysis identified preoperative international normalized ratio (INR), serum bicarbonate, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and creatinine as the four most predictive variables for postoperative 30-day mortality. The LGBM model offers a novel and convenient method for preliminary prognostic risk stratification among non-cardiac surgical patients. This model can assist clinicians with early risk evaluation, though it cannot independently guide targeted clinical treatment decisions.

Article.Title: Prediction of pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in locally advanced lung adenocarcinoma: a multimodal machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Liu B.; Fu Y.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in locally advanced lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains clinically challenging. We aimed to develop an explainable machine learning framework to predict pCR and stratify patient prognosis. This retrospective study included 627 driver-negative LUAD patients (2020–2025). Fifteen baseline clinicopathological, metabolic, and inflammatory features were integrated to evaluate four algorithms. The optimal model was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and validated for progression-free survival (PFS). The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model exhibited superior discriminative performance (AUC = 0.872), significantly outperforming traditional logistic regression ( P < 0.001). SHAP analysis identified PET-CT SUVmax, CEA, and PD-L1 expression as the primary predictors, unveiling their non-linear thresholds and synergistic interactions. Decision curve analysis confirmed its clinical net benefit. Furthermore, patients stratified into the high-probability group by the AI model demonstrated significantly prolonged PFS, even within highly malignant sub-cohorts ( P < 0.001). This SHAP-enhanced XGBoost framework shows significant potential as a proof-of-concept model for predicting pCR and stratifying long-term survival in LUAD. However, given the artificially enriched cohort, prospective multicenter external validation is required before it can be considered a definitive clinical tool for optimizing individualized neoadjuvant therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: Evaluation of mandibular molar mesialization by various methods with finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Uzun B.; Uslu F.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical behavior of sliding mechanics of mandibular molar mesialization with different force application models using finite element analysis. Four models were created to simulate different force applications: force applied from the miniscrew to the second molar hook (Model 1), force applied from the miniscrew to an extended lever arm reaching the center of resistance of the second molar (Model 2), force applied to the second molar hook with indirect anchorage (Model 3), and force applied to the second molar hook with dental anchorage (Model 4). Maximum and minimum principal stresses in the tooth, alveolar bone, and around the miniscrew; Von Mises stress distribution; and tooth displacement patterns were analyzed separately for each model. In Model 1, mesial tipping of the molar was observed with concentrated stresses around the molar and miniscrew. Model 2 demonstrated a near-parallel displacement tendency of the second molar with more evenly distributed stresses. Models 3 and 4 showed similar tipping and mesialization of the molar but differed in stress and strain patterns. Applying force via an extended lever arm directed toward the tooth’s center of resistance produced a more parallel initial displacement of the second molar together with a more balanced stress distribution. Within the limits of an initial, linear-static analysis, miniscrew anchorage reduced the stress and strain transmitted to the adjacent teeth compared with dental anchorage.

Article.Title: Carotid artery disease diagnosis comprehensive review and two stage artificial intelligence framework
Article.Authors: Salama G.; Safy M.; Hassanin D.; Kamil C.; Khalaf A.; Abd-Ellah M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carotid artery occlusion is a major risk factor for stroke and cerebrovascular disease, often developing silently without warning. Early and accurate diagnosis of carotid artery plaque is crucial for improving treatment outcomes and reducing potential complications. Thus, there is a great demand for computer-aided diagnostic techniques for the early diagnosis of carotid artery disease with improved accuracy. However, existing literature remains fragmented, typically decoupling initial classification from detailed lesion tracing. This research is organized under three primary axes to bridge this clinical and technical gap. The first axis includes a structured review-of-reviews study that evaluates previously published review papers, while the second axis presents a complete methodological overview of authenticated techniques utilized in carotid diagnosis, such as carotid lumen segmentation, plaque segmentation, carotid classification, and IMT measurement. By mapping the limitations within these domains, the third axis presents a practical two-stage framework, including classification of the carotid artery into normal and plaque-containing, and then segmentation of its plaque to mirror a radiologist's natural decision-making hierarchy. Five lightweight transfer learning networks with multiple preprocessing filters were tested for carotid classification on an independent external clinical dataset. It is followed by a YOLOv11n-based segmentation head used to delineate plaques using expert-generated annotations. Methodologically, ShuffleNet combined with local laplacian filtering produced the best classification results, achieving 98.25% accuracy, 96.17% sensitivity, 100.00% specificity, 100.00% precision, and 98.05% F1-score. Crucially, this screening gate protects the subsequent segmentation stage from processing normal scans and eliminates false positives. The YOLOv11n-seg pipeline achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient of 90.84%, a mask recall of 77.73%, and a mAP50 of 83.21% on unseen clinical scans. By filtering out healthy frames early, this dual-stage pipeline reduces computational overhead to processing times of 6.37 ms for screening and 6 ms for segmentation per frame.

Article.Title: Flexible PVA/SA–ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanocomposite films with tunable optical band gap and enhanced dielectric performance for optoelectronic devices
Article.Authors: Mohamed H.; Wissa D.; Ismail A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aims to develop novel poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/sodium alginate (SA) nanocomposites reinforced with mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ (ZnAl) nanoparticles to enhance their structural, optical, and electrical properties for advanced electrical and optoelectronic applications. The novelty of this work lies in the incorporation of mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanoparticles at different loadings (2–8 wt%) into the PVA/SA matrix to achieve tunable multifunctional properties through optimized nanoparticle dispersion and interfacial interactions. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of 43.3 nm, while the crystallinity of the nanocomposites varied with ZnAl concentration. Attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy indicated hydrogen bonding between the polymer chains and ZnAl nanoparticles. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed a morphological transition from smooth PVA/SA surfaces to granular structures upon ZnAl incorporation. The optical band gap exhibited a non-monotonic decrease from 3.30 eV for PVA/SA blend, reaching a minimum of 1.45 eV at 6 wt% ZnAl, and then rising to 1.73 eV at 8 wt%. This effect is ascribed to defect-induced localized states at low and moderate loadings, as well as to nanoparticle agglomeration and microstructural heterogeneity at elevated loadings. Dielectric analysis demonstrated enhanced electrical conductivity and dielectric constants with increasing ZnAl content, with the optimum performance achieved at 4 wt% owing to the formation of interconnected conductive pathways. Complex modulus analysis further confirmed the ionic conduction mechanism. These multifunctional nanocomposites exhibit tunable optical and electrical properties, highlighting their potential for flexible electronics, UV-shielding, and optoelectronic applications.

Article.Title: Multiwavelength fluorescence imaging using a CEA-targeted fluorescent agent and indocyanine green to increase surgical precision in patients with colorectal liver metastases
Article.Authors: Warmerdam M.; Dijkhuis T.; Bijlstra O.; van Ravens T.; van Dam M.; Hartgrink H.; Burggraaf J.; Crobach A.; Cailler F.; Vahrmeijer A.; Mieog J.
Article.Abstract: Complete (R0) resection is essential for curative treatment of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). Fluorescence-guided surgery with indocyanine green (ICG; emission wavelength ~ 800 nm) is increasingly being adopted as standard care because it enhances lesion detection and improves R0 resection rates. However, unintended R1 resections still occur, while the limited tumor specificity of ICG may lead to false-positive resections. Multiwavelength fluorescence imaging, combining ICG with a tumor-specific tracer, may overcome these limitations. SGM-101, a carcinoembryonic antigen-targeting fluorescent antibody (emission wavelength ~ 680 nm), enables tumor-specific visualization of colorectal cancer cells. This prospective feasibility study therefore evaluated the feasibility of simultaneous multiwavelength fluorescence imaging using SGM-101 in addition to standard ICG-guided CRLM surgery. Ten patients with high-risk features for R1 resection received ICG (0.5 mg/kg) 7 ± 1 days and SGM-101 (10 mg) 4 ± 1 days before surgery. Feasibility was predefined by four criteria: surgical usability and patient experience assessed through surveys, absence of spectral interference, and SGM-101 sensitivity > 80% for CRLM detection, considered necessary for potential intraoperative R1-margin identification. Three of the four predefined feasibility criteria were met. (1) Surgeons reported excellent usability; (2) patients experienced no burden from additional tracer administration, and (3) no spectral interference was observed. The prespecified sensitivity criterion (4) was not met, with an overall SGM-101 sensitivity of 50% on a lesion-level and 70% on a patient-level. However, in an exploratory subgroup analysis, sensitivity increased to 90% in lesions with higher tumor cell density (tumor regression grade 3–5). SGM-101’s specificity for lesion and margin discrimination was 100%. Importantly, all R1 margins were identified intraoperatively by at least one of the two tracers. These findings support further evaluation of multiwavelength fluorescence imaging in larger clinical trials. Refining preoperative patient selection may be key to improving sensitivity in future studies.

Article.Title: GWO-CatBoost based approach for prediction of live-bed scour around circular bridge pier
Article.Authors: Kandakatla R.; Das B.; Devi K.; Khuntia J.; Naik B.
Article.Abstract: Prediction of scour depth under live bed conditions is becoming a major challenge in the field of hydraulic engineering due to the complex interaction between turbulent flow and sediment transport. Empirical equations that are developed for specific site conditions or particular range of data will struggle to achieve high accuracy when applied to the different site or broad range of data. Especially in the case of live bed scour, empirical models will suffer due to the inter-parameter correlations of physical variables, necessitating advanced hybrid models that follow hydraulic laws. To address these limitations, the present study proposes a systematic comparison of ten computational models, including eight hybrid architectures and two standalone models with four established empirical formulas. Rigorous dimensional analysis has been performed using Buckingham \(\pi \) theorem to reduce the variables into a functional relationship \(\left( {{\text{d}}_{{{\text{se}}}} /{\text{b}}} \right) = {\text{f}}\left( {{\text{u}}/{\text{u}}_{{\text{c}}} ,\;{\text{y}}/{\text{b}},\;{\text{b}}/{\text{d}}_{50} ,\;\sigma ,\;{\text{Fr}}_{{\text{b}}} } \right)\) . To check the influence of each input parameter, the present study evaluated the correlation and feature importance analysis along with feature selection techniques across 448 rows of dataset. The unique contribution of the present study is to develop a data-driven empirical equation using Gene Expression Programming (GEP) to capture real hydraulic trends. This equation serves as a physics constraint in the PINN framework. The results demonstrate that the GWO-CatBoost model achieved superior predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.869, RMSE = 0.139, Rel % = 95.556%), compared to all other models and also serves as a reliable tool for engineering applications. The findings suggest that GEP-PINN model successfully bridges the gap between hydraulic laws and machine learning models. Together, these methodologies provide a reliable, high-fidelity tool for enhancing bridge pier design and flood-risk assessment.

Article.Title: Contemporaneous and longitudinal analyses characterize associations between parental educational aspirations and adolescent depressive symptoms in China
Article.Authors: Zhang E.; Ba G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Whether parental educational aspirations are associated with later adolescent depressive symptoms or mainly reflect same-wave family differences remains unresolved. Using four waves (2016–2022) of the China Family Panel Studies, we separated contemporaneous, prospective, reverse-direction, and within-person associations and verified aspiration reporters as each adolescent’s recorded mother or father. The 2022 core comprised 1,547 adolescents aged 10–15 years (weighted model $$N=1,428$$ ); prospective analyses covered 3,708 transitions among 2,532 individuals. In 2022, a one-category higher aspiration was associated with a 0.941-point lower symptom score ( $$b=-0.941$$ , 95% CI $$[-1.643,-0.240]$$ ). The negative association was not corroborated prospectively ( $$b=-0.140$$ , 95% CI $$[-0.473,0.192]$$ ) or within persons ( $$b=-0.099$$ , 95% CI $$[-0.538,0.340]$$ ); both intervals included zero. The reverse-direction coefficient attenuated and its interval crossed zero when the same parent reported at both waves; quadratic and three-wave indirect-path estimates were also imprecise. Together, these estimates distinguish a negative contemporaneous pattern from longitudinal estimates compatible with modest negative or small positive associations. Temporal order and reporter continuity are therefore essential when interpreting parental aspirations as correlates of adolescent depressive symptoms.

Article.Title: Adaptive deep reinforcement learning–based regenerative braking control for coordinated energy recovery and safety in electric vehicles
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Lu J.; Sun L.; Song W.; Jiang P.
Article.Abstract: Regenerative braking control in electric vehicles is challenging due to the coupled influence of driver intent, following safety, and battery charge acceptance, making it difficult for conventional rule-based or static strategies to ensure both safety and energy recovery performance simultaneously. This paper proposes an adaptive constraint-aware deep reinforcement learning (ADRL) strategy for longitudinal motion control. The proposed framework unifies the battery charge acceptance limit and tire adhesion boundary into a physically feasible domain and embeds it into the policy learning process. An adaptive parameter mechanism is further introduced to estimate battery electrochemical–thermal states and to identify road adhesion conditions in real time, enabling online updates to the regenerative power upper bound and the slip safety threshold. Hardware-in-the-loop experiments under multiple cut-in scenarios show that ADRL increases the electric braking proportion by 17.3 and 5.1%, reduces hydraulic braking proportion by 22.0 and 6.4%, improves braking smoothness by 27.5 and 7.8%, and enhances cumulative energy recovery by 13.8 and 6.7% compared with rule-based and conventional DRL strategies. These results demonstrate the superior adaptability and efficiency of the proposed strategy under complex driving conditions.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of fractal analysis and canny edge-detection algorithms for the quantification and classification of bone trabecular patterns in cone-beam computed tomography
Article.Authors: Habibi K.; Vadiati Saberi B.; Hendi A.; Khosravifard N.; Ostovarrad F.; Ghaffari M.
Article.Abstract: While gray scale density metrics are susceptible to cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) noise and calibration inconsistencies, advanced image processing algorithms offer a potential non-invasive, objective alternative. This study presents a comparative evaluation of Fractal Analysis (FA) and Canny Edge-Detection (CED) algorithms for quantifying and classifying distinct bone trabecular patterns. In this ex vivo experimental study, 120 bovine rib bone blocks were categorized into four morphologic groups (D1-D4) and imaged using a standardized CBCT protocol. A single standardized 50 × 50-pixel region of interest (ROI) was analyzed on a selected two-dimensional reconstructed slice from each block. FA and CED quantified structural complexity and edge count, respectively. Group differences were evaluated using analysis of variance with multiplicity-adjusted post hoc tests, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to estimate pairwise discrimination. Both FA and CED values differed significantly across the four morphologic groups ( p < 0.001). FA differentiated every pairwise comparison ( p ≤ 0.014), whereas CED did not differentiate D2 from D3 ( p = 0.717). Exploratory AUCs ranged from 0.77 to 0.99 for FA and from 0.64 to 1.00 for CED. Within this controlled ex vivo model, FA and CED provided objective, reproducible quantification of distinct trabecular bone patterns on CBCT images. FA excels in differentiating intermediate densities (D2 and D3), while CED offers superior performance for denser and looser bone patterns (D1 and D4). The complementary performance of the two algorithms supports their potential as quantitative adjuncts to visual bone-pattern assessment.

Article.Title: Receptive field organization in macaque vlPFC neurons
Article.Authors: Abolfathi Y.; Noroozi J.; Rezayat E.; Dehaqani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While receptive fields (RFs) in ventral and dorsal visual areas are well characterized, their organization in the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC), a region involved in visual processing and cognition, remains largely unexplored. We examined the RFs of 132 vlPFC neurons in macaque monkeys to characterize their spatial response properties, using extracellular recordings with a high-resolution, unbiased random-dot paradigm during passive viewing. Analysis revealed substantial heterogeneity in RF structure, allowing neurons to be classified into three types: uniform, full-field, and nonuniform. More than 85% of neurons exhibited large RFs with multiple high-response regions spanning broad portions of peripheral visual space. These findings reveal the complex organization of vlPFC neurons and provide a foundation for understanding how this region supports flexible visual processing and cognitive computations.

Article.Title: Robustness evaluation of YOLO-based fracture detection in low-quality radiographs
Article.Authors: Xue F.; Zhang Y.; Zhao W.; Wang Z.; Maimaiti A.; Zhang J.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Detecting fractures on radiographs remains challenging because low contrast, noise, anatomical overlap, and projection may obscure subtle abnormalities. We evaluated CLAHE preprocessing, input resolution, and P2 feature integration in a YOLO-based framework using FracAtlas. Single-run ablations were followed by three-seed robustness and size-stratified analyses and a single-institution evaluation of 993 hip radiographs collected at the authors’ institution. In the matched single-run head ablation, CLAHE-preprocessed YOLOv8m and YOLOv8m-P2 both achieved an mAP@0.5 of approximately 0.68 at 960 × 960 pixels. Across three prespecified seeds, mean mAP@0.5 was 0.59 ± 0.03 and 0.58 ± 0.07, respectively, with no consistent P2 advantage. Recall in the smallest internal bounding-box quartile was identical (0.40 ± 0.05). The fixed primary checkpoint achieved an institutional-cohort mAP@0.5 of 0.72 and recall of 0.73. However, median normalized target area was approximately sixfold larger than in FracAtlas, and the cohorts differed in anatomical scope, class distribution, acquisition, and annotation. These findings are cohort-specific and do not demonstrate improved generalizability. P2 provided no consistent benefit, while the single-run CLAHE and resolution findings remain exploratory.

Article.Title: Increased myocardial [64Cu]Cu-DOTATATE uptake is associated with subsequent cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction in rats
Article.Authors: Hoeeg C.; Binderup T.; Madsen J.; Dawoodi I.; He Y.; Kjaer A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Doxorubicin-induced cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) remains a major clinical challenge, often progressing to heart failure. Early detection is limited by the lack of sensitive imaging biomarkers. This exploratory study evaluated whether positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (PET/MR) with [ 64 Cu]Cu-DOTATATE, targeting somatostatin receptor-expressing macrophages, enables identification of early changes during CTRCD development. Male Lewis rats (220 ± 20 g) received intravenous doxorubicin (10.5, n = 10 or 12.5 mg/kg, n = 5), with untreated controls ( n = 4). Cardiac function and tracer uptake were assessed by simultaneous PET/MR at baseline, week four, and week seven. Blood and tissue samples were collected for hematologic and transcriptomic analyses. Doxorubicin treatment induced CTRCD with a > 10% points decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), however, only one rat survived in the 12.5 mg/kg dose group. Cardiac [ 64 Cu]Cu-DOTATATE uptake increased dose-dependently and week four uptake correlated with LVEF at week seven. Hematologic analysis revealed anemia and immune cell alterations. Transcriptomics showed enrichment of pathways related to engulfment of apoptotic cells, extracellular remodeling and vascular perturbations. Increased myocardial [ 64 Cu]Cu-DOTATATE uptake was associated with later decline in LVEF, suggesting that [ 64 Cu]Cu-DOTATATE PET/MR may capture early changes during CTRCD development. Larger studies are needed to determine if this approach can guide cardioprotective interventions and improve clinical outcomes.

Article.Title: Seaweed-associated bacteria from the Gulf of Mannar show prey-lytic and predator-like activity
Article.Authors: Rao A.; Dhurka M.; Sreya P.; Vighnesh L.; Biswas R.; Mahesh M.; Mariya C.; Sasikala C.; Ramana C.
Article.Abstract: Prey-predator interactions are crucial for maintaining the diversity and stability of the ecosystem. In contrast to the extensively studied macropredators, the diversity and ecological significance of the micro-predators remain understudied. The aim of this study was to understand the diversity of bacterial predators and to isolate the predators associated with algal samples collected from the Gulf of Mannar. Sixteen out of twenty-eight algal samples showed prey-lawn lesion formation. Newly isolated strains of Pseudomonas paraeruginosa , Nitratireductor aquimarinus , Shewanella algae, and Alcaligenes phenolicus were identified with previously unknown predatory-like traits, and showed a broad spectrum of prey range. The scanning electron microscopy images showed candidate predator–prey contact consistent with epibiotic interaction. Further, in vitro enrichment followed by metagenomics suggested the presence of candidate epiphytic prey-lytic bacteria associated with Caulerpa sp., highlighting algal-associated candidate predatory bacteria.

Article.Title: Interpretable crop-environment regime analysis using robust unsupervised clustering in arid agro-ecosystems
Article.Authors: Algarni M.; Jamshed H.; Alashwal M.; Waheed U.; Zwawi M.; Hussain A.
Article.Abstract: Interpreting crop-environment patterns in arid agro-ecosystems is challenging since soil properties and weather conditions interact in complex ways, while reliable crop labels, yield records, or field-level suitability classes may not always be available. This study presents an interpretable unsupervised clustering analysis for identifying and explaining crop–environment regimes using seven variables: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, temperature, humidity, and rainfall. A controlled twelve-crop analytical subset was organized into six post-hoc crop–environment regime groups. The comparative evaluation included K-Means, Gaussian mixture modelling, DBSCAN, and hierarchical agglomerative clustering. The crop and regime labels were retained only for interpretation and were not used during unsupervised model fitting. Cluster validity was assessed through internal validation metrics, k-sensitivity analysis, repeated-run stability testing, pairwise adjusted Rand index analysis, and DBSCAN parameter sensitivity. The selected six-regime K-Means solution achieved a Silhouette Score of 0.4836, Davies-Bouldin Index of 0.8181, and Calinski–Harabasz Score of 4948.41. Repeated K-Means analysis across 30 independent initializations showed stable performance, with a mean Silhouette Score of 0.4825 ± 0.0060 and mean Davies-Bouldin Index of 0.8179 ± 0.0010. DBSCAN produced a valid seven-cluster density-based structure with near-zero noise, indicating possible finer substructure within the crop–environment feature space. To improve interpretability, a high-fidelity Random Forest surrogate was trained to reproduce the final K-Means cluster assignments. The surrogate achieved an accuracy and macro-F1 score of 1.0000. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) identified rainfall, nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, and humidity as the main variables contributing to cluster discrimination, while temperature and pH showed comparatively lower explanatory influence. The findings show that robust unsupervised clustering combined with surrogate-based explainability can support transparent crop–environment regime interpretation without claiming direct crop recommendation, yield prediction, or field-level suitability assessment.

Article.Title: Efficacy of combination treatment by ustekinumab and exclusive enteral nutrition in adult patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn’s disease
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Wan H.; Yin A.; An J.; Su J.; Kang J.; Wang J.; Wang W.; Li J.; Ren H.; Zhou Q.; Lu Y.; Tang Z.; Chen W.; An P.
Article.Abstract: Despite growing evidence affirming the therapeutic efficacy of ustekinumab (UST) in the treatment of Crohn’s disease (CD), optimizing clinical responses to this biologic continued to pose a significant challenge in clinical practice. From October 2020 to September 2024, a retrospective study was conducted on 114 patients with moderately-to-severely active CD who received optimized ustekinumab by 2 initial intravenous doses in three inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) centers. The patient population was divided into two cohorts: 56 patients received combination therapy of UST and a concurrent 16-week Exclusive Enteral Nutrition (EEN) (UST + EEN cohort), while the remaining 58 patients were treated with UST monotherapy (UST cohort). Clinical and biological outcomes were meticulously evaluated, with endoscopic response and mucosal healing assessed via colonoscopy at both week 16 and week 52. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics exhibited no statistically significant discrepancies between two cohorts. UST + EEN cohort demonstrated superior outcomes compared to those treated with UST alone, achieving higher rates of clinical response (94.6% vs. 70.7%), clinical remission (89.3% vs. 55.2%), endoscopic response (95.2% vs. 58.8%) and mucosal healing (90.5% vs. 37.3%) at week 16. This therapeutic advantage was maintained to week 52, with 88.2% clinical response, 80.4% clinical remission, 87.5% (colonic lesions) and 87.1% (ileum lesions) endoscopic response, 71.9% (colonic lesions) and 71.0% (ileum lesions) mucosal healing. No severe adverse events were reported. Combination treatment of ustekinumab and a 16-week EEN provided an efficacious and optimized therapeutic strategy, demonstrating robust efficacy for both induction and maintenance treatment in patients with active CD.

Article.Title: Supportive care needs of family caregivers of patients with cervical cancer: a latent profile analysis
Article.Authors: Miao S.; Zeng Y.; Zhou Z.; Bai H.; Fu H.; Long L.; Luo L.; Pang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To identify latent profiles of supportive care needs among family caregivers of patients with cervical cancer and explore factors associated with profile membership, as well as to compare differences in supportive-care-needs across these latent profiles. A cross-sectional study using convenience sampling was conducted from March 2024 to September 2024. 531 participants completed the Supportive Care Needs Scale, Social Support Scale, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and Caregiver Readiness Scale. Latent profile analysis was performed to identify the latent profiles of family caregivers’ supportive care needs. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with membership in different supportive care needs latent profiles. This study identified the latent profiles of three supportive care needs of family caregivers: “High supportive care needs” ( n = 205, 38.61%), “moderate supportive care needs” ( n = 143, 26.93%), and “low supportive care needs” ( n = 183, 34.46%). Multinomial logistic regression revealed that CPS, CD-RISC, marital status, current work status, and daily care duration showed partial significant associations with profile membership, with mixed directions across pairwise profile comparisons. Marital status and daily care duration exhibited significant inter-profile associations. No statistically significant inter-profile differences were observed for the remaining covariates The supportive care needs of family caregivers of patients with cervical cancer can be divided into three latent profiles. Healthcare workers need to pay attention to family caregivers with moderate and high levels of supportive care needs, and provide corresponding support and guidance according to the characteristics of different family caregivers, so as to enhance their ability to cope with and care for patients and improve the quality of life of patients.

Article.Title: Oxidative stress profiles in spent culture media of day 3 and day 5 frozen-thawed embryos: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Karamustafaoglu Balcı B.; Altun Akpınar A.; Demir Ö.; Baki A.; Akgül C.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to compare oxidative stress parameters in the culture media of frozen-thawed cleavage-stage (Day 3) and blastocyst-stage (Day 5) embryos and to evaluate their association with implantation outcomes. In this prospective cohort study, 101 infertile couples undergoing IVF-ICSI treatment were included, with 50 women receiving frozen-thawed cleavage-stage (Day 3) embryo transfers and 51 women receiving frozen-thawed blastocyst-stage (Day 5) embryo transfers. Following embryo thawing and prior to embryo transfer, spent culture media samples were collected for oxidative stress analysis. Total Antioxidant Status (TAS), Total Oxidant Status (TOS), and Oxidative Stress Index (OSI) were measured using standardized colorimetric assays. Clinical pregnancy was defined as the presence of fetal cardiac activity confirmed by ultrasound at 6–7 weeks. Live birth was defined as the delivery of a live infant after 24 weeks of gestation. Oxidative stress parameters were additionally compared between patients with and without clinical pregnancy separately within the Day 3 and Day 5 groups, and stage-adjusted logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether each biomarker was independently associated with clinical pregnancy. A total of 101 patients were included, with 50 undergoing Day 3 and 51 undergoing Day 5 transfers. Clinical pregnancy rates were significantly higher in the Day 5 group (52.9% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.033), and the live birth rate was also higher (47.0% vs. 28.0%, p = 0.036). Day 5 spent culture media had higher TAS ( p = 0.005), lower TOS ( p = 0.001), and lower OSI ( p < 0.001). However, within both developmental-stage strata, TAS, TOS, and OSI did not differ significantly between patients with and without clinical pregnancy (all p > 0.20). In stage-adjusted logistic regression, TAS (aOR per 1-SD increase: 1.30, 95% CI 0.71–2.40; p = 0.399), TOS (aOR: 1.00, 95% CI 0.64–1.55; p = 0.991), and OSI (aOR: 0.97, 95% CI 0.61–1.54; p = 0.885) were not independently associated with clinical pregnancy. Day 5 embryos were associated with a distinct oxidative stress profile characterized by higher TAS, lower TOS, and lower OSI, as well as higher clinical pregnancy and live birth rates, compared with Day 3 embryos. Nevertheless, the absence of within-stage differences and the negative stage-adjusted regression analyses indicate that TAS, TOS, and OSI primarily reflect embryo developmental stage or biological selection in this cohort rather than provide independent information on clinical pregnancy. Larger prospective studies are needed before these measures can be considered candidate non-invasive biomarkers for embryo selection.

Article.Title: Systemic safety and immunophenotypic profiles of human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell exosomes: A comprehensive toxicological assessment
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Ha D.; Cui S.; Yoon S.; Cho B.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exosome-based therapeutics derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are emerging as promising candidates for regenerative medicine due to their potent immunomodulatory and regenerative effects and a favorable safety profile. In this study, safety was evaluated through general toxicity (4-week repeated-dose study including immunotoxicity), genotoxicity, and safety pharmacology studies of an exosome isolated from human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ASC-Exosome) under OECD guidelines and GLP regulations. Toxicological assessments were performed at doses of 2 × 10 9 , 6 × 10 9 , and 2.0 × 10 10 particles/animal/day in a 4-week repeated-dose toxicity study via subcutaneous bolus injection to male and female mice 3 times weekly. In addition, the Ames test and in vitro and in vivo micronucleus tests were performed to assess genotoxic potential. To assess potential effects on major physiological systems, a series of standardized tests was carried out, including telemetry-based cardiovascular assessment, central nervous system (CNS) functional observational battery, respiratory function analysis, and cardiovascular system tests such as in vivo telemetry system and in vitro human ether-à-go-go-related gene (hERG) channel assay. General toxicity assessments revealed no adverse changes in clinical signs, body weight, hematology, clinical biochemistry, or macroscopic and histopathological findings. Immunophenotyping showed that alterations in lymphocyte and monocyte counts were attributable to redistribution and physiological uptake by the phagocyte system, respectively. Furthermore, ASC-Exosomes exhibited no mutagenic potential in either in vitro or in vivo genotoxicity tests and showed no adverse pharmacological effects in the safety pharmacology core battery. Taken together, these findings indicate that ASC-Exosomes were well tolerated under the conditions evaluated, with no adverse effects observed across a comprehensive battery of toxicological and pharmacological evaluations. These results establish a favorable safety profile for ASC-Exosomes, providing a robust non-clinical foundation for their advancement into clinical development.

Article.Title: Pharmacological preconditioning with cilostazol reverses steatosis and protects the liver against ischemia-reperfusion injury in steatotic rats
Article.Authors: Holländer S.; von Heesen M.; Gäbelein G.; Mercier J.; Laschke M.; Spiliotis A.; Alic M.; Glanemann M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease markedly increases susceptibility to hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury during liver surgery. We investigated whether short-term pretreatment with the phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor cilostazol protects steatotic livers in a fructose-induced rat model. Steatosis was induced by a 6-week high-fructose diet in Sprague–Dawley rats. Animals received cilostazol (5 mg/kg/day) or vehicle by oral gavage for 3 or 7 days before 60 min selective lobar ischemia followed by 2–24 h reperfusion. Hepatic arterial flow and microvascular perfusion were assessed by ultrasonic flowmetry and laser Doppler fluxmetry; serum transaminases were measured spectrophotometrically. Histology and immunohistochemistry were used to quantify steatosis, MPO-positive neutrophil infiltration, apoptosis, and hepatocellular cell-cycle-associated activity. Cilostazol pretreatment reduced steatosis, improved hepatic arterial and microvascular perfusion, limited hepatocellular apoptosis, and increased hepatocellular cell-cycle-associated activity compared with controls. Neutrophil infiltration was higher in cilostazol-treated animals than in controls after 2 h of reperfusion. However, it subsequently declined, whereas it continued to increase in controls, resulting in lower neutrophil counts in cilostazol-treated animals after 24 h of reperfusion. Overall, cilostazol pretreatment attenuated warm ischemia–reperfusion injury in steatotic livers by reducing steatosis, improving perfusion, limiting apoptosis, and increasing cell-cycle-associated activity, supporting further evaluation before hepatic surgery in steatotic livers.

Article.Title: A modeling framework for OAM integrity of super Lorentz–Gauss beams in turbulent free-space optical communications
Article.Authors: Dehdashti Jahromi H.; Daneshmandi O.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a rigorous semi-analytical model for characterizing the propagation behavior and quantifying the orbital angular momentum (OAM) integrity of super Lorentz–Gaussian vortex beams (SLGVBs) through atmospheric turbulence. By projecting the received field over the full two-point spatial mutual coherence function via the extended Huygens–Fresnel integral and employing a Hermite–Gaussian expansion of the SLGVB’s non-Gaussian amplitude profile, we derive a closed-form expression for the average received OAM mode power spectrum. This framework allows for the systematic analysis of how the SLGVB’s unique structural parameters—the topological charge ( l ), amplitude orders ( a , b ), and the Lorentz–Gaussian mixing ratio ( \(w_{ls}/w_{gs}\) )—influence link viability. Our findings reveal that structural complexity imposes a significant penalty: the OAM mode purity is inversely proportional to both the topological charge and the amplitude complexity, with high-order configurations collapsing rapidly under turbulent conditions. To bridge the spatial statistics to the temporal domain, we utilize Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis to derive a closed-form analytical expression for the time-averaged OAM purity as a function of the receiver integration window. Furthermore, we evaluate communication performance using a physically grounded on-off keying bit error rate model under spatial crosstalk and receiver noise. The entire theoretical framework is independently validated against classical analytical limits and numerical split-step Fourier wave-optics simulations, showing close quantitative agreement with a root-mean-square error of less than \(2.4\%\) in the weak-to-moderate regime. This verified framework provides essential tools for designing and optimizing structured light sources in high-capacity free-space optical communication systems.

Article.Title: Modeling interrelationships among climate variables using PLS-SEM: evidence from coastal Ghana (1981–2020)
Article.Authors: Osei I.; Baafi-Adomako A.; Boadu D.; Maji J.; Carie C.; Anamalamudi S.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how climatic variables interact through interconnected pathways remains a challenge because atmospheric processes are highly interdependent and often exhibit multicollinearity. This study applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to investigate the direct, indirect, and conditional relationships among minimum temperature (TMIN), maximum temperature (TMAX), wind speed (WIND), rainfall (RAIN), and relative humidity (RH). Monthly climate data from six coastal meteorological stations in Ghana covering 1981–2020 were analyzed. The structural model explained 50.5% of the variance in TMIN, 47.6% in RH, 7.8% in RAIN, and 1.8% in TMAX. Maximum temperature showed the strongest positive association with minimum temperature ( β = 0.688) and the strongest negative association with relative humidity ( β = -0.734). Wind speed was positively associated with both temperature variables but negatively associated with rainfall and relative humidity. Mediation analysis identified six significant indirect pathways, indicating that temperature and rainfall transmit several climatic associations. Relative humidity significantly moderated five of the six hypothesized interactions, demonstrating that moisture conditions influence the strength of key temperature-rainfall and wind-rainfall relationships. The principal structural relationships remained stable across four decades, supporting the temporal robustness of the estimated pathways. These findings indicate that the observed climatic variables are linked through interconnected statistical pathways rather than isolated pairwise associations. Although the estimated relationships should not be interpreted as physical causal mechanisms, the study demonstrates that PLS-SEM provides a useful complementary framework for investigating complex climate interactions using observational environmental data.

Article.Title: Understanding surface settlement in mechanized tunneling through integrated analytical and predictive approaches
Article.Authors: Safa M.; Tabrizi A.; Chakeri H.; Unver B.
Article.Abstract: Surface settlement is one of the major challenges in mechanized tunneling, as it can significantly affect ground stability and existing infrastructures. Despite extensive research on surface settlement in mechanized tunneling, the combined investigation of parameter sensitivity using GRA, the numerical assessment of shield conicity, and the comparative evaluation of mathematical prediction models based on real large project data has received limited attention in previous studies. This study investigates the parameters influencing surface settlement using Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) method, evaluates the effect of the shield’s conical configuration through numerical modeling, and estimates the long-term surface settlements using mathematical models. A comprehensive quantitative dataset obtained from the Tabriz Line 2 Metro project was employed to perform a data-driven analysis and enhance the reliability of the results. The GRA results indicate that tunnel depth is the most influential parameter affecting surface settlement. Based on these findings, key parameters were selected for numerical modeling, and the impact of the conical shield geometry was analyzed under three different geotechnical stratifications. The numerical simulations using PLAXIS show that the shield passage can induce settlements exceeding 40% in soils with varying structural characteristics. In addition, long-term surface settlements were predicted using Semi-logarithmic, Hyperbolic, and Hybrid mathematical models. The comparative analysis demonstrates that the Semi-logarithmic approach provides more accurate predictions compared to the other methods. The results highlight that integrating data-driven analytical techniques with numerical modeling can significantly improve the understanding and prediction of surface settlement in mechanized tunneling projects. The novelty of this paper emphasis on the utilization of mathematical correlations in the log-term settlement magnitudes which is based on a large field data and can reduce both project costs, controlling time, and possible design or construction risks.

Article.Title: Quadruped robot foothold intelligence for safe locomotion on hazardous terrain
Article.Authors: Djeffal S.; Ghoul A.; Latreche A.; Morakchi M.; Bendriss B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Safe quadruped locomotion over hazardous terrain cannot be reduced to selecting the locally safest foothold, because a geometrically reachable contact may still deteriorate the subsequent support phase, increase actuator demand, approach friction limits, or leave insufficient clearance for the robot body. This work presents STEP-CBF+, a reduced-order predictive foothold-and-posture screening framework that couples terrain-risk memory, DCM/ZMP-based support prediction, discrete-time barrier screening, energy-aware motion regularization, three-joint torque feasibility, friction-cone constraints, and anticipatory body-height adaptation within a single candidate-selection layer. The study considers a 13.5 kg quadruped with 3-DOF legs executing a crawl gait with duty factor 0.75 and evaluating 49 foothold candidates at each decision. Six hazardous-terrain conditions are examined over 25 randomized terrain and payload realizations and compared with nominal, risk-only, and reduced-order convex-MPC strategies. Performance is quantified using independent fall and slip outcomes, distance before failure, dynamic support margins, tracking accuracy, actuator and friction utilization, computation time, and component-wise ablations. Across all scenarios, STEP-CBF+ reduces the mean fall rate to 4.0% while increasing the stable-step fraction to 77.3%, compared with 16.7–18.7% falls and 72.2–73.7% stable steps for the three comparators. A particularly revealing result appears on inclined terrain, where stable time reaches 86.0% and the minimum dynamic margin improves to $$-0.032$$ m while peak actuator utilization is reduced. In the confined duck-under scenario, anticipatory posture adaptation enables collision-free traversal and zero falls, whereas all non-height-adaptive strategies fail. The method retains a mean selection time of approximately 13.6 ms, compared with 30.5 ms for the reduced-order convex-MPC implementation. The results indicate that the main benefit of STEP-CBF+ emerges when contact feasibility must be evaluated together with the consequences of the next support phase and body posture, providing an interpretable intermediate safety layer between terrain perception and lower-level locomotion control. The conclusions remain limited to reduced-order randomized simulation and do not constitute a whole-body nonlinear invariance proof or hardware validation.

Article.Title: Normative and maladaptive personality traits in borderline personality disorder: a comparative and hierarchical analysis of HEXACO and PID-5
Article.Authors: Weiß M.; Hepp J.; Seitz K.; Lai Y.; Kleindienst N.; Steinmann S.; Bertsch K.; Niedtfeld I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dimensional models of personality pathology invite the question of how normative and maladaptive trait systems jointly characterize borderline personality disorder (BPD). This study examined how the HEXACO model of personality and the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders trait system, operationalized with the Personality Inventory for DSM–5, differentiate individuals with BPD from mentally healthy control (HC) individuals, both separately and jointly. Data from two assessment waves of a large clinical research program were combined into a final sample of 575 participants (233 with BPD, 342 HC). A joint item-level PCA was conducted to examine seven- and eleven-component solutions, and a Bass-Ackwards analysis was conducted to examine the joint hierarchical structure of HEXACO and PID-5 items. Both instruments were administered as self-reports. Compared with HC, individuals with BPD showed lower HEXACO Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Conscientiousness, and higher Emotionality, as well as higher scores on all PID-5 domains, particularly Negative Affectivity and Disinhibition. In the combined domain model, low Extraversion and high PID-5 Negative Affectivity, Disinhibition, and Psychoticism uniquely predicted BPD status. At the facet level, low Social Self-Esteem (HEXACO) and high Emotional Lability (PID-5) were especially discriminative. Joint item analyses yielded a seven-component solution in which six components corresponded closely to the six HEXACO factors and a dominant seventh component represented broad maladaptivity, with PID-5 items loading positively and HEXACO items largely loading inversely. Group differences were almost entirely confined to this broad component. These findings suggest that BPD is characterized by both a broad maladaptivity dimension and a more specific trait profile involving affective instability, interpersonal insecurity, irritability, and reduced behavioral control. The findings support integrating normative and maladaptive trait models in the dimensional description of BPD, while indicating that the dominant joint dimension cannot be interpreted unambiguously as a substantive general factor of personality pathology.

Article.Title: Reconfigurable CMOS ternary inverter based on charge-trapping-enabled VTC modulation
Article.Authors: Moon H.; Kwon T.; Kim T.; Kim J.; Song W.; Gu J.; Park D.; Jang E.; Yun H.; Kim S.; Woo S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A major challenge in complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS)-based ternary inverters is achieving a balanced combination of power consumption, switching speed, functional flexibility, and compatibility with conventional CMOS technology. Despite various efforts, simultaneously achieving competitive power consumption, fast switching, and functional flexibility within a CMOS-compatible framework remains challenging. In this work, we propose a reconfigurable ternary inverter that leverages charge-trapping-layer (CTL)-induced threshold voltage ( V th ) modulation to enable controllable modulation of voltage transfer characteristics (VTC). By selectively integrating CTLs into different transistor types, we demonstrate that the VTC can be modulated either vertically or horizontally depending on the device location, enabling precise control of the intermediate logic level and switching boundaries. Based on this mechanism, the proposed inverter supports dynamic reconfiguration between ternary and binary operations through programmable V th tuning. The use of a silicon-oxide-nitride-oxide-silicon (SONOS) FinFET structure provides improved electrostatic control while maintaining compatibility with conventional Si CMOS technology. Through technology computer-aided design (TCAD)-based mixed-mode simulations calibrated with experimental data, we demonstrate that the CTL integration location strongly influences both VTC modulation and circuit performance. Among the investigated configurations, low-threshold-voltage transistor (LVT)-CTL integration enables binary/ternary reconfiguration while maintaining a VDD/2 power consumption of 173 nW and average propagation delays of 5.10 and 4.77 ns under ternary and binary operations, respectively. In contrast, the high-threshold-voltage transistor (HVT)-CTL integration exhibits a pronounced propagation-delay penalty under ternary operation, highlighting the importance of CTL placement in reconfigurable ternary inverter design. These results suggest a general design strategy for VTC engineering in multi-valued logic (MVL) circuits, in which CTL placement serves as a key design parameter for controlling the VTC modulation mode and associated circuit-performance trade-offs.

Article.Title: Impact of the morphology of the left ventricular thrombus on the clinical outcomes
Article.Authors: Cai Y.; Yang Q.; Quan X.; Lang X.; Zhu J.; Liang Y.
Article.Abstract: The impact of thrombus morphology on the outcome of patients with left ventricular (LV) thrombus is uncertain. Our objectives were to evaluate the association between thrombus morphology and clinical outcomes and to explore whether anticoagulation duration differed according to LV thrombus morphology. We enrolled patients prospectively from 2020 to 2022 and retrospectively from 2010 to 2020 at the National Cardiovascular Center of China. Patients with a history of LV thrombus < 3 months were included. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) Cox modeling was used to estimate associations between thrombus morphology and outcomes for the endpoints of thrombus resolution, the composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and rehospitalization for cardiovascular events. Propensity score matching (PSM) and multivariable Cox regression models were adopted in additional sensitivity analyses. We included 623 patients, the majority of whom (84.9%) had mural thrombus. Congestive heart failure was diagnosed in 477 (76.6%) of the patients. Patients with protuberant thrombus received longer-duration anticoagulation (145 days versus 87 days, P < 0.001) and were more frequently treated with direct oral anticoagulants. In a median follow-up of 402 days, protuberant thrombus was associated with a higher probability of LV thrombus resolution in unadjusted and propensity-based analyses; however, this association was not confirmed in the multivariable Cox regression model (HR 1.08, 95%CI 0.81–1.43, P = 0.605). No significant differences in MACE were observed; however, the study was underpowered for clinical endpoints because of the low number of events. Protuberant LV thrombus may be associated with thrombus resolution in certain analytical settings; however, this association was not consistent across statistical models. In addition, the independent contribution of thrombus morphology could not be fully distinguished from treatment-related factors, including differences in anticoagulation duration and type. No significant differences in clinical outcomes were observed, although the study was underpowered for these endpoints. Therefore, the findings should be considered exploratory and interpreted with caution. Trial registration : This study was a combined cohort from two studies (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04970381, NCT 05006677).

Article.Title: LIO-EAC: gravity-referenced external altitude compensation for LiDAR-inertial odometry
Article.Authors: Jung J.; Seo K.; Jung S.; Song J.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) using Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors often exhibits degraded altitude estimation in environments with irregular terrain or weak vertical observability. We show through first-order error propagation of the point-to-plane update that pitch or ground-normal errors produce altitude errors scaled by the mean forward range of supporting ground points, making open terrain with distant ground returns and few vertical structures vulnerable to vertical drift. Based on this analysis, we propose LIO-EAC, an external altitude compensation module for Fast-LIO2 that does not modify its iterated extended Kalman filter state vector. The module derives a gravity-referenced pitch cue from simple moving average-filtered accelerometer measurements and estimates a lumped, slowly varying pitch bias from its residual with the iEKF-implied pitch. The pitch cue provides a proxy surface normal for point-to-plane updates, while the estimated bias realigns the stored map about the current position under an event trigger. LIO-EAC is evaluated against Fast-LIO2 in a level open field, a multi-level underground structure, and an indoor–outdoor round trip with sloped transitions. Four repeated trials, ablation studies, and geometric consistency metrics show reduced altitude drift without additional sensors or modification of the underlying estimator.

Article.Title: Curing behavior and performance evolution of epoxy asphalt reclaimed binder and mixture
Article.Authors: Zhong Z.; Xu M.; Guo D.; Wang P.; Han L.; Shi F.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To clarify how curing-induced crosslinking in epoxy asphalt reclaimed systems affects mixture compaction quality, we investigated curing behavior at both the binder and mixture scales using epoxy asphalt reclaimed binder (REAB) and epoxy asphalt reclaimed mixture (REAM), respectively. Tensile, Brookfield viscosity, dynamic shear rheometer (DSR), bending beam rheometer (BBR), and fluorescence microscopy tests were conducted to characterize the phase evolution and high- and low-temperature rheological behavior of REAB. The compaction characteristics and mechanical properties of REAM at different curing stages were evaluated based on air-void content and indirect tensile strength. The results showed that, as the epoxy system content increased from 10 to 50%, the tensile strength of REAB increased from 1.2 to 3.0 MPa, whereas its elongation at break initially increased and then decreased. With increasing curing time, the viscosity of REAB showed a stagewise transition from slow growth to a rapid increase, and higher curing temperatures advanced the onset of this rapid increase. Curing-induced crosslinking markedly enhanced high-temperature stiffness and elasticity, with the rutting factor increasing by more than 110%, but reduced low-temperature relaxation capacity. The air-void content of REAM initially decreased and then increased, whereas its indirect tensile strength initially increased and then decreased. Three-factor factorial analysis of variance showed that temperature, time, epoxy system content, and their interactions had significant effects (p < 0.01). These findings clarify the stagewise evolution of epoxy asphalt reclaimed systems during curing and provide a reference for determining the allowable construction window and controlling the compaction process of epoxy asphalt reclaimed mixtures with high RAP contents.

Article.Title: Clinical efficacy analysis of laser-assisted preoperative design and syringe-guided subcutaneous progressive tension sutures in abdominoplasty
Article.Authors: Wu C.; Xia L.; Liang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abdominoplasty is an effective procedure for correcting postpartum abdominal wall laxity and rectus diastasis. However, conventional techniques often face challenges such as asymmetry in preoperative design and a high incidence of postoperative tension blisters. This study aimed to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and surgical efficiency of a modified abdominoplasty technique combining laser-assisted preoperative design with syringe-guided subcutaneous progressive tension sutures (PTS). A single-center historical controlled study was conducted. Fifty-five patients who underwent the modified technique (laser-assisted design + syringe-guided suturing) were assigned to the modified group, while 48 patients who received traditional abdominoplasty (manual drawing + conventional suturing) served as the control group. Baseline characteristics, including age, body mass index (BMI), and rectus diastasis width, were matched between groups. The primary outcomes were operative closure time (efficiency) and abdominal symmetry at 14 days postoperatively (absolute difference in distance from bilateral anterior superior iliac spines to the midline). Secondary outcomes included complication rates (focusing on tension blisters), intraoperative blood loss, and surgeon-rated ease of use (Visual Analog Scale, VAS). No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics between the two groups ( P > 0.05). The modified group demonstrated significantly shorter incision closure time compared to the control group (47.02 ± 3.80 min vs. 67.92 ± 3.27 min, P < 0.001). Postoperative symmetry was significantly improved in the modified group at 14 days (0.53 ± 0.16 cm vs. 0.89 ± 0.20 cm, P < 0.001), with sustained benefits at 6 months. The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the modified group, primarily due to a marked reduction in tension blisters (3.6% vs. 75%). Additionally, intraoperative blood loss was reduced in the modified group ( P = 0.005). Surgeons rated the modified technique highly for design convenience and suturing ease (VAS scores: 8.75 and 8.24, respectively). Furthermore, drain removal time and total drainage volume were significantly lower in the modified group ( P < 0.05). Laser-assisted preoperative design ensures precise and symmetrical marking, while syringe-guided subcutaneous PTS effectively reduces tension and shortens operative time. Compared to conventional methods, this modified technique significantly decreases the incidence of tension blisters, improves aesthetic symmetry, and offers operational simplicity, demonstrating high clinical value. This method is simple and easy to implement, making it suitable for widespread clinical application.

Article.Title: Maternal exercise is associated with more oxidative skeletal muscle and beige adipose tissue phenotypes and improved early post-weaning glucose tolerance in rat offspring
Article.Authors: Fujita N.; Tabuchi R.; Sato S.; Ishii Y.; Sakakura K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing prevalence of childhood obesity has highlighted the need for effective preventive strategies during early life. Maternal exercise is a promising approach to improve offspring metabolic health; however, whether these benefits are established during the peri-weaning period and how they are influenced by the postnatal environment remain unclear. This study investigated whether maternal voluntary exercise induces early metabolic programming in male offspring and examined skeletal muscle and adipose tissue adaptations associated with improved glucose metabolism. Female Wistar rats were assigned to sedentary or voluntary wheel running conditions before and during gestation. Male offspring were assessed at PD35 using a glucose tolerance test and histological analyses of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue. A subset of offspring was fed a high-fat diet from weaning to evaluate the influence of the postnatal nutritional environment. Offspring from exercised dams exhibited improved glucose tolerance, accompanied by oxidative remodeling of skeletal muscle, maintenance of beige characteristics in subcutaneous adipose tissue, and reduced visceral adiposity. The improvement in glucose tolerance was attenuated by high-fat feeding after weaning. Maternal exercise therefore may contribute to early metabolic programming that improves glucose tolerance in offspring, although the resulting metabolic phenotype remains plastic and is substantially influenced by the post-weaning nutritional environment.

Article.Title: HCE-Boost: hierarchy-constrained expert boosting for imbalanced multiclass intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Zhang R.
Article.Abstract: Imbalanced multiclass network intrusion detection presents three coupled challenges: dominant classes can absorb structurally similar rare attacks, global reweighting cannot target the resulting class-specific confusion, and unconstrained specialist models can distort evidence for unrelated attack families. We propose hierarchy-constrained expert boosting (HCE-Boost), a fully supervised ensemble that addresses these challenges through three coordinated modules. First, a leakage-controlled protocol fixes the training, validation, and test roles before any transformation or model selection. Second, equally weighted XGBoost and LightGBM experts estimate the global class distribution, while validation errors activate a local specialist only for a semantic family or rare-absorption group that satisfies fixed criteria. Third, a probability-mass-conserving output rule allows the specialist to revise within-group proportions without increasing the total probability assigned to that group. Under fixed, class-complete evaluation with five matched seeds, HCE-Boost attained mean macro-averaged F1 scores (macro-F1) of 64.99%, 93.73%, and 92.39% on NSL-KDD, the supplied CIC-IDS2017 subset, and edge-IIoTset, respectively. These values were the highest among eight methods evaluated under the same protocol and exceeded the strongest corresponding baselines by 2.20, 0.71, and 0.28 percentage points. Component analysis showed a consistent specialist benefit on NSL-KDD, an inconclusive mean benefit on CIC-IDS2017, and no specialist activation on Edge-IIoTset. The results support validation-governed hierarchical correction as a method for improving minority-sensitive classification within the evaluated fixed-split setting. They do not establish operational edge deployment, which requires model compression and hardware-level latency, memory, throughput, and power measurements.

Article.Title: Delirium prevalence and associated factors in critically ill neonates hospitalized in the NICU and their neurodevelopmental implications
Article.Authors: Alinejad-Naeini M.; Faghir-Ganji M.; Tajalli S.; Choobdar F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the vulnerability of the developing neonatal brain, delirium remains a largely unrecognized complication in the NICU, with its prevalence and associated factors still poorly characterized. This condition is increasingly recognized as a potential indicator of acute brain dysfunction. However, evidence regarding its neurodevelopmental consequences remains speculative and requires longitudinal investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to identify factors associated with the development of delirium in neonates admitted to the NICU and to explore their neurodevelopmental implications. This prospective observational study with a cross-sectional analytical design was conductedin three Level III NICUs between November 2023 and January 2025. A total of 243 neonates were included. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire and the Cornell Assessment of Pediatric Delirium (CAPD) scale. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics. A multivariable logistic regression model was developed, with covariates selected a priori based on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to minimize bias. The model’s quality was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, Area under the Curve (AUC), and Nagelkerke R 2 . The final multivariable logistic regression model identified several independent factors: Corrected Age (OR 0.964, 95% CI 0.941–0.989, p = 0.004) and Birthweight (OR 0.872 per 100 g increase, 95% CI 0.815–0.933, p < 0.001) were protective factors, with higher values decreasing the odds of delirium. Being a first-born neonate significantly increased the odds of delirium (OR 18.834, 95% CI 6.152–57.662, p < 0.001). Jaundice (OR 5.221, 95% CI 1.559–17.485, p = 0.007), Sepsis (OR 5.615, 95% CI 2.092–15.069, p = 0.001), and Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) (OR 8.558, 95% CI 2.061–35.538, p = 0.003) were strongly associated with increased odds of delirium compared to prematurity. Conversely, Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN) was associated with significantly lower odds of delirium (OR 0.126, 95% CI 0.027–0.599, p = 0.009) compared to other diagnoses. Delirium is prevalent among NICU neonates and is significantly associated with factors related to brain development, including lower corrected age, lower birth weight, first-born status, sepsis, RDS, and jaundice, while TTN appears protective. These cross-sectional findings highlight a high prevalence of delirium in the NICU and identify several associated factors. While the results support the need for systematic screening, causal relationships and the clinical utility of screening for improving neurodevelopmental outcomes require confirmation through prospective interventional studies.

Article.Title: Clonal sharing of antimicrobial-resistant bacterial clones and homogenization of the microbiome in the oral, nasal, and endotracheal sites of intubated ICU patients
Article.Authors: Yasutomi Y.; Nishihama S.; Kawayanagi T.; Asakawa M.; Nishi H.; Kawada-Matsuo M.; Hisatsune J.; Sugawara Y.; Shiba H.; Kawaguchi H.; Shime N.; Takeshita T.; Sugai M.; Komatsuzawa H.
Article.Abstract: Colonization by drug-resistant bacteria in intubated patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) often causes serious infections. Therefore, assessing drug-resistant status and flora at multiple sites in patients is important. To compare the microbial composition of the oral or nasal cavity, and endotracheal intubation site (subglottic secretory site), we isolated Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant S. aureus [MRSA]) and third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Gram-negative rods from 61 ICU patients. Whole-genome analysis of isolates was performed, and clonal concordance across sites was assessed using core-genome SNP distances. The 16S rRNA gene analysis was used to examine the microbial composition at these sites. S. aureus , MRSA, and gram-negative drug-resistant bacteria were isolated from 57.4%, 16.4% and 18.0% patients, respectively. In some patients with the same bacterial species isolated from multiple sites, SNPs among isolates were 0–9, suggesting shared clone or closely related lineage within individuals. Microbial flora analysis, based on PCoA using UniFrac distance, showed that the bacterial communities at three different sites in ICU patients were closely related. These findings suggest similar colonization of three different sites. The finding that similar colonization of three different sites was observed is expected to contribute to developing future infection prevention strategies in ICUs.

Article.Title: Memory guided adaptive spatiotemporal forecasting for city level cellular traffic
Article.Authors: Hu F.; Huang Y.; Lin X.; Zhang S.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of city-level cellular network traffic is essential for proactive resource allocation, congestion avoidance, and quality-of-service management in next-generation mobile networks, including under the ongoing evolution toward IPv6. Existing spatiotemporal forecasting methods face two limitations: graph-based approaches rely on pre-defined or statically learned adjacency structures that may not adequately reflect time-varying inter-cell dependencies, and most architectures lack explicit mechanisms to encode recurring traffic patterns at both global network-wide and local per-cell granularities. To address these limitations, we propose CellMem, a memory-guided adaptive spatiotemporal network that combines a DLinear backbone, dual-branch prototype memory, a prototype-driven dynamic graph, and a prototype-aware gated residual. Its core novelty is an end-to-end shared- \(\mathscr {W}_g\) coupling: the same global prototype attention weights retrieve pattern-specific correction features and mix learnable low-rank sub-graphs into a sample-specific adjacency matrix. On the Milan Telecom Italia dataset under one-step-ahead forecasting, CellMem reduces Internet RMSE from \(155.17 \pm 1.68\) (SA-GCN) to \(143.05 \pm 0.57\) and improves \(R^2\) from 0.9579 to 0.9642, with consistent gains on SMS and Call traffic. Source code is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21835202 .

Article.Title: Improved prediction of bimodal soil-water characteristic curves for expansive soils from mercury intrusion porosimetry using machine learning
Article.Authors: Al-Mahbashi A.; Abbas Y.; Almajed A.
Article.Abstract: The soil-water characteristic curve (SWCC) occupies a central position in unsaturated soil mechanics, yet for expansive soils its direct experimental characterization is challenging by the concurrent demands of resolving a bimodal pore material and tracking suction-induced volumetric deformation across a measurement process that routinely exceeds several months. To avoid these constraints, the present study develops a microstructural-machine learning (ML) framework for predicting bimodal SWCCs over the entire suction range, including low to high swelling potential expansive soils. Mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) was conducted on compacted specimens, and the recovered pore-throat size distributions were converted to equivalent matric suction profiles through the Young-Laplace equation; systematic corrections (for suction, s , and degree of saturation, S ) were then applied to reconcile MIP-inferred retention with laboratory-measured values by incorporating suction scaling factors and the volumetric shrinkage history recorded along the full drying path. Fourteen regression algorithms were benchmarked under identical cross-validation conditions; XGBoost was selected as the most defensible architecture on the basis of its balance of predictive accuracy and resistance to overfitting rather than the single highest cross-validated score, achieving R² = 0.997 on the held-out test partition, a level of accuracy comparable to several other tree-based ensembles evaluated, but combined with materially greater generalisation stability. Shapley additive explanations analysis decomposed this prediction into contributions from individual inputs and identified five key physical descriptors. Those five descriptors were subsequently adopted as the terminal alphabet for gene expression programming, which produced two transparent, computationally inexpensive closed-form analytical models whose predictive accuracy was preserved against nine independent experimental datasets drawn from the open literature, the primary practical contribution of this work. Furthermore, the model serves as a vital tool in unsaturated soil mechanics to ensure the safe and cost-effective design of infrastructure founded on these problematic soils.

Article.Title: Chitosan-stabilized Ag–Ni bimetallic nanoparticles for quantitative antibacterial evaluation and prospective wound-coating applications
Article.Authors: Sadiq M.; Ali S.; Naeem-ul-Hassan M.; Alotaibi A.; Ullah R.; Nishan U.; Abbas A.; Kifle D.; Assad N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bimetallic silver–nickel nanoparticles (Ag–Ni BMNPs) stabilized with chitosan were synthesized and systematically characterized to evaluate their antibacterial properties and potential for proof-of-concept wound-coating applications.
