Article.Abstract: Detailed knowledge of axillary nerve anatomy and its relationship to a proximal humeral locking plate is important for reducing iatrogenic nerve injury during percutaneous minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis (MIPO) for proximal humeral fractures. Twelve adult upper-limb cadaveric specimens were dissected, and PHILOS plates (Synthes) were positioned using a standardized protocol. We recorded the distance between the axillary nerve and each plate hole, the acromion-to-axillary nerve distance (AAND), and arm length (AL), defined as the distance from the acromion to the lateral epicondyle. The axillary nerve index (ANI) was calculated as AAND/AL. Pearson correlation and ordinary least-squares linear regression were used to examine the association between AL and AAND. The six proximal holes (A1–C2) and three distal holes (F–H) were more than 5 mm from the axillary nerve in all specimens, whereas D, E1, and E2 were within 5 mm. Mean AAND was 6.4 ± 0.5 cm (range, 5.6–7.2 cm), mean AL was 29.4 ± 2.0 cm (range, 26.3–32.4 cm), and mean ANI was 0.22 ± 0.01 (range, 0.20–0.23). AL and AAND were positively correlated (Pearson r = 0.902, p < 0.001). The equation derived from this dataset was AAND = 0.2356 × AL − 0.5684 (in-sample R² = 0.813). In this cadaveric series, holes D, E1, and E2 were closest to the axillary nerve and require direct nerve identification and protection during screw insertion. The regression equation is exploratory and has not undergone internal or independent external validation. Although the minimum observed AAND was 5.6 cm, a 5-cm distance should be regarded only as an approximate anatomical reference rather than a universally safe surgical corridor.

Article.Title: A stability-oriented framework based on adaptive hunger games search for non-convex economic dispatch
Article.Authors: Mustafa A.; Jan A.; Iqbal A.; Abbasi M.
Article.Abstract: Economic dispatch becomes challenging when valve-point effects, transmission losses, ramp-rate limits, prohibited operating zones, and spinning-reserve requirements create non-convex, discontinuous, and multimodal search spaces. This study proposes an adaptive hunger games search (AHGS) algorithm that integrates quadratic shrink control, a unified directional update, hunger-controlled crossover, greedy selection, and linear population reduction to improve the stability of the original hunger games search (HGS). AHGS was evaluated on 21 ED benchmark systems ranging from 6 to 140 generating units and compared with HGS, PSO, DE, L-HMDE, and PTBO under common within-case settings and a unified feasibility-restoration framework. Across TC1–TC17, AHGS achieved the best Friedman mean rank of 2.18. Nemenyi analysis showed statistically significant differences between AHGS and HGS and between AHGS and PTBO, while AHGS remained statistically comparable with L-HMDE, DE, and PSO. Relative to HGS, AHGS reduced run-to-run standard deviation by 57.06%–99.52%, with an average reduction of 77.49%. AHGS also required lower total wall-clock time in all 21 cases, with reductions of 2.41%–24.76%; however, this advantage is interpreted together with the lower realized evaluation workload produced by population reduction rather than as universally lower per-evaluation complexity. For TC18–TC21, AHGS recorded three statistically significant wins and one nonsignificant comparison against HGS. Additional evaluation on ten CEC2020 functions using 12 runs per function yielded a mean rank of 3.20 for AHGS versus 7.50 for HGS. Overall, AHGS provides a stability-oriented improvement over HGS while remaining competitive with strong contemporary optimizers.

Article.Title: NOTCH1 activating variants identify a high-risk subgroup of adenoid cystic carcinoma in a nationwide Japanese cohort
Article.Authors: Noguchi T.; Okumura T.; Miyagawa M.; Shigeto S.; Konno S.; Tateishi A.; Uehara T.; Kosho T.; Makishima H.; Kanda S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) follows a heterogeneous clinical course, and because systemic therapies have limited efficacy, active surveillance is offered to selected patients, yet no validated molecular biomarker guides the choice between surveillance and intensive treatment. We retrospectively analyzed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) and clinical data from 584 patients with ACC (491 head and neck, 93 other sites) in the nationwide Japanese C-CAT database (August 2019–October 2025). NOTCH1 variants were classified as activating (heterodimerization-domain missense or PEST-domain truncating) or non-activating, and overall survival was assessed in 213 patients using Kaplan–Meier estimates, multivariable Cox regression, and propensity-score matching. Activating NOTCH1 variants occurred in 15.5% of survival-evaluable cases and conferred markedly inferior survival (median 20.9 versus 64.7 versus 86.0 months for activating, non-activating, and wild-type). The effect was independent of age, sex, stage, and tumor mutational burden (adjusted hazard ratio 3.93, 95% confidence interval 2.18–7.09) and was confirmed by propensity-score matching. Actionable ERBB2 alterations occurred in 3.1% of patients. CGP therefore delineates clinically distinct ACC subgroups: activating NOTCH1 variants identify one in six patients for whom active surveillance may be inappropriate, and a small subset is eligible for HER2-directed therapy.

Article.Title: ThermoPix: an electronic-photonic temperature sensor array with microsecond row readout
Article.Authors: Udoy M.; Dang D.; Li W.; Gupta S.; Datta S.; Aziz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents ThermoPix, a CMOS-compatible electronic–photonic architecture for high-spatial-resolution temperature sensing. The proposed system converts temperature-induced wavelength shifts in a photonic interferometric sensor into timing information that can be processed by CMOS circuitry. We use a valley photonic crystal Mach–Zehnder interferometer (VPC-MZI) as the sensing element, whose temperature-dependent spectral response is detected using an integrated waveguide photodetector and translated into a time-varying photocurrent. A CMOS readout circuit employing a phase-transition-material device performs threshold detection and generates a timing signal corresponding to the temperature-dependent crossing event. Circuit-level simulations yield a temperature sensitivity of 3.12 ns/K, a row readout time of 2 µs, and a circuit-level sensing power–delay product (PDP) of 0.152 fJ. The 3.33 ns timing quantization corresponds to a nominal temperature resolution of 1.07 K, while Monte Carlo analysis including process and laser wavelength variations yields a post-calibration MAE of 0.49 K and RMSE of 0.66 K. The required optical power per photonic cell is 150 nW, enabling energy-efficient array operation without requiring cooling or special environmental arrangements. We also present alternative photonic layer architectures for optical power distribution across the array. In one approach, we use different tap ratios along the row, while the other uses identical tap ratios with bidirectional excitation. The resulting average photonic cell pitches are 23.26 μm and 38.52 μm, respectively. These simulation and variation results indicate the potential of the proposed ThermoPix architecture for scalable integrated temperature sensing arrays that combine photonic sensing elements with CMOS-compatible timing-based readout.

Article.Title: Terrestrial gamma radiation level and the activity concentrations of natural radionuclides in crude oil-impacted soils of Okuregbe Creek, Nigeria
Article.Authors: Emelue H.; Inyang S.; Isinkaye M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the terrestrial gamma radiation and the activity concentrations of natural radionuclide ( 40 K, 226 Ra and 232 Th) in crude oil-impacted soils of Okuregbe Creek, Ogoniland, Nigeria, using both in-situ and laboratory measurements. A GQ GMC-500/GMC-500 + digital Geiger-Müller counter was used for in-situ measurements, and a CsI(Tl) detector was used for the gamma spectrometry. The activity concentration 40 K in the crude oil impacted area varied between 218.2 and 477.3 Bq/kg, while 226 Ra and 232 Th ranged from 23.4 to 52.3 Bq/kg, and 24.9 to 87.0 Bq/kg, respectively. Although the oil-impacted soils show higher mean activity concentrations for 226 Ra and 232 Th than the control soils, the measured ranges remained largely comparable with worldwide soil radioactivity reported by UNSCEAR. The estimated mean absorbed dose rate in the oil-spilled creek was higher than the control but remained below the global baseline. Similarly, all the calculated radiological hazard parameters fall within their international permissible safety limits. The results of this study show that while petroleum exploitation has technologically enhanced naturally occurring radioactive materials in Okuregbe Creek, the soils currently pose no immediate acute radiological hazard to the local population. Continuous environmental monitoring is recommended to safeguard against long-term ecological bioaccumulation.

Article.Title: Characterizing acid-reacted crude oil to elucidate asphaltene sludge formation under operational conditions
Article.Authors: Sharifzadegan A.; Dehaghani A.
Article.Abstract: Asphaltene sludge formation during matrix acidizing is governed by multiple operational parameters, yet the underlying interfacial mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study employed an integrated framework using viscosity and interfacial tension (IFT) measurements, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, inductively coupled plasma–optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES), and sludge tests to investigate how acid type and concentration, acid solution salinity, ferric ion concentration, acid-to-mixture volumetric ratio (AMR), and temperature influence sludge formation in crude oils with distinct physicochemical properties. Increasing the HCl concentration (7.5–28 wt%) appeared to promote the accumulation of protonated asphaltenes at the acid–oil interface, as evidenced by increased IFT and reduced viscosity and polar aromaticity in acid-aged oils. These changes were accompanied by elevated vanadium and nickel concentrations in the acid phase and increased sludge formation, whereas spent acid resulted in negligible sludge. Compared with acids prepared using 20-times diluted seawater, seawater-based acids produced lower IFT, higher viscosity, greater polar aromaticity, and less sludge formation. Increasing the ferric ion concentration from 500 to 2000 ppm was associated with stronger acid–asphaltene interactions, whereas AMR values of 0.2 and 0.8 were associated with weaker interactions, potentially reflecting an imbalance between acid ions and asphaltenes. Lowering the temperature from 90 to 70 °C resulted in crude oil-dependent variations in asphaltene precipitation. These findings provide mechanistic insights into acid-induced asphaltene sludge formation under various operational conditions, supporting the optimization of matrix acidizing treatments with the potential to mitigate sludge-related operational complications.

Article.Title: Time-scaled quantum simulation of dissipative nanoelectronics with zero gate overhead
Article.Authors: Przygocki M.; Kotas R.; Zubert M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simulating open quantum systems (OQS) is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics and materials science. However, noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices are severely bottlenecked by limited coherence times and gate infidelities. Conventional quantum simulations of Amplitude-Damping Lindblad dynamics requires active dissipative gates and ancilla environments, leading to spurious qubit flips, state saturation, and a significant two-qubit overhead. While recent methods exploit intrinsic hardware noise for quantum simulation, they mainly rely on tailored decoherence-inducing gates or complex error mitigation. Here, we introduce a hardware-intrinsic time-scaling methodology that completely eliminates active dissipative gates. By mapping the processor's continuous energy relaxation (T1) explicitly via native delay instructions, our protocol captures targeted dissipative dynamics with a strict O(1) algorithmic overhead, bypassing conventional mitigation sampling costs. We experimentally demonstrate this efficient approach on two IBM quantum architectures, successfully emulating tight-binding parameter regimes. These include nanosecond magnon propagation in yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spin chains, as well as ultrafast picosecond phonon dynamics across 1D transport channels within 2D molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and multi-site graphene lattices. Furthermore, to mitigate error accumulation in multi-site arrays, we implement a depth-dependent scaling protocol. Finally, the proposed method is extended to the fermionic domain, emulating the femtosecond relaxation of an isolated charge carrier across 4-qubit topologies. This methodology provides a scalable pathway for robust, hardware-tailored materials simulations.

Article.Title: Quokka swarm defensive optimization-based ensemble deep learning for disease prediction using remote monitoring data
Article.Authors: Santoshi K.; Shaik S.; Rout A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate disease prediction from patient monitoring data is essential for enabling timely clinical intervention. However, existing approaches often exhibit limited generalization and reduced robustness to noisy or incomplete physiological signals. To address the challenges, this article proposes a novel approach called Quokka swarm defensive optimization algorithm-based Ensemble deep learning (QSDO_Ensemble DL) for disease prediction. At first, physiological signals, like II, III, AVL, AVF, and Arterial Blood Pressure (ABP), are used for anomaly detection, and it is carried out by using a weighted average method. In parallel, the same set of health parameters is used to predict Pulmonary Arterial Pressure (PAP), and it is done through an Adaptive Hybrid Attention Network (AHANet). Subsequently, the outputs from anomaly detection and PAP prediction stages are fed into a disease detection system. Here, disease prediction is done using Ensemble deep learning (DL) classifiers, including ResNeXt, AHANet, and Shuffle Attention Network (SA-Net). In addition, the hyperparameters of the ensemble DL are tuned by QSDO, which combines the Quokka swarm optimization (QSO) and Offensive Defensive Optimization (ODO). Experiments are conducted on the MIMIC-II database, which is used for model training and evaluation. Moreover, the QSDO_Ensemble DL achieved an Accuracy of 96.90%, a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 95.87%, and a False Positive Rate (FPR) of 7.22%. The results indicate that QSDO_Ensemble DL provides robust and reliable disease prediction from physiological monitoring signals.

Article.Title: Distributional burden of the English urology elective waiting list after the 2024 reporting reset
Article.Authors: Drobot R.
Article.Abstract: Headline referral to treatment metrics can conceal where waiting-list mass lies. This study quantified the distributional and operational burden of the English C_101 Urology Service waiting list in the post-reset series, defined as April 2024 onward after consultant-led community service pathways were excluded from RTT submissions. A population-level analysis used all public NHS England Commissioner RTT incomplete-pathway workbooks from April 2024 to February 2026 and February 2026 flow workbooks. Outcomes included list size, 18-week performance, long-wait tails, the integer 92% standard gap, pathway-weeks beyond 18 weeks, flow balance and cross-specialty ranks. Trends used heteroskedasticity-and-autocorrelation-consistent regression. National 2019–2023 trends were shown descriptively but were not combined with the post-reset models. In February 2026, 385,949 urology pathways were incomplete; 246,524 (63.9%) were within 18 weeks and 139,425 (36.1%) were beyond 18 weeks. The integer gap to the 92% standard was 108,550. There were 6,799 pathways beyond 52 weeks, 448 beyond 65 weeks and 91 beyond 78 weeks. From April 2024, total incomplete pathways fell by 7.8%, pathways beyond 52 weeks by 63.9% and the 92nd-percentile wait by 6.4 weeks. Urology ranked seventh of 23 treatment functions by incomplete pathways and by 52-week burden. Its 63.9% within-18-week performance was above the estimated national 62.6%, although both were below the 65% interim benchmark. The long-wait tail contracted substantially, but a large operational standard gap remained. Aggregate C_101 pathways do not identify indication, urgency, cancer status or clinical outcomes; distributional auditing should therefore complement, not replace, patient-level clinical prioritisation.

Article.Title: Statistically grounded evaluation of demographic bias in deep facial representations using FairFace and UTKFace
Article.Authors: Nemavhola A.; Viriri S.; Chibaya C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep facial representation learning has achieved remarkable performance in computer vision applications; however, high overall accuracy does not necessarily ensure equitable performance across demographic groups. This study presents a unified framework for evaluating the quality and demographic fairness of pretrained deep facial representations. ResNet50, MobileNetV3, and the Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT) were evaluated using ImageNet-pretrained weights on the FairFace and UTKFace datasets, representing balanced and unconstrained demographic settings, respectively. Feature embeddings were assessed using one-nearest neighbour (1-NN) retrieval to measure the intrinsic discriminative capability of the representation space and Logistic Probe classification to evaluate the linear separability of demographic information. Fairness was examined through overall accuracy, subgroup performance, race–gender intersectional analysis, fairness gap, coefficient of variation, and statistical significance testing. Logistic Probe classification consistently outperformed 1-NN retrieval across both datasets, indicating that pretrained facial representations encode demographic information that can be effectively separated using simple linear classifiers. ResNet50 achieved the highest overall classification performance, whereas MobileNetV3 demonstrated more consistent subgroup performance in several evaluation settings. Intersectional analysis revealed persistent demographic disparities despite improvements in overall accuracy, underscoring the importance of fairness evaluation beyond aggregate metrics. The proposed framework provides a reproducible methodology for jointly assessing representation quality, demographic fairness, and statistical significance in deep facial representation learning.

Article.Title: Inflammation-associated hsa_circ_0054391 regulates epithelial-mesenchymal transition and vasculogenic mimicry in colorectal cancer via the miR-1252-3p/VEGFA/ZEB1 axis
Article.Authors: Xiong C.; He Z.; Liu X.; Ou Z.; Gui K.; Lin C.; Wang H.; Tang M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To define the functional role of hsa_circ_0054391 (circ54391) in CRC progression and to evaluate its potential as a serum biomarker. Circ54391 was identified from databases and its expression was validated in CRC tissues, cell lines, and serum from healthy controls ( n = 34), colorectal polyp patients ( n = 30), and CRC patients ( n = 69). Diagnostic performance and clinicopathological correlations were analyzed. Functional assays were performed in vitro (proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, VM) and in vivo (xenograft models). Mechanistic studies focused on the circ54391/miR-1252-3p/VEGFA/ZEB1 axis. Interactions and downstream effects were assessed using FISH, qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and dual-luciferase assays. Circ54391 was highly upregulated in CRC and correlated with advanced invasion, lymph node/distant metastasis, and TNF-α levels. Serum circ54391 yielded an AUC of 0.7257 (95% CI, 0.6365–0.8150); when combined with CEA, the AUC increased to 0.8224 (95% CI, 0.7515–0.8933). Silencing circ54391 suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and VM in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circ54391 acted as a sponge for miR-1252-3p, leading to upregulation of VEGFA and ZEB1, thereby driving EMT and VM. Circ54391 promotes CRC progression via the miR-1252-3p/VEGFA/ZEB1 axis and supports circ54391 as a serum-accessible biomarker candidate for CRC.

Article.Title: A consistency-oriented adaptive power allocation method for battery energy storage systems under seasonal wind–photovoltaic scenarios
Article.Authors: Xiao X.; Liu Y.; Wang R.; Liao Y.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the continuous increase in wind and photovoltaic penetration, battery energy storage systems (BESSs) have become an important supporting resource for power balancing and flexible regulation in renewable energy stations. However, during the long-term operation of multi-cluster parallel battery systems, state-of-charge (SOC) inconsistency continuously accumulates owing to inter-cluster capacity differences, deviations in initial states, and operational nonuniformity. This accumulation further leads to unbalanced cluster responses, premature triggering of boundary constraints, and a reduction in the available regulation capability of the system. To address these issues, this study proposes a consistency-oriented adaptive optimal power allocation (COAO) method for seasonal wind–photovoltaic operating scenarios. First, daily operating feature vectors are constructed from annual wind power, photovoltaic, and load data, and fuzzy C-means clustering is employed to extract four typical operating scenarios corresponding to spring, summer, autumn, and winter, thereby establishing a unified cross-season evaluation framework. Second, for multi-cluster electrochemical energy storage systems, a consistency-oriented mathematical model is developed that incorporates cluster-level SOC dynamics, SOC safety boundaries, power constraints, ramp-rate constraints, and a directional exit mechanism. Furthermore, a cluster-level priority scoring function is constructed by comprehensively considering direction-related SOC margins and capacity differences, and adaptive weight adjustment together with feasible-region optimization correction is introduced based on consistency indicators. In this way, both power execution capability and consistency maintenance capability can be achieved under engineering constraints. Finally, under the four seasonal representative scenarios, the proposed method is systematically compared with three benchmark allocation strategies, namely state-of-charge proportional allocation (SCPA), maximum residual power-based ranked water-filling (MRWF), and model-predictive-control-based SOC balancing (MPC-SOC), over 30 paired simulations. The results show that COAO consistently achieves the lowest mean SOC range and SOC standard deviation and also provides the best overall power-tracking performance across all four seasonal scenarios. This study can provide methodological support for the refined operational control of multi-cluster energy storage systems in renewable energy stations.

Article.Title: Beauvericin exhibits antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer cells: Integrative analysis suggests potential modulation of the KEAP1-NRF2-HMOX1 axis and survival signaling pathways
Article.Authors: Yu X.; Liu X.; Ouyang J.; Li L.; Liu R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the anticancer effects of Beauvericin (BEA) and elucidate its potential mechanisms in pancreatic cancer cells, a malignancy characterized by marked heterogeneity and frequent chemoresistance. The effects of BEA on the proliferation, migration and apoptosis of Mia PaCa-2 cells were evaluated via CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell and flow cytometry assays. Systems biology was used to prioritize candidate targets, and molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate a putative BEA–KEAP1 interaction computationally. Western blotting was used to detect the expression of key signaling pathway proteins. In Mia PaCa‑2 cells, BEA reduced cell viability (IC₅₀ = 1.45 µM), suppressed colony formation at 0.5 µM, decreased migration at 1 µM, and increased apoptosis to 50.06% at 2 µM. Docking suggested the presence of putative interactions between BEA and KEAP1 (estimated docking score/energy of -9.45 kcal/mol) and between BEA and HMOX1 (-7.82 kcal/mol). MD simulations supported the stability of the predicted BEA–KEAP1 complex (RMSD ~ 0.5 nm). BEA treatment was associated with the modulation of KEAP1/NRF2‑related signaling and reduced the phosphorylation of AKT, ERK1/2, and STAT3, which is consistent with the attenuation of key survival signaling. Proteomic profiling revealed enrichment of differentially expressed proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation and ribosome‑related processes following BEA treatment. BEA had dose-dependent effects on Mia PaCa-2 cells and affected multiple signaling nodes. These findings support further investigations of BEA in additional PAAD models, including chemoresistant settings, to evaluate its translational potential.

Article.Title: 3-O-Acetylrubiarbonol B induces apoptosis of colorectal cancer cells by activating JNK/p38 MAPK and ROS generation
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Joo S.; Yoon G.; Park J.; Shim J.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to be a significant health issue, claiming millions of lives each year. The challenge is exacerbated by resistance to anticancer treatments, which reduces therapeutic effectiveness and calls for strategies to combat drug-resistant cancer. In this study, we explored the anticancer effects of 3- O -Acetylrubiarbonol B (ARu-B) in human CRC HCT116 cells, both with and without oxaliplatin (Ox) resistance. ARu-B effectively inhibited the growth of HCT116 cells as well as the Ox-resistant strain HCT116-OxR, as evaluated through MTT and soft-agar assays. IC 50 values were 5.4 µM and 4.0 µM in HCT116 and HCT116-OxR cells, respectively in 48-h incubation. ARu-B induced apoptosis by increasing the phosphorylation of JNK and p38 MAPK, arresting cell cycle at the G2/M phase, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, mitochondrial membrane potential dissipation, and caspase activation. The essential roles of JNK and p38 MAPK phosphorylation were validated by preincubating with SP600125 and SB203580. Additionally, preincubation with N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) highlighted the significant role of ROS in mediating apoptosis. The apoptotic induction via caspase activation was confirmed by the prevention of cytotoxicity following Z-VAD-FMK pretreatment. In summary, ARu-B inhibited the growth of CRC HCT116 cells effectively, regardless of Ox resistance. Future studies are anticipated to develop effective anticancer agents based on ARu-B.

Article.Title: Rock microstructural and mechanical constraints on the 2021-ongoing hydrothermal unrest at La Fossa Caldera (Vulcano Island, Italy)
Article.Authors: Falasconi A.; Buono G.; Pappalardo L.; Di Traglia F.; De Astis G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Volcanic unrest associated with increased hydrothermal activity is often difficult to interpret, yet it may culminate in hazardous steam-driven explosions or slope failures without magma intrusion. At La Fossa Caldera (Vulcano Island, Italy), recently affected by the 2021–ongoing unrest episode, we identify a porous scoriaceous horizon at ~ 615–655 m depth that is consistent with the inferred hydrothermal reservoir and confined by mechanically competent lava units. We combine field observations and borehole stratigraphy with high-resolution X-ray microtomography, petrophysical analyses, and in-situ uniaxial mechanical testing within the micro-CT system to characterise the pore structure, transport properties, and geomechanical behaviour of representative lithologies. Our results indicate that the porous scoriaceous horizon provides favourable conditions for fluid accumulation, whereas the surrounding low-porosity lava units act as an effective mechanical and hydraulic seal, allowing overpressure to build up to values comparable to the tensile strength of the overlying rocks measured on fresh samples. These conditions may promote fracture propagation and episodic gas release without the need for shallow magma intrusion. Our findings highlight the fundamental control exerted by the physical and mechanical properties of volcanic rocks on fluid storage, pressurisation, and migration. We propose a physically based framework for interpreting hydrothermal unrest during the 2021–ongoing episode by linking subsurface rock properties with fluid overpressure and geophysical observations. This framework provides a transferable approach for integrating geological, laboratory, and monitoring data to improve the interpretation of hydrothermal unrest in active volcanic systems.

Article.Title: Exploring community members’ experiences during COVID-19 social distancing: a qualitative study in Iran
Article.Authors: Asghari E.; Hosseinzadeh M.; Mirghafourvand M.; Rahmani F.
Article.Abstract: Social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic was implemented to slow viral transmission and prevent the healthcare system from being overwhelmed. However, this measure also caused psychological stress, weakened community bonds, and created socioeconomic challenges. Limited qualitative research has examined these effects in Iran’s collectivist context. This study aimed to describe culturally influenced experiences of community members during enforced social distancing, focusing on three novel dimensions: (1) disruption of Taʿarof and mourning rituals as a source of psychological distress; (2) the manifestation of hypervigilance as an erosion of trust in interpersonal encounters and community spaces; and (3) culturally specific pathways of post-traumatic growth through family solidarity and communal commitment. This descriptive qualitative study utilized semi-structured interviews with 19 participants representing diverse socio-demographic backgrounds, conducted between December 2020 and April 2021. Data were analyzed using conventional content analysis until thematic saturation was achieved. The analysis identified five core themes: confronting an existential threat, the fracturing of the social fabric, hypervigilance and eroded trust, the struggle to adapt, and post-traumatic growth with renewed bonds. Participants reported grief, anxiety, economic hardship, and social isolation, findings that align with global evidence. Three culturally specific dimensions emerged: disruption of Iran’s politeness ritual (Taʿarof) and Islamic mourning ceremonies, resulting in incomplete bereavement and a rupture in cultural identity; hypervigilance, manifested as heightened interpersonal caution and diminished trust in community spaces and relationships, particularly pronounced in Iran’s collectivist context; and post-traumatic growth, characterized by strengthened family solidarity, renewed appreciation for communal rituals, and a deeper commitment to collective well-being. These findings demonstrate that social distancing in Iran was a significant cultural disruption, intensifying distress by disrupting essential socio-religious practices. Nevertheless, resilience emerged from strong family and community bonds. These results underscore the need for culturally responsive public health strategies that preserve social and ritual continuity during crises. Policymakers should prioritize initiatives that strengthen community connections and adapt support systems to respect and preserve culturally significant practices, thereby promoting psychological well-being and social cohesion in future emergencies.

Article.Title: Insecticidal activity of Metarhizium anisopliae-mediated nanoparticles and fungal metabolites against the red palm weevil, Rhynchophorus ferrugineus
Article.Authors: Alshammari F.; Aldaghmi A.; Hafez E.; Alghamdi S.; Alqarni L.; Alhathlaul N.; Elmenofy W.; Hammad M.; El-Sayed G.; Galal F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the insecticidal activity of green-synthesized metallic nanoparticles (Ag, CuO, and ZnO) and the ethanolic extract of Metarhizium anisopliae against the red palm weevil ( Rhynchophorus ferrugineus ). Physicochemical characterization confirmed the successful synthesis and stability of the nanoparticles. Among the tested materials, AgNPs exhibited the greatest larvicidal activity (LC₅₀ = 568.0 ppm), outperforming both the fungal extract and the reference insecticide abamectin under the experimental conditions. GC–MS analysis of the M. anisopliae extract identified several bioactive metabolites, including 1,2,4-benzenetriol, oleic acid, and naphthalene derivatives. Enzymatic assays demonstrated that AgNPs markedly inhibited digestive enzymes, particularly amylase and protease, indicating disruption of nutrient metabolism. Gene expression analysis revealed treatment- and time-dependent modulation of inflammatory (IL6 and TNF) and detoxification (CYP450) genes. Molecular docking further suggested that fatty acid derivatives, particularly oleic acid, exhibited favorable binding affinities toward multiple insect protein targets, supporting their potential contribution to the observed insecticidal activity. Overall, these findings provide mechanistic insights into the insecticidal effects of green-synthesized metallic nanoparticles and M. anisopliae metabolites and support their potential as promising candidates for red palm weevil management. However, further field-based studies are required to validate their practical efficacy under natural conditions.

Article.Title: Integrated multi-omics analyses reveal the role of PAXX in colorectal cancer progression and the tumor immune microenvironment
Article.Authors: Cao J.; Wang Z.; Luo X.; Hou S.; Chen X.; Yuan P.; Sun Z.; Zhang S.; Li C.; Jiang T.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract PAXX is a DNA double-strand break repair factor involved in classical non-homologous end joining. Although elevated PAXX expression has been reported in colon cancer, its functional role and downstream mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain incompletely defined. This study investigated the role of PAXX in CRC progression and its association with the tumor immune microenvironment. Public transcriptomic, proteomic, genomic, and single-cell datasets were integrated with clinical sample validation and functional experiments. Stable PAXX knockdown models were used to assess CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth. RNA sequencing, Western blotting, and EGF-mediated rescue experiments were performed to evaluate EMT-related alterations and MAPK/ERK signaling. PAXX was upregulated in CRC tissues and cell lines and was associated with poorer overall survival, although its standalone prognostic discrimination was limited. PAXX knockdown suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth and attenuated EMT-related molecular alterations. RNA-seq and enrichment analyses showed coordinated suppression of MAPK signaling and EMT-related transcriptional programs following PAXX depletion. Consistently, p-MEK1/2 and p-ERK1/2 levels were reduced without substantial changes in total MEK1/2 or ERK1/2. EGF-mediated pathway stimulation restored MEK/ERK phosphorylation and partially reversed the inhibitory effects of PAXX depletion on malignant phenotypes and EMT-related alterations. High PAXX expression was also associated with distinct immune and stromal characteristics, while single-cell and CellChat analyses identified heterogeneous PAXX expression and predicted HGF- and VEGF-related intercellular communication. PAXX is associated with CRC progression and unfavorable prognosis. Functional and rescue experiments support MAPK/ERK signaling as a partial mediator of PAXX-associated malignant phenotypes. Immune and intercellular communication findings remain computationally inferred and require further validation.

Article.Title: Preferences regarding disclosure of cancer diagnosis and prognosis for self and family members: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wattanapisit S.; Ruanpech P.; Wattanapisit A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine intentions to know one’s own cancer diagnosis and prognosis and intentions to allow family members to know the information. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults without a history of cancer diagnosis. Data were collected using a questionnaire capturing participant characteristics, intentions to know cancer diagnosis and prognosis, and intentions to allow loved ones to know cancer diagnosis and prognosis. The proportion reporting each intention was estimated. Factors related to not allow loved ones to know cancer diagnosis and prognosis were examined using univariate and multivariate regression analyses. Of 607, most participants were female (80.2%), with a mean age of 43.1 ± 14.7 years. Intentions to know one’s own cancer-related information were consistently higher than intentions to allow loved ones to know the information: cancer diagnosis (79.9% vs. 70.5%), prognosis regarding cancer stage and chance of cure (80.7% vs. 72.0%), and end-of-life prognosis (77.1% vs. 67.1%). Participants who did not wish to know their own cancer prognosis had significantly higher odds of intending to not allow their loved ones to know cancer diagnosis and prognostic information. Future research should focus on developing and evaluating approaches to assess preferences for cancer-related information disclosure.

Article.Title: Kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio and inflammatory cytokines in people living with HIV from a metabolomic perspective
Article.Authors: Fadhilah F.; Indrati A.; Dewi S.; Santoso P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metabolic dysregulation and infections have a bidirectional relationship; metabolic dysregulation increase susceptibility to infections, while infections exacerbate metabolic dysregulation. Coinfection of HIV and tuberculosis (TB) leads to persistent immune activation, depleting the body’s energy and nutrient reserves and weakening immune defenses. This study aims to evaluate the kynurenine/tryptophan (K/T) ratio as a biomarker of metabolic dysregulation and its correlation with pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-17 in HIV-infected individuals with and without active or latent TB. A total of 72 subjects aged ≥ 18 years, consisting of 24 HIV-infected without TB, 23 with latent TB infection (LTBI), and 25 with active TB, were enrolled. Serum levels of kynurenine and tryptophan were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and IL-6 and IL-17 cytokines were analyzed via flow cytometric bead array (CBA). The mean K/T ratio was significantly elevated in the HIV-active TB group (0.032) compared to HIV without TB (0.015) and HIV-LTBI (0.015) groups ( p = 0.005). No significant differences were observed in cytokine levels among groups; however, IL-17 tended to be lower in the HIV without TB group and higher in the HIV-LTBI group compared to the active TB group. No correlation was found between the K/T ratio and levels of IL-6 or IL-17. The kynurenine/tryptophan ratio effectively differentiates metabolic disturbances in HIV patients with active TB but shows no correlation with T lymphocyte activation markers IL-6 and IL-17. Further studies are necessary to elucidate the mechanistic pathways and clinical relevance for patient management.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of rating curve estimation methods for data-scarce mountainous rivers in the Indian Himalayas
Article.Authors: Saxena N.; Sen S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Direct gauging measurements are commonly used to estimate river discharge through stage-discharge relationships (rating curves). However, accurate rating curves are difficult to develop in high-gradient mountain rivers under data-scarce conditions. This study compares three methods for rating curve estimation across three gauging stations: the traditional power-law method, Heteroscedastic Maximum Likelihood Estimator (HMLE), and Bayesian inference methods. The stations include two located 40 km apart on the main stream and one on a highly dynamic tributary within a single 307 $$\:{\text{k}\text{m}}^{2}$$ catchment. We evaluated predictive performance using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) for both real-space and log-transformed measures of goodness of fit. Results show that model performance is highly sensitive to the assessment metric and cross-sectional stability. The classic power-law technique had the highest prediction accuracy for stable watershed outlets. Performance was mixed at geomorphologically unstable and data-scarce tributary stations, with the HMLE framework outperforming in statistical fits in log-space ( $$\:{\text{R}\text{M}\text{S}\text{E}}_{\text{l}\text{o}\text{g}}\:$$ of 0.311–0.333 vs. Bayesian 0.399–0.406) due to its effective optimization of data-dense low-flow regimes. However, purely statistical approaches such as HMLE produced hydrologically unrealistic, near-flat discharge paths during high-flow extrapolation. In contrast, the Bayesian approach, although slightly weaker in fit in log space, preserved hydraulic consistency during extreme occurrences through the formal integration of prior physical knowledge of channel geometry and roughness. These results show that statistical curve-fitting optimizes interpolation in low-flow regimes, but physically constrained probabilistic techniques are needed to provide trustworthy, hydrologically realistic discharge predictions when extrapolating hydrological information in dynamic mountainous catchments.

Article.Title: Missing data imputation for wearable time series
Article.Authors: Ling Y.; Shahmoon E.; Brandeau M.; Yamin D.
Article.Abstract: Continuous physiological monitoring via wearables enables early disease detection, diagnosis, and treatment. However, accurate estimation of missing data is essential. Wearable-derived physiological signals often have periodic structure in observations, while the missingness mechanism may follow distinct patterns. Most imputation methods ignore these underlying cycles. We introduce a Periodic Multi-scale Imputation (PMSI) framework to impute missing data, modeling multi-scale periodic dependencies for both observations and missingness patterns. The process follows three stages: (1) identify candidate periodicities; (2) transform series into multi-dimensional tensors aligned with selected periodicities; (3) optimize hyperparameters using a two-layer minimization of Akaike information criterion. PMSI first models the missingness mechanism and generates synthetic masks for optimization, and then estimates missing values using periodicities. We validated PMSI using a smartwatch-derived heart rate dataset, consisting of 558 participant-month series in a high-adherence cohort and 1,957 in a low-adherence cohort. Spectral analysis revealed daily and 3.5-day (likely smartwatch charging) periodicities in the missingness mechanism, and daily and weekly periodicities in observations. The optimal PMSI algorithm used hourly resolution and daily periodicity, and outperformed five standard imputation methods: k-nearest neighbors, autoregressive integrated moving average, convolutional neural networks, piecewise linear interpolation, and last observation carried forward. PMSI performed the best: RMSE (7.53 vs. 8.18–10.01) and MAE (6.04 vs. 6.60–8.16) in the high-adherence cohort, and RMSE (8.81 vs. 9.02–15.86) and MAE (6.60 vs. 6.96–12.44) in the low-adherence cohort (all adjusted p < 0.05). PMSI improves imputation accuracy by modeling periodic dependencies and has broad potential applications for health-related time series.

Article.Title: A high resolution urban energy atlas for spatiotemporal energy-demand assessment of 1.69 million buildings
Article.Authors: Nematchoua M.; Wiberg A.; Orosa J.; Attia S.; Donatien N.; MacLeod D.; Asadi S.; Roshan G.; Reiter S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The building sector is central to achieving climate neutrality because of its major contribution to final energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. However, regional energy planning remains constrained by the lack of high-resolution spatial and temporal datasets capable of simultaneously representing residential, tertiary and industrial buildings. This study develops a high-resolution interactive Wallonia Energy Atlas that combines cadastral information, regional energy statistics, building archetypes and standardized temporal load profiles. The proposed methodology combines detailed cadastral information for approximately 1.69 million buildings with regional energy statistics and building archetypes to estimate annual energy indicators using a hybrid top-down/bottom-up approach. These annual estimates are subsequently reconstructed into 8,760-hour profiles using standardized BDEW load profiles for five energy indicators: Heat Consumption (HC), Heat Demand (HD), Electricity Consumption (EC), Cooling Electricity Demand (CED) and Heating Electricity Consumption (HEC). The resulting energy data were spatially aggregated at four administrative levels (regional, provincial, arrondissement and municipal), covering 5 provinces, 20 arrondissements and 262 municipalities, and implemented within an interactive web application developed using Python, Dash and Plotly. The reconstructed hourly profiles show substantial differences in energy magnitude and temporal distribution among building categories. At the aggregate building level, average hourly heat consumption ranges from 3.33 kWh for semi-detached houses to 18.53 kWh for apartment buildings; these absolute values reflect differences in building size and dwelling aggregation and are therefore complemented by area-normalized energy intensities. In the tertiary sector, transportation facilities record the highest electricity demand (40.07 kWh), whereas culture and sport buildings present the largest average heat consumption (18.26 kWh). Industrial facilities display considerably greater modelled energy requirements, with chemical industries reaching average hourly heat and electricity consumptions of 7,275.5 kWh and 2,843.0 kWh, respectively. Validation against seven monitored residential, tertiary and industrial cases showed a mean CV(RMSE) of approximately 27%, although the monitored cases primarily provide empirical evaluation of HC and EC. Load-duration analysis shows distinct reconstructed temporal patterns across sectors, with stronger seasonal variation in residential profiles, schedule-related patterns in tertiary profiles, and relatively persistent loads in industrial profiles; these temporal characteristics are partly inherited from the assigned BDEW archetypes. The Wallonia Energy Atlas therefore provides a regional-scale integration of cadastral data, annual energy estimates, standardized temporal profiles, multi-scale GIS aggregation and interactive visualization, supporting preliminary energy-system planning and regional decarbonisation assessment.

Article.Title: Predicting measles outbreak magnitude via modeled population susceptibility evidence from pre-vaccination data
Article.Authors: Dor E.; Yaari R.; Huppert A.
Article.Abstract: We characterized pre-vaccination measles dynamics using a discrete-time mechanistic model that integrates incidence time series and demographic data to estimate key epidemiological parameters and to quantify the relationship between the reconstructed population susceptibility and the observed epidemic magnitude. Weekly reported measles incidence data from England and Wales and its five largest cities during the pre-vaccination era were analyzed. A discrete-time age-of-infection model incorporating seasonality was fitted for each year. Several parameters were fixed using values from the literature, while others were estimated via maximum likelihood. Reconstructed susceptibility at the start of each year (S 0 ), inferred from surveillance and demographic data, was evaluated as a predictor of subsequent observed outbreak magnitude. The model accurately reproduced the temporal dynamics of measles across all regions. Reconstructed S 0 was strongly associated with observed attack rates in the following year, demonstrating its practical value as a surveillance-based predictor of epidemic size. The discrete-time age-of-infection model enables exploration of the mechanisms underlying observed incidence and epidemic dynamics. It captures the feedback between the susceptible pool and outbreak amplitude and supports one-year-ahead predictions of observed outbreak magnitude based on reconstructed susceptibility.

Article.Title: Bedside infrared thermometry compared with continuous zero-heat-flux thermometry– an experimental and clinical study
Article.Authors: Makkonen O.; Silvasti-Lundell M.; Lindroos A.; Virtanen K.; Mäkinen M.; Pesonen E.
Article.Abstract: This study compared standard infrared thermometers used in emergency rooms (ER) and wards to a Zero-Heat-Flux (ZHF) thermometry device and evaluated its feasibility for continuous bedside temperature monitoring. In 60 volunteers, five alternative ZHF sensor placements were assessed against the conventional forehead position (“ZHF-forehead”). Based on these results, continuous ZHF-forehead monitoring was evaluated in 24 hip-fracture patients in an ER (21 patients) and ward (11 patients). Concurrent ZHF and infrared forehead (“IR-forehead”) and ear canal measurements (“IR-ear”) were compared using Bland–Altman analysis (bias, limits of agreement). Among alternative placements, the neck (“ZHF-neck”) showed the closest agreement with ZHF-forehead (0.2, -0.5–0.8 °C). Compared to ZHF-forehead, ZHF-neck did not show improved agreement with either IR-forehead (ZHF-forehead: 0.0, -0.5–0.5 °C vs. ZHF-neck: -0.3, -1.1–0.5 °C) or IR-ear measurements (ZHF-forehead: 0.2, -0.3–0.8 °C vs. ZHF-neck: -0.1, -0.8–0.7 °C). All ER patients showed stable ZHF-forehead temperature profiles, whereas 4 of 11 ward patients had unreliable measurements. Bedside ZHF-forehead measurements in the ER and ward showed moderate agreement with infrared measurements (0.2; -0.4–0.7 °C). In conclusion, ZHF-forehead thermometry showed moderate agreement with point-of-care infrared methods in volunteers and patients, and provided stable continuous bedside temperature measurements in the ER and ward.

Article.Title: Phase equilibrium simulation and optimal experimentation for the hydrothermal alkali treatment of Rb-rich microcline
Article.Authors: Dong C.; Ma H.; Liu C.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: The hydrothermal alkaline decomposition of Rb-rich microcline was systematically investigated using KOH and Ca(OH) 2 as combined additives. By integrating quantitative analyses of liquid-phase composition with crystallographic evolution of solid products, this study addresses three central aspects of the KAlSi 3 O 8 –KOH–Ca(OH) 2 –H 2 O system: reaction kinetics, process optimization, and thermodynamic partitioning behavior of major and trace elements. Under optimized conditions, potassium and rubidium extraction efficiencies reached 93.0% and 90.56%, respectively. Tobermorite (Ca 5 Si 6 O 16 (OH) 2 ·4H 2 O) was identified as the dominant solid-phase product. These results demonstrate that the coupled KOH–Ca(OH) 2 hydrothermal system enables efficient potassium recovery while simultaneously enriching rubidium in the alkaline solution, providing a potential pathway for the integrated utilization of feldspar resources.

Article.Title: APEO-free black ceramic inkjet ink formulations based on Ni-substituted CoFeCrO4 spinel pigments
Article.Authors: Faraji S.; Atapour M.; Emadi R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study reports the development of high-performance black digital ceramic inks based on a Ni 0.5 Co 0.5 FeCrO 4 spinel pigment. A series of Ni x Co 1- x FeCrO 4 ( x = 0–1) pigments was synthesized via solid-state reaction. Calcination temperature (900–1100 °C) and post-calcination milling duration were optimized to obtain phase-pure spinel with primary particle sizes predominantly below 400 nm, as confirmed by XRD, FTIR, and SEM analyses. Optical properties and color performance were evaluated using UV-Vis reflectance spectroscopy and CIE colorimetry. Among the investigated compositions, Ni 0.5 Co 0.5 FeCrO 4 pigments exhibited the deepest blackness ( L* = 29.5 after firing on glaze) and were selected for ink formulation. An APEO-free non-ionic polymeric dispersant (Dispex ® Ultra FA 4488, BASF) was employed as the sole dispersing agent. Within the investigated concentration range (1.0–3.0 wt%), the formulation containing 3.0 wt% dispersant showed the best overall performance, with a viscosity of 13.5 mPa s, a contact angle of 28.6° on ceramic glaze, and a zeta potential of -40.9 mV. After application onto glazed tiles and firing at 1200 °C, the selected ink formulation developed a deep, uniform black color. These results demonstrate that the combination of Ni 0.5 Co 0.5 FeCrO 4 pigment and Dispex ® Ultra FA 4488 enables the production of stable, environmentally compatible black ceramic inks candidates for industrial consideration.

Article.Title: Impact of adjuvant chemotherapy on renal impairment patients following radical nephroureterectomy in upper tract urothelial carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective study
Article.Authors: Ikarashi D.; Tamura D.; Abe M.; Fujita N.; Kobayashi M.; Shiga M.; Kandori S.; Fukuhara H.; Sato T.; Myoen S.; Onagi A.; Ogawa S.; Inoue T.; Morozumi K.; Narita S.; Kaiho Y.; Miyazaki J.; Kojima Y.; Adachi H.; Ito A.; Tsuchiya N.; Hatakeyama S.; Obara W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate the impact of adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy (AC) on oncological outcomes in high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) patients with postoperative renal impairment following radical nephroureterectomy (RNU). Among 1050 patients who underwent RNU at 10 affiliated hospitals, we retrospectively evaluated 136 UTUC patients with ≥pT3 and/or node-positive UTUC and postoperative eGFR 30–59 mL/min/1.73 m². Patients were divided into an AC group ( n = 52), who received gemcitabine plus cisplatin (GC) or carboplatin (GCa), and a non-AC group ( n = 84). Oncological outcomes, including disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS), were evaluated using propensity score matching (PSM). In the AC group, DFS and OS were also compared between GC ( n = 33) and GCa ( n = 19). The median follow-up was 48.6 months. Before PSM, three-year DFS was 61.5% versus 27.2% in the AC and non-AC groups, respectively ( p < 0.0001), whereas three-year OS was 76.8% versus 68.6% ( p = 0.16). After PSM, AC remained associated with longer DFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.18–0.70; p = 0.0019), while no statistically significant difference in OS was observed (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.34–2.01; p = 0.676). Within the AC group, cisplatin dosing in the GC regimen was determined according to postoperative renal function. No statistically significant differences in DFS or OS were observed between patients treated with GC and GCa. Platinum-based AC was associated with improved DFS in selected high-risk UTUC patients despite postoperative renal impairment, supporting consideration of GC or GCa according to renal function.

Article.Title: Phi027 prophage shapes Clostridioides difficile virulence through the SinR/SinR’ axis and the flagellar switch network
Article.Authors: Frankowska N.; Iwanicki A.; Nowicki D.; Bury K.; Szarek K.; Lalowski P.; Wultańska D.; Kabała M.; Pituch H.; Negri A.; Obuchowski M.; Hinc K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clostridioides difficile is a major nosocomial pathogen whose virulence depends on toxin production and can be shaped by prophage carriage. Here, we dissect the molecular basis of phi027-dependent phenotypic differences between the clinical RT176 strain 500/12 and its prophage-free derivative CKH08. Comparative transcriptomic analysis showed that loss of phi027 is associated with reduced expression of the sinR / sinR ′ operon, broad downregulation of flagellar biosynthesis genes, and a shift of the flagellar switch towards the OFF orientation. In total, 166 genes were differentially expressed (|log2FC| ≥ 1, adjusted p < 0.05), including 114 chromosomal host genes. These transcriptional changes align with previously observed reductions in adhesion, sporulation efficiency, and toxin-associated phenotypes in CKH08. To determine whether phi027-dependent differences extend to a whole-organism context, we compared the virulence of strains 500/12 and CKH08 in the Galleria mellonella infection model. Larvae infected with the phi027-lysogenic strain 500/12 showed significantly reduced survival ( p < 0.001, log-rank test) and enhanced melanization relative to those infected with CKH08. Collectively, our findings indicate that phi027 carriage is associated with extensive rewiring of virulence-related regulatory pathways and implicate the SinR/SinR′-SigD-flagellar switch network as a key mediator of phi027-dependent phenotypic effects. These results support prophage-mediated regulation as an important contributor to the pathogenic potential of epidemic C. difficile lineages.

Article.Title: Deformation characteristics and outburst mechanism of coal mass ahead of working faces under dynamic disturbance induced by roof fracturing
Article.Authors: Xuan D.; Zhang J.; Huang G.; Zhang Z.; Xu D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For working faces in soft coal seams closely (especially directly) overlain by hard rock strata, intense dynamic disturbances induced by roof fracturing not only increase the susceptibility of coal and gas outbursts, but also lower the critical gas threshold for disaster initiation. However‌, existing studies on the outburst mechanisms of such working faces remain insufficient, resulting in low pertinence‌ and poor practical effectiveness of prevention measures. In view of this, systematic study was carried out through numerical simulation and theoretical analysis, with a typical working face as the engineering background. Discrete element software (PFC) was adopted to conduct numerical simulations on the critical process of coal mass deformation and failure under the dynamic disturbance induced by roof fracturing. On this basis, the evolutionary process and initiation conditions of outbursts were analyzed, thereby elucidating the outburst mechanism. The results show that under dynamic disturbance induced by roof fracturing, the coal mass with an approximately triangular cross-section in the upper zone near the working face rib undergoes preferential failure accompanied by more intense damage. Combined with relevant existing research, it can be inferred that dynamic disturbance increases the gas desorption rate and initial expansion energy of coal mass, aggravates the outburst susceptibility and reduces the critical gas threshold for disaster initiation, and this effect is most pronounced in the upper area of the working face. On this basis, engineering implications for the prevention and control of such outbursts are drawn. Key emphasis should be placed on the upper coal zone, which serves as the critical outburst-prone area of the working face. Meanwhile, dynamic stress induced by roof fracturing should be mitigated while implementing gas drainage and static stress relief. Accordingly, a targeted outburst prevention scheme using near-roof boreholes is proposed, and field industrial tests confirm its feasibility and effectiveness. This study provides a theoretical basis and engineering reference for the mechanism understanding and disaster prevention of outbursts at working faces under dynamic disturbance induced by roof fracturing.

Article.Title: Enhancing bending load prediction of CaCO₃-filled polypropylene composites via data augmentation and ensemble machine learning
Article.Authors: Pan S.; Zhan K.; Luo S.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predicting the mechanical properties of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)-filled polypropylene (PP) composites is crucial for their industrial applications. However, conventional experiments are costly and time-consuming, resulting in limited data and challenges for accurate modeling under small-sample conditions. This study proposes a machine-learning–based framework to accurately predict the bending performance of CaCO₃-filled PP composites using limited experimental data. An integrated analytical methodology, combining orthogonal experimental design, cubic spline interpolation, and machine learning techniques, is developed to achieve this objective. An orthogonal experimental design is first conducted to obtain an initial dataset of 32 samples. Subsequently, cubic spline interpolation is applied to expand the dataset to 63, 125, and 249 samples. Three machine learning models—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)—are constructed and optimized using grid search and five-fold cross-validation. The results demonstrate that data augmentation significantly improves the predictive performance of the models. Among them, the optimized XGBoost model trained on the 249-sample dataset achieves the best performance, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.8061 and the lowest mean squared error (MSE). Furthermore, correlation analysis reveals that the particle size distribution is the most influential factor affecting the bending load of the composites. Overall, this study presents an integrated framework based on cubic spline interpolation and ensemble machine learning methods, providing a viable approach for estimating the mechanical properties of polymer composites under small-sample cases.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a noninvasive liver fibrosis screening model incorporating GP73 in a health examination population
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Qiu R.; He W.; Han Y.; Xing Z.; Zhao Q.; Sun J.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the association between serum Golgi protein 73 (GP73) and liver fibrosis and developed a noninvasive screening model for a health-examination population. This cross-sectional study included 758 participants without previously diagnosed liver disease. Liver fibrosis was defined as liver stiffness measurement ≥ 7.3 kPa. Participants were randomly divided into training and testing cohorts at a ratio of 7:3. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram. Random forest (RF) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were developed for comparison. Discrimination, calibration, threshold-based performance, and clinical utility were evaluated, with FIB-4 and APRI serving as conventional comparators. Age, AST, GP73, and BMI were independent predictors. The logistic regression model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.768 and 0.788 in the training and testing cohorts, respectively. Testing-cohort AUCs were 0.789 for RF and 0.773 for XGBoost, with no significant pairwise differences after Holm adjustment. The models demonstrated acceptable calibration and positive net clinical benefit. GP73 was higher in participants with liver fibrosis but correlated only weakly with other clinical indicators. A model incorporating age, AST, GP73, and BMI showed acceptable performance for liver fibrosis screening. GP73 may provide complementary value when combined with routinely available clinical indicators.

Article.Title: Effect of Artemisia Annua on oxidative stress and antioxidant gene expression in Nile tilapia after chlorpyrifos toxicity
Article.Authors: Ashry A.; Abdelhiee E.; Saad A.; Elkamshishi M.; Abdo S.; Albadrani G.; Sayed A.; Abdel-Daim M.; Fadl S.; El-Gammal G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, the toxic effects of chlorpyrifos (CPF) on fish antioxidant enzyme activity in serum and transcriptomic levels of oxidative stress-related genes in liver tissue and histopathology of the liver tissue of Nile tilapia were examined. Additionally, the effects of Artemisia Annua (A. annua) , either alone or in combination with the CPF-contaminated water, were investigated. To accomplish this goal, 120 fish were randomly assigned to four distinct experimental groups. In the control group (Cont group), fish were fed a formulated diet and reared in normal water without toxicity. In the chlorpyrifos group (Chlo group), fish were fed a formulated diet and reared in water containing chlorpyrifos at a concentration of 15 µg L⁻¹. Artemisia Annua group (Art group), fish were fed a formulated diet enriched with A. annua at 5 g kg⁻¹ and reared in normal water without toxicity. Artemisia Annua+ chlorpyrifos group (Art+Chlo group): Fish were fed a formulated diet enriched with A. annua and reared in water containing chlorpyrifos. The experiment was done over 30 days. The results of the present investigation indicated that exposure to CPF-contaminated water significantly increased malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and decreased catalase (CAT) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity as compared with the control group. Furthermore, CPF exposure led to upregulation of genes associated with oxidative damage, including heat shock protein 70 ( Hsp70 ) and apoptosis-related cysteine peptidase caspase-3 ( Caspase-3) . Moreover, CPF disrupted antioxidant gene expression by upregulating the Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1( Keap1 ) and downregulating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ), CAT , and glutathione peroxidase ( GPx ). Liver histopathological examination of the chlorpyrifos-intoxicated group showing marked necrotic changes within the pancreatic tissue associated with leukocytic cell infiltration and marked vacuolation of the hepatocytes. However, A. annua supplementation mitigated the deleterious effects of CPF through increased activity of serum antioxidant enzymes and decreased levels of lipid peroxidation. Additionally, A. annua supplementation downregulated the genes associated with oxidative damage, including Hsp70 and Caspase-3 . Also, it improved antioxidant gene expression by downregulating Keap1 and upregulating Nrf2 , CAT , and GPx . Moreover, the hepatopancreas of the A. annua+ chlorpyrifos group shows normal hepatocytes and decreased necrotic changes within the pancreatic acini with infiltration of hemosiderin pigment.

Article.Title: The marine drug plitidepsin alleviates osteoporosis in estrogen-deficient mice by suppressing ROS-mediated NRF2/HO-1 signaling and osteoclast formation
Article.Authors: Liao J.; Liao L.; Li Q.; Xu Y.; Su P.; Liu X.; Zhao J.; Cheng J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Marine-derived compounds represent an important source of innovative therapeutics owing to their structural diversity and broad bioactivity; however, their potential in osteoporosis therapy remains insufficiently explored. This study investigated the effects of plitidepsin (Pli), a marine-origin cyclic peptide, on osteoclast differentiation and bone loss associated with estrogen deficiency. Osteoclastogenesis was induced in mouse bone marrow–derived macrophages using receptor activator of nuclear factor-κ B ligand (RANKL) and macrophage-stimulating factor (M-CSF). The impact of Pli on osteoclast formation, resorptive function, and intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) was evaluated. Osteoclast-related gene expression was quantified by qPCR, while key signaling pathways involved in oxidative stress and differentiation were examined by Western blotting. An ovariectomized (OVX) mouse model was employed to assess the in vivo effects of Pli on bone mass and microarchitecture. Pli suppressed osteoclast formation and function in vitro, as evidenced by reduced multinucleated cell formation, disrupted actin ring assembly, decreased bone resorption, and downregulated osteoclast-specific genes. In OVX mice, Pli alleviated trabecular bone loss and preserved bone microstructural integrity. Mechanistically, Pli attenuated ROS accumulation and enhanced antioxidant defense through activation of the NRF2/HO-1 pathway. Plitidepsin effectively mitigates estrogen deficiency–induced bone loss by inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and activity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for osteoporosis.

Article.Title: Evaluation of crystal violet adsorption onto phosphorylated microcrystalline cellulose and phosphorylated date seeds powder: isotherms, kinetics, mechanisms, and thermodynamics
Article.Authors: Taha G.; Mansor E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The discharge of synthetic dyes into aquatic environments remains a major environmental challenge, necessitating the development of sustainable and efficient adsorbents for wastewater treatment. This study presents a novel comparative analysis of Phosphorylated Microcrystalline Cellulose (PMCC) and Phosphorylated Date Seeds Powder (PDSP) as adsorbents for CV removal from aqueous solutions. Through isotherm modeling (Langmuir, Freundlich, Hill, Sips), kinetic studies (Pseudo-First-Order, Pseudo-Second-Order, Elovich), and thermodynamic profiling (30–80 °C), the adsorption performance, mechanisms, and feasibility of both materials were systematically evaluated. Characterization using FTIR, SEM, XRD, and BET analyses confirms successful phosphorylation and the development of additional surface functionalities and porosity. The results showed that both adsorbents exhibited high affinity towards CV, with maximum adsorption capacities of 104.4 mg/g and 106.5 mg/g for PDSP and PMCC, respectively. The adsorption process was spontaneous and exothermic, while the adsorption data were best described by the Hill isotherm and Pseudo-Second-Order kinetic model, indicating surface heterogeneity and the involvement of surface interactions during dye adsorption. Optimal CV uptake occurred at pH 8, with PDSP demonstrating faster adsorption kinetics. The enhanced adsorption performance was attributed to the presence of phosphate and hydroxyl groups, which promoted electrostatic attraction and hydrogen bonding with CV molecules. Although both adsorbents demonstrated excellent adsorption performance, PMCC and PDSP exhibited high capacity under near-neutral pH and ambient conditions. In addition, PDSP offers an additional sustainability advantage as an abundant agricultural by-product. These findings highlight the potential of phosphorylated cellulosic materials as low-cost and environmentally friendly adsorbents for dye-contaminated wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Clinical characteristics associated with advanced therapy optimization in inflammatory bowel disease in the Brazilian GEDIIB national registry
Article.Authors: Andrade A.; Fróes R.; Sassaki L.; Faria M.; Parente J.; Bezerra G.; Pertence P.; Baima J.; Herrerias G.; Almeida N.; Fortes F.; Surlo V.; Santos C.; Skaff G.; Zabot G.; Zaltman C.; Souza H.; Demetrio W.; Demetrio M.; Fontes J.; Serrão L.; Salgado V.; Araújo S.; Penna F.; Parra R.
Article.Abstract: Although biologic therapy has transformed inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management, a subset of patients still requires treatment optimization to achieve therapeutic goals. This study aimed to identify clinical and disease-related characteristics associated with advanced therapy optimization, including biologic and small-molecule therapies, in Brazilian patients with Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC). This was a retrospective observational analysis of data from the National Patient Registry (NPR) of the Brazilian Organization for Crohn’s Disease and Colitis (GEDIIB). Data were retrospectively extracted from the registry for the period from June 2023 to June 2024 and included historical information on patients’ advanced treatments and treatment optimization. A total of 4,382 registry records were identified, including 2,253 patients with CD and 1,957 with UC; 41 records had unclassified IBD and 131 contained incomplete data and were excluded from the analyses. Advanced therapy use was higher in CD than in UC (77.5% vs. 31.6%), and treatment optimization was more frequent in CD than in UC (33.3% vs. 26.2%; p = 0.003). In multivariable analyses, patients with CD classified as A1 (≤ 16 years) and A2 (17–40 years) had a higher prevalence of optimization than those classified as A3 (> 40 years) (adjusted PR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07–2.36 and adjusted PR 1.36, 95% CI 1.07–1.74, respectively). Perianal disease and abdominal surgery involving an ileal pouch were also independently associated with optimization (adjusted PR 1.31, 95% CI 1.08–1.59 and adjusted PR 2.03, 95% CI 1.56–2.63, respectively). In UC, previous surgery, chronic liver disease, and herpes zoster infection were statistically associated with higher prevalence of treatment optimization in the multivariable model (adjusted PR 1.62, 95% CI 1.02–2.58; adjusted PR 3.18, 95% CI 2.33–4.33; and adjusted PR 3.58, 95% CI 2.51–5.10, respectively). These findings identify clinical characteristics associated with advanced treatment optimization in CD and UC and may support individualized therapeutic decision-making.

Article.Title: Integrated sustainability and risk assessment of spectrophotometric methods for determining a veterinary drug combination
Article.Authors: Hagag M.; Nadim A.; Kamal M.; Abbas S.; Fahmy N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Effective, sustainable, and white spectrophotometric methods were developed for the analytical assessment of both rafoxanide (RAF) and Levamisole HCl (LEV). Both components were resolved by constant multiplication coupled with spectrum subtraction (CM-SS), ratio subtraction coupled with spectrum subtraction (RS-SS), LEV was additionally determined by derivative ratio (DD 1 ), or progressively by absorbance subtraction (AS), amplitude modulation (AM), and concentration value (CNV) methods based on isosbestic point and a normalized divisor. For RAF and LEV, the linearity range was set to be either 3.0–40.0 µg/mL or 1.0–15.0 µg/mL and 1.0–13.0 µg/mL, respectively. All proposed methods were validated in accordance with ICH guidelines. No significant differences were found compared to the reported methods. The developed spectrophotometric procedures adhered to the principles of green analytical chemistry (GAC) and were evaluated using the Green Analytical Procedure Index (GAPI) and Analytical Greenness Metric (AGREE). The blueness assessment was conducted using the Blue Applicability Grade Index (BAGI). Whiteness was additionally assessed using the RGB 12 tool. Furthermore, a recent approach to risk assessment was conducted using the Cumulative Validation Score (CVS) to evaluate the methodological risk of the methods. The proposed approaches provide practical and sustainable options for routine QC.

Article.Title: UPF4ROS2 for integrating planner independent task planning into ROS 2
Article.Authors: González-Fernández I.; González-Santamarta M.; Martín F.; Roveri M.; Matellán-Olivera V.; Rodríguez-Lera F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The lack of standardized interfaces remains one of the main barriers to the adoption of automated planning in robotic systems. To address this challenge, the AIPlan4EU project, part of the European AI4EU initiative, developed the Unified Planning Framework (UPF), a planner-independent ecosystem designed to facilitate access to automated planning technologies through a common API. This work presents UPF4ROS2, an open-source package that integrates the Unified Planning Framework (UPF) into ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2), enabling interaction between planning and execution modules. UPF4ROS2 was integrated into PlanSys2 and MERLIN2 and evaluated through controlled replanning experiments and application-oriented robotic scenarios. A comparison against PlanSys2 baseline over 20 dynamic missions showed equivalent mission-level behaviour and equal plan lengths under the selected unit-action-count metric, with sub-second planning-service latencies in the controlled replanning experiment and quantified additional overhead in a more demanding temporal-numeric benchmark. The results indicate that planner-independent integration can be achieved without compromising autonomous task execution under the evaluated conditions.

Article.Title: A multi-algorithm generative framework for urban design: integrating road networks, green spaces and building forms
Article.Authors: Sun H.; Zheng Y.; Yang J.; Wang Q.; Shi Y.; Wang Y.; Chen X.; Zhou Z.; Zhang C.; Sheng H.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: The challenges in urban design are becoming increasingly complex, underscoring the value of intelligent algorithms in enhancing efficiency and scientific rigour through rapid prototyping. However, existing approaches often treat such algorithms as isolated tools and rarely integrate them into end-to-end design workflows. This paper presents a comprehensive, multi-algorithm urban design framework that supports the entire generative process. By decomposing the urban design scheme into its essential spatial elements, the framework follows a systematic generation sequence—first establishing the road network as the skeleton, then the green space layout, and finally the building form—to ensure the spatial rationality and coherence of the final proposal. These algorithms are further encapsulated into a visual platform, enabling the framework to adapt to different design phases and different sites. The total end-to-end generation time for a 10 km 2 urban design scheme was 3 min and 48.23 s. Experiments conducted across 20 sites of varying scales and contexts demonstrated the generalisability of the framework. This study highlights the potential of AI-aided workflows to advance urban design practice and offers a baseline model to integrate broader sustainable development goals in the future.

Article.Title: Sensorimotor coupling underlies individual differences in speech synchronization
Article.Authors: Magallanes-Aranda C.; Assaneo M.
Article.Abstract: Behavioral auditory–motor interaction in speech reveals a striking individual difference: while some individuals readily synchronize their produced syllabic rhythm with the perceived one (high synchronizers), others show impaired synchronization (low synchronizers). The mechanisms underlying this distinction remain debated. One account attributes it to differences in the strength of sensorimotor coupling, whereas an alternative proposes differences in the relative contributions of feedback and feedforward control. Here, using an online protocol, we evaluated participants with an adapted version of the Battery for the Assessment of Auditory Sensorimotor and Timing Abilities (BAASTA) and found that high synchronizers exhibit both stronger synchronization during paced tapping tasks and greater rhythmic stability during unpaced tapping tasks. Crucially, we adapted a biophysical model in which motor behavior is represented as an oscillator coupled to sensory input, and simulated individuals as differing in coupling strength. The simulations closely match the empirical observations, demonstrating that stronger sensorimotor coupling is sufficient to reproduce the observed differences in speech synchronization.

Article.Title: Perceived indoor environmental quality and facility satisfaction across four university housing facilities in Taiz, Yemen
Article.Authors: Al-Alali G.; Gamil Y.; Al-Azazi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract University housing in service-constrained settings requires evidence that distinguishes occupant perceptions from measured building performance. We conducted a cross-sectional post-occupancy evaluation of four institutional housing facilities in Taiz, Yemen, using 253 complete resident questionnaires and a separate specialist appraisal of 31 participants.
