Here, we present a spectrally resolved study of this effect around the K-shell absorption edge in diamond. Our results exhibit pronounced signatures of polaritonic hybridization, which we visualize by introducing a polariton spectral map and analyze by help of theoretical modelling. We find that the hybridization at this absorption edge results in substantially higher coupling strength than previously reported for a non-resonant case and reaches well into the strong-coupling regime. In addition, we demonstrate how our measurements of polaritonic XPDC allow us to extract the refractive index for bulk diamond at high spectral resolution around the carbon K-edge.

Article.Title: Preconcentration and simultaneous determination of five anticancer drugs in biological and wastewater samples using Vortex-assisted magnetic dispersive micro-solid phase extraction coupled with HPLC
Article.Authors: Morvati E.; Lotfi S.; Alikarami M.
Article.Abstract: The simultaneous measurement of anticancer drugs in biological matrices using a rapid, sensitive, and precise analytical approach remains a challenge for improving therapeutic monitoring and pharmacokinetic evaluation. In the current work, a novel and reliable method has been developed for the simultaneous determination of five anticancer drugs (silibinin, docetaxel, taxifolin, cisplatin, and paclitaxel) in biological and wastewater samples. This method employed the vortex-assisted dispersive micro-solid phase extraction (V-d-µ-SPE) with magnetic nanocomposite (MNC) adsorbent followed by HPLC with UV detection. To investigate the structural properties of the nanocomposite, several analytical methods were utilized, such as Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), and Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX). The influence of effective factors in the V-d-µ-SPE method was investigated comprehensively through the design of the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) of the Box–Behnken design (BBD) based response method and the utility function. To optimize the extraction efficiency, the following parameters were optimized: pH of the sample, adsorbent amount, adsorption time, desorption time, eluent volume, and desorption solvent. Under the optimum conditions (pH = 4.5, adsorbent amount = 25 mg, adsorption time = 4 min, desorption time = 2 min, desorption solvent = methanol, and eluent volume = 31 µL), the linear ranges (LR) were obtained in the range of 0.1–850 µg L − 1 with coefficients of determination (R²) greater than 0.9936. The limits of detection (LODs) and limits of quantification (LOQs) ranged from 0.045 to 0.21 µg L − 1 and 0.15–0.69 µg L − 1 , respectively. The relative standard deviations ( n = 5) were in the range of 2.6–5.1%. Ultimately, the method’s applicability was assessed through the extraction and determination of analytes in human serum, urine, and wastewater, yielding satisfactory results.

Article.Title: Comparison of new and recurring post-acute infection syndrome – results from a German population-based cohort
Article.Authors: Frost J.; Peter F.; Glaser N.; Pfrommer L.; Fasshauer J.; Opel N.; Gekle M.; Behrens T.; Tüscher O.; Mikolajczyk R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract New respiratory infections after or while experiencing post-acute infectious syndromes (PAIS) can lead to resurgence of symptoms. Data comparing symptoms, related impairment, and duration of first and recurring PAIS episodes are lacking. This cross-sectional study was conducted in September/October 2025 within a large population-based digital cohort in Germany (DigiHero, registered under DRKS00025600). We included data from 2,801 participants retrospectively reporting a respiratory infection between September 2024 and August 2025 with subsequent long-lasting symptoms ≥ 12 weeks after infection. We compared self-reported first and recurring PAIS episodes. Of detected PAIS cases, 57% ( n = 1,609) were the first episode and 43% ( n = 1,192) already experienced a PAIS episode in the past. While symptom patterns were broadly similar, those reporting recurring PAIS without full recovery from a previous episode ( n = 308) displayed a higher number and longer duration of long-lasting symptoms and a higher level of impairment due to their symptoms compared to those with first PAIS episodes or recurring cases that were fully recovered at the time of the new infection ( n = 303). Among participants with recurring PAIS who compared their most recent with their first episode, 43% reported similar impairment, while 32% reported greater and 26% lower impairment. While after the COVID-19 pandemic PAIS is still occurring, a substantial proportion of all PAIS cases in 2024/25 in the DigiHero cohort resulted from those with recurring PAIS. Symptom profiles were in general similar for first and recurring PAIS episodes. However, recurring cases exhibited greater impairment and longer symptom duration, when they did not fully recover from a preceding PAIS episode before the new infection.
Article.PubMedTypes: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
Article.MeSH: Respiratory Tract Infections; COVID-19
Article.Keywords: Post-acute infection syndrome; Reinfection; Respiratory infection

Article.Title: Vibration model test and seismic performance evaluation of polypropylene fiber reinforced concrete lining of mountainside tunnels in Loess Plateau
Article.Authors: Hu J.; Li R.; Zheng P.; Chu C.; Ma J.; Li H.; Li R.; Shu C.; Wang G.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Currently, tunnels are key infrastructure projects for traversing the Loess Plateau and ensuring rail connectivity. However, seismic damage surveys indicate that tunnels built along mountainsides in the Loess region suffer severe damage during earthquakes due to their low structural damping and inadequate seismic performance assessments. Therefore, this manuscript is to develop a new method for evaluating the seismic performance of mountain-adjacent tunnels under the coupled effect of earthquake and slope deformation in loess region. This method proposes a concrete mix design for polypropylene-fiber-reinforced concrete (PFRC) tunnel structures built along mountainsides in the Loess Plateau. Through shake-table model tests evaluating the seismic performance of such structures, the study analyzed their seismic performance and the underlying mechanisms. The tests revealed that concrete strength first increased and then decreased as the fiber content increased; the optimal concrete strength was achieved at a fiber content of 0.9%, representing a 15% improvement over ordinary concrete. The PGA amplification factor for the slope increased nonlinearly with elevation, with a quadratic amplification phenomenon observed at the slope crest. The seismic response of bending moments of the PFRC tunnel lining at the arch, invert arch, and left and right side walls were reduced by 8.9%, 8.5%, 15.2% and 12.4%, respectively, than that of ordinary concrete. This indicates that incorporating fibers into tunnel lining can form a highly damping composite structure, yielding good seismic performance due to the continuous energy dissipation from fiber friction, crack opening and closing, etc. Meanwhile, compared to traditional lining structures, the fiber-reinforced concrete lining has advantages such as simple construction technology, excellent environmental adaptability, and low maintenance costs, which can solve the seismic problem of mountain-adjacent tunnels in loess areas.

Article.Title: First demonstration of in vivo estimation of Young’s modulus in cancers using poroelastography with experimental validation
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Islam M.; Majumder S.; Ewing A.; Serpelloni S.; Taraballi F.; Righetti R.
Article.Abstract: Ultrasound elastography (USE) is a real-time non-invasive imaging modality widely used to quantitatively reconstruct the mechanical properties (i.e., stiffness) in tissues. The longstanding challenges associated with solving inverse problems under in vivo conditions include achieving high accuracy, fast convergence, and broad applicability. In computationally simple and fast mathematical framework model of traditional USE techniques, poroelastic tissues are assumed to be nearly incompressible (Poisson’s ratio of nearly 0.5) and are represented by using linearly elastic models. These assumptions can lead to inaccurate estimates of the tissue material properties. We employ Eshelby’s theory in combination with a poroelastic model based lateral strain correction to extend the in vivo estimation of Young’s modulus to tissues with varying degrees of compressibility. This model involves knowledge of the steady-state strain components, remotely applied stress, and the underlying geometry of inclusion. We validated the proposed method by using standard finite element (FE) and ultrasound-based poroelastic simulations of complex clinical scenarios, with an average percentage relative error of less than 5%. Based on an orthotopic murine model of human breast cancer (MDA-MB-231), we present, for the first time, a poroelastography-based in vivo estimation of Young’s modulus, experimentally validated through ex vivo mechanical tests, with a percentage relative error of less than 15% for most of the cases. This approach holds promise in attracting cancer researchers aiming to connect tumor mechanobiology with cancer initiation, progression and treatment strategies.

Article.Title: Physics-guided deep learning improves UAV multispectral estimation of strawberry canopy LAI and SPAD
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Ting T.; Liu X.; Pan Q.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of strawberry canopy traits from UAV multispectral imagery is important for agricultural productivity but remains difficult under greenhouse conditions because illumination variation, canopy overlap, shadowing, background interference, and coupled structural and biochemical responses weaken purely empirical relationships. We propose DeepRT, a physics-guided multi-task framework for the joint estimation of leaf area index (LAI) and canopy chlorophyll status represented by SPAD. DeepRT combines PROSAIL-generated spectral priors with modality-specific learning from calibrated reflectance, vegetation indices, and texture descriptors. A reliability-aware fusion module adapts the contribution of each modality, while synthetic supervision, latent-domain alignment, and a physical-feasibility regularizer constrain learning under limited field labels. The study comprised 34 temporally ordered UAV campaigns and 310 quality-controlled sampling-unit observations. A chronological train-validation-test split, five repeated runs, and time-series cross-validation were used to limit temporal leakage. DeepRT achieved \(R^2\) values of \(0.92\pm 0.015\) for LAI and \(0.84\pm 0.018\) for SPAD, with RMSE values of \(0.32\pm 0.018\) m \(^2\) /m \(^2\) and \(2.8\pm 0.18\) SPAD units, respectively. Predicted uncertainty was positively associated with absolute error, with Spearman correlations of 0.612 and 0.587. These results support physics-guided heterogeneous fusion as a reproducible approach to greenhouse crop-trait retrieval while also identifying illumination-dependent and high-uncertainty conditions that require cautious interpretation.

Article.Title: Influence of alkaline activator concentration on the mechanical, microstructural properties of geopolymer mortar using Class C fly ash and M-sand
Article.Authors: Deeba S.; Arun Kumar A.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the mechanical performance and microstructural characteristics of geopolymer mortar produced using Class C fly ash as the sole precursor under ambient curing conditions. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and sodium silicate (Na 2 SiO 3 ) were employed as alkaline activators, using NaOH molarities of 8 M, 10 M, 12 M, and 14 M alongside silicate-to-hydroxide ratios ranging from 1:1 to 2.5:1. The effects of activator molarity, silicate-to-hydroxide ratio, curing regime, and binder-to-aggregate ratio on early-age mechanical properties were investigated. Compressive, flexural, and direct tensile strengths were evaluated up to 28 days. Results show that a NaOH molarity of 12 M combined with a silicate-to-hydroxide ratio of 2.5:1 provides superior performance, achieving 28-day compressive, flexural, and tensile strengths of 40.50 MPa, 4.77 MPa, and 3.70 MPa, respectively. 8 M resulted in insufficient aluminosilicate dissolution; 10 M and 12 M molarities enhance dissolution, gel formation, and mechanical performance, whereas higher molarity 14 M promoted crystalline phase formation without significant strength improvement. Microstructural analyses confirmed dominant geopolymer gel formation, with XRD revealing a strong amorphous phase and increased baseline shift at 12 M. FTIR spectra confirmed Si–O–T (T = Si or Al) bond formation, while SEM images indicated a denser matrix. EDAX elemental ratios at 12 M indicate enhanced aluminosilicate network formation and effective charge balancing. Microstructural analyses (XRD, FTIR, SEM, and EDAX) confirmed that a Ca/Si ratio of 0.18, Si/Al ratio of 4.46 and Na/Al ratio of 1.18 at 12 M signify an optimally cross-linked aluminosilicate network and denser matrix. The 12 M sodium hydroxide with a 2.5:1(silicate: hydroxide) ratio, cured under ambient conditions, produced a compressive strength that was 15%, 5%, and 9.5% higher than the 8 M,10 M,14 M mixes, respectively. The increase in flexural strength was found to be 8.4%, 2.6%, and 6%, while the direct tensile strength showed an increase of 13.9%, 5.7%, and 8.8% compared to the same molarities. The 12 M NaOH concentration improved the dissolution of silica and alumina, producing a denser matrix with a compact microstructure, improved bond between the binder and fine aggregate, providing the alkaline environment for geopolymerisation, resulting in a higher strength.

Article.Title: Evaluation of renal function tests and serum electrolytes in diabetic and non-diabetic individuals: a comparative cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Abbas A.; Al–Arabi D.; Al-Samman G.; AL-Maliki T.; Ahmed M.; Al-Samman O.; Alhaj M.; Al-Faqih K.; Al-Qadi S.; Raweh M.; Al Fakih A.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease associated with impaired renal function and electrolyte balance, which may contribute to an increased risk of renal and metabolic complications. This study aimed to evaluate and compare renal function tests (RFTs) (urea, uric acid, and creatinine) and electrolytes (Ca 2+ , Na + , K + , and Cl − ) in individuals with and without diabetic disease. A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted with 300 participants, including 150 diabetic patients and 150 healthy individuals. Demographic data and laboratory measurements of RFTs and electrolytes were collected. Univariate analysis was employed to compare the two groups; Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to assess correlations between variables; and binary logistic regression was utilized to identify independent factors associated with diabetes. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Most demographic characteristics did not differ statistically between the two groups. Diabetic patients showed significantly higher levels of creatinine (0.5926 ± 0.2134 vs. 0.5463 ± 0.1284, P = 0.0242), urea (25.47 ± 8.986 vs. 22.25 ± 6.639, P = 0.0006), and K + (4.707 ± 0.5688 vs. 4.527 ± 0.3470, P = 0.0012), while the levels of Na + (137.4 ± 13.42 vs. 144.1 ± 3.496, P < 0.0001) and Ca 2+ (2.397 ± 0.1456 vs. 2.441 ± 0.06213, P = 0.0009) were lower in diabetic patients compared to healthy individuals, with the mean absolute magnitude of the differences limited. Pearson analysis revealed statistically significant weak positive, weak negative, and moderate negative correlations between RBG and urea ( r = 0.1713, P = 0.0415), creatinine ( r =-0.1623, P = 0.0496), and Na + r =-0.3644, P < 0.0001), respectively. Binary logistic regression analysis showed that urea (OR = 1.0522, 95% CI = 1.0166–1.0890, P = 0.0038), uric acid (OR = 0.6956, 95% CI = 0.5441–0.8894, P = 0.0038), Na + (OR = 0.9610, 95% CI = 0.9382–0.9843, P = 0.0011), and K + (OR = 1.8766, 95% CI = 1.0460–3.3667, P = 0.0348) were significant independent factors associated with diabetes. In conclusion, diabetic patients exhibit significant differences in some renal function and electrolyte indicators compared to healthy individuals, with a limited number of these indicators showing independent association with diabetes after multivariate analysis.

Article.Title: An explainable driver risk classification framework using GWO-XGBoost and vehicular behavioural analytics

Article.Title: On the correlation between mechanical and electrical properties of pure and Ag doped ZnO nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Mohamed M.; Ismail Y.; Bouzidi M.; Khan Z.; Sedky A.
Article.Abstract: We present here structural, mechanical, and electrical properties at different values of temperatures (30-150 °C) for Zn1-xAgxO nanoparticles (NPs) with x = 0.00, 0.02, and 0.04. All NPs samples show wurtzite structure, tensile stress, and brittle character. Ag doping resulted in a slight increase in crystallite size, along with reduction in dislocation density, micro-strain, specific surface area, porosity, particle size, and M-O spacing. The FTIR spectra exhibit various bands between 3450.69 and 411.3 cm-1 for all samples, with most shifting to lower wavenumbers as x increases. With increasing Ag doping content up to 0.04, the Debye temperature, effective mass, elastic moduli, hardness, and wave velocities all gradually increased. The dielectric constant, dielectric loss, AC conductivity, and F-factor increase with increasing temperature (T) or doping content (x). In addition, the activation energy of the charge carriers, determined using the Arrhenius equation, decreased with increasing x or f, ranging from 0.187 to 0.68 eV across all samples. In general, no relaxation peaks are observed in the tan δ curves for x = 0.00 and x = 0.02 across the entire temperature range; however, for x = 0.04, clear relaxation peaks appear at 110 °C and 150 °C. The relaxation peaks are also evident in the electric modulus (M) and impedance (Z) curves for all samples, with their peak frequencies increasing with T or x. The frequency exponent (0.05 < s ≤ 0.55) indicates the conduction mechanism is the correlated barrier hopping. Meanwhile, the binding energy (0.163-0.345 eV) decreases as either T or x increases. The Cole-Cole plots reveal ideal semi-circular arcs corresponding to parallel RC representations for all samples. The impedance of grains, grain boundaries, and the series resistance (ranging from 2 × 104 to 108 Ω) decrease with increasing x or T, whereas the effective capacitance increases (0.005-38.73 µF). These findings establish a correlation between the mechanical and dielectric properties and highlight the promising potential of Ag-doped ZnO nanoparticles for further exploration in electronic and energy-related applications.
Article.Keywords: Dielectric properties; Mechanical properties; Plastic deformation and drug delivery; Solar cells and supercapacitors; Telecommunications; Zn1-xAgxO NPs

Article.Title: Bone morphology influences asymptomatic knee kinematics across the flexion range: a dynamic CT study
Article.Authors: Teule E.; van de Groes S.; Verdonschot N.; Janssen D.
Article.Abstract: Considerable inter-individual variability in knee kinematics exists even within asymptomatic populations, yet the extent to which this variability relates to underlying morphology remains poorly understood. This study aimed to identify morphological features associated with asymptomatic knee kinematics across the full knee flexion range. Dynamic CT data from 100 asymptomatic participants performing a knee flexion-extension movement were analysed, of which 73 knees met the inclusion criteria. Tibiofemoral and patellofemoral kinematics were extracted from the dynamic scans, while morphological features of the femur, tibia and patella were automatically quantified from the static CT scan. Associations between morphology and dynamic knee kinematics were assessed using mixed-effects models across the full knee flexion range. Tibial plateau morphology and the lateral femoral condyle radius were significantly associated with tibiofemoral internal-external rotation and anterior-posterior translation. Regarding patellofemoral kinematics, Wiberg angle was associated with patellar flexion, whereas Wiberg index, patellar width, and medial and lateral trochlear inclination were associated with patellar tilt and mediolateral translation. Several of these associations varied with knee flexion angle, indicating that morphology-kinematics relationships are dynamic. Improved understanding of these relationships provides a foundation for future morphology-based prediction models that may contribute to personalized treatment strategies.

Article.Title: Glycans located upstream of the furin cleavage site in SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein influence its processing and functions
Article.Authors: Lavie M.; Louvet E.; Patron J.; Hanoulle X.; Belouzard S.
Article.Abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S) glycoprotein, which plays a central role in viral entry, consists of two subunits: S1, which mediates binding to the ACE2 receptor; and S2, which induces fusion of the viral envelope with the cell membrane. The S glycoprotein also contains a polybasic motif at the S1/S2 junction that is recognised by the furin-type protease family, modulating its entry functions. Several of the 22 N-glycans that decorate S are located near the S1/S2 boundary and are likely to influence S cleavage, which is crucial for inducing fusion—a key step in viral entry. This study characterised the importance of the N-glycans N603, N616, and N657 for S cleavage and its ability to induce fusion and entry. Our data revealed that S harbouring mutations at these three sites relies on a basic residue at position 634 for cleavage. Furthermore, while these N-glycans and R634 were necessary for the ability of S to mediate fusion and entry in the G614 and D614 variants, mutations in these residues had a milder impact in the XBB.1.5 Omicron variant. Consequently, the roles of N603, N616, N657 and R634 in S cleavage, fusion induction and viral entry have evolved alongside these different variants.

Article.Title: SOCS3 knockout of donor transplanted cells exacerbates GVHD associated with a high-fat diet in murine allogeneic HSCT
Article.Authors: Wu S.; Ishiguro H.; Suwabe T.; Yoshiike M.; Kanome H.; Kobayashi T.; Tsuchida T.; Katagiri T.; Fuse K.; Masuko M.; Annenkov A.; Ohashi R.; Araki M.; Nakagawa Y.; Hirai H.; Shindo T.; Sone H.; Ushiki T.
Article.Abstract: Suppressors of cytokine signaling (SOCS) proteins are negative regulators of cytokine signaling that are required to prevent excessive cellular responses. SOCS3 suppresses inflammation caused by metabolic stress, and a high-fat diet (HFD) accelerates the progression of systemic inflammation in systemic SOCS3 knockout (KO) mice via severe granulopoiesis. An HFD induces metabolic stress and chronic low-grade inflammation, contributing to graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) severity. We investigated the effects of SOCS3 deficiency in donor cells and HFD administration to recipients on the development of GVHD. Transplantation involving a wild-type (WT) donor and a recipient fed with an HFD resulted in skin and colon GVHD and shortened median survival time. Transplantation involving an SOCS3 KO donor and a recipient fed with an HFD exacerbated GVHD via increased CD4 and CD8 effector memory T cell ratios. Splenocytes after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation also showed high expression of CD49d, CD62L, and CD25 in CD4 + T cells and low expression of programmed cell death protein 1 and CD69 in CD8 + T cells. Analysis of recipient spleen cells 30 days after transplantation revealed higher interleukin-6 expression in groups receiving transplants from SOCS3 KO donors fed with a control diet or a HFD, compared with the group receiving transplants from WT donors fed a control diet. These results suggest that SOCS3 suppresses HFD-induced GVHD.

Article.Title: Comparison of EDTA- and glycolic acid-based irrigation regimens with or without chitosan for calcium hydroxide removal from artificial internal resorption cavities: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Mıdoglu G.; Karakoyunlu E.; Gürler K.; Yılmaz K.
Article.Abstract: Complete removal of calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH) 2 ] prior to obturation is critical for optimal sealer penetration and long-term success of root canal treatment; however, its elimination from complex anatomical regions such as internal resorption cavities remains challenging. This study evaluated the effectiveness of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-and glycolic acid (GA)-based irrigation regimens with or without chitosan in removing Ca(OH) 2 from artificial internal resorption cavities. Sixty extracted human mandibular premolars were prepared, standardized artificial internal resorption cavities were created, and the specimens were filled with Ca(OH) 2 . The teeth were randomly allocated to four experimental groups (n = 15) according to the irrigation protocol: EDTA, EDTA + chitosan, GA, and GA + chitosan. Residual Ca(OH) 2 was evaluated using stereomicroscopic scoring and quantitative ImageJ analysis. For stereomicroscopic assessment, the tooth was considered the experimental unit, and the scores obtained from the two root halves of each tooth were combined to generate a tooth-level score. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test followed by the Dunn–Bonferroni post hoc test ( p < 0.05). Significant differences were observed among the experimental groups ( p < 0.001). The EDTA group exhibited the highest combined stereomicroscopic scores, whereas the GA + chitosan group showed the lowest scores. No statistically significant differences were observed between the EDTA and EDTA + chitosan groups or between the GA and GA + chitosan groups in the stereomicroscopic analysis. In contrast, both GA-based protocols demonstrated significantly lower residual Ca(OH) 2 than the EDTA-based protocols. Quantitative ImageJ analysis corroborated this pattern, with the GA + chitosan regimen showing the lowest percentage of residual Ca(OH) 2 surface coverage. Within the limitations of this in vitro study, GA-based irrigation regimens resulted in less residual Ca(OH) 2 than EDTA-based regimens, although the specific contribution of chitosan could not be established.

Article.Title: Magnetophoretic modulation of BaSO$$_4$$ scaling: laboratory investigation and industrial case study
Article.Authors: ElMassalami M.; Silva G.; da Silva M.; Elzubair A.; Queiroz Neto J.; Pinhal N.
Article.Abstract: Scale formation in supersaturated BaSO \(_4\) -bearing fluids poses a persistent challenge in domestic and industrial settings due to the scalant’s extremely low solubility, high mechanical strength, and resistance to removal. We revisit the long-standing question of whether magnetic fields can mitigate such a scaling. Under our current experimental conditions, our analysis shows that magnetic-field effects on BaSO \(_4\) -bearing fluids are negligible in magnetically clean fluids. In fluids containing ferromagnetic or ferrimagnetic particulates, which are common in practical settings, strong field gradients can induce particle polarization and magnetophoretic drift, promoting the coalescence of nanoscale particles into larger agglomerates. These agglomerates can act as heterogeneous nucleation templates, thereby modifying crystallization kinetics and deposit morphology. As a result, precipitation may be partially redirected from undesirable surface-bound fouling toward volume-bound suspended particulates that remain entrained in the flow and can be more readily removed. This shift toward heterogeneous nucleation and growth provides a possible field- and contamination-mediated mechanism for rationalizing many disparate reports on magnetic anti-scale treatment across laboratory, domestic, and industrial settings, including hydrocarbon oil and gas environments.

Article.Title: Stochastic modeling for uncertainty quantification in COVID-19 dynamics using Euler Maruyama approximation
Article.Authors: Rios-Gutierrez A.; Arunachalam V.; Torres S.
Article.Abstract: We propose a stochastic extension of a compartmental epidemiological model for COVID-19 to describe the transmission dynamics in Bogotá, Colombia. To account for intrinsic variability in infection, incubation, recovery, and vaccination processes, random perturbations are incorporated into key model parameters. The resulting system of stochastic differential equations is approximated using the Euler-Maruyama method, enabling likelihood-based parameter estimation. We derive an extended basic reproduction number, along with its associated uncertainty, providing a statistically grounded measure of epidemic potential under varying conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully captures the variability observed in the epidemiological data and highlights the importance of accounting for parameter uncertainty in public health decision-making. The model is statistically tractable, computationally efficient, and adaptable to other infectious diseases and urban settings. Possible extensions include incorporating reinfection dynamics, integrating additional data sources, and using Bayesian inference to enhance uncertainty quantification.

Article.Title: Computational identification of antifibrotic microRNAs targeting hepatic stellate cell activation
Article.Authors: Sciaraffa N.; Martorana A.; Carreca A.; Calascibetta F.; Carcione C.; Spanò D.; Lo Pinto M.; Timoneri F.; Iannolo G.; Li Greci A.; Bruno S.; Scilabra S.; Coronnello C.; Chinnici C.
Article.Abstract: The complexity of liver fibrosis highlights the need for therapeutic strategies capable of modulating multiple pathways simultaneously. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), as multitarget regulators of gene expression, represent promising antifibrotic candidates. Here, we developed an integrative workflow combining cellular models, quantitative proteomics, and bioinformatic analyses to prioritize antifibrotic miRNAs. Activation of LX-2 hepatic stellate cells with TGF-β1 induced a profibrotic phenotype and enabled proteomic identification of upregulated proteins. These proteins were integrated with two miRNA-target prediction approaches, including experimentally validated interactions from miRTarBase and computational predictions generated using the miRNA binding sites (MBS) tool. The collagen-maturation enzyme prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunit α2 (P4HA2) was selected as a proof-of-concept target. Screening of five miRNAs predicted to target P4HA2 identified hsa-miR-9-5p as the most promising candidate, significantly reducing P4HA2 protein levels and suppressing profibrotic marker expression during LX-2 cell activation. Direct interaction with the P4HA2 3′UTR was confirmed by a luciferase reporter gene assay. These effects were further confirmed in HepG2/LX-2 co-culture liver spheroids, where collagen modulation was observed in a subset of cells, likely corresponding to the stellate cell compartment. Collectively, these findings establish our computationally guided prioritization strategy as a platform for identifying therapeutic miRNAs with broad applicability across diverse disease contexts.

Article.Title: Past and present resistance status to pyrethroid insecticides of Aedes aegypti from New Caledonia
Article.Authors: Dupuis B.; Russet S.; Mahossem M.; Drain A.; Pol M.; Kilama S.; Tutagata J.; Cheilan F.; Guillaumot L.; Cannet A.; Pocquet N.
Article.Abstract: Dengue is a major public health concern in the Pacific region, including New Caledonia (NC), where control strategies have targeted Aedes aegypti for a long time. However, increasing insecticide resistance has reduced the effectiveness of these approaches. NC has recently implemented a Wolbachia -based strategy to reduce dengue transmission, though its success may be compromised by high resistance levels in local mosquito populations. We analyzed historical data from 92 Ae. aegypti lineages collected in Noumea between 2003 and 2018 and assessed 17 populations sampled across NC in 2020–2021 using WHO tube bioassays with deltamethrin. Resistance was evaluated through mortality rates and knockdown times. Molecular analyses identified kdr mutations in the VGSC gene and copy number variation at the 1011 locus were assessed. Deltamethrin resistance increased markedly over time, with median mortality declining from 95% to 46%. Recent populations showed widespread resistance, especially in urban areas. Two mutations, F1534C and I1011M, were detected. F1534C frequency increased substantially, while I1011M was only observed in heterozygotes and associated with gene duplication. Ouvea populations remained fully susceptible. These results indicate widespread resistance driven by specific mutations and gene duplication, highlighting the need to reconsider insecticide-based control and support alternative strategies such as Wolbachia .

Article.Title: Cultivar variation has a stronger influence than crop type on the properties of maize and sorghum residues and derived biochars
Article.Authors: Mbava N.; Zengeni R.; Muchaonyerwa P.
Article.Abstract: Conversion of crop residues to biochar can enhance soil carbon storage and reduce carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from agricultural soils, with these effects being influenced by crop type and cultivar, and pyrolysis conditions. This study characterized residues from two maize cultivars (SC701 and R201) and two sorghum cultivars (AS8 and PAN8816), and the biochars produced from them at 350 and 650 °C in a muffle furnace and at about 400 °C in a kiln. Feedstocks and biochars were analysed for proximate composition, elemental composition, chemical properties, surface morphology and functional groups. Significant differences were observed among cultivars within each crop, whereas crop type had comparatively smaller effects. Increasing pyrolysis temperature decreased moisture content from 12.79% in feedstocks to as low as 2.08% in biochars and increased ash content from 6.50 to 11.48% to 41.82-46.13% and pH from 4.26 to 5.09 to 10.58-11.40. Fixed carbon increased from 12.23 to 14.10% in feedstocks to a maximum of 47.13% in R201-B650, while kiln-produced PAN8816 and SC701 biochars retained the highest nitrogen contents (4.55% and 3.77%, respectively). Increasing pyrolysis temperature also reduced volatile matter and the H: C and O: C ratios. Cultivar-specific differences in feedstock physicochemical characteristics, including lignin content, elemental composition and other chemical properties, together with pyrolysis conditions, were more important than crop type in determining the properties of the resulting biochars. These findings highlight the importance of selecting cultivars with desirable feedstock characteristics and appropriate pyrolysis conditions when producing biochars for carbon sequestration and soil fertility improvement.

Article.Title: Probabilistic tsunami fragility: an uncertainty-aware framework for disaggregated building damage estimation
Article.Authors: Vescovo R.; Adriano B.; Mas E.; Koshimura S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tsunamis, while infrequent, can be some of the most damaging natural hazards to coastal communities. The unpredictable nature of tsunamis necessitates the development of robust methods that quantify probable damage and inform the development of mitigation strategies. While this critical need is recognized by the scientific community, probabilistic frameworks to assess risk given the range of tsunami hazards are still in their infancy. Tsunami Fragility Functions represent the state-of-the-art for building fragility estimation, they link hazard to risk, and are central to these frameworks. These models provide a notion of the expected building damage given a measure of the tsunami. However, they have seldom been studied directly as building damage estimators, hence their capacity to inform downstream tasks remains largely untested. Furthermore, the current state-of-the-art lacks a method to handle input and output uncertainty, which is crucial for holistic frameworks such as recently proposed probabilistic Hazard-to-Risk frameworks. In the present work we propose a novel bayesian ordinal regression framework, inspired by fragility functions, for disaggregated building damage estimation to fulfill this need. We fit our method on 2011 Tohoku Earthquake and Tsunami data and provide three case studies to highlight the model’s generalization capabilities and limitations.

Article.Title: Triglyceride–cholesterol–body weight index and incident cardiovascular disease in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a CHARLS cohort study
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Zhang Z.; Cao Y.; Qiu H.
Article.Abstract: The triglyceride-cholesterol-body weight index (TCBI) integrates serum triglycerides, total cholesterol, and body weight in a single nutritional-metabolic measure. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), we examined whether TCBI was associated with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) among middle-aged and older Chinese adults classified into cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0–3. The prospective analysis included 8,030 participants; cumulative-exposure and pattern analyses used a landmark cohort of 4,583 participants. In fully adjusted Cox models, each one-unit increase in log-TCBI was associated with a 15% higher CVD hazard (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.07–1.23) at baseline and an 8% higher hazard (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.04–1.13) for cumulative exposure; both dose–response relationships were nonlinear. K-means clustering separated participants into persistently high, moderate, and low groups; the low group had less CVD than the high group (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.59–0.82, P < 0.001). Findings were consistent in Fine-Gray competing-risk and sensitivity analyses. Higher baseline and cumulative TCBI were associated with greater CVD risk among adults with CKM stages 0–3, suggesting that repeated TCBI assessment may add information for risk stratification.

Article.Title: Integrative computational analyses prioritize the host target IL15RA and the candidate compound Zafirlukast for investigation in flaviviral encephalitis
Article.Authors: Ramesh V.; Gautam N/A.; Puttahonnappa S.; Kamble N.; Sathish N.; Palavesam A.; Khatoon M.; Mambully S.; Hiremath J.; Pattnaik B.; Srikantiah C.; Patil S.
Article.Abstract: Arboviral infections, particularly West Nile virus (WNV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and Dengue virus (DENV), pose increasing global health threats, yet effective broad-spectrum host-directed therapeutics remain elusive. This study employed an integrative systems biology framework to identify conserved candidate host target across flaviviral infections. Using WNV as a discovery model, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) of transcriptomic data identified immune-neuroinflammatory modules associated with severe disease. A core signature of ten hub genes was identified through integrated network analysis and further prioritized using machine learning classifiers (AUC > 0.80). To enhance robustness, and overcome single-cohort limitations, these candidates were subsequently evaluated using independent RNA-seq datasets of ZIKV and DENV infection. Among the prioritized genes IL15RA, IRF1, and GBP1 consistently exhibited significant upregulation ( p < 0.05) across all three flaviviruses, supporting their identification as conserved pan-flaviviral host markers. Structural evolutionary analysis indicated that the predicted ligand-interaction region of IL15RA is conserved across mammalian species. Drug repurposing analyses computationally prioritized Zafirlukast, a cysteinyl leukotriene receptor antagonist, as a candidate compound predicted to interact favorably with IL15RA, while molecular dynamics simulations supported the predicted stability of the IL15RA-Zafirlukast complex (RMSD ~ 0.35 nm) relative to other candidate compounds. Collectively, these findings computationally prioritize IL15RA as a candidate host target and identify Zafirlukast as a candidate compound with a favorable predicted interaction profile. Together, they provide a rationale for future experimental studies to evaluate the biological relevance of the predicted IL15RA-Zafirlukast interaction and its role in host inflammatory responses during flaviviral encephalitis.

Article.Title: Energy-aware heart disease prediction system using hybrid metaheuristic optimization and deep learning for IoT-enabled healthcare environments
Article.Authors: Krishnasamy R.; Shukla V.; Krishna Kumari L.; Uvaneshwari M.; Mohan B.; Sundaravadivel P.
Article.Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) allows different devices to connect and share data easily, which helps improve healthcare services. When IoT is combined with artificial intelligence and machine learning, large amounts of medical data can be analyzed to support accurate medical decisions. Deep learning methods are especially useful for identifying complex patterns in healthcare data and improving disease diagnosis. This study presents an energy-efficient framework for heart disease prediction tailored to IoT-driven healthcare environments. The proposed framework has two main stages: data transmission and disease prediction. In the transmission stage, a hybrid Ant Colony–Genetic Algorithm (ACGA) is used to select suitable cluster heads, and clustering is performed using Manhattan distance. This helps reduce energy usage in the simulated IoT network. In the prediction stage, patient data are initially processed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for feature extraction and feature compression. This step helps reduce unnecessary data and improves the model’s capability to generalize. A Self-Adaptive Deep Neural Network (SA-DNN) is then used for heart disease prediction. The network parameters are optimized with an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) to improve prediction performance. The predictive model was evaluated using the Cleveland Heart Disease, South African Coronary Heart Disease (CHD) and Framingham Heart Study datasets, which are offline tabular clinical datasets, while the IoT communication environment was evaluated separately through software-based simulation. No real wearable devices, edge computing platforms, or physical IoT hardware were used in this study. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed method improves energy efficiency and prediction performance compared with existing methods. The proposed model achieved classification accuracies of 96.7% on the Cleveland Heart Disease dataset, 98.56% on the South African CHD dataset and 95.05% on the Framingham Heart Study dataset after 50 training epochs. The system also achieved high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Furthermore, 5-fold cross-validation and statistical analyses were performed to validate the robustness and consistency of the proposed approach. Computational complexity and deployment feasibility were also analyzed, indicating that the proposed framework has the potential to support future IoT-driven healthcare applications.

Article.Title: Geochemical characterization and health risk assessment of soil-derived dust in the sistan hotspot: an integrated climate–statistical framework
Article.Authors: Ahangar A.; Piri J.
Article.Abstract: The Sistan region of southeastern Iran represents among the most persistently dust-affected regions documented globally, where interacting climatic and environmental drivers have produced a sustained air-quality burden of documented public-health significance. We propose an integrated climate-statistical framework coupling robust time-series analysis with geochemical characterization and probabilistic health-risk assessment, applied to a 31-year record (1990–2020, Zabol Station). Trend analysis reveals a highly significant intensification of dust-storm days (Z = 6.83, p < 0.001; Sen’s slope = 4.95 days yr-1), culminating in a structural break in 2004 (bootstrap 95% CI 1998–2010) identified consistently by the Pettitt, SNHT and CUSUM tests, with the Sequential Mann–Kendall crossing at 2007 within that interval and coinciding with the near-complete desiccation of the Hamoun wetland, which shifted the mean from ~ 40 to ~ 145 days yr-1. Rescaled-range exponents computed on the raw series exceed unity and are therefore not admissible Hurst estimates; within the post-2004 regime, where the series is approximately stationary, exponents fall to 0.67–0.79, indicating ordinary persistence. Spectral peaks near 9.8 and 5.8 years are not separable from a red-noise background over a 31-year record. A bounded generalized extreme value model, fitted in the logit domain of the annual dusty-day proportion, projects a post-2004 10-year return level of 158 dust days yr⁻¹ (95% profile-likelihood CI 153–166); the corresponding 100-year level of 162 days yr⁻¹ is exploratory, being conditional on the post-2004 GEV model and extrapolated beyond the record length; a likelihood-ratio test decisively favours a non-stationary formulation, so return levels beyond the 10-year horizon are reported as exploratory. Transfer entropy provides no statistically significant evidence of directional coupling in any direction once estimator bias is corrected (smallest surrogate p = 0.29); these results are reported as a null finding. Geochemical profiling indicates enrichment of Pb (EF = 11.5), Cu, Zn and Ni relative to crustal background; the inhalation hazard index is 24.9 and the total incremental lifetime cancer risk is 7.4 × 10⁻⁴ as an upper bound. Annual-mean PM10 (435 ug m-3) and PM2.5 (308 ug m-3) exceed WHO guidelines 29- and 62-fold, with modelled exceedance probabilities approaching unity up to 20× and 50× respectively. On the balance of physical reasoning and the changepoint chronology, hydrological restoration of the Hamoun basin is advanced as the most plausible structural mitigation priority, a hypothesis these data support but do not establish causally.

Article.Title: Comparative clinical and reproductive outcomes following non-invasive versus biopsy-based preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy: a multicentric cohort study
Article.Authors: Talwar D.; Shah N.; Meseguer M.; Aggarwal R.; Murdia K.; Murdia N.; Singh B.; Rathore S.; Chandra V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A) is emerging as a newer technology alongside conventional trophectoderm biopsy-based PGT-A, aiming to avoid embryo biopsy while enabling genetic assessment through analysis of cell-free DNA. However, its clinical utility in improving reproductive outcomes remains uncertain, particularly in real-world settings. This retrospective multicentric cohort study evaluated reproductive outcomes following niPGT-A and conventional PGT-A in 6,215 patients underwent intracytoplasmic sperm injection across 48 centres of our organisation between January 2023 and July 2024, comprising 15,635 tested blastocysts. Clinical outcomes were analysed in 3,179 frozen embryo transfer (FET) cycles, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to adjust for confounding factors. Across both the overall cohort and euploid FETs, PGT-A was associated with improved reproductive outcomes compared with niPGT-A. Live birth rates were significantly higher following PGT-A in the overall cohort (46.2% vs. 34.5%) and among euploid embryo transfers (46.5% vs. 34.4%), accompanied by significantly higher clinical and ongoing pregnancy rates. These findings remained consistent across single- and double embryo transfers reproductive outcomes. Additionally, after confounders adjustment, PGT-A was still significantly associated with approximately twofold higher odds of clinical pregnancy and live birth. Collectively, these findings suggest that niPGT-A needs further refinement to improve its reliability and clinical efficacy for embryo selection.

Article.Title: Suppression of electrical crosstalk in 6047 pixel-per-inch ultrahigh-resolution white tandem organic light-emitting diodes on silicon via a trench structure
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Shin J.; Bae N.; Joo C.; Sim S.; Kang C.; Jang H.; Cho H.; Cheon S.; Byun C.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interpixel electrical crosstalk caused by lateral leakage current remains a key challenge in high-resolution organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) displays, leading to severe color distortion in full-color panels. In this study, a trench structure incorporated into a 6047 pixel-per-inch (PPI) stripe-based high-resolution pixel structure is demonstrated to effectively suppress electrical crosstalk in top-emitting white tandem OLEDs on silicon. The trench deeply etches the insulating layer between bottom electrodes, substantially increasing the effective path length of lateral leakage current. In addition, cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy revealed that the organic layer of tandem OLEDs on the trench sidewall was approximately seven times thinner than that on the pixel electrodes, increasing the sheet resistance; this was further supported by simulations. Consequently, the lateral leakage current was reduced by more than sevenfold in the 6047 PPI pixel structure with tandem OLEDs. Furthermore, two-dimensional spectroradiometer measurements show that light leakage into adjacent off-state pixels was reduced from approximately 13–15% to approximately 2% relative to the active pixel luminance, in excellent agreement with the reduction in lateral leakage current. These results demonstrate that the trench structure provides an effective strategy for suppressing lateral leakage current and improving color fidelity in high-resolution OLED displays.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of PET-modified concrete with PET granules and manufactured sand as fine aggregates
Article.Authors: Selvarajan K.; Krishnamoorthy S.; Muthusamy S.; Balakrishnan B.; Chan C.; Singh S.; Dixit S.; Kumar S.
Article.Abstract: Food and beverage packaging frequently uses polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and most of these products wind up in landfills. The primary problem with plastic waste is that it can harm the environment and is not biodegradable. Toxic gasses like dioxins, which can be detrimental to human health, can be released during incineration as a treatment approach. Recycling PET and using it in the building sector is one possible way to address this issue. The building industry is in dire need of inexpensive materials that strengthen concrete structures. This experiment aims to determine whether waste PET bottles may be used to partially substitute fine aggregate in concrete, hence reducing the concrete’s self-weight. A control mix was prepared and compared to concrete that contained 1%, 2%, and 3% PET bottle particles as fine aggregate. After seven and twenty-eight days, the cube, cylinder, and beam specimens were cast, cured, and their strength was assessed. Test findings for flexural strength, split tensile strength, and compression were contrasted with control samples. Compression, split tensile, and flexural strength increased by 2% of PET granules. The increasing need for fine aggregate can be satisfied by using PET bottle granule substitutes. The quantity of river sand needed for concrete is decreased when PET fine aggregates and manufactured sand (M-sand) are used in place of traditional river sand and plastic granules have also been shown to be more economical.

Article.Title: Gut-selective integrin-targeted therapy improves metabolic pathways in the early immune activation mouse model of autism spectrum disorder as revealed by untargeted metabolomics
Article.Authors: Fanelli G.; Lelli V.; Potenza R.; Ricceri L.; De Simone R.; Boirivant M.; Butera A.; Timperio A.
Article.Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder with complex etiology, often associated with gastrointestinal dysfunction and immune dysregulation. The microbiota-gut-brain axis is emerging as a crucial pathway in ASD pathogenesis, mediating the communication between gut, immune system, and central nervous system (CNS). We hypothesized that gut inflammation mediates metabolic reprogramming underlying ASD-like behavioral deficits. In this study, we thus evaluated the metabolic changes associated with ASD behavior and investigated their relationship with the presence of gut inflammation in a mouse model of ASD induced by early-life immune activation (EIA), a double-hit model, including both prenatal (Poly I:C) and postnatal (LPS) immune challenges in which we previously described gut inflammation. In this model, we demonstrated that inhibition of gut inflammation through a selective blockade of inflammatory monocytes and gut experienced lymphocyte homing to the intestinal lamina propria by the administration of an anti-α4β7 blocking monoclonal antibody rescued the social novelty deficit observed in EIA mice. Here, using untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics, we analyzed serum metabolites in EIA mice and in EIA mice treated with the anti-α4β7 monoclonal antibody. Our findings reveal significant metabolic disturbances in the EIA model, particularly in pathways associated with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and nucleotide metabolism. Notably, treatment with anti-α4β7 antibody restored several metabolic alterations related to gut inflammation, although it did not fully reverse changes in purine and pyrimidine metabolism. These results suggest that, after developmental immune activation, gut inflammation significantly contributes to the ASD phenotype and highlight the potential for targeting gut-immune interactions to modulate metabolic and behavioral outcomes in ASD.

Article.Title: Thermal aware fast EV charging and intelligent energy management using CNN-BiLSTM under highly variable renewable energy conditions
Article.Authors: Yadav I.; Bajpai R.; Gupta S.; Dixit S.; Shukla A.
Article.Abstract: Extremely fast charging of electric vehicles (EVs) requires higher-capacity charging stations, which may pose an extra burden over the utility network if the charging station is supported by renewable energy sources having frequent power interruptions. Adaptive Sliding Mode Control (ASMC) offers robustness and consistency; its capability is restricted in the multi-objective functionalities such as battery state of charge estimation, thermal control, and power optimization during highly dynamic operating scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a CNN-BiLSTM-assisted adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC), hereafter referred to as CBA, for renewable energy-supported EV charging stations connected to the grid. The CNN-BiLSTM model is used as a forecasting feedforward module to estimate the charging demand, uncertainty in renewable power, and battery thermal management control, while ASMC is employed for robust closed-loop trajectory tracking and constraint enforcement. This control framework executes rapid charging control, improved temperature management, and appropriate power sharing amongst renewable energy sources and the utility grid. Simulation and experimental results illustrate that the CBA controller achieves a battery state of charge (SoC) of 85% within 900 s compared to 80% in the standard ASMC controller, which is an increase of 6.25%. The experimental validation demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed technique, as 84% SoC is achieved in the same charging time, whereas ASMC achieves only 80%, which is an increase of 5.0%. Furthermore, the peak battery temperature is reduced by 8.33% in simulation and 10.2% in experimental validation using the suggested controller, with a reduction of the peak battery temperature from 48 °C to 44 °C and 49 °C to 44 °C, respectively. The proposed strategy also improves charging efficiency, stabilizes DC bus voltage, enhances renewable energy utilization, and reduces grid stress under highly dynamic operating conditions without sacrificing charging speed and battery health.

Article.Title: Nanopropolis mitigates cisplatin-induced submandibular gland injury by modulating oxidative stress and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Alanazi H.; Elturki F.; Gehani G.; Alruwaili M.; Ahmed K.; Alqarni A.; Alhedyan F.; AlGhamdi S.; Alshahrani F.; Alaklobie M.; Wahba A.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin is a widely deployed chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical utility is constrained by dose-limiting toxicities, including injury to the submandibular salivary gland mediated primarily by oxidative stress-driven apoptosis and progressive fibrotic remodeling. This study investigated the protective potential of Nanopropolis against cisplatin-induced structural, molecular, and ultrastructural alterations in the rat submandibular gland. Thirty adult male albino rats were allocated into three groups (n = 10): control, cisplatin-treated (single intraperitoneal injection, 8 mg/kg), and cisplatin + Nanopropolis (10 mg/kg/day orally for 14 days). Glandular injury was evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin histology, Masson’s trichrome histochemistry, BAX immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy, and quantitative real-time PCR for SOD1 mRNA. Cisplatin induced marked glandular pathology characterized by acinar degeneration, cytoplasmic vacuolation, ductal disruption, vascular congestion, and extensive collagen accumulation (29.66% of tissue area). These changes were accompanied by strong BAX upregulation and profound SOD1 mRNA suppression (0.223-fold vs. control), reflecting heightened apoptotic activity and oxidative stress. Nanopropolis treatment substantially reversed these findings, preserving glandular architecture, reducing collagen deposition to 5.72%, downregulating BAX expression, and restoring SOD1 expression to near-control levels (1.042-fold). TEM confirmed recovery of mitochondrial cristae integrity, secretory granule content, and ductal basal infoldings. Nanopropolis confers robust cytoprotection against cisplatin-induced submandibular gland toxicity by simultaneously attenuating oxidative stress, suppressing apoptotic signaling, and limiting fibrotic remodeling. These findings support Nanopropolis as a promising adjunctive strategy for preserving salivary gland integrity during cisplatin-based chemotherapy.

Article.Title: Adaptive dual-space discriminator for large-scale multi-objective optimization
Article.Authors: Xue Z.; Cheng K.; Liu X.; Li Y.; Xin G.
Article.Abstract: Numerous real-world applications involve large-scale multi-objective optimization problems (LSMOPs) with hundreds or even thousands of decision variables. Although multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) are effective for such tasks, relying solely on objective-space information often provides insufficient selection pressure in high-dimensional settings. To address this issue, an adaptive dual-space discriminator is proposed to coordinate selection strategies from both the objective and decision spaces through a state-aware adaptive operator-selection method with a recurrent selector based on direct population-improvement feedback, and a corresponding algorithm termed MOEA-RLD is developed by integrating dual-space selection, online strategy adaptation, a bounded population pool, and APD environmental selection. Comparative evaluations on the LSMOP benchmark suite against five representative large-scale multi-objective evolutionary algorithms show that MOEA-RLD achieves favorable average rankings across the tested settings. Further evaluations on three real-world application settings provide evidence of both the practical performance of the proposed method and its limitations.

Article.Title: Distributed learning-enabled federated large language model for fake news detection
Article.Authors: P P.; Kshirsagar P.; Krishnan S.; M R.
Article.Abstract: Fake news detection is the process of detecting misinformative or crafted content spread through social media. Fake news causes social instabilities, increases the data leakage risks, and affects the user's privacy. The prevailing fake news detection models failed to tackle certain challenges, including overfitting issues, reduced generalizability, and computational complexity. Hence, the research proposes the Biometric Authenticated-Distributed learning enabled federated large language model (Bio-DFLLM) to detect fake news. The utilization of the hybrid biometrics enhances multiple users' privacy by sharing data with the aggregator center. The introduction of multiple feature extraction techniques learns intricate features and simplifies the detection process by lowering the computational demands and mitigating overfitting challenges. Furthermore, the pretrained response fact checker strengthens the research reliability using its domain adaptation and reliability reinforcement characteristics. In essence, the TensorFlow mirrored strategy-based distributed learning and Federated learning reduce the computational issues and enable better scalability using their data parallelism and model aggregation characteristics. Experimental results prove the superiority of the fake news detection model by achieving 98.35% accuracy, 98.40% sensitivity, 98.27% precision, and 98.40% recall using the dataset named fake news detection, for 90% training.

Article.Title: Reconstruction of pretelescopic and early telescopic solar activity cycles from auroral records
Article.Authors: Petrovay K.; Magyar L.; Hayakawa H.
Article.Abstract: The historical record of low-latitude aurorae is essentially a poorly sampled record of the largest space weather events (SWEs). Its use for the identification of individual solar cycles is hindered by the low event rate and by the fact that the solar cycle profile of the occurrence of SWEs does not closely follow the variation of sunspot numbers. Based on recent studies of the solar cycle dependence of the occurrence rates of large SWEs, here we construct Monte-Carlo simulations of a large number of activity cycles to identify the optimal procedure to infer the characteristics of underlying solar cycles from the sparse record. We find that a reliable reconstruction of the cycle phase (>90% of reconstructed minima corresponding to actual minima within ±2 years) is possible whenever the long-term mean event rate (annual mean number of space weather events resulting in low-latitude auroral sightings) reaches or exceeds a value around 3. This condition is found to be satisfied during most of the the Early Modern Active Period (EMAP), a century-long period of normal solar activity between the Spörer and Maunder Minima. For the numbering of solar cycles in the EMAP we introduce the "telescopic era", where Tn denotes the nth cycle from the first telescopically observed cycle, T0, ongoing in 1610. Using our optimal procedure we reconstruct a series of 8 solar activity cycles from T-5 to T2 (1560-1640). Earlier cycles starting from 1540 can be reconstructed with a somewhat lower degree of reliability. Comparing our results with radionuclide-based reconstructions and sunspot observations we find a good overall correspondence, with the exception of the last cycle before the Maunder Minimum.
Article.Keywords: Aurorae; Cosmogenic radionuclides; Solar cycle; Space climate

Article.Title: A comparative study of wave scattering by a submerged porous breakwater in wall-bounded and unbounded domains
Article.Authors: Kalathil H.; Barman K.; Saha S.
Article.Abstract: Wave scattering over porous structures plays an important role in the design of coastal and offshore protective structures. The present study investigates the scattering of water waves over a finite porous region with three primary objectives: (a) to compare the hydrodynamic behaviour under two scenarios: bounded by a rigid wall and unbounded; (b) to examine the influence of turbulence by comparing two resistance coefficient models, one incorporating the turbulent term and one neglecting it; and (c) to analyse the hydrodynamic coefficients for varying physical parameters under each scenario and model. The resistance coefficient is formulated by incorporating laminar, inertial, and turbulent terms, and the eigenfunction expansion method is employed to find the hydrodynamic coefficients. The numerical results reveal that incorporating turbulence gives significantly greater energy dissipation and reduced net wave load, particularly in the low frequency range and for structures with lower porosity. This study presents a mathematical approach to wave scattering over porous structures, offering a basis for future nonlinear models. Beyond its mathematical contribution, the present analysis also provides guidance into the practical performance of porous structures in different coastal engineering configurations. In particular, the findings offer practical guidance for two common design contexts: minimising wave induced loading on breakwaters attached to quays or seawalls, and maximising the attenuation and coastal protection afforded by free standing offshore breakwaters constructed from coarse, highly permeable material.

Article.Title: A study on the mechanism by which outdoor sports embodied experiences affect young people's sense of life meaning
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Li Z.; Luan T.; Fan Y.; Che W.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Under the dual influence of digital technology and the fast-paced modern lifestyle, outdoor sports have gradually become an important way to alleviate the anxiety of young people. This study adopts a mixed research method to explore the impact of different types of outdoor sports (fitness and physical training, leisure and entertainment, adventure and off-road exploration, and outdoor expansion training) on the sense of meaning in life of young people. Through random sampling, a cross-sectional survey was conducted on 508 young people who had participated in outdoor sports. The results show: (1) The participants were mainly young men aged 21 to 30; (2) The direct effect test indicates that there is a significant positive correlation between the physical experience of outdoor sports and the sense of meaning in life, among which fitness and physical training outdoor sports have the strongest correlation with the sense of meaning in life (0.241, p < 0.001); (3) The mediation effect test shows that emotional value and flow experience play a chain-like mediating role, among which adventure and off-road exploration outdoor sports have the strongest correlation with the sense of meaning in life (0.098, p < 0.01). Based on this, relevant suggestions are proposed: (1) Start from school physical education classes to cultivate attitudes and habits of outdoor sports; (2) Build a multi-party collaborative support system; (3) Regularly organize sharing and exchanges to enhance community belonging.

Article.Title: Reinforcement learning-guided multi-objective trajectory planning for obstacle avoidance in robotic manipulators
Article.Authors: Zhao Z.; Hao S.; Jin B.; Liu L.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Robotic manipulators operating in cluttered environments require collision-free trajectories that remain executable under kinematic and dynamic constraints. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-guided multi-objective trajectory planning framework, termed RL-MOP-HNE, for a 6-DOF UR5 manipulator. The planning model simultaneously minimizes path length, energy consumption, and execution time while satisfying collision-avoidance, kinematic, and dynamic constraints. A tabular SARSA agent is embedded into the evolutionary search to adaptively select search behaviours according to the current optimization state. To improve the balance between exploration and exploitation, a Gaussian-perturbation adaptive hybrid crossover operator is integrated with a hierarchical neighborhood evolution (HNE) strategy, enabling progressive population refinement throughout the search process. The proposed method is evaluated in three representative environments with increasing planning complexity, including single-obstacle, narrow three-obstacle, and irregular five-obstacle scenarios, and is compared with MOEA/D, MOPSO, MSCLPSO, NSGA-II, and RL-NSGA-II. Experimental results show that RL-MOP-HNE generates feasible trajectories in all test cases and achieves the lowest dynamic-stability-prioritized composite scores among the compared algorithms. The planned trajectories exhibit smoother joint motion and lower velocity fluctuations, although these improvements are generally accompanied by longer execution times. Complementary analyses, including time scaling, manipulability, clearance evaluation, statistical significance tests, and ablation studies, further explain the performance characteristics of the proposed framework and quantify the contribution of its key components. The proposed framework is therefore well suited to robotic applications where motion stability and dynamic executability are of greater importance than minimum-time operation.
Article.Keywords: Multi-objective trajectory planning; NSGA-II; Nature-inspired algorithms; Reinforcement learning; Robotic manipulator

Article.Title: Design, RLC equivalent circuit modeling, and ML/DL-based performance prediction of a graphene MIMO antenna for 6G THz systems
Article.Authors: Haque M.; Riyad A.; Ammar M.; Alkhaibari A.; Tiang J.; Singh N.
Article.Abstract: Intense interest in ultra-high-speed, low-latency, and large-capacity wireless communication has accelerated the development of terahertz (THz) antenna systems for sixth-generation (6G) networks. This work presents a compact graphene-based 1 × 2 multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) slotted microstrip patch antenna on a low-loss polyimide substrate for wideband terahertz applications. To improve impedance matching, mutual coupling, and radiation performance, the proposed configuration comprises designed slots, a defective ground structure (DGS), and a vertical copper decoupling strip. With a super-wideband from 0.62 to 3.46 THz, the antenna resonates at three frequencies: 1.2928 THz, 2.177 THz, and 3.1717 THz, covering 2.84 THz of bandwidth. The simulation results show that it has a peak gain of 12.2 dB, a radiation efficiency of 96.47%, a mutual coupling of less than − 30.12 dB, an envelope correlation coefficient of 0.000167, and a diversity gain of 9.9992 dB. A similar lumped-element RLC circuit model is built in ADS to confirm the electromagnetic behavior at the circuit level using the R, L, and C elements. Therefore, the RLC-based reflection coefficient is in perfect agreement with the CST full-wave simulation results, corroborating the validity of the proposed antenna design. Moreover, ML and DL regression models are employed to predict antenna performance based on geometric design parameters. We evaluate ten classic ML models and two DL models, which are a small multilayer perceptron and a residual multilayer perceptron architecture, in a leakage-safe grouped cross-validation procedure. The Gradient Boosting regressor outperforms all other models in predictive accuracy, with an R² of 0.9932, an MAE of 0.0529, and an RMSE of 0.0859. The result indicates that the proposed graphene-based MIMO antenna, validated by RLC circuit analysis and predicted by comparative ML and DL modeling, is a promising candidate for future 6G THz communication, high-speed sensing, biomedical diagnostics, and intelligent IoT applications.

Article.Title: Multiscale model of advanced recording system for enhancement of HAMR performance by FePt-based ECC media
Article.Authors: Pantasri W.; Meo A.; Chureemart P.; Chantrell R.; Chureemart J.
Article.Abstract: Heat Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR) is a novel high-density magnetic recording technology that leverages thermal assistance during the writing process to achieve ultrahigh areal densities beyond 4 Tb/in². Optimizing both the writing process and the magnetic medium properties is crucial to realize this potential. In this work, we developed a multiscale approach based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch (LLB) equation of motion parameterized using atomistic calculations. Atomistic simulation provide the required temperature dependent input quantities for the LLB equation. This multiscale approach makes it possible to accurately describe the physics of the magnetization dynamics at temperature close to the Curie point while overcoming the computational limitations of atomistic model when dealing with large systems. In this work, the model is employed to investigate an alternative exchange-coupled composite (ECC) medium structure composed of a hard FePt phase and a soft Fe-like material with a higher Curie temperature ( \(T_{\textrm{c}}\) ) than FePt, aimed at enhancing HAMR performance. The advantage of the ECC system lies in its ability to achieve magnetization reversal by lowering the maximum temperature ( \(T_\textrm{max}\) ) of the laser pulse. Using multiscale model that integrates atomistic and micromagnetic simulations, this study examines the magnetization reversal behavior during the recording process. For comparison, granular films composed of single grain FePt with high anisotropy and an ECC structure are simulated to investigate the switching probability ( \(P_{SW}\) ) of the writing process. We find that the ECC structure gives rise to an increase in switching probability. In particular, the ECC medium yields a \(P_{SW}\) of over 90% with a reduction in maximum temperature and pulse duration of 10% with respect to an FePt medium. The proposed ECC structure delivers significantly improved HAMR write efficiency, outperforming current FePt media and providing a viable pathway for next-generation high-density recording.

Article.Title: Facial dermal exposure-related parameters and skincare behaviors among adult women from six cities in China
Article.Authors: Hu R.; Zhu J.; Cui J.; Wu Q.; Chen F.; Liu Q.; Ning M.; Liu Y.; Tang Y.
Article.Abstract: The face is a primary site of exposure to skincare products, cosmetics, and sunlight. However, population-specific data on facial dimensions and product use among adult women in China remain limited. Current dermal exposure assessments often rely on default parameters derived from European or North American populations, which may introduce uncertainty when applied to Chinese consumers. This study aimed to describe facial dermal exposure-related parameters and skincare behaviors among adult women in China and to explore their associations with sensitive skin status and objective skin biophysical measurements. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 5081 women aged 18–65 years from six Chinese cities, conducted between March 2025 and June 2025. Total and regional facial areas were measured using two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) imaging. Data on skincare practices, sun-protection behaviors, sociodemographic characteristics, and skin-related variables were collected using standardized questionnaires and objective skin biophysical measurements. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, agreement analysis, between-group comparisons, cluster analysis, chi-square tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA). The mean age of participants was 40.7 years, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 23.4 kg/m 2 . The mean total 2D and 3D facial areas were 21,173.4 mm 2 (211.7 cm 2 ) and 39,381.0 mm 2 (393.8 cm 2 ), respectively; the 3D value (393.8 cm 2 ) was lower than the SCCS default facial application area of 565 cm 2 but close to the EPA-derived estimate of approximately 380 cm 2 . It should be noted that the proximity to the EPA-derived estimate does not constitute external validation of the measurement, as boundary definitions and measurement methods differ across sources. Valid 3D data were obtained from 4740 participants; 62.0% reported performing skincare twice daily. Total 2D and 3D facial areas were moderately correlated (r = 0.667, P < 0.001), while calibration, Bland–Altman, and ICC analyses demonstrated systematic differences and poor absolute agreement, indicating that measurements from the two systems were not interchangeable. Exploratory clustering suggested heterogeneous skincare behavior patterns, although cluster separation and stability were limited. This study provides system-generated facial-area estimates and descriptive data on skincare behaviors among adult women from a six-city convenience sample in China. The findings illustrate heterogeneity in facial-area measurements and skincare practices and may inform the development of localized dermal exposure scenarios. However, the facial-area estimates are device-specific and require independent validation, and the observed behavioral patterns and skin-related differences should be interpreted as exploratory cross-sectional associations rather than stable subgroups or causal relationships.

Article.Title: Harnessing machine learning and multi-source data fusion for regional geohazard risk assessment of a rapidly urbanizing mountainous region
Article.Authors: Li H.; Wang Y.; Wu Y.; Wang J.; Shi K.; Luo L.; Zuo L.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Rapid urbanization in mountainous regions often intensifies the conflict between engineering activities and the geological environment. in southeastern Sichuan Province, the study area is experiencing heightened geological disaster risks driven by its accelerated urbanization. To quantify this conflict, we developed an integrated hazard–vulnerability–risk assessment workflow. Hazard susceptibility was modeled using nine conditioning factors and three models—Information Value (IV), Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and Random Forest (RF)—while vulnerability was mapped using a game-theory weighting method based on four socio-economic indicators. Results indicate that the RF model achieved the best discrimination (AUC = 0.936), significantly outperforming AHP (AUC = 0.798) and IV (AUC = 0.865). The RF-based high-hazard classes covered 36.79% of the area and captured 94.73% of historical sites. Population density and road density were the main contributors to vulnerability, with combined weights of 0.351 and 0.324, respectively, and the high and very-high vulnerability zones accounted for 21.13% of the study area. The high- and very-high-risk zones covered only 8.07% of the study area, including 4.72% high-risk and 3.35% very-high-risk areas, and were mainly concentrated along the riverside urbanization belt and areas with dense population and infrastructure. These results provide a basis for targeted monitoring, spatial planning, and geohazard risk management in rapidly urbanizing mountainous areas.

Article.Title: Multi-omics profiling identifies neuroinflammation-related genes and exosomal miRNA as robust diagnostic signatures for Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Wu D.; Ma X.; Chen H.; Liu H.; He J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Neuroinflammation is a pivotal driver that amplifies the pathogenic cascade within the Parkinsonian brain. Nevertheless, the pathogenic drivers connecting neuroinflammation to PD prognosis remain unclear. To elucidate their therapeutic implications, this research sought to identify key neuroinflammation-related genes (NIRGs) and exosomal miRNAs in the PD. Methods: To comprehensively identify neuroinflammation-related genes (NIRGs) in Parkinson's disease (PD), we conducted an integrated multi-omics analysis.
