The experimental findings demonstrate that the suggested method achieved a higher privacy value of 0.034, greater restoration values of 0.970, and the lowest False Rule Generation value of 0.483, which is better than existing methods. Therefore, the hybrid PSBOA approach enhances key generation, offering robust security and resilience against unauthorized access, highlighting its potential for practical deployment.

Article.Title: Association of relative telomere length with glucocorticoid therapy in critically ill patients with severe COVID-19: a preliminary study
Article.Authors: Behar-Lagares R.; Martínez-González Ó.; Algaba-Calderón Á.; Martín-Parra C.; Alonso-Fernández M.; Manso-Álvarez M.; Mallol-Poyato M.; Pozo J.; Torrejón-Pulido Y.; Navalón-Hernández M.; Virseda-Berdices A.; Rodríguez-Grande C.; Jiménez-Sousa M.; Fernández-Rodríguez A.; Blancas R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Glucocorticoids (GCs) have proven to be a key therapy in mitigating the systemic inflammatory response in severe COVID-19. Relative telomere length (RTL) is recognized as a biomarker of cellular aging and biological stress, with its role in acute critical illnesses being of growing interest. Chronic exposure to GCs or stress are strongly associated with telomere shortening. This study aimed to explore the association of RTL ratios with GCs therapy. Methods: A prospective, longitudinal study involving patients over 18 years of age with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia was designed. Patients were admitted to the ICU of a university hospital. GCs therapy was standardized to dexamethasone equivalent doses based on the RECOVERY study. Blood samples were obtained upon admission and at least one year after discharge to determine telomere length using the Cawthon method (qPCR). RTL ratio (one year/baseline RTL) associations with GCs were calculated using generalized linear models (GLM). Results: A significant association was found between RTL ratios and the duration of GCs therapy (p=0.007). The dexamethasone equivalent dose also showed a significant association with RTL ratios (p<0.001). These associations were particularly significant in the male population (dexamethasone equivalent: p=0.028; duration of therapy: p=0.001), with no significant associations observed in women. Conclusion: In critically ill patients with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, this study reveals a significant association between RTL, the length of GCs therapy, and the equivalent dose of dexamethasone, especially in males. Further studies are needed to determine the effect of GCs on RTL admitted to de ICU for other critical conditions.

Article.Title: Localised force in direct-printed TC-85DAC clear aligners after thermal deformation and recovery cycles: a single-material in vitro study
Article.Authors: Shahrul A.; Ashari A.; Mokhtar M.; Zamani N.; Suhaimi N.
Article.Abstract: Direct-printed clear aligners fabricated from shape-memory photopolymer resins have been introduced as an alternative to conventional thermoformed aligners. Tera Harz TC-85DAC is a photocurable shape-memory resin developed for direct aligner printing. This study aimed to evaluate the localised force generated by 0.5-mm direct-printed TC-85DAC clear aligners around the maxillary right central incisor after 50 thermal deformation–recovery cycles. This single-material in vitro study evaluated 12 direct-printed TC-85DAC clear aligners. An anonymised maxillary digital model was modified to retain the maxillary right central incisor and selected posterior teeth, with a rectangular attachment placed on the labial surface of the central incisor. Baseline force was recorded as T0. Each aligner was then subjected to 50 thermal deformation–recovery cycles, with force recorded after every 10 cycles from T1 to T5. Localised force was measured using Fuji Prescale pressure-sensitive film and analysed using image-processing software. Repeated-measures analysis of variance was used for statistical analysis, and intra-examiner reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient. The mean force ranged from 5.07 ± 0.57 N at baseline to 5.27 ± 0.51 N after 50 cycles. The highest mean force was recorded after 10 cycles, at 5.49 ± 0.64 N. No statistically significant difference was detected across the six time points, F(5, 55) = 1.076, p = 0.384. The intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.87. Under the specific in vitro conditions tested, localised force remained relatively stable across 50 thermal deformation–recovery cycles, with no statistically significant change detected. Absolute force values were likely influenced by pressure-film interposition and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Further studies using clinically representative models and comparator materials are required.

Article.Title: Adaptive transformer-based deep learning model for fetal abnormal health and status assessment using ultrasound imagery
Article.Authors: Alymani M.; Mansour S.; Eltahir M.; Almejalli K.; AlHashimi H.; Almehmadi A.; Alanazi A.; Alanazi R.
Article.Abstract: Fetal development is a crucial stage in prenatal care, necessitating the prompt detection of abnormalities in ultrasound scans to ensure the well-being of both the fetus and the expectant mother. Medical imaging is vital for identifying fetal abnormalities. However, despite considerable advancements in ultrasound technology, accurately identifying abnormalities in prenatal images remains challenging, often requiring significant time and expertise from healthcare specialists. AI is transforming medical imaging for diagnosis, with deep learning (DL) leading image analysis due to its exceptional pattern recognition, specifically in domains like fetal imaging, where several studies demonstrate DL aids in detecting abnormalities and measurements, supporting clinicians beyond human capabilities by automating intricate tasks and offering faster, more precise insights. In this article, we concentrate on the development of an Adaptive Transformer-Based Deep Learning Model for Fetal Abnormal Health and Status Assessment (ATDL-FAHSA) using Ultrasound Imagery. The main objective of the ATDL-FAHSA approach is to accurately classify fetal health, demonstrating significant potential for clinical deployment to prevent maternal and child mortality, thereby contributing to improved prenatal care outcomes. Initially, an input images endure systematic pre-processing, involving noise reduction, intensity normalization, and contrast enhancement to improve the clarity and diagnostic quality of fetal anatomical structures. Subsequently, deep spatial features are extracted using the ConvNeXtV2 model, enabling the capture of fine-grained morphological patterns from ultrasound images. For the classification process, a hybrid deep learning architecture utilizing an attention-driven DL network is employed. The proposed ATDL-FAHSA architecture adaptively merges convolutional and transformer-based reasoning, resulting in robust performance for both abnormality detection. The simulation analysis of the ATDL-FAHSA model has been performed employing the Ultrasound Fetus Dataset from the Kaggle repository. Extensive comparative result reports the encouraging performance of the ATDL-FAHSA approach over recent state-of-the-art models.

Article.Title: Production and characterization of exopolysaccharide and whole-genome analysis of Leuconostoc mesenteroides LmPQ23 isolated from pulque
Article.Authors: Cedeño-Hernández L.; Loera-Muro A.; Escobedo-Fregoso C.; Ramírez-Sánchez I.; Chávez-Vela N.; Morales-Domínguez J.
Article.Abstract: Leuconostoc mesenteroides is a lactic acid bacterium recognized for exopolysaccharide (EPS) production, but comparative studies have revealed substantial strain-level diversity in biosynthetic potential and functional traits. Despite its ecological relevance in pulque, integrated genomic and functional characterization of native isolates remains limited. A native pulque isolate, L. mesenteroides named LmPQ23, was characterized using comparative genomics and phenotypic analyses. Genome sequencing confirmed its taxonomic identity and revealed an open pangenome, with strain-specific and accessory genes associated with carbohydrate metabolism, stress tolerance, and environmental adaptation. No acquired antibiotic resistance genes were identified, supporting the biotechnological safety of the strain. As complementary evidence of its biotechnological potential, comparative genomic analysis identified an expanded repertoire of five GH70 glucansucrases, the largest identified among the L. mesenteroides genomes analyzed, and antiSMASH detected a class IIb bacteriocin-related biosynthetic cluster. Under selected conditions, LmPQ23 produced 37.4 g/L of EPS which was structurally characterized as a branched dextran-type α-glucan with approximately 18% α-(1→3) branching. The cell-free supernatant exhibited antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative indicator bacteria, associated with organic acids and a low-molecular-weight peptide fraction. GC-MS analysis identified several volatile metabolites, including compounds previously reported to exhibit antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insecticidal activities. LmPQ23 combines an open pangenome, an absence of acquired antibiotic resistance genes, an expanded glucansucrase repertoire, high dextran-producing capacity, and antimicrobial potential, highlighting the genomic and functional diversity of pulque-associated L. mesenteroides . This integrated genomic and phenotypic characterization supports the biotechnological safety and potential of LmPQ23 and provides a foundation for future characterization of its glucansucrases and antimicrobial peptides.

Article.Title: Small-world organization as a representation-dependent signature of nonlinear dynamics in biological time series
Article.Authors: Alves C.; Bellone C.; Hoelter J.; Thielemann C.; Sallum L.; do Rosário R.; Toutain T.; Kalbasi A.; Campanharo A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Small-world topology is usually interpreted in connectivity networks, but graphs derived from individual time series have different node and edge semantics. We examined how three common time-series representations—Quantile Graphs (QG), Gramian Angular Fields (GAF), and Markov Transition Fields (MTF)—shape the topology inferred from single-signal data. We analyzed stochastic and deterministic synthetic series, including a logistic-map benchmark spanning periodic, chaotic, and period-3-window regimes, together with functional magnetic resonance imaging, magnetoencephalography, calcium imaging, simulated microelectrode-array recordings, and physiological signals. For the primary biological analyses, each representation was converted to a Q -node undirected binary graph at fixed 10% density, and small-worldness was quantified relative to degree-preserving random graphs. Small-world classification was not representation invariant: QG most often yielded $$\sigma >1$$ , GAF was below the $$\sigma =1$$ criterion in most datasets, and MTF showed mixed or near-threshold behavior. In the logistic-map benchmark and an iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier transform surrogate analysis, topology depended jointly on dynamics and representation. These results show that small-world organization in graphs derived from individual time series is a representation-dependent signature of nonlinear temporal structure rather than a universal property of biological dynamics.

Article.Title: Development of biphoton entangled light spectroscopy (BELS) using Bell pairs
Article.Authors: Desai V.; Armitage N.
Article.Abstract: We introduce Biphoton Entangled Light Spectroscopy (BELS), a quantum spectroscopic technique that employs polarization-entangled Bell pairs and two-photon interference to probe material properties. In BELS, the measured signal arises not from single-photon intensities but from changes in the joint polarization and path correlations of biphoton Bell pairs transmitted through or scattered by a sample and analyzed via cross-channel coincidences. A key concept of BELS is the explicit mapping between Jones matrix operations and transformations within the Bell-state manifold. Optical elements that are equivalent under classical polarization optics can produce qualitatively distinct signatures in the coincidence landscape when interrogated with entangled photons. We demonstrate that linear birefringence and Faraday rotation generate orthogonal admixtures of Bell states, yielding experimentally distinguishable coincidence channels within a single measurement. We measure birefringence in an anisotropic dielectric and Faraday rotation in Tb 3 Ga 5 O 12 . By mapping the changes to the photonic entanglement, BELS establishes a new framework for future entanglement enhanced spectroscopy–a potentially powerful approach in characterizing quantum materials, nanophotonic devices, and light–matter interactions perhaps eventually at a fundamentally quantum level.

Article.Title: Fabrication of a novel silicone-matrix composite reinforced with a 3D printed polymeric lattices and graphene oxide
Article.Authors: Derakhshandi R.; Seyedraoufi Z.; Mirzavand K.
Article.Abstract: Interpenetrating phase composites (IPCs) combining architected lattice structures with multifunctional matrices offer significant potential for lightweight and energy-absorbing applications. In this study, IPC specimens were fabricated by integrating 3D-printed lattice frameworks with a silicone matrix reinforced by graphene oxide (GO). The lattices were produced via fused filament fabrication and subsequently infiltrated with a silicone–GO mixture to form a continuous interpenetrating structure. The influence of GO content, lattice inclusion, and compression speed (2.5, 5, and 7.5 mm/min) on the microstructural characteristics and mechanical performance of the composites was systematically investigated. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed effective matrix infiltration into the lattice architecture and visually and apparently uniform dispersion of GO within the silicone phase, promoting strong interfacial bonding and improved load transfer. Microstructural observations indicated that GO sheets contributed to crack deflection and deformation stability, while the lattice framework provided a continuous load-bearing network. Mechanical characterization through uniaxial compression testing demonstrated a substantial enhancement in performance for lattice-reinforced specimens compared with matrix-only samples. Yield strength increased from approximately 0.65–2.10 MPa in NL specimens to about 18 MPa in lattice-containing IPCs, accompanied by a significant rise in toughness and energy absorption capacity. Stress–strain and force–displacement analyses showed that the IPCs exhibited distinct elastic, plateau, and densification regions characteristic of architected cellular materials. Increasing compression speed further improved post-yield resistance and energy absorption due to strain-rate sensitivity of the silicone–GO matrix. The results confirm that the mechanical behavior of IPCs is governed by a synergistic interaction between microstructure and architecture, where GO enhances interfacial reinforcement and the lattice structure controls stiffness and load-bearing efficiency. The developed IPC system demonstrates promising potential for applications requiring lightweight structures with high strength and energy absorption capability.

Article.Title: Improvement of chaotic maps for k-NN classification using Lévy-flight whale optimization: multiple dataset comparison
Article.Authors: Mat A.; Gündüz M.
Article.Abstract: Metaheuristic feature selection is frequently used to improve distance-based classification on tabular datasets, yet the empirical value of adding chaotic dynamics to already enhanced optimizers remains unclear. This paper presents a controlled multi-dataset benchmark of a binary Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) feature selector combined with Lévy-flight refinement and a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifier. Four fixed chaotic-map pairs, namely Logistic+Cubic, Sine+Sinusoidal, Singer+Circle and Iterative+Tent, are then applied to the same selected feature subspace and evaluated against the WOA+Lévy + k-NN baseline. The experiments use eight publicly available tabular datasets covering diagnostic, voting, signal-processing, combinatorial and chemical classification problems. The evaluation uses repeated stratified cross-validation, train-fold-only min-max scaling, a fixed k = 3 classifier, and non-parametric statistical testing with Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank and Holm-Bonferroni procedures. The results do not support a general claim that chaotic-map combinations improve the baseline. On the contrary, the WOA+Lévy + k-NN baseline obtains the best average rank for both accuracy and macro-F1. The Friedman test indicates a statistically detectable difference among methods for macro-F1, but the rank pattern favors the baseline, and no chaotic-map pair significantly outperforms it after Holm correction. Dataset-level analysis shows that chaotic transformations can occasionally help, as in Tic-tac-toe, but they more often degrade or leave performance unchanged, especially on Breast-cancer-wisconsin, Ionosphere, Sonar, WDBC and Wine. The contribution is therefore a reproducible boundary-condition analysis rather than a claim of a universally superior optimizer. Although the benchmark includes a raw k-NN control, a standard WOA ablation, and an EvoMapX-inspired population evolution analysis, its conclusions remain limited to the evaluated post-selection integration strategy and the four representative fixed chaotic-map pairs rather than all possible chaotic optimization designs.

Article.Title: Pre-treatment prediction of EBV-DNA status in nasopharyngeal carcinoma using CE-T1WI radiomics combined with clinical features: a multi-sequence MRI radiomics study
Article.Authors: Li W.; Hou J.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA is a critical biomarker for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) diagnosis, treatment response, and prognosis. Noninvasive pre-treatment prediction of EBV-DNA status using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics may provide additional clinical value. We aimed to develop and validate an MRI radiomics-based model for predicting EBV-DNA status in NPC patients using a fully leakage-free, nested validation framework. A total of 277 NPC patients with complete multi-sequence MRI (T1WI, T2WI, and contrast-enhanced T1WI [CE-T1WI]) and EBV-DNA measurements were retrospectively enrolled from a public dataset, and 2553 radiomics features were extracted per patient. Feature stability was assessed with the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC > = 0.75) in 30 patients with repeated tumor segmentation. The complete modeling pipeline—median imputation, z-score standardization, feature filtering, LASSO feature selection, penalized logistic regression fitting, and decision-threshold selection—was nested within repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (10 repeats), so that every outer test fold remained fully unseen. Multicollinearity among clinical variables was assessed using variance inflation factors (VIF), and a parsimonious clinical baseline (age, sex, N stage, VCA-IgA status) was prespecified. Robustness to scanner and voxel-geometry heterogeneity was evaluated using scanner-stratified analyses, isotropic 1-mm voxel resampling, and ComBat harmonization fitted within training folds only. Calibration was optimized with Platt recalibration within folds. Incremental value over the clinical baseline was assessed with the DeLong test, Brier score, and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Prognostic value was evaluated in 251 patients with available progression-free survival (PFS) using multivariable Cox regression with multiplicity control. The combined CE-T1WI radiomics–clinical model achieved a leakage-free area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.801 (95% CI: 0.742–0.854), significantly exceeding the parsimonious clinical baseline (AUC 0.628, 95% CI: 0.563–0.691; ΔAUC 0.173, 95% CI: 0.104–0.242; DeLong p < 0.001) and improving the Brier score from 0.196 to 0.178; IDI 0.052 (95% CI: 0.027–0.078, p < 0.001). It outperformed the single-sequence CE-T1WI (AUC 0.694), multi-sequence (AUC 0.671), T2WI (AUC 0.636), and T1WI (AUC 0.587) models. Performance was consistent across scanner subgroups (AUCs 0.762–0.812), with 1-mm isotropic resampling (AUC 0.792), and with ComBat harmonization (AUC 0.788). After Platt recalibration, the calibration slope was 1.00 (95% CI: 0.81–1.19), and decision curve analysis showed net benefit over threshold probabilities of approximately 0.10–0.55. The multi-sequence Rad-score was independently associated with PFS (adjusted hazard ratio per 1-SD increment 1.38, 95% CI: 1.05–1.82, p = 0.021). With leakage-free nested validation, CE-T1WI radiomics combined with a parsimonious clinical baseline provided moderate, scanner-robust discrimination of pre-treatment EBV-DNA status in NPC, with established incremental value over clinical variables alone. External validation in independent cohorts is still required before any clinical application.

Article.Title: Dispersion transition entropy: dual-modal feature fusion based on global attention mechanism for time series feature representation
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Dong W.; Lin J.; Zhang X.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A new entropy measure-Dispersion transition entropy (DTE) has been proposed for the analysis of complex dynamic signals in mechanical fault diagnosis. The DTE method combines the static pattern analysis of Dispersion Entropy (Normalization cumulative distribution function-based symbolic mapping) with the dynamic interval characterization of Global ordinal pattern attention entropy (GOPAE), enabling enhanced feature extraction under noisy conditions. Through systematic evaluations on simulated signals (AR (1), Chirp, MIX) and real-world vibration data (bearings and planetary gears), DTE demonstrates superior stability and discriminative power compared to six existing entropy methods. Experimental results show that the DTE-ELM framework achieves the highest classification accuracy (93.7% mean) with the lowest standard deviation (1.2%), while maintaining competitive computational efficiency (3.88 s). The proposed method provides an effective solution for improving fault detection performance in rotating machinery.

Article.Title: Morphological classification of radiographic insertional enthesopathies of the nuchal ligament in asymptomatic show jumping horses
Article.Authors: Turlejska M.; Michlik-Połczyńska K.; Kozdrowski R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Insertional desmopathy of the nuchal ligament in sport horses remains a poorly characterized orthopaedic phenomenon, with limited and inconsistent terminology in the scientific literature. This study investigated the prevalence, morphology, and localization of nuchal ligament enthesopathies in a cohort of actively competing horses using clinical and radiological assessments. Pathological changes were detected in 91% of evaluated individuals, predominantly as asymptomatic lesions identified during routine imaging. Two principal morphological types were discerned: rounded and coronoid-like bone formations, with comparable distribution among sexes and age groups. Lesion localization most commonly encompassed both the upper and lower regions of the occipital plate but was rarely confined to ligament attachment alone. No correlation was found between lesion size, shape, or location and sex, breed, or age, but horses over 7 years have greater length, depth, sum, and surface area of the new bone formations and more frequently display lesions in both the upper and lower positions than only in the upper. None of the studied horses exhibited related clinical symptoms. The functional relevance of these changes remains to be established, suggesting the necessity for long-term follow-up and further biomechanical investigation to determine potential effects on equine performance.

Article.Title: Technical validation of label-efficient blueberry instance segmentation under extreme annotation scarcity
Article.Authors: Kang M.; Zhang Y.; Zeng X.; Jin H.
Article.Abstract: Pseudo-label selection becomes particularly fragile under extreme annotation scarcity because confidence-based filtering can reject low-confidence masks that remain valid instance hypotheses. We address this problem with a label-efficient blueberry instance-segmentation pipeline that combines image-adaptive teacher-confidence filtering with a geometry-based Rescue mechanism. The adaptive branch accommodates image-level variation in teacher scores, while Rescue selectively reconsiders rejected candidates using task-specific mask-shape cues based on circularity and solidity. Under a 1% labeled protocol on the Mega Blueberry benchmark, Adaptive+Rescue achieves a mean Mask mAP50 of 0.777 ± 0.021 across three labeled-subset realizations and three student-training seeds. Relative to the matched adaptive-confidence branch, Rescue yields a mean paired improvement of +0.0241 Mask mAP50, with a crossed-bootstrap 95% confidence interval of [0.0020, 0.0416]. A ground-truth-linked audit further shows that 95.08% of the 2,478 Rescue-only masks match annotated instances at IoU \(\ge 0.50\) . These results show that task-specific mask geometry can provide a complementary reliability signal for pseudo-label selection when confidence filtering alone is insufficient, supporting label-efficient blueberry segmentation under extreme annotation scarcity.

Article.Title: An intelligent model for managing visual comfort and building energy consumption through facade control using reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Noroozi A.; Mohammadi M.
Article.Abstract: Building facade characteristics have a significant influence on energy consumption for lighting and on occupant visual comfort, yet these two objectives frequently conflict with each other. Increasing the amount of incoming daylight reduces energy demand while simultaneously raising the risk of glare. Most prior studies have addressed these objectives in isolation or through offline optimization, and relatively few have focused on learning an online control policy that is sensitive to both goals simultaneously. In this study, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent was designed to control a three-state building facade (closed, half-open, and open). The reward function incorporated, in addition to the Energy Use Intensity (EUI) index, an explicit penalty term for the Daylight Glare Probability (DGP) index. The model was trained on real climatic data from three cities with notably different climates: Tehran, Mashhad, and Tabriz, in order to examine the generalizability of the learned policy across diverse solar conditions. Evaluation on the test dataset showed that the trained agent reduced hourly energy use intensity from the baseline of 12 W/m² to an average of 7.7223 W/m², predicted the optimal facade state with an overall accuracy of %96.465, and brought the mean DGP index to 0.0310, compared to 0.130 in the uncontrolled scenario. A comparison with prior studies indicated that the proposed method differs from similar work in its simultaneous coverage of multiple climates within a single model and its use of online decision-making rather than post-hoc optimization. This study presents a facade control framework whose energy and glare outcomes, at this stage, hold only within the simplified simulation setting described above; extending it toward real building deployment is left for future work.

Article.Title: Green synthesis of novel acylsulfonyl hydrazide derivatives: high regioselectivity in Michael reaction
Article.Authors: Nedaei M.; Imanzadeh G.; Gholami M.; Shamkhali A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, a highly regioselective and green synthetic method was developed for the synthesis of novel N ′-alkylated acylsulfonyl hydrazide derivatives via the aza-Michael reaction between acylsulfonyl hydrazides and α,β-unsaturated esters. This reaction was carried out efficiently under solvent-free conditions at room temperature in the presence of potassium carbonate as a mild base and tetrabutylammonium bromide (TBAB) as an ionic liquid Media. A wide range of substrates, including compounds with electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents on the aromatic ring, as well as various alkyl chains in acrylate esters, were successfully converted to the corresponding products in good to excellent yields (58–88%). The method exhibited very high selectivity, directing the alkylation preferentially to the sulfonamide nitrogen atom over the amide nitrogen, which can be explained by charge distribution and stabilization effects. DFT calculations further supported this observation. The structures of all synthesized products were confirmed by IR, 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR spectroscopy, along with Mass spectroscopic data of 7c, 7f., 7i, CHN analysis of derivative 7f., and single-crystal diffraction analysis of compound 7c. This protocol provides a practical, mild, and efficient method for the synthesis of functionalized hydrazide derivatives and contributes to the advancement of green and selective methods for C–N bond formation.

Article.Title: A tiered deep learning and symbolic reasoning framework for safe, explainable disease diagnosis
Article.Authors: Khaled Ali Odhaib A.; Zaki Ali Abdulrahman Al-Maflehi R.; Gharaei N.; Gemci C.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a modular, AI-powered disease diagnosis system that combines deep learning, neuro-symbolic reasoning, and structured automation to support early, scalable, and explainable clinical decision-making. Built upon the large-scale DDXPlus dataset, the system processes over one million patient records into standardized, multi-hot encoded vectors representing binary symptoms, normalized age, and sex, and addresses overlapping symptom profiles by stratifying diseases into three tiers—high, medium, and low symptom-overlap tiers—using Jaccard similarity. High-overlap tiers contain fewer but more symptomatically similar diseases; low-overlap tiers contain more diseases with distinct profiles. The core diagnostic model is a residual multilayer perceptron (MLP), trained separately for each tier with transfer learning, class weighting, label smoothing, and tier-specific loss masking to improve generalization and mitigate class imbalance, while a post-inference neuro-symbolic safety layer enforces ICD-10-aligned clinical rules, blocking unsafe or incomplete predictions and triggering context-sensitive follow-up questions when needed. The system is deployed via a FastAPI backend and orchestrated with an n8n-based automation pipeline, where a large language model (LLM) acts solely as a routing agent to ensure deterministic and auditable logic flows, enabling flexible deployment across telemedicine platforms, triage tools, and digital health assistants. By integrating symbolic reasoning with data-driven models in a fully automated pipeline, this approach advances AI-assisted diagnosis toward more trustworthy, interpretable, and clinically viable solutions.

Article.Title: Nceh1 protects against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury by suppressing oxidative stress and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Wang B.; Yang B.; Qin M.; Xu Y.; Li K.; Zhong S.; Yu M.
Article.Abstract: Our previous research found that expression of Nceh1 in cardiac tissue decreased obviously in the myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury model, but the relationship between Nceh1 and MI/R damage has not been observed. In this study, 933 coronary artery disease (CAD) patients were enrolled, DNA methylation status was detected with an Illumina 850 K chip, and the patients were followed up. We upregulated expression of Nceh1 in MI/R-induced cardiomyocyte injury models in vivo and in vitro to observe whether Nceh1 regulated myocardial injury. The results demonstrated that DNA methylation of cg14338526 was significantly positively associated with the risk of death CAD patients, moreover, pearson correlation analysis revealed that DNA methylation level of cg14338526 was negatively associated with the mRNA level of Nceh1 , suggesting that expression of Nceh1 transcriptional levels inversely predicted CAD mortality risk. By applying rat MI/R model and cardiomyocyte injury model of H9C2 cells, the experimental evidence demonstrated that Nceh1 overexpression markedly attenuated MI/R injury through suppression of oxidative stress (OS) and apoptotic pathways. In order to investigate the mechanism of how Nceh1 inhibits OS and apoptosis, according to the result of RNA sequencing, our results showed that the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling activity significantly enhanced, overexpression of Nceh1 activated the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. H9C2 cells were pretreated with Nrf2/HO-1 pathway inhibitor ML-385, the results demonstrated that ML−385 abolished the protective effects of Nceh1 overexpression, as evidenced by decreased cell survival and increased OS and apoptosis. In conclusion, Nceh1 suppresses OS and apoptosis via Nrf2/HO−1 activation, thereby attenuating MI/R injury.

Article.Title: Intelligent analysis and interpretation of coffee production of Koraput district of Eastern India
Article.Authors: Dash A.; Rath A.; Mishra M.; Kumar B.; Panda G.; Sahoo J.
Article.Abstract: Coffee has become an important cash crop for tribal farmers in the highlands of Koraput district in Odisha, Eastern India. Its production, however, varies widely from year to year, which makes planning and support difficult for district agencies. This study analyses twenty years of block-level coffee records (ten administrative blocks, 2006 to 2025) from Koraput district and asks a practical question: can the productivity type of a block in a given year be discovered without labels, and can that type then be used to predict whether the block will record a high-production year? To answer it, we develop a two-part procedure that combines cluster-then-classify (CTC) and cluster-augmented features (CAF). In the CTC stage, block-year records are clustered on three agronomic ratios, namely yield per hectare, export ratio and productivity per farmer, which yields three stable performance tiers. A bootstrap analysis gives a mean adjusted Rand index of 0.77, and a supervised model recovers the tier of an unseen record with a macro F1 of 0.79. In the CAF stage, the tier label is fed back as an input to a classifier that predicts high-production block-years. Adding this single categorical feature raises F1 from about 0.27 to 0.60 on average across eight classifiers and lifts the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from roughly 0.57 to 0.83; a McNemar test confirms that the improvement is significant ( p = 0.039). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values show that tier membership ranks among the strongest contributors to the prediction, alongside lagged production. The same records also yield a four-group spatial map of the ten blocks and a six-group grouping of the twenty seasons, which together identify the district’s persistently weak blocks and its two crisis years. A cross-resolution check shows that the block- and year-level groupings agree moderately with the panel tiers in time but diverge in space, indicating that block-year panels carry information that spatial averages lose. The framework is simple, reproducible and interpretable, and it turns an unsupervised typology into an operational signal for targeting.

Article.Title: Effect of support properties on product selectivity in aqueous-phase Fischer–Tropsch synthesis over Ru catalysts
Article.Authors: Gebreyohannes T.; Park S.; Lee J.; Lee J.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: The effect of support properties on 5 wt% Ru catalysts was investigated during aqueous-phase Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) over H-ZSM-5, SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 , ZrPO x , TiO 2 , ZrO 2 , and γ-Al 2 O 3 at 150 °C using a H 2 /CO ratio of 2 and an initial pressure of 3.0 MPa. Ru/SiO 2 -Al 2 O 3 showed high activity (7.5 mol CO mol Ru −1 h −1 ) and the highest chain growth probabilities (α = 0.93) for both hydrocarbons and oxygenates. Product selectivity varied strongly with acid strength, with stronger acid sites suppressing oxygenate formation and shifting the product distribution toward hydrocarbons. Ru/H-ZSM-5 completely suppressed oxygenate formation in both aqueous and cyclohexane media and exhibited comparable normalized hydrocarbon formation rates, yielding 46.0% selectivity to jet-fuel-range paraffins (C 8 –C 16 ). Ru/H-ZSM-5 also showed the highest normalized CO consumption rate. These results demonstrate that support acid strength influences product selectivity in aqueous-phase FTS and enables selective synthesis of jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons over Ru catalysts.

Article.Title: Blue Rings reveal thermal thresholds of wood formation in Low Arctic tundra shrubs
Article.Authors: Hole G.; Büntgen U.; Buchwal A.; Rees G.; Wheeler H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low Arctic tundra shrubs experience short growing seasons, prolonged cool conditions, and episodic cold extremes, but the effects of these events on wood tissue formation remain poorly understood. Here we identify thermal thresholds associated with lignification processes in two dominant shrub taxa ( Alnus alnobetula and Salix spp.) along a 68–69°N transect in northwestern Canada. Using wood anatomical indicators of incomplete secondary cell wall lignification (blue rings) and freezing-induced cell collapse (frost rings), we show that wood tissue development is sensitive to thermal stress at the beginning and end of the growing season. We identified thermal thresholds constraining shrub wood formation. Incomplete lignification resulting in blue rings was associated with cumulative August cold exposure below taxon-specific thresholds (~ 2 °C in Alnus , ~ 4 °C in Salix ) and contrasting sensitivities to cumulative cold exposure. Early growing season frost injury in some cases followed prior-year incomplete lignification. The results indicate that contrasting forms of growing-season cold stress constrain distinct phases of wood formation and highlight taxon-specific thermal limits controlling shrub growth. By quantifying climatic controls on lignification failure and frost injury, we link sub-seasonal cold extremes to specific phases of wood formation, which may shape tundra vegetation responses under ongoing Arctic climate change.

Article.Title: Diagnosing landslide segmentation across geographic clusters with limited target annotations and no access to source imagery
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Weng C.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Landslide segmentation models that perform well within their training distribution can degrade sharply when transferred to a different geographic region, limiting their reliability for rapid post-event mapping. We study this problem when the original training data are unavailable and only a small target-annotation budget is permitted. Using six geographic clusters from Sen12Landslides, we separately probe decision-threshold calibration, trainable parameter scope, annotation and optimization budgets, and target-unlabelled adaptation. Three independently trained source chains obtain mean positive-class pixel $$F_1$$ scores of 0.181, 0.199, and 0.180 on matched support-excluded query pools. Oracle scalar thresholds selected using query labels improve these scores to 0.221, 0.256, and 0.212, whereas BN-clean decoder-plus-head fine-tuning reaches 0.199, 0.220, and 0.203 and full-network fine-tuning reaches 0.260, 0.289, and 0.270. The paired gains obtained by additionally opening the encoder-like path are 0.061, 0.069, and 0.067, with positive cluster-level differences in five, six, and five of six clusters. Across the tested prevalence-preserving sampling regimes, larger support sets are associated with higher but heterogeneous mean scores; because support identities and support-excluded query pools differ across K , this comparison does not isolate the causal effect of tile count alone. Under the historical independent-overlap component convention, mean patch-component recall increases from 0.116 to 0.205, with a corresponding false-positive cost. Class-balanced pseudo-label self-training also raises the mean for all three source chains, whereas entropy minimization collapses positive-class prediction. In a single-seed CAS analysis, one of two full-network variants ranks highest within the finite candidate set for each of five held-out events. Together, these results identify encoder-inclusive full-network updating as the strongest supervised repair path on average among the evaluated interventions and establish a reproducible diagnostic and annotation-budget analysis for source-free cross-cluster landslide segmentation.

Article.Title: Controlling the diffusion of fullerene-wheeled nanovehicles using hybrid curved substrates
Article.Authors: Bakhtiari M.; Fathi M.; Shamloo A.; Ghasemi S.; Majidi H.; Ahmadian M.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, several types of nanocars have been developed, demonstrating significant capabilities in molecular transport, bottom-up assembly, and other mechanical tasks. This study proposes an approach for converting the diffusive movement of nanocars into guided motion by adding a gold impurity line to a silver cylindrical substrate in which the width of this gold line, depending on the angle of the arc facing it, varies between 120°, 150°, and 180° from the circumference of the complete cylinder; and the movement of C60, nanotruck, and nanocar on these substrates is investigated. The findings show that gold impurity acts as a repellent barrier, especially at 150°, effectively preventing C60 from entering the silver region even under high-temperature conditions, though the entry eventually occurred at 600 K. Nevertheless, a sufficiently large gold impurity acted as an impermeable obstacle for both the nanocar and nanotruck even at a high temperature of 600 K on 180° and 120°, respectively. The considered geometries effectively restricted deviations from the desired path. Furthermore, the effect of varying impurity line thickness is studied. The results reveal that adjusting the impurity line thickness leads to long-range motion and sufficient diffusion coefficient. The 150° and 180° substrates are optimal for C60 and nanocar across various temperatures, while the nanotruck performs best on the 120° substrate due to its rigid chassis. The presence of impurities within the substrate significantly limits the range of motion in nanomachines by acting as a repellent obstacle or snatching trap.

Article.Title: Experimental evaluation of a remedial educational program for improving spelling skills among students with learning disabilities
Article.Authors: Alamri A.
Article.Abstract: This study examined an experimental evaluation of a remedial educational program designed to improve spelling skills among third- and fourth-grade students with learning disabilities (LDs). A randomized controlled experimental design was employed, assigning 50 students to an experimental group ( n = 25) that received a structured remedial spelling intervention and a control group ( n = 25) that received regular classroom instruction. Before and after the intervention, students completed a standardized, validated spelling test. The 20-session remedial program included explicit rule-based teaching, phonological awareness activities, multisensory learning strategies, and immediate corrective feedback. Postintervention analysis showed that the experimental group demonstrated significant improvement over the control group, with significant reductions in phonetic, omission, and substitution errors. These results underscore the importance of specific, evidence-based interventions for students with LDs and inform educational practice and future research.

Article.Title: Optimizing soil fertility, malt barley yield, and economic returns through integrated compost and nitrogen fertilization: yield, soil, and economic analysis in the Ethiopian highlands
Article.Authors: Wole A.; Nebiyu A.; Ousman Y.; Agegnehu G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malt barley is an important crop in the Ethiopian highlands, where productivity is challenged by soil fertility decline, inappropriate agronomic practices, and high dependence on inorganic fertilizers. This study evaluated the effects of compost and inorganic N fertilizer application on yield and yield components, soil chemical properties, and economic returns of malt barley during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons in the central highlands of Ethiopia. The trial was arranged in a randomized complete block design with factorial combinations of five N rates (0, 23, 46, 69, and 92 kg N ha -1 ) and four compost rates (0, 2.5, 5, and 7.5 t ha -1 ), with three replications. The results showed that integrated application of organic compost and mineral N fertilizer significantly increased yield and yield components, and improved selected post-harvest soil chemical properties, including soil pH, available phosphorus, total nitrogen, total organic carbon, organic matter, and cation exchange capacity, compared with the control treatment. The combined application of compost and mineral nitrogen fertilizer significantly increased days to 50% heading, plant height, seeds per spike, above-ground biomass yield, straw yield, and harvest index, and grain yield compared with the control treatment. The 2023 growing season increased plant height, seeds per spike, grain yield and above-ground biomass yield, and total nitrogen content and available phosphorus, while the 2022 growing season delayed phenological parameters such as days to 50% heading and days to 90% physiological maturity and suppressed overall productivity, demonstrating that seasonal conditions strongly affected treatment performance. However, integrated application of compost and mineral nitrogen fertilization consistently improved malt barley productivity across both growing seasons. The highest grain yield value (3856.59 kg ha -1 ) was obtained from the application of 7.5 t compost ha -1 + 92 kg N ha -1 of fertilizer rates, showing a 143% yield advantage over control and a 24% increase over sole mineral N application. The economic analysis identified the combination of 7.5 t ha -1 compost with 69 kg N ha -1 fertilizer as economically advantageous, giving the highest net benefit and marginal rate of return. Overall, integrated nutrient management significantly enhanced malt barley productivity, selected soil chemical properties, and economic returns within the conditions of the current study. However, the results are limited by a single site over two growing seasons, lack of long-term soil assessments, and reliance on local market prices for economic analysis.

Article.Title: Integrating artificial intelligence and quantum chemistry for sustainable pharmaceutical retrosynthesis
Article.Authors: Raef N.; Hamedi F.
Article.Abstract: In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) has brought about major changes to computer-assisted retrosynthetic planning; nevertheless, currently developed approaches are mainly oriented towards the prediction of reactions rather than taking both mechanistic plausibility and sustainability of such processes into account. In the current work, we introduce a clear-cut multi-criteria computational approach that combines transformer-based retrosynthetic prediction with density functional theory (DFT) computations and green chemistry considerations in one decision-making approach for sustainable drug design and synthesis planning. The novelty of the approach is based on the quantitative combination of these three aspects. Justification for the selection of ibuprofen as the primary focus for case studies is provided. When used along with quantum chemistry calculations of activation energy, HOMO-LUMO gap and Fukui indices, AI-assisted filtration reduced the number of potential reactions. To evaluate the environmental performance of this pathway, atom economy, process mass index (PMI), and E-factor were all taken into account. The optimized pathway had a score of 0.94, atom economy of 87.3%, PMI of 16.8, and E-factor of 12.6 in total. The ranking of the pathways did not change with 10% variations of the weights of the corresponding criteria, which was confirmed by sensitivity analysis. Rather than simply proposing a novel retrosynthesis method, this work presents an established methodology that includes AI prediction, mechanistic validation and sustainability impact assessment in synthetic pathway selection.

Article.Title: A sustainable techno-economic off-grid energy systems feasibility and power generation performance analysis under various solar tracking configurations in different regions of Bangladesh
Article.Authors: Nazir K.; Shimul A.; Sharif M.; Khan T.; Kabir R.; Biswas B.; Islam A.; Rahman M.; Solre G.; Benghanem M.; Elboughdiri N.
Article.Abstract: The dependable electrification of off-grid communities in Bangladesh continues to be a significant challenge, with the techno-economic feasibility of decentralized solar photovoltaic (PV) systems heavily impacted by the selection of solar tracking configurations and notable regional variations in irradiance. This study assesses a photovoltaic-based off-grid hybrid energy system in five sample regions of Bangladesh, especially for presuming the community exhibits a diurnal peak pattern primarily driven by daytime activities, aiming to determine the configuration that provides the optimal combination of economic, technical, and environmental performance. Three solar tracking systems; Horizontal Continuous Adjustment (HCA), Vertical Continuous Adjustment (VCA), and Two-Axis Tracking (TA) are methodically evaluated in comparison to a Fixed Tilt (FT) baseline. The optimization systems were performed using the HOMER Pro with an emphasis on power generation performance analysis in the representative regions, with evaluation based on Net Present Cost (NPC), Cost of Energy (COE), Return on Investment (ROI), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), payback period, capacity deficit, unmet load, surplus energy, and renewable energy portion. The findings consistently indicate that the FT Case I (PV-Diesel-Battery) configuration is the most sustainable option across all five regions, achieving the lowest NPC ($ 456,000–480,000) and COE ($ 0.207–0.218/kWh), alongside robust investment metrics (ROI: 27–30%; IRR ≈ 30%; payback period: 3.0–3.5 years). The arrangement exhibits substantial operational reliability, with a capacity shortage (CS) of roughly 0.07%, an unmet load (UL) of about 0.01%, and a moderate excess energy (EE) ranging from 14 to 24%, signifying adequate system sizing. A continuous renewable proportion of 75–85% yields significant emission savings compared to traditional diesel-based systems. The results offer quantitative direction for the implementation of economical and dependable solar hybrid systems in off-grid areas of Bangladesh.

Article.Title: Association of the TyHGB index with incident stroke in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a 10-year prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Wan Q.
Article.Abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of disability and death among middle-aged and older adults in China. We investigated the association between baseline triglyceride/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose-body mass index (TyHGB) and incident stroke in 6956 Chinese adults aged ≥ 40 years who were free of stroke at baseline and followed for 10 years in the Luzhou component of the China Cardiometabolic Disease and Cancer Cohort (4C) Study. Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline analysis, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. During follow-up, 342 incident strokes occurred. In the fully adjusted model, the highest versus lowest TyHGB quartile was associated with higher incident stroke risk (HR = 1.843, 95% CI 1.289–2.636; P for trend = 0.003), and each 1-unit increase was associated with a 5.6% higher risk (HR = 1.056, 95% CI 1.015–1.100). Restricted cubic splines indicated a positive, approximately linear association (P for overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.276). Stand-alone discrimination was modest but slightly higher for TyHGB than TyG or BMI (AUC 0.598 vs 0.559 and 0.560). TyHGB may provide complementary metabolic information for stroke risk assessment.

Article.Title: Examining weather impacts on urban travel demand in Nanjing, China during the COVID-19 pandemic
Article.Authors: Dong J.; Li N.; Song J.; Zhang F.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Accurately characterizing variation in public transport demand is important for urban traffic management, especially when weather conditions and public-health disruptions jointly reshape travel patterns. Using monthly transportation statistics and weather observations for Nanjing, China, from February 2019 to December 2022, this study examines associations between weather conditions and passenger flow across buses, taxis, and the Rail Transit System (RTS) during the COVID-19 period. Random Forest (RF) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-based interpretation were used as exploratory tools to examine the relative associations of weather variables with passenger-flow variation. The results show that RTS remained the dominant travel mode in Nanjing, followed by buses and taxis, and that passenger flow for all three modes declined sharply at the onset of the pandemic before gradually recovering. During the study period, temperature generally increased, whereas other weather variables showed changes in varying directions. Although the importance rankings derived from the RF and SHAP methods are not entirely consistent, both identify temperature and precipitation as important weather factors influencing changes in traffic demand. In addition, the pandemic was associated with a marked shift in modal structure: before the pandemic, passenger-flow shares were relatively balanced across modes, whereas afterward taxi and RTS accounted for a larger share and bus ridership declined. These findings provide may offer a preliminary reference for adaptive transport planning.

Article.Title: Floquet spectral–spatial modulation using Fourier contours and windowing for multi‑beam control in next‑generation wireless systems
Article.Authors: Hamdi B.; Aloui R.; Aldalbahi A.; Llamas-Garro I.; Delleji T.; Mhatli S.; Zairi H.; Aguili T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a unified approach for modeling and synthesizing multi-beam radiation patterns in large, strongly-coupled antenna arrays. The method combines Floquet spectral analysis with Fourier-based contour windowing to efficiently handle both regular and arbitrarily-shaped array layouts. Starting from a single unit cell described by periodic (Floquet) boundary conditions, the electromagnetic response of the entire array is reconstructed via spectral modulation and inverse Fourier transformation. The formulation is solver-agnostic and compatible with numerical methods including the Method of Moments, its equivalent circuit variant, the Finite-Difference Time-Domain, and the Finite Element Method. The proposed technique is particularly suited for emerging systems including 6G communication, Massive MIMO, automotive radars, and IoT networks, where beam-forming, beam-steering, and low-cost computation are critical.

Article.Title: Prediction of overall survival in patients with colorectal cancer using baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics
Article.Authors: Wang N.; Zhu H.; Dai M.; Liu Y.; Jing F.; Sun Y.; Zhang J.; Wang J.; Zhao X.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To predict 3-year overall survival (OS) in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) using baseline 18 F-FDG PET/CT radiomics. This retrospective study entrolled 166 patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) , who were randomly assigned into a training cohort ( n = 133) and an internal random hold-out validation cohort ( n = 33). The optimum subset was screened out from 2446 radiomic features via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression. Significant clinical characteristics identified by Cox analysis were combined with radiomic score (Radscore) to construct a combined prediction model. The Akaike information criterion (AIC), Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were applied to evaluate model performance. The complex model had the lowest AIC, highest C-index with optimal efficacy across both cohorts. In the training cohort, its AUC was superior to the single radiomics (0.877 vs. 0.784, p = 0.027) and clinical model (0.877 vs. 0.774, p < 0.001), with no significant difference between the two alone (0.784 vs. 0.774, p = 0.878). In the internal validation cohort, its AUC differed significantly from the clinical model (0.896 vs. 0.822, p = 0.012). By contrast, no significant differences were found between the radiomics model and the complex model (0.707 vs. 0.896, p = 0.094), nor between the radiomics model and the clinical model (0.707 vs. 0.822, p = 0.400). Baseline PET/CT radiomics enables effective prediction of 3-year OS in patients with CRC. The complex model could further improve the predictive efficacy of the clinical model alone.

Article.Title: Dapagliflozin-metformin combination enhances oocyte quality and reproductive outcomes in PCOS patients undergoing IVF/ICSI: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Fakhreddin M.; Forghani F.; Jahantigh D.; Salahi E.; Mousavi M.
Article.Abstract: To determine whether eight weeks of dapagliflozin plus metformin pretreatment improves oocyte quality, increases BMP15 and GDF9 expression, and enhances pregnancy outcomes in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI). In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 103 women with PCOS were screened and 92 randomized to four groups: placebo, metformin (500 mg BID), dapagliflozin (5 mg BID, total 10 mg/day), or combination. After eight weeks of treatment, 80 patients (20 per group) completed the study. Primary outcomes were mature oocyte count and good-quality embryo count. Secondary outcomes included clinical pregnancy rate and metabolic parameters. For primary endpoints, significance was set at P < 0.025; for key secondary endpoints, nominal P < 0.05 was considered significant; exploratory correlation analyses are reported with nominal P-values without correction. The combination group showed significantly lower HOMA-IR (3.66 ± 0.55 vs. 4.64 ± 0.40, P < 0.001) and total testosterone (0.71 ± 0.26 vs. 1.34 ± 0.43 nmol/L, P < 0.001) versus placebo. Combination therapy also significantly increased BMP15 and GDF9 expression ( P < 0.001), mature oocytes (12.85 ± 4.05 vs. 6.35 ± 4.05, P < 0.001), good-quality embryos (5.35 ± 2.40 vs. 1.65 ± 1.25, P < 0.001), and clinical pregnancy rate (75.0% vs. 15.0%, P < 0.001). Intention-to-treat analysis confirmed these findings (62.5% vs. 13.6%, P < 0.001). Nominally significant improvements were observed for BMI ( P = 0.003), waist circumference ( P = 0.012), leptin ( P = 0.004), and AMH ( P = 0.011); these should be interpreted as exploratory findings requiring confirmation. Eight-week dapagliflozin-metformin pretreatment was associated with improved metabolic profile (HOMA-IR), reduced hyperandrogenism (total testosterone), enhanced oocyte and embryo quality, higher clinical pregnancy rates, and upregulation of BMP15 and GDF9 expression in PCOS patients undergoing IVF/ICSI. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger trials with live birth data.

Article.Title: Establishment and internal-external validation of a clinical-adipometric prognostic model for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Article.Authors: Gong Y.; Abuduhalike R.; Duan D.; Mahemuti A.
Article.Abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is the reference standard for quantitative body composition assessment. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) carries a poor prognosis, but practical risk prediction tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic nomogram integrating CT‑derived body composition metrics with clinical characteristics for predicting the composite endpoint in HFpEF patients. This multicenter retrospective cohort included 459 HFpEF patients from two tertiary hospitals (January 2021-March 2023). From one center, 328 patients were randomly split 7:3 into training ( n = 232) and internal validation ( n = 96) cohorts; the other 131 patients from the second center formed the external validation cohort. The composite endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or heart-failure-related rehospitalization. Body composition parameters were extracted from T12 vertebral level CT images. Independent prognostic factors were identified via LASSO and multivariable Cox regression, then incorporated into a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by time‑dependent ROC curves, calibration plots, restricted cubic spline (RCS), decision curve analysis (DCA), and Kaplan-Meier analysis with log‑rank tests. Among 459 patients (50.11% male; mean age 61.30 ± 10.93 years), the composite endpoint occurred in 252 (54.90%) over a median follow‑up of 50.26 months. Five independent predictors were selected: fasting plasma glucose, intermuscular adipose tissue index (IMATI), logBNP, total cholesterol, and skeletal muscle index (SMI). The nomogram achieved AUCs for 2‑ and 3‑year predictions of 0.728 and 0.772 in the training cohort; 0.714 and 0.762 in internal validation; and 0.724 and 0.769 in external validation. Calibration and DCA demonstrated good fit and net benefit. RCS showed a positive association between IMATI and the composite endpoint risk and a negative association for SMI. Kaplan-Meier curves revealed significant prognostic stratification (high IMATI or low SMI associated with worse survival; low nomogram scores with better outcomes). SMI and IMATI were independent predictors. The nomogram showed favorable discriminative ability compared with the MAGGIC risk score. In conclusion, the proposed nomogram incorporating CT‑based body composition metrics and clinical factors provides robust the composite endpoint prediction in HFpEF. If prospectively validated, this tool may facilitate risk stratification and aid in identifying high‑risk patients for more intensive monitoring in future clinical practice.

Article.Title: Protective effects of trimetazidine against pembrolizumab-induced cardiac injury: biochemical and immunohistochemical evaluation
Article.Authors: Admis O.; Sezgin E.; Ozkaraca M.; Haciyeva S.; Mammadov R.; Suleyman B.; Cam S.; Suleyman H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pembrolizumab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor targeting programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1), has substantially improved cancer treatment outcomes but may induce immune-related cardiotoxicity characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Trimetazidine is a metabolic modulator with antioxidant and cardioprotective properties. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of trimetazidine against pembrolizumab-induced cardiac injury in rats. Twenty-four male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): healthy control (HG), trimetazidine (TMZ, 5 mg/kg/day), pembrolizumab (PBZ, 5 mg/kg/day), and trimetazidine plus pembrolizumab (TZPZ). The treatments were administered for seven consecutive days. At the end of the experimental period, cardiac tissues were analyzed for malondialdehyde (MDA), total glutathione (tGSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Serum cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels were determined. Oxidative DNA damage and apoptosis were evaluated immunohistochemically using 8-hydroxy-2′-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and cleaved caspase-3 staining. Pembrolizumab significantly increased cardiac MDA, IL-1β, IL-6, and serum cTnI levels, while markedly reducing tGSH, SOD, and CAT levels (all p < 0.001). Severe 8-OHdG immunopositivity and moderate caspase-3 immunopositivity were observed in the PBZ group. Trimetazidine treatment significantly reduced MDA levels and improved tGSH, SOD, and CAT levels. It also suppressed the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, reduced serum cTnI levels, and markedly decreased 8-OHdG and caspase-3 immunoreactivity (all p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between the healthy control and trimetazidine-alone groups. Trimetazidine attenuated pembrolizumab-induced cardiac injury, accompanied by reductions in oxidative stress, inflammation, oxidative DNA damage, and apoptosis. These findings suggest that trimetazidine may represent a promising adjunctive cardioprotective strategy for preventing pembrolizumab-associated cardiotoxicity. Further mechanistic and clinical studies are warranted to confirm these findings and facilitate their translation into clinical practice.

Article.Title: Effects of dietary thymol–formic acid blend on production metrics, carcass characteristics and meat quality in turkeys
Article.Authors: Champati A.; Bhanja S.; Rokade J.; Madheshwaran M.; Sonale N.; Wadajkar P.; Landge R.; Chakma J.; Choravada D.
Article.Abstract: With increasing consumer demand for safe and high-quality animal protein, poultry producers are shifting towards alternative species such as turkeys to complement the chicken production and diversify the protein source. Organic acids and essential oils have been widely evaluated as sustainable growth promoters in chicken production, replacing conventional antimicrobials that pose risks of antibiotic residues and antimicrobial resistance. This study evaluated the effects of a dietary blend of thymol (crystal powdered) and formic acid on final market live weight, feed conversion ratio (FCR), carcass traits, meat quality, and sensory attributes of turkey meat. A total of 240-day-old turkey poults were randomly assigned to six dietary treatment groups (5 replicates each) with male: female ratio kept as 1:1 per replicate and reared up to 16 weeks of market age: T1 (basal diet, BD), T2 (BD + chlortetracycline, 50 mg/kg), T3 (BD + thymol 240 mg/kg + formic acid 2.5 ml/kg), T4 (BD + thymol 360 mg/kg + formic acid 2.5 ml/kg), T5 (BD + thymol 240 mg/kg + formic acid 7.5 ml/kg), and T6 (BD + thymol 360 mg/kg + formic acid 7.5 ml/kg). Production metrics dictated a significant ( p ≤ 0.001) improvement in pre-slaughter body weight and final FCR in dietary thymol-formic acid blend treatment groups (T5 and T4) over control group. Post-slaughter evaluation revealed that thymol–formic acid supplementation ( p ≤ 0.05) improved carcass yield and cut-up parts compared to the control groups (T1 and T2). Meat quality indices, including pH, water-holding capacity, extract release volume, and drip loss, were enhanced ( p ≤ 0.05) in supplemented groups. Notably, T4 and T5 exhibited superior oxidative stability ( p ≤ 0.05), reflected by the lowest TBARS values and increased antioxidant activity (ABTS + and DPPH+ assays). Sensory evaluation further demonstrated ( p ≤ 0.05) improved juiciness and overall acceptability in the T4 and T5 groups relative to the control. In conclusion, the dietary blend T5 (Thymol 240 mg/kg + Formic acid 7.5 ml/kg) was practically most effective in enhancing carcass yield, oxidative stability, and sensory quality of turkey meat, while significantly attaining heaviest market weight with improved FCR.

Article.Title: Subjective well-being mediates and mindfulness moderates the relationship between perceived discrimination and altruistic behavior in college students with financial difficulties
Article.Authors: Xie Q.; Zhou Y.; Li J.; Wei M.
Article.Abstract: Altruistic behavior is an essential positive psychological trait for college students. College students with financial difficulties are more likely to perceive discrimination, which may decrease their altruistic behavior, hindering personal growth and social stability. Our study examined the relationship between perceived discrimination and altruistic behavior among college students with financial difficulties, while also exploring the mediating role of subjective well-being and the moderating role of trait mindfulness. We conducted a cross-sectional survey using the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale, Index of Well-Being, Perceived Discrimination Questionnaire, and Philosophy of Human Nature Scale, collecting data from 1201 Chinese college students who are experiencing financial difficulties. Results indicated that: (1) Perceived discrimination significantly negatively predicts altruistic behavior; (2) Subjective well-being plays a mediating role between the perceived discrimination and altruistic behavior; (3) Trait mindfulness moderates the mediating role of subjective well-being in the relationship between perceived discrimination and altruistic behavior, with a weaker mediating effect observed when individuals have higher levels of trait mindfulness. This study validated the relationship between perceived discrimination and altruistic behavior among college students with financial difficulties, along with the mediating role of subjective well-being and the moderating role of trait mindfulness, thereby providing theoretical and empirical insights for deepening the understanding and promoting the altruistic behavior of this population.

Article.Title: Comprehensive techno-economic and environmental assessment of sawdust–polypropylene co-pyrolysis adsorbent for Cu²⁺ adsorption at laboratory scale
Article.Authors: Wongcharee S.; Kanjana W.
Article.Abstract: Co-pyrolysis of sawdust and waste polypropylene represents an avenue for valorizing residual lignocellulosic biomass and non-recyclable plastic products. This investigation focuses on the adsorption of Cu 2+ ion by SPB-500, biochar prepared at a temperature of 500 °C. Factors considered in this study include adsorption kinetics, adsorption capacity, and adsorbent reusability. Moreover, economic costs, carbon footprints, and cost of carbon removal were analyzed in detail. The total cost involved in the entire project amounted to 6,978.57 THB (about 194.93 USD), resulting in an average cost of 64.62 THB per each data point (about 1.80 USD). Around 45% of the total costs corresponded to the purchase of equipment. When compared to other studies that use commercial carbons, SPB-500 proved more economical in terms of lower cost per experiment (about 64% reduction) and reduced costs of production ($8.83/kg) and the lack of any supplementary chemicals. The performance to price ratio of this study is estimated to be 14,330 mg USD⁻¹ which is better compared to those of other experiments conducted using commercial activated carbons. As for the carbon footprint of this research, it reached 16.03 kg CO₂-eq, with the highest contribution (58.2%) coming from the consumption of electricity. However, the monetary value of carbon emissions is relatively low 8.02 THB (0.22 USD), only 0.11% of all expenses. Despite its minor economic contribution (~ 0.11%), carbon cost was retained as a complementary metric for monetizing the greenhouse-gas externality rather than as a major determinant of experimental expenditure. Thus, energy consumption plays a major role in the carbon footprint, whereas its monetary value is relatively small.

Article.Title: Leveraging neural network models for drug repurposing: a case study on cardiac hypertrophy
Article.Authors: Magnusson R.; Johansson M.; Hagvall S.; Synnergren J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Drug repurposing has emerged as an attractive strategy in contemporary pharmaceutical research, presenting an opportunity to expedite drug discovery, minimize developmental costs, and mitigate risks associated with developing new pharmaceuticals. In this study, we investigated a novel approach based on deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms for systematic identification of additional therapeutic potential in preexisting drugs. We trained a composite feedforward neural network model using gene expression data sourced from the ARCHS4 compilation of the GEO, encompassing extensive human datasets. Subsequently, disease-associated gene expression data were generated from our stem cell-derived in vitro model of cardiac hypertrophy induced by Endothelin-1 stimulation. These data were employed to identify latent variables associated with genes showing differential expression due to Endothelin-1 stimulation. By examining the differential expression profiles within the model's latent space, we successfully correlated the disease signal with known drug targets found in pharmaceutical compounds cataloged in DrugBank. The model accurately encoded additional disease-related genes beyond the curated gene set, demonstrating its ability to generalize disease associations. Leveraging the model, we identified potential drug candidates, such as lapatinib and amiodarone showing promise in mitigating proBNP concentration associated with cardiac hypertrophy. This study demonstrates the power of deep learning of human transcriptomic mechanisms in swiftly identifying new therapeutic potentials for existing drugs, highlighting the pivotal role of artificial intelligence technologies in accelerating drug development for other complex medical conditions.
Article.MeSH: Drug Repositioning; Cardiomegaly; Neural Networks, Computer

Article.Title: A thermophone-based FM sonar for airborne ultrasonic sensing under drone flight noise
Article.Authors: Yamada Y.; Hasegawa K.; Watabe Y.; Sasaki S.; Asada T.; Hiryu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bats achieve agile navigation, including obstacle avoidance and prey pursuit in complex environments, using a remarkably simple active sonar system consisting of a single sound emitter and two receivers. Their biosonar highlights the potential of broadband FM pulses in simple sensing architectures. Here, we present a bat-inspired FM sonar system for drones, employing a single ultrasonic transmitter and two receivers. The system integrates a lightweight thermoacoustic emitter (thermophone) capable of generating broadband frequency-modulated (FM) pulses, including echolocation-like signals. Owing to its resonance-free operation, the thermophone provides wideband ultrasonic emission with low voltage input. Using onboard cross-correlation processing, we demonstrate object detection, two-dimensional localization, and low-speed two-dimensional obstacle avoidance using ultrasound alone during autonomous drone flight. The proposed system successfully detects narrow obstacles even under flight conditions in which the raw onboard microphone signals are dominated by drone flight-induced noise. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of thermophone-based FM sonar for airborne ultrasonic sensing during drone flight and establish thermophone technology as a promising platform for future bat-inspired aerial sonar system.
Article.Keywords: Cheap robust design; Echolocation; LPM signal; Thermophone; UAV; Ultrasonic sensing

Article.Authors: Remil A.; Reguig A.; Saidi M.; Bouchama A.; Monir M.; Fatmi M.; Alomairy S.; Althagafi T.; Smerat A.; Abualreishh M.; Yaylacı M.
