Finally, two examples are presented to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed criteria.

Article.Title: Synergistic optimization of the Han-to-Wei project under dry conditions via the MOEA/D-PFE: a case study of the Huangjinxia reservoir
Article.Authors: Sun X.; Zhang B.; Lu Y.; Yuan K.; Zhang X.; Hui W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most Inter-basin water transfer (IBWT) projects contribute significantly to regional water security and yet suffer substantial operational trade-offs due to hydrological uncertainties. The study takes the multi-objective operation of the Huangjinxia Reservoir, the key water source of the Han-to-Wei IBWT project, focusing on the intense conflict between mandatory water diversion and power generation during 75% dry years. Furthermore, in order to alleviate the solution clustering drawback of traditional multi-objective algorithms in dealing with highly nonlinear constraints, we introduce a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition with Pareto front estimation (MOEA/D-PFE). By dynamic weight remapping, MOEA/D-PFE effectively captures the geometric manifold of the objective space. Performance comparisons with NSGA-II and standard MOEA/D show that: (1) At the mathematical level, MOEA/D-PFE can greatly improve the uniformity and convergence of solutions, which has been confirmed by the hypervolume (HV), spacing (SP) and the Wilcoxon Rank-Sum Test; (2) At the engineering level, the algorithm produces a more continuous and extensive Pareto front, providing superior decision support for balancing conflicting water-use objectives; (3) The optimized rules accurately reflect important strategies, specifically high water-level operation to compensate for head and prioritizing diversion over power generation during dry periods. The research provides a robust quantitative framework for the refined management of complex IBWT projects under climatic risks.

Article.Title: A short-term spatiotemporal load forecasting method for power systems based on an improved salp swarm algorithm
Article.Authors: Ji M.; Lin J.; Lv Y.; Wang Z.; Huo W.; Tao P.; Ding J.
Article.Abstract: Traditional power system load forecasting methods frequently suffer from limited accuracy and stability when processing complex and volatile data, as they fail to simultaneously model spatial dependencies and effectively optimize model hyperparameters. To address these coupled challenges, this paper proposes a short-term spatiotemporal load forecasting framework that integrates an Improved Salp Swarm Algorithm (ISSA) with a Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (TGCN). The core contribution lies in a novel two-stage optimization strategy within ISSA, which incorporates an adaptive attenuation factor to balance global exploration and local exploitation and introduces a dynamic learning mechanism for followers to prevent premature convergence. This strategy synergistically optimizes the hyperparameters of the TGCN, which explicitly captures both temporal dynamics and grid-topology-based spatial correlations. Experimental results on a provincial power grid dataset demonstrate that the proposed ISSA-TGCN model achieves superior prediction accuracy, attaining a normalized fitness value of 0.14 within only 10 iterations, corresponding to a root mean square error (RMSE) of 17.12 MW on the original load scale. Its predictions closely track actual load trends, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art benchmarks across mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), RMSE, and mean absolute error (MAE) metrics, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed methodological innovations.

Article.Title: Multimodal fertility cues in chimpanzees: how body odours complement sexual swellings
Article.Authors: Kücklich M.; Zetzsche M.; Dolotovskaya S.; Siepmann J.; Schmidt L.; Wiesner C.; Weiß B.; Widdig A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To attract mating partners, female mammals communicate their reproductive status through one or multiple sensory modalities, providing redundant or complementary information. Chimpanzees ( Pan troglodytes ) are an excellent model for studying multimodal communication. Exaggerated sexual swellings of females serve as visual proxy for ovulation but their temporal imprecision suggests that olfactory cues may exist in addition to swellings to pinpoint fertility more accurately. Here, we combined gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, hormonal analyses, and two-choice sniffing bioassays to examine (1) whether female anogenital odours change during the fertile period, and (2) whether males are able to detect these changes by odours alone. Our chemical results suggest that complementary changes in chemical profiles linked to menstrual cycle phases exist in addition to prominent changes of anogenital odours associated with swelling stages, even if they are statistically less strongly supported. Male responsiveness in behavioural bioassays was too low to draw conclusions regarding their ability to detect these subtle shifts when presented with anogenital odours only. Overall, our chemical analyses of female anogenital odours suggest the existence of a multimodal fertility cue in chimpanzees, wherein visual signals seem to be complemented by subtle changes in odours’ chemical profiles associated with menstrual cycle phases.
Article.PubMedTypes: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
Article.MeSH: Odorants; Fertility; Pan troglodytes; Sexual Behavior, Animal
Article.Keywords: Anogenital swelling; Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry; Menstrual cycle; Olfactory communication; Olfactory fertility cue

Article.Title: Applications of large language models in anxiety and depression patient care: a cross-model comparative analysis of dialogue quality
Article.Authors: Min J.; Jiang R.; Yang T.; Wang Q.; Xu Q.; Xu G.
Article.Abstract: The disease burden of anxiety and depression is becoming increasingly severe, and the shortage of mental health clinical resources restricts patients’ access to care services. Large language models offer a new pathway for digital psychological care, yet standardized horizontal comparisons of response efficacy among different mainstream models in anxiety and depression care consultations are lacking. A cross-sectional comparative study design was adopted. Thirty standardized open-ended questions covering six themes (Diagnosis, Symptoms, Risk factors, Assessment, Management, and Outcome) were constructed. Uniform prompts were used to batch-query five tested models and collect responses. Three evaluators implemented two rounds of blind independent scoring with a 2-week interval, quantifying scores across five dimensions (Accuracy, Integrity, Relevance, Diversity, and Interpretability). Data processing and statistical testing were conducted using ICC, Spearman correlation, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Kendall’s W, and PCA principal component analysis. Effect sizes and degrees of freedom were reported where applicable. GPT-5.3-Codex (21.35 points) and Claude-Opus-4.6 (21.25 points) showed the highest overall scores, whereas Gemini-3-Flash showed intermediate performance. The overall between-model difference was significant, F(4, 145) = 10.251, p < 0.001, η² = 0.220 (95% CI, 0.10–0.32), indicating a large overall effect. Significant pairwise contrasts were accompanied by moderate-to-large or large effects (Cohen’s d = 0.68–1.62). Test-retest ICCs were in the moderate-to-excellent range, and Spearman correlations between the two rounds were positive across all model-rater combinations (ρ = 0.549–0.864; df = 28; all p < 0.01). Wilcoxon signed-rank tests showed no systematic retest shift (all p > 0.05; effect-size r = 0.006–0.310). Within-model inter-rater correlations were generally strong. All models scored higher descriptively on Risk factors and Symptoms items, whereas Diagnosis showed the lowest overall mean score. Claude-Opus-4.6 had the highest mean scores for Accuracy and Interpretability, GPT-5.3-Codex for Integrity, and Gemini-3-Flash for Relevance and Diversity. PC1 and PC2 cumulatively explained 64.0% of the total variance. GPT-5.3-Codex and Claude-Opus-4.6 demonstrated the highest comprehensive efficacy under the standardized simulated consultation framework. Each model showed distinct performance patterns across themes and evaluation dimensions, which may inform future model optimization and prospective validation. Further real-world evaluation is required before these findings can support scenario-specific clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Improving QAOA feasibility and hardware performance for vehicle routing via linear chain and ramp schedules
Article.Authors: Azfar T.; Ke R.
Article.Abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is difficult to deploy on near-term hardware for constrained routing problems because feasibility constraints produce dense interaction graphs, deep transpiled circuits, and costly parameter search. We study this challenge for Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) instances using a hardware-aware QAOA workflow that combines linear-ramp parameter initialization, Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization, and a Linear-Chain QAOA (LC-QAOA) surrogate that retains local ZZ interactions to reduce two-qubit depth. A matched full-QAOA versus LC-QAOA feasibility comparison is performed for 4-node instances, while the 5- and 6-node experiments characterize circuit executability and low-probability optimum recovery at the tested depths. In 4-node hardware runs, LC-QAOA increases mean feasible-sample probability from 0.182% to 0.917% and mean optimum-sample probability from 0.045% to 0.239%, giving approximately \(5\times\) improvement over full QAOA. At 6 nodes, a full-QAOA circuit at \(p=1\) already has large transpiled two-qubit depth, while LC-QAOA remains executable and samples CPLEX-certified optima in selected hardware runs at depths p =10–13, albeit with low optimum probability. Overall, the results identify LC-QAOA as a hardware-efficient surrogate heuristic that trades Hamiltonian completeness for lower depth and improved feasible-solution sampling on noisy quantum hardware.

Article.Title: Multi-scale residual network-driven regional cultural color feature extraction and intelligent cultivation pathway for rural art design talent
Article.Authors: Lu X.; Gong Z.
Article.Abstract: The preservation of regional cultural color heritage faces mounting challenges from urbanization and aesthetic homogenization, while rural art design education lacks effective integration of intelligent technologies. This paper proposes a unified framework addressing both computational color analysis and talent cultivation for rural cultural revitalization. On the technical side, we design a multi-scale residual network (MSResNet) that employs parallel dilated convolutional branches with channel attention-weighted fusion to capture hierarchical chromatic features from regional cultural artifacts. A cross-modal semantic association mechanism further embeds extracted color features into a culturally annotated latent space, enabling context-aware interpretation beyond purely statistical description. On the educational side, we construct a three-stage intelligent cultivation pathway—comprising cognitive tutoring, database-driven practice, and personalized competency assessment—that operationalizes the model’s outputs within a pedagogically grounded framework. Experiments on the purpose-built RCC-6 K dataset demonstrate that MSResNet achieves a macro F1 score of 0.912 and a cultural association index of 0.831, outperforming representative baselines. A 16-week quasi-experimental pedagogical study with 86 vocational college students shows that the intelligent pathway yields a composite competency gain of 29.9%, significantly exceeding the 14.6% achieved under traditional instruction. These results confirm that structurally integrating multi-scale deep learning with semantic cultural grounding can advance both the computational characterization and educational transmission of regional color heritage.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of heparin anticoagulation response and dose recommendation during atrial fibrillation catheter ablation
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Bao Z.; Ge W.; Yuan R.; Gong H.; He Y.; Sun G.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates activated clotting time monitoring and individualized heparin dosing during atrial fibrillation catheter ablation. Data from 1175 patients treated at the First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University between January 2020 and December 2022 were collected; after eligibility screening and preprocessing, 1144 cases were analyzed. Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, DNN, LightGBM, and TabNet were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with each case serving once in a held-out validation fold. In the six-model comparison, DNN achieved a mean accuracy of 0.81, a Kappa coefficient of 0.68, macro-recall of 0.75, and macro-F1 of 0.72. In a separate five-fold DNN class-balancing analysis, the unbalanced mean accuracy was 0.786 and standard-category recall was 0.485; SMOTE-DNN achieved a mean accuracy of 0.812, Kappa of 0.683, macro-recall of 0.758, macro-F1 of 0.752, and standard-category recall of 0.654. For initial-dose agreement, the mean error was 728 IU, R-squared was 0.68, and 70% of predictions were within 1000 IU of the administered initial dose. In a separate matched ablation involving a 63-case post-outcome-defined subgroup, residual-based sample exclusion reduced dose MAE from 4008 to 3627 IU and increased the 1000-IU hit rate from 17.5 to 23.8%; however, R-squared remained negative, indicating limited absolute accuracy for subsequent-dose recommendation.

Article.Title: Evaluation of pH-responsive release behavior, antioxidant activity and cytotoxic potential of quercetin-loaded sodium alginate gellan gum hydrogel beads
Article.Authors: Abbasi R.; Emam-Djomeh Z.
Article.Abstract: A bio-based hydrogel system comprising sodium alginate (2% w/v) and gellan gum (0.5% w/v) was developed for the encapsulation and pH-responsive release of quercetin. This study explores the potential of this matrix for quercetin delivery, focusing on its physicochemical properties, antioxidant activity, and cytotoxicity. Beads were prepared by ionic gelation using calcium chloride and Tween 80. Two formulations were selected based on their encapsulation efficiency: sodium alginate–gellan gum hydrogel beads prepared with initial quercetin contents of 1% (SAGG beads A; loading capacity: 20%) and 0.5% (SAGG beads B; loading capacity: 11.1%), which exhibited encapsulation efficiency (EE) values of 84.30% and 93.26%, respectively. FTIR and XRD analyses were consistent with quercetin incorporation and reduced apparent crystallinity within the hydrogel matrix. TGA showed modified thermal behavior, and FESEM revealed spherical beads with a porous surface and internal microstructures. In vitro swelling and release studies showed quercetin release, particularly in SIF, with cumulative release after 8 h of 37.2% for SAGG beads A and 35.9% for SAGG beads B. Fresh SAGG beads A and SAGG beads B showed DPPH radical-scavenging activities of 89% and 77%, respectively, which decreased to 85% and 62% after two months of storage. In MDA-MB-231 cells, free quercetin showed the highest cytotoxicity, with an IC₅₀ of 32.7 ppm, whereas extracts from fresh and two-month-stored SAGG beads A showed apparent IC₅₀ values of 147 and 149.5 ppm, respectively, based on nominal extract concentrations. These hydrogel beads show potential as carriers for quercetin delivery and antioxidant activity retention during storage.

Article.Title: Demographic and clinical characteristics of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis in renal vasculitis in the Japan renal biopsy registry
Article.Authors: Morinaga H.; Sugiyama H.; Usui J.; Ogawa Y.; Tsuboi N.; Sato H.; Yokoyama H.; Shimizu A.; Maruyama S.; Yamagata K.; Wada J.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the clinical and demographic characteristics of biopsy-proven rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN), with histological evidence of renal vasculitis. We focused on five vasculitis-related nephritides: MPO-ANCA, PR3-ANCA, anti-GBM, IgA vasculitis (IgAV), and lupus nephritis, —using data from the Japan Renal Biopsy Registry (J-RBR). Among the 35,870 native kidney biopsies, 2,285 (6.4%) were classified as RPGN. RPGN prevalence was highest in anti-GBM nephritis (90.4%), followed by MPO-ANCA (73.2%) and PR3-ANCA (53.5%). Age and sex distributions varied across diseases, with ANCA and anti-GBM nephritis predominantly affecting older adults, whereas IgAV and lupus nephritis were more common in younger populations. Severe proteinuria was frequent in all groups. The KDIGO risk classification revealed a high proportion of very high-risk cases of ANCA and anti-GBM nephritis, with age-related increases in IgAV and lupus nephritis. Patients with anti-GBM nephritis showed the lowest median estimated glomerular filtration rate, indicating severe renal impairment at the time of the diagnosis. RPGN cases mirrored these trends, with IgAV-RPGN patients skewed toward an older age. This registry-based analysis highlights the distinct clinical and demographic profiles of vasculitis-related RPGN and underscores the need for longitudinal studies to assess disease progression and outcomes.

Article.Title: Assessing the impact of construction material waste drivers on project cost overrun across material processing stages: a structural equation modeling approach
Article.Authors: Kamal L.; Yamany M.; Hosny H.
Article.Abstract: A considerable quantity of materials supplied to construction sites becomes waste, hence escalating project costs. Nevertheless, research lacks a thorough assessment of the intricate, indirect, and non-linear correlation between material waste drivers at different processing stages and project cost overruns. This research study investigates this correlation using an advanced multivariate statistical technique known as structural equation modeling (SEM). Data were collected through a questionnaire survey to evaluate the construction material waste factors (CMWFs) and their association with cost overruns in construction projects in Egypt. An exploratory factor analysis was conducted to categorize CMWFs into material processing phases: (1) design and documentation, (2) material procurement, (3) material handling, storage, and transportation, and (4) on-site management. An SEM model was developed to uncover the impact of latent material processing phases on project cost overruns. The model's consistency, reliability, and accuracy were verified employing various performance metrics, including Cronbach's Alpha, composite reliability, and root mean squared error. The results demonstrate that factors related to material handling, storage, and transportation exhibit the highest correlation and impact on project cost overruns, as reflected by an R2 value of 0.441 and a p-value below 0.05. This research helps decision-makers prioritize mitigation strategies for material waste and cost overruns, hence enhancing construction project performance.
Article.Keywords: Construction projects; Cost overruns; Material waste; PLS-SEM; Structural equation modeling

Article.Title: Correction: Mixed-maturation fisheries compromise productivity and resilience of Chinook salmon
Article.Authors: Gayeski N.; Swanson D.; MacDuffee M.; Rosenberger A.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Correction: Cardiometabolic risk factors are affected by interaction between FADS1 rs174556 variant and dietary vegetable oils in patients with diabetes: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Fallah Z.; Vasmehjani A.; Aghaei S.; Amiri M.; Raeisi-Dehkordi H.; Moghtaderi F.; Zimorovat A.; Yazd E.; Madadizadeh F.; Khayyatzadeh S.; Salehi-Abargouei A.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: FCAE-Mixer: frequency-aware convolutional autoencoder with dual-branch mixing for time series anomaly detection
Article.Authors: Li L.; Tong Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The core of complex time series anomaly detection lies in the effective extraction of multi-dimensional features. However, existing methods often separate the synergistic mechanism among local temporal, global variable, and frequency domain features. To this end, this paper proposes a network that balances temporal, variable, and frequency domain features. The model innovatively combines a one-dimensional convolutional autoencoder and a multi-layer perceptron to extract local temporal transient features and global variable spatial mappings, respectively. Furthermore, an FFT-Attention module is introduced to enhance adaptive focus on low-frequency spectral modes while suppressing high-frequency noise. Finally, the dual-branch reconstruction error is used as the anomaly judgment basis, and anomaly samples are identified via the reconstruction error, which jointly benefits from both time-domain morphological and frequency-domain spectral processing. Evaluation results on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average F1 score (without point-adjustment) of 0.3317, outperforming all compared baseline methods with a 10.50% relative F1 improvement over the suboptimal baseline Transformer with an average F1 of 0.3002, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-dimensional joint modeling in time series anomaly detection.

Article.Title: Evaluating soybean genotype-by-environment interactions and multi-trait stability across South African environments
Article.Authors: Makuya V.; van der Laan M.; Salmerón M.; Bellocchi G.; de Beer A.; Shayanowako A.; Mangani R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soybean is one of the significant legume crops in South Africa, yet genotype × environment interactions (GEI) complicate reliable cultivar selection. Despite this, GEI, performance, and stability of soybean genotypes have not been comprehensively evaluated across South Africa’s major soybean–producing provinces (Mpumalanga, North–West and Free State). Therefore, this study assessed GEI, performance, and stability of soybean genotypes across key agronomic traits using multi–environment trials (METs) over three growing seasons. Additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) and genotype plus genotype–by–environment (GGE) biplot approaches were used to quantify trait variation, identify best genotypes, and characterizing environmental relationships. Stability and performance were further assessed using multi–trait stability index (MTSI), weighted average of absolute scores (WAASB), and weighted average of absolute scores and yield (WAASBY), while chord diagrams visualized inter–trait correlations. Results indicated that environmental effects dominated trait variation across all traits. Which–Won–Where patterns revealed that no genotype excelled across all environments, but G5 (LG60260IPRO) was the best genotype across all evaluated traits, particularly in cool (E1) and moderate (E2) environments across seasons. Vector analyses showed positive correlations among environments within the same location and negative correlations among contrasting environments. WAASB highlighted G8 (PAN1521R) as the most stable and high–performing genotype across all evaluated traits with dominant performance in moderate environment. WAASBY identified G5 as a superior genotype across all traits, with superiority particularly evident in cool and moderate environments. MTSI identified G2 (DM59I60 RSF IPRO) as a consistently stable genotype across all evaluated environments. Chord diagrams revealed predominantly positive inter–trait correlations across all traits in E2 and mixed correlations in E1 and E3 (warm environment). Overall, the identified superior, high–performing, and stable genotypes are promising candidates for cultivar recommendation and soybean breeding programmes targeting productivity, stability, and adaptation across South Africa’s diverse environments.

Article.Title: Mechanical characteristics of friction-welded copper-silver junction with iron tip via molecular dynamics simulation: influence of initial temperature
Article.Authors: Alkhafaji A.; Alaloosi W.; Albalawi H.; Singh N.; Al-zahy Y.; Fadwi R.; Taner M.; Naser H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employed molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the atomistic response of a copper–silver interface under simplified friction-welding-inspired loading. The mechanical response of the tool-modified copper–silver interface was analyzed, focusing on the influence of the initial temperature (300–400 K). The research methodology was divided into two phases: first, the physical stability of modeled samples was assessed at an initial temperature of 300 K by monitoring key physical parameters, such as kinetic and total energy. Subsequently, simplified friction-welding-inspired loading was applied to the equilibrated sample, followed by mechanical deformation to evaluate the resulting interfacial response. This approach enabled a detailed analysis of temperature-dependent mechanical characteristics, including stress–strain behavior, radial distribution function, interaction energy, mean square displacement, ultimate strength, and Young's modulus. Results show that increasing temperature increases thermal energy, weakening the interatomic bonds between copper and silver atoms and thereby reducing the ultimate strength and stiffness of the tool-modified interface. Specifically, the ultimate strength decreased from 1490.27 MPa to 1348.88 MPa as the temperature increased from 300 to 400 K, while Young's modulus decreased correspondingly. This study provides atomistic insights into how initial temperature affects the mechanical response of a copper–silver interface under simplified friction-welding-inspired conditions.

Article.Title: Geometric and quantum kernel methods for predicting skeletal muscle outcomes in experimental chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Article.Authors: Alavi A.; Khalili H.; Chan S.; Kouchmeshki F.; Usman M.; Vlahos R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Skeletal-muscle dysfunction is an important extrapulmonary feature of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but advanced computational representations require conservative evaluation in small preclinical cohorts. We analysed a cigarette-smoke mouse model of experimental COPD comprising 213 animals with blood and bronchoalveolar-lavage biomarkers to predict tibialis anterior muscle weight, muscle quality, and force. We developed a kernel-geometric quantum hybrid method in which synthetic symmetric positive definite (SPD) references are mapped through a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space, compressed using train-only random projection, normalised, and supplied to low-dimensional simulated quantum regression circuits. We benchmarked this approach against classical Ridge/kernel models, SPD relational representations, and quantum-kernel regression using identical condition-stratified repeated cross-validation folds. Results were endpoint-specific. Biomarker-only Ridge had the lowest RMSE for force, indicating that a compact linear model was sufficient for this endpoint in the present cohort. Synth_ROSE had the numerically lowest RMSE for muscle weight and muscle quality, but paired fold-level testing did not establish statistically significant superiority after Holm adjustment. These findings support leakage-controlled, endpoint-specific benchmarking of SPD and simulated quantum feature maps, not claims of clinical readiness, quantum hardware advantage, or definitive superiority over classical learning.
Article.PubMedTypes: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
Article.MeSH: Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive; Muscle, Skeletal
Article.Keywords: Quantum machine learning; Quantum-kernel regression; Skeletal muscle outcomes; Small-dataset learning.; Symmetric positive definite manifold; Synthetic data augmentation

Article.Title: An in vitro framework for screening salinity tolerance in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) using a trait based and membership function approach
Article.Authors: Gopera S.; Sandal S.; Singh A.; Bansal A.
Article.Abstract: One hundred forty-four distinct Sesamum indicum L. genotypes were evaluated to build an efficient in vitro screening framework for finding salinity tolerance during the germination and early seedling phases. To identify the best salt concentration for screening, seeds of 15 representative genotypes were randomly selected and germinated in vitro under seven NaCl concentrations (0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, and 175 mM NaCl) in a complete randomized design (CRD) with four replications. Morphological characteristics, including germination %, shoot length, root length, seedling fresh weight, and seedling dry weight, were recorded to establish the optimum screening concentration using the Salt Injury Index (SII). Based on an average growth reduction of about 50%, 125 mM NaCl was determined as the optimum concentration and subsequently utilized to examine the salt tolerance of all 144 genotypes under the identical experimental conditions. Salt tolerance was examined using the Mean Membership Function Value (MFV), which categorized the genotypes into five categories: 10 highly salt-tolerant (HST), 6 salt-tolerant (ST), 105 moderately salt-tolerant (MST), 14 salt-sensitive (SS), and 9 highly salt-sensitive (HSS). Correlation and multiple regression analysis showed shoot length as the most accurate feature for fast assessment of salinity tolerance, displaying the highest correlation with the overall salt tolerance index and membership function values (MFV). The suggested membership function values (MFV)-based screening methodology provides a quick, reproducible, and cost-effective approach for testing salinity tolerance in sesame at the seedling stage and offers a helpful tool for selecting prospective parental lines for salinity breeding programmes. This study is the first comprehensive trait-based membership function framework for large-scale in vitro salinity screening in sesame and provides a viable foundation for merging phenotypic screening with future molecular breeding approaches.

Article.Title: Karenia cristata from the 2025 South Australian harmful algal bloom produces potent toxic compounds
Article.Authors: Rolton A.; Kumanan K.; Murray S.; Thompson L.; Rhodes L.; Smith K.; Selwood A.; Greenhough H.
Article.Abstract: For more than 12 months from March 2025, an unprecedented harmful algal bloom (HAB), dominated by the dinoflagellate genus Karenia , caused catastrophic marine mortalities in South Australia, yet the mechanisms of toxicity remain unresolved. We assessed the toxicity of five bloom isolates (three strains of Karenia cristata , one strain of Scrippsiella sp., and one strain of Karlodinium veneficum ) using fish gill cell line RTgill-W1 viability assays. Only K. cristata strains were toxic, causing nearly 100% fish gill mortality at screening concentrations of ~ 5 × 10 3 cell ml -1 for the crude extracellular fraction (culture supernatant) and 2 × 10 4 cell ml -1 for intracellular and extracellular methanolic extracts. Bioassay-guided fractionation showed toxicity in the crude extracellular fraction and both methanolic extracts but, not in methyl tert-butyl ether extracts, indicating the involvement of moderately polar organic compounds. Results were compared with brevetoxin analogues: brevetoxin-3 was non-toxic up to 50 µg mL -1 , while brevetoxin-2 was toxic at concentrations far exceeding those detected in toxic K. cristata extracts. Toxicity in the crude extracellular fraction and methanolic extracts was detectable within 15 min and increased over 24 h, demonstrating progressive cellular damage. These results suggest K. cristata produces multiple intra‑ and extracellular toxic compounds, with brevetoxins contributing minimally to RTgill‑W1 toxicity. These compounds may contribute significantly to marine mortalities during K. cristata blooms, highlighting the need for their characterisation to improve understanding and management of future blooms.

Article.Title: Spectral modeling guided by data and prior knowledge discriminates flue cured tobacco flavor styles
Article.Authors: Xin X.; Huang M.; Li N.; Li P.; Jia T.
Article.Abstract: To address ambiguous discrimination of intermediate flavor styles and low overall accuracy in existing flue-cured tobacco flavor style classification methods, we propose an innovative spectral modeling approach integrating data-driven and prior knowledge-guided strategies. Specifically, a pre-trained tobacco spectral model and limited labeled spectral data are used as prior knowledge, enabling pseudo-label annotation via transfer learning and self-training. Consistency training and an improved prediction confidence metric are further introduced to enhance pseudo-label reliability. The proposed discrimination model captures multi-level, multi-particle internal vibration characteristics of organic molecules in tobacco. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reaches an accuracy of 94.0% in identifying medium-flavor flue-cured tobacco within the constructed dataset. It delivers better classification performance compared with several mainstream algorithms adopted in this field. This approach alleviates the difficulty in distinguishing medium-flavor tobacco samples and improves the overall classification accuracy for the three typical flavor styles of flue-cured tobacco.

Article.Title: The urinary and vaginal microbiota in postmenopausal women with and without overactive bladder
Article.Authors: Villadsen A.; Bundgaard-Nielsen C.; Holm-Jacobsen J.; Hagstrøm S.; Kornum J.; Glavind K.; Leutscher P.; Jeppesen P.; Schmidt Arenholt L.; Sørensen S.
Article.Abstract: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a common condition, particularly prevalent in women after menopause. Previous studies suggest that OAB is related to an altered urinary microbiota, indicating a potential microbial etiological component. However, establishing a solid association between the microbiota and OAB has been obscured by use of heterogenous study populations with broad variations in age and menopausal status, both factors known to influence the composition of the urinary and vaginal microbiota. In this study, we investigated the urinary and vaginal microbiota in postmenopausal women with and without OAB. None of the participant women were receiving estrogen replacement therapy. Microbiota profiles in catheterized urine, midstream urine, and vaginal swab samples were determined using 16S rRNA gene sequencing targeting the V4 region. Our analysis revealed no significant differences in alpha- or beta-diversity measures between women with OAB and non-OAB in any of the three distinct sample types when examined individually. Nevertheless, a notable difference in the overall microbiota composition was observed when the combined urogenital microbiota was analyzed. These findings indicate that OAB is unlikely to be characterized by a single, consistent urinary microbiome signature but instead appears to be associated with broader perturbations across the urogenital microbial ecosystem, underscoring the importance of assessing the combined urogenital microbiota rather than the bladder alone.

Article.Title: Intelligent diagnosis model for rolling bearing faults based on multi-representation feature fusion
Article.Authors: Sun L.; Shen J.; Zhao L.; Zhang J.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rolling bearings of high-speed trains are in long-term service under high-speed, variable-load and intense noise conditions, and the collected vibration signals exhibit prominent non-stationarity and non-linearity. This makes it difficult for fault diagnosis methods based on a single feature or single modality to stably characterize fault information. To address the above issues, this paper proposes an intelligent diagnosis model for rolling bearing faults based on multi-modal data fusion, namely MultiFuseAttenNet. First, experimental samples are constructed using the 48 kHz vibration signals from the drive end of the bearing test rig, and locally stationary samples are obtained through data cleaning and a sliding window segmentation strategy (with a window length of 1024 points and an overlap ratio of 50%). Second, starting from the bearing fault mechanism, vibration features, time-domain statistical features and frequency-domain statistical features are extracted, and time-frequency images are generated via the Synchrosqueezing Wavelet Transform (WSST), so as to construct a dual-modality representation of "numerical features + time-frequency images". Furthermore, a dual-branch fusion network consisting of a Swin Transformer-based image branch and a SENet-based numerical branch is designed to achieve collaborative learning of local impact information, global time-frequency patterns and statistical feature information. Finally, the performance of the model is comprehensively evaluated with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrix and t-SNE visualization, and a comparison is performed with mainstream baseline models including 1DCNN, LSTM, GRU, Transformer and VGG16. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 99.95% on the test set, and its overall diagnostic performance outperforms the compared baseline models, which verifies the effectiveness of the multi-modal feature fusion strategy for rolling bearing fault identification.

Article.Title: SrTiO₃-loaded SA/ε‑PL composite hydrogels with piezocatalytic and osteoimmune regulatory functions for infected bone repair
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Zeng J.; Wang K.; Song Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacterial infection and persistent local inflammation severely hinder the healing of bone defects, and conventional bone repair materials fail to achieve antibacterial treatment and bone regeneration regulation at the same time. As mechanical cues can modulate cell behaviors and osteogenesis, piezoelectric materials can convert ultrasound stimulation into bioelectrical signals and reactive oxygen species for bacteriostasis and osteogenic regulation. In this work, we prepared a composite hydrogel by incorporating strontium titanate into crosslinked sodium alginate/ε-polylysine networks. This material exhibits obvious pH-responsive release in acidic inflammatory microenvironments and realizes highly efficient sterilization under ultrasonic assistance. In vitro experiments confirm its outstanding biocompatibility. It effectively regulates macrophage polarization to relieve inflammatory responses and greatly promotes the osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. This study establishes a feasible fabrication strategy for multifunctional therapeutic hydrogels and provides a promising platform for the comprehensive treatment of clinically infected bone defects.

Article.Title: Multi-omics insights into the effects of Citrus reticulata-derived Bacillus C3X-5 on the fermentation quality of cigar tobacco leaves
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Jia Y.; Zhang Y.; Chen C.; Zhou L.; Hu W.; Jia S.; Li D.
Article.Abstract: Although Citri Reticulatae Pericarpium (CRP) extracts can enhance cigar tobacco leaf (CTL) quality, the specific contributions of CRP-associated microbiota to CTL quality remain unexplored. This study investigated the potential of Bacillus cereus C3X-5, a strain isolated from CRP, as a bio-enhancer for improving CTL fermentation quality. The physicochemical analysis, metagenomics, and untargeted metabolomics were employed to systematically evaluate the strain’s impact. Results demonstrated that C3X-5 inoculation significantly elevated amylase and protease activities of CTL, and the sugar content and free amino acids content of CTL significantly reduced. Metagenomic analysis revealed that C3X-5 directed microbial community succession, reducing overall diversity while enriching beneficial functional genera such as Aspergillus . 66 key differential volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were identified with GC-IMS, which showed that C3X-5 treatment significantly increased desirable aroma compounds, including pyrazines (nutty, roasted notes) and ketones (fruity, sweet notes), while effectively suppressing green off-notes associated with 1-hexanal. Metabolomic and correlation network demonstrated that C3X-5 optimizes the CTL metabolic profile through a dual strategy: promoting key aroma-forming microbes and their metabolic pathways while competitively inhibiting fungi responsible for undesirable fatty acid derivatives. The CRP-derived strain C3X-5 enhanced CTL quality and provides a scientific basis for developing novel bio-starters for the cigar industry.

Article.Title: Molecular study of specific virulence genes of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from sub clinical bovine mastitis cases
Article.Authors: Ibrahim E.; Dorgham S.; Eid R.; Abdel-latif E.; Khalaf D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa -caused bovine mastitis has received increased attention recently because it results in large financial losses for dairy farms and the dairy sector overall. P. aeruginosa mastitis is a complex illness that requires host, pathogen, and environmental interactions. The objective of this study was to examine the distribution and presence of virulence factors in 13 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates that were isolated from 70 milk samples from subclinical cases of bovine mastitis, with an incidence of 18.57%. The Vitek 2 system (bioMerieux) verified each isolate. Pseudomonas aeruginosa produces virulence factors, which give it significant roles in the cause of the disease These virulence factors are encoded by virulence genes found on the Pseudomonas chromosome. The ecfx gene was identified in 13 (100%) of the 13 P. aeruginosa isolates, according to molecular identification of the bacteria and detection of specific virulence genes. Additionally, all of the current genes ) lasR , rhlI , pqsR , lecA , lasA , proC , toxA , exoS , and pelA ) were found in 6 out of 13 isolates with an incidence of 46.15%.
Article.PubMedTypes: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
Article.MeSH: Pseudomonas aeruginosa; Mastitis, Bovine; Virulence Factors; Pseudomonas Infections
Article.Keywords: Pseudomonas aeruginosa; Mastitis; Virulence genes

Article.Title: Nanoenabled alginate and chitosan based liposome formulations for therapeutic management of E. Coli diarrhea in broiler chickens
Article.Authors: Solanki P.; Kumar A.; Kumar R.; Rokade J.; Tiwari P.; Saxena H.; Gupta M.; Kumar M.; Shukla R.
Article.Abstract: In the present study, alginate and chitosan-based liposomes were synthesized for the delivery of carvacrol and cinnamaldehyde to evaluate their therapeutic efficacy against Escherichia coli (MTCC No. 723, strain H-10407, serotype O78:K80:H11, CFA/I + LT+ ST+) infection in broiler chickens. The formulations were prepared using the ionic gelation method and characterized for pH, zeta potential, zeta size, and polydispersity index. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of characteristic peaks for both polymers and bioactive oils, while SEM images showed uniformly spherical, smooth, and compact vesicles. The encapsulation efficiencies for both formulations were approximately 90–92% and show sustained drug release. Birds were orally challenged with an E. coli broth culture for in vivo therapeutic evaluation. Treatments were administered for five consecutive days post-infection, and evaluations were conducted at onset of diarrhoea and after treatment. Efficacy was evaluated based on faecal E. coli counts, production performance (body weight, feed intake, feed conversion ratio), haematological parameters, biochemical indices, serum cytokine concentrations, histopathological observations. The combination of encapsulated carvacrol and cinnamaldehyde, as well as the antibiotic-treated group, showed marked reductions in faecal E. coli counts and significant improvements in haemoglobin, liver enzyme activities, cytokine levels, H/L ratios, total protein, electrolyte profile, and intestinal damage compared with the disease control group. The findings suggest that a combination of encapsulated carvacrol and cinnamaldehyde formulations can serve as effective alternatives to antibiotics for managing E. coli infection and enhancing gut health in broiler chickens. This approach also suggests an effective approach in addressing the highly important current global crisis of antimicrobial resistance.

Article.Title: Similarity detection of light industry printing images by integrating object detection and feature enhancement
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Qi Y.; Cao H.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: This paper focuses on post-press image quality inspection in light industrial printing, and proposes an innovative image quality inspection framework that integrates YOLO-World, CLIP, and Enhanced Siamese Network (ESN), aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of inspection. In light industrial printing, the traditional manual post-press image inspection method is inefficient and error-prone, while the complex image inspection still relies on manual labor under the current smart manufacturing technology. The development of deep learning technologies brings an opportunity to solve this challenge, such as YOLO-World for target detection and CLIP for cross-modal feature extraction, but they have limitations in print image quality inspection applications, and the existing twin networks are not sensitive enough to subtle differences. In the framework proposed in this paper, YOLO-World detects and crops key regions of print images in real-time by flexibly setting the threshold value to reduce the amount of subsequent computation and background interference; CLIP extracts deep semantic features from the cropped images to provide rich information for image comparison; and ESN utilizes the EfficientNet-B4 and the attention mechanism to further improve the accuracy of the image similarity metric. The experimental results show that the framework has achieved some success in print image quality detection, with good performance in metrics such as recall rate, and increasing the number of training rounds can improve the model generalization ability. However, the framework still faces some challenges, such as the balance between YOLO-World detection capability and operation efficiency, the dependence of CLIP on the quality of the pre-trained model, the need to improve the sensitivity and specificity of ESN in dealing with biased datasets, and the need to further validate the effectiveness of the loss function. To address these issues, future research can be conducted by optimizing model hyperparameters, adopting richer data enhancement strategies, exploring the capability of CLIP models, and improving the ESN architecture and loss function to enhance the overall performance and application value of the framework.

Article.Title: Optimization of stopping mining coal pillar width for fully mechanized top-coal caving face based on advance abutment pressure evolution
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Han W.; Fan Y.
Article.Abstract: The width of the stopping mining coal pillar critically affects the long term stability of main roadways after panel extraction. In the Gaohe Coal Mine, severe convergence and roof collapse in main roadways frequently endanger production safety. To address this, we deployed in situ stress and displacement monitoring stations at the W3303 fully mechanized top coal caving face, combined with limit equilibrium theory and FLAC 3 D simulations, to determine the optimal pillar width. Field monitoring shows that the strong disturbance zone of advance abutment pressure extends 80 m ahead of the face, with the stress peak at 13–18 m. Theoretical calculation, based on the limit equilibrium zone and periodic weighting interval, gives a pillar width of 68.9–75.3 m. Numerical simulation reveals that as the face advances, the peak abutment stress increases and shifts deeper into the coal mass, while the overburden undergoes progressive upward plastic failure. Roadway deformation and stress concentration rise sharply when the pillar width is less than 80 m, identifying this value as the critical stability threshold. A one year industrial test on the northwest return airway, protected by an 80 m pillar, confirmed that roadway convergence remained within safe limits and the bolt cable support system never exceeded its load capacity. Integrated field, theoretical, and numerical results demonstrate that the 80 m pillar effectively isolates mining induced stress, ensures main roadway long term stability, and balances safety with coal recovery efficiency.

Article.Title: Differential effects of formal and informal environmental regulation on green innovation: the roles of climate policy uncertainty and physical risk
Article.Authors: Cao W.
Article.Abstract: As global carbon neutrality targets continue to advance, countries are increasingly investing in green technology innovation to balance economic development and environmental protection. Green innovation (GI) has therefore become a key priority for regions pursuing sustainable development. While existing studies have examined individual environmental regulations in isolation, few studies have compared their heterogeneous effects within a unified analytical framework. Furthermore, the moderating and threshold effects of climate-related external shocks remain insufficiently explored. To address these gaps, this study uses panel data from Chinese cities between 2011 and 2023 to examine the differential effects of formal environmental regulation (FER) and informal environmental regulation (IER) on GI. Moderation and threshold models are employed to investigate the roles of climate policy uncertainty(CPU) and physical climate risk. The results show that: (1) FER significantly promotes GI, whereas IER exhibits a U-shaped relationship with GI; (2) climate policy uncertainty weakens the positive effect of FER on GI and strengthens the inhibitory effect of IER on GI; (3) the positive effect of FER on GI declines after physical climate risk exceeds the identified threshold values; and (4) the effects of FER and IER vary across regions, development levels, and resource availability.

Article.Title: Peak and post-peak behaviour and multi-bolt load sharing in randomly fractured rock under water pressure
Article.Authors: Xu Q.; Hu H.; Bai H.; Zou S.; Xia Z.; Huang G.; Shang X.; Qiao Y.; Fan Y.
Article.Abstract: Fracture water pressure reduces effective normal stress on connected fractures and can weaken the load-bearing capacity of bolted fractured rock masses. Fracture opening, slip and coalescence also alter network hydraulic connectivity and the extent of the fracture network subjected to water pressure. In this study, a two-dimensional randomly fractured rock-mass model was established using an experimentally calibrated continuum-discontinuum element method. After selecting an appropriate computational-domain size, peak and post-peak load-bearing capacity, the distribution of fractures subjected to water pressure, and load sharing among multiple bolts were investigated for different numbers of bolts and water-pressure conditions. Without applied water pressure, increasing the number of bolts from 0 to 10 raised peak strength from 5.43 to 6.93 MPa and the prescribed post-peak strength at an axial strain of 80 × 10 − 3 from 1.71 to 4.66 MPa. Under 0.13 MPa water pressure, the corresponding strengths of the 10-bolt model decreased to 5.93 and 3.33 MPa, reductions of 14.4% and 28.5%, respectively. In the 6-bolt model, the water-pressure-affected fracture-pixel fraction increased from 5.2% to 39.4% as loading progressed. Water pressure also increased the number of bolts reaching the 251 kN axial-force reference value, while shear-force concentrations broadly coincided with pronounced slip along adjacent fractures. The results show that the post-peak expansion of hydraulically connected fractures is closely associated with reduced post-peak capacity and more uneven load sharing among bolts. These findings provide a basis for evaluating post-peak capacity and selecting bolt-support parameters in water-rich fractured rock masses.

Article.Title: Tempered fractional GMV self-tuning control of PV-fed boost converters with causal prediction and closed-loop stability analysis
Article.Authors: Guesmi T.; Elloumi M.; Alqunun K.; Alturki M.; Albaker A.; Alshammari B.; Naifar O.
Article.Abstract: Regulating the DC-link voltage of a boost converter fed by a photovoltaic (PV) source is complicated by stochastic irradiance, fluctuating loads, and drifting component characteristics. Fractional-order descriptions can encode the memory that such hardware exhibits, yet the power-law kernel of a conventional fractional operator weighs the distant past too heavily: adaptation slows under nonstationary operation, and the resulting regressors become long and numerically ill-conditioned, which degrades on-line identification. Here we attenuate that kernel exponentially—a tempering that yields semi-long memory—and build around it a complete adaptive scheme, the tempered–fractional generalized minimum-variance self-tuning regulator (TF–GMV–STR). The development proceeds in four steps. (i) An operating-point linearization links the fractional averaged converter model to a discrete model class; within this class, a one-step predictor in innovation (ARMAX-type) form is constructed from a truncated tempered Grünwald–Letnikov basis and rendered strictly causal by an explicit monic normalization, repairing an algebraic flaw common to naive fractional predictors. (ii) Minimizing the quadratic GMV cost—rather than postulating the controller structure—produces an offset-free incremental control law in which the \(\rho /\hat{b}_1\) weighting of the controller polynomial emerges from the optimality condition itself; a finite tempered Diophantine identity and a recursive extended least-squares estimator with projection complete the loop. (iii) The closed-loop characteristic polynomial is proved to admit the factorization \(\widetilde{C}\,[\,q\widetilde{B}+(\rho /\hat{b}_1)A_\Delta \,]\) , so stability reduces to a verifiable frozen-time (small-signal) Schur test, verified here uniformly over the entire admissible parameter set of the reported configuration (worst-case root modulus 0.54); a conditional boundedness proposition and the leading-coefficient bound \(z_0=\hat{b}_1+\rho /\hat{b}_1\ge 2\sqrt{\rho }\) follow, while large-signal operation is probed numerically through a full-range start-up and disturbance transients on the nonlinear averaged converter. (iv) Performance is assessed against two baselines—an integer-order GMV–STR and an untempered long-memory fractional GMV–STR—using common random numbers and paired hypothesis tests across 40 realizations, spanning fixed-reference regulation, set-point steps, load/source disturbances, a deliberate memory-mismatch experiment, and closed-loop operation on the nonlinear averaged fractional converter. In regulation, the proposed scheme is statistically indistinguishable from the long-memory fractional baseline ( \(p\ge 0.69\) ) and ahead of the integer one in ISE only (paired \(p=0.042\) , a small effect, Cohen’s \(d=0.33\) ). The unambiguous gains are realization-side and orthogonal to regulation quality: the tempered scheme runs on 2– \(4.5\times \) fewer memory taps and carries a \(\sim \!38\%\) lower information-matrix condition number—properties well matched to embedded power-electronic targets.

Article.Title: Ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 regulates autophagy to promote renal cell carcinoma progression through mediating the Akt/mTOR signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Meng Y.; Zhang L.; Ma R.; Yan B.
Article.Abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a type of malignant kidney tumor characterized by high morbidity and mortality, yet its mechanisms of development and progression remain incompletely understood. Although ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 (RRM2) has been confirmed to play a regulatory role in the progression of various tumors, its clinical significance, biological functions, and underlying molecular mechanisms in RCC still require systematic investigation. In this study, based on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis (GEPIA) databases, we identified RRM2 as a differentially expressed gene in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), and validated its expression using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemical assays. Through a series of in vitro and in vivo functional experiments, we further explored the biological effects and mechanisms of RRM2 in ccRCC. The results showed that RRM2 was significantly overexpressed in ccRCC tissues, and its expression level was closely associated with adverse pathological features and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). In vitro experiments demonstrated that overexpression of RRM2 enhanced autophagy, promoted malignant phenotypes of ccRCC, and was associated with inhibition of the Akt/mTOR signaling pathway. Conversely, activation of the Akt/mTOR pathway reversed RRM2-induced autophagy, thereby suppressing cell migration and invasion and promoting apoptosis—a finding consistently supported by in vivo animal models. This study reveals a novel mechanism through which RRM2 regulates autophagy and promotes ccRCC development in conjunction with inhibition of the Akt/mTOR signaling pathway. RRM2 may not only serve as a potential prognostic biomarker for ccRCC patients but also represent a promising therapeutic target for this disease.

Article.Title: Evaluation of the ammonium nitrate fuel oil-nitromethane energetic material sensitivity
Article.Authors: Biessikirski A.; Pytlik M.; Dworzak M.; Nachlik S.; Baziak A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ammonium Nitrate Fuel Oil is a widely used non-ideal explosive, though its relatively low detonation performance and high insensitivity limit its efficiency. This study examines the effect of partial substitution of ammonium nitrate(V) with nitromethane (4.0–9 wt%) on energetic material sensitivity, and thermal exposure. Brisance was evaluated using the Hess method at 40 mm and 60 mm diameters to capture scale effects, while friction and impact sensitivities were determined according to standardized procedures. Thermal stability was assessed after 48 h at 75 °C. Brisance increased systematically with nitromethane content, however, the magnitude of improvement was strongly diameter-dependent. The 40 mm configuration reflected near-critical detonation, whereas 60 mm enabled more complete energy release. Sensitivity results, revealed a selective response: friction sensitivity remained unchanged (> 360 N), while impact sensitivity increased, with thresholds decreasing from > 50 J for ANFO to approximetly 40 J for modified systems. This indicates that sensitization is governed by compressive hot-spot formation rather than shear mechanisms. Thermal testing showed no bulk decomposition, though minor phase redistribution occurred. Overall, nitromethane enables controlled enhancement of ANFO performance without compromising safety, emphasizing the importance of scale-dependent interpretation in non-ideal explosives.

Article.Title: Burden of infectious disease–related mortality among cancer patients in the United States
Article.Authors: Mali B.; Mali A.; Mali A.; Hammad M.; Abu-hadid H.; Abdulrazzak M.; Jobran A.
Article.Abstract: The bidirectional relationship between cancer and infection is well established, with individuals diagnosed with cancer facing an elevated risk of severe infections, especially given the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance. As cancer survival rates improve, optimizing infection management has become critical to reducing the mortality burden of infections and supporting overall outcomes in this population. This study utilized data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, encompassing 17 registries and approximately 34.6% of the U.S. population. Infection-related mortality was assessed among cancer patients diagnosed between 2000 and 2021, including deaths due to tuberculosis, syphilis, septicemia, pneumonia and influenza, and other infectious and parasitic diseases, including HIV. Causes of death were analyzed according to demographic, clinical, treatment-related, and cancer-specific characteristics. Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated across survival intervals. Between 2000 and 2021, 6,891,191 patients in the United States were diagnosed with malignant disease, of whom 82,415 died from infectious illnesses, representing approximately 1.2% of the cohort. The overall standardized mortality ratio (SMR) was 1.59, with the highest SMR estimate of 4.07 occurring within the first year after diagnosis. The greatest SMR elevations estimates were observed among patients diagnosed in more recent years (2011–2021), males, and individuals from racial or ethnic minority groups, whereas married patients exhibited lower SMR estimates. Patients with advanced-stage disease and those receiving chemotherapy experienced a higher SMR estimate, while those who underwent surgery or radiotherapy had lower SMR estimates. Pneumonia and influenza accounted for the largest proportion of deaths; however, other infectious and parasitic diseases, including HIV, were associated with the highest relative excess mortality. Notably, the greatest increased SMR estimates were observed in Kaposi sarcoma, hepatobiliary cancers, and hematologic malignancies. The present findings reveal patterns of relative excess infection-related mortality, which may guide future research and inform public health strategies aimed at reducing infection-related mortality among cancer survivors. Additional research incorporating detailed patient-level factors, such as comorbidities, treatment modalities, and socioeconomic determinants, is necessary to clarify these associations and improve outcomes in this population.

Article.Title: Structural basis of condensate formation of VAPB protein
Article.Authors: Furuita K.; Enomoto-Kusano M.; Togawa W.; Komuro R.; Nakayama K.; Kobayashi N.; Kodama T.; Miyanoiri Y.; Fujiwara T.; Kojima C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated protein B (VAPB) is an endoplasmic reticulum protein implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) through its P56S mutation. Although pathological function loss and condensate formation of the VAPB P56S mutant are crucial for disease progression, the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we investigated the structural basis of VAPB condensate formation using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, turbidity analysis, and microscopy. Our results show that the major sperm protein domain of VAPB undergoes temperature-dependent condensate formation, a process regulated by localized structural dynamics. We identified a pH-sensitive hydrogen bond that functions as a switch to autoinhibition of condensate formation, as well as a flexible loop whose slow dynamics facilitate the multivalent interactions essential for condensate formation. The ALS-linked P56S mutant exhibits markedly enhanced condensate formation, which is associated with increased conformational heterogeneity that may promote aberrant intermolecular contacts related to pathological function loss. These findings reveal how specific dynamic features within a folded protein can drive condensate formation, providing a molecular framework for understanding both VAPB function and its pathological condensate formation.

Article.Title: Robust terminal sliding mode control of a permanent magnet synchronous motor for electric propulsion applications
Article.Authors: Yao W.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Conventional speed regulators for SPMSM drives in industrial applications often suffer from sluggish dynamics and inadequate immunity to disturbances. To address these challenges, a composite IGTISMC-IASTA scheme is presented. By designing an enhanced Gaussian terminal integral manifold, the strategy resolves the inherent contradiction between fast transient response and integral saturation. Concurrently, an effective chattering suppression adaptive super-twisting algorithm is employed to ensure finite-time convergence. The Lyapunov-based stability analysis confirms the robustness of the closed-loop system. Comparative experiments conducted on a TMS320F28379D-based test rig verify that the proposed method exhibits superior dynamic performance to the tested sliding-mode baselines under the laboratory conditions considered, with a no-load startup time of 0.35 s, negligible steady-state error, and strong robustness against step load, sinusoidal disturbance, and flux mismatch. Further validation in realistic propulsion scenarios, e.g., under wave-induced loads and higher power levels, may be performed prior to practical system deployment.

Article.Title: A risk analysis of irregular coal pillars subjected to impact from multiple fault cutting in deep mines
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Li D.; Ji Y.; Wang T.; Wang Y.; Zhao Z.; Wang W.; Sun C.; Sun B.
Article.Abstract: This study takes the rockburst risk assessment of a section coal pillar in a high-impact rockburst mine in Shandong Province as the engineering background. Through field monitoring, theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and other research means, it investigates the impact risk after the section coal pillar is intersected by multiple faults. The main conclusions are as follows: A mechanical calculation model was established to analyze the stress distribution within the irregular coal pillar region. The analysis indicates that when the coal pillar width is 106 m, the stress within the pillar is approximately 42 MPa; when the width is 158 m, the stress is about 33 MPa. In this study, the stress field distribution in the coal pillar area was analyzed at various stages: after the extraction of the 1306 working face, and as the 1310 working face advanced to 50 m, 100 m, 190 m, 250 m, 380 m, 593 m, and 850 m. The results revealed the following dynamic process: Before mining the 1310 face, high-stress zones were primarily concentrated near the fault and the acute-angle area of the 1306 goaf. After the 1310 face advanced 50 m, the high-stress zone began to expand toward the front of the 1310 working face, while the high-impact risk zone remained predominantly within the acute-angle region between the 1306 goaf and the fault. When the 1310 working face advanced by 100 m, high‑stress concentration zones were mainly distributed in two areas: one around the 1310 working face, and the other primarily in the acute‑angle intersection region between the 1306 goaf and the fault. At an advance of 190 m, a “square‑off” effect appeared in the 1310 working face, with high stresses concentrated mainly in the acute‑angle intersection zones of both the 1306 goaf and the 1310 working face with the fault. After the 1310 working face passed through the “square-off” effect zone and before its expansion, high stress was mainly concentrated in the acute-angle intersection region between the 1310 working face and the fault. Following the expansion of the 1310 working face, the coal pillar width decreased from 158 to 106 m. The reduction in pillar width led to a significant increase in overall stress within this section, as confirmed by both theoretical calculations and simulations, indicating a risk of full‑scale impact. Research of this type provides a valuable reference for the safe mining of working faces intersected by multiple faults in deep coal mines with high rockburst risk.

Article.Title: POU2F2 promotes the progression of clear cell renal cell carcinoma by regulating the JAK/STAT signaling pathway through SPI1
Article.Authors: Hu Y.; Yu Y.; Luo J.; Qi L.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common malignant tumor of the kidney, and effective therapeutic strategies are still lacking. Recent studies have indicated that the POU2F2 gene is abnormally expressed in various cancer types and is associated with poor prognosis. This study aims to investigate the impact of POU2F2 on ccRCC development. To begin with, we employed bioinformatics to verify the expres-sion of POU2F2 across cancers and found a significant upregulation of POU2F2 in ccRCC, which was associated with poorer survival outcomes. Next, we used genetic measures to up- or down-regulate POU2F2 expression in different ccRCC cell lines and results showed that the POU2F2 promoted ccRCC cell proliferation, reduced apoptosis, and enhanced cell migration and invasion capabilities. By using the The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset, functional enrichment analysis and Gene Set Enrichment Anal-ysis (GSEA), we scrutinized POU2F2-associated genes and signaling pathway. We also found that POU2F2 enhance ccRCCC cells invasion by activating the JAK/STAT sig-naling pathway, and the POU2F2 knockdown-induced reduction of JAK/STAT pathway key protein can be rescued by overexpression of SPI1, a transcription factor that is as-sociated with progression in multiple cancers and has a strong positive correlation with POU2F2 expression. In summary, POU2F2 promotes the progression of ccRCC through the activation of the JAK/STAT signaling pathway via SPI1. Our study sug-gested that POU2F2 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for ccRCC.

Article.Title: Image quality analysis of multi-dose chest CT based on KARL 3D reconstruction
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Wu T.; Lao Y.; Tang Y.; Long Y.; Li L.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: A study on the impact of Filtered Back Projection (FBP) reconstruction versus Knowledge-based Adaptive Regularized Reconstruction (KARL) 3D iterative reconstruction at different strength levels on chest CT image quality, and an investigation into the improvement efficacy of KARL 3D reconstruction under varying radiation dose conditions (ultra-low, low, and standard doses). This prospective study enrolled 240 patients who underwent non-contrast chest CT between January 2024 and August 2026. Patients were equally divided into three groups (n = 80 per group) according to tube current–time product: ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT, 21 mAs; CTDIvol 1.775 mGy), low-dose CT (LDCT, 130 mAs; CTDIvol 10.993 mGy), and standard-dose CT (SDCT, automatic mAs; CTDIvol 18.012 mGy). Scans were performed on United Imaging uCT-780 and uCT-710 scanners. Images were reconstructed using filtered back projection (FBP) and KARL 3D at levels 3, 6, and 9. CT values and standard deviation (SD) of noise were measured in the trachea, descending aorta, paravertebral muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and lung parenchyma; signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were calculated. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with the least significant difference (LSD) post-hoc test was used for comparisons. Subjective image quality was scored by two radiologists using a 5-point scale, with inter-observer agreement assessed by Cohen’s kappa. An a priori power analysis was conducted to verify sample size adequacy. For all dose groups, KARL 3D significantly reduced image noise and improved SNR and CNR in a strength-dependent manner compared with FBP (all P < 0.001). Compared with FBP, KARL 9 reduced noise by 37.5%–48.2% (mean 42.9%) in ULDCT, 31.6%–46.3% (mean 39.6%) in LDCT, and 30.0%–44.7% (mean 38.2%) in SDCT. The noise-reduction benefit of KARL 3D was greatest in the ULDCT group. CT values of the aorta, muscle, and adipose tissue showed no significant differences among reconstruction methods or dose groups (all P > 0.05). Subjective scores increased progressively with KARL level and dose (all P < 0.05). Inter-observer agreement was excellent (kappa > 0.75). Power analysis demonstrated Cohen’s f effect sizes ranging from 0.56 to 1.63, yielding statistical power > 99% for all primary comparisons at α = 0.05 with n = 80 per group. KARL 3D iterative reconstruction substantially improves chest CT image quality across all dose levels, with the greatest benefit at ultra-low dose. KARL 6–9 is recommended for ULDCT to achieve diagnostic image quality with substantial radiation dose reduction, while KARL 3–6 provides optimal balance for LDCT and SDCT. These findings were validated across two scanner platforms, supporting broad clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Association of adverse adulthood experiences with cardiovascular kidney metabolic syndrome
Article.Authors: Hong K.; He Q.; Wu Y.; Zhou J.; She Y.; Wang S.; Peng J.; Liu N.; Su D.; Fu J.; Zhang S.; Zhe X.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the associations of adverse adulthood experiences (AAEs) with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. In addition, we conducted a cross-sectional mediation analysis and a joint analysis to examine the associations of depressive symptoms with advanced CKM syndrome. AAEs were determined by five questionnaire indicators. The evaluation of depressive symptoms utilized the 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Advanced CKM syndrome refers to stages 3 and 4 of CKM syndrome. Logistic regression, cross-sectional mediation analysis, joint analysis, subgroup analysis and sensitivity analyses were applied in this study. This study included 5601 participants drawn from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The average prevalence of advanced CKM syndrome was 34.87%. After adjusting for all covariates, compared to low AAEs, the risk of advanced CKM syndrome was 1.83 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.26–2.67, P = 0.002] for high AAEs. In joint analysis, compared with the group with no depressive symptoms and low AAEs, the presence of depressive symptoms and high AAEs showed a higher risk of advanced CKM syndrome [odds ratio (OR) = 2.49, 95% CI: 1.87–3.32, P <0.001]. Depressive symptoms showed a possible association in the relationship between AAEs and advanced CKM syndrome. Compared to low AAEs, the ORs for medium and high AAEs were 1.011 (95% CI: 1.007–1.020, P < 0.001) and 1.024 (95% CI: 1.014–1.030, P < 0.001), respectively. Our study found AAEs were associated with an increased risk of advanced CKM syndrome. The findings are driven primarily by the psychosocial AAEs, while health-related items likely reflect disease-related factors. Besides, depressive symptoms showed a potential cross-sectional association with the relationship between AAEs and CKM syndrome. In addition, an combined association was noted between AAEs and depressive symptoms concerning advanced CKM syndrome.

Article.Title: Diagnostic and prognostic utility of rapid point-of-care GFAP and UCH-L1 testing in traumatic brain injury
Article.Authors: Yoon H.; Ro Y.; Jeong J.; Jung E.; Park G.; Jung Y.; Oh B.; Song S.; Shin S.
Article.Abstract: Timely identification of traumatic intracranial injuries and prediction of long-term outcomes remain critical challenges in traumatic brain injury (TBI) care. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have emerged as promising biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of TBI. This study evaluated the diagnostic and prognostic utility of a novel point-of-care testing (POCT) platform in a real-world emergency setting. We conducted a prospective, multicenter case–control study across five emergency departments. A total of 200 TBI patients with CT-identifiable intracranial injuries (CT + TBI) and 200 TBI patients without intracranial injuries (CT– TBI), all presenting within 24 h of injury, were enrolled. Serum GFAP and UCH-L1 levels were measured using a rapid multiplex POCT platform (VEUPLEX™ TBI Assay). Diagnostic performance metrics were calculated. Associations between biomarker levels and 6-month survival and neurological outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression among the CT + TBI patients. Median serum concentrations of both GFAP and UCH-L1 were significantly higher in the CT + TBI group compared to the CT– TBI group (medians [IQR] for GFAP: 129.95 [30.83–823.41] vs. 5.27 [3.48–6.14] pg/mL; UCH-L1: 262.23 [75.88–1170.04] vs. 58.49 [20.91–165.69] pg/mL; both p < 0.001). The combined biomarker assay demonstrated high sensitivity (0.910; 95% CI, 0.870–0.950) and negative predictive value (0.878; 95% CI, 0.825–0.931) for detecting CT-confirmed intracranial injuries. For long-term outcomes, the combined assay was significantly associated with reduced 6-month survival (AOR: 0.09; 95% CI, 0.01–0.84). Elevated UCH-L1 alone was significantly associated with decreased odds of favorable neurological recovery (AOR: 0.17; 95% CI, 0.05–0.62). Rapid bedside measurement of GFAP and UCH-L1 enables early detection of intracranial injury and is associated with long-term outcomes following TBI. The combined assay provides complementary diagnostic and prognostic information, supporting its potential role in acute TBI evaluation and risk stratification.

Article.Title: Association of the cardiometabolic index with hepatic enzymes and metabolic profiles among adults with overweight and obesity
Article.Authors: El-Sehrawy A.; Kandil I.; Maashi M.; Alharbi S.; Abohassan M.; labib S.; Alanazi M.; Yusuf S.; Salah A.; Abdalla R.; Eid E.
Article.Abstract: Growing evidence suggests that composite metabolic indices may offer valuable insights into obesity-related complications. The Cardiometabolic Index (CMI), a surrogate marker of adverse lipid profiles and central adiposity, has emerged as a promising indicator of cardiometabolic risk. Nevertheless, its association with liver-related biomarkers and metabolic phenotypes in overweight and obese populations has not been sufficiently investigated. This study aimed to examine the relationship between CMI and liver enzymes, as well as to characterize metabolic phenotypes across different levels of CMI in adults with overweight and obesity. In this cross-sectional analysis, 582 adults aged 18–65 years with overweight or obesity were included. Anthropometric indices, blood pressure, and biochemical markers—including lipid profile, hepatic enzymes, and fasting glucose—were measured. Participants were categorized into tertiles of CMI, which was calculated using established formulas. Individuals in the highest CMI category exhibited greater central adiposity and overall fat mass compared with those in the lowest category. They also had significantly higher levels of triglycerides, fasting glucose, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), as well as a higher prevalence of metabolic syndrome (all P < 0.05). These associations remained statistically significant after adjustment for potential confounding variables. Higher CMI values are associated with unfavorable metabolic characteristics and higher liver enzymes in individuals with overweight and obesity. Future longitudinal studies are warranted to clarify causal associations and underlying biological mechanisms for the associations between CMI and metabolic and hepatic enzymes in individuals with overweight or obesity.

Article.Title: Theoretical investigation of capsaicin adsorption on doped magnesium oxide fullerene-like nanocages for drug delivery and biosensing applications
Article.Authors: Alhowyan A.; Obaidullah A.; Mahdi W.
