Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employs density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations to elucidate the adsorption behavior of Capsaicin (CPC) through the carbonyl and hydroxyl groups on fullerene-like magnesium oxide-based nanocages, including pristine Mg 12 O 12 , aluminum-doped Mg 11 AlO 12 , and aluminum-nitrogen co-doped Mg 11 AlNO 11 structures. Results demonstrate that CPC binds spontaneously and exothermically via its carbonyl group, preferentially coordinating through oxygen atoms, with adsorption energies of − 0.848 eV (Mg 12 O 12 ), − 0.908 eV (Mg 11 AlO 12 ), and − 1.01 eV (Mg 11 AlNO 11 ) in aqueous media. Charge transfer analyses indicate a transfer of approximately 0.275 |e| from the cage to CPC, reducing system hardness and elevating chemical potential, thereby enhancing chemical reactivity. Notably, the CPC-Mg 11 AlO 12 system exhibits the highest dipole moment increase (23.53 Debye), implying improved solubility and potential for biosensing applications. Solvent effects reveal that water stabilizes excitons and enhances absorption features, whereas chloroform induces redshift and spectral broadening, as shown by TD-DFT spectra. Infrared vibrational analysis underscores strong carbonyl interactions, highlighting the role of doping in tuning adsorption characteristics. Our findings illustrate that Mg 11 AlO 12 is more sensitive for detecting the CPC (46.45%) than Mg 12 O 12 (18.65%) and Mg 11 AlNO 11 (6.93%) to exploit as a biochemical sensor. Collectively, these findings suggest that Mg 11 AlNO 11 cages are promising solvent-dependent platforms for biosensing and drug delivery, with tunable optical and electronic properties influenced by environmental conditions.

Article.Title: Lung ultrasound with Doppler pulmonary artery assessment for early detection of pediatric necrotizing pneumonia: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Grochowska M.; Strzelak A.; Peradzyńska J.; Urbankowska E.; Marczak H.; Kulus M.; Krenke K.
Article.Abstract: Necrotizing pneumonia (NP) is the most severe complication of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in children. While lung ultrasound (LUS) is a well-established tool for diagnosing CAP, its role in NP remains understudied. Our aim was to evaluate the utility of LUS for the early diagnosis of NP in children. In this prospective cohort study, we assessed hospitalized children with CAP at a tertiary hospital from January 2023 to August 2024. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings, including chest X-ray (CXR) and LUS with color Doppler (CD) and Pulsed Wave (PW), were analyzed. A total of 108 patients were included, of whom 41 (38%) developed NP. Hypoechoic lesions (HLs), fluid bronchogram, and hypoperfusion on CD LUS were significantly more common in NP vs. non-NP group (90.2% vs. 6%, 85.4% vs. 51.5%, and 87.8% vs. 11.9%, respectively, P < .001 for all). HLs and hypoperfusion were strongly correlated with NP diagnosis (Cramér’s V = 0.841 and 0.749, respectively). HLs demonstrated high sensitivity (90.24%) and specificity (94.03%) in diagnosing NP (CXR was used as the reference standard). PW pulmonary artery measurements showed triphasic high-resistance flow with a median resistive index of 0.92 (IQR, 0.88–0.98) and pulsatility index of 2.8 (IQR, 2.2–3.2). HLs on LUS allowed detection of necrotic changes a median of 4 days earlier than radiolucencies on CXR. HLs and hypoperfusion on CD are the most characteristic LUS features of NP. HLs on LUS can detect necrosis early with high sensitivity and specificity and may serve as a diagnostic tool for NP in children.

Article.Title: Trends over two decades in prostate biopsy volume and cancer detection alongside adoption of MRI before biopsy in Yamanashi, Japan
Article.Authors: Mochizuki T.; Sawada N.; Sugimura K.; Tsuchida T.; Furuya R.; Shimura H.; Kira S.; Kamiyama M.; Takeda M.; Mitsui T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prostate biopsy practice has evolved substantially with the introduction of pre-biopsy magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), but long-term regional changes remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed annual prefecture-wide aggregate data from Yamanashi, Japan, for fiscal years 2004–2024 and 2,929 institutional biopsy procedures performed at the University of Yamanashi Hospital during fiscal years 2011–2024. Temporal trends were assessed using linear and grouped quasibinomial regression, and policy-period associations were evaluated after adjustment for fiscal year. Across Yamanashi Prefecture, 20,192 biopsy procedures were reported, with 10,365 cancers detected. Annual biopsy volume decreased by 21.1 procedures per fiscal year (95% confidence interval [CI], − 29.5 to − 12.8; P < 0.001), whereas the cancer detection rate increased from 39.4% to 69.5% (odds ratio [OR] per fiscal year, 1.069; 95% CI, 1.061–1.077; P < 0.001). Institutionally, pre-biopsy MRI utilization increased from 10.2% to 97.7%, while overall and clinically significant prostate cancer detection increased significantly; Grade Group 1 detection did not. After temporal-trend adjustment, a significant post-policy level difference was observed only for MRI utilization (OR, 9.295; 95% CI, 3.562–24.257; P < 0.001). These findings suggest increasingly selective biopsy practice, while improvements in cancer detection likely reflect multiple evolving diagnostic factors rather than MRI policy alone.

Article.Title: Machine learning-assisted energy-efficient routing framework for MANET-based smart healthcare communication
Article.Authors: Sitharthan S.; Balamurali R.; Chellamuthu P.
Article.Abstract: Mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) are being used as a viable approach to decentralized communication infrastructure in health care as they can be self-configured and work independently of any infrastructure requirements. Yet, traditional MANET routing algorithms like Adhoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) and Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) face problems like excessive routing delay, losses in packet transmissions, and energy wastage in dynamic environments. In this context, this research paper aims to provide an energy-efficient routing mechanism using machine learning. The proposed work combines reinforcement learning (RL) based dynamic routing approach along with QoS (QoS) aware parameters such as the amount of remaining node energy, link quality, queue density, and transmission time. This model is analyzed under healthcare oriented communication system for real time monitoring of neonatal incubators. Performance comparison reveals that the developed approach is capable of providing a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 93%, beating the existing approaches namely AODV and DSR by delivering 78% and 74%, respectively. The suggested solution also helps decrease the end-to-end delay down to 140 ms and increases the throughput up to 260 kbps while minimizing the energy consumption to 0.72 J. Moreover, the ML-based prediction module attains an R 2 score of 0.98 with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.2 and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.8. Hence, the achieved results reveal that the suggested intelligent routing framework can be considered quite effective in terms of increasing communication reliability and QoS performance as well as reducing energy consumption.

Article.Title: Geometry-controlled gamma-ray transport in fractured rock masses: coupled effects of discontinuity orientation and infill composition
Article.Authors: Golmohammadi S.; Noorian-Bidgoli M.
Article.Abstract: Reliable prediction of gamma-ray attenuation in rock masses remains challenging because most previous studies treat rocks as homogeneous media and neglect the structural role of discontinuities. In fractured rock systems, however, joint orientation and infill composition can significantly modify the effective photon path and produce direction-dependent attenuation behavior. This study addresses this gap through an integrated experimental and numerical investigation of gamma-ray attenuation in jointed rock masses. Five representative lithologies—granite, magnetite, hornblende, travertine, and salt rock—were selected to cover a wide range of densities and mineralogical compositions. Artificial discontinuities were introduced over a full directional spectrum, with dip angles systematically varied from 0° to 90° in 5° increments. Experimental measurements were performed using a monoenergetic 137 Cs gamma source (0.662 MeV) coupled with a Geiger-Müller detector to determine transmitted photon intensity. In addition, different infill materials, including low-density fillers (clay and lime) and high-atomic-number materials (iron oxide, lead oxide, and metallic lead), were incorporated to evaluate their effects on attenuation behavior. In parallel, photon transport simulations were conducted using the MCNPX code to reproduce the experimental configuration and extend the analysis beyond laboratory constraints. The results demonstrate attenuation is governed by coupled discontinuity geometry and infill composition across the angular spectrum. Variations in dip angle modify photon transport geometry, resulting in direction-dependent attenuation behavior. High-density and high-Z materials exhibit greater attenuation capacity, while low-density materials show reduced sensitivity to geometric effects. Infill materials significantly influence attenuation, with lead-based fillers producing the most pronounced enhancement. A strong agreement between experimental and numerical results confirms the reliability of the modeling framework. Overall, gamma-ray attenuation in fractured rock systems is governed by coupled material–geometry interactions rather than intrinsic properties alone, highlighting the importance of incorporating discontinuity orientation and infill characteristics in radiation shielding design.

Article.Title: Effects of supervised reformer pilates and home-based mat pilates on menopausal symptoms and related health outcomes in postmenopausal women with obesity: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Kocamer M.; Atılgan E.
Article.Abstract: To compare the effects of supervised Reformer Pilates, home-based Mat Pilates, and a lifestyle education program on menopausal symptoms (primary outcome), as well as menopause-specific quality of life, depressive symptoms, sleep quality, body composition, and blood lipid profile (secondary outcomes) in postmenopausal women with obesity. This three-arm randomized controlled trial included 45 postmenopausal women with obesity who were randomly assigned to a Reformer Pilates group (n = 15), a Mat Pilates group (n = 15), or an Education group (n = 15). Pilates interventions were performed twice weekly for 8 weeks, whereas the Education group received a structured lifestyle education program. Menopausal symptoms were assessed using the Menopausal Symptom Evaluation Scale (MSES). Secondary outcomes included menopause-specific quality of life (MENQOL), depressive symptoms, sleep quality, body composition, and fasting blood lipid profile. Mixed repeated-measures ANOVA was used as the primary analysis. ANCOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons was performed for outcomes with baseline imbalance. Menopausal symptoms, the prespecified primary outcome, demonstrated a significant Group × Time interaction ( p < 0.001). After adjustment for baseline values, both the Reformer Pilates group (adjusted mean difference = − 6.47, 95% CI − 8.83 to − 4.12; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001) and the Mat Pilates group (adjusted mean difference = − 5.24, 95% CI − 7.63 to − 2.85; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001) showed significantly greater improvement than the Education group, whereas no significant difference was observed between the two Pilates interventions. Significant Group × Time interaction effects were also observed for MENQOL, body weight, body mass index, body fat percentage, lean body mass, and blood lipid parameters (all p < 0.05). Depressive symptoms and sleep quality improved over time in all groups, but no significant Group × Time interactions were observed (both p > 0.05). Both supervised Reformer Pilates and home-based Mat Pilates were more effective than lifestyle education in improving menopausal symptoms, the primary outcome of this study. Reformer Pilates also demonstrated greater improvements than Mat Pilates for menopause-specific quality of life and selected body composition outcomes. Improvements in depressive symptoms and sleep quality were observed across all groups, suggesting that non-specific behavioral and contextual factors may also have contributed. Larger randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are warranted to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Dielectrophoresis-enhanced rejuvenation of water-tree-degraded XLPE cables under an AC electric field: a particle trajectory analysis
Article.Authors: Fadakar F.; Hosseini S.
Article.Abstract: The study investigates the rejuvenation of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cables affected by water tree degradation using a combination of an applied AC voltage and the resulting dielectrophoretic force. The finite element method in COMSOL Multiphysics is implemented to show that the integrity of the cable is heavily compromised due to an intensified electric field around water trees. Two rejuvenation scenarios were examined: one with the cable de-energized, and the other with a fraction of its nominal voltage applied. In the meantime, the particle trajectory instrument is employed to analyze the motion of rejuvenation fluid in relation to both its development and accumulation within the water tree region. Dielectrophoretic forces cause the rejuvenation fluid to focus on the water tree region under an AC electric field. This leads to the idea that the application of controlled voltage during the rejuvenation process may enhance fluid penetration and has potential relevance to the reliability of XLPE cables.

Article.Title: Elevated plantar pressure during gait is observed in male ACL-deficient non-copers compared with copers and healthy controls
Article.Authors: Golparian A.; Anbarian M.; Mansoorizadeh M.; Golparian M.
Article.Abstract: Patients with anterior cruciate ligament deficiency (ACLD) exhibit altered gait biomechanics, but plantar pressure distribution patterns across functional subgroups (copers vs. non-copers) remain unexplored. This study investigated plantar pressure distribution during walking in 50 male patients with ACLD (25 copers, 25 non-copers) and 23 healthy male controls. Plantar pressure data were collected using the Footscan pressure platform (254 Hz). Maximum plantar pressure (N/cm 2 ) across ten plantar regions, the symmetry index, and relative timing of roll-over phases (% stance time) were compared between groups using one-way ANOVA (post-hoc comparisons with Holm's correction; α = 0.05). Maximum plantar pressure did not differ significantly between copers and controls in any of the ten plantar regions (all p > 0.10, |d|≤ 0.47). In contrast, non-copers exhibited significantly higher pressures than both copers (all p ≤ 0.05, d ≥ 0.58) and controls ( p < 0.05 in eight of ten regions; d up to 1.97), except at the hallux and midfoot. Symmetry index did not differ significantly among groups in any region. Non-copers showed a significantly shorter initial contact phase than controls ( p = 0.03, d = − 0.66), the only significant difference among the roll-over phase timing variables (all other p ≥ 0.10). Plantar pressure distribution during gait differed markedly between ACLD functional subgroups: copers showed loading patterns broadly consistent with healthy controls, whereas non-copers exhibited significantly elevated maximum plantar pressure across most plantar regions relative to both groups. These findings indicate that the functional consequences of ACLD in non-copers extend to measurable alterations in plantar loading. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be regarded as preliminary evidence, and future diagnostic-accuracy studies are needed to determine their broader clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Pilot comparison of nine large language models generating radiological reports from dental panoramic radiograph pathology notation
Article.Authors: Chęcińska K.; Chęciński M.; Turosz N.; Bartoszewski B.; Hoppe A.; Madabushi H.; Iacoviello P.; Sikora M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) may help convert structured pathology notations derived from dental panoramic radiographs (DPRs) into radiological reports, but comparative data remain limited. This pilot head-to-head study evaluated nine publicly available LLMs across five domains: correct tooth numbering, correct diagnosis assignment, avoidance of confabulations, proper radiological terminology, and avoidance of repetitions. Nineteen anonymized DPRs from an open-source repository were converted into standardized pathology notations by an experienced clinician. Nine LLMs generated reports from identical prompts and identical input data without task-specific fine-tuning. Report quality was rated on a 3-point ordinal scale. Between-model differences were assessed using the Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc comparisons; accuracy and F1-scores were also calculated. Significant between-model differences were found in correct diagnosis assignment, avoidance of confabulations, and proper radiological terminology, whereas differences were smaller in correct tooth numbering and avoidance of repetitions. The strongest overall performance was achieved by o1 and o3-mini (accuracy: 0.91 and 0.92; F1-score: 0.95 and 0.96), with o3-mini-high also performing strongly (accuracy: 0.87; F1-score: 0.93). No model consistently met expert expectations across all domains. Performance differed significantly between models. Reasoning-oriented models, particularly o1 and o3-mini, performed best overall, especially in correct diagnosis assignment and avoidance of confabulations. LLM-assisted radiological reporting appears promising, but current performance does not support autonomous clinical use and still requires expert oversight. Moreover, the findings reflect model versions available at the time of testing and should not be interpreted as a definitive ranking of LLM performance.

Article.Title: Early-onset gout is associated with an increased risk of genitourinary cancers in a nationwide cohort of 6.5 million young Korean adults
Article.Authors: Lee B.; Lee K.; Ahn J.; Han K.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gout is prevalent among older adults, yet its incidence is increasing in younger populations. Gout has been linked to higher genitourinary cancer risk in middle-aged and older populations, but its long-term impact in early-onset gout remains unclear. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance Service data of adults aged 20–39 years who underwent health screenings between 2009 and 2012. Gout was defined using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision code M10 and prescription records. Participants were followed up until December 31, 2023. The primary outcome was cancer incidence. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. Of 6,511,300 young adults, 35,946 (0.6%) had gout at baseline (mean age, 33.38 ± 4.33 years). Early-onset gout was associated with increased risks of renal (aHR 1.80), bladder (aHR 1.80), and prostate (aHR 1.63) cancers. The coexistence of gout and chronic kidney disease (CKD) substantially elevated risks of renal (aHR 5.59), bladder (aHR 7.01), and prostate (aHR 5.65) cancers, with significant interaction effects ( p < 0.01 for all). Young adults with gout have an elevated risk of prostate cancers, which is further amplified in the presence of CKD. These findings suggest that awareness of long-term oncological risk and proactive management of modifiable risk factors may be warranted in young adults with gout, particularly those with coexisting CKD.

Article.Title: Extended logarithmic TODIM framework based on MACONT for visual effects evaluation of 3D animation production based on computer graphics under probabilistic linguistic term sets
Article.Authors: Yan B.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: The 3D animation production visual effects evaluation model based on computer graphics is an inherent fuzzy qualitative expert opinion, interdependent multivariate evaluation criteria, and uncertainty multiple-attribute group decision-making (MAGDM) problem. Hence, it involves reliable and adaptive multiple-attribute decision-making (MADM) methods to yield scientific, feasible, and consistent assessment results. This explains why advanced methods have been applied to ensure credible evaluation results for the most recent industrial animation projects. This paper proposes a method based on Logarithmic TODIM (LogTODIM) and MACONT (Mixed Aggregation by Comprehensive Normalization Technique) to deal with such complicated MAGDM problems. Given the uncertainty of quality evaluation, Probabilistic Linguistic Term Sets (PLTSs) are used to collect and represent the evaluation information. A PL-LogTODIM-MACONT model to conduct the MAGDM under the PLTS environment is presented. The MEREC method derives the objective weights of criteria. Finally, to validate and demonstrate the applicability of the proposed integrated method, a case of visual effects evaluation of 3D animation production based on computer graphics is illustrated and analyzed in detail.

Article.Title: AI-assisted high-density near-infrared spectroscopy system for cerebral oxygen saturation measurement in a porcine ischemia model
Article.Authors: Yu S.; Kim T.; Kim H.; Kim J.; Park H.; Kwon W.; Koh B.; Lee J.; Bae H.; Ko S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stroke is one of the leading causes of mortality and is characterized by a sudden interruption of cerebral perfusion, resulting in neurological impairment. Especially in large-vessel occlusion (LVO), the absence of timely reperfusion therapy can lead to severe ischemic injury, causing permanent disability or death. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is a non-invasive technique that estimates regional cerebral oxygen saturation ( $$\hbox {rSO}_2$$ ) by analyzing near-infrared light transmitted through biological tissue. Despite its portability and cost-effectiveness, commercial NIRS systems that employ spatially resolved spectroscopy (SRS) algorithms lack sufficient reliability to distinguish between normal and stroke-affected conditions because of oversimplified assumptions. In this study, we propose an artificial intelligence–assisted NIRS system that analyzes high-density optical measurements to estimate cerebral oxygenation beyond the simplified assumptions of conventional SRS algorithms. Trained on an MRI-based synthetic dataset using cortical $$\hbox {rSO}_2$$ as the target label, the proposed model leverages measurements obtained at multiple source–detector distances to exploit depth-dependent spatial information and improve sensitivity to cortical oxygenation signals. The proposed system was validated through a porcine common carotid artery occlusion experiment and compared with a conventional SRS-based NIRS system. Both systems showed decreases during occlusion and recovery after reperfusion, but statistically significant baseline-relative changes after multiple-comparison correction were observed only for NIRSIT-X. Furthermore, we compared the measured oxygen saturation against jugular venous oxygen saturation ( $$\hbox {SjvO}_2$$ ) as a physiological reference. In conclusion, based on linear mixed-effects modeling, the proposed system demonstrated a substantially stronger association with $$\hbox {SjvO}_2$$ than the conventional system, achieving a markedly higher marginal $$R^2$$ (0.561 vs. 0.177), indicating stronger physiological relevance for cerebral oxygenation monitoring.

Article.Title: Mechanistic investigation of Rhodamine B adsorption onto MWCNT/AgNP nanocomposites under complex aqueous conditions
Article.Authors: Erol K.; Akveran G.; Karasartova D.; Tatar D.; Veyisoğlu A.; Gökmeşe F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The efficient removal of persistent organic dyes under realistic wastewater conditions remains a major challenge in environmental remediation. Herein, a multi-walled carbon nanotube/silver nanoparticle (MWCNT/AgNP) nanocomposite was developed and systematically evaluated for Rhodamine B (RhB) removal under complex aqueous environments. The material exhibited a high adsorption capacity of 286.5 mg g⁻¹ with rapid equilibrium within 45 min. Adsorption followed the Langmuir model (qₘₐₓ = 279.0 mg g⁻¹) and pseudo-second-order kinetics, while thermodynamic parameters (ΔG° = −5.6 to − 6.9 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔH° = +12.7 kJ mol⁻¹) confirmed a spontaneous and endothermic process. Notably, high adsorption performance was maintained at elevated dye concentration (3000 mg L⁻¹) and under high ionic strength, indicating strong resistance to environmental interference. Mechanistic analysis suggested that RhB adsorption likely involves the synergistic contribution of π–π interactions, hydrophobic effects, electrostatic attraction, and weak Ag-mediated interactions. Unlike conventional adsorption studies under simplified conditions, this work provides a condition-dependent interpretation of adsorption behavior by linking surface chemistry to adsorption performance in complex aqueous media. These findings highlight the robustness of the developed MWCNT/AgNP nanocomposite under the investigated conditions and its promising potential for advanced wastewater treatment applications.

Article.Title: Psychometric properties of a fathers’ outcome expectancies of lifestyle behaviors instrument for father-child reciprocal reinforcement
Article.Authors: Jimenez-Garcia J.; Musaad S.; Arredondo E.; Beltran A.; Morgan P.; Rayward A.; Rueda J.; Soltero E.; Zachariah J.; Baranowski T.; O’Connor T.
Article.Abstract: We propose reciprocal reinforcement as a bidirectional process through which fathers and children mutually shape lifestyle behaviors. Treating the father as the starting actor, we introduce a father-focused instrument that assesses outcome expectancies for lifestyle behaviors across eating, physical activity, and screen use. The instrument comprises two complementary scales: Self-Oriented Outcome Expectancies of Lifestyle Behaviors (SOEL), indexing expectancies organized around fathers’ own health, and Child-Oriented Outcome Expectancies of Lifestyle Behaviors (COEL), indexing expectancies organized around influencing the child through visible modeling and signaling. Using baseline data from the Healthy Dads, Healthy Kids for Hispanics efficacy trial, confirmatory factor analyses supported a higher order Lifestyle factor for both scales across the three domains (eating, physical activity, screen use), with theoretically consistent loadings and evidence of reliability and convergent and discriminant validity. Conceptually, this instrument advances the study of reciprocal reinforcement by operationalizing a potential initiating mechanism: fathers’ purpose driven lifestyle behaviors that serve self-benefit and dyadic influence, thereby setting conditions for iterative, mutually reinforcing exchanges. The SOEL and COEL scales provide a brief, theory grounded tool for testing father driven pathways of reciprocal reinforcement and for informing family-based interventions targeting sustained change in diet, physical activity, and screen.

Article.Title: Immune priming reprograms the maggot secretome to enhance anti-Leishmania activity
Article.Authors: Malekian A.; Maleki-Ravasan N.; Sardari S.; Abdollahnia A.; Bahmani K.; Vazirpour Y.; Babaei J.; Karmian F.; Parvizi P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cutaneous leishmaniasis remains a major unmet medical need due to treatment toxicity, emerging drug resistance, prolonged therapy, and persistent tissue damage. Lucilia sericata (Diptera: Calliphoridae) larvae are a promising source of bioactive secretions with antimicrobial and wound-healing properties. Here, we investigated whether immune priming of L. sericata larvae with Leishmania major modulates the anti-leishmanial activity and metabolic profile of larval-derived products. Larvae underwent oral, intrahemocoelic, or combined priming, and their excretory/secretory (E/S) products and total-body extracts were evaluated against L. major promastigotes. Combined priming produced the strongest anti-leishmanial activity at 24 h, reducing parasite viability to 35.26% in E/S products. IC₅₀ values were 176.9 µg/mL for total-body extracts and 248.5 µg/mL for E/S products. LC-MS profiling revealed extensive metabolic remodeling, characterized by enrichment of molecular features putatively associated with antimicrobial peptides, flavonoids, and lipid metabolites, alongside depletion of several primary metabolic intermediates. These findings are consistent with a shift toward defense-associated metabolism and enhanced antiparasitic activity following immune priming. Overall, immune priming reprogrammed the larval secretome and enhanced its in vitro activity against L. major , supporting further investigation of cell-free larval-derived products as candidate bioactive preparations for cutaneous leishmaniasis.

Article.Title: EEG based brain computer interface using multinomial regressive transformer learning for chronic neuropathic pain detection
Article.Authors: Divya P.; Selvy P.
Article.Abstract: Chronic neuropathic pain is a stressful health problem caused by a dysfunction of the nervous system severely impacts a patient’s life. Early chronic neuropathic pain detection model utilizes the deep learning and machine learning techniques. However, traditional methods faced challenges in achieving accurate and timely detection. To improve the accuracy of chronic neuropathic pain detection, a novel M ultinomial R egressive S tochastic G radient O ptimized T ransformer L earning (MRSGOTL) model is developed. EEG signal pre-processing is performed to improve the signal quality using Hilbert–Huang transform. Then, the deep transformer learning is performed for chronic neuropathic pain detection. Transformer learning uses Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifier model to classify the different degrees of neuropathic pain severity with less error through the Stochastic Gradient grasshopper optimization algorithm. The model achieved superior performance metrics, including 96% accuracy, 0.97 of precision, 0.98 of recall, 0.97 of F1-score, along with the time of 151 s, significantly outperforming traditional models. The finds highlights that the proposed model supports clinicians in early diagnosis and making effective treatment decisions.

Article.Title: Effect of the multimodal vestibular training on balance and quality of life in stroke survivors: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Mishra P.; Rizvi M.; Sethi P.; Kumari S.; Sharma A.; Shaik A.; Seyam M.; Raza S.; Ahmad F.; Anwer S.; Iqbal A.; Alghadir A.
Article.Abstract: Post-stroke balance impairment is multifactorial, and limited evidence is available on whether Multimodal Vestibular Training (MVT) provides additional benefits when added to conventional balance training. This study investigated the effect of a four-week MVT program on balance, functional mobility, and quality of life in chronic stroke survivors. After screening 25 stroke patients, 21 eligible chronic stroke survivors were enrolled. Participants were aged 30–75 years, had stroke duration of at least six months, could walk at least 10 m safely under supervision, had MMSE scores ≥ 24, and had Berg Balance Scale scores > 21. Participants were randomly assigned to the experimental group ( n = 11), which received MVT with conventional balance training, or the control group ( n = 10), which received conventional balance training only. Both groups received three supervised 45-minute sessions per week for four weeks. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, Berg Balance Score (BBS), and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life questionnaire (SS-QoL). Eighteen participants completed the post-intervention assessment and were included in the final analysis, with nine participants in each group. No significant baseline differences were observed between groups. Post-intervention analysis showed significantly better TUG scores in the experimental group than the control group, ( p = 0.002), and significantly better SS-QoL scores ( p = 0.006). Post-intervention BBS scores did not differ significantly between groups ( p = 0.924). Change-score analysis showed significantly greater improvement in the experimental group for TUG ( p = 0.042), BBS ( p = 0.013), and SS-QoL ( p = 0.023). The findings suggest that MVT, when added to conventional rehabilitation, may be associated with improvements in functional mobility and selected quality-of-life outcomes in chronic stroke survivors. BBS scores improved over time, although the post-intervention between-group difference was not significant. Given the limited sample size and short intervention duration, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and confirmed in larger adequately powered randomized controlled trials. Trial registration: The study protocol was prospectively registered online in the Clinical Trial Registry India (CTRI) at https//www.ctri.nic.in/ with the identifier CTRI/2023/12/060822 dated 18/12/2023.

Article.Title: AI-powered, seismic hazard-integrated modeling of hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure in the Zagros Lurestan Provinces
Article.Authors: Valizadeh T.; Maleki Z.; Saidi A.; Sharifi R.; Kianoush P.
Article.Abstract: The increasing global demand for resilient subsurface energy systems requires understanding how active tectonics influence hydrocarbon trap evolution and reservoir pressure behavior. Tectonically active regions, such as the Lurestan provinces of the Zagros Fold-Thrust Belt, pose persistent challenges due to structural complexity and pressure instability. This study adopts a multiscale, hazard-integrated approach bridging seismic risk assessment and adaptive reservoir modeling. No assertion is made that individual modern earthquakes directly control million-year pressure evolution. Rather, modern seismicity correlates with long-term fault slip rates (R² = 0.84) and InSAR strain rates (R² = 0.79), and persistent seismic cycling—documented by paleoseismic records—maintains elevated pressures through a fault-valve mechanism. It is emphasized that the analysis demonstrates spatial correlation between modern seismicity patterns and reservoir pressure, not temporal causation. Modern seismicity serves as a spatial proxy for where long-term tectonic deformation—and thus elevated reservoir pressure—is concentrated. Unlike prior studies, this work establishes quantitative linkages between seismic hazard parameters and reservoir pressure through province-specific formulas, representing a novel integration of AI, blockchain-secured geofluid tracing, and geomechanical simulation for active orogenic belts. Earthquake density, magnitude, and hazard maps were synthesized with AI-enhanced modeling, InSAR-derived strain fields, and blockchain tracing. Quantitative analysis reveals distinct province-specific pressure profiles: North East Lurestan (brittle fault-dominated) exhibits the highest pressure (42.7 ± 2.1 MPa); Central Lurestan (interference zone) shows moderate pressure (36.4 ± 1.8 MPa); and South West Lurestan (deep-rooted attenuated) maintains lower pressure (28.1 ± 1.5 MPa). The GeoCognitive Reservoir Intelligence (GCRI) framework enables near-real-time simulation of trap evolution, seal integrity, and pressure dynamics under seismic loading. These findings establish a methodological framework for adaptive hydrocarbon management transferable to other active basins following local recalibration.

Article.Title: Multi-modal lesion mapping of expressive aprosodia
Article.Authors: Peters J.; Boes A.; Griffis J.; Bruss J.; Tranel D.; Kliemann D.
Article.Abstract: Affective prosody facilitates the communication of emotions by modulating paralinguistic features of speech (e.g., pitch and rhythm). Patients with brain injuries may exhibit impaired expression of affective prosody, referred to as expressive aprosodia, adversely impacting social interactions and quality of life. Despite many previous lesion studies, relatively few studies have investigated neural correlates of expressive aprosodia using a combination of lesion location, as well as associated structural and functional network mapping, within a large patient sample. There is especially a need to advance our understanding of the neurobiology associated with expressive aprosodia in the chronic phase (i.e., >3 months after lesion onset) given the practical importance of long-term outcomes in regard to social functioning and quality of life. The present study therefore aimed to characterize how expressive aprosodia relates to lesion location and disruption of associated structural and functional brain networks in a large sample of participants with chronic focal brain lesions (N = 673). Using a clinical expert evaluation of prosody and multi-modal lesion mapping, the results showed that expressive aprosodia was most strongly associated with i) lesions affecting right-lateralized fronto-insular-striatal regions, ii) prominent disconnection of right-lateralized cortico-subcortical pathways, and iii) damage to regions exhibiting functional connectivity with subcortical (basal ganglia, thalamus) and cortical ventral attention/salience networks. Overall, these findings are consistent with a previously proposed dorsal stream for expressive aprosodia and provide further insights into the neural architecture whose damage is associated with chronic expressive aprosodia.
Article.Keywords: Affective prosody; Aprosodia; Brain lesion; Emotion; Lesion mapping

Article.Title: Distribution and age-interactions of cortical thickness associated with specific classes of medication used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder: Results from the international ENIGMA consortium
Article.Authors: Ivanov I.; Dzinalija N.; Abe Y.; Alonso P.; Ameis S.; Arnold P.; Baker J.; Balachander S.; Banaj N.; Bargalló N.; Batistuzzo M.; Benedetti F.; Beucke J.; Bollettini I.; Brennan B.; Buitelaar J.; Calvo R.; Cheng Y.; Ching C.; Cho K.; Dallaspezia S.; Denys D.; Diniz J.; Ely B.; Ferreira S.
Article.Abstract: MRI studies have revealed structural brain abnormalities in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Less is known about how age and medication influence them. We analyzed cortical thickness (CT) data from the ENIGMA-OCD Consortium, the world's largest OCD MRI database (46 datasets from 35 centers). Subjects comprised 2057 healthy controls, 1167 unmedicated individuals with OCD, and 1073 individuals with OCD taking one or more psychiatric medications at time of scan. Using a harmonized FreeSurfer protocol, each MRI was parcellated into 68 cortical regions. Linear mixed models controlling for site and symptom severity mapped associations of OCD diagnosis and medication-any psychiatric medication and the medication classes serotonin-reuptake inhibitors (SRIs), tricyclics, antipsychotics, and benzodiazepines-on CT and their interaction with age in each region. Findings surviving FDR-correction included: 1) Unmedicated OCD participants showed thicker cortex and/or lesser CT decrease with age than controls in precentral, inferior parietal, superior parietal, and superior temporal regions (p < .001-.002); 2) In several regions, OCD participants taking any medication had thinner cortex than unmedicated; negative associations of age with CT were similar to controls (p < .001-.005). 3) Findings for SRIs resembled those in for any psychiatric medication. 4) CT was lower in participants taking benzodiazepines than in unmedicated participants in 30 regions (p < .001-.014). No associations of CT involving tricyclics or antipsychotics survived FDR-correction. Commonly prescribed OCD drugs may influence CT in ways that vary with cortical region and medication class. Potential mechanisms are discussed.
Article.Keywords: Aging; Cortical thickness; Obsessive-compulsive disorder; Pharmacotherapy

Article.Title: Highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM) in a 16-year-old male: Investigating involuntary autobiographical memory with questionnaire and laboratory methods
Article.Authors: Barzykowski K.; Santangelo V.; Kvavilashvili L.; Moulin C.
Article.Abstract: Highly Superior Autobiographical Memory (HSAM) is characterized by an exceptional ability to recall personal past events with remarkable accuracy and detail. While the mechanisms underlying this ability have begun to be elucidated, research so far has largely focused mainly on voluntary retrieval processes. The present study aimed to investigate autobiographical memory functioning in a single HSAM case (KCL), with a particular focus on involuntary autobiographical memories (IAMs). We combined standardized HSAM screening procedures with a multi-method assessment of autobiographical memory, implemented remotely under continuous researcher supervision. General autobiographical functioning was assessed using the Autobiographical Recollection Test and the Survey of Autobiographical Memory. Additional measures captured general memory functioning, mind-wandering, metacognitive and phenomenological characteristics, cognitive control, and affective and personality variables. IAMs were assessed using both self-report (Involuntary Autobiographical Memory Inventory) and a laboratory vigilance task with incidental cue-words and probe-caught thought sampling. KCL met established HSAM criteria and exhibited a markedly elevated frequency of IAMs relative to a comparison group, both in self-report and laboratory measures. Crucially, this increase did not reflect a general rise in spontaneous cognition, as overall task-unrelated thought frequency remained comparable, but rather a selective bias toward autobiographical content. At the same time, KCL did not differ from the general population in overall phenomenological experience of remembering, although he reported elevated autobiographical memory ability alongside increased confidence in memory accuracy. The results highlight the central role of involuntary remembering and point to altered cue sensitivity and lowered retrieval thresholds as key mechanisms underlying exceptional autobiographical memory.
Article.Keywords: Autobiographical memory; HSAM; Highly superior autobiographical memory; IAMI; Involuntary autobiographical memories; Threshold model

Article.Title: Clarifying the scope and boundaries of the motor simulation theory: A constructive perspective for motor imagery research
Article.Authors: Guillot A.; Lebon F.; Vogt S.; Zentgraf K.; Stinear C.; Di Rienzo F.
Article.Abstract: Motor imagery has attracted renewed interest in recent years, along with renewed debate about the Motor Simulation Theory, which posits activation of motor-related neural systems to internally simulate action without execution. While recent work has clarified some empirical limits of imagery, particularly in feedback-based learning, other critiques misinterpret the theory's core assumptions. This paper distinguishes between empirically grounded challenges that refine the Motor Simulation Theory, such as those involving executive processes and partial motor activation, and conceptual misunderstandings that mischaracterize the theory. Claims that the theory predicts exact timing equivalence or complete neural overlap with action execution, or supports sensorimotor adaptation overlook the functional equivalence principle at its foundation. We also argue that alternative, behaviorally focused theories often neglect robust neurophysiological evidence underpinning the Motor Simulation Theory. We advocate for an integrated perspective that maintains its predictive value while accommodating valid critiques, aiming to clarify its boundaries and relevance for imagery research.
Article.Keywords: Mental imagery; Mental practice; Motor cognition; Motor learning; Neurofunctional equivalence

Article.Title: The role of extra-striate areas in conscious motor behavior: A registered report with fast-optical imaging
Article.Authors: Colombari E.; Parisi G.; Mele S.; Mazzi C.; Savazzi S.
Article.Abstract: Disclosing the brain areas responsible for the emergence of visual awareness and their timing of activation represents one of the major challenges in consciousness research. In particular, isolating the neural processes strictly related to consciousness from concurrent neural dynamics, either related to prerequisites or post-perceptual processing, has long engaged consciousness research. In this framework, the present study aims at unraveling the spatio-temporal dynamics underlying conscious vision by adopting a distinctive experimental design in which both awareness and motor response are manipulated, allowing the segregation of neural activity strictly related to awareness from response-related mechanisms. The study included 32 participants. We employed a GO/NOGO detection task, in which participants responded or withheld responding according to the experimental condition. Critically, during the performance of the task, participants' brain activity was recorded by means of Event-Related Optical Signal (EROS) technique, which provides accurate information about brain functions both from the temporal and spatial point of view within the covered regions, simultaneously. The combination of this experimental design with EROS recording enabled us to pinpoint the neural correlates underlying conscious vision and to disentangle them from processes related to the response. Extra-striate areas, specifically the Lateral Occipital Complex (LOC), showed greater awareness-related activity independently of motor response. Our findings support the view that LOC plays a key role as a proper correlate of visual awareness, rather than post-perceptual or response-related processes. They also show that awareness modulates motor activity only when a response is executed, clarifying how conscious perception influences downstream motor processing.
Article.Keywords: Fast Optical Imaging; No-Report paradigm; Visual awareness

Article.Title: Dystextia due to impairment in spatial operation on a smartphone: A case report
Article.Authors: Hayakawa H.; Hatakeyama M.; Otsuki M.; Takahashi T.; Tsuboguchi S.; Ishiguro T.; Ishihara T.; Onodera O.
Article.Abstract: Smartphone texting has become indispensable in modern life. Although dystextia (texting disability) has been reported, dystextia without aphasia or other cognitive impairment remains rare, and its pathophysiology is not fully understood. In Japanese text entry, the consonant is selected first on the screen, and the vowel is then determined by slide direction. Thus, accurate text input likely requires a sequence of processes, including segmentation of morae into consonants and vowels, followed by the spatial operation corresponding to each. Here, we report a patient with dystextia associated with impaired key-position and slide-direction processing. A 57-year-old right-handed Japanese woman developed difficulty with texting. Standard neuropsychological testing showed no aphasia, agraphia, or other cognitive impairment except for apraxia of speech and mild attention/executive dysfunction. Accordingly, dystextia was diagnosed. In addition, the patient had difficulty identifying keys corresponding to consonants and the slide direction corresponding to vowels. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a subcortical infarction in the left cerebral hemisphere. Single-photon emission tomography showed hypoperfusion, including in the left dorsolateral frontal lobe. The left frontal lobe is thought to contribute to spatial operations on digital devices. Therefore, diaschisis of the left dorsolateral frontal lobe secondary to the subcortical lesion may be associated with impairment of key-position and flick-direction processing, which may have contributed to dystextia in this patient.
Article.Keywords: Cerebral infarction; Diaschisis; Dystextia; Putamen; Smartphone

Article.Title: Beyond dual hubs: Task and aging shape taxonomic and thematic semantic relationships in the human brain
Article.Authors: Kuhnke P.; Martin S.; Chapman C.; Hartwigsen G.
Article.Abstract: Semantic knowledge about concepts and their relationships is central to human cognition. Taxonomic relationships link concepts belonging to the same category (e.g. dog and bear), while thematic relationships connect concepts co-occurring in the same events (e.g. dog and leash). The dual-hub theory proposes that taxonomic relations preferentially engage the anterior temporal lobe (ATL), whereas thematic relations preferentially involve the temporo-parietal cortex (TPC). However, it remains unclear whether taxonomic and thematic representations depend on the concurrent task and how they change with aging. The present fMRI study addressed these gaps by jointly investigating the effects of semantic relationship, task, and age on semantic processing. 41 young and 34 older adults performed taxonomic and thematic judgments on picture pairs that were taxonomically related, thematically related, or unrelated. Our results do not support the dual-hub theory: Both TPC and ATL preferentially responded to thematic over taxonomic relationships. Moreover, their activity was task-dependent. Semantic control regions flexibly responded to task-relevant semantic relations, while inhibiting task-irrelevant relations. Finally, aging was associated with a decline in domain-general and domain-specific semantic control, more bilateral ATL engagement, as well as behavioral and neural shifts from taxonomic towards thematic processing. Increased thematic activity was associated with higher accuracy but slower responses. These findings support accounts of age-related neural dedifferentiation and semanticization: Older adults require increased cognitive resources to maintain accuracy at a high level, but this comes at the cost of efficiency.
Article.Keywords: Aging; Concepts; Dedifferentiation; Semantic memory; fMRI

Article.Title: Beyond “more synchrony”: Frequency- and phase-specific effects of fronto-parietal theta tACS in enhancing episodic memory
Article.Authors: Aktürk T.; Sack A.
Article.Abstract: Theta oscillations support episodic memory and long-range communication between prefrontal and parietal regions. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) offers a way to test how theta dynamics influence memory. In our previous work, stimulation 1 Hz below the individual theta frequency (ITF-1) improved episodic memory, and this improvement was correlated with changes in fronto-parietal connectivity. Here, we tested whether dual-site fronto-parietal theta tACS produces frequency- and phase-specific aftereffects on episodic memory and theta-network dynamics. Neurotypical adults (N = 42) were assigned to ITF-1 or ITF+1 groups, with ITF estimated from pre-tACS resting-state EEG. Participants completed three counterbalanced sessions of dual-site tACS over left prefrontal and posterior-parietal locations: in-phase, anti-phase, and sham. Pre- and post-stimulation assessments included episodic memory measures, namely free recall and temporal order judgment (TOJ) with confidence ratings, as well as EEG recordings. TOJ accuracy showed a significant Session × Group interaction, driven by greater improvement in ITF-1 than ITF+1 following anti-phase stimulation. In ITF-1, confidence-accuracy discrimination (metacognitive separation) decreased after in-phase relative to anti-phase and sham. Resting-state, but not event-related, theta connectivity showed an anti-phase-specific divergence in fronto-parietal coupling, increasing in ITF-1 and decreasing in ITF+1. Within ITF-1 anti-phase, larger increases in resting-state fronto-parietal connectivity were associated with greater TOJ gains. These findings indicate phase-, frequency, and state-specific modulation of episodic memory and fronto-parietal theta networks by tACS. While the behavioral advantage of lower-frequency stimulation aligned with our hypothesis, the selective benefit of anti-phase stimulation suggests a more flexible, task-dependent reconfiguration of long-range connectivity rather than a uniform increase in synchrony.
Article.Keywords: Brain oscillations; Episodic memory; Phase-lag; Theta; Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS)

Article.Title: Grounding meaning in social and emotional experience: Challenges and opportunities
Article.Authors: Solana P.
Article.Abstract: Within the broader debate on how the mind and brain represent meaning, multiple representation theories have positioned social and emotional experience, along with their underlying neural systems, as key sources for concept grounding. In this article, I review the current evidence for this proposal and discuss several conceptual and methodological challenges, including the limited capacity of behavioral evidence to support this view, the difficulties associated with interpreting neuroimaging findings, the need for stronger causal evidence, and the importance of adopting open science practices. I argue that these limitations converge on a common concern: in their current form, many findings taken to support multiple representation theories of socio-affective grounding do not provide sufficiently diagnostic evidence to empirically adjudicate between them and competing accounts of semantic representation. In response, I outline a set of methodological recommendations and underexplored ideas that may help refine the theoretical framework, generate more decisive tests, and guide future research.
Article.Keywords: Conceptual knowledge; Embodied cognition; Emotion; Multiple representation theories; Social interaction

Article.Title: Resting-state and picture-naming EEG reveal aberrant connectomes and outcome-associated dysfunctomes in Cantonese post-stroke aphasia: A multi-frequency exploratory analysis
Article.Authors: Cheung C.; Kong A.
Article.Abstract: Post-stroke aphasia (PSA) is increasingly understood as a network disorder, yet its electrophysiological connectome has been characterized almost exclusively in stress-timed Indo-European languages, and rarely with phase-locking connectivity sampled across multiple frequency bands and recording states in the same cohort. We acquired 61-channel resting-state and overt picture-naming EEG in 31 chronic Cantonese-speaking individuals with aphasia and 14 demographically matched neurologically healthy controls, computed surface-Laplacian-transformed phase-locking-value connectivity in six canonical frequency bands (delta, theta, alpha, low-beta, high-beta, low-gamma), and used Network-based Statistic to identify within-group aberrant naming engagement subnetworks, between-group aberrant subnetwork, and outcome-associated dysfunctomes (subnetworks associated with seven clinical outcomes). Best-supported band × state dysfunctomes were identified through cross-band Akaike model comparison. Results showed that HC and PWA relied on qualitatively different oscillatory subnetworks to shift from rest into naming, with PWA displacing engagement into right-hemisphere and domain-general frontal regions and failing to disengage central alpha. Between-group contrasts highlighted slow-wave-dominant hyperconnective subnetworks in the canonical left temporal regions, reflecting passive cortical dysfunction. Outcome-associated dysfunctomes identified resting-state alpha as the best-fitting candidate for overall aphasia severity, spontaneous speech fluency and informativeness, overall naming, and confrontation naming, and resting-state low-beta as the best-fitting candidate for auditory comprehension. Together, the disrupted naming-engagement subnetworks and peri-lesional slow-wave aberrant connectomes offer mechanistic markers of aphasia-related network reorganization, while the resting-state alpha and low-beta dysfunctomes provide candidate targets to guide outcome-specific precision neuromodulation for PSA.
Article.Keywords: Aphasia; Cantonese; Connectome; EEG; Functional connectivity

Article.Title: The cross-modal spread of attention is highly automatic
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Ma F.; Zhou Y.; Xie J.; Zhou C.; Feng W.
Article.Abstract: Attention can spread across sensory modalities so that when attention is directed to the visual component of a multisensory object, its task-irrelevant auditory component will also be bestowed with enhanced processing, which operates in either a stimulus-driven or representation-driven manner contingent on whether the visual component is attended based on object category. To date, the visual-to-auditory attentional spreading has been widely hypothesized as an involuntary, automatic process, but this core hypothesis has yet to be tested. In particular, the supraliminal auditory components employed in prior studies might have received some sort of voluntary attention after being consciously detected, which impeded the examination of this hypothesis. The present event-related potential (ERP) study examined it in male and female humans (N = 30) by rendering bimodal objects' auditory components sub-threshold (and hence free from being actively attended) in an object-selective visual recognition task wherein ERP correlates of the representation-driven and stimulus-driven attentional spreading could be dissociated. Our ERP data showed reliable stimulus-driven (200-400 msec post-stimulus) and representation-driven (300-400 msec) attentional spreading to the sub-threshold auditory components, and the estimated neural generators of both included regions of the auditory cortex. Meanwhile, multivariate pattern analysis showed that the object categories could be decoded from ERPs to the inaudible sounds, confirming neural processing of these sounds in the absence of awareness. Collectively, these findings offer strong evidence that the visual-to-auditory attentional spreading is highly automatic, which paves the way for elucidating the psychophysiological mechanisms underlying cross-modal attentional spreading.
Article.Keywords: Auditory cortex; Automatic; Cross-modal attentional spreading; ERP; Involuntary; Multivariate pattern analysis; Sub-threshold sound

Article.Title: Neural signatures of harm aversion predict later willingness to exert effort for others' rewards
Article.Authors: Contreras-Huerta L.; Yu H.; Prosser A.; Lockwood P.; Rojas-Thomas F.; Crockett M.; Apps M.
Article.Abstract: Prosocial behaviours, central to human social life, are actions that benefit others. Two key domains are harm aversion, where individuals forgo personal gains to prevent harming others, and prosocial effort, which involves exerting effort to benefit others. Although previous studies suggest a relationship between these behaviours, it remains unclear whether neural responses in one domain can predict prosocial motivation in another. Here, we tested whether neural sensitivity to morally salient information in harm aversion could predict prosocial effort later. Participants (n = 66) completed two tasks: a harm aversion task during fMRI, in which they traded off monetary profit against delivering electric shocks to another person; and, one week later, a prosocial effort task outside the scanner, in which they decided whether rewards for others were worth the required physical effort. We focused on three regions implicated in cost-benefit decision-making and social cognition: the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), anterior insula (AI), and temporoparietal junction (TPJ). Behaviourally, greater harm aversion was associated with increased prosocial effort. Neurally, AI responses to others' harm predicted sensitivity to others' rewards in the effort task, consistent with a role in representing others' outcomes across positive and negative valences. By contrast, TPJ responses to profit from harming others predicted decreased sensitivity to others' rewards, suggesting a role in context-dependent valuation that may constrain prosocial behaviour. These findings reveal that neural responses to morally salient information in one context correlate with prosocial motivation in another, suggesting mechanisms that bridge moral sensitivity and effortful prosociality.
Article.Keywords: Anterior insula; Harm aversion; Prosocial effort; Social decision-making; Temporo-parietal junction

Article.Title: Who owns what? Comprehension of gender information in German possessive pronouns and determiners in aphasia
Article.Authors: Urbanczik G.; Lampe L.; Hanne S.; Arslan S.; Nickels L.
Article.Abstract: Cross-linguistic studies have demonstrated that people with (agrammatic) aphasia often exhibit difficulties in pronoun comprehension, but the role of gender marking has been largely overlooked and prior research has concentrated on only certain pronoun types. This study focused on gender cues in an understudied pronoun type, possessives, in German. German possessive determiners (e.g., seinmasc-efemGabelfem 'his fork') and possessive pronouns (e.g., ihrfem-efem 'hers') comprise two distinct gender cues, with a stem and a suffix providing information about who (possessor) is possessing what (possessee object), respectively. Twelve individuals with a variety of post-stroke aphasia classifications and 31 language-unimpaired controls completed a phrase-picture matching task with parallel eye-tracking requiring identification of the object that was congruent with the possessive form for possessor and possessee gender from an array of four. The off-line accuracy data revealed that the control group performed at ceiling, whereas all participants with aphasia showed difficulty identifying the correct possessee objects. Moreover, a subgroup of participants with aphasia also exhibited impairments in possessor identification. These distinct processing patterns were supported by the on-line eye fixation data. However, the two patterns were not associated with the type of aphasia. We place these findings in the context of previous research on pronoun processing and theoretical accounts of deficits in syntactic comprehension in aphasia. Moreover, we propose possible underlying processing impairments, including differences in the processing of grammatical and semantic gender, and implications for both clinical practice and research.
Article.Keywords: Comprehension; Gender agreement; Possessives; Post-stroke aphasia; Pronoun resolution; Sentence-picture matching; Visual-world eye-tracking

Article.Title: Salient affective scenes compete with concurrent visual responses in the absence of task demands
Article.Authors: Mirifar A.; Ayomen E.; Engle H.; Gilbert F.; Melville G.; Hammes E.; Lee A.; Mathews C.; Keil A.
Article.Abstract: Visual attention systems of the human brain resolve competition between concurrent inputs by prioritizing information that is relevant to an observer's goals, motives, and biological states. Research shows that concurrent distractors-especially emotionally salient stimuli-reduce task performance and visual responses to task cues. In many naturalistic viewing situations however, there are multiple competing cues with no obvious demarcation between task and distractor. The present study examined whether viewing two overlapping task-irrelevant stimulus streams produces emotion-dependent competition in visual cortex. Steady-state visual evoked potential (ssVEP) frequency tagging independently quantified visuocortical activity elicited by a picture (6.7 Hz) stream that overlapped with a central fixation-cross flickering at 15 Hz. We replicated established interference effects within the picture stream, showing that rapidly changing emotionally salient (pleasant and unpleasant) pictures elicited a strong reduction in the 6.7 Hz ssVEP envelope relative to neutral pictures. The 15 Hz ssVEP to the flickering fixation cross paralleled these findings, being more attenuated when competing with emotional, compared to neutral pictures. Change-point analyses indicated that competition latency varied with picture saliency, occurring earlier for pleasant and unpleasant than for neutral streams. Together, the present study suggests that visuocortical mass activity displays emotion-modulated competition effects in the absence of task demands.
Article.Keywords: Limited capacity systems; Steady-state visual evoked potentials; Time course of competition; Visual cortex

Article.Title: Neural correlates of phi and reverse-phi motion aftereffects: Temporal dynamics of ON–OFF pathway interactions
Article.Authors: Akyuz S.; Kafaligonul H.; Pavan A.
Article.Abstract: Sensory processing is dynamically shaped by neural adaptation, allowing the brain to adjust to recent sensory input. Phi and reverse-phi motion provide a framework for probing adaptive processes and ON-OFF pathway interactions in visual motion processing. We recorded 64-channel EEG while 30 participants completed a rapid motion-adaptation paradigm. Participants adapted to contrast-preserving phi motion or contrast-reversing reverse-phi motion for a short (188 msec) or long (752 msec) duration and then judged the direction of an ambiguous counterphase-flickering test grating. Behaviourally, adaptation duration primarily determined perceptual bias: short adaptation produced a modest same-direction, priming-like bias, whereas long adaptation produced an opposite-direction motion aftereffect. Test-locked event-related potentials (ERPs) revealed a robust Duration × Adaptation Type interaction over early posterior scalp regions (128-160 msec), primarily expressed in the N1 range. This interaction reflected greater differentiation between phi and reverse-phi adaptation after long than short adaptation. Exploratory whole-scalp topographic analyses indicated that the interaction involved changes in scalp-response configuration rather than uniform amplitude modulation. Adapter-locked analyses further showed that phi and reverse-phi motion elicited distinguishable ERP responses during the initial adaptation period and separable multivariate EEG patterns from approximately 50 msec after adapter onset, indicating early neural divergence between the two motion types. Together, these findings provide electrophysiological evidence that rapid adaptation to phi and reverse-phi motion leaves distinct neural traces that differentially influence subsequent processing of an ambiguous motion stimulus, advancing our understanding of rapid sensory adaptation and ON-OFF pathway interactions in human motion perception.
Article.Keywords: Electroencephalography; ON–OFF pathways; Rapid motion aftereffect; Reverse-phi motion; Visual adaptation

Article.Title: What counts as an error in nonword reading? A methods study of acquired phonological dyslexia
Article.Authors: Tree J.; Zakharchenko V.; Jones A.; Jones B.
Article.Abstract: Acquired phonological dyslexia (PD) is typically characterised by impaired nonword reading, but defining what constitutes a nonword reading "error" is challenging due to variability in how even healthy readers pronounce nonwords. This study examined different methods for classifying such errors using data from younger adults (n = 41), older adults (n = 25), and a case series of individuals with suspected acquired PD (n = 6). Three scoring approaches were compared: (1) a mode-response accuracy method, which matches responses to the most common pronunciation; (2) an average response-overlap method, which assesses similarity to the full distribution of control responses; and (3) a singularly distinct response count, which identifies responses not produced by any other participant. Results showed that older adults exhibited greater variability than younger adults across all measures, suggesting that age significantly affects nonword reading performance. This highlights an important methodological issue: using younger normative data to assess older individuals may overestimate impairment. In the patient group, all three scoring methods broadly agreed in ranking severity across cases. However, the singularly distinct response metric provided clearer separation between patients and controls and captured a wider range of impairment severity. It also revealed that unique responses are relatively common even among typical readers, an underexplored finding. Overall, the study supports the importance of age-appropriate norms and more nuanced, response-level scoring methods in assessing acquired PD, with singularly distinct responses offering a potentially sensitive marker of disruption.
Article.Keywords: Acquired dyslexia nonword reading

Article.Title: Decoding the time course of intonation planning
Article.Authors: Erden H.; Chen Y.; Meyer A.; van der Burght C.
Article.Abstract: The temporal relationship between sentence-level intonation planning and word-level phonological encoding remains poorly understood. Prosody-first accounts predict that an abstract intonation frame is established before lexical information is retrieved, whereas prosody-last accounts predict that intonation is encoded after lexical information. The present study used EEG combined with time-resolved multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) to investigate when intonation planning occurs relative to other levels of linguistic encoding during spoken word production. Thirty native Dutch speakers named pictures of simple nouns using two different intonation contours, as either questions or exclamations. The target words were disyllabic Dutch nouns that varied in animacy, lexical stress, and manner and place of articulation of the first phoneme. Intonation became decodable after animacy and around the same time as place of articulation. Exploratory analyses revealed that intonation decoding emerged earlier for words with word-final than word-initial stress, suggesting that the temporal profile of intonation planning is shaped by the word's stress pattern. On a methodological level, these findings demonstrate that intonation planning is neurally decodable in an overt production context using EEG. The implications for theories of language production are that sentence-level and word-level prosody closely interact and evolve together during planning rather than being encoded independently.
Article.Keywords: Intonation; Lexical stress; MVPA; Prosody; Speech production

Article.Title: How right dorsomedial lesions lead to neglect: A functional network-level framework
Article.Authors: Grande E.; Baldassarre A.; Committeri G.; Bartolo A.; Esposito V.; Ciavarro M.
Article.Abstract: Spatial neglect-a disorder characterized by impaired exploration of contralesional space-has only recently been reported following lesions to dorsomedial regions of the right hemisphere. Consequently, the mechanisms underlying the occurrence of neglect in this context remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigated whether alterations in functional connectivity could account for this phenomenon by longitudinally assessing resting-state fMRI in a patient before and after tumor resection. A 71-year-old male underwent resection of an oligodendroglioma involving the right superior frontal gyrus and cingulum. Neuropsychological assessment and resting-state fMRI were acquired before and after surgery. Peripersonal and personal neglect were assessed with two different cancellation tests and the Comb and Razor Test (CRT). System Segregation (SyS), i.e., the balance of within and between network functional connectivity, was computed at both whole-brain and network-specific levels and compared with 20 age-matched healthy controls using Crawford's modified t-test. While no sign of neglect was observed preoperatively, the patient exhibited both peripersonal and personal neglect after surgery. Compared to controls, postoperative data revealed a significant reduction in whole-brain SyS (p < .001). At the network level, the ventral attention network (VAN) showed preserved segregation preoperatively but a marked postoperative decrease (p < .001). These findings show, for the first time, that the clinical manifestation of neglect after right dorsomedial regions may be explained by lesion-induced alterations in large-scale functional connectivity. In particular, reduced VAN segregation may reflect impaired functional differentiation underlying deficits in spatial attention, thereby shedding light on the mechanisms underlying dorsomedial lesions neglect presentation.
Article.Keywords: Glioma; Graph-theory; Neglect; Resting-state fMRI; Supplementary motor area

Article.Title: When rhythm guides speech production: Insights from Parkinson's disease and spinocerebellar ataxia
Article.Authors: Fumel J.; Mairano P.; Ott L.; Contreras Roa L.; Devos D.; Moreau C.; Basirat A.
Article.Abstract: Rhythmic auditory exposure modulates subsequent speech processing, yet its effect on speech production remains poorly understood. People with Parkinson's disease (PD) or spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) suffer from dysarthria, for which there is no treatment. Using a rhythmic priming approach, we investigated whether brief rhythmic primes modulate speech production and facilitate it in people with PD and SCA considered here as clinical models of basal ganglia dysfunction and cerebellar dysfunction, respectively. Fifty-eight native French speakers (20 controls, 24 people with PD, 14 people with SCA) read sentences following a regular prime, an irregular prime, or silence. We measured accuracy and the temporal features of speech production including speech initiation time, speech rate, and rhythmic metrics. Bayesian mixed-effects models were used for the statistical analyses of these outputs. Accuracy showed no effect of rhythmic priming. Regular primes consistently shortened speech initiation time in all populations, but the benefit of regular primes was smaller in people with PD than in controls. In People with SCA, speech rate decreased after regular primes. The impact of rhythmic priming on rhythmic metrics was limited. Together, these results indicate that perception-to-production rhythmic priming mainly affects global, rather than fine-grained, timing control of speech during speech production. They also shed light on the implications of the basal ganglia and cerebellum in the modulation of speech by rhythm. They also provide insights for speech production models, which currently lack an explicit mechanism for external rhythmic inputs. Clinically, they help inform rhythm-based speech and language therapy methods.
Article.Keywords: Speech production; basal ganglia; cerebellum; perception-production link; rhythm

Article.Title: Two reading routes, two white matter tracts: Evidence from dyslexia following brain tumors
Article.Authors: Kahana Levy N.; Friedmann N.; Singer N.; Gurevitch G.; Arzi M.; Bergman L.; Azolai L.; Yogev R.; Dunetz G.; Richetta C.; Shahar T.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive models propose that reading aloud relies on two routes, a lexical route for familiar word recognition and a sublexical route for graphene-to-phoneme conversion. Selective disruption of these routes results in surface or phonological dyslexia, respectively. Although the dual route model is well supported behaviorally, its white matter substrates remain incompletely characterized. This study examined the anatomical correlates of acquired lexical and sublexical reading impairments in patients with high-grade glioma in the dominant hemisphere. Thirty-seven patients underwent diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and a comprehensive reading battery. Reading aloud of regular and irregular words, and pseudowords was used to classify patients as having intact reading, surface dyslexia or phonological dyslexia, based on normative criteria. Six language-related white matter tracts were reconstructed individually for each patient using subject-specific tractography. Each tract was then systematically segmented along its longitudinal axis, allowing diffusion parameters to be extracted from anatomically defined subsegments. Lesion-tract overlap measures were computed to quantify focal tract involvement. Fourteen patients exhibited impaired sublexical reading, 12 impaired lexical reading, and 11 intact reading. Deficits in the sublexical route were more frequent among patients with arcuate fasciculus lesion overlap, and sublexical error rates correlated with global tract integrity. Deficits in the lexical route were associated with the posterior temporal segment of the inferior longitudinal fasciculus, where surface dyslexia errors correlated with reduced fractional anisotropy. In contrast, uncinate fasciculus involvement was more frequent among patients with intact reading, indicating it does not contribute critically to either reading route. These findings provide a fine-grained structure-function mapping of the dual route reading model onto white matter pathways.
Article.Keywords: Arcuate fasciculus (AF); Brain tumor; Dyslexia; Inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF); Reading; White Matter Tracts

Article.Title: Mean position of hits in unilateral spatial neglect: An empirical validation
Article.Authors: De Luca M.; Ciurli M.; Matano A.; Nardo D.
Article.Abstract: Numerical indices used to detect and quantify neglect in cancellation tests have traditionally relied on omissions count, which may be misleading, as the derived laterality indices (LIs) do not capture the spatial continuum of responses. More recent approaches (e.g., Mean Position of Hits, MPH) quantify neglect based on the spatial position of hits. The MPH approach relies on a theoretically-founded statistical model, which returns a neglect index and a diagnostic label without the need for a control sample and cut-offs. However, such an approach has not yet been empirically validated in patients. Here, we applied the MPH to three common cancellation tests (Letters, Stars, and Lines) in a consecutive sample of right-brain-damaged stroke patients (n = 173) and determined its diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, and its ability to quantify neglect severity against an independent reference standard that combines conventional neuropsychological tests (excluding the three cancellation tests) and a structured clinical observation. Sensitivity and specificity of the MPH were 88.6% and 84.1% for Letters, 87.1% and 95.3% for Stars, 65.2% and 97.7% for Lines. We also compared the MPH diagnostic accuracy with that of two alternative procedures based on a classical cut-off approach (MPH with cut-offs and LIs). Such alternative procedures yielded comparable diagnostic accuracy. Regression analyses showed that the MPH index corresponded more closely to clinical ratings of neglect severity than LIs. Overall, our results show that the MPH is a valid and user-friendly approach for both clinical assessment and research applications, which allows comparisons across time, settings, and cancellation tests.
Article.Keywords: Cancellation; Diagnosis; Neglect; Sensitivity; Severity

Article.Title: Effects of mind-wandering on cognitive and neural processes: Identifying specific impairments in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
Article.Authors: Horáková G.; Weibel S.; Tissot U.; Pham B.; Costache M.; Bonnefond A.
Article.Abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by symptoms of inattention and/or impulsivity/hyperactivity. Although not a core symptom, excessive mind-wandering (MW) is commonly associated with the disorder and may contribute to symptoms as well as performance deficits observed in these patients.
